Yommeh ! Hawker style seafood with restaurant level price (beware of how much you order!) . I'd say the food was great. For a group of six we ate like kings.  Tried the grilled stingray, oyster omelette (so good!), chilli squid, chilli clams, kang kung belacan, beansprouts, grilled chicken wings, and a few others. The dishes were quite delicious. Everything went inside my mouth without any problems. I'd say go with a group of friends to be able to order more.

I think my expectations were too high for the place, and maybe I was tired, but I just found newton a bit too aggressive, noticeably more expensive, and lacking diversity in the menu options. Disclaimer: We did go on Vesak day and some stalls were closed.We went with a mee goreng, a lemon chicken (seemed pricey at $15?), and an oyster sauce green vege dish. Had the bean curd for dessert. Everything was just average I thought. The lemon chicken probably the best dish but I should hope so at $15 in a hawker centre! I would have liked to have seen some more noodle and rice options...maybe I hadn't done my research well enough? Because I know this place gets good kudos. It was the hard sell from the stall owners that really put me off though.Meh, won't be back.
An easy way to get all the local delights under 1 roof- indian rojak, BBQ stingray, murtabak, satay, etc. It's overpriced, there're too many tourists, but it's still tasty and convenient

With endless food options in Singapore, Newton Food Centre feels pretty mediocre.  As with any other hawker centre (aka food courts), Newton has plenty of seating, a decent variety of food, and prices are pretty standard.  It's outdoor seating, so it might not be the first place I'd choose if it's raining or if it's sweltering - just a thought. I just don't really like hawker centers ha!
Very interesting. Lots of Singapore street food and seafood. Is a great tourist destination.

I visited Newton Hawker Center on 26th Feb and at 730pm, the car park was almost full and the parking attendant was making his rounds and issuing parking fines! Do note, they do not have a gantry system, so have your parking coupons ready!There are a lot of BBQ Seafood stalls in Newton and most of them sell the same stuff. Do note that though they tout and push each shop, every customer has the right to say NO! The touters get commission based on what they sell to you. To avoid getting cheated, pay upon ordering and INSIST so, else you might end up with a 3 digit bill at the end of your meal, with no explanation.Here's a review of the food we shared amongst 6 people, 4 of which were yelpers :)The Ocean BBQ  #01-016 We just picked the stall we sat right next too, but I did notice that the stalls facing the inner circle seemed to be more popular. This ocean BBQ, is one of the outside stalls facing the car park.1. Lemon Chicken $15I loved lemon chicken and we ordered this. Expecting to be a thick chicken cutlet, I was surprised to see it served as fried cubed chicken. Some pieces were of the thigh meat, hence more flavourful, some pieces were breast meat and very dry. The sauce itself was decent, very lemony and you can taste the slight blend of honey. But I guess having cubed-sized chicken makes it easier for sharing.2. Sambal Singray $15Jie Ying mentioned that the sambal was nice and it was! It was slightly sweet and for someone like me who doesn't eat spicy. This was the perfect sambal stingray for me! The stingray was meaty and the meat was easily separated from the bones. 3. Sambal SotongA similar sauce from the stingray was stir fried with the sotong, hence making the sotong abit sweet. The sotong tasted fresh and the serving was big enough for the 6 of us to share. Chances is, I might hit this stall up again, the next time I'm here. Definitely in love with their sambal!Bedok 85 Fried Oyster #01-0401. Oyster Omelette $5They were very generous with the oysters, The egg was crispy on the top layer, but on the bottom layer, it was soggy and was very mushy. I didn't quite like it in the end. If you want really good oyster omelette, try Kim Keat at Bradell.2. Carrot Cake White/black $4Even though their sign boards still says the carrot cakes are sold in $3 portions, They have increased their prices. The black had alot more egg and was sweet. The white wasn't crispy and tasted bland. Overall, another upsetting local dishKwang Huat #01-015 Steffenie was patiently waiting for this stall to open at 745pm! And at 730pm the owners were ready to take orders, but we didn't get our food till about 750pm.1. Hokkien Prawn Mee $5For $5, you get a satisfying plate of prawn mee with a lot of gravy, and 4 big prawns. The gravy is truly tasty and yummy. Although you can tell they did not use any lard, so it's missing that special taste. Some sotong and egg is what you get with the prawn mee, no three-layer pork meat either. I guess this stall is now muslim-friendly. 2. Char Kway Teow This was a rather OK dish at best. I couldn't taste the wok-hei and there were a lot of cockles and no other ingredients, there were like 2 slices of 50 cent coin sized fish cakes.. I do not like cockles, so I found this very upsetting. Char Kway teow to me is my most favourite dish in Singapore but I wouldn't come back here for this.Singa Cafe #01-014 Their sugar juice drinks are $1.50 and can drinks are priced at $1.50. Very reasonable pricingSoursop Juice $2I loved that their soursop juice was full of soursup meat. The drink was served with a plastic spoon, which you will need to scoop up the fruit.For those unknown to the benefits of soursop.Soursop contains a number of natural substances that have biological benefits such as, relieve stomach distress, fever, pain and respiratory problems such as cough and asthma.TKR #01-030 After walking around, we realized the prices were standard for the chicken wings $1.30 and 60cents per satay. We decided to go with TKR as it was a chinese stall, which meant they sold pork satay!1. Pork/chicken/mutton Satay 60 cents eachWe ordered 10 sticks of pork, 10 sticks of chicken and 10 sticks of mutton which added up to $18, and they gave us 5 bowls of satay sauce. The pork satay had alot of fats in them, which for me, I actually enjoyed. For the health conscious, you might want to just take the chicken sticks, which were more tender. The mutton was considerably drier than the chicken and pork, but it didn't have the weird smell. So I was okay with it.2. BBQ Chicken wings $1.30 eachThe chicken wings were pretty good. I enjoyed the crispy roasted skin. The meat was very juicy and I felt that for BBQ chicken wings, these weren't too oily and is a good choice for me! I've had BBQ chicken wings dripping with oil and that's usually the reason why I avoid them.They were presented very nicely on the styrofoam plate. They definitely gave some thought into present

The vendors here are AGGRESSIVE.  Every one sells more or less the same items but beware of getting ripped off.Some things I would recommend:-Freshly squeezed juice (soursop since you can't get that in the states)-Cereal prawns-Oyster pancake-Fish cake wrapped in a leaf-Chicken skewers-Chicken wingsEven though it's a hawker center, I wouldn't expect to pay any less than you would at a normal restaurant.  Food is still yummy though.

There are just too many good food centers in Singapore, with top notch hawkers dishing out food you will always go back for, despite a long line. With such competition around, Newton Circus is just one of many and has the misfortune to be seen as a tourist trap. It did not help that there used to be touts (maybe there still are?) from the seafood stalls (usually) targeting and annoying the diners who may just want to browse first before deciding on what to order. The only good thing about Newton Circus is that it is opened till very late at night and used to be my one of my "go to" places for supper after clubbing. I never knew it is also open in the day time until a few years ago. I think day time stalls cater more to the people working or studying in the area, as well as those heading to Malaysia. There is a causeway link bus leaving from the car park which takes people across to JB. So in the wee hours of the morning, at least one stall will be open (the bak chor mee stall facing the car park is open 24 hours) to serve customers who need sustenance before their trip to Malaysia or heading to work. By 8 am, more stalls will be open (mostly those facing the car park) - bak chor mee stall, Malay stall and a few drinks stall. From 11 am, the stalls on the row facing the car park will all be open, plus a few other stalls facing the inner court yard area, to cater to the lunch crowd. The seafood and bbq chicken wings stalls are mostly open in the evening. The stalls I usually frequent:Fish soup: all the 3 stalls are good with fresh fish. - stall facing car park, next to Thai stall -- very fresh fish slices but cost much more than the others. Also serve tang hoon fish ball soup.- stall facing car park, towards the end near Malay stall -- better for fried fish soup with milk- stall behind of the row facing car park, next to Indian drinks stall -- also food for fresh fish slice soup with no milk. Duck stall (yu kee I think) facing car park -- one my of favorite place for duck porridge (only $3 which is cheap for Newton pricing) and duck kway teow or set. The soup is herbal and the stallholder is very generous about giving refills. The chili is fantastic with fried crispy ikan bilis in it. For the Malay stalls, I prefer the corner one nearer to the bus stop along Bukit Timah road. It has one of the cheapest nasi padang around. The corner Malay stall facing the car park is pricier and generally attracts more customers because of the location. The sardine curry puff and fried chicken wing are good though. The popiah stall facing the car park is Hokkien style and is something of an acquired preference. I only like it after trying it a few times. You need to order a minimum of 2 rolls and is open a bit later in the day, after 1230 pm or so. The Thai stall is open closer to 12 pm and is very popular. You will need to wait for a while. It has pretty good Thai food like the usual pad thai, basil chicken rice, etc. The tom yam soup is not that nice though. The nasi lemak stall near the Thai food is fairly new and is overpriced and not that good. For a small plate of fried beehoon with a tiny piece of luncheon meat, it cost $3. The chili is of the Maggi variety. The highly recommended fried chicken is also not worth it. Just normal. Fruit juice and fresh fruits are better at the stall facing the car park. Pricing is ok too, when compared to Orchard area. Hot and Cold Dessert stall facing the car park is another hot favorite for many. Pricing is also of the affordable type, cheaper than food court in the malls. In general, I think the stalls which are opened during the day has reasonable hawker pricing and you will not think they are overpriced at all. I think the bad rep for Newton Circus hawkers about over-charging is usually referred to the seafood BBQ stalls or those stalls which are open at night.

Pretty good hawker center, I liked that it is just around the corner from the MRT station.Came on Sunday morning and it was pretty dead but this was my first time seeing places offer Sting Ray so that was impressive. $12 is quite a splurge but I really enjoyed it, tasty and not greasy at all like your typical hawker fare.It was annoying that I could only find lemon tea in cans. What's that all about?

Well, I simply could not get enough of these food halls, so when I got off the MRT station at Newton to visit a street named after my namesake, I knew I had to go and check this place out. Okay, it is a bit out of the way, and there is nothing around here that I am aware of that would cause anybody to come here (unless it is to check out the hawker's market) but it was still worth it. Well, when I was here it was still reasonably early on a Monday morning, so most of the shops were closed, but there were still enough for me to partake in some of the offerings. As can be expected, there are quite a few stall, and even though it was raining, there were still enough undercover seats for me to sit at.

If you're visiting Singapore, you can't miss out on going to a hawker center. Now this one here is more tourist oriented since it's near the touristy area. This means that1. It's more pricey2. You don't get as much The stalls here sell a variety of Singaporean foods. When you first come in you just sit down on a table and either go up to a stall and order something or people will come up to you. They're pretty aggressive in selling their food. Some sellers will help you find a table (but they expect that you buy food from their stall in return). You might as well let them do the work for you though. At worst they'll just be a bit unhappy.Food that you should try here: 1. Oyster Pancake - A egg like mixture with fresh oysters. 2. Sugar Cane with Lemon (Drink) - freshly ground sugar cane with lemon yum. 3. Chili Crab4. Stingray - If you can tolerate spiciness make sure to smear the entire thing with chili. It's not very flavorful by itself.

Newton Circus - the famous food centre for tourists. Prices here are definitely higher than your typical hawker centre/ neighborhood food centre due to it being a popular tourist destination. Nonetheless, I wouldnt say that the quality of food is compromised.Service here is surprisingly good. There are stall helpers helping you find a table... but they may also pressure you to ordering from them. They are pretty active in coming up to you and asking for your order, but you can simply say no. Ventilation here is also decent. Close proximity to town, so I definitely recommend bringing foreign friends here to try the local fare, especially since Gluttons Bay can get really crowded at times.

My bf and I came here on a Tuesday afternoon to check out a real hawker center and were surprised to find it a little bit dead with many stalls closed.  I thought it would be bustling all day long, but perhaps all the action takes place at night?I was really hesitant at first, because the vendors were really pushy, and the place looked a bit run-down and dirty, but we settled on a guy who waved a wriggly crab at us.  We ordered a chili crab (male, because we weren't quite sure how to eat a female), spicy kang kong, black pepper beef, fried rice, and a large bottle of Tiger beer to share.Surprisingly, the food was DELICIOUS.  I normally don't like the taste of chili, but the crab was really fresh and yummy.  There is something to be said for seafood that is still alive when you order it.My only regret is that we omitted the mantou (steamed bread) due to the fried rice order.  We should have gotten mantou to sop up all the chili crab sauce.So lesson learned:  Looks may be deceiving.  Despite the initial letdown due to the grungy exterior and plastic and styrofoam dishware, the food turned out to be fantastic!!  AND DON'T FORGET THE MANTOU!!!

Hawker food is a specialty that one has to try when coming to Singapore. Newton Food Center is one of those places that is located near touristic areas, so it's not 100% the real deal (you get that if you have locals taking you by car to more distant food centers), but it's very close to the way it should be.I have always found the food to be great, and I do not complain about prices being a little higher than the standard Hawker food places, after all I am not a local and it's cheaper than eating in other restaurants. "Must tries" are the stingray, the sugar cane drinks, the chili crabs, but generally as you pick the food that is served to you, anything that picks your fancy is a good choice!

Newton Food Center used to be so good. When I was growing up, they had one of the best of everything that represented Singapore hawker scene. Now it's a sucky tourist destination.Part of the reason is that they stopped using pork lard in their cooking. This is to cater to the huge influx of Muslim tourist from the region.Really nothing against Muslims, just saying the food isn't the same. Pork lard is essential in Chinese cooking. Like ghee is to Indian cooking. We have a saying, "No lard, no good".But the main reason is the high rental cost. Lots of the original hawkers left and sub-leased the stall.There's still a few good stalls but most of them is crap. Go to Old Airport or East Coast Lagoon instead.

I did a yelp to see what restaurants were nearby. This popped up as being very close to our hotel at the Sheraton Towers.  Hubby was under the weather as he caught a bad cold after our two week cruise that started and ended in Singapore.  I thought to order room service but did I want to pay $25 SGD for a burger?So I drag hubby along to Newton's.  Now this is what hawking food is all about.  Menus being pushed under our noses.   Eat here.  Eat here.  We settled on a noodle place.  We ordered and he asked what table number are we at.  We asked table number?  The idea is to grab a table first.  You pay after your food is brought to you.  What I noticed later about most food courts including this one is that there are sinks where you can wash your hands before and after you eat.  This food court is the epitome of all food courts.  Read about it in Wikipedia.

Came here in my first night at Singapore and I enjoyed a lot of its night market food style. You can order multiple items from most of the stalls. These are: meat, seafood, and other skewers; sausage; mantis; fried shrimp; beer; sugar cane juice; veggies; naans; fried noodles; and many more. However, the food can be a bit greasy if you are not used to it. In addition, there can be fight for seating from time to time as the number of seating can be very limited. But these shouldn't hold you back from coming to this place to eat a wonderful dinner.

While Newton tends to be a bit more touristy than other hawker centers, I love the cereal prawn and don't mind the constant beckoning from the other aunties and uncles attending to their stalls ;). Be prepared though, if heckling bothers you go elsewhere.Come with friends and enjoy an assortment of dishes from the various stalls. It's conveniently located near an MRT station too.

Much better hawkers in Singapore, bait and switch , buy the photos of food and eat elsewhere. Lau pa Sat , main tourist trap. But it's also in middle of central business district packed with locals. Much better food and value.

Consistent and delicious Chicken or Tofu Laksa and the Mini wok noodle with side of soup. You must give this place a try during breakfast, lunch, and dinner time. Dinner time this center is packed with people from local to tourists. The Fish soup stall is to die for too which is about 3 stalls to the left of the Chicken Laksa stall.It's worth coming here at the Newton subway stop.

Newton Hawker Centre is one of the larger centres in Singapore with lots of food options to choose from. It is also the centre with more staff approaching patrons with menus and one to one sales techniques. I opted for the imfamous Soon Wah Fishball and Bee Heng Popiah! Soon Wah Fishballs are made in the traditional Teochew way. Each ball is handmade, kneaded for bounce and airyness. Fish meat is gentlely folded in, thereafter. Fish dumplings (probably best fish dumplings in Singapore and probably in life) are made from fish paste wrappers with meat filling. Each bowl is topped with crispy lard for texture and flavour! Yum! Soon Wah deserves to be in the Fishballs hall of fame!Bee Heng Popiah is also a legend in this hawker centre. Soft thin crepes are filled with combination of ingredients including bean a sprouts, lettuce leaves etc. It is sweet and savory with crisp texture. This centre is what hawker legends are made of! If you love food, you must visit Newton Hawker Centre!

Went here last night... although tired and very sleep deprived... the star attraction of the night was the crab! Was very tempted to order soooo much more... Chillie Crab $36SG for 700gram from seafood alliance... $3 for the marn tdou bun.. my ping ting is non existent..  it was medium size crab enough for 2.  Meat was fresh nice and firm. But definitely can not compare to the Australian Darwin mud crab!!! which is more flavourful. Well IMHO was good but i don't think is the best... the sauce / gravy was a bit too sweat.. over the years of coming in and out of SG I still haven't found a "WOW" Have been coming here on and off over the years and SG and I still haven't found a place that I can say... YEP I WOULD DEFINITELY RETURN for the crab. Any friendly yelpers out there with good suggestions... ideas most welcomed! :)) Chicken wing... wooooah!!! I'd come back for that alone!! Maaaan it was right size and had the chargrill flavour.. add the lime provided and a little dip into that sauce!!! Wooow! Overall it was a great experience washed down with a large bottle of Tiger for $7.50SG!! The growling jungle beats playing in my stomach due to hunger was very quickly replaced by carnivale!!!!

Recently renovated. Lots of stalls with variety of foods. Got the pepper crab but didnt enjoy the flavour - the meat itself was good however. The satay beef and chicken was their best food item in my opinion

Great hawker center, definitely one of my favorites. There are quite a few stalls here. I had some satay, chicken noodle dish, samosas and mango snow ice (my favorite!). Everything was so yummy. I liked this place because you gave them your table number and they would deliver the food to you. Like most hawker centers this one is pretty inexpensive and there's some great people watching. Overall, a good afternoon spent, definitely recommend a stop by, it's right near the Newtown metro stop.
My favorite was oyster omelette from heng stall no.28 and bbq stingray from all best grilled seafood stall no.39..CONCLUSION = RECOMMENDED!!

Eeeeep. Not the nicest hawker centre around, and DEFINITELY not a good hawker centre for a vegetarian!I came here to meet friends and figured I'd be able to find at least one or two things suitable to eat, because so far Singapore has been ridiculous easy for me to navigate as a vegan. But hawker centres can be trickier, and this one was definitely the least vegan-friendly (let alone vegetarian-friendly) hawker centre that I came across.Plus I felt hassled by all the food vendors. I mean, yeah, I get it, they're hawkers, they're gonna hawk -- but they all seemed more aggressive here than anywhere else. I walked around in endless circles, trying to find something (ANYTHING!) non-meat and non-seafood to eat, and as a white person I kept getting asked, "You want fried rice? You want fried rice?" It was kinda funny but mildly insulting at the same time. Just because I'm white doesn't mean I want plain fried rice because I can't handle spicy or exotic foods.Finally, I grabbed a lychee drink (overpriced) and managed to find one lonely vegetarian plate on offer at an Indian stall. It was a curry (I specified no ghee and they grunted something that I assumed was acquiescence -- maybe they don't use much ghee here, I dunno). It was super-spicy (thank God someone sensed that my pasty complexion belies a spice-loving interior -- or more likely they just didn't care). It was actually pretty yummy, but more expensive than anticipated, and the lady that made it was sweating buckets over the stove, rings of sweat under her armpits, so I felt like my dish may have come with a tangy human-sweat aftertaste, but whatever.There were also pillars of smoke billowing everywhere, which was making a lot of people (I'm talking actual locals, not precious tourists) cough and wave their tissues in the air in front of them.Really not a pleasant hawker centre experience. There are better ones in Singapore. ESPECIALLY if you're vegetarian (much less vegan).

Decent hawker right off the Newton MRT. I like that it is open-air and spacious. The soliciting can get a bit annoying but a strong "no" gets the message across in most cases. Because of its close proximity to Orchard Road, it's a good option for a cheap meal.

This food center became my girlfriend and my local normal spot. There was even a week where we came here every night for the entire week, we just love it here so much.My favorite stalls are #43 for their grilled black pepper tiger prawns and pretty much all of their seafood and fried rice, and stall #46 for their Indian food. Sometimes I get the tiger prawns without any topping and dip it in the Butter chicken curry. The curry from stall #46 is surprisingly sweet and many of my friends who don't like curry can actually eat this one with some good naan bread from them.Love it here and will keep coming back!

I was super excited to land in Singapore and couldn't wait to hit up some of the local eatery.  My taxi driver suggested I go to Newton as we passed by because that's where all the locals eat and since it was pretty much within walking distance from the hotel I thought why not?My first impression of SGP was man it's hella hot and humid here!  It's crazy to walk outside in the sun but my stomach was leading the way.  It was my first introduction to what is known as "Hawker stands".  These are small restaurants the size of a public storage shed that sells cooked food for cheap prices (cash only) while you dine on shared tables in the courtyard.  All the food prices are all competitive so other than looking for a specific dish, there's no real need to compare prices.  I really wanted to try these gigantic prawns and saw them advertised at $8/100 grams.  Ok gimme two and and a small plate of Cha Kway Teow.  My total came to $37 SGP which equates to about $27 usd.  Later when I was introduced to the better hawker stands, I realized how much I been ripped off by Newton.  The locals pay no more than say $15 SGP and that includes a drink!  My friends told me that Newton is frequented by tourists which was the exact opposite from what the taxi driver told me.  There are over 100 Hawker Centers in Singapore and once I was introduced to these better ones, I would never think of coming back here for overpriced food.

My favourite food court. An open space with several tiny stalls offering their specialties. Good place to enjoy traditional seafood in many varieties. Also satay is a "must have" at Newton Circus Food Centre. Explore this lovely place in the evening. It is really enjoyable.

This is actually one of my least favorite hawker centers and it has little to do with the quality of the food. Many of the stalls here do a great job and serve very good food and I like the round design of the place which gives a nice overview.The issue here is however that people constantly bother you and trying to get you to order stuff. I mean if I sit with my food I do not want to be interrupted every 30 seconds by some placing a menu in front of me, asking me to order or even worse just trying to place a plate in front of me and pretend I ordered it. I was actually a bit surprised as I even had to tell one guy really harshly to stop bothering us. Also then saw the same guy screw some tourists that did not have the same sense out of 25 SGD for a plate of carrot cake.Perhaps unfair to all the good places here but I just find myself annoyed when I go here. I still occasionally go as friends live close by but then we usually take the food with us to avoid all the people bothering us.
I went here for dinner. I ordered the kurobota pork katsu. The taste was good. The cabbage salad is unlimited refill. The service was okayCONCLUSION = RECOMMENDED!!

Reliably good tonkatsu. A little better than Saboten, in my opinion. Pork loin was light but tasty, the curry is $3 extra and a great addition, sweet without being overwhelming. Free flow cabbage and tea was a nice touch.

The Kurobota tonkatsu is good, but if you crave tonkatsu, the best place is Tonkatsu by Ma Maison at Mandarin Gallery across the street (not to be confused with the Ma Maison outlet just opposite)! They have more choices, and the rice (choice of brown or white) and miso soup - both with unlimited refills along with the cabbage - are several levels better! The different promotions are kind of rearrangements of the same stuff, not much savings.

I had lunch here a few times with my friend during our stay in Singapore. Weekday lunch menu is affordable and not really crowded. Has big portions. Inside is tender, outside is so crispy. I enjoyed their katsu! Comes with sesame seeds in mortar and pestle. So you can choose to grind it coarse or fine. It suppose to mix the sesame seeds with the Tonkatsu sauce. Casual place to enjoy lunch with affordable prices.

Maybe it was a Monday evening, maybe it was the end of the night but regardless, I just didn't get a good dining experience here. On the outside it is set up well. Tonkatsu, Kagoshima Black Pork. Tick. Roasted sesame. Tick. Free flow rice and cabbage. Tick some more. This looks like it could be very lovely..I decided I wanted it all and ordered the Hire & Rosu Katsu set, while my partner ordered the Hire Katsu Don. Anticipation. Especially since many reviews have said this was an institution. Maybe my expectations were too high. Or the Monday /end of the night reasoning again. The server brought out the plates and it went downhill from there. Rice was best described as soggy or mushy. Not eloquent at all but that's how I would describe it. The lettuce was on the side which was ok. Except when you've had it at other establishments in a lovely chilled separate bowl. The katsu was over breaded. The breading had a roughness to it which cut into the roof of my mouth. Orange slices, placed on our table before we had finished eating. Like I said, maybe it was a Monday evening, maybe it was the end of the day and everyone wanted to call it a night.Overall, not terribly exciting. I would suggest you look elsewhere. There are many options available and this is not one I'd recommend.

extremely average tonkatsu joint. they really need more kurobuta options besides just loin. if you are expecting mai-sen quality tonkatsu, this is definitely not it, but then again, only mai-sen is mai-sen quality. for what you can expect to find in SG, this is probably as good as it gets.their crab croquette was utterly lacking in crabbiness, flavor, and umai-ness. the tonkatsu itself is relatively flavorful and crispy, but lacked the extra light crunch that top tier tonkatsu joints deliver. their curry is also decent, but nothing to write home about. i've had better curry at your neighborhood ringer hut (the equivalent of a denny's in japan, if they didn't already have denny's in japan).

Flavouring aside, perhaps one has a greater desire for a tantalising texture in pursuit of attaining an exceptional meal experience. Any good piece of meat is capable of cropping up a challenging time, from the moment of selection, preparation to cooking. But all things cannot be achieved without a sophisticated rearing process in the case of swine production, especially when the legendary Iberian pig becomes the spotlight and well sought after by the culinary kitchen. If there are 2 things I should encode in my memory for 2012, it will be "Tapas" and "Iberico pork". The two are often spotted on the dance floor, if not seen on the stove top. Almost synonymous, they are nearly everywhere you see in the dining room. You probably have sank your teeth upteem times, tearing the meat effortlessly that follows by a lardy smooth melty sensation in the mouth with this prized meat - bathed in hot oil. While others had them at some popular Japanese eateries, I tried mine at Tonkichi - a Tonkatsu specialty chain - under the Pokka Food Corp.In the month of December, the breaded Iberico tenderloin makes it to the menu for the first time - Iberico Pork Hire/Rōsu Katsu Set. Priced at $32, I received 3 fillet cuts, each half the size of my palm. Given a choice of hire (tenderloin) and rōsu (loin) cut, I often opt for the former as it came with lesser amount of fats and most delicate. In fact, the meat runs along the central spine of the pig, with the loin muscle making a larger part for locomotion and a much smaller segment merely for posture then becomes less fibrous - tenderloin, found near the end of this loin. Make your choice over hire or rōsu, either part of this Iberian pig will serve alongside with some refillable shredded cabbage & rice, tsukemono (pickles), chawanmushi, miso and fruits.I fought hard to resist its buttery texture, these golden crisp fillets weren't floury. I am always amazed by the Japanese batter, so well formulated that it shatters every time. Aren't you tempted by the craggy exterior when confronted? I succumbed to this swine tyrant uncontrollably, too weak to defend. Although the crumbs can be edgy and caused some discomfort when met with parts of my soft oral linings, the moisture kept in the fillet under the crisp sheath soothed the pricks I had. What makes it marvellous was the less greasy and ultra-tender composition. This acorn-fed Spanish black pork is definitely worth trying. The additional 10bucks is the price to pay for the premium specimen, 50% for that regular hire katsu set going for $20.90. Be sure to dabble the meat in Worcestershire sauce, better yet, coat them in the powdered sesame seeds you crushed earlier on. The caramelised condiment adds a fruity punch to the meat. Unless you wanted more heat, the yellow karashi (Japanese mustard-paste) will be helpful. For simplicity, squeeze the lemon wedge for that extra zest and to fuse any additional oily secretion - if any - but wasn't present in my case.I guess the meat is the only item I have greatly enjoyed, other than the good mannered service and a timber wood layout. Although I questioned on the quality of the rice which was mushy, the worst being the fruits - watermelon - all time syrupy in its unnatural form.

I thought this was really excellent, worth the higher prices than Romankan Yokohama which is my other favorite. I might like this more than Saboten also. The texture of the meat and the breadcrumbs and the taste of the sauce were very high-quality.

The first time I had Tonkichi, I thought it was excellent. The tonkatsu was crispy and flavourful and I thoroughly enjoyed grinding my own sesame seeds to make the sauce for my tonkatsu. Subsequently, I started to dread going there. I still enjoy 'making' my own sauce and in fact, that is one of the reasons why I always order the tonkatsu set instead of my favourite Japanese dish, katsudon. What I wasn't so hot for was the crumbs with which they coat and fry the pork. While it was indeed crispy, it also felt like an assault on my gums. After the meal was over, my gums would feel more raw than they had ever been and my mouth would actually be tired of chewing. The coating of crumbs was rough and hard enough to constantly rub against my gums while chewing and the meat was a little tough as well. Perhaps my jaw is too weak and my gums too delicate, but for that reason, I tend to avoid eating there nowadays especially if it's going to cost me $30 for a meal that causes me pain. It is nevertheless a delicious meal with free flow of shredded lettuce and a decent houji cha for those who are not looking to eat the tonkatsu.

I went here for lunch. I like their food. The services are the best. Staff were super friendly and attentive. Since i dont like spicy soup, i ordered the chicken soup and tomato soup. Both soups were delicious. The meat quality is also good. It is a good restaurant to bring your family along. There is also free manicure station and playroom for kidsCONCLUSION = RECOMMENDED!! MUST TRY!!

So yummy! Ultra delicious soup, quality ingredients and good service. Definitely worth a visit or rather multiple visits!!This is my first visit to Hai Di Lao. We were seated promptly as we had a reservations made for 16 pax. So I did not have the opportunity to experience their free manicure station, fruit juice bar and snack bar. Most are complimentary for guests waiting for their tables, based on my friends, they mentioned waiting time average around 1-2 hours.We were given a private room, and each individual's gets to have a personal pot to themselves. Most steamboat offer a communal pot.We use their iPad to place our orders and had a personal server who most wait on us. She made sure everything is in order and arrive promptly, she was super detailed and polite. we absolutely love her, service is awesome here!! I ordered a chicken soup base. It was SO SO good. The best I ever had!! My friends ordered tomato base and ma la base, they were really good too. Food was really fresh and everything taste fabulous. I wish I can give them 10 stars, they are that good - well, also because I didn't have to wait. I might drop the star ratings if I were made to wait for over 2 hours.

First of all, their service is really one of excellence. Many restaurants should take a leaf or two from them to really enhance diners experience. Secondly, their food items are really fresh and appetizing. I would like to specially mention the pork balls. They don't have the porky taste and each bite is QQ and full of flavour! Super win! I usually don't enjoy eating meatballs because so many people kill it for me. Their pork balls is currently my top ranking ones in terms of taste and texture! We chose the herbal black chicken soup base and their signature mala spicy soup base. I requested for really low level of spice as I don't know what to expect. Turned out it still packed quite a punch though it's low spice level. Their chicken soup is white and full of flavour. Even without anything in it, I could have drank bowls and bowls of it already! And to give them credit for using REAL stock, I didn't feel thirsty even after me drinking a lot of soup by the end of the meal. Dessert and condiments counter, we opted for this at an additional $4 per pax but to me, it's really worth it. Not only I can mix my own dipping sauce the way I like it, there is a nice selection of fruits and Chinese desserts. Today, they had rock melon and watermelon which were nice and sweet. As for the Chinese desserts, I enjoyed their chilled Beancurd and white fungus especially. All in all an excellent meal! Totally satisfied and already planning when to return again. Surely a sign of an excellent restaurant!

Everyone mentioned how Hai Di Lao is known for their service, but I do not think it is that extraordinary so I have no idea what is the baseline for comparison. I think the staff is cordial and efficient. The only difference is they will hand you a hot towel once seated to clean your hands? They also offer aprons and cloth to cover your bags on the chair. As reservations can be made for lunch, we didn't have to wait for a table and make use of their manicure services and fruits refreshment. You are given a tablet to order your food. Somehow ours was set to the Chinese language and unfortunately most of us could not read it and order. Finally a friend who can read it found there was an option to switch to English (upper right corner). They should consider putting "ENG" or something when the menu was in Chinese mode and in Chinese characters when in English mode so the monolingual can select the language option. Alternatively you can also flag down a wait staff for assistance. The food is good. Fresh and appetizing and of better quality. I did not expect cod in the seafood platter. The soup is also tasty and the Szechuan spicy soup (mala) is actually drinkable. It did get spicier after a while. Take out the chili to reduce the spice level or ask to top up the soup to dilute the spiciness. The chicken soup is delicious too. I am also surprised the cost is lower than expected. I thought it would be similar to Imperial Treasure Steamboat pricing (about $100+ for 2) but it turned out quite reasonable. Maybe it depends on what we ordered too. For a table of 5 girls, it came to around $140. We had a seafood platter, slice beef, beef balls, mushroom platter and vegetable platter. We did not add the self service free flow seasoning for $4++ each as we did not fancy the desserts or fruits. We were full with what we had, with room for dessert elsewhere.This is a comfortable place for hotpot but it is very crowded and so it is very noisy too. I still prefer to have steamboat at home but I will not mind returning if since reservations can be made. No way will I queue for this though. The usual wait time is about 2 hours or more. Another slightly cheaper option with equally fresh and good food will be Shi Li Fang at Orchard Central and Icon Village.

HDL (both outlets) is my spottt. Drunk or sober, the bubbling caldron of spicy goodness is easily one of the better mala hot pots in Singapore. And the place is so incredibly silly. You can do your nails, snack on popcorn (fresh from the popcorn machine), and leave your loud ass kids in the play pen while you wait for your table haha. The place stays open forever too. Come around 1am-2am, and you'll witness the shift in demo from the afternoon family crowd. Prices are on the higher end, but worth it especially in a group of 6 (it's the magic #). Try to get reservations or go at odd hours -wait is impossibly long otherwise. FOOD (must tries): - chicken herbal & mala soup base- hand pulled noodles - dumplings - homemade tofuSERVICE: - good (some servers don't speak english well) COST: - around $50-$70 / personOVERALL: - recommend for groups - great for late night- be ready to poop fire

everyone has heard of its great service and it is true.to the extent when my friend accidentally spilled water on her feet, the server bent over with tissue and cleaned her feet. totally awkward but shows you the extent that they are willing to provide top notch service.food wise, i think this place is great. love the flavorful soup base; we had black chicken stock and tomato. I decided that next time i will just order half portions for the ingredients; HDL's portions are actually quite big in comparison to other steamboat places so beware if you are more of a variety type of person and not too concern over quantity. the only downside of my entire experience was that i didn't know how to fold a paper crane so i couldn't get the free $6 dish. what dish is it you ask? it remains a mystery. next time when i go there again and if i manage to either solve the rubix cube or fold a paper crane then I'll update this review.

Probably my favourite chinese restaurant in Singapore. I'm a huge fan of steamboat, and since this branch opened, I've been making reservations here and rounding up the family to head there regularly! Everyone knows the service here is top-notch (hot towels, popcorn & herbal tea & fruits & manicures while you wait, ziploc bags for phones, aprons, hairties, etc), but I wouldn't come here if not for the amazing amazing food. For steamboat the broth is paramount and basically defines your meal. And the broth here has been consistently good. I always order the ma la with either the mushroom (they call it San Xian) or black chicken soup. No steamboat restaurant has the same reverence for and focus on the soup: it's served to drink alone with parsley and spring onion before you even add any ingredients, and on its own, it's already so addictive. It comes with ingredients too - actual black chicken, and two types of mushrooms & fishballs for the mushroom one. I am a huge fan of ma la tang, and the one here is tasty in itself, even after I scoop out most of the chili oil. It's actually drinkable !!!The dishes here are also fresh and inventive. You can order half or full portions - we usually order half portions and add on later if we like the dish. My faves: -Noodles - freshly spun and cut at your table. A rather small portion though, so order more if you'd like to enjoy more of this silky soft handmade la mian. -Pork and chives dumplings - YUM. Too many steamboat places are sloppy on their dumplings. The filling is fresh and juicy, while the skin tastes just like mee hoon kueh / like the la mian. Delicious. -Fish glue - my family loves this. It tastes very distinctly of fresh prawn here, compared to other places where it may taste more like fish or fish cake. -Meats like U.S. beef and black pork - thinly sliced and delicious on its own, even cooked in lighter soups like chicken/mushroom soup. The portions are not that large though, so savor them! -Meatballs - none of that tasteless frozen synthetic junk here. Tastes just like fresh meat. I'm also addicted to their chilled beancurd, served along with their sauces and condiments ($4 each). I'd usually balk at paying for this at some other steamboat restaurants but never hesitate at Hai Di Lao: besides the chilled beancurd (which is impossibly fine and soft and light and delicious and I eat maybe 5 portions each time), there're a few traditional cold dishes like peanuts and beancurd skin, fresh and actually very ripe fruits like watermelon and cut oranges, and a ridiculous display of sauces. Tbh I don't know why someone would have Korean gochujang or fermented beancurd sauce with steamboat...but definitely impressive variety. I feel like I need to say something bad about Hai Di Lao after raving for so long...so let me rack my head. Okay, it was a bit of a pain to make reservations because the line is often busy and can't get through. But just keep calling and make them, because you don't want to watch hungrily outside for 2 hours. I've never waited. This usually means I make reservations a few days or a week ahead. Of course Hai Di Lao is pricier than the usual run-of-the-mill steamboat restaurant. Orders of two types of broth already totals to more than $20 for the table. But it's not meant to compete with more casual places - Hai Di Lao offers a relaxed, quieter, more formal ambiance, where you can leisurely cook and sip at your soup and chat while enjoying your meal. IMO that's worth paying for occasionally, and frequently if you can afford it!

Food is good and display of the ingredients are nice but price is on the high side for steamboat. Noodle performance fusion meals is a great add on. Service is also great. Standard is pretty on par with the Chinese outlets. Seems to have a lot of such steamboats coming into Singapore

This is actually the 2nd branch of the well known 海底捞 chain from China. They are pretty known for their service and quality of food. The service staff is generally very courteous and attentive. The usual practice is that after the soup boils, the service staff will offer to pour out some soup and add some gsrnishing for you before you actually cook your food. If you have trouble with the menu they will be more than willing to help you out. Also when you do order prawns, they will check if you'd like them to remove the shells for you and if you would like to have the prawn heads in the soup. I would say that the 313 branch is slightly less crowded and easier to get a table. They now have a new concept of small individual pot as an alternative to having one big pot with 2 separate soups. Price wise, it's slightly higher as they do provide more than just food, free manicure session for the ladies if you have to wait very long for a table and a kids playing area.

There is no doubt about it, the Steakhouse serves one of the better steaks in Singapore. Much better value than some of the more high end Steakhouses, but giving little, if anything away in terms of quality. I have not tried their starters, nor have the group I have eaten here with ordered anything except the steak or the lamb. Good selection of steaks both in terms of cut and from USA, Australia and Ireland!  Normally more of a ribeye than a sirloin person, the Irish Grass Fed Sirloin is well worth trying, as are the Grain Fed ribeye. One of our group swears by the Tenderloin.  Sides are good quality, service is pretty good, sometimes a little brusque, but that's a trademark of Singapore service unfortunately. Carnivores should give this a try.  You won't be disappointed.

great fillet steak and as expected at a higher prized restaurant, perfectly cooked medium rare. took it classic with butter, salt and pepper but if you wish you can also cover your great meat in blue cheese sauce as so many do. side dishes are good but nothing spectacular. wine list is good, even the house wines. had oysters as starters, also, good quality. oysters, steak with mashed potatoes and 2 glass wine plus martini = 180$

For a full review, please visit: urbanjourney.com/food-an…The Steakhouse delivers a sizzling, sophisticated culinary experience inside with an impressive menu of premium Australian and US Black Angus Beef and a delectable selection of seafood appetizers that have all the making of a perfect surf & turf experience. We started off with the New England Clam Chowder, which as natives of Boston, we are always skeptical of ordering outside my hometown, but Chef Manuel Gruber has an interesting take on this Boston classic, piling in a hearty portion of New Zealand mussels and bacon bits to give it a flavor all its own.When it comes to the meat, our cut is almost always the intricately marbled US Black Angus Rib-Eye cooked medium rare (closer to rare) sprinkled with a bit of salt to lock in the full flavor of the meat.  For the sides, you can't go wrong with Creamed Spinach or Grilled Green Asparagus with Bearnaise Sauce and either the Potatoes Gratin or Mashed Potatoes as welcome accompaniments.If you've saved up enough room for dessert, then we recommend diving into the White & Dark Mocca Mousse, which is a delightful set of flavors that nicely balance off the salty meat flavor from earlier. Put all that together with some friendly conversation and a couple glasses of their admirable red wine collection, and we are all but certain you will walk away satisfied, albeit quite full and a bit lighter in the wallet.

The golden pearls don't taste different than other pearls, but it makes Koi unique. The tea itself was very good --not too milky and the texture and consistency of the pearls was spot on! Would definitely come back here when I'm in Singapore again!

better than gong cha! To taste is to believe. Can't be in SG and not queue at koi. Their tea is very flavorful, the boba not hard nor half cooked.  I like the lemon black tea and the milk tea variants.
Love, love love the bubble tea here and so do many others as the line is always long.  They have every type of tea you can imagine.  Great location.

What would I do without boba... I don't know.  Not live?  Hahaha, just kidding.  Even in Singapore, I had to have my weekly dose of bobalyfe!  Was recommended to come here by some of the locals, and although a chain, it did not disappoint!  I would warn that you get less sweet (especially if you don't have a sweet tooth, and even if you have a minor one, I'd still recommend less sweet).  There's something about the people in Asia, but their love for sweets far exceeds mine.  According the the locals, their current 70% sweet used to be the original 100% sweet... meaning, they diversified their sweet scale to accommodate a larger spectrum of less sweet and more sweet.  If I remember correctly, it ranged from 0% to 120%.  O_O  I got 50% sweet and still found it a tad bit sweeter than I like, but definitely anything over that and I would've been unhappy with my drink.  I had the plain milk tea with boba and found a well balanced drink and plenty of boba!  I didn't get a chance to try the grass jelly but I hear that's quite popular as well.If you're in Singapore, give it a try!  I had to, it was #milkteasunday.

Regular and large sizes available. The pearls are fresh and have a mild chew. You can get varying degrees of sweetness. I liked the milk tea barely sweet and also the passion fruit green tea. Every time I went they had a queue so be ready to wait for just a few minutes.

Really good milk tea right outside Bugis +.Pro: They offer a large size while a lot of the Gong Cha's in the area do not.Con: There's no seating unless you want to be a dick at sit at the MCD tables.Warning: "golden bubble tea" is not made from a magical golden tea. It refers to normal tea and their golden colored pearls.  The lady said they taste like caramel but I couldn't really see that.

Very long line, I tried the regular milk tea with 25% sweetness. Nice milk tea flavor, and the lower sugar level kept it from being cloyingly sweet. For $2.90 you get a decently sized milk tea. I would come again to try other flavors.

I stopped by to try the bubble tea of this place for some Singaporean friends told me not to miss their bubble tea when in Singapore. The taste was regular, can't say it's better than Gong Cha or other bubble tea places. But this Koi Cafe was satisfying my thirst that afternoon. Don't mind to get another big glass of their bubble tea again next time I'm there.

I can still remember the first time I tried Koi bubble tea! It was so different from the usual ones you can get around the neighbourhood. The tea tasted so smooth and the pearls were really 'Q' and chewy. Koi began with only one outlet at Toa Payoh a few years ago, and now there are several outlets and the one at Bugis+ is definitely one of the most popular ones.But the question is, is it worth the queue? The queue at Bugis+ outlet is almost always very long. The wait can be about 10-15min. To be honest, this isn't a very long wait for a delicious drink that you can indulge in once in a while, but what I am most disappointed with is the service at this outlet. My friends and I had bad experiences at this outlet. The aunties at the counter are pretty hostile and arrogant. There was once my friend made a minor mistake in ordering because she mixed up the name of the drink and sugar level with the other one offered by another popular bubble tea chain, and was given condescending remarks. Even though the drink at Koi is delicious, such bad service is unacceptable. Avoid this outlet!

The queues are long but the drinks are 'meh'. I've drank KOI a number of times but I honestly dont know what the fuss is all about. I cant put a finger on why there are so many snaking queues around and why people bother to stand in line for so long.Maybe its something about the pearls are something I havent ordered before but as far as I know, its not my favourite bubble tea outlet. Maybe the queues put me off abit but that's just how it is i guess. The longer the queue, the higher your expectations are of the drink/food.

This Koi cafe is located at the first level of Bugis + (its new name) just next to Macdonald's, and it faces the main road so not easy to miss it. I particularly like this outlet as although sometimes the queue can be pretty long, like all other koi outlets who put service as their priority, the staff would come out of the counter to take orders. Even if the staff doesn't do that, the queue still manages to clear quite fast and customers just have to wait a maximum of 10minutes or less to get a thirst quenching drink. I have been to other outlets and the queue is long too but the waiting time can go up to 20-30 minutes which is madness. I like their variety of drinks and coffees, and particularly the bubble milk tea which is the most basic drink there. The tea just tastes so natural and once you try the tea from this stall you wouldn't want to buy any other bubble tea from other stall cause they just don't taste that good anymore. The yakult green tea and black tea macchiato are also must tries.

Koi Café is my favorite bubble tea spot in Singapore. When I first had bubble tea in the states it was just too weird and popular for me to enjoy.  However, now that I am at home in Asia bubble tea seems perfectly natural and downright delicious.  I alternate between straight up milk tea and the other awesome flavored teas at Koi.  The line is absolutely horrific in length so make sure you plan ahead.  The Bugis+ location offers delivery to your office.

value for money!simple selection but big in quality.i love the cheese platter, the oyster bar, the salad bar (kale,quinoa,romaine, assorted nuts, sauces), and the mountain of scones!they also serve salmon and tuna sashimi, beef stew, veggie pastry, prosciutto di parma, polo bun, curry puffs, assorted sliders and a lovely 2 tier dessert tray served directly at your table with unlimited refills of items. drink wise, you have a choice of fresh juices, tea, coffee and chocolate if you opt for no champagne. Excellent service and great speed of food replenishment. would love to return soon!note: if you prefer local food then this high tea is not for you.

Afternoon lunch buffet with a local flair! Not quite what I expected but probably more suited for tourists looking for a more Singaporean experience than I was lol. Huge spread of food including salmon and ice cream.. definitely great for lunch

The lunch buffet has limited items, and almost no local dishes, but what's there is fresh - salads, oysters, a few sandwiches, 2 kinds of sashimi and 1 sushi, 2 kinds of cheese, fruits, scones; hot items include a soup, a pan fried dish made to order, excellent crab cakes, good curry puffs. Service is swift and pro-active, by far the best among all the outlets we've been to at the Grand Hyatt (Straits Kitchen, mezza9). If you have the Hyatt Club card and there are only two diners, the 50% discount makes the reasonable lunch outstanding value!

I have to leave an updated review. Someone left a 2-star (or is it 1-star? Sorry, goldfish memory) review which needs correcting. The service we received for our Saturday 3-5pm seating was great. Vanessa our captain made us feel at home and all her staff were attentive and friendly. Our champagne glasses were never empty for long and our plates were cleared promptly the minute we left to take more items from the buffet table. The only reason this is not a 5-star review is because I think the food (at the buffet table) isn't as good as before. Oysters are still there, but the range of cheeses is more limited now. Just one variety of blue cheese. The desserts are good but I find the number of savories to be limited too. Just some sushi, popiah and three stations of hot food (one was lentils. Really?!). Anyway, I go purely for the champagne. So I am very happy each time I'm there. Hahahaha!

Having heard many rave reviews of this place, we decided to give it a try on the 4th day of Chinese New Year even though we are High Tea newbies.First thing that we noticed is the attentiveness of the staff, all the way from making a reservation, to seating us, to patiently explaining the different kinds of teas to us. We were thrilled to discover that the High Tea is replenishable with selected items being available from the buffet counter (cheese, fruits, sushi, chinese new year crackers, sauteed beans, popiah etc). The tea we chose from the menu is replenishable as well.Another plus point we enjoyed was the seating area. Towards the end of the high tea session, servers placed candles on our table creating a soft, soothing effect which is very good for relaxing.One thing that we noticed was the high tea edition came with a small plate of yu sheng given that it was chinese new year season. We had great fun having another round of lo hei!It was such a cosy experience that we would definitely come back here again. Minor downside is that the price for high tea per pax is abit steep.

lovely place.  Ice cold beer. nicely decorated.  comfy chairs. As nice as it was I wasn't  sure if I would get a drink.  Whenni did,  i didn't know if i withs ever leave. Eventually the guy that sat me asked the girl that gave me my menu if she had taken my order.  I often find that in Singapore that unless you are frantically waving your arms around,  that means you don't want anything but this system only works if the person that takes orders ocasionally looks around the room.  Luckily the guy who sat me noticed that 15 mins later I was still waiting and didn't have anything.  Very patiently I might add. The beer was cold and a fair price for Singapore and I got some nice free nuts.  However when I wanted to get my bill I was similarly ignored until some people sat next to me got their menu (mind you a girl walked past me about 6 times without looking up once. ) This was my chance and i waved frantically enough to get noticed.  Almost embarrassing to wave like that. I thought it would be uncool to yell out in a peaceful bar like this. i would have happily drank 2 beers in my 1 hour that I was there but it was too difficult and I didn't have 2 hours to spend. I feel bad giving this review as it should be 5 stars and when i did get served the girl was lovely. She was clearly doing some work innthe computer which maybe her boss made her do but her service makes me only dare go here if I have some time to kill which today luckily I did.

Afternoon high-tea at the Grand Hyatt? What can be better? After all, it's the Grand Hyatt so I do expect to be blown off my feet. And $80 for food and free flow champagne, oh baby! There are two sessions available, one from 12-2:30 and another one from 3-4:30. We opted for the former, treating our high tea as brunch! The spread was decent but quite limited for a buffet, only 1 table. The spread includes the likes of  sushi, soup, small sandwiches and pastries, fruit, cakes, bread, cheese platter, and...raw oysters! The raw oysters were definitely my favourite! The next best thing was the cheese spread! There was an assortment of 8-10 different kinds of cheese, 3 of them were blue! If you like blue cheese (like moi) + champagne then the $80 was definitely well spent. The other food, meh? I had much better. The savoury/sweet tower of pastries/scones/puffs were not bad but not great. My friends swore by the crab cakes, but I was less than impressed. Too dry and not enough crabmeat, and not to mentioned, canned crab meat. The snob in me was appalled. I preferred the scones...a little bit of butter, some raspberry jam...YUM! Some champagne with that? HEAVEN! Okay, the bad: This is possibly the worst service I've ever seen at a 5 star hotel and definitely not on par with what the Grand Hyatt supposedly offers. We had to clear our own plates and refill our own champagne and water glasses. The waiters were simply talking to each other in the corner. I ventured into the kitchen, not once, but twice to ask them for the tea selection. When we brought the champagne bottle to our table (like any decent alcoholic) they were not pleased. Well, if it takes 10-15 minutes to refill an empty glass, I think we might as well keep that bottle at our table, especially since operation was only at a 25-50% capacity. You know what I'm sayin'? Overall, would I return? I think not. The service was really bad and there are much better high tea places elsewhere (with a better spread, food, and, most importantly, service). For about $50 more, it is possible to enjoy a much wider spread for Sunday brunch + the free flow champagne. This was not a good experience. Major fail Grand Hyatt.

From the ambiance to their service, 10 Scotts amazed me. They have an extensive list of tea to choose from, be it hot or cold. The buffet spread and tea-tray spread was curated nicely to compliment a nice afternoon tea any day. It is definitely a place I would come back again.

If you like a peaceful place to chill and catch up with friends, 10 Scotts is a great place to go to. Unlike the SPG filled Martini Bar at the Mezzanine, this is the place for High Tea and cocktails! It is comfortably lit with nice sofas and private corner sittings.High Tea runs till 5pm and if you can't make it in time for high tea, the cocktail happy hours run from 6pm to 10pm daily. With a minimum spend of $100, you can claim a complimentary car park coupon as well. Make sure you try the crab cakes because they're good!

We were here for weekend high tea. Simply described, it's a la carte high tea with a decidedly upper class slant.Double tier high tea trays are filled with nibbles like sandwiches, cakes and canapés. Also includes local bites like popiah and curry puff. All refillable. Scones are served with clotted cream, jam, and kaya for a touch of Singapore.Buffet table includes cheeses, ham and dessert like brownies and cakes. The plum with hazelnut ice cream in grand marnier is potent. A wide selection of tea and drinks is included to go with the food. Decor is cosy, in a lounge like environment. Sofas and armchairs are plenty for those who prefer to laze. Definitely different atmosphere to the busy straits kitchen opposite.Good service.

Nothing like its sibling the Martini Bar upstairs, 10 Scotts is a more chilled out and uber chic locale that serves up a good offering of champagne cocktails. And with the happy hour running an hour longer (from 6pm to 10pm daily), you know you're in for a jolly good time here. There's plenty of nooks and corners you can plonk yourself at should you want to enjoy a little privacy, unlike the crowded Martini Bar upstairs and one of the better spots we've found was right at the back of the lounge where you can sit back and enjoy your drink in peace. Other than the price ($11), the fact that they use Perrier-Jouet champagne to craft these drinks makes it all the more worthwhile. And if you can't drink on an empty stomach, there's a cleverly assembled Best in Show menu that features top eats from the various dining options within the hotel. The crab cakes and remoulade sauce are one of the better ones!

High Tea Buffet anyone? 10 Scotts is the place to be or rather the place to been seen. Delightful canapés are served on a two tiered silver tray and best of all they are refillable! My personal favourites being the crab falafel and the fig & brie on a bite size toast. If you have not tried figs, the sweetness they exude is a perfect match with the lightness of brie so be sure to give that a shot! Finally what would a high tea be without dessert, from mini éclairs to Japanese red bean pancakes, 10 Scotts has it covered.  There are two seating's on the weekend being 12pm - 2pm and 3pm - 5pm (This seating is always full, it's tea time obviously so be sure to book a day in advance at least!).

quite popular and not easy to find seating.  sometimes have to wait up at the martini bar upstairs (quite the martini menu selection there).  recommend to bring out of town guests here as a starting point for the night.

This place is serious about chicken rice. The wait can be long but don't let that stop you from checking this place out. My party of five had waited about an hour in line on a Saturday night and needless to say our stomach was growling. Luckily we knew what we wanted and quickly placed our orders right after we were seated. The lime juice was perfectly tangy and refreshing on a hot summer night. We started off with the thick soup with dried scallop, crab meat, and sweet corn (slightly sweet and seafood flavors), the deep fried bean curd with Thai style sauce (super smooth tofu and evenly fried exterior), and fried long bean with beancurd cube, nuts and minced pork (loved the salty and nutty flavor). The signature boiled chicken was of course the main event and the most prized dish on our table. The boneless chicken was amazingly smooth and could have done without any sauce or dressing because that's how tasty it was by itself. We also had the braised Chinese cabbage and the vegetables in sambal sauce, which were as excellent. This was a great and satisfying meal for the entire table and I would be more than happy to return.
Hainanese Chicken Rice is one of my favorite local delicacies. Chicken is well-cooked, tender and juicy and goes really well with the gravy! A must-try food if you ever get to visit Singapore.

Before I traveled to Singapore, I did a little survey with my friends who had been there before to see which restaurant has the best Hainan Chicken. I got about 50/50 vote for Tian Tian and Boon Tong Kee. And I tried both - Boon Tong Kee won by miles.-) Hainan Chicken Rice: I was blown away by the taste of their chicken. It's super soft yet tender (hard to explain), super moist, and with strong "chicken smell" (meaning it doesn't have a "frozen smell" sometimes you may experience if the chicken isn't well prepared). You have to try it in person to understand how it felt. The rice, although it looks like regular steam rice, it has a strong chicken taste; not very moist but if you eat with the chicken it will be the best combination.-)  (馬拉盞) Belacan Vege: another great dish. The chef cooked it very well; fresh vege and nice smell similar to shrimp paste. Very good to go with rice.-) Coffee Ribs: I heard it is a famous cooking method although it was the first time I tried. Very unique; it does have a strong coffee smell. Personally I like coffee a lot so this dish was another wonderful one.-) Crab Meat Fish Stomach Soup: pretty amazing again; a lot of crab meat and fish stomach, the soup itself can make you full. Well cooked.Definitely Boon Tong Kee is the restaurant I look forward to the most when I go Singapore again. It is a chain store with 4-5 restaurants; did a bit of map research and this location is probably the easiest accessible one for tourists staying in downtown. Right next to subway station, and Singapore Subway map is pretty self-explanatory too.I can't wait to go again!

Crab meat fish maw soup: awesome! Flavorful. Add some vinegar and white pepper powder for more taste.Chicken: Rice is delicious not too oily. Chicken is smooth and not fatty. Fresh slices of cucumber. Chilli sauce has just the right combi of chilli lime and ginger.Pretty pricey since this is a sit down restaurant. You can get their chilli to go in a glass bottle for $3.50. Expires in a year.

The main dish is chicken rice, of course, and the taste is quite different from other chicken rice. The best part is the rice, IMO.The packaging for a take away order is nice as well.In summary: still considered as the best chicken rice in Sg!

One of the best Hainanese chicken rice that I have ever had at Singapore. The restaurant is very crowded, but the service is friendly. +++ Chicken rice: The chicken meat is amazingly moist, tender and tasty. The chicken skin looks semi transparent with a layer of chicken broth jelly. The chicken rice that goes with it has this bold tasty flavor. The rice is not very moist for me, but it's tasty. It's an excellent dish. +++ Fish filet: The fish is fresh and crispy.  The sauce that goes with the fish is tasty and fresh. Again, there is spiciness in the sauce, yet you can still taste every single herbs and the freshness of the fish in the dish. +++Coffee pork ribs: The pork ribs were crispy and tasty. The coffee aroma woke up all your senses.  +++ Fried bean curd: It was an amazing simple dish. The bean curd was medium firm, the flour coat was crispy, but the bean curd melt in your mouth when you take the first bite. You can almost taste the tofu maker get up in the midnight and he/she put the soaked soy bean into the grinder,  followed by broiling and straining dry the beans. That's how fresh it is. +++ Seafood spinach:  The seafood broth is thick, fresh and sweet. It goes perfectly with fresh greens. Mr. Q and I were surprised by the most traditional Singapore food here, the dishes were tasty, but yet it didn't make you feel thirsty at all. If you have a short Singapore trip, but you still want to try the best local Hainanese chicken. Save your time searching, this is the place. I highly recommend this place to all my Yelpers.

Boon Tong Kee has delicious chicken rice with its own unique sambal. It's quite different from other chicken rice that I've tried since it doesn't offer soup to come with it. The vegetables with belacan is super awesome must try. I think it is one of the best veggies side I've ever tried in my life. I went there for dinner with colleagues and wanted to take a group photo using an iPhone. But it seems that the old lady servers have never used an iPhone before. Lol.

BTK is another popular chicken rice brand in Singapore, and one of my favourite too, the other being Tian Tian. Both are equally good, with its chicken meat being tender and tasty. However, BTK does come across as lighter in taste while Tian Tian is a bit more saltier. Really depends on individual liking but I like both equally.

You'll always find a seat at this food court in MBS. Not a very big fan , however it is one of the only cheaper options within MBS.The one thing I tend to eat here is from the "Jia Xiang Kolo Mee" store. I always order the fried fish fillet mee - satisfying fragrant bouncy noodles topped with two large pieces of battered fish. That being said, the fish soup is very mediocre - stock is watery, noodles tasteless and the vegetables bitter ... don't eat it unless it's the only store that is still open.Another highlight from my visits. People manning the dessert / drinks stall are really rude... I ordered a cheng tng and forgot to tell them to take-away . It wasn't very crowded and when I tried to tell them to make it take-away, they started kicking up this big fuss and bitching about me to my face. Wow. Service A+ man. Oh yeah, and the cheng tng sucked anyway.

Here's a fun fact that few people know about: Rasapura is run by food court chain Koufu!I expected this food court to be jaw-droppingly expensive when I first visited, but it's actually not so bad. Granted, S$6.90 for a plate of char kway teow isn't exactly cheap, but for a fancy place in a fancy area, it's cheap in comparison. I was expecting nothing less than S$10, truth be told, and I'm glad that's not so.On to the food: you can find all the standard good court here: local stuff, Indian food, Malay food, Italian food, Jap food, and more. There's a sizeable dim sum stall, and I like selection over at the fruits and juices stall. The char kway teow I had was oily, but pretty good. Same goes for the Hokkien prawn noodles. The good in general is good, and the place not a shabby choice to dine in if you're looking for something more affordable in the area.There are lots of seats, which is great. I've always managed to find a seat in less than 10 minutes no matter how crowded it was. If it's more crowded than usual, you can grab some of the standing tables and get burn some fat as you pile on some more!
So much choice!! The dim sum we're really good though always a line. Many good noodle dishes. Try it all!!Make sure to visit maxwell food center though as it has even more choice!

i went here probably 4-5 times since we stayed at the MBSthere are plenty of food options.. it's a bit pricier than hawker stands.. but you get a cleaner and air conditioned environment.. the various noodle soups are awesome.. the hokkien mee noodle soup is fantasticnot all the stalls are opened 24/7..

Tong Fong Fatt Hainanese Chicken rice: as sacrilegious as it might sounds found imthis place no less enjoyable than Tian Tian Chicken rice. Singapore proves foodcourts can be done well. Service and value are great for the Marina Sands venue. Repeat: only if in the Sands expo area.

For the American in you, the Marina Bay Sands Hotel is the Hotel from the "Crazy Rich Asians" movie.  Expensive hotel that looks like a boat and has a futuristic up-scale mall adjacent to the Hotel and Casino.  This is a rating for the food court in the adjacent shopping complex.Indoor, Bottom Level, Air-Conditioned Food Court.Bright, Lots of Tables, Lots of Food Choices.  Close to 15+ food choices.Part of the Marina Bay Sands Shopping Complex, so you know it's going to be pricey compared to typical Hawker Stall Complexes that are not Air-Conditioned.These fast food places are not staffed by Client / Service oriented personnel.  One step above rude!Watch for up-selling and pay close attention to specials which are usually the best deals.  Incorrectly worded menu items causes much confusion!So after all that, we bought stuff from two shops:  Raspura Coffee and BBQ Chicken Wings.  Both lousy service.Raspura Coffee - Ipoh and Three Level Coffee, both sweet and rich,  pricey at $2 SGD and $3.20 SGD, respectively.BBQ Chicken -  Wings are 3 for $6.60 SGD and small Rojak Vegetarian at $6 SGD.  $2.20 for a scrawny, skinny chicken wing is not a good deal.  You have to buy a minimum of 3.Conclusion:  Nice, clean, modern, air conditioned, up-scale, relatively expensive compared to nearby Hawker Stalls.  Just rude people serving you.
crowded food court for expo shops.  the hokkien mee just ok on flavor and wet sauce. LIM hainan chicken rice very good though.  juice ok.  currently under expansion

I think given the many stalls of varying quality (from good to not so great), a 3 star is appropriate. I've had the char kway teow, which was actually rather disappointing since it wasn't that flavorful. The Satay stand on the other hand (Huat Huat BBQ), was solid. The dim sum stand on the other hand, had good soy milk but their BBQ pork buns were sitting in the steamer for WAY TOO LONG.  The bottoms of the buns were literally mushy because they were too saturated with water. It became like holding watery paste every time you grabbed the bun. So 3 star it is.

This food court can be overwhelming at first glance, but only because there are so many good food options! It was nice knowing that I could come here with my family and everyone could find something that they liked given the array of food stands and cuisine types. Generally, the area is clean with staff standing by to clear tables and pick up trash. Would definitely recommend this spot for a quick meal. This place is especially nice during the off hours as the crowd dies down significantly. I particularly liked the Noodle Star, which makes hand made noodles, the Hot Plate place which gives you sizzling meats and pepper rice on a hot stone plate, and the fruit stand that gives you fresh juices
The beef noodles was actually very good! I opted for small (= no soup) but portion of beef chunks was generous. The gravy for the dry version was savory and yummy!
Pretty decent food court in the MBS shopping mall. Good variety of options and neat and clean as well. I tried the Malay Mutton curry which was very good.

I always like to check out food courts in foreign countries. In my opinion, this is much higher quality than your typical food court fare. I actually ate there twice, as the selections were good, the prices reasonable, and the location at the bottom level of marina bay sands mall, convenient. I had chicken and rice that was really really good..my wife had fish soup that she thought was too "fishy" but once she added some spices it was better. I thought the iced coffee and iced milk tea at one of the stalls was amazing and helped overcome the jet lag blues. We didn't test it out but a few of the stands are supposed to be open 24 hours which would be nice when your mental clock wakes you up at 3am.

Rasapura Masters is nothing but an overpriced mall food court. Commercialized versions of local dishes that completely lack character and cost three times as much as hawker stalls. Total tourist trap.

1 star off for the prices. A simple bite for two easily goes over $50 (thanks to the all famous Service Charge and GST, which are conveniently not included in the menu).Otherwise a great place. Delicious German food and beers!It's mostly indoors with a couple of outdoor tables if you still prefer to sit outside.

We love this place :) just tried out this location because it's a bit closer to home. We got the spicy chicken sausage. The sausages are delicious. It comes with a cold potato salad which is average but not a big cold potato fan. We got the three trio with the chicken sandwich, burger, and salad. All really great taste 3 for 15$.
