Now I wonder if we would appear somewhere in their marketing materials. Food:Too much option! Japanese, cold seafood, Asian, Mediterranean, Western, Dessert. Check out its website for a sample menu and it can make your head spin. carouselbuffet.com.sg/Do…For the cold seafood, there were plenty of crabs, lobsters, prawns, mussels, scallops, clams, snails, freshly shucked on the spot oysters, and plenty more. there was a huge (was it whole?) cold salmon next to the shellfish. Sashimi and sushi could be better but still ok. The roast beef rib from the rotisserie was excellent and you could ask for how thick or thin you want the slices to be. It also has one of the better yorkshire pudding (crispy and not too doughy) and jacket potato. The lobster risotto was also nicely done and the highlight for me was the fried prawns in salted egg yolk (/) sauce with curry leaves. Absolutely yummy. The Indian food was equally good. I spied or nee (yam paste) in the dessert section. The bread and pudding was highly recommended by my friends but I did not get to try it. I had the creme brulee which was delicious and I just loved cracking the burnt sugar on top. There were two beverage machines which dispense all kinds of coffee (regular, cappuccino, latte), tea and even hot chocolate. There were just too much food in the dinner buffet but not enough space in the stomach to try everything. I heard it is very popular and you may need to book it at least one month in advance, especially for weekends and if you have a big group. This is also one of the few halal buffets available in Singapore.

High tea at Royal Scott's Carousel... again! It was a branch Christmas / New Year gathering cum treat by our boss. We went there as a big group. Honestly, I always re-realise how small an eater I am whenever I attend such buffets. I honestly just do not know how to enjoy buffets. I see my colleagues finishing plate after plate, and there I was, already grabbing desserts on my second plate. Even then, I drove home feeling like puking in my car the whole entire trip. So bloody full!!Anyways, food-wise... what can you expect from an ultra high-end 5-star hotel restaurant like Carousel? Quality. Yes. Quality food. Quality service. Quality seats. Haha! Yeah well, we managed to book the reserved priority section in the restaurant. I quite like the spot as it gave our team of colleagues some privacy as it was separated from the normal seats with some sort of screens.Food choices were vast that I couldn't decide what to start with. I personally loved their shepherd pie the most. The mashed potato was just perfect and smooth. I wasn't too impressed with their Akashiyaki balls. It would have been better if they had just stick with Takoyakis -- my favourite Japanese food. I even had fun making my own bowl of ice-kachang. The irony was that I never loved the kachangs (beans) in my ice-kachangs. Lol! Just scooped some jellies and cendols. Overall, Carousel is definitely a great place to eat if you feel like having some classy dining.

Unlike other places such as Japan and New York where the cupcake wave has retreated as a popular pastime, cupcakes continue to hold sway in Singapore as more bakeries and cafes enter the scene to fight the sweet pie  cake. Here comes the Artisan Cupcakes, modern savvy interpretations of that humble confection by the skilled patissiers of Gourmet Carousel at Royal Plaza on Scotts. Tasting all the 12 different flavours made me feel as if I was the Alice walking in (cupcake) Wonderland, my heart filled with trepidation as I confronted never-seen-before items like the Olive Polenta & Salami. Looking like a red velvet cake, it tasted nothing like an average cupcake, but still legitimate to be called one because it is polenta (a kind of cornmeal) cake fitted into a cup. Folded in with smoked black pepper chicken, salami and covered in a royal purple potato mousseline, the cake reminded me of the savoury loaves known by the French as cake sales, bumped up with richness and piquancy. Don't let this stop you if you aren't very acquainted to the idea of savoury cupcakes. I love the Salted Egg Yolk, not just because it is beautifully adorned with a "sunny side egg" constructed of a mildly tart mango ravioli and whipped cream, but because the salted egg yolk bits and crunchy Chinese melon nuts gave this an oriental festive twist. Like celebrating Chinese New Year and Mooncake festival at the same time.I thought the Salted Egg Yolk was already quirkily tasty but the Corn & Scallion was even better. This one has a very sour greenish potato mousseline frosting that was not overpowered by the scallions, an ideal contrast to the cake that is marginally sweetened with crunchy kernel corns. I have second thoughts on whether the "Healthy" cupcakes are truly the healthiest trio of the batch because they were so sinfully loaded with dried fruits and nuts, surpassing the rest with their strong flavours and density. Take for example, the Fruity Muesli, which landed itself midway between a fruit protein bar and a beloved Christmas fruitcake. Similarly, the Carrot is a moist carrot cake that left me feeling wholesome and satiated but the ultra-sweet carrot kneaded from marzipan-icing could be an "overkill". I prefer the Honey and Figs, seductively nuanced flavour of molasses and cinnamon accents. The toasted brioche and mascarpone cream cheese lent a savoury touch to the cake.                    In case you might be too enchanted by the whimsical combinations, don't leave the Originals behind. I highly recommend the Chocolat; transcendent, luscious, perfectly deep cocoa flavours. Hats off to the chef who managed to grasp the essence of chocolate. The Red Velvet exudes an easy-going charm with its moist fluffy interior and cream cheese frosting. But like all meringues, the topping of a raspberry meringue ball is on the very sweet side, so be warnedThe sugar level for the Raspberry Lemon is too good on the high side but there is always the 70% Varlhona chocolate version to fall on. The most impressive element was the chocolate espuma, which has an extremely smooth mouth-feel and so light as if I was biting into chocolate air.

Was here recently with my colleagues for a lunch buffet and I'm here to say all of us enjoyed it so much!A really nice and pleasant environment to dine in, and very nice and personalized services. I was pleasantly surprised when I got called by first name (they knew this because I made the reservation) by one of the service staff as she wanted to confirm the birthday celebration plan for one of my colleagues. Not only that, one of my colleagues also got served personally by a chef at the Mediterranean food corner :)And about this spread of food! We were all happy with the variety. Taste wise, not the best, but not too shabby! I personally enjoyed the desserts most. My personal favorites are bread pudding and frozen yoghurt! Yums yums yums :)Anyway, I heard that they can get fully booked pretty fast for festive seasons. So better act fast or be sorry!

I've eaten hear about 5-6 times during my visit to Singapore, mainly because I stayed at Royal Palace and had a bunch of work meetings here. At first I really disliked this place. It was very expensive (e.g. appx $50pp for lunch buffet) and there was nothing special about it. Overtime though, I started to fall in love with the place. Something about the same staff that always smiles as you when you get there in the morning. The ambience music was also a nice touch. I was at first, disappointed with the selection. Nothing too special with it came to options. Bread, congee, noodles. Nothing I can't get across the street for $5, however. I finally gave each item a chance and realized why people love this place. With the simple/basic items, they do it very well. The soup was seasoned to perfection. Bread pudding, congee, ice cream, were all done consistently well.

Dinner buffet for five people - also worked without reservation on a weekday Buffet is pricy but covers everything: sushi, DIY salat, soup, pasta made to order, Indian dishes, lots of meat, chocolate fountains to cover your choice of fruit, ice cream, frozen yogurt, creme brûlée, cake etc.Nobody should worry about finding something to eat here with this selection. The waiters are okay, some quite attentive, others not so much.We were seated at a round table on colorful plastic chairs, which wasn't that comfortable but not as noisy as the other parts of the restaurant with "real" chairs.Altogether a nice evening with okay food and a bottle of wine to share, but not too fancy if you consider the price.

Carousel has won several awards for its buffet and it's one of my favourite buffets in Singapore.I'm not really a buffet person, given that my *ahem* capacity for food has lowered over the years, but when someone gets me to Carousel, I can't turn it down.I love the desserts section. When I'm there, I have the urge to skip the mains and head to desserts. This may come surprising to some, since Carousel's known for their international cuisine and array of seafood. The food's generally good - meaning fresh prawns are cold and oh-so-succulent, local Chinese delights are good, especially the fish that has such clean tender meat. But it is the three dessert stations that light up my eyes and appetite.Their tiny cups of mousse are well-done without being overly sweet. Plus, they look so dainty and cute. The bread butter pudding melts in your mouth and is so smooth it glides from your spoon. I enjoy playing at the chocolate fountain, the mix of chocolate flavours inside are very delectable, the way I eat it is to pour it all over anything else and make it instantly better.

As soon as you step into the restaurant, you will see a wide area and alot of food choices to select from. First comes the Japanese and seafood section where you will see an array of cold crabs and sushi and soba and tempura too. Then there are other sections like the cooked food which are all nicely covered up in a warmer mostly Chinese dishes and some other international dishes.At the far end of the hall there is also a hainanese chicken rice 'stall' and pasta 'stall' too. As the variety was wide i thought that the food would be delicious and blow my taste buds away, but to my surprise it was the total opposite. The pasta got cold really fast and it was hard, not edible at all. The rice was not the grainy kind of chicken rice that i loved to eat, it was clumpy and a little mushy.The sushi was not bad as i have not been very particular about my sushi all along, as long as it was edible. The last resort to save the day was the dessert section which did help a little bit, judging from the fact that i did not eat much from the whole buffet due to the disappointment. Overall bad choice and waste of money, it was quite expensive.

International buffets never come cheap and Carousel doesn't stray too far from that saying. However, I have to state that you every cent you spend is totally worth it. With a Seafood section that has the freshest selection of tiger prawns, slipper lobsters atlantic salmon and more, chances are you'll be spoilt for choice at this section alone. However, if you aren't a seafood lover, you should just skip the buffet as it won't make sense cost wise. The Rotisserie Section is a personal favourite as you can request as much meat as you like and they'll slice it according to how thick or thin you like. The rest of the buffet includes the usuals like chinese, indian and other western fare.

I thought this would be a great buffet place but turns out that the food is at best, average on overall. When I go for buffet I usually come out of it remembering one or two dishes from each particular buffet line but unfortunately there wasn't much to remember from this. Perhaps the only thing that really struck me was the fact that they had oysters from four different countries and there was a station to ensure the oysters were freshly shucked.From the looks of it this place focuses more on fresh seafood because I find that they have a pretty large selection of fish / prawns / lobster and the earlier-mentioned oysters. But their cooked food section is normal and there's nothing memorable.For the price you pay, I would say your money is better spent at Melt. Or even The Line.

this place is a local favorite that i never knew about until i started asking around.  it is about the biggest buffet that i have seen in a while.  it has Japanese, Indonesia, Indian, Malay, Turkish and western... and was excellent.  since i cannot speak for the pricing since i went for work i was very satisfied with the quality of the food and the selection.  this place gets packed so you will need a reservation but you should check it out.

If you visit Singapore, but don't go to food court, then you short-changed your trip and didn't get a full experience. I 110% implore you to look into going to a food court when in SG. It's as down-to-earth and local as it gets- well, some food courts are more local and some are more touristy, but you get the point. Bukit Timah is my favorite food court in Singapore. It's very old school. There's a small wet market downstairs, and  the second level is where the food court is. The Singapore Laksa from Terry Katong is excellent. I found the broth to be very robust with chili flavor. Still not as delicious as Malaysia laksa (haha), but still absolutely delicious in its own right. Also, the carrot cake from Seng Kee Carrot Cake is a nice sharable side. Also, get the Hailam Chicken Rice. I got mine from Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice.

My neighborhood retro kopitiam! This place is the best - it opens early, closes late, is pretty clean, very affordable, and has everything you're craving! You could stop by any time of day and be satisfied with the various local offerings to dine in house or get to go. The Beauty World MRT station is right outside too, and has a covered walkway all the way to the doorstep. A must if you love Singaporean food!

Sin Chew Satay Bee Hoon  Stall #162They are known as the worthy replacements of the now retired Ming Kee folks at East Coast (Ming Kee was crowned Street Food Master in 2007). Their sauce is perfectly balanced, it is sweet, spicy, savoury, nutty and yet smooth.  The cured cuttlefish is softly chewy. The lean pork, prawns and cockles all comes fresh, just slightly pink. The bee line here day and night is a proof for their diligence and craft. They sold out at 9pm when we were there on a sunday night!Check out the satay sauce covered bee hoon. I know for sure, that the next time I order this, I will have to top up for more stay bee hoon sauce! The bee hoon portion is enough for 1 hungry person or also enough to shared amongst 2. It comes with 2 prawns and sizeable pork slices.Sin Chew Satay Bee Hoon ($5.50) and Kang Kong cuttlefish ($3.50) is always one of the rave about stalls that make it to the must try list when visit the food centre.The sauce with the kang kong and cuttlefish is sweet, similar to that of the sweet red sauce that you eat with yong tau foo. The cuttlefish was delightfully chewy with lots of bean sprouts to crunch on with every bite.Overall, Sin Chew satay bee hoon has its uniqueness in the taste, those prefer the creamier gravy and less pungent in the peanut flavor may please with the dish.Xie Kee Hokkien Mee 謝記福建面 Stall #174Probably one of my favourite Hokkien Prawn Noodles around. The noodles are so wet, even after waiting for 10 minutes, the noodles aren't dry! The noodles are cut so small that you can polish up this plate with just a spoon. For $3, you get 2 prawns and sufficient noodles for 1 pax, but if you're hungry go for the bigger servings. The noodles itself was soft and very flavourful.The sauce is very addictive and I was so tempted to get more. They are very generous with the sotong (squid) and the squid was delightfully chewy and together with the prawn mee sauce, it was very enjoyable.All in all, if you're in the Bukit Timah Food centre, do not leave without trying a plate of this!

Many stalls with good local food in this market at level2. Fried Carrot cake is frequent with long queue. many stalls here selling this cuisine, you need to go to the correct one located at the corner stall on the third row facing the road, you will never forget the egg taste that blended well with white carrots cake. just another row in front is the famous Penang fried kway teow, the chef was previously a high rated chef in hotel line. so see what you can taste at a lower price as in hotel restaurant. Need to mentioned the long queue Satay Bee Hoon & cutter fish Kang Kong. both are not to be missed. Fried Oyster Omelet is still in the original Singapore taste is hard to find now, you can get it here at the last second row. Chinesr Satay are famous here, fish soup, goa hiong, rojak, fried kway teow etc are all in original Singapore taste here. you will never regret to dine here. A place not to be missed.

Xie Kee Hokkien Mee (#02-174): You know the food is good when they tell you "no customization", even when you're willing to pay for it!! Haha. I'm talking about the Hokkien char (or as Singaporeans call it, Hokkien Mee). There are two stalls but I always go to that particular one which the apprentice is a boy of late teens or early 20s. If you're unlucky you'd have to wait for 30minutes just to buy a $3, $4, $5 or $6 worth of noodles. Is it worth it? Please look at my rating for the stall - this was in spite of the semi-smug reply about no extra egg, and long wait in the muggy Singaporean weather. I live close by so I like to takeout (or "tabao") my food to eat in the comfort of my a/c-ed home. Yes, it may be a little soggy but I kinda like it a little soggy, that's when you get the prawn/shrimp stock beautifully infused into the noodles. The sambal paste is pretty good too. All in all, it's darn good, despite not entertaining my extra egg request (they batch cook). Yum yumSoon Kee Coffee & Tea (#02-200): There's nothing really special about it, pretty standard offering, except they have a nespresso machine. Price is decent $2.50-$3. Thunder Tea rice - I'll update this another time.

Why am I always here?First of all, my family normally buy fishes (open spaces store with the twins), meat (at the center), vegetables (center towards the end) and fruits (store at the rear owned by elderly couples). Been a customer of theirs since 1999 when I moved to Singapore for school.Second reason, food of course. I recommend getting the Pad Thai noodle (Tasty Thai Hut) and the boneless duck rice set here. Great price for great taste. Fried carrot cake and Chee Chong Fun (plain) is good too. I realized that they sell Terry Laksa here too when I walked around the food center one day. There is also a bread store which I highly recommend (opposite the boneless duck store) for its fresh baked goods and price. Better than branded bread store I shall say.Third reason is because of the tailor store and another store that my family bought prepaid cellphone cards from (Rarely visit these stores).This market had also been remodeled to give a better outlook which attracted more customers like myself and others. Will continue supporting the businesses till we leave the Bukit Timah Area :)

Four of the five dishes my dining companions and I had here were excellent. The white carrot cake, chicken rice, fried and drizzled pork, and the hokkien mee were all quite tasty. Wasn't sure what the final noodle dish was but was mostly eaten by my friend - fine by me given that I didn't like it!Nice banana shakes and good lime juice. My favourite dish was definitely the chicken rice though. The layout is awkward; seating is cramped and far less room than maxwell, for instance. Prices are fine though, and the dishes come in healthy servings. Bring a couple friends, "chope" a table, and send everyone out to grab a dish!

Conveniently located at the heart of Bukit Timah. There are lots of choices of local food over there with reasonable prices. My personal recommendation is the Seng Heng Chicken Rice stall which is quite decent. There is a parking lot beside the place but finding a parking during lunch and dinner can be difficult! So go there early to enjoy the local food!

This place holds much of my childhood lunch memories. It is a frequent hangout for me after school hours for lunch for most of my formative years, and I've grown very fond of this food centre. It recently went through a facelift so the place is much cleaner, although most of the stalls are still around.I love the Hokkien Mee, the carrot cake, the scissors curry rice, the chwee kueh, and the dessert stall selling thai red ruby. Food here remains affordable despite the slight price increase after the upgrading. Highly recommended!

Pretty good food here - reputation isn't as widespread as lets say Old Airport Rd, but still relatively well known for a few stores. The Carrot Cake here delicious, and they have two soya bean stalls that are pretty good (Soyato and Mr Bean, I think), but I prefer Mr Bean as they don't pre-add sugar into their soy milk, unlike Soyato.Their Scissors Cut Curry Rice is also delicious, and if you're a vegetarian like me, their vegetable options are strictly vegetarian (and they don't mix woks up too - in case you're as staunch as they go).

Who would've thought that in the middle of posh Bukit Timah that a little market like this would be able to survive?! Okay fine so it's no big mystery... This place has been around so long I used to come here when I was in school, And even that was 15 almost 20 years ago!The carrot cake is still amazing. In truth that really be all you need to read to be convinced of its merits. But of course there's more. The fish soup is clear, sweet, and fresh, And the teochew fishballs are humongous. You have to try them to see what I mean. There are a bunch of other famous stalls too, and you know you'll never have to cough up too much cash for a decent meal here.

Bukit Timah Market and Food Centre is a place packed with a wide variety of hawker food. While the wet market below is abuzz in the morning, the food centre above is pretty crowded throughout the day on weekends. I love the place for its variety and the fact that there are many hawker stalls that serve quality food. My favourite foods from Bukit Timah Food Centre include the ngoh hiang and fried bee hoon from zhong zhong fine spice and the pasta from Pizzaria Creation. The mutton soup stall in the same row of stalls as zhong zhong fine spice is pretty awesome too, but I can't remember its name off hand unfortunately. My only qualm is that the walkways between the stalls and the tables are very narrow and on the Sunday evening when I was there, trying to get from one row of stalls to another proved extremely difficult, especially when there is a queue at one of the stalls. The human traffic jams can be pretty frustrating and unpleasant when it gets really crowded.

Good place to come for simple brunch food and a cup of coffee. I had a tomato and egg sandwich for brunch and was really satisfied. Super chill vibe - although a bit of a tight squeeze - but that adds to the charm of the place. prices are reasonable and don't break the bank - and quality of the food was good. Great place to go for something simple, since there aren't lots of food selections.

I know this joint is known for its coffee but I come back to it for the food.The cod mash sandwich is my perennial fave - light and flavourful, keeps my tummy happy without feeling overly bloated. I also enjoy the generous truffle fries - if you're a truffle fan, you're in for a treat, they're not stingy with the truffle oil. I also enjoy the gourmet beef hotdog with ottoman topping (green tomatillo, carrot ketchup, diced tomato and sesame) - super yum. I can't wait to have a go at the the other flavours!As for the much-hyped coffee, it's not one of my faves - for the connoisseurs, the coffee here has a brighter acidity, which means, for the uninitiated, it has a slightly sour aftertaste. That doesn't make it bad, it's just that everyone's got a different palette for their idea of the perfect cup. But I do give them props for sourcing fair trade coffee, which means these beans were produced with the workers' conditions and welfare in mind, so the beans may cost more but its for a responsible cause.Final verdict:  Forty hands down one of the best foods in a place known for its coffee!

Primarily coffee for the connoisseurVery much part of Tiong Bahru's recent hipster renaissance, 40 Hands has always been about the coffee. It is a joint venture between Harry Grover and the Spa Esprit group, which explains why the decor is signature Spa Esprit's industrial chic, right down to the murals and roughly hewn stools and tables. The name comes from its philosophy of the third wave coffee movement, referring to how many hands the coffee bean passes through before it reaches your cup. As a responsible business, it ensures a direct provenance between the people who grow your beans and you - theoretically, this ensures these farmers receive fair trade for their hard work.But would you pay $4.50 for your coffee? That's not a very high price these days for premium coffee, and the java here is exceptional - for regulars, the baristas will know exactly your preferred blend, and will extract the perfect cuppa for you. Mine is always a flat white, with a bit of bright acidity (sour) to perk up the smooth blend. Foodwise, I like the truffled mushroom sandwich and will rarely venture past that.

Forty Hands is a café in the up and coming Tiong Bahru area. It was one of the first cafes to pop up in this now hip and trendy area and in my opinion remains one of the best. Their coffee is a bit pricey but its very smooth and strong (not like Starbucks) but my favorite here is the food. They have a nice selection of sandwiches, hot dogs, desserts and on weekends there is brunch. My favorite is the vegetable stack sandwich, served warm with roasted and grilled veggies and pesto. Their brunch menu is very reasonable and yummy. I tried the eggs with truffle and mushrooms, served with toast which was very satisfying. Their desserts are pretty great too. Try the dark chocolate tart--so good! Oh and they also serve some great Aussie beers! A nice place to chill and spend an afternoon.

One of the first few hip coffee joints located in the sleepy Tiong Bahru area, Forty Hands serves up a strong brew of Australian coffee and finger food. Using only organic beans, the coffee brewed here is strong and packs a punch. The décor is decidedly old school, and their food comes served in old tiffin metal plates. As part of the Spa Esprit Group, you'll find the desserts similar to what's found in HOUSE and Skinny Pizza. That said, the staff are friendly and efficient, waiting times are kept to a minimal. It's a perfect getaway from the hustle and bustle of modern Singapore. The crowds here are also less boisterous and more of the type that comes in to have a coffee and read a book. A perfect addition for one of the most nostalgic and quaint parts of Singapore.

I visited 40 Hands when they were hosting an event. Pretty sick taste of music I must add. I tried their Kong Ba Pau ($10 for 3 buns), and was very satisfied with the presentation and taste of it. Kong Ba Pau is one of the dishes commonly seen during Chinese New Year. So the cafe adopting this in their menu is very ingenious. The fatty-pork melted in your mouth and well-complemented with the fluffy white bun. 40 Hands is also famous for their coffee, which I did not get to try, and hope to go back one day to check it out, as well as the exciting places around the Tiong Bahru belt such as Social House and more.

Coffee here is good and the ambience is fun and casual. I tried the pearl barley salad, which is also available, in a far bigger portion at House @ Dempsey. Much prefer the version at House though, which not only comes in a much bigger serving, but packs more of a punch with the crispy quinoa. If I'm not wrong, they're almost the same price too.More of a fun place to hang out, particularly in the courtyard at the back (too narrow and tight in the cafe itself), as part of the "Tiong Bahru experience". If I wanted better food, I'd probably head elsewhere. Probably the same for coffee too, since Singapore is not short of cafes serving good coffee these days.
Food & coffee are good!! But service is poor, the cashier completely ignore my presence (standing in front of her) and continue her game on iPhone. Poor Latte art looks stress up with big bubbles.

Australian inspired and Australian owned, Forty Hands brings quality coffee and coffee art to Singapore. Tucked away in a narrow shop house in Tiong Bahru, these are one of the novel coffee places that are on the rise in Singapore. Their menu includes the usual Aussie favourites from breakfast plates to truffle sandwiches (A must try - great truffle/earthy flavour). This place started out as a quiet place for great coffee and some reading but media attention recently took away that serenity.  Despite the intense crowd, service standards have not fallen but coffee prices have risen and now there are even options for coffee sizes, something I personally do not like. Coffee should not come in soup bowls.  With that said Forty Hands is still a great place to spend your afternoons on the weekends and if you can afford the time, weekdays would be even better!

Singapore's take on hipster coffee is about what you'd expect. Very good coffee at a premium price with good, though sometimes pretentious service. The drinks are excellent, especially the cold brew. It can get quite crowded with young hipsters having brunch, so grab any seats you can. The sercmving sides are fairly big, but so are the prices.

Located in the historic 1930's Tiong Bahru art deco estate district on the west side of the city, 40 Hands serves up a fine cup of coffee and delicious mocha on Yong Siak Street.  Easily accessible via the Tiong Bahru MRT station, just a few short blocks away, one can enjoy modern and hearty breakfast meals in a small, but nicely designed hip space.  For a little more elbow room, there is a limited number of outdoor eating available as well.  If you're not ready for a full meal, pastries and sandwiches are also available for purchase.

This place doesn't seem as popular as Tiong Bahru Bakery, perhaps because of it's out-of-the-way location. However, there always seems to be a decent amount of people whenever I pass by, so I guess they have their own dedicated followers.I grab a takeaway coffee here every now and then if I need a pick-me-up after lunch at the neighboring eateries. Due to my lack of coffee connoisseur skills, I'm just going to say that my cappuccinos have always turned out good!I did visit the cafe once with my husband during the weekend. They had this odd system in place, though- we had to wait to be seated, which led me to believe that they would have waiter service. However, this wasn't the case- we had to go up to the counter to order and pay, to which they gave us a number for the table. Despite the strange ordering system, we did enjoy our Asian sliders.I thought the cafe felt very cramped, but this may not be the case anymore as they just completed renovations during the latter part of March. Guess another visit is in order to see if there's improvement!

Came here the morning after landing in Singapore to wake up with some flat whites! They were delicious and the restaurant is adorable. We didn't try the food but it looked great and the entire place smelled strongly of truffles, so they must be doing something right. What a great little neighborhood spot! Be sure to check out the cute book stores across the street.

If I could put 40 hands together for 40 hands coffee, I would; But I don't have so many hands. Hah.Tucked away in a corner of Yong Siak Street, 40 hands is a respite from the bustle of heartland and downtown malls. My grandparents used to live in the charming Art Deco themed Tiong Bahru estate, and whenever we visited, one could feel the stoicism and tranquility that sets it apart from the rest. So when I went to this cafe for the first time, it brought back some good memories.Anyways, was introduced this place by Q (he is my trusty source of makan joints and whatnot), and we actually went there on the 3rd day of CNY, but it was closed when we got there. Unwilling to give up, the same group of us went again weeks later, and finally got to try their much publicized kopi! We sat at the little courtyard behind, which was seriously a tad too warm if you ask me. However, the aircon inside the main part of the cafe doesn't justify sitting inside, because it felt a bit stuffy there, so basically, I conclude that sitting at the seats outside (facing Books Actually) is the best. I know this to be true because recently, I went back again, this time with Ter, and we sat outside, right below a ceiling fan. Shiok.40 hands, like PPP and Loysel's Toy, is a champion of fair trade and sustainability in the coffee industry, so every cup of coffee that you enjoy, has gone through (in very civil service terms) the proper channels to get to you. There is nothing to complain about their coffee, though the second time when I went, I thought the acidic aftertaste of my cappuccino was a wee bit strong. But other than that, my friends and I have only good things to say about their coffee. Read from their website that their baristas undergo months of intensive training, so no blind button-pressing (that would be me and my Nespresso!). They have divine truffle fries btw! Much better than PS Cafe's, in my opinion.Even if you are not big on coffee, 40 hands is good for brunch and truffle fries as well. After a nice cuppa, you can take a stroll in the surrounding estate and infuse yourself in its nostalgic charm, or swing by Books Actually opposite; they have vintage knick knacks and classic Penguin paperbacks. And oh, remember to display sufficient parking coupon if you are driving. Apparently the parking aunties usually come out after 6pm, as advised by a resident of the estate. Caveat emptor wrt the advice!

The drinks at Forty Hands was heavy-bodied and typically nutty which I believe is easily accepted by most locals. I felt the piccolo latte I had was a little over-extracted which led to a slight bitter aftertaste. But I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt as I believe it really depends on the hands behind the machine.I also picked out two dessert which were calling out my name. One - the orange peel pound cake and two - the chocolate tart. I was more impressed with their dessert as the pound cake had the delightful citrus twist I love in my cakes. The chocolate ganache in the tart was rich and luscious though it was a bit of a challenge to cut into the tart without making a huge din since it was made crunchier than usual.My friend had the truffled mushroom sandwich from the food menu which was delish from the bite I had. So I reckon their food and dessert menu is on the whole a good plus point for the cafe.Will be back to try their coffee and decide on this one again.

Really nice cap in a great ambiance. Will return to try their toasties  (panini) they looked really big and bread looked awesome. Although we sat inside the back downstairs indoor/outdoor area seemed really cute. Loved this place.

out of all the coffee joints in sg, 40 hands wins at most hipster. other places have the design aesthetic down but few so deftly recreate an urban outfitters catalog with their crowd alone, it's almost impressive. i think this place specializes in hot dogs as they have a whole page of them with quirky names, which run from $12-$15. they point out their meat is grain-fed, not sure why, since meat is either grain or grass-fed, with the latter being superior. it's like a sushi place saying, "we use farm-raised salmon." tried the big bang hot dog and found it pretty mediocre. points for pilling on a galore of toppings, but the sausage didn't taste particularly gourmet. i didn't care much for the jamaican pork ($11) sandwich either since it was too sweet for me (possibly due to the mango sauce). the saving grace were the truffle fries (HUGE portion) and coffee (long black).i think the prices here were really decent compared to similar places. it's possibly worth checking out again for brunch, but i don't have high hopes for the food.

This is a rather popular gem in Tiong Bahru neighbourhood. One of the best coffee in Singapore, with delicious (but simple) food that are well executed. Highly recommended, especially the eggben, tao sa bao and pork sliders.
Probably the best coffee you can get in Singapore! Makes TCC look like a big joke... I recommend ordering anything espresso. The food is also pretty good!

What it lacks in space, it makes up for its good food! Situated along a stretch of amazing small shops and restaurants, this little place has one of the best servings. I was there with two friends for brunch and the place was packed. As we order, some tables started clearing up and we were able to move to better seats. I ordered the Big Boy Breakfast and it was delicious. My particular favorite are the bacon, sausages and the fluffy eggs, which is how I like it when scrambled. The food was described as organic. Plus it was served with greens, mushrooms, flatbread and chili. For my drink, I got an Iced Mocha. It would have been a great place to chill place to study or work, if only there is WiFi connection. Otherwise, it's a great place to talk and hangout.

Come here for the coffee! Theirs has a really strong, bold flavor and well crafted. We came here on a Sunday around noon and the place is pretty packed. Didn't have to wait to be seated thou.I read on previous reviews that food is average so I came here with low expectations. The food is decent yet nothing to rave about. I had the Mediterranean Lamb Sandwich. We paid $40 for 2 sandwiches+ truffle fries and 2 cup of coffee. I would come back on a lazy afternoon when there is less crowd and I can sit for a cup of coffee and read a book.

Forty Hands was one of the first in the Tiong Bahru estate to set up shop if I am not wrong. They probably opened up the floodgates for the rest since they have made the place 'cool'. It is named so because apparently it takes 40 hands for a cup of coffee to be made. The shop itself is very small and very crowded on weekends with hipsters. The food itself is quite quirky as they sell everything from your normal ang moh salads and sandwiches to kong ba paus and local types of snacks. I had tried their eggs ben before (I think), and it was quite good. The coffee, I am not able to judge since I cannot tell good coffee from great.

Mate was away in Bali but offered to let us stay at her apt so 2 of us  got to have it all to ourselves for a few days 2 wks ago! Arrived at midnight on Christmas day and walked downstairs from apt@11:30am the next morning and voila - 40 Hands is literally downstairs - no effort n queuing up required! Got espressos which were tasty. For food, since they call it the "best red bean pau in Spore", got it and yep - it was so tasty, that got 2 more! Also got the jamaican jerk pork sandwich which was very good - even the bread was tasty and the plum chutney hit the spot! Extra star is for the effortlessness of it all.

The regular Cappuccino is one not to be missed. Rich in taste but not too overwhelming in terms of bitterness (they use Fairtrade coffee beans!) and added with the right amount of milk, I felt that it was just right for me. Coffee is something this place is popular for, so trying is believing! The Truffle Fries is also something to order here. One of the cheaper truffle fries around, it is nonetheless crispy and tasted great. Only the gourmet hotdog selections and certain sandwiches were available as we came on a Saturday dinner. The Big Bang is one of the gourmet hotdog. It is made with scrambled eggs, bolognese, sour cream and bacon accompanying the guinness beef and pork sausage. This accompanies well with beer (I was having coffee so I had skipped that) The Ang Mo Classic is also another gourmet hotdog which looked like a normal hotdog meal except that this came with cheese and gherkins and smeared with mustard and ketchup. You know what to have with for a complete enjoyment.Overall, this is a great place to come to if you are having brunch or a late night dinner around the area.

Been here twice, and have heard friends' reviews - lukewarm, but this place used to be so much better in 2009/10 when it was the new kid on the block (and not yet owned by a conglomerate, from what I heard). Prices have definitely risen here, the food standards slipped, the staff (once a healthy mix of Singaporeans and foreigners) has since become an all-out Filipino cast (how did they manage that?).Made a recent trip there wanting to do some work, but I found that all the power sockets had been strategically 'blocked' by appliances, or hidden. Another huge pet peeve - if you're paying up to $15 for a mediocre sandwich and a coffee - I should expect a power point or two for a quick boost to customers' batteries, but no (I believe they used to allow this). Music was also blaring. The interior is still charming, the coffee's still pretty good, but I'm disappointed to see how the standards have slipped after the corporate buy-over.
Love the Tiong Bahru neighborhood and this cute coffee shop.  We went to the Tiong Bahru market then stopped in here for some coffee.  Great coffee, plenty of seating.  They serve breakfast too.
Came here for some drink. The drinks were ok. The place was also ok to chill and relax. It looks a bit empty and not a popular place to come. But the place is clean and a bit spacious.

Popular brunch spot in Tiong Bahru. Good coffee and brunch dishes. Particularly like the scrambled egg which has a nice creamy texture, avocado toast, and the tar sau pao. Portions are quite big. Ambience is a bit cramped and there is usually a line so would recommend going off peak hours on the weekend.

After our lunch at Jumbo Seafood, my sister suggested to go Tiong Bahru. I said we could go anywhere provided there was air-conditioning since we been sitting outside Jumbo at the non-AC area. She went outdoor had no air-conditioning, but the inside the shops or cafes all have AC. I like ok, I not going to be a party pooper and besides I was curious where she was bringing me. My brother said he would come along too. He called for a Grab (somewhat like Uber) and off we went. Both started saying where we could go get some iced coffee. My sister suggested we could go 40 hands. When I opened the front door, it did not look like there were any empty table. My brother walked in and checked with the staff, and signaled us girls to go in. Apparently, there was another seating area all the way inside, almost like a level down. I quite like the rustic feel of this café.We were each given a menu and were told to place our orders in the front of the café near the front door. After my iced mocha at Coffee Bean yesterday, i could not take another mocha. I ordered the iced chocolate instead. We also ordered the ondeh ondeh $9 cake and banana walnut cake $4.50.Our cakes and drinks arrived about the same time. My iced chocolate was really delicious. I assumed the hot chocolate version can rival the hot chocolate made by my favorite Starbucks barista.The ondeh ondeh cake was good but a tad rich, best to share it with 2 or more persons. The banana walnut cake was the best cake between the two. It was so moist and the flavor just spot on. I wish I can bake this cake at home and enjoy it with a cup of tea.Not sure I would make it back here again, I am just not familiar with many places in Singapore anymore.Still, I would recommend this place to anyone in this area :)

40 Hands are one of the veterans in the on-going gentrification of Tiong Bahru and I know I used to like it a lot. On my past visits it does however appear as if it has lost some of its charm and quality. The place is immensely popular on weekends so I usually go on weekdays but if going on weekends a good tip is to sit outside as the tables are usually available here and it does actually not get that hot as they are shielded from the sun and the inside is also not that cool since it is over-crowded and the air-con usually struggles the keep things cool enough.They serve up some standard cafe food here and I recall that used to have excellent food here but on my latest (last, perhaps) visits they have not really delivered the desired quality. The sandwiches with french fries have been mediocre at best and the french fries on several occasions the type you buy for almost nothing in the store and barely even fried (even sent them back once). The french toast with bacon and banana is not bad but it is by no means the best french toast you can have in Singapore. The main redeeming feature here is the quality of the coffee, the cold brew is excellent and they can also serve up some really good espresso based beverages. Unfortunately they do not serve any filter coffees but the coffee is what saves them from a 2 in rating as a place with this quality of coffee deserves a 3.

A thumbs up for Forty H4ands.We've been hearing of this place for ages and finally had the chance to try it out for ourselves. Being one of the pioneers of the ever changing landscape of Tiong Bahru, Forty Hands has done well to keep themselves ever popular. Located further inside Tiong Bahru at Yong Siak Street, Forty H4ands offers a pretty decent, yet streamline menu, choosing to concentrate on quality and not quantity. Unfortunately we didn't get the chance to try their signature "Kong Bak Pua" or "Tau Sar Pau" as we decided to try out their heartier breakfast selections instead. Big Boy Breakfast served with Pork SausagesA wide selection of goodies on a plate! The scrambled eggs (there's an option for sunny side up, eggs Benedict, over easy or scrambled) were very nicely done. Perfectly season, the eggs were nicely seasoned and probably one of the better done scrambled eggs ice had in a while. The mushrooms ragout and Beef Bolognese made a great addition, especially to stuff the pita bread with, along with the generous amount of fresh salad it was served with. Unfortunately, the sausage that it came with was... Well... Disappointing. While generous in terms of size, the sausage itself was hard and had a very very tough casing. Tasted as though it was cooked early in the morning but reheated and refried before serving. Not very good at all. A disappointment considering that the rest on the plate were really pretty good! Banana Bacon French Toast.Seems to be the trend recently, having extremely crisp bacon served with maple or in some sweet concoction. While that was great, the Banana portion was just a tad too little. Considering the size of the toast it comes with, a little more banana would have really given this dish more fulfillment but overall, it was still a pretty good french toast. Picolo latte This Is now my official "let's see how good their coffee is" drink. It allows me to taste just how good the coffee is, without taking it espresso. While the coffee is nicely balanced, it isn't THE best I've had so far, but, it's a good cuppa for those who don't want an overly strong or potent coffee. The beans apparently came from "The Common man coffee roasters" which to me, was pretty disappointing (food wise) but I suppose they did a pretty good job with the coffee.Overall, a great ace to meet with friends and it does have a pretty good breakfast. A bit on the pricy side but as compared to some of the other cafes out there, this one still serves a very satisfactory breakfast! Would have been perfect, if not for the sausage.

Two stars because (wish I could give 2.5):-this place gets, surprisingly, overcrowded during the weekends.-The food is ok but the value for money is low. I ordered the salmon and hash(=French fries!). There was very little salmon in the dish and while the sauce that came with it was very good it should have been on the side. What I ended up having was a few pices of salmon floating in a little bucket full of sauce. Not great and terrible for digestion.Pros:-Food presentation is nice.-Coffee is good (but slightly too acidic).-Lovely little patio on the back.Conclusion:A hype Tiong Bahru place that is over priced. Second time there and I don't understand why it gets so crowded.

How is it possible that I have not reviewed this place? Been here like a gazillion times, complain about their coffee, complain about the prices, but still keep going back because I love their breakfasts!!! Oh so good, oh so pricy, oh can you please do something about your coffee (and I don't care that you are famous for your coffee ) So...breakfast for two with two cups of coffee would be a little less than $50... Ish. So... Ya.. Breakfast - can do no wrong. Eggs Ben (with really good hollandaise sauce) (comes with a great side of roasted potatoes), their poach eggs with mushroom, baby spinach (oh sooooo good) and a side of crusty bread and big breakfast (order one to share and regretted cos I could have finished one on my own). Well prepared breakfast with quality ingredients. Coffee - their milk based coffees are ok. Not THAT bad, just that I had better. The espresso and Long black are a bit too sour for my liking. Me no coffee expert but heard a SK told me before that it has something to do with the water temperature, while another SK told me it has something to do with the acidity of the beans * SK = Sien Ka (Cantonese) - go figure.....The place is always packed. Despite the prices (Singaporeans are rich eh?), people still flock in. I love that they open early (not very common for cafes around here), though they do close by 5pm.

Sizable portions, at a price. Quite crowded on the weekends, but the extra seating "downstairs" is not bad with the fan running. I ordered the Pesto Chicken Panini with a side salad (instead of fries) along with the Orange Carrot Juice. The most impressive part about the panini was its size, and the juice was fair (nothing impressive). The panini cost $17 and the juice cost $8. My friend ordered the Eggs Benedict with steak and the Truffle Fries. I will admit her selections tasted better than mine, but again, nothing special.Given how crowded it can get here during peak hours and how mediocre the food is compared to its price, I don't foresee myself coming back anytime soon.
Great vibes for a cafe in hipster Tiong Bahru. Coffee is fairly decent as well. Definitely see myself chilling out here for an afternoon.It can get noisy though!

This place is 10 percent more expensive than similar restaurants but it's worth it. The food is good quality and the portions generous. I enjoyed the big breakfast - cooked to a turn.  The truffle fries are scrumptous.  The only constructive criticism I have is the places needs to be way cooler. A more powerful air con wouldn't be the worst idea. Will definitely go back sometime.

Forty Hands serve very good coffee.  It's the best coffee in Tiong Bahru and I would even say it's one of the best in Singapore.  I have also had one of their brunch items, the Eggs Cocotte, it's essentially a poached egg inside a pot.  It's quite delicious and they used truffle oil to cook it.  Yeah, so how can it taste bad?But the reason I am not giving it 4 stars (which its coffee deserves) is that the place is way too crowded on weekends.  It's one of those places dragged down by its own fame I guess.  For me, a cafe should be a place where you can sit and relax and chat with friends and not bother about when to leave.  But the last time I visited on a saturday the place was so crowded that I was sitting shoulder to shoulder with the person at the next table and once you finished your food, you were shoved out and I find that completely unacceptable.  Not that you would want to stay in the place any longer given the crowded condition but that just takes away from the cafe experience.  If, however, you find yourself in the neighborhood on a weekday, it's worth a try.

Being busy is great for a restaurant but the logistics here suck - seat people so they don't have to queue through the entire restaurant to place their order. Wait on them and have waitlist guests stand outside. It's ridiculous and makes it a cluster f$&k. I left when I realized once I got a seat I'd have to queue again for order!
Fantastic vibe. It is in the hip Tiong Bahru neighbourhood. Food was great! I will definitely comeback again.

Decent 3rd wave coffee place - the gleaming chrome Synesso machine assures you of a decent, if not stellar brew. Coffee is par for the course where 3rd wave is concerned - $4 - $6 depending on how much milk and water you want to desecrate your coffee with. Brews tend toward the brighter end of the flavour spectrum, as these places tend to do. Food is on the pricey end, especially considering that its located in a sleepy (but rapidly gentrifying) old neighbourhood - and all the associated good and bad that comes with that. If you're familiar with Spa Esprit Group's other F&B offerings - House @ Dempsey, Skinny Pizza etc, it's more of the same rustic-chi-chi vibe that tries to convince you that it's an organic, spontaneous, design-conscious place, whilst simultaneously charging you $16 for a mushroom sandwich drowned in synthetic truffle oil. If that's your vibe, you'll love this place. Me, i just come for the coffee.

Their coffee is so lovely! I'm not a coffee person though so all I know is that it tastes nice to me! The Truffle Fries are really good too. Ideal for popping over after a book buying spree at Books Actually, on the same street, and reading your purchases!!

Never had the chance to dine in cos it's ALWAYS so crowded.The nearest I got to was to do a take-away of some pastry from the counter and scoot out cos I simply do not like to stay too long there with SO many people squeezed in a tiny cafe.Bought a chocolate walnut orange Scookie (supposedly a mutant of scone + cookie) and I guess I like what I tasted. The texture was good and it's not too sweet. It crumbles nicely but gets a little messy cos you get crumbs falling out with every bite.If you are not fussy and just a quick take-away of beverage and pastry, guess it's not too bad a place. I still wish that one day I can finally sit down and dine in properly though. Heh.

We had a bit of a trek to get out here on my friend's recommendation for breakfast. If I had been based in the neighborhood I would have been happy enough with the menu choices and food quality but wouldn't go out of my way to reach this place. It is self service and that is quite clear (living in the UK for 7 years I'm not normally shocked by service quality but Singapore was definitely a bit of a disappointment!)

Yup its a solid 5 from us.   Food, service and ambience checks out.   oh my the humus and cheese are simply divine.   tried all version of meat chicken, lamb, beef as well shrimp.   excellently grilled and taste wonderful. Ok one qualification - Baclava need to inc pastry ratio.

I struggled between 3 and 4 stars for Shabestan, because the restaurant has some nice offerings. What I liked were: location, service, food, ambience. But ultimately, the price point was a bit high for the experience. We sat inside, and ordered the platter for two and the hummus app. The food is good considering there isnt much competition for Persian cuisine in Singapore. Meats were well seasoned, and the portions are generous, which I find true for most Persian restaurants. The lamb and chicken were definitely the highlights, but I would've liked to try a salad as well. I'd recommend you under order on the protein/platter (get a platter for 2 as a table of 3), so you can try another app or salad. Also, remember to ask for a small serving of garlic yogurt and chili padi sauce. They're delicious and help bring everything together. If you come for dinner, then you might also be welcomed by some lively music and belly dancing. I enjoy dinner entertainment, but if prefer privacy ask for a table inside -it's less audible. We ended up paying $189, which was the premise of the 3 stars, but I'd come back. The food is good, and I think you can fare better with a little menu hacking and a bigger group.

First time tonight for dinner and I realized it's going to be one of my favorite restaurants in SG, (not just a favorite Persian one) as soon as I tried the hummus and the stuffed grape leaves. I'm a sucker for lamb kubideh and have tried the best from LA to Istanbul. Shabestan can give any of them a run for their money. The service is quite attentive and personable and with a smile. I always demand something spicy whether it's chili flakes, chili padi, chopped jalapeño or grilled peppers. Not only did the host/manager give me and my fiancé two big bowls of mouthwatering spicy sauce each, he also made sure I had plenty of green peppers on the side, grilled to perfection. I can't praise this place enough. The chicken kubideh was delightfully memorable too. Can't wait to go back even though we were there 30 mins ago.

I really do like visiting Shabestan when I'm in the mood for some good Persian food. We normally begin with a cider or cocktail, but they do have mocktails available as well. We often times start with the Halim Bademjan ($13), which is pureed eggplant with braised, tender lamb and green lentils, garnished with sun-dried yougurt and mint sauce. It's basically babaganoush and is a wonderful appetizer, but not Paleo if paired with their bread. They will bring you cut up veggies if you request, and it's delicious! The hummus ($10) is also a great option, but still a Paleo cheat.I've also had the Soup E Jow ($11), which features barley, herbs, vegetables and chicken. The North Dakota girl in me adores this comfort-food soup, but the Paleo angel on my shoulder disapproves! Our go to entree is the Shabestan Platter for Two ($95). It comes with minced lamb, chicken, fish, prawn, and a lamb or beef fillet. We always opt for the beef.In addition to the food, they have a belly dancer on Friday evenings, beginning around 8:00 pm. It's never too hard to get a table here, and we've had luck every time even when we haven't made reservations.

A little pricey but worth it. Gave us a lovely table with a nice view of the water which made for great ambience. A belly dance performance was included but wasn't the very best I've seen.The food was done perfectly, very flavourful and well balanced. I recommended the platter for two which comes with with an assortment of meats and rice.

We had such a fun night here - the food is delicious with generous portions.  They have a great wine selection and at weekends, a belly dancer provides entertainment during courses.Due to cute lighting and candles, outside seating offers an intimate environment while much brighter lighting (that unfortunately can't be dimmed) makes for a fun group setting inside.

We ordered some Kofte as appetizer and a couple of different kebabs as mains.  All three dishes were really tasty.  Well, the good about this place ends here...  The front of the house staff has no clue!  I ordered a glass of red wine; it must have came out of a freezer (not a wine cooler)!  Sent it back, to a waitress who did not understand what was wrong with red wine chilled at the same temperature as a frozen Margarita.  I did not get it back for a while, neither I was told whether i was going to get another back...  the the brought me a new glass.  Right then the first main came, it was mine, they placed it in front of me.  The second main comes out two mins later.  Obviously it's not mine, I already have one and my wife has an empty table in front of her.  The guy, manages to land the second dish in front of me too... the look "are you kidding me" was not clear to him.  His boss saw him, and signaled him to move it!  Doh! :-)  Then a belly dancer came out.  Fun show, just lower your music!  Especially when there is the part with crazy tribal drums.  We are here for dinner...In the end, the bill.  The price is 2x your average Middle Eastern place in Arab street.  I don't think it's worth it.  Yes, you are right on the Singapore River, and yes the food is well done.  But there are quite a few things to improve!  Well, when we sat down on Sat evening, the place was almost completely empty, and Brussels Sprouts next door was fully booked.   Now it's clear why...

There are four things I go to Kampong Glam Cafe for: their teh halia, the soto ayam (only after 3pm, alas), the fritatta thing they have at lunch, and on occasion, their cheese brownies. Which is to say, pop by when you're hungry and don't feel like kebab, or something a bit upmarket at other parts of the Arab St area. The menu shifts a little from breakfast to lunch to dinner, so you could eat all three meals here and not repeat a thing!

This is a great budget eat along the touristy-priced food available in the Arab st / Bussorah area. And you get local food like the maggi goreng, horfun, fried rice, teh peng - it's a fuss free menu with equally fuss-free prices to boot.Plus you also get a good view of the Sultan mosque straight ahead as you dine al fresco on the pavement. It's usually very crowded in the evenings, a favourite supper joints of many. Also provides a good place for people watching - you might spot some Malay celebs who love to frequent the place.My usual order will either be the maggi goreng or beef hor fun, good old comfort food best served with good company!

The char kway teow here is da bomb! It is sweet with loads of wok hei. the dining area is out door, so beware when it rains, lots of customers smoke here but it's pretty airy so you don't suffer from second hand smoke so much. the nasi goreng pattaya was also damn good. Their iced lemon tea is pretty diluted, i would avoid that

Malay food in arab st. Was expecting to chow down some shawarma, kebab etc but my friends recommended this place. We were directed on the upper floor (but its too hot upstairs even with open windows, ceiling fan and wall fan on) so we settle on the side of the street. No sign for smokers and non smokers areas (i'm a non smoker) and i can smell smoke from our place :(But the food greAt, the service is fast and the servers are friendly. I love the blue ice lime soda.

I LOVE this place. I've been here probably a dozen times already, and it's just fantastic. There's a great ambiance on the weekends, when everything is lively outside, and it has a great view of Sultan Mosque. The service is always super fast and the dishes are really cheap! My favorite dish is the Maggie Goreng with egg and an Ice Teh Tarik. I could eat here everyday, honestly. It's a must try if you're in the super hip Bugis area!

Maybe it is because I don't know Malay food but I don't understand what the hype is about this place.  It's casual and relaxing and it is popular but the food only tastes ok to me.  There was no English menu and I have no idea what anything is so I did what a desperate tourist did: point at what everyone else is eating.  Perhaps I would have a better experience if I came with a local or somebody who knows what they are doing.  /meh  The tea was good though.

Great late night place with greasy food and iced Milos.  In fact, you cannot go wrong with a Milo Dino which is a regular iced Milo with EXTRA Milo powder on top.I love the outdoor feel of all the restaurants on Arab Street, especially on a warm and breezy night.  Kampong Glam was a great place because there are an abundance of seats compared to some of the other places.

I love this unpretentious place. The food is actually really decent. My friend's mee soto was Yummers although the mee siam was average to me. My Mee Bandung was spicy and gave it an awesome kick. All in all, including our drinks, our bill came up to S$14.90. Not bad at all!!! I'll be back to try their Mee Pattaya (fried noodles literally wrapped in an egg omelette).

i came here for some dinner after shopping on haji lane.  this was the restaurant that was most packed, and i had seen it on yelp.  however, as some other yelpers said, right when you sit, you feel pressure to order, b/c the uncles start standing over you.  i didn't know what i wanted yet, but i just ordered mee siam, b/c i hadn't had it on this trip yet.  i totally ordered the wrong thing!  while tasty, it was soooo tiny.  no wonder singaporeans are so small; the portions are anemic!  i had a lychee drink to go w/ it, and that helped fill me up a bit.  i later looked around (should have done that first!) to see what others were eating, and i totally should have gotten a rice plate.

This place is damn good for a low budget meal, or just to sit down and have some tea with friends and chit chat. The service is pretty good too. As soon as you grab a seat, one of the uncles will come with a menu and they're not the kind to pressure you into ordering but are attentive enough to notice you when you want to order.I had the kway teow goreng and a teh peng. Awesome stuff! I throughly enjoyed the kway teow and I made sure I didnt leave anything on the plate.The tea was also thick enough and not overly sweet.

I always love walking by this Cafe - there are always people eating, congregating, smoking, talking, etc. It's right smack in the middle of Arab Street - facing the Sultan Mosque - it has a very fun, lively and loud sorta vibe, and people are usually there just to people watch. I love the energy of this place - it's not commercial like boring Orchard Road - you can feel the energy of the people there - and when you hear the Azan from the Mosque - makes you really feel like you're in Southeast Asia.What I Love: The food and prices here are amazing. I've had the Mee Rebus here before, and it was great. It's nice to see local food here. It's hard to get nice Mee Siam at times. Their Teh-O is yummy too. A meal would set you back $5? (Drink included)Officially they are suppose to close at midnight - but they always seem open! I think they close whenever they feel like it!What I Don't Love: Absolutely nothing!

I have been here a few times, I think the attraction of this place is its location and hours. The first few times I was there for late night snack and it's the few lively places still open in the arab street area.  Prices are quite cheap (if you go to any other middle eastern/turkish restaurant on Arab Street, they would have cost considerably more) but it's Malay food (not turkish or moroccan in case you are looking for those).  It's your usual mee goreng, roti, teh tariq but it's a pretty good spot for people watching, you also get a really nice view of the mosque as your backdrop.  Service is friendly and efficient and food is simple and unpretentious, good option for visitors if they want a taste of truly local food.

For my friends and I, Malay food wouldn't be our choice if we're hanging around Kampong Glam. It's so easily accessible at many places so we usually try out something exotic if we're around the area.On the other hand, food is considerably cheaper at  Kampong Glam Cafe. We were tight on cash too, so one day, we had dinner at this place. I heard that it's always crowded at night, so we got there just before the dinner crowd came in. The menu includes the usual Malay fare but we weren't disappointed with the food! We loved the kick from the beef rendang, lontong and sayur lodeh. We paid an average of $5 per head for our meal. If you're broke and hungry, Kampong Glam Cafe is one of your best options.

They couldn't have a better location: KGC is the de facto breakfast, lunch, dinner and supper spot for all who find themselves in the Arab St area at various times of the day. It helps that the food is good and cheap, too.They have the usual nasi padang stuff, which is not bad, but their mee goreng and maggi mee goreng and other fried noodle varieties are excellent. Things tend to be spicy by default so if you can't have spicy food, tell them to tone it down (poor you, it's awesome spicy).Chilled out. You can just sit here and lepak all day, drinking teh tarik...

My most favorite place to hang out all night long with friends! Reasonable priced delicious food and drinks. First timers must try their famous Gado Gado! Chunks of rice cakes, fermented beans (tempe), tofu, potatoes and shredded vegetables soaked in peanut gravy. It's really good! And I always start my meal with their ice milo! This place is often packed with people especially on weekend nights so it may not be that easy to get seats but it's sure worth the wait.

I used to come to kampong glam a lot for a late dinner. There's a wide variety of food available here, and at affordable prices. The food can be quite spicy, so do make sure you order a drink to help quell the fire! I find the milky teh Penn here very good for that.Not only do they offer your usual nasi Padang dishes with a generous portion of rice, they also have dishes such as mee soto, mee rebus, mee siam and nasi goreng pattaya. All these dishes are pretty tasty in their own right.Prices are affordable, and service is efficient and fast. The staff are pretty friendly and will even joke around with you. An average meal will cost around $5 and above.I have to say, I think the standard has dropped a little over the years, but it's still satisfying and great value for money. Parking here can be really difficult, but this place is open till late at night, so you can drop to satisfy late night cravings!

I've been coming here for more than 5 years. The chicken is tender and boneless. And there is also achar on the side. I love their chicken liver and gizzard dish. The sauce is just right. I also called bean sprout and the Thai style tofu. I love this place and will come back for more delicious foods. They have lots of side dishes that you can order. Overall, this place is a must try! Parking might be difficult but it depends on the timing. Enjoy!

The chicken rice is very average; hidden costs include paying for the rice and the vegetable dishes are very expensive ($6 for a small-ish serving). The portions of chicken are also rather small (for $3.50 excluding rice), and the taste is nothing to rave about.

This eatery is located at the end of a stretch of other coffeeshops. It's one of the few places in Singapore that whips up halal duck rice. There's chicken rice too, but we can easily get that elsewhere, so we got the duck rice here. They care enough to debone the meat for you, so there's no need to dirty your hands.  They've got lots of variety in their menu. We also ordered the deep fried tofu, kailan and  omelette to go with our duck rice. The rice was fragrant and the duck meat was tender and cooked to perfection. Plus, it didn't cost a bomb! We were contented with the meal.

the chicken rice is awesome. The seafood dishes are so so... Well It is called evertop chicken rice. Heh. what I don't like about the place is that you'll need to walk up to the counter to place an order and the menu is only accessible at the counter. and the drinks is ordered separately. well, it won't stop me from eating here again but it'll be better if the management sort this out.

If you're looking for halal duck rice, this is one of the few chicken rice joints that serves it. They used to be the famous halal chicken rice store at tanglin halt but have since moved to clementi. I like the range of choices in the menu, you can choose from roasted to hainanese chickens to duck. If you're in a group, you can order a bunch of dishes and share and it won't bust your budget either! My favourites off the menu are the roasted duck and/or chicken, chap chye vegetables, omelette - it's a very satisfying meal just sharing those 3 dishes. The only thing I don't enjoy sometimes is that the chicken or duck is served cold. The rice is usually hot so I guess that makes up for it? Otherwise, it's a great place for halal chicken and duck rice!Final verdict: Not always evertop in quality but good enough to come back for more!

Great place at east coast for your Italian food cravings. Once you step in, it's got the ambience of Italy. Old wood furniture and smells from the open kitchen is something that always amazes me. Pizzas cooked in a traditional wood fire oven. And pastas made to your liking. My go-to place for Italian food.Whilst the food is good, be prepared to wait a long time to get in, the service isn't particularly good. So be prepared. But I'm sure you'll end the night pleasantly. I hope. Try it if you're around the area!

Al Forno definitely has a fan base, and I respect that. We stopped by during a public holiday and the restaurant was packed, so without a reservation we took a table outside.As there are a lot of Italian restaurants in the area to compare to, we chose the caprese salad to start. I went the pizza route by ordering their Pizza Al Forno (a specialty) while Migs tried one of their squid ink pastas.I wasn't too impressed with their caprese, considering it was $18. Their tomatoes were nothing to shout about, and the black olives didn't add much flavour either. I would've preferred kalamata olives instead.The Pizza Al Forno was very filling, and my takeaways fed me for 2 meals afterwards! It's halfway between a thin crust and thick crust. Toppings included mozzarella cheese, sausages, ricotta cheese, and spinach, yet I still felt that it could've had more flavour. Either a better tomato sauce, a good olive oil, or perhaps some red pepper flakes could help take it to the next level.Unfortunately service was very hurried and clearly the staff looked overwhelmed with all the guests in house. Once our food was served we could no longer get anyone's attention to deliver our check so we had to go in (twice) to get it.Not exactly the best first impression, but I'm willing to give them another try.

I have been a quiet fan of Al Forno's for about 20 years already (seriously, I'm that old). I remember my fondest dates here with my then-boyfriend-now-hubby and the food is STILL as good!Focaccia Blanca - we wanted a starter and its nice. Think it as a pizza base without the sauce and ingredients. It's fragrant and goes well with soup. It's also a hit with the kids.Calamari - the squid rings are nicely battered and fried but I would have liked them seasoned more. Though the rings are tender and crispy, its a little bland for me.Pizza Alforno - our first time ordering pizza. I love how moist the pizza tasted with the feta cheese and spinach toppings!Pizza Con Carne - essentially a meaty pizza with ham slices and salami slices. Hub likes it enough.Spaghetti Cartoccio - my all-time fav baked spaghetti with seafood. They serve it in a tin foil that you cut open to reveal its goodness. The seafood is fresh and generous in amount and the spaghetti cooked till al dente even when baked. Al Forno remains my favourite Italian restaurant of homage.

Everytime i pass by this resto always full. So finally tonight got a parking spot nearby, as i went there early. I had tagliatelle with tomato and lobster, kids had pizza, hubby had calzone, a friend of mine had meatballs penne. Everybody was happy with their meals, the portion also generous ( too much for my 13 yo kids). Mine pasta was fresh, well cooked, fresh sause also.Service was good and fast. Will definatelly return here and added this place to my list to go for dinner:)

We came here for our company holiday party. Thank God I didn't need to pay a single penny bc if I did, I would have written a nasty review. Well, one that might be nastier than this one. Disgusting. Seriously, I don't think anyone at our table finished any of our food. Well, except for the appetizer consisting of mozzarella + Parma ham because to create that bad version of that dish would make this restaurant an Olive Garden. Al Forno hasn't hit rock bottom like Olive Garden, but it's close. Some things that were wrong: 1. My colleague's parmesan eggplant was just soaked with cheese - which in my opinion means that it wasnt fresh. The taste test proved my suspicion to be true.2. The seafood spaghetti (their speciality) was tasteless. I had 3 bites and was fed up. My colleague gave it a tried and gave me a face after his one bite. Yuck.3. My colleague's halah order was a simple take out box. They didn't even take the time to present it nicely. Fine, fine, BUT we had to ask at least 3 times to bring her food! Muslims need to eat too! 4. The service! Ugh. We had to repeat our requests many, many times. I'm not going to get into service in Singapore, but you know what I mean. The winning grace was the pizza, which I've had much better elsewhere.There are so many other better restaurants on East Coast Road. Pass on this one. Just pass.
Probably the best and most authentic pizza I have had on this side of the world. The beef filet was sheer perfection with the high quality delicious cut of meat!

When we walked into this place everything seemed wonderful this old east coast landmark has the look of an Italian tavern, the service was friendly, when the food came the portions were hearty, the food looked good but right from the appetizer to the soup, the pizza and the pasta nothing had flavor or character, it was all limp! And that was not because the Chef tried to make the food light or bland it's just that nothing seemed to click , it was just ok...It should have been 3 stars, the extra star is for the dessert (tiramisu) & coffee and the overall ambience since you do get the feeling of being in rustic (in a nice way) Italian tavern, but the prices btw are not of a rustic tavern!

Al Forno is great if you;re looking to have a classic italian meal. I suppose the food's that good cos the chef is italian himself.I'm an east coast kid so obviously I;ve been to Al Forno's countless times and everytime I'm there, the food's just as good. It really doesnt matter if you order pasta or pizza and some other main course. The food is well cooked and you're greeted by classic italian flavours in every bite.One of the starters that I particularly enjoy are the clams in white wine sauce. They weren't sandy (which is very imp) and the sauce was white wine sauce was delicious. I'd highly recommend it if you're a seafood junkie.

I heart Al Forno. It's buzzy, with frazzled wait staff at peak hours, and dishes up superb Italian. I haven't found a place that does pizza better than Al Forno yet. Not wafer thin crispy, not overly bready - it's the right balance of crunch, chew and char. I only ever order pizza when my go to pizza maker is around - he's the Italian dude in a thin white tee, with more hair on his arms than his head. It's a wonder why the pizza oven hasn't burnt off all the hair on his arms yet. Other go to orders are the clams and spaghetti cartoccio. The pasta, served in a giant aluminum foil pack erupts a cloud of seafoody steam when opened. If that's not what dreams are made of... Wait, I take that back. That's what MY dreams are made of. I'll usually get a bottle of proseco as well, if I'm in a celebratory mood. Prices are not gentle, but not extravagantly placed either. Don't expect to be served limoncello even if you spend a bomb though; the owner only reserves it for his friends.

For authentic Italian food in the East, look no further than Al Forno's. When I was studying overseas, pasta was our instant noodles and so I'd never think of eating pasta at a restaurant knowing how easy it is to cook it. Yet, whenever I think of Al Forno, my mind immediately conjures up tasty memories of their seafood pasta and I almost start salivating.
