5 star for the beautiful indoor decoration.4 star for the infuse tea. 1 star for the service. After I tasted their tea during afternoon high-tea at The landing point, I wanted to bring some of their tea back to US. The store is beautifully decorated with a whole wall of large tea cans. There are designed tea cans from small to big. The infused tea were similar to Tea-forte, the tea spot and Teavana. The salesman has this snobby facial expression on his face all the time.Why is he so arrogant about selling tea leaves?  After I purchased a few of their infused tea and macarons, the female cashier looks very annoyed when I tried to take a picture of the store" No pictures". She waved her hand right in front of my camera lens. And the guy who just sold us the tea pretended it wasn't his business. Cuz his job was done, right after we paid him.  Wow, Really? I assumed this is not a fashion store, it's just a tea store. What's so secretive about the store that I can't take picture with it? If there is a no-photograph policy, you should just mention it in a polite way instead of being a bitch. This TWG is trying to be an upscale store,but unfortunately the people who work for them are discourteous.

Tried all 3 fish I.e salmon, sea bass and cod.   All done well.  Tried the imperial rose and lemon bush tea and they all turn up well.  We also got the chocolate fudge as well as the apple tartan. Both were equally tasty and well executed.  Wifey had the imperial rose but I thought my lemon bush tea came out ahead perhaps because I like rioobos tea to start with.  Service is good despite being a busy lunch time.

The place is just beautiful so its nice to sit and just enjoy your tea.  The cutlery and plates are just so pretty!When you go to this place, make sure you are not rushing.  Their tea menu is so extensive, that it will take you at least 15mins to select one.  The tea was great with the subtle flavors.The let down was the dessert --- it looked very pretty but the flavors were not there -- felt like it was not good chocolate.  It was just sweet...I went for afternoon tea so did not try any of the dishes.

No doubt a unique, fun location situated right in the intersection of 2 halls, on a raised platform while shoppers walk with envy....sort of.  Guess it's not your traditional British-style high tea in a hotel setting like the fabulous one back home at the Fairmont in DT but to us, was just a touristy thing to do.Will give props to the overall marketing of their tin cans, easily recognizable.Scones were a bit dry, and the sandwiches were OK.Of the 3 macarons i added to the set menu, probably the caramel was the best but nothing like back at home.  Not as chewy or sweet haha.Will say that service was impeccable, as a few different servers served us, and acted quite professional more than friendly, if that makes any sense.
Good rating, mainly atmosphere, nice view,  just had wine and olives/apps.  Very attentive staff,  nice stop over after s stroll throughout the gardens
Mediocre food and overpriced. Unless you are really into tea or like paying for ambiance, steer clear.

I ended off my visiting friends' short stay in Singapore with a posh afternoon hi-tea experience. So some basic information about the place. TWG is a tea boutique franchise based in Singapore, set up by a Singaporean and French pair of friends who met in Morocco. They aim to transform the tea experience - which I understood to mean poshing it up many levels higher to trump the usual coffee&tea places. I like that idea as afternoon hi-teas are supposed to be posh, posh.Ambience: I have visited the TWG tea parlour branch at Ion Orchard. I prefer the branch at MBS as it is more spacious and enjoys more natural light. This is a fancy tea place - but somehow some patrons dine in shorts and tee-shirts. So please dress up nicely. Expect proper napkins, cutlery and fancy tea sets!Service: Impeccable - tonnes of servers milling about making sure that you are well-taken care of!Tea: Such a huge selection of tea flavours to choose from. Apparently, their white teas are quite popular. But they cost approx $26/pot. The more ordinary teas such as Holiday in Paris (I loved it) and Earl Grey are approx $13/pot. Quite pricey for tea ... and when I was at the Ion Orchard branch, they did not refill my tea pot with hot water though my girlfriend said they did so at the Taka branch for her. I ordered a tea milk shake when I was at MBS (the Asian tea flavour) - which was so satisfying - wasn't too thick nor too sweet - and you could sense good tea in there with all that milk and sugar!Food: or rather, confectionary. I'm a huge huge macaroon fan. The macaroon flavours here are all tea-inspired! I tried quite a few flavours that day ... I can't tell you my favourite as I need to try more of them to decide. Don't expect Laduree/Piere Herme sort of premium macaroons ... but these macaroons are still decent macaroons, good enough for a posh afternoon hi-tea experience. and we had the creme brûlée tart as well - it was rather underwhelming :( And I heard the savoury options aren't too impressive either.If you want to posh it out slightly in MBS (as a tourist or local), I would definitely recommend coming here. But don't expect much of the food.

This is just one of the two TWG outlets at the Shoppes and is situated right above a man-made river running through the mall where gondolas glide across the waters. As with all its outlets, the table settings and decor exude a sense of luxury and class. My friends and I swung by from their ION outlet which closes rather early at 9:30 daily. To say they have an extensive collection is putting it mildly. Their menu is choke full of choices and amusing names, especially the tea blends. Be sure to ask for the tea book if you want more details about a specific tea. I ordered a pot of Silver Moon tea, a green tea blend which was meant to be shared by two. I was told I could pour about 3 cups from the pot. It turns out that the fancy tea pot with an insulator only poured out two cups worth of tea leaving us disappointed but we did fill out cups up pretty well so I gave them the benefit of the doubt. What you're really paying for is the location and the ambience. I'd definitely bring a date here to round off the evening with a good cup of tea.

I had the tea set with scones, macarroons and a choice of tea, and subsequently ordered an extra pot of tea (total cost was $40). The tea selection here is Extensive - I capitalize the E for the added effect. Request for the tea manual - where each tea is explained in much detail. A tea connoisseur will probably spend hours sipping tea here from the finely designed tea cups and plates. The setting here is lovely too, as it is located right in the middle of the bustling MBS shoppes.

tea service is pricy.. but the desserts are pretty good.. it's pretty popular so we had to wait to get seated.. it's a great place to sit and just people watch and relax inside a mallthe store also has plenty of teas and you can buy them in individual wrapped bags for a quarter of the price than in their TWG canisters.. we bought 4 different teas back to the u.s. and bought some canisters of amazon..

I was staying at Marina Bay Sands and decided to do tea time before dinner!In America we don't have TWG so I was excited to try it out!As soon as you walk in you'll feel like you got transported to a Parisian cafe! The ambience, decorations even music was on point!I loved how they were playing Andrea Bocelli the entire time!We ordered macaroons and champagne! The macaroons were sensational!Also! Big thank you to the staff for never letting my glass get empty! Can't wait to come back!!

You can't take photos in the store but you can whatever you want if you're having tea!  Service was outstanding and the truffle sandwiches were so good.  The Parisian tea set with two teas and snacks for two was $70.  So worth it.  And you can drink from the $200+ teapots and admire all the TWG branded swag like the linens, all porcelain, etc.  They have so many teas - it's ridiculous.  I'd recommend coming here at least once!

My boyfriend loved this place. Hands down, of all the places we went to, we went to this place TWICE because he liked it that much (the pasta). Our first dining experience here was amazing---service was spot on and spectacular. Second time, we had to flag down our server several times and it left us feeling a certain way we didn't care for. The place is situated right in the middle of mall which certainly gives  great opportunity to people watch. Definitely worth the trip depending on what server you get!

TWG is very old tea house and famous.  They have multiple locations..  This store is located inside the shopping mall next to Marina Bay Sands.   Very small place but have everything to enjoy afternoon tea.  So many choices of teas to choose..  I took the recommended tea and loved it..  It was summer something (can't remember the exact name).Price of the tea is not cheap but it will be great experience since they are not instant teas. Relaxing and enjoying the afternoon tea with sweets...  it was very meaningful.  Most of all, my wife loved it..
Fancy tea place in Singapore.  Bit overpriced but a huge selection of teas. Great ambience.. well deserved 3.5 stars.

What a classy tea shop,  great tea selection, not inexpensive but worth every penny.  Their macaroons are to die for, so many delish flavors and they always look so good displayed in their window.  Service is always courteous and friendly.

Makes buying tea seem like you're purchasing fine wine! Loved the teas that the staff took time to share (sniff test), sans pretentiousness. The tea I tried was delicious! Enjoyed their macarons as well. Would recommend stopping by for a spot of superb tea (at at least 11$ per person depending the tea you order, it better be) and a civilized discussion with friends. They've at least one restaurant and one store. It ain't cheap, but it's worth it.

Doubting between two and three stars here:Food and drinks: definitely two stars.I was extremely disappointed to discover that these huge & attractive tea pots are served less than half full while the cheapest tea is 11 S$. As a huge fan of cream tea, I decided to go for the 19 S$ set which offers two scones, jam and clotted cream plus a tea of your choice (as long it is the 11 $S kind though). I honestly fell disappointed and cheated upon, the scones were tiny but what I thought was even worse was the amount of tea served. Like indicated above, the pots are filled less than half, more like a quarter.I must admit that the scones were nice but considering the price and size I take that as a given, additionally the clotted cream was not really clotted cream.Service and atmosphere: three stars.Overall the service is average, they do provide you with extra lemon slices for your tea when asked but the real reason for going here is the location: this place is in the middle of MBS, which is one of the poshest malls in Singapore and you sit in "the luxury circle" surrounded by Prada, Louis Vuitton and others. So it is excellent for people watching and you feel like you are part of that luxury world (what do you want after paying 11 S$ for a empty-ish teapot).So would I go again? Nope as I think it is horribly overpriced but I guess you pay for the location. Any other TWG in Singapore would get two stars.

+Before we begin, It was 10.30pm when I got there. The first thing I asked out loud was "Where'z the coffee"true story.--------------This place, when you sit down, you don't just watch people. People watch you.So when you eat, a good tip is to eat like a lady.-----------------I had the chocolate Earl Grey tea. It was damn nice. I loved it. It smelled and tasted of chocolate and tea.The only horrible thing was they only served 1 pot and the cups were too dainty.Give it to me in a beer mug and a barrel of tea , i SAY!Food..i had some foie gras salad thing and chicken.I'm sorry if i can't give you the exact details. 10.30pm was way past my bedtime and they don't seem to serve coffee.Chicken was meh. it was alright. tasted like chicken. I've had better chicken elsewhere.I think i had better chicken at a hawker centre.¯\_(ツ)_/¯Foie Gras...meeeehno opinion. sorry guys-----Tea FantasticFood MehFrench Waiter Cute but my singaporean accent threw him off

Lovely place to chill, chat and hide from the heat. Decided to take a break after walking quite a bit in town and at the mall. We were there on a weekday afternoon so it was rather empty and we were served promptly. The waiter sits you down, hands you the menu and help with placing the napkin on your lap. The "classy" experience they try to portray and carry. Not too bad I must say.The tea menu is ultra long. It's about an A2 size back and front printed with font 12?! AWhat I usually do is have the waiter make some recommendations based on what kind of taste I feel like having today. Otherwise, I will probably take around 1hr to choose! And a Tea Book which is sort of a dictionary for the tea offered. I asked for Sweet and Flowery. He recommended Silver Moon tea and Alfonso Tea. Took the silver moon option, tasted great. Pleasant and smells lovely.My friend had a chocolate earl grey. It did smell like chocolate but tasted funny.Ordered a tarte which was average. They have a decent selection of food, appetizers and snacks too. Love to hang and chill at this cafe with friends. The atmosphere is very classy and soothing, allows you to chat at a comfortable volume unlike the local kopi shops which are great just a tad noisy.

Seated promptly but had to flag down a server before our orders can be taken. Water is bottled so it's not free. No tap water available. We ordered the tea set with sandwiches,muffins and macaroons and your choice of tea. I was disappointed when the tea cannot be refilled with water. So it's only  1 serving so if you are sharing it might not be enough to go around. For $39 I expected more.

"TWG Tea is a brand of tea which was established in Singapore in 2008. The company promotes itself as a luxury brand. TWG stands for The Wellness Group." - Wikipedia / TWG website.This is a classic example of how money cannot buy you class. The location is great, the furniture is great. These two alone must have cost TWG a pretty penny.The look and feel of the brand screams "Twinings". And Twinings have been around for 300 years. TWG, in the age of the internet, surely you cannot expect people to buy into your "been around since 1837" myth? Also, for extra credit, homework tonight: Read about the lawsuit filed by another tea company over TWG's logo. Good reads!Back to TWG!Even with the great location and ambience, TWG disappoints in all three areas: Tea, Food and Service._The Tea_Ahhh, a tea shop! Prides itself on the range of tea and knowledgeable staff. What I got was snotty, rude wait staff. No help with the tea selection, no charming conversation about the brand. Just a slightly grotty thick menu with a lot of BIG words describing tea._The Food_The food was overpriced, and just NOT good. Example of overpriced: SGD$32 for a "Chic Tea Set"- 3 finger sandwiches, 2 baby scones, 1 glass of iced tea. - SGD$32! ANYWAY....if the finger sandwiches were good, or IF the scones were fresh or IF the iced tea was topped up, it wouldn't be too bad. But nope. It was just NOT good.Macaron - $2 each. Pretty enough, I pointed to the colours not flavours. There were no signs identifying the flavours. I just chose the prettiest ones: Purple and Blue. Later, in my bill, I find out it was vanilla and passion. (Passion?) The macarons were soggy inside and crumbled too easily. Where's the almond meal? Where's the flavour? Where's my macaron!!?Iced Tea (in a glass) SGD$11. I was so beyond disappointed by this time, I had no energy left to rage about the $11 iced tea._The Service_Cold, unattentive service. At some points, there weere 8 staff on the floor, 3 behind the counter looking busy, the other 5 with their backs to the tables, talking to the staff behind the counters. (Wow, sorry about that long sentence.)They didn't seem to know the menu very well, or if they did, they sure didn't share their knowledge. In summary, stop kidding ourselves. TWG (since 2008) is not what it makes itself out to be. May get better, may even live up to it's self-generated hype. But till then, let's spend our money elsewhere.

Everywhere I look something is sparkling: gold, fine china and most precious crystal, which you can likewise purchase. We see the most wonderful wooden tea tins, which are filigree hand-painted. The rear walls are covered with huge tins full of fine teas. It is not surprising at all, that TWG is known for its innovative tea variety.There is, for example, a tea from Japan, which is usually not sold out of the country. Only TWG may offer it outside of Japan. In addition, there are also some sorts of tea, which are offset with gold. Later, when the very nice tea master opens one of the large tins, golden tea dust gets swirled up. A visit to this store is truly an extraordinary tea experience.

I've been here a few times over the years and it's been consistent about two things: it's high price for honestly, pretty mediocre food. Tonight, was the final straw. A couple of friends and I were in a pinch and went in to grab a quick bite. My friend paid $9 for tofu, fish and rice from the (not so) econo-rice stall. I had the faux ayam penyet and veggie from Sumber Ayam ($9) and it made me sick. I went home and exploded from both ends. NEVER AGAIN!
Limited selections of stalls only the popular staples like roast pork and chicken meals,assortment of noodles, Korean, Chinese and Japanese food.Nice decor. Air conditioning is a plus.

It's a Food Republic. So you know it's gonna be pricey. That being said, there are a couple of stalls I come back to. The yong tau food stall has old school soup properly brewed with soy beans so that the umami is there. I like that they separate the fried ngoh hiang on a plate for you without you having to ask. The roast meat stall is not cheap, but if you're a big eater, the twin roast set meal with dumpling soup and poached veggies is just the thing. It's about $12 but you can pick a combi of duck, char siew, roast pork or chicken. The dumplings are good - sturdy stuffing of meat with identifiable and reasonably sized shrimp and crunchy woodear in HK style. The Toastbox is like any other Toastbox and it has a good selection of egg tarts, probably targeting the office workers in the neighbourhood who pop by for tea. I'm always baffled by why everyone queues at the Toastbox for coffee. The drinks stall is also Toastbox owned and operated - hello? Food Republic owned by them? So you can skip the queue and get your coffee fix from the drinks stall too.

Draws a touristy crowd who is willing to pay $7-$12 per meal.Hipster ambience. Food is good though.But you could always cross the road to SMU and go to the basement via any escalator. Walk to the food court at SMU. And pay half the price for your meal as you would at Food Republic.

Rather pricey food that has a certain standard-a meal here will easily set you back $6-$9. Love the atmosphere here as well as the variety of stalls (restaurants more like) including beef brisket king, Bangkok gem, a Japanese restaurant etc amongst others. Try the individual stalls to find out more!

I don't know why I'm reviewing a Food Republic food court except to say- don't bother when there's a ton of great food within a one block radius! Just walk down Waterloo street and head for the coffee shop down the road that has way better food and not at tourist prices. This Food Republic has air con and a Toast Box in it. That's all that's worth mentioning.

Nice wings!! Everybody comes here for wings! We ordered the cheesy squid stew to go with the wings. Not bad a choice. Very apetitizing. The spiciness is a bit bland, so next time I will ask for more spiciness. Paid before 7.30pm and get 20% off.

Everyone here is so cheerful and friendly! I'm in a rush so just order takeout. The smell of their food is so good I want to come back again!! Guess what?!! They just served me watermelon smoothie because my food is not ready yet! This place didn't cease to amaze me!!I'll be back!!

My favourite place for fried chicken wings - I adore their soya chicken wings which are perfectly fried to a crisp while remaining moist. They also serve several other variations of fried chicken but really, why waste your calories when the soya one is the most awesome. It is a little pricey at 12 bucks for 4 chicken wings but I think it's very much worth it. We also ordered the bulgogi fries and tteokbokki cheese and seafood stew. The fries was tasty with beef that wasn't overly cooked. The stew was a tad too sweet and spicy for my liking. The watermelon soju was interesting but taste wise I think it's mediocre. I tried to make reservations an hour before I arrived and the staff curtly told told me to just show up because reservations are not necessary. When I arrived, the place was full. So that was rather annoying. Emil was friendly and offered recommendations because he thought we may have ordered too much for our party of 3. Unfortunately, it was a little off putting when he insisted we write a review on FB and show him before letting us leave. He did make up for it with a 1-for-1 voucher for dessert but it did mar my impression of the place. Multiple outlets exist but I've only visited this branch.

Went there with friend. Tried their boneless chicken, seafood topokki and watermelon soju.1. Service: it was great. The food was served less than 15 mins after we place order2. Environment: good place for gathering but it's slightly too dim... 3. Food: the boneless chicken fried with rice cake in sweet and spicy sauce. Something look totally different from the photo in the menu. But it was great. While seafood topokki, I counted it was only 4 rice cake... 4 rice cakes for $20.... I am not really happy about it. 4. Drink: the watermelon juice is diluted with water, not premium type of soju... And it cost $38!!

If you want to save a bit (20% off food bill), settle your bill and leave by 730pm. I think it is quite a good incentive for diners to eat and go instead of lingering and chatting among themselves long after the food is gone, and a big crowd is waiting outside for a table. Having read about the crowd if you go at the usual dinner time, we decided to go early and arrived around 6pm. The place was already half filled by then. At around 7pm, there was a line of people waiting for a table and it was only a Monday night. Having spied the early bird special of getting 20% off, we decided to try to leave by 730pm and let others have our table. A feat as we had two friends who only arrived close to 7pm and had just 30 minutes to finish the food. They ran out of the watermelon shell for the watermelon soju so we skipped that. Instead we tried the corn cheese which was really just average. A bit too creamy and cheesy that it was quite jelat (very rich) after a while and it was already shared by 4. The ganjang chicken wings (soy sauce) were really good and I must say I prefer the wings to the actual fried chicken pieces. The fried chicken were cut into 4 pieces and the breast meat was a bit on the dry side and not that enjoyable after a while. It would be worse if you did not order the chicken with any sauce. We had spicy up (not that spicy after all) and yangnyum up (like sweet and sour sauce with a bit of spice). The skin was crispy and delicious and the meat (except breast meat) moist and tender.I think 4 diners are just the right group size to try 2 different types of fried chicken and a side of chicken wings as you get 2 chicken pieces and a chicken wing. It may be different if you are very hungry or have a group of guys. The buffet is still available though they limit a 2 hour window for that.

Who doesn't love a good fried chicken? Ever since my first taste of Korean fried chicken at Mad for Chicken in NYC (they go by a diff name Tt escapes my pre-caffeinated brain now), I've been longing for those robust and exhilarating flavors again.The search ends at Chicken Up. Exceptionally tender and juicy chicken with a light and superbly crispy batter. BonChon can screw its double fried a** staleness that it claims to be authentic. Yes I'm still darn pissed about Tt crappy chicken that I had there a yr ago at the Bugis+ outlet. Anyway, their mild up spicy isn't that spicy to me so i'll go for suicide chicken next time. I absolutely went gaga over the soya chicken. My gawd. Droolicious I tell ya! First time trying the Andong chicken stew and my.. It was such a silent killer. Be very careful eating this one. I didn't pay attention and a little of the soup went down the wrong pipe and I was coughing and tearing for a long time. That said, it's actually not outrightly spicy if you are careful. Well flavored chicken that falls off the bone. They also have the glass noodles in them.Chicken lovers, this is the place to be! They do a chicken buffet with a beer option. Do check them out!

I'm going to have to disagree with the other reviewers here. While this place is billed as serving Korean style fried chicken, I felt like I was eating a Korean-inspired promotional item from KFC, at a Kko Kko Na Ra price.Yes, the chicken pieces were large and generous. But the quality of the batter was lacking and the crispiness didn't keep well. The sauces didn't deliver the same punch as Kko Kko Na Ra's or 4 Fingers's.

FRIED CHEEEEKEN!!!!!!!Just 2 of us for dinner today and certainly over ordered. Started off with fries - scratch that a humongous pile of fries. It was tossed with a good serving of kimchi - great combi to the super crispy fries. Shoved it all the carbs down with servings of yakult soju (no surprises here - it's just soju + yakult).Ordered wings, 4 of them - can't remember what it's called but the wings were generously glazed with something syrupy and sprinkled with sesame seeds. So much glaze, so crispyyyy.Main dish was 1/2 chicken (cut into 4 pieces) of spicy cheeken. Supposedly Chicken Up's highlight and I vouched for their recommendation! How do they make it so tasty and crispy!?

When an #overrated food met an #overpriced reality, disappointment emerges. Only at Chicken Up, Tanjong Pagar. Go there to experience #lousy #service as a bonus.#chickenup #chicken #up #tanjongpagar #tanjong #pagar #singapore #dreadful #badfood

Really its 4.5 stars. Rejoice! I think I have found my go-to drinking and KFC place on the island. The variety, the vibe, and the sheer portions of the chicken is indeed one up from the rest.The moment you walk into Chicken Up, you feel this warmth about the place- Kpop featured on the big screen, beer and soju all around, call buttons for service... this feels a bit like home (Ktown LA). Simulated and having the concept of "rounds" when partying in Korea, I believe that Chicken Up is perfect for "Ee-Cha" (2nd round- more drinking and noshing on snacks) before heading out for Karaoke. Something that Singaporeans should really start adapting to.Lets get on with the food, shall we?Original Fried Chicken: Amazing. The skin is fried perfectly and well seasoned, while the meat is super juicy and moist. Honestly delicious. It takes me back to the ones in Korea.I don't even know why real KFC or Popeye's exist when you can have this chicken. Seriously, one of the best.Soy Chicken Wings: Also a delicious marinade. 4 wings, large and meaty with ample soy garlic. Very delicious.Sweet & Spicy Chicken: A bit too sweet for my liking, was hoping to have a bit more kick, but equally delicious.  They also serve a "popcorn chicken" version of this sauce the comes boneless. **Tip for all you Americanized people- this is the closest to Orange Chicken you will get in Singapore. Screw Panda Express, Chicken Up's popcorn chicken + a bowl of rice may very well be my go-to meal at least once a week. It's THAT good.**Odeng Tang (Fishcake soup): I was feeling a bit under the weather but the spicy broth hit the spot.  The portion of fishcake was VERY generous.Cheese Corn: Gooey, Rich, Creamy- honestly perfect for beer.Truffle Fries: Ample seasoning, good portion for sharing.Beverages: Korean drinks, Hite, Soju, Draft, Asahi, Maggoli, you name it, they have it. Outstanding.Only downfall- the radish cubes were not marinated as well as I liked it to be, but this is a very minor detail.so, why come to Chicken Up? 3 reasons.1. $25 AYCE Chicken Dinner, with $15 AYCD Beer top up. Best deal in town. Perfect for guys2. Perfect place to unwind with your friends, snack, nosh, and catch up on Kpop3. Large and delicious portions and a good variety of Anju (Korean Tapas) Now all they need is a noribang next door and my Ktown experience would be complete here in Singapore.

Routinely one of the busiest restaurants in tanjong pagar (even on weekdays), Chicken Up brings us a simple menu built round its infamous fried chicken combined with a great environment and friendly staff. The Ganjang (garlic soya) was the first of its kind for me and it never disappoints.

All I can say is if a) you're super hungry after work b) you love fried chicken, approach Chicken Up with caution. The dude and I are not buffet people. We took the buffet because it made sense to pay $25 to try a few flavors since even though he's half Korean, we both had no idea what Yamyung (?) or Andong stew was. Not being buffet people, we were therefore also set on just enjoying a slow meal, appreciating the flavors and talking instead of trying to cram as much food as possible down our gut.Here's the problem.The fried chicken here is really, really good. I would say it ranks second or slightly on par with No. 5's har cheong gai in terms of fried chicken execution. Very crisp on the outside even after the chicken has cooled, ridiculously juicy on the inside. We had the soy sauce, spicy, curry and popcorn flavors and then a stew each. The stew is quite light and we love the kick from the chillis bouncing off the sweet sauce.Ended up eating way too fast, probably too much and we were very full. Happy too. The "truffle" fries (there's really sparse specks of truffle shavings in the salt) were nothing to scream about but they were well fried too. The salad was wilted. But you're not there for these sides.Next time I visit it's probably going to be Hite beer + wings.Oh boy.

We wandered into Chicken Up on a lark as it was one of the only places still open when the hunger instinct hit one Friday night, but we wound up swearing to return, and soon!Due to the late hour, we erred on the side of over-ordering, although to be fair, the outcome would probably have been the same at the normal dinner bell.We decided on some Korean beer, the mild original fried chicken, the popcorn chicken, the cheesy corn and an order of truffle fries.  Everything was delicious, but it was the cheesy corn ($15) that upped the table tension.  El Queso Grande and I took one look at the hot cast iron surface with sizzling sweet corn and melty cheese and God only know what other fatty and tasty additives (I suspect butter and mayo) and IT WAS ON!  Jealously, we eyed one another's progress as we grimly munched and marched towards the exact center line of the sizzling plate, our taste buds writhing in ecstasy.The truffle fries were also quite incredible, easily the best fries I've ever had at a chicken joint.  We asked and got some Japanese mayo, which made it even better.  Each fry was perfectly crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside...we fervently hope that they come that way each and every time.The popcorn chicken ($20) was good...as another reviewer mentioned, it's the closest you get to an orange or sesame chicken in Singapore.  We found the mild original chicken to be decent, but we are looking forward to trying some of the other varieties next time.PARTING THOUGHT: We can't wait to go back for more of that cheesy corn!

This place is delicious. I went with friends and we did the all you can eat, and just went with the flavors that were suggested to us. The chicken was perfectly fried to order, all the sauces were super flavorful, and the chicken was juicy. Throw in sides, which you should try not too eat too much of because... CHICKEN. Just be prepared to feel fat and disgusting afterwards.Worth it.

Loved the watermelon soju! Refreshing... I could drink buckets of that stuff. The fried chicken was so tasty. Juicy and crispy. That's how I like it. My fave was the original crispy fried chicken. That was the tastiest. The spicy fried chicken was alright. Not especially spicy nor flavorful. I recommend getting the original rather than the spicy. The soy fried chick was yummy too.Go for the buffet at your own peril. We walked out of there feeling really sick. Really really sick and swearing off fried chicken for the next few months or year. That's because the chicken cuts are pretty big. Like KFC size pieces. So it's not the same as eating wings elsewhere. Go slow... And pace yourself. They took really long serving our chicken so we stuffed our faces with those oily bits and were so happy until that feeling kicked in. Also go for the cheese corn. It could have been more sizzling but it was delicious even unsizzled. Enjoy!

A Vegetarian's Point of View Came here with fried chicken eating friends and had low expectations on my eating options. Surprisingly, there was stuff for me to eat and the chicken smelled and looked really good!The place doesnt look very welcoming from the street but dont let it fool you, the inside is warm, the staff is friendly and their is Girl Generation k-pop playing on a continuous loop. Food-wise, the chicken were huge pieces, kinda like the friend chicken from home where the chickens are genetically engineered. never seen chicken so big in Singapore before. What they call 'Popcorn Chicken' was really the Americanized Orange Chicken from Panda Express only bigger. Looked delicious even though i didnt eat it.Ended up getting the Cheese Corn (fairly good), the salad (good) and the truffle fries (really good). All the portions are huge so bring your appetitive

Call me a fat slob but you cant really go wrong with copious amounts of beer and fried chicken. And that's what you get at the aptly named Chicken Up! - a popular fried chicken outlet from Korea.First, lets talk about the beer. On the menu is something called Suicide Beer. It is essentially a 1-litre mug of Heineken draught. Yep, 1-litre! Not difficult to understand why I like the place, eh? On to the food. Not your usual traditional Korean fare and not quite KFC. One of the side dishes is actually steamed Korean dumplings which are light and delightful, an excellent contrast to the fried chicken. All patrons also gets served free salad and pickles the moment you place your orders. Definitely good to partake in a little greens before the unhealthy stuff.  The chicken is served spicy or spicier, Korean chilli style! Crispier than crisp on the outside; soft, juicy and tender on the inside. Recently, South Korea's plans for world domination through the incredibly formulaic yet insanely infectious kpop has been gathering pace at an alarming rate. One fortunate by-product is Chicken Up ending up on our shores. This tiny eatery is everything Korean down to their staff, most of the regulars and the insanely annoying yet addictive kpop tunes and programmes broadcasting on their tv. Definitely not one for people who cant stand the kpop phenomenon and prices are more restaurant side than fast food eatery.

Hard to find much to complain about here- the chicken was excellent with a wide variety, and the beer kept flowing, even if it was not great beer. A fantastic price if you want to eat an insane amount of chicken.

Just check in here again for the MSG intoxication fix and we got it for sure.  Please to report they are still as good as ever.  The fav is the yam fritter? It is nothing like any place we have in Singapore.  Seaprch with brocoli also a winner.Please don't order the mango pudding and the PamelonSego they are basically the same base with an added mango pudding.

Overall pretty good dim sum (3.5-4 stars), similar to Imperial Treasure although I think I still prefer the latter. But it was a nice change and they had 雪山包 which is filled with custard rather than salted egg, which I prefer over 流沙包.Char siew - 3.5 starsNot exceptional. Ever-so-slightly on the dry end. Wish it came with a sauce as I was craving hawker-style char siew rice.

My first time at Wah Lok was filled with mouth-watering dim sum.From the usual Har Gao, Siew Mai to the Bo Lo Bao and Lotus Leaf rice... each bite just gets more and more intriguing.. at least for me.. :PA good dim sum always makes me happy and I'll love to come back for more soon.Just remember to order their bo lo bao to try... the crust is crisps, bread soft and the char siew is juicy... Love love love!!

Was told that dim sum here was really delicious, and on first impression, they do look scrumptious, but soon realised that it's the skill of the photographer of those pics in the menu. Could not for the life of me understand how they managed to win so many 'awards' that lined the wall behind the concierge!The prawn dumplings were bland, and not even decently presented in the basket, rather it seemed thrown together. The BBQ pork puff with preserved vegetables did not have any preserved vegetables in them. The radish cake fried with XO sauce arrived cold as was the century egg porridge, which I subsequently sent back to be heated up. We also ordered a stir-fried vegetables with macadamia nuts - also cold, and bland, and looks like some home cook stir-fry! The siu mai is good, but one dish out of the 10 we ordered is dismal indeed.

Invited to celebrate the signing of a $100M+ project with senior executives.  Seafood menu was selected.  8 courses of well crafted meals added to the good company.  One of the highlight meals so far in Singapore.

(this is a review of our chinese new year dinner - a tad late, folks!)wah lok has always been a steady bulwark of the fine dining cantonese scene, and it well deserves its reputation - food is outstanding, service is utter old-school goodness, and the place is modern (wnone of that outdated furnishing you see so often in these restaurants) but amenable to cosy family dinners.we started with a soup of whelk and chicken, chewy pieces of the seafood in a deeply-flavored, golden chicken soup (very good with lots of white pepper). comforting and cleansing, and a good start - we cantonese put great stock (oh, haha, punny) in our soups.and of course we had yusheng, especially since they had the parang fish my parents like - a small wolf-herring, the traditional choice before salmon became the in thing - I liked this for its heavy addition of nuts and sesame seeds and not-too-sweet-or-oily quality.it's been a tradition (ever since they started popping up in singapore) for us to have poon choi/pen cai as part of this first dinner; essentially a basin full of chinese-style dried seafood and meats cooking in a luxurious brown sauce, it's a symbol of abundance and prosperty - and therefore very luck-y.I took up their suggestion of soy sauce chicken as a substitute for the more traditional roast duck (which we dislike for the gamey-ness permeates the entire dish while braising), and this dish was pretty much close to perfect. chockful of stuff, this had 1. whole dried baby abalone 2. mud carp balls (crazy-delicious) 3. dried oysters 4. large dried shitake 5. pan-fried live prawns with caramelized shells 6. soy-sauce chicken 7. braised pork shank (tender and fall-off-the-bone) 8. black moss 7. tian jin cabbage (soft, and delicious from absorbing all the good stuff) 8. tender radish pieces 9. cubes of fried yam.we finished with a round of dessert, all mildly sweet renditions of cantonese mainstays, and a good soft finish to the elevating meal. I was beyond impressed - which I'm sure shows - and looking forward very much to my next meal here.

Sorry, not impressed. I wanted to like it as I have many Cantonese friends and they said it was great and one of the best Canto places in Singapore. I went for a work dinner and we went for the evening menus. I was the only one eating vegetarian there and I really wasn't very impressed. The first course I got was a salad with strawberries and loads of mayonnaise. Some of the dishes were ok like the thick mushroom (gloopy) soup, and the pepper filled with nuts but others really weren't up to par. I would give it another go for dim sum but really was not so happy with the meal. mylifeinsin.com/2013/11/…

Nice place, think they upgraded quite recently so it's fairly modern and chichi looking. We made reservations but it wasn't that crowded when we were there around 1pm. We had dimsum for lunch - Decent food though I thought portions felt a little small. I liked the Po Lo Bao, freshly made, soft bun with gooey char siew filling. Rest of the food was ok - nice but not particularly outstanding. The chee cheong fun with fried you tiao was oddly a lot more you tiao than chee cheong fun, and you had to add on the sauce separately. The steamed carrot cake is served in a dessert-looking-container, couldn't identify what it was at first!I liked that they could do exact numbers for some of the dim sum - so everyone was ensured 1 pc without too many leftovers. They served lukewarm towels at each table instead of disposable wet napkins, felt a bit like I was on a plane.

Before I start my review, I would like to commend a short-hair female staff named Siew Chin, for her excellent service and impeccable attention to the table. It was rare chance to be served by such a warm and lively lady who always carried a smile on her face and everyone was impressed with the service even though we did not feedback to the management.  We were there to have a family dinner and tried some alacarte dishes. I am not a keen fan of expensive ingredients and thus I cannot comment on the taste of some food but those who had them enjoyed the delicacies.Mee Sua with Crab in Huatiao Stock ($12) was originally with Mee Sua with Lobster($22) but with opted for crabs since they were cheaper and the stock base remains the same. This was surprisingly simple but flavorful and mildly sweet. It was highly recommended by the staff and now by me because it is a nice change from the usual Yi Mian or fried noodles/rice.Hokkaido Scallops in Golden Sauce was better than the fish. The scallop was undeniably meaty and cooked to right doneness but the thin layer of fried flour batter wrapping the scallop was unnecessary.
Since Cathay restaurant is now closed, we have been visiting Wah Lok for their dim sum selection. Great service, and yummy classic dim sum dishes, executed well. Highly recommended.
Quality still as good as ever, but the portion sizes have shrunk so much it's almost funny - when I saw the size of the puo luo bao after 2 years overseas, I had a double take.

We went to Wah Lok for an aunt's birthday lunch and on retrospect, we should have picked Hua Ting for assured quality Cantonese food instead of being all experimental. Didn't think it was at all value for money either.Food: OK it wasn't lousy, but it wasn't fabulous either. The deep fried white bait was soft and soggy, most disappointing. The steam prawn dumplings and steamed shrimp with pork and roe (har gau and siew mai respectively) were very average, and the steamed rice rolls with dough sticks tasted oily, flat and soggy. The fried beancurd skin prawn roll was too oily and the sliced fish congee had a thin consistency with very little ingredients. Mango pudding was the only decent thing we had. Overall disappointing.Ambience : Too dimService: Manager was very nice but service otherwise unimpressive. Pfft.So will not return.

I wanted to like Wah Lok as I love me some good dim sum. However, having just returned from Hong Kong a few days before my lunch at Wah Lok, I was disappointed to discover that the dim sum at Wah Lok, despite being one of Singapore's best dim sum restaurants, still can't compare to the typical dim sum restaurants in Hong Kong. The porridge was boring (perhaps its the nature of the dish?) and unmemorable but more significantly, I thought it was overpriced. The Po Lo Bao receives rave reviews online but I was let down by the thick pastry crust and overly starchy char siew filling. I prefer a light, fresh and crisp pastry crust. The chee cheong fun was also thick, and did not have a delicate, translucent texture, which I would have preferred.Perhaps standards are dipping. I'll probably check out other dim sum restaurants in Singapore.

4-stars for the bakery on ground level.  3-stars for the subterranean restaurant. While there is great variety, the price ends up similar to a full service meal. Yes,  you have to get your own food and utensils. No matter how well they decorate like a Swiss chalet,  the plain fact is you are eating in a b-2 bomb shelter.

The decor alone was enough to pique my curiosity and want to give this place a try. I have returned many times since for the food. As you make your way down to the restaurant, you are greeted with various Swiss-themed characters that actually move. Once you enter the restaurant, the food takes over.Everything is presented well, you can choose what you want and then give your card to the person serving at that station to add to your bill. At the end of your meal, you present your card to the cashier and pay. The concept is good and there are many options to choose from though paying for each item as you go can add up. My favorite thing is to choose from their special promo- they have one for lunch and dinner- you get an entree plus a homemade drink. At lunch it is only $8.90, quite a bargain, though it does go up some for dinner.They also have tasty sandwiches and other treats available upstairs. All in all, still a good value and worth giving them a try.

Yum - I had a lovely wholemeal baguette with Ham and Swiss Cheese here. I had it fresh, but they would have toasted it for me. I was a generous size, good serving of ham and fresh Swiss Cheese.  All good. The range of breads and sandwiches is great, come here if you're hungry for bread!

Get ready to rumble. Make sure you are hungry. One stall is better than the next. Everything is fresh and prepared right in front of you. Scope out the place because the servings are large and the options aplenty. Paella, crepes, wood burning pizza, veggies, soup,  Caesar salad, sandwiches, sausages...the list goes on. They are great marketers for a number of reasons--1) they give you a card to swipe so you can keep going back and purchasing things (small lemonade was $4.50) and then you have sticker shock at check out; 2) there is a great play area where, after you have spent $10.90 on one of their kid meals, you can safely dispatch the children to play; 3) it's located under a mall at least two floors down and it's cool (with the Singapore heat you'll pay almost anything for relief) and 4) the food is fresh, fresh, fresh. $92.50 for three adults and one child for lunch, and I'd do it again. It's nice to have some not-so-Asian food and you get it at Marche.

I like the concept of Marche, always have and probably always will. It is actually quite like a cooler version of a food court where you are given a card to pay for food from the various stalls and then you settle the bill in your card before you leave. Of course, it is far more expensive than a food court as well and serves primarily Western food with quite a few Swiss dishes such as its popular Rosti. When it comes to outlets, I still prefer the one at Vivo City. The food at the 313 outlet, particularly the rosti, is not as good as at Vivo City. The rosti is usually overcooked and the queue is usually very long depending on the time of day. An average meal comes up to about $25 and so far, I don't feel that it's worth the price. The pork and chicken leg we had the last time was rather dry. I do, however, quite like their selection of breads in the bakery outside.

I remember visiting Marche often as a kid when it first started out in Heeren. Till today  queues to get in are still as crazy on the weekends. The one dish that screams Marche till this day would have to be the Rosti with the spiral sausage or smoke salmon. I have not found or tried better Rosti so far. A huge dash of sour cream and extra chives and you're good to go! Yet another dish that has stood the test of time would be the savory crepes. My personal combo would be salmon, mushrooms, cheese and salad all packed into the crepe. This is a fairly heavy dish and is perfect to share between 2. The only downside however is that drinks are on the pricey side with fruit juices costing almost $8. If only there was ice water on the house. Overall a great place to enjoy a hearty meal!

I generally avoid dining at hot spots of Orchard but decided to try this place on a friend's recommendation. Honestly, this place was a let down. Apart from the ambiance, which I would say is interesting, the food was slightly below average and given the price you pay, I was bitterly dissapointed. To add to the dissapointment, service was bad. I guess I will continue to avoid hot spots in Orchard.

I had a hankering for some western food after having spent 7 days eating local food. Not that I minded cuz I grew up on it but variety is the spice of life.Anyway I walked by the Marche by Movenpick so I decide to try it. I walked into the downstairs restaurant and was given the lunch specials for the week and a credit card. I was a little confused but soon figured out the process. Simply go to any of the food stations and order your food, drink or dessert. Hand over the card and the charges are added into it. Then find yourself a table and start eating. When you are done walk to the exit and hand over the card to the cashier. He will figure out what you owe and after paying you are on your way.Firstly the process was easy enough to figure out by watching others. Secondly some of the food stations can have pretty long lines and you might have to wait a while for you turn. Thirdly, the food was pretty good but a little too salty but that could be the dish I ordered (Swiss Rosti with salami and tomato chutney). Fourthly service is mostly absent as it was all self serve.I would give it 3.5 stars if I could and I would try some of the other dishes next time.

I really like this chain. So many choices and I haven't found anything that's bad yet. They can get quite busy on weekends but it's still a good place to go if you have kids (so many choices!). This location wasn't too crowded when we went and the bakery looked yummy.
Yeah still a so so place in terms of food and the staff really are collectively unhappy people. I still think their bakery is really good when you get it fresh.

I've been to Marche in 313 Somerset a few times now. You'd never know there's a massive restaurant with a ton of variety lurking one floor beneath the bakery emitting heavenly smells. You go inside and take the stairs to the right. You are greeted at the bottom by someone handing you a card at the bottom. You will use this card at all of the food stations you decide to order from. They put the information on your card and you will use it to pay at a station as you leave, so don't lose it!Now for the food. I haven't seen this kind of variety anywhere else besides MEDZ's in the basement of Orchard Central, which is no longer open. The produce is really fresh and they offer filled crepes, salads, veggies, and meats ranging from fish to chicken and steak. You hand them your card when you order and they either hand you the food or tell you how long the wait will be. You go grab your food from the same station if there is a wait. You also seat yourself, and seating is plentiful. I did venture down here one day for lunch during the weak during the peak hour and it was a bit crowded and daunting, so I recommend hitting them during slow times if you don't love crowds.They got something for everyone and are good for large groups or just a solo dining experience. They made it very easy for me to follow the Paleo lifestyle! Worth checking out.

Marche provided a different binge experience for me when I shared another meal episode with my relatives. Different primarily because (a) cuisine-wise - so not Asian; (b) decor-wise - like I was at a luxury-type family camp; (c) price-wise - up to three times more than the usual Kopitiam; (d) location-wise - not only in town, but buried deep under like a bunker...freaking awesome; (e) atmosphere - casual, relaxing, family-friendly, with a *BEAST* A/C that made me forget the infamous Singapore heat; and (f) experience-wise - worth doing at *least* once (in my case, just twice).Both times in this..."Western-styled Kopitiam"...was a breath of fresh air. Each of us were given a card (the kiddos were particularly excited about their "credit cards") to use for keeping tabs on whatever dishes we ordered within the establishment. It's so easy to get carried away...just order something, pass the service staff your card, get swiped, pick up your dish...and head back to your table to eat. However, *please* don't lose this freaking card. I asked the lady at the payment counter and a lost card was like $150'ish. (Come to think of it...can you imagine if a whole group goes in, charges all cards with a drink each, and then spam orders everything else on just one card and then "loses" it? $150...? Only? Sure! LOL, okay, please don't do that...this is Singapore afterall...the consequences will...s-u-c-k!)So while the decor, location, and overall atmopshere were all great...they failed to shine in the most important area: le' food.The food was just okay. It was presented so well on the plate...but was just so...okay. It tasted fresh and the quantity was decent...but the taste was just okay.Okay, just okay, get it? Only 3-stars...because this place is just okay...especially when my own tab came up to $70+ both times. (Oh family, what I do to hang out with you all...)NOTE:No pictures at or around the stalls. The service staff were pretty quick at making it *very* clear.Yelp 100: 56/100/My-last-3-weeks-in-SG

This is a buffet-style restaurant which has nice atmosphere and decorated in the Alpen style.Service is good, food is very fresh and not bad. It is a bit on the expensive side but you pay for what you get. I love everything there especially the savory crepes, beef goulash and caesar salad with roasted chicken. My partner really loves the rosti with smoked salmon though. It is best not to go during the lunch hour or dinner unless you don't mind constantly queueing for the table, then the food and drinks. However, local people don't mind queuing and I suppose they get used to it in the hawker centres and have become their culture. I won't go there for a relaxed meal unless it is not in the busy time and it is far from ideal when you have children in the group.Another thing I want to highlight is that this place is also good for vegetarian and health concious people as they serve organic or food that are preservatives free and the ingredients of the food were fresh.

Somehow it has a great concept but the food and quality do not justify the price they charge for their food. I had a pizza and it was dripping in oil and it was rubbery as well. I will not eat nor recommend this place. The staffs are like robots.Cashier asked me how the food was and I told her how it was which was oily, she never replied not acknowledged my reply. I guess they have to refer to the training manual for the reply to dissatisfied customers

Marché has a great selection of fresh, well prepared food. IF you are the kind of person who want some of everything you can blow your wad pretty quick. 2px for lunch spent around $140 which is kind of insane as you could have gone to fine dining for that. The roast beef and potatoes was good, as was the rostey, the coffee and cakes were so so. I did have a sandwich from the bakery this morning and it was a reasonable 4.90 so depending on what you order YMMV The sandwich was good and will go back if for nothing else beside that or a rostey (hash brown)

Oh Marche, there's not enough words in Webster's dictionary that describes how much I love your establishment. From the Swiss cliché props, wooden tables and  great food presentation, this place is a comfort spot for me. As you descend the stairs down to the restaurant, a friendly worker will hand you a card. From there, you decide what you want to eat, drink and how much you want. When you add things to your tray, you hand the worker behind each counter your card which keeps tabs of what you'll be consuming. I usually go during lunch, since their special can't be beat. $8.90 for a meal + one of their handmade drinks. Seeing as their drinks are usually $4-5, having them include it in the lunch special is a steal. Their lunch menu is updated every week online and they usually offer four different options every weekday. I've never been disappointed with my meal at Marche. My go to drink is the pineapple lemonade which goes perfectly with many of their meal options. Their rotisserie items, Swiss rosti, and pizza selections are always a safe bet. Be sure to grab one of their free apple card candies on your way out, and also stop by their bakery upstairs. Their beignets, rolls and sandwiches are also a must try.

Marche is a Swiss restaurant that has a unique concept. Unlike other conventional restaurants whereby you order, pay and consume, each customer is issued a Marche card. They then enter the restaurant and order their dishes from the various stations. These include fresh fruit juices, other beverages, roasted dishes and soup. The rosti is absolutely delicious. Image this; sinking your teeth into strips of potato dripping in butter sauce. You can choose to eat this alone with a dollop of sour cream, or with sides like smoked salmon or sausage. After dining, simply swipe your card at the exit to get your total bill, pay and proceed to exit. If you're not in the mood for a full meal, the Marche bakery offers a wide selection of breads at affordable prices. All breads are baked on the spot, with rows of freshly baked crispy breads in the background. Truly a feast for the eyes. But at the end of the day, the most important thing is the taste, which also did not disappoint. The Rosti-Bacon roll is delicious and fragrant, but a little too hard for my liking. Try the swiss-hot-cross bun that are soft, fluffy and slightly sweet. Perfect for a light afternoon snack. It also offers a variety of pastries and open sandwiches that are drool-inducing just by looking at it. The fruit tarts glisten attractively with fresh fruits packed atop of the pastry. Complete your afternoon pick-me-up with a hot cup of tea, coffee or even canned drinks if they suit your preference!

Love Marche's dinning concept. Beautifully decorated and it's a WOW, everything must try when i get to the restaurant. All the food there are so alluring. Nevertheless, i still go for my standard choice, Plain Swiss Rosti with Sour Cream, this is a must try in Marche. One of their signature dish. Always in long queue when u head into Marche.The crust is crispy and together with the sour cream, thumbs up!I will always order their mushroom soup as well. Nice thick mushroom soup. Now, it's the dessert time. I'm always a fan of Marche's waffles! Together with the best ice cream in the World, Movenpick ice cream, best combination you could ever ask for. Totally fabulous!Even though, Marche is a bit pricey. It is really a good place to hang out with your brunch of friends.

Marche has an interesting concept whereby they give you a card (which you must NEVER lose if not you gotta fork out $100 whether you ate that amount or not) and you go round the various stores ranging from grilled food to salad to soup to desserts. I am quite partial to their rosti.. I mean seriously, you've gotta try their rosti at least ONCE in your life. Who the heck goes to Marche and not eat their rosti? Their desserts are tons of misses (don't get me started on their bread and butter pudding.. oh the horror..) .. the only thing they got right are their crepe desserts and their Movenpick ice cream sorbet (which are heavenly). Their soups and pasta are delicious as well.. and their crepes.. mmm.. do give Marche a go when you want something a little bit unique.

I've been to Marche a few times and finally tried the one at 313 a few days back. Overall, I did enjoy my food, but kind of expected something better than what I was given.I like the unique concept of how to pay later and all transactions in the restaurants are made via the Marche card. Word of caution here, DO NOT or rather, NEVER lose that card. You pay hell a lot more than what you will be eating if you lose it.The must try at Marche are the Rosti and Soup! I wouldn't recommend desserts there nor a place to chill and hang out. If you must, head up to Blue Mountain Cafe, located in the same mall for drinks and coffee.

I've always been a fan of marche  and I was quite sad when the heeren outlet closed down. Thankfully now there's one at 313 and its still awesome food. Obviously everyone knows about the rostti from Marche. Its gotta be rostti with smoked salmon for me. The crepes are pretty great too and so are the soups. The pizzas here - I would give a miss. I like my pizzas with the tomato base. What they do here is places tomato slices under the toppings. Honestly, I don't know how that adds any sort of flavour to the dough. So just a heads up.
I have never been to the restaurant but they have great bread. I especially like the circular buns that look like cinnamon rolls but are filled with cheese and ham.

Egg noodles with prawns and pork rib ($11) - 3.5 starsLoved the crunchy texture of the noodles and the pork rib was well done. However the three prawns that came with it (I could only stomach two) tasted fishy and not fresh. Gross. Portion is also small and didn't taste very authentic. Also, I don't know of an actual Vietnamese dish that looks like this so perhaps I'm ignorant.

Have been seeing Nam Nam with ridiculously long queues but finally had the chance to try it at PS (yes, slow, I know).Not sure what to expect but everyone knows how hard it is to find good Vietnamese food in Singapore. I must say I was please tot surprised! The soup was nice and delicate and everything tasted fresh and crisp, the way Vietnamese food should be. The Spring Roll's skin was a little bit starchy as compared to others I've tried but the Pho was delicious! Over the course of 2 visits, we tried the beef slices, pork ball, beef ball and mixed beef. The beef balls were a little touched than your average beef ball, and the beef slices were lacking that fat content, making it turn hard and dry very quickly, however, the pork balls are to die for! We even had the chance to try their friend banana with coconut cream and that was lovely as well. It's a good casual place for a reasonably price bite in orchard (sandwiches at $6.90 and Pho's starting at $9.90).The only setback about the place was the service. Staff were a little rude and the last at the cashier always gave this "matter-of-fact-ly" tone, while they had no idea which direction they wanted customers to queue to pay. Was a bit chaotic at the entrance while customers who are there for the first time, aren't sure if they should order and pay before being seated or after as the queue to be seated, leads straight to the cashier. However, despite the service, the food comes out at a decent place and it's a great place to grab lunch as their lunches come with a free drink, which is great for a simple yet tasty lunch.

I always have a thing or two for Vietnamese noodles - one of my favourites in my list. This restaurant always catch my attention whenever I enter the entrance or the extended building. I have been here a couple of times, but to be honest I haven't been convinced by the quality of the noodles and soup. On this trip, I ordered the beef combination beef clear noodles and it cost $11. Don't be misled by the size of the bowl, it looks huge but when I saw the portion of the noodles, I was disappointed and left shaking my head especially to my friend who was as bewildered as me. The noodles and soup are average, I taste better ones at food courts and at a lower price, so my overall experience was a disappointing one and not to mention the meal was hardly filling. Perhaps 1/2 full? My friend ordered the sandwich and it looks small but he found it to be nice. As for the service, it was slow, perhaps short-handed. To order your meal, you have to go to pay first before your food comes. For this part they get points for it as the food was served quite fast. Overall, I am not in a hurry to come back here, there are other better Vietnamese food outlets out there I feel.

Nam Nam will never be my first choice for Vietnamese food, but in Singapore, beggars can't be choosers. The great thing about Nam Nam is it's convenience:. It has two locations in Orchard and another one in City Hall. I usually order the beef pho and/or chicken meatball baguette. I say and/or because I would order the beef pho and then take out chicken meatball baguette for dinner :P I like the beef pho broth here bc they add cinnamon so there's an extra kick of flavor. The noodles are usually too soft and I always have to request for extra mint, but overall, not bad pho for Singapore! As for the chicken meatball baguette, the pate is chicken pate. So, ask for extra! This particular branch isn't bad and is quite roomier than the Wheelock one. So I suggest popping by this branch during peak hours as opposed to the one at Wheelock. Tip: If you're doing takeaway, make sure you tell the staff. Take away orders get to jump the queue. Do note, they charge an extra 50 cents per each item for takeaway.

Order at cash desk and pay directly. Cash and credit card works. Staff is neural to customers - neither overly friendly nor rude, mostly preoccupied with cleaning and serving the dishes.Food arrives rather quick after paying at the cash desk. My pho was okay but nothing fancy. Asked for extra herbs and bean sprouts - still trying to find them in my bowl... The iced jade tea needed a lot of sugar before it was drinkable.

This place was alright. The Pho beef noodle soup I had was good. The broth one of the best I have tasted in Singapore after a bit of searching. Don't expect any service or direction from the staff. It was all very confusing. I suddenly realised I had to fill out a form for my food. This is fine as long as there is some sort of direction to do so.Also the place also seemed slightly unclean with fruit flies buzzing around.

OK - for being relatively close to Vietnam, I've had some very mediocre Vietnamese food in Singapore.  I admit I have yet to visit the country, but after dining at Vietnamese restaurants in the States, Namnam left me puzzled.  For starters, the system was annoying.  You get seated first, only to immediately go back to the cashier for your order.  Second, the pho did not come with any of the usual toppings like basil, bean sprouts, or peppers.  The noodles were also quite different - thicker, and the portion was small with little meat.   Still hungry, I then ordered a bahn mi, which was marginally better.  While the pork was decent, the texture was mushy and I could really use some mayo rather than cream cheese.  The bread, however, was delightful - perfect for the sandwich.  The place was packed and popular at lunch, but for me personally, it fails to deliver.

Been to this chain noodle bar many times before. Although there's slight taste difference between outlets, they're generally consistent. Love the clear soup and generous use of herbs. Keeps us coming back, and most importantly pocket-friendly, especially with the passion card 15% discount. Highly recommended.
Good vegetarian food, good ambiance. Good find. Buffet style and nicely spiced/flavourful. Feels authentic.

Pros: The buffet is very good with a nice variety and lots of flavor. I always enjoy it and walk away satisfied. Cons: I don't think any of the employees are happy people. They can be very weird about giving you a seat. They should wash the tablecloths; it's rather unsavory to see them flick away the food crumbs from a table then seat the next guests. Makes me wonder where else they're taking shortcuts on cleanliness. I also dislike listening to the servers snorting their snotty phlegm as they walk around the dining room.

We had a craving for South Indian food and this was right across the road from the hotel and hence got into this one. However the management was fairly rude - as soon as we entered an elderly lady asked us if we had reservation and since we didn't have one she gave a discourse on how we should have a reservation on weekends and that too when 50% of the restaurant was empty!! We still wanted to try the food and hence sat down..the food was just about decent. The moong dal and the potato curry was good but the rest of the food was just average. The management definitely needs some lesson on hospitality! The only good thing is that they let the customer decide the price depending on how satisfied you are.

Extremely busy place at lunch. Food is great, place is clean, buffet style, and pay what you think is fair. What more could you ask for?My opinion is that $7 for lunch is fair. This was confirmed by the indians i work with. So, i think $7 for lunch and $10 for dinner is appropo.

Operated by the Temple of Fine Arts, Annalakshmi is an international chain of non-profit vegetarian restaurant run by volunteers. It lives by the concept of "Eat as you want, Give as you Feel", so there are no prices on the menu. Instead, patrons leave a donation of how much they think the food is worth and all the proceeds go to charity.Adorned with Indian decorations and lined with a haze of sweet smelling incense, it is obvious that the restaurant has a deep-rooted culture waiting to be revealed. Indeed, this culture is apparent from the authenticity of the dishes. The food at Annalakshmi is lovingly prepared by the volunteers and served on a buffet table. The wide array of selection incorporates flavours from North and South India, with dishes ranging from poori to oothapam and masala to dhal, amongst other gravies and sauces. With food so authentic, you can almost taste the tradition! The dishes are rotated periodically and vary within branches so that regular patrons are offered more food options.
Three stars for the concept. Food is very average as its made by volunteers who have a different day job. Good for when you are in a charitable mood.

Nice philosophy (not for profit restaurant that contributes to arts and charities)... we stopped in for lunch and it was pretty average... nothing exciting...  one of the dishes was spicy and tasty but the rest were pretty uninteresting...   also, the buffet food was only vaguely warm...

"Eat what you want, give what you feel"Yes, Annalakshmi is THAT restaurant, the one that doesn't charge but leaves it to you to offer what you wish to. It's fully staffed by volunteers, and is the culinary arts expression of the Temple of Fine Arts (TFA), an artistic and cultural organisation dedicated to serving the society through arts, music and dance. They've been around in Singapore since 1986, and I remember visiting them at the beautifully decked out Excelsior Hotel outlet, which then moved to Chinatown Point, and now Central Square. The buffet is my favourite part of dining here, with its free flow of lassi and masala chai, and the line-up usually has a great variety of dhal, masala vegetables and a curry or two. Bear in mind that it's pure vegetarian, and that it's not polite to waste the food that's been carefully and lovingly prepared by the volunteers. Always a great experience.

I used to frequent the Annalakshmi at Chinatown Point until they moved that outlet to Central Square in Clarke Quay (not to be confused with Central Mall). Was afraid that it would be a different experience at the new outlet but my fears were unfounded! The decor remains as beautifully intricate and this outlet is definitely much brighter than the previous and also much bigger too. One of the best thing about this place is that its a pay-as-you-wish indian vegetarian restaurant - its run by volunteers and the money you pay at the end of your meal goes towards an organization that cultivates Indian arts and cultural development - it sounds like the perfect arrangement. You may wonder how they keep the business running by letting customers pay however much they like but you'd be surprised how much people can feel generous after a good meal!It has a good selection of vegetarian Indian food from rice to poori to naan to oothapam and a few types of vadai. The drinks also have a good selection, the mango lassi is one my faves and I like to end my meals with a nice hot cup of spiced masala tea. If you come on friday and weekends, it's a buffet for lunch and dinner - not a bad selection but limited to only whats on the buffet table. Come for dinner on mon to thursdays to have the best selection of food from the menu.Final verdict: One of the best feel-good restaurants- good food, good ambience and all for a good cause!

I have been going to Annalakshmi for years. It is one of the best places to find Indian vegetarian food in Singapore. This place is very interesting as it is run totally by volunteers and patrons pay what they like. They either have a full buffet or ala carte and everything is fresh and very good. You can order a selection of drinks like lassi or chai masala tea. It can get pretty crowded here sometimes so it is a good idea to make a reservation. The staff are all volunteers and sometimes they can be a bit grumpy.

Thank you Yelp for helping me find this place, as trying to locate a stall inside the overwhelming Chinatown Complex hawker center can be a daunting task. This place does not disappoint. I had 10 steamed XLB which costed me $5.50 SGD ($3.82 USD). As I slurped each of the delicate and succulent XLBs, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the broth has a sweet umami flavor. The skin was tender but strong enough to keep all the fillings in without breaking when I picked up the XLBs with my chopsticks. Many reviewers have compared this place's dumpling to DTF - an unfair comparison given that DTF is a huge global franchise. In my opinion, this place is way better than DTF. I would not hesitate to come back again and again.

Yes, the xlb is really good. Nice broth and tasty. The stall is found in the southeast corner of the Chinatown Complex, which is behind the CK Dept. Store. Everything is made to order, so you do have to wait a few minutes.

This is my new favorite food stall at the Chinatown Smith Street Hawker Center. Excellent dumplings! Cheap! Only $4.50 for 10. The xiao long bao are great, but you HAVE to try the potstickers. They take a little longer to fry up, but definitely worth the wait. The spicy dumplings are a close second. The hawkers are really friendly and never turn anyone away when they are trying to close. (Although once the sign goes off you'll only get xiao long bao.) I've noticed that there are a lot more fellow ang moh in the queue with me lately. Probably no coincidence that so many reviews start with "I was going to Good Beer Company and..."

$5 for 10 awesome xiao long bao!  One lunch my colleagues and I descended on the stall like a horde of locusts ordering over a 100 of the xiao long bao along with wontons, pan fried dumplings and la mian.  Every dish was tasty and consistent in quality.  While the xiao long bao may not be as thin skinned as "the best" restaurant dumplings, they are my favorite on this island especially given their incredible value for money.

The xiaolong baos were better than I would have thought. The soup was sweet and delicate, and it was just pretty delicious. The boiled dumplings were pretty decent as well, with loads of chives, but not as good as the xiaolong baos. I have to try the potstickers next time! :)

Went for dinner and found this stand on the second floor of the Chinatown complex. I was on a mission to find this stall along with the Good Beer Company and it was a sucess.  I ordered 10 "steamed mini buns" for $5.50 and the uncle there was busy hand making them.  Mine were premade as they were not busy when I stopped by so they already had some waiting but they did taste very fresh.  I ate them both with and without the ginger vinegar dip and actually preferred them without the vinegar.  They were already very juicy!

Xiao Long Bao in my opinion better than Din Tai Fung and cheaper. 10 for $5.50. The xlb are tasty and soupy. Made fresh in front of you and served steaming hot :) I appreciate the simplicity of the ingredients yet the complexity of the flavors. Such a simple dish but so tasty. I'll definitely be back. Others were also ordering the Szechuan dumplings or wonton which looked really good too.

Food: 2.5/5.0Service: 2.0/5.0Value: 3.0/5.0Decor: 1.5/5.0Overall: 2.5/5.0Everyone wants to be a hipster, and that means taking really mediocre food in dingy stalls and talking it up like it's some gift from above.  Lets get real, these are at best decent XLB for a hawker stall, but even trying to compare these to DTF is absolute fake news.  The non-XLB items are completely mediocre (read: ugh).  Pass.

In terms of hawker xlb this would be one of the good ones. I still think the soup should be more oily and sticky. The skin is correct. I suppose so far din tai fung will be the most authentic although a bit " too clean" in flavor. For the price I think you get your money's worth. 6 for 10.

The only place I've ever tried XLB was at Din Tai Fung in Seattle. Even though others love it, I never thought it was that good and just assumed XLB was supposed to be that way. My views on XLB changed after going to Zhong Guo La Mian. For about $4.50 USD you get 10 amazingly juicy and perfectly steamed XLB that packs so much amazing flavor that you'll crave for months. If I can find a way back to Singapore, this spot is a must stop.

All-in-all, Din Tai Fung still wins in my opinion, as I prefer the flavor of the DTF xiao long bao filling. The skin here was somewhat inconsistent, and if you weren't very delicate and careful, it would break, letting the soup leak out. Everything is clearly handmade fresh here though; you can see them hard at work in the hawker stall kitchen, making each dumpling one by one and steaming the baskets. Of course these are not as aesthetically pleasing as DTF, but if you're looking for soupy dumplings at an affordable price then this is the place for you.We also ordered one bowl of beef noodle soup, one plate of pan-fried dumpling, one plate of boiled dumplings, and one plate of szechuan spicy wonton. For a group of six, the total was just S$7pp! The beef noodle soup was very delicious, and I'd definitely order that on its own again. The pan-fried and boiled dumplings were excellent as well. The pan-fried is probably more unique and requires more effort to cook (also more unhealthy). The szechuan wonton is a unique flavor of vinegar and spicy oil, and it's not for everyone. It might be an acquired taste, but none of us foreigners were really a big fan of the szechuan spiciness with vinegar.
