I love the sweetness from the condensed milk. The eggs were done perfectly and the toast had a good amount of coconut jam (kaya) and was crunchy enough to soak up all the egg deliciousness. Tip: Don't be afraid to add soy sauce to the eggs because it adds a extra layer of flavour to the egg and sweet bread combination.

Love this place, fatty but amazing! The Kaya toast had coconut Pandan and egg white the flavors are sooooooo good! If you are a pineapple bun fan you will definitely love this! I was in Singapore for 3 days and came here every day!!
Chicken curry is a better choice compared to the mee rebus. I don't think I can appreciate this kind of food. The staff is nice though.

Long time visitor, one of my favorite breakfast place in Singapore. I've tried the kaya toast, nasi lemak, curry chicken, and mee laksa, never disappointed. Loving the white coffee, too. Come early in the morning (they open from 6am), it gets busier around 9ish.

This landmark kopitiam is where I go when I'm usually craving a quick bite of unhealthy local fare. (I'm here like maybe once a week) It's not air-conditioned and has a very old-school feel. The food is admittedly pretty average, but it is always crowded with locals at all hours. I always get the laksa (although personally, I feel the Katong Laksa tastes better) and chee cheong fun. My friends are fans of the mee siam.I like their teh-si peng which is just nice in its sweetness. I top my meal off with a local dessert like cheng tng or grass jelly with longan.  Price-wise it's still in the cheap range although it's expensive for a kopitiam. The manager (?) of the restaurant who takes my orders is this friendly Chinese woman who is always happy to have a chat and a laugh.

7am and they are packed like sardines in a can.from taxi drivers to policemen to working crowd on their way to the office.seating space can be a little crampy.you order at one counter, pay at another then grab a sit and your order will find it's way to you.a french loaf set is only $4.85.you get a good cup of teh c.2 half boiled eggs, mine was slightly overcooked todaylocal sized baguette, toasted well to melt the kaya and butter spread within.it can be messy to eat as a result but they have an easy to access tap for washing up afterwards.parking is definitely a nightmare and tickets will fly for illegal parking around here.

Epitome of the meaning, "a little goes a long way". The menu is quite simple with just a couple of main breakfast items. The ambiance is very local and can feel like an old school breakfast cafe in the colonial times (maybe i am overdoing that but still feels authentically Singapore).Kaya Toast w/ Butter - The basic high calorie high fast working mans breakfast. Chicken Curry w/ Roti - a great go to local breakfast meal. Be careful as the curry splashes.Laksa - Same thing...splashesAssorted Breakfast drinks but my favorite is the Ginger tea w/ Milk. These are the only things I eat when I break bread here. I guess I am a creature of habit. I tell you though with their consistently good turn around I can gather that the everything else is good stuff to.

This is the place where it all began. Where everyone is treated as an equal, and where the lines know no end. There was a time when Kaya toast was hard to find. When half boiled eggs were a rarity,and dark sauce symbolized true darkness. Not anymore, but I'll still keep coming back here for both the good vibes and the memories.

A favorite haunt of mine, it's great for ol'fashioned breakfast after a night of clubbing or an intense mahjong session. I've been coming here since my secondary school days just to hang out with friends when I get sick of Starbucks and the like, and need some good ol' kaya toast with soft-boiled eggs. Never really liked their laksa, but the chee cheong fun here is pretty decent as well, should you not feel like kaya toast! The prices here are cheap, and service is quick. I also enjoy the random meetings that occur here with friends I've not seen for a while.
Nice kopi; even better kaya toasts.One thing that grabs your attention is the many humorously pessimistic excerpts on marriage stuck on the walls.
Great little clinic-looking Killiney joint with zero ambience to get your daily kopi jolt and observe the kaleidoscope of humanity around you all enjoying the same.

This is the ORIGINAL Killiney Kopitiam. As in the very first one. Indeed, you get a real sense of nostalgia when you step in and sit and the old school marble kopitiam tables. You know they have been there a long time, not the sort that people buy at furniture stores for the "vintage look". The curry chicken and mee rebus here are famous, and for good reason. The curry chicken is one of the best, if not the best I have tried in Singapore. It's super thick and aromatic and the chicken and potatoes are cooked just right. You can really taste the fresh spices and coconut that have gone into making that delicious gravy. It also has a real kick of spiciness, not like the lousy curries you get in food courts that are oily and one note. If i were to nitpick, I would say that sometimes the chicken has that faint chickeny taste you get when the chicken used isn't super fresh.

I wanted a taste to see what a typical Singaporean breakfast would be like. This place was really packed in the morning. I ordered two types of sweet toast and some fried noodle rolls. Everything was super sweet. It was definitely unique and worth a try especially if you are a tourist.

Stopped by here one morning to have breakfast during my visit to Singapore.It was not a great experience. It was a combination of language barrier, overly spicy food for breakfast, and a jam-packed interior. Most of what we ordered was not available, their boiled eggs were essentially raw, even after we made a request for done eggs.Not coming back to this particular one for sure.

Yes, yes, and more yes!  Simplest breakfast foods ever, but SO GOOD that I had it twice during my stay in Singapore.  Kaya Toast, soft boiled eggs, and soy milk with grass jelly cost no more than ~5 SGD!!!  Walk up to the counter, order, pay, sit down, and out comes to the food.  Nothing fancy, just plain and simple.This place is an institution and has a lot of history to it.  Great to visit and to try especially how cheap it is.  This one is also the original in Singapore, so def visit.  Consider also getting a jar of the kaya spread.  You can even try to make it yourself at home.  I did.  *___*
Honey ginger tea- they use real ginger and the tea is strong and soothing. For $3 it's a pretty good dealIt's cash only

Grabbed breakfast here. Got coffee, soft boiled eggs, rice cake, and some type of toast. Coffee has condensed milk in it, so it was super sweet. The toast was also really sweet as well, I'm not a fan of sweets really and I don't usually eat breakfast either. Definitely not my first choice, but my friends liked it. Service was nice and attentive.

Hands down the best traditional S'pore breakfast I've had during my week here.The first kaya breakfast I had in my life was at the big chain, Ya Kun Kaya Toast. You can see it in the food levels of Singapore's many malls around the city, or like we also did, visit the original location on China Street in between Telok Ayer and Chinatown. But Killiney's original location on Killiney Road a little walk's away from Somerset was just as quaint and much more delicious in my opinion.Their system of ordering is at the cashier once you've found a table. You can't order items unless you can provide a table number, so if you're with a buddy, have them take over a table while someone else puts the orders in. MAJOR KEY. We had their soft boiled eggs and kaya toast, mee cheong, mee siam, and iced tea/coffee. We ate like kings for about $20-$30 I believe. I don't remember the actual amount, but it should be around that price--pretty great for Singapore.My favorite was their kaya toast. SO much thicker and still crisp compared to Ya Kun's, and their spread was less sugary like Ya Kun does it. I even bought a jar of kaya spread to take home to the States! I loved it THAT much (kaya is essentially pandan, coconut milk, eggs, and sugar). I can't wait to use it on my toast at home. Their iced tea was SO good, not overly sweet like at Ya Kun, and definitely freshly made with fresh foam on top of my cup. We were so excited about our first order, that at the end I put in an order for mee siam after looking around their shop at the photos. That wasn't my favorite item, but the egg was cooked to perfection, and the sauce was a hint spicy with lots of flavor. Service is QUICK and their workers are all bosses at efficient food running and order taking. Hats off.

I love finding little local spots like this. Full of locals so you know it has got to be good. I recommend the laksa and french bread kaya toast (over the french toast). The coffee is pretty good as well. I've eaten a lot of laksa over the last few weeks and I think Killiney Kopitiam has the best laksa broth.  Its very flavorful and well balanced. The toppings are pretty basic in comparison to most places but it gets the job done. It's just so good. Don't miss out on ordering it. They have a system for ordering. This is important. I travelled solo, so it was a little difficult to get it down. Step one, find a seat and mark your territory (put an umbrella down on the table). Step two, note your table number. Step three, go up to the front, place your order, you must give them your table number.  You'll see a menu on the wooden panel on the left side of the cashier, point to things if you need to (I did). Step four, wait for your food and enjoy.

Killiney Kopitiam is a great place for a fast meal/snack. It is in every way a Kopitiam with stools and rough tables and nothing much. The atmosphere is noisy. Order and pre-pay your food. About the only service is when they serve the Food. This is not a criticism. The food is good and reasonably priced for Singapore. We liked the Chicken curry, Cheong Fan, French Toast with Kaya, Bread Roll with Kaya, Chendol and Kopi. If you are visiting the area, try it, it still has the character of yesteryears.My only fault with the place is it is not wheel chair friendly! There is a step down from the adjoining shops and from the 5 foot path.
Delicious kaya toast and French bread. The egg was nice and runny-- perfect for dipping.

From the Regent Hotel the walk is about 20-25 minutes.  Arrived at around 6:15AM jet lagged and a hungry early bird looking for a worm.  This place did the job.Had the coffee with sweetened condensed milk (very sweet and strong).  Also had and loved the soft boiled egg and an order of French Toast. Both very good.The system is simple here: You pay first and they deliver your food to you.Was disappointed that the Laksa wasn't available but I think it's only a lunch item here.I enjoyed the random jokes and philosophical tidbits scattered about the cool white walls.  For some reason, I enjoyed the cool intensely white lit interior of the establishment.  Normally, this kind of vibe gives me a migraine, especially in the morning but it worked here for some reason.I tried a couple of the Malay dishes but didn't like them as thought they were too sweet. I ate them quickly only as a matter if formality.Will finish with the insightful philosophical message posted on a sign on the wall here that put my morning in perspective:"Teens: You have all the time and energy but no money.Workers: you have the money and energy but no time.Oldies: You have all the time and money but no more energy.Lesson: Enjoy life and all the things you have at the moment because you can't have everything at once.";)

My mom found this place thru a guidebook in Japanese and decided to try it.  We ordered Kaya butter toast and it was delicious!!!  I could eat a dozen of them.  We never got to try any other item but maybe next time.  The place is very small and very crowded so you gotta hover around the tables (there is no waiting list for the tables...you just gotta grab it).  We later found out that there is another location at the airport, so you can try their kaya toast without making your way all the way to this location.

A very special restaurant, high quality ingredients without some of the ostentation and pretentiousness that is typical of newer joints.We had a charcuterie platter, grilled hamachi collar, black mash and the deconstructed Tim-Tam for dessert. The lardo from the cold cut platter was especially good, as was the black mash. We also really enjoyed watching the Josper grill in action behind the kitchen counter. We were pleasantly surprised by the wines, as the selection is excellently curated. Ended up having a Merlot that well surpassed our expectations. Service was really good, despite it being really crowded on a public holiday eve. Overall, one of the best dining experiences in Singapore. Only annoying thing is how hard it is to find parking on Purvis St. Will be back for sure!

I was taken here on a Friday night and wow, the place was roaring busy. We had the charcuterie platter, chicken hearts, wagyu, scallop ceviche, and kangeroo, finishing off the meal with their complimentary Anzac cookies.I really enjoyed the platter, with a variety of meats that they cured in-house, which is a rarity in Singapore. I suppose the humid climate doesn't help, making this quite an achievement I must say. The scallop ceviche, wagyu, chicken hearts and kangeroo were decent, but nothing to shout about. Very solid execution, nothing to complain about at all.I really enjoyed the cookies,  which were very crispy. Since they were complementary, I suggest you make room for them and keep them in mind when you order!

Recently opened (~ 6 months ago) by the ex- executive chef of the W hotel,  it provides a new streak of meals that may be less common in Singapore.   The menu is creative, with a broad range of high quality preserved (prepared by the chef) and fresh meats presented in very elegant forms. Chef Andrew is very friendly and chatted and explained about the meats and dishes.  Opted for a watermelon and mint juice, highly refreshing.  The deserts, chocolate and peanut butter ice cream and  pearls were fabulous and the cookie with bacon finale was awesome!  I eat those before I had a chance to photograph!Overall, this is an Avant-garde restaurant at the creative cutting edge in Singapore and has MAJOR potential to be at the top end.  For my friends, SG yelpers and interested visitors/tourists, this is a must-try if you haven't  been already. Go with an open mind, and enjoy every bit, but remember, this is no chicken rice!!See pics.

Sort-of new kid of the block located along Purvis Street where the big boys' rules' - from fine dining establishments like Garibaldi Italian Restaurant and Gunther's to local favorites; Yet Con, Chin Chin eating house, Saveur among others. I really like Salted and Hung for its beautifully designed interior - spacious and not too dark, tongue-in-chic graffiti on the wall, background music that is not too loud but still entertaining at times, and of course the all-star team led by Chef Andrew Nocente, an Australian. The food and drinks menu is rather extensive, so I would suggest you go through one round and decide which to choose from each category. Here's the list of what we ate throughout the 4-hour dinner last night: -  Small Plate Sweetbreads - with cabbage, granola and saltbush ($10) Tripe (fried) - with tongarashi, Szechuan and caponata puree ($15)Chef's selection of charcuterie ($28)Crab - with uni, apple and asparagus ($25)Corn (roasted) - with spiced cheese, manchego and chives ($9)Kale (roasted) - with homemade cheese and nuts ($10)Burrata - with pickled tomato, basil oil and pine nuts ($12) Cauliflower -with burnt butter tahini, piccalilli and dandelion ($10)MainOP ribs - 1.2 kg of ribeye ($198)Iberico pork collar - with apple, nuts and mustard ($42)Roast chicken (half) - with beer sauce, house rub and black garlic ($22)DessertChocolate salami - with salted caramel and chocolate meringue ($16)Figs - with yogurt ice-cream, nasturtium and Pedro ximenez sherry ($14)Popcorn - with corn and raspberry textures ($10)Chocolate tart - specials. (forgot!)Anzac cookie - complimentary! It was a hearty meal for sure as we paced ourselves eating, talking and laughing away while the kitchen consistently churned out one dish after another. A few dishes I really like include roasted kale and corn, the iberico pork collar is out of this world and the desserts deserve a standing ovation to end a very satisfying meal. We don't get fresh figs here in Singapore so seeing it on the menu is something refreshing and "exotic" at the same time.  The total bill came up to $552 (without alcohol) to be shared among 5 people. Reasonable for the amount and quality of food we ordered. I'm definitely coming back to try out their lunch offerings one of these days or just walk in by myself for a treat to combat those dark, stressful days at work.

The restaurant was dimly lighted with open kitchen. There was no much customers for weekday lunch. Looking through the menu, I decided on the 3 course lunch set ($35++).Pork BellyApple, cucumber & mustardThe pork belly was cut up into small pieces, tasted quite juicy. The apple and cucumber shaved into thin slices made a very tangy side.Red SnapperDashi broth, fennel & sea herbsIt was steamed fish in light broth. The fish was firm and juicy, while the broth was light and flavourful. The thinly sliced fennel lent a citrus taste to the simple dish.PopcornRaspberry & popcorn textureIt was served in shades of pinks, but it was a different story in the mouth. Closed one's eyes, it was like butter popcorn which one usually have when watching movies, with popping effect in the mouth.I finished the meal with a cup of chocolaty latte and a piece of Anzac Biccies which tasted of bacon and salted caramel, totally different from the Anzac I used to have back in Australia.

To be really honest, after hearing much reviews on the food, I was disappointed. They weren't bad, but I find them not particularly flavorful even though the different ingredients seemed to be rather interesting and unique individually. Some of the dishes were also rather flat tasting, like just a touch more salt would have perked up the flavors more. The happy hour deal is good though 1-1 drinks and a few snacks for less than $10.

vagabond's loss, purvis's gain!5th quarter reborn as salted & hung!never have i seen such crowd, at 5th quarter, as i have at freshly minted salted & hung.the change makes me happy for andrew, as it is an acknowledgment of all his good work that every mouth and stomach in singers should bear witness to.a distinctly casual dress down from the previously, opulent decor of 5th quarter.the move here has also given andrew greater rein to salt, hang and deliver extraordinary culinary exotica to our ever critical and fickle palate.now there is also greater interaction with andrew and his kitchen crew, something that was lacking somewhat at 5th quarter.the mingling with the chef makes the dining experience beyond just, stuffing of the face, enjoyable.yes, tap is not available and some might complain as such.but the norwegian still or sparkling, charged per head, is indeed worth it's volume and definitely better than newater?so what's good?some animals are more equal than others, so i guess that choice will be somewhat specific to each individual.having tried both their lunch and dinner menu, you can't go really far wrong with any of their dishes be it from the land or sea.four legs good, two legs bad?hardly, the chalkboard special roast chicken was actually one that stood tall!better order the whole chicken instead of just half, like i did.the lively gastronomy scene along purvis street, just got livelier(except on a sunday)!quickly get salted & hung before they decide to reincarnate, again!?p.s. do hurry as a 20% opening discount will expire after 27th june!

A very, very disappointing experience at Salted & Hung on Purvis St - formerly known as 5th Quarter at the Vagabond Hotel. I had desperately wanted this to be good as I had been wanting to go since its previous incarnation. The place itself has a nice casual, mildly edgy vibe and the staff were well-trained and knowledgable. However a) specials board was not visible and b) staff didn't explain the "concept" to us, I.e. Which were small plates, how many portions were recommended to order for 2 people etc. Ultimately, service and decor take a back seat to food and flavour for me and this is where S&H really fails to deliver.All the produce and ingredients were great quality and well-cooked, however were totally underwhelming in taste. Wagyu rib - sous vide and grilled, was very high quality and extremely rich but lacked any beef flavour. I was just aware that I was chewing on protein. The green sauce ("Hulk sauce") was actually unpleasant and reminded me of the smell of cut grass / wheatgrass juice. Crab and uni also didn't pack any punch. In fact there was no sweetness one would expect from crab meat. Burrata and tomatoes was a complete injustice to burrata. The head cheese and beef rillette, part of the house made charcuterie board, were excellent though. I thought the best part of the dinner were the free bacon and caramel Anzac biscuits that came at the end of the meal....Damage: $125 nett food onlyWe were in and out within an hour.

Very solid Australian fare.  We went as a group on a Thursday night and it was not very crowded.  The menu is built for sharing and we had fun exploring different & exotic food (pig ear / kangaroo!).  Not for the light-hearted.  And the traditional hardcore meat grills were to perfection with a twist.  The dessert was also done nicely which ended the meal with just the right touch.  The wine list is full of good Aussie selection and the great shout out is that they are trying to be environmentally friendly and thus produce the sparkling drinking water in-house - very commendable.Recommended for date night, small/ big group.

This is an excellent restaurant and great value for money. I loved the open kitchen and watching the owner sharing his knowledge with his staff. Husband and I tried the Chef's Pairing Menu. Most of the food was excellent. The crisp bread that went with the charcuterie was excellent, loved the caraway seeds. I'm not a beetroot fan but my husband loves it so was a big fan of the beetroot tartare. The pork sausage was delicious and made me realise how much I miss good sausages. Next was the fish tail which looked amazing but was a bit dull. The last savoury dish was Wagyu tri tip and it was AMAZING. I could just eat plates and plates of this forever. Dessert was a peanut butter tim tam which was pretty tasty. The wine menu is decently priced and you can add a beer pairing to the dinner menu which sounds very interesting and which I may well try on my next visit. This is definitely one to add to your list.

Sunday lunch time and by accident I turned into a courtyard with many different restaurants and bars.The Mexican caught my eye and I had no trouble finding a table outside in said courtyard.The offer for a set lunch with soup, main dish and brownie / ice cream for desert - 18S$ - had to be checked out.Portions are not too big but as it's three courses I was still quite stuffed afterwards. Everything was tasty and at least as Mexican as Chilis ;)The waiters were nice and always checked on me, asked before serving the next course etc. They even managed to bring the ice tea without sugar but a little pot with sugar on the side.Really liked the place as you can sit outside in the shade and with a fen if you like. The food is good and inexpensive, the staff really nice, so where else to go for a lazy Sunday lunch and some book reading?

This is probably the closest to real Mexican food you will get in Singapore. Food was delicious and it was close enough that it made me feel at home. The jarritos are authentic so you must try them. I would give this place 5 stars if the prices weren't so outrageous. Expect to pay quite a bit for a burrito.

Is this the best Mexican food in Singapore? Hell to the no. Is this the best TEXMEX in Singapore? Hell to the YES! I came here on a Friday night with Michelle M. and there was a small band jamming and singing in Spanish! What a perfect way to start our TexMex adventure. We ordered nachos, crab enchiladas, beef burrito, and beef tacos. I didn't try the beef burrito, but the crab enchiladas and beef tacos deserve an ole! The enchilada sauce wasn't as flavorful as I would like, but it definitely tasted like enchilada sauce so me gusta! It didn't taste much different from Chevy's enchiladas, which I faintly recall. Plus, the nice chunks of crab meat gave it a distinctive local flavor. Kind of like chili crab but no need for messy hands or a bowl of lemon water. The tacos are also worth the $17 as the price included 3 soft shelled tacos, rice, refried beans, and a small salad. Not bad considering Lucha Loco charges $11 for just one taco. The refried beans were also delicioso, def. an item I'll order as a side or even as an appetizer. I'm no nacho lover, but Viva Mexico's nachos blew me away. They came with REAL jalapenos! Nice big, fat vinegary ones!   ¡Salud! I was so happy I almost burst into tears...do you know how difficult it is to find jalapenos in Singapore?? My homemade Mexican food just doesn't taste the same without them. Viva Mexico (and Subway, I guess), tell me who your distributor is, por favor! I need them jalapenos! This certainly isn't the best TexMex I've had in my life, but for Singapore, I'm thoroughly impressed. For the price, atmosphere, and food--me encanta! For those who really crave Mexican food, visit Siem Reap, Cambodia. ¡Mi numero uno!

This a a review of a Tuesday evening dinner with a friend at Viva Mexico.First, I want to be clear,  in California, this would NOT be a four star review.  For a Mexican or Tex-Mex restaurant, It might only be a two star review.  But I am not in California and I have to adjust my expectations to where I'm at. I will also note that on their site, Viva Mexico claims to be  traditional Mexican food and not Tex-Mex.  While they have some moles, from what I saw of their menu, it is mostly Tex-Mex.  Plus, the fajitas seem to be pretty popular.  They are as Tex-Mex as it gets.My goal was to find a place that served decent US chain (El Toritios, etc..) quality Tex-Mex food.  My mission was a success.  In almost every way, this is exactly what Viva Mexico is.  This is true from the ambiance to the food.Speaking of the ambiance; it is festive.  Well, it is in the festive get out the decorations for taco night sort of way.  But it sets the mood for having a margarita or two.  And speaking of margarita's theirs are pretty good.  Nothing to write home about, but good enough to keep the Viva Mexico mood going.  It seemed like everyone there was in good spirits and enjoying their meals.  For me, this was a nice plus to the overall ambiance.The staff was friendly, professional, and prompt.  This was maintained throughout our meal.  This even included a moment where the power went out.  But that was only a very minor hiccup.The food was quite good.Nachos - We started with some nachos.  We enjoyed them very much.  I sought out the jalapeños.  My friend did everything she could to eat around them.  The chips were crisp.   The cheese was all melted.  This is all just as it should be.tinyurl.com/bz5eu8nGuacamole - We also ordered a side of guacamole.  This was also very good.  There were lots of fresh ingredients.  They had also insured not to over mix it so there was still some texture.tinyurl.com/aleeo7jFajitas - I ordered chicken.  She ordered beef.  I thought both were good.  I love fajitas.  I love food where you get to do a little bit of combining and playing while eating.  Being her first adventure with fajitas, my friend did not embrace this part as much.  She abandoned the create your own fajita taco and stuck with the fork and knife.  I thought that both the chicken and beef were cooked well.  They were both tender and had nice seasoning.  The veggies were still very crispy.  All in all -  two good sets of fajitas.tinyurl.com/abmcj9qOverall - This was a fun meal.  The food was good.  The service was pleasant.  The ambiance was on the festive side.  Good stuff!  I will be back.

The food is quite good. The portions are definitely on the small side. It looks like the side of rice that comes with the enchilada was measured in a 1/4 cup container and it retained the shape. The steak that came with the fajitas was big. Everything was well flavored.

I have to agree with J N, I'm really struggling to understand why this restaurant has received such great reviews. I don't claim to be a TexMex expert but the "kitchen sink burrito", which has received plaudits on both Yelp & Foursquare, was clearly prepared well in advance. The tortilla was stale, as were the nachos we ordered, and this is simply unacceptable. The cardboard-like texture of microwaved corn chips is not something I enjoy, much less am willing to pay for.The main reasons I've given this place two stars instead of one are the service and the vibe. Staff were quite attentive, friendly and hospitable and the al-fresco setting on Cuppage Rd is a winner. This is a great place to have a bucket of Coronas but if you're coming for the food then you will leave disappointed.

In fairness, if I could give this a 3.5, I probably would. The food was very tasty but having 'grown up' on Mexican, I am a pretty harsh critic.  We had the fajitas (beef), the crab enchiladas and my oldest daughter had the tacos. All were pretty darn good.  The beef in the fajitas was especially tasty. The service was good and the price was pretty reasonable too - we had three adult meals, a kids meal, a couple of cocktails and an appetizer for $160. Well worth it!  I will definitely go back (it was my wife's second time so you know she liked it).

If you want Mexican food cooked by non-Mexicans, you pays your money and you takes your chances.The "Mexican" sauce tasted exactly like Heinz BBQ sauce + Tabasco.Went here a years ago, and while it wasn't real Mexican then either (check out the kitchen and staff and see for yourself), it was slightly better than this trip.The food was awful and the portions didn't match the cost. Another overpriced tourist trap.
A bit pricey, but good Mexican food. Friendly staff. A nice place to have spent Cinco de Mayo.
One of the better Korean restaurant in town, in my opinion. Good spread of marinated meat; very nice. Love the pork belly and the Kimchi is good too. Service was average and expensive.

This is a decent Korean bbq place. Prices are a bit high even for SG standard for what you get. However the quality is good and the service is friendly.  If you are in the area I'd recommend this place.

We first tried 8 Korean BBQ in Seoul. It blew our mind. When we heard about them opening a store in Singapore, we jumped at the chance to try it. The taste didn't failed us. Meat was succulent and well marinated. Just like how we tasted it in Seoul. Although we are limited by the variety of vegetables we can get in Singapore, it did not diminish the whole experience.Price here is on the high side compared to Korea. The price for 2 pax in Singapore would feed 3 in Seoul.

Been here twice for dinner, and got varying flavors of the pork belly. I have no idea why they put kimchi on the grill, yet not provide kimchi as part of the banchan unless asked to. Bewildered.Both times I've gotten a kimchi jjigae, and it is okay. The pork belly flavors are a bit of a gimmick. After the staff kindly cooked the meat, they all tasted pretty much the same. The prices are also on the high side here. I was not impressed.

Maybe the BBQ/Grill meat will be the better option. We did not order that as our focus was on the Army Stew.Apparently most places' Army Stew was big enough to feed 3 or 4 persons. As it was just two of us, we were looking for a smaller portion and 8 Korean BBQ had that. My first experience with Army Stew and I was not too impressed with it. It was nice but it was not spectacular. Instant noodle in a Kimchi broth with some vegs, a cheese slice, ham, hotdogs and luncheon meat (spam). I could not see or taste the luncheon meat though my friend said it was there, in tiny pieces. We also ordered a kimchi fried rice which was quite good. The highlight would be the banchan. It was different from other places with the ubiquitous kimchi, anchovies and huge bean sprouts. Over here, there were only 4 but they were all tart which were very appetizing. I love the strips of cuttlefish which were salty sweet and sour. Maybe I would have to order the grill meat next time. The 4 or 8 color pork belly were huge! Definitely enough for sharing.

Good quality tasty and nice casual ambience.We had the Ginseng Black Chicken soup and Pork Belly Kimchi Stew. Both came out piping hot and smells great. They have served the side dishes which were usual in Korean fares.The side dishes presents Kimchi, Cuttlefish strips, white carrots (radish?), beansprouts, & small potatoes, all nice starters for the main meals.We like the Ginseng Black Chicken the best. The soup is almost thick and flavourful, almost collagen-like. I think it's a whole chick in there, stuff with rice. The portion is definitely large enough for two. The pork belly kimchi stew when compared to the Ginseng chicken is less impressive. On its own it would be a nice meal, though it is stingy on the pork belly. Lots of kimchi and the stew is spicy and appetizing enough. I finished my bowl of rice with it.On the whole, the ambience is casual, and probably surprisingly nice as we left the place without smelling like food. And the pricing is exceptional, $38.

We tried out 8 Korean BBQ last night and I'm a huge fan. The place was hopping and I'm happy we had a reservation. There were three of us and our server was very helpful in explaining the menu. We started with the vinegar soju with plum and then  ordered the pork belly, the ribeye and the seafood stew with bean paste. I was happy with the drink, but my husband may have found it a bit girly for his tastes. The meats and kimchi were awesome. I was really impressed with how everything was cooked at the table and the level of service we received. It wasn't 5 minutes since the time we ordered that the table was swarmed with servers toting a ton of food. What an experience! We'll definitely be back.

Without a doubt the best Samgyupsal (Pork Belly) in Singapore. This is the same franchise as the one in LA's Ktown and Korea (although in LA, it's called Palsaik, which essentially means 8 flavors anyways) I'd been to Palsaik in LA (and became a fan!) and was eager to try it out here when I read that they opened about a month ago. One of the things I miss most about LA when I'm in Singapore is the good korean food and was hoping it'd taste just as good here. It did, if not, better. 4.5 stars... Here's why,When you first arrive, you're greeted by a dim interior, with Kpop girls dancing around on the TV screens attached to the brick walls. The space isn't particularly big (and I can see it becoming really crowded, once word hits the street) but it's very well decorated with a nice hip underground feel to it. The staff are super friendly and showed us to our table as soon as we got there. The thing to order here is definitely the '8 flavors' samgyupsal. It sounds like a lot of food but it's really not as it's essentially one thick strip of pork belly for each flavor (good for 2-3 people). The 8 flavors are: Wine, Original, Ginseng, Garlic, Herb, Curry, Miso, Red Pepper. Every single flavor tasted good, my favorites being Wine, Ginseng, Garlic, Curry and Miso (okay I guess that's almost everything) Now, what makes the singapore branch BETTER than the LA one? The service and the flavors.The service: Service here is top notch. Possibly the best I've experience in such a restaurant (of course, not comparing with fine dining type places). Aside from being super friendly and attentive, they cook your food to perfection. Yes, perfection. Sure, there are countless amazing korean bbq places in LA but the one thing I find annoying is they often start cooking your meats for you and then walk away and come back too late only to have it become slightly burnt, overcooked or resulting in you having to flip it over yourself. Not here!! They flip it at the perfect time, cut it up, and then turn off the fire and transfer it onto a small plate for you after it's perfectly cooked so it does not get burnt. This results in pork belly perfection.The food: The Samgyupsal here is actually better than their branch in LA because, the flavors are more distinct. In LA, they do the 8 different flavors as different "cuts" of pork belly as well as marinates. However, though yummy, I didn't think the flavors were very distinctly different from each other there. Also, with the different cuts, there were cuts of the pork I didn't like as much resulting in a lot of uneaten meats. At 8 flavors here in Singapore, however, every flavor is made with the same pork belly. This allows you to differentiate and really taste the change in taste with each flavor. The cut aside, the flavors itself really are most distinct too. Super well marinated and bursting in flavor, you can no doubt tell wine from miso from garlic etc etc. The only slight downside for this place is the price point. For a plate of 8 flavors, you're looking at $98. This is before soups, drinks etc. And since (if you're a big eater like us - heehee) a plate of 8 flavors only feeds 2-3 people, you can imagine it becoming really pricey with a big group. Thus, I had to knock of 0.5 stars (but only because of the price) Still, I'll be back, and 8 flavors has no doubt earned the title of best Samgyupsal in Singapore in my books. I just hope the service and food quality remains just as good, even when they start to get super busy (because I know they will soon enough).

Delicious.I came here with my sister and here are the dishes we got:- 4 color pork belly ($58) - we are pretty big eaters and could have easily finished the 8 colors, but we wanted to try other dishes too so we settled with 4. We chose garlic, smoked, curry and miso. All of them were tasty, with my favorite being smoked - it's just downright divine when wrapped in one of those crunchy lettuce. Curry is a close contender.- beef bean paste stew ($18) - tasteless and not nearly enough beef. I'd skip this- steamed eggs ($12) - this was just alright. The texture wasn't what i expected. Korean steamed eggs are usually more soft and smooth, but this one has a rather rough texture and might have been overcooked. Portion is huge though.- kimchi fried rice ($8) - SO delicious!! And this being relatively cheaper than other dish with good size portion, i'd definitely get this again.Overall, i'm pretty impressed with this place.
Like the concept of different types of marinated meats. However, taste is average. Side dishes are limited, a bit overpriced compared to other Korean restaurants along Telok Ayer/Tangjong Pagar area.

(Let's put aside the fact that I'm vegan. There are times I will socially eat meat. Don't hate.) GETTING THERE: The restaurant is located in The Central Mall on the 2nd floor. Near the escalators. This mall is like a labyrinth so try not to get lost. DEJA VU: When I saw "8 Korean BBQ" I immediately thought of Palsaik, a Korean bbq joint back in Ktown LA. The menu looked especially familiar. The flavors were the exact same as Palsaik's. Turns out the two restaurants are under the same owner. TASTE: I used to be a hardcore carnivore. Meat and carbs all day. So I know a tasty piece of meat when I encounter one. 8 Korean BBQ is legit yo. I didn't expect much because if you've dined at Koreatown LA many times before, you know what's hot and not. 8 Korean BBQ is hot. Their pork belly is JUICY. Their kimchi is a bit salty though. At least the day I had it. So awesome they had brown rice instead of white rice. Puts a smile on a health nut's face. INSTRUCTIONS: Take a piece of lettuce, place on a pink round radish, a slice of pork, then some kimchi. Wrap it up and into your mouth. Repeat. PRICING: 8 Korean BBQ is pricier than Palsaik. The set of eight flavors at Palsaik costs $50. The similar set, if not exactly the same, is double in Singapore's sister location. But if love K-bbq, it's worth every penny. Their juicy pork belly will not fail to disappoint. CONCLUSION: If you ever miss Koreatown LA, you know where to go... 8 Korean BBQ. Make sure you order a bottle of soju with your meal. Gunbae! Cheers! And if you get drunk, don't fall into the river. Those stairs are steep. Please have a designated walking buddy.

Fantastic food and service. Hailing from my hometown of Ktown LA, this is the same owners as Palsaik, which in Korean means "8 Flavors".  They have recently re branded and decided to situate themselves here in Singapore.  I was super excited and eager to try this awesome place before it got super packed.OG Website: palsaikbbq.comDecor/Ambience: Very modern and urban. Clean use of concrete, exposed brick, the whole nine yards.  The grill is customized with "8" logos on the corners and everything is shiny, new and clean. Very sterile.  The unique designs of the seat is that you can lift the cushion up and it serves as a "locker" for your bags and such so no pork fat or grease will get on it.The service: Great! Man, the Singaporean manager was very helpful, friendly, kind and attentive.  She answered all questions quickly and we also had the chance to meet one of the LA quality control guys, Jae.The food: Amazing! Pork lovers rejoice! The 8 flavour combo comes in: Wine, Regular, Ginseng, Herb, Miso, Curry, Garlic, Gochujang. Comes with an array of banchans as well as grilled kimchi and bean spouts for you to build your own wrap.  The stew was good and had plenty of seafood however after reducing on the flame it got super salty.  As a treat, Jae ended up making bokumbap for us with the leftover stew which was the highlight of the meal.I highly recommend coming here for some of the most authentic Samgyupsal in town. It will be packed within weeks- I just know it!

So we wandered around Central Mall, looking for somewhere we both could agree on for dinner. Husband: "I don't really like Korean"Me: "Oh, so this place is no good then?"Husband: "Never said I didn't like Korean BBQ"So we manage to get a table on a Saturday night. Outside. By the lights of Clarke Quay. We choose the 4 color pork, wine, original, miso and garlic. Service was a little slow, I managed to devour the kimchi before I could even imagine our meat arriving. My 3 year old didn't have many options other than rice. So she played with that a while. Finally our meat came out with the seafood broth. The meat was delicious, cooked so well and so full of flavor. Surprisingly, my non seafood eating husband, not only tried the soup, but went back for more and then some. I'd say that's testament in itself that we wandered into a good Korean BBQ place. Best I've been to so far in my 30 years!

I have only compliments for the food = 3 thumbs up!But behind the "friendly" faces lurk rude and insulting servers. Most visitors probably compliment the "good" service because they do not understand what the Filipino servers comment when they exchange communication amongst themselves in Tagalog.I visited the restaurant today with a friend who understands and speaks fluent Tagalog but is Chinese. The servers, Joey and Del, didn't suspect one bit that she understands Tagalog and continuously exchanged insulting and rude comments about us between themselves in Tagalog while masking their insults with wide smiles - while serving us.Good food but such service standards would make anyone lose an appetite.

A Serendipitous Find!We had the 4 colour set at 8 korean bbq. The  4 colour set comes with four flavours of BBQ Pork from a total of eight flavours and we also ordered the pork belly kimchi stew as part of the set.The stew - tastes savoury and rich, has a smooth texture, and is not too thick. it's one of the BEST Korean stews I've ever tasted. I try a few pieces of the pork meat in the sizzling stew and they are delicious, too.The meat - It is juicy, savoury, succulent, and tastes perfect no matter how you eat it: I wrap it with kimchi in cabbage, eat it with the multi-grain rice, and dip it in sesame oil. No matter which method I try, the meat still tastes oh-so-fabulous!Beer - Had the Korean Hite Beer while indulging in the 8 Korean BBQ feast. Light and refreshing with a smooth texture, and has a nice bittersweet aftertaste.Overall, everything was good. The meat tastes heavenly, the stew is delicious, and we enjoyed good service throughout. It was surreal. My bf & I are both completely satisfied. Check out our full review and photos at eatandtravelwithus.com/2…

I'm from LA and this place is a disappointment compared to the original. Around $90 something for 8 different kinds of pork belly, with less side dishes and smaller meat portions. In LA, i think it's around $38 for better everything. I guess I can't complain though that there's now a 8 saik in Singapore.  The only upside to this place was its kpop atmosphere fit for pregaming.

As a person that has tried the original in LA (called palsaik), I can say this tastes better. However, the LA one has different cuts of pork and this place just has 8 different flavors. Each 8 flavors are bursting in taste and immensely delicious. The price is about 2.5 times more expensive than the one in LA but its probably bc the overhead is higher in sg. And the quantity is much smaller as well. 98 bucks for 4 people but honestly, 2 people can finish that portion.  I would say its probably one of the best in korean bbq in singapore but thats not really saying much bc korean food in sg is not that great.

Came for lunch on a Sunday and the restaurant was the only one doing brisk business in this place. No surprise as its mainly a office building so parking was a breeze. There was a queue at THW but moved rather quickly. We ordered a whole bunch of their dim sum including their promotion specials - fried dry Hor Fun with chicken and prawns. What we had and verdict - Glutinous rice in lotus leaf - very good Har gow - $6 for 4 is quite expensive and on par with Chinese restaurants in hotels. That said, it was competently done with thin skin and crunchy shrimp filling. Siew Mai - same feedback as the Har Gow. Malay cake - fluffy soft and not too sweet. Wu Kok with Chili crab filling - interesting. Not badSpinach and shrimp dumpling - loved this with its chewy transparent skinShrimp Cheong fun - decentCheong fun with sesame sauce - won't order this again as its quite boring and the sesame sauce was on the stingyHot tea is chargeable but refillable.

Overhyped. Overpriced. UnderwhelmedDISCLAIMER: we got there at 2am so the supper menu was available (which is not as extensive as their regular menu) but it made such an impact, this is the first and last time ill ever visit a tim ho wan.Also, they asked us for our last order at 230am, so not quite sure if they 24 hrs everyday. Pl call ahead to check. We had the fish porridge, beef brisket noodles, har gow, chicken feet, veggie of the day (poached lettuce) and shrimp/pork wrapped in beancurd skinOf all the dishes, we liked the veggies the best!!!Har kow prawns were big/fresh but skin was chewy.Beancurd skin was also chewy. The beef brisket was very tender but tasteless, as was its Soup. The porridge was average and the chicken feet is braised, so if youre expecting the usual chicken feet dim sum dish (which we were), youll be disappointedAll in all, it cost us close to $50.You are better off heading to swee choon for your late night dim sum fix. We only ended up at tim ho wan cause it was a tues and swee choon was closed
Food was Delicious. Service was excellent. Extra bowls was delivered without as needing to ask for.The famous baked BBQ buns are a must there They were also voted best restaurant in Asia this year.

I still assume that Tim Ho Wan is one of the best dim sum restaurants in Singapore. Not many variety of dishes but the quality of each dishes are awesome!Recommended menu: the bun! The minus side is just you almost always have to queue to enjoy Tim Ho Wan, because normally it will be so crowded!

After the Monday to Friday grind, there's nothing like a good food adventure to kick start the weekend right!  El Queso Grande was interviewing a candidate for a job, so I had the morning free to run wild and so I ran all the way to Tim Ho Wan at Aperia Mall near Lavender MRT to check out the famed heavenly dim sum.There were a few larger groups waiting for tables, but as a solo diner, I scooted in right away with my little clipboard for ordering.  The placements have pictures of all the items, which makes ordering super convenient.  The one downside of dining solo is having to rein in the ordering...I settled on two of the four heavenly kings, the pork buns and the carrot cake and one wildcard: the spring rolls filled with egg whites.  The buns were adorably round and with well balanced sweet and savory flavor.  The carrot cake was good, sinfully gooey inside with crisp corners.  I would have liked even more crispiness on the top and bottom, but I have no limit to the amount of crispiness I can handle.  The spring rolls were delicious too with tiny baby shrimps stuffed inside with the egg whites.Service was snappy though you could tell the staff were bracing for the weekend rush when waits can top an hour (or so I hear).The space is airy and bright with street views and only a five minute walk from the MRT.PARTING THOUGHT: they should install a THW live line cam, so you can plan when to go!

finally, a tim ho wan that i'll write a review about ah!:)yes, yes, everyone knows they have a michelin star!yes, yes, everyone knows how cheap they are!yes, yes, i've been to their hong kong outlet in sham shui po and fought the horrendous hordes and emerged victorious ah!but this outlet is opened 24/7!!!what?!yes, you can eat your favourite BBQ baked bun, no it is not a polo bun, here at any time, any day!your chances of scoring a seat, without a fight or a long ass queue, is that much higher here!and thus far, i did not have to queue at all lah.and this outlet serves a special breakfast and supper menu outside of their regular meal hours.granted during those ungodly hours, to some, there is no table service!no big deal, just order from their simplified set menus during those periods and collect your choice at the kitchen counter when your number is up lah.parking here is also easy at the new aperia mall.what?!yes, aperia mall, yet to be fully occupied and a work in progress.so once again, no crowd, best bah!isn't it amazing how there are now more tim ho wans in SG than in HK!?and soon, you can even enjoy their big 4 heavenly kings down under lah, wunderbar!

This HK Michellin star awardee is sprouting up all over the island. Personally, i find their food ok but not as fantastic as what many make it out to be. This outlet is good as the queues aren't that crazy. Food taste authentic and true to the taste of their HK flagship store which i tasted. I was really dissapointed at their congee, tasted really bland. I would say that the food in general is a good bang for the buck but the French should try a couple more Dim Sum joints and they will realuse that they will be dishing stars to many other Dim Sum places.
I thought the food was very average considering how much people talk about them. Service is, ehrm, Singaporean.  Definitely not your culinary experience to talk about. Wouldn't recommend.
This is a fast food dim sum place. I preferred a real Cha Lo. Limited dim sum selection. Nothing outstanding.
Char siew Char Siew. But not worth the queue. Service is prompt. Porridge is a tiny bowl. Just mostly the Char Siew. My Fav!

Possibly the best happy hour deal on the island. When you've been walking all day and then see that Tomo Izakaya has a crazy hour from 5-6:30pm with Sapporo drafts for only $3.90++ ... YAAAS! Rest my weary feet and hand me a beer (or five). They also have all you can drink packages for later in the evening if you want to do some true damage. It's truly quite perfect to grab a beer by the river as a gentle breeze hits you while the sun slowly sets. Vacation winning.

I came here with my mom after a bumboat trip on the Singapore river looking for a some place where we could eat late without being in a very loud club-type environment so we ended up at Tomo Izikaya as it is one of the places near the Singapore river at Clarke Quay which look cosy and less crowded.The atmosphere was certainly worth 4 stars, it is nice to sit next to the river and enjoy the view of the tourist boats passing by. However, the food is only so-so and you obviously pay for the location. The highlight of the different foods we got was the steak bites, they were tasty and nicely marinated. However, the tempura and sushi were just ok, not what you expect for this price.One more plus of this place is that the alcohol is cheap (compared to other places in Singapore), we paid 8$ for a gin tonic and 11$ for a beer which is quite good value!Would I return? Probably not, if I would, it would be for the view or the cheap drinks than the food but I guess there are so many other places at Clarke Quay which have better food options so why return?

Tomo Izakaya is right in the middle of the action in Clark Quay, and it has both an indoors and outdoors section.  The outdoor section overlooking the river is a nice spot to grab some food and drinks and Tomo has above average Japanese fare and some great drink specials.  We tried a variety of dishes - sashimi, sushi, kushimono, and some fried foods.  The sashimi was fresh and sliced well.  However, it's a bit of mystery why the sushi rolls were a bit weak, using krab in the California roll and having a bit too much rice.  We tried quite a few of the skewers - beef, chicken, pork with mushrooms, and bacon wrapped asparagus.  The chicken and pork enoki were quite good, while the beef seemed to be bit overpriced for the quality.  The Korokke was very tasty, though.  The drink specials were also quite good - haf off frinks until 7, so I was drinking draft Sapporo for $5.50!  And even afterwards, 180ml of house sake which is quite decent was only $8.  Overall, while Tomo is not the best for any one thing, I would recommend their sashimi ,some skewers and agemono.  They also have some great drink specials and prime location so it's a great place to wind down or pre-funk in Clark Quay!

1. Buta kakuniStewed pork belly- Some pieces were less tender and more dry than others. - The sauce was very thick and flavorful so if you like sauce, this is definitely your dish.- Overall ok. 2. TonkatsuDeep fried pork coated with fresh bread crumbs- They were very generous in the slices of pork (thick, crispy, juicy slices). - Wished that it was more flavorful though. Perhaps marinated with something before it was fried? or maybe toss in some spicy seasoning (those power kinda that the Taiwanese street stalls always sprinkle upon their fried chicken)- Overall still good. 3. Vermicelli in a beef broth with thin beef slices and an poached egg (forgot the name of this dish. Nigi-something...) - This was sooooo GOOD :) - The beef broth was flavorful and slightly sweet :) - Mixed with the poached egg and Vermicelli noodles it was divine!!! will come back just for this dish. Ambiance is great! nice deco!

My husband and I usually come here on Friday nights, since it's pretty close to his office. It's also a good compromise for when I want sushi and he wants Japanese style steak, as they offer both here!Happy hour is a good time to go, as it's not too crowded and the beer prices are affordable. Miguel usually enjoys his steak, though sometimes they do overcook it and it does turn out a bit dry. They don't have the best sushi in the world, but so far I haven't gotten sick from it, so it's A-OK in my book. The tempura and their udon soup are also solid choices.The last time we were here, the service left much to be desired. First off, they delivered our dishes out of order. I ordered agedashi tofu as an appetizer and sushi for my main, and the sushi came first. Also, they forgot about our green tea, which came halfway through our meal. For some reason, Miguel's steak was taking a long time (maybe that's why it came out dry and overcooked?) and I finished my meal by the time his was delivered. At one point, they even gave us a soup that we didn't even order! It didn't help that the majority of the servers looked like little lambs lost in the woods, trying to figure out which dish belongs to which table. To top it off, Miguel asked for an extra serving of rice which was never given to us. Of course, it was added to our bill, so we had to wait even longer for them to fix the issue and give us the correct bill. Usually, the service isn't that bad, but man, were they wayyy off their game for a Friday night.Overall, I think prices are on the higher side, and probably because of the Clarke Quay location. With the numerous amount of restaurants in Clarke Quay, this is a decent choice, but not a place to go out of your way for.

this is a great spot for all around Japanese food, not just sushi.  they have some great skewers that are interesting mixes of flavors, like minced chicken in mushrooms or mushroom, roe, wrapped in bacon with a cheese topper.  the sake selection is pretty good, as i was able to get a sake that you can basically only get in Japan.  They have a happy hour that is 1 for 1 (2 for 1 in the US) for Sapporo beers.  the tuna sushi that i had was some of the better sushi i have had in Singapore.  I look forward to trying more of the selections.we went early on a Saturday night and it filled up quick so if i were you i would get a reservation.  The place seems to be a lively place, so if you really want a quite night i would not recomend coming here, or Clarke Quay for that matter.

My friends and I were in search of some good place for Japanese food for a gathering with our Japanese teacher and we ended up at Tomo Izakaya at Clarke Quay. It didn't look like a very special place at first, and it was barely filled when we reached there. But subsequently, more people came in and it became quite a lively and vibrant atmosphere.I have to say I really love the whole ambience of this place, with simple decorations and warm lights. It is pretty spacious and even if you have a big group gathering, they would have done the arrangement for you in advance. The service is prompt and good too. And of course the food! The food's good. We were skeptical about the sushi at first, but it turned out that the sushi and sashimi is as good as the grilled items as well. Moreover, this restaurant operates till late on Fridays, Saturdays and public holidays. It's a comfortable and cozy place to hang out at, even in big groups.

I like this place because it has a nice selection of sakes at affordable prices, and super awesome for big groups who just want to sit down, drink sake and not have to yell over the table to be heard. It is quiet enough to talk, but not too quiet to be boring. Some of the food items are pretty good (fried stuff), and they almost always have some sake promotions. In big groups, you can drink a lot at an affordable price.

This is a pretty unremarkable izakaya place. The food is decent, the service is marginal-to-poor, and the prices are comparable to other Clark Quay restaurants, which is moderately overpriced. They have a nice outdoor seating area on the river, so if you are looking for an attractive place to meet some friends over sake, Tomo would be adequate.

I came here with a small group during the week and rather late- wasn't too crowded and we were seated immediately. The service was okay- started off great but we had to flag her down later in the meal. On to the food! The sashimi was wonderful- very fresh! I was lucky enough to snag one of the ama ebi with a bit of roe! Yum. I love tiny fish eggs :) The yellowtail crudo was delicious. I wasn't impressed with the rolls. Everything had a drizzle of kewpie on it. Don't get me wrong I love japanese mayo- but not all over my sushi rolls. The small kitchen plates were good- we had the karaage and the roasted pork. The tamago was made in house but was a unpleasant gray color and fell apart. Tasty but sad to look at.  We washed everything down with plum wine that was on special- buy one bottle get one free! I'd go back again. The location is nice- smack dab in the middle of Clark Quay so you can party after your meal :)

Have been going there for last 2 years and must say that things have only gotten better. They have new pizzas and beer to match these. New desserts and new starters as well.Recently, attended the sausage festival where their handmade sausages of chicken, pork and lamb were a big hit. They were very tasty and had a good spice flavour.Biramisu - Their version of tiramisu using beer, is still as excellent as ever. Well, the only difference is that now one needs to make a reservation before going else you will be disappointed as the place is usually full quite a lot of times that i have been there.Keep it up!!

I've only ordered from Pizza Fabbrica through ubereats, but with my struggle with finding good pizza in Singapore this would likely take the lead.Cooked Neapolitan style and like everything else in Singapore, pretty pricey, but this reminded me of home and was easily one of my favorite meals. I've had the margherita and truffle- despite the thicker than expected crusts, they were still light to eat and both selections were excellent. Highly recommend.

We arrived very late, most places in the alley had closed shop for the night and we just tried our luck and asked whether they were still open and served food.Yes they were, but pizza only - exactly what we wanted. My heart leaped for joy when I saw that they actually had a true wood fire oven at the back.We went for the draft beer, which our very nice server recommended, and ordered pizza capricciosa and a margarita. Priced at 20 S$++ for my margarita, as the least expensive on the menu, it is on the medium to upper end of the spectrum.The pale ale arrived shortly thereafter and tasted wonderfully fruity. The pizzas did not take long either and I honestly don't think I have had such a good pizza for a long time. This place is a little out of my way but I would always gladly return!

excellent place. You wouldn't notice it if you were not looking for an Italian place. In a street where there are many other restaurants. Great food and great service. The Chianti is excellent too. The owner Sumit is very helpful. And they deliver too.In the last 45 days- have eaten 5 times.

Looks fancy but tastes between awful and bearable.The PANCETTA FUNGHI CAPRINO E SCALOGNO - basically goat cheese on a bread base. Tastes fine if that's what you know you are getting.GNOCCHI MELANZANE BUFALA E POMODORINI - overcooked and soggy.TRUFFLE PIZZA - gratuitous use of the main ingredient, again, if that's what you want then you will be happy. Although I find excessive use of truffles is like taking a blunderbuss approach to cooking.I don't think they understand what makes a good pizza. Stick to their products which come in bottles - they have a nice selection of beers.

Had dinner here with a small group of friends and truly had an enjoyable time. The service was really good even though it did take a little longer for food to arrive but it was a fairly busy time for them. I simply loved their bruschetta..it has the classic tomatoes, one piece with pumpkin cream and another with ricotta. Amazing! we had both pizzas and pastas and everything was really good. My favorite was the snow peas and potato pizza..weird for a pizza but oh so good! And ended we a saffron panna cotta and a chocolate Java cake which all of us will go back for!!

Great environment and located in the "Arab St" neighborhood. While the dishes were beautiful and rather tasty, I must say I'm still much more partial to Cicheti which has a similar menu, but bolder flavors.

I walked by this place a few weeks ago and looked at the menu. I realize, I couldn't eat anything there. No real meat or veggie dishes, without carbs or dairy.So, when my freind invited me last night and said it was highly recommended, I cringed!Then when I finished my dinner, I was pleasantly suprised.THere were only 2 meat based mains.Ribeye and Seabass.I ordered the seabass. encrusted with zucchini and served with a tomatoe salsa. it was a good 150gs, and tasty.Apparently, the ribeye was 300gm, which would have been too much.It was Very nice! Healthy, light and perfect!My freind and others told me that their pizzas were absolute junk, but I can't and won't confirm that.My friends both ordered pastas. The portions were generous, for pastas, (but since I don't eat carbs, what do I know?), and they said the flavours were pretty good.We ordered a tiramisu with coffee and been infused and even though I couldn't eat it,  my freinds said it was average at best, and that the addition of the coffee and beer ruined it.Overall, the ambience was nothing memorable, although they blared radio music, which was beyond strange and a tab uncomfortable.It's definitely the last time I'll dine there.

I grapple between 4 and 5 stars, this is definitely a 4.5 star place in my book. Just opened for 2 months, this place had showed great promise when we walked past it a month ago. The draw is wood-fired pizza but surprisingly, I enjoyed the pastas better than the pizzas. More importantly, this modern chic italian joint serves a good variety of both craft beers and wines, which is rare for italian restaurants, and they believe in beer and food pairings instead of just the typical wine and food. Also, the prices for the mains are well priced for a nice restaurant, ranging from 18-24 bucks for a very generous portion of food. I had the homemade gnocchi with eggplant and olives and the sauce was sublime. The gnocchi was soft and starchy and the sauce was obviously home-made with cherry tomatoes and eggplant. The pasta with bolognese sauce was excellent as well, a respectable home-made sauce worthy of Bologna, and pasta was served al dente. The husband really liked the four cheese pizza, I liked the taste of the gorgonzola cheese of it, but I had it when it was already slightly cold so could have been better. The green pea soup of the day had a really well-balanced taste of pea with a hint of mint, really tasty albeit a little watery (more pea please!). This is our new favorite italian restaurant in Singapore. Oh, and if you are a fan of bloody marys, you HAVE to try their italian bloody mary, it is divine.
Just love the banana walnut pancakes... And the fact that its inside the beautiful botanic garden makes this restaurant a nice place to visit for brunch on weekends.

This is a great little spot for brunch after a walk around the Botanic Garden. Service was quick and impeccable! We'd read about the berry and chocolate pancakes on a blog post and decided they were a necessary addition to American-style eggs, toast and bacon and an order of chicken laksa. The pancakes were tasty but not particularly special for pancakes. The homemade brioche toast was a clear winner, as was the laksa. The lattes were perfect for cooling down after the humidity of the gardens. Overall, a perfect spot to grab a bite.

If you're visiting the gardens and looking for a nice, casual dinner, this is the place to go. Unlike the other restaurants in the botanical gardens, the atmosphere here is very relaxed and child-friendly. There's a playground outside and plenty of indoor space for kids to run around (they seem to throw good birthday parties, too).The food here was pretty good, albeit a little expensive. It's one of the only places I've found in Singapore that serves good quality, authentic Western food. For $20, I got a nice portion of grilled barramundi with basil pesto and a huge serving of mashed potatoes. The artisan burgers are nicely prepared too, at around $10, plus extra if you want drinks and fries. I also HIGHLY recommend the basil mayonnaise for $2 more. It was so good, we ate it with just about everything, even though it was intended to be eaten with just the fries!The drinks and desserts were nothing exciting, though, and rather pricey. A regular can of soda costs $3, and the specialty Pellegrino sodas are a bit more. The red velvet cake was the biggest disappointment of all. It was very dry and the frosting tasted like unsweetened cream cheese. Definitely not worth $6. Overall, eating here is a very pleasant experience, as the staff is very friendly and accommodating. The food comes out in a timely manner, and the waiters will wait to bring things out (i.e. dessert) until you want them to.

I came here one late Sunday morning for brunch. And sure enough, the crowd was thick. The problem with a popular place on a Sunday morning is getting seats and I believe they do not do reservations. So the troop of us, about 6 managed to squeeze ourselves on to a single small table in an odd corner of the place. The menu is a replicate of the one found in the other branch at Queen St. Nonetheless, the space and ambience fortunately makes up for the lack of a waiting staff. I would imagine that need to hire a lot more if they were to get people seated by waiters, the dining space is sprawling, indoors and out. The food, I had the works. And a beer on the side. Yes, Sunday morning beers. Heh. We had to line up at a counter to place our orders and pay for them at the same time. They advised that the food would be served in 30 minutes or less but in actual fact they came in about 10. Very fast and efficient I thought! The food was as expected, good. All in, a rather enjoyable Sunday morning for all us.

Food for Thought started out as a little café in the Bras Brasah area and has now expanded to include a restaurant in the Botanic Gardens. They serve no frills comfort food at a pretty decent price. The branch in the Botanic Gardens is huge and it's a nice place to go for lunch or brunch after a walk in the park. They've got a wide array of desserts, Western and local mains, as well as breakfast. Most of their dishes have a cool local twist to it. I tried the banana pancakes which was served with gula Melaka syrup. I would come back here for sure for brunch.

average brunch food at the botanic gardens - some dishes (the simple ones) better executed than others. this placeIs rather popular, and I can see why. it's a large open space, completely casual canteen-seating predominates, and the menu is likewise expansive.it's not the best brunch I've had - really, not even close - but I don't really think that's the point. it feels rather more like a place you go to to be convivial, or bring your screaming children along - without too more recrimination, with a dash of decent food to help lubricate conversation.it's a casual place, this - you shimmy up to order at the cashier and food gets served to the table. the partner had his mind set on the trio of sliders: the kaffir lime fish, spicy thai chicken and pulled pork. served alongside fries, these were all average - the bread was soft and giving though, and we'll recommend the chicken: it was tender, moist leg meat, seasoned well.I took the salad-as-lunch option. the plate of sugar snap peas came tossed in a soy-sesame mix - refreshing in its simple greenness. the peas are untrimmed though, and I had to remove all the threads myself - avoid this if you're on a first-date-first-impressions kind of deal.the smoked salmon & broccoli plate was a great mix of flavors. chargrilled broccoli, cold hot-smoked salmon and roast beetroot - all delicious.I might return. that salad was good, and the place does brunch proud - a vibrant atmosphere, nothing too awe-inducing or surprising for the first meal of the day. comfortable like those old pyjamas you can't bear to throw away.just don't come expecting mind-blowing food, and get in on the chillness of it all.

This was our third visit within a month of moving to Singapore. Location is within the grounds of the Singapore botanic gardens and has an interesting concept where you queue and order and then your food is delivered to your table - which are organized by number. There is indoor and outdoor seating as well as a nice but small play area for kids. Today we ordered the laksa, mee rebus, house breakfast, pancakes with chocolate, and a toddlers egg, bacon and toast combo. To drink long black, flat white, lime iced tea and rosemary blood orange juice. The OJ was particularly enjoyable.The food is reasonably priced, super fast and oozes a kid friendly vibe.The chocolate pancakes are my daughter's favorite, two large cakes with a generous portion of chocolate chips that melts as you spread it around!The eggs and bacon are pretty standard fare as was the laksa and rebus. Overall worth a visit and will be a place we frequent.
tasteless food...though they do look somewhat good.the playground is way too small.please bring back the old old food court with jalan kayu roti prata stall.

When I first heard that FFT had opened an outlet at Botanic Gardens, I was excited to check it out. Afterall, I was fond of its concept- a cause to support, breakfast components dissected to variable portions and trendy marketing: whats there not to love?Sad to say, I was disappointed both times when I went to visit. While the interior of the place is gorgeous (plants growing out of tables, mind you)- I found the ordering system counter-intuitive and user-unfriendly. The restaurant expects you to first find yourself a table, (have someone to) chope the seat, and queue at the ordering counter. When ordering, you are supposed to tell them exactly where you are seated (basically screwed if someone else takes your seat) or they will refuse to let you order until you have found an alternative seat. I can imagine what a hard time this would give single diners, or worse, having to split up lovey-eyed couples by forcing one to queue thereby subjecting them to a painful 20 minutes wait before they reunite! The 'choping' mechanism also makes me feel very ugly- I once had to tell someone with a crying baby on hand that basically all the seats around me were reserved. It is also very Singaporean, which surprises me, because Botanics is afterall a touristy place which attracts people whose culture might be vastly different from ours. I imagine this system to be completely indiscernible to them (I have seen foreigners bitch at staff over it).Even the food is not comparable to the other outlet. My scrambled eggs came too buttery, it was like drinking oil, but I didn't even feel like sending it back because it would possibly mean having to wait for another half an hour. The menu is also different from the other outlet's- so if you are thinking of heading to this one for a specific dish, remember to check the online menu before you make your trip down.

Out of all the Food for Thought outlets in Singapore, this is the least impressive. It's located a midst the greenery of the botanical gardens - which means it has great potential. Unfortunately, the branch is let down by lackluster service, with the wait staff being under-trained and confused. Food wise - it's okay. It has greater variety than the other Food for Thought outlets, and is pretty cheap. This unfortunately is insufficient to overcome the terrible seating system they have - which is confusing to locals and tourists alike.

Double chocolate muffin ($4) - 2.75 starsNot too sweet and had a good bittersweet chocolate flavor, but it was a bit too dry. I'd get it if, like today, I really wanted a jumbo chocolate muffin.Update 25 Apr 17Afternoon tea set ($10) for a cake and coffee. Options: NY baked cheesecake, Oreo cheesecake, rainbow cake, carrot cake, chocolate fudge cake. Apple pie not included.Hot dark chocolate with mini marshmallows - 4 starsThe mini marshmallows melted too quickly! And the foam dissipated quite quickly so the actual amount of hot chocolate wasn't that much. But I liked the taste - not too sweet!Chocolate fudge cake - 4 starsI liked this cake! They warmed it up but it was only slightly warm and quickly cooled down to room temperature. It tasted better at the start. Soft and quite moist. A bit later the fudge icing melted and got too runny so my top layer of cake fell off. Still good though.Might try the cheesecake the next time. Wanted to get it but it looked too smooth and not cake-y.

Convenient and good portions. My niece and I wanted a quick bite and walked to the Singapore Botanic Gardens. I was expecting a food court but instead, Food for Thought had taken over the space. My niece had the spaghetti bolognese (kid's meal), and I enjoyed a big breakfast. Scrambled eggs, bacon, ham came with nicely toasted brioche and I loved the sauteed mushrooms. I enjoyed my meal. The eggs were a little on the overdone side, but I did not leave hungry. The decor is a little run down. The servers were helpful once you spoke to them. You have to walk to the order and pay station.
Cool little place to have lunch or a snack while strolling around the Botanic Gardens.  Good variety of options to choose from and a good place to get out of the heat and humidity and cool off.

A casual place that is good for family time due to the large space and playground outside to occupy the children.Food is decent but nothing special to be honest. Maybe except the Gula Melaka granola. But prices are more than fair and nett.

Located inside the Singapore Botanic Gardens on Cluny Road, Food for Thought at Botanic Gardens  possesses a truly tranquil atmosphere. The place looks modern and well-decorated with brick styled counter, wooden tables, clear white chairs and an innovative ceiling. Kids can hang out in the close-by playground while adults are having meals. Especially, a catchy 5-step slogan sitting comfortably on a white long wall is something you can't miss for a wonderful selfie.Recommendation: Banana Walnut Crepes, Full Breakfast/Brunch PlatterFor more, visit us as: thecoupleeats.com/singap…

A nice place in the botanic gardens; nice ambience great for brunch and a quiet gathering Very spacious space; great for events The food was passable ; not extremely fantastic but still pretty good. Had the pulled pork pasta - pork was a little too salty; wasn't spicy enough and slightly too oily : however it was okay Latte was Normal as well; so was the carbonara - nothing too memorable. Wouldn't go back especially for the food but is a good chill and nice hang out place after a run in the botanic gardens or for brunch out of the city

Surprisingly empty for brunch on a Saturday (reached at 12.30pm). Food was decent but not great. Tried their basic breakfast ($9) and my friends got the full breakfast ($22) and their special of the day, banana walnut toast ($12). The banana walnut toast that came topped with yogurt was too sweet for my liking. The toast also tasted more like a muffin. The scrambled eggs and brioche were decent though. Not the best brunch place in town, but good for a casual catch up. Also appreciate the lack of GST and service charge. Coffee ($5) was out of the machine and not good at all.

Had a lovely brunch out here with friends and kids. I had a bangers & mash and it was good! Hub had a pasta with Broccoli and prawn. That was good too!
