Instead, fine-dining is far too distant from my experience for which the place is less intimidating but harbor a sense of friendliness and a perfect spot for a daytime botanical meal.The lunch is a quick meal intended with no fuss selection except for a top-up if you want a Riso pasta or a Kaya Toast as dessert. A 3-course is priced at $38++ while you may go for a Luncheon Discovery menu which offers a 5-course at $88++ when you have a more generous lunch hour. We were led to our table swiftly and they were very attentive to our needs. We were given amble time to decide on our choices and we were brief on the idea behind the dishes and the assembles on our plate each time we were served. That's the whole service I give honor to as I care extensively about what I eat and how they flavored my dining exposure.They came around with a bread basket piling with fresh baguette and wholegrain slices for you to pick out. I was look forward to the small heap of Yves Bordier French butter - very rich and creamy. Like we did, sprinkle a few sea salt flakes on your buttered bread and bon appétit!We were presented with the Marinated Norwegian Salmon Trout for a start. I am not a big fan of any cured fish except for certain meat. Nevertheless, the teaser wasn't a turn off but was quite lovely given a gentle sweet hint in the creme sauce underneath the bed of salad pyramid with onions, celery strips while the petit flying fish roe went popping in my mouth. The salmon is nice without a fishy note, very nicely cured.I had the free range chicken instead of the Riso Pasta (supplement of $8), the latter reminds me of Orzo pasta which I once had at The Waterfall Cafe and am still liking it. I didn't want too much carbs so the chicken dish appeals to me. The Free Range Chicken has a very fine texture, baby tender like a juvenile. The skin is lightly pan-seared although its thick fatty tissue is somewhat freaking me out. Jason uses a mix of white and yellow corn kernels for the key flavor which heightens the taste a notch further with natural sweetness. The foam like I guess was supposedly the poultry emulsion patterning the plate.I tasted the impressive "The interpretation of Kaya Toast" (supplement of $8) and was feeling complete! The taste of Gula Melaka has made a strong statement in the dessert while the pandan scent has went into hidding. I love the intensity of the coconut palm sugar, mirroring the chendol we once knew. The muscovaldo sand bits adds bites to the cream along with the citrus element in the yuzu sorbet - heavenly match.Alternatively, you may choose to go with the Soursoup Sorbet which is no inferior than the kaya toast. It has a smooth texture with a robust Soursoup accent that arrived with a sweet indication. Not overly nectarous when accompanied by a bed of Morello cherry compote. The pretty-looking meringue extends a light crunch to the frictionless construction. It gives you a soft and dainty closure to your afternoon meal. However if you adore a loud booming ending, go for the kaya toast which conferred a long lasting impression as it did on me.Oh they have free buggy service, ring them up and check on the pick up within the botanic garden.Bon appetit, yelpers!!!

The corner house restaurant is a converted bungalow in the botanical gardens. As such its location Is quaint and very beautiful. Service is attentive and very professional. The food is excellent. Each course was sublime, carefully prepared and presented as a piece of art. As expected its pricy. Perfect for that special occasion. Very romantic. A great place for couples to pop the question. The chicken was one of their signature dishes. Deceptively simple but the breast was brined and sous verde. The cooking and preparation method ensured that it was tender and succulent with the brine intensifying the flavor. The dark meat was brined and pan fried. 2 methods, very different and went well in contrast.

Consistent food and drinks. One of my favorite prata shop to satisfy the prata and Maggie goreng cravings.I have been visiting RK House for years. Sometimes visiting them 3-4 times a week or even more!! It is opened 24 hours a day, I have visited them for breakfast, lunch, dinner and supper. Teh Tarik, Maggie Goreng and any prata options never fail to disappoint. They do have a wide variety of options, tried a couple previously and they weren't as good.RK house is also famed for its insanely huge Milo Tower, Bandung Tower and Teh Tower. These towers are usually spotted in club serving beer, as it is a halal establishment, they used them to serve local beverages instead. Great for large group!! Reason why I minus one star is for their sneaky habit of adding/upgrading your food to more expensive versions. For example when I ordered maggie goreng. The guy would ask if I would like chicken or mutton. You have to explicitly state that you want them plain. Adding the mutton/chicken usually cost $3-5, the portions are pathetic and they are often not tasty! Beware of this sneaky habit. Despite this naughty habit, we still love RK house very much.

The indian food served here is decent. However u need to ask specifically how much does the food cost because they might upsell you. My conversation with the staff:Me: 'i want maggie goreng'Him: 'chicken or mutton'Me: 'chicken'Him: 'Fried chicken or chicken?'Me: 'Fried chicken? Wow.'Him: 'ok'Me: 'how much for fried chicken?'Him: '$7 something'Me: 'normal chicken?'Him: '$5 something'I ended up eating the pratas. My colleague ordered tissue prata & it came in a ridiculous size & shape. The doughs are far too oily, which leave me bloated the entire day. :( I said the food is decent because it taste ok. will not return so soon.

Indian Roti prata stall located in a busy neighbourhood area. Always pretty crowded around here with lots of food fanfare. Food is good and prices are pretty affordable except for sneaky staff trying to upsell their food umpteen times.Staff are dishonest & sneaky. They would ask you what kind of curry you would want with your roti prata, and when i said chicken curry, they would serve me a whole chicken with curry! Literally!I went a second time again and they tried to do it again. You have to tell them VERY literally. Just curry sauce, no meat!Service is slow and below average, so is their sanitary practices it seems. My utensils have food stains and i felt compelled to take them into the washroom for cleaning.
24-hour joint. Great place to hang out with friends. Better at night since there is no air-con.One of the few prata places where you ask for less sugar in your teh tarik, it really comes less sweet.

This place is like an institution in the Serangoon Gardens area. It has been around for decades and is a favorite spot for late night supper. It has the usual prata, briyani, Indian rojak, fried noodles, teh etc. I love the kosong prata which is squarish and is slightly crispy around the edges. The egg and onion prata is also good but it is softer and not that crispy so just order kosong (plain) if you prefer the crunch. The not so good thing is they do a bit of mis-representation. They will ask if you would like chicken or mutton curry to go with the prata. This is actually an additional order and is not an option for the complimentary curry which usually comes with prata. So just say you want the usual curry if you do not wish to have mutton or chicken curry. The usual curry has a bit of assam which I like as the tangy taste kinda refreshes the taste buds. The indian rojak is also very good with moreish peanut sauce which is not too spicy. The bee hoon goreng comes with bits of mutton and is yummy with hints of charred bits. Teh tarik is nicely pulled and is not too sweet. Since this is open 24 hours, you can literally have all your meals here.

You sure clean up good, RK. After the recent reno works, you look pretty fresh, and it's not like the previous look turned me off... it's more that I actually want to sit inside now, instead of always camping out at the alfresco seats, hoping for more ventilation.The food's just as good as before - there's the tandoor selection with delicious naan, or your staple myriad of pratas, and then there's the indan rojak... I'm a littl biased - I love the stuff at Suriya, which isn't too far away, but this place has a pretty good variety of offerings too, and since they are pretty busy, you know the food's fresh.It's a great place to come to for a late night snack, or if you've got Chomp Chomp fatigue.

The good:  If you happen to get the right staff/server, you are in for a treat.  I've managed to figure out who does what well here, and it totally matters.  When done right, I can get a spicy mee goreng (with gravy, a must) and iced teh tarik for less than it would cost for a 6' Subway sub.  That's what Charlie Sheen refers to as winning.  They also have a prata that continually puts neighboring prata stalls out of business.  They must be doing something right, right?    The bad:  If you get the wrong staff/server, you are in for a terrible treat.  I've had orders mixed up, been overcharged and witnessed some questionable sanitary practices.  You have to be stern and direct with what you want and how you want it, or they will do it the way they feel like, which usually means costing you.  The ugly:  I've grown to enjoy the "what will happen this time" element, so all and all I'm a fan.  I have equally as many, and now humorous, stories as I've had tasty meals.  It really just depends.  Normally such an establishment would receive 2 or even 1 star from me, but there is always a handful of staff that dig deep and deliver.  Plus they make me laugh, either intentionally with a joke or facial expression or by doing something so ridiculous you can't help but laugh it off.  Stick to the basics, take note of who does what well and you'll be happily content.

RK House is a eating place in Serangoon gardens. While it has been popular for it's traditional Malay dishes such as mee goreng, nasi goreng, etc. It became even more popular after someone recorded a prank about requesting for pork dishes in RK house with the angry stall holder threatening to call the police. After gaming at a LAN shop nearby, my friends and I dropped by RK house for supper. Surprisingly at 4am, they still had a full menu instead of a reduced menu most restaurants would do during wee hours. I ordered a favorite of mine: nasi goreng ikan bilis (fried rice with anchovies) and a cup of iced milo. The dishes came fast and it was cheap ($3.50). The nasi goreng tasted up to standard and I enjoyed having it. My friends who ordered prata and mee goreng had a decent meal as well. Just remember: Do not ask for non-halal dishes. I'm sure the waiters have put up with enough of such jokes over the years already.

This 24-hour restaurant with the yellow and green signboard has a great location at the Serangoon Gardens Circus. Anytime of the day that you're craving some prata, this is the place you can stop by. I used to frequent the prata places along Yio Chu Kang Road, but R K has a better parking situation and is just more convenient for me. Simple kosong pratas, or something fancier like Mushroom Cheese pratas, it's decent here and priced about the same as most places.

A solid prata house, if you are in the area. The pratas here are fluffier than the normal, giving a false notion of them not being too oily (which I'm not complaining about...) If you get the plaster pratas (prata with a sunny side up), remember to tell them that you don't want the yolk overcooked. The mutton curry was super oily but tasty as well. Definitely a great place to curb that prata craving if you are in the area....

I ate at this branch of Nam Nam the day after I dined at the City Hall branch, and I have to say, I appreciate the niche that this new chain fills. The food is of good quality (in my opinion), and personally, quite reasonably priced! Although I tried the pho at the other outlet, I'm not going to say that much about it here since that would technically be a different review. (I liked it though!)Instead, I had the 5 spice pork belly bahn mi. Considering (from what I've been told) that this chain is a sub-group of Annam, the Vietnamese restaurant by the Les Amis group, I was surprised it only cost me $5.90. I've had better bahn mis at a similar price point, and while they were a touch generous with the bread, I thought the flavours worked and the portion was alright for the amount I was paying. I would've liked more picked veggies, but I thought there was a good amount of pate, and personally enough pork belly too. Accompanied by an ice water, it was a quick, fast, and affordable meal that was precisely what I needed!

Always busy so expect a queue as would be expected at a great food stop.  Been here several times and have not been dissapointed.  Fast, quck and delicous and very reasonable..  In the fast comfort food catagory of the market there would be no reason not to give this group 4 or 5.  Concept well done.

best lunch deal in townl! $9.90 for a bowl of pho, fresh spring roll and a drink. this totally explains the long line during lunch but I'm glad to say the line moves pretty quickly so give it a try and don't get put off by the snake of people waiting. once inside  be prepared to be shoulder to shoulder with strangers as seating space is really tight. the food's served very quickly if you order the lunch set and a tad slower for the sandwiches.
Delivers consistent fresh flavors.  The chicken in the pho is remarkably tender.  Only thing that sucked are the desserts.  Give those a miss.
The noodle of Pho seems to be made from instant noodle not the fresh one like shops in Vietnam. The food used to be good but the quality is getting worse recently.

We frequent the branch at Plaza Singapura when shopping there but have been to other branches too. They have great food and quick service. This is not a normal sit down restaurant. You get assigned a table, fill out a ticket and pay at the counter and then have the food delivered to your table. You grab your own utensils from a station. My wife and I shared some fried spring roles and duck noodles with two drinks and were stuffed. We often have the fried banana fritters with coconut sauce for dessert. The serving size is huge and they are hot and tasty and a great value for the price.

I tried the banh mi with pork belly and pate. The meat was tender but overall, I thought the sandwich lacked flavour. The meat was so-so, and there weren't enough pickled vegetables and cilantro (I would have thought it wouldn't cost much to be generous with those). I probably wouldn't go back unless I was really desperate for a banh mi fix. I would rather continue my search for a good banh mi elsewhere...

You would think that with a large demand for good Vietnamese food in Singapore, someone would step up. This place was crazy busy and you have to wait in 2 different lines just to get your order in, it's got to be the most inefficient way of getting business done, but somehow people still come here. Why? Anyways, after painfully jumping through lines and hopes and finally getting our order in. The wait to get the food was not too bad. However the food was bland and small portions and the garnishments were so nonexistent. Not as bad as some other Vietnamese places here in Singapore though, but that's not saying much.

utterly fantastic vietnamese food at the basement of the wheelock place shopping mall. this place is such a gem, and really, it's the best food I've had for quite a while since coming back to singapore. great, tasty, savoury, and wholly satisfying food at great low prices - made even more reasonable within context of its location - this is one place worthy of fandom.photos here: andmorefood.wordpress.co…
Agree with Ray L.  Overall dining experience for what it is is quite good and efficient, but fundamentally the dishes have a lot of sauces that take away from the natural born flavor.

I had Nam Nam for breakfast! Honestly I never thought of it as a breakfast place. But after a run, the meat ball pho soul just smells amazing.But don't be in a rush to gobble it. Just take a deep breathe and feel the rich aroma caressing your poor tired soul. Then only shall you slowly take a sip of the soup and let it gently slide down your throatTreasure the first sip for it will be the best and subsequent sips shall never come close to tasting as good...

Love NamNam,  located in wheelock kinda between Ion and wheelock. Take a look at the menu while in line, check off what you want on the Order sheet and turn in and pay for your meal, grab a table and wait for some yummy food to come out. All of their options are tasty so go with what sounds good to you.  The lime soda is my drink of choice here.

Love this little Vietnamese joint! Their breakfast is super reasonable and delicious! I had their vegetarian bahn mi sandwich with Vietnamese coffee for only $4! What a steal!!! What a little treasure

The Nam Nam Noodle Bar was founded by Director and Owner Chef Nam who was born in Vietnam. Under the Les Amis Group, it is considered one of its cheaper restaurants. The casual restaurant is know for its banh mi and pho with no GST and service charge. One of the best deals in the restaurant is its value breakfast set. $5.90 for choice of any banh mi (excluding wagyu beef) + Viet coffee/ Lotus tea/ Bottled water$6.90 for choice of any pho (excluding pho wagyu beef) + Viet coffee/ Lotus tea/ Bottled waterI had tried its pho before and wasn't a fan of it as I felt it was rather tasteless. So I decided to go for the banh mi this time. Caramelised 5-spice pork belly ($6.90 ala carte)Toasted baguettes stuffed with savoury meats, topped with chicken pate, mayonnaise, hot chilli peppers, pickled carrots, daikon, cucumber and fresh cilantro.Quite a yummy combination with the tangy pickles, melt in the mouth fatty pork belly, and the creamy pate (I though it was tuna mayo at first as it was too creamy to the point of watery). Quite messy to eat with the pate dripping all over.Had it with a cup of hot Viet coffee with condensed milk. The drink was served in a metal cup which the older generation would had it associated with the poorer time. The coffee was a bit too bitter, but there was condensed milk on the counter to help oneself to. The drink tasted more better after that.Service was fast, may because there wasn't much people for a weekday morning.

I wandered here to find something for breakfast. I wasn't disappointed. I have never understood how or why people eat cereal or fruit for breakfast. It's cold, sweet food that my tummy just isn't ready for. But after traveling to Asia, it finally hit me - these are my people! Seriously, when everyone around you sits down at 9:30am to eat pho, you'll get what I mean. I ate the rare beef and meatball pho, and the broth was super flavorful. They provide jars of fresh "lemons" (they look like miniature limes) on the tables. There are tons of seeds, so be sure to squeeze the lemons into your soup spoon to catch them. The amount of food was pretty decent. My breakfast deal included a drink (I chose a bottle of water) and was super affordable (about $6 USD). I wish I lived here. I would be all over these food courts all the time!

We wandered in, seduced by the well-constructed , vaguely oriental hipster decor, and the promise of a warm bowl of luscious rice noodle soup. I've never been to Vietnam, and can only say that Nam Nam have a fair account of the cuisine - their pho was tasty but lacking in top note aromatics e.g basil and coriander. The banh mi was heavy on the bun, but light on filling. That said, the addition of cream cheese to the lemongrass pork banh mi was a surprising touch, imparting a hint of musty sweetness to the sandwich. Drinks were served with a suspiciously generous bouquet of aromatics - lemongrass sticks, coriander, mint leaves etc. It took us a few minutes to discover the bamboo straw through which we were to slurp up the precious little liquid which the clump of aromatics helped to pad out. It might have some strange rustic aesthetic charm, but seriously folks - bamboo straw = bad idea. Lousy control over flow rate, liquid either fails to be drawn up the length of the straw or gushes into the mouth in a massive torrent. And don't get me started on how sanitary the bamboo straws are...However, what disappointed me the most about this outlet was the very surly (lack of) service. Forget smiling - I don't think a single word was spoken to us throughout the meal service. We were vaguely ushered in by a dour faced waitress, and then treated to an unending stream of silent wait staff shoving our orders at us. I've eaten at various other Nam Nam outlets in the past, encountering varying degrees of unfriendliness, but this one has to be the most unwelcoming. The fact that the owners went to great lengths to present a very attractive facade but no apparent effort into customer experience, shows that this place is all style and no substance.

Update: 29 August 2013I went back to Nam Nam recently and tried the Bahn Mi (grilled chicken with chicken pate). The bread was about the size of a sub, but it looked bigger and fluffier. Set against so much carb, the meat filling seemed pitiful. Bread : Meat ratio 3:1The bahn mi underwhelmed me. Maybe I did not order the correct filling. But the whole thing was fresh which was good, and for just $5.90 one should not complain as it did fill your belly nicely. Add $0.50 for take-away. I also tried the pho (beef slices) again and the restaurant people probably took note of feedback as the basil had disappeared! No more herbs in the soup though the soup was still tasty. I must say I prefer this version as I am no big fan of too much basil leaves in my pho.=======================================3 March 2013I am on the fence about the pho. It is actually pretty good except for the strong herbal (probably basil) tasting broth. The beef was not overcooked and the noodles were smooth and soft.I prefer the Canadian style where you are served a plate of sprouts, basil, lime and cut green chilies and you can customize it to your liking. At least Nam Nam has the hoisin sauce and chili sauce to make your own dip for the meat. Not many places provide that.  I would like to try the banh mi next time though. The place can get crowded during dinner time but the food is served pretty fast. It is probably not a place for you to linger over coffee during the peak meal times.

It is 3 stars for the food, price,convenient locationFoodIt is decent, thus 3 stars. Nothing fancy. PriceAny bowl of noodle soup with few slices of beef under $10 is a steal apart from the food court or hawker centre's beef noodleConveniently located in quite a few malls now and it is long queue most of the dinner time

Oh...only if the queue is shorter...Yes, I would have given this place a 5 star if they managed their queue a bit better and change their ordering and waiting system which is a bit odd.  Nonetheless, I love this place.  Their pho is good and so is this pork salad that comes with it when you order their lunch special.  And the best of all, lots of cute girls are eating here :D  And an awesome place to people watch ;)I recommend this place if you are working nearby or want to get a quick bite to eat while you are in City Hall

This eatery is located behind an escalator -- which is easy to miss. I only found it because I was dying of hunger. The staff was very nice and my food came out pretty quickly. I got fried pork and shrimp spring rolls and chicken wings. Not too shabby.

Located in the basement of Wheelock Place, right where the Paterson Link begins, it's understandable why Nam Nam gets a lot of foot traffic. My husband and I always see a good amount of patrons at this joint, so naturally our interest was piqued.My husband ordered the beef pho. I thought the broth was on point. However, we didn't like how they included the chili in the bowl. We would have rather had it on the side, so we could adjust the spiciness to our liking. Also, they didn't serve what we felt are the traditional garnishes: bean sprouts, basil, and lime. (Well, it did have lime, but only a small wedge was thrown in.)Next up was my banh mi. I ordered the first option, which is the 5 spice pork belly. At $5.90, it seems reasonably priced, as banh mi should be. However, the moment it was served to me, I had immediate buyer's remorse. The bread was way too thick. If you were serving me an Italian hero, it would've been perfect; but for banh mi, it's unacceptable. Second, the filling was very weak, with only 1 layer of meat and a paltry serving of pickled veggies and cilantro. The taste was there, but it was overpowered by the huge chunk of carbs in my mouth. Then, they had the nerve to charge us $1.60 each for small bottles of water, which are about the size of the Maggi seasoning bottle that they have on each table. To top it all off, their coffee machine wasn't working, so Vietnamese coffee was out of the question. And this is on a Sunday evening!This place had so much fail, I couldn't handle it. Next!

That's what happens to a decent chain having done well and expanded greedily ..... my last visit was a year ago and I was startled to witness how badly the food quality had deteriorated. The pho was hard and dry (either undercooked or raw material went out of control), beef slices and beef balls definitely over-cooked (being hard and dry). The broth was overly peppery.  Really do not know what had happened this evening. We were seated right next to the food service counter .... and horrified to see cleared dirty plates placed right next to cooked food which were awaiting delivery to the tables - all on the same counter top and next to each other!!!! A used dirty napkin that was atop a cleared plate flapped over a plate of fresh rice rolls that was awaiting delivery - and the service staff just removed the dirty napkin and matter-of-factly brought the tainted rolls out to the customer for consumption!!! Help!!!

Oh Nam Nam. Why you put so much bread and so little inside meat and greens in your Banh mi. subway gives more toppings that you do, la. :DIf you look at Nam Nam's Banh Mi, 70-80% of the circumference of the Banh Mi is bread! Talk about cheap servings.The Pho. Well the pho is put in a bowl so small, it might as well come from a kids menu. Pho served in a huge white bowl!  the beef is good, but again the portion is small...Very disappointing, indeed...

These guys serve acceptable, occasionally even good and tasty food. But the Banh Mi's are mostly just bread - larger than life buns with measly little bits of filling. So the possibly nice flavors are lost. Try Viet Baguette - generous portions and better taste -  and you will never think of coming back here.  And some taste hidden in little morsels is no recompense for their idiocy - "we don't serve water! Haha." Wake up - chasing away customers with your inanities and soon there will be another Name Name in the history book of closed restaurants. Hospitality business!! Haha.

Okay, I'm Vietnamese so my review is very valid ;)Damn shiok.My boyfriend told me not to bother trying Vietnamese cuisine in SG because they're crappy and nothing back in the states, until Nam Nam popped up.  I was so surprise how yummy the PHO and BANH MI were. So for those reviews that say it's not authentic pho, what do they know? None of them are Vietnamese.  Chef is Vietnamese for one and we all know how much Vietnamese just LOVE cooking their food with MSG  (yes downside).  Well, since their pho is yum, I'll let it fly.  For drinks, skip the Vietnamese coffee, it's too watered down.  Get the coconut juice instead.  So yum!

After many failed attempts at eating here and turning away at the size of the queue, the moll and I headed in on a Sunday mid-afternoon. There was no queue and we get a table under the stairs. Spacious it's not, but we were not expecting acres of space and besides we were there for the food. We ordered pho bo, spicy chicken salad and the chicken and chicken pate banh mi. All of this washed down with hot vietnamese coffee with the sweetened condensed milk and two kinds of Vietnamese beer. The verdict?  Food was wonderful. Pho Bo had all of the right flavors although customizing with five different types of sauce on the table is easily done. The spicy chicken salad was great with just the right amount of spiciness and crunch in the salad. After tasting the delights of banh mi in Hanoi we waited to try it with some trepidation. We should not have worried. The bread was so crusty on the outside and melt away goodness on the inside that we could have eaten it on its own and enjoyed it. The chicken and chicken pate filling just added to the taste. The beers were good, the coffee strong and flavorful and it's a place we will return to again. Great value compared to comparable pricy Vietnamese restaurants and much better tasting than most. Thoroughly recommended.

Overall, I appreciate the setup of having customers put in their own orders, followed by table service, and I thought the atmosphere was pretty casual and light without being cheap. However, I wasn't a big fan of the pho or the bahn mi. I think the the restaurant just adds ingredients in proportions that are not appealing to my palette.The pho (I had the beef steak slices pho) looked to be about 60% noodles (which were a bit overcooked and mushy), 25% broth, 10% meat and 5% herbs; I prefer less noodles, and more meat and herbs. Additionally, the beef slices were not cooked-- which is a good thing (as the hot broth is supposed to do that for you), but they tasted too tough after they were only put into the broth for a minute. And the broth was sort of sweetish and sour-- vs. savory and brothy, which is my preference. Oh, and I also didn't like the fact that they automatically added chili slices to the soup (I'm not a chili fan and had to pull out each individual slice myself); I much prefer Vietnamese restaurants where you can customize your own intake of herbs.I liked the bahn mi more than the pho (I had the caramelized 5-spice pork belly and pate bahn mi), but once again, the proportions were off. The pork belly was tender and succulent, but all I could barely make out the pate and all I really tasted was the bread-- which was sort of fluffy and airy. And once again, they had chili in it, which I had to take out (although in this case, it probably would have dulled the bread taste somewhat).All of this said, there don't seem to be many good, affordable Vietnamese restaurants in Singapore-- so this is one of the better ones, but definitely not somewhere I'd frequent.
If you love great flavours, you'd love the pho here. It's vibrant & exciting! Prices are reasonable as well. Definitely one of my favourite places to eat in Singapore.

Aussie Roll is absolutely fantastic! They have cheap sushi rolls of a huge variety of flavours - beats the other big sushi chains around the area hands down! They have fillings such as teriyaki chicken, bulgolgi beef, soft shell crab, and also the traditional tuna, salmon and vegetarian options.  As everything is prepared already, the line although quite long at lunch time moves very quickly, and you can either eat the entire roll as it is, or have the servers cut it up into smaller pieces for you. Also love how they leave the packets of soy sauce and wasabi outside for you to help yourself, so you don't have to keep going back to the counter to ask for more, and also give you a packet of tissues with your purchase. Very classy. I always forget to bring a packet of tissues with me when I'm out for lunch so it comes in very handy indeed!Also, they have a buy 2 get 1 free promotion every day after 6.30 or 7pm (can't remember exactly) - but it's a great deal so if you are still around raffles place at that time, drop by to pick them up!

I found my favorite rolls to order:- salmon avocado for the typical sushi- spicy soy chicken for the incredible slightly spicy and a tad sweet sauce. The chicken could be more tender but the sauce helps to make any hard bits palatable. Rolls which I want to try but have not- seaweed salad- garlic king prawns- calamariI like how this place runs like clockwork. The line may be long but it moves very quickly, so don't be put off by that. I usually get it to go as the place is too small for dining in, plus the tables are usually taken.While waiting in line, stare at the big poster board on the wall to think of what to order. Once you get to the display cases, you will need to tell them what you want. A bit hard to try looking at the actual rolls at the two display cases and then tell them as you do not want to hold up the lunch crowd line. Tell them how many rolls you are getting first so they can get the correct size box for you. And say yes when asked if you want them cut (sliced) unless you like to hold it in your fist and eat it like a wrap.

Sushi by the roll. The menu consists out of more than 20 different sushi roll combinations, mixes of vegi, meat or fish. Prices range between 2,6 till 3S$ and each roll is cut into 4 pieces. The sushi is really fresh and in the evening after 6pm it is happy hour: buy 2, get 1 free. It is a great place for fresh and tasty sushi, but you only find the classic maki, no other types are served here.

I think this place has a great concept, but compared to Maki-San at Dhoby Ghaut, Aussie Roll falls short.The Good:- Each roll is around $2.40-$2.80 so relatively cheap. Plus, after 6:00 PM they do a buy 2 get one free deal. Perfect for those after workout quick fix.- The rolls can be cut into four slices or eaten like a handroll.- Unlimited supply of wasabi, soy sauce, and utensils. There's also a sink for you to wash your hands! Ginger and mayo do cost extra though.The Bad:- There's no alternative healthy options, ie brown rice. If you're a health nut, then I think you'll be limited to very few options.- The queue can be relatively long during lunch hours.A great, cost-effective option for fake sushi lovers like myself!

I'm pretty divided on Aussie Roll. The concept is great in theory, but it fell short on the quality-to-value scale. Aussie Roll basically caters to the average, rushed office employee who needs a quick lunch that's fuss free, inexpensive and portable. For those who don't like raw food, would like more protein and dislike vegetables, the cooked meat rolls *look* delicious and helpings are generous compared to say SSB, your average supermarket sushi roll or the mass market restaurant chains. It's relatively cheap too. So basically these are tummy fillers for the rushed.What I didn't like about the food was  that there wasn't much effort put into the flavors and it felt like I was eating a soulless, mass produced roll. If you've had some of the fast fusion food coming out the food truck scene in the U.S (mind you, I dislike making cross country comparisons but this felt especially relevant) for example, a bulgogi sub or taco cone can still taste excellent if you had each of the ingredients on it's own. That wasn't the case here with the rolls as a whole or with the ingredients pieced apart, which is what I ended up doing when I realized it was going to be a chore to finish my lunch.I had the beef bulgogi, teriyaki chicken, spicy prawn and salmon avocado. First thing that hit me was the rice was pretty bland, coarse and slap dashed together. Even for a supermarket sushi type chain, this seemed like a big flaw to me because 50% of sushi is the rice and you're serving it to Asians. The meats weren't great either - the beef bulgogi was tough and crumbly, that and the teriyaki chicken was too salty. The seaweed, was you guessed it, soft and rather tasteless.To save the day though, the aunties manning the counter were really funny when I asked them for recommendations. I can't reproduce our politically incorrect conversation but they were hilarious. Bottom line, Aussie Roll probably works for some and will last awhile because it serves the perfect market in Raffles Place.

Craving quick takeaway sushi you can eat at your desk? Bored of staring at sushi conveyor belts? Get a quick fix at Aussie Roll,  right in the heart of CBD. This review is going to be simple.  Aussie Roll has a great appeal. The queue is long during lunch peak hours but it moves really quickly.  The 3 or 4 service personnel there have a good system going. There's a huge variety of sushi to choose from. Its listed on a wall inside which you can stare at while waiting in line -  another great idea! A few of my select favourite include the king prawn variations and calamari sushi! All really tasty. Choosing a particular 'roll'  of sushi gets you 4 pieces each and my normal meal consists of 2 to 3 rolls on average. By all means have more if you can. Soy sauce and wasabi takeaway sachets are also available just right after you are done paying. Almost production line like,  but if it works it works! Did I mention how affordable it is? At $2.60 to $3.20 for each roll,  you would hardly ever spend more than $12 here. Which is great for that much sushi. They are not stingy either in terms of how packed each roll is. Apparently the rolls go at 2 for 1 after 6pm, so hey,  pop over for dinner too if you are in the area. A much recommended fuss free joint if you want some no frills sushi and if you aren't too particular about sushi in general. This gets my stamp of approval.

I'm kind of in between and 3 and 4 on this - I wish they put more veggies together with the meat, the balance isn't quite there. Also, the sushi rice is really just mashed together rice "paste" almost, kind of what you'd expect from machines/not very good rice. That being said, it's pretty cheap, so I guess I shouldn't complain so much.Good "happy hour" deals! M-F 6pm onwards, buy 2 rolls get 1 free! Woohoo :) Each roll is around $2.60-$2.80, and they cut it into 4 for you if you say yes to cutting.I had:1. Spicy soy chicken - ratio of meat to flavour was not quite there - a bit lacking in flavour given how chunky the meat was! Eaten with the sushi rice, it became a bit bland overall. Good meat though.2. Korean BBQ beef - pretty good! The second piece started tasting a little salty though.. Which made me actually eat the rice to balance it out. Nice that there was a bit of lettuce and some cucumber to add crunch3. Korean spicy pork - I think this was my favourite! At first I liked the beef, then on my second piece (I ate 2 pcs of each roll) that started getting a bit too salty. So this one had the best balance of flavours. Wasn't that spicy to me, but I have pretty high tolerance for spice.They also have your more normal rolls like cream cheese salmon, salmon avocado, seaweed salad (for vegetarians), deep-fried sweet potato, lobster salad (pity there weren't any left!) and all types of breaded seafood (I was trying to steer clear of deep fried stuff).

I'm pretty sure this place changed names to Dusk. Has tapas and other stuff including drinks to enjoy with an epic view. Service is very nice. Tip: get a membership with the faber group for unlimited cable car. Also give you discounts at shops and 20 percent off the bill which should pay for itself. I think going for 20sgd now. May be a promo.

The view is absolutely gorgeous, over viewing the sparkling city of lights, the bay and the lovely island, and it's especially better at night. The decoration is very well done, with LED strips on the stairs, soft lighting in the roof, and a fake candle on each table. The restaurant is flexible to dietary requirements, but not all of them. The restaurant generally isn't too packed, and the atmosphere is great; quiet with good music playing in the background, and the air conditioning helps loads in the hot Singaporean heat. Also located next to the Bell or Happiness (look it up if you don't know what I'm talking about). The food was also pretty good quality for what we ordered. The Chilli Crab, whilst the chilli was mild, was ABSOLUTELY FLIPPING DELICIOUS! The chips were perfectly cooked, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. The beer and wine was good, but the wine glass could be bigger, but the wine is extremely expensive, one tiny glass is worth a whole bottle. The chicken wings were greasy, but otherwise enjoyable. On our night, a group of four were dancing to the music, not sure why, but they were. The service is quick, and efficient, so I was happy about that. I'd definitely recommend this place for a good night out, but be prepped for some expensive items, and some reasonable prices items.

I'm only rating this place 2 stars and not 1 because of the beautiful location and ambience.I ordered the tapas Thai green chicken curry served with rice crackers. I have to say, this has got to be the most awful "curry" I've ever had!The curry was served with minced meat, there was hardly any broth or curry of any sort. There was nothing curry about it, it was SOLID. To add to it, the whole thing was served with dry rice crackers with the overly salty minced meat titled "green curry".Overall, I have to say I'm REALLY disappointed. One of the worst meals ever.

I can be very short on this review. After having walked the entire day, we were warmly welcomed, got a table with an amazing view. The menu was a bit shortened due to holiday period, was there was still enough choice. We took the roasted chicken, which was one of the recommendations on Chope. And boy, they were right. The chicken was so tender, full of flavor and the sides just matched perfectly. Great diner, great views !!

We were there on a Friday night and it seemed like a very family-friendly place - lots of kids running around. Might be better for a (fairly expensive) family outing than a date.Food was pretty good - we had the cod with soba and the pasta with clams in white wine sauce. 3 stars for the quality and maybe a bit more for the large portions! We couldn't finish.Ambience was a 2.5-3 star though - tables and chairs were made from poolside plastic and kind of tacky for the prices and setting. Kind of a confusing place. Maybe I'd go for brunch instead.

We had dessert after walking and taking in the gorgeous views around the park.The restaurant itself has beautiful views as well. Service was nice and efficient.  Our desserts were worth going back for.

Great view!  Starters were good, particularly the potato skins with chilly crab. The salads were also good. However, the linguini and mushrooms wasn't too great. The big issue here was fast service on starters, but exceptionally slow service on salads and pastas.

Maybe it was from all the walking at Mount Faber, our lunch here was fantastic. This restaurant has floor to ceiling windows with excellent view of Sentosa and the islands.Spuds and Aprons serves an international menu but we decided to try the local dishes. Hokkien Noodle, Curry Chicken, and Singapore Laksa were delicious. Will recommend and come back again.

Spuds and Aprons offers fantastic view of the ocean and Sentosa. You can even watch the fireworks at Universal Studio at 8pm from the restaurant. The food is slightly pricier than Faber Bistro, which is opposite, but more variety available. I always order their Foie gras, and their steak is also great. Among the many times when I was there, their dish presentation had never been the same - maybe their creative way of trying not to bore returning customers. Tip: call early to reserve tables that have the best view.

Well had the off chance looking for ozone of my favorite dim sum restaurants I experienced in Taiwan.Was super happy they have multiple locations in Singapore. One was just a short walk from my hotel in China town. Located in the shopping center right near Chinatown MRT station.I placed my order for Steamed pork and vegetable dumplings, a set of 10.A set of 10 pork and shrimp shumai,Wonton pork and shrimp soup.Egg fried rice and jasmine tea.Also had a frozen mango pudding!!The service is as fast as expected. Since the cooks make the dumplings fresh for each order. The waiters bring each part of the order as they come from the kitchen. I'm glad I came on a weekday. Weekends can be a long time waiting for a seat. This chain Resturant is very popular and often has full booking.The price is average for the meal and I don't mind the price for the quality of meal I received.Totally recommend This Resturant for the Dim sum hunter!!!

I really enjoyed their starter salad. It's got bits of tau gwa, vermicelli and seaweed and their special sauce. They also have very nice xiao long bao of course. Soft skins and juicy, tasty pork fillings. In terms of lamian, I enjoyed their chill sauce tossed one. What caught me unaware was their beef brisket lamian soup, my uncle ordered that and I thought I'll just try it. Wow! The beef chunks were so soft and tasty!! The soup broth was also hearty and flavourful! Totally enjoyable!Overall awesome meal!!!

This was my least favorite branch of the famous dumpling chain.  The food was good and consistent with other locations, but the atmosphere and service felt flat.  There's a more robust location in the suntec center.
The steamed pork dumplings oh my god.  Divine.  I probably looked like a idiot shoving them in my mouth.  Also loved the spicy cucumber dish....was very tangy and tasty!

I once naively thought that all Din Tai Fungs were created equal.I now know better. This branch does not have the truffle xiao long bao (which is awesome and you should totally try it if you haven't).It does do everything else as you'd expect of a Din Tai Fung, and admittedly it's less crowded than most of the other branches, but not having one of my staple menu items does mean it's generally just not as good as most Din Tai Fung branches in my eyes.

My go-to comfort spot for xiao long bao. I find this outlet to always have available spots, so there's never any of the dreaded wait as there typically are in other outlets around Singapore (and, actually, around the world if you think about it). Their fried rice is very good too, as are many other of their dishes. While you might be tempted to chomp down an entire 10 piece order of the xiao long bao, do save some space for some of their other dishes. I always find it a bit pricier than Paradise Dynasty, but it's never anything too scandalous (for Singapore, anyways). Also, while you're there, why not enjoy a nice Taiwan Beer?

The Steamed pork dumplings or xiao long baos are really fantastic here. Add some black vinegar + ginger as a condiment and they make a delicious, juicy mouthful.My office-mates either loved or hated it and those that hated it did so mainly because of the price. Their argument is that you can get as good a quality food from the hawker store nearby, and that is true. But for something different Din Tai Fung is a nice option.

I am not really a fan of Xiao long bao. but sister's bf is picky on food... a plate of duck spring roll is expensive... I can get a plate of duck for the same price but I get duck. Din Tai Fung only give me 6 tiny slice of duck.

I've taken a lot of my friends here and am extremely fond of this place. For 8.50 SGD a plate for the Chicken Biryani & 9 SGD a plate for the Mutton Biryani, is a steal for the generous quantity that is served!Most importantly, the Biryani that is served here is of truly excellent quality albeit the taste can be a tad bit inconsistent at times. Sometimes the rice feels powdery & a bit dry but that was probably because of the weather. The key to a great Biryani is that the meat & rice needs to be slow cooked in traditional spices for it to be at it's juiciest best. That is exactly how the owner approaches this complicated & subtle dish.This is as authentic as it gets & it's NOT that brown goop they serve with yellow rice at most places which even the owner at Bismillah agrees is an abomination! Biryani was the dish of Mughal emperors & soldiers & signified feasting in a royal manner. It was considered a complete meal in itself & it is with that respect for tradition & flavour that the owner/chef Arif bhai cooks it. It is his love for crafting this complex dish that adds to the old school charm of this place in addition to the brilliant food. Try chatting up with the owner if you visit the next time, he's a wonderful gent with a well informed viewpoint on food & life...& throbbing passion for what he does.

Still weary from our flight the night before we tracked this place down because of "The Layover" and you know what?It was damn good.Our first proper meal in Singapore did not let us down, thanks Anthony B. (I wonder if you have a secret Yelp account?)Anyways...A Lamb Biryani with a Mango Lassi on the side and I was in heaven. Perfectly floral and fragrant and slightly spicy to my Canadian tongue. It was exactly what I needed to get going.I had been to Little India 6 years before and vividly recalled the smells and colours that slapped me across the face on my own 5 hour Layover. What a gem. Once again you did not disappoint!Someday I'm gonna have to go to Big India though.

No idea why this place can even be ranked above a 2.  Soggy rice.  Mutton is ok.  One side diluted white sauce no clue what that is.  Had lime juice that taste more like plum juice.  Horrible.  For those that give this place above a 2, i dare you to try Ali Nachia Briyani Dam and rework your review :).

Probably one of the best biryanis in little india....if you go at the right time. The ambience and look of the place is not the classiest for sure. In fact it looks slightly run down and you might have questions about the hygiene levels of this place. However no doubt, this biryani, both chicken and lamb are pretty solid. There's a trick to this though. You need to go at a certain time, which changes on a daily basis and can be luck oriented....it's when you get the scoop of the biryani that takes in the most amount of the masala that you enjoy this biryani in it's peak form. I recommend 330 - 4 pm for an afternoon biryani

Quick stop here to try the chicken biryani. I had never had it before and it was ok, I can't really compare it to much else. I guess I expected a different taste? I can imagine finding better versions in this enormous city though. I was a little star struck by the owner, regardless. Also it was a gigantic portion so three of us split one and tried the lime juice and mango lassi as well.

Bismillah has been heralded by some food bloggers to be the 'best biryani'. It certainly is one of the contenders for "one of the better biryanis in Singapore" but it isn't the best.Many of the biryanis we would be used to here would be the southern kinds. Bismillah is different, serving a very northern style of biryani (and even then not quite a Lucknowi biryani... they're Pakistani). It's decent and it will fill you up, but I wouldn't say it was superb.

Having eaten the gold standard Indian biryani from Hyderabad, my food snob radar was on high alert while trying this place. I have to say that the radar stayed silent throughout the meal. The biryani was very good - by far the best I have had in Singapore. It was cooked in the Pakistani/North Indian style, and packed a solid punch of flavor, grease and meat. Would go down really well with an ice cold beer.Before I forget, the mutton biryani has a clear edge over the chicken version.
Yes the place is dark, dinghy, and on a crowded alley - but I came there for the food. Great dum biryani - doesn't matter chicken or mutton. The boiled egg inside was definitely a +.

Famous / Michelin recommended biryani restaurant. The biryani here is rich in flavor / full of spices. The chicken is soft and tender. The portion is big though they give way too much rice compared to chicken. Would prefer if the ratio is more balance.Very authentic according to my Indian friends.

Delicious, flavoursome Biryani. Its pretty expensive for this dish - $20 each for a Biryani plus a drink - but you get what you pay for. The Lamb Biryani was succulent and rich, and the Lamb Chops excellent. Desserts were pretty good too - worth trying! Service was fast.

It's all about the mutton soup and the kulfi here. And if you get biryani, get the mutton one. The chicken can be very hit or miss, and mine came out quite dry while some of the others had chicken that was more moist. Sometimes the biryani will come in a neatly packed dome shape, and other times it'll come a bit disheveled and shoved in front of your face. All up to your luck and their mood I guess.Don't expect much in the way of service here. It's pretty low-maintenance. You have to call over the waitstaff pretty insistently for anyone to come and help or serve you. Kulfi is a really interesting indian ice cream that's not too commonly found in Singapore. It's simply ice cream with some spices/pistachios in a little plastic cup. You have to rub it in between your palms to get the popsicle out. The ice cream also has various spices and pistachios sprinkled in it. Quite simple, but also quite comforting and refreshing; a great way to end the meal.

This place is all hype. Food : 6/10, I got the baby goat biryani. I've had better for cheaper. The white sauce on the side was watery. The meat itself was tender and tasty. The rice felt old. Service: 1/10, I felt pretty unwelcome honestly, like it was a burden for me to show up for lunch. Was not handed a menu, offered a drink, or asked how I thought the food was. Fuck that grumpy old man. Price: 2/10, rip off. This guy is still riding the "Bourdain visit" train. And I fell for it. Ambiance : 2/10- the place is dirty and gross. I should have just walked out and tried some place else but that thought of "if Anthony Bourdain liked it..." Kept creeping back in my head. Avoid this place, trust me. You're not missing anything. I regret wasting a space in my stomach and money  from my wallet on this place.

Came here about 8pm on a weekday night, to grab takeaway of mutton briyani. I would not recommend eating in as it can get pretty hot, and the fans within don't do very much.Mutton briyani, $15 - worth it?The style of the briyani is the dry kind, with the mutton cooked within the rice, and some raita is provided. The rice is well-spiced, spicy, aromatic, but can be slightly mushy in some parts from meat juice, and for $15, there was sufficient meat within, and not too much bone. Meat is tender and comes apart easily. I am just unsure if it is worth the $15 price tag. I'll return if I happen to walk past.

The decor makes it feel like a construction site canteen,there's usually a queue,you won't be greeted nicely (if at all),if you get served, someone has just done you a favor.The whole place is as auhentic as it gets, and it serves what is undoubtedly the best briyani in Singapore. (To qualify this, I'm a North Indian)The flavor (like the ambiance) is authentic, the meat (lamb & chicken) is very tender.Skip the raita (watery yoghurt accompaniment)I'd recommend you SMS a pre-order for take-away/pick-up.

Coming from the US, I have been pretty disappointed with the typical dum biryani found commonly here in Singapore. This place, however, has the best biryani I've ever had hands down, let alone in Singapore. Both the chicken and goat biryani were delicious. The rice and meats were fresh, moist, and flavorful.The place itself is pretty run down (and not in a charming way) and the service is mediocre, but who cares when the biryani is this good!
Overrated on many blogs, but reviews here are generally accurate. Average food, not a great place for a meal. Skip it.

I agree with Sean B. It's all hype. I've had better biriyani for cheaper. The rice was half cooked & the sauce was watery. Don't expect any customer service cause you ain't gonna get any. Moreover they make you feel like they are doing you a favor. Food quality : 5/10Customer Service: 1/10Overpriced: hell yes

The place doesn't look so hot - the shophouse is a bit rundown. But the dum briyani is the bomb. The rice is fluffy, aromatic from the spices and entirely greaseless because the owner cooks with safflower oil rather than ghee. Happy me cos then I can down the whole plate without feeling like I swallowed a rock but carbo-phobic eaters might wanna avoid this place cos like all briyani places they're generous with the rice. The chicken is tender and fall off the bone.But what the aficionados go for is the mutton and kid goat briyani. The latter is only available on certain days but the portion of meat is super generous for $15. I'm scared of gamey meat, but my foodie friends swear by the mutton and kid goat, so next time I shall drag them along and pinch some off of them to try.The lassi is fabulous - rich and creamy, and not sweetened to tooth aching levels. I'd advise going early cos when we went at noon place was full and a queue was already forming. And the owner said forget it during fasting month cos the queue starts at 5.30am which is when he starts cooking the briyani!

Ma Ma Mia!Tonkatsu by Ma Maison has been one our favourite, if not favourite restaurant for Tonkatsu. Naturally, the star of a Tonkatsu restaurant should be.... Well the Tonkatsu but as important and glorious as that piece of beautifully fried pork should be, I personally feel that the side dishes that comes with it plays a very big part too. There's no use having a great piece of protein, only for it to be ruined by a lousy bowl of rice or a soggy salad. Thankfully, that's the part Tonkatsu by Ma Maison gets perfectly right.There are a few option of meat to chose from here but after trying a few, I would highly recommend getting the Rosu (Pork Loin).Jumbo Rosu Katsu Set ($29.80)This is for the ultimate meat eater. 250g on perfectly fried, juicy pork loin served with rice, soup and free flow salad. First, the loin. A perfect balance of fat, ensuring that every night is a good one. Mix it the perfect crispiness of the breading and the Rosu Katsu in the fantastic Tonkatsu. It's seasoned beautifully, perfectly fried and juicy with every bite. Perfect! The salad that comes with it is perfect as well. It may only be cabbage, but the freshness, crispness and sweetness of the cabbage helps cut down the oil in the Tonkatsu, making it easier to finish. The soup that comes with it is perfect as well. These aren't simple bowls of pre-mixed miso soup as well. Made with carrots, Radish (daikon) and pieces of pork, these little bowl of soups are stars of their own, helping ensure the sweetness of the cabbage and its sesame sauce, doesn't over power the pork loin, allowing its umami-ness to shine through. To ensure that we don't over eat or overload ourselves, we tend to order a Jumbo Ruso set with an additional rice set ($4.00) to share, which is more than enough for us. Overall, we really love the restaurant and really can't find any fault with it. Simply love the Tonkatsu here and still our go to place whenever we have the craving for it!

For a weekday night, the place packed fairly quickly. The menu consisted of deep fried meat and seafood. Most of items in the menu was in set, which served with rice (choice of white or jyukkokumai (multi grain rice)), tonjiru soup ( miso soup with pork), cabbage and pickles and all were refillable. Each meal was accompanied with roasted barley tea, started with a small dish of grated radish and ended the meal with a bowl of plain looking jelly.There was goma (sesame) dressing and soyu on the table to add to the shredded cabbage. For the deep fried items, there was sweet and spicy Tonkatsu sauces to dip with. Want add kick, add some freshly grated sesame seeds.Mille Feuille Truffle Katsu (S$33.80++)Truffle chips, Top quality truffle salt, Special truffle pasteOne could smell the truffle when it was served. As the meat were thinly sliced and layered on top of each other, the patty was tender and soft.Cheese Mille-feuille KATSU Set ($26.80++)Deep-fried Multi Layered Sliced Pork Cutlet with CheeseSimilar to the truffle version, the meat was tender and soft. The melted cheese really stretched and very long too.IBERICO PORK Rosu (Pork Loin) Set ($34.80++)The most disappointing dish out of the 4 ordered items. The meat was quite tough and dry. One could not if there was any different from the usual pork loin. A waste of money for this dish.Katsu Don ($21.80++)Deep fried pork loin topped with egg and special soy sauce Although it was the cheapest among the 4 dishes which we ordered, it tasted not bad.As the place was packed, one had to wait for the bill. There was some error with the bill but it was swiftly corrected.

Regretted ordering the oyakodon with pork katsu the moment it arrived. Covered by both egg and sauce, the crisp outer layer quickly became disappointingly soggy. The meat within was nothing special either and wasn't as tender as expected. The dry one that came with rice on the side fared much better. The crispy katsu tasted pleasantly mild, without the all-too-familiar stench of reused oil. However, it's definitely not worth the price at ~$25-35 per set. Service was impeccable. The waiter checked in on us regularly, ensuring that we had no shortage of rice and cabbage. Also, I quite like the DIY aspect of it all where sauce is poured at our discretion onto the little platter with demarcated wells.

One of the most expensive pieces of fried meat I've eaten. Can't say I'd eat here often or even come back again, but I felt pretty satisfied after polishing off my set meal. The restaurant was half empty(full) when we walked in around at almost 9pm on a Friday evening. They had a "MisoKatsu Fair" special at the time: sizzling negi miso rosu katsu set (pork loin with negi miso sauce and egg) for ~S$24++. Pork fillet went for a dollar more. FYI pork fillet is also known as tenderloin and is the leanest of all cuts, so it's a healthier choice. My friend got the pork fillet, and it was less flavorful in my opinion. The chefs cook the meat in a open kitchen right in front of the bar, so you can see the marbling of the meat before they fry it up. To be honest, I expected the pork to be cooked with a bit more skill or technique. Although the meat was very high quality, the end result was just like another fried piece of meat. The sizzling platter was a nice touch as it kept the food warm, but it wasn't a testament to the cooking. The side dishes were nice, but nothing spectacular or unique.After adding on a chocolate cake dessert (just for good measure), the damage came up to about S$35. Glad I tried it, but not willing to pay this much again for some fried pork cutlet.

Tried this place for the second time, when I come to Singapore for business trips I normally stop nearby so it's within walking distance. The place is nice, good sevice and quite similar to a Tonkatsu-ya in Japan, food is not exactly cheap.I loved the miso, tsukemono, brown rice choice and all the sauces. Shame for the main thing, which is the tonkatsu, it wasn't all that great, quite dry despite me ordering the Kurobuta Hire which is meant to be the best pork that they have on offer.ALl in all I have had better, but it's a decent option if you are in the area and really want to eat Tonkatsu.

This has always been one of my staple Tonkatsu restaurants despite its higher than average price tag. The quality is decent for the katsu itself but recently when I returned its tonjiru that's always served in the teishoku was weak and flavorless. The tea jelly dessert too was pretty awful. I'd return just for the katsu and the delicious rice!

2 stars - this place isn't the best for tonkatsu, but if you're at the mandarin gallery and are craving it, then don't hesitate. They give you a scoop of rice, japanese cabbage salad both with unlimited serving and a small bowl of miso soup. I get that they serve many types of pork but the quality just isn't there. I have had much better tonkatsu elsewhere. I was really disappointed with my dish. Since you can't go wrong with rice and cabbage, my grief is with the other items on the plate. I had the mangalica rosu katsu and guess what, the meat was stale, not crispy, not tasty, and jerky. Other people who think this place has the best tonkatsu either they haven't had real good ones or I was just unlucky to be facing a gruesome experience here. It's really a nightmare for me. The cashier was nice though. On the side note, you may want to put the sauce on the side, because your tonkatsu might get soggy by the end.

This tonkatsu is to die for!!! I loved it. Well, I also haven't been to Tonkichi in a really long time and that used to be my go-to place for gd tonkatsu, but my bro said this place won over Tonkichi when he went on a tonkatsu hunt with his gf. Anyway, I don't like very fatty cuts of meat, so I went for hire-katsu and it was deliciously juicy! As other reviewers have mentioned, the tonkatsu tasted really light and not soaked in oil as is typical of not-so-good places. It was amazing and made me very happy. I got the 120g portion, which actually didn't look like very much but was pretty filling. $22.80++The tonjiru soup, pickles, and cabbage are all free flow. Soup was delicious! And had a ton of ingredients.. Very comforting and brothy and hearty. Cabbage dressing was also very good, went well with cabbage. OH, big plus for being able to get brown rice! I LOVE brown rice. and at no extra charge. Makes me even happier :)Only thing is that I like Tonkichi's actual sesame seed grinder (sort of like mortar and pestle) as opposed to Ma Maison's plastic container thing that effectively does the same thing. Oh! But Ma Maison had both spicy and sweet tonkatsu sauce, never had the spicy one before. Pretty interesting. Liked both of them!Orange jelly that came after the meal was really strange and artificial tasting though, skip that.. Service was okay, took a while to get anyone's attention, I suppose things were getting busy on a Thursday night. It took a while for them to give us warm water and I had to keep asking for more though.

A long time ago, I had a really good dinner here with a friend and remembered it for a year and a half whilst away from Singapore. When my craving for katsudon hit me last week, I made the rare special trip to orchard on a weekday to have some katsudon and was sorely disappointed. I'll cut to the chase. The service was appalling. I understand being rushed and busy. I was perfectly happy to wait. However, I do not appreciate being shooed out of the restaurant and made to feel like it was my fault while the manager, I think, scolded the waitress for almost sitting us before another couple that we (and apparently the waitress) hadn't realised was waiting. Embarrassed, we walked out and endured the glares from that couple although all we had done was said 'table for two?' When we were seated, the appetiser came in a very rushed rambling of the description as though he didn't have time for us or this at all. We then proceeded to wait eons for the food until, after realising we kept looking over, the manager finally came over and said 'There's some quality issues with the white rice. We are cooking a new batch now. I think you should change to the brown rice.' When told that 'no, we would prefer to wait for the white rice, thanks', he kept trying to convince us to change our minds before, defeated, he went to the kitchen to check how long it would take. Incredibly, two seconds later, we were told that they weren't sure the second batch wouldn't have the same quality issue (in the white rice? Really?) and we should take the brown rice. 'Should' was being used in a 'you should take it or you have no rice' sort of way. At this, we had no choice but to agree to the brown rice. At this point, I'd like to say that I have nothing against brown rice, but my partner really did not want brown rice and was willing to wait for the white rice anyway.The katsudon did arrive with very little rice drowned in the sauce. It definitely wasn't a good katsudon sauce either and the lack of rice made for a too salty too sweet katsudon. Perhaps they were running out of brown rice, seeing as there isn't any white rice apparently. There wasn't an apology though he did appear at the end of the meal and asked 'did you like the food'. We just smiled, as we didn't want to deal with him anymore, but it was an awfully disappointing experience. In fact, I was still thinking about that satisfying katsudon I never had the next day, and went to Ginza bairin for dinner promptly. I wouldn't recommend people not to go for the tonkatsu, but just a word of caution about the service. Also, I've heard the service at the Bugis branch is much better anyway. For that price and quality though, I'd just go for the cheaper Ginza Bairin's chicken katsudon set. It's much much more gratifying.

I came here because Ippudo had a que but I did hear that this place has some of the best tonkatsu in Singapore and I would have to fully agree. Ok, take this as you will, I'm from nyc and obviously not from Japan, so my opinion might be a bit skewed, but still very much honest. I have had tonkatsu many times in nyc/nj but at ma maison, it was the best I've ever had. The service was great, super friendly and very helpful. It's hard to find good service like that here so it was really refreshing to see that again since I left America. The miso beer and sweet potato sochu...awesome! My boyfriend ordered the black pig tonkatsu and he wasn't impressed. The meat was tough, and I'm not sure if its because it might have been a little overlooked or maybe that's just how the texture is naturally. I actually enjoyed his dish. Yes, it was a bit tough and chewy, but it was still juicy and flavorful. I had the tonkatsu fillet and, again, the bomb! That dark sauce is salty and flavorful, plus the nice shredded PILE of cabbage. The sticky brown rice was also fantastic. It was nutty and hearty, just awesome. I want to find out how to make that, because I can get used to that kind of brown rice! Not cheap though. 2 drinks and 2 meals was $100. Thank god the food was good.

Sometimes when I go to a place like this I am afraid that I want to give them five stars only to justify how much I spent, so I don't feel like a sucker. This meal was excellent, probably the best tonkatsu I have had in Singapore. I am not sure if it was worth $80 for two people with no drinks. The condiments are amazing and the service is great. I am just not sure it is worth spending 2.5 times more than Romankan Yokohama to go here. The black pork tenderloin is really big and satisfying.

This place serves pork cutlets that are crispy on the outside yet very juicy on the inside. I never hesitate to pay a little more to get the Hungary Mangalica Rosu Katsu set at $31.80. The meat is more tender than the other options which are sometimes too dry due to the lean cut.I love the free-flow cabbage as I can gluttonly feast on my favourite sesame dressing that they provide on every table. It also helps me to feel less guilty to eat more vege to balance out my sinful meat.They also serve tea-jelly at the end of your meal. I always enjoy this humble looking jelly as it washes your pallete after the feast.Tonkatsu is a very popular dinner spot. Be prepared to queue at least 45 minutes if you are going at 7pm.

So we were there for an early dinner, and it was a toss up between Tonkatsu and Ippudo. Having never patronised T before, it was a clear winner on the freshness list, and we were warmly greeted by chirpy servers. We were quickly served balls of chilled, grated radish and a detailed look through the menu saw us ordering up Mameton, their self proclaimed bestseller, an Iberico pork set, and an Ebikatsu set. All orders come with a side of rice (plain or multi grain), pickles and soup.Taste wise: wow. It's a clear difference between pedestrian pork, dished out in the Mameton set, and Iberican pork. The breaded crust (panko?) was delightful to bite into, and not cloyingly oily as katsus are wont to be. The Iberico was well marbled, I.e. fatty, which provided a juicy burst or meaty goodness with each bite. It's not to say that the regular version was shoddy, but it just paled so much in comparison when side by side with the Spanish cut. The ebikatsu wasn't too bad, though strangely I adored the side of finely shredded cabbage. Icy cold, the servers would come around offering extra servings of fibre, which went very well when liberally doused with the accompanying sesame dressing. In addition, the meals come with roasted tea and a small cube of jelly as dessert. The flavours seem to vary daily, and ours was peach - cold, clean tasting, and not overly sweet. Price wise, three sets came up to shy of $100, though it also has to do with going for the premium pork. I do enjoy the service though, we're hard pressed to find sincere and friendly waitstaff around here. And the fact that it consists of cute Japanese blokes makes it so much more of a rarity!

The good:  Unlimited rice, cabbage and oh man the condiments.  By the end of the meal my food companion had to stop me from dipping my finger into the sweet, sweet sauce.  I guess my table manners go out the door when it comes to succulent sauce.  Next time I'm bringing a zip lock bag and bringing some home, no joke.  Also worth noting is the breading; light, fluffy and full or flavor.      The bad:  Lots of inconsistencies all around.  The temperature rivaled Antarctica and as a result we shifted not once, not twice but three times until we finally found a spot where we could feel our toes and fingers.  Service was spotty, sometimes we got what we asked and sometimes not.  I'm guessing they were as confused as their logo which is (and I'm not making this up) a pig serving pork.  Speaking of pork, I ordered the one from Hungary and although it's supposed to be fattier than the rest,  it was 40% fat.  I lost almost half of my meal to chewy, inedible swine bits.The ugly:  Given the options, price and location, this is probably as good as it gets in Singapore.  I feel with a little quality control and management direction this spot could skyrocket to the real deal, but it probably wont.  Why?  It doesn't need to, it's the best in Singapore...for now.

My favorite katsu place in Singapore. Although on the pricey side, their pork katsu are always juicy and tasty. Warning though, I brought some senior citizens here once and they complained of too much 'chewing' lol. Their pork katsu are always perfect to me though. I especially love their giant prawn katsu, it's the size of an adult's arm but the meat is still sweet and tender! I also love their miso soup which comes full of yummy veggies and fried tofu skin.

I dream of crispy panko fried porky goodness!One would never guessed that you can open a restaurant with a menu based on Katsu pork. These guys offer fillet and loin cuts from you basic pork, black pork (more fatty tasty), and pork from Hungary (even more fatty goodness). Sized from 180g to 250g. Go with friends and try the different cuts.Comes with free refills of brown or white rice, Soup, and cabbage.

Tried this place for the first time. The daily set lunch was pork stuffed with filling that included roe. My lunch partner had the ebi-tonkatsu. I must say that we both enjoyed the meal and that it definitely met expectations. The portions were good and service was efficient. I would recommend this restaurant and would certainly return again.

Like a lot others, I was pretty skeptical to pay 3x higher than normal price for pork katsu. But considering it's inside the Mandarin gallery, the thought of overspending during vacation, and words from friend that actually have tried it, I decided to go - and boy, I'm happy that I did! Had a tough time deciding between the Hungarian or black pig rosu katsu, but I finally chose the Hungarian after seeing how fat the pig is in the in-store brochure. The set comes with soup, radish (which said to negate the negative effect of fried food such as katsu), bowl of rice, plenty of cabbage, and jelly for dessert. The meat is tender with the right amount of fat just I like it, the batter is crispy. I just used the sauce provided in the table, but you can ordered few special sauces for extra $. You can sit at the bar if you wanna see the cook prepared the meal for you. If you don't like pork, it also serves few seafood katsu options.

wow rocket, how you have grown!(你长大了！）come october you will be 10 years old and i think it's time i chipped in with this review.your transformation is now complete after getting a much deserved, gorgeous facelift last year.i really like how you have matured, like a good wine.from willin's days as a lawyer home chef for hire, to him taking that plunge to ditch the legal fraternity with only a passion for the chef apprentice's apron and then learning the way of the  kitchen on the job before striking out with a modern singaporean creativity as inspiration.his gregarious personality and boundless creativity made him a hit from the start, albeit not with me.don't get me wrong, his food was good but in his early days i felt it lacked that polished finish which always led me to think i can also do that leh.nonetheless, he became a cult figure almost instantly.i thought he was but a pricey fad but boy has history proven me wrong.i think willin and his team kept on learning, innovating and did not stay put in their comfort food zone.sure people still ask for that laksa pesto dish and i'm sure he will still whip one up for you, but his repertoire has grown many folds.there is also now a sophistication much like how your pony tailed girl will one day be adorned with foundation, blusher, mascara and lipstick.and of course, it's beyond just mere cosmetic changes.the blossoming comes from within, how she carries herself oozing with confidence, speaking with maturity and a dad-i'm-not-a-little-girl-anymore look!that is when you know, for sure, she has arrived.and all of that shows through his current omakase offerings.every dish left me eagerly anticipating the next and lifted, slowly but surely, the ratings to a solid five!willin has been a celebrity chef for years now.he does not need any affirmation, least so from me.but after a delectable dining experience here last night, i knew i had to finally put in my two cents worth.yes, i got out of bed at 4.45am just to penned this.yes, i think wild rocket will wow you too!

The place was packed for lunch during Saturday. I decided on the omakase lunch which was consisted of 7 courses (S$97++). My only request was the dessert not to be the restaurant's signature Wild Rocket Chendol which I just had a couple of weeks ago. Ice water was served after placing order.Course 1 : Bah Chor MeeNegitoro (minced fatty tuna) topped with chopped spring onion and chilli padi, crispy lards, fried shallots, on top of a bed of warm glass noodles.Course 2 : Thai Pomelo SaladServed with tiger prawns & frozen coconut dressingThe dressing was like a scoop of ice cream and made of coconut, chilli, fish oil, and shallot. It tasted quite lemak. Having it with mint leaf, pomelo, and cilantro, it tasted quite refreshing with hint of spicy and sweetness of fruit. Course 3 : Chilli CrabCrab cake made of blue crab and spanner crab, served with chilli crab sauce.The crab cake was packed with nothing but crab meat. Quite juicy and yummy on its own.Course 4 : Hokkien MeeFresh pasta cooked with prawn stock, and hae ko (black shrimp paste). It was quite flavourful but a bit too salty for me.Course 5 : Wild Rocket Strawberry CheesecakeIt served deconstructed style in a Martini glass. Creamy without too sweet or sour.I was surprised that I was served dessert before my main. I later asked the staff who thought I already had it.
