The waiter approached us checking whether we would want some iced water while we decide on our orders. It was a nice professional gesture from their end. After browsing through a one double sided menu, I decided to order the following.1) Wanted to order root beer but it was out of stock. Same with my friends' orders of Ginger beer.2) Decided to order Snapple's pink lemonade instead.3) Chilli crab pasta sounded good at that moment so decided to order that. They ran out of Fettuccine so I had to change the pasta to spaghetti instead. Verdict: pasta was warm when it was served, chewy and tender in terms of texture. The  deep fried soft shell crab were both delicious and crunchy (managed to get the ones with eggs) and the Crossings' own chilli crab claw meat sauce were flavorful and hint of spicy made the dish special. (definitely recommended)4) My friend ordered fish and chips. The fish batter was pretty good and the portion of the fish fillet was bigger than expected too. 5) Hazelnut molten cake with ice cream. The dish was warm when it arrived to our table. The chocolate was a little bitter but the cake was moist and soft. Combined with the vanilla ice cream, it is one of best lava cake in Singapore. Overall, price wise it was quite affordable and considering that profits will be directed to charities made this place a gem. The service was excellent too as they checked on the customers' needs quickly when customers raised their hands. As my friends and I left for this place, we were also greeted with a thanks. Will be back soon for more yummy goodies :)

I always go cos I want to support this local social enterprise cafe. They hire kids with disabilities or are disenfranchised or marginalized. For this fact alone, I will go support them. But more importantly, I love their coffees as they are yums and come in nice mason jars. Additionally, their sweet potato fries are substantial for an appetizer and very yummy. Oh gosh. I am drooling.

This is one of the best Italian restaurant in Singapore, in my opinion. The quality of the cooking is in the league of Valentino's although they do not have as much traditional cooked items (and I am not complaining as long as what is on the menu is done well). In terms of ambience, I am glad they have shifted to Greenwood Avenue from Jln Pemimpin. The restaurant offers modern, chic, casual dining and is much larger with both indoor and outdoor seating vs its previous location. Its staff strength has also swelled to cater to the larger seating capacity.  Marcus and his team always makes me feel welcome whenever I drop by. If you drive (and parking is a bitch here), there's a valet service. I love the squid ink pasta and squid ink risotto which you don't need to pre-order, unlike Valentino's. You can taste the freshness and tenderness of the seafood, plus the pasta and risotto are done al dente (and I am pretty fussy that this basic stuff ought to be done right) as it should.  They are prepared using authentic squid ink sauce and not squid ink pasta.  The pizza is good too (thin crust) with just the right amount of balance between cheese and ingredients and their seafood is one of the freshest you can get. I was told the seafood is hand-picked at the fish market every morning.  I have no complaints about the steak, nicely grilled on the outside and juicy and tender (not chewy) on the inside, cooked as well as can be expected. In summary, the quality and consistency of the food here is amazing considering the copious amount of food being prepared for its ravenous crowd.And the chocolate verdant dessert is to die for, crispy on the outside and soft molten chocolate lava flowing from the inside.  We tend to over-eat and often end up with no room for dessert. When we are here, we make sure we exercise restrain so that we don't miss out on the dessert. The wine menu has also been much improved and now comes with a much larger variety of Italian wine.  It's a great place to dine with a large group of friends or with the family. And having said that, I should organize a group dinner here soon. I am glad to see that it is crowded and the restaurant is doing well so that more people in Singapore will continue to enjoy quality Italian fare.Bon appetit!!

Lunch set at $19.90++Be warned, the set lunch portions are SMALL! It started with a cioppino (3 stars). The seafood didn't taste very fresh and the soup/stew itself was unremarkable. The main, a spaghetti aglio olio (3 stars) with tiger prawns, was cooked al dente. Major plus points. But again the prawns didn't taste fresh and had the sort of crunchy flavorless texture that makes me dislike prawns. Lastly, you get coffee/tea OR tiramisu. We had the tiramisu (3 stars). The small slice didn't wow - I thought my aunt's tiramisu tasted better.The pizza we had came with artichokes, black olives, Parma ham (4 stars). This was far better! Thin crust, but not very generous with the ingredients.Don't think I'll be in a hurry to come back.

Three words... All day brunch.  How can anyone say no to that?  I mean the Genius!! And they also offer organic options, free flow Procecco, I mean how can you say NO!  That is the genius of this restaurant.  All of the best offerings are here, no need to go anywhere else.  Best of the best dishes? Of course the organic Eggs Benny.  fish and chops are also to fire for. crunchy inside and not soggy or to great.  chips are nice and firm with a bit of a softness on the inside, the best are the beef meatballs.  yes, I who does not eat meat on the regular for dietary reasons, cannot get enough of these.  These meaty morales are flavorful and succulent ...OH I could eat some now just thinking about it!!I digress,  they do have an awesome full Italian menu but honestly, u cannot get past the all day brunch.  Service is speculation ask for vijay he will give you the best wine recommendation.
Love this place! Delicious food, LOVELY service, and a nice atmosphere. This is my go to place for weekend lunches, but it's honestly good for any occasion.

Great service with the staff giving us a delicious dessert platter upon finding out that one of our party were celebrating his birthday, food that shines with the deliciousness of the produce and surprisingly reasonable prices. There's basically nothing much more you can ask for. The drinks list is quite comprehensive as well.

Based off lunch.Went there for lunch one day with my sister because we were tired of Lucky Place Coffee Shop and Pepperoni's. Will never go back again. I think the only okay was the coffee. Oysters had sand, the rest of the food was difficult to finish... service was poor. They don't bother waiting for you to finish your food before bringing out the next course... (and why the rush? There were, what, 3 occupied tables?)Horrid experience, although the ambiance was nice, being quiet and well done up. Bright side was that the food was so bad we could focus on conversation.

Very delicious food and portion side was perfect......portions tend to be small in Singapore restaurants.  Tasted fresh and service was the best I have experienced in Singapore.  I had Linguine Vongole, clams were well cooked with a light white wine broth.  My husband had seafood pasta in a bag.  It was really cooked in a bag.  The tomatoe sauce was light and did not over power the seafood.  The owner was very kind and welcoming.  My husband and I had a very pleasant conversation with her.  It was very nice of her to take time from her busy restaurant.  She was very attentive to all customers and her wait staff was well trained in providing great service.  Well worth the price.

Modern-chic space with ample seating options, indoors and outdoors. Wait staff attentive and knowledgeable (of the menu). Menu with quite a wide variety of modern Italian fare. Food was delicious - we went for dinner and had the Scallop Pasta as well as the Burrata and Parma Ham Pizza. Both were delicious.
Really liked this place. Great food and service. Price accordingly to quality of the food. Definitely worth a come back. Burrata was excellent.
Very good Indonesian.The grilled squid (for which the restaurant is named) is fragrant, sweet, slightly charred, and delicious. So is the sate madura, various fish dishes, and the chendol.Awesome!

I don't have a lot of experience with Indonesian food, and while I enjoyed the food, I'd categorize this establishment as upscale hawker, primarily because it is a sit-down restaurant with air conditioning.Table settings, chairs, etc. are basic, and while the service is efficient, it is not overflowing.Dan's review is spot on.  Portions are very ample, while prices are fair (see photos)  Beer is $6/bottle. While the quality was good, I think the squid could have used more time absorbing the flavors, instead of getting much of the flavor from the generous amount of sauce.Bottom line: I didn't think the food was all too compelling to want to return to, yet if you seek authentic Indonesian food, and particularly if you're with others eager to share multiple dishes, this will satisfy you.

The food is amazing and I am so please I get to try this before I leave Singapore. I recommend this place fully in terms of satay and beef rendang but mostly I was suprised with the chicken curry. This is full of lemon grass flavour. I had ro order another bowl of rice just for the sauce that was left over. I would have even lick the bowl if I wasn't at the restaurant. The satay was amazing and I could eat it all day, slightly different from street one. As it tasted like sweet char sui but with hint of spices. The meat was very juicy and so succulent. One skewer can shared for 2 people but I would say order one each as I didn't want to share because it was that good! Finally the beef rendang was amazing this was melt in your mouth tasty. The sauce was perfect with the right amout of spices and it doesn't  have a runny  sauce (the authentic way)! All in all I would give the food 5 stars, the reason for 4 stars was because it says it is open at 11:30am. We went there at 11:34am the staff says they are not open until 15 mins time. So we had to find somewhere to wait, which it wasn't easy.

great for big groups as the portions are really huge and best for sharing. Don't be deceived by the limited seating downstairs, the upstairs seating area is huge and true to style, they have several tok panjang (long tables) that can sit up to 20 or more. It is not halal though and even though it says "Bali" it is not Balinese food but more Nasi Padang style. In the day time they have assorted dishes displayed for you to choose from, nasi Padang style. So eating alone is no problem but night time, the solo diners will be more limited in choice. apart from the grilled squid, my favourites will definitely be the sate ayam (chicken satay) which is draped in delicious dark sauce and the portions are huge. One stick is enough for one person's main course. Another specialty is their Ikan bakar (grilled fish) which is more like a fish wrapped with otah. the portions are huge and meant for more than 2. haven't really tried anything unsatisfactory here before but the wait can be long at times especially when crowded.

Good place, I like that you can assemble your own breakfast platter for a pretty reasonable price (~$10 or so). Good coffee and Hokkaido brioche, stuff like bacon, eggs and vegetables are pretty par for the course though. Oddly enough some of the baked pastries aren't as good as the rest of the food. Very friendly service. Hope to be back someday.
I really wanted to like this place, but sadness. My coffee was burnt and undrinkable. My croissantwich was dry and room temperature. The staff seems pleasant though.

A hidden gem (can I still say this? It's getting less and less hidden by the week!) in the currently low traffic Galaxis. Prices are very reasonable, and the coffee, breads, pancakes and dessert are fantastic. The sandwiches are decent but not outstanding.The flat white in particular is executed skillfully, with a roast that isn't too acidic, topped off with smooth, creamy microfoam.The wife enjoyed the sweet pepper vegetarian sandwich while my toddler who's been having a bad week cheerily gobbled down the classic scrambled eggs on toast (rye bread).The butterscotch & berries pancakes were soft and fluffy (get this!), and we couldn't get enough of the banana coconut bread pudding with gula melaka caramel and vanilla ice cream (get this too!)Give the cookies a miss though - they were dry (we prefer soft and gooey) and were a tad too sweet.

I love this place simply for the fact that they make their own bread! As you walk in on your right, you see massive glass doors that lead into the kitchen. They have huge mixer bowls and all sorts of fancy, commercial grade baking equipment.They sell their bread too, you can buy half a loaf for $4-5 or a whole loaf for $8.They have free wifi, water, and baking magazines to browse through. You order at the counter and for sandwich items, you pick them up at the collection counter when your buzzer rings. For breakfast platters and other non-sandwich items, the staff will serve the food to you. Everything on their menu is nett priced and sounds and looks delicious!1. Smoked Chicken Sandwich $8Sandwiched in a very crispy country bread, are smoked chicken slices, long beans, mustard and melted cheese. The exterior of the bread is almost biscuit like and it does take some jaw muscle to bite in. The chicken slices are breast meat sort of, with the mustard and gooey melted cheese. The chicken tasted so good! The smoked flavour wasn't very evident, mostly covered up by the mustard. The long beans provided as crunch in the sandwich as well as the "green" for the sandwich.

Wow this place is NOT good. Ive been using Yelp since 2010 especially when I moved to a new continent to help eliminate trial and error. It's not often that I get disappointed by highly rated yelp and this is one of them rare instances.We ordered the butterscotch & berries pancake and a Norwegian. The pancake was average and the Norwegian was a disappointment. For me salad (came w the Norwegian) isn't just a garnish, it's food. The cucumber was seeded (ok) and hard (not ok), the hollandaise sauce that came w the poached egg was not impressive (watery). The Hokkaido bread was quite ok. The smoked salmon was v average. The grilled asparagus on the other hand was really good. Unfortunately that's forms only 5-10% of the dish.The service was pretty good and people are Super friendly. Alight I'll bump them up to 3.

The coffee here is pretty legendary. Its gentle flavor with a hint of nuttiness swaddles your tongue in warm dulcet tones, leaving you wanting more. Its the kind of coffee you'd want to being home to meet your parents, and they wouldn't even ask all the normal embarrassing questions because its personality is just that charming. And then you'd get married, it'd be a simple wedding, with just a few guests, and you'd wake up every morning wondering what you did to deserve such a good coffee. And then you'll have kids, and it'd be the cutest little cappuccino ever, and your life will be perfect. And then one day, you'll wake up in horror to find that you've drunk your little cappucino, brown stains still around your mouth as they drag you away to jail, kicking and screaming about how it was just one sip.Oh and the bread pudding is pretty great too. More like that girl whos kind of cute with the funky hair that youd hang out with a few times but overall not too bad either.

5-stars for the price for value at Bread Yard. You can construct your own Egg's Benny for under $10 ($6 for poached eggs with Hollandaise sauce + $2-3 for either back bacon or smoked salmon). I would say the bacon is a better bet than the salmon--the latter was a bit salty the last time I had it. Sandwiches are also passable, while the mashed potatoes with gravy were delicious! Home-brewed iced team should be skipped.Seating is often easy to come by, but the space is small. Bread Yard is tucked away inside one north, but it's a comfy place on a Sunday morning or afternoon. Take a walk around to catch a glimpse of the architectural work of the late Zaha Hadid!

I love their coffee. I usually get their iced latte (or iced mocha - it is powder based and not sweet - if I am feeling like an afternoon pick me up). Their sandwiches are quick and easy for in between classes at INSEAD.

Can't believe that I forgot to review this when I had been going here for quite some time already. iO is definitely a hidden gem in the Hillview neighbourhood, but once you tried it, you would feel that the long travel there is all worth it.iO serve various italian offerings with some Chef Specials that is rotated every once in a while. My recommendation from their menu would be the meatballs and eggplant parmegiana for starters. They tasted really great that I have always ordered them whenever I'm around. Another thing you should get would be their pastas. Their pastas are just really good and I don't think it's commonly offered in other western restaurants here in Singapore. Other than that, you should try their Chef Specials. They are significantly more expensive than other offerings but it was well worth the price.If you happen to have a sweet tooth, maybe it's wiser to come down on weekends since they have more selections of desserts on weekends. Price, I would say were quite steep. However, it was all justified by the responsive and cheery staff (never before I encountered staff that would still make small chats with you in SG despite how busy it was), chef that actually bothered to go around and ask us about our opinions, great food and ambiance. Overall, I am happy to give this place a 5 stars. Good thing to note (as I believe others have reiterated countless times) is to reserve your seats beforehand, they're pretty busy around dinner time!

Authentic, simple, good italian food. Good service. Only thing, it closes way too early--not Italian on that, but I guess they had to localize something! :-) Too bad for the location a bit off the beaten road.

I don't usually like Italian food, but this place is not too bad. I always have the pig's ears pasta for lunch here with colleagues, and have had a taste of other pasta dishes and appetizers here. While you can't go wrong with fried seafood or bruschetta with truffle paste, the food here is safe and on the pricey side.Meat and fish mains come up to about $30-$40 which I feel is pricey for the location which is very out of the way. Now that HillV2 has stopped their shuttle bus from my office to their mall, I doubt I'll be popping by on purpose for my Italian fix.

Wow - by far now our new favourite Italian and likely top 2 restaurant in all of Singapore.   The atmosphere was awesome - loud, fun, friends having a good time and just felt like a house full of food loving people.   The food was done to perfection all well within a good price for Singapore.   We had various plates but the pizza appetiser with crunchy crust was over the top good and the mushroom bruschetta was outstanding.   We will be back for sure as this is a gem in Singapore.

Was gonna order main on the menu, but the waiter recommended the "daily special",  the Sea Salt Baked Sea Bass, claiming it was "much better" When the bill came, this daily special turned out to be $78. I would not recommend iO Osteria where so-called "friendly" waiters are deceitful in conveniently leaving off the price of a dish 3x more expensive than the dish we were about to order. There are better authentic Italian restaurants in Singapore that do not have to resort to such tactics to stay afloat!!!

My wife and I had the salami pizza and some meatballs. It was very tasty and the price was reasonable. I think about $40 for a large pizza and the meatballs. You can have a bunch of tapas type small meals for about $8 to $10 each. The place looks cool and it was pumping full of people but the service was still friendly and fast. Didn't Get to try their coffee but I will be back to try that as it smelt awesome. We are looking forward to our next visit.

Awesome place! I am really surprised by this place given that it is located in such an inconspicuous place. I was there on a Saturday night and it was full (so be sure to make a reservation to avoid disappointments!). You can choose to order the pastas on the menu or opt for classics by telling them what you want. I would highly recommend the pesto pasta (not on the menu) which consists of generous servings of pesto sauce and parmesan cheese. Service was pretty good and I would highly recommend this place!

iO is a newer Italian place at Hill V2 in a gorgeous space overlooking the neighborhood.  While it is mainly a restaurant, they also offer quite a bit of Italian goods for sale and the open space is seamless.  As for the food, it's quite good with a solid selection of starters, pastas, and main.    We started off with a couple of starters which were both awesome - the stuffed Schiacciata and burrata.  The schiacciata was very tasty - bread stuffed with cheese and mushrooms with truffle flavor.  The burrata was also quite good, as it was accompanied with prosciutto and greens, and we went for a double order for the table and had no trouble polishing it.  We tried a few pasta dishes as well.  The bigoli with seafood was quite nice, but the taglioni with walnut sauce was less accessible. The seared snapper was also solid, and next time, I would love to try some of the meat dishes as well.  There is a short wine list, with an interesting choice for house wine, where a full liter will run you only $48.  While it doesn't drink like a fine barolo, it's a great bargain, although I wish  they wouldn't chill the red wine.  Overall, while the prices may not seem very cheap, the portions are generous, especially when compared to my fave - Osteria Mozza.  Definitely worth a visit and also with a larger group!

Quite a trek to get to, but may be worth the hike. The store front doubles as a bakery, and store also sells dried, bottled and canned goods. The ceiling to floor windows help greatly with making the place appear big, and inviting. The place is always full, lending a nice 'bustling' atmosphere. Despite this, the staff are all attentive and very friendly, with the owner and chef helping out with front of house from time to time.I personally recommend sticking to the 'street' type food - the pizzas and breads are good, especially the schiacciata. The starters and pastas are decent. The only secondi we ever tried over several visits really disappointed us and resultantly, have stayed away from them. So far desserts have been hits and misses! Generally a relaxed place to have a casual meal with friends.

The naan and butter chicken are perfectly executed and paired. - bring it on!!!  The service is awful, but the food makes up for it.  Be prepared to be ignored, and you'll have no worries ;-)  Last time we also tried the spicy prawn masala and it was great!  Oh, and the aloo gobi shouldn't be missed.  Cauliflower is the thing now, don't you know?Skip the fish head curry; it just ain't worth it.  Hyped to the rafters.  Go mainstream and you'll not be disappointed.

Inspired by Andrew Zimmern 's "Bizarre Foods" episode where he visited Banana Lead Apollo (BLA) and had the so-called "famous Fish Head Curry" and raved about how flavorful it was, I found myself nearby at the Temple and opted to trek a few blocks further into Little India to this establishment to whet my appetite.  Although it is on 48 Serangoon Rd, the entrance is on an adjacent st. (on Hastings Rd) about a block from the Little India MRT station.  If you walked passed Campbell Lane, you've gone too far.  Yesterday, while I was there, it was intensely crowed because of a parade that appeared to be going along Serangoon as part of the Pongal Festival (a Harvest Festival).Oddly, upon entering BLA,  I noticed that it was only around 25% occupied, if that, on a crowded Friday night.  The interior is cold lit with what appears to be around 4-5 kitchens where there are staff preparing dishes at their respective stations and you'll often find them unsettlingly staring deeply at you while you're eating.Perusing the menu, I saw the Fish Head Curry selling for around $S22-28 depending on the size you wanted to order.  If you order this, I suggest you get the small to share with another person.  I ordered the medium and it was ridiculously too large.  In addition, we ordered the chicken Briyani (an Indian equivalent to chicken rice), some garlic naan, stewed curry vegetables.   With the dishes comes a complimentary serving of these circular chips that tastes like dried pig skins or shrimp chips.  I tried one and it was awe-ite.  The lingering housefly noticed I wasn't too keen on it and obnoxiously laid claim to it.Note that the green mat is actually a banana leaf that you can place your food on.  That is to say: the mat=plate. The chicken Briyani was pretty good and came with two sauces: 1) a curry based sauce; and 2) an interesting tangy yogurt with chopped cucumber (favorite sauce here)  While the rice was aromatic, the chicken lacked flavor and wasn't very appealing.  And now to the Main Event: the Fish Head Curry.  The server placed this huge bowl and a gigantic fish head in a red, curry based sauce.  This "secret sauce" pretty much tasted like any other curry based sauce in any dish in any Indian Restaurant.  While it made an excellent dipping sauce for the naan, would you pay $S26 for a naan dipping sauce?If anything, I was perplexed at how much meat there is in a fish head.  The fish head meat is soft (especially the cheek meat) and has a stewed consistency.  Honestly, it is more hype than anything.  Yes there is some quality, but it didn't "wow" me at all, especially given the price.The curry stewed vegetable dish was blegh.  Didn't do much to my palette and this is coming from a person who walked into this establishment very hungry.All in all the fish head curry is a dish where you're guaranteed to get your hands dirty as it's a messy dish.  That means unfortunately, you will have to wash your hands in the filthy bathroom located at the back.  Word of warning, do not use the washroom prior to eating.  If you do so, you will lose your appetite.The service is pretty reliable.  Though at times, they rush and do not listen carefully as the staff person gave us something we were only considering to order (a mango lassi which was actually not bad) but didn't commit to.All in all, the experience is a unique one, but I doubt that I'd ever need to stop by here again.  Thumbs up slightly on the quality and service.  Thumbs down on the atmosphere (especially the third world quality wash rooms).For these dishes and a Tiger beer, it will cost you around $S65.

Authentic Indian food. Served with class and finesse. All the dishes are very well made and whats the best if that its free flow of papadoms(an indian cracker)All their dishes are reasonably priced. Curries and Dhal is always very good and full of flavor.Do make your reservations to avoid disappointment. Indians love to sit and enjoy their food. So if its packed. don't bother waiting.

Pretty solid fare here, but doesn't stack up to some other, smaller joints in Little India. The butter chicken was tasty, but the naan breads (butter as well as garlic) were a little dry. The place was pretty much empty on a Friday evening which was slightly strange, and the service was slow despite this fact. My eating companion and I were in a pinch so we chose this place more based off of proximity than reviews. Not horrible, but would not recommend if you have time and want to find some lip-smacking Indian food in this part of town.The prices are also slightly less than palatable given the service and quality of food.

This is a review of a dinner with a colleague at Banana Leaf Apolo.The room is very basic and functional. It is a clean space though.  It was not very busy (a Wednesday evening) when we were there.The service is friendly and polite but basic.  Your order is taken and your food is brought out.  The food came out in a timely procession.  It was neither delayed nor rushed.As you probably already know, the food is eaten from a banana leaf instead of a plate.  Possibly because we are westerners, we were provided with forks and spoons.   So, we didn't really do the eat with our fingers things.The food was all pretty good. Some of it was even great.  It was all freshly prepared.  While nothing fancy, the  food was presented in a pleasing manner.Vegetable Samosa - Personally, I prefer the larger style samosas with more filling.  But these were good.  They were crispy on the outside and tender and flavourful on the inside.  They went well with the provided sauce.tinyurl.com/crp68poVegetable Pakora - These were  tasty.  But they were not as piping hot and crisp as I like them to be.  I did enjoy them though.tinyurl.com/cysvgkjButter Chicken - This was a sweet and buttery dish.  It was pretty much exactly what I expect from Butter Chicken.  They were generous with the chicken and it was very tender.No PhotoSpicy Prawn Masala - This was a very nice dish.  It was not very spicy though.  As with the chicken, the prawns were tender.  For my tastes, the prawns were perfectly prepared.tinyurl.com/cge9zxqAloo Gobi - This is not something you will hear from me very often.  My favourite dish was the Aloo Gobi.  Yep, the vegetarian dish won the evening. There was just so much flavour and it all worked so well together.  The cauliflower and potatoes were both cooked just right.  So good!tinyurl.com/bojsrtlRice and Garlic Naan - Both of these were well prepared.  I could have personally handled a bit more garlic on the naan.  But, all things considered, it was a good take on one of my favourite breads.Overall - This is a basic shop that serves better than basic Indian food. I would love to try some of their other dishes.  They offer both southern and northern Indian cuisine.  We really enjoyed the food.

One of my favorite places to have fish head curry. First the fish is fresh and they don't overcook the fish (well, most of the time). Secondly, they have a ton of other dishes to jazz up your meal or cater to vegetarians or non-fish head lovers. Those dishes are also quite good. Service is not quite tight especially when busy but just wave your hand and someone will come to you very quickly. Seating can be a bit squeezy in the main dining area.

visited last night for the regular dose of indian (god bless this amazing island called Singapore), the restaurant was full and 95% angmoh. not being rascist here but it can be pretty intimidating and might even appear to be a tourist trap to some.rest assured, it isnt.had garlic and butter naan accompanied with palak paneer (spinach and cottage cheese) and butter chicken and it was great.bill was ~25sgd/pax for all that and 3 orders of masala tea (which kinda lacks punch for some reason)naan was crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, perfect.portions were decent, just right for 2 ladies...but we could do with some more pieces of chicken. service was excellent and rather entertaining; the guy who was waiting on my table was humorous and friendly, something rare in such a busy restaurant. efficient service, freeflow of pappadum and veggies(if u have rice) and they dont try to rush you off. it was a great evening.

The drill used to be bestie and I would have lunch at Banana Leaf Apollo, and then get our eyebrows threaded at Vanessa Beauty (see other review). Now whenever I make a trip back, this place is always on my to-eat list. The staples are always chicken masala, bryani rice, fish cutlets and sometimes fishhead curry depending how many people are eating. This time I also discovered chicken 65 - can't believe that I never had it all these time!

This place is over the years the most consistent top performer i've come across in Singapore. If you want to go out for a guaranteed good meal come to banana leaf apollo on serangoon road. I vouch that all the food items here are good. It's not cheap but i suppose if you want consistently good quality, you gotta pay for it. The food is also always served on banana leafs. The meat, vegetables, rice, bread everything i've ever ordered here was always good. The variety of food here is wide and so my best suggestion to you on each page is close your eyes and point randomly. You can't go wrong with this place unless your broke.

Had an Indian craving so did the customary investigations on yelp and open rice before settling on this place, which appeared to be in the heart of Little India. Service was slow, even though they were not busy when we arrived. Had to call for a waiter 3 times before someone bothered to come take our order. Had butter chicken, mutton masala, chicken samosas and garlic and plain naan. Yes, the typical westernised indian faire. Taste was ok but certainly not the best (or anywhere close) that I've had. It was clearly an indian restaurant who catered to the western market (as evident in their inflated pricing). However, it was good to see quite a number of indians dining in the restaurant. At the end of the day however, was quite disappointed and hence, not likely to return.

A happy meal here is an order of fish head curry, and all the refills of rice and vegetables you could want, served by men walking around with silver buckets of food. NOM. I've never quite understood why a curry fish head restaurant had to also serve other things like tandoori chicken, but not everyone likes their food looking back at them. I remember Apolo as the one with the chandeliers (yes, really), and it's really a sign of how much fish head curry is part of our national identity that busloads of tourists come by ever so often for it.

I don't often walk away from restaurants feeling annoyed, but tonight I did. I ordered a burger and instead they brought me a salad. I was hungry and didn't want to wait even longer, so I accepted the salad instead.I had to reorder a side of fries they hadn't brought out to me. At the end they tried charging me for the salad which was more expensive, even though I saved them money by not having them cook the burger I ordered. Over all I felt the staff didn't handle their mistake well and weren't apologetic in a

I've known Hard Rock since I was a kid and always felt it was an overpriced commercial gimmick overplayed, but I'd have to say after looking for a solid place to park my flip flops, allow the kid and wife to refuel while I sample cocktails, this place still has rock n roll left in it.Ribs were monsterous for the price, and the cocktails are not watered down . Generous pours , and good sized glasses. This is a welcome retreat from the heat in Sentosa. Calling this my Sentosa Refuge... singapore sling, chaching!
Very friendly and helpful service. This cafe is not yet participating the the new Hard Rock Rewards Program. No AAA discount.

I'm a regular at most Hard Rock Cafe's around the world. This one was a little bit old or at least it felt like it. But you get everything a hard rock has. Okay food, cold beer and great ambience.  My service was pretty decent so that's why I gave it a three star.

Going to Hard Rock Cafe almost makes me feel like a tourist, even if it is simply in Sentosa. Hard Rock Cafe has been on Earth for as long as I can remember and I enjoy trying out the Hard Rock Cafes in the different countries I visit. Awhile ago, a friend from school decided to visit me in Singapore and as she was a tourist and I felt like being one, we went to Hard Rock Cafe for dinner. It is not very different in design from other Hard Rock Cafes. It is dark inside with a bar area and loud music. Apparently there is live music on some nights, but there wasn't any the night we went. The food though was very different. Serving sizes are definitely smaller than those overseas, or at least those that I'd been to. We ordered the Hickory smoked Bar-B-Que Combo with ribs, chicken and smoked pulled pork since we couldn't make up our minds. It was beyond disappointing when we took our first bites and the meat was dry. The BBQ ribs were covered with a thick layer of sauce but the flavour had not even begun to enter the meat. I've had much more appetizing smoked pulled pork and the overall look of the dish was all the more unappetizing. The food looked like it had simply been thrown on the crowded plate and the sauces mixed with each other. Perhaps it is because I had expected much more from Hard Rock Cafe that has led to such disappointment. We decided to round off our meal with cocktails. It was the first cocktail my friend has ever had and she said that she probably would not have another one again. Given the rather expensive prices, I probably would not visit this Hard Rock Cafe again especially since I can get better American food elsewhere.

I've been pass "Togather Cafe" numerous times and have yet to try it until today. It was around 645pm when my family and I stepped through the sliding doors. The aroma of coffee greeted us as we were shown to our little booth. Thankfully, there wasn't a queue!We ordered 3 main dishes - Vegetarian Pasta with tomato based sauce ($8.90), Italian Herb Crusted Fish n Chips ($9.90) and a Seafood Aglio Olio ($9.90). I had the Vegetarian Pasta.The pasta was cooked to perfection - it wasn't too mushy neither was it too crunchy; just the way I like it. The sauce was amazing as well. It didn't leave a garlic after taste in your mouth like some sauces do. The pasta had vegetables like broccoli, carrots and cauliflowers. And the portion was just enough for 1.However, I didn't quite like the service I received. Maybe the guy was just having a bad day or maybe it was me, but I didn't find them too friendly - there wasn't a "service with a smile" feeling. :IOverall,Togather Cafe is value for money and it has a great atmosphere for getting a cup of coffee with a group of friends or just chilling with a book.ps apparently, it does get pretty packed so it's recommended that you make a reservation by calling them at +65 6445 1011Hope this helps! :)

So my friend and I decided to go to this place for dinner. We chose this place due to it's rave reviews. Before patronizing, I decided to check it's opening hours (please refer to image) and phone number to make a reservation. Unfortunately, my call was not answered despite dialing them thrice. Thinking that the restaurant's pretty busy at that point in time, we decided to just walk-in. Upon our arrival, we noticed that the restaurant was closed due to renovations. It was so disappointing! They could've updated the status of their cafe online or at least passed the information via an answering machine. We wasted our time and money traveling all the way to Bedok for nothing!

Love love love this family owned joint! If you love a noisy yet relaxing  place where everyone jst chatter all at once, then come on down. Not to mention the grub is not too bad too. Just be ready to fight for your place with the students after school.

Was in the area and decided to pop in for a after-dinner thingie...What struck me first was how beautifully put together (no pun intended) the cafe was designed and decorated. It is evident that the owners put a lot of themselves into this cafe! The theme of the cafe is simple and every small detail is aligned with the whole feel of the cafe. I can't explain well, you need to come and experience it for yourself. I was so moved by the cafe that I was inspired to (one day...far far later) own a cafe of my own and to have my own feel translated into the cafe.Now to tell you a little more about the food. The desserts are actually quite good. Not sure if they make them on-site but it's good nevertheless. The drinks are no bad as well. All in all, a great place to just come and hang and talk and chill!

Set in a neighborhood in Bedok North, just at the back of the famous block 85 Fengshan food centre is this unique cafe in the neighborhood. It is absolutely friendly for students as they are entitled with discounts on weekdays! It is cosy and though the place is small, you don't feel crowded and also retain your privacy with friends. The name and decor tells it all that it's goal is to help people gather with good food and a condusive place.  The baristas and servers are also friendly, making this place utterly comfortable and relaxing to be.The drinks here are priced very friendly and if you can't find a Starbucks nearby, it is more than better as an alternative. The cakes are delicious. Tried their chocolate truffles cake and enjoyed it loads. Gonna try their dinner menu soon and update on this review.

a lovely place to end the night in a part of the country that i hardly ever go to.this little gem in Bedok North is nicely tucked in a rather quiet part of the neighborhood. i love the cosy and warm decor (apparently it recently got remodeled and expanded as well) and the ample space throughout the cafe gave me plenty choices to choose where i want to be seated; there were booths for 4 as well as single tables for 2 or huge tables for groups inside and out. the prices are really reasonable and one of the lowest throughout all my cafe hop experiences and I'm glad to see the quality as good as those cafe charging higher prices. definitely a place worth checking out and returning to.
Affordable price for a cafe around the Neighbourhood. Love the atmosphere here, very lively and renovated well. The food portion is good and it's often crowded.

Always a fantastic place to have authentic South Indian food. The service is fast and the owner ensures that all the patrons have a great experience. Their banana lassi is fantastic as is their filter coffee. In many ways, I find the food in this restaurant to be a bit better than Komala Vilas. Their VIP thali is fantastic and you have the choice of either poori, bhatura, chappati or parotta. They also make sure that they refill all the curries in time. I only wish that they take credit cards. Other than this, this one of my favorite restaurants in Singapore.
We came here for its so called famous "fresh goat milk" coffee. However, it wasn't that great and it didn't taste that great. In addition, the waiter served us our drinks in dirty cups.

Met my ex-school mates at this Indian Dosa restaurant in little India section of Singapore. It was good to see them there and it was a good time to catch up on life. I ordered the marsala dosa paper thin version. It came in a steel plate with three compartments. The dosa and potato filling was good and so were the dipping veggie curry and sauces. I enjoyed very much and service was pretty efficient but not super attentive. Try the bru coffee (pronounced brew) which is supposed to be a coffee from India. It was delicious and strong. Fortunately the restaurant has a/c so it will be great for tourists. I will come back again should the opportunity arise.
Very good Indian food in a no-fuss environment. I had a massive thali plate with more vegetarian dishes than I could eat for less than $10.

Good and authentic south indian vegetarian food.. Has all the staples and also makes fresh appams. Good for breakfast, lunch or dinner. Pleasant service and decent menu with some indian-chinese options as well.

One of the most charming little joints in little india. They have a really really good aloo paratha. Its like a a paratha with lots of ghee on it and potato inside. You'll have one and you know you'll want one more. They have lovely appams as well served with milk and this nice sweet orange sugar. The mock biryani here is huge and is really yummy. It's very reasonably priced and the service is decent.

at least 10 locations just in singapore, and 5 stars for the crab pork dumpling, which is chili crab 40% larger campaign currently through Aug-Sept.  some other different items like a chocolate lava bun.  had some fried vegetable pork dumpling and noodle soup, no wait.

Best pork dumplings. Why wait 2 hours in line in LA, where they have an abundance of DTF in most Asian cities? No wait.You sit, you eat, and you're done in 40 minutes. Then you get to burn off those calories in the sweltering Singapore heat.

It was my first time dining at a Din Tai Fung Restaurant. This happens to be in Sentosa and near the entrance of Universal Studios/S.E.A. Aquarium. My husband and I just finished our self tour of the S.E.A. Aquarium and wanted something light to eat. We were seated at a table for four, but there's just the two of us, it just means more room for us. The server placed the menu and the order slip on the table for us as well. We ordered the Steamed Pork Dumplings (10 cts), Steamed Pork Buns (3 cts), and Steamed Sesame Buns (3 cts). Then realized that we had forgotten to order our drinks. We then asked the server for two hot Jasmine teas. The first order to come out were the dumplings! Which were porked filled and also filled with a soup broth. So when we bit into the dumplings the soup would escape out and tastes so wonderful. I really enjoyed the Steamed Pork Dumplings, it's definitely one of my favorites. Both sets of buns came out right after we finished the dumplings. The pork buns were decent, nothing too special, I did like the breading on it rather than the pork meat. The sesame buns were really good, according to my husband, but I was not a big fan of the sesame buns, since it was my first time trying that kind of paste. It's not something I would eat too often, but my husband said it was pretty good. Once we finished all our buns and teas, we went out to pay. The service was alright, but the refilling of hot tea was very good, since our teas were never empty. My husband mentioned that the servers could have been a bit more friendly. I really liked how they had several cooks/dumpling makers in the see-through room making dumplings right in front of us. It's pretty neat and it shows how fresh each dumplings were when made to order. I would definitely like to come back for the Steamed Pork Dumpling. It was quite fun to eat, but could be seriously dangerous if you bit into one when it's super hot! Beware of hot, fresh dumplings! Take your time to eat them or just open the dumpling to release the soup before enjoying, if it is too hot to eat the whole thing at once.

I have been to many restaurants of this chain but this one is by far the worst in terms of service! I asked for water refill many times and only got it after 15min. By the way, they charge for water. The food is of course good, but be wary of the waiting time. We ordered the Xiao Long Bao and it came as the last dish! The server told us that it needed another 8min to deliver because it needs 15min to cook but we ordered it 30min ago. I am very disappointed with the quality of service, will not come back to this location again.

Din Tai Fung has consistently good food. Waitresses and staff are all business - almost like non human robots. Very efficiently run chain restaurant. Diners mark selections on a clipboard either while waiting for a table or immediately when seated.  We go about once a month, all the locations are pretty consistent and we often tend to order the same things on each visit.  Sliced Cucumbers with Garlic, Xiao Long Bao,  Shrimp and Pork Dumplings, Shrimp and Pork Shumai, Pork Buns, Fried Rice with Fried Pork Chop, Wontons with Vinegar and Chili Oil are all extremely good.Today, we ate at the Resorts World Sentosa location.  It's a large restaurant and geared for the large groups and tourists.  Today, we waited about 10 minutes for a table.  The number display was broken so the hostess had to shout out the numbers in a shrieking voice that was as annoying as the sound of a very loud dial up modem (I'm telling you - they're all robots!)   I believe the prices here are a little higher for the tourists.  They also do not serve complimentary green tea after you are seated.  The food today was a little better than normal DTF quality - meaning it was excellent.There is often a wait for a table so the trick is to arrive early before the peak rush. They open an hour earlier at 10am on weekends.  Din Tai Fung is a great place to bring out of town visitors for dim sum.  Even the most constipated westerner will find this food appealing.

Oh Din Tai Fung. I love you. The dumplings are always great. ALWAYS. Beautiful little thin skinned juicy pork dumplings full of soup and deliciousness. So so good. Also get the egg and prawn fried rice, wontons in black vinegar, spinach with garlic and the red bean with sticky rice. Service is solid. This location is busy because it's in a touristy spot, but the wait is worth it. Love it.
DTF's dishes are no doubt the best.But this one branch isn't just my favorite.

Almost invariably wonderful Din Tai Fung reduced to a very missable. Take a shrieking hostess on a 120 decibel PA system  yelling numbers off a painfully long waitlist (mainly of wise guys who have long since deserted) - God save the unwitting who have decided to wait. Add inept manager and newer staff. And strange for DTF not their usually high standard of food. Far better idea to enjoy the delights at Malaysian Food Street next door, especially if is a warm or balmy day since the air-conditioning is just right. Or try something in the food stretch - Bali Thai and Ruyi sound good. Else maybe just go back into town to DTF at city hall, paragon (my favorite decor) or Wisma. If you do decide to stay, wait patiently and try get a seat in the much more pleasant dining area that is further inside and has more windows and open space. Try and enjoy but of course don't let this one color your view of DTF overall. Hopefully they'll sort it out.

I really enjoy the maki rolls from this place because there are quirky references to "the sushi roll" everywhere plus the ingredients are fresh and healthy (depending on what you select to go in it, of course). I mean how many places will offer to stuff your maki with items like dried cranberries, sunflower seeds, crunchy jellyfish, honey soy chicken and Yuzu Honey Vinaigrette? Hey, I think I just created a roll, albeit not one I would suggest though. See how simple that was to order a customized roll? Can't decide or in a hurry? Just pick one of their House Sushi's that they've already created for the indecisive customers. I just wished they didn't have to put each roll into those fancy boxes, especially if you're going to eat-in.Seems like such a waste. For those with nut allergies ... Beware: "Our food is prepared at a facility that uses NUT ingredients." So roll yourself outta bed and go get some!

As Halloween is coming, the outlet has come out with a new limited edition flavour of sushi roll  known as The Black Magic Roll. It costs $8.90 a roll and only available at the Cathay outlet, via mobile application and online ordering.The sushi roll is stuffed with roasted peppers, kani stick, shredded chicken, roasted pumpkin, deep fried soft shell crab and tomato based chilli sauce. The soft shell crab gives a crispy and crunchy texture, while the pumpkin gives it a sweet and buttery texture. Although the chilli sauce looks a bit dark, it actually tastes not bad giving it a sweet taste with a hint of spicy. Together it gives a explosive combination in the mouth.So don't forget to try it. It is only available from now till end of this month.

I love this place with a passion. Customizable sushi in beautiful packaging reminiscent of Bankaku-style boxes - what isn't there to love?Located at the foot of The Cathay, I would sneakily suggest you buy a roll and bring it to the cinema if you have the munchies. I especially love brown rice in my sushi, and this is the place to get it. I won't go into detail about what works when it comes to maki rolls, because everybody has differing tastes, and what works for me may suck for you.What I want to talk about is the speed of rolling makis. The team is inconsistent with their efficiency. Some days I get my maki super quick, some days I get it super slow. I always go about 6pm and they have the same number of staff each time I go, so I assume this is a business processes issue. Maybe they'll improve on the speed in future - this is fast food after all.P.S. They don't take credit cards. Cash is king here!

i'm lovin' itYes, I realize this is the slogan of a certain fast food chain but it describes perfectly my thoughts about Maki-san. It came with high expectations (both Yelpers as non-Yelpers recommended this place) and was a bit afraid that it would be a let down but this concept is just plain awesomeness.Is it the best sushi I ever had? Nope* but they offers good quality sushi at a decent price and the concept is fantastic. As previous reviews described, this is Sushi meets Subway and coincidently I love sushi and I am a subway fan so this restaurant was right up my alley.I am a big fan of the possibility to customize your dishes (yes I am THAT person who takes longer to order a starbucks drink than to drink it) and I am always having a hard time picking sushi as I always end up thinking: "this roll has xyz that I love but I wish it came with abc which comes in this other roll...". Maki-san solves that problem by letting you design your own roll. For eternal doubters as myself it is still a chore as it creates even more choices but it gives you a strange sense of empowerment.I went for the combo which included a mega-san, a canned drink and a snack which came in under 13 S$. My roll was super tasty (maybe because it hit all the right spots since I could pick my own ingredients ) and the snack I chose was super delicious! I would have never expected that crab stick tempura would be something I would rave about but the dough was super light & fluffy and the cheese dip which I picked for it made it a match in haven.Although I have rated it the full five stars I do have some minor points of criticism:1) it is filled with teenagers which made me feel out but a) this is not maki-sans fault; b) it might be due to the time of the day and location (film theatre on a Saturday late afternoon) and c) I might just having to accept that I am getting older...2) I like to drink a lot with my food, in the meantime I have accepted that in Singapore there is seldom a bottomless soda but since there is quite a queue it is difficult to purchase an extra drink if you want a refill so a soda fountain /a water dispenser would be welcome, or even a way to purchase another drink without having to queue in the food queue.Overall this place is amazing. I was going to start a petition: "I want Maki-San at Holland V" but I figured it would lead me to go there more than once a week  and not eat anything else anymore so I am happy for now since the Cathay is not too far away either.* in case you are wondering what for me the best sushi is: without a doubt I would pick a place in Japan. No competition possible, sushi is just so much better there.

Came here on a sunday at 1130am just as they were pulling up the shutters. The biggest selling point about maki san is that you get to make your own maki.. something like subway, except with sushi-ingredients.I went with the little-san $7.90, you get to pick 1 wrap (seaweed or healthy soy +$1)1 rice  (japanese white rice or healthy brown rice)3 essentials (avocado, steamed ebi, ebiko aka prawn roe)1 sprinkle (tempura crunch)1 house sauce (japanese caesar)And you get to watch them make them in front of you, which I think the staff was abit nervous and though he placed 5 prawns in the maki, admist his fluster whilst rolling up the maki, one shrimp fell out! *the horror*I enjoyed the maki. The tempura crunch was a good choice and it was very crispy instead. The prawn roe was rather fresh and the prawns were fresh and crunchy. The brown rice was also a nice healthy touch to the maki so I rarely see japanese maki with brown rice.All in all, a good choice for a quick lunch but a little-san to me, is still too big for me to finish on my own. The Mega-san is definitely big enough to share amongst two.
Love the packaging and the idea! First time trying it and got the egg crepe roll with brown rice Had Unagi, asparagus, ebi roe, avocado with miso sauce Healthy and fast!

Pretty Japanese wrapping that won my heart! Not to mention, the food here is delicious, healthy, and customizable.Grab a clipboard and flyer and start creating your very own roll! You want brown rice? Check mark that! Salmon sashimi? Check mark that! Some wasabi mayo? Check mark that! It does take a while for the rolls to be made (they're fresh!) so spend some quality time Facebooking, Instagraming, and Yelping ;) Don't forget to claim your Perx! Before you know it, your beautiful roll will be ready for consumption in pretty Japanese wrapping! Check mark that Maki-San! Or rather, bookmark Maki-San now!

Think of Subway, or The Counter, but for sushi.For those of you that are sushi purists who enjoy tasting the unique flavors of various raw fish, this might not be the place for you.  However, if you want to experiment with delicious ingredients presented to you as a maki roll, this place is heaven on earth.I went with my roommate, and we split a seaweed white rice mega san roll (which came out to $9.90), which allows you to choose 5 essentials, 1 special, 1 "sprinkles," and 1 sauce.  If you get a little-san, you can choose 3 essentials, 1 "sprinkles" and 1 sauce--however, I recommend getting a mega-san, because only with that option can you get the yummier ingredients (salmon sashimi, tempura shrimp, fried soft-shell crab, grilled eel, etc.).  For the amount that you receive, $10 is a pretty decent price, especially given that sushi is never cheap and that the average roll at a sushi bar costs around $12.We chose boiled shrimp, egg omelette, Japanese cucumber, avocado, and tobikio (flying fish roe) as our essentials, grilled eel as our special, pine nuts for our sprinkles, and garlic aioli as our sauce.  It tasted amazing--the combination of all those ingredients was even more tasty than it was in my mind.  The fish was fresh and so were the other ingredients, and the sauce added the perfect touch without overwhelming the roll with flavor.  I highly recommend the combination we got.The restaurant also offers pre-set rolls too for the indecisive ones like me.  They sell snack items as well, and serve miso soup in a coffee cup!  But what really takes the cake is the cute box that the sushi is served in.  The only sad part of my experience is that garlic aioli got on the box, or else I would have really wanted to save the box as a keepsake.At the basement of the Cathay, it's not too hard to miss!  It's make-your-own-sushi, and I feel like any combination of ingredients would be tasty.  But then again, when is sushi not the best thing ever?

Craving for good yet excellent sushi in town area? Look no further as this place serves both flavorful and budget friendly sushi.Located at the basement of the Cathay is this store (near to the escalator too). I've also seen a few people posting pictures of the sushis and the packaging box for the sushi. Decided to takeaway the Child's Play (House Sushi).As it was past lunch time, there were not a lot of people queueing. And as this is my first time stepping into a "customized sushi" store, I had no clue besides looking up at the head boards which specified the house special sushis, little or mega san sushis (different ingredients). After skimming through the menu of the house sushi, I decided to get the Child's Play as it sounds tasty.After ordering, you will receive a round-shaped thing with the order number on it while the "sushi masters" prepare the different sushis. While waiting, I realized that they have either seaweed wrap or healthy soy wrap and you could choose white rice or brown rice if you are to customized your sushis. There is a step-by-step form you can use to order the customized sushi which made it simpler for the "sushi masters". For the house sushi, they only come with a seaweed wrap and white rice with the ingredients listed according to its names.Consumed my sushi a couple of hours later. Even though the paper wrap inside the box was wet from the sushi itself, the sushi was still in perfect order (the box helped it not to spill the ingredients inside it). It was definitely flavorful and it has quite a number of ingredients which leave you with a tangy feeling of wanting more of it. It came in 6 pieces and the cut was a thick cut. The seaweed added flavor to the sushi itself. The packaging of the sushi was colorful and at the center of it, the logo of the store was clearly labelled too. For takeaway, they will provide a pair of wooden chopsticks, two packets of soy sauce and a packet of wasabi.Overall, it was definitely a good choice to try this place out. Will come back for more sushi soon :)

This place is like a Subway's for sushi-- customizeable, healthy and efficient.You can either choose a pre-set option, or customize your own sushi roll or salad.If you choose the latter, this is how it works:1. You pick up an ingredients list for either a sushi roll or salad2. You check off the appropriate ingredients you want (e.g. brown/white rice, seaweed,  tempura shrimp/smoked duck/salmon sashimi, caramelized japanese sweet potatoes/asparagus/corn/carrots, wasabi mayo/caesar dressing, etc.)3. You give your order to the cashier and pay the appropriate amount4. Cashier gives you a buzzer to let you know when your order is ready5. Pick up your order when your beeper buzzesI almost always choose a brown rice option with soft shell crab tempura, avocado, sunflower seeds and a few more things. The ingredients are all fresh and healthy and the service is very friendly.If you order the sushi roll, there's this robotic contraption that cuts the sushi-- which looks really nifty.It's decorated in colorful furniture that's clearly painted Ikea furniture and works really well with the simple, artsy style of the place.Relaxing atmosphere and good for grabbing a quick bite with friends.Not the cheapest of places, but sushi never is.Thumbs up

This shop is one of my favourites for a quick lunch and dinner. I love their Chips !!! sprinkled with curry powder and along with their baked quarter Chicken with black pepper sauce. The chicken can be a little dry but the sauce just compliments it.Cheap prices at about $12 for a CBD lunch is worth it. Remember to ask for Chicken Thigh! Chicken breast is too hard.

I love a juicy chicken which is roast nicely, even better if the skin is crispy. Besides the chicken, I like the variety of sides you can choose here. You can select your 2 sides from either the hot section (cooked vegetables - corn, peas, cheese cauliflower or mash potatoes) or the cold section (all kinds of salad which rotates regularly). Quinoa or couscous salad will be my weakness here. I also like the spinach salad which is to come with beet and feta. Unfortunately I was there after 2pm and so it was mostly just spinach. The server was kind enough to check the kitchen if they still have more back there. There was but not much beet or feta was in that stash, so he tried to pick the beet for me. Kudos!The fish and chips was average. Chips were nice and the fish was ok I guess. It fell apart when I took a bite to try. I also like the hot sides as they are comfort food. I wish we can choose all 4 though. The cashier was also very kind to check what I wanted to have and suggested I take the salad as my side for the chicken and order the hot sides separately as that will cost less. The a la carte price for salad is around $9? I don't remember now, but definitely higher than the $4 a la carte price for hot sides. Fantastic customer service displayed. This is a good place for a bit of simple home style cooking of roast chicken with comfort side vegs and quinoa salad. Have I mentioned how much I love the quinoa salad here? It will be better to go earlier for lunch as you get to see the full spread.

Very busy over the lunch hour on weekdays, as this is a popular spot for CBD workers.The quiche ($8) was reheated and quite bad; very watery and lacked flavour. A paltry salad was added on the side but did not justify the price. Seating can be tough to find between 12-1, but after that it's nice to sit outside in the shade and read a book if you can find a table.Not sure I'll return to try the chicken, which seems to be their specialty, but I suppose that could be a saving grace.

Rotisserie was my absolute favorite lunch spot back when i was working at raffles place. They are cheap, yummy, and somewhat healthier than the other options around here. $11.50 gets you a generous portion of quarter chicken and a choice of 2 side salads, or chips, or mashed potatoes and veggies. Their paninis are not bad too!They get super crowded during lunch, so it would be a good idea to come really early or really late.Even though I don't work in the area anymore, I still come back here for a meal every now and then!

Come here if you want fresh roasted chickens and good salads. When the Rotisserie first opened, they offered something like a quartered roasted chicken and two sides (great salads or mashed potatoes) for $9.50, which was a really good deal. It was such a good deal that the place got popular really, really fast and now you're almost not likely to get a seat if you're in the food queue later than 12.15pm. I like the roast chickens because they're minimally seasoned and roasted crisp with the juices retained in the meat. It's not hard to roast a chicken if you have a good oven, but I guess most people don't invest in good ovens or thermometer! The Rotisserie also serves ribs, fish & chips and other stuff but they aren't as noteworthy.The quarter chicken meal now costs $11 but beers are still cheap at $32 for a bucket of 5. The order system is quite fast - you line up at the cashier to order and pay, then proceed to the food counter to receive your meal with the order chit. It feels a little cafeteria-like but the restaurant makes up for it with speed. The decor here feels very modern Australian/Californian bare concrete floors and wicker chairs. I think the owners have struck gold with this simple concept and they're expanding to two more outlets in the area.

Love the generous sides that come with the mains. Try the rocket salad, coleslow or couscous salad as sides. Reasonably priced juicy roast chicken, perfect for a paleo meal. go for half a chicken if you are a big eater. Alternative choices for sides are fries and vegetables. Note that it's one or the other and you can't mix.

Yes. The Fish Head curry is consistently good.Much like a Zhi Cha place, they serve a variety of dishes, but the most popular is the curry fish head. I like both the signature and the asam version.Not the cheapest, but sits in airconditioned comfort eating spicy food. Nicer then Al fresco.

The server made a mistake by serving me a lychee drink. I thought it was plain water and had a sip.Much to my astonishment, thereafter they wanted to charge me for the drink. There was a little argument and I refused to pay for the drink.They are incredibly calculative and wanted to charge me for their mistake. There is no knowing what other penny-pinching tricks they may be up to in the kitchen.I will never be returning.

I hadn't been here in a while, but in recent months I got to visit a few times. Unfortunately it seems that their standards have fallen greatly and the curry fish head is more watery and is in a smaller portion. Their service is very poor, particularly during peak hours.

So I finally got the chance to eat here!!Assam Fish - we opted for fish slices version with Assam curry. The fish slice was the deep fried type you eat in fish soup. I thought its a little queer but still tasted good as the curry is good. It's not super Assam as it's lemak too. Kinda the best of both worlds. :)Golden Claypot Chicken - another awesome dish. Pre-fried chicken pieces coated wiTom Yum Soup - not great. Taste like it's made with instant paste. Can skip the next time. Sambal Lady's Fingers and Sambal French Beans with Prawns - both very good. Vege were stir-fried with good wok-Hei. Cannot stop eating. A meal here cost is $80 so while it's not cheap, it's very affordable. Will be back again for the nice and affordable fish head curry.

West Co'z Cafe serves amazing food options for westies, and is particularly a great option when you have a group of at least 6 people. They are well known for their fish head curry, which lives up to its hype. The seating here is great because they have plenty of round tables which can seat around 8 people. I came here for lunch during the week and found the group of 8 to be perfect in trying their set menu + few add on items ala carte from the menu.The restaurant is clean, well ventilated, and easy to find. Highly recommend!
Good sze-char. Their specialty is the fish head curry. Other dishes are good too. Reasonable prices and comfortable environment (air-conditioned).

Cheap and cheerful "zi char" place transplanted into a mall.It shouldn't work, but it does.A big plus: it's halal.It's also pretty good. The curry chicken, Assam fish head, golden claypot chicken and other signature dishes are winners. The fried rice dishes also have the requisite 'wok hei' flavour. I think it's way better than most of the "zi char' places around here.

I'm a resident of the West Coast area and when it comes to great food around here, it's pretty hard to match West Co'z Cafe. As other posters have pointed out, it's a venue that specialises in Halal "zi char" (stir-fry), so you get the usual dishes like sambal kangkong, hot plate tofu, shrimp paste chicken wings, cereal prawns, etc etc...basically the zi char experience in an air-conditioned mall (very similar to what you get at Far East Plaza), with a strong consistency across dishes.The specialty of this place is Curry Fish Head. Seriously, if you come here, just get this, otherwise you're just wasting your time here. It costs $16 and comes in a generous portion that feeds 4 (I get aggressive sometimes and order this even when there's only 2 of us here). You'll notice that every table has one of this and they do both the Nonya and Assam style, so pick your poison. They do enough quantities on a daily basis that it's fresh and cheap.One thing to note is that this place generally gets very crowded during mealtimes, but they do take your number and ask you to take a walk around the mall. Turnover is pretty quick, usually a 10-20mins wait, so don't get frightened off if they ask you to come back later!And oh, did I mention, a zi char place that takes American Express cards in Singapore? Yeah, this place is weird like that but so convenient!

A gotta-try someday halal zi-char cafe.Like many other zi char stalls, their dishes are available in three different sizes and they have set meals for groups of people at reasonable prices as well. I also absolutely LOVE their lemon chicken rice! The cafe is located on the third storey of West Coast Plaza. The wait staff have always been very polite and attentive even when they're busy (which is almost always).The cafe offers a satisfying meal and I have not been disappointed with their food or service so far.
Signature fish curry head is worth to try, i do not like curry at all normally but fish curry head is good and acceptable curry taste. this cafe is in west coast plaza

Nothing else is comparable to the noodles here. This is evidenced by the long lines every day, and I do mean every day! We were there at 10.30am on a wednesday and there is a line of 10 persons! Once we joined the line, 5 more were behind us immediately!Tip: morning is cooked by the boss himself, lunch hour his "sous-chef", dinner another worker. I only go when it is either the boss himself or the sous-chef. It is all in the number of nano-seconds the noodle is cooked! Yes, technicalities of Asian hawker food!

Totally worth the wait and everytime I've been here, there will definitely be a wait.The crispy fried flatfish is what makes all TW difference for this bcm.Order a bowl of too soft but nonetheless tasty dumpling soup to round off your meal after all that waiting!

First things first, the queue is VERY LONG. And it's not those fast moving queue, so you do need quite a bit of patience if you want to get a taste of this bar chor mee!My friend told me that the 'dry' one is what people think is the better one, so I tried it. But in my humble opinion, the soup one actually taste better overall. Nothing very spectacular in my opinion, so I'm not very sure if I'll come back, especially with such a long queue.............

I have lived away for some 12 years and every time i come backto Singapore, which is about twice a year, i head straight here, the morning after my arrival, for my fav authentic hawker food. Each time, the noodles do not disappoint. The secret is in the mix:  the sacue is sufficiently vinegary and sweet and sallty, the ingredients are fresh and of good quality, and the noodles are always cooked just right. What really seals the deal for me is the stock which is amazing, Over the years the prices have escalated so that my visit each time runs up a bill close to $50, for two persons eating there and a to go order for three at home. Notwithstanding the prohibitive cost I return. MY one complaint right now is that for to go orders, they do not offer you the soup sp you have to purchase a soup bowl to go!

This stall was previously located in Marina Sq Food Court and always has a long queue for the bak chor mee. Even foreigners that come here want to try the noodles before they return to their countries.The special feature is the Chilli sauce and the flavourful soup! Their pig's liver is also done very nicely. Cooked for just the right amount of time, resulting is tender slices of liver heaven. I was sort of shocked when i saw that the whole bowl was filled with oil, but i was told that this is actually the yardstick for all Bak Chor Mees in Singapore. Anyway, i was not disappointed with the taste, not too salty and very flavourful with just a highlight of sourness coming from the vinegar.I also liked the fried bits of lard and the liver bits, which wasn't too overpowering and given in the correct amount. The crispy fish was also a nice addition to the usual bak chor mee dish. A must try.

I'd known before making my way down to Lavender that Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodles was a popular bak chor mee stall, with some food bloggers going so far as to claim that it was the best bak chor mee stall in Singapore. I was all ready to give it the benefit of the doubt, seeing as how it was a family-run stall dating back to 1932. Despite the knowledge of all these facts its snaking queue on a Wednesday evening managed to surprise me anyway, and contributed to the already high expectations that I'd had of the noodles here.Um sadly. Wasn't impressed.I kind of get why Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodles has its loyal following. The gravy here has a much higher ratio of vinegar than most bak chor mees do, which I suppose goes down well with those who like their noodles with an acidic kick. The fragrant and crisp pieces of ti por or fried solefish provided a nice crunch that provided a pleasant contrast with the springy mee kia (thin noodles), and the pork used here in all its forms - minced, sliced, livers and balls - is fresh, chewy and of good quality. Oh, the one thing that I liked about the bak chor mee here was the broth that came with it. I could literally see a meat cloud in it, which was a precursor to how intensely meaty and flavorful it tasted.I'm going to go all out blasphemous and say that I don't get the hype about the bak chor mee here. At all. This was okay bak chor mee, yes - but to call it the best bak chor mee in Singapore when I can't even decide if I prefer it to the ones sold by the hawkers in my neighbourhood? Nahhh, I'll take convenience any day.Just a note of caution if you're thinking of heading here for bak chor mee: They're supposed to close at 9 pm, but their actual closing time is when they run out of ingredients for the day, which, on the day I visited, was 7.30 pm.

This is so underwhelming. I can't believe I queued 40 minutes for this during lunch time! It was time to see what's the fuss about when I decided to join the snaking queue in this coffeeshop tucked away in a sleepy estate of Crawford Lane. All I can say is I don't see what is so special about it. Add in the waiting time and I feel cheated. The noodles were quite stiff and starchy, and there was so much sole fish in it and too little minced pork.I had a better time with the homemade iced lemon tea from the same coffeeshop - be sure to order that if you need to try the noodles!
Fave bcm in town! but be prepared to queue for this, usually it will take me around 30-45 mins depending on the length of the queue and how many orders per person.

Not sure what else I can say other than that this is most definitely the best Bak Chor Mee in Singapore.Once you can get past the queue in this little kopitiam, you'll finally find yourself holding onto a bowl of the most perfectly cooked noodles, doused in a casually good vinegar base. One of the best parts of this is how well cooked their minced and sliced pork is - soo tender and juicy considering how fine they are. The pork balls are also very tasty without having that artificial flavour to it, and to crown it off, they add some bits of crispy deep fried dried fish, which adds that bit of crunch and saltiness to the whole bowl. One wonders why this doesn't feature in more minced pork noodles sold everywhere because it makes such a good combination! The soup on the side is so well brewed as well, you can actually taste the pork from which the flavour comes from. None of that artificial flavouring that we frown upon, I don't think!
Be prepared to queue. It is worth it. Is there a better pork noodle out there? Nope there never will be

Hands down the best bak chor mee in Singapore! I love the vinegar with the chilli and so much porky goodness in the soup! Super long queue so make sure you bring some entertainment! Wait times can be up to one hour at peak times.

I'm of Chiu chow descent so trust me when I tell you I love love love bak chor mee. We came here right before it opened to get a number tag for the cue. We made it about 10 mins before they opened and got #9. The whole wait time was about 20-30 mins. Definitely get there before they open because the line goes out the door the moment the store actually is open for orders. Once the restaurant opens, they take the numbers first and then everyone else in the line. It was our last meal in Singapore so we definitely went all out. Instead of one $10 bowl, we both got two $5 bowls which meant more food for the price! It's pricier than other hawker stands and other restaurants that serve it.  You can taste the difference and it tastes good. I can see why they got a Michelin star. The bowls are small though. The people there speak little English and mostly mandarin. Ordering was easy though because there aren't too many choices. The bak chor mee dry is definitely the way to go. It's vinegary but not overpowering and the noodles are a perfect texture. I hate soggy noodles so this was a big deal to me. There isn't a lot of meat but most dishes don't come with a lot of meat in south east Asia. We also got the meatball soup! Yummy! I would definitely come back as long as I could avoid the lines. Definitely go a little earlier, even if it's like 2 minutes. The line gets long, fast!
