For those who get tired of fried food easily or find it too oily, this place might prove to be the answer.

The restaurant was located at Eat At Seven in Suntec City. It was the first outlet in Singapore and was known for its long queue. Recently it had opened a second outlet in Boat Quay. As the queue was not long with about 10 persons in front of me during peak dinner hour, I decided to join the queue. The restaurant was small in size and packed. It took me about 25 minutes to get a seat. The place didn't smell.Menu was limited with mostly its signature Tendon in original($15++) or vegetable version, served with original sauce or spicy sauce. The set was an additional of udon soup with a topup of $4.50++. One could upsize the serving of rice with an additional of $1.50++. Looking at the menu, I decided on KOHAKU Tendon set ($19.50++). Iced water is provided free of charge.KOHAKU Tendon (S$15++/ ala carte)It looked great with a small bowl in it to put the the small hill of tempura on. There's pumpkin, baby corn, french bean (2 pieces), mushroom, chicken, crab stick, squid, and prawn (2 pieces) tempura. The vegetable ones were great but the prawn ones suck. Tasted strongly of stale oil, which covered the prawn's taste, made one felt jelat and wanted to gag. The udon soup was served simply with a slice of fish cake, tempura crumbles and chopped spring onion. The noodles was thin type, which was smooth. The soup was light and flavourful.Overall the food was overrated and quite expensive too. But then it was difficult to find a tendon place that did not smell.

And we're back! Yes, that is how much we enjoyed Kohaku. I don't normally write second reviews of the places I've visited but after the service I've received, I can't help but shower praises for the restaurant. Firstly, while we were waiting for our table, the restaurant manager had already seen us and given and acknowledging smile. We weren't sure if this was just an "I acknowledge you're next smile" or "oh I recognize you smile". This time round, we were seated at the bar and I have to admit that, you do smell a bit of the oil from the frying, but, they've probably improved their ventilation and it isn't as bad as some of the other places I've been. This time round, I decided to go with the Spicy version and OMG.... I'm in love. But more on that later. Upon ordering, the manager actually came up to us and thanked us for coming back! He actually recognized us! Which is brilliant considering the number of patrons they get a day. Having the chance to sit at the bar now, it gave me a good chance to oversee how they're operation works and I have to say, I'm nothing but impressed. I've received enquiries from friends asking how the place was and that they've heard that the waiting time and speed of service is horrendous. The kitchen and the front of house works like clockwork. I did wonder initially why the staff sometimes left tables empty when there was a queue outside and sitting at the bar showed me that. 1) The kitchen staffs don't just aimless and blindly fry the tempuras. They pace themselves based on orders and after 2 rounds of frying, they painstakingly remove all the little bits of floating flour in the oil, ensuring that they do not char and add that bitterness into the oil. 2) to ensure maximum freshness, they will only fry a batches of 5 at a time. After each round of sieving the oil, they will remove the fresh ingredients from the chiller, batter them and fry.3) the belief in absolute perfection. This I have to admit came as a big surprise for me. While placing the tempura's on each bowl, the chef had accidentally dropped a long bean on the counter top. Now this isn't any counter top, it's the one strictly used for plating. From where I was, it looked immaculate. Clean, shiny yet instead of placing the long bean back, he threw it away and told the cook to fry one more long bean immediately. Not fry with the next batch, but ONE long bean to add to the bowl (the fryer was empty then).Even the Japanese chef in charge of making the green tea does it with absolute precision, ensuring that each jug contained exactly the same amount of green tea powder to water ratio. I think it helps a lot when the manager, executive chef? (Not sure if you could call him that) and the main chef preparing the batter and drinks are all Japanese. There's a level precision with everything they do and you could sense that perfectionist attitude that the Japanese are known for. In all honesty? I don't mind waiting a little longer than usual knowing that so much care had gone into the preparation of my food. Now for the main highlight, the Spicy Kohaku Tendon Firstly, the smell. When the bowl came, that mixture of sweet, salty and spicy really got my palette racing. I couldn't wait to dig in! Secondly, I was so happy that they didn't give Okra. Instead, we got a slice of pumpkin today which was very well received. Do note that the vegetables here will vary so I won't be surprised if I get Okra the next time I return. Thirdly, that sauce. I thought I loved the original, until I tried the spicy version. It was perfect. The spiciness was prominent without overpowering the umami-ness of the sauce yet delivering a nice kick that helps elevate the dish. Amazingly, if I thought that our first visit was good, the food this round tasted even better. As we left the restaurant, the manager again showed his appreciation my giving us the lowest bow (90 degrees and maybe a little more) I've ever seen anyone give! A true sign of just how appreciative he was of us returning. That summed up our impression of Kohaku for us and if I could give it a 5.5-6* rating I would. Thoroughly impressed and delightfully satisfied, we're counting down the days to our next visit!

Not a fan of tempura but this blew me away. The long queues on regular days piqued my curiosity, and I decided to give it a try. The ordering process is really simple-you choose from spicy/non spicy, all veggies or veggies, seafood and chicken, and whether you'd like it as a set (with udon) or not.I ordered the regular with veggies, seafood and chicken. The bowl was filled with prawn, beans, corn, and chicken breast tempura. The batter was a thin layer that coated the various ingredients and was not too filling, while all the ingredients remained crunchy and did not lose their original flavour. This was especially so for the chicken breast, which was surprisingly not dry and went well with the tempura batter. I particularly enjoyed the mushroom, which was chewy and juicy. Priced at $15, this is indeed worth a trip down for a try. (Just note the gst & service charge which inflates the price as usual)

There is always a queue outside this and I've only been patient enough to wait twice to eat here. Limited menu should make its service faster but the seating is for maybe 20 so reminds me of many such family run establishments in Japan. Good value for money and tempura was not too greasy

Ordered a bowl of Kohaku Tendon, and added an extra portion of rice. Came very early to avoid the snaking queue that was forming at the end of my meal.The food was incredible. Everything was well-seasoned, and the tempura batter was crispy; it was clear the restaurant used quality ingredients. Also, I loved the brown tempura sauce drizzled over the dish, although some may probably find it a little too sweet and overpowering. The only low point was the chicken, as I found it too overwhelming in size, and not tender enough. However, it was still a very solid bowl of tendon.Highly recommended.

We came here just to check it out and to compare it to Ginza Itsuki in Tanjong Pagar.Tempura here is too greasy and some of them are burned/over-cooked.The koromo is too thick and it definitely kills the flavor of the ingredients.Tempura don here is $1.1 more expensive than the one in Ginza Itsuki and the taste isn't even comparable. Overall Verdict: 2Taste: 2Amount: 3Price: 2 (because it's more expensive here than Ginza Itsuki)Atmosphere: 2If you are looking for a good tempura place, stick with Ginza Itsuki.

The place looked great with lots of cartoon character figures around. I was shown to a chosen table which I later found that the chair had oily stains on.Quite a lot of choices on the menu. Prices were more on the high sides. Wonder Woman's Box Office Power Drink ($10.90++)An ice-blended beverage created with all-time favourite salted caramel popcorn flavourThe drink was quite sweet and lacking of the popcorn taste which one was expecting. Instead it tasted more like oreo cookie. Maybe it should have a change of description.Paradise Island Mac & Cheese  (S$18.90++)Conchiglie rigate baked in special 5 cheese  sauce and mentaiko sauce, flavoured with white button mushrooms , turkey  bacon and garlicMy first choice was pancake but I was informed it was not available more than 10 minutes after I had placed my order. The pasta was well cooked and flavourful, although one could not taste the 5 distinct taste of cheese nor the pollack roe which was commonly found in mentaiko sauce. The dish itself was a tab dry. Didn't really found any garlic, but there was shrimps in it. Needed another change of description here.

This place isn't somewhere you'd come for the food, but for the DC comics theme.  My sister is a fan, so we decided to come here for a meal.  Everything here fits the super heroes theme;  the restaurant interior, the menu, the food items.Regarding the food, passable but not great.  Prices are ridiculous.  Even a refill for tea costs money.Not worth the price or time to eat here.  And the staff here aren't very helpful.

The DC cafe has fantastic themed decor and menu items. There's a LOT of options to choose from and it's a cool place to look around if you're into the comics/movies, and they have a lot of neat replicas. I got a chocolate themed drink (don't remember the name) that was a chocolate OVERLOAD. It was chocolate ice cream with gobs of nuetella, chocolate syrup, toasted marshmallow and whipped cream topping. It sounds really good, but the chocolate they used tasted so artificial that it ruined the drink for me. I usually don't have high expectations for novelty drinks, but it was really hard to even drink the fake chocolate taste. The service was also very, very slow. There was no one in the cafe but we had to wait 20 mins at the cashier for someone to see to us. It seemed like the staff was avoiding us at one point. The concept of the store is cool, but I would suggest going for a simpler drink if you want to visit.

Finally got the chance to try out this cafe! Their menu was really nicely designed. A lot of choices you could choose from. There is alcoholic range too. Desserts wise are good. Their coffee are smelling nice and taste good too. Their side snacks are quite a range too. We ordered their truffles fries and it was good.  And for their dessert we ordered their waffles. It was decorated beautifully. Makes us really happy. Beside their cafe, they have a retail shop selling the DC characters products ranging from clothing to accessories. Their service isn't good enough. Their staffs wasn't attention to us. We have to keep signalling to them. Didn't try out their main dishes yet but definitely still will visit again next time.

Absolutely horrible. Came in and was greeted with a I-could-not-care-less attitude. The whole purpose of those cafes are the concept and the deco. When I stopped to take a photo before I was seated, my Friend noticed that the waitress let out a sigh of impatience. It's 615 on a weekday and the place only had a few tables taken - there were plenty of empty seats. Sat down ordered 2 drinks off the menu and a glass of ice water. For food, two cakes and one portion of truffle fries. After 5 mins, was told that two cakes are not available. Friend asked to see the menu and waiter said ok, but never came back.Two strawberry coolers came when we just ordered one. Fries came. At least the fries were good, hence the single star for this place. After a while, we reminded the waitress of our order of a drink and water which has not come. The waitress looked at me as if I was stupid and said - we don't serve ice water here.Seriously now... So I just ordered mineral water with ice.... But after 5 mins or so, a glass of ice water came. Friend was a bit frighten to drink the unidentified looking water.... Have not paid yet. Typing this here and hopefully the paying experience itself won't require me to update this already nasty review even more....
Nice DC decor. Menu selections are good . Food quality can be better . For the price point , there are better ones out there that serve quality western food .

I'm not a typical beer drinker, if there is even a standard for that.  But when I stepped into Druggists, I just felt that the environment was so welcoming.  The friendly and helpful beertenders, the chic decor, the spaciousness, cleanliness and the idea that there are 23 taps of beer is just mind-blowing for me!  I had no idea which beer to choose because they are all craft beers - made from small breweries.  The idea is really attractive, I'm supporting small enterprises!  Still, it's challenging for me to choose a beer to start, given that my knowledge of beer is so limited.  If you are like me, fret not, the beertenders are able to recommend you a beer according to your preferences and they have been spot on for me!  Both Nad and Julianne recommended me beers that I haven't heard of and I like them all!Even though I set indoors, the acoustic in the dining area is conducive for conversations as the sounds from the customers kind of gets absorbed into the walls.The small bites are also very delicious!  I've tried the Prawn Paste fried chicken wings and french fries with chilli crab dip, all so yummy.  Although I would prefer more chilli crab dip in the first serving instead of having to order a second round of dip.Overall, it's been a very enjoyable hangout place for me and my friends and I will be coming back here whenever my beer-drinking friends want to meet up.

Wide selection and good recommendations, I don't think any of their beers really stood out though. I'm not sure why they have so many sour beers either. Nice decor and atmosphere, but chairs are pretty uncomfortable. It's OK, but not really worth the trek out unless you're already in the area.

If you like trying different craft beers from all over the world, you've come to the right place! They constantly introduce new beers, as long as one runs out, they'll replace it with something interesting. As a result, there are times when the menu is friendly to certain taste preferences, and others when you struggle to find something to drink.You can ask to taste anything before you order and their staff are very knowledgeable! I usually let them know what kind of beer I like and they'll recommend something that is close to the flavor profile you've described.The first time I came here, I had really awesome beer that was light, fruity and delicious. The second time I came, they only had rather tart beers - like one that tasted like pickles, another that was lemon, and one with sour cherries. It's luck of the draw, but if you like hanging out somewhere chill with your friends where you can actually talk, this place is perfect.

Druggistnoun, North Americanplural noun: Druggists    a pharmacist or retailer of medicinal drugs.Origin:early 17th century: from French droguiste, from drogue 'drug'.the only medicinal drug that they sell here is beer!given that moderate beer drinking can have positive health effects on diabetes, forms of cancer, inflammation and even weight loss, i am more inclined to re-visit this druggist than the gym!;)i have been here 3 times and every time my beer has been cold!not as cold as the coldest pint of kilkenny from molly malone's irish pub in boat quay but categorically cold.the staff here have been nothing but friendly, helpful and knowledgeable.each time, they recommended something that suited my palate and/or disposition. on my last visit, i was introduced to De Molen Mooi & Meedogenloos, Beautiful and Ruthless!beautiful it was, dark and sweet and definitely ruthless in it's alcoholic content!i like this the best of the three i tried and it paired perfectly with a plate of pork roll that was plump full of distinctively flavoured minced pork with a tangy side salad and sweet, black dipping sauce.i could totally taste the freshness of the roll and the portion was indeed generous.yes, they do have a small but well thought out food menu for those who can't drink on an empty stomach!you can choose to sit alfresco out front, in the main air-conditioned hall, in the small, hidden lounge beyond the bar or way behind where the toilets are.if you like your beer and body cold, do stay in the main hall!clearly, this place is not for everyone.clearly, the price you pay for beer in SG is also not for everyone!clearly, i'll be back for my regular but moderate, over-the-counter prescription again!;-)

This place serves 23 craft beers (last I walked past) on tap from various nooks and crannies of the world. The place is tiny, has bad air-conditioning, and the size just makes sound reverberate in a really bad way.Came here on a Friday night and it was so loud we had to shout, and when you're paying $8 a glass for beer, it ought to be COLD. Within 5 minutes, my beer tasted like warm piss. I don't care where this beer was brewed, I don't care whether it is ale or pilsner or whatever, I do care about the temperature of my beer. Something needs to be done about the storage capabilities of this place. Mid-priced warm beer coming out of the wall in some location not really near an MRT? Errrr okay.I did take a look at their snacks menu - looks promising and very local, but I didn't try. Also, they don't allow you to taste test anything, with some clueless and overworked waitstaff at the cashier to collect your money and vaguely recommend you a brew. This place would be good if they allowed a shotglass tasting of all the beers they have on tap for an amount, say $20, maybe someone can suggest this to their owner.P.S. Amex not accepted

Druggists has been my favorite beer place of late, and having a selection of 20+ beers on draft certainly doesn't hurt.  The list is primarily European, with a few American beer as well.  There is always a good selection of Mikkeller beers, and the other night, I also enjoyed one of my favorite beers of all times, Delirium.  They do go through kegs very quickly so don't get too attached to a particular brew.  All beers available by the half glass as well, which is great when trying types.  The food menu is also interesting with a global sliders list, some quite decent wings, as well as some nods to local fare. The place is small, but there is also seating outside if you are ok with the heat.   Definitely a great place for draft beer and no crap on tap here!

Ok, I think Singapore may not be totally ready for Druggists.  The fine folks at The Drinking Partners (thedrinkingpartners.com) decided to come up with The Great Beer Experiment and got some good buzz from beer enthusiasts that made the trek all the way out to Pasarbella at The Grandstand.    So, toes dipped and the water temperature promising, putting the whole foot in involved launching Druggist in Tyrwhitt Road, where the gestalt is decidedly more hipster, low rent enough not to go the whole hipster hog (just opposite Jalan Besar Stadium) and not totally slumming it at a hawker center.  The evening traffic, IS hipster, or so I've been told by the beertenders.  I've never hung around long enough to find out for myself, opting to scurry away before the sun climbs below the multi-story carpark at Jalan Besar Sports Complex across the street, like a Carpathian hay farmer fleeing the lengthening shadows.  So I'm really glad for the Drinking Partners that they had the stones to put Druggist out there, but that's just me, the beer nerd talking.  If it'll help, they have my undying loyalty and oh, here's a virtual string of garlic and a wooden stake from Crate and Barrel carved with calculated indifference...the only thing to put the hipster undead down for good, or maybe put Tactical Nuclear Penguin on the menu.Man shall not live by bread alone and beer businesses shall not live by beer nerds alone.  We may love and understand everything you do, but we also understand that you cannot pay the rent and all those enthusiastic young people on beer nerd custom alone.  You have to do the hard thing which, the almost impossible thing, which is to "educate the customer".  No scarier words have rung in the ears of those who dabble in the dark art of F&B.  My hat's off to Lincoln and the Drinking Partners!!So here are my recommendations for Druggist:Beer Nerds.  Show up early.  Preferably when they open.  Keep asking for the tasting flights which should have been launched by now.  Early is good since you have the place to yourself and you get to properly taste the wonderful rotating kegs (new kegs come in every Tuesday) in peace without being distracted by the bone chilling miasma of indifferent cool.   You get a bit more individual attention from whomever is tapping that day as well if you need to find out a little more about each tap.Ratebeer.  Whip out that smartphone, type Ratebeer into the search bar.  Get very useful rating information plus an invaluable guide to what to expect.   None of the Druggists offerings are below a 90 rating. Useful supplement to whatever the staff at Druggists are already telling you about what's behind each tap.  You get information on what other beer nerds from around the world are saying about this very beer that has your eye.Parking.  Multistory carpark across the street.  Basement parking also available at Jalan Besar Stadium, but a little creepy, but for me nothing compared to the threat of being mobbed by hipsters.  Street parking if you're early.Flights.  I wish they had them, but I just do my own when at Druggist.  So you don't rapidly reach a point of diminishing returns, you ask for about 100ml in each glass  taste it and then move on.  You end up paying for the full glass, but you don't waste good beer and you don't get wasted and you get to be a better person for having a more experienced palate for beer!  Still waaaaay less expensive than tasting single malts...Ok, to close, here's the sermon.  Beer in Singapore is close to where coffee is, a budding culture backed by people with a passion for their product, armed only with what little capital they have and a fierce belief that Singaporeans are ready to dig deeper and to understand the origins of beer, appreciate its traditions and explore the cutting edge of where global beer culture is headed.  I think we're getting there.  There is a nucleus of enthusiasts and a general open-mindedness about spending a little more to try something new, to explore outside the conventional, the commercial and the safe.  Maybe, just maybe that rich amber brew with the off tan head bearing that slightly funky fog of sweat sock going at $17 a glass might be a life changing experience, an epiphany.  The fine folk at Druggists are betting the farm that Singaporeans are willing to take that gamble and I for one am hoping fervently that my fellow Singaporeans are ready to roll the dice!

I finally made it out to this place! Druggist! A place of wonderful rotating 27 taps of awesome beer. If you are looking for tiger or any other light beer, sir please turn around because you will be disappointed ....or maybe don't...and instead bask in the hoppy, bitter, full-bodied experience of craft beer! My beer count is going to rise slightly this week now that I know how to get here.The promotion got me excited till I read it more carefully...then I was just sad , then I ordered beer and I was happy again! Singapore continues to amaze me. The place gets pretty full, I went on early Saturday so it was fine. Best part, it's right next to a food court, so go get drunk and sober up for cheap!

First time having brazillian bbq and the experience was just MEH! Could be a good thing in that my expectation was non-existent to begin with. but could also be a bad thing because i was not amused with Carnivore's attempt to match the awesomeness that is Pampas in California. the dining experience was kind of weird. for a supposed fancy dining, the dining tables are placed right in the middle of the mall. there was no warm ambiance, only the bright lights from the mall. & the servers come out to you with sticks full of meat where they carve it out to you on the table. i think i would have preferred a better dining decor to match a high $$$ dining experience. salad bar was just alright. i'd rather fill myself up with the meat that would have costed a lot more! all the meat were rather kind of cooked well done. so they were dry and really hard to chew. my teeth got tired after the second round when i just gave up on getting any more meat. the only good one i would say was the bacon wrapped beef which would have been the only juicy one. service is meh. they seemed annoyed when some of us rejected their meat. tip* you can switch to the red color if your table has a lot of meat on their plate and want to stop them from coming to your table. it's kind of like a "do not disturb, i'm busy devouring my meat" card. probably wouldn't come back. too pricey for mediocre cooking of meat.

It's no Pampas in Palo Alto. What a nice concept but poorly executed. I did not imagine the dining area would be in the middle of the mall but I had it on my bookmarks so I was determined to try it. We waited for quite some time before anyone gave us plates and asked us what we'd like to drink. The salad bar was good. I went up a few times. There was this lamb thing, like stew that was delicious. The lamb was super tender. The tuna salad was also good. That was all I came up for.... walk through mall traffic to get to the salad bar from the dining area.The first round of bacon wrapped chicken was super dry. The second round was a lot better; the chicken was juicy but not flavorful. Really under-seasoned. The ham was salty. Most of the cuts of beef I tried were tough and over-cooked. Unlike Pampas (even the place I despise: Fogo de Chao), they would ask my preference: rare, medium, well done). This place did not ask... Service was friendly but I would not return.

Totally awkward eating in the middle of MBS. Meat is what you expect. The salad bar is JV to Fogo's, but it's worthy enough. If you need meat sweats while your at a biz conference, no worries. Carnivore is within reach.

Carnivore inside the MBS opened several weeks ago. I went here versus its other locations because I expected a top notch venue in the MBS and a great churrascaria experience, something one normally would not expect in Singapore. The actual experience could not have been more disappointing.Service= non-existent. We asked to be moved because for 10 minutes after seating, we were ignored completely. Then, after more minutes, we had to wave someone down to ask to order since no one was attending to us even after we asked to be moved because "we felt we were being ignored". We said this to the waitress but she did not act on this after she moved us. We ordered our caipirinhas and then waited again patiently for someone to come take our food order. Finally , someone did. The way the servers serve the various meat on the skewers was unusual. They stuck the entire skewer directly onto our plates instead of on their mini plates. There were no tongs for us to grab the meat slices, as would normally occur in a churrascaria. Instead, the entire skewer was placed on our plates and the large knife slicing the meat seemed to loom uncomfortably and dangerously just a few inches from my face. I had to move myself back in my chair to avoid being too close to the knives.We ordered the Pao de Queijo (Brazilian cheese bread) three times before it came. The first time we ordered it with a waitress who knew what it was and said it would be coming. After the food arrived with no bread, we asked the meat server who had no idea what that was. When I said it in English instead of Portuguese, "cheese bread", he still had no idea and left us to ask someone else. That other someone, another waitress, came by, and after repeating our order, she left not understanding what we wanted. Finally, the first waitress came with a basket of it and gave it to us. Sadly, the bread was overcooked, was hard at the bottom, and tasted nothing like Pao de Queijo should.The variety of the meats on offer was sparse- just 2-3 cuts of beef that were not flavorful, and a lot of non-beef meats, such as pork, chicken wrapped in bacon, etc. Overall, very disappointing quality of food.The decor of the place seemed sad and old, not modern and did not appear recently opened.  The spacing was tight and the buffet was in front of the diners at the entrance of the restaurant, blocking the view of the diners sitting inside from anything else but the buffet.The service continued to be non-existent throughout the meal.Our final bill with no wine was $160 for 2. As a churrascaria and as any normal restaurant, this is a big fail on all fronts.  The only exception was the caipirinha, which were reasonably priced and very good. We left very disappointed at the end of the evening.

Very good service with very witty staff who joked with us as we ordered. I had already eaten elsewhere and so ordered only a creme brûlée and my friend ordered a jug of lychee iced tea. The tea was refreshing for a hot summers day. We sat outdoors and enjoyed the music from the live band. They have live music from Tuesdays to Fridays according to a sign on their window.

Food was decent, a bit on the pricier side. Decor was really lovely, but it was a bit noisy on the inside, probably because of the huge rowdy party that was being held a few tables down. Perhaps they should have some private area specifically for parties as it was quite disruptive to the normal diners. Combined with the live music it was unbearably loud and my table were practically shouting at each other to be heard. Outside was a calmer atmosphere but was quite humid that day so would have been really warm.

Service - service is good and prompt. Manager was attentive to your "eye contact" and she will approach towards your table to ask if there were any help needed.Food - plenty of choices that you wldnt know which one to order, but overall taste was pleasant. Manager introduced orange and ice cream soda (something like that?) and it was awesome. My mum said it taste like "vintage" soda drink which she had seldom come across.Price - I find it was abit overpriced for the food ordered. 2mains, 2sides and 2drinks for 4pax and it was about $110?Atmosphere - we went during day time. So, the sun was kind glaring but it was fine.Overall, if you wish to dine in somewhere quiet and if you've got a car, do consider! :)

Met up with friends and we decided to check out Spruce. I loved how the old Firestation now looks like a swanky makan joint with their ceiling to floor glass walls. Some reviews shared that their service is not that great and in a way, that's kinda true. Ice water was only served when requested but after that, the servers were attentive enough to clear our plates and refill our water often. Between the few of us, we ordered:1) Clam Chowder - good amount of ingredients and the clams were juicy and big. Good!2) Steak Frites - a fairly thick slab of beef that is a pretty good cut too! Seared nicely outside and still juicy and tasty! Absolutely best!3) Spruce Burger - for $18, it's a very good serving size. The meat patty is very tender and accompanied with bacon, relish, onion, lettuce and somehow fragrant bun, total package of Yumz. Hubby loved loved loved this. 4) Salmon Steak - my friend had this and she said its nicely done to get a crispy exterior with a moist interior. Nice she said. The steak frites was costly at $36 but very nice lah. Definitely a place to pull my heart strings for a return trip. :)

The space is converted from a fire station, which has the high ceiling and industrial feel that comes with it. I have been here a few times and the food has certainly not been disappointing.One of their famous dishes is the beef burger, which is delicious. I feel that the burger is a little greasy, but it still is a feast for those who enjoy it.Tuna tartar is delicious as it comes with avocado and crispy bread. It is a good starter for sharing.Dessert is surprisingly great, with their double chocolate cake. You might want to give it a try to satisfy your sweet cravings. Since it is so great, why am I only giving 3 stars? I guess the service is nothing out of spectacular and the price tag that comes with the taste of the food, I guess it is also not spectacular. And it takes you to drive or take a cab to get to such an out of the way restaurant as well.
Eating in a former Fire station -- pretty cool !Relaxed atmosphere, good food, decent pricing (although not cheap) for quality, trendy.Recommended, will probably return.See pictures

Spruce, in my opinion, is your average yuppy brunch joint. There's nothing bad about that but there's also nothing special that would make me eat there repeatedly. Whether it's at Tanglin or the Firestation. It was an average to decent dining experience that I'm writing this review about 2 months later.The decor is reminiscent of a NY loft or some of the restaurants at Dempsey. It's set in a relatively quite fire station as you head towards Upper Bukit Timah. It's not difficult to get seats on a weekend or a public holiday so I guess that's a plus if you're going with the 'rents who don't like waiting. We tried the Spruce burger, the benny's and pancakes. I could really sum it up as not bad but not great. So there. Can't really add much because the experience was that non-descript.

Really lovely place with a great vibe. Menu wise it is still already with choices of things such as Eggs Benedict, breakfast set with Choice of Eggs, Sausage, bread and others. Food taste great, for me I had the Crab Cake Eggs Bennie. Definitely a place I would go to just to relax and have a nice meal.
Good food, thats where it ends... If you're okay with that then go for it... Not the place to go if your in a bad mood...

Here's the quickie: mediocre-slightly good food, coffee shop ambiance, service with a scowl, but very friendly patrons. The location on Scott's Road is much nicer however the food there made me sick last time. Btw, the hot chocolate at s$7 is real authentic dark chocolate cocoa (semi-sweetened), albeit slightly expensive.

I love having breakfast as an option anytime of the day so Wild Honey wins me over just based on that alone.I think since they opened another outlet at Scotts Square not too far away, the crowd here has lessened, came here on a friday evening just before dinner and didn't have to queue.For such pricey food, I'd expect to at least have a waiter take my order while I'm seated instead of going to the counter myself to order.You get ushered to your seat and then you have to order at the counter where there's a picture menu on a ipad you can scroll through to make your decision. Was feeling like ordering healthy with my partner so we chose salmon dishes - he had the scandinavian (grilled salmon on potato rosti) and I had the norwegian (poached eggs with salmon and asparagus). The norwegian was a very hearty dinner, 2 servings on the poached egg and salmon on top of generous thick brioche and a nice detail of salmon roe on top.The scandinavian was slightly bland, but there's salt rock and pepper on your table for you to season it yourself to your liking, it just needed that little bit of pepper.Final verdict: I'd only come here when I crave for exotic breakfasts during dinner, other than that, not really worth the high price.

This store has a very homely atmosphere as the cafe comprises a mix of armchairs, normal chairs and benches. Its other outlet is newly opened at Scotts Square!The Norwegian is highly recommended with its generous portions and solid ingredients. The fresh sweet smoked salmon is paired with ikura, grilled asparagus and two poached eggs, and drenched with well-made hollandaise sauce and served on two thick whole-wheat challah brioche.The Tunisian ($18) which is distinctively Middle Eastern is a must-try here. It consists of Shashouka, and its basic ingredients consist of a thick spicy tomato stew cooked in a skillet. A few eggs are then poached in the tomato stew and it's served piping hot with some salad and fresh bread.

When i first arrived there, i was taking some time to decide on what to eat. I ordered English Breakfast. Portion looks small at first but it was really filling. Moreover, fod is abit overpriced.I would have to say the service at wild honey was really bad. Even when i asked for an extra plate, the waitress gave me an attitude.I mean like after hearing so many review on wild honey, no doubt the food is nice. But with the service provided there, i seriously doubt i will be back again for their food.

Great breakfast / brunch food! So many amazing options it's a real struggle to decide. The English Breakfast was the popular choice at my brunch on Sunday, and everyone was satisfied (and stuffed) after eating it. The toast was thick and fluffy, scrambled eggs perfectly done (not too runny, not at all dry).I chose the Californian which had a healthy-but-still-yummy feel. The tofu gave the scramble a nice creamy texture (if you like tofu, that is!). Also tried the Sweet Morning which was delicious and not too sweet. French toast slices were nice and thick.The table got some donuts to share which had raspberry filling. Good fluffy donuts, not overwhelmed by the filling. We were all just too full from our mains to finish them...Only downside was the timing of the service... meals arrived spread out over the course of 20 (or more?) minutes. One friend received her french toast at least 10 minutes before anyone else got their food, and my dish arrived 10 minutes after everyone else had already been served. Made for a very disjointed meal. But, have to say the food was good enough to make me want to come back. Maybe I'll just try a different location next time, and hope we fair better!

I came here for Sunday brunch with some friends and honestly, I was super excited! I wanted to see what all the hype was about. I ordered the special (some potatoes with pastrami and poached eggs with hollandaise sauce)... My husband ordered the steak sandwich and both were pretty disappointing. They meals were lack luster and everyone in the group felt like the food was just okay... Like it missed the mark. Also the waiter told us that from the moment we are seated we have 90 minutes to order, eat, and leave. Wtheck is that about? I've never heard of that before. Oh yea, the vinyasa juice was good so I guess that counts for something!

I love breakfast food.  Just not for breakfast because I don't really eat breakfast, I eat brunch on occasion, just not breakfast.  So, in my quest for a place to have good breakfast food, I discovered Wild Honey.  My process for making the decision to go to a new restaurant is actually quite intense and I do a fair amount of research which involves looking at reviews, yelp and others, blogs, and the restaurant website.  As I took a look at the website for the restaurant (which is very well designed, bravo - you can tell a lot about a place by the attention to detail on the website) I realized there are actually two locations and they both do not offer the same menu, there are some differences, which I didn't particularly like because it added another decision I had to make.  Ugh, decisions.  I am fairly decisive when it comes to work, but when it comes to my personal life that is a completely different story.So, we go to the Mandarin Gallery location.  It is packed, and the wait time at 3 pm on a Saturday for two people is about 30 mins, but they give us the option to sit at the bar area and we take it because we can be seated immediately.  We go in, sit down, gulp down some water, and then go back to the front counter to place our orders.  The week we went they were offering the crab cakes Benedict special, which is called something else I can't quite remember now, so, my husband, true to form orders that and I finally decide on the English breakfast.  Both turn out to be pretty good choices.  As someone that was raised in Maryland, which is known for Chesapeake Bay, blue crabs and all cuisine which involve them, I am quite the discerning crab cake connoisseur and actually can't say the crab cakes were what made the meal, but it was good.  The English Breakfast was very good and I highly recommend that to anyone that finds themselves in a situation where they just simply can not decide.  In addition to our two entrees, I ordered a caramel latte.  It was a little too sweet for my taste, but that didn't stop me from drinking it.  Just be prepared for the level of sweetness if you order it.    I am not sure if we will go back again, there are so many restaurants to visit in Singapore, but we did enjoy our dining experience and suggest to anyone looking for a good place to have breakfast/brunch food make a stop at Wild Honey (Mandarin Gallery).  Can not say anything about the other location.Also, note, if you plan to take away your food because you have leftovers, they do not allow you to take your eggs.

So I've been on a search for a good plate of Eggs Benedict in Singapore. I like my perfectly poached egg with the whites soft and pillowy, the yolk nice and runny. You'd be surprised the number of times I've ordered poached eggs in Singapore with high hopes, only to discover my egg whites rubbery and the yolks are mushy. The hollandaise sauce has to be creamy but not stick to your stomach cream. Its gotta have a little runny-ness to it. I ordered the Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon at Wild Honey and requested a perfectly poached egg of soft pillowy whites and runny yolk. I was pleasantly surprised to find that they did it right. I enjoyed the dish and had a pleasant experience here while I typed away working on my computer (had a deadline). The iced tea I ordered was also delicious. Not too big a fan of the prices but whatevs, its Orchard road area, service was decent, and ambience was eclectic homey.

Comparing Wild Honey to Clinton Street Baking Company back home, I'll say this: The waits at CB are longer and the food is better.However, I happen to be one of those people who have no trouble rising a bit early (these days, in fact, it's mandatory) and I always manage to snag a table with a 15-20 minute wait. I'll let you in on a secret; if you get there by 10:30 the wait times tend to be shorter than they state. If you end up here later, wait times are long but you don't have to line up or wait in the sun.. just take a stroll through the mall until you get a call from the guys at the restaurant.I will say that the Wild Honey at Scotts Road is bigger and has more character than this one, but traffic has a way of adjusting itself. My wait times have been consistent between the 2 locations, and the food tastes nearly identical.I like that the menu items are organized by the country/region they are inspired from, and then Wild Honey does a fun little take on it. The food is closer to a tradional breakfast than a whimsy one, but they manage to keep it exciting. One of my favourite things to get here is the Tunisian (made veggie) - spicy shakshouka served with bread and salad. The eggs are nicely done, with runny yolks, the taste is spot on, even though the accompanying bread and salad are a bit of a disappointment. If your tastebuds are craving a good old kick in the nuts, try the spicy mex burrito. The portobello road, which is a modified eggs florentine, has decent flavours as well but is a bit more monotonous. Among the sweeter offerings, you could try the Belgian - which is a tropical country's take on the waffle. The texture of the waffle itself is a bit chewy but the flavours work so nicely together. At Scotts Road they have the Caribbean waffle with passionfruit, which is lovely as well. They have an adequate menu of coffee and milkshakes etc, but with their portion sizes I'd advise you to share the heavier beverages. The only thing that I found completely ridiculous is that they charge 10$ for Orange Juice!! And I even found a pip in mine the first and last time I ordered it.Service has usually been presented with a smile, and they are child friendly. Go enjoy!

We had the Tunisian and the Parisienne. The Tunisian was a spicy tomato stew served in a small skillet with merguez sausage and a couple of eggs on top with toast on that side. It was good but small. I was still hungry afterwards. The Parisian was kind of like a croque monseiur in that there was a soggy sandwich with cheese and ham in the middle, then it was topped with two eggs and I think Hollandaise sauce. It felt like a variation on eggs benedict. I went there with a Korean girl from the countryside and she felt right at home because its ambiance is similar to cutesy kitsch coffee shops with lounge chairs. I really wanted a fresh squeezed orange juice but I didn't want to pay $9 for it.

I really want to like this place, but I can't. It's like one of those -- oh, it's so great, or it should be, but it's not -- type of places.It has got EVERYTHING right which is why it's so frustrating. An awesome space that makes you feel warm and happy immediately. A good vibe. An innovative concept. Something that nobody else had. At least when it started.The food is okay. That's the problem: it's not amazing. It should be. I wish it was.I also don't want to queue so much for something that isn't amazing, especially on weekends. Sigh.

The original outlet in Mandarin Gallery, this branch of Wild Honey gets insanely crowded over the weekend and evenings and you can't make reservations here, pfft! If you do manage to get a seat in this small outlet, then you can enjoy a nice meal in a homey cottage-like setting.Wild Honey serves up breakfasts from all around the world, and I usually end up getting the English or Parisienne because I like me some eggs, but my friends rave about the Tunisian. You have to order at the counter which is equipped with spiffy ipad menus so you can see pix of what you're ordering. The pastries and desserts on the side also always look absolutely delectable!It's not the cheapest, but it does serve up pretty good food and service is friendly, but I'd pick a very off-peak hour to come here because I'm not queuing up for hours just to get in...

Located at mandarin gallery, this restaurant is well known for its all day breakfast menu. It is one of the upmarket all day breakfast and you would have guess the food is on the pricey side. During high tea hours , the queue can get extremely long and I was there once where the waitress informed me the waiting time is 1 hour. The interior design has a woody touch, giving a homely feeling. The food comes in different type of cuisine menu. For example the European style, Mediterranean style and many others which you have to see from the ordering counter.Personally I would recommend the European , it is served with bacon, poached eggs and sandwiches. Try to avoid the flower tea as it tastes like syrup water. In all, this place does serve quality food and great ambience , but if you are on a tight budget you might want to visit food for thought or the hatched for a all day breakfast fix.

Wild Honey is an all day breakfast joint. It has a nice and cozy feel, the staff are super friendly and the food is decent but honestly, they place is WAY TOO overrated. There is almost always a wait for a table and you would think that would mean it was a fantastic place to eat. Dont get me wrong, the food is good. but SO NOT worth the money that you pay. $22 for two pieces of french toast? or $25 for 2 eggs and bread? or a $20 sandwich? You feel like you are being ripped off. Portions can be pretty stingy as well. Wish i could give them more stars, but honestly way too much money for dishes that are so simple.

Planning for Wild Honey was like planning for an overseas trip. I went to a lot of food blogs to ogle at the pictures. It was glorious - the amount of eggs and sausages and all towering on the plates, of course my expectations went waaaay up.Upon reaching the place, we saw this long list of country names scrawled on blackboards - why do ALL new and upcoming restaurants love using blackboards as their menus these days ah? But anyways, there was an iPad at the counter, allowing you to swipe and check out what each breakfast set looks like. Not very helpful not very fast, especially since we were a group of 8 people. Luckily I already knew what I wanted. The English breakfast set.It was okay - very fulfilling, with emphasis on FILLING, small wonder that some of my friends found it too oily and heavy. The music that was playing then was kind of headache-y, it sounded like the repetitive null and heavy beats that Inception has towards the end of the movie when all the dreams fall apart.They don't take reservations by the way.

I keep thinking that it's a nice place to have a quiet breakfast date with myself and then am surprised when I show up. It's a breakfast place, but not quiet by any stretch of the imagination--it's not so much the crowd at the time I go (but by 10am 70% of the tables are occupied, with a mix of tourists, business people, and ladies who erm brunch) but the music. So it's not so much a place for a quiet reflective start to the day, more a place to fuel up--and what a place! Round the world in eighty-eggs, with an assortment of creative drinks, both alcoholic and non. Try not to think of how you can make most of the egg dishes yourself at home, and you'll be just fine.

Like others had commented, the egg Benedict was delicious as well as the coconut waffle. Unfortunately the portion is small. Maybe I am used to the American portion even though I'm currently in Singapore. Price wise it is also a little high as it is located in a more expensive mall. Will probably drop by again next time :)

This was one of my favorite brunch places in Singapore before I gave up on them after too many service snafus and general service arrogance.Over the course of over a half-dozen visits, my major complaints:1) Wish they would allow for sides of eggs, so that it is possible to order pancakes with eggs. 2) They take your name and estimate the time, but will seat out-of-order to maximize table use. So, my 2-person party kept getting pushed as multiple 4-person parties would put their names down and were seated before us. Forty-five minute wait become almost 2 hours on one occasion.

I really enjoy the food here. Ive had a hard time finding good brunch places and I find their food to be inventive and good. Its not the MOST original but its served up well and is very tasty. I loved the tunisian and the mexican. They serve up good coffee but its not really the reason to come. I do admit the lines can get long and they dont take reservations. The service isnt stellar but you have to go up and order your food anyways. The staff is nice but one thing I noticed is that you cant just sit and enjoy coffee and conversation after youre done. They pretty much come by and ask you to leave if you take to long. Not exactly the most welcome feeling.  But really you come here for the food in a nice comfy setting.

Love it ....This place offers a wide variety of Breakfast style ..... Late wakers like me still get to taste awesome brunch at any time of the day.My Girlfriends treat me Brunch for my Birthday and i heard lots rave about this place. 3 of us order 4 dishes to share as its our 1st time visit. Sounds greedy ya.I couldn't really recall the name of the dish we ordered but when the food is served we are amazed by the portion as its really big.... 3 ladies + 1 young kid finish all the food and its really yummy. The table were alittle to small for us to place our food.Please do note that its alittle cramp so pls do not go with big groups like 4 to 8 pax.Been there twice till date, can't wait for my 3rd visit .....

This is an outstanding place.  3rd time yesterday. The food and the service never disappoints. Have tried quite a few things on the menu- Flinder's Lane,  Norwegian,  Parisienne, the French Toast,  coffee. Always have the Languedoc wine with breakfast and love it. Family came to Singapore and took them there. They loved it. The Norwegian -  poached eggs with salmon was just out of the world.

Ordered the English and I have to say... That breakfast was packed. I particularly enjoyed the Kurobata sausage, Canadian bacon, eggs, mushrooms and toasted potatoes! The plate also contains two brioche, baked beans and half a tomato which I could do without. The 4-star rating is basically for that awesome sausage. Must-try!

Wild Honey does a great breakfast, no matter what time of the day you visit. This is just fabulous for not-so-early birds like me, who can't get enough of their Caribbean waffles, eggs benedict, or Norwegian smoked salmon bundles. I think they cater to the true Foodie, who has a soft spot for rustic comfort food, yet craves that extra little je ne sais quois. The only downside I have ever experienced with this chain is their sub-par customer service, long lines (but you can make reservations at Scotts!), and inordinate prices. Perhaps if the waitstaff were more attentive, I wouldn't feel as bad hashing out so much dough for breakfast...but they're not, so don't expect to be waited on courteously or promptly. If you're just there for the nosh, then you're all set!

Met up friends for brunch at Wild Honey but we couldn't book a table so we had to wait in the queue. But the good thing is they would text us when the table was ready so we could walk nearby to do more sightseeing of Orchard Road.There are a range of Western breakfast from around the world - English, European, Tunisian, Italian, Mexican..etc. As well as sweet and savoury dishes to suit whatever taste buds you have that day.I had the egg benedit which was okay but not as good to what I can get in London. I thought the other dishes such as the Tunisian was more interesting. But I found it spicy and not my preference to kick start the day with fire!I had the grapefruit juice with my breakfast. It was refreshing and a nice alternative to having the usual orange or apple juice.Overall I think it is a nice concept to have breakfast from around the globe.

Breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Sadly, it's a meal most of us go without. The solution? All day breakfast! Their meals range from the traditional eggs and bacon to salads to steak sandwiches, and don't forget the coffees. The quality of food is pretty decent. All that you would expect from a cozy restaurant located in a higher-end mall.  Oh and if you prefer your toast thick, then you've come to the right place. However, if you can cook a half decent egg on toast, then you might want to give Wild Honey a miss. $20 for eggs on toast isn't my cup of tea. Just a heads up. Expect to wait at least 15 minutes for a seat if you come on weekends.

5 of us + 3 year old boy went for brunch on the last Sunday of 2014. Had reservations so were seated promptly. 2 of us shared the following:-EnglishBfast- Scrambled eggs, back bacon, Cumberland pork sausage, sautéed mushrooms, baked beans, breakfast potatoes, grilled tomato & brioche. Everything was delicious esp. the eggs which I usually find quite "heavy" after a while but found these to be "light" although still very tasty. Breakfast Hangover-Scrambled eggs, back bacon, roasted pearl tomatoes, Swiss cheese & spicy tomato chutney on grilled ciabatta with breakfast potatoes - tasty!Also shared a starter which had fried "sticks" of goat cheese - very tasty.My flat white was just perfect as well. We all also had a couple of glasses of sauvignon blanc each which went very well with our meal.Extra star is for the good service and de rigueur bustling brunch vibe.

I had brunch here once and I loved the concept of this place where they try to replicate breakfast meals of different countries such as American breakfast, English breakfast etc. It is breakfast dishes inspired me from the west. But it works because it has a good variety of choices. I had the Spanish hash and I loved it! Although I found it a little pricey I still enjoyed my experience there.

This place is pretty fantastic! Being American, I sometimes just miss traditional breakfast food from home. I ordered the Belgian waffles with coconut cream and grilled mango- perfection! I also loved the ambiance of this place, very cozy feel. The only downside is that I wanted to order a side of scrambled eggs and of course because it isn't "on the menu" they could not accommodate me, even though I could see other dishes contained scrambled eggs in them. Pretty typical of Singapore, pretty hard to get things customized or get people to think outside of the box. But, overall, very positive experience! Be ready to pay though, for two of us the bill totaled 71 SGD.

So, I made a pact with myself when I arrived in Singapore that I would not have any western food while there. My friend convinced me that if I didn't have breakfast here I would regret it. I tell you what....he was right. I had the Parisianne breakfast. Three thick cut pieces of ham and cheese stuffed toast with a hollendaise over it. That wasn't even the best part. My friend had the Hangover Sandwich. I tell you what I never seen a croissant loaded so well.  My buddy had ordered a side of bacon. When it came out it wasn't the two or three pieces that that the US usually has but a literally boat dish full of fresh cut bacon. The only down side of the experience was it took forever to get our coffees. The decor is great. I loved how comfortable the chairs were. The furniture was more chic hipster than traditional which made the whole place jive well.

The food is decent, but they Nickel and Dime you for every thing. Ice water is $1. Coffee is $5 and there are no refills. Also the menu is really inflexible. Aside from the 8 sides listed, you cannot add anything else. As a girl who loves breakfast options, and was in search of something reminiscent of an American brunch experience, I'd pass. If you want to be overcharged for ok food, go for it.
Good food good service good ambience.  The salad we had was a wee bit too sweet for our liking otherwise all good.  Heading back again next Tuesday.

Good brunch place in Orchard. British-style brunch options - our favorite is the classic English breakfast - a simple dish but well-executed. We also like the pancake overall despite being slightly too sweet. Coffee was so-so. Ambience is nice / lively and a good family/friend brunch option

Of the many restaurants in the Mandarin Gallery building (Mandarin Orchard hotel) in Singapore, Wild Honey stood out - with its buzzing atmosphere and delectable brunch menu - this is a good spot to enjoy brunch. Not many restaurants in Singapore served champagne and this one had Taittinger on its list which was positive. I had the European breakfast - essentially poached eggs, prosciutto ham & grilled mushrooms on toasted brioche topped with hollandaise sauce. A glass of champagne + breakfast + cappuccino came up to SG$55 so it wasn't cheap but go ahead and treat yourself!

Go early in the morning if u wanna skip the lines. Breakfast is over priced and the food quality has decreased over the years. I like their eggs benedict but so far the menu has stayed the same over the span of 7 years.... not impressed. Still a cozy place to catch up with friends over breakfast

The Italian ($24 after GST and service charge) - 3 starsThe portion is fairly small - I was surprised when it arrived with just one slice of ciabatta. It filled my stomach, but I wasn't too hungry to begin with. There was barely any buffalo mozzarella on it, but ample mushrooms and artichoke. The Italian salad that came with it fit into a tiny ramekin - one you'd use for holding ketchup or a sauce.Like I've probably mentioned in my review for the outlet at Scotts Square, I like it for the ambience. I love the quirky furniture and plush armchairs. But it's a much better brunch place at least for me. It's a bit too dark for my liking at night and almost all the items on the menu contain poached or scrambled eggs, salads, or sandwiches, which I seldom crave for dinner. Having said that, the prices are more suited for dinner.

My favourite go-to place. Never leave this place dissatisfied. MUST GET THE ICED LATTE! I feel the need to take a photo/video every time as the coffee comes in little ice cubes then you pour the milk ontop. It will leave you speechless. Their menu is huge with so many options so no matter what you are in the mood for you are most likely going to find it. Their English breakfast is a nice twist to a traditional one, really nice sausage choice. The Canadian waffles are to die for. Must go!! 10/10.

I've had brunch and breakfast-for-dinner here a few times, and I love the wide range of breakfast plates they have.I've had the English, Canadian, and Norwegian, and I absolutely love the English brekkie. I am very impressed by their very own baked beans that don't come out of a can, unlike most places.I wouldn't recommend the Norwegian, just because the eggs are iffy and get cold very quickly. It's sort of overpriced for just two strips of smoked salmon enveloping two eggs on very thick-cut toast. When it gets cold, the toast feels like cardboard with the weird, cold yolk/sauce on it. Canadian - not everyone loves the sweet-and-salty combination, but I do! Pancakes and bacon - yes yes yes!My pet peeve on the weekend is the excruciating waiting time for brunch, so go on a weekday for dinner, and book a place online on the webpage. Eat well, and expect to pay!

Great range of all day breakfast available! I personally tried the Tunisan all day breakfast with a Vanilla milkshake on the side.The portion was huge considering i came straight for a lunch without breakfast I still felt sufficiently full. ;) Milkshake was great as well, it was made just nice and  not overly thick. Will definitely be coming back sometime in the not so distant future for the English all day breakfast! ;)

I can't say I'm impressed with the prices coz it really isn't cheap.  But the deserts and drinks are quite good and clever.  I just cannot wrap my head around matching the prices and menu items.   But if nothing else, the ambience is sublime!  nice get away from the heat and sit down for a cold beverage before getting onto orchard again.

Wild Honey in Mandarin Gallery is one of these places that seems to be extremely popular with a lot of people and when I finally visit I can just not really get what all the fuss is about. The focus is on all-day breakfast and that is something I am a fan of - we were however here early in the morning as we were meeting friends who have kids waking up early. That also fits well with us believing they do not take reservations, apparently they do that now (they previously only done it at their other location but now also here)The style of the place is very much that I would expect to see in an American franchise of restaurants but at least we had comfortable seats. When I started browsing the menu I did find a  lot of things that sounded interesting. The concept of having different types of breakfast menus from around the world is a good one. I tried the English with scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages, mushrooms, breakfast potatoes, grilled tomato and brioche.It was also coming with beans but I asked if it could removed and that they could add something extra of the other things - response was that it was not possible to add anything but they would try to remove it but could not promise. Still decided to go for it and that was a mistake. Bacon was soggy, scrambled eggs felt pre-made and the mushrooms and tomatoes did not feel fresh. Sausages and brioce were however ok. Others around the table were more happy but cannot for sure say if it was a result of lower standards or better food but I will admit that the Canadian looked good.For the coffee I ordered a French press and it took forever and then it appeared on the table. My first question was how long it should still brew (when to press it down and pour into the cup) - waitress was just looking at my as if was crazy and said it does not matter and this had been standing around for a while. I tried explaining to her that coffee may taste differently depending on how long it actually is brewed but just got the response that she does not drink coffee. I tasted it and it was just so over-extracted and bitter so it was undrinkable. Had to send it back and instead asked for a cappuccino - that was actually pretty good.We also sampled some of the pastries and those were better but nothing special. In general I was not very impressed by food nor service and then taking into account it is hugely busy and prices are a bit higher than other brunch places I cannot really see any good reason to visit again unless I am dragged here with friend.

Well loved by everyone, need me say more? The food is good though I'm always pretty disappointed with their eggs benedict cos the egg yolk dont flow! :( But overall taste is good and servings are HUGE. I can never finish a set on my own.Compared to their other outlet at Scotts Square, this original outlet is a lot smaller and tables are really close. The last evening my friends and i were there, we could hear 2 guys talk about molecular science topics so passionately beside us. While we werent really entertained (sorry, molecular science isnt really our cup of tea) but we were very happy that they actually found each other having such great interest in a topic that few would really like to talk about over dinner. Isnt that sweet! :)They also have a new queue system now so you could key in the no. of pax into this tablet at the entrance of the restaurant, leave your name and contact no and you will receive a e-queue no via your HP. Instead of having to wait at the door, you can roam ard the mall till you receive the phone call when your table is available.Till the day i finish all the breakfasts on the menu, every dining experience will be an adventure!

Food is so so only.The long black I had is very bitter and acidic. Same for the cappuccino.The poached eggs on the Portobello are over-cooked. The yolk is more or less solid and not gooey.Music is too loud, not able to hold a decent conversation at all.

I was eager to try this wine bar due to the other reviews I had read. I was sorely disappointed. I went on a Friday night. As a single diner, I love sitting at the bar. However, I was told I couldn't sit at the bar because they were using it to put things on there and to clean. Really? And, I saw it was covered with things and stuff. That should have been my first sign. I decided to sit inside anyways in front of the lovely wine cellar. I asked the waiter what was good on the menu and felt he didn't know the menu too well as he stumbled for explanations. I ordered a glass of Pinot (it needed to open up greatly) and one of the savory tarts flambé. I patiently waited for this as I listened to the children (!) from a few tables over scream and run back and forth to the door. That wasn't the relaxing dining experience I was looking for after having a 14-hr work day. My tart finally came and it was dry and lacked the savoriness I expected. I ate it and paid the check. For $42 SG, it was not worth the food nor the experience. Hence, I went to another place to have a proper dinner as I left hungry.

Farther off Robertson Quay is Rodyk Street, which was for a bit, a hipster spot (thanks to Toby's Estate). Even though i used to frequent this spot, i've not noticed Verre, formerly a wine bar hidden behind dark and heavy drapes. Thankfully, after a relaunch, Verre Modern Bistro and Wine Bar has lost all that darkness and brought light, and great food to its mix. The new direction cannot be a better choice really. With their expertise in wine (they have over 750 labels of fine wine mainly from Bordeaux and Burgundy), Verre is able to provide great pairings with their Modern French dishes created by Chef Consultant Masashi Horiuchi (who also manages Shelter in the Woods). We had an extensive night of food and wine pairings, something easily done since one could have over 30 wines by the glass with your food choice.A good start to a meal at Verre would be the creamy Chicken Liver Parfait ($24) paired with a reduction of port wine, madeira wine shallot, balanced with a tangy mandarin orange jelly and a dehydrated honeycomb-like mandarin orange. This was paired with a dry lemon lime Paringa Estate Riesling 2012 ($19.50). The Half Lobster Salad ($38) features a sweet Maine lobster cooked in court bouillon, with a creamy guacamole and a refreshing calamansi and honey dressing. I would order this dish for the sweet and tangy dressing! The wine pairing was the Stick Chardonnay 2013 ($18) with flavors of grapefruit, white peach, citrus and oak spice.I loved the Black Garlic Soup ($19), which was made with a white wine chicken stock and black garlic. That clove of roasted black garlic was icing on the cake and gave the soup a slightly tangy sweet preserved plum flavor. We had the dark fruity Massalino Dolcette D Alba 2013 ($18) to go with this.The Pan-seared Scallops with Sweet Corn ($38) was an absolute stunner. The corn flavor was immensely intense and the pickled konbu gave the dish an umami lift.Onto the bigger dishes. I'm not a fan of the Seafood Papillote ($30) of oven baked seafood. It was a little too bland for my liking though that toasted dill bread with gruyere was perfect for mopping up the stock. Do not go away without having some of that gorgeous Suckling Pig ($42) done 2 ways. One part slow roasted for 4 - 5h and braised with spices; and another slow braised for 12h with a tangy Asian marinade of orange, honey, and spice. Give me a bun and make me a slider out of this pulled pork mix with Iberico ham and pickled onions already!I was extremely pleased with the meat selection at Verre. The Fillet of Wagyu Beef ($62) can have my body and soul. Just look at that pink flesh (best enjoyed slightly rare)! And hand over that umami American potato truffle fries, seasoned with truffle shavings and truffle oil. I'm sure there's some soy sauce in there somehow. No bottled ketchup here by the way. We'll go with the homemade mushroom ketchup made with madeira wine and pickled mushrooms. Have this with the classic full bodied Massolino Barolo 2010 ($32) and you'd be in cow heaven. After that heavy meal, I was grateful for the light refreshing desserts. I enjoyed the deconstructed Apple Mille-Feuille ($16) A LOT. We had apple in all forms- macerated apple with lemon juice, sorbet, compote, and caramelized, with layers of caramalised filo pastry and vanilla custard cream flavored with Calvados. That cream THAT CREAM!! The dessert wine award goes to the Caprilli Moscadello ($15), a silky and refreshing drink which was sweet but light enough.Other hits include the Saint-Honore ($10) filled with the mind blowing vanilla pastry cream and chantilly! The Canele ($4) was pretty good too but could be more crisp. Certainly one of the better ones because I

It's hard to believe that I'm the first to review Verre, as it's in a very popular hood and it is a fantastic wine bar.  The room is beautiful and spacious and very roomy.  Definitely a lot quieter and more intimate than some of the larger places like Wine Connection.  It's also a bit different as it offers some formal main courses, but first let's talk about the wine.While their by the glass choices are decent, around 6-8 whites and same for reds, their deep by the bottle offerings are the real star of the show.  In particular, they had a solid offering of French, both Bordeaux and Burgundies, and many are quite reasonably priced.  By biggest pet peeve however is that our Bordeaux arrived cold!  OK, it wasn't ice cold, but still colder than ideal and with some condensation, so that was annoying.  The by the glass selections did not have such an issue.As for the food, don't miss out on the tarte flambe.  These are basically flatbreads, but much better.  Loved the savory toppings, and we ordered a swecond one as a starter too.  The entrees are interesting.  The beef bourguignon was very good - super tender morsels of beef in a super rich stew.  But why are the mashed potatoes so gummy?  The duck and steak frites looked delicious, while the salmon looked good but a bit small.Overall, Verre has a lot going for it. I would definitely go back for some wine and tarte flambes.  There are a few miscues, such as bottles being refrigerated too much and the gooey mess of a mashed potato.  But I applaud them for their ambitious menu, and with a few tweaks, they could be even better.

Solid spot.  Headed over to have dinner with a friend on Friday night, and it def. did not disappoint.  Solid service, nice atmosphere, and good food.  We had a bottle of SB, which was decent (I'm not a SB fan, but I didn't want to hurt my dining partners feelings) and started with the asparagus and melon app, both were excellent.  The asparagus came with salmon which was different, but very tasty.  I had the scallop dish which was excellent.  He had some kind of meat dish that just looked okay.  All in all, a solid dining experience, good date night, or just quick drink.

Singapore does have many wine bars but not really an abundance of wine bars with good selection of wines at decent prices. Verre does in that sense fill a gap, and a bit surprisingly (perhaps not in having a good wine selection but decent prices seldom goes hand in hand with this area) it is in a rather touristy and expat heavy area.This bar/restaurant is located along Robertson Quay and has both nice outdoor seating area as well as a fairly large dining room. It has never been very busy when I have been here so have always been able to get a seat without reservations. Service has always been friendly and fast so a big plus for that.The wine selection is pretty good, I counted 8 reds and 8 whites by the glass and 1 sparkling. Very decent prices and for their happy hour it is really good (from 4-7 pm on weekdays and 4-6pm on weekends) with buy 1 get 1 free offer on the wines by the glass and some beers. Their champagne by the glass is for example the excellent Guy Charlemagne Brut (for a review of thier 2008 check out thewinecurious.wordpress…) and at 18 SGD for 2 glasses it is excellent value for money.The selection of wines by the bottle is also good, a lot from France but also from other parts of the world. Prices are pretty good as well so really a pleasant experience.They do also have a full food menu. I have had the food and it is not bad but also not something very special. I mainly come here for the fine but occassionally also eat here and have never been really disappointed but also never really escited about it either. Expect pastas and other European dishes on the me u.Overall this is one of my favorite places for wine in Singapore.

Since my last review, I must have been here 30 more times. This is my second home from 6-7pm most days :-)The staff is amazing, the wine selection is great (especially if you go for the fancy cellar), and the location is perfect--right on the river. And the happy hour prices are unbeatable!
Superb great service! Good job Manager! Keep it up.Great wine selection though the prices are slightly on the high.

So my Brit-mates sprung me a surprise visit in Singapore on a Tuesday - and they were flying out on a Wednesday! That warranted much worry as it meant I had only 16 hours to show them how awesome Singapore was. I initiated them to my lovely home country with an epic night-out in the BING style ... and kick-started my chain of bar/club-hopping with OverEasy - the first place which came to my mind!OverEasy is definitely my favourite chill-out bar in downtown Marina Bay. It is lovely both indoors (with a live DJ on most nights ... darkish romantic ambience) and outdoors. The crowd is a right mix of local and expat yuppies (the crowd DOES contribute a lot to a place's ambience and 'feel'). Get a table (there are couches or high tables) outdoors ... and sip your cocktail or wine while admiring the magnificent Marina Bay Sands. Be here at either 8:00PM or 09:30PM daily to catch MBS' light and wonder show from the comfort of your couch/stool (my touristy friends were quite in awe)!Drinks are priced quite decently as well. Good place to have a civilised drinks catch-up with friends before hitting Butterfac next door!

I was really disappointed by this place. I went here to get a hotdog which I was really looking forward to, but the bread was stale and was generally a let down. I asked for regular fries, but got truffle fries which I hate. Also, I saw a few cockroaches running around which was rather surprising as I've never seen a cockroach in Singapore before. But I guess at least they enjoyed the food. If you're looking for a hotdog NEVER go here, I'm sure their other food isn't so bad though, we also had chicken wings which were pretty decent. Their cocktails are actually pretty yummy too. If it wasn't for them this place would get 0 stars.

This cool joint is perfect to start your clubbing night (Hipster Butter Factory is just next door) or a great place to enjoy the view of Marina Bay at night. Opt for the outside seats - it may be a little more humid but it's easier to hold a conversation and airier to boot.The bar grub is good - my favourite is the famous cheese steak sliders which are small and 2-bite-sized. Food in general is also quite nice, though one might feel the more breakfast like food seems a bit pricey...Still, I'd recommend this to anyone who wants a nice night out with friends and beer!

I will admit that OverEasy provides welcome respite and clean toilets from the uncomfortable crowds converging for butter factory. However, I really like OverEasy for its great ambience and the amazing al fresco seating area that overlooks the water, with a lovely breeze blowing through at times.The tunes they play here at are also pretty chilled out or funky. Very comfortable with the vibes here. Staff are attentive, even f they are sometimes a little slow.I've not eaten much here, but is tried the mini sliders here and they are pretty good! A juicy chunk of meat cooked to a medium rare perfection is nestled in between the buns. I'd definitely recommend coming here for a pre-party, post-dinner drink with friends.

One of the main draws of Overeasy is its location. Apart from the fact that it's conveniently located near Butter Factory, making it the ideal pre-drinking spot for those who can afford it, it has a wonderful sea-front view, facing straight into MBS (so obviously you get all the sights around it too).They have a great selection of alcohol to boot, collecting some favourites from around the world. One of my favourites is the Little Creatures pale ale, which isn't stocked at many places (I picked this taste up from The Plain, of all places).Overeasy also do surprisingly good food. I know their burger comes highly recommended, as do their slides, especially when the market closes below a certain index (then they go for $1!). I went for lunch once and enjoyed the breeze as I dug into the most perfect bowl of truffle mac and cheese with mushrooms.
