It's hard to imagine how something that sounds so simple can taste so amazing. I don't think it's just the 'whole truffle oil makes everything magic' idea, because the cheese was toasted to such perfection, topped with some crumbs to add a crazy mix of texture to the whole dish. The mushrooms were pretty good as well, not the cheap button mushroom sorts, but the nice kind you'd expect from a restaurant. Loved it so much. a Five-star dish if I've ever had one. Must try!

Overeasy is located right opposite Raffles Place and is easily accessible by public transport. Drinks during happy hour are decently priced. The secret though is to check the status of the Singapore stock exchange for the day - if the market ends down, the bar serves mini sliders at $1 per pop. Even in Singapore where food prices are relatively lower as compared to other developed cities, it is hard to find any other bar which can beat Overeasy. Overeasy is also located right on the bay front, making it the perfect spot to chill alfresco with your friends. The sea breeze ensures that you never feel hot and sticky, though you might want to style your hair accordingly (hairspray!!)
Food is poor, drinks are expensive.  Location is its savior.   Though service is friendly.

I quite enjoy this place.  It has a nice vibe to it.  Not too quiet and not too rowdy.  Come by sometime Saturday night and enjoy good music with a live DJ.  Oh, and don't forget to try the Truffle Fries :)Based on the atmosphere, I think this place is perfect for small groups.

I love Overeasy for its waterfront location and outdoor seating where you can get great views of the bay while basking in the relaxing evening sun. You can see why it's so popular with the afterwork corporate crowd. In particular, Overeasy has a great happy hour. You get can 1-for-1 drinks including Kirin and Heineken on tap (that's just $7 a pint) and housepour wines and spirits. It's always a happy day when the market closes lower for the day (if you're not a trader) because Overeasy has a slider promotion where you can get these lovely mini burgers at  $1 each. The sliders are really good too. Proper chunks of sirloin with cheese sauce sandwiched by a bun, they go great with a beer.

Great spot to chill with pals in the city area post-work or pre-club, with an amazing view of the bay. Drinks are a little pricey but the sliders are delicious, and cost $1 when the STI drops. Lemon drops here are good.

American brunch place. Average food overall. Had the standard American big breakfast (fried eggs, bacon, ham, baked beans, sausages, grilled tomatoes, etc.). Food was a bit underwhelming - it was cooked fine but nothing particularly stand-out and feels like a bit like a dish you can make at home with a few times of practice...Usually don't have high standard for brunch dishes since there's a limited scope you can work with eggs/classic breakfast dishes but some brunch places just execute it really well. Unfortunately, this is not one of them.

OverEasy is one of the many restaurants overlooking Marina Bay. Prices are crazy high, but I guess that's to be expected along the water, with gorgeous views of the hotel/casino. I happened to come on national day, and all the tables were reserved for later in the evening, but the staff did accommodate us and let us know we'd only have a short time to eat/drink before the reservation. The menu has a good selection of food and beverages. Again, prices are a little crazy. My passion fruit iced tea was $10 and alcoholic beverages range from $18-$25. They do have "happy hour" but it's only for one particular drink each day. On the day I was here, happy hour only applied to whisky. Lol. The service was friendly and efficient, we had a really great view and it was overall a really great experience.

The main reason to come here is the view, especially at night when you can catch a good view of the light show at Marina Bay Sands. For as busy as they were the service was pretty good. The food was alright, it was enjoyable but not really memorable. A few vegetarian options here that were good, my favorite was the truffle mac n cheese.
I come here for the malt milkshake and the view of the MBS. Other food is ok, but definite share the milkshake because the portions are huge!

One of my fav hangout place when in mood for some fancy burgers. Best part? They operate till late, 3am on a Friday night! Go for their signature truffle burger. I love how the beef patty integrates so well with taste of the cheese! Always looking forward to the burger. Ask for truffle fries if U're in for a little more truffle! However I would say that the standard and portion has dropped some fair bit. A pity but still good on the taste buds. Also ordered their buffalo wings with spiciness on a scale of level 2. Not too spicy for locals but definitely a bomb for foreigners. Disappointment of the entire meal was... The buffalo wings were uncooked!! Didn't ask for a change as the staffs looked under-manpowered. Overeasy Fullerton was quite obviously under staffed, but can't be helped as they're popular, sporting a large crowd with guests queuing for tables on a Friday late night! Had their chicken BLAT burger too, was quite appetising with the soury mayonnaise. The mayonnaise taste very much like the same kinda mayonnaise we can easily find from our 'neighbourhood' cafe haha.There's a lovely draw to this place. Maybe It's the droopy lightings. Maybe it's The 'hype' atmosphere and airiness of this overeasy chain. It's quite relaxing, u can watch MBS's laser show here too as it's right smack ooposite from MBS!

I like the food. The service not so much. Truffled mac and cheese with wild mushrooms, anyone? The smell of the truffle is enough to send me to 7th heaven, until I get sick of the scent. Best to share it as it can get a bit too much after a while. The spicy wings are equally good. Spicy sour with the blue cheese dressing to neutralize the heat. The steak frites is delicious with the truffle fries and bearnaise sauce. Drinks are not watered down and juices are refreshing.Note: Service can be a bit slow. And I do not like their system where they need to hold your credit card (when you are not requesting the drinks to be on tab) just because you want to utilize the happy hour promotion. I don't understand why they need to do that, especially when credit card fraud is so common now.

We came on a weekday evening and chose one of the tables outside. What happened was really disappointing - it started raining and everyone just fled from their tables. We were all standing in the sheltered area. Plates, cutlery, glasses and beer bottles were still standing soaking the rain while the waiters hurried shifted the tables in one-by-one. It was almost amusing seeing them frantically trying to make sure the customers didn't run away without paying, and also to re-seat the customers who left stranded.Among the two of us, we shared two plates of mini burgers (I think it was 6 burgers on a plate), a caesar salad and a prawn pasta. I got an Asahi to go with the food. We first ordered a steak but the order didn't come after we had finished everything. My friend was gathering exasperated by the inattention of the waiters; we changed the order into another plate of mini burgers.Well, he really did enjoyed those burgers, which I hear is famous over here at Overeasy. I found them to be just okay - i like burgers with leafy salad, tomato, cheese and all. These burgers only had a patty (it was like a cut of steak and pretty juicy, though slightly too cooked for my liking) enclosed with two buns and a toothpick to hold it together.The salad was just okay, I think I can make better salad lolCan't remember what the white sauce on the pasta was but the prawns were really fresh! It was moderately okay, and it did remind me of the copious amounts of pasta I used to eat (and make myself) when I was in the States.The bill came up to 50+ per person. A little ex, but considering the nice location (you can see the whole marina bay front from the dining tables outside), it would still recommend this place.

Consistent! Been to this joint (as well as the just-opened branch at Orchard Road) several times due to its location. Service is still really crappy. Long waits, disorganised. Staff feeling entitled. Ambience is also almost non-existent, more like a create-your-own environment. Other than happy hour drinks, all the other elements were absurdly painful. Food is terrible - too greasely or overboard. Saving grace is the fries. Great texture

The venue earned the 4th star, the food is decent but nothing spectacular.When the stock market is down, sliders are $1 each which is great since 5 of these little burgers cost you $16 on the regular menu. This $1 deal ends at 7pm, so be sure to get there early. I like that the sliders are cut up steak pieces rather than minced patties. The handcut fries with parmesan and rosemary is great. Almost as perfect as fries can get.Happy hour 1 for 1 ends 8pm. If you have UOB card, it ends at 8.30pm.

Went to over easy for the first time in June 2015 with a group of about 10.What to say, we left extremely disappointed.Starters were ok, little slider burgers, Nachos etc and really the only reason I'm not giving two stars as combined with happy hour cocktail prices it's not too badMains however were terrible. Basic burgers and for $20+ a meal I thought they should be great but they weren't even good, much better burgers available in Singapore for at least $10 less.One of the guys even sent their meal backService was ok, not great.

Nice dining establishment near the Fullerton Hotel. Husband and I came on a Friday evening so it was hoppin' with locals and tourists alike!I ordered the 'to die for' burger and my husband got the truffle Mac and cheese. The truffle Mac was to die for! My burger, not so much. I enjoyed the "special sauce" (dear God I hope nothing bad is in it... ahem) but I found the patty a bit bland. I think the staff mixed up my order because it had cheese, which I didn't order because it's an additional $2 and I'm a cheap ass, and it was served well done instead of medium. However, I was hungry so I wasn't about to send it back. So sorry to the person who got jipped with my burger. (Sucker... Wha?)Since it was a busy Friday night, the staff seemed a bit stretched out. Service wasn't good, as they forgot to give me a bottle of ketchup, no one checked up on us after we got our food, and it took a while to get the check. Overall, nice place to have dinner, but too busy on popular nights. Might be best to go during lunch (if they're open?) or off peak weeknights.

I've heard a lot of good things about this place but I've never had a chance to check it out until recently. Everyone recommended the "To die for" burger.For a $20 burger, it was a bit on the small side, with a small pile of fries on the side.The burger was not bad but nothing to die for... I liked that it was a substantial, meaty burger patty and not the mushy stuff you tend to get at a lot of joints in Asia (think Mos Burger).After I finished my lunch, I was still a bit hungry.This place is just okay in my books.

This place is very noisy especially indoor. There is air conditioning too but the doors are open and the place is packed. Kinda stuffy. Being lazy people, we decide to settle our dinner there too. I ordered a spicy linguine and my friend a burger (can't recall the exact name but it's their popular burger). My linguine was not bad, springy pasta and prawns. The spiciness doesn't overpower. But for the burger, it wasn't quite what we expected. My friend requested to change the fries to salad. The salad was a pile of arugula with dressing. Won't it be boring to have one kind of green in the salad, in terms of mouthfeel and taste? At least that is what we thought. Midway through, we changed to outdoor seats. Which is way better as it is fresher air and music isn't confined. Great view of the skyline and laser show at MBS that go well with a pint of beer. Oh, and thumbs up for the attentive server for the outdoor area! :)

So I'm pretty much in love with this place for a few reasons. There Mac N' Cheese is probably the best I've had in Singapore, there Chicken Wings pack a mean punch, and there Malt Milkshake is the bomb. Seriously, this place has become my go to American diner and I can't applaud the service, the food, and the all out amazing-ness that is OverEasy enough!

Overeasy serves really good bar grub, and I love the American Diner's design concept that guides every aspect of the experience here. They've got a great outdoor seating area as well, and I generally prefer getting a place out here because, unfortunately, Overeasy's indoor space tends to get as cacophonous as a dim sum restaurant. It gets incredibly loud in here, what with the loud music and patrons straining to have a conversation over it. For your sanity and comfort, I strongly recommend getting a place outside, but it does get crowded very quickly on weekends, so try to head down in the early evening or call ahead for a table.

1 for 1 happy hour and spiked milkshakes.  Mediocre sliders, but they're only a buck when the STI is down.  An extra star for being the site of the Berkeley club of Singapore happy hour locationIn general the food isn't great, and the drinks are pricey,  but Overeasy is a big after work bar in SG so all this is expected. All that said, t's nice having the view of the bay and the MBS light show in the evening

I've only eaten here once or twice and spent the rest of my time drinking. This is one of those places where you go because it's there and you need a drink. They have a good enough booze selection and the service is competent enough to get totally forgettable while still delivering your drinks in a reasonably timely manner.The highlights are the double-whammy view of Marina Bay on one side and hilariously drunk punters streaming out of Butter Factory on the other - depending on which time of the evening you go, of course. Oh and they have Oban 14, my favourite single malt. Huzzah!

I like that this is nearer home plus it is air conditioned. The wait is still at least 20 minutes on a Sunday after 2pm. If you are dining in, you need to get a table first before placing your order. There is a machine which accepts cash for takeaway orders. So you place your order and the queue number is written at the top. Go to the pick up area and wait for your number to be flashed on the board. If there is more than 10 or 15 digit gap, go outside and walk around. The chicken is nice but I think the one at the original hawker stall in Chinatown food center is better. The white meat is not as tender here. Same for the char siew and sio bak. I like the noodle and the sauce though. For just under $5 a plate, this is better quality food and value than those served at generic food courts or coffee shops. I will still come here as it is near home and parking is easy. Once the underpass from Tai Seng MRT to the building is open, this will be even more accessible.

Came at around 2.45pm on a weekday. The working crowd has dissipated and its all alone for me and my chicken. First of all, I followed the guy before and ordered extra noodles for the soya sauce chicken. Boy was I shocked at the huge quantity of noodles and wondered if I were able to finish it. After the first bite.. the chewiness, the sauce, the chilli paste, the green chillies I added... oh so many emotions. I may be exaggerating slightly, but it ain't totally.The noodles were chewy, and not disappointing. It soaks up and pairs with the soya sauce pretty well. The sauce is a little sweet and very flavourful. Noodles paired well also with the refreshingly cold green chillies. Next surprise: the chillies they gave. It's not spicy as I thought it would; in fact it was very mild, but there is a ever-so-slight prawn paste taste to it. I love it! Soya sauce chicken was tasty and the chicken is not like fantabulous so keep your expectations around there. Although its one michelin star, its hawker food for the masses after all. Chicken's soft enough for me and I quite enjoyed it. I just wish there were lesser bones. Some people said that the one in Smith Street is better; I hope to try that out someday. For now, this brings soya sauce chicken to a consistently good level.  Seriously impressed!

After hearing that this place earned a Michelin star. My husband and I decided to pay this a visit.Located in 18 tai seng, this place really gets crowded during the lunch hour. Avoid at all cost. Wait times could be 30mins, at least we waited that long for our order to be ready.So, we got our order, everything looks glistening. First note, it was oily. A lot of oil swirling around my noodle and our bean sprouts. My soy sauce chicken hor fun was good, but I didn't think it was better than others of the same. The chicken was smooth and tender, so are some that I've tasted elsewhere. The bean sprouts were crunchy but it was not any different from other stalls who also serve this. We also ordered a side of char siew & siew yok, I felt the siew yok was so tender that it had not texture. Could've been better if there was some bite.Overall, I don't think it was any better than other soy sauce chicken dish. I hold my praises for this.

This is the newer of the two and has AC (it makes the food more enjoyable). Keep in mind you still have to order first and then find a table. Best tip is to divide and conquer especially if you have a big group. One person wait in line while others find and reserve a seat because that is how it works. Order the chicken and pork and you won't regret it. Use the tray they give you NO matter what you think you can handle. The sauce can spill easily so don't risk it. They do accept credit card and enjoy your meal.

Crazy queues on weekend, really hectic trying to get a seat and he place is jammed packed and clearing of tables are really slow. Somehow didn't feel like michelle start quality. Had many others good soya chicken. Prices are also higher than Chinatown original

When to their toa payoh branch. Order the chicken BBQ pork and noodles . Chicken is of the small type meat is tender and the skin is delicious. The system in ordering a bit new so some confusion . BBQ meat is good and delicious chicken rice smell good also.

When I asked my Singaporean friends what Singapore breakfast items I should definitely not miss, roti prata twice came up. Roti was originally an Indian dish, as "roti" means "bread" and "prata" means "flat", but regardless of its origins it's really become a staple food in Singapore.So I had to get some. Actually, this was the third spot I went to. I tried to go to two other ones before this and one of them was closed for three days, and in the other one they screamed at me and told to leave. lol. But this place looked really friendly. It seems to be a popular prata place, and it has all kinds of prata - a ton of combinations. I got one plain, one with cheese, and one with garlic. The garlic one tasted really... garlicly! It was beautiful, looked like a house. The regular one had a crispy and flaky outer shell, and was chewy on the inside. I'd literally been running all around Singapore for this. This bread went well with fish curry (no big pieces of fish there though) and lamb curry. Soak the pieces and eat! Tasty!The egg and cheese prata was incredibly wonderful! Less crispy but still awesome.I bought a barley drink there also and it was good.

Standard has dropped quite a lot over the last few years. Had the masala thosai, but the potatoes were quite bland and not spicy at all. Briyani was so-so only, and sometimes the prata can be quite tough too. Hope it gets better!

When it comes to prata, Casuarina Curry is one of my hangout place for supper. Not the best but one of the more consistent ones I have had.  Traditionally Roti Prata is eaten with curry, sugar, condensed milk or plain. On some days I would just order egg prata with chicken curry, on some other days I would order plain, cheese, banana, chocolate, onion or even paper prata. Once you ordered, prata is served right away. Do make sure the prata they served you is hot as sometimes they precooked a whole bunch when it gets crowded. Service is fast, you get what you want when you ask for it. Tips: - Ask for piping hot prata as they do cook a bunch of prata ready to serve whenever someone orders.[010/100]

Still good.   just be there early before the place goes crazy.   Particularly impressive was the base curry that comes fox with your kosong.   It was thick and a little spicey unlike most place watery.   Had the mutton curry also.   Most of the meat tender some were chewy though.   All in all quite satisfied though a little far from east coast.   Tried Macpherson branch just was not good.

Went there last night. So far, this serves the best crispy prata as well as curry ever. I always order Onion Prata with Teh Halia  ( ginger tea ) - not sweet. If you do not like your drinks too sweet, you have to let them know cos they are very generous with sweetened milk My prata came exceptionally quick - like within 5 min. It was really crispy. Drizzle a little chicken curry sauce ( or more if you desire ) and it is ready to be eaten. They serve chicken or fish curry sauce for the prata. Chicken curry sauce is thick n smooth. While is fish curry sauce is more watery and it is spicier, in my opinion.Oh, not forgetting their Bee Hoon Goreng is worth mentioning. The chef made it kind of tze-char like and it is very tasty. Order it without chilli if you cannot take too spicy. Either version is good. I had non spicy last night.Too bad it closes around 11.30pm nowadays. So no midnight prata supper anymore.

First lunch of the new year with my family at Casuarina Curry! We originally wanted to eat at crispy prata on Upper Thompson but parking was a b**** so we settled for Casuarina, which also required about a 10 minute wait and hawkish parking skillz before we finally got a lot.This old dame serves up large, soft with a slight crisp prata. If you want crispy, The Prata House is where you need to be. We're not too fussy so Casuarina was fine. We ordered all manner of prata - kosong, egg, onion, cheese and banana. I liked the egg and banana prata the best (latter was stolen off my brother's plate). We got chicken and mutton curry as well and while they weren't exactly chilli spicy, it was evenly spiced with the likes of cumin etc. Drinks are your standard kopitiam teas, coffees and lime juice. By the way, if you get the pot belly uncle taking your order. Do take a moment to marvel at his amazing memory. He took our complicated prata order for 4 people, curries and drinks (teh halia kosong, teh c siu dai, lime juice...) WITHOUT a notepad!

It's located just across my house, so whenever I feel hungry, I'll just walk across for a quick meal. One thing I love about Casuarina Curry is that the whole place is air conditioned! Why is this a big plus for me? Because I perspire easily! To top it off, I will be having curry with my prata so perspiring is definitely expected! Whenever I go there, I usually order their mushroom cheese and egg prata which is $3.50. It's quite big in serving and filled quite nicely with the ingredients and I just love the crispiness of the prata. I tried their murtabak once and regretted it because it was HUGE. So I will recommend sharing the murtabak with your friends unless you are a big eater. Do try their lassi as well! It's delicious! I am very partial to their strawberry lassi. It's a great and affordable place for dinner and a late night snack with your significant other or a big group of friends!

First of all, for a typical Indian prata place, this place has got one of the better service around. Especially when you compare it to the prata shops at Jalan Kayu, this shop's service come out tops.Food wise, it was disappointing though. We used to specifically made detours just to visit this shop for pratas but over the years, declining standards have made us visit this place less often.The last 2 occasions we were there, I was disappointed to find that the pratas were pre-cooked. They came to us less than 2 minutes after we placed our orders and were stone cold. The chocolate prata fared slightly better, it was cooked to order but it was over-cooked. Instead of the usual crisp texture, it is now chewy.The last visit was simply too much for us when everything we ordered came cold and the pratas were too chewy. With that, this place got relegated to just for coffee.

Purely based on quality of food and drinks, 3.5 at most, but additional 0.5 stars for the free wifi. This cafe is quietly tucked away on the second and third levels of one of the shophouses in holland village. I came here on a weekday afternoon and easily got a seat. I love how this cafe offers free wifi. It's getting harder to find cafés with free wifi in Singapore to prevent customers from staying excessively long but I that similarly deters me from visiting them! My order was taken by a pleasant and good-natured barista who recommended the tea time set. This is basically a drink (lattes etc) and a slice of one of the featured cakes for a price of $6.50. My mocha alone would have cost $5.80. This cafe serves up a decent cup of mocha. It was aromatic and flavorful, and the chocolate was not overwhelming. The Oreo cheesecake on the other hand was a disappointment. While the tea set does come across as a good deal, I would pass on the dessert the next time round.

Spotted this cafe while walking around holland village area in search of food for dinner. From the outside it looks like a plain building. Need to climb a flight of stairs to get to the counter where you will be ordering your foods and drinks. Seating area there is one on second floor and one on the third floor. There is a lift that brings you up and down in case you do not want your serving trays to spill over while climbing on the steps.Seating area is rather small for a cafe but have to admit that the second floor interior design was good. It has the outdoors components inside. Third floor is just more like office hang out interior design. There are a number of staffs working but you need to self serve but they will clear your plate away. Food wise, I had a portebello pasta (mushroom pasta) in cream sauce. Price wise it's a bit on the higher end. I'm a little disappointed with the pasta as the sauce is dry and there is not much taste to it. My friend who had bacon carbonara commented the same.I am not sure how the coffee tasted here as I cannot drink coffee. There are a few selection of TWG teas in packets and Arizona teas in the bottle. Overall it is a nice concept for a cafe and it is good environment to hang out with friends. Next time round I will order their bake goods instead.

Espresso - a small volume of potent coffee, partially covered with a medium brown crema. There were some citrus notes, but they were secondary to the intense bitterness which followed in the aftertaste, and which lingered long after the shot had been finished. The bitterness is dominant in this shot, with some harsh elements present also. This may not be an issue for pour over coffees, or americanos, where the end product is diluted with hot water, however an espresso shot is more concentrated, which can exacerbate harsh notes. There are a number of different types of coffee beans available however, and D'Good offers customers the option of choosing their own preferred type. It may be advisable to highlight this more prominently at the ordering counter though - it is certainly a selling point that not all cafe's in the area offer. Cappuccino - there are some large bubbles present in the foam, but not in sufficient quantities to affect the texture. The latte art is nicely executed also. The mouthfeel is dominated by the texture and taste of warm milk, rather than the hybrid of milk and microfoam that can work in conjunction to form a smooth hybrid of taste and texture. The flavour of the underlying espresso shot is somewhat diluted by the milk, but the bitter aftertaste is still discernible. This may be entirely subjective, but the intense citrusy bitterness described above may work better with pour over coffee, rather than with milk based drinks. However, as there are a number of bean varieties available, and the ability to customise drinks, this can quite easily be fixed, and may not even be an issue from week to week.Staff are friendly and accomodating to requests, noticing when customers are looking for sugar or water, and stepping in to help. Also, thought and effort has clearly gone into the decor and layout, with an intelligent use of space allowing for lots of seating space, as well as a very pleasant al fresco area on the upper level. Busy periods can cause delays however (just as they would in any cafe), with a delay in used cups and plates being cleared, and tables being cleaned. Staff seem clustered in the kitchen and ordering counter area instead, but it should be noted that they did collect plates from the upper level before the end of my visit. Increasing the frequency of staff checks on the upper level may help.The ordering counter can become crowded, and as a result customers collect drinks after they have been prepared. This may be to keep the ordering counter clear, but one minor issue is that drinks can be slightly less warm when the are collected. This is a minor issue though, keeping the ordering counter and roasting space clear is a good reason for doing so. At $14.50 for a single espresso and 2 cappuccinos, the prices are about right. There is also a selection of cakes and baked items available, as well as syphon and pour over coffee.Overall, this is not a bad cafe by any means, with some admirable traits - a good selection of beans and brewing methods, and a micro roastery - everything I look for in a quality cafe, and I genuinely want D'Good to succeed. With some minor changes to the beans used for different drinks, and to the frequency of checks on the upper levels, this could be a very good cafe in a great location.

One of the few places where I get to choose my type of coffee roast and brewing technique. Tried out my favourite coffee (the Ethiopian Yirgacheffe) and it was a steal at 5.50! Ambience was nice, though I only tried the seats at The Lawn (level 2) - it had a swing and power points too. Will definitely be coming back!

Oh I love this place simply for the fact that it has a swing?!Now where can you find swings nowadays? Some parks don't even have it!What's better then sipping a cuppa and swinging away?The faux grass carpet was a bit prickly so don't take off your shoes!

This place is one of two including Jimmy the Monkey at One North where I would say you can get an excellent coffee and where I would dare order a macchiato and expect to get a real one. Tried the scrambled eggs. On toast which was small but ok value since it was only $7.50. Mainly this place is great for a coffee. Has free wifi and staff are efficient.

It's a cute cafe with a relaxed ambiance. The only thing that's stopping me from rating it higher is the 'designated study space' being only on the third floor. Clearly the cafe was empty on a Monday morning but they insisted that I HAD to study on the packed loud third floor when there were many empty tables on the second...which was a little bit of a bummer :(

This is one of our favorite cafe.  Good coffee with lovely latte art.  Each cup comes with a different design.  The menu expends every now and then which is awesome.  There's something new to try when one feels adventurous than ordering the usual.  Egg Benedict is yummy and the eggs are cooked perfectly each time.   The seafood lobster bisque is one of my favorite.  The soup is delicious and licked clean every time.  Be Careful though if you come with a few friends and order all at once.  They sometimes will group your order together before buzzing your pager, so food could get cold while "waiting".  Their strawberry ice cream is super creamy and yummy!  They wouldn't tell me where they got it from.  Dang it!   Chocolate lava cake is heavenly by itself or with the strawberry ice cream  d'good is a self service cafe and they get quite busy on the weekend.
Overall an "OK" experience. We had several brunch / lunch items: salmon, toast, etc. and everything was standard - not particularly good or bad. Space is a bit cramped.

Ordered the pancake Apple crumble. It is sweet and tasty. Cost $12. Filled with Apple crumble. I really like it a lot. The texture of the pancake is soft too. Yummy ! My friend ordered housemade English breakfast. Cost $16.50It looks yummy and smells good too. She ordered the Cold Brew and I ordered the Chamomile tea. Total bill cost $44.95 with gst. This cafe have a outdoor seating on the 3rd floor. 2nd floor have a two seat designed as a swing facing the window. But the spaces are limited. The ambience is nice. Thumbs up!

Love the *Smoked duck pancake*! Thin eggy crust :) as opposed to your usual fluffy floury pancake which might be too gelat.Worth the  $13, would order again!My friend had the *Eggs Benedict Portebello* which was wayyyy too small in portion for a meal... for $14.50

An excellent cafe in terms of food quality and decor! My friends and I went for early lunch on a weekday and got to sit on the lovely swing on the second floor. The table can spin so be careful when you put stuff down. It is self service which is fine as you pay the price stated on the menu. The set meal was a pretty good deal. They pay attention to small details like giving a soup bowl with a handle on the side. The aglio olio with prawns tasted as good as it looked. My aglio olio with real crabmeat was also satisfying although my friend found the flavour too strong. The tomato-based pasta with soup was rather small in portion compared to the other dishes. I was too full for dessert but my friends enjoyed the pancake with sweet potato, matcha syrup and vanilla ice cream.

Quaint cafe serving pretty classic brunch dishes in humble portions and great to get some work/studying done. Although a sign says no laptops on the 2nd floor, there are clearly people who set up shop there. There's a couple outlets, so if you can snag those tables then you're good to go for some time. The swinging porch chairs facing the street are also so adorable!
Maple sea salt cheesecake ($9) - 2.5 starsToo creamy and not cake-y enough for my liking. It also tasted burnt. I was disappointed.
Coffee is too good!!! Another outlet opening in September at Takashimaya! Must be back to try their food and pancakes.

I've been to other breakfast cafes like Wild honey, common man, and W39, and I've found a new favourite in d'good. I came across it on Yelp, so I thought I'd give it a try as I'm always looking for new places to get quality coffee and good food. From the outside it has a hipster grungy feel as it is hidden away down a side street. On the inside it is very trendy, and with 3 rooms to choose from to eat in, it caters for a range of people. It also has a roof top bar if you don't mind the heat. The coffee is really good! The food is great and affordable. I had the egg upon egg, which filled me up (and I'm a big eater).The service was exceptional. All the staff were very welcoming, friendly and helpful.

Cute cosy cafe with yummy drinks. Affordable too!Came across this as we were randomly walking around Holland V. It's been awhile since I visited this area. Many cafes and restaurants come and go, and we were excited to try something new.D' Good Cafe caught our attention when we realize we could enter by the "back door". Climbed up the stairs and it felt like we entered another world all together. The lighting done right, adorable decor all around. Suits the hipsters and young students.We were told to pick up the menu and find a seat. It's a self service place where you place your order, make your payment and will be issued a pager to pick up your food when it's ready. We ordered a tea time meal which comes with an orange juice (there are other options) and a waffle. Initially I was expecting a full waffle unfortunate it turned it to be half a waffle. Urgh. Who got the other half! Anyway, i ordered a green tea matcha frappe thingy. It was absolutely delicious. It's been awhile since I drank a decent cup of green tea frappe. The price is fairly affordable and hence the throngs of students. The upper floor was really pretty however was super turned off when I saw the whole area filled with students on their laptop and notes. Almost felt like a classroom or tuition centre. We were on the 2nd floor which didn't have any students mugging but still had dating students cuddling on swings and cozy seats. Overall, a nice stopover for an affordable and delicious tea break. Strong air conditioning is definitely a plus too.

Young, hipster land, lots of chatter, noise, whimsical decor. A place for coffee and dessert. Go on a date. Instagram your food pics with ample light on the 3fl (Alfresco seating available in addition to inside) Third floor tends to get the high decibels, bordering on canteen levels, while the second is more hushed. Brunch maybe, but keep expectations low and order the same as your partner. As I type this, my bangers and mash has been consumed, and my better half's lemon grass chicken is 37 min after ordering and still not here! In the end, it took 40min to be plated. The kitchen is tiny. Stick with the easy to prepare dishes. Stick with the coffee which is decent. They are passionate about their beans. Mains are meh. Lastly, the price points are on the higher side. In sum, I wouldn't go out of my way. 2.5 Just average.
The  food and drink are very good. I had the croque madam and caramel frappe and they are both very good. The food does take a while to be made so budget some extra time to compensate.

D'Good Cafe is a whimsical spot to swing your worries away, right smack in the heart of Holland Village. It sits in a funky shop house unit that has 2 entrances and the layout reminded me of that children story about a house in a boot with many children (uh huh i really don't have much of a childhood).D'Good Cafe specializes in single-origin coffee beans, which are roasted in-house. The owner is some crazy coffee fanatic and you can get your Ethiopian, Guatemalan, Jamaican beans done the siphon, drip, pour-over or espresso way. You wouldn't be able to miss the Elektra espresso machine at the counter! If you're up for something more exotic, there's the famous Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) from the Wahana Estate in Sumatra for $38 a pop. You can also make your own blend here at D'Good Cafe too.Here's what we had. The Prawn Aglio Olio ($16) was a little on the dry side, especially after it cooled a little (it became clumpy). I thought it could use a little more salt but it's certainly quite well flavored. The prawns were nicely done and crunchy.I liked the Bacon Carbonara ($15) more than the previous pasta. It's creamy (more on the milky side) and certainly more satisfying (only if you like cream). Generous portions of bacon too. It would be perfect with some fried bacon bit and an egg.The Eggs Benedict ($13.50) was a sad sad portion. I was terribly disappointed by it in fact. The brioche was nice but was too thinly sliced. As a result, it was soaked through by the eggs. Too much vinegar was used in poaching the eggs and that contributed to the papery texture of the whites and that acidic taste. Holladaise sauce was weak too. Certainly not something i'd recommend ordering. Add on $3 to the breakfast sets for a Latte that is well balanced with a nice crema. I must say we were all happy with our choice of caffeine. The Earl Grey Lavender Latte ($7) was aromatic without being overpowering. I'm fearful of lavender because it just smells and tastes a little like air freshener but this was just right. The Caramel Hot Chocolate ($7.50) will satisfy your sweet tooth because it's on the sweet side but i found the chocolate a tad artificial. The foam had somewhat of a brulee texture which was interesting. And if you like latte art, they do a lot of cute animal prints.We concluded that the best part of the meal was the maple sea salt cheesecake ($9). You cannot miss this smokey sweet and creamy cheesecake. The cheese was rich but not too heavy and it went perfectly with the crunchy and compact graham crust. I suspect a lot of butter went into it but it's awesome. Repeat after me: Butter is awesome (especially salted ones).D'Good Cafe also has a rooftop area for alfresco dining. This would be perfect at night or on an extremely cool day. Pretty isn't it?I'd certainly be back for more cheesecake. Tried the Strawberry Cheesecake and it just didn't cut it after the mindblowingly good maple sea salt one. Enjoy this one!

The cafe has a warm and cozy atmosphere on the second floor.  It's third floor is dedicated for people studying and planning on squatting for a while. The cutest part is a swing where you can enjoy your coffee/food while looking out on the street. The coffee is typical "cafe coffee" but the food is pretty good. Even though it doesn't leave the deepest impression, I find myself frequenting it often because it's reliable, cozy, and right next to the Holland V mrt.It's often busy so make sure you check to see if there are seats that you like before ordering your coffee/food.

Love the atmosphere and food in this cafe. I tried the Green Tea Lava Cake and a kiwi fruit juice, both of which were good. I will admit that the lava cake was a bit sweeter than I hoped though. Cute seating on swinging benches by the window. Seats can get limited during peak hours so watch out!

Mouth-Watering Food, Wide Variety, Reasonable Price!This is definitely one of my favourite place for mala steamboat! The restaurant is decorated with many oriental elements such as the Chinese red lanterns hanging at the sides of the restaurant, numerous Chinese inscriptions, wooden tables and chairs, and traditional Chinese utensils. They have 4 types of condiments available for us to mix. 3 types of broth for steamboat and we had the chicken and of course the ma-la. We had the lunch buffet and there were a large variety of food for us to order and it was fresh. We ordered many many plates of fish paste, veg, meats, fish and others.Sweet and Savoury Tidbits - each person is serve a set of tidbits such as dumplings, xiao long bao, Egg Coated Glutinous Square, Fried Roll Buns, Water Chestnut Jelly & eight Treasures "Black Rice" or Mixed Fruits in Syrup.Overall, this steamboat is reasonably priced for the wide food range and superior quality. Service is generally decent but when the restaurant is fully packed, the staff might get busy and forget your orders. Otherwise, they are generally prompt and courteous. Worth a try! Check out our full reviews and photos at eatandtravelwithus.com/2…

Eat-all-u-can for dinner.  I love spicy steamboat, but only one in family who can take it.  Their sauce is their secret and I think it's worth a vote.  Prawn was good, but others don't expect so much.火鍋です。辛党な私はどこでも好きなのですが、ここのソースはなかなか辛いです。タレには独特の風味と旨みがあります。エビが美味しかったのと、皿にスープを掛けて剥がすスミレのような食べ物は初めてでした。他の具材は食べ放題なのでそれなりのレベル。酒なしで1人50SGD程度ですかね。わざわざ出向くほどではありませんが、ご近所さんなら一度試してもいいかも？

Two out of three ain't bad.The room is relatively nice.  The main room is definitely nicer than the back room that we were seated in.  This room was a little cramped.  There are some nice accents that provide an ornamental feel to the ambiance.  This is a step up from the purely functional feel of my hot pot places.The food was very good.  So, there are the two positives.  Then there is the negative.The service ranged from functional to downright rude.  They pretty much do the steps they plan to and when they plan to do them.  Outside of that, they seem pretty put out if you ask for anything.  Plus, come on a buck for a glass of tap water.  Now, that doesn't make any sense.However, whether you call it steamboat or whether you call it hot pot, the food was very good.Our soup was half mild and half sort of spicy.  My friend does not like really spicy food so we couldn't go all out on the spicy side.tinyurl.com/95lyapeWe pretty much went with the scattergun method. We ordered one of the sets.  Plus, we picked a number of other things from the ala carte menu.  We had a little bit of everything.  My favorites were the mushrooms, the beef, and the prawns.  But, everything that went into that soup pretty much came out good.  tinyurl.com/9a5dk8ktinyurl.com/8zhrsqptinyurl.com/9uhrk95tinyurl.com/9o8uue2Well, the one exception for me was the frozen mussels.  I am not a hot pot pro.  I would not have thought of ordering mussels for hot pot.  I certainly would not have expected them to be frozen and really had no idea what we should do with them.  We overcooked them.  I do not think I will be revisiting the idea of mussels in steamboat.  If you can overlook the service and focus on the fun of cooking your own food and it being very tasty, then give The Magic of Chongqing Hot Pot a chance.  I enjoyed it.  If there were not so many other steamboats to explore in Singapore, I would return.

When I want to have a hot pot in some comfort with my mates, this is the place that comes to mind.Chong Qing hot pot is great if you have a group of rowdy friends that wanna celebrate an event, maybe a birthday and feel like having some steamboat. This place is only fun if you have enough people to book a private room. Only then, is it worth while. Make sure you ring in advance for a room booking!This place is kind of pricey for simple steam boat. The quality varies from time to time but it's never bad. It ranges from good to pretty good. As with most hot pot places there's a variety of soup bases to choose from (I like the herb and Ma La Chilli oil). The fun part is to have the comfort of air conditioning and a room where you can have your own private little hot pot party. You can make as much noise as you want!Being a ala carte buffet all you can eat style restaurant, the usual is thrown in, some special dishes that's one per person and a dessert (the man tou is good). Good company and the private room is key here!

This place is just awesome and I would definitely come back here again. The steamboat soup is just so flavourful, and that's even before you start throwing in the ingredients, so you can imagine just how good it tastes after adding in prawns, fish and the like. Definitely have not tasted anything as good in other steamboat restaurants in Singapore.The condiments and sauces which they serve go really well with the meat, fish and prawns.As they are really good, come prepared to pay slightly more than you would expect to pay for a typical steamboat restaurant (like those in Bugis) but overall still very value-for-money because the quality truly trumps other places.If you have a big group of around 10 people you can request the private dining area for a more cosy, intimate group gathering.

Tried and tested favourite hotpot destinationHaving been put off by one too many seamy, questionably insalubrious, budget-priced hotpot restaurants (inevitably recommended by an enthusiastic friend), it's always a relief to come back to ChongQing where the quality is assured. All at the princely buffet price of ~$20 for lunch and ~$30 for dinner. I prefer the Tanglin outlet over the more modern and brisk one at Suntec, here the pace is comfortable and friendly, with servers comprising Chinese girls and local 'aunties'. Making at least 4-5 visits a year, dining at ChongQing has a happy familiar routine. First, mix the special sauces that will reduce the sting of the mala soup - it's a mix of sesame paste, sesame oil, garlic+chilli, and sweet chilli. Then start cooking your favourite vegetables and dumplings in the soups - mine is usually the milk bone chicken and mala. While many at least 90 minutes in contentment as the food keeps flowing - prawns and pork belly are part of the buffet menu too, if I recall correctly. Enjoy cooked items in addition, and part of dessert is usually the eagerly awaited fried mantou bun dipped in condensed milk.

Their service is just impeccable. I ordered through Food Panda and they called me up to say that the briyani rice was slightly overcooked and that they didn't want to serve it to their customers, offering the cumin rice instead. The entire phone call, he was terribly apologetic and kind. Such a joy to support their business!Fish Tikka Masala - 5 starsTender on the inside with a perfectly grilled crust. This beats any sort of chicken tikka masala hands down (I don't eat chicken, and the ones I've eaten in the past have always been dry).Fish Briyani Rice Set ($11.77 on FoodPanda) - 3 starsThe one dish I'm not impressed by. It comes with only 3 small pieces of fish - fish that's breaded similar to the orange-colored frozen fish filet in a McDonald's burger and some shredded cabbage, carrots, cucumbers and tomatoes. The fish was cooked well - it was tender and not overcooked. But I'd still order rice and dishes like the fish tikka masala separately the next time. Usually rice and 2-3 dishes (spinach, fish, palak paneer) can easily last me 4-5 meals.Spinach ($7.49) - 4.5 starsA bit on the soggy side this time. But there's always ample cooked spinach!

Food is tasty, service is friendly, but food is dammmmmnnnnnnn slow.Ordered what we thought would be the most basic food - plain dosa. Ended up taking what felt like more than half an hour to arrive, by which time our chicken tikka was completely cold. Dosa was ok, but the gravy / Dhal was pretty stingy. If you're in this area, much better off going to Karu's on top of Sime Darby Centre.

Why this place has two N's, we will never know.  Stopped in here for dinner before soccer camp after a little snafu with my ability to read military time.I got the chicken tikka masala and was annoyed that I had to order my carbs separately. The chicken was really juicy but the sauce wasn't as creamy as I'd like. Friendly service and very cold water though!

For the price, this is a very good option for north indian food. Casual setting but very tasty preparations. All the regulars like butter chicken, chicken tikka masala, naan breads are well executed. Service is pleasant too.Would skip the more expensive sixth avenue options to come to this place. Parking is easier too.

they used to be along the road facing the second hand car shops.they also used to be non air conditioned.now they are in a spanking new location opposite omakase burger within the retail complex itself.now they are air conditioned with the option for alfresco dining if you so choose.they open at 10.30am just as we arrived.only vegetarian choices available until around 12pm.and that's when we managed to get our hands on their yummy yogurt tender chicken tikka with a tinge of spiciness.before 12pm, you just have to settle for their stir fried cabbage with spices and dried chillies.very sedap!mixed vegetables consisting of cauliflower, chick peas, potatoes, carrots and long beans was a little stodgy.chick pea curry was creamy good.kosong bawang is my favourite prata.plain prata with plentiful sweet onions!their masala thosai was crispy outside with soft potato filling inside.a healthier option when compared to the prata.finish off with their teh halia, not too sweet and not too gingery.

The restaurant is full for lunch during the weekends and although the front-line staff are working hard, the food takes a bit longer and orders can get mixed up.The food is good, place is clean, and pricing is reasonable.Enjoyed the curry and ice-lime juice.

I like Curry Gardenn for it's reasonably priced (average $5 per dish) and delicious North Indian dishes. While it's not as good as some other North Indian restaurants in Singapore, I would still recommend Curry Gardenn because it's really good value for money and it just has a really good vibe. The owner's are nice and friendly and the service is efficient. I've tried the Palak Paneer, Butter Chicken, Mango Lassi and Garlic Naan and enjoyed all of it.Curry Gardenn is also situated in an interesting location. It's really quiet at night, parking is abundant and free. However, I've heard that Turf City has been bought over and is due to be renovated so I'm not sure what will happen to Curry Gardenn. Better go quick!
Fabulous fish Masala with different spices coming forth. The prata was light and crispy.  The butter chicken and Masala Dosai were also flavorful. Food service is a little slow but worth the wait.

This place has quite a strange name with two "n's" in its name, but anyway we decided to come here since we were all craving for some good Indian food.We got here at about dinner time and found the place to be pretty much packed with people. We decided to wait around and luckily managed to get a seat not too long after we arrived.We had to wait quite a long while for our food to be served, but I guess that is to be expected given the crowds around here. Anyway, we had the following dishes such as the curry fish head, chicken masala, all kinds of naan and rice. The curry here is absolutely amazing! The curry ws just rich enough and not overpowering, the degree of spiciness was also just right for me.Overall, this is definitely a great place to eat some good Indian food.

So, what we have here is a bar where the price of the beers go up and down based upon the sales in proportion with each other. Thus the price of a popular beer goes up, while the least popular beers go down (which is probably why they don't have VB on tap). It's a cute concept, but since I've become a bit of a beer snob I don't let the price of a beer dictate whether I am going to buy it or not (though I have done so in the past). Other than the cute concept of rising and falling beer prices, they aslo ave a decent collection of beers available - I ended up having the strawberry beer, which I have to admit was different.

We saw this restaurant recommended on several blog posts about salted egg yolk dishes. But please please don't bother coming. Even if you're drunk, go to MacDonald's. There was no one in the bar/restaurant at 6:15-7pm on a Friday night. My Sister and I had to walk around the bear to grab someone to sit us. And again when we wanted to order and the bill.The selection for beers were disappointing even though it was recommended for beer. There is nothing interesting on it's menu other than the way it is displayed like a stock market. We tried the salted egg yolk pizza and chicken wings.  No salted egg yolk flavour for either. Also the pizza is like a cheap frozen thing you buy from a convenience store. The chicken wings were juicy but the skin was oily and lacks salted egg yolk sauce. I will not come back even if we get free food..

Full range of beer available for you, located at the heart of Clarke Quay. Finding the place is not difficult, the atmosphere is not bad but at that time I went, there wasn't any band performance and that's the only downside of it. Prices of the drinks are standard - reasonably priced and you have to come here to try exotic ones that you can't get elsewhere.

On paper, the idea of Beer Market is a novel one. Like a stock exchange for beers, prices fluctuate according to demand. Sounds brilliant eh? Nope. A cool premise but the execution is all wrong. First off the selection of beers arent exactly extensive. Second, the prices arent cheap in the first place. So the remotely decent beers are perennially expensive. The layout of the place isnt fantastic as well. Feels like a narrow alley with twists and turns. So one you are at one end, its hard to get the attention of the service staff.But its not all bad. Food is relatively decent. And for smokers, you have your own enclosed smoking cubicle within the 'Market'. They also have a pool table and a dedicated darting area with 4 boards. So to me the concept is a fail but the food and darts saves it a star.

Rolled into Beer Market on a Sunday night around 7pm. The place was empty, but gradually filled up for the band. Left around 10pm+ $3 wings are amazing. 4 full wings, cut in half and made with either chill (excellent), honey (good) or crispy-fried (average)- the market is rigged. When we arrived it was empty, so I ordered an Asahi, the next half hour "update" almost all the prices went up. Clearly there was no demand for 20+ drinks. We recorded the prices every half hour, and went up on average $2 over the 3 hours - not a stockmarket at all - a scam! (oh wait, that IS a stock market)- the $3 sausage and $3 nachos are terrible - remove them from the menu- the music was too loud. When you can't talk and get deaf, what is the point?

I think there's a very interesting concept taking place here - the prices of the beer change according to the demand for it in the past half hour. The stock market concept is meant to appeal to financial-types who have nosh to spend on beer after a long day slogging it out - very clever of the owners of this place! Also, prices shown for the beer is after GST and that makes it easier to calculate the total cost you're paying. But, what I really love about beer market is the fact that Shili and Adi perform here on Thursdays and Fridays. They are an awesome band (disclosure: they're my friends back from Uni days) who have gotten better since going commercial. But, that means those days are typically the most packed and you'd better book in advance before coming.Beware - getting couch seats means you need to spend a minimum of 300. Make sure you're aware of this before taking one that's offered to you

Loved the concept of Beer Market where the prices of beers rise and fall based on demand at the bar. Enjoyed a San Miguel Light (Philippines), Lychee Beer (Japan) and Little Creature Pale Ale (Austrailia). The only reason for the lower rating was that there weren't THAT many beers. Cool concept regardless. Might get a higher rating next time if there is a band playing.

Situated on the Clarke Quay beat, this bar's most distinctive feature is the way in which beers are priced according to the 'beer market'. Working like the stock exchange, the prices of the beers fluctuate according to how popular they are. Being an Asahi drinker myself, that is usually all I order once I see it on the menu. Imagine my horror when I saw the price of Asahi nudging towards S$15 when others, such as Chang, stayed stagnant at slightly over S$10. It can be pretty fun to keep track of the price of your favourite beers and strategise your next move, but after a while, the novelty wears off and you barely notice the large screen at the bar. They have a good space for events and those have always been fun. There is space to move around and choose a quiet table towards the back, and the central set-up is conducive for live music acts and talks. Beyond the occasional event, however, there is definitely no motivation to head back and experience one of their regular nights. It just doesn't leave that kind of impression.

I love live music venues and the concept of fluctuating beer prices depending on demand and supply makes this place interesting here. Truth is, alcohol is never that cheap in Singapore so it's more of a novelty. Truth be told I'd rather be drinking at home.The lineup of the bands seem to change plenty here but I've enjoyed watching some pretty good live bands here. The spread of beers here is wide so you'll have a nice selection to choose from.The only downside was that the crowds that go there don't seem to be there for the live music and that's a waste for me. i think this place could have a much more party atmosphere if the crowds were less stiff.

Fun concept bar that offers a range of beers with prices that fluctuate or 'crash' due to demand. It makes choosing a beer a fun game to play, hoping that you're picking your lager at a good price. There's also live music and apparently this place pumps on a weekend. We went on a quieter Sunday evening and found the stock market pretty easy to play, as everything we ordered went up after! Still, we amused ourselves in our skilful ability to play the stocks in a way that could never translate in reality.

The concept of this bar is kinda fun - fluctuating beer prices depending on the popularity of that particular brand. It's something of a conversation starter, checking the beer prices every half an hour to see if you scored a good buy! The price boards can be a little mind boggling at first if you're not a financial person, but it's easy enough to understand after a bit. The beer selection is quite wide and this system actually encourages you to try the lesser known and less popular beers which are usually a little cheaper.Haven't had the chance to try the food yet, but I probably will come back again some time, just because!

This place is located just beside liang court, pretty interesting idea to have a stock market for the pricing of beer , though it doesnt really concern me much or perhaps I wasnt really paying attention to the prices. Frankly speaking , I couldn't find the real purpose of the stock market , it wasn't as interactive as you think.Beer are actually quite expensive , the place looks pretty crammed and its just not a place that you will feel comfortably to chill out, They have their own live band but sometimes they do need to have some quality check before allowing some bands to go up the stage and perform.In general, not too bad as a bar but it definitely lacks the X factor which does not make patrons to revisit again.

Beer Market has a slightly gimmicky concept. Beer prices are displayed on an electronic scoreboard, with prices fluctuating every 10 minutes or so, rising or falling based on demand. Again, slightly gimmicky - but hey, it provides for an interesting conversation topic should things at the table get stale. Beer wise, Beer Market has the usual beer options - Tiger, Erdinger - and carries some less common labels too (e.g. kopparberg cider). Beer Market occasionally has live bands performing as well. Oh, one really convenient feature - it has a smoking room located in the 2nd floor which is rather well ventilated. No more trooping down stairs on unwieldy beer legs for a cigarette anymore!

It's a hit or miss here. This time they tried to rip my colleagues off by overcharging them by $60 and the old lady who owns the place said she made a mistake. She never makes mistakes on any bill I have had here before. I was mortified and embarassed by this place. Be Aware!

The place can get super crowded, especially after 7pm and on weekends. This is my 2nd visit, with the 1st visit a few (or was it several) years ago. I am pleased to discover the food is still as good as before and the place looks a bit more spruced up.It is a homely place with pretty authentic home-style Thai food. It has none of the sparkling glitz of the more modern Thai restaurants. It is a more down to earth place which focuses on cooking good food and not on its ambience. The menu is old and fraying at the edges, with several items either not available or only available for lunch. The main dishes are still there though. Order using the chit and someone will come along to take the order chit. We had the basil chicken, seafood tom yam soup and green curry chicken to share. All were delicious even though they did not look very appetizing, especially the green curry chicken and seafood tom yam soup. Cash only. The pricing seemed average, around $10 or more per dish (depends on the size).

I simply love this place.  Not the service or lack of A/C but their food is quite amazing and CHEAP!  Having been to Thailand many time, I must say this is comparable to what you would find there and it's not too far from where I work.It might be hard to find but it's definitely worth a visit.  FYI, this place closes on Monday.

The service at this restaurant is one of the worst I have encountered in all my life. The waitress refused me water when I requested for some upon seating by pointing at some house rules flyer they've put up. When I agreed to pay for my water or a drink she said that she refuses to bring anything till the whole group comes in. We were waiting on 2 friends who were at Bugis + which is about a 5 minute walk away from this place. I was extremely thirsty from all the walking & where I come from we don't even turn away our enemies when they ask for a sip of water. It is considered not just rude but extremely hostile to refuse someone drinking water in many cultures let alonein the hospitality business. She came back only to toss the menu at our faces instead of laying it down properly on the table & walked away without even paying attention to our reactions. When she came to take the order, she started giggling when my friend started asking her questions about the food & the restaurant's specialty dish. It didn't help that she repeated our orders by mumbling in a very thick accent with little regard for if we were following her or not. I found her entire demeanor extremely unpleasant, ill mannered to the restaurant business & wanted to throw the menu at her face at this point but for the sake of public decency I waited on silently to see if the food was worth all this.The food in all fairness was not bad but there was nothing extra special about it either. I tend to enjoy my food more when I'm positively disposed & where the service is keen, attentive, efficient or at least pleased to attend to a paying customer!I've had equally if not better Thai food at Thai Smile Cafe, Spicy Thai, Lerk Thai, Jane Thai, Bali Thai, Jai Thai & E-Sarn Thai which in my opinion tops the list.I am a firm believer in service quality especially when it comes to food which everyone is rather emotional about. Cordiality immediately translates into Kitchen etiquette vis a vis hygiene & nutritional concerns. Disrespecting your customer to the callous point where they want to walk away from your establishment & being brash with your clientele can make its way into poor food hygiene practices. Give this place a miss if you don't want to be subjected to the worst service ever, unimpressive food & an ambiance without an A/C that boasts of dated Elvis Priestley photos.

I think this is one of the best value Thai places around Bugis. There are other competitors but the cooking is done to a higher standard without being too fancy.Am a regular of the lemon chicken - most places make the sauce over-guey and sweet but here its a light sauce, and the fried without being too greasy. Papaya salad is great too but only served at lunchtimes. I also recommend the coconut juice - freshly cut with copra.Sometimes the service is a bit off but I bear it given the quality to value ratio of the food.Don't be surprised if you have to share a table!

I have heard many reviews about this place, but I seldom see a crowd here whenever I pass by which is strange. It is definitely a no frills Thai eatery with authentic Thai fare at affordable prices. The Tom Yum Seafood Soup was a good dish to start off the meal. It was a good balance of spiciness and sour, and the tanginess made the dish really appetizing. The seafood was sufficiently fresh too, and at a generous amount. My favorite Thai dish to try at restaurants is the Phad Thai, so I had to try it here too. It was passable and rather flavorful but not exactly up to the standards of most other Thai restaurants. The service was pretty disappointing too. They are inattentive and they ignored us a few times despite seeing that we have called for them.

The food here was very good. Spicy and authentic. I visited this place a few years ago, with a local, during lunch time. It was airy and resembled one of the local coffee shops. The menu was pretty extensive, with pictures to depict each dish. We ordered a variety, as there was a large party of us. I remember that the pandan leaf chicken was very tasty and I thought the Pad Thai was of decent standard - better than what you get in the US but not up to the standard of what I've had in Thailand. The fish cakes and olive fried rice was also very tasty, though the latter was a bit greasy. We didn't order it but I recall seeing fragrant rice being served in a pineapple husk at other tables, at it looked very tasty. We had a filling lunch, and barely had space to stuff down any dessert, but at the recommendation of my local friend, we tried the mango sticky rice, which tasted very rich, creamy and wonderful. A little too much for me, so I managed half a bite. it was very tasty, like the ones I had in Thailand, but tasted fairly fresh and not like those that are prepacked and sold from the fridge. Our meal ended up being fairly pricey at almost 80 USD for three people, since this wasn't even a restaurant, but it was well worth it for an authentic Thai experience in Singapore.

My favorite South Indian restaurant in Singapore so far.  It's a chain from Bangalore, and the Singapore branch, opened earlier this year, is the first one outside India. Their masala dosas are amazing, the crispiest and lightest I've had anywhere. I've also had a few new dishes I'd never had before, such as bisele bath, which is sort of like a tomatoey rice stew, made with rice, lentils, cashew nuts, carrots, and other goodness. My other favorite is kharabath, which is kind of like an Indian polenta, made from semolina with a bunch of spices.The older gentleman who takes your order at the front counter is very helpful and friendly, and patiently explains and recommends different dishes. He also backs up the talk - today, he told my friend and me to try their freshly ground coffee instead of just ordering Cokes, and said if we weren't happy with it we should come and see him afterwards. Thankfully, there was no need for fisticuffs with the old dude, because the coffee was damn good.

One of the best places to have Indian Vegetarian cuisine. Spice combinations are delicious. Prices are very affordable. Might get a little busy during normal meal hours but definitely worth the wait. Rawa Masala Dosa and Onion Uthappam are highly recommended.

Excellent vegetarian restaurant with amazing bisi bela bhaat, good dosas, decent idlis. Ordering is a pain and almost negates all the good. The set up is plain silly - you will spend ages queueing in the cramped entryway. Everyone takes ages to decide. Huge menu. Several 'day of the week' items + daily specials complicate things further. Always sell out of some so you choose and choose again. And worse, typically gluten free South Indian dishes (such as idlis and dosas etc) have been modified to add "rava" which is semolina and thus wheat-based. Wish these guys would find someone who could help them fix the simple things that make a great restaurant concept with pretty good food a mediocre experience.Suggestions if management is listening - Change ordering location and system. Add simple descriptions of dishes. List ingredients. Simplify the menu - put day of the week dishes and daily specials on a separate one or board. Let people enjoy the whole experience.

I went there when it first opened, on a Sunday and they applied a surcharge for Sunday, making it about a dollar more expensive for each item which I found odd. They might have been working out some kinks as it was fine, but not amazing when we went. I had a dosai, which was good, interesting texture (thicker and crispier than usual), with a layer of coriander sauce on the inside and a good filling, but I found it a bit too strong on the ghee for my taste. mylifeinsin.com/2013/06/…Not everything is available at all times of day, I really wanted the chilli pakoras but they are only available during "snack" times of the day. We had dosai, poori, chapati, and a rice dessert.

Uddin vada- similar to a donut. Very good... Fried crispy but inside was softPudi masala dosa- has a spongy texture. Came with potatoes on topMini meal set- tastings of five different rice "stew" sampler

Some amazing South Indian food here! Its a very distinct style though, something I've not tasted so far! The dosa is thicker than usual but oh so crispy!! Loved the vegetable special dosa.. unique texture and great taste. The rice idli and coffee was amazing too.. will be back for sure!!

I wasn't wanting for vegetarian but was very happy I sought out MTR is Little India.  Authentic curries and breads stuffed with all good things, such as potato and onion.  Popular with the locals too, so you know you are into a good thing.  Do try it!  If it's veggie curry in a hurry you're after, you won't be disappointed.

We went to MTR for breakfast two days in a row as we loved it! Food was freshly prepared and tasty. The restaurant was very clean and well kept. The staff was attentive. It does get pretty crowded on weekends. As soon as you enter the restaurant you need to place the order at the counter before being seated. Hence it's better to take a look at the menu, which is placed outside the restaurant before entering so that you don't feel rushed. I would highly recommend this place for good old Indian breakfast.

Nothing more you can ask for a early morning Dosa.  Crispy and spiced just nice.  Came here at exactly 8:30am Saturday and was the first customer.  No issue finding parking which is mostly a drag for eateries around here.  Place is clean service is excellent.  Before 9 it was packed.  Back again July 3rd with the in laws and yep this as good and efficient as ever.

Great place to enjoy Indian vegetarian food. Food is heat and the ordering And delivery is really fast and efficient.  Across between sit down dining and quick service. Everything seems to be priced at $5. Very clean and new, as well.

Recommended by a colleague. They're a famous chain in India and have set up shop in Singapore.LOVE this place. The restaurant is a bit on the small side and they must be popular as there was a small queue when we arrived on an early Saturday afternoon around 2pm. They have a good system to minimize waiting by allowing you to place your order and pay while in the queue then being seated closer to when your food is ready as all orders take about 10 minutes.My guess is b/c everything is made fresh to order. They specialize in South Indian cuisine and everything is vegetarian. The place is spotless, well lit, and air conditioned. A big pitcher of water with napkins are also available at all tables which is totally worth the extra few dollars you'll pay per dish than at say Banana Leaf.Everything was delicious, especially the tomato rice dish (wish I remembered the name). The set meal I had was also good, comes with a couple of fluffy pooris, white rice, daal, etc and good value for money.I think we've found a new favorite Indian spot in Singapore!

Most variety for a south indian vegetarian place in Singapore. Everything is made in ghee.. This adds to the taste but also to the waist.Everything is good but the place next door has a homely feel and super tasty dosas.
Awesome place. Fantastic food and great service. The quality of the food matches what one is used to back in Bangalore. Love going here and will surely go back there soon.

The dosas both masala & rawa were excellent, the best part is that the accompanying sambar for each dish be it the dosas or the vada or rawa idli was distinct! And each of them were pretty good particularly the accompaniment to rava dosa which was similar to avial, the good old sambar was pretty good as well.The vada was excellent, the rawa idli & filter coffee were good.Overall a very good addition to Singapore's Indian Food scene

Was thinking of bringing the Girl to somewhere Japanese but not selling ramen. Searched on Yelp, and discovered this place. Here's my review (taste is in point 3)1. The atmosphere is nice and really casual. As some of the reviews have mentioned, if you do a reservation they will write a simple greeting card for you. And the wet towels they provide are also hand decorated. The effort to personalize your meal is notable, and I applaud it. This act certainly stands out from most restaurants.2. This restaurant has a lot of emphasis on your personal interaction with your food. I got an unagi "rice bowl" and the Girl got a salmon "rice bowl", and we were supposed to mix the rice with the butter and soft boiled egg a la Pepper Lunch. And another customer came and they ordered Green Peas, and there was a "challenge" by the staff in which the customer was given 1 chance to grab as much green peas with 1 hand as his dish. Such interaction certainly makes your visit more memorable, and probably makes the food taste better.3. Now for the food proper. I got the Unagi Meshi ($19.80), and mixed the rice myself. Considering the price, the piece of unagi in my stone bowl is ok-ish in size - it's about palm size. Nonetheless, it was marinated well and had a good texture! (I'm a fan of teriyaki unagi) the rice was nice, soft and not too sticky (there was butter in the rice so that could have helped). The only point is the rice crust that forms from the rice being stuck on the hot stone bowl, but that can't really be helped. I also ordered the Masuzake ($9.80), which gave me 180ml of Sake. It is served in an wooden box and a "shot glass" (you probably would see it in other reviews), and definitely eye catching. However though, it's not as strong "alcoholic-ally" sake as I expected it to be. So it'll be good for those who haven't tried sake before. But for sake lovers this sake might, in my limited opinion, not provide enough punch (that burning sensation down the throat). Nonetheless, the sake was pleasant and very nice to drink down!Overall, I would bring my friends along to try this place due to the interesting interactions that they can get. Price wise... Considering it's right at Boat Quay, it's not too bad. Good place as a date too! But the reason for 4 stars is, the food is not that impressive that would leave a lasting impression in me.

$12nett set lunch, what's there not to love! A good variety of about 8 types of rice bowls from the regular chicken don to more interesting ones with raw salmon and tuna, not forgetting the eel! You know that these folks are serious about offering you a good value lunch as it's not just the run of the mill type rice bowls that offered. Feeling bored and wanna get creative, grab a marker and doodle on their wet napkin wrappers. Overall an enjoyable lunch place with good value and if you fancy a view of the Singapore River, ask for a seat at the alfresco area!

Cheery quick service, I like having lunch here. Its good, simple, includes salad and miso soup..all for $12. They do a good karaage and tebasaki. I love the salty powder and tangy sauce for the tebasaki which is $1.50 a piece.I like that they are flexible to give me the sashimi bowl with all salmon instead of tuna. And quite often they will have a daily special. I've brought many different people there for a quick catchup lunch as you can have a conversation, get willing service, take your time to eat since the food came quick and the funny part is thereafter, I often walk in with someone else and see someone I had brought before bringing someone else for lunch!It works for a regular stop in this busy raffles place area. $2.50 at lunch gets you a huge glass of housemade lime juice!I haven't played but I've seen someone playing the edamame game. Basically if you order edamame, you have to play scissors paper stone with the server. If you win you can grab a handful of edamame from the basket with all 5 fingers. If you lose, you can only use 3. But I saw an expatriate lady who lost..and the staff very nicely gave her a second chance.
