Total ~S$80; all scrumptious!  The service was excellent: - Our orders were brought out piping hot; tea cups and water glasses kept full throughout; empty dishes promptly cleared away; wait staff pleasant and helpful.My wife and I like the setting and service in this branch better than those in Taipei and Los Angeles. The quality and variety of dishes are typical of Din Tai Fong fame, however. After such a fabulous experience, our friends then told us that there were 7+ DTF branches in Singapore! Oh boy,  I envy those LUCKY Singapore people! Peterskis3, Jan 2013

Always been overrated but I still love this place! I think Paragon branch is the best I have tried so far. The soup dumpling is tastier and food portion is a little bit bigger in general. Hence, although this place is always crowded regardless the timing, it's worth the wait! I can't get enough of soup dumplings! Any other huge fan of soup dumpling out there, care enough to share some underrated place for similar dish to me in Singapore? Hit me up! However, no matter which branch of DTF you are at, try ordering their Earl Grey Lemon Tea! It's like the best of both worlds.... The earl grey tea is pleasantly strong and the lemon taste makes it fresh!

It is my occasional place for dinner whenever I crave for fried rice pork chop. Yes, you heard me. The pork chop here is delicious! Fried rice that comes with crumbly eggs are tasty as well. Other than this dish, I normally just head to Paradise Dynasty for the xiao long bao & noodles with pork broth. Not to digress, DTF is always packed and have long queues for dinner. Hence, be prepared to queue.

I was there for an early lunch today and it was already getting packed with diners (we are looking at 11.30 am on a Monday). Even though not all the tables were taken up, we still had to wait for about 5 minutes. 2 groups of diners were ahead of us. Service was good. We were warned the xlb and other dishes would be about 10-15 minutes wait, and only the "xiao cai" would be served immediately. But the xlb came within 10 minutes. I like that. Warn the customers and then serve the food earlier than expected, making it a good experience. Our tea was topped up very often without us having to ask. It had been quite some time (probably a couple of years or longer) since I last dined at the Paragon outlet and it had expanded since then. There were more tables available and I guessed people do get seated quickly despite the perennial long lines during dinner time. That was always daunting and explained why I hardly dined there. The xlb was still as good. Thin skin with a flavorful soup, enough to fill my spoon, and yummy meat. The fried rice was not as good as remembered though. It used to be really fragrant and just made you want more. Today's version was a bit wet, the rice stuck together and was quite a disappointment. The dumplings in vinegar and chili oil were average, mainly due to the thicker skin, so they were more chewy. I would say focus on the xlb and xiao cai, the others would be quite secondary.

Whenever i feel like easy fast lunch in orchard i go to this place. Nice dimsum, cheap, clean and decent place. Kids love it too. Come earlier, as its long queue most of the time when its lunch or dinner time. But no worry its goes fast.

A friend and I met with our children at Din Tai Fung tonight.  We were seated rather quickly considering the crowd. We ordered a lot of dumplings, spinach, and dates. Our food was delivered timely and it was delicious. There is lots of room for improvement in the service department at Din Tai Fung. My friend and I ordered a bottle of wine to split. The waitress brought us the bottle and two glasses and just set it on the table and left. Fortunately it was a screw cap so we could manage to pour our glasses ourselves, but needless to say that is a training issue. We also had to ask for water six times. Yes, you read that correctly, SIX times. Our children were thirsty, we wanted water and we asked for it six times. It was finally brought to our table. The food is very tasty, but the service is lacking.

I still like Jollibee's fried chicken though the size seemed to have shrunk. And when did they start offering a spicy and original option? Trying to be like the other fried chicken joints here?I usually go around 1130am when it is quieter. I was surprised to see a crowd at 1230pm ish on a weekday. My colleague told me to avoid going on Sundays as it would be packed to the gills. It seemed like the queue system has changed. Instead of a snaking single line leading to the many cashiers, it went to the typical many lines. And it also looked like they allowed people to find a table first before waiting in line. Luckily we still manage to snag a table after looking hard. The fried chicken was still good. We had a mix of original and spicy. The spicy was pretty hot though it was only confined to the skin. So I would suggest getting original and dipping the meat into chili sauce instead. The fries were still bad. The buttered corn was good and mashed potato decent.

In this review I will be comparing this Jollibee to the stores in America because the only other country I've had jollibees is in America (specifically California and Florida). This Jollibee is located on the sixth floor of Lucky Plaza. It's a pretty big store with a lot of seating inside so you won't miss it if you're walking by. The employees are abundant and friendly. They were still taking orders and letting people in past 9PM which was great for us because we walked in super late. Unfortunately, they only had a few pieces of original chicken left so we ordered whatever they had left.The chicken wasn't as crispy as I remember it being but that might've been because we ordered all the leftover chicken right before they closed. The menu was a bit limited - they didn't have some of my favorite desserts like the peach mango pie or halo halo. They also don't have sliders. However, I'm not sure if Singapore Jollibees stores have a different menu than the ones in America.I felt that the serving size was smaller than the sizes in America. The mashed potato side I had was very little and left me wondering if I should have ordered more. As for flavor, everything tasted consistent. I am still obsessed with Jollibees gravy - I can pour that on anything and be able to eat it.Overall, an average Jollibee with okay food and good service. Even though it is a bit cheaper here than in America, I'm still missing my favorite menu items and the larger American portion size.

I think this is only a place to reminiscence the taste and feel of home, not to get real food. The spag honestly tastes like rubber and I feel that the microwave ready meals at 7-11 taste way better. The spicy chicken was okay but not worth the line and the trip all the way to lucky plaza. You can get the same chicken at KFC or even your neighborhood western food stall at the food court

So Jollibee finally launches its first outlet in Singapore...and there happens to be a bunch of idiots running a Facebook page screaming for people to boycott Jollibee Singapore...for some illogical reason that only their neanderthal brains could possibly understand-to-be-logical.Anyways, I'm glad whoever these tards were...they didn't add to the obviously insane queues that welcome this amazing establishment in Singapore. Our first attempt of a UYE here failed miserably when our tiny group was not even allowed to join the line at 1830 hrs because THERE WAS JUST TOO MANY PEOPLE! Having finally witnessed such a ridiculous line, I made note to myself not to come back here for another month or so.ENTER...my fine lady, who is so sweet in every possible manner and always ever thoughtful. She remembered that the last UYE was a flop and asked if I wanted to give it a shot again. Of course, I'd love to give it a shot again...when the LINES are - maybe - GONE? X)I don't know about any of you BUT lines are always a turn-off EVEN if the food is spectacular UNLESS I'm in line with amazing company. The two hours we were in queue was probably one of the most fun moments I've had in a LONG time. Chatting, joking, playing stupid games on the phone, and making ridiculous jokes about the world, we slowly worked ourselves through the hordes and eventually got to order.So, if you think I'm going to stop at 1 chicken joy...after being in queue that long, THINK again...3x Chicken Joy1x Burger Steak2x Burger Yum w/ TLC2x Spaghetti2x 1pc Chicken w/ SpaghettiOkay, I ate most of it...and my sweet lady helped out. I bought a little extra as well to treat two Filipino friends who didn't believe that Jollibee was in Singapore.All-in-all...a good day.*******RECOMMENDATIONS:If you're going to bother lining up, make sure you try the Chicken Joy...makes Popeyes, KFC, and Church's (I mean Texas Chicken) look like they don't know fried chicken.Everything...else? Comfort food only for those who grew up eating it.Yelp 100: 21/100

I find the variety of food more interesting than the other fast food restaurants. Spaghetti and Beef patties in particular are not bad. Currently this is the only brunch in Singapore and avoid the long queue by going there either before or after meal hours. Avoid going on weekends as it can be so packed that you won't have much appetite to eat by the time your turn comes.
I think you want to avoid this location on Sundays. However, if you do want to try out this staple of Filipino fast food culture, the Aloha burger combo is a delight.

First try for Jollibee. Was surprise that even though the queue is long but it moves really fast so you won't really have to wait too long to dine in. Their service is better a lot, they do smile at customers while serving. Their chicken is good, colleagues say their chicken is better which also have a sauce which is provided too. The fries is better, the mash potato is better, the beef double yum burger is better and the butter corn is also better. This fast food is awesome! Will definitely go back for more.

Why is it more fun in the Philippines? Because their bees are jolly and they sell chicken!What kind of bees make milk?Boo Bees!!Okay, I think that's enough bee jokes for this review... ANYWAYS, this famous Filipino fast food chain finally came to Singapore and there were way too many people excited about this, so I wasn't able to taste the goodness 'til a few months later. I've been to the Philippines before; however it's been a hot minute since I've experienced the bee!I ordered the Chickenjoy and spaghetti combo- delicious and well priced at $6.60. Filipino spaghetti sauce is different in that it's sweeter, but it ain't truly Filipino unless you put hot dogs or Vienna sausage in it! The piece of chicken I had was crispy, juicy, sizable, and soooo much better than Popeye's!I've also tried the fries, but they're nothing to write home about. They do come with chili sauce, which is ok and not spicy.I've only visited during off peak times, and they're still quite busy. They've really mastered keeping the line moving, so the wait isn't bad. I think they still have a few pesky restrictions in place, ie your entire party has to be present and you can't order more than one meal per person, so keep that in mind if you decide to stop by.If I like it so much, why don't I just give it 5 stars and marry it? Well, first off, I'm already married, and second, it's a fast food chain- to keep my reviews and ratings distribution fair, it's my personal policy to give fast food chains 3 stars at most (unless they go above and beyond and save my life... Or give me a lifetime supply of free food. Just sayin'.)

the wait is finally over!:)has it been 3 months already???according to my reliable source, it has.since the day Linda, Jireh, Cindy and I failed to even get in the queue for a Jollibee fix, I have not been back.by chance or fate, I somehow scaled the daunting escalators of lucky plaza following my nose.it is the best GPS that money can't buy!once at the summit, it was a simple visual cue, no queue!!!so in I went at 5mins to closing and bravely ordered 2X 6piece buckets to go.I could sense it was to their dismay actually, as it was nearly time for them to clock out.I was then advised of a 30mins wait for my order, as if challenging my resolve, to which I immediately said yes to!What is 30mins in comparison with 2hours, right?excitedly I waited and somehow time just flew by!my reliable source quickly advised me, upon hearing of my purchase, to make sure the hot steam gets well vented away so as to ensure maximum crispiness.upon reaching home, the prize was eagerly unwrapped.it was late but who can resist eating a piece of still piping hot golden fried chicken?it probably is the best late night snack till date!super thin, crispy skin giving way to succulently juicy, simply tasty meat!it took great discipline to stop at one!Arnold's has long been top on my list when it comes to fried chicken but Jollibee might jolly well topple that ranking should they ironically manage to keep those 2hours queue away.

Great place to hang and meet friends for a quick lunch or dinner. Friendly prices that won't break the bank and  also brings back fond memories of home as you bite into the juicy burger or crunchy chicken joy.Great for kids and families

Ever since Filipino fast-food chain Jollibee (which specializes in their fried chicken) opened their first outlet in Singapore at Lucky Plaza, crowd here has never failed to get shorter, with queues stretching over to the neighbouring units. However, the queue clears off fast as well, though be prepared to wait at least 15 minutes to make your order.The 2-piece Chickenjoy with Rice and Drink ($6.60, +$0.20 to up-size drink) is the signature dish of the place. It's not hard to see why. The chicken is crisp on the outside and juicy on the inside. As such, oiliness of the fried chicken is kept to the minimum. The rice and chicken is best mixed and dipped into the gravy provided, which tasted similar to the chicken gravy used in KFC's Whipped Potato.If you do not want rice, the 1-piece Chickenjoy with Spaghetti and Drink ($6.60, +$0.20 to up-size drink) is an alternative. This meal was topped up with additional fries ($1.50). The spaghetti is sweet and is full on tomato taste. The fries are crisp but is certainly not one of their highlights.Definitely one of the better fried chicken joints around the Orchard area. Don't let the queues repel you from going!

Finally the crowd has died down. Came here at 4pm. The queue is long but fast. I waited for maybe less than 10 minutes for my turn.Oh well anyway, their fried chicken is not bad. Tender and juicy. It's not thickly  coated with flour and is well marinated. Just that I'm confused with the combination. Personally I think rice and fried chicken don't go well together as they are rather dry. The chicken is already good enough enough to eat on its own so I used the gravy for the rice. Again, the gravy and rice don't taste right together and I don't mean the combi is awful. Maybe the gravy would be more suitable for grilled meat? Good fried chicken but I won't make a special trip down:)

Jollibee was fun only because I got to queue with my fiance! It was a very long line, but that fried chicken called Chicken Joy truly brought Joy to my hunny, which in turn brought joy to me! heheMy fiance bought every item off the menu (well the hot foods) to make sure to try them all. The soy induced burger was good, the chicken was awesome, the beef patty....uh...not really a fan of the gravy!Other than the super long line---it was fun! If you're a fan, or the food brings back different wonderful memories...might as well make a stop by Lucky Plaza! MMmmmhhh!

So my colleague said "We HAVE to leave at 11am to queue" and was met with incredulous looks and then unceremoniously pelted with paper bullets. After some negotiating, a bunch of us left for a super early lunch at 11.30am only to be met by a snaking queue at Jollibee. A queue that took 1.5hours. A queue that a quarter way in, I'd exhausted all my Candy Crush lives. Imagine the horror. Seats were easily found, and we got our Chickenjoy. With all this hype, I'd expect rainbows to shoot out of our mouths at first bite. Or for angels to sing as we tore apart our meat. But alas no rainbows or angels there. Sure, the chicken is moist and homely tasting. And there's an interesting pat of rice served with your fried fowl. Which goes ok with the accompanying gravy. There's a bee mascot making his/her/its rounds, and getting terrorised by the kids in the restaurant. The kids relentlessly smack the bee's (padded) butt and stab his/her/its eyes but the bee's minder doesn't interject, which is a bit strange. Sure, it makes for entertainment but it's also a bit like animal abuse no?Don't stone me for saying this but... I don't get the hype. Possibly because in my books, nothing without rainbows and angels is worth a 1.5hour wait. And.. don't kill me for saying this but... I kinda prefer KFC for a more robust crunch and spicier packeted chili sauce.

When we arrived for lunch, the queue was so long we were afraid we wouldn't e able to fit it into our schedule. But I must say they've got their system down pat and they process the orders really quickly so it was fifteen minutes despite the great snake. That for me was the most impressive part. I was gonna give it three stars cos the chicken is just above average, id say I prefer it to Popeyes, but my fellow yelper Li ting says I should give it 4 stars because the chicken is so tender. But I don't think we'll be going back anytime soon, we haven't gotten over the guilt.

After looking at the wine connection (next door) disappointing selection and pricing of sparkling wine by the glass we stumbled across this tapas/Spanish restaurant next door. My expectations were fairly low but as they had two Cavas at 7 SGD per glass I was convinced to give it a try.We also ordered some different tapas for the table to share. The patatas bravas were acceptable,, the croquettes pretty good while the cheese and cold cuts can rather be skipped and the same goes for the padron peppers. In general the food is nothing to get excited about but as a snack when having a drink they are perfectly fine.The cavas were not the best I had but for this price it was a bargain. Nice outdoor setting and friendly service will encourage me to come back.

Came here after a very long day at work and I loved the food. Had the paella (can't remember the name and can't seem to find anything similar on their online menu, but it was the only one with no seafood in it) which was really good, well-cooked and satisfying (or maybe it's just because I was super hungry LOL). One of the best ones I've had in Singapore, on par (or perhaps even better) than the version in Serenity. Way cheaper too! Came in a large pan which was more than enough for 3. We also had the Catalunya pizza ($13)- really simple with only a topping of anchovies and vegetables but well-excecuted. The crust was thin yet flavourful, and very cripsy. And it was big for its price! Dessert was the Crema Catalana ($10) - essentially Creme Brulee. Nice but not sensational, but big enough for 3!. Still, it was a very good meal and worth it for the prices. 3 dishes filled the 3 of us up quite well- a feat considering that we'd been starving for 9 hours before that!Found it quite difficult to get the attention of waiters but they were helpful and polite when they finally came to our table.

This review will probably be of little use to most of you, given the circumstances of my visit to Barraka. The time is 2.15am on a Saturday night and we have just been ejected from The Chamber nearby where we were watching a big football match. They decided to close at half-time, those bastards. We walk around for a while in the Robertson Walk area looking for an alternative and Barraka pops up. The screens are a bit on the small side but there's space, they're open and willing to serve us booze. Moreover, the manager invites us in without malice, despite us being supporters of the team currently beating his 1-0.But the best part? The bill. Four whiskies = $28. That is just simply amazing in Robertson Walk. I have no idea if they had a deal or a happy hour or something, I didn't ask, I just stared at my bill in stupefied amazement.Well I lie actually, the true best part was when my team (Arsenal) won 2-0. But that's some thing the poor, Liverpool-loving Barraka manager had little control over.

Second time here and very pleased with the food, drinks, service and ambience. They have a good variety on the menu that I'm sure will please most tastes. We stick to a Paleo diet and the Polo (grilled chicken breast and vegetables) hits the spot. The prawns and mushroom tapas dish was awesome as well. The entire menu is very Paleo-friendly. The drinks are the cheapest we've found in town - and they're good. I really enjoyed the traditional sangria. The food is also very reasonably priced. Our service tonight has been awesome. This has easily become a large player in my roster of go-to restaurants.

I didn't try any of the food so I cannot comment on that. But Barraka is a nice casual hangout that serves a good selection of beer at fairly reasonable prices considering its central location. So how can you not like that? You do, however, have quite a lot of choices at robertson quay. So Barraka is not a bad choice but not exactly a standout choice with all the other restaurants and bars around.
Sucks! The staff manager of the place attitude!!! Yell at client and still say client yell at him. Please don't waste effort going.

This place is getting more and more crowded.... You are actually spoilt for choice when wanting a cuppa coffee in Tiong Bahru. Whisk is but one of the many cafes around the area offering you a decent cuppa coffee and pastries. Price range is about the same as most others. Pastry and cake selection not as wide. But still a nice place to just people watch (right at the cross road where Tiong Bahru market is) or just read a book (not as busy as Tiong Bahru bakery right across the road, and definitely not as noisy...). No wifi though and I don't see power points around...

Clean and cool inside. They have some kind of neato popsicles but didn't try those. Hokkaido milk flavor was one that stands out. Honestly ducked in here to use the restroom bc I didn't wanna use the ones at the market. The hub got some English tea and a cream pastry which he said was alright. It was bright inside. And the bathroom was super cute and clean although outdoors kind of so felt hot. Still grateful to be able to use it. They also have French macarons which were v pretty. Not sure of the taste though.
Pastries are so-so, coffee and other drinks just average. So sad that the former roast meat store occupying this space was replaced by a generic cafe.

The croissant was delicious. It was flaky and chewy at the same time. Tough combo to get outside of France. Not as buttery as a French croissant, but those are hard to find outside of France.  The price was good and overall the service was good as well. The place is nicely air conditioned for those hot days.
Newest cafe in the area. Not a bad place to pick up a drink on the way to work. Quick & Easy unlike the other cafes up near Kim Tian.

The burger bar is situated at an excellent location in town. I ordered the classic cheeseburger during my first visit to this place, since the classic should never go wrong. The meat patty is succulent and juicy, complete with fresh vegetables, cheese and burger bun! I enjoyed my food FRESH, and this did not disappoint!Food ordering is techy, head up to the tablets and tap what you need for the day! When your food is ready, number will flash and head over to collect it from the friendly service staff. There are classic burgers which you can choose from, or build your own burger! The sides are fantastic too! We ordered the onion rings which are crispy and oily. But well, there doesn't seem a way which they could drain the oil off the rings.TBB is a franchise co from Fatboys, by Singapore DJs, Vernon A and Justin Ang famously known duo as Muttons! I love how people open eateries with the concept of sharing the food they love.Definitely be back again as I'm a Fatboys fan too!!

The Burger Bar by fatboy's concepts. I think they grew. From the reviews I was expecting a small, nook in the wall but it was much bigger and could seat way more than 12 patrons. Low ceilings and 3 high speed fans make sitting on the long bench a breeze. 4 more booths for a less communal affair. Simple, minimal frills but still well themed. Reminding me of a 50s diner. I can like that.The burger. Up for review, the bacon cheeseburger. Lovely, juicy and tender patty. Bacon and cheese blend well. I much prefer this beef to bun ratio. The juiciness of the beef will soften the bun but everything is well contained. Default is the burger by itself which is great if you're not that hungry. Or go with the assortment of side orders and appetisers. Enough said. This guy cares about the product. No corners are cut with the condiments. Heinz ketchup, French's mustard. A corner to wash your hands and clean up after your meal. These lovely, small touches get a big plus from me. Highly recommended to get your burger fix here.

Well, this is a lovely hidden gem in the basement of Far East Plaza! This outlet is a pint sized version of your typical Fatboy's establishment, as there are only 12 seats available.They don't have any specialty burgers here; the concept is more build-your-own. The iPad ordering system is pretty straightforward and efficient. Even though Miguel and I ordered separately on two iPads, they were able to combine the orders seamlessly so we could pay one bill without any problems. Love!I ordered a cheeseburger on a brioche bun, no other extras- amazing! I thought the patty was dense and filling, and the brioche bun held everything perfectly even though the patty was very juicy. We also had an order of onion rings and I was amazed at how they were perfectly breaded and crispy.Unfortunately, the drinks from the cooler weren't cold that day (not sure if it's because they were just put there, or if something was wrong with the cooler) but we appreciated that the staff was upfront with us and let us know before we ordered. Other than that we were happy with our experience and wouldn't hesitate to come back again!

A well known burger bar chain under the Fatboy's group, Burger Bar has finally opened its door in the Balestier area. Terrific crunchy, hot sweet potato fries and chocolate milkshakes. Friendly service despite the new opening rush. I see an extensive selection of beef, chicken and lamb burgers plus mushroom and veggie options for the less-red toothed. Try one and let me know if you enjoyed it! A Western star in an otherwise local food haven known for its chicken rice and hawker eats.

Probably the best burger joint I've been in singapore! You can customize your burger, have as many extra patties you want; beef, lamb, you name it, all kinds of sauce; teriyaki, mayo and any veggies, etc. It was my first time there, and I ordered my burger which comprise of a beef patty, caramelized onion, portobello mushroom, some veggies, and I just wanna tell you guys the most important sauce you guys should be having; truffle mayo!!!!

The burgers here are excellent, its by the same people that do fat boy burgers and they taste just as good.They have a slightly different model, with an electronic self service ordering and pickup system.The food is presented with more of a fast food feeling, wrapped in grease paper, and delivered in a basket.Whilst the food is excellent, it feels a little over priced  for a self service, more fast food like restaurant.

If you blink you just may miss this gem located in a tight corner in the basement of Far Eat Plaza. Our service alone is a reason to go back. Timely, seamless, and extremely friendly.  The concept is you order your burger your way from a list of many options on an iPad. Pretty easy.My only negative would be that I had to ask for my burger to be cooked longer as it was pink in the middle still.  It was taken back and cooked to perfection.

I can't believe this place isn't getting the love it deserves! I must say that this was my favorite burger joint in Singapore! First of all, the concept is great - you make you own burger right from the buns to the sauce. They offer a wide selection of everything so you can definitely create the burger of your dreams! And I am proud to say to have done just that many times. So if you're a burger love, I definitely suggest that you give this place a shot! #awesome

The theory behind this place is fantastic. You come and can build your own burger from the bun up. Various options are included free of charge with extra add ons if you want to get fancy. I was really excited about my burger prospects when I placed my takeaway order and was drooling watching someone eat their burger and fries while I waited for mine to be done. When my turn arrived, my fries were drool worthy but my bun was completely soggy. Perhaps this wouldn't have been an issue if my burger had been eaten right away instead of needing to wait about 15 min to be enjoyed, I will try dining in next time. The only drawback there is that seating is very limited so if you go during a popular time finding a spot can be a challenge. Overall, my burger had good flavour, I will give them another go.

Location is superb; best burger within 100 meters.  Ordering is simple and efficient with a nice ipad app.  Lots of options from bun to meat to toppings and sides - you literally get to build your burger (no avocado or salsa for those looking for a Southwest burger). Server is friendly and fast.  Other customers are challenged with ipad app and understanding what a burger is and what they want on it - probably not the place to go to debate whether you should get cheddar cheese or provolone.  Then the wait begins.  The fries come out quickly; and they are tasty - I got the standard potato but the owner assured me the sweet potato fries are great.  Finally the burger comes out and it is everything you ordered... Hot, fresh, and satisfying... I would like my bun toasted a bit more and the patties to be flatter and wider; basically less spherical or meatball like.  Meat is pretty good and they do have Heinz ketchup to make it all real.  All in all a good burger at a good price with no ambience or frills.

Chili crabs are a must when in SG. We initially planned to visit Jumbo but ultimately went to King for the fact that they accept reservation. I had no chili crab baseline to compare to but King's was really tasty! Very saucy - my husband slurped it up like a soup, I drowned every grain and green in it. A good balance of buttery aroma and sweet chili. Fried buns are a must for soaking up every drop. I easily downed a whole dozen myself. Salted egg fried shrimp - apparently salted egg on every edible item is a huge trend in SG right now (ie fish skins, chips). Salted egg fried shrimp - another genius invention. Crispy head on shrimp dusted in  broken salted egg. Perfectly seasoned - I ate all parts shells included. Curry crab noodle soup - hugeeee pot! Very soothing - not overwhelmingly curryful which allowed the crab's natural sweetness to fill up each bowl! Soy steamed local fish - I can't recall the name of the fish (I was told it's not the most attractive). But the meat was so moist, flaky, and sweet! They also offer a deep fried version. Stir fried egg noodles - yummm, plenty of wok flavor and heat. Nothing like the Chinese version, the flavor was spot on. A great balance of sweet, salty, and spicy. They also offer a handful of non seafood dishes (mushroom beef tenderloin, general tso chicken). They were fine but I would stick to their seafood items tho. Overall - we enjoyed our meal tremulously! Don't forget to ask for gloves+bibs and get ready for a feast!

One of the best places I had for Chilli Crab. The man tou (bun), is crispy when its hot and perfect combi for the chilli crab gravy. The bamboo mussel is delicious with the mouthful of garlic topped on it.Can't miss this pan fried carrot too. It's my favorite dim sum item and yummmmmmmy!

The Chillie Crab is to be had here.  It's an open setting with plenty of options for 'set meals' or 'a la carte' - you can't go wrong.  The crab is served first, and sadly the other items arrive haphazardly after... Singapore has a horrible service industry.  I am told they do not pay their waitstaff and therefor will not find professionals until they do.
For big group of business meal or family gathering, I think ok to dine here. If you are focusing on food quality itself, I think soso only.

It was finally time tonight for me to try Black Pepper Crab.  I chose Long Beach Seafood because I wanted to explore a new District so I MTR'ed to Mountbatten to try it out over in Kallang.The entrance has an odd air of cacophony as multiple workers each with title badges parade about doing what they do best from the supervisor supervising to the cashier person pricing things.  Although they speak English, an awful lot got lost in translation which left me an uneasy patron unsure where I stood with regard to the pricing of what I was ordering.  As an illustration, I asked for a glass of beer (@$7.75) but wound up with a jug of beer ($23-ish) because the owner assumed I wanted a jug because I'm a stupid tourist or because I look like the type of person who wants a jug or he wanted to maximize how much money he could get out of me and simply willed me to have more than what I asked for.  I didn't appreciate that even if the intentions were good.Also, communicating our order was a bit of a guessing game.  The menu lay-out was confusing.  It had pricing but it seemed difficult deciding what to order.  The Crab menu was baffling too.  No pricing but evidently the "large" weighed between 800-900 Grams (whatever that means...too bad I didn't have a measurement converter ap on my phone) or the larger Sri Lankan crab weighing at around 1,000 grams.When we asked the server, it wasn't clearly explained to us and came off as if the price were $62 for either order which made no sense.  Because the communication wasn't clear, my appetite was waning.We ordered a few other items such as baby gai lan, a shrimp dish, and this fried tofu dish.All in all the dishes were ok.  I must admit that I was still excited about the Black Pepper Crab and when it arrived, I was in for a battle.  There was quality in the flavor and it became the only focus of my attention once it was plopped there in front of me.  Black pepper crab is buried in a pepper sauce giving the crab an almost medicinal flavor to it.  Initially, it's strange but then it becomes good.  It took me forever to eat that crab and I was a complete mess by the time I finished it.  That became a problem because all the other dishes, which I ignored, became cold by the time I was done.Throughout the eating process, I felt an uncomfortable "chi" there.  Staff were constantly darting by my table and seemingly marking me too often which was distracting.On the other hand, they were good about tending to my needs such as clearing away my plate that had carved out shells.  The service was also very prompt in general.  Food came pretty quickly, etc.But the overall vibe here made me uncomfortable for some reason.  It wasn't a fun place to eat at as the sound acoustics were noisy and the staff constantly rushing by made me dizzy.  I guess the table wasn't a good location giving the working dynamics of this restaurant.By the time it was over, we left paying over $200 and didn't really feel it was worth it.  If anything, I wouldn't pay that much to come here again even though the food was pretty good.I wouldn't recommend this place for a tourist, but, they do give their best and the place had certain good qualities to it like high traffic and clean overall facilities.Loved the tank filled with lively Alaskan King Crabs to the right of the entrance.

I know so many people that like crab but hate the work that goes with it.  Well, at Long Beach King they will make you very, very happy as the staff is willing to take the meat out of the claws for you!  During our recent visit to Singapore, we had a fabulous dinner here.  Long Beach's Chili crab was the best according to my husband.  I'm sure that them shelling the crab for him helped to make that declaration!  They served the crab with these buns that you use to sop up the chili crab sauce.  The buns look like regular old buns, no big deal. But when you take a bite, WOW, they are amazing!  Apparently, they steam the bun first and then deep fry it!  It is like an unsweet donut.  yelp.com/biz_photos/long…My personal favorite dish during this dinner was the Dong Bo Spare ribs.  These little gems were tender and flavorful.  I loved it.  You can tell they were slow cooked as the sauce reduced down to a sweet and savory glaze.  It had me thinking of trying to recreate it when I got home.  yelp.com/biz_photos/long…Long Beach King had a dish that I've never seen before.  They stuffed tofu with minced prawns and then deep fried the whole thing.  Everyone loved it.  yelp.com/biz_photos/long…The service at this restaurant is impeccable.  We had our plates constantly changed and our teapot was never empty.  When we make it back out to Singapore, we'll definitely be back.

Good crab but a bit pricey. Bamboo clam is alway my favorite. Fried rice is not worth trying . Fried mee goreng is ok. Fried tofa ok only. Best part still the black pepper crab. Chilling crab is ok but is not spicy and more for overseas European guests.

We had great pepper crab and great chili crab here... service was super friendly, but it was a bit slow. We had to order a couple of things twice as orders were just not turning up.Overall, it's a pleasant restaurant with reasonably good food... and worth a trip for the pepper crab and chili crab alone :-)   ...however, make sure you bring a credit card ;-) - it really isn't inexpensive...

We love coming to this long beach cos the chili crab here is phenomenal!! We have had so many other chili crabs around and this is always our fave go to place for seafood! Get the deep fried man tou and dip in the chili sauce! The black pepper crab is also to die for! The black pepper is fried very well and is extremely fragrant! Must try!

Tasty food... Everything was wonderful (black pepper crab, chili crab, spinach with oyster sauce, bee hoon noodles with clams, and steamed buns). The sauce of the chili crab was amazing and you will need the buns to dip into that sauce. Don't try chili crab at a Hawker Centre; go to this place that specializes in chili crab... Huge difference.

The cafe was located just in front of the Sixth Avenue MRT. The first level is for dine in while the second level is the shop. The place offered healthy fusion dishes with options for vegans, vegetarians and gluten free.6th AVENUE ROSTI ($18.50++)herbed sweet potato rosti, smoked salmon, asparagus, onion, poached egg, wasabi aioli Although the serving looked small, I was quite full after having it. The rosti looked quite thin and dry but there was a sweetness which came from the sweet potato in it.SKIN SMOOTHIE ($8.50++)banana,orange, raspberry, strawberry, soy lecithinIce blended, the drink was thick, smooth and fruity in taste.Overall food was delicious and the place was quite cozy there was only a couple of tables occupied during sat morning.

There is no place for arrogance in the restaurant business. While 3 of the food items we order were very good, the avocado cucumber soup was basically uneatable as it had such contrasting and spicy tastes, neither my wife or I could eat it.  We told the inexperienced, young server about it and she had no reaction, just took it away. When the bill came, they refused to give any restitution for it. That is a bad business practice in the service industry. Shows a lot of arrogance. We certainly won't return again. Way to pricy for the quality of food too!  Guess you can't believe all the reviews all the time.

Feeling like raw, fresh, vegan food? Come here!We came here on a Friday night for dinner, for two. This place doesn't get that crowded, so no reservations were needed when I called to check. We got the veggie brown rice bowl, zucchini pasta with pesto, and mushroom soup to share. We felt sufficiently filled as their portions aren't stingy.I really enjoyed the brown rice bowl, because it was topped with a mix of veggies, chirashi style, and had a choice of two sauces over it. Tasted like a brown rice topped with guacamole ingredients - so yum! Our mushroom soup was filled with the goodness of mushrooms, and because this place is dairy-free, this soup is not the run-of-the-mill cream of mushroom, but rather, a blended, chunky emulsion of mushrooms. Very tasty. I really enjoyed the zucchini pasta, which is spiraled raw zucchini, tossed with a pesto. Carb-free, guilt-free, and raw.We finished it off with a raw chocolate "cheesecake", which had a nut base, and the "cheese" in the cake wasn't very apparent, but it was a pleasant chocolate "custard" of sorts. I really enjoyed my meal here, without feeling that something had to give for the dairy and meat that was missing. I would revisit again with no qualms!

If you're a health concious homo sapien living in Singapore then this will be your holy shrine. Literally the BEST place that I recommend any of my health loving friends to visit in Singapore.First off - the staff are so friendly. I would come here to eat lunch everyday in Singapore if I could. They are just so bright and cheery. The ambience is very chilled and laid back and the food is wonderful. There is no booking so if you're coming for a weekend brunch, I would recommend coming early because the place does fill up very fast.There is a lot on offer to order on the menu and I feel there is something for everyone. If you're vegan then this is heaven on earth but if you're not, you won't think your friend has just brought you into hell either. There are burgers and meats on the menu but I feel The Living Cafe has gone out of its way to offer the best quality food possible for each category. No hidden nasties here.They also have a big fridge filled of yummy raw treats! I remember how excited I was to find The Living Cafe in Singapore after having discovered raw treats in the US and the UK. This place had become Utopia. Upstairs you will find a huge selection of books which make excellent additions to any food lovers library. They also sell bits and bobs that health freaks (me) in Singapore generally have a hard time finding such as Bee Pollen, Coconut Oil, Spiralizer, Vitamix..Even if you're not that 'into' being healthy I would definitely give this place a go to see what its all about. And if you're brave enough, try one of their Wheatgrass shots. Take them instead of Tequila. Same bitterness but the after effect out weighs it, I assure you! ;).

Somehow, it's really hard to find genuinely healthy food options that aren't salad or the healthy afterthought on a menu. But this place has got it all - raw food, vegan, vegetarian, gluten free, and nut free items. Literally everything here is healthy (perhaps except the desserts, which while made with natural ingredients, are still sweet).The kids menu is healthy too - none of those burgers and fries stuff. Wholewheat bread, brown rice, etc.Good stuff. Your heart will thank you.

The menu is about a half raw and half cooked dishes with lots of vegetarian selection. There's enough on it to keep you coming back to try things even though it's temping to re-live delicious dishes. I'm not a raw foodist but I've certainly been to raw restaurants all over the world and would say this is a good one. Also having it not exclusively raw is nice for feeding diverse groups of people.The service is... well Singaporean... I'm not sure what happened but it went from surprisingly good to quite poor over the period I've been going there. So that's sad but not unexpected.They also sell raw food ingredients, desserts-to-go, juicers and they give raw "cooking" classes. Lots going on here and while it's never packed when I go in, it's certainly never empty either.

Having been surrounded by vegan options in Los Angeles, it can be a challenge to maintain such a diet when traveling in Asia. Thus it was such a pleasure to discover Living Cafe. Dining here felt like I was back in the LA vegan scene. I thought of it as a cousin to Cafe Gratitude. I started off with a Pure Green (wheatgrass, celery, spinach, parsley). It's a drink for those who chase after nutrients as opposed to flavor. The Zucchini Pesto Pasta also tasted healthy. It's for those who enjoy bland dishes. I am one of those people so I liked it. The desserts and smoothies are sweet. Try the yummy Spirulina Mintball. The mint is the superstar ingredient. The heart-shaped cookies made of dehydrated raspberries were an unguilty pleasure. The Chocolate Monkey (cashew milk, banana, dates, cacao) made a delightfully filling post-dessert. Will definitely be coming back to Living Cafe for more nutritious goodies!

I love the living cafe so much, I could cry. Located on Bukit Timah and 5th Avenue, I'd be here day after day if it weren't so far and out of the way from where I lived. As I try to get away from the plethora of oil laden carb heavy hawker food and onto the raw foods wagon, I start to realise how much Singapore is lacking in it's healthy, organic, gluten/dairy/refined sugars free cafes. In fact, if I'm not wrong, The Living Cafe is the only of it's kind so far here in Singapore (if someone knows of another raw cafe, please let me know!)The Living Cafe specializes in food that nourishes your body, from the inside out. Most of their menu is raw (meaning, they are all raw vegan foods that have not been heated above 115 degrees fahrenheit in order to preserve it's nutrients). I know, sounds like they'd only serve salads, correct? Wrong. My favorites on the menu include their Zucchini Pesto Pasta (note: this isn't actually pasta but zucchini shredded to look like spaghetti and pesto sauce homemade uses herbs and nuts), their Raw Lasagne, Raw Vegetable soups (cold - perfect for a hot day), their Living Rolls (rice paper rolls), Tofu Avocado Rolls, Raw Zucchini Dip (with Flaxseed crackers to dip) and not forgetting their AMAZING AMAZING raw/gluten/refined sugar free desserts. Honestly, the desserts in itself make a trip down here worth it (imagine tiramisu that actually tastes like tiramisu but made solely out of coconut, dates, nuts and other whole ingredients that give you a sugar fix WITHOUT the sugar high)I love raw foods for it's long term benefits as well as for how good it makes me feel right away, however, making raw foods is truly an art and without the proper knowledge and creative skills, you'd end up eating salads everyday. The Living Cafe truly makes it easy to eat raw from time and time with their creativeness and amazing sauces that liven up otherwise tasteless vegetables. On top of that, service is very friendly and the space is nice (nice enough to sit all day with a book) with a small area for your kids to play while you enjoy lunch too. My advice? Go for lunch (they close for dinner), get dessert and take a look at their little store upstairs after (they sell things like the Vitamix, Raw Cacao, Chia Seeds, the Zucchini Pasta maker and much more!)

Delicious healthy food. A bit expensive, but worth it once in a while. The vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free options here don't taste like rabbit food (which is sometimes how they taste), but are wholesome, filling, flavorful meals. The servers are incredibly pleasant and efficient. I will absolutely be returning for another meal.

At the heart of TLC menu is RAW Food or RAW-Fusion Food. It uses no red meat, no cow dairy, no white sugar, no preservatives, no additives, no artificial colorings and include gluten free alternatives. So if you are quick to spot the (loop)holes, this place is not entirely vegan, as it serves things like salmon and goat cheese.Starters were the hand-cut Sweet Potato Wedges ($4) that were earthy and good. Lightly baked with olive oil, it did not had the tempting smell of fries from fast food outlets but an alluring scent of coriander seeds. Some might find it rather firm but these were perfect for napping in the home-made mayonnaise (made of cashew nut milk, lemon juice, water, olive oil and salt but no egg yolks.)Follow that up with TLC cheese burger ($15): a dehydrated patty of portobello mushrooms, almonds and sunflower seeds, topped with tomatoes, sprouts and romaine lettuce. I stared in disbelief at the bun-less burger as those burgers from the opposite tables had buns and cheese.Though the mushroom patty had a robust aroma, it was tough and dry, not aided by an unidentified bland orange sauce Wished it was a simple grilled Portobello mushroom with garlicky herbs. But there were good things like the Mexican-inspired Raw Taco Boats ($12). My trepidations of greasy wheat glutens dissipated when the two large sized mock meat turned out to be made of dehydrated walnuts. The light guacamole and mango salsa sauce had a touch of Indian flavors, probably because this dish used similar spices such as cumin.  While the savoury food were wholesome, it was the RAW desserts that blown us away. Each had their own merits and everyone declared our own favourite item. I love the Raw Dark German Chocolate Cake ($8.50) made with Dates, Zucchini, Coconut oil, Cacao Powder, Irish Moss Honey and Macadamia. It was compact and chocolatey, not too sweet despite a toffee-lookalike honey layer on top. The shards of fragrant toasted coconuts were a bonus.As for the Raw Blueberry Cheesecake($8.50)made with coconut oil, agave, cashew and lemon juice, we could not be bothered by the alien-sounding ingredients such as psyllium husk, soy lecithin, Irish moss, as we dived straight into the delicate mousse and crunchy base. A bit of sweet and a bit of summer fruity flavours, we did not miss the sharp tang of cream cheese.Tiramisu (actually we all did)  was made of natural coffee extract and sitted on chalky and fragile almond-flour cake base. This is literally an authentic tiramisu sans the fats from Mascarpone Cheese and Raw Egg Yolks (Yes, tiramiusu is made of raw eggs too). And who says tiramisu must have the alcohol to taste good? Honestly, I left the place feeling more satisfied than I had expected (perhaps it's due to eating "Real Food" ). However, the fact that nearly every dish were full of (grinded) NUTS, drove me nuts a little. Perhaps I would still pick Indian/Chinese style vegetarian food from Raj Restaurant over TLC.  That said, don't leave without trying TLC's desserts which had not been compromised on flavours. Hoping that they can satisfy my sweet tooth while bring less harm to my health, I happily dabao (takeaway) more items home

Let me start off by first saying that I'm a red-blooded, meat-eating American who was just looking for a healthy change for a weekend brunch. I usually can't get too full from just eating vegetables and had to order a number of items to feel satisfied here.We started with the living cafe roll, which contained an assortment of fresh vegetables, wrapped in daikon sheets and had two splotches of different sauces on the nicely-presented sides of our plate. While clearly fresh and juicy (and the creaminess of the avocado was a good complement to the fresh peppers and lettuce), I feel like the sauces needed to be either thicker or just marinated into the vegetables-- as I needed to dip my pieces several times to get a flavorful bite. And because there's no real binding agent, the pieces also fall apart fairly easily, unless you put a whole piece into your mouth-- which can be a bit challenging.On the other hand, the raw zucchini lasagne was flavorful and fresh, but a bit small in its portion.I also ordered the acai kickstart, which was a very tasty balance of bananas, oats, honey and acai-- until you ate past the top inch and are left a bland layer of with frozen acai filling up the bottom 2/3 of the cup.Because I still wasn't full after the three orders, we also had the poached fresh salmon-- which has pieces as small as you'd find in sushi nigiri and was clean and unsalted-- and the hand-cut sweet potato wedges-- which were huge potato segments (they used both the traditional orange sweet potato, along with a purple variety) that were pretty decently fried, without being oily.The flat white coffee with soy milk is pretty decent (although they had run out of the hazelnut milk that we had initially wanted to try).Overall, I wasn't a huge fan of the place, but I think that it lives up to its concept and will please raw foodists and other healthy living enthusiasts in Singapore.Very nice, casual atmosphere too with very clean, polished setup. The crowd seemed to consist of a lot of Caucasian mothers who took/take prenatal yoga classes.

This place is quite interesting. It's an eatery under a wellness center. They provides fruit and veggie juices with ingredients that are hard to come by in many healthy restaurants I've been to. They have juices with coconut water, goji berries, cilantro, wheatgrass, etc., but they also add supplements to some of their juices like Vitamineral green, lecithin, maca powder, etc. Their smoothies and shakes are vegan, made with nut or rice milk, a refreshing change if you want to cut dairy out of your diet. The food menu, however, is not 100% vegetarian. They have chicken and fish on the menu from what I remember. The night I went, I had the TLC roll and the TLC Cheeseburger, both of which are vegetarian. The roll did have homemade mayo so I'm not sure if its totally vegan, but the quality of the ingredients are definitely very good. The price sort of matches that, reasonable. I paid $40 for a fruit and veggie juice, a roll, the cheeseburger and a vegan/gluten free chocolate cake.This place also sells supplements, tools to make things at home like a nut milk bag, mason jars and the like, as well as ingredients like salt, vanilla extract, palm sugar, etc. Not gunna lie though, those items were expensive and I know that I can get these same items for cheaper back in the states or even in other shops in Singapore.

It's my first experience with RAW food andI went in really raw and clueless about what it is all about. Don't worry, they don't expect you to dine a la neanderthal style, bloody meat and all. The raw part comes from the emphasis on raw vegan cuisine, no dairy or meat products, food cooked below 48deg Celsius. It's all quite healthy really and of course the food would preserve more of the vitamins and nutrients when it's not overheated. What I had was a special kiwi menu created by The Living Cafe but that kinda gave us the idea how food is prepared here. A lot of nuts are used, in making dehydrated crackers and tart base. It gives it a crunchy texture which I like. If you have allergies, pray stay away.There are also cooked food available and different cuisines as well. Italian and Thai are among them. It's not that intimidating trying raw food and I think TLC makes it really easy for you to forget its even raw in the first place. Do give it a try. TLC is part of the Balanced Living Asia group located at the same compound. You can find out more about the benefits of RAW food here.

My only conclusion as to why this cafe is rated almost 4* on Yelp vs the sub par experience I had on Saturday was this:  the standards for service are low and people are desperate for a semblance of raw/vegetarian food that they will overlook a lot of shortcomings.I live in the area and have driven past the Living Cafe and it looked like a place I should try because I enjoy eating clean and I am willing to pay higher prices for quality (and some serenity even). My better half is also a gluten-free eater. Well I walked in on a Saturday morning and there was one table occupied. No one greeted me and so I figured I'll just sit down and wait for service. 20 minutes later I was still ignored while another party came in, sat at the table at the back of the cafe and was waited on immediately. I also observed the same for the next two tables that walked in. The cynical part of me would say maybe I wasn't the right skin color, but nice let's-give-them-the-benefit-of-doubt side would argue maybe the service just is bad.So I got myself a menu and managed to order my food by getting one waiter's attention. Service was better from there as said waiter was efficient in delivering the food, but that's about it. I ordered the granola crunch bowl, pancakes and vegetarian omelet. When the food came, I got the same surprise I had a few months ago at the other cafe down the street, the LITTLE diner. Yup folks, small portions for not so small prices. And it was not like I was eating anything particularly unique or outstanding. The pancakes were on the rubbery side with a *sprinkle* of blue and strawberries and a sparse drizzle of what tasted like honey. The omelet was tasty and went well with the multi-grain bread but again, I felt kind of ripped off because this was easily something my mum could make, bigger and for cheaper.I guess this places is a convenient snack place after yoga class but I really wouldn't make the effort to eat here otherwise. Onaka, 7 Sensations and even Whole Earth offer much better value considering the creativity that's put into reinterpreting dishes, the portions and the quality of ingredients.

If there's one thing exceptional about my palette, it's the fact that I don't like vegetables. Nadda, not one vegetable. There is no exception, I might eat the occasional veg if I'm too lazy to pick it out of my noodles and its soft, but otherwise, I really don't like vegetables. Something about the texture and taste as a whole.So for me to visit a place that specializes in raw vegan food... definitely an experience.Eating uncooked food is quite an acquired taste - I am Chinese and I like my food hot, thank you very much. There was a raw mushroom soup I attempted - think uncooked mushrooms pureed into soup-like texture akin to Gazpacho with a really strong raw mushroom smell. I only managed one scoop of that. There are also raw pizzas and raw pastas (it's sliced up zucchini!), and even cakes for those who like this sorta thing.Thankfully, there are options for the less refined palettes, I had a cooked pizza with a mysterious "cheesy" sauce, inverted commas and all. While cooked, it was healthier with a whole wheat base that reminded me of digestive biscuits, but overall quite yummy.Raw vegan food does come at a price though - the portions are not very big but the prices are still the pricey bistro sort. Also, make sure you have time because the food is all freshly prepared and takes quite awhile to come.

I LOVE that they have a raw food menu as well as a gluten free menu!  These are two concepts that are ridiculously challenging to find in Singapore, and I commend the Living Cafe for having put in the effort on both fronts.  Having moved to Singapore from Los Angeles where gluten-free and raw food restaurants are aplenty, I must admit that the food at Balanced Living is lacking a bit of creativity.  Their raw pizza is nothing more than a salad atop a flax crust.  The salad menu is much smaller than I would expect from a health food restaurant.  The raw zucchini pesto pasta is quite nice.  Their raw desserts really do hit the mark:  raw cheesecake, raw german chocolate cake, raw chocolate mud pie, raw apple pie, raw chocolates, raw spirulina balls,  etc.   I like that they actually do have meat as an option.  My husband loves coming here because he can still get a "real meal" while I enjoy my raw food!Hopefully more people will go to the Living Cafe and they will be able to both grow and refine the menu a bit!

I've been going to Tomi for a few years and the standard has been pretty consistent. Quality sushi and sashimi served at solid prices. Service is polite and generally fast. Decor isn't anything fancy; I wouldn't recommend this as a date place. The lunch specials are pretty worth it. $25 for a sashimi lunch set (sasimi, rice, pickles, soup and appetizer, fruit and salad) and $28 for a chirashi don set (chirashi don, soup, salad, fruit and chawanmushi). I've ordered a la carte (from the regular and monthly specials menu). It was very good but it added up quickly! Tomi renovated a few months ago and while the prices and quality for the lunch specials haven't changed, the portions have gotten a tad smaller! I guess something had to give. A new addition with the renovation: they now sell bottles of sake to go, at a slightly cheaper price than dining-in!

Quality sushi and sashimi served at this family-friendly restaurant. They're serious about the quality of the food and it shows. Prices can run up a little if you order a la carte but you get what you pay for - the freshest cuts for a reasonable price.I had the lunch set of the day, which came with salad, chawanmushi, 8 pieces of nigiri sushi, about 5 pieces of anago (salt water eel) tempura, miso soup, and coffee jelly. At $28++ or $33 net, I'd say this was a steal.

A warning late last year that tsukiji fish market will be closed for about a week at the beginning of 2015 resulted in me having to curtail my japanese cravings till after.obviously, tomi was not a bad option after one week of fasting.the daily lunch set on display, outside the shop, attracted me like bees to honey and the daily lunch set it had to be!for those who can't decide, their numerous sets, many seasonal specials plus ala carte options, will leave you even more undecided!but thankfully their helpful photo menu does seduce you, with their visual appeal, to arrive at a quicker decision.my strategy has always been to stick to any particular specials or sets that they might be promoting. these are normally the freshest and also most bang for the buck.for sushi fans, the rice here may be more generous than you are used to but it is only because they use Niigata KOSHIHIKARI rice, the best brand in Japan, and wants you to have more of a good thing!:)as for their special purpose soy sauce, i can't really taste the subtle difference, quite possibly one being saltier than the other?tomi invaded SG back in 2010 with much fanfare for it's flagship parco outlet.back then my taste buds were not as refined and tomi was sort of a revelation.but since then the tsunami of really good sushi joints have left tomi@parco in it's trail of destruction, which eventually led to it's closure.i'm glad this tomi has sprouted and is so near to me.for those days that i just need my fish to be fresh and tea to be hot, i come to tomi.

Nice Japanese restaurant in Novena Square. Quite crowded when we got there. The sashimi was quite fresh and the tempura was crispy and delicious. The Kaisen don was also good. The beef was also good. Quite authentic Japanese food.

Quality Japanese food at reasonable prices that are highly that your sushi tei but lower than your tatsuya. There are monthly and seasonal menus to keep your taste buds excited each visit. Friday night was packed and the order took a while to arrive. A couple of mistakes in the order were made but luckily quickly rectified. No point making a second order on the busy night because the food will take forever to arrive and likely after you are done with four first round of ordering. Service was trying when there's a crowd but still acceptable.

I have been wanting to try Tomi Sushi for the longest time and finally got the chance to do so. After reading reviews that the sushi is better than the other items, I decided to go for the daily lunch special ($30++) instead of the Nigiri Sakura set. The daily lunch special includes deep fried salmon cheeks in sauce, sushi, chawanmushi, miso soup, salad and fruits. I find the sushi is ok, it is better than the usual sushi chain, but not as good as expected. I guess I should have tempered my expectations a bit. The fish is fresh but the uni could be better. The salmon cheek pieces were drenched in the sauce that it was too salty sweet for my taste and there were so many bones and scales to make it enjoyable. Pork cheek it is not. My bad for equating cheeks to tender morsels of meat. The chawanmushi was a nice surprise. No bubbles in it. It was silky smooth and slid down easily. The miso soup was average. The salad had too much dressing in it. I should have ask for all sauces and dressing to be on the side. Fruit dish was the nondescript slice of watermelon and grapes. The service was ok, they only went round topping hot tea when the room was packed which was about a quarter past 12. I like the bright and airy dining room which makes it a pleasant dining experience. There is another section which is the sushi counter where you can watch the sushi chefs slice and dice and make your sushi in front of you.

This place did not let down my tastebuds addiction to sashimi and my ever increasing draw to any Japanese seafood. I had one of the bento box type dishes with sashimi, miso, rice and some white fish. The price for decent Japanese can be expensive in Singapore with a lack of quality. However I assume this place is actually run by Japanese that want to hold up there reputation for fresh food. Lovely fresh sashimi and sushi rolls, good price. Recommended for locals of Novena & Newton.

Really good quality sushi made with care and value for money. The lunch sets are a bargain - although Ichiban Boshi around the corner attracts the queue. I'd rather pay a bit more for the better quality sashimi and sushi here. The lunch chirashi bowl is really worth the money. Had the unajyu set really and it's the best value for unagi I've had in singapore. It's $50 but the substantial chunk of eel is beautifully grilled, tender and the sauce is not sweet and full of umami.

I often walk past this place on the way to the gym but this is my first time trying it. The place always looks very empty and I always had the impression that it would be very ex. Nevetheless, my review is that this is really high-quality Jap food. Unfortunately, my Jap friends do not know about this place although the franchise apparently came from Japan.We opted for the sets - tempura and cord fish. It's quite a small serving though. For the cord fish, you also get salad and sashimi. Round it up with pickles, miso soup and fruits make for a delightful meal. The place is clean and brightly lit. The staff are friendly.

My fave sushi joint for an affordable but filling lunch set at good quality. They fly in their fish supply from Tokyo at least once a week and all the rice is from Niigata. Always a good sign when the sushi and sashimi soy sauces are different (one is lighter and more fragrant, the other saltier and stronger flavored). Service is good and the owner is Japanese, though the counter chefs appear to be mainly Chinese with one Japanese (head?) chef. Always packed at lunch so avoid peak hours if possible.

Tomi Sushi has in the recent month opened up another outlet at Velocity (Novena Square), tucked at a corner. This place comes highly recommended by many and being a japanese food lover, I decided to check it out.This place prides themselves for bring the best japanese from Niigata and is very particular about the rice and soy sauce used.  The restaurant caters to people of different needs. It is suitable for families and private party too. I have checked out the place during lunch and decided to try out their lunch sets. I ordered their salmondon ($15).  The sets are value for money and if you are in the mood for some hot soba, you can top up and change the miso soup.  They do have limited and seasonal items that you can order too.  If you are in the mood for ala carte, do prepare to pay a bit more as it can get rather pricey.
One of a few authentic Japanese sushi stores in Singapore. Price is reasonable given its good food quality.

This is THE sushi place according to my father, who had excitedly rushed us down for lunch on a Sunday to bring us to his favourite local Japanese restaurant for the first time. Claiming that he never eats sushi in Singapore from any other restaurant, my sushi-loving siblings were more than eager to go but...there were a few hiccups and we were late. We arrived at 2pm on the dot, just as they were closing the kitchen. After much negotiation with the waitress, she let us in on the condition that we finish our food by 2.30. However, we were informed that the kitchen does not serve hot food anymore, and as I'm not a huge fan of sashimi and sushi, we were somewhat bummed. A minute later, this was fixed by my father talking to the chef so I'd say, 2 thumbs up for service excellence. The food was excellent, especially the sushi sets. I can't comment on sashimi that I don't eat but the sushi sets at lunch were worth the price, although the other dishes such as tempura and maguro katsu pale in comparison. If you do visit, you're better off ordering a pure sushi set because I have to concur with my dad but I don't think the other dishes were quite as worth the while. Do arrive on time though because rushing a meal is never good for digestion.

Tomi Sushi is a very solid option in Novena which delivers some very good sushi at a reasonable price.  Tomi sushi is a small chain that hails from Niigata, which is famous for its rice and sake.  They are definitely proud of both at Tomi, and also pay attention to many details, such as using a different soy sauce for sushi versus sashimi.  I dropped by for a late lunch, and found myself overwhelmed with many choices in terms of lunch sets.  I picked the reasonably priced Sakura Nigiri set, which included 8 pieces of sushi, a small salad, chawanmushi, chicken kara-age, miso soup, and fruit - all for $28. The sushi was excellent, and as the wasabi is already in the nigiri, there is no additional wasabi. The style is definitely very close to what you will eat in Tokyo, and the sushi was very good.  The rice was good, but the texture was different from what I usually expect - it was less firm here, but still very good. The sake list focuses on selections from Niigata, which is one of my favorite regions, and the prices were reasonable.  I'll definitely be coming back, as they are having some unagi specials including Hitsumabushi!  Very highly recommended  for a more traditional, authentic taste without blowing the bank.

Not what it used to be. Very disappointing to see one of my favorite restaurants for past years go so far down hill. I hadn't eaten at this location for more than a year because of my last experience, but thought I give them another shot. Bad decision. Last time it was service and food, this time service was okay, but food mediocre at best. Although, the service staff seemed to have a problem with English. That's a shocker in Singapore. Biggest compliant is they no longer serve bread with meals. Although, the still have a bread plate. I've never seen a soup and pasta restaurant that didn't have bread on the menu. Soup is still good, but the pasta was dry and way too much garlic. Sorry, CPK, it's Jamie's Kitchen next time.

It's been over 2 years since I last went to a CPK in the US, so I had the singapore one on my list as a place to satisfy my craving of the old memories.  sadly..as usual...things are never as good as you seem to remember them. I opted for the Milan thin crust pizza. it was just a thin and with that crisp edge that I love. the toppings had a good serving of cheese and sausage, yet somehow I feel like something was missing.  it was kinda bland. not much flavor. maybe the caramelized onions were not mixed in well. not sure...it just wasn't the same. or maybe the US ingredients are just different. either way, the pizza was decent...the drink was great - cold and refreshing..just what a cooler should be. just think it's slightly over priced...8 bucks for that glass.. I wouldn't say I've scratched CPK off my list....its just not gonna be on my top must go to places. it will be a "if I'm in the area and craving pasta..." place. also..did CPK stop giving bread as a starter? or is that just a USA thing?

There are not as many traditional american fare as one hope in a cosmopolitan city, but cpk comes as good as it come if you like the US menu pallate and portion size. Too bad waiters aren't quite trained and familiar with american condiments i.e., mustard, balsamic vinegar, etcOther than that, good place for those who wants chilis or aplebees alternatives

Definitely not like the CPK in the US, that's for sure.  I needed a quick somewhat healthy salad and had an hour to kill on a Saturday between appointments.  I sat at the bar, and ordered my usual, the Thai crunch 1/2 chicken salad.  No.  The salad was old looking, the chicken looked like it was either frozen, or came out of a bag somewhere, and the dressing was clumpy.  It looked like they at least make their pizzas homemade, but definitely stay away from the salads.

I love salad, so the volume and variety is salads they have is wonderful.  Pizza is average American Pizza, nice.  Pasta is above average - I think overall quite ok.サラダは日本人にとって嬉しいボリューム、味も悪くないです。ピザはアメリカンピザそのもので、いわゆるシカゴ（PAN）ピザとは違います。パスタも特別すごいという訳ではありませんが、美味しく食べられます。家族にはオススメできます。
Nice find in Orchard road! Great spring rolls and good pizza plus a good wine selection! Nice cozy place with good service!

This is a place that is serving good food minus the pretentions that comes with most of the outlets these days. This is probably the first restaurant that started to serve gourmet pizzas like peking duck, chipotle pizza etc.Nice and if I can say healthier pizzas with lots of fresh vegetables. Servings are good and pricing is as reasonable as they can be. Cheaper than any of the places in any of the quays or dempsey.Will definitely be back and might make this as a regular place for us.

I ate here with my family again.  The last time we came here I ordered chicken quesadillas.  The so-called "chicken" quesadillas barely contained any chicken at all leading me to complain.  They gave me more virtually chicken-less quesadillas and some coupons so I could return and give them another try.That's what we did today.  We gave them another try.  I had chicken quesadillas again and, once again, the "chicken" quesadillas were practically chicken-free.  I can only conclude that this is how they serve "chicken" quesadillas at California Pizza Kitchen, with almost no chicken in them whatsoever.As God is my witness, I didn't know chickens could get polio.

Went to California Pizza Kitchen for my friend's birthday celebration. We heard that they are good at their skinny pizza.Ambience was good, not too noisy, and they have 2 levels, level 1 and basement. We had a table at the basement and arrange a surprise birthday cake to be served to my friend. We ordered 2 pizza to share with. I love the unqiue sweet taste of the pizza. Something to do with the pizza dough, which i find it really nice.

To me, pizza is the kind of food that comes to mind when I'm stuck at home feeling hungry and lazy on a rainy Saturday night. This is until I head down to CPK for their popular wood-fired peking duck pizza. If you haven't tried wood-fired pizza before, I assure you this will be one of the best pizzas you've ever tasted.  The crust is slightly thin and crispy and filled with a hint of smoky aroma of the wood-fired oven. Topped with with duck slices, garnishes and crispy crackers, the peking duck pizza is one of the must-try dishes at CPK. The ambience of the restaurant is pretty modern and cosy at the same time --Probably due to use of amber lighting. The staff's service, especially the branch manager's, is extremely good. The branch manager was very helpful and courteous in acceding to my questions and request for an extra serving of deliciously fresh guacamole dips. What I have learnt from my visit: You have not tried real pizza if you've not try wood-fired pizza! (holds true at least for the ones at CPK)Must tries: Peking duck pizza, tortilla spring rolls
I think they took what is already a borderline mediocre chain restaurant in the US and made the portions smaller and the prices higher.

California Pizza Kitchen was a favorite restaurant of mine back when I was studying in the US. It reminds me of eating at Cheesecake Factory, it's a restaurant that you know serves good food. Not only good food, but good old American comfort food.Here in Singapore, California Pizza Kitchen has smaller servings compared to what they serve in America of course but what remains is the great tasting food and service. I've never ordered anything I didn't end up liking, that includes the Wild Mushroom and the Mushroom Pepperoni Sausage but I usually go for the pastas.California Pizza Kitchen is a great choice for group gatherings as the restaurant is spread over two floors and rather spacious.

The food was a hit-and-miss: oysters are a must-try, fish catches cooked in the style of grilling or pan-searing are a fail-safe, pastas are a hard pass, and squid, done any way, is a cannot miss.1) For oysters, Canadian Golden Mantle ($4) are best for people who love big bold flavours; whereas the Canadian Mary Point ($4) is for people with a sweet tooth, the Irish one ($4) will be preferred by people who like things delicate (this was my favourite), and the French Gillardeau ($8) is for people who think only good thigns come in big packages, which probably explains its double pricetag.2) Hot Seafood Platter ($99): a massive medley of half a Boston lobster, grilled prawns, fish skewers, NZ mussels with garlic, littleneck clams in white wine, char-grilled Mediterranean squid, oysters mornay with caramelised onions, grilled octopus in spicy vinaigrette mesclun, and fries. It looked a rustic mess, but was deliciously value-for-money. Standouts include the squid and octopus, both were executed flawlessly.3) Squid Ink Linguine ($21.95) - slicked with the moreish essence of squid ink: I liked that it was generously dotted with perfectly cooked calamari.4) Scallop Cioppino ($23.95): an unusual but wonderful combination of spinach pesto-ed spaghetti and spicy arrabiatta, but let down by overcooked rubbery scallops.5) White Truffle Linguine ($23.95) - white truffle tapenade swirled into parmesan cream, and flecked with shitake aplenty: waaaay too rich, this got cloying about halfway through.6) Char-Grilled Atlantic Halibut ($32.95): delicate and beautifully burnished, drizzled with a velvety herbed butter, and sided by grilled asparagus, broccoli and marinated cherry tomatoes. Fantastic stuff, even if I found a number of bones embedded within. 7) Pan-Seared Atlantic Cod ($29.95): perfectly flaky and luscious, and served with grilled zucchini, eggplant, broccoli, herbed cherry tomatoes, atop a bed of fluffy mash
Probably not the best place for seafood in Singapore. They have a good selection but most of the seafood is from overseas and could be fresher. I'd recommend the octopus.

I've not dined in the Bistro, but I've bought seafood there numerous times after my mum found their shellfishes and fish really fresh. Being fish lovers, my mum would lovingly search for fresh fish at the market. But when we want 'ang moh' fishes, it may not be so easy to find it at local wet markets. Greenwood has a good variety and they advised my mother which fishes are suitable for grill for our barbeque once and after chatting, my mother ordered the next batch of fresh wild salmon from them.
