The lady running the store may be the meanest and most sarcastic person I've ever met but that 10 seconds of interaction would hardly change my appreciation of how well they cook their food here. First thing, get the smallest bowl of congee ($3). It's has more than enough in it to fill you up. Getting anything bigger would be overkill. Secondly, get the Yu Sheng/Fish Salad, it's layered with so many flavors and textural contrasts and it would only set you back $3. Now I've got to start planning when I'm going back.

Feel like I may end up being smote by some Foodie God for not giving Zhen Zhen Fish Porridge a 5 star review but here goes.Do not underestimate the mettle of this store. Maxwell is a stone's throw from my office so I frequent it often enough to be certain that this mystical porridge holds an amazing sway over the masses - the storefront is almost never without a snaking queue. Waiting time is anywhere between 30 - 45 mins, so bring along a book or play many rounds of scramble with friends to avoid ending up questioning your sanity. Patience has never been one my strongest suits so the wait made me a tad grouchier and enraged my expectation of the food to a few notches too high.Let's start with the best bit of the meal. The yu-sheng was spot-on - I can almost confidently say it is the best I have tasted in Singapore. Fresh fish slices are lightly marinated before being tossed with fragrant sesame seeds and crunchy spring onions. Patrons get to top it off by squeezing on some zesty lime juice. The hawker lady generously threw 6 limes into my box of $5 yu-sheng and I was a little perplexed by this plentitude but decided to go for 3 which turned out just perfect.   On to the porridge. The uniform consistency of the thick white gruel is certainly a feat. Every single rice grain has been subjected to prolonged methodical stirring that has ensured the gruel's acclaimed homogenity. And therein may also lie the reason as to why I am a staunch 4-star fan - being Teochew, my ideal porridge has got to have fluffy bits of rice grains still intact so this doesn't quite cut it for me.Despite my irrational porridge discrimination, I must say that stall is generous with the ingredients that go into each bowl. I ordered the century egg and sliced fish porridge and had a sliver of meat to go with every single spoonful - a rarity nowadays. All in all, try this if you aren't going to lose your temper over the wait. I am definitely more of a true blue Zhen Zhen Yu Sheng fan.

Undoubtedly my favorite stall at Maxwell Food Centre! It serves the best yu sheng (aka raw fish) in Singapore, and unbelievably smooth congee. The yu sheng tastes good because there is no bone (there are so many out there which has small bones still stuck on the fish) and are sliced thinly. It tastes good with the sesame oil, black and white sesame seeds, and the garnish. For the porridge, even if you order the plain one, trust me it's smooth and tasty. It probably does not have the Crystal Jade plain porridge standard, but with the generous amount of sesame oil and sesame seeds, it's perfect to go along with the yu sheng.It gets sold out pretty early, and the wait can be pretty long. But I assure you that this is definitely worth the wait!

One of the few hawkers I know to sell out and close for the day by lunch time.  Zhen Zhen serves a well-cooked porridge that is neither too sticky nor wet. Fresh fish and ginger strips further enhance the overall flavour of the porridge. Raw fish or "yu sheng" is also a popular add-on dish to accompany the porridge. The raw fish is dressed in vinegar, sesame oil and a multitude of other sauces topped off with fresh spring onions and chopped chilli. Before you jump to any conclusions, the fish is extremely fresh and the seasoning kills any taste of rawness. The only downside is queuing but don't all good things take time?

Soon Heng RojakHDB HubToa PayohI was number 15 in the queue.25 Minutes before I received 2 packets (sauce packed separately) and 1 plate for me.It is too sweet. Told the woman taking the orders but unfortunately talking to her is like talking to a wall so one can't be sure if she heard or not. She heard that I didn't want turnip and taupok but not the less sugar part. It was still cloyingly sweet. So sometimes she hears and sometimes she doesn't. Don't bother repeating because she wouldn't answer anyway. So irritating. I like the rojak except that it's too sweet.The takeaway packets came with sauce separated (you must make a request).Verdict: Not as good as Hoover Rojak (Whampoa Market) when the old man was still around but is better than his son's.

warning: if you are allergic to peanuts, stay away!warning: if you are trying to cut out sugar as per what ritual suggests, stay away!warning: if you do not have at least 30 mins to spare, standing in queue, stay away!hidden beneath toa payoh bus terminal is gourmet paradise .hidden away from SG's trademark humidity and home of soon heng.at the bottom of a short escalator ride, you will be met by THE queue.the perpetual queue that has discouraged many a weak.but if you are not weak, you will be rewarded.yes, rojak is like a salad.the only difference is, rojak is not healthy!if you see the amount of sugar that goes into making this salad you will understand how it can never be healthy!even when i asked for no sugar, the end product was still really sweet!the uncle seems to do a better job mixing and tossing than the aunty, not that it is something you have control over.but yes, there is an art to it and all the ingredients need to be skillfully combined in the right proportion and each individual entity needs to be well coated with that artisan shrimp paste mix.and like any good salad bar, you can actually customize what goes into your rojak.some may not like jicama, i personally prefer no tau pok in mine.you can also add more of something you like(more crispy you tiao, anyone!?) mostly at a $1 supplement, be it a choice of pungent century egg or even cholestrorific cuttlefish.do note that the cuttlefish here is not the dried sheet version but the fresh brown ones ala cuttlefish kangkong.but the icing on the cake here has to be the abundant coating of roasted rough chopped peanuts that envelopes everything like sand on a beach.and finally, enjoy your eclectic mix thus created.

Great value for $3.. Lots of cuttlefish, crispy dough fritter and a generous serving of nuts! A very Shiok snack.. To enjoy in the comfort of the air conditioned basement food court of HDB hub :) my parents eat this basically on a daily basis since their office is close by. But it's def something that I too could munch on daily as a snack!!! :) the sauce is sweet and savory!! :)

The queue is amazingly long every time I'm here. I came at 830 on a weekday evening and the queue this time was just made up of three people. I was swiftly able to get my hands on the famous rojak.At 4 bucks, I got a large serving of cucumber, benkoang, juicy pineapple, tau gay, puffy taupok and crispy you tiau doused with a delicious sticky sweet sauce and celebrated with nuts all round. It is a sumptuous side to my main and also a little too much for two, hence I overate .

This is gooooood! It's rather on the sweet and wet side, and really worked to taste oh so yummy! The auntie preparing the Rojak seemed to just throw everything into the mixing bowl, but you'll be amazed how she got all the proportions right. I love how the cuttlefish compliment this Rojak. No wonder there's one plate of Rojak on almost every other table, and the long queue at the store during lunch time. Will Rojak be the next Singaporean dish that Gordon Ramsay will challenge? ;)

don't be intimidated by the queue,  it is definitely worth the wait. sauce is thick; thickest i've ever had in my life.generous serving of cuttlefish, peanuts and fresh fruit. (no, im not exaggerating. )this is probably one of the last places where you can get a bang for your buck, 2,50 SGD yields a decent portion, tell me if you can find another stall that serves the same amount or more for the same price- it's rare. my advice? go for the 4sgd size. extra chilli. you wont regret it.

Starting with humble beginnings with 49 Seats (this is how they got their name) at Kreta Ayer Road in 2012 and now they have move to a bigger shop space in Orchard, Centrepoint. 49 Seats are known for their Western Fusion Asian dishes at affrodable pricing.Interior was casual with a good similar industrial chic look that contains bright hanging lights, metal chair. What caught my attention was the items that was sprayed coated in silver that sticked onto the wall. Totally Creative! Initially I thought they were just the usual props made especially for decorations but as I touched it, I realized they were all recycled items. How interesting with plastic cups, spoons, forks, plates, egg trags and even egg trays.Tom Yum Seafood pasta is rated as A spicy lover must try. Looks like this dish is highly raved because of its uniqueness. The Tom Yum was served cream base with seafood like mussels and prawns. It packed a good punch of sweetness, sourness and spiciness in every mouthful of spaghetti. This is in fact semi spicy and the bestseller here.Tom Yum Seafood - $14.90Another recommendation on its menu will be their Seafood Marinara and a good alternative if you are not keen in spicy Tom Yum. Pasta is pretty tasty with mussels and prawns paired with tomato sauce.Seafood Marinara - $13.90Adding $4.90 to my pasta for set of additional soup of the day and 1 soft drinks. I had the Cream of Brocoli with garlic bread by the side of the double layer bowl. The soup was not quite hot, however still able to warm up the tummy.The environment did leave a good impression. As we were only there for pasta, we have not tried out the other western food dishes. It will be good to be back again.

First time finding this new restaurant at Chinatown , was really hard, I've to find by iPhone map device. But finally managed to found it ! The ambience is good but is a no when it's crowded , it would be super noisy and it'll not be romantic anymore. I saw many good reviews about the seafood marinara so I wanted to try it out , I thought it would be normal to the others but wow , when I tried , one word ; AWESOME ! I just love the flavor of the rich tomato base . And is worth it cuz they give the portion just nice for you . And the pasta is just too QQ and soft . The prawns is cooked perfectly . But I don't quite like the ice lemon tea , cuz when I tasted , is like its comes from the normal can . I thought it would be homemade . But overall 10/10 ! I would love to takeaway the pasta if possible !

Named for the number of seats available in this whitewashed, industrial style pub/diner hybrid, 49 Seats is more known for its happy hour that runs daily from 4pm - 9pm than its food.Meeting up a couple of friends there for the first time, the place was mostly filled with people who were enjoying a quick pre-dinner drink or just getting started to get sloshed with alcohol. For me, it was the food on offer that captured my attention. I had the Sirloin Al Scampi ($19.90) which was done according to the done-ness I wanted and tasted wonderful. And the prices are pretty affordable as well. It's a pity really that more people don't discover the food they have and go for the simple pub grub to go along with their drinks.

Overall a place that looks better than how its food taste. It takes good skills to do good Asian fusion and unfortunately 49 Seats does not cut it. After hearing good reviews about  the Tom Yam pasta, I decided to give it a shot and big mistake, Tom Yam is better as Tom Yam soup. The pasty base just did not blend well with the pasta at all. I can't even remember the ingredients in it as well. I was pretty put off but thankfully it was happy hour and the cheap drinks made up for it and I guess best of all I didn't have to pay so yea for all that it was a two star experience but if I had gone there solely for a meal, it might have been one stat or below. The place looks inviting with its dim lighting but more emphasis should be placed on the food.

Enjoyable space on the 2nd floor of Bugis Junction. I think the decor is suppose to be French, but there's also a bunch of mish-mash of things that had me guessing for a little bit. It was a comfortable, casual environment. Anyway, the menu has a pretty good offering of dishes, including escargot in garlic butter. The pork tonkatsu was moist but a little fatty for my liking. The panko crust was delicate and didn't leave you that oily mouth feel. The Tonteki pork steak was good too and pan-fried perfectly. The fatty parts had a nice char and the meat was tender and juicy. Usually, the Tonteki comes smothered in their "Original Tonkatsu Sauce" which I'm glad I asked for on the side because although it was tasty in a Worcestershire sauce kinda way, it would have overwhelmed the pork steak. Plenty of beer and wine selection to choose from. Didn't have room for dessert, but there is a large offering of it if you are so inclined to indulge in. The service was excellent throughout the dinner service, even more so than many other fancier places. There is a set lunch menu that changes daily. The entrees includes a "healthy salad and drink" it says. Great place to grab a meal, a drink, and/or dessert.

The food is probably overrated. I ordered a day carbonara spaghetti , hamburger steak and clam chowder soup. It taste regular and nothing really stood out. The spaghetti was good but too oily. Other than that, the restaurant renovation and atmosphere still quite acceptable

I came here by myself after work and sat at the bar counter (kinda awkward sitting in a table when all the other tables are pairs...). I like sitting on the counter though, you get to peek at one the cooks are doing through a glass pane.Like everyone said, the decor of this place is super cute and cozy, modeled after a small B&B or something. They also play this adorable jazzy french music in the background.I got the sizzling hamburg steak since that seems to be getting rave reviews. It's not bad for $19.90. Tasty and fills me up - it comes with fries and a bed of bean sprouts. Kinda reminds me of a glorified pepper lunch. It was served in an interesting manner too - The waiter will pour some sort of liquid on your egg and burger, and it would light up for awhile before she pours another liquid on top of it to put the fire out.After serving your meal, your waiter will give you a key which you will then take to the cashier to pay your bill and "check out" of this lovely B&B. cute eh?

This is a review of a Sunday lunch at Ma Maison in Bugis Junction.After a quick discussion of places to have lunch, we decided on Ma Maison.Upon arrival, we were quickly seated.  Throughout our meal, the service was prompt, professional, and polite.The ambiance is relatively basic but it is a step up from most of the other restaurants in Bugis Junction.The food ranged from average to very good.  However, only one dish made it beyond the average mark.Breaded Prawns - This was my favorite part of the meal.  I enjoyed the  breading.  The prawns had a very fresh flavour to them.  The presentation was very appealing.tinyurl.com/cy8fu65Chef's Pizza - This was a basic pizza.  It had some small shrimp and other general ingredients.  There was nothing that stood out about this pizza.  I am NOT saying this was a frozen microwave pizza.  It did remind me of one though.tinyurl.com/a2txw22Paella - My friend ordered the paella.  She enjoyed it.  I tried a bite or two.  The rice was dense.  It seemed to all hold together ok but it did not stand out to me.  Even with the fresh seafood, it seemed bland.  The presentation for this dish was nice.tinyurl.com/arcgp6dOverall, if you live or are shopping in the neightbourhood, this is a decent option for lunch.  The room is nice enough.  The service is solid.  While the food may not rock the world, it is good enough to make for an enjoyable lunch.

When you go to Ma Maison.. regardless of which branch you go to.. the service is always quite consistent.. a nice greeting... waiters/waitresses with initiative to take away your plates, fill up your water... Food is also quite consistent. Tried their famous breaded pork cutlet here and it's the same as the one at Clarke Quay Central. Their escargot is affordable and did not disappoint as well. So if you are around the area and you are looking for affordable french food, Ma Maison is it!

I am very late to the Ma Maison game thanks to general blurness on my part. Last year, while looking for places to eat on a Friday night at Liang Court, I stumbled across this strange French cottage-looking restaurant with tons of ladies waiting outside. Couldn't put two together and moved on. Earlier this year, after moving to my new workplace at Suntec, a friend suggested we have lunch at Ma Maison at Bugis Junction. When I walked in (once again, there was a line for lunch), everything clicked!I've only had the Ma Maison set meals with grilled steak, hamburg steak and tonkatsu because someone told they're really good at the hamburg. Why order anything else if a restaurant is great with it's grill right? All of those dishes have been fantastic, with the hamburg steak taking the cake no matter what sauce I've had it with. Plus if you're feeling thirsty, they have a good range of beers by the bottle and some very appetizing tarts that I've *yet* to try.What really rocks my boat however is the service. For Singapore standards, the Bugis outlet has some of the best service I've experienced in this country. From the usual embarrassing welcome you get at Japanese restaurants to accommodating substitutions, explaining sauces and keeping my water glass filled, the staff here get top marks. It's one of the few times I find myself saying, "boy do the Japanese know how to train their service staff right" because they all look happy and serve professionally. I do notice that the Japanese managers pay more attention to Japanese customers, but hey I would too if I was working in a foreign country and the "less attentive" level already exceeds most competitors. However, I would point out that service at the Parco Millenia restaurant is not great and borders on rude on occasion because, well you guessed it, there are no Japanese managers on site and the outlet seems severely understaffed. One can't have everything so I suggest sticking to Bugis Junction. Lastly, come early or past 1pm during lunchtime to avoid lining up for long. Forget dinner on Mondays (ladies happy hour) or Fridays if you're starving and don't want to wait.

Have you never had the hamburg steak? it's only the bestest, moistest, most tasty patty of beef you can find... but not between two buns. I guess I'd call it a mod-Japanese/Western dish, and this is pretty dang fantastic. Plus it comes with a sunny-side-up egg on top. And that sauce...I really should also tell you I had the company of the lovely ladies Kathryn B and Michelle L (now M) at lunch, and all I can do now is talk about this food... guess I'm not a very gracious dining companion eh?I think they'd agree that the food was pretty awesome, and the service deserves a good mention too - every staff member was available, without being intrusive, and for newbies, I guess the only odd thing was when one of the staff handed me a key as I asked for the bill. What do I do with this now? He told me to bring it to the cashier, and when I handed it over, it hit me - it's a kitschy form of "checking out" of the restaurant, and it completes the cottagey/B&B-themed experience.Decor aside (which really isn't bad), I'd go back for that hamburg...

First restaurant I've been to that offers a fusion of French-Japanese cuisine! Not what I expected at first, although I'm not sure what exactly I thought it would be.The ambiance is quaint, with French themed furniture and finishings. The soft lighting and wood interiors really set the tone of a small French cafe.We started off with the Escargot, served in the shell, with a garlic-buttery sauce, which was quite good. Followed these up with Camembert Cheese Fritters that were also really yummy, although I would have preferred a different sauce, the one we had oddly resembled Thai sweet chilli.The Beef Stroganoff served with Buttered rice and omelette was a bit disappointing despite my love of Japanese rice. The omelette threw me off a bit and overall the meal could do without.The desserts were the real treat here. We ordered the Banana Tart, Mixed Berry Tart and Blueberry Tart ($4.90).The Banana was by far the best with a layer of banana cream on the tart base, topped with chopped banana halves, dollops crème and walnuts. Not my favourite for lunch but highly recommended for a bit of light tea and dessert

Expect a queue when you come by Ma Maison after work on every day of the week. I waited about 10 minutes to get a table today, which wasn't too bad, considering that it was "Ladies Night" on Mondays. 20% off ala carte items - score!The decoration of the place is lovely. The lighting's a little dim, but it adds to the cosy atmosphere of the restaurant. I had the Gratin with Prawns and Scallops ($13.80), which was pretty good, but they were rather miserly with the actual prawns and scallops - there were only two pieces of each in the large bowl. My friend had the Fresh Greens salad ($6.90) with Japanese dressing - I wasn't too impressed with that. We ended the meal with a Strawberry Tart ($8.80) - the most popular out of at least five different flavours of tarts - and it was not bad. However, the tart base was almost like a very dry cake which I feel did not complement the texture of the strawberries.Ma Maison is known for their sincere approach to food, and it shows through their simple yet delicious dishes. Their prices are also very affordable, so you can try a number of dishes without breaking the bank. It's my go-to dining option at Bugis Junction!
Squid ink spaghetti and escargots were great! It's better if u make a reservation as the queue is always long. Waiting time was 15-35 minutes, and they will not seat u till all members are present.

Since the first time I been to this restaurant, I love it.  They have the two cuisine I like under one roof... french and japanese.  So far,  this is one restaurant that I have not been disappointed with the items I ordered and I haven't felt a dip in their services or quality.Some of my favorite items here are their scallop capaccio, escargot, french onion soup and their tonkatsu set meal.

Italian restaurant in Holland Village. Good solid Italian food. Both pizza and pasta are good though not excellent. Price-wise, a bit on the high side for the quality of the food. Usually gets packed during weekday lunches when they offer good value set lunch.

The food is decent (pizzas are excellent; lobster ravioli so-so; wet risotto very wet and quite unusual but not great; forget about mediocre antipasti). However, it is satisfying, almost like meals cooked by a loving grandma who is not a fabulous chef. The place has two qualities: it is very good value (especially when special 1-for-1 offers are on), and service is exceptionally warm and friendly.

I've come here so often since I found out about the 1 for 1 weekday lunch special. It applies to pizzas, pastas and main courses, and is such a great deal for delicious food!! Reservations are usually required for large groups though, and if you're in a group larger than 5 you may end up seated at the upper floor where service is much slower. The food, though, is so solid. It's become my go-to Italian place in Singapore & I always try to find weekdays I could visit it during the holidays. Most recently, I had the pappardelle (Homemade Pappardelle Pasta with Oxtail ragout and Rosemary) and La Nonna signature pizza. I've also tried the main course once (ribeye I believe). Service is usually quick and glasses are always topped up quickly. My friends and I rarely have anything to complain about La Nonna. I've never come for dinner though, so can't speak to the dinner or set menus. It's such a great location that you can always head across the road after to The Daily Scoop for Ice Cream or Sunday Folks for waffles!

Food is decent, worse than on a previous visit a year or so ago, but I'd go back mainly for the ambience and fantastic 1-for-1 pasta/pizza/main offer during weekday lunches.The starter bread rolls/crackers looked pale and under-baked so I didn't even bother trying them. We shared the lobster ravioli (3.5 stars), which my friend really enjoyed, and the crabmeat linguine (3 stars). I'd had the former on a previous visit a year ago or so and it seemed like the standards have dropped. For the latter, we asked for an aglio e olio sauce instead of the tomato cream sauce it typically comes with so this review isn't of the crabmeat linguine on the menu. I'd had the dish here a year ago and thoroughly loved it but this time it was rather lackluster. Ample crabmeat, but somehow the dish wasn't very flavorful. I'll have to hunt down another place for crabmeat pasta now...I was a little annoyed that the waiter misunderstood us when we asked for the crabmeat linguine to be prepared with an olive oil sauce, brought a plain aglio e olio pasta, then said he'd have to charge us for it since they'd prepared it for us. Nice try buddy. I pointed out (nicely) that it was an error on his part and he agreed to correct the order, though he emphasized that he was making an exception. One of the other waiters who helped us out made a couple of jokes and we appreciated his friendliness! Service really depends I suppose. Other than that I adore the ambience, and we paid $15 each so I can't complain! Wasn't too crowded on a Tuesday afternoon but it's easy to make reservations. I made reservations two hours before.

Came for lunch with friends and ordered:Calamari - still the same, crispy but can do with more seasoning.Portobello - this is a starter I shared with friends. Plump mushroom grilled to perfection. Delicious!!!Squid Ink Pasta - not to be consumed on first dates!!! But since Im only out with friends, eat away!!!! Pretty tasty and ingredients were also fresh. Just wish there were more really...An enjoyable meal nevertheless as they do make very decent pastas.

How could the quality go down so drastically in such a short period of time?? The prosciutto e rucola pizza we loved so much was sad. The prosciutto was way too chewy and the arugula was wilted. The only improvement was the quick service and the fact that they opened up the 2nd floor seating. I hope this was just a miss and La Nonna is not compromising quality due to the large flux of customers during lunch hour.

Although La Nonna has been around for a while in Holland Village, I have not checked out the restaurant until earlier this year.  Homestyle causal Italian dining is brought to us by the guys who own Senso. A friend organized a lunch meet up there and since, I have been dining there for lunch when I am in that neighborhood. Well, why lunch? Coz they have an attractive promotion 1-for-1 for entrees between 12pm - 2.30pm. Alternatively, you can try their 3 course set meal with coffee/tea at $22 ++.  The lunch portions were rather generous too! I usually end up sharing with my friends as I can't finish a portion myself. The dishes that I tried and love here are Mozzarella e Parma, Carpaccio and their lasagna. Definitely great for lunch meet up.

La Nonna is an Italian restaurant in Holland Village. This place is actually pretty good and I had a pleasant experience dining here. They have an indoor and outdoor sitting area (outside is nicer). I ordered the gnocchi last time I came and it was pretty tasty and cooked well. It can be hard to find good gnocchi here in Singapore but this place was good. No problems with the service. A nice place to get Italian food in Holland Village.

decent-enough desserts at this well-known trattoria along lorong mambong. this place is known more for their well-reasonable set lunches - but that's paltry. sweets! we came here for desserts-only after lunch at al hamra; and it did us well enough, even if it was nothing too special.they have a menu of typical italian desserts - we settled on the lemon meringue tart and a pannacotta, the latter of which really is indicative of the skill of the restaurant. the tart had a great crust - buttery lemon curd (though slightly gelatinous) and sufficiently-fluffy meringue on top, and it tasted the way it ought (average food truly don't make for descriptive adjectives).that pannacotta, though - I'm still on the lookout for a great rendition. this one is a little on the stiffer side, but still creamy enough not to offend. it didn't have those beautiful black seeds though - so I'm guessing extract in this one.it's difficult to be more descriptive - but if you're skipping it all to the last line - this place is alright if you're in the area, though I wouldn't travel for it.

The Mee Rebus was so good here - the noodles soaked up the curry. The toast was okay but the hot food was the standout.  I'd come back for the hot food.  This is a popular place but the pastry cabinet had ants in them and most people just had a coffee and toast.  They have plenty of seating so I think that's why it's also popular.  Fast and efficient!  Good place to grab a quick bite.

Meh breakfast. It turns out there are a ton of other restaurants in this huge shopping complex. I loved the milk tea and the coffee here was also really delicious. I had the thick egg toast with cheese. It was basically thick toast with a fried egg and cheese on top. It wasn't bad. Other dishes were the ham and cheese toast. The were basic and mediocre at best, not something I would purposely eat. Overall an ok breakfast stop, seems pretty chain like.

Wandered into this place while looking for a late dinner in Chinatown our first night in Singapore.  Most of the surrounding shops in the mall were already closed, but this place was a bright beacon of light that beckoned us into its cute, pristine white cafe.The set laksa menu for SGD 6.10 pulled us in for our first taste of authentic Singaporean food.  But alas, they only had one portion left, so we had to settle for the SGD 5.00 Mee Siam set as the second option.Both noodle soups were creamy with a heavy taste.  The Mee Siam was quite sour with scary-looking greyish noodles that looked like squid tentacles to me.  :OBoth sets came with a refreshing barley tea.  I would say this is a nice place for a light meal or snack, and it's a chain around town, so really convenient to drop by for a visit.

Not a bad option if you are looking for an indoor place to escape the Singapore heat & have a quick meal. You can certainly get better kaya toast in one of the other hawker centers nearby though, so be aware.
Great view over the CBD. The food, while good, is less creative or exquisite than some other Italians nearby, like Osteria Arte or Braci. Good-value set lunch.

[Restaurant Week Review]Right in the heart of the CBD, you get a spectacular view of the Marina Bay area.I've always been skeptical of Restaurant Week, because there isn't much to do/show when you limit a restaurant to a certain price point. We came here on a Monday night as a party of 3, and had the trout carpaccio, angus steak, oysters to share (add-on), and a chocolate dessert of sorts.I think Zafferano's has outdone my expectations and blown my RW biasedness out the window. We were surprised by the thick succulent slices of trout, which had a much milder and sweeter flavor vis-à-vis salmon. They were generous enough, with at least 4 thick slices for an appetizer. The beef was the star of the meal, done just nicely, quite pink (the way I like it), and accompanied by roast potatoes and asparagus. Oysters - just okay, but nobody comes to an Italian place specifically for oysters, hey?The chocolate dessert was your usual, with very nicely tempered white chocolate on top. Must have been a good dessert person hard at work.I thoroughly enjoyed my RW experience here, even if Italian isn't my thing. Yum.

I'm going to post this out first. There was only one negative to this place. The air conditioning was FREEZING. While they were prepared for this and had a shawl for my partner they really need to turn it down. PLEASE READ ON THOUGH...As soon as I walked in the door to Zafferano the service was outstanding! Our waiter was very friendly with an great sense of humour. There was no pretentious feeling that comes with some fine dining restaurants. The food you ask....Well the food was unreal. I had the ravioli which melted as soon as it touched my mouth. I never knew pasta could be so soft and then exploded with flavours. Then the Pork Belly which equally melts in my mouth. I didn't know Pork could be cooked so well. Lastly the Lava Chocolate Cake. In my experience these can be ultra rich and hard to eat. But of course not at Zafferanos'. It was just right!Thanks to Zafferano for a great night.

It's hard to put much faith in restaurants like these where they occupy the highest floors of any Bayfront buildings (or any restaurant with views). They always tend to be touristy with mediocre food and ultra premium pricing (except Jaan). I was right for this one.I was taken here on a Friday night dinner date and was immediately turned off when I expected the restaurant would have the best views but instead find out that the views can only be seen by people at the outside bar patio area. We are seated at a table against the window that literally stares out at the people at a booth in that outside bar area. It's around 7:30 pm on a Friday evening. Mind you, the restaurant itself is pretty dead but the outside bar was full of the CBD people. However, service was somehow horrible with our server constantly standing on his own never looking at us. My girlfriend ordered a cocktail that tasted horrible and I finished my Negroni and was never offered a second. The waiter acted a bit pretentious and pompous as well. I ordered the oxtail agnolotti and my girlfriend ordered the spinner crab linguine. Note that the linguine isn't freshly made pasta and was very bland. And my agnolotti was okay but nothing special.Our waiter never checked up on us until we had to call him through the very kind gentleman that pours the water and cleans the plates, yet I saw him standing at a distance by himself (again it's a quiet Friday night).Very discouraging experience. You don't even get any view to enjoy unless you go outside. Below average food, poor drinks, terrible service, venue where you don't get a view, not worth the price. Not coming back unless its to have a beer or two in the outside bar area.

Failed to deliver on many levels - definitely not worth the price!My husband and i came here for a lunch at around 1pm on a weekday, as a break from work.I had the business lunch as follows:-1. Tomato Mozzarella Salad with Basil - bland, dry and absolutely tasteless until I drowned it in balsamic vinegar that was at the table!2. Spinach and ricotta manicotti type dish - rolled up stuffed pasta tubes - also very bland, and no one even offered me parmesan cheese, which we saw sitting on the counter when we walked out.My husband had the a la carte menu as follows:-1. Tomato and Burratta salad - tastier than my mozzarella salad;2. fettuccine with mushroom and black truffle - this dish was basically like eating raw truffles - they put SO much into the sauce and even shaved more on top, that you only got one ridiculously strong taste of truffles, it was so overpowering and not pleasant!3. Beef short rib cubes - bland and tasteless (again, need to be drowned in vinegar perhaps?!), not to mention quite a contrast from the overpowering fettuccine, and the meat tasted like it was boiled and then slapped on the plate! In addition to the food being sub-par, the service was super slow and inattentive, despite them not being busy at all.  It took ages to get a glass of wine, bread, or to even get someone's attention to ask for anything.In the end, the prices are absolutely ridiculous for the shoddy service and very below-average food - surprising this place is still in business in such a high-end office building!

Restaurant week experience!I've avoided restaurant week for a few years now, after my last incident with crappy food and food poisoning to boot, so this restaurant was my first after a very long hiatus. I was here with 2 fellow Yelpers on a monday night.Zafferano is located at the top of Ocean Financial Centre at Raffles Place, and there were large windows with awesome views of the Marina Bay area. Good for deep conversations over a dinner date and the like. There's also a cozy outdoor lounge, and I imagine it would be wonderful for drinks after dinner, as it has large glass panels to shield you from the crazy winds 43 storeys up in the air, but still open enough for the occasional gentle breeze.The restaurant was crowded but not packed. We were seated in the middle, near the cool red circular bar in the middle of the restaurant. It was quite dark but I could still see my food so all's good.We had the trout carpaccio, black angus beef + foie gras, oysters to share, and cake (mandorle... - almond wafers, mascarpone cheese, chocolate mousse).The trout carpaccio was delicious, well-marinated (flavourful, not too salty) and smooth. It was quite a large portion, just enough for me to feel satisfied but not stuffed and ready for the next course!Black angus beef was done medium (we couldn't choose because they grill all of them together or something) which was fine by me, still slightly pink in the middle and very soft and tender, not dry/tough at all. The foie gras came at an additional $10 and was ok but not fantastic and I would not recommend adding it to your dish.Oysters were ok and priced decently at $18 for a half-dozen. Not the freshest I've tasted but of acceptable quality.Dessert was nice but nothing too special. I wish there were more of the mousse, while my friends liked the wafer more... you can't please everyone.We ended up paying about $95 per person after the additional foie gras, oysters and wine to go along.I feel that the current 2.5 stars doesn't do this place justice- I'd give it 4 stars for the restaurant week experience! And really, service was decent.

This is my first time in the restaurant, though I had met the restaurant manager Paulo in a previous wine dinner at Robuchon. The restaurant ambience is nice but not especially elegant. Nonetheless service by Bala was attentive and very good. We had a special menu, not all is available on a regular basis. The first course, a wagyu beef carpaccio was excellent, made special by the addition of castelmagno cheese from Piedmont. The pan seared pigeon was special, perfectly seared rare with vanilla reduction which produced an incredible aroma. Tender and flavorful. This pared perfectly with the 2011 Cruanza which has a very strong caramel and vanilla overtone. Then we had the carnaroli  Saffron risotto, unusually with a pork sausage ragout with toasted rosemary, paired with the Resalte 2010 reserve, a 93 rank wine spectator. What a wine. Elegant, smooth and creamy. Notes of vanilla, burnt caramel and cassis. Full bodied and almost jammy. The risotto was cooked el dente. Perfect. The final dish, a Sous vide rack of lamb, then roasted. Paired with a limited edition grand Resalte 2009, a 90 point Robert Parker. Just like the previous wines, notes of vanilla and caramel. Intense and full bodied, silky smooth and mellow. Exceptionally balanced and complex. Perfect pairing for the dish which was perfectly done, rare and super tender with an intense syrupy jus. The meal finished with a mascarpone valrhona chocolate mousse, a little sweet for my taste although my wife and daughter were fine with it. Overall an excellent dinner. We took a look at the regular menu. A limited selection but based on the meal tonight I have no doubt that it will be well prepared. Prices are reasonable and value for what you get. I recommend this restaurant and will be back for more.

Was here for a business lunch so I knocked 1 star off assuming if I had to pay for what I got. We all chose the appetizer buffet and I had the seafood tagliatelle as main. He appetizer buffet wasn't bad, decent choices with Parma ham, salads etc. once I finished a plate, they quickly removed my cutlery and placed a potholder there in preparation for the pasta. That meant no seconds for the greedy folks out there! Pasta was mediocre and service was a little distracted. But poor execution when two of my colleagues fish mains were undercooked! The bulk of the middle was completely raw and had to be sent back. They were gracious and replaced it with a new dish, but for a restaurant billed to be one the high end, I think it's pretty poor. Dessert was so so and we had to call the waitress over several times to take our coffee and tea orders. I wouldn't come back on my own dime.

Very poor dining experience. It gets so much flat out wrong.We were a group of six, on a quiet evening (Wednesday). What went wrong:1. the table rocked badly, as in you put your elbows on it, and it rocks2. the service was mainly absent, and otherwise aloof and had attitude. We had trouble getting attention even though the restaurant was half empty.3. we had the six course tasting menu.  All six of us found the food to be substandard, unremarkable and/or bad. Meat asked to be medium rare came out well done. 4. the wait between dishes was too long and ponderous. 5. Asking the waitresses to speed up was difficult due to hard getting their attention 6. The price tag at the end was a shocker. And they took a long time to return the card.All in all, we vowed never to come back and to review the place (it had been scantly reviewed before I made the booking).  AVOID

Located on the highest floor of the newly-renovated Ocean Financial Centre, enjoy your dinner with spectacular views when you dine at Zafferano.I headed there for a dinner date and was astounded so much by the views of the spectacular skyline that I almost forgot to eat! It's can get really windy up there, so girls, poufy skirts might not be the smartest choice. The food we had was excellent and very authentic Italian (I thought it was Spanish, thanks to the name). The Frutti di Mare I had, had lightly-tossed pasta with clams, mussels, prawns and fresh greens and was served perfectly al dente. Service was excellent as well, and to avoid queuing, I'd say its good to call in advance to reserve a spot.

Sister to the Michelin star rated Zafferano - London, this newly opened restaurant/bar is going to have a tough time living up to expectations.Recently launched in Singapore, Zafferano offers a unique dining experience at the top of Ocean Financial Center in the CBD Raffles Area. The panoramic views are breathtaking, better than even New Asia Bar at the Suissotel the Stamford. The ambiance is no less. They host an elegant circular bar in the very center of the restaurant, surrounded by floor to ceiling glass windows. The interior dining area isn't too big, covering just about half the restaurant, the balance has more of a lounge feeling. The dining space extends onto the balcony, covering the entire circumference of the restaurant with magnificent views.The food was a bit disappointing, although i'm sure this will settle in over time. Highly recommended for a few drinks after work with colleagues or even a quiet evening with friends.
Excellent food and wine. Can thoroughly recommend the Moletto Colmello with the pan fried veal. il cibo era fantastico, servizio excellente. Il personale è bon informato e molto ben presentato.

Medzs has been a regular spot for us because it's a 5-10 minute walk and offers enough variety to please any crowd. It is located in the basement (B2) of Orchard Central. You walk in through a variety of different counters with all kinds of different Mediterranean and European foods on your way to being seated at a table with a menu similar to one you'd find in a sushi restaurant. You record your order on the menu and flag down a server to enter it. The place is pretty big and offers quite a bit of seating. It's good for groups and kids. The bar has been hopping on the weekend evenings we've been there, which is largely in part due to their 1-for-1 drink special. As folks following a Paleo diet, we're definitely fans of the Badger Cider. We're always pleased with the variety of foods that fit our lifestyle and we normally fall back on Medzs when we're looking for comfort food that isn't a cheat. We'll most likely be bringing any picky-eating family members here when they visit!

Was a little disappointed that Kilo on the second floor wasn't child-friendly, so we came here instead. No queue during Saturday lunch as the place is large.Four of us had the tapas platter (23.90), eggs benedict ($14.90), lamb tajine ($16.90) braised lamb shank ($26.9), rosti with sunny side egg ($9.90), lamb shish kebab ($17.90), la opera ($7.90) and hazelnut feuilletine ($7.90). Yeah, we're big eaters.There's LOTS of variety (in food and price), so there's bound to be something for everyone. The lamb tajine was the best dish, though the spices were slightly one-dimensional. I'd give the la opera a miss next time. You'll get a better rosti at Marche, and eggs benedict - the brunch special - is probably the best value for money.We paid $33.76/pax.

Medzs is a Marche-styled restaurant, meaning that there are many stalls inside selling different types of food, and you go around ordering from them using an electronic card that registers your purchases. With such a wide variety of foods, it is preferable to go in a group so you can share the items around.Medzs specialises in Mediterranean food, which means lots of seafood. They also serve pizzas and pasta if you're not a big fan of seafood.  The drinks section also features a large variety of milkshakes, fruit juices, and daily specials - if you're health-conscious or would like a palate-cleansing beverage, this place will attend to your needs.Being a big fan of paella, I ordered a seafood paella for $14, and collected it after 10-15 minutes of waiting. The rice was nicely coloured and cooked - not mushy, not crunchy. The sotong and prawns did not have any fishy smell and were cooked relatively well. Overall, the dish was pretty decent for the price range (I wasn't expecting amazing quality if I paid under $20 for paella in Singapore, and would have been pleasantly surprised otherwise).The ambience is cosy, with warm Mediterranean colours and decor. Tables tend to be spaced out, meaning that you don't have to jostle for space with the people at the next table. It also makes for a more relaxing experience.

Medzs is a 200 seater European/Mediterranean restaurant which is located at Basement Two of Orchard Central. I always walk past the restaurant when heading over to yoga class. The place works like Marché, which uses a card system to record your orders. There are 8 stations which provide a variety of cuisine from French, German, Greek, Turkish etc.For S$15, i thought the Duck Confit wasn't too shady. S thought that it was kinda pathetic for such a small leg at first but i'm not expect huge ones like those served at Le Bistrot (read about my review here). You get what you pay for. Surprisingly, the leg was cooked nicely. The skin was a thin golden brown crisp that crackles when you bite into it but the meat maintained its tender and moist texture. The meat may be a teeny bit leaning towards the salty side though. The sauce was a savory gravy that gave the meat a little more moisture. This is not a bad dish and it is almost comparable to La Petite.I had the Beef Shish Kebab (S$11.90), which IMHO is fantastic. Piping hot and fresh beef on skewers, seasoned simply with spices, herbs, pepper and salt to bring out the natural flavors of the meat and served on a bed of vegetables. What more can you ask for? I love the Bulgur rice (If i wasn't mistaken) which was served with the meat. It has a nice tomato flavor to it and cooked almost like the Valencia Paella style with some diced peppers and onions. The short fat grains are fluffy, moist and slightly chewy and they go perfectly with the savory grilled meats. I would definitely be back to try the other kebab dishes. They look and smell fantastic.

A good place to go to if you are with a group of friends in town and need somewhere for beer and nosh. (Beer being the priority, of course.)The place offers a wide array of beer and I was happy to find many of my favourites displayed by the bar. That's not all, the beers are also super cheap if you purchase them by pairs. Food-wise, there are "stalls" representing cuisine of different countries like France, Turkey, etc. I was craving for some good meat so I ordered Beef Shish Kebab from the Turkey spot. Also had grilled chicken with truffle butter from the France spot. The food was decent, not noticeably rich in flavour or spices.Good strategy to carry out: reserve a table, grab a couple of bottles, go make your orders, collect the buzzers, return to table to continue on beer and wait for the buzzers to light up when your food is ready. You also get 10% off the menu when you check out before 10.30pm, which was a pretty good way to clear off most of the crowd before they close at 11pm.

My friend was out of confinement for NS and needed some special food, and he wanted to come here. HUGE fan of Mediterranean food, so I gave in the idea almost immediately!Got the Beef & Apple Tajine ($15.90), which was a 'claypot' of some light yummy stew, hoice chunks of beef, and served with a pretty small dish of coucous. No complaints about the taste - pretty above average stuff (although a Moroccan restaurant on Haji Lane would probably do one that tasted better), and the part of this experience that saved the experience from being just a meh-day out would be the desserts!The pastry chef won my heart, with her explanations on the desserts, and her generosity with the chocolate & vanilla sauces. I had the Caramel Pound Cake ($3), which was a thick slice of caramel-based pound cake, with almond ganache (which she adds when you order, for freshness), and the chocolate sauce sealed the deal. A taste of it and you could tell it wasn't your run-of-the-mill chocolate, but dark, heavy duty stuff. Delicious! Food is pretty meh, but the dessert counter won my heart over!

Located at the basement of orchard central, this restaurant serves Mediterranean cuisine. It is similar to marche style where you are given a card at the entrance. The restaurant is spacious and would easily fill around 200 people but the interior design and deco could have done more to give the Mediterranean feel.There are many stalls for you to choose and you can consider a few dishes to start with . The duck confit , and kebab. However it could be because of the Mediterranean style of cooking, the food tasted very salty and the rice does not really match their kebab. If you are a fan of rosti, you will be starving as they really cook real slow. It took about 40 minutes to cook and serve. Overall, food is expensive and serving is not worth the money. For such an exotic taste, it only means that you need to be adventurous for the day.

I appreciate this place for the ambiance and the fact they are a sit down type restaurant but do not make you pay service charge. The decor is tasteful and there is plenty of seating so it makes for a more relaxed and enjoyable experience. They have good drink specials but since you pay per item ordered your meal can get expensive fast. I did see an advertisement for a value lunch special from 11-3 for S$6.90 which I will check out but am curious to see the portion size.

This is one of those places where you get a card at the door to rack up your bills in, and then pay upon exit. You order your food and get a little buzzing counter, which vibrates when it's time for you to pick up your food, so no standing around looking too bored... The food is laid out by country, with food from Spain, Turkey and France just to name a few. I enjoyed the Hot Plate Kebabs (get some pita bread to go with it!), the mushroom pizza was pretty crispy and yummy If you're just looking for a drink, there's a bar section separate from the rest of the dining. I'm particularly fond of the large selection of international bottled beers here - 1-for-1 promos also don't hurt.

Although I am not exactly a big fan of Mediterranean food, I had pretty good experiences at Medz. The style at Medz is a little like Mar*he, but serving a slightly different variety of food. It would be best if you go with a group of people, say about 6, so that you can get a variety of dishes and share them. What's more, at Medz, there are lots of credit card promotions that give you special discount. Also, their 1-for-1 bottled beer deal is pretty attractive as well. You can not only get local beers, but also imported beer from different countries, such as Korea, Japan, Germany, etc. One thing to note is that there is no reservation after 6pm. So get your buddies and head down to avoid the long wait!

Think Marche but Mediterranean and Middle Eastern Food.The food at Medzs to generally decent. Each station has a regular list of main courses, as well as a small list of daily specials. These normally range from above average in taste, to the wow-I-want-more!Desserts though, are quite sucky.

Who would have guessed that this place is by Food Junction! Marché in concept, this place appears to offer reasonably authentic Mediterranean food at fair prices. The lamb tajine comes with couscous garnished with some magical rose flavored onions! and the  pork belly skewer is good too.  Worth returning to try out the other stalls.

This Thai restaurant has been in Bedok for the past 2-3 years! When it first started the queue were crazily Long because it was really good! The regulars would always come back to have Tom yam soup! Then just 6 months ago a shop took over Nakhon Thai. But Nakhon open 2 shop away from it. Now we have both Thai restAurant and both are having a long queue. The price are similar in both of them. Nakhon is definitely better still. Great price, good portion and amazing quality. Thumbs up!

I've heard many great things about this outlet and there is always a queue when I am in the area. Not only is there a queue to sit and eat-in but there is a queue for to-go order pickups. Post-lunch time, there wasn't a wait but there were still people coming in to be seated. Overall, the meal was satisfying and I was quite pleased. Thai iced tea (Red), Pad Thai, and Papaya Salad. I'd say the papaya salad was my favorite as it tasted most similar to what I've had in Thailand. The Pad Thai, in my opinion didn't taste as authentic but was still good. The Thai iced tea was not overly sweet which was nice too. I'll have to try the green Thai iced tea next time. Service was good and seemed to be pretty attentive at the time. They also provided water. Atmosphere, pretty chill and more open so it was warm but there were fans so that is nice. I'd recommend and would come back here for Thai food. Tip: if it's during busy hours, order for pickup which may save you some time

Ignorant of the largely rave reviews, I swung in a few minutes before closing time to dapao some dishes. The crew were a cool and friendly bunch and the food was quickly prepared. They don't accept card so remember to have cash in hand.Popping open the goods at home was a bit hit and miss. Two of the dishes, the olive pork and green bean chicken were micro portions whilst the olive rice and green curry were of a good size.Overall the flavours were good, Birdseye chillies dotted around in the rice are the main spice factor, otherwise nothing was particularly spicy. Definitely better than taking away from Thai2go.Not impressed with portion size.

My friend introduced this Thai restaurant in 2012, I remembered there was a long queue back then, so long that we waited almost the duration of a football match but the wait was worth it. The food that came along satisfy both my stomach and feet which had to endure a punishment similar to the days during National Service. The place is located on the first floor of a HDB block. It may not look glamourous, but the cost of the food is cheaper than its competitors but the quality of the food makes up for it. I enjoy every spoonful of Tom Yum soup which may be spicy to some and had a bit of difficulty finishing it. The main dishes that came along with the soup are fabulous. The Basil Beef and Pineapple Rice are my favourites. Since the queue is long, there should be a timing for the every customers, as some of them take their own sweet time finishing their food! (Annoying). Overall, I enjoyed the food this restaurant offers, whether its the best remains debatable but certainly is one of the better ones out there.
Love their food! Price is reasonable too! Their basil chicken and pad Thai are my favorites! And for dessert is the red ruby, hands down! Doesn't get any better else where!
No wonder this place always has a queue! Had a Pad Thai that was scrumptious!!! It had an average price but the foos was amazing! Would recommend this place if anyone craves Thai food!Pad Thai- 9/10

Nakhon Kitchen is a hidden gem in the Kovan neighborhood in the North-eastern corner of Singapore that serves authentic Thai cuisine in a friendly and kooky Thai atmosphere. Once you step into the shop, you'd be transported to the back alleys of Bangkok with all that upbeat Thai pop tempo, mouthwatering waft of hot delicious food and the friendly smiles and eager to please faces of the servers. The Pineapple Fried Rice (S$6) is a standard dish that i would order here. The sweetness of the pork floss goes perfectly with the slightly curried Thai rice which is slightly fluffy and chewy. I like that it is not too dry. The rice is fried with shrimps, cashew nuts and raisins and best eaten with Green curry! Almost every table had an order of this. Nakhon used to serve this in a pineapple but i guess it was too troublesome for them. A Thai meal is never complete without Tom Yam Soup and Nakhon has 2 different types, 1 thick base and 1 clear, with the option of Seafood, Shrimp or Chicken (S$6). The milky base is the less spicy option with some tomatoes added to neutralize the acidity. I personally prefer the clear base. It looks innocuous enough but boy that chili padi in the soup can kill. It's a clean and sweet taste with tartness to it in your first mouthful. Amazingly addictive but u may feel that acid biting into your stomach after.Awesome and affordable thai food right this way!

I love this place for Thai food but not the queue. There is always a long line of people waiting in the evening. The queue may move fast, but really it depends on how quickly the diners wolfed down their meals. This is not the place for a nice relaxing dinner but it is the place for good and affordable Thai food. The tom yam soup (noodle or just soup) is fiery spicy. I find both clear and the milky versions to be equally tongue-numbing, but the clear soup has a a sharper tartness to it. Other dishes to order will be the green curry chicken and pandan chicken. The pad thai, pineapple rice and olive rice are good but not something that linger in the mind. They do a mean iced thai tea though. A bonus is the take-away counter at the other side of the restaurant. Instead of going straight to the cashier inside, you can now place an order at the counter for take-out. You can also call ahead to order before doing a pick-up. With this, I can see myself ordering food more often for days when I do not want to face the long queue and want some basil chicken rice.

We went very late (past 9pm) and the crowd has slowed so the wait wasn't long. Definitely rather authentic thai food with a very reasonable price, which explained the humongous line every evening if you are here at peak meal times.No aircon and you sit below a HDB block, I guess you can't get more local than that.The dishes:- tomyum soup clear: flavorful but oh-so-spicy that we had to tell them to tone it down. They brought it back to add more broth and we received "these two are such lousy chilli eaters" looks from fellow diners - Thai fish cake appetizer: as good as any you get in Bangkok. Totally yummy.- Thai basil chicken: very good. I like that they use real chicken pieces instead of minced chicken like some other Thai places- pad Thai tang hoon: for a difference to the regular pad thai, we went with glass noodles stir fried pad thai style. If you like pad thai, you will still love this dish. A good version of pad thai, which is a simple dish not always well done.Adding two lemongrass drinks each, the bill came up to $30. Great value!

This is hands down my favorite Thai food place in Singapore. The prices are amazing for the quality of food you get - $6 on average for noodle dishes e.g. pad thai as well as rice dishes e.g. pineapple fried rice. 90% of the stuff on the menu is under $9, and they don't skim on the portions either.I love the pandan fried chicken - succulent chunks of marinated chicken wrapped tightly in pandan leaves and deep fried. They come in plates of 4, which I can easily mop up all by myself because it's that yummy and yes I'm a glutton. I order it every single time and I'm still not tired of it.Another must-have is the thai style kang kong, served in a stylish elevated dish. It's very tasty, but I usually tell them to go easy on the chili padi. The tom yam soup is extremely extremely spicy. Which isn't to say it's not delicious and addictive in a masochistic kinda way. Like your tongue is already on fire and instead of putting the fire out you just wanna douse it with more delicious fuel. Piece of advice: share it with someone or you'll spend the entire night in the bathroom.I've tried the pad thai, pad see ew and pineapple fried rice, all of which are authentic and great complements to the spicy dishes. Oh and if you love cereal prawns but hate to peel them, they serve their cereal prawns half peeled. For some magical reason the prawns remain juicy even though they're cooked without their shells, and they're buried until a TON of cereal which goes great with pretty much everything.And finally, red ruby and mango sticky rice for dessert. If you have to pick one, go with the red ruby. It's not too sweet and is extremely refreshing after a spicy meal. Plus the milkiness puts out whatever fire you induced into your mouth.Definitely go there with a bunch of friends and share as many things as possible. Try to go early, like before 11.30am for lunch and before 6pm for dinner, or be prepared to queue.

I pass by this stall almost every day as I live around the area and there hasn't been once where I've gone past this shop without seeing a long queue of people waiting for a table. I used to think that they were just slow at serving food and clearing tables, allowing the queue to form, until I tried it out for myself.In contrary to what I initially thought, service at Nakhon was quick and efficient. Despite the seemingly long queue, the wait for a table was not more than 15 mins. The staff took down my order while I was still in the queue so the food came almost immediately once we got a table. However, do not expect immaculate service here at Nakhon. Probably due to the busyness of the restaurant, the staff can be rather impatient when dealing with customers. Food is cheap and good! It is cheaper than restaurant chains such as Thai Express, yet I find it more authentic. I really enjoyed the Clear Tom Yum Soup they serve, as well as the Thai Mango Salad and their Phad Thai. I have reservations about their green curry though, as I have had inconsistent experiences with it. The first time I had it, it was thick and flavourful but my recent orders of green curry have been disappointing. The green curry has recently become pretty diluted, with fewer chicken and mushroom pieces. Overall, I would still recommend Nakhon as a good place to go for affordable, yummy Thai food. Go early for dinner (around 5-ish pm) if you want to avoid the queue!

This trusty gem of a neighborhood eatery is what most of us Hougang peeps turn to when we're looking for a quick Thai fix. That the restaurant is staffed entirely by Thais should be an obvious sign of authenticity.At dinnertime, there's almost always a 30 minute wait to be seated at Nakhon Kitchen, even on weekday evenings. I wouldn't dream of coming here for dinner on weekends, so I don't know how crazy a Saturday or Sunday queue can get. Once you're seated, however, service is prompt and your dishes are served in no time.Pineapple Fried Rice, $6.00 - One of the few non-spicy dishes on the menu, the pineapple fried rice here at Nakhon Kitchen is lightly curried, sweet, and nicely complemented by raisins and a light sprinkle of pork floss. Pretty average, but nevertheless useful to have this on hand if you're ordering the tom yam soup.Black olive fried rice with minced chicken, $6.00 - If you're not a believer of fruits in your rice, you've got another carb option in the form of olive fried rice. I actually prefer it to the pineapple rice, as the salty fragrance of olives and siew dam (a dark, syrupy Thai soy sauce) pervades every grain of rice in on that plate. The accompanying chopped raw onions and cashew nuts add a welcome crunch to each spoonful of rice as well.Tom Yam Soup, $6.00 - Ah, the tom yam soup. Where do I even begin? If you're one of those people who have no problem at all with spice, by which I mean you're capable of eating baby red chillies without breaking into a sweat, then you'll enjoy this. Objectively speaking, this is very good soup - it's filled with the distinctive aroma of lemongrass and has a satisfyingly tangy taste due to the addition of tomatoes. Generous serving of fresh seafood within as well.Thai vermicelli salad with seafood, $6.00 - Don't be fooled by the deceptively mild appearance of the yam talay here. I used to find this salad incredibly spicy, but after drinking the tom yam soup this yam talay seems to possess the spice level of a Happy Meal. That metaphor doesn't even make sense, but I trust you understand what I mean. Sour, fiery and refreshing, this vermicelli salad functions as an excellent palate cleanser and whets your appetite for the dishes to follow.Kang Kong Belachan, $6.00 - When my conscience is niggling from all that pigging (wa I'm a poet), this stir-fried veggie dish is something I always order to try and make myself feel better. Like oily vegetables will negate the effects of the other dishes from hell that I'm eating. The kangkong served at Nakhon Kitchen is crunchy and nicely infused with the fragrance of fried garlic as well as the shrimpy flavour of belachan. Only gripe is that it could be a little less oily.Stir-fried minced pork with basil leaves, $6.00 - This dish is a must-order for me every time I visit. Basil leaves are an acquired taste for most, and to me they taste wretched when consumed in isolation. They remind me of liquorice, which I happen to be terrified of. I do, however, think they're excellent when they lend their flavour to stir-fried meats. Nakhon Kitchen's rendition of pork and basil is one of the best there is.The more observant among you would probably have noticed that the dishes reviewed in this article all cost $6.00. Split between three, it works out to a reasonably priced dinner. Plus the food's great, which makes this place is one of my favourite Thai eateries in Singapore. Just a gentle heads up, in case you haven't realised what I've been repeatedly driving across - the spice level here isn't for the faint-hearted. This is value-for-money Thai food that packs a lethal punch, and I'd advise you to come prepared for your stomach lining to bear the consequences of your meal.

Go to this place if you do not value your time, money and body.This place is so overrated, the service is so rotten and the food is so pathetically ordinary on all levels, I cannot believe how bad it was after my experience in contrast with what I've read about it online! I went there early, fully intending to skip the crowds before they form. By 5, I arrived and true enough, I got a table immediately without a wait. So there is NO excuse whatsoever for the surly service. The waitress behaved like the patrons owe her a living. Really! She should consider a different career choice, because she's clearly unhappy with what she's doing. The average service standards in Singapore are beyond appalling in general, when compared to service in the US, Japan and Bali. But this place takes the cake in bad service, even by Singapore standards! Service is several notches below norm in Singapore. When we asked her something, she didn't bother to reply, appeared to mutter something and walked off rudely. If this restaurant was in any city in the US, ANY city, it wouldn't last beyond six months with such appalling service and mediocre food. The food is extremely mediocre. I've had much better Thai food anywhere. The Thai seafood curry was watery and flavorless. The fish cake was bland and dry.How reviewers here even think this standard is anything above ordinary is beyond me.Oh there is an air-conditioner in the restaurant, but because the restaurant has no doors, it's as hot as an oven whether you sit inside or out.

This tiny casual restaurant can be located about a 5 minutes walk away from Kovan MRT station. It is located somewhere near kovan superbowl but at the opposite side of it. There is always a long queue and even longer during dinner time and the wait can go up to 30 minutes or longer.Somehow this place just manages to draw people back to the restaurant despite the not so cheap pricing, the super long waits and queue, and the small portions of food. Probably like me, people would rather come nearby to satisfy their cravings for thai food rather than go to town area.I do like their thai fish cake, pandan chicken, green curry, pineapple rice and tom yam soup though. Maybe the taste is hard to wrong but i don't mind the wait and slightly over-priced meals. Once in awhile dining here would be fine. So it's really up to individual people's opinion i guess.

Great Thai food that is reasonably priced! Serving all you Thai favorites from Pad Thai to Basil Chicken rice, this place is a winner. Just look at the queue for dinner if you don't believe me. I am not going to talk about the food here but instead I am going to highlight their efficient queuing system. When you're in line,  up till the 3rd or 4th person, your order is being taken concurrently so by the time you're seated, your food comes, saving all the frustration from having to order and wait yet again. This system has worked well obviously as many customers are satisfied to queue because they know the line moves fast and they will not be kept waiting once seated. The length of the queue is testimony of how good the food is so don't be put off by the long line!

Come here hungry!  There are so many good here to eat including those delicious $$$ green and purple grapes from Japan!  So many things to see and checkout on the weekends - many Japanese products and sushi.  I even bought a pig placenta serum from Japan $60.  The grocery store is insane and has a serious amount of cheap and tasty sushi.  We spent the afternoon here and Orchard Road.  So fun and easy to grab a Grab car.  I'd highly recommend eating and shopping here, especially when it's during the rain!

The stalls have generic names (like 'Chicken Rice', 'Prawn Noodles', 'Yong Tau Foo', 'Cutlet Speciality', 'Fried Carrot Cake', 'Korean Cuisine', etc), so that stall holders can be replaced without much drama. This also means they cannot induce brand name hawker stalls to come - a strategy adopted by Food Republic at its 3 food courts (ION Orchard, Wisma Atria, and Isetan). No wonder the quality of the food is at least one notch below the others. - the food at the 'Indian Cuisine' stall is downright horrific, and choice limited; avoid it! On top of that, seating place is more limited, AND must be shared with brands that are not in the food court (SaladStop, ToriQ), whereas these brands do have their own seats and tables at Tangs and ION, respectively. But, given the prime position of Takashimaya, at meal times this is always packed solid; more than once I have seen customers fights over seats. Along with the Lucky Plaza food court(s), this is probably the worst on Orchard Road, although the Far East malls are positioned to be more downmarket, so that is less of a surprise.

This place is fantastic. Granted, I am partial towards Japanese food which you will find lots of here. Prices are reasonable and the quality top notch. The vendors happily provide samples. You will find Japanese items with a Singapore spin, like Dorayaki filled with durian. I am a sweets lover so my brain nearly exploded from all the bakeries, waffles and even mini doughnuts. High quality Japanese rice is sold as well as seafood items and dim sum.

Like all Japanese department stores there's always a food court serving up great goodies. That's true here too. Mouth drooling especially on an empty stomach as my sister and I were.  We settled on this stall listing steamed buns but noticed folks queued up for something only listed in Chinese.  We can't read Chinese characters so we asked what was it.  Steamed little rice cakes.  Then topped with minced dried turnip.  So we went with that.   Yummy.  At another stall, it was all deep fried offerings.  Anything deep fried is a good thing.  I got the curry puff and the durian.  Yummy again.Not a whole lot of seating but we took our goodies to go.

Actually not so much this food court but the surrounding kiosks in this food area basement. I find it's really nice food. The food court itself is better quality imo than other food courts. It's a notch above your typical food republic.

I love Tokyo Takashimaya because it has great food court in the basement.Singapore Takashimaya food court is not as great as Tokyo Takashimaya but it's still good.YakisobaTakoyakiYakitoriMochiRice crackers Mmmmm now I am hungry...

This is one big and busy food court in Singapore malls, and is one of the best that I have seen here in Singapore. It gets real busy during meal hours - finding a place to sit can be a challenge. The good has many options to try, ranging from Chinese, to Japanese, to even Italian and French.

Not from Singapore but been in love with this place everytime I come and visit Singapore since I was a child. The stalls has not changed at all, some of the dishes that were offered 10 years ago are still around. My regular round would be the roast duck noodle. Followed with takoyaki from Tako Pachi. Yum! It's just finding tables can be a little annoying. Be aggressive in order to feast in peace.

I love the hustle and bustle of this place and the wide variety of international foods you get to eat in close proximity of each other. From specialty swiss and belgian chocolatiers, to german cake shops to japanese bakeries to artisan teas and coffees...the list goes on. It has this vibrant, marketplace vibe that goes on as people wander from stall to stall, tasting samples, browsing prettily packaged foods. It can get a little too crowded on weekends and that makes it pretty frustrating to get around as the aisle are pretty narrow. Weekdays tend to be emptier and you can take your time to walk around and browse without worrying about blocking someone's way.One may argue that it has become a tad bit touristy and can be a little overpriced, but I suppose that's the price you pay for specialty imported foods.

Good food at a very reasonable price what more can you ask for.It can get quite congested and finding a seat can be a challenge but if you can get past that then the end result will be sumptuous.There is a lot of variety there from Singaporean Chicken Rice to Chinese to Desert and the reasonable does not sacrifice quality so definitely try it out if you can.

Currently going through a lot of Singapore withdrawals (I was in Singapore for 6 months in 2016) and what better way to relive my experiences than to write a review about one of my favorite places to go to for happy hour lol. Like many spots in CBD, The Black Swan is quite a fancy. Right when you walk in, it almost feels like you're walking in to a 5-star hotel especially with its elegant furniture, extravagant interior and semi-dimmed lighting. But when you go to the Powder Room, it feels like you just walk in to a ballin speakeasy. The room is pretty dark and has nice velvet couches, perfect for a more intimate setting.I've only come here for their Happy Hour menu and had their $2 oysters, truffle fries, calamari, and sliders. For the most part, I thought their bar food was quite decent especially for the price. The $2 oysters were always a huge hit in my book. Happy hour prices on wine and beer are pretty similar to most places but with its very sophisticated atmosphere, I feel like the happy hour drinks are more worth it here compared to other places in CBD. Place gets packed pretty fast so highly do recommend calling beforehand to make a reservation (especially if you want to be in the Powder Room). Service is pretty top notch as well. I've come here close to when HH was ending and the server still let me place my order and wasn't stingy about it. There was another time where one of the servers let me charge my phone by where the sound booth was.
Great place for lunch, especially if you are in the mood for something substantial but still quick. The avocado salad is great. Tasty hamburger--beware of the fried egg on it! :-)

The Black Swan is all about the 1920s sophistication. Think fine European classic dishes served in an equally classy and Art Deco building (The Quadrant) at Cecil Street. What i hear is that the bar is rather spectacular for an after work drink but don't miss out on their food! The Black Swan recently updated their menu and it now features classics such as Chicken Velouté, Steak Tartare, and Duck Leg Confit We hear that the Head Chef watches his team like a hawk to ensure the traditional preparation of these dishes are adhered to. Starting with the Raw Bar, the Black Swan Seafood Platter ($148) is a good starter to go with the selection of martinis and cocktails with its mix of Alaskan king crab, oysters, Maine lobster, Obsiblue prawns, Uni, and clam ceviche.If hot is more your thing, then pick some from the Small Plates selection. I highly recommend the Chicken Velouté ($18), a comforting and luscious soup of poached chicken chunks, fried maitake mushroom, and Pain de aisses.The Steak Tartare ($26) uses coarsely chopped beef from USDA 365-day grain-fed cows and is served in a tangy bbq/ketchup and mustard marinate. This is more American than European i think but yummy nonetheless. Great with the toasted bread! Alaskan Snow Crab Salad ($24) features generous chunks of briny snow crab. This was a refreshing dish with the avocado, mango, orange, grapefruit, and citrus vinaigrette mix.Bigger plates will fill you up. If you're coming in a big group, i'd highly recommend that you make an 2 days advanced booking for the Roasted Suckling Pig ($148). Only baby  Spanish  pigs are used here and the tender meat is brined for 24 hours, marinated with herbs and then sous-vide for 6 to 8 hours before being roasted to crisp perfection.
