I know, that's a lot of ANDs.You'll read al the other reviews for their selections, but I suggest just one thing. Try the sambal petai with prawns. I'd never liked petai before, and I may never eat it anywhere else, but here, and with that sambal? I'll get it every time.It stays at three stars because I'm not sure about the price to food ratio... but others love it, so come and try it out anyway.

It is difficult not to like Ivins- absolutely satisfying food, great service, spacious restaurant. I've never been properly introduced to peranakan food until I have been to Ivins, because the low prices make it absolutely possible to order more than what I usually would. I especially love the beef rendang- the beef is melt-in-your-mouth delicious, the sauce is not too thick but packed with all the spices, and the portion is just right so you dont feel too gelat after just one dish. The egg omelette is also pretty popular especially with my two nephews, and its not hard to see why. Not only is the egg fluffy, they are also extremely generous with the ingredients (chai po etc). Another classic would be the honey pork, which consists of small thin chunks of pork carefully marinated with honey and cooked in dark sauce (even though I've always been puzzle why they serve it with boiled green peas because no one seems to eat them!). On days when I crave for something light, I always go for the chicken macaroni which is simply macaroni cooked in clear soup. I also have a super sweet tooth, so I never give the desserts a miss no matter how full I am for lunch. My favourite has to be the bo bo cha cha- the yam is cooked to perfection (crumbles when eaten but firm upon serving), the starchy balls give great texture to dish, and the milk is light and creamy. Their tau suan is also especially well done, not too sweet with just the right amount of starch. A caveat is that the place is not especially well ventilated, so for the office workers who want to avoid smelling like food for the rest of the day, it would be best to visit for dinner.

I got introduced to Ivin's a couple of years back by my peranakan friend who has a bad habit of dismissing anything that doesn't come from her grandmother's wok. So when she grudgingly rated Ivin's as the place to have decent pernakan food at extremely affordable prices, I knew I had to give it a shot.Since then, I have returned to the restaurant many, many time and I always end up over-ordering because I can never make up my mind about what I want. A must-try is the ayam buah keluak - a dish that is so damn good with rice but an absolute nightmare to cook. If you don't know why, go google the recipe. Other than that, the sambal that comes with the lady's finger dish is extremely tasty without being overly spicy. One last dish that you should order is the sotong/fish hitam - chopped onions along with sliced green and red chilli are lightly fried in delicious dark sauce before being slathered on seafood. A great place for a pleasant surprise in terms of food and price. Thumbs up!

Not having been here in a long while, we were pleasantly surprised that the reasonable prices had not changed. The food was also good and well reflected in the long lines waiting to be seated on a weekend evening. They could certainly do with more staff though as it seemed like there were only 1-2 persons taking orders, serving and checking out customers all at the same time.

I recommend coming here with a huge group of people because each individual dish is ridiculously small, but the delight comes when you're able to get a taste of multiple items at a great price (think what happens with dim sum, the more the merrier and things doesn't quite work as well with small groups). Now I don't know my Peranakan food at all, so unfortunately I can't tell you what I ate (other than the ayam fish head and mince meatball soup which were divine), but what I can tell you is that every dish was awesome. We ended up paying $12 per person for more than 10 dishes to share and each of us ordered our own dessert.

As Singaporeans we all love home-style cooking and one such great place to find great home-style food is at Ivins. Although predominantly Peranakan, the food is similar to what we eat at home on a daily basis. Best of all, this home style restaurant is reasonably priced hence the immense crowd as well. Local favorites include Fish Head Curry, Sweet Pork with Peas, Mince Meatball soup , Sambal Kangkong and many more. I can't pick personal favorites here as every individual dish is wonderful so I recommend going in a group of 3 or more so you can share an array of dishes and truly experience the exciting flavours Peranakan cuisine has to offer. Despite the crowd, food does come quick which is a huge plus!

Wow where do I even start? Our family has been going to Ivins for as long as I can remember, and it's one of the best and most affordable places for Peranakan food outside of Mum and Grandma's kitchen.Food : I come here solely for the pong tau hu ... the broth is out of this world as are the pork-tauhu-prawn meatballs. Perfectly proportioned with excellent texture ... gotta love it! One of my chief comfort food dishes. We also really like the ayam curry ... I much prefer my curry chicken Nyonya-style than any other style as the complexity of the spices and herbs used really come through. Love the egg fuyong as well ... not really an authentic Peranakan dish ... I always thought of it as more of a Cantonese dish as we always used to see it on the cold dish platter at Chinese wedding banquets. Parents love the sting ray but we all feel the babi pongteh was a bit too lean. We quite like the sambal udang as well. The honey pork was really crisp and addictive and I quite like the ayam buah keluak as well ... half the fun is digging out the paste in the buah keluak, mixing with the rice and ayam and exclaiming "sedap"! Chendol and gula melaka sago could be better if they crushed the ice to a finer texture.Ambience : Simple family friendly bustling atmosphere.Service : Efficient and no frills. Very good food especially for the prices and the amount of work one would have to put in if cooking even one of those dishes at home. I highly recommend it! Might be a bit hard to find parking so either go early or very late.

4 Fingers Bonchon Crispy Chicken is Korean styled fried chicken from New York and it really is super addictive! There are two sauces to choose from - soy garlic and hot & spicy ... both are equally awesome depending on your mood and preferences. What I love most is the crispy crunchy skin and how it stays that way even after an hour or two. The skinny fries are also pretty good ... but really, the star of the show really is the chicken!

Whenever I find myself at Ion and I get hungry, this is my go-to place. The signature wings are consistently tasty and crispy. This is better than the drumstick. Sometimes the fries are soggy though. My bugbear is the uncomfortable bar-type seating at the big table. I guess it's their way of making you eat and run to ensure fast turnover!
Over 15 minute wait for my order! No apologies. And there wasn't even much of a line! I got an order of six wings and kimchi fries, finally. Never again.

I do like the small size fried chicken here and I am glad it is still around since it opened a few years ago. The menu has expanded over the years and now includes rice, wraps and salad options. I decided to try to the chicken rice set which has 3 pieces of chicken (wings or drumlets), kimchi coleslaw and rice. Combo gets you a drink. The rice, sprinkled with seaweed strips, reminded me of Tori-Q's rice. It was not the usual rice, maybe it was Japanese or Korean grains? The kimchi slaw was interesting, creamy and slightly tart, not spicy to me. The chicken which I requested for a mix (soy garlic or hot) and they were a bit on  the salty side. They were also not that spicy to me. I still like them though. I would stick with the basics next time and just focus on the crispy chicken and either have that alone or with fries. The fries were pretty good, based on previous experiences. The queue is madness during lunch time and after. I realize it is because there is usually one cashier doing everything - taking order, getting drinks, payment. Plus it does not help the entire menu is only on the counter, and with so much choices, first time  or indecisive customers will also hold up the line. Those items on the board are only the popular or standard items. Then you get those who ordered take-away but still sat down on the dining-in chairs, giving another illusion of a packed place.

One thing I dislike about many of the Korean fried chicken joints in Singapore is that these joints never seem to change their oil. Don't get me wrong, 4 fingers is pretty darn good (similar to Bonchon in NY in taste but horrible cooking) and it def has a lot of potential, but the actual restaurant itself screws up the chicken during it's frying process. I don't know if they are just being shady and super cheap with the oil changing or if they overfry the heck out of the thing, but most of the time when I place an order, my fried chicken comes out looking more black than normal. Korean fried chicken I know has a light brown/gold color that is plump and juicy in taste. Instead, I get dark brown/near black chicken that is so tough to chew that it leaves me feeling frustrated, because the sauce is great and I could've had a great chicken. 4 fingers, please. change. your. oil! at least once a day please! (or more, since you usually have lines forming out the restaurant)

This outlet always has long lines. Try coming at non peak hours.that was my tip from some time back...to my surprise when i went on a Monday evening, there was no line.I placed my order for a seafood salad to go and it wasn't too long before i receive my order.sadly, i made the wrong choice to have that to go because the salad was overly soggy when i got home. bad move- i could hardly finish it because it was too salty!!i do have to say service was better than the last time i was there. maybe because they have a new cashier and the kitchen staff weren't as rude. however, there was loud slamming of trays in the kitchen followed by some staff shouting during my short wait in the restaurant.

During my stay in SIN I kept walking past the ION outlet and seeing the queues out the front. Initial impression was it was a KFC (Kentucky) knock off but upon investigation, I found out it was the other KFC (Korean) and had to try some. So I braved the queue one evening and got some take out to bring back to my hotel. I got the #1 combo which was 6 pieces of chicken, a serving of kimchi fries and a drink.I was afraid that in the few minutes it would take me to get back to hotel the chicken would lose some of it's crispiness. Boy I was wrong, this was the most crunchy morsels of chicken I have ever had - and I eat a lot of chicken. The double or triple frying technique definitely has worked without drying out the centre of the chicken. The spicy batter with the crispy skin was awesome and I will be no advocating bring 4 fingers to Australia! The kimchi flavoured fries were great and held quite a bit of punch.The high turnover ensures you get freshly fried chicken and fresh fries so I suggest that you only buy when there IS a queue!

Dragged here by a friend who claimed the chicken served here is "out of this world", I  guess I have to agree with her. Just that it's horribly bad. It's either too Sticky and sweet, or with the soy garlic, too salty. The portions are tiny and the prices they charge, I think its ridiculous. I rather go to a hawker centre and get BBQ chicken wings there. I really don't get the fuss about this place, and I've yet to return. Maybe it's just me that's weird.
Probably one of the best KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) in Singapore!Worth queuing in their forever-long-queue at peak hours!

My friend introduced 4 fingers to me as an upmarket KFC. I beg to differ. To me it trumps KFC, and is possibly in a different league altogether. It is true that it is pricier but if you love fried chicken as much as I do, you will understand why I'm that willing to part with my money for 4 Finger's chicken. Perhaps their flavours do the trick. Both Soy Garlic and Hot & Spicy pack a punch and are fantastic but I tend to prefer the Hot & Spicy as I love anything/everything spicy. The chicken is tasty through and through and the skin is absolutely sinful yet irresistible. The chicken is fried nice and crisp on the outside, yet remains really juicy and tender inside. A paradise for fried chicken lovers!

All the hype + perpetual queues regardless of time of day, I had to check this place out. I ordered a mixed box which consisted of 3 wings and 3 drumlets in both flavors, soy and garlic, and hot and spicy. The chicken was too salty, especially the soy and garlic flavor. Also, I would recommend going for either drumlets or drumsticks. Don't bother with the wings because to achieve the level of crisp, the chicken pieces are over fried. Hence, the wings become very hard and dry. At least the drumlets remain juicy on the inside. Still prefer KFC any day!

This place is my guilty pleasure! I know it's not the healthiest option but it's definitely one of the tastiest! The chicken is always super crispy and the taste is just right. Its good food fast. Only problem I've encountered at this location is seating. Since its always packed there is never any seating. No worries though - if you stare at someone long enough - they'll tend to eat quicker and get up!

One of my favourite fried chickens! 4 Fingers is why I go to ION, and it's even why I don't mind the New Delhi airport so much (they actually have one there..!). I love it THAT much.I guess it's because it is crispy and tasty and it comes in two flavours that are very east Asian in taste: soy garlic, and hot & spicy. The outside of the chicken is crispy and crunchy, the two sauces are both fantastic in their own way, and the insides of the chicken are adequately marinated. Guilty pleasures.

Giving KFC a good run for their money is 4 Fingers! I am surprised why they haven't managed to get more outlets up and running considering a place like Wendy's has mushroomed across the island giving burgers a bad name.I don't know how 4 Fingers does it but they manage to get the chicken crispy and crunchy on the outside but still extremely tender inside. You get to choose between soy garlic or hot & spicy flavour - both fantastic marinades that coat and cling to the crispy chicken skin. Get a bucket of chicken, a stash of beer and head home to while the evening away with a good movie.

In spite of the New York themed decor, this is not an American wing place.  Instead, it features Korean style wings that are crispier than their American brethren.  That being said, the wings are quite tasty.  I slightly preferred the Soy Garlic flavor, but the spicy wings are also good.  Surprisingly their fries were the best I have had thus far in Singapore as well.So, why four stars?  The wing pieces are on the small side (the drumsticks are fine) and the price is a bit high, lowering the value proposition.  I'll definitely go back though and next time I will ignore the decor and go in without expectations of American style wings.

Dude, this place should be called CRACK CHICKEN. Really good. Only compliant is that the portions are small and it does take a while to get your grub on especially if you are in a hurry for lunch. Highly recommend the Chicken Burger. Their recommended Katsu Burger is also quite unique, filled with kimchi coleslaw wrapped in a fried golden bao. This would be a great concept back in the US!  Overall, I think that all Korean food in SIngapore is over priced, but at least this one has some damn good chicken! Will be back.

This was an unexpectedly pleasant place for a lazy sunday brunch. Along a stretch of Robertson Quay that's better known for coming to life at night.My fiance and I have a standard brunch habit - we almost always order salmon poached eggs and pancakes. They didn't have salmon and poached eggs in their menu but I requested that the eggs benedict be replaced with a salmon and they accommodated it just fine, no need to pay extra, etc. Just for kicks, we also ordered the huevos rancheros - that's what mexicans have for brunch and its made of scrambled eggs, refried beans, salsa, avocado and crispy tortillas. The avocados needed abit of salt but otherwise I really enjoyed this dish! Just dump everything on the crispy tortilla and enjoy the mini mexican party in your mouth. The poached eggs and salmon were scrumptious and satisfying. The pancakes were generous but we've had better. Overall, we left as happy campers and all set for the rest of the lazy sunday...Final verdict: Just like a boomerang, I'll definitely be back.

If you are an AFL footy fan, the Boomerang Bars show AFL on the big-screen, in two locations: (1) Boat Quay (right next to Raffles Place ie the CBD if you area-get off at the Raffles Place MRT station) ; and (2) Robertson Quay as well,

I ate here for dinner one night and it was pretty decent. Not a place I would come back to though, as there are better places around the River Valley area in my opinion. I had the calamari and the mezze platter which was good enough but nothing fantastic. A bit overpriced actually I thought, for the quality of the food. The crowd is mainly expats, lots of Aussies and people who live around the area. Its a nice enough ambience, overlooking the river.
Good pizza. Plenty of hubbub, even during weekend brunches. Trivia nights on Tuesdays are alright. Do not love the sports streaming constantly on the TVs.

Classic (Aussie) bar food favorites. Stopped by on the way back to my nearby hotel. Ordered the grilled chicken with bacon sandwich (added avocado) and a Caesar salad. The chicken was a bit overcooked and tough, while the Caesar dressing was a bit dull. They have all the comfort foods and a great spot outside, but keep your level of expectations at bar food and drinks.

I agree with most on here.  Food is nothing to write home about but prices on buckets of beer is decent. It Has a nice view of the river and outdoor seating. We would come back to share a pizza and beers. Pizza also decent. Just come knowing it's a meh but decent.

Went for lunch brunch with my family and it was a pleasant experience. Food was simple, no frills but fresh, tasty and good value for money. The coffee was also decent. Service staff was friendly and this place is very child friendly. Love it!
I've given this restaurant a few shots and left feeling the same each time. The food is either bland, greasy, or the flavor and food combinations are just disagreeable.

Planned to go to Boomerang (grrr, Boomarang??)on a Friday evening. Made online reservationists just in case. Heard nothing, so made a follow up phone call and confirmed our reservations. We do not live anywhere near Robertson Quay so getting here was quite a trek. Hindsight, believe or not, should have driven.Finally get to Robertson Quay and we are dodging gobs of free range dogs and kids roaming about the area. Gobs! Clearly this is a very family friendly part of town. Show up to the restaurant on time. There is no record of our reservation. Kind of bugs me, but only kind of. The place is about half full so no big deal. We are seated. There is indoor outdoor seating, a nice sized well stocked bar area and tons of TVs playing a variety of sports. Another plus is the restaurant sits alongside the waterway and you can watch the tourist boats gliding by. Aside from the reservation snafu, service was really top notch. We ordered our food and it was out within ten minutes. The waitress was really great. She was very attentive.Our starters were the kangaroo sliders. And a side order of garlic bread. Sliders were very good. We ordered rare and they were rare. After the sliders, the rest of our dinner was okay to not good.. I ordered the fish and chips. It included a little salad. The dish was good. The fish was nicely  fried. But the plate that was used was too small so fries were constantly falling onto the table. My companion ordered the lamb. He got a much larger plate, weird, since his portion was smaller. Lamb was very tough and flavorless. We decided to pass on dessert.All in all our experience was okay. I now realize It might have been a better experience for my partner and I if we approached Boomerang as a pub and not a restaurant. So on our next visit (via cab) maybe do a Tuesday trivia, stick with the bar menu, and let loose! Hopefully darting children will be safely tucked into bed as I stumble home.

One of my favorite places in Singapore around Robertson Quay area.  Lots of seatings, tons of TV to watch rugby (go All Blacks!), fans (all seats are outdoor or open air) and lots of friendly people everywhere.  Why only 3 stars?  Their food needs little more improvements!

Decent morning brunch menu, with multiple options. Chose the vegetarian omelette with long black coffee and was not disappointed.  Nice ambience along the river and staff was reasonably efficient. A little hard to find for visitors, but overall a nice experience.

Good steak. The portion is just nice to go with a vegetable side dish. We ordered a plater of grilled sausages, prawn and lamb. It was ok, nothing amazing. The price is slighly on a higher end I must say.

The food here was way below my expectations.  We had the pancakes which were too thick and dry and the french toast which was way too sweet for me.  The fresh squeezed orange juice was good, hence why the review is 2 stars and not one.  I would avoid this restaurant for breakfast .

I pass by this place often but until recently have avoided this magnet for boisterous salmon-tinted overfeds reeking of beer.I finally went and was pleasantly surprised.  My husband and I went on a date and put our well-behaved kids at a table on the other side of the restaurant.  It's a good venue for decent Westernized food.  If I had endless resources and extremely high metabolism, I'd come here more often, because the atmosphere right by the river watching the Australian Football League and people watching can be fun, and the food is tasty.  However, I don't, and the food here is pricey.  It's typical bar fare priced at about $40-$50/head.  My small tumbler-sized margarita was $20.  The service is not impolite but just indifferent.Note that the kids meals are only appropriate if your children don't really eat.  They are tiny.  It's like one of those "Where's the beef?" commercials.  Hamburgers are sliders.  Each of my kids needed to get a whole 'nother meal after their kids meals.  Six people - I only had a salad, 4 kids meals, 2 pork cutlets, a margarita and 2 beers, 3 lava cakes = $200+ with kids leaving saying: "We're still starving!"

A friend of mine wanted to hit this place up because she wanted to bring her dog out to spend the day with us. I liked how it was an out door kind of place with a good view of the Quay. It wasn't quite western so it was in line with my pact to not eat anything I can find in the US. So, when I saw that there was a Kangaroo meat pizza it was a bit intriguing. Why not? I had never had it before and the rest of the menu seemed run of the mill American esque.  It was the most disappointing thing I ate the entire trip. It was small slivers of meat on each slice. The only good thing was the buttery flakey dough. My chai latte had way too much milk. I wish the service was nicer or at least a bit more cheerful. Rather they acted like the customers were an inconvenience. Should have picked a better profession if this were the case! Eh, at least the company and conversation made the day good.

Boomerang featured prominently in a list of top kid-friendly brunch spots in Singapore...Perhaps after being featured among such august company, the restaurant decided not to bother anymore, because the effort was seriously lacking at brunch one sunny, Singaporean Sunday...The harassed wait staff managed to weave around shimmying, speedy scamps while completely ignoring our requests for condiments and unapologetically refusing to replace an incorrectly entered entree.  (Frankly, I'm not sure how you justify this when you have two open face melts with the same name)...Our vegetarian friend was left staring aghast at an open face turkey melt...The only saving graces were the wonderful company and the lovely, riverfront setting...and at least my eggs were served over medium as ordered...PARTING THOUGHT: For an Australian restaurant, there weren't many Aussie options on the menu...

Very good coffee. Great atmosphere for brunch and dinner. Food generally high quality. Can be very busy but I find the staff very attentive and helpful. Nice range of dishes. Perfect spot for watching sports with some friends. Right on the river so nice ambience. I go here all the time and quality is consistent. Only reason I didn't give 5 stars is it is very very expensive. 10 bucks for a mug of coffee is nuts even for Singapore. But it is superb coffee..

An australian pub directly at the Singapore river. Happy hour from 7 to 10. And on Wednesday one of my favorites: Burger and beer, for 22 dollar. Last time I tried the Kangaroo burger. The meat is a little bit dry dispite medium doneness, but with the served topping it is really delicous. So you can sit here in nice atmosphere, watching some rugby other other sports stuff on the flatscreens and simply have a good time.

Old school vegetarian Chinese cuisine in Liang Court. Food generally tastes ok with some dishes better than others. We particularly like the taro/yam dim sum and soup. Overall, comment would be that there was too much flour-based items / mock meat and not enough actual veggies, tofu or mushroom. Price-wise is what you would expect from a sit-down Chinese restaurant

This quaint highly rated vegetarian restaurant in the Orchard Road shopping district does a very nice job with local produce and with a Chinese flair.  I've had two business dinners here and the quality of food is consistently high.  Both occasions we've had the set menu (S$55 pax) which was 6 or 7 courses.  The restaurant is primarily aimed at vegetarians but will veganize even the set menu when asked. They do serve beer but not hard liquor I'm told.  We enjoyed fresh juices tonight. The building in which they are housed has been under construction for some time now.  Hopefully they'll be done soon.  Otherwise I may need to purchase a hard hat. Credit cards taken and reservations are suggested.  Enjoy.

Oh I love this place :p Actually, it seems like I love most vegetarian places! Lol. Perhaps cos they have to be more creative with food for it to be palatable to people. Not very cheap though.We arrived on a Friday night around 8:30pm or so.. Still had to wait a while for a table! Their soups were excellent - bamboo spinach soup with enoki and vermicelli (mm!), and white asparagus soup with mushroom, potato and celery bits. $7 and $11/serving, respectively, if I recall correctly.Our appetizer order of vege satay ($16 for 4 gigantic sticks) came first, actually, I think. Skewers of mushrooms, peppers, beancurd skin, water chestnut.. Quite filling. And delicious peanut sauce :p I love peanut sauce!I think my favourite out of all the dishes was this phyllo pumpkin roll - SO GOOD. phyllo is amazing. and so is pumpkin!! Came with some sweet (maybe also pumpkin? or mango) sauce.Edamame beancurd w mushrooms and xiao bai cai were very interesting.. The sauce had something that I couldn't identify, but was delicious! Gave the mushrooms a different flavour. Very soft beancurd, different texture thanks to the edamame.Side note - we were at a 2-person table and there was a family at the table next to us (it was quite close by) and this kid was so intrigued by us/our food. A little creepy but kinda cute :p

Yum! This is my favorite Chinese vegetarian restaurant because fresh vege is at a max and mock meat is at a minimum. there is a small selection of dim sum available for takeaway, but really, the thing to go for here are the fresh stirfries--fresh lotus bulbs are sweet and crunchy, there are more varieties of mushrooms (that never saw the inside of a can--monkeys' head with chilli is a favorite). They do try to bring in fusion elements but those are a bit of a hit and miss--try them anyway, just don't let the waitresses oversell.If you can't decide what to eat, there are good set menus for pairs and larger groups. It is a bit difficult to find though--if you drive, just park on the 5th floor and find their entrance direct from the carpark. Otherwise, find the Liat Towers lobby behind Hermes and take the lift.

I had a healthy phase about 3 or 4 years back where I tormented everybody with my sudden fascination for all things vegetarian. So for my birthday, my mom decided to make reservations of at LingZhi for the family dinner - that  meal probably convinced quite a number of people that being vegetarian was not impossible.Mock meat is probably a word spat on in this restaurant. Instead, they emphasize a lot on using fresh and natural ingredients to create flavourful and tasty dishes. Crispy mushrooms tossed in a fresh salad, lightly sautéed lily bulbs and egg noodles with crunchy vegetables - you get all the flavour without the guilt. Price-wise, it is reasonable in terms of the quality of food we got. My only lament has nothing to do with the restaurant but my visit got me thinking that we have very few places in Singapore that offer such standard of vegetarian food at more affordable prices.  A pity.

Great hotpot place with yummy dumplings (though some of the dim sum items are a hit or miss). They have the usual spicy and non-spicy broth with slight herbal taste. Wonderful selection of mushrooms and veggies. They even have a few cooked dishes in the buffet line as well as some nice desserts and definitely try the herbal Yuzu tea.

A lovely setting for beautiful food, Antoinette is just the kind of cafe I would expect in posh Mandarin Gallery. From its lavish French decor to its many cream-based desserts, it probably does not come as a surprise that the prices are equally 'atas'. The one area that was lacking though is the service that could have been better suited to the environment. There seemed to be a shortage of staff the last time I went, and it not only took us awhile to be served, but the waitress did not seem very happy to be serving either.The desserts, in my opinion, are very French with lots of mousse and layered treats, and rather innovative and delicate-looking. The tastes had a few hits and misses. I quite liked Le Royale and most of their chocolate-based desserts. The earl grey in Antoinette was hardly there the first time I tried it but delightfully infused the second time. I did not like the Baba pastry very much. I would definitely be back, mostly for the ambience and the gorgeous desserts but I wouldn't go too often.

it's pricy.. but they have pretty good desserts.. i had one of their specials desserts that looked like a small coconut which was actually a chocolate shell filled with coconut mousse and filled topped with pineapple.. pretty tasty and not too sweetmy wife had a white chocolate mousse cake with berries which was also pretty goodmy coffee was meh.. but maybe i'm being a bit picky since i can get a great cup of joe in seattle

One of the best crepes ever! Great place to grab a hot drink and a dessert after lunch or for a break from shopping. I think we found out perfect match when we saw nougatine. It's a crepe filled with Nutella and caramel. Has on top nougatine ice cream. Yummy as shown in the photo

The place was relatively empty for a weekday night. The selection of cakes on the display were rather limited. 2 of the cakes which I was planning to have were not available.Yuzu Green Tea Bubble Bath ($12++)Jasmine green tea with yuzu, dill, mango and lime meringueThe drink was part of the Dilmah Tea Inspired Menu from 1 June to 31 July. It was served with a rubber yellow duck sitting on the meringue. So cute looking. The drink was refreshing with cubes of mango sitting in the bottom. Interestingly it was not served with a spoon and had to request for one.French Toast with Ham and Cheese ($14++)Served with creme chantilly Brioche bread sandwiched with Swiss Gruyere  cheese cream, Paris ham served with salad tossed in house dressing.Could not taste the cheese cream in the bread, nor could see it. The bread looked average not the kind of brioche bread which I was expecting.Ondeh Ondeh Queen's Castella Cake ($11+)Made using fresh fragrant pandan leaf, and studded with gula melaka bits with hints of coconut.It was like pandan chiffon cake, with filling in between.

Ordered their Antoinette's breakfast. Eggs are cooked nicely and tasty. Bacon are good too. Sausage are juicy. But the toast are quite hard to be cut though. Viennoiserie looks good but have to take them away as the main plate itself is quite filling for me. Friend ordered Pork Ragu Fusilli. I tried that too. It is also really nice. I'm contented. With the ambience too, everything are great !

Marronette ($55/$110) - 5 starsFrench chestnut creme Chantilly layered with chestnut cake, orange confit and black sugar crumble, perfumed with dark rumAnother pricey but delicious light cake.Opera matcha - 2.5 starsThe cake was light, the matcha flavor wasn't strong enough and my mom found it too sweet. An unremarkable cake.

Located in Orchard, this French restaurant is a nice option in town if you want to experience an European setting without burning a hole in your wallet. Prices are not cheap but pretty decent given the nice ambience and dedicated service. I had the shrimp pasta. The pasta had absorbed the essence of the shrimps. It did seem a bit like Chinese style bee hoon which is a surprise but not deal breaker. The pancake with chocolate ice cream is really enjoyable and just nice for two people to share. I would certainly want to drop by again.

It's funny how people still cannot differentiate the difference between a macaron and macaroon. When in doubt, always remember there is a dictionary or internet.So let me start by reviewing my favorite to go place to have a nice afternoon tea in Singapore. Antoinette ie. The decor, ambience and pastries, there is nothing I dislike about. I love them all. It is definitely the kind of place I feel in harmony with. If I ever have a cafe, I will model it after Antoinette.Antoinette to me is a place for pastries/tea, a place for great ambience and a place where girls can go and enjoy having a nice get together. Someone I know dislike the place, called the atmosphere at Antoinette too stuffy. Oh well, if one can't sit/behave properly, enjoys talking loudly/crudely or basically prefers fast food joints, this is definitely not a place I will suggest. The pastries, though not a huge variety, have always been very good. I am someone who always look for quality and not quantity. The orchid tea is excellent, something that I do not find it in anywhere else. The French toast with caramelized banana is to die for too.Service here ranged from good to very good. I wish the place takes reservation, I do not fancy standing in line at all. Looking forward to my next visit when I travel to Singapore. Hopefully, everything I love about Antoinette remains the same.

Went on a weekend and waited 30 mins for the table and as soon as we sat down, the lady informed us that we have to spend $20 per head otherwise have to leave in 30 mins. We just found this ridiculous and unprofessional for a cafe. We would have spent around that much anyways but decided not to stay there and went to wild honey instead.

Location: ExcellentFood: Wide selection of unique 'classy' dessert, tastes a little above average though, however the pricing is way beyond average. Basically you pay just for the ambiance and status, not the food. Their specialty is crêpe both sweet and savoury types.Drink: They have wide selection of hot teas as well and you are welcome to get a refill of hot water (if you don't share the tea). Cold drinks suck though.Ambiance: The interior design and tablewares make you feel like you're the most important person on earth. The decor is like classy french dominated concept that's perfect just for tea time. Price: Super premium.
Pro:Ambience was decent, no much noiseSeafood Ogli was not badFrench Kiss tea was pretty good Con:Have to waitGarden of Antoinette was basically patches of grass with some roasted duck breast

Quaint little cafe tucked on the top floor in Mandarin Gallery. Love their macaroon, especially the earl grey raspberry!Ambience is great for afternoon tea and chilling with a good friend for a hearty chat. It can get a little chilly so bring a sweater :)

Antoinette is a really classy joint, with their matching monogrammed crockery and cutlery, and their plush sofa chairs. Named after the last queen of France, they serve all sorts of decadent pastries and desserts, as well as western cuisine.I was really impressed by the attention to detail. It felt very parisian and proper, which had very strange effects on me. I felt like I had to sit up straight, drink tea with my pinky finger raised and say "Oui" a lot. I ordered the Classic Eggs Florentine, and it came on a monogrammed plate, of course. The toasted brioche used was exceptionally good, the eggs perfectly poached, and the salad on the side was fresh and light, balancing my meal perfectly.I also had the French toast with salted caramel, which my taste buds adored. It came in 3 thick slices drizzled with maple syrup and a light dusting of icing sugar. Large dollops of crème chantilly, which is basically whipped cream. But at Antoinette, their whipped cream is extra creamy and rich!Coffee here was rather disappointing, even if it did come in a pretty monogrammed set. My pinky dinger refused to bend, no matter what I did.I would definitely recommend this place for a special date as the ambience is really more romantic and cosy. Or a girly tea gathering. Oui. It's not a big restaurant, so do make bookings if you are coming during peak hours on weekends especially. Will update my review once I try their dinner menu! :)

The theme of this place is French/Royalty-Glamour - with a notion to take you back to the age of the last Queen of France, and be spoilt with French decadence. From the Versailles decor to the Menu - the place does reek of French design, classy and not gaudy. The line is very thin - but the restaurant manages to look chic and exude that seamlessly - from the cutlery, to the tea, to the service, etc. This place is famous for it's Macaroons, though I was so stuffed after dinner that I had no space for them. But my friend took some away! Like a whole box!!What I Love: The Menu has all-day breakfast, which I love. It wasn't the typical American breakfast, hash, etc. - but the eggs were semi-done, the bread was yummmmy... and the sausage was fresh and very very tasty. The main comes with bacon too, which I so loved! I got the set, the Antoinette's Breakfast - which comes with a main, pastries and a drink, for which I got the hot chocolate... it really was melted chocolate - and not just a standard mix. The last time I had such hot chocolate was in Paris itself!What I Don't Love: The prices. It's pretty steep.... like $20 for a main, if you get a set? But a set and a drink will set you back $25-$30.

Went there for their all day breakfast, but it was disappointingly mediocre - I honestly could have done a better job. If you do visit this place for its gorgeous interior and plush furniture, have lunch elsewhere and come here after for a nice pastry and cup of tea (although very expensive).  The pastry selection on display just as you step into the entrance of the restaurant will make you drool! All sorts of croissants, tarts and macaroons are displayed with their buttery finishes and glazes shining under the light (seriously they were shining).  The service staff aren't very well trained though.  The waiter tried clearing my plate before I was finished and I had to stop him with my plate already mid way in the air cos he was so fast and didn't even ask if I was done, and when the bill came they had overcharged us by placing another item that we hadn't ordered on the bill. So do be careful to check your bill before paying!

With Chef Pang Kok Keong at the helm, Antoinette prides itself as the "quintessential Parisian pâtisserie" . According to her website, Antoinette "will set the benchmark for the pastry and dessert scene not only in Singapore, but also in the region with her takes on time-honoured French classic desserts". After reading this tremendous boast, one would expect this to be among the best pastry stores in Singapore. Unfortunately, they fell short.Enter the Antoinette, an earl grey infused chocolate mousse cake topped with raspberry coulis. While the mousse was smooth and luscious, the thick sac spoiled the experience for me. (Haha) I'm not sure what the deal with the sac was, but it was extremely hard to pop. Extracting the coulis while maintaining the integrity of the cake was a chore.When a consumer buys macarons, they look for the most aesthetically pleasing one. Unfortunately, most of the ones in Antoinette's display case had a bumpy surface. The dense macarons tasted as bad as they look.While it would be unfair to compare Antoinette to established tea salons such as Laduree, it is safe to say I won't be back.Don't believe the hype.Note:Props to the design & marketing team for trying to appeal to the francophile in us.

I have heard a lot about Antoinette and have been looking forward to trying it as a Salon de Thé in Singapore is a rare concept. Having used to patronise Canele in the past, I was surprised to find many similar elements here as Canele. The crepes are presented in the same manner, and seeing the Strawberry Shortcake, Mont Blanc, Le Royale and certain macarons on the display was uncanny. However, Antoinette definitely covered the Salon de Thé vibe well, almost felt as if I was in France. The tea selection was extensive and the caramel tea I had matched my hopes exactly. Macarons were not bad either, though not the best I've tasted. The onion soup was a slight let down - although the flavour of the broth was good, I personally prefer a thicker and heartier soup, and the cheese crust that covered the top of the bowl did not do the soup any favours.

Smoked salmon Blinis (16.50) ain't great, don't get them especially if you aren't a great fan of doughy pancakes! Hot chocolate (7.00) is pretty much a must try, not too sweet neither too thick and creamy, proportion + taste was 'just nice'! You wouldn't believe it, but It makes a good thirst quencher! Ps: love the interior decor with its fine upholstery. Absolutely comfortable and lovely! Simply Western :)

This year, Antoinette has come up with 3 Christmas macarons along with 4 other Christmas cakes which are upsized versions of its regular petit cakes.Rum and raisin macaron/Fruit Cake/Orange Flower In all, these Xmas flavors like fruit cake are not exactly what I prefer but is certainly a welcome innovation. The macaron shells are slightly dry and hard. Hence they are fairly decent but not the best versions in town so far.

This seemed like a very valiant effort to recreate Paris's Angelina in Singapore. The hot chocolate was excellent and the creme chantilly was unusually thick but still good. The Kyoto dessert was excellent. The aircon was on too high though.
Alright food, great cakes, ...but bring a sweater.  The air conditioning in this place is set at below freezing, and apparently it cannot be adjusted :-s

The Bottom Line: Good quality and service, but the portions are on the smaller side.Try:Grilled Chicken Burrito BowlPro:The service is fast and friendly, and the restaurant itself has a good vibe. It has a slightly chic-er take on Chipotle.The food itself is pretty good! Don't expect authentic Mexican, but it is pretty good for what it is. Good flavors and seasoning, and all the right ingredients. I'd come back for sure.Con:The portions are a bit small for the price.

Mex Out is one of the better Mexican joints in Singapore.I agree with Michelle that their food tends on the salty side (still) but it wasn't as overpowering as described in her review. Perhaps they got the message and took the salt down a notch, but just a notch - so maybe my burrito had only 2 days worth of daily recommended allowance for sodium but it was still a worthwhile treat.I had a large pork burrito with cheese and sour cream (an extra $0.50 each) with a side order of big chips which comes with your choice of salsa and a canned drink or water. Everything clocked in at just under $20 which I've begrudgingly resigned to accept as the norm around these parts.Service is quick and courteous with a lot of comfortable seating options inside and outside.The queue can be quite long during peak lunch hours so come during off-peak times to enjoy your burrito in peace.

I don't know, man.Mex out is like a friend that you want to maintain relations with, but the drama continues to ensue and you're left wondering whether it's worth it or not.I really want to be friends, Mex Out, I really do! It's been over a year, and this time I tried the small 10-inch chicken burrito (to save money and calories.) Luckily it wasn't as salty as last time but the chicken was a bit too dry for me, and the rice seemed like it was drenched in tomato sauce and slightly undercooked. At least they set up the burrito right, as I got a taste of all ingredients during each bite (unlike Baja Fresh, which really needs learn the basics of burrito making.)Maybe I'm just ordering the wrong thing. Should I be doing tacos? Barbacoa burritos? Carne Asada burritos? I still love the branding and the vibe, and it's definitely a nice place to chill and have a beer... but I have yet to find the one food item that'll make me add one more star.

For a place that's thousands of miles away from Mexico with limited mexican food option, Mex Out is decent. It's by no means authentic and it's not even trying to be. I agree that it reminded me of Chipotle.I like getting either the salad bowl or the rice bowl - the latter being if i'm ESPECIALLY HUNGRY because it's kinda a lot of food. The you can mix and match your own meat, beans, sauces, and whatever add-ons you want to your dish. Whatever you do, go with the pork - it's good. For sauces, I like their mango salsa and picante.And that's all really. I've been going here for my mexican fix because of the convenient location (it's in the CBD). But truth to be told Singapore is still in the market for a good, proper mexican food.

Well the first thing I thought about when going to this place is whether it would be even close to Chipotle in the US.  Whoever opened this place obviously thought chipotle was a good business model. While I cant say its as good in the burrito department they have some good food. Its more of a quick eats type place. You can pick between a burrito, taco, salad and nachos.  Then you add on a variety of toppings. The rice was ok but I miss the lime cilantro rice from chipotle.  The toppings were good, the veggies were very tasty and they had a variety of good salsas.  With the meat and beans added in it became a bit soupy so I think they should do a better job at draining it before adding it in to the burrito.  You can also get beers, margaritas and tequilas which seems fine but not when your heading back to work, maybe after.   Its a nice place, good service, not really chipotle but the closest youll get in singapore for sure.  Definitely worth checking out so if you like mexican food give it a try.

There are few Mexican restaurants in Singapore. However, be that as it may, Mex Out has just shot to the top of the list. Yes for all you Singaporeans searching for good Mexican food,  the search is officially over. For sure designed to be a Chipotle style restaurant it really does hit the bullseye.Very fresh food, great flavors, chips and salsa on the money, 7$ Negra Modelo's and margaritas during happy hour. What's not to like?Just about perfect.

Chipotle gets it right on so many levels I was excited to try this Chipotle knock-off.  After waiting in live for bit I ordered a salad bowl with black beans, chicken & guacamole. The beans were under-cooked and the guacamole was browning and starting to turn. I had to scrape around it to avoid it because it tasted so bad. Plus, at about S$12.50 it cost more than I would have paid at Chipotle for a similar dish. Bottom line: its a Chipotle copy cat that charges more for lower quality.

Haaaaa. I seem to be saying this a lot but I really wanted to like this place. I received the invite to their opening party a while back and didn't go. But I was so excited at the prospect of a burrito place that was "chipotle-like" according to a certain publication that I forwarded the info to a number of my friends working in the area. Side note, I've learnt to not trust recommendations from said publication because I've had several blah experiences based on their rec's to date.Anyway I went to Mex Out yesterday with my friend, J, who was/is my bestie from our time at UVA. She had the tacos and I had a burrito with cochinita pibil, pinto & black beans, sour cream, lettuce, 2 salsa's and guacamole (why do I have to pay $2 more for guac?). The portions were decent if you consider how much an average meal costs in Raffles Place (or at least that's what I keep telling myself everyday).How'd it go? Uh it was really salty. At first I thought hmm maybe it's just the beans. Took that out and ate the pork with the rest of the ingredients...nope still salty. I eat hawker food pretty regularly (hello salty chwee kuay at ghim moh) so it's not like I had some salt sensitivity issues. So I still finished my burrito like a good Asian person but boy did I have that icky "man I need some water" feeling afterwards. Actually now that I've read some of the reviews below, I realize I'm not the only one who felt their food was salty. Oh well, maybe I'll be back for the alcohol?

I've been to Mex Out twice, and while I while readily volunteer that I always end up there a little past peak lunch hour, I've never, ever, had warm food. The filling, in addition to being "not generous", has just always been cold. Between my colleagues and I, we've tried both tacos and the burritos, and Mex Out has disappointed both times.This is my first one star review, but I've never dined at anywhere that I could say with such certainty. I'm never going back.

The pork and guac were good. They were not kidding when they named the mini burrito, it was about a third of the size of the normal burrito. It was almost a taco. I think the black beans were also too salty and the margarita was mostly ice.

Good spot for a casual bite. I met a gf for a few drinks and some eats. Beware, there's not many options... beer, margaritas and sangria, but happy hour from 6-8pm is a decent bargain. Table service isn't really an option, you order at the counter so it's very cafeteria style. We had some corn chips and guacamole... the corn chips were freshly fried and the guac was chunky and fresh. Decent snack for $6.We both had the rice-bowl (effectively the burrito without the tortilla) which was a good size and well tasty... go down the cafeteria chain and choose your beans, your protein, the salad, and your salsa (lots to choose from). Guac and cheese costs extra (which I don't agree with, but whatever). The tacos looked like a good share option, as do the nachos. Service was mixed... the guys were friendly, the sole girl looked like she wanted to be anywhere but behind the counter. Maybe some edgy music could give the place a bit more vibe? It was lacking in atmosphere somewhat but if you're just after something tasty to fill the belly, then maybe this is for you. I'd go back for a quick bite... or maybe go for drinks at one of the numerous neighbouring bars and then go to Mexout to soak up the alcohol!

I had such high expectations from Mex Out especially after hearing about their Chipotle-like concept. Similar to another reviewer, I am a native Texan, born and raised. So I have sorely been missing quality Tex-Mex in Singapore. I was ready to make this place one of my regulars. Until that is I actually went there to eat. I discovered the only thing about this place similar to Chipotle is the assembly line approach to making your food. I ordered a burrito and it was extremely pricy for what you get. It was filled primarily with rice and little meat. The guacamole was not guacamole...Maybe it was just a bad batch that day but the avocado wasn't even ripe making it hard and chunky to eat :( sad to say, I am still searching for tasty tex-mex in Singapore...

If you want Mexican food in a more casual setting similar to Chipotle, this is a good spot.  The flavors are authentic, the ingredients are fresh, and the prices are decent compared to other Mexican places around town.  I had a chicken salad bowl that was pretty decent, but my friend's babacoa was far tastier.  And the side of guacamole was  plentiful and delicious.

Tiong Shian Eating House is conveniently located right inside Chinatown on New Bridge Road. The place is just 5 minutes walking from Clarke Quay. Food here is tasty, authentic and reasonably cheap. Frog porridge has an undoubtable sweet taste. The frog is chewy, moist and juicy. We really love to drizzle extra sesame oil on top, which obviously gives an interesting twist to the taste. Century eggs porridge, in addition, blows us away with its creaminess and fragrance. Apart from being a perfect treat to have on a rainy day, a bowl of century egg porridge is also great for people who are sick, as it's wholesome and hearty.Recommendation: Frog porridge and century eggs porridgeRead our Singapore Food Guide: thecoupleeats.com/singap…

The flurry of 4 star ratings for this place really puzzles me. Came here with a friend on a Monday night at 10pm (they apparently close on alternate Mondays so we got lucky).We got a bowl of century egg porridge with an added raw egg, a pot of gongbao frog, plain porridge, and some raw fish. I really wasn't impressed with the century egg porridge, because I only tasted the soy sauce they liberally put, and it was watery and insipid. The raw fish was reasonably fresh, with chilli, lime, ginger; nothing spectacular, and the frog was just... meh. I don't know how much this place costs... but any price is too much for this (lack of) standard(s).

Since CNY is round the corner, why not head down to Chinatown for a little squeeze with the crowd at the street market and have a sumptuous frog-leg porridge to round up the experience! The portion is pretty generous and the gravy is not too spicy. For a tender tongue like mine that cant tolerate too much spiciness, this is great. If you want a kick for your tastebuds, just ask them to up the intensity of the spiciness! Add a plate of raw fish to increase your appetite as the freshness of the fish doused with the acidity of the lemons livens up your tummy.Fresh, flavourful and warm. One word - YUMS.

Location is at Chinatown, just beside CK department store opposite People's park complex. There are many choices of porridge to choose from and it was tasty - one of the better ones over here. Besides that, there are selection of side dishes to choose from and the ones my friend ordered were pretty tasty. This eating place opens until late at night and is popular among the locals and after trying it for the first time, I certainly recommend it.

Awesome Porridge! Even better "sides". I was in Singapore for business and was taken here by my coworker. She ordered everything. It's not fancy at all, just tables on the sidewalk. As always with night market vendors, find a table, then go get food. Food was so flavorful. I wish I could go back!!

No frills coffee shop near chinatown, supposedly porridge is awesome so dragged my parents here on Sunday after church to check it out!Pick your dishes and order/pay at the little counter.We paid:1. $4.20 for yusheng - not bad, but there were bones! are there supposed to be bones?? I was somewhat confused. I guess they are edible, but somewhat disconcerting to feel the texture on one's tongue, nonetheless2. $8.80 for claypot gong bao fish slices - pretty gd sauce, wasn't very thick sauce, but went well with the plain porridge3. $5 for you choy (sauteed veg) - shanghai greens, apparently. Mom buys these veges from NTUC regularly, very easy to steam. Anyway, came with nice sauce! Garlic soy mixture of some sort.4. $0.60 per bowl of plain porridgeI wasn't super-wowed, but it's a fairly good meal for the price. It's kind of hot there though!

There is only one place to go for supper in Chinatown and that is Tiong Shian. It is so popular that there are always cars and people clustered around the corner coffeeshop even at 11pm. Having had work in the area before, its one of the few decent food options available by that hour. Word of advice though for those who drive, good luck finding parking. And when business is brisk, good luck finding a table too. As the name states, they are famous for their porridge. Every possible kind with every possible ingredients / toppings is available here. Called me a traditionalist, but I often go with the staple Pork porridge with century egg. I like the portion sizes especially after a long day at work or play for you clubbers out there. As with most supper porridge stalls, they also serve frog legs porridge. And for those of you who irk at the thought of eating kermit, I will tell you the same thing my parents told me when I was a kid squirming at the very same idea, "It tastes the same as chicken, only much nicer!". Its really true as frog meat is lighter and sweeter in texture, and the flavours goes into making the porridge sweet and light too.And for more variety sake, they also serve a very good standard bbq chicken wings and also raw fish (chinese style not japanese sashimi) to go with plain porridge if thats your cup of tea.

Famous porridge, parking pains.This is probably one of the most busy porridge places in chinatown. Located on a very visible part New bridge road. Tiong Shian porridge centre is never short of customers.As you would expect, you have a good variety of choices, century egg with lean pork meat, fish, pork innards, pork liver, cuttlefish, prawn, frog legs... you can have your porridge in any way you like. Prices here are reasonable and the only downside is the possible long queue and the impossible parking woes you might have. Plenty of cars park illegally along the street, order up and then leave. Keep an eye your vehicle if you choose to do so. Fines are issued quite regularly here.I order only a couple of things on the menu regularly and that's the clay-pot gong bao fish slices or the clay-pot  gong bao frog, the fish porridge, pork porridge and occasionally the raw fish (nothing special).I have to say, if the queue is really too long or if there isn't enough seating space, don''t waste your time. Just go to the other porridge place next door called 'Sinma'. The claypot gong bao frog there is very decent and there's hardly a queue there ever.

To call Tiong Shian an institution in Chinatown is hardly an overstatement. Their porridge is among the best, if not the best in Singapore (and that's not an exaggeration either). Alas, it's so popular (and parking in the vicinity so scared) that sometimes, there's a long queue for the tables. Fortunately, they have recently expanded their premises into the shop at the back (in addition to the unit above) which helps with crowd (but not the car parking). Their porridge comes in many different variety - pork, fish, chicken, cuttlefish, etc. The porridge is in fairly large portion too. In addition, Tiong Shian offers a large assortment of side dishes that you can order to go along with your porridge. You can be spoilt for choices (the regulars, however, will always pick the same stuff that they like).

Most people will know of this place for supper but standard has since dropped so much that I feel it is not worth visiting anymore. The porridge is blend and doesn't live up to its name.There is also a second floor above the coffee shop to choose to have your porridge.What most people order is the frog leg with porridge but I usually get the century egg with lean pork meat porridge.Although there are many who agree with me that standard has dropped but it really is a good place for supper and there are still long queues throughout the nights/

Tong Shian is most famous for its porridge and frog legs, but those are not the dishes that bring me here on a regular basis. Yes, the porridge is good, but the side dishes are the ones that really stand out and make the trip to Chinatown worth my while. I always order a plate of their bean curd, vegetables and raw fish. The bean curd is generously sized and nestled in a delicious sauce, whilst the raw fish is simply prepared with lime, chilli and ginger. I don't think I could ever get tired of either of these dishes. It can get pretty crowded, and you may have to wait a while for tables on a busy night. They have more tables at another outlet besides the small provision shop, so take a walk down that way if the main area on New Bridge road is full. To order, you will need to make your way to the cashier, so don't expect to have anyone come by and ask what you'd like to have.

The porridge here is good and the side dishes you can order makes dining here worth the trouble of searching for parking .There's a large selection of choices for porridge (usually pork for me), and they come in fairly large sizes. Throw in an egg, add a couple of side dishes and you'll have a sumptous spread for supper that anyone would be pleased to have!

The store is inside a normal hawker center, opposite CK shopping mall. Tiong Shian sell porridge and claypot frog with different variety and reasonable price. The store is open air and without air conditioner. Tiong Shian operates from 8 am - 4 am. It will be a good place for dinner and supper. The atmosphere here is great at night with hot porridge. You have to make your order and payment at counter and inform them your table number. They will serve your foods within 20 min. Out of so many varieties, a must have item are dried chili claypot frog with plain porridge. The plain porridge with the sauce is yummy, but the porridge too diluted. You can order other side dishes like vegetables, tofu etc with the porridge.

For my birthday, my friends decided to get me this amazing chestnut cream cake with crunchies and fruit on it.  It was possibly one of the most delicious cakes I have ever had.  The sponge was light in texture and deliciously moist. The chestnut mousse was amazingly balanced in creaminess and sweetness. The crunches (cereal?) adds an added layer of texture in the cake. Overall... yes, I'm in love, and I don't even like cakes that much! Excellent option for a cake!

Amazingly balanced earl grey lavender cake, if you like these flavours. The chai cake was very strongly flavoured, but it would be interesting to get if you like chai. The maple cheese tart was not bad. This place has totally overpriced drinks though. You might want to get a hot pot of tea to share.

I understand that many come for their Japanese-French style cakes. But I came here to check it out but primarily to try their Ice Cheese Tart! Wasn't feeling a craving for cake, maybe another time. Given it was my first time here I gave their original a try. It was good. A nice almond crust and good balance of not too too sweet cheese filling. It was perfect to eat there because they cut it into fours for you and it doesn't get warm too quickly, etc. Yum, they had so many other flavors. I'll definitely be back to try their Earl agree :) Their other cake slices looked a little pricey and small. Their tea was cute in clear glass pots heated by a candle so it wouldn't get cold. Cool, but not worth $10 for a homemade blend in my opinion. Same with the iced coffee, $8 seems a bit steep for a normal size tall glass. Anyways, the atmosphere was nice, loved how bright and simple the decor was. Overall I feel the patisserie is kind of pricey but it is a specialized niche so I guess it can get by. As I said I'll be back for their ice cheese tarts :) plus I found the Duxton Hill area is a nice area to walk around too. Tip: come to hang out and share a pot of tea with some nice treats Tip2: no wifi availTip3: variety of treats to purchase from full cakes to packaged goodies too.

Excellent customer service.Recommendations on what's new really helps. I was hovering for probably a good few minutes at the seemingly endless choices.Cake was dense,quoting the boyfriend,a value for money.The mango topping was the best mango i had in a cake in my life! it wasnt glazed to death with syrup.

I will add my praises to the other Yelpers who have reviewed here and thank them for helping me find this gem.I played it safe and ordered the tiramisu which somehow they managed to lift above expectations, the cream was heavenly and each mouthful melted into my mouth.Claire tried the strawberry napoleon, which I scored a mouthful of which was also lovely; I only have a two days left but I hope to return and try more.

I was surprised to see how small the space is. Some tables and chairs to accommodate 6 and another 3 stools along a small bar counter. Outside the shop, there're dining space for another 8 perhaps? I reckon it's more of a bakery for cakes to go. But anyway we decided to camp there for a while to enjoy the cakes.  The green tea cake is very light and this is very typical of Japanese cakes. I love the Japanese cheesecake with that cow logo on it. I can finish at least half a cake in a sitting (i swear it). It doesn't feel sinful at all. Every mouthful simply disappears into a fragrant mix that glides down your throat. It feels like a dream because you're not sure if you really did eat it at all. The matcha is strong but not overpowering and the green tea sponge cake was also very airy and moist. I like the green tea jelly which sits on top of the cake. It adds an additional dimension to the creamy texture, kinda chewy but not much? Flor uses the Kyoto-uji matcha for the pristine flavor and aroma and it's a damn good choice.The Waguri millefeuille was also very nice. Same quality to the sponge cake. I would reckon that their toufu chiffon cake would have the same texture. Z had it before and said that it's pretty good but pricey for a chiffon cake ($13.80 for 1 if i didn't remember wrongly). There's a nice mix of custard and cream with the puff pastry.Typically, a mille-feuille would have 3 layers of pastry and 2 layers of creme but this only has 2 layers of pastry. I'm not too picky about stuff like that. I personally thought this has a nice pastry to cream/cake ratio. Any more and i would feel like i'm trying to sandpaper the insides of the throat.Pastry was well done, has a nice bite to it and wasn't at all moist or flat from the creme. The chestnut paste goes down really easy. I've tried several chestnut based desserts such as the Mont Blanc from Antoinette but they are kinda dense and dry as compared to Flor's. Z and i had a discussion about the chestnuts that were used to made these desserts and if they differ from those we typically see at the night markets. Think it's the same?Anyhoo, the cakes didn't even take up much space in our tummies and we ordered their iced cheese tarts. They have quite a couple of flavors e.g. orange chocolate, caramel, green tea with yuzu and a couple of others. It has an almond cookie base and is filled with a lightly salted cream cheese filling (Flor's signature) and goes for $3.20 a pop. I would liken the experience to what eating dry ice would be. It simply sublimes in the mouth and vaporizes. Imagine cheese that does that? It absolutely defies logic but it's really interesting. I was confused and surprised for a bit on my first mouth. We had the caramel one and it wasn't too sweet (which is great). Go try it for yourself.

Hmm. I'm a little torn rating this place.My friends and relatives love it, but it just doesn't hit the spot for me. The cakes are indeed good by objective standards - light and fluffy but not floury, well-balanced flavours, not too sweet, not too creamy. But I prefer richer and heavier cakes that make you sick when you eat too much of them.

decent-alright japanese-styled-french cakes at this tiny cafe in duxton hill. flor patisserie is pretty well-known for its light, japanese cream-type cakes, but I hadn't gotten to it previously on my dessert circuit precisely because of those characteristics: I like my cakes hefty and substantial, and these fluffy, creamy things do little for me.but for its class, the desserts are good - certainly worth a visit if you're into this sort of thing. there's no way to get around this - this place is pretty much fantastic for women (and persons inclined toward the delicate and feminine). it's a small white-walled space with a large window that lets in plenty of light at brunchtime, and the counter is laid full with colorful, dainty little cakes with all sorts of fancy frosting and glazes.we had five cakes from the selection on offer that day - mango (the unanimously-declared winner of the day), strawberry, yam, chocolate and blueberry - and whilst there was a mix of textures from millefeuille and the sponges, all the cakes felt the same.everything's certainly gorgeous - but all a little too light and substantial. of course, this opinion speaks more of my preferences than the skill of the kitchen; if you're into this sort of thing, it does well enough (and you might also want to try its famous ex-chef's new venture: his eponymously-named chef yamashita).
It's very subtle the tastes. To be honest by the look, nothing looks too impressive. I just think it's a food bloggers dream in taking pics but I think nothing special.

I've recently became a fan of cheese tarts and popped by this place after hearing about it from a friend. Their "Ice Cheese Tarts" is OK for me, not overly sweet but lack the "oomph" I would normally expect. The almond crust was good and made up for the lack of cheese-:)
Love the strawberry souffle and the berry berries cake. the cake is light, the cream was good too and it didn't leave any after taste :)Ice cheese tart was good, but the cakes are far better.

With the kitchen and ovens helmed by Chef Yamashita and his disciple, Heidi, Flor's Pâtisserie is a pretty picture of a little cake store sitting upon Duxton Hill. It is completely unassuming and humble in its simplicity but selling hand-made and heart-made delicate desserts that can sweeten up anyone's day.While many of us here in Singapore are used to French style desserts in which tastes are heavier and richer, Heidi shares that Flor's Pattiserie is all about Kansai-styled pastries: light, fluffy and working with loads of fruits. It is ridiculous if I said everything in the display was good? Probably not at Flor's. Particularly note worthy Earl Grey Chocolat and the Waguri Millefeuille. It is hard to find cake with good chestnut cream in SG. This is where you can get it.Also, pack home some iced cheese tarts in a variety of flavours home to share. Your family will love you for it!

A tiny, quaint bakery and cafe on Duxton hill, the cakes here are as pretty as they are delicious. I love the attention to detail and the decorating is exquisite, making it almost seem like a sin to stab these beautifully presented cakes with a fork. Looking through the showcase at this selection, it was extremely difficult to make a decision, but we eventually settled on the millefeuille and strawberry soufflé. The latter was delightfully moist, whilst the millefeuille was surprisingly light even with the layers of pastry. We were extremely happy with both our choices, and I certainly look forward to returning to try more of their creations.

If you have a sweet tooth and a dying love for cakes, then Flor Patisserie will be your desired place to go to!The kitchen helm by renowned Chef Yamashita, you know you'll never go wrong with your choice at Flor Patisserie. My friends introduced it to me and I finally got to try the cakes a few weeks back, during a birthday celebration.I tried the Wakakusayama (green tea base) and the Mont Blanc. Honestly, I didn't really like the green tea one as the taste of matcha was too overwhelming for me. This is just a personal opinion as I'm never a big fan of green tea. The only tea I enjoy is Winter Melon Tea.Anyway, the Mont Blanc was fabulous! The cake is soft and so yummy! I loved it. I also ate most of the birthday boy's cake. Too hard to resist if you ask me.
Awesome cakes with the right amount of sweetness and fluff! The only thing is the place is a bit small so it is only good for small group of people :) I love their chestnut cake!

This little cake shop  is located in the increasingly popular Duxton Hill.  The japanese styled cakes served here are very similar to that of Glace Pastisserie but with a difference touch. After all, Chef Yamashita did a stint at Glace before opening up Flor. I find that the cakes served here are more fruity themed.  The cakes are pretty and delicious yet not overly done up with cream and fondant.  Unlike Glace where it has only has a storefront, Flor has some limited dine-in space for customers.

Flor has got to be my favorite cake shop. Opened by Chef Yamashita, who is Japanese, it is a French-Japanese cake shop that has the most delicate and exquisite cakes. It is as if they are the exact opposite of the cakes you get at neighborhood shops of coarse and simple flour and eggs.The shop is located on the sleepy stretch of Duxton Hill and has a blue signboard. It is also diagonally opposite Littered With Books, an indie bookstore. Note that the place closes at 7pm and runs out of cakes quite early so be sure to go early too!Try the strawberry cream cake and Mille feuille. I find their chocolate cakes slightly too rich/sweet. I prefer their lighter creations instead.

Led by Chef Yamashita who learnt his baking tricks from Japan, you can be sure to find some authentically Japanese pastries in this little cafe along the swanky Tanjong Pagar area. Japanese pastries differ from their Western counterparts because of the careful attention to detail, and lack of reliance on artificial elements such as baking powder and preservatives. Each piece of pastry in Flor, especially the cakes, is a carefully assembled masterpiece that sometimes look too good to eat. But don't worry, they taste as good as they look. I usually order any cake that is a combination of sponge, fruits and cream, as I'm a fan of the Japanese style of baking such cream cakes - the texture and flavour of the light sponge, tart fruits and non-cloying cream is delicious. (I've made it a point to never order such cakes from non-Japanese bakeries as I've had many bad experiences)The staff are friendly and approachable, which makes this place a delight to visit every time!

It was my first time going to this small cozy sort of cafe x restaurant . It was just a random walk in as the display outside was just too tempting . I ordered matcha soufflé while my friend ordered a pancake soufflé (or something?) The matcha was not too sweet and is just right . The service was efficient and fast . And the service crew is friendly too !
overrated.the queue is so darn long and i dont think there is a great thing in their desserts at all.perhaps i shall try the original one in japan instead.

After reading so much about the hype over this Japanese kopitiam, we decided to head over during a weekday evening. However, this trip made me realise how inefficient communication in the kitchen can actually hold up the queue and upsets diners even though this usually happens in Gordon Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares.Speaking of the food, the baked curry rice was delicious as the beef curry sauce was really thick and savoury. The soft egg yolk enhances the richness of the rice. It has been years ago since I had my Japanese curry rice.The pancake souffle is nothing spectacular and was a little tad dry and less fluffy than a mc pancake. Hence had to rely on the brown sugar syrup to finish this although they gave us the maple syrup which we did not choose. The puny little salted whipped cream was definitely not enough to go with the pancake. But to pay for extra cream? Definitely no way. Fortunately, the matcha souffle saved the day. Even though it did not rise to a considerable height, it was filled with sweet matcha custard and thus this warm pud was really comforting one to enjoy. The only dish that I would recommend one to try.In short, this place is definitely not worth queuing so better to avoid peak hours. I think it is very adventurous or bold for a newly opened restaurant to offer so many soufflé items as they require long waiting time. However, this must be provided that the orders run smoothly without missing out or leaving out any item, only to have realized that the kitchen had left out the order after customers' reminders.

Ok as I am still shock as the sticker price of hand dripped coffee, my husband wanted to try this place. As I was getting hungry to, why not see what is so special with pricey coffee. Well I totally put my foot in my mouth, this was amazing coffee, it was strong and had a seriously amazing after taste that I just can't describe, let's just say I didn't even really need to sugar or cream at all. Now what totally sold me on this place was their Hoshino Souffle blew my mind as I never had anything like it. It was tomato fried rice at the bottom with this creamy fluffy egg like whip cream topping. It put the Omu rice to the side and now not worst eating.  The teriyaki chicken sandwich was good too. The sevice was ok but at least here is a button to call them.

Personally I didn't like their blended coffee.  It's more like a tasteless Starbucks roast. After I inquired, the cook did admit they don't use Mocha (which is unusual for a Japanese blend that I've tasted in most coffee shops in Japan having lived there for 10 years). Certainly doesn't warrant the S$5.80 per cup.  The milk (not cream...ok, fine) was not even warm.  Looked forward to their Pancake Soufflé but was turned off by the 30 min wait requirement (which means I will finish my coffee long before it shows up). Had the French Toast instead which was nice.

This review is long overdue. Wanted to rave about one of my favourite places in Orchard Road, but just didn't get to do it till now (excuses I know hahahahah). So, here's the story. Celebrated my birthday at this cafe in May this year with my gal friends. 4 of us ordered a few mains and a dessert to share. I gotta say we were all very happy with the food. I especially love the 2 main dishes: Fuwa Fuwa Hoshino Soufflé with Porcini Rissoto Tomato Cream and Omu Rice with Shrimp & Mozarella. Just writing about them and looking at their yelp pictures are making me hungry now. Their dessert item, Double Pancake Soufflé Style is also recommended. It is so big I am sure it can feed 8 instead of the 4 of us. Love the service here! Definitely one of the few places in SG where you can enjoy good and cheery service at a mid-priced eatery. Good service is just super hard to find in SG #sadfactoflife.I have been coming to this cafe chain over the years. My favourite outlet is still this Plaza Singapura one.
