The service is average, typical of such old school Chinese restaurant. It can be better, and it did get better for those who know the people there.

More like 3.5 stars but I'm feeling generous.The food here is good but not exceptional. There are many better places to eat in Singapore. But I'd come back.Lunch is always busy as its in the heart of Chinatown. Lots of high rise office buildings so there are loads of people.Give it a try.

Went here for dinner with a large group and had one of the private rooms in the back. I thought the food was very good and the service very attentive. I especially liked the roast suckling pig. Even with a large group, the food was served in a timely am fashion and every dish was hot when it got to us. The steamed fish was also very very tasty. I would certainly go back. The meal was reasonable priced as well.

really, really surprisingly good chinese food at this dodgy-looking, super old-school restaurant in chinatown. the place definitely seems to have had better days - the exterior is just as worn and outdated as the interior, the servers are cantankerous and grouchy, but the food - the food is good.and - I meant surprising in the sense that I didn't actually expect the food to be good, with expectations further tempered when I saw the restaurant, and it all turned out to be decent - with some dishes actually much better than average (objectively, all other things aside).let's talk about the restaurant first - the unimposing entrance to the place completely belies the hugeness of the dining area. we're talking old-school, banquet-able (in the region of 20-30 tables, possibly more?), with a huge stage in the middle and private rooms surrounding the side. it looks like it would have been impressive in its heyday, but the furnishings are now pretty worn out, and the staff looking nearly as tired as their surroundings.but thankfully, the food completely outshines all these (not that it's terribly difficult to do so). there are some proper cooks in the kitchen that churn out proper cantonese/ teochew food, most of it arriving at decent intervals.the duck: skin was well-browned and crisp with the fat well-rendered away, and the meat was succulent (even if the duck was slightly on the skinny side). a pretty good start.the mainstream sauteed dishes were also pretty decent - silky mushrooms with greens, and pork cubes in a sweet-savory sauce. the latter was a tad fatty - but that's how the old folkies like it, and that's almost definitely their target demographic.the seafood dishes were better, like our steamed prawns or a DELICIOUS steamed fish? we finished with stir-fried noodles (not many ingredients apart from veg and noodles, but it wasn't oily, and was properly dry-fried) and a dish of mashed yam (orh nee). the first arrived when we were rather too full to appreciate it properly, but the latter went down in spite of the too fullness (my dad had seconds, rather impressively).

Excellent place for dim sum and other local delicacies. The fried chicken feet were a little strange for my taste but my Singaporean friends loved them. Place crammed for lunch Large choice and good value for money.
not good mexican food.  soggy chips, bland flavor.

As far as service goes it's consistently some of the best I've found in Singapore. The food is always good, maybe not amazing but but I've always been greeted with a smile, received my food quickly and been checked on to make sure things were to my liking. The waiters are always friendly and the prices aren't bad for the location. If you're looking for a solid laid back Mexican place, this is a great option. Ask for Jessy, she's the best!!

Bottomless chips and salsa, no extra charges (ie wet napkins and nuts you don't necessarily want), relatively fast service, and the ability to split a check are pretty clear indicators this is in fact owned/operated by Americans. So all of the aforementioned made the dining experience quite nice.As far as the food goes it's all pretty OKAY. I tried the shredded beef burrito, red snapper burrito, quesadillas, nachos, and churros. Everything was a pretty good rendition of what I'm used to back home in Texas, but nothing really could compare to even middle of the road tex-mex places. However based upon the standard of Mexican food in Singapore, it's not bad. The drinks were pretty weak though, I could barely taste the tequila.This restaurant is really over priced though. Expect to spend around $30-45 a head for just an entree and not much more. Overall I wouldn't mind going again, but the pricing and food isn't overall good enough to make this a regular spot for me.

It's not easy to find good Mexican food in Singapore, especially at a wallet-friendly price. Sadly, this place doesn't come cheap either but the food is not too bad. At night the place is crowded with chatter and an alfresco dining concept. I had the chicken chimichanga which is sort of like a fried burrito, which was not bad, but nothing to shout about. Portions are huge, so bringing an appetite is a must. Overall I might come back here again for a Mexican fix, but only because there's not many other good Mexican places.

I don't know my drinks very well so this review will be more about the food and atmosphere. You can definitely tell it is a Mexican restaurant as soon as you step close to the greeter podium - the Latin music that gets your feet doing a little dance and the Mother of Mary statue standing tall just behind the cashier. The menu is pretty typical Mexican food - burritos, fajitas and they have free flow of chips and salsa! Gotta love that chips and salsa since that is pretty rare to come across in Singapore. I ordered a plate of green chili stew. My first impression - is this what we ordered? If you are used to the more traditional green chili stew, this dish will not live up to your expectations. It DOES NOT look or taste anything like green chili stew AT ALL. BUT, I do have to give them a thumbs up for that dish because it was a pretty flavorful stew. It tasted more like a meat and potato stew with Mexican spices. The stew came with salted steamed black beans and Spanish rice. They also served it with a side of two tortilla. I would definitely get this dish again on my next visit. You just have to not expect the traditional way here. Go adventure!

Have always been a fan of this place. I first came here like 3-4 years ago-ish and fell in love with it then. There weren't seats by the riverside then. But it was (and still is) very festive and authentic. Plus, I didn't know of any other Mexican restaurants in Singapore - so it was quite the routine - to go there and have a jug of margaritas (to share, or, er... not) and Mexican fare.What I Love: They have great drinks. Their margarita flavors are pretty cool. A jug is $57 from 8-11pm. But if you get one after, it's like $39 or something? Which is quite a deal actually. I like that they have half-price and Post Happy Hour prices. They have a pretty cool comprehensive menu detailing their Half-Price discounts. I LOVE their menu - its comprehensive, easy to read and clear. Their drinks and tequila menu is pretty great too. Have tried their Quesadillas, Fajitas, Tortillas, and other stuff that's pretty darn good. Try and explore the menu!What I Don't Love: Their prices. Can get pretty steep. Good to share.

Might have taken a munch or two out of my friend's food but I don't recall ordering my own. Their food - Don't think its as good as Chipotle, one can only pray that they will move to Singapore, or Margaritas @Dempsey but definitely better than Tacco Bell... but this place is great for drink and chips (free flow). I would recommend 1. Margaritas (might be bias towards this)2. Chips & SalsaTips: Happy hour! 1. Before 8pm, drinks are priced cheaper. 2. After 11 pm drinks are 30 - 40% off. The place can get super crowded on the weekends and they use to not take reservations but now I see a widget for it so maybe they finally have decided to embrace technology! hurray!

As good a Mexican as you can get in Singapore. Iguana is consistent and of good quality, not cheap but they don't have a service charge. We are multiple repeat customers. Had to post a positive comment after two negative ones today on other Mexican restaurants here.

Had dinner with 8 ppl last night, it was sunday nite, thiught it'd empty, but i was wrong. Had to wait 25 mins coz its full! But the food here always good, big portion too. Margharita was nice too. Fajitas was nice, chimichangga was big and good! Great place to spend easy dinner with ur mates!

I've been coming here for years since the days when we had a fairly boring F&B scene and the Brewerkz/Iguana combo was magical and new.I still come here from time to time when I want straight up decent margaritas or other poison spiked with lots of tequila, and snacky food. I no longer come here as much because there are now better places to drink at, and also because it's gotten so popular with tourists it's hard to get a place unless you come very early.Still an oldie but goodie, though.

Cafe Iguana is run by the same folks at Brewerkz, but their specialty over here is Margaritas rather than beer. Their house margaritas pack quite a punch, and you can get them frozen or on the rocks, and there really isn't anything better than sharing a huge glass (really, too much for one person) of frozen margarita with your friends on a balmy night.The food menu here is Mexican, haven't really had the chance to try it, but like Brewerkz, this place also gets crowded on the weeknights.

I have been visiting Café Iguana for several years and it is probably the best Mexican you can get in Singapore. The food quality is consistently delicious, and the margaritas have never failed on me. I especially enjoy the steak chimichangas and order them every time I'm there. Unfortunately, this establishment is a little on the pricey side but the service is good with friendly and efficient staff so I don't quite mind at all.

Chips and salsa are served at your table. The salsa has a nice fresh, salty flavor, similar to what's served at Chili's restaurants. The chips are thin and crispy. We ordered the pork green chile with rice and beans to share. The dish that came out did not at all resemble green chile, instead appearing red with a thick, milky consistency. I'm not sure if we got the wrong thing or if they don't have the same impression of what pork green chile is. Nevertheless, we were quite pleased by the spices and hearty flavor of the dish. The side tortillas made nice for wrapping up black beans, rice, and the chile together. The black beans were standard without any special sauce or seasoning. The rice was no longer white, but still very bland in flavor, as is customary in many Mexican restaurants. Overall, the chile was quite good. Along with the chips and sides, this made for a good light two-person lunch. Note that this place has differential margarita pricing throughout the day, so it pays to start first thing in the morning and pass out shortly after noon.

Don't mind me, I'm only here for the guacCafe Iguana's a really fun place to hang out in big groups--you can get a margarita for yourself, or you can get one of those ginormous ones to share (I'd always wanted one, but eww, disease vector). The salsa and guacamole and chips flow, and so does the conversastion, deep into the night...

Nice mexican Restaurant in Clarke Quay and a serendipitous discovery. I had some really good Fajitas with chicken. If you arrive early enough, try a jug of Margarita with one of the three different flavours, strawberry, lime or ... I think I forgot the last one. Anyways, a really nice venue at the Singapore river.

I'm a Texan and the food itself at Cafe Iguana is somewhere between okay and pretty good -- but by Singapore standards, it's amazing. It was so comforting to have proper tortillas, chips and salsa, guacamole, margaritas (which get outrageously expensive the later they're ordered), cold water, fork and knife, and cloth napkins. Get the jug of margarita for two people; the glasses are tiny and they are a bit weak.

This place is one of my favourite places to get margaritas in Singapore. I'm not really a fan of Mexican food so I've never really eaten much but their margaritas by the jug are really something you cannot miss when you come here. My friends swear by the Kiwi, Lime and Pink Guava. If you want beer, they do have some selections but you're better off hopping over to Brewerkz just a few doors down (and owned by the same company)

I always get the Borracho Bean Dip here. All of the things I want (rice, beans, cheese, guacamole, pico, veggies, sour cream) in my burrito or taco or whatever without actually having any outer holder like that. Which is too bad, but it works out to be the most economical item on the menu for me, price- and food-wise. You won't find all of those items together in any other app or entree on the menu. Service is also uncommonly pleasant, prompt and mistake-free on a normal evening.

We have been on the hunt for some good Mexican food in Singapore for a while - this place is the best yet.  Freshly fried tortilla chips, fresh salsa, and well-seasoned meats make the food here authentic tasting and delicious.  The staff was super friendly and got us a free salsa and chips after watching our 3-year old mow through the first batch.  Prices are pretty standard for this area of town - more expensive than in a lot of other places in Singapore.  Only complaint was they forgot her order, or maybe we didn't order it clearly enough.  It's outside, so keep that in mind - there's no AC.  The smoking section is also right next to the nonsmoking section...

Happy hour at Cafe Iguana ($40 for a jug of magaritas before 7pm or after 10pm). Waiting for my buddies to arrive, I managed to instagram the moment. Brings us back to our JC days n years ago Pricing of food was rather expensive between 25-40SGD (how did we afford it back then??). Food was so so. Yay:Chips and salsa - free and delicious Guacamole side - quite yums and flavorful Calamari: nicely fried, awesome sauce Quesadilla with chicken $21 - I love melted cheese! Decent fish, nothing wow or meh about it NahChimichangas - dough quite thick, so so stuffing, too much sour cream Pork carnitas tacos - not the pulled pork I expected, but still yummy pork chunks. Taco skin was a fail. 2 out of 3 skins were abandoned Nachos $20 - overloaded with ingredients, must be shared by 4 or more otherwise wont be finished, chips were very thick unlike the free bowl which was nicer and crispier If I will be back it'll be for the happy hour original/peach magaritas (which was beyond sad after it melted in an hour) and the one tiny bowl of chips and salsa. Nice chill out atmosphere along Singapore River at Riverside Point. Don't expect much from service - very crowded so just keep waving to get attention. #happyhour #mexicanfoodinSGismeh #chipsandsalsa #JCfriends #peachmagaritas #drklingeats

Walked by this place from my hotel. Was very conveniently located. And the outside seating was excellent. The evening view of the riverside bridges and buildings made it a very tranquil environment.I ordered the Mini Chimichanga made with chicken as an appetizer. And for the main course I ordered the chicken fajitas. Everything was served timely and hot. The ingredients were fresh & tasty. I tried three different margaritas. Remand they have so many more selections of them.  Premium margarita was great and cooling.Tried their Patron margaritas with raspberry and the last one was Pink guava. The price was very reasonable. And from 10pm till closing the margaritas are half off their house selection. Can't wait to come here again. Very satisfied and happy!!!!!!

With a good selection of Mexican special cocktails and Margaritas, it is not surprising to see that business is booming even on a Tuesday night. The Red Snapper Burritos ($25) made a stunning entrance like a curvy oblong-shaped parcel, only to reveal a luscious interior of fish, borraco beans, Mexican rice and strands of Mozzarella-cheddar melting mid-way. This could be a potentially great dish if the snapper was not too dry. Puerco en Chile Verde ($14) sounded exotic but it striked a nostalgic chord even if you had not experience any Mexican life before. There isn't so much firepower in this spicy pork stew. But being thick and warm, it goes ideally with the toasted tortillas or simply a direct fast track into your mouth. How does having some tequila in your seafood sounds? The Prawn Brochette ($35) is a skewer of roughly 5-6 lime marinated prawns with smoky tequila glaze, served with grilled vegetables on a stick. It has a heady aroma, though the glaze was short of the wild character of liquor. Nonetheless, the Tequila glaze was an instant hit with the 1/2 Chicken ($28) as the toasty caramelized taste emerged from the skin which retained the moisture of the meat.  The standout dish was the Shredded Steak Chimchangas ($25), a golden crispy flour tortilla that is deep-fried to perfection such that it kept the juicy strands of beef warm and comfortable while displaying resilience any sogginess. Drenched in generous amount of sour cream and guacamole, this giant plate of meaty "Popiah" roll is messy but speaks right to your soul. I don't fancy banana desserts but I may have to take back my statement on the Banana Chimichangas ($14) here. Just like the earlier savoury chimichanga, the filling is substituted with bananas, deep fried till the shell turned into a crunchy fritter. Wallop a huge scoop of fragrant and buttery avocado ice cream and you'll get something that is ten times better than any chocolate lava cake or any hot-cold dessert. There is also the Sauteed Kahlua-glazed Bananas ($14) for those who are less keen on deep-fried food. This ain't no flouncy haute style ala minute flambé bananas but a rustic tropical dessert that sits on a rich and decadent sauce. Other selections include a gluten-free Ancho Chile Chocolate Cake ($14) and Churros ($12) but the former two banana desserts are more satisfying for the bucks and calories.Spice-wise, the dishes are tuned to a temperate palette, yet there were moments during the feast when I thought I was eating Indian briyani. No wonder they say that Indian and Mexican cuisine are actually quite similar! In fact, I was told that about 50% of the customers are Indians. Well, there are three different kinds of authentic Mexican hot sauces aplenty of the table for you to adjust the heat to your preference. Both indoors and outdoors seating are non-air-conditioned but I highly recommend the indoors seating if you want to enjoy the food heartily away from any outdoor smoking.

Touristy spot serving barely edible tex-mex.I liked the riverside atmosphere and funky decor - brightly colored paint and images of Frida Kahlo plastered on the wall. However the food really really let me down.I'm convinced that the guy in the kitchen has never had a real burrito in his life. What came out was a dry, chewy flour-filled abomination that barely resembled one. The enchiladas were not much better. They arrived slathered in cheese, but the taste was barely registering on my tongue. I was left clutching the bottle of habanero sauce attempting to add some zing to what was left sitting on my plate.Maybe my expectations are elevated cos of the years living in CA, visiting the local taco stand, and crossing the border into TJ.I'm wondering how this place gets 4 stars... Maybe it's the margaritas talking.

This trip was my second to Cafe Iguana and my first for dinner. Obviously I thought the first stop warranted a return. The food is pretty darn good, the service is as good (even on a Friday night) and the location and ambiance are first rate - no question the location makes the experience even better. We started with the chips and salsa, ordered some guacamole and had the chimichangas - all were served promptly and the chimichangas (beef) were tasty. I had the chicken fajitas (which arrived sizzling hot and with ample veggies and salsa, guava and sour cream) and my Wife had the beef burrito. All of which were really good (and portions excellent). We had the little ones with us and the staff was also pretty fun with them as well. I'll go back! It's a fun place to spend an evening and you can leave satisfied with your meal!

New menu and none the better. The margaritas are still fantastic and the setting on the Singapore River is lovely, but the food is in steady decline.  We ate on a very quiet Sunday evening. Jumbo, the restaurant next to Cafe Iguana, was packed, but we were one of only a few active tables at Cafe Iguana.The meal started with flavorless and exceptionally cold (a theme for the meal) salsa. The refrigerated salsa tasted like pureed tomatoes with little added to that. Tortilla chips without any salt or flavoring at all on them and the free appetizer seems designed to keep people from wanting seconds.I had the shrimp burrito with the oddly named carne de puerco en chile verde. On the positive side, the pork green chili stew was the best thing on the table all night. Genuinely delicious albeit oddly named as there was absolutely nothing green about it. Very standard reddish brown chili/stew color without any visible green capsicum or anything green.  Sadly, the burrito itself was a huge disappointment... very few shrimp (but those that were there tasted pretty good) mixed with isolated clumps of different ingredients (i.e., so you get several servings of nothing but beans, followed by one serving of nothing but shrimp, etc.) on a tortilla that was mostly raw and topped (after "cooking") with raw (unmelted) cheese (see photo).The kids had the mini tostadas and a quesadilla.  Both were mostly left on the plate.The taco salad did little to resemble a taco or its typical ingredients. Essentially a load of plain lettuce sitting on a pancake flat raw tortilla with a dab of sour creme hidden under the tortilla that my wife didn't even find until after she stopped eating. Only about a third of the salad was eaten.  Finally, service was painfully slow and we had to ask four times to get someone to bring a glass of water. What used to be an almost iconic Mexican restaurant in Singapore has matured into a tired and uninspired disappointment.
My wife and I eat here all the time, its consistently good. The fajitas are my personal fav. This with a few IPA and its a great way to spend Sunday afternoon.
An easy option if you're seeking Mexican food and Margaritas in the Clarke Quay area. Persistently great atmosphere on evenings. Get there before 7pm to enjoy discounted Marg pitchers!

I'll just reiterate what others have said: get a few friends and get the giant jug of magarita! It's signature tequila cocktails are also worth a try. It's a great place for either after dinner drinks, or drinks before you hit the rest of the night scenes.If you're more of a beer person, like I am, there are also some beer to choose from.I can't think of anywhere else in Singapore where you can get a Mexican menu as comprehensive as this. Quesadillas, fajitas, tortillas etc. are all aplenty. I also like the grilled prawns on the hotplate thing.The atmosphere of the restaurant is great, and the decor unique. I like that the music isn't too loud so that conversation can flow easily. Definitely a great place to hang out.

Was so intrigued by the Makgeoli, had to come back a second time, but this time sans the coworker who only liked beer. Had the normal Makgeoli small bottle. It has a stronger kick of alcohol than normal. Was very tasty. Didn't try the standard Makgeoli out of their beer tap, the waitress mentioned it wasn't as strong and was lighter.I've tried the Army Stew, raboki, kimchee Prawn pasta, and bossam. All were good hits to the palate. Bossam - the pork was on the fatty side, but was nicely braised. The cabbage had a unique lemon flavor. The dikon kimchee had nicely grilled garlic that I enjoyed. Definitely a winner dish.Army Stew - spicy stew with sausage, noodles, green onions and other yummy ingredients. I'm used to seeing spam as well though it seemed to be missing. Good and tasty dish.Raboki - a traditional drinking accompaniment (anju). Tubes of rice cake with fishcake tempura in a spicy red sauce is the duk bokki  and you add the Ramen noodles to make it a rraboki. Ramen + duk bokki = raboki. Kimchee Prawn Pasta - really enjoyed the Korean twist to the traditional Prawn pasta dish. Good Korean bar with tasty anju. Liked the Makgeoli theme and the place is pretty chill. Seems you need reservations to be seated on the 2nd floor.

I've been here twice, mainly for their yummy frozen makgeolli drinks. The food here is alright, but probably not my first pick for Korean food. There are many other Korean restaurants I would prefer although it's kind of hard to beat a location like this, with the right combination of finger foods and great drinks.They have more than a dozen (if my memory serves) types of makgeolli in all kinds of flavors - from passionfruit to strawberry. There's a sampler but you can also get them in jugs to share. One evening, we popped by before closing and managed to get a table in the packed restaurant. We were led to a table upstairs where it was much more quiet and thus great for having a chat over drinks. They had every flavor available so we chose yuzu and passionfruit.I would definitely recommend the passionfruit - it was sweet and sour, and full of fresh delicious flavor, and you could see all the little seeds in there so you know it's made with fresh passionfruit. The yuzu was a little on the subtle side, I think I'm used to that delicious fragrant kick you get from yuzu tea so I had high hopes that were slightly deflated. It was super refreshing regardless and a good crowd-pleaser.I took away one star for slow service and relatively boring food options. Quite nice for drinks though!

This is a quaint little modern Korean place. I popped by with a bibulous friend on a weeknight and had chicken wings, the makgeolli sampler, and regular makgeolli to wash everything down.Oh my. They have good wings here, and I'm not even a wings kinda gal. Juicy, crispy, with garlic bits on it, you will not regret ordering em here.I particularly enjoyed the makgeolli sampler, though I cannot for the life of me remember the flavors. If you have a girlfriend or a date, she will most certainly enjoy the sampler; doubles up as a dessert for someone with a sweet tooth!Did not try dinner items as we came here post-dinner.

i want nobody, nobody but joo!i want nobody, nobody but joo!nan dareun sarameun sirheo niga animyeon sirheo!   i want nobody, nobody, nobody, nobody!joo marries two of my favourite things from korea.makgeolli(fermented rice alcoholic beverage) and budae jjigae(army stew)!!!there is no shortage of korean restaurants in SG.tanjong pagar and chinatown are full of them.but joo has that little something special.a sexy, charismatic aura that draws me in.there are no rough edges here.everything is smooth and suave.from the decor to the staff.the food and beverage is thoughtfully created mostly from scratch and you can taste the quality.the simple banchan they served me, was simply polished off.they are not mere fillers but side dishes that whets your appetite and enhances the overall dining experience!from the sweet, spicy and sour radish, to the soft and creamy macaroni egg salad, to the crispy fried tiny fish, you can taste the love that goes into it!budae jjigae!what can i say!best eaten in the cold harsh winters of korea!a very humble army stew that comprises hot dog, spam and ham mixed with gochujang and kimchi plus instant ramen!they get the ratio just right here!the consistency, heat and spice will light up a winter's night!and it's a single serve portion, unlike many other places where you need to share with 2 or more people.makgeolli!since my seoul mate introduced me to this drink at a specialty makgeolli bar, i have never looked back.no soju, just makgeolli for me, please!just like i have a fetish for cloudy apple juice and cloudy sancerre, i have to have makgeolli!here it is home brewed, organic, made fresh daily, no aspartame.so expect the original version to be slightly sour instead of sweet.but they do have sweet versions with fruits, if that floats your boat.i would recommend the yucha slush makgeolli.you will hardly notice that you are drinking an alcoholic beverage.the baby eel paper, thin sheets of small eel pressed and deep fried are mas-issneun!best accompanied with alcohol!then there's their secret weapon!homemade thin cut crisps, always sliced and fried fresh daily!no overnighters allowed!so if you come late at night before closing and sit at the bar, they will all be yours to eat, for FREE!:)i want nobody, nobody but joo!i want nobody, nobody but joo!how can i be with another, i don't want any other!i want nobody, nobody, nobody, nobody!

This newly-discovered place by me is my current go-to place to indulge in chill K tunes, drink makgeolli and dine on fusion Korean food that is oh-so-yummy.Verdict:- Makgeolli Sampler Set - Good to try this on your first visit to get a taste of the different flavoured Makgeolli. If you're a Makgeolli veteran, I suggest that you skip this. The portion is small  (of course, it's just a sampler) but looks great for pics. There are 5 in the set - Original, Yuzu, Lychee, Peach and Strawberry and my personal preference is in the order listed.- Yuzu Makgeolli (large size) - Very refreshing and one of my favourites. The large size is good to share among 2 ladies.- Braised pork belly - Per serving comes with a few slices. Honestly, this dish had a chef recommended symbol on the menu but the pork slices were quite tough and chewy. Not something I would order again.- Home-made Tapioca chips - Yums! Goes great with  Makgeolli with two dips given.- Gangnam Dreaming cocktail - Had a 7up initial taste but faded to a bittersweet berry aftertaste.- Insadong memories - One of the best cocktails I've tasted during my trips to Joo Bar. Refreshing, sweet and had a great cinnamon ginger taste. Double like!Been here 4 times within the past 2 months and will keep coming back for more mod Korean food!Tip: Sit near the bar if you're not here for dinner as it is pretty interesting chatting with the bespectacled bartender Eddy, and see how he mix the drinks for you. Also, you tend to get a bucket of FOC chips if you're sitting at the bar compared to ordering drinks at the usual table.

You got a tree in your backyard growing money for you and you LOVE  (Korean rice wine) as much as I do, this is your place.I laughed at the idea that they had  in draft.  But it was yum to the me. bo ssam was delicious and the use of citron is quite brilliant.  Pork belly was delicious.Three stars for such an arrogant pricing and failing to win me over with portion.On a side note, where the hell are these young kids making money?  Or are they just spending the hard-earned money so foolishly on some creative cocktail using makkuli??

Very impressed on my first visit here. That dark interior with white washed walls gives Joo Bar a cozy and chill feel. The food would entice any korean food fans. I particularly like the Joo Bossam and the minced beef. Try the set of  makegolli of 5 @ $35. Good for a gathering of friends on a weekday night.full review on my blog.

We had curry chicken and seafood pasta on a cold weather. The curry is thick and the flavour is strong but it does feel very filling after a while. The food is good but the price is a little on the higher side. It'd probably more worth it to have tea here at $15 per pax as their cakes and pastries look so appetizing and beautiful.

I was on one of my regular trips to Gardens by the Bay. Yes, I love heading to the gardens for a nice stroll. This morning I was kind of hungry so I thought I could drop by at the Bakerzin located near the ticketing office.Originally I just wanted maybe a croissant and a hot beverage. Then the staff gave me a full menu. When I saw they have Fish n Chips, I did not think twice and decided to have a heavier lunch. I always love a good plate of Fish n Chips; unfortunately the best I ever tasted was still the one in London. I have also ordered a hot chocolate, I know Fish N Chips does not really go with hot chocolate, but who cares? Lol!!The order of hot chocolate came first. It was not too bad. Hot chocolate usually makes me happy. A good one of cos. Soon the Beer Battered Classic Fish N Chips arrived at the table. The portion was a little too big for me but trust that I would not have a problem if it turned out to be good.First bite - hmmm.. what kind of fish was that? Definitely not cod. It was kind of oily. I took a look at the picture I took off the menu, leather jacket fillet? What was that? If this is a Classic Fish N Chips, I want my regular tartar sauce & vinegar. The tartar sauce looked like cocktail sauce. Turned out it was Asian tartar sauce. Huh? Ok my bad, I did not look at the description of the Fish N Chips before I ordered it. So zero star for the Fish N Chips. Ambience was alright. I wish it was a lot quieter. I had been wondering which customers were talking that loudly. Turned out it was the staffs who were chatting and talking so loudly as if they were just next to me :O Service received was great - 4 stars but I had to deduct 2 for the noise they generated. It was not a pleasant experience to constantly hearing the staffs talking so loudly. Mind you, I was sitting all the way inside and tucked in one corner.

Slow service, small portions, average pricey food and drinks. My 2nd visit after more than a year. This is the nearest causal eatery after you spend hour(s) walking through the Flower/Cloud Dome. So in a way, beggars can't be choosers.My family just done the Cloud Dome and wanted a quick break before heading for the Flower Dome.We seated ourselves at the outdoor seating as no one was mending the outdoor area at that time. Shortly, the staff just came by and dropped off the menu without saying a word. My sis had to walk into the cafe to have a staff come over to take our orders. We ordered a long black, cappuccino, root beer and a plate of potato wedges. The coffee were average and wedges were slightly above average but portion was really tiny for the $8.90 price! Likewise we had to walk into the cafe to request for the bill. Overall, it's a little overpriced cafe with a nice ambience. It's lovely to sit outdoors but be warned that service will be slow and almost nonexistent.

I came here to hide out from the relentless rain. It seemed like almost everyone had the same idea. It was fairly crowded with few empty tables and seats. It took a while before a server noticed the line of people waiting to be seated.I chose a counter seat outside which overlooked the gardens or shrubbery since I just wanted a drink. Again, it took some time for my drink to arrive and also to get the bill. Service was just slow. The place itself was pretty nice. A good place to just chill with a book and drink and dessert. It is definitely not a place to grab a quick bite or where you want attentive service. Yelp Feb 2014 Challenge: 7/28

The tables were tiny and imbalance.People gets "wet" at this place quickly. The man that splash his ice tea over his friend and we splashed ice chocolate over ourselves. Here at this place, they serve room temperature food with a cold face. There is no facial expressions on any of them.--+The only thing that is edible at this place is baked sausage. Bratwurst sausage is not overly salted, sauteed potato and the mushrooms looks awful together,  but it tasted way better than it looks. --- Mushroom soup looks like a bit bowl of snot, it tasted over salted and it didn't have much aroma of mushroom.  --- Bratwurst linguini looks gross when it came. It looked like hot  dark chocolate sauce over the linguini.   Balsamic vinegar was over powering the soggy linguine. Gross. +++Iced mango passion float in sprite is refreshing and nice. It wasn't special, but at least, it wasn't gross. --- Iced chocolate was overly sweetened. Save your money and go somewhere else.

The only thing I could find in Gardens by the Bay that wasn't too far away and of a decent price range. I'd been to Bakerzin at Suntec before and had a pretty good experience there, so I thought this would be fine. I ordered the Aglio Olio for $13, which was a decent price considering where we were. The service, however, was absolutely awful. The manager came round about 10 minutes after I'd ordered and slammed a creamy mushroom pasta in front of me (he really did slam it onto the table) and barked, "your pasta." and walked off. I had to spend the next few minutes trying to catch the attention of one of the staff to tell them that this wasn't what I'd ordered. And then manager came, took it away, and only after I said, "Erm, 'scuse me?" did he turn around and say,. "Oh, sorry." I was really annoyed because obviously his mistake has nothing to do with me. II hope it was just a bad day. The pasta, when the right one arrived, was pretty bland and hardly like how an Aglio Olio should be, although that's a mistake many Singaporean restaurants make. Disappointing, especially when I was looking forward to good service and got the exact opposite. From the manager! tsk.

Upscale Italian place on Club Street. The food is consistently good across the board but not spectacular. Specific details based on our order below:- Bread basket - ok / standard good. What you would expect from this type of restaurant- Burrata - Ok - good quality of burrata cheese though I definitely have had better -creamier, fresher than this one elsewhere in Singapore. The accompanying parma ham and veggie are good though- Shrimp starter - good but nothing outstanding - high quality shrimp - grilled well - served on an eggplant puree with zucchini- 1M Pappardelle with Ragu - one of their signature dishes. Ok. The pasta is al dente and the meter long is appetizing. However, the Ragu is lacking / underwhelming and the sauce does not fully come together with the pasta- Spaghetti with lobster in tomato sauce - also ok. The dish is very tomato-y. While the tomato is fresh and tasty, it overpowered the entire dish. I wish there was a better balance with the diff ingredients- Seabass - cooked very well. Perfectly crispy skin and the right texture on the fish. - Tiramisu - ok / standard goodService is a mixed bag - some ppl are nicer / more attentive than others.

I was taken here on a Saturday night, and we didn't sit in the open-air courtyard, but instead in the ACed interior, which was tastefully decorated. We were seated at a round table which was a bit awkward for two people. The friendly Sicilian sommelier recommended a great white for us to go with our meal. For starters, we got the prawns and the burrata, which was a bit of a happy mistake for me. The burrata came with 8 slices of ham, rocket, and cherry tomatoes while my companion only got 2 prawns! Needless to say I needed some help to finish my burrata. Perhaps it should have been shared between 2 people. The prawns were large and crunchy, very delicious, while the burrata was good, but not as soft as I'd like. My companion was very hungry and suggested we share a pasta, the Pappardelle Xxlong, with wild boar ragout. I wasn't too sure about the choice, but it sounded fun - a meter-long pappardelle... sure. They had split the portion for us to share, so I had a 0.5m long pappardelle instead. I wasn't expecting it, but I was completely blown away when I bit into the pasta. It was perfectly cooked, with enough bite, and not at all mushy, with just the right thickness. The ragout was good and the boar/pork was soft, but I could have eaten the pasta in any other sauce and finished it. I would definitely come back just for this dish. We both got the lamb rack each for our mains, and it came with carrot purée and a rosemary garlic crumble which I really enjoyed. The lamb was cooked exactly the way I wanted - medium rare. What I found strange about this main, was that my companion's lamb had 4 ribs in total, while mine had 6! I swapped out 3 ribs for 2, so we would have an equal amount of meat. It was funny how the entire night I kept having a gargantuan portion relative to my companion's. I finished the meal with the chocolate explosion, which the waitstaff kindly handed me the dessert menu before I finished my main. The chocolate explosion required 15 mins wait, which was good timing. It turned out to be a chocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream and berries. The interior of the lava cake was flowy and molten. Absolutely delicious with the ice cream, which presumably was of decent quality, with no pesky ice crystals' crunching.Would I return? Yes! And have the pappardelle all to myself.

Senso used to be one of the better Italian eateries in Singapore when it first opened. Now, there are at least a dozen restaurants where the food is better, more creative, or both. Yet, prices are at the same level as the best in town. Service is competent, but old-fashioned and not pro-active. Sure, the patio is nice and the ambience pleasant, but I'd rather have the better food at Braci, Osteria Arte, Garibaldi, etc.

This is really nice. Location is very central and in the heart of hip Club Street. Set in a conservation shophouse, the front houses a bar where you can have drinks and there is a good wine list. In the heart is a courtyard for alfresco dining but for our party we had the private dining space in air conditioned comfort. Service here is excellent and the food as expected to be delicious. I chose scallops for my starter which was fantastic and the lamb rack which was beautifully done to mediumness. While I've had better panna cotta elsewhere, it was still good here and as it was my birthday, the restaurant arranged a special treat of their  tiramisu.

The restaurant is pretty and nicely decorated. It is a good place for a date or other special events. The Italian food is superb! I would recommend a few including lamb ribs, squid ink pasta and tiramisu. Service is great, you will be well served after entering the restaurant.

Well, that didn't take long. Returned the next day, exceptional hare and pumpkin risotto. My Italian lunching partner loved his fresh pasta. Another member of staff spoke French (is this place French run?).Still 5* to me. Still my go to lunch spot in Telok Ayer.

Had a birthday party here. Nice wines good desserts. Good service in a more colonial setting. Courtyard garden. We had fish, beef in thick brown sauce and tasty italian breads. Our host had the tables full and we had the whole restaurant to ourselves.

This place is nice.Like, really nice.A comfortable, impeccable service kind of nice.A step inside and immediately find a secret courtyard in the city kind of nice.A pleasantly dim and dark interior dining room kind of nice.It's so nice that it kind of all just evens out. My tagliatelle was so perfect it got kind of bland. That sounds bad. What I mean is, because of the price and environment, your expectations are hitting a whole new level and I'm not sure Senso reaches them. I think that's what the other reviewers are getting at. If you want a wonderfully executed modern Italian lunch, then by all means come here. If you're iffy about spending $40 on it, I can't promise you'll feel like it was worth it.

Review for the Sunday prosecco brunch. Really nice experience for a weekend getaway from the kids. Service is stellar. The buffet spread is decent with some high points (chilled shrimp, different cheeses and nice little shot glasses of soup) and a few misses (no omelette bar and not such a great selection of oysters), but the made-to-order small plate menu earns the fifth star. You will be hard pressed to find a better deal in Singapore for the price. You can dine inside, which has chilly AC or al fresco in the courtyard. Senso also takes part in the entertainer program.

A very pretty restaurant with some great Italian food!Everything we ordered was very tasty and the service seemed to be very good, although got very spotty as the restaurant became busy with big groups.They were kind enough to give me a pillow for my back so I am more comfortable and the food was very tasty, although definitely on the pricier side.

Two sad-looking seared scallops plopped into an under-seasoned cream soup, lumpy polenta in a sauce that had separated, strange "fruit minestrone" and acrid olive oil. Service was good, however, I was offered tea three or four times and the mignardises zero times. I guess they forgot.

Went here for a business lunch. Fancy interior, nice service and pretty good value for executive lunch ($40S three courses and coffee with chocolates at the end).The quality of food was so-so, bordering on mediocre. I had a veal carpaccio which was bad, smothered with rather odd liver-tasting sauce, lamb cutlets for main which was competent and a 'minestrone of berries' which was berries in sugary liquid, not so good. Chocolates and coffee at end was pleasant but the coffee was drip, no offer for espresso or with milk.Its not a great place, but passable for a quick business lunch. Dinner is much more expensive and. given the quality, not worth it.

After looking at furniture for about an hour, decided to have lunch at the Ikea restaurant. It was near to 2pm, and there was still a queue extending back pass the drinks & coffee island. But luckily the queue moved fast.We ordered the 2 must do - the meatballs and the fried chicken wings. Additionally, we ordered the fish& chips and the confit of duck. We also had the Swedish fruit flavour drinks.The meatballs goes well with the sauce and cranberry sauce. There were lots of meatballs with a good amount of boiled potatoes.The duck was also good and it came with boiled potatoes and steamed vegetables (carrots). The duck meat was tender and goes well with the given sauce. it was tasty. You get an entire duck drumstick. The chicken wings was crispy and moist. It was marinated very well and was tasty. It was very good.The worst dish was fish and chips. It mediocre and basic. You get a breaded fish with chips. It came with the normal tartar sauce. The fried part of the fish was crispy but overall it was rather cold probably it was dished on the plate out of the heating lamp waiting for some poor customer to take it.The Swedish fruity drink was refreshing as it was very fizzy. Unfortunately Ikea does not provide ice at this location. So the cold drink quickly became room temperature while you dig in to the main course. It was very refreshing and cool when you first got it from the dispenser. It seems that all drinks are refillable
Cheap eats in a nice setting minus the crowdWhat more can we ask for when the feet is tired and the kids are grouchy. Food and drinks.If the food is good and better when is cheap. Heavenly.

My family loves IKEA Alexandra and it's restaurant. We just do. Many complain but we're still fans. They have a new dish on the menu and it's Pork Ribs with Fries. Well, the ribs are a generous slab of about 5 ribs. Tasty wise is ok but a tad too dry. It's without sauce so the overall pretty dry. The other dishes are well covered so I won't add on. I'll be back definitely!

Hard to fault this place. Cheap food. Quick service. Amongst the best chicken wings in Singapore and you'll be able to get some furniture shopping in after you're done eating as well. Most of the dishes worth having are "Western" but the curry is among the best that you can get in a fast food-ish place. Free flow soft drinks for a dollar as well as free baby food. Can't deny that my wife and I are just in love with IKEA.
My friends and I love going to IKEA, not for any furniture, just for dinner. We like the meatballs and the smoky salmon:)

A great place for a casual meal of comfort foods and snacks! The foods here are affordable but you do everything yourself, from queueing up, to getting your food, all the way to clearing your own table, but for the affordable prices they offer, you can't really complain. It is also children friendly, with a special corner allocated for families with children, complete with baby chairs and toys to entertain them while the parents have their meal.They do great swedish meatballs and their chicken wings are especially yummy too! They often have set meals that are worth getting and drinks are refillable! Their desserts are also pretty cheap and interesting. Try their Daim tart! Sweet and nutty goodness in every bite!

This may seem strange but I literally come all the way down the IKEA exit bistro just to get cheapo but tasty hot dogs.I find the prices here absolutely ridiculous for a filling meal. At $1 a hotdog I never stop at just one, or two. A hotdog and a drink sets you back a mere $1.50, so you're set for a complete lunchtime bite. You even get the thrill of squeezing the sauces out of the udder-like contraptions, which is always  fun sight for kids. You could even get a soft serve ice cream cone here for 50 cents, and you know they'd do it better than Macdonalds does it. Despite their limited menu I really adore how quick and efficient everything is, and the fact that I can have a very filling and satisfying meal for under $5. What I usually do is grab meself a hotdog and walk around their little food collection next to the counter so see what Swedish food tempts me. An entertaining lunch in a very odd way!

I've always been a greater fan of Ikea's food rather than its furniture, and its bistro is the greatest reason why. The bistro strangely epitomizes the proud qualities of ikea- fuss free, brainless assembly and shopper friendly. Things are kept simple here: you first place and pay for your order at a counter, then move along in a somewhat production-line fashion to wait for your food to be prepared upon presentation of your receipt. The magical part is there is hardly ever a queue so you are literally seconds from a hot steamy sausage bun.The hotdog is of course the best seller. Its so ridiculously simple, cheap and good it makes you realize those people paying for $5 hotdogs outside zouk must be seriously drunk. It consists of a boiled medium length chicken sausage (ain't no bratwurst) sandwiched between a fresh bun, and you move on to dress it with the sauces of your choice, my favorite being an excessive amount of mustard and chilli sauce. Since last year they have also introduced a chilled chocolate doughnut that is not mind blowing but still sweet enough to fix that sugar craving.The only thing I never liked from the bistro is the signature lingonberry drink. It tastes so weird and doesn't appeal to my Asian palette at all. I have never met anyone who likes it, I wonder why they insist on keeping it on the menu. Also, I don't think the drink goes well with the food on the menu because I truly think a hotdog is best enjoyed with good ol coca cola!

Enough said , when you think of Ikea, immediately the swedish meat ball will be the top of mind. Everything here is self service, ranging from collection of eating utensil, food to clearing of tray.The meat ball comes with their own sauce as well as their lingo berry jam which taste lovely when you eat them as a whole. if you are a fan of the jam, you may request for more sauce. Another food not to be miss is the fried chicken wings, it is well marinated , sinful as it may seem, one will succumb to indulgence. Also, for sweet tooth, the dessert section offers unique pastries and cakes, one of them is the princess cake that is covered with a sweet green kaya layer.During rush hours, tables might be hard to get and queues might be long but the food is definitely worth the hassle.

IKEA has been our go-to source for Swedish meatballs for as long as I can remember. They have expanded their offerings to include a selection of local and other Swedish options, with a daily evolving menu so one is almost always guaranteed to be able try something new.Food : The meatballs are a mixture of beef and pork meatballs. Accompanied by a tasty gravy and lingonberry jam with a side of steamed potatoes, it is one of the signature dishes of the restaurant. The fish and chips are quite good, as is the poached salmon. The chicken wings are pretty awesome and the baked chicken leg comes in a generous portion. The soup changes daily but are usually quite decent. There are also daily breakfast options from 9am with a selection of pancakes, hash browns, scrambled eggs and waffles.Ambience : Busy and casualService : Self service but the IKEA staff serving at the counter are pleasant

We used to go there once a week, after school. Now I go a lot less, but hey, where else can you go to get a mix of chicken wings and nostalgia? Other than the crowdpleasers (meatballs, chicken wings), watch out for their specials, though not everything is worth eating (to wit, their Swedish crayfish special was meagre). And save room for dessert! Daim pie (yes Daim as in the candy) is a favorite, as is princess cake when it's available. If you like the food, do check out the food shop downstairs, because a lot of that stuff is available frozen to bring home.

Defiantly a 4.5 Star if that was possible.This place has a variety of dishes. And the Thai side of the menu is very good. The service is fast, even on busy times and the bar is well stocked. Have ordered Hot Basil chicken twice and got the happy burn on my tongue. The Pad Thai noodles were sweet and spicy. I also tried the Chicken Tikka and the taste was good.I like the closeness of the Resturant to my hotel and the outdoor seating is enjoyable. The price for the meal is very reasonable. The Noise level can get moderate at night with the drinking.For the variety of foods and drinks I'd recommend this place for parties and fun meals. The cons are the toilet is a single patron toilet and a bit beat up. On my next visits I'll be stopping but for some more enjoyable meals!!

One of the better places along the water at Robertson Quay. In general I am a bit skeptic about places that do a lot of different food and here they serve Thai, Western and Indian food. I have not sampled the Western food but I have been pretty happy with both the Indian and the Thai food. Neither is any OMG-experiences but both are well above average and at very decent prices.I like the relaxed atmosphere here and they have always been very friendly and service-minded so it has been pleasant to visit here. The good food is complemented by a beer selection of craft beers that is perhaps not amazing but also well-above what many places have. The fact that they also do not automatically add a service charge is another plus in my book.What is however not a nice experience is the men's room. It has been verging from dirty to disgusting on all occasions I have been here and that is just not ok and I always make me wonder how spaces in the restaurant guests are not seeing look.

This appealing joint is very conveniently located on the prettiest part of Robertson Quay, facing the river, and very close to Robertson Bridge.On first impression, it is like a privately-owned, hipstered-up mini hawker centre with a bar and three stall-like kitchens. It is conceptualised as a coffee-shop, where customers won't pay neither the dreaded service charge nor tax. Instead, customers are encouraged to get a "proper" drink at the bar, since drink sales are what pays for the service crew. That explains the 15-dollar pints.Nothing can go wrong when you have three kitchens with very different kinds of food, and this is a good example. The three kinds of food being served are Thai, North Indian and Western. So far I've tried the Thai and North Indian, which is my favourite (since I'm such a sucker for Indian food). The good thing about this kind of variety is that different cravings can be satisfied on a single visit.The food is good and prices are quite affordable. Drinks are a bit overpriced but, as explained above, it's for a good reason. The staff members are friendly and attentive, though at times they seem overwhelmed. Overall, it's a very good place to have a relaxed meal by the river with friends while watching people and enjoying variety. Above all, Bar Bar Black Sheep is a good statement that diversity is strength.

I love coming here to get the Indian food, people watch, and relax.  The guys that work here are awesome. They're friendly and efficient with service.I'm not a fan of the Western food here.  However, the Thai and Indian are pleasant.

Great location for a drink but everything was very mediocre. The concept is cool, trendy bar meets hawker stand, but everything fell short for me. We tried entrees from each food stand, all were sub par with tiny portion sizes. We ordered drinks, they brought my boyfriends beer right away, I had to ask for my wine not once, but twice after ordering. Solid eh.

This is a great place to go to with a big group of people as they have three kitchens, Thai, Western and Indian. You can order a selection off all three if you wish to; however, this review is for their Indian kitchen. We actually had this place recommended to us by our property agent as we live a couple of doors down. She recommended the Indian food so off we headed the next time we had a curry craving. We really enjoyed the curry although we found the outside seating uncomfortable as there are no cooling fans that work. Since this experience, we always get a take away. My husband is a chicken curry fan although he finds that as thigh meat is used here, they are not quite to his taste, he is a breast man! I'm a fan of mutton curry and have enjoyed each one I have tried so far. I would especially recommend the Makani Dahl, I always order an extra portion to keep in the freezer for a later date.

Been to a few of their other branches and thought they were great. This outlet however was a disappointment. The food was oily and not palatable. On top of that the area were infested with flies. Not a very pleasant experience. Their toilet however was clean. Not much of a celebration

This lovely dining experience is complemented by a great menu. Variety is one of its biggest hits at Bar Bar Black Sheep - Offering Thai, Indian, and western food. This often leaves customers indecisive and anticipating the tastes to come. On another note the butter chicken with garlic naan should not be missed!Its excellent service creates an environment that allows the customers to settle in with ease. The staff is known to be attentive and friendly, even on a busy afternoon.This rustic ambiance is complete with the river-side. Having three locations, the other two in Katong and Bukit Timah, displays the success of the restaurant. Bar Bar Black Sheep Robertson Quay still boast the best ambiance, leaving many customers coming back for more. Opening HoursSun: 9am - 12amMon-Thu: 11am - 12am Fri-Sat: 9am - 2am Price/Pax: S$17 - S$40

This outlet has only recently opened. Bar bar black sheep's first outlet was at Cherry Ave, near Sixth Avenue, where it was extremely popular with the alcholics in the vicinity. If you're up for some good grub during town, head over for their $11 nett lunch set meals. For example tom yum soup as starters and the mains are either cheeseburger, black pepper chick burger and aglio olio.The latest addition is air-conditioned (unlike the outlet at Sixth Avenue), and is a great place to rest amidst Singapore's unforgiving weather.The laidback ambience is an ideal place for an office worker to kick back, relax and just enjoy a pint of the freshest brew.

Stumbled upon this newly opened fastfood joint on the first day of its opening, when i was walking around my neighbourhood looking for some 'light' dinner.  Being a fan of japanese food, I decided to give it a try.  As per its name, one can pretty much guess what they serve... they serve low carb burritos-sized sushi rolls. I tried their " Rising Sun" ...Its pretty good... except I would preferred it with less wasabi.   They also served other side dishes. On the whole, its pretty yummy! Would love to go back and try the other items on their menu.

The oultet was located at the ground floor of one end of 100AM. There was limited dining in area. So I had the food taken away.SIGNATURE FRIED BACK ROLL ($6.90/ half roll)MAIN: Crab Meat, TamagoGREENS: Lettuce, Cucumber, AvocadoTOPPINGS: Flying Fish Roe, CheeseCal: 227 kcal The roll looked ugly. It had quite oily taste although it had the right texture with the chewy rice, juicy crab meat and tamago, and the popping fish roe. But it was just too oily to have. SAMURAI CHICKEN ($6.90/ half roll)MAIN: Fried Popcorn ChickenGREENS: Red Green Yellow Capsicum, Green Coral Lettuce, Japanese Cucumber, Takuan, AlfalfaTOPPINGS: Togarashi Powder (Spicy)Cal: 228 kcal Crunchy vegetables, although wished that the popcorn chicken was be crispier.TUNA SASHIMI SALAD ($7.90)DRESSING: Wasabi & Yuzu SauceCal: 250 kcalThere was not enough dressing to coat the salad evenly. The tuna sashimi tasted a bit off to me.FOREST SALAD ($7.90)MAIN: Sauteed MushroomDRESSING: Wafu SauceCal: 200 kcalThe mushrooms were well cooked but the dish was let down by the over used of black pepper here. It just tasted of black pepper which covered the nature taste of mushrooms.Service not bad, but the food got to improve some.

I had the beef sushi burrito and that was pretty tasty. The half portion was quite big. It did get messy towards the end as unlike a proper wrap, it is only the paper covering the end of the roll. I do wonder what will happen to the other half when someone just order a half portion. The potato salad was good, typical Japanese style. The salad was also refreshing but it was not very filling. So do not order just that if you are feeling hungry. The can of royal milk tea was not that great as it was not sweet or milky enough for my liking. Maybe I am too used to the Taiwanese style milk tea now.

Great place for pre or post workout snack. The Skinny Sumo contains a great mix of protein (tuna, salmon and "crab") and veggies (lettuce, cucumbers, avocado and radish).  No rice. Perfect for the healthy eater.

A highly disappointing meal. Got the rising sun (salmon and crab meat) burrito ($6.90 for half) and was attached by an overpowering taste of wasabi on the first bite. The wasabi sauce was unevenly squeezed and the burrito was not wrapped properly, causing bits of salmon, crab meat and lettuce to fall out even before the third mouth. I wouldn't have minded the mess if the taste made up for it, but it was nothing exceptional (maybe exceptionally messy and exceptionally overpriced). The seating here is spacious but there are few tables available, though it is rather empty during a weekday lunch hour (while the nearby toastbox, tsujiri and subway are all filled). Overall, I wouldn't recommend this place unless there is really no other choice - it wouldn't make good for a quick grab as well as the waiting time for the food was also significantly long.

What is a sushi burrito? A big fat sushi. Sucks because you only get one flavor. The bottom line, a normal roll is better. I prefer my sushi bite sized and small enough so that I can dip them in my wasabi soy sauce concoction. Overall, this wouldn't be a place that I would come too often. Funny bc I'm currently the Duchess as I write this post, and the reason why I checked three times was because I purchased three Groupon vouchers. I would come back, but not because of cravings, solely bc of convenience. At the same time, I prefer the standard supermarket sushi downstairs at FairPrice Finest.  The food isn't anything to rave about and definitely can't be compared to the sushi rolls we have in the States (Lion King or Dragon Roll anyone?).

Who doesn't like a good Mashup. Two great cuisines. Mexican style with Japanese ingredients, the concept is amazing. After a short metro ride and 300m walk from the station we made it to Sushi Burrito. I was so hungry that I quickly ordered a beer and a fried back roll. This was a roll filled with crab meat, tamango, lettuce, cucumber, and avocado. I was really happy with my order. I'd definitely come again.

I often get take out for my family. It's a relatively healthy option that's also low carb - it's stuffed full of ingredients and rolled with minimal rice. The flavour can't be compared to mid-range sushi restaurants but hey, it's a very respectable value-for-money burrito. Great all in one meal.

Not a great home delivery choice - maybe it's better when you dine in. The tempura roll was the lesser of two evils (2.5 stars) but the rice was mushy so don't expect any bite in the seaweed. Perhaps they could pack their seaweed separately so it's dry and crispy for you to wrap on when it arrives - Equinox and Swissotel used to serve their sushi at their Sunday brunch buffet like that. I couldn't take more than two bites of the other option (which had what looked like crabstick and raw tuna or salmon - my friends placed the order so I don't know what they're called) (1 star). The raw fish didn't taste fresh and made me nauseated.

I brought a friend to Clifford Pier for their Sunday brunch buffet. It was SGD52 per person and offered a wide variety of local foods. It was a great way for my friend to taste a mix of all the local foods in a beautiful historical setting. There was Chicken Rice, Satay, Kway Teow, dim sum, congee, sushi, rojak, laksa, chilli crab and other delicacies. Each dish is clearly labeled (especially with ingredients so if you have any food allergies you can avoid them). They also served local desserts and ice cream. Of course you could find better quality food at specific hawker locations or restaurants, but if you dont have time to hit various locations, this was a central location allowing my friend to have small samples and go in for repeats. The buffet also doesnt have a time limit, so we were there from 11:30am till 2:30pm (when they close). I am not sure how the a la carte menu is priced, but I would go for their buffet selection based on price and quality. Worth the visit and surely a place I will bring future guests who are on a short stop and never had any of the local flavors!

5* Hotel but not the food. (The Peranakan Special Edition)I have wanted to dine at Clifford Pier for ages. It's a gorgeous restaurant in a gorgeous hotel, with an even more gorgeous view, so when The Clifford Pier promoted that they were having a Peranakan Cuisine showcase by guest Chef Philip Chia, I knew we had to give it a try. The menu isn't extensive, just the highlights of Peranakan Food like Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi Pongteh and Nonya Chap Chye but with all the essentials there, it was enough for us to give it a shot. Ayam Buah Keluak ($28) The benchmark of any Peranakan Reataurant has to be the Ayam Buah Keluak. You can usually determine how good or bad your dinner is going to be from the way this dish was prepared and it was no different here. The sauce was very fragrant and very good. Lighter and slightly more watery than those I'm used to, it still had distinctive taste from the Rempah (spice blend) with a hint of the Buah Keluak. The Buah Keluak itself was something special. We're used to having it either as it is, or with the "meat" dug out , mixed with minced pork and stuffed back in but this one was special. They dug it out, mixed with with the rempah before stuffing it back in the shell. This made the Buah Keluak meat very flavorful and less pungent, which is good for beginners. Only thing is the way they cracked the shell. We usually open it down the side but because the opened it at the top and made it a pretty small opening (smaller than the teaspoon give), it made it very difficult to dig out the filling with a knife. The let down though was the chicken. They gave three chunky pieces of thigh yet every piece was cooked till it was dry and tough. Very very disappointing. Babi Pongteh ($28)Another easily recognizable Peranakan dish, the Babi Pongteh is a wonderful stewed pork dish with a bean paste. The flavours again was very nice. The sauce was fragrant and wonderfully thickened by the fat from the pork belly. It is a bit sweeter that the Pongtehs that I'm used too but it wasn't by any means overpowering. The problem again was the cook of the meat. While the fat was wonderfully melt in your mouth and the meat around the fat was tender and juice, it got extremely dry and tough as you reached the bottom. Another case of overcooked protein. Nonya Chap Chye ($18)Probably Peranakans most well-know vegetable dish, a Nonya chap Chye is more than just putting vegetable together and boiling it in a pot. There's a lot of care that goes into it with each vegetables different cook time. The key to any Chap Chye is ensuring the sweetness of the cabbage shine yet allowing strong flavors of the fermented soya bean and dried Beancurd skin to come come through. Too much or little of either and it'll lose the balance of the dish. The version served here is easier on the palette for those who do not like the taste of beancurd skin or fermented bean paste. It's naturally sweet   With that hint of saltiness from the bean paste, however, I hate to eat it again and again but.......... It was overcooked!The cabbage was mushy, the carrots were so soft I could mash it with my tongue and even the black fungus, that normally offers a nice crunch to the otherwise soft texture, was cooked till I could break it apart without biting. Lemon Barely ($5)This had to be the most natural tasting lemon barleys I've ever had. No artificial, cordial lemon barely here. It was straight up boiled barley drink (yes with the cooked barley in the glass), rock melon and lemon juice. A good way to counter the richness and spiciness of the Peranakan dishes. On a whole, the dining experience was decent but certainly not 5 star quality. The ongoing trend here was that, while the flavors were good, the main protein and veg were all over cooked. Chicken, pork, vege, all cooked way over than it should be. I understand the need to leave them in the flavor the dish but there's a ceiling and unfortunately, all the dishes here went way way way over it. Oh and unfortunately, service wasn't up to standard too. 1) servers were not strategically placed. It took a while to get someone's attention as all the wait staff were near the entrance while we were near the rear. 2) they were preparing for an event outside. I know there's a need to have background music but a. Did they really need to blast the music and fill hall with bass-y chill out longer music? Considering that the guest hadn't even arrive? b. To rectify the issue, they ended up turning up the ambient music in the restaurant! Not till it was deafening because we could still talk but to a point that it was above the comfort range. So overall: Venue: 5*Ambience: 3* (thanks to he music) Service: 3* Food: 3* I would love to give this experience a 4 but I'll wait till my next visit before determining.

There are two restaurants within Fullerton Bay Hotel, so make sure you go to the correct one. The other one is called Clifford Restaurant so look out!This place is a beautiful dining hall overlooking the MBS side, with nice chandeliers, big big vases of white orchids, and soft background music playing by a live band (for dinner). It is a very, very pleasant experience to dine here. Service here is impeccable, and waitstaff are attentive and prompt.Let's come to the important bit. The food.Cuisine here is Singaporean hawker food, served with an upmarket touch. The prices here are a steep mark-up from the usual hawker fare, so be prepared to shell out some heavy dough. I came here with a companion and we started with two popiah rolls (thin crepes stuffed with turnip, prawns, egg) ($12). I had the laksa with lobster ($36), which I enjoyed, apart from it not having cockles... My grouse was that my laksa was not Instagram-worthy, with bits of chopped lobster scattered in the laksa. Come on guys, for 36 bucks++ the laksa better look good.My companion had fried snapper with brinjal/eggplant. He rated it 6/10. You have to order rice separately, which is $5 extra, but you have a choice between white and brown rice, which is freeflow. Pretty sweet. I like the brown rice option. Plus point for having healthier choices!We ended the meal with a key lime pie for him, and an ice kacang for me.The key lime pie was good, and had a good digestive crust. They were very accommodating when I mentioned I didn't want peanuts and red beans inside my ice kacang. The ice kacang differs from the hawker one - the ice is very finely blended/ground, so that it is soft and is melt-in-the-mouth, unlike the crunchy feel from the hawker ice kacang. Our bill for two came up to 200 because we had two beers and a glass of champagne (they sell Perrier Jouet by the glass ehre ($30)). If you don't drink, I think this meal is still affordable - comparable to a normal restaurant meal.Would I come back? Maybe. Definitely not getting alcohol next time!

Ambience - classy and cosyFood - can be betterService - goodThe restaurant is overlooking Marina Bay Sands and is situated right on the spot of the old Clifford Pier where people board the boats to go to nearby islands. Although the place has been given a new wardrobe, the stuctures still remain and feels very nostalgic!

This is an upscale "coffee Shop" in Fullerton Bay Hotel. Food is an eclectic mixof local and western. Dishes are generously portioned but average. Flavors are somewhat authentic but skewed to western tastes. We had the key lime pie and rum baba for dessert. Avoid like the plague. It was terrible. It is somewhat better than your average coffee shop in ambiance and service. But with 3 star prices, it's a place to chill out for brunch or lunch in the weekend but ultimately not a value.

You come here for the big hotel lobby ambience and the view of the Marina Bay Sands and all that. Food - not so much.We came for Sunday brunch, which featured mostly Sing/Malay stuff. They also have dim sum of sorts including some steamed stuff that is wheeled around in carts. It was all tasty enough, but really nothing special at all. And at S$48 per adult, it's expensive fare for what it is.

Had a colleague in town, and this was a nice respite after walking all the way along the Singapore River from Clarke quay MRT station. Definitely a nice place to bring visitors from out of town, as the place looks impressive, and you can show them google photos of that the Pier / area used to look like. Service is ok. Quality of food not too bad, but definitely on the pricey side. 12 sticks of satay for more than $20, and the meat on the skewers were strangely flat. The kong bak paus were pretty nice.
Likely the worst Italian food in Singapore.... :-( Ended up here for late dinner after Esplanade Theatre.

Ordered the smoked salmon bruschetta, garlic fries, vongole and some oriental pasta Great view, definitely take the outdoor seats, it's much more cooling, with a better view. The inside was stuffy with the smell of oil and cooked food, another reason for me choosing an outdoor seat. Nice oak tables, great for Instagram flatlays. The fries and bruschetta was good, so was the oriental pasta - but not stunning nor irreplaceable. The vongole was a huge huge disappointment, I would recommend nobody order it. Great chill out place but don't see myself going back there anytime soon.

Having been to Supply & Demand twice, I guess you can pretty much say that it fulfils the "hipster dining experience" in the cultural location within the Esplanade.The food and range of options on the menu is not too bad. Taste is good but not wow. The service is average and sometimes rather unenthusiastic. If you want a view, go up to level 2 where they have an alfresco bar. For dining, its still more comfortable to dine at Level 1. But the tables are close and sometimes a huge table may house 2 separate groups at the same time. So if you want a private place to chat, this may not be an ideal location as you will probably find yourself straining to hear your friend speak or having to talk over the noise around you.

Took a late afternoon walk in the Marina Bay and walked by.  Saw people sitting on the rooftop bar quite relaxed so decided to pop in.  You cannot really see the bay on rooftop because of the tall trees by the water.  But you can still enjoy a cold beer watching the skylines lit on gradually after the sunset.  Ordered a nine inch two-in-one pizza, half signature half pepperoni - a fine bite.  Waiters were friendly and willing to chat, though the background music could be a bit too loud for conversations.  All in all, a relaxing dining experience.

Friendly efficient service. My truffle pizza was ok. I was hoping for better instead of the biscuit-like crust. In other words, I would prefer the traditional wood fired oven pizza. I'm a pizza snob though because I have lived in NYC and also in Switzerland near the Italian border. It's hard to find good pizza in Singapore.

Cozy and cool rooftop bar. Great music and ambience. Good for chilling and catching up with friends. Alcohol is a little pricey but still reasonable like most places. Although it is lacking toilets you wouldn't mind walking to esplanade as you get to see the good view of CBD and MBS.

The food over here has good standards. This is a Peruvian Italian restaurant and as staple dishes or chicken and fish with a Peruvian Italian twist. The style of Peruvian food due to the huge Asian influences on Peruvian food. Dishes to try would include their Pizzas, Peruvian Chicken, Steak fries with dipping as well as their Sausage platter. While I thought that nothing was particularly mind blowing, I felt that each dish was executed very well and tasted great. Besides they do serve $10 happy hour Belgium beer with a rooftop bar with an excellent city view.Conclusion:This is a new restaurant, located just outside esplanade mall. Nice ambiance and decor. As it is a new restaurant,  there are still a few issues such as staff training. But overall, an excellent place to have a quiet dinner and to hangout with friends.Do note that restaurant will only be open for F1 ticket holders from 19 Sept - 23 Sept, as they are located within the zone 3 & 4 of the Singapore GP Circuit Park. They will be accessible to the public from the 24 Sept, Tuesday onwards. Recommended for food, ambiance and friendly service :)

This place caught my eyes when i was over at the makan sutra place a few weeks ago. Italian Peruvian? Sounds good to me!We got 3 things from the Chicetti menu and one large pizza and it was more than enough for the both of us.Here's what we ordered:- Beef Antichucos - delicious! Loved the green chili sauce that came with it- garlic truffle fries - i love that it's chunky cut instead of the usual skinny fries. Couldn't taste much of the garlic though- Suppli - fried risotto croquette, it's my favorite out of the 4 things we got!- The morning after pizza - decent, but i've had great morning after pizzas elsewhere too.They serve peroni and mac's on draft, and they're $11 a pint during happy hour.The place has a nice decor and ambience too. Not too much seating, but maybe there was an outdoor component that i missed? They have a rooftop bar but we didnt get to check it out.Would totally come back again!

Sweet potato fries were yummy. Didn't like the carbonara too much as it was kind of sour. Returned it once only to be served with another carbonara with the same taste. My friend ordered the rib eye steak which was good except that the fat of the steak was not rendered down. Overall, the ambiance was nice and it's a good place to have group gatherings.
