1. Affordable drinks - The only bar along the clark quay stretch that has 1for1 alcohol all night long (till 11pm) on weekends :) yay!!! Other bars usually close their drinks promo by 8-830pm. 2. Unlike most bars, they have real food instead of just bar food. - The dessert was pretty decent :) - Probably because they are a restaurant as well.3. Great service! despite our party being huge (20pax+++)  and constantly moving around/mingling and changing seats, the waiter knew exactly what everyone ordered and served each person his/her correct bill. Very impressed.The person I spoke to was also very accommodating to our big group, suggestion menu choices, drinks etc. Emailing me personally. Other bars I checked out, Harry's, Cafe iguana along the same Clark Quay stretch weren't as efficient or helpful. Cafe iguana was probably the worst! I practically had to chase down the manger to get a quote on food etc. 4. Good view of the Singapore river. 5. Also, not too noisy, dark or smokey like other bars. - Perfect for having a conversation with friends or networking while enjoying your drink at the same time. I didn't have to shout into my friends' ears to be heard.

It is extremely unfortunate that my experience with this place has been less than exceptional on the one visit that I have been here since I started using Yelp. I visited SQUE for the first time about 2 years ago, for Restaurant Week and both the service and food was extremely commendable. Since then, I have become a semi-regular here because of their amazing Happy Hour deals (from 5pm - 7pm and then 9pm - 11pm, that's definitely my tip for coming here). I have been very fortunate to have been served for the same lady the last 2 years, perhaps it was by coincidence that she is always here when I visit.However, on today's visit she was not one of those who were on duty and I can definitely say that the service here is less than exceptional. I was here for first drinks with my girlfs after dinner nearby and stayed after they left to have drinks with the boyf who came for dinner / to send me home. While here with the girls, it took us 10mins to try and get the attention of the waiter just to order our drinks - which in all honesty is not great when you have about 5 - 6 waiters around. SQUE is not an exceptional huge place, and I don't expect this to happen because I have always been served under 5mins in my previous visits. Perhaps you could say that I have been pampered by my precious waiters here, but I would expect some level of service at least when it is a lull period. The boyf came at 9:20 while my girlfs left at about 9:30 - and while I would think that the place was a bit more crowded than an hour plus before, most of the tables had already been served. He ordered a soup and pizza, and while the pizza did not come until 9:40 which I would say is understandable but, the soup had not arrived. We decided to cancel the soup order since appetizer had not arrived before the main course and we were denied that cancellation. Their reason - the soup and pizza are done in different ways and that our soup was being prepared. While I understand that, I really don't think that a soup that has been pre-prepared and reheated would take 35mins to come. Even making the mushroom soup from scratch would have taken less time than that! The soup was extremely salty and didn't seem like a freshly made soup at all. The bread that came along with the soup had dark black toast burn marks, but it was still soft as if it wasn't toasted at all. This was DEFINITELY NOT a dish that would have taken 35mins to make. I wouldn't recommend coming here for food, and definitely not for drinks outside Happy Hours. The service here is below expectations (compared to my expectations of other restaurants and not with my previous visits to SQUE itself because I think that would be unfair - probably that waitress that usually serves is was one of the best here) and unless you're prepared for slow service, I would recommend heading to Clarke Quay and its myriad of better restaurants.

Many other reviews are from people who "noticed food on the menu, but didn't order it," opting only for drinks instead. As the one poor person who ordered food here, let me give you a stern warning. Absolutely, do not order any food. Only go for the double-priced 2-for-1 happy hour drinks. We ordered a burger and wings. The burger was served completely raw, while the wings were dripping with frozen ice water and had blood near the bones. Beware!

Lunchtime around Clarke Quay is pretty quiet as things don't start to liven up until mid-afternoon then go late into the night. Even so, this place is open for lunch. Actually, the billboard displays of their dishes don't really do their food justice. The Soup of the Day I had (Pumpkin) was average but the Tomato & Mozzarella Salad with Tuna was very good. I was pleasantly surprised, I admit. The riverside location with people and boats going by makes a very relaxing lunchtime atmosphere. The sandwiches I saw being served to other diners look great too.

1 for 1 daily happy hour starts at 9pm.I have only had drinks + small bites here. Tried the quesadillas and ceasar salad. Both were pretty ok. The quesadilla was much better than the awful one I had at Chili's. But we are here only for the drinks. yeah to happy hours. The place is also rather big and thus, we never had much issue finding a table. Small AC area only, but do sit outdoors, you get a nice view of the Singapore river facing Clarke Quay.

I haven't eaten there, so I am basing this review on the bar. Specifically, on the fact that they have hundreds of different beers to choose from. Ask them for the full beer menu if they don't offer it initially. There are lots of craft beer from around the world to choose from, although I'd like to see more more American beers. Of course, the extensive list has it's drawbacks. They apparently run out of popular beers often, because I walked away disappointed on two different occasions when they didn't have any Stone IPA. And you will pay a premium for the variety and the location. It is just steps away from the Clarke Quay MRT, right on the river.Update:  I finally tried the food and was pleasantly surprised. The roasted chicken sandwich was great. Juicy and flavorful with fresh, crispy wedge fries. The happy hour really takes the bite out of the prices. Two-for-one draft beer after 9:00, and half price bottles after 10.
What you would expect for American food in Singapore. Fish fingers for the kids are excellent. The rest of what we are (quesadilla and sausages) was pretty mediocre.

I am a big fan of Cedele, so whenever possible, I make sure to pick up a sandwich or salad from the nearest Cedele for lunch or a quick pick-me-up in the afternoons. This particular Cedele in Novena Square is a little small and feels cramped. It's also along the route to the MRT station so there's always lots of traffic going by, making this place pretty noisy as well. I wouldn't recommend staying here for your meal, especially since it'll be hard to get a table in the first place, but the food is, as always, excellent, and it's totally worthwhile to grab something to take away.

Oh dear.My most recent visit here was an unfortunate reminder of why I don't come here in the first place. I was looking for something fast and healthy-ish, and needed a break from my usual lunch rotation. Looking at the menu, the pastrami sandwich caught my eye. I was pretty hungry, and thoughts of a nicely stacked pastrami slices for $8.50 seemed like a good idea.When my buzzer went off, I fought through a crowd of people waiting to be served, only to finally reach the counter and see a plate with a high-tea sized sandwich. Check out my picture. There were 2, at most 3 slices of pastrami. 3 out of 4 of the bread slices were a bit too toasted, and 1 slice wasn't even toasted at all. More evidence that my bread was no good? I had to use a sizable amount of force to bite through it, causing crumbs to fly to the nearby tables (which are pretty close together, by the way.) It was pretty painful, as by the end the roof of my mouth felt... abused. It was as if it were burned!As I struggled to get through the saddest sandwich in the world, I longingly looked at the Burger King opposite, wishing I went there instead. That's saying something, as I'm team McDonald's all the way!
I like the place! It's inside the mall and they have really nice scones. Their pear tart is amazing too! Ask for the scones to be heated and to be given with butter.

Terrible service, male server mumbling other female server not sure what's going on?? Ordered  scrambled eggs on toast, out came X1 mon toasted bread and watery scrambled eggs. No apology was offered when I asked for it to  be toasted...poor ambience has no feel to it won't be back...

For organic products, prices are kept considerably affordable at Cedele. I had tea at their branch in Novena Square yesterday with two friends. With so many interesting items on their menu, it was hard deciding what to get! In the end, we had some of their sweet breads, Raspberry Thumbprint and their vegetarian Mexican's Wedding cookies. While the Raspberry Thumbprint cookie was crummy and a bit of a letdown, the flavourful scones, buns and Mexican Wedding cookies were delightful.This branch is quiet, so we were seen to promptly and had no problems getting seats. The polite, patient staff and cosy ambience in the cafe enhanced the pleasure of the experience and we exited with happy bellies.

I had heard about this place for years but had never tried it. It's a no frills place with cheap and extremely flavourful Thai food. As a vegetarian, the menu is extreme extensive and all the dishes are pretty decent. My favourites are the mango salad, pad Thai, basil tofu and green curry. The only thing id recommend staying away from is there desserts which just never seem to hit the spot for me.

A no-frills place: come for the good food and value, not the atmosphere!Recommended!Looking for a quick lunch while strolling on East Coast Rd, and came across this little Thai place. We decided to give it a try despite the low Yelp rating, and we were glad we did!Food:We ordered Thom Yum Seafood soup, Pineapple Rice, a green Chicken Curry, a coffee and lime juice. The soup was delicious, with wonderful lemongrass flavor and a decent amount of prawns, fish, and squid. The green curry was flavorful, as was the Pineapple Rice. I wouldn't hesitate to order these again, but the menu is interesting and I'd love to try other things! The lime juice was just ok, being a bit too sugary for my taste. The coffee was, well, instant. At least the server was up-front when we placed the order.Cost:$24.20, which was very reasonable for the portion sizes. They also have a set menu for lunch that's less ex.Service: They were prompt in taking the order and the food was served quickly. After that, they didn't stop by the table at all.Atmosphere:Quite utilitarian, and could benefit from some attention to the paint and interior design.Overall:I wouldn't hesitate to come back for the food and sample more of the menu!

We took a chance with the mixed reviews. If you want cheap & authentic Thai food, go to Nangfa in Bedok. This is possibly my worst ever Thai food in SIngapore. The waiters are disinterested in serving as well. This is below average for me.

Standards have dropped since they changed owners. The food used to be really fantastic but not so anymore. Now the food is a tad too salty. They seem to have lost the Thai flavors..They were out of many dishes that we wanted to order.

Not sure where goes into their dishes. I couldn't finish my dinner set, because it was simply yucky. It was greasy, gooey, and had none of the flavours you'd expect from Thai dishes. Curiously though, the place is packed every time I walk by. Maybe because it's cheap. Not worth it. Really not worth it, even if it's dirt cheap!

Right by the bus stop along East Coast Road, so you can't miss it! What I love about this place is that they have so many options for everyone. Besides the regular menu, they also have a vegetarian menu. And it's not like 3 dishes thrown in as an afterthought. It's a full menu with plenty to choose from. It's rare that a vegetarian is spoilt for choice at a non-veg place, but that's exactly how it is here. You have to ask for the menu as they don't usually present it with the regular menu. My favs are the Beancurd with Pepper and Garlic ($5 for a small portion), and there are like 5 other tofu varieties for you to choose from. They're all good! The tom yum is also mandatory, and there do a really good vegetarian option. So spicy, but not to the extent that it's more pain than pleasure to eat. A small bowl is $5, but I recommend going for the medium at $7. There's a whole lot of vegetables to choose from too, all at $4 or $5. You can have a whole meal with a friend or 2 for less than $20 among you. It's really good value for excellent food. :)Vegetarian Menu: jai-thai.com/menu-vegeta…

One word to describe Jai Thai - YUM.Whenever I'm there, I order the green curry chicken and thai fishcakes. Thats usually if I'm eating alone. Depending on how hungry I am, sometimes that isnt enough but more often than not, those two dishes are sufficient.Taste wise there really isnt anything to fault Jai Thai. The flavours are authentically Thai and even the simplest dishes are fragrant and tasty. Easy on the wallet too.

This is another place to go for authentic Thai food if you want alternatives to Nakhon Kitchen. In fact, they are cheaper then Nakhon which is already pretty decent in terms of their pricing.Taste-wise, I'd say their style of making Thai food is a bit different from that of Nakhon. I believe that Thai food varies from region to region in Thailand, and that's probably reflected in the differences. The beef they use in their green curry is more stringy, and the curry is less spicy as well.I also tried the fish cakes here, which I thought were superb. Really awesome and in fact I'd say better than Nakhon for this dish.Phad thai and Pineapple fried rice were decent, but nothing to shout about. Tom yum soup was also pretty decent but not the memorable type that you will remember after the meal.

This is a good place for lunch if you are working nearby, since they have a cheap lunch set. It comes with a drink and a dessert and you can choose from 5-6 main dishes like pad thai, chicken curry, tom yum soup, etc. While the a la carte is not very much expensive, the olive rice is rather oily and hardly has much ingredients and condiments as compared to many other thai food places I frequent. There is also a stale oil smell if you eat in. It may not be wise if you are meeting clients after, it gives me a slight headache smelling the stale oil on my clothes for the rest of the day.In spite of all that, I think the tom yum soup is quite good here, spicy enough and has a good balance of lemongrass and sourness. The a la carte dishes are slightly small. They claim a medium can feed 4-5 people but the portion really feeds 3 of us. I'm not sure if it's a difference in eating culture since they service crew there are all petite thai girls. If you live nearby and you don't wish to pay too much, Jai Thai could be the place to go since they are very wallet-friendly as their tag line goes.

Lovely staff who greets with a smile when you enter and says goodbye when you leave. Much different from the service staff at Thomson (please refer to my review there). I had a lovely cup of skinny latte, which had a chocolatey, roasted and creamy profile that was right up my alley. For the food, I had the sunny lovin. It was a generous smear of avocado guacamole on TOP each half of the English muffin and topped with a poached egg. Was under seasoned but nothing a pinch of salt didn't fix.

This is a good local neighborhood coffee shop, good coffee, good food, good service. I've been here a couple of time to get coffee and met friends for breakfast once as well. It's a bit small and can get crowded, but they tables to sit at and enjoy your breakfast with table service after ordering at the counter and they have high chairs as well. They don't have a kids menu, and their food portions are rather large. The coffee is good, the chalkboard showing all the different coffees is GREAT, you can get an coffeducation while waiting for your drink, maybe even change up your next order. The coffee price and portion seems a bit expensive, compared to Starbucks, but about on par for small neighborhood coffee shops. They have free filtered water at a self service station, which is always a major plus for me.Convenient parking in the Siglap V garage down below as well.

This is a place I drive by everyday. Either on the way to work or on the way home. What always attracts me is the soft lighting and the wood furniture. It gives me a very calm and soft feeling. So decided to finally give it a try. Walked in and was greeted by the staff. Nothing short of what you'll expect at cafes nowadays. Didn't bother to look at the menu, as I feel to operate a cafe, a good coffee is always necessary. So I got myself a iced latte and a cappuccino. Took a whiff of the coffee, and it was strong. I remembered I had something so strong was back when I was in Greece. But once you mix in the milk and the espresso together. It became a symphony of flavours. The coffee they use are a little more towards the acidic side. I love the flavours that linger in my mouth. For me this is indeed one of the best coffees in Singapore. And what I love is that this is a no frills place. No pretentious staff and decor. It's nice, pleasant on the eyes and it relaxes my soul! Yes! Even with my coffee, it doesn't take long before I start feeling like I need a nap. So when you're around the area, do drop by for your cuppa.

Understandable if you're a bistro that makes mediocre coffee. But when you call yourself a "speciality coffee house" and with a name as "craftsman" and serve up slush that they do... Food is average but exorbitant. But the coffee here is a complete joke.Word of advice - don't be pretentious by calling yourself a speciality coffee house.

I absolutely love this place. When I first saw this cafe on burpple, I went onto their website and looked for the menu. One look at the menu and I knew I had to try it out. So I did. And I was not disappointed.I had their Fruity Buttermilk Waffle ($15-$16) and a regular sized Chai Latte ($5). It took a while for the waffle to come out but it was definitely worth the wait. The waffle was topped with bananas, blueberries and strawberries along with maple syrup. It was superb! Also, the Chai Latte was one of the best Chai Latte's i've had in Singapore. My first Chai Latte was in Tokyo's Dean and Deluca and nothing has lived up to their standards. But this did. I was delighted to have finally found a place which serves good Chai Latte. ahahahaOn the downside, I wished they had a few comfy chairs so I could chill there with a book and also served muffins!!However, the atmosphere was real cosy, perfect for working or studying! :)

I literally drive past this café every single day after work. The fact that this place is just a 7-min drive from my home, questions my sanity. Every time my car stops at the stoplight at the T-junction facing Siglap V, I contemplate. "Should I go? Should I not go?" I have read too many positive reviews about the café that it made me super curious and intrigued. So yes. Curiosity finally slaughtered the cat in me. I gave in and went today; along with my two willing colleagues.Why didn't I come here sooner? Why? Why?!! Every single thing we ordered were brilliant. I ordered a glass of their Butterscotch Latte, whilst the rest of the food were shared amongst us three. We ordered Cinnamon Churros Ice Cream, Milo Dinosaur Waffles and Salted Caramel Pavlova. Fwoah!! If that's not enough sugar rush for you, I don't know what will.I think these were the best churros I've had so far. They tasted really crunchy and authentic. You could really taste the perfect cinnamon flavour. They were served in a glass with a scoop of chocolate-drizzled vanilla ice-cream in between.As for the pavlova, I opted it since I saw the words, 'Salted Caramel' plastered onto it. I love salted caramel. Watching the staff cut a slice off the pavlova with a big knife was an enthralling watch. Haha! My colleague and I had our eyes glued. The meringue was baked into perfection. Even the caramel was brilliant.Moving onto our chocolate waffle, this was served to us the last. Firstly, I have to applaud on the presentation. Loved the mini marshmallows that were used as toppings. So cute! They had a dollop of vanilla ice-cream in the middle, topped with Milo powder. Another thumbs-up from all of us. Although, one of my colleagues commented that it would have been nicer if the waffle was a bit spongier.Overall, we loved the desserts. All of us ended up feeling contented after the sugary meal; no thanks to the stress at work. The service too was commendable. The lovely staff girls were all very friendly and considerate enough to tell us that the cakes are all Halal (supplied by a young local Malay baker, Farah H. Affandi -- go google her cake creations!).And oh! Parking slots are available at 3 convenient places. You may either park your vehicles at the basement carpark of the building itself, the lots behind the building, or the basement carpark at Siglap Centre located right across.For now, I think a hot glass of green tea is in order!

Can't complain about the lack of coffee spots in the East anymore with so many sprouting like mushrooms! I actually visited Craftsmen Specialty Coffee at Siglap V, just opposite Siglap Centre, when they first opened (that was months back). Well, it took this long because well.. it's just another cafe... who gets its beans from somewhere else, and in this case from Dutch Colony Coffee Co., which opened its outpost a few streets down... And as the story goes....First, the coffee. The Craftsmen blend is 40% El Salvador Finca El Carmen, 30% Ethiopia Konga natural Yirgacheffe and 30% Sumatra Triple Picked Mandheling. You get balanced notes with a hint of ripe lemon and dark chocolate finish. The coffee was bold and robust, just the way i like it. Drinks are in the $4-$5 range. Our latte and flat white were both $4.50 each. To differentiate itself, Craftsmen also has a brew bar which does V60, Chemex, Siphon, Woodneck and French Press coffees ($6-$8).  You can also get your hands on the usual coffee making products- Hario, Bodum blahblah.Food wise, we weren't impressed. Quiches ($9) and sandwiches ($15-16) are made in house. We had the Pulled Pork sandwich ($15), which was MEH. The meat wasn't seasoned well. It tastes of meat that's bland and tough. Where's the spice man? The choice of bread was also kinda off with a thin waxy brown skin and a strange center with a chewy pull. Well because the meat was so dry, it remained separated from the bread.Thankfully, they chose the right cake and pastry supplier, Fathis, who apparently supplies to many cafes (i can't be sure of that) but anyhoo, i was thoroughly impressed with their moist and chunky banana walnut bread with a dollop of of cream cheese frosting. Other cakes available include a Salted Caramel Popcorn and Blueberry Cheesecake, and they look really hearty!So well, head over to Craftsmen for coffee and a piece of cake if you're in the area. After all, it beats having the usual Coffee Club mudpie, or Udders ice cream.

Craftsmen Specialty Coffee is now open!Yes! After a temporary closure due to staff training, Craftsmen Specialty Coffee, which specializes in coffee and cakes, had a reopening just few days ago.Besides from the food options, they also have appliances for sale here.Dutch Colony Coffee Co.'s blends are used here. The Flat White ($4.50) tasted strong and firm, yet has a low acidity that everyone can enjoy.The bakes and pastries here are supplied by online bakery Fathiscakes and Bonheur Pattiserie. The Salted Caramel Popcorn ($8.90), one of the cakes baked by Fathiscakes, is firm and satisfying. The caramel taste is just right; flavourful and not too sweet. Add a pinch of salt with popcorns on every mouthful and this will became a delightful cake to have.The location also meant that it is a quiet respite for people to relax with a cup of coffee or to study in during the day. With its reopening, the Siglap / East Coast area has now yet another cafe to be added to its list.

With Craftsmen open right in front of my doorstep, there's really no more reason to spend time searching for new cafes ;)Coffee? Check. The good people at Craftsmen use Dutch Colony beans, which are one of my favourite beans (apart from Sumatran!). The many times I've been here, I've never been let down by their coffee thus far - I recommend their cappuccino, their lattes, their mocha - heck, try it all.Food wise, nothing that special. I've tried their poached eggs on english muffin, wasn't wow'd by it. However, I haven't really tried much else so don't be deterred by that. My only irk is that due to the interior decor (minimalistic, high ceilings, enclosed), it tends to get rather noisy and sound echoes a lot.I'm still a sucker for their coffee ;)
They serve excellent coffee that is so aromatic.. wonderful big serving of food.. The staff is friendly and they provide great service.. what more can you ask for?
Love the coffee here, always constantly good and presentable. The food also nice, always come here simply for its coffee or breakfast.
Ordered 2 coffee drinks when the place was not crowded ... Took 10 mins to get my coffee :( ambience is nice but the pace is really slow ...

For all that I've heard about PS Cafe while in Singapore, my one experience proved it's overrated. Service is a joke, you'll spend more time flagging down a waiter than actually consuming your average tasting food.The truffle fries weren't the best I've had, but the fries were thin and crispy and while it could have been more balanced with the truffle topping, it itself was delicious.I ordered the mushroom croque monsieur as my main as a reco from a colleague- also just "good", but overly cheesy and blocked any flavor coming from the three different kinds mushrooms in the dish. The sourdough bread however is delicious. Perhaps worth a one time visit, but this location is overly crowded, especially during lunch time  so be wary of the wait.

PS. It's average. Just another outpost of the original in order to extend the franchise with hopes of further monetization of an established SG brand. Nothing special or remarkable positives except it's in a convenient place while premium shopping. Service was pretty spotty--wrong order, food coming out at wrong times, having to beg for water.PPS. You're probably gonna wait in a queue as well.

Compared to the other PS. Cafes, this is not one I like very much. The area is very small, and shares the space with a bag retail shop. I enjoyed the automated queue system which notifies you by a phone call when your table is ready. You can also check how many tables are ahead of you to estimate your wait time!I usually enjoy open kitchen set ups but this one was not well-ventilated and ended up spreading intense smells into the dining area. With the recent haze situation, my nose is especially sensitive, and my throat and nose were annoyed.We had to wave at the servers to get their attention, and also had to wait a long time before our food arrived. The servers only refilled our waters after long periods of time..That said, even though the venue and servers were really disappointing.. the food was as good as ever. TRUFFLE FRIES. one of the best i've had in Singapore and the U.S. Although there were some overfried ones, the flavors are still so delicious! I also had the honey and lemon hot drink, and that was nice and smoothing for the week.I probably will not go back to this branch of PS Cafe. It is in one of the most busy areas in orchard, and probably that's why there is such a wait even after lunch hours!

Always trying different dishes but never disappointing each time.If it's your first time, try out the truffle fries and any cakes that catch your eye. Ambience is 5/5.(Just try to avoid peak hours)Service is great. Worth the money. P.S cafe @ Paragon Mall is convenient. I personally like to chill out at the one in Harding Road if I'm not pressed for time

I stop by PS Cafe at Paragon on Orchard somewhat frequently these days because I'm in that area a lot and it can be tough to find food that fits my Paleo lifestyle anywhere else. They have an electronic queue system at the hostess stand that is user-friendly and you will get a text or call when your table is ready if they have a wait. In the meantime, you can wander around Paragon and get some shopping done. I've found you have to grab the employees attention when you are notified your table is ready. They tend to not really look at you otherwise.The food here is on par with all of the PS Cafe locations I have visited. I really enjoy their veggies with three dips and the long blacks are actually sizable here. No problem getting honey on the side for the Paleo coffee drinkers. I ordered the Brioche and Portobello Stack for breakfast. They wouldn't substitute the bread for anything else like tomatoes or potatoes, which I found pretty limiting. I skipped the cheese and actually found the portion to be a decent size, even without the bread. Service was friendly, but we had to ask our server for my husband's truffle fries a few times in addition to flagging them down to take our credit card after dropping the check. They just seemed a bit frazzled. Overall, it gets a 3.5 in my book for not being more flexible with healthy substitutions and for having to constantly flag down servers. I'll keep going back just because not everything on their menu is fried and the location is very convenient.

3.5 stars, but rounding it up to 4 stars.For some odd reason, I am angry whenever I enter this shop. Angry, or perhaps hangry (angry+hungry). Bc I'm only really hangry for the first 30-40 minutes. Service is so damn slow!!! Though the PS.Cafe here isn't as busy as the one on Dempsey or Club Street, you still really need to flag down waiters. My friends and I came here after a morning run at MacRitchie, starving! Hangry! And dizzy (bc of the accommodated amount of lactic acid in our stomachs)! We had to ask the waitress three times for water before it was brought to us, about 20 minutes after we sat down. It was cucumber-flavored water so we were pleasantly surprised and a bit less hangry. Our hangry level spiked again when we saw a table that ordered after us being served their mains! Excuse me! We havent even gotten our appetizer yet! We ordered one burger, two salads, and veggies & dips....how hard and long do they take to prepare? After staring miserably and hangrily at each other for the next 10 minutes, our food came out...fantastic! I loved the presentation and the food was delicious! The salads were nutritious and large! Super filling though at SGD 18, it was quite steep but worth every penny. My favorite is the lemongrass ginger--lemongrass dressing with fresh shaved ginger on a bed of pea sprouts, snap peas, bean sprouts, carrots, and chicken? YUM! I've tried to recreate this recipe many times, but I just can't get the tartness right. This salad def. grants PS.Cafe a few more visits. The Veg & Dip (SGD 22) is quite expensive, but the richness of the dips (especially the hummus) makes it worth it. Plus, the veggies are so fresh and you just feel GOOD eating here.    But, ugh. Service in Singapore. There's a rant coming along, but I'll save it for another day since my belly was full with delicious food instead of simply lactic acid. I know I shouldn't be angry, but I really wasn't. I was just hangry.

Good spot for some catch up over coffee and dessert but whether you sit inside or out makes a lot of difference.It's nice and cozy on the inside but much brighter and exposed to the rest of the mall outside. I would request a seat inside if you want a more intimate experience. Back to dessert, I really dig the steamed ginger pudding with the earl grey creme anglaise. The ginger cake is wonderfully moist and the creme anglaise has the right amount of sweetness balanced by the tea. Very satisfying.A little pricier but serving sizes are larger. Just the steamed ginger pudding is reason enough for a return visit.

P.S. Cafe in Paragon is rather small as compared to other branches. There are like 2 separate area and both are quite cramped. If you're planning to catch up with friends, maybe it's a good idea to sit at the outside area (the one opp of escalators) as it is rather less echoey. Much like what others said, we do need to catch the attention of the waiters despite the fact the waiter was like right across us. Nevertheless, they are still attentive and warm once you caught their attention. We tried their truffle fries and banana cheesecake, along with some coffee drinks. The truffle fries was good.. It was truffle-y enough (if such word exists) but not too overwhelming, which is my main complain about truffle fries at other establishments. The banana cheesecake was a let down, however. It was decent enough but does not have that oomph factor to make it memorable or outstanding. The coffee beverages were also quite meh as I find it a bit too acidic without the distinct coffee smell (almost felt like the beans are stale). Then again, I'm just very particular about how my coffee should be done, so each to his or her own in this case.Overall, P.S. Cafe at Paragon is a nice place to sit down and catch up with your friends in the middle of Orchard.

For the amount of hype this place received, it was definitely not worth it. Though the cafe has a nice ambience, the food is mediocre, not worth the hype it receives. I was especially disappointed by the truffle fries, those of which lacked anything special, and in general were just overpriced fries with some cheese.I was especially upset with the price. Too pricey! I would be willing to pay if the food was better, however I was very disappointed. Will not be making a trip again.

Planned to have light bite and coffee here, ended up with full lunch. Had cesar salad, croque madame, and late. Have to say, its all to fresh and tasty, hearty portion too. They spread generous gruyere on my cesar salad! Wild mushroom sauté on my croque madamme was delish! Yummy!

this is my favorite cafe chain in singapore - it's an oldie, but a goodie. the cakes are consistent, the places are modern-cool and casual, and you never have to deal with too many teenagers at the joints.the prices aren't cheap, especially if you do dine-in and they deign to scoop a bit of ice cream over your sliced cake, but they make good puddin' consistently - and that's merit enough: it's frustrating when you make up your mind to forego tight bottoms and then be disappointed by dessert.I've never been disappointed here.my tastes run to chocolate (but of course) - they have rich options like the doorstop, which really is an excuse for eating a mountainously-sized excuse for a snickers bar made into cake - but the tiramisu is a good light option, and its sponge cakes are hefty, substantial choices, it's the steamed puddings that stand out - a moist, tender, palm-sized cake sitting in a hot pool of caramel, topped with a scoop of ice cream - and feature most prominently in my thoughts about this place.the joints do a fair amount of business, so it's always buzzy - in a good way - and there are so many of them, there's absolutely no reason you can't sit down for a bit of cake whenever you fancy.

P.S. cafes are my to-go for a fancy-but-do-not-cost-a-bomb restaurant. Good quality food items across the menu. Its staples like its famed shoe-string truffle fries, caesar salad and sweets never fail to disappoint ... and they taste pretty awesome across all outlets.Fav sweets none other than its Chocolate Nut Doorstop (def the dessert course of my version of three-course last supper) ... and sticky date rice pudding!The Paragon branch is obviously not as fancy as the other outlets ... but it's really the only P.S. Cafe outlet with no queues on a Fri / weekend evening. Service at this outlet has improved over time as I think they recruited more waitstaff.

The service was terrible even deciding to patronize the café for the second time. The waiters ignore our presence and to be fair, we weren't demanding or upset. Haha. Thought it was just us but apparently, my friends felt the same way. Stop visiting the place since then. We would go to Sushi Tei at the same building or the basement for food.

I love this place - it's not as crowded as the other P.S. outlets if you come by early enough, and I can spend a good few hours lingering over nosh, drinks, and flipping through magazines that are conveniently hung around. When the wallet is willing, I tend to drop by for brunch at say.. 11am, pick out a good seat inside, and while my day away. I'll usually go for the turkey cranberry sandwich, or one of the burgers - portions are big, and quality is assured. Prices are also steep, but that's true in all P.S. branches. There's usually not much room to stomach dessert after, but the sticky date pudding is not to be missed. Just spend some time over a pot of tea, and you'll be good for round two in a bit. Also, the A/C is usually tuned to freezing, so you'd be better off bringing a sweater before rocking up.

Take a mini trip to Paris and stuff your belly with 3 courses of incredibly well executed bistro fare for only $32++?  Cannot be, right?  Oh but actually...CAN...most certainly CAN, at least during lunch hours at Bistro Du Vin, Zion!The first thing that struck us on our first visit was the beautifully delicious bread and butter...nothing zany or cutting edge...just delicious, soft warm french bread paired with sweet creamy butter...dangerously delicious and although we usually get a table for 2, we've still been guilty of asking for more bread...it's that good!The aforementioned 3 course lunch for $32++ is the best reason to go and the best options for each course are...drum roll please...Best Entree: Foie gras ravioli with toasted hazelnut & Port wine sauce (one large round ravioli stuffed with rich foie gras and covered with hazelnut gravy)Best Plat Principal: Duck leg confit with pommery mashed potato (some of the time we pay a little more to substitute the amazing truffle fries [every fry is perfectly crispy] or truffle mashers...the duck is absolutely perfect...fall off the bone fork tender meat with perfectly crispy skin)Best Dessert: Baked apple tart on puff pastry with coffee and cardamom ice cream (warm flaky pastry, soft spiced apples and delicious ice cream...how can you go wrong?)PARTING THOUGHT: In case that wasn't enough value for $32++, you also get coffee or tea for FREE!  And that includes your fancy coffee like your latte and cappucino!  Love it!

The set lunches at BDV is seriously good value.  Food is decent, all delicious while nothing exciting.  For set lunch, the portions were not minimised so be prepared for a hearty meal!What I really want to applaud is the service level.  We had a big party of more than 10 adults and kids, it was a chaotic lunch on Sunday. Luckily there weren't many other patrons, and the staff remained calm and composed, never lost their cool with all the usual requests by big groups.

Just a wonderful bistro to get your french fix.  Think amongst all the dishes we had it was the heart chocking Foie Gras that stole the show.  It was done just right with a slight crisp on the outside but melts in your mouth like butter.  The dish that did nit quite make the mark was Cassoulet.  Feels like a dish of left over put together as a dish.  We are not a big fan of soufflé as the last memory of it was the smell of raw egg.  They did very on this as it is airy, light and looks absolutely nice paring it with a scoop of ice-cream.  So take away is.....i shall be back. And oh yes..the French host was rather entertaining :).
The foie gras, beef cheek, and ribeye were delicious! The servers were kind and attentive. We definitely plan to come back!

You have to try the beef cheek. It melts in the mouth!!! Do check out the daily specials as well, they have exotic stuff and worth a try.I just tried the white asparagus from the special menu today. Enjoyed it very much!! It was crispy !!

First time here. Le wife suggested this place months ago but never got the chance and fortunately we got a table inside with the air condition.Service was prompt and the owner(French guy) was friendly and funny. Making jokes the way I like it . Food came quick and it was awesome. Everything was done right and as of now I am already looking forward  to my next visit there !

First time dinner at Bistro Du Vin. Nice pleasant ambience. Very French Bistro. Service was very good but then it was a slow night on Thursday. We ordered foie gras, scallops, escargots and their special gravlax. Outstanding was the gravlax. Unfortunately it's not always available. The escargot was a disappointment with bits of grit. The mains were all very good. Best was the confit of suckling pig belly. Which was crisp and meltingly tender. Again preorder if you want this as this sells out fast. We finished with a brace of desserts, all well done. Overall a very nice dinner. Larger than normal portions, value for money and highly recommended. A great place to bring a first date as the atmosphere is unthreatening and relaxing. Had a good time.

For the price, this French bistro by les Amis is amazingly good value. We were there for dinner.Ambiance is very classic french bistro, which is great. Service was also very good. Our waitress was friendly and not pushy.Wine - they have reasonable wine by carafe. Two thumbs up!Food: Pan fried foie gras is great. Not the best I've tried, but the best were in restaurants that cost many times of here. So I would gladly eat the one here again.Daily special of butter poached pink trout - so so good. the trout is deboned and so succulent and tender. Perfectly cooked and not dry. Add the french beans and toasted almonds, it has a wonderful combination of taste and bite. Love this dish!Daily special of mussels in white wine sauce - the white wine sauce is great, very flavorful and a good amount of wine taste, garlic and many other goodies. However, the mussels were way too tiny! they looked so shrivelled and sad that I think it totally did an injustice to the wonderful broth.Grand Marnier souffle - 20min wait time, but so worth the wait. Exactly how a good souffle should be. Order it.

oh my, can someone say dessert please? this one's a good choice, the first time I've made it to the lauded bistro du vin - and only for dessert (after dinner at indochilli, just a few doors down).they have a proper, legit chocolate fondant full of dark chocolate and not too much sugar, with oozey batter coming out a nice crusty cake. dee-licious.speckly vanilla ice cream on the side too, but you don't expect any less do you?annnnnnd, a slightly eggy creme brulee with a crackly sugar top browned enough for flavor and satisfyingly charred in a couple spots - pretty good, though there's really nothing to beat chocolate.the top pictures were of the mont-blanc - chestnut, vanilla ice cream, rum, meringue, whipped cream, chocolate pearls & chocolate sauce - and a lot less interesting than it sounds. skip this.so yes, desserts pretty good - and I've heard good things about the food. pretty much worth the calories.

Bistro du Vin is one of Les Amis Group's restaurant that serves classic French bistro food. The place is kinda cool/chic with its French feel.We had onion soup for starters and it was good. Nothing extraordinary, but it was up to its standard. The highlight of the meal was the pork chop. Now, pork chop may seem to be a very simple dish, but it is very easy to screw it up. But theirs was perfectly moist and tender, without being too fatty. The caramelized onion & shallot on top was a perfect compliment to the pork.The Grand Marnier souffle was a very good end to the meal. It is everything a souffle should be.

The food was great and the manager was very friendly and helpful. We had the cheapest marinated beef and I was glad we got that instead of the more expensive ones because it was very good. The Kimchi soup is also great. I think it is pork inside which makes it more flavorful than usual.My Korean fiance eats here for lunch several times per week.

One of the best Korean meals I had in Singapore. We booked in advance and got a private room, this is one of the few places I ate Korean BBQ without having the BBQ smell after the meal.The Kimchi fried rice was savory and was packed with ingredients. The portion was huge and we couldn't finish it, as we over ordered. We ordered the Ginseng Chicken soup and it was fantastic, one of the best I have tasted.The main highlight was the BBQ, the meat was fresh and well marinated. Will definitely be back to try their other dishes.

Family dinner - the restaurant seems to have taken a bad drop in food quality and service standards... The marinated Meat was tasteless but worst part of the experience was there was very little service attention. When the servers wce around, they were rushing around and not paying attention to details... Definitely not coming back

Located at the second floor of Amara Hotel, this Korean joint is one of the pricier places where corporate drones opt for during special occasions like Christmas or birthday parties. Do come dressed in a smart casual attire to avoid feeling too out of place, especially on weekend nights. They serve one of the best beef bbq I have tried, and the best part is there isn't any chance you will mess up any great quality meat with our own less than satisfactory bbq-ing skills, as the staff will do the cooking right in front of you - something like Teppenyaki style but more casual! Their meats are soft and tender but with just the right amount of crispiness on the outside, and is skillfully cut by their waitressing staff from the bone into small manageable pieces. They also portion it out equally amongst those seated at the table, so no ugly squabbles over the last piece! If you're feeling a tad adventurous, you can try ordering a plate of their beef innards, which are various segments of cow intestines. These are slightly more pungent and chewy and takes some getting used to the taste, but is definitely one of the must try items on their specialty list! To end it off, they serve a sweetened persimmon drink to help cool down the body and soothe the throat after a heaty bbq - really great service with attention to detail.

The highlight of this restaurant is that it is a great Korean BBQ place where you can emerge after the meal and still smell reasonably fine (no BBQ smells in your hair and clothes, yay!).The BBQ meats here are of good quality. And their kimchi soup and banchan are also very yummy.A possible downside would have to be the slightly higher price. But on one of the occasions, my friend who had the korean tourism card scored us a great discount=) So if you have one of those, then you should look out for the next promotion period. But even without the discount, Hyangtogol is still one of the better Korean restaurants in Singapore. A must try for all Korean food fans based here.

This is one of my favorite places when I don't want the long queue and I just want some peace and quiet meal time. You shouldn't take a date here since you might get slapped (it's at Amara Hotel so she might get a wrong idea but then again, you might want to. Wink wink).

Authentic and reasonable Korean food. How do you know? There are Koreans! Restaurant's private rooms are perfect for group dinners and family birthdays. The sides can feed an army. Ventilation is good- you don't smell like BBQ!

I don't get the appeal of Loof. I have given this place many chances but everytime I have come, I leave disappointed. First of all, its just really uncomfortable--super hot everytime I have come. Yeah I know it's a rooftop bar and its Singapore, but you would think there would be a bit more of a breeze. They should get better and more fans. My main grip about this place though is the service. There is only one word for it--TERRIBLE. I have never been here and not had to wait an insane amount of time for my drinks. The bar is so disorganized and the staff is running around all the time and not getting anything done. Also, $18 for a beer? Really? Don't come here. Head to a rooftop bar in Club Street instead.

April 19, 2014. Attended  Record Store Day promotional event which  started at 7pm. It is rooftop but on an outside rooftop about one third up the building.  Nice open area and nice bar.    Several of us asked where the small event was being held.  We were directed to what looked like a small table with one tiny box of vinyl with about 3 local artists featured along with some Loof logo wear.  I would not call this mini gift shop level display let alone an event.  A lot of folks turned around and took the elevator back down.  A poorly staged event does nothing to increase your F and B totals for an evening.  Once is enough for me.  Will not be back.

I'm now a big fan of Loof. Pre-renovations, the bar was looking kinda tired. But now, it's suddenly become a lot more spacious, and dare I say it, chic! Loof attracts a working crowd who is not afraid to get down to party. The bar is also becoming an increasingly popular spot for events - come for their weekly Thursday Loffapalooza. The bar spins a dance inducing mix of British bands, and there's just enough space for you to dance - a nice change from the often way too crowded indie nights at Poptart. Service at Loof is also excellent. The staff here are charming and friendly, without coming across as being 'try-too-hard'. All in, you're pretty much guaranteed a good night whenever you come to this bar.

Love this hidden gem in Singapore!  Though it's not on top of a 50 floor skyscraper (it's on the 3rd floor of an office building), Loof is unpretentious, has great eats and drinks, and has a great outdoor patio vibe.Some coworkers took us here for happy hour after one one day.  Drinks and appies were on special ('cheap' by Singapore standards).  Boozy bubble tea? I'm sold!  They even serve it in a bubble tea plastic cup and straw.  The appies were good but the BEST were the chili crab waffle fries. TBH, it's actually chili crab DIP but it was DA BOMB!  Next time I am back i Singapore, I will definitely make a return visit up on the Loof!

3.5 starsWhereas a lot of rooftop bars are snobby affairs, Loof is everything except snobby. This bar has a fun and relaxed vibe. Additionally, the happy hour is one of the better deals you can find in Singapore: glasses of house pours, wine and pints of Asahi for $5++, hard to find a better deal!But unfortunately this bar has also some minor downsides:- the red wine comes chilled (WHY?)- the food menu looks inventive and attractive but has never managed to fully convince. The Ramly burger is probably my fave, but as far as the other dishes I feel like the food is: "nice try but try again..."But overall this is one of my goto rooftop bar's and I have been back several times so when in doubt between 3 and 4 stars, I decided to give them 4 stars cause I think the concept is great, it is decently priced and just because I like it there! Also, when I think about this bar, I cannot help it but  sing in my head: "the loof, the loof, the loof is on fire!!"

Came here with work crew for happy hour; it was a great location with an amenable atmosphere the staff were pleasant but not overly friendly which is odd for a bar.We came to happy hour but were surprised that beer was not really included in the cheap drinks, only basic spirits and house wines; and even with the spirits they seemed unwilling to offer shots and it took an amount of negotiation to get this.We tried a lot of the food, from platters, snacks, finger foods and everything was well made and had a good amount of spice if the dish warranted it.The place was really happening by around 10pm; and it's great that they take bookings so if you wanted to head out at that time you can.

Drinks were rather expensive. For a rooftop bar, it also doesn't have much of a view, since it's dwarfed by every other building surrounding it. Happy hour is ok though.Come with your expectations lowered, and you'll be fine - think of it not as a rooftop bar, but as an upscale dive bar that happens to be on a low rooftop

Need a great happy hour spot or after dinner drinks? Loof is a good call. I was drinking their non-alcoholic Spa Splash with cucumber, mint and apple juice. Light, refreshing and not straight sugar. I was a happy girl. Not on the happy hour menu, though. The food menu consisted of some creative bar food. Chicken lettuce pockets were great, as were the chicken wings. The French fries came in a huge portion. The salad with calamari was awesome and probably the healthiest thing we ordered. Trying to follow paleo diet? This place isn't for you!The atmosphere was hopping with music cranked and patrons enjoying what appeared to be a game of beer pong. It was fun, but a bit tough to hear our company. Single lady? This place seems to be swimming with guys in their 20s and 30s. Just saying. You're welcome!

I love Loof and it's time to tell people why. I'm gonna share it with everyone, cos I'm nice that way. HahahaAlright. So Loof has some really yummy dishes but my two faves are still their chicken wings (damn, super addictive!!!) and their chili crab fries (super Moreish!!!). These are just simply fantastic - like, mouthwateringly, finger-lickingly goooooood. Great wait staff. Service with a smile. My friend and I sat the bar, and suddenly the bartender sends us shooters he created. Just for fun. To let us try. For free. We compliment him on a refreshing shooter; he beams. And before we know it, he makes another round for us. On the house. Like, whaaaaaa?!?Ok. No no. All of that are great. But the reason why Loof deserves five stars is this -- their happy hour deals on house wines and house pours. 5-6pm = $56-7pm = $67-8pm = $7'nuff said. You're welcome.

Great location; outdoor watering hole. Review for the ambience and HH only. I like the chilled vibes and they have happy hour that goes by the hour e.g $5+ at 5pm; $6+ at 6pm etc. ends at 8pm. I missed out on HH this time because of a private event but will be back next time for HH and the food (interesting Asian fusion menu like chili crab cheese fries)!

Loof is great for one reason and one reason only: Beirutin less classy circles, this would be referred to as Beer Pong, but all of us Ivy boys know what the true name is and will always be. Loof is one of the few places in Singapore where you can play this game. the tables are too short and too low, but they have cut outs for the cups which is pretty damn convenient.it's a little bit too hot for me, as it's outdoors on the roof, and me being an American i just can't handle singapore's heat. the drinks are nothing to write home about, as stated, Beirut is the only reason why Loof deserves a visit.

I was there for the Bobbi's Pole Studio Amateur night and honestly I was not very impress with this place because well, the service is just interesting. As the place was quite crowded I had no choice but to take a standing table... I informed the staff that my ankle was injured (due to a sprain) and I hope to have a chair for me.. and the staff had to ASK for permission before a chair was brought over to me. I was like really? Ask for permission to let an injured person sit down? If not, do I have to stand for the whole night? Really makes you wonder. Honestly, I found the place a  bit too cramped for my liking and I was quite fascinated with how the waiting staff kept running about and not saying "excuse me" while nudging their way through the crowd.. I thought they will at least have basic courtesy to say "excuse me." but i guess I was wrong. Drinks wise its ok and I can't say much about the view as its blocked by buildings higher than where the Loof was situated. So yeaps. I guess it's alright?

The newly renovated rooftop bar atop Odeon Towers has been hosting events since its inception, ranging from more high-profile ones such as the Giles Peterson events, and more recently, Tete-a-Tete which is an event where people get together and converse in foreign languages. The bosses of Loof were highly successful in marketing their concept, and have since opened The White Rabbit and Tanjong Beach Club. What sets Loof apart from your average bar is the choice of bar snacks. Tiger Toast ($9) with minced tiger prawns placed atop a lightly toasted piece of bread was very special. Their Loof Flies ($9), which essentially is French Fries with a variety of dips (wasabi, curry, chilli) was extremely addictive. It came in a bucket, and before the bucket was half full, we asked the waiter to get us another plate of sauces. Other interesting things on their menu are crayfish and babysquid, perhaps will try it another day.As for drinks, they have a standard range of wine and spirits. Try their Loof Life ($17), it is most refreshing with the zesty lime aftertaste. The Gummiberry ($17) is a drink I would recommend the girls, as the meringue (which the bartender slightly burns with his flame before serving) looks really pretty in pictures and tastes just as sweet as it looks too. Post-renovation, they updated their cocktail list to feature "Asian Sensations" - Ho Chi Mint, Penang Padi etc. Will definitely go back to try those ingeniously titled cocktails one day.

One of the more touristy places/bars. Drinks- Gummiberry (definitely a must try for ladies who love meringue). It's a fragrant concoction of forest berries, gin, Cointreau and French meringue. - The chocolate martini is an interesting concept but taste pretty average. - The other stuff is pretty standard. Food (typical bar finger food)- They use to have Monday Satays but now it's gone :( their satays were great! - Mini salmon pizza - pretty decent. Ambiance- It's a outdoor bar so it's pretty nice to when the weather isn't too hot or if it's not raining. Otherwise, probably should pass for the night. - The have limited number of indoor seats, comfy tanks with big fluffy pillows (as I recalled).  If you can score one, it's probably a good place to catch up with friends. - Occasionally, they have a DJ too.

I had been to Loof numerous times since they first opened back in the day, and I have to say that the recently renovated night spot is certainly new and improved. Not only have they updated the interiors, the concept has been revamped and I love the strong Southeast Asian slant that guides Loof's latest identity. The menu offers local favourites such as the chilli crab dip with fried mantou (watch out: this is spicy!) and the ramly burger with "secret sauce". Cocktails include Asian-inspired concoctions that take Bandung, Penang and Ho Chi Minh as their muses. There's even a booth by the lift that sells nostagia items from Singapore, and there will definitely be items that will stir some memories in you. However, despite this refreshing and original facelift, my experiences at Loof are still marred by their terrible service. When I was there last, reminding them that our drinks had not arrived was usually received with the apologetic response, "Sorry, the bar is jammed." Given that they've been around for a while and know that it can get crowded on the weekends, I am surprised that they haven't been able to solve their issues. The worse, though, is that they are really sloppy with returning credit cards and change. If you've had a few drinks, make sure that everything is back in your wallet before you leave!

Amidst lanes of asian cuisine and hawker stalls, this American diner stands out with it's visual aesthetic. I'm always a sucker for buffalo wings so when I saw this on the menu, I decided to give this place a try. For starters, my dining buddy had the pork slider that was recommended to us by Cristine (I think she's the restaurant manager, I'm not exactly sure) and I had the 6 piece buffalo wings. We weren't exactly hungry so this was just an excuse to watch sports on the telly, have some male bonding time and kick back with some beers. On tap, Smokey's has a range of Archipelago beer. They offer the regular, the blanc and the dark. I'm not particularly fussy with beer so I went with the dark. If you're into wine. They offer a pretty large selection of bottled wine from Chilli, New Zealand and Oz. Being an American style diner, they had a whole fridge full of import bottled beers that range from $10 to $20 a bottle. You can choose to sit at the bar counter, indoors or outdoors under the big umbrella shades. The mains, which we didn't get a chance to try range from about $20- $30. My buffalo wings didn't disappoint and I wished that I had space for more. It has a nice atmosphere with friendly staff and it's a really good place to enjoy a warm day outside.

I love this place! It is a journey for us to get there but so worth the trip for a good BBQ meal. Every time we come I have to get the buffalo wings spicy style and they have a great happy hour beer special which is the perfect combo. The portions are beyond generous, last time I ordered a side of fries and they came out with a whole plate so needless to say there was plenty to share!Most of the staff are very friendly and helpful, there has only been one time where we felt our server was less than an average standard of professionalism but perhaps we caught him on a bad night.This place is as close to true southern style BBQ as you will get here and is worth checking out.
One of the better barbecue places in Singapore. A pity that the beef ribs were not available due to supply issues. Will be returning to sample the rest of the dishes.

Best American style ribs in Singapore!And good value too.Try the baby back ribs, beef brisket and St Louis style ribs. It's much better than Tony Roma's and the other chain stores. Service is good and the restaurant fills up on weekends with plenty of expats. Ribs are only available for dinner. Parking is an issue as the only parking lot nearby services many restaurants in this very competitive stretch of eateries.

I thought I'll give this place a try. Definitely not worth it. Food is so-so which is fine but my server  Kavin just brought it to the lowest level. Rude, can't be bothered attitude, and has a face as if I owed him loads of money. Go to chuck wagon if you want to have a good time. Great buffalo wings and ribs. Service is excellent. Definitely not coming back here.

This place has great food. The chicken wings are the best I've had in Singapore. Make sure to ask for spicy. The ribs are great. Good beer and a nice atmosphere. It's not the best southern BBQ ever but it's the best in Singapore.

Unfortunately, in my opinion, this formerly great little restaurant has lost its focus. Not only have they been overtaken in the taste and quality stakes by Naught Pigs in Tanjong Katong, but the quality and service has nose dived. Where to start.... the service is almost non-existent, even on a quiet night I was ignored when entering and had to move myself when it started to rain, they forgot my fiends order and we were ignored thereafter, to the extent that I had to stand up and wave a serviette to get someone's attention away from the game on the TV. The food is bland, bland, bland - the BBQ sauce is vinegary and dull, the ribs are minuscule, the fries were cold and the coleslaw was watery slop. The beers are OK and you can watch F1 or a game while you eat, which is probably not worth it these days because everyone seems to look at their mobile phones while they eat. Anyway, go there with mates for an average steak or ribs and to watch a match but don't go there for the food and be prepared to be ignored. If you mention the lack of service they will be sympathetic but are UNABLE to deduct it from the bill LOL - so just ask for a discount. My advice? Don't bother.

This is supposed to be quite a popular American BBQ place around Joo Chiat, and we decided to venture into this place to see if it lives up to its popularity.The place had a great ambience and we managed to grab a seat fairly easily. The staff were very patient and attentive, and made several recommendations to us.I got the signature BBQ baby ribs and suffice to say that I was not disappointed in the least. The meat was very tender and had a distinct smoky flavor to it which I really liked. The baby ribs also came with coleslaw and steak cut fries, and I really liked the fries. The fries were very crispy on the outside and the inside was really soft and smooth. Near perfect fries.We also ordered a couple of beers, and they were good.Overall, this is a great place to have American BBQ at very reasonably prices, at a very comfortable place for a gathering.

The last remaining outpost of the once vast Smokey's empire.  I'm actually glad they consolidated, even if it means that I now have to traipse all the way to the east to get a familiar tasting BBQ fix.  I'm encouraged by the fact that they made the painful but obviously correct decision to scale back on quantity to keep quality staunchly high!  Kudos, Smokey's, you've done a most un-Singaporean thing and kept that eagle eye on the only thing that matters, the honest thing, the quality of what comes out of that smokin' kitchen!  All too often the first victim of a threatened food or drink empire is quality.  Ingredients are sacrificed for scale and economy; foolish and short-sighted, but an understandable reaction.  It takes innards of titanium to serve good food in Singapore in a durable fashion and for doing just that, Smokey's get's my permanent 5-star rating.  I still have a huge soft spot for Smokey's because they were the very first to start serving up serious BBQ, food that not only put contentment in my belly but also my heart.  You know you've stumbled onto something special when you feel elevated after a meal.  Smokey's always did that.  My all-time​ favorite here is still the Angus Beef Rib.  Call ahead to make sure they have it as they tend to run out.  There is usually​ ample street parking and there are parking lots nearby.  Very decent beer bar and bottle establishment right next door.  Very solid stop for some good BBQ and a bottle of suds.

We go here a couple times a month. The atmosphere is fantastic, very casual and very comfortable. They have a half indoor / outdoor seating. I enjoy sitting outside on a nice Singapore day. Pretty much everything on the menu is a good choice with one exception, their Pulled pork sandwich. I don't think they put enough sauce on it, it is too dry. I think they'd be better if they simply didn't just pour the sauce on top, but mixed the meat and then put on the bread. Their beer selection is decent, they've got a fair bit on tap which bumps up their rating. There is also a small craft brew store right next door. As a frequent patron, I'd make a couple more minor suggestions to make their services better. First off, their wait staff needs to be a little more attentive. Sometimes it is tough to get their attention and they don't come to the tables nearly as often as they should. And the second suggestion would be to provide more variety on the TVs. It seems that every time I'm there they either have Rugby or Soccer on the TV. I'm not opposed to those 2 sports, but this place fancies itself an "American" style restaurant. Americans watch Hockey, Football, Baseball, and Basketball, we seldom watch Rugby or Soccer unless were trying to blend in with UK/SG/Aussie crowd.

Sad Thanksgiving Experience,,, We were very excited about trying their Thanksgiving menu... Only to be served 2 slices of Subway quality sliced Turkey for $30 Ridiculous! Will never come back... What a ripoff!!!

Finally made the short trek to Smokies for some home style comfort food and left feeling VERY comfortable (and somewhat homesick). The food was better than expected and made me miss my smoker!We started off with some jalapeño poppers that admittedly were nothing special but still hit the spot. I had a sampler platter of the baby back ribs and pulled pork for my main. The bbq sauce had a very nice peppery hint and the pulled pork had just a touch of Carolina vinegar to it. The coleslaw was a great addition as well. My wife had what she described as the best burger she has had in Singapore. We both left feeling fat and happy!The service was quick and adequate and it was a nice evening so we enjoyed sitting out with the nice mix of couples and families. Definitely will be making a return trip!

The portions are HUGE!  Did I say Huge?  My half rack of baby back ribs had so much meat in it and the BBQ sauce is spot on, but the meat itself is a little dry.  The wife ordered the pulled pork sandwich, which came a little bit dry as well, unfortunately.  Best pulled pork burgers we've had is from Two Burgers followed by The 1925 Microbrewery. There was nice ambience and the daughter was dancing away to the songs although it gets a bit warm with the open concept.  We also had the broccoli soup which was so so, but the fried button mushrooms is very yummy!   The jug of pink lemonade is yummy but we can't finish it either. It's definitely very American; huge portions, ambience, may not be the best tasting food, good sauces.

Friend from Tokyo was craving good ol' American eats and this place did not disappoint! We happened to dine on a Wednesday and much to our chagrin they have all day/night happy hour specials on Wednesdays, sweet! $1 wings, $6 pints. US prices! The brisket were outstanding and I felt a bit nostalgic with the huge California flag and TVs playing major league baseball. The best part: first place in Singapore I've seen carrying Lagunitas beer! My favorite IPA. Can't wait to come back the next time I'm craving BBQ.

A true American restaurant here in Singapore.I went here once over three years ago and loved it, life got in the way and I have not been back since, also because every time I think to come, it is a holiday or occasion and they have long since booked up. I made it back this past weekend and was not disappointed at all. It addresses my homesickness in two categories, unlimited Diet Coke refills, not skunky cans, but soda guns, and good mozzarella sticks. But there is more to this place than soda and deep fried bar snacks, the barbeque is great, real smoked meats with a great flavour. This is not the kind of place that sets out a six pack of sauces to cover your meals with, they just have one good tangy barbeque sauce they use to accent the smoked meat flavour. We did also order the chili, which had a good taste, but might be a stretch to call chili, it was shredded beef, with a sauce and a lot of melted cheese on top along with sour cream and (I think) pickles. One important fact to keep in mind about both of these dishes, Barbecue and Chili are hotly debated US dishes, depending on the region and the proper preparation method, so take my review for what it is worth and don't argue with me about direct or indirect, dry or sauce, spaghetti, beer or beans. I'm just telling you what they serve and that I enjoyed the result, but do acknowledge there are many different ways to go about it. The atmosphere is nice, all open air, but comfortable inside with lots of fans and the recently completed construction next door has I'm sure improved the dining experience. I'd highly recommend this place and intend to plan better and be back before another three years passes.

This is a review of a dinner with colleagues at Smokey's BBQ.When I first arrived in Singapore, a group of colleagues arranged a dinner at Smokey's.  It was for my arrival and for another person's birthday.What I was hoping for was BBQ that was equivalent to the larger BBQ chains in the US and that is what I got.The service was very friendly and professional.I like the open-air feel of the place.  With the hot humid weather, it has the feel of a summer BBQ in the south and the decor plays to this.  It is perfect for BBQ & Beer.tinyurl.com/azxnqexI had the baby back ribs.  They were good but not great.  They were tender enough.  I thought the sauce and rub could use a bit more zip.   For a BBQ place, they were a little stingy with the fries and they weren't that great.tinyurl.com/a9nj6j5The other folks enjoyed their food.Overall - If reviews were only based on food, this would be a three star review.  But I am giving them a bump for friendly service and an ambiance that plays to the cuisine.ps - i really wish they would open for lunch!

street parking is not so easy to come by but free after 5pm.your best bet is the open air coupon parking located at the corner of tembeling rd and joo chiat place.they are non air-conditioned, so be prepared to sweat a little or dress down for the occasion.on tue-fri, during the hours of 3-7pm, they have their happy hour(closed on mon).we ordered jugs of archipelago belgian wit beer @$26.the staff let me try their lager which was also tasted interesting.we started with their sampler which is a combo of breaded button mushroom, mozzarella sticks and jalapenos.the chef special of the day was a venison chillies nachos which had a good blend of flavour and texture.for mains, we tried a full slab of their both their baby back and st. louis spare ribs.the baby back were smaller in size but bigger in taste.buffalo wings were crispy and spicy with a cooling sour cream.we ordered additional coleslaw which were not overly sweet like most normally are.bill came up to about S$45 per person, not cheap.staff needs to be more proactive instead of being asked to provide things all the time.they are probably 3 leaning towards 4 stars but not quite there yet.p.s. a celebrity couple was spotted  whilst we were there.

We've been coming here since Smokey's opened and have to say the food is top notch and only seems to keep getting better. I don't even eat much meat and usually have the salmon options but I'm still really impressed with those and the quality of the fries and salads. You rarely see good cuts of meat in Singapore so it's you're a frustrated carnivore this will be soul food for you. One detail that has made this slip from a 5 to a 4 star rating is ambiance. It used to be all non-smoking (which is how it would be in the US, and we were overjoyed to find a smoke free patio) but that was different last time we were in. The patio began to really fill with smoke just as we finished dinner and we decided to flee rather than stay for dessert. You can go and smoke your brains out like it's 1975 anywhere in Singapore, I really don't think this place needed to stoop to that to keep people coming in.

Been here a few times and the food has never disappointed. This time had the buffalo wings and St. Louis ribs, both were excellent.The service really need to step up there game though. Was getting a but frustrating to never be able to get someone's attention. Hope they can improve the quality of wait staff

Food coma. I came, I saw, I ate. And am about to be in... food coma.The full slab of St Louis ribs and the buffalo wings are all I remember. They were very tasty. And once I started putting the meat in my mouth, I couldn't stop. Smoky, tender, and easy enough to rip apart with your hands.Those ribs came as a full, overflowing plate of meat, and a full slab was enough to feed maybe five of us? I don't know if everyone was as full as I was though *guiltyface*Excuse me while I pass out.

this should be a 5 star... but their parking stinks, since you have to park on the street... this in itself would not make them lose a star, but when we ordered they did not have the hand cut fries or beef rice.  so that was the bad, which really wasn't too bad minus the fact that we missed out.now onto the great!  if you like FOB (fall off the bone) ribs, this is your place!  we tried the baby back ribs and these were better then most places in the US for perfectly tender ribs.  we also tried the brisket.  once again, awesome!now lets talk about their chicken wings.  i have been looking to for a go to place in singapore for buffalo wings and these are about the best that i have found.  the wing sauce was thick with wonderful spice.  the wings were large and fried to perfection and the dressing enhanced the flavor combination.  they were pretty messy but more then worth it.  i will be coming back for beer and wings very soon!an added bonus is that they have a nice, imported craft beer selection from the States.  if you want a piece of home this was a great spot and made me feel like i was any place in the US.if it is too busy, stop by next door at The Outpost Trading CO for a beer or glass of wine

It's a place with nice ambience and good food; we tried the pork ribs, which were really good and a burger which was decent, however the chicken sliders in the kids meal were not really there. They have archipelago draft beer collection and a decent wine list. Overall a pleasant experience

The food tastes really nice! And the set menus look very appealing, though they all seemed to have at least one item that I'm not a fan of. Had two dinners here, one with a party of three and one by myself. This review covers both. When we arrived as a party of three there was a short queue. After a little wait we were moved to the intermediate waiting area where they have magazines and menus to explore. Good way to make a longer waiting time seem shorter. Service was very quick and precise. Orders are noted on a piece of paper (or pieces of paper in case of separate checks), checked if the order is correct and later on checked if all the ordered items have been delivered. I normally judge a sushi place by the crispiness of the nori, but the only item I had with nori (really) were hand rolls and those are somehow usually always crispy even though other nori items may not. Only one of us had a set menu. It looked really nice, but I can't judge about the taste. I really liked the texture of the salmon and the fact that the tamago wasn't too sweet. The ebi tempura was also very nice. The shrimp meat perfectly cooked. When I revisited this restaurant by myself. I choose to be seated at the bar as that would obviously go faster. The advantage of sitting at the bar is that the food goes straight from the chef's hand to you and you can watch the chefs prepare all the food. Disadvantage is that the conveyer belt keeps moving tempting dishes by at about exactly the right height and distance to grab some more (-;I have had a look at the 'fish market' where they sell all sorts of ready made sushi and fish to be prepared at home. The ready made sushi looked so much better that those of the supermarket on the same floor. Price indication (1 person):1 tamago (2 pcs)1 maguro (2 pcs)2 salmon nigiri (4 pcs)1 salmon hand roll7 pcs salmon sashimi1 diet coke SGD $31,50

Sigh. I think I set my expectation too high because my Japanese friend recommended this place. I got the Kurobuta Goma Shabu Udon, and while the pork was good, the whole thing was just... too sesame-y. You know how they sometimes serve you sesame dipping sauce at a Chinese hotpot place? It's almost exactly like that, except in this case the udon was drenched in very thick and creamy sesame dressing. It was nice at first but too much after the 4th bite.
