The place was spacious and comfortable, though. My friends and I ended up staying for almost 3 hours just hanging out. They also have a pretty extensive menu, will probably give it a second chance and try their sushi/bento box.

Simply love this restaurant and the sushi options and its sake, if I could I go everyday to take away or eat in. It's a shame that it is inside of a shopping mall and the fidelity card is also very confusing system, I did not get my free aka and cashier took my card after first prize but there were three more to go.The combo was really good and enough of food for two.

I've had countless meals here and only reviewing now. My fav includes:1) Ichiban Jyu - this is my hubby's fav as he digs the fresh salmon slices and the spicy chilli padi 2) Salad with Jap Sauce - I forgot the menu name of this salad dish but I simple love love love the thick salmon and tuna slices and that Japanese sauce that I cannot find outside!! I have always enjoyed my dining experiences here.

Ichiban Boshi used to serve up very decent Japanese fare. Not any more. I've patronised Ichiban from day one, when they were first located at Novena, and originally positioned as a mid priced offshoot of Kuriya. I dare say the quality (and quantity) of food and service has gone down the drain. Sashimi is barely fresh. Portions have gotten smaller. And quality of ingredients has become mediocre. Barely value for money as it were. Service is harried at best, occasionally surly. And the kitchen misses orders with a regularity that is - frankly - quite embarrassing. This place is a shadow of its former glory. Its mediocre Japanese cuisine at best, and a bright shining example of all that's wrong with over-expansion and mass market mentality. Only eat here if you've no choice. Still better than other mediocre chain outlets like Sakae Sushi or Sushi Tei. But only by a bit.

Came here for lunch with a few friends - no wait at 12.30pm. They have many set meals as options - curry, soba, udon, tempura, rice bowls etc and some hot dishes and of course ala carte sushi. No special lunch deals so pretty pricey for what you get. I didn't try the sushi so not sure that's good/value for money.. But the set menus are overpriced imo (average $20 and you don't get too full; maybe we just eat like pigs?!). Won't be back given so many other Japanese places to check out and with lunch specials.

This is a pretty average sushi place, but my colleagues and I come here for lunch anyway because it's a short bus ride from the office and the prices are fair, considering the quality of the food and the atmosphere.The weekday lunch queue can look a bit intimidating, but exercise a little patience and you'll be seated within 20 minutes. I'm also surprised at how efficient the service is, as we usually go in a group of 6 and everyone usually gets their food around the same time.Their bento sets are pretty good; my only complaint is that the amount of food you get can be a bit too much for someone who's not very hungry. My favorite is their aburi sushi; it comes with around 7 pieces and you get a clear soup with it.If you're not one to wait for a mass-market sushi meal, check out their Kuriya takeaway area. (Note: I'm not sure if this is something that I should separately review, as Kuriya and Ichiban share the same space and cash register, but have different names.) They have an amazing variety of rolls, bowls, nigiri, aburi... basically, a lot of what you can order off the menu at Ichiban, and a lot better than what I see at Fairprice and Cold Storage. I've bought a few things from them before and really enjoyed them!Overall, nothing to go out of your way for, but a decent choice if you're in Great World City.

The Great World City has a rather nice setting and fair conveyor belt sushi with decent service. No one thing is extraordinary - but decent + decent + decent has to be much more thank decent, right? So in summary has a few things consistently right. The set menus look appealing though impatience takes hold and I have yet to try them. The agedashi tofu, most handrolls and Hokkaido cheesecake are worth a try.

This is located in the Orchard mall - on the highest floor. This was another michelin restaurant I accidentally stumbled upon. The restaurant itself is pretty unique, it is a single floor space with 5 or 6 concept restaurants in one. When you are seated, you have the opportunity to order from the many menus. The michelin awards caught my eye and I got the Italian Ramen. It was definitely quite unique - I did not know what to expect. The closest thing I ever had to this was a cheese ramen I ordered in Culver city at Yamadaya and I was not a big fan of that.The flavor itself was pretty subtle and wasn't as cheesy as I thought it would be and that was definitely a good thing. Your mind will try to process the flavor as you take every bite and the proscuitto was a great touch to counteract the milkiness of the broth. I would definitely try it again

Quite an interesting concept, you can order from any of 6 different ramen joints at one shop. I had the shoyu ramen with yuzu, the broth was a mix of fish and chicken stock, and the noodles were made from whole wheat, so a little more absorbent than usual. The yuzu was a nice touch, and the pork was juicy and served in generous portions. Overall, this was quite a nicely done ramen, although it deviated quite a lot from the traditional style. Probably the best ramen among the few outlets on Circular Road. I'd like to come back and try some of the other ramen types.

This shop was so tiny, it can be easy to miss. We walked maybe 5 minutes from Raffles Place MRT along the busy Circular Road. There's 3 other ramen shops along this area so be sure to find the right "Takumen".It has a very cramp seating arrangement, maximum of 5 people per table? So do note, if coming in big groups that you will be split up! The shop seriously reminds me of when I was dining in Japan. The shops in Japan are so tiny, just like this!The Chibakara is one of their more famous dishes that gets sold out. Known as the "Super thick noodles", it reminds me of lor mee. My sister and I ordered this to share. I strongly recommend any lady who comes here to share. Their portions are HUGE!The shop is very considerate of ladies and provide hair bands for you to tie up your hair, to prevent your hair from falling into the soup.For those eating the spicy "ma la" Bingiri, you will be provided an apron, so that you don't split any of the "ma la" oil onto your clothes.1. Chibakara with Char Siew $23.90++The waitress asked if we wanted extra veggies, it's free so we said YES! We were not expecting a whole amazon rainforest in our ramen bowls. We also requested for the "Japanese" flavours, rather than the "Singaporean" flavours, which meant that our soup and broth were stronger. The char siew was soft and tender. One of the best I've had, unlike the ones you eat at Ramen Champion, whereby you just peel off the fat from the meat. This one, the fat is infused together, and there isn't too much fat. More meat than fat infact :)You can also order the normal chibakara for $18.90+ and get one slice of char siew. The noodles as you can see from the pictures, is that they're thick! They absorb a lot more of the broth than normal ramen. It is chewy and has a QQ texture to it.2. Bingiri 17.90++It was spicy beyond spicy. Your tongue gets numb from just eating this. It doesn't come with char siew but with minced pork instead. They provide you with two spoons to eat this. One for you to drain out all the soup and eat the noodles and meat. The other, is like a normal ramen soup spoon. The bowl was laced with onions! So beware those who do not like onions.3. Ontama $2++Instead of getting the normal hard boiled egg, I got the soft boiled egg instead. Strangely it was cold and not hot. But it was nice to spread it over the chibakara noodles, it added more flavour to the thick noodles.Chibakara with Char Siew and Bingiri were two huge bowls by themselves. Bring friends to help share the calories!The chibakara with char siew was on a separate bill, this was for two normal chibakara and the bingiri.All in all, an authentic japanese ramen shop. But I did feel very bloated from drinking just a tad bit of soup which had me reaching for iced water, which thankfully they serve to you.
Best ramen I tasted in Singapore so far.   Bery close to the original tasted in Japan!

It is ok. What is interesting is that you get 6 types of soup broth and ramen in one shop, so it can be a good place if you and your dining companions like different things. One can have his tonkotsu broth and the other a chicken broth.I tried the Sakutaya ramen which is a mix of pork and chicken broth, and comes with a special ramen that is thicker and thus much firmer than the usual. First thought when it arrived: the broth is so so oily! Yes, it is very full-flavored but it is also much too salty to my liking. The char siew is also nothing to rave about. I only ate one of the two slices served.For each ramen, they also have various suggested toppings. So note that the onsen egg is not always included in the standard bowl.The line gets seriously crazy at lunchtime. If you are a ramen fan anyway, come try it. But I think there are too many other good ramen places within walking distance from here to warrant a return trip for me.

This would have been a 2.5 stars if not for the gyoza. Pls chide me for coming to a Jap shop and craving for xiaolongbaos. The gyoza tastes exactly like one!! With the piping hot and delicious soup encapsulated within the dumpling. Place it on a spoon and take a bite of it. The skin is just so thin ala XLB and soup just oozes out nicely. Yum! (I can already see some raised eyebrows from Jap or Chinese in comparing their dishes. Take a chill pill bro)The ramen is nothing much to rave about. The soup is too plain and I had to add a lot of garlic and chilli powder. In fact, it was quite tasteless O_OThe chashu was large enough but just okay. It was cold! Tamago was well prepared with the yolk oozing out too. Noodles were moderately springy. There are many Jap shops nearby along circular road which I'm definitely going to try out. Not so sure about the ramen here though. The good thing - its one of the shops that open late.

It's interesting to see how ramen moves from reality to virtual space and back to ramen again. Japan's online ramen delivery store, Takumen, has launched its first restaurant not in Japan but in Singapore. Small, brightly lit and minimal, the space is just like a typical ramen-ya in Japan, minus the enthusiastic welcome shouts and loud slurping noises. It currently showcases the signature bowls from 6 famous ramen shops in Japan, each prepared from scratch by one single Japanese chef who has amazingly mastered all the secret formula and recreating the same quality to the smallest detail in the tiny kitchen.Ramen is hardly the lightest grub out there and this perfectly oily chicken-broth based ramen by Hajime is no exception. My mouth tells my brain to go on because the broth is pretty flavorful but my eyes tells it to stop because the layer of glistening oil globules is too conspicuous to go unnoticed. This is a dilemma that has yet been resolved but this is the most competitively priced ramen at $14.90. On the side note, the thick chewy noodles did not provide much satisfactory texture compared to the rest, though the "Chicken Char Siew" or chicken breast meat was indeed tender. Ramen Jiro is a ubiquitous Tokyo brand that has earned a cult status for its unmistakable mountain of vegetables toppings and eye-poppingly thick rounds of char siew. However, this Jiro-Inspired Ramen from Chibakara($18.90) looks wimpy in comparison and the meat was tough to chew on the rims, though there was still hearty helping of bean sprouts and sweet cabbage. After giving it a good toss, it does reflect a stark resemblance to our local "Lor Mee". Diners can choose to customize any ramen here for the healthier "Singapore" version (less oil and salt) and we decided to experiment with this bowl. Yet the flavor after customization remained persistently rich and mellow, and I could imagine how robust it would be if we had the original Japanese version. For the Tonkotsu purists at heart, Honda Shoten's Ramen Kurume ($15.90) proved a truly wise investment of calories. It's difficult to argue about the quality of the broth with this shop that hails from Kurume, the city that gave birth to the first Tonkotsu broth in Japan. The bowl is indulgently rich and full-flavored, finished off with two thinly sliced gelatinous char siew that would send you to porky wonderland. But the silver shreds of sour ginger pickles, sesame seeds and crunchy black fungus pulled everything back to reality, leaving a first-rate aftertaste. Can ramen ever be spicy? Yes, when the noodles are not doused simply with mild Japanese ra-yu (chili oil) but attempt a bold and dangerous affair with grinded Sichuan peppercorns that sat afloat the dark red broth. No, I'm not exaggerating to say that this Katsura-style Tantan noodles from Bingiri ($19.90) is a flavour bomb. The spiciness did not really hit at first but built up as I worked on it and my tongue eventually went into temporary numbness. Yet the heat was so addictive and I caved in again. One amazing fact is that the spicy chilli oil is intensified with not one but THREE kind of pepper and blended with soy sauce base instead of sesame paste. To put off the fire in the tongue, one can munch on the sweet crunchy onions whose supply seemed to be endless in the large bowl. Alternatively, top up $2 for that beautiful onsen (soft-boiled) egg, which really helps to mediate some of the heat. On the hindsight, the more commonly seen parboil egg was slightly overcooked that day. The basic version of all noodles here does not come with any soft-boil eggs or parboiled eggs. However, I doubt this is a major problem since most self-respecting ramen fans would not bear to miss it. A second outlet has already opened one day after this first outlet and given Takumen's impressive online inventory of over 100 ramen, it is not surprising if these prized 6 ramen spots will be filled up by new brands in 2015. I wait eagerly to see what will be up next.

I tried the Bingiri, and was pleasantly surprised by the pungent tongue-numbing sensation brought on by the generous amount of Sichuan peppercorns. The waitress asked if I'd like the pepper to be served on the side. I said sure, but ended up dumping the entire small bowl of crushed peppercorn in the broth. It reminded me of Sichuan Dan Dan Mian, and tasted wonderful. Sure the broth was oily, but it was rich and flavourful. Not the healthiest food on earth, but I don't think ramen is meant to be anyway. Service was very good. The staff also offered a paper bib to me since the ramen I picked is potentially a big threat to one's white shirt :)

This place had amazing Dim Sum, we didn't order much else as that is what we were craving.Service was friendly with a smile and they were happy to answer any questions we had on the food.Would love to come back and try the buffet order off the menu. Sounds weird but still want to test it out.

Came here twice. Once on a weekday, the other a weekend. There was an April only promotion - 50% off for 4 pax.My first visit, weekday lunch starts at 11am. So there were 3 of us and the promotion would not apply to us unless we bought a 4th pax and we would enjoy the 50%. The usual price was $48++ per person. And so we did as recommended by the manager.Peach Garden is located in the Amara Hotel in the Havelock area.. Parking here can be pricey if you come on a weekday. We parked some distance away off Chin Swee Road, in the residential area and took a short walk to the hotel.Once we sat down, we were promptly attended to. We ordered our tea and took a look at the menu. The promotion menu is on a piece of print out where one would be required to mark what we wanted.Our first dish was the deep fried Soon Hock (Grouper). The dish was excellent. Every part of the fish was edible, even the tail because it was so crispySoup: we ordered a mix of clear sharks fin broth & thicker version. Both were tastyAbalone & wasabi. This turned out a little disappointing. The salad was rather bland. There wasn't a key item for the eyes to feast on therefore killed the dish for me.Fried shrimp. Slightly oily but tasted great. Would've preferred lighter/less batterSpinach, tri-egg in broth. This dish is a must have.On my second visit being a weekend, there were 2-round seating, one being 11am, the other being 1pm. Therefore be aware you cannot sit leisurely for lunch.The menu had fewer soup items, and a few additional items. This time, the manager told me that the Soon Hock is not available. This was a huge disappointment because this time, we brought our grandmother who loves fish. And we had to order other fish dish.This time, everything was salty. The saltiest item we ordered was the spinach noodle in Mapo Tofu sauce. We returned it. What we ordered that we did not the other day were Indonesian curry shrimp. The shrimps were fresh. Flesh was tender. Curry base was tasty. Would've loved it better if some yew tiao were provided to soak up the sauce.Steamed PaTing fish, slightly fishy, but still quite good. sauce it was sitting in was good with rice.Herbal shrimp. This was so good, we each drank up all the herbal soup that the shrimps were sitting in.Deep fried fish skin. It was good but was a little soft by the time the skins were served.I would definitely come back again but will only do it when there's a promotion. Otherwise, it's just too expensive.

Peach Garden 30% off Dim Sum.The dim sum menu items on the menu has only 17 varieties. Most of the normal dim sum was on it. The most expensive item is the shark fin dumpling with abalone being S$20 per bowl. The rest of the items starts from S$5.80 onwards.Entrance from the car park goes directly into the dinning area. You have to make your way to the front to meet the maitre'd. Service after that was fast. The waitress asked which tea would we like but actually she only had one type, so why bother to asking? Chances of someone ordering the tea she carries is like 1 in 70 due to the number of tea combo there are. There were numerous occasions that the waitress brought us the wrong order, sure the restaurant was crowded but not full.We ordered the normal stuff, prawn dumplings, meat dumplings, chicken legs, steam pork rib, various buns, century egg and pork porridge, fried carrot cake and the $20 shark fin dumpling. Unfortunately the shark fin dumpling was not that good and does not worth the $20. The pork ribs was lean and so after steaming, it was really tough. The various prawn and meat dumplings was average. The char siew pow was above average and was the only item worth ordering. The century egg and lean pork porridge was rather expensive as it was like 7 spoons of porridge only. The carrot cake was also nice but it was $18 and comes with prawns.Overall the food is just average and it was rather expensive But hey this is a after all an hotel restaurant.

This will be a more of a photo diary because I don't even know half the things being ordered and I just eat!Had the AYCE menu where you'll just submit on a piece of paper what you'd like to eat so we kind of went overboard~This tea on the right side is Longan Tea which was really bitter here... & had to ask  for more hot water to water it down ):Shiu yok - So under-rated but tasted so good for some odd reason. Shrimp soup - supposed to be good but it was plain and nothing special. Crunchy fish fins or something like that - which actually didn't taste so bad because it kind of melts in your mouth.Wasabi shrimp dish - Even though I hated wasabi, I still tried it... and nope, it wasn't for me.2 Big pork dishes - The pork on the left tasted really good. It almost tastes like pork shoulder (I could be wrong) and the sauce tasted sweet and savoury.Peking duck!!!!! - Always awesome, not on the menu, ordered separately I believeShark fin that they served - it was under this section of the menu where there were 4 options and each person can choose one. I chose the shark fin. Even though it probably is made out of chicken broth, etc... I still enjoyed it.This was the other option - abalone soup. Yes, that is the abalone which looks so small like a clam. It was totally not worth it.Tom yum prawn soup - Actually so spicy. So so spicy but fills up my soul.Lots of dessert options as well! - Little colourful jellies, hahaha. This dessert is sweet and simple - suits my tastes exactly.Table overall was just so full all the time with tons of food. Was yummy... but like I said, we over ordered. Oops.Peach Garden is a nice huge restaurant with huge tables (seemingly only for special occasions or big groups) and high ceilings. The manager who tended to us was nice but the server was kind of awful. When we asked for items, she didn't get back to us or she forgot about it... & She has this snobbish attitude while serving us.PS: The restaurant may look fancy, but don't expect the washroom to be just as fancy.

We came here for weekend dinner. service was crappy, the waitress asked if we made our reservation and what time slot was given to us?? we didn't receive any specific 'slot', as our booking was at 730pm, but we arrived earlier at 7pm. She then went on saying that if we made the booking over the phone, the person would have told us about our timing to eat - which we weren't given at all?? after that she went and came back and said ok, we could eat and our last order was till 915pm. Really strange service, and food took awhile to come. Food was meh. We paid total for 6 pax, per person at around $30++ after the 'promotion'. I think we could have had better quality food at a regular zi char store with much tastier food. The worst we had was the 'char siew with bones'. Seriously? Nope. Never again.

A lovely spot in the middle of the garden. Great air conditioning and nice ambience. Lovely patient wait staff is a nice bonus. Food wise, the dishes were average. I don't feel wow'd but they are decent. Skip the beef cheek Benedict though. While tender and soft, it was devoid of any beefy flavors.The waffle is worth a mention. Love the crispy outside!

The setting and ambience look nice but don't be fooled. Beneath the shiny veneer is some really lackluster food that's not worth the asking price. Had brunch with family here and service was spotty and the food wasn't timed well at all.  Dishes were coming out sporadically with long waits between them. Someone had asked if they could omit bacon from the avocado wrap but we were told they couldn't because they are pre-rolled. I mean that's pretty lazy shit if you can't make an avocado wrap to order. Ironically I ordered the avocado roll and was among the last to be served even though it was already pre-made and all they did was microwave it. You can taste the lack of effort in the wrap which was a trend repeated among all the other dishes from salmon in broth to the angus cheeseburger - sloppy, lacking flavor, and miserly portions. The only saving grace is that the space is quite comfortable but hardly worth the price. You can get way better elsewhere.

The food is good and the setting in a garden is pretty! The service was bad as it was obvious the restaurant is understaffed for a Sunday lunch/brunch. Ignored 3a few times by the waitresses to take orders. It took the next table to help let the waitress know of our existence. Thought we were smiling and friendly? Or is it our color?

The only bright spot about this place is that it has an outdoor seating area for dog owners and their pets. And that is about as good as it gets. Many have commented about the food, which is just decent, nothing spectacular. I'm not so generous. It was food that I could have prepared at home, and probably would have made it better. And for the price they charge, you do feel cheated. Especially since it's park land, and rental suppose to be lower. And then there's the service, which many point out as a positive. I do agree, the staff are friendly, but they could be a lot more efficient and attentive to details. For example, we were a table of 6, but they only provided 5 sets of cutlery in the little pail, coffee came without the sugar etc. And so there was always the additional need to summon their attention when it could have been avoided. And don't get me started about how long it took to settle the bill, longer than it took to eat my salad!So go, but only if you have a dog. There's little reason otherwise.

Peaceful environment to catch up with friends and family.Sometimes it's the environment that sets the tone for your meet up. The peaceful and considerably quiet environment created a nice, calming ambience which is great for catch up with friends without the need to shout across tables. We had 1 toddler and 1 baby in toll, felt the environment made the kids more relaxed.I have been to this park many times but this is my first time dining at this cafe. We were there at 9am, and were the only customers for quite awhile before 4 more patrons arrived.Almost all of us ordered the grilled breakfast. A decent size/portion for the price. It was enjoyable and filling. Their coffee was not great though. Latte felt bland.The parking lot is directly in front of the cafe which is great. There are also bus stop which are very close by too.Overall, a peaceful cafe to hang out with friends and families.

Such a lovely setting for a restaurant but I was disappointed by the food. It wasn't bad but it could have been so much better. My daughter had chicken nuggets and French fries. The nuggets looked and tasted like cheap, frozen ones - they're so easy to make from scratch! I'm pretty certain the fries were frozen out of a bag too. I had the cheese burger which while tasty, loved the bacon jam, came on a pre-made bun. Again, so easy to make from scratch. Husband had the avocado wrap which looked and tasted great.Service was pretty good and as I mentioned it is a lovely setting inside the park. I'm thinking that if you just did the brunch options the food might be better but I was quite underwhelmed by the experience.

Nested within Bishan Partk- this restaurant is quite a quaint and green departure from the usual restaurant concealed within a shopping mall ... or perched, semi-alfresco, off the ground floor of a restored shophouse! Ordered its eggs benedict, which was described on the menu to come with "perfectly poached eggs" - at below $15! Eggs were indeed "perfectly poached" Sufficiently savory, but somehow lacklustre as a whole! I guess the poached eggs could really do with more hollandaise sauce!Had its sticky date dessert dish which was the only tempting item in the sweets section of the menu! Would give it a 6 out of 10!Lovely service! Good prices! But the place is just a tad too inaccessible for diners who don't drive. For diners who drive - loads of parking lots just outside of the restaurant on a Sunday afternoon!

The canopy garden dining and bar is set within the refurbished bishan park which makes it a nice setting for a weekend brunch or drinks after dinner.Their eggs benedict and eggs florentine are both quite good. I have also tried their okonomiyaki pancake and it just tasted a bit strange. I just didn't get it.I have been here for drinks and would not really reccommend it for the quality for their drinks. But the ambience is actually quite good for a quiet chat. So, just focus on the surroundings and your company, more than the drinks available.Another thing about canopy is that dogs are allowed in here, which is very cool. So there are quite a few pet owners with their dogs here especially during weekends. Hence, if you are allergic to furry cute dogs, it may be a good idea to steer clear during the weekends.I think the food, drinks and service really warrants about 3 stars but I just really like the idea of dining within a lovely park so this gets 3.5 stars! Do try this place if you are in the area.
a really nice spot in the park so much potential but the food was so so. service was extremely slow. cant say id recommend it unless these things changed

Not really sure how to categorize this place since it is a restaurant and cafe in the day that serves brunch and mains, but in the evenings they kinda turn into sort of a 1 Twenty Six type of garden bar/pub. I do know that this is quite a hidden find and a cool spot to visit. Situated in the very pleasant Bishan Park, you can drive in and park quite easily. Walk a little inside and you're surrounded by greenery. It is very cooling even in the day and doggie-friendly. At night it transforms into a great place for some drinks (slightly overpriced) with a easy and open-air atmosphere.For a place like Bishan/AMK, this place just adds a bit more of the chic-ness to the area that is not too heartland. Great for dates!

Got lost in Orchard Central (as always) while looking for a restaurant and chanced upon Sumiya. I glanced through the menu quickly, saw a $4.90 beer, grab-as-much-as-you-can edamame and nabe-style porridge. The latter two items jolted my memory of Wong Ah Yoke's review a few months back and I figured this place can't be that bad if he thought it warranted a review in the Sunday Times.Sumiya comes pretty close to replicating the izakaya experience you'd get in Tokyo. They've got high tables with bar stools, sit down tables sectioned off by...plastic shower curtain things (totally cracked us up) and quirky cartoon masks on the walls and waitresses' arms. We loved the weird Japanese vibe and I half expected a robot with a chain saw to pop out. The menu is pretty extensive and varied. The vegetable based dishes, sushi and sashimi are all less than $10 a serving, while the proteins are around $8-20. The great price points mean you can throw down some beers AND try new dishes without blowing a hole in your pocket. We started our meal with a Singapore roll that was simple but fresh, with crunchy cucumber sticks paired with salmon and roe. Then came 2 salads: a pumpkin mash with sultanas that was absolutely delicious and a "sesame fresh veggie" dish that had dou miao and julienned carrots cooked in a mushroom broth, topped with what tasted like yuzu shavings. Both these salads were light but with a very interesting blend of flavors and textures.With 1 round of beer down, we ordered a grilled amberjack head ($9!!), grilled skewer plate, deep fried squid and oysters. The amberjack head was fresh and grilled crisp, so we picked it clean like good Asians should. I don't think Sakuraya even sells grilled fish heads this cheap so this dish made me doubly happy. The deep fried dishes were decent and i liked the spicy sauce paid on the squid, though some of the batter on both dishes got soggy quick. Finally, the skewers were a little disappointing as all of them seemed just under grilled and lacked the charcoal "wok hei" you normally get from a master kushiyaki chef.Overall we had a delicious meal and the Asahi drafts were, get this, bone cold chilled. Think of all the sad insipid beers you've had that withered in Singapore's heat. Yep our beers came in chilled glasses, a good inch + of head and the golden body was ice cold. I almost weeped. The servers at Sumiya were also very quick and attentive, delivering the food the minute each kitchen station put them out, which is critical when you want hot food to go with your beer. Lastly, it feels like everyone was happy to be at Sumiya, which is something I don't see often at restaurants here. Sure the food isn't fancy, but its executed pretty well. We had an unexpectedly great evening here and if you don't take my word for it...half the house was Japanese, so it must be up to their standards at least!

We were greeted with the drumroll, a welcome chant, and seated near the window with high stools. Note that in the evening, you cannot see the night view because of the glass reflection and the bright internal lights. The food is economical and reflective of the standard. The Wagyu beef skewer is priced at $11 and I wonder if the chef cooked the wrong beef. The Unagi rice was interesting that can be eaten on its own or mixed with soup.

If memory serves me well, this place was better a couple of years ago, when I last visited. Prices have soared. Beer used to be $4.90 (as it should be at an izakaya!) but it's now $5.80 during happy hour (ends at 7pm), and $8.80 after. The fun "edemame grab" used to be $6 and it's now $18!! Whaaaaat.Food was ok, some items better than others. The grill/skewers are good, as was the beef tongue. The current uni (sea urchin) promotion is disappointing. $24.80 for a little tray, which is fine, but then the uni were really small and not particularly tasty. :(

utterly fantastic and amazingly fun izakaya at the top of the stupidly-designed orchard central. today, I bring you a gem. I visited this place for an invited tasting - and the food was great, the atmosphere authentic and incredibly fun - and I know, pffffff. invited-schmited what-had-I-expected.so I sent my parents on to the restaurant the weekend after my visit for a proper litmus test, and they came back full of praise for the place. which makes me really glad - because now I can be utterly effervescent without qualm.I can't quite recall the last time I ever described a place as fun - and I'm not really that sort of bouncy jovial person anyway (I might swing a little too much to the other side of things) - but that's all I thought while there. izakayas are boisterous places - plates of good food and never-empty glasses of beer to lubricate conversations and wind down after a long day, and staff who know how to keep the place cheerful and loud enough for you to do so; this place has all those qualities in spades.as it is, the dishes are both familiar and well-prepared - don't come expecting overtly innovative preparations and poncy arrangements. the food surpasses my favourite conveyor belt place - and while it isn't posh japanese fine-dining, it truly is very good. fresh ingredients simply prepared, an array of comfortingly familiar flavors, and served at a well-met pace.n.b. get the yakitori with the leeks - those were some delicious things. the place is genuinely lovely: a vantage point over town, and a location so exclusive as to be both intimate and cosy - and it truly does remind me of japan. there is proudly-displayed vintage paraphernalia strewn all over - and the place is divided between three historic styles of izakaya dining, onward from the '50s. my memory is a little wonky - so let's call them the low-one (cosy and casual), the tall-one (more glamorous by the floor-to-ceiling-windows) and the outdoor-one (where you barbecue your own meats).the staff were friendly, enthusiastic - and gracious the way only japanese can be. be prepared for a boisterous night - I've been told the asahi is the cheapest here at $4.90 a mug, which might account for it - and if not, it's a welcoming place where you can, like me, clink your water to your friend's beer mugs, and call it a day.and if that all weren't enough, here's the kicker: almost every dish on the menu is priced at less than a tenner. I think that's completely ridiculous (by which I mean stupendously good) pricing, and it certainly made my parents happy when they got the bill. great ambience and good food (and cheap beer, if you're into that) - I certainly will be coming back.

The beef on menu $20+ was decent, the soup for the oysters was so good. However the umi bamboo steamed rice was quite ddisappointing. Their sushi is quite decent too. The fried prawn (not tempura) has roe!

Excellent and a breathtaking view over the city on the 11th floor. This is the only place where I can go back again and again for their grilled cod first marinated in a sort of broth of hich I still want to find the recipe. Also very priceworthy: this dish also has 3 types of vegetables, rice, mushi, miso soup (gindara saikou yaki set) at 16.80!

Service and atmosphere was good.  Unfortunately the bottom line food just not good.  Trying too hard to be too creative.  Went there after reading a lot of great review including this one as well as hungrygowhere but hugely disappointed.  Wished i have photos and can write more details but it was not much i can remember and won't try :).

Cute décor and decent food.I'm surprised there hasn't been more reviews for this place. The name definitely came up often on other sites and blogs. My friend and I came here for brunch on a Sunday. The location is quite convenient and easy to find in the Cathay. The food was presented nicely but tasted just okay. So are the lattes. I would give 3.5 stars overall if possible but round up for the nice and chic design.

Assemble it is.  Place is cosy I suppose really good for people to hang out to eat, talk and perhaps even do some work.  Had lunch there and got to say it was good.  Got the pulled chicken sandwich.  Came hot, nicely grilled toasted with crispy fries and side of salad.  Wife and boy had the spicy beef and the spicy sausage pastas and they were done just rite. Exact words from my better half.... Better value than Cedele!!???  Oh oh....watch out Cedele.  All in all service at least from the recept to the table was attentive and taking of order was super easy.   Best of all water is free this is getting to be a rare commodity.  We'll be back for sure.

Great little place for a quick bite in the Cathay. I opted for a burger and it was very, very good. The fries were excellent as well. As it was Sunday evening, it was pretty quiet and we had no problem getting a seat of enjoying a great conversation. I will definitely go back!

I arrived at assembly ground on a weekday evening and it was relatively empty with a few groups of people enjoying cups of coffee. While I know their coffee is recommended, I've never been a huge fan of coffee. So, I hesitated ordering a cup expecting my coffee addict of a boyfriend to order one that I can try a tiny bit of. However, he surprised me by ordering a pint...a latte it was for me, and a good thing I did too. The coffee was a good blend in my opinion, less acidic and with a great robust flavour. The milk tasted somewhat creamy which made me slightly suspicious but all in all, it was a good drink. My friend also seemed to thoroughly enjoy her ice chocolate, for those who don't particularly like coffee. I had the coney dog, while my boyfriend had the blackened tuna burger and my friend ordered the beef ragout with rosti. I wouldn't say it was spectacular, just a regular frankfurter it seems with a slightly sweeter than expected beef chilli but it fulfilled my chilli dog craving and as such, I'd give it 3 stars. The remaining star comes from the fact that my companions seemed to quite enjoy their food and the decent portions, and we were served by an exceptionally friendly waiter, who was key to our whole experience being delightful overall. To that waiter, you might think you're just doing your job but thank you for doing it so well!

I didn't try their coffee, so no comment on that. This is a review on their The Assembly Wagyu Burger ($24.50). I don't really like beef, but I ordered their wagyu burger nonetheless cos I heard some good reviews about it. I am so glad that I did take a chance cos their wagyu burger was really good. All the burgers menu was served with sesame brioche bun + spiced fries. The sesame brioche bun was very very good. It was toasted with just enough butter, and it was still warm though it had been sitting for more than 10 mins after being served. Since it comes with fries, so for girls, you might have some difficulty to finish this dish. I came there HUNGRY (it was past 12 pm and I haven't eaten anything since morning) and yet I couldn't finish the dish. But I guess being served too much food is better than being served too little food, right? ;pAbout the wagyu beef patty it was very thick - however texture wise it was perfect. I could easily cut & chew it with no problem at all. No complains. Taste wise it was very good as well. It was juicy and just right salty. Though I really like this dish overall very much, I can testify that the fries (though also tasted good) but was loaded with lots of MSG (I got very very thirsty afterwards) drinking like 6 cups of water total. So if you were on diet, it's probably a good idea to just skip the fries and go straight to the burger. My hubby got Ragout of Beef with Rosti (S$23). Based on the menu description, it was slow-roasted angus, rosti, trio of mushrooms, onion jam, creamed spinach, & 62C egg. When it came to our table, the smell was very nice and tempting. However when it comes to the taste, the beef was very lacking. In conclusion, if you're feeling to eat smth beef-y, I vote for the wagyu beef burger all the way!Last but not least the place has ample seating space. They also offer free wifi for customers, however when I tried it (Assembly 1) it doesn't work... :/ [came here on July 11]

The Assembly Ground used to be one of my haunts when I worked in the city area. The coffee was good, meals were a bit pricey and the portions were a little on the small side.  Revisiting this place after about a year, I was disappointed by how far the quality had fallen. I had their set meal - chicken skewers with aglio olio pasta which came with the soup of the day and a choice of drink. The soup of the day was pumpkin- way too sweet although the texture was nice. The main was... a joke. The pasta was barely enough for my 15 year old nephew and parts of the chicken were undercooked. On a more positive note, some of my friends who ordered the ala carte said their food was good. Avoid their set meals at all costs.

This is their Rosti Benedict ($17). Looks good and taste wise is not bad. Friends ordered their Assembly Brunch ($20), Rendang Mac and Cheese ($18) and Rotisserie Chicken ($18). The Rendang Mac and Cheese smells really nice ! The assembly brunch have really a large portion. The Rotisserie Chicken taste good. The chicken is very tender. Once in a while, spending this much.

Chili crab mac & cheese ($18) - 3.75 starsAmerican duck pizza ($22) - 3.75 starsSkinny green tea latte ($6.50)No soy milk here.Note that the prices don't include the 7% GST.Ambience - 2 starsI don't usually comment on this. In this case it's a negative. Way too dark to read inside and the music was loud and annoying. It gave me a headache.

Nice setting and central location that is not overrun with crowds. There seems to be live music at certain timings. The colorful metal chairs are actually more comfortable than they look. I had matcha latte which was fragrant. The latte art is not bad. Food wise the portion and ingredients were decent but not spectacular. It is not a place that I will specially go to for the food but it is a good option if you are in town and want to relax somewhere without burning a huge hole in the wallet.

This cafe is located on the ground floor of the Cathay. It does have a very hipster feel and look to it but is more frequented by random shoppers in the area. Service was nice, friendly and fast (but I struggled to understand the Singlish that the staff were speaking) They serve up some standard pastas and pizzas but also a very good wagyu burger that I can strongly recommend. That is the standout dish as most other things are pretty average. They serve coffee from Nylon so the beans are clearly of good quality and they are pretty decent and making the coffee here but by no means the best place in town. If you are however in the area this is a good place to go for your caffeine fix.They have free wifi and it can be nice to sit and slack in the sofas by the entrance for a while before heading out for more shopping. All in all a nice place if you are in the area but not worth to actively travel to.

Located right on the ground floor of Cathay is this hipster looking cafe. One must wonder how much do they make, to afford rent in such a prime location! But nonetheless, the staff greeted me politely as I walked in and showed me to a table.The bicycles on the walls were very strategically placed above each table with rather dim lighting. The whole cafe has a very rustic feel to it.As I was waiting for the movie to start, I decided to just grab a cuppa and this matcha latte hits the spot! Perfect mix of green tea and sweetness. The aroma itself woke me up! I am definitely getting another cup of matcha latte here! All in all, a great place to chill out without burning a hole in your pocket.

A popular bistro within The Cathay, The Assembly Ground serves up really good pizza and pasta. To top it up, they serve pretty good lattes and they all come with a scoop of vanilla ice cream!I personally really like the Matcha Latte. With a scoop of ice cream, it's really a filling dessert! The pizzas are thin crusted and i really enjoy the duck and arugula pizza. Good for about 3 pax to share together with a serving of a side to add variety to the meal. The idea of truffle fries is always very appealing. Lightly salted with truffle salt, that's pretty much they have to offer here at The Assembly Ground. Not the best that I have tasted, really just enough to give you a good whiff of the truffle on regular fries.More food to try, I hope to be back soon.

Used the Entertainer app to get a free main here - do note that burgers and sandwiches are t included in this deal. We ordered beef cheek pappardelle and a roast chicken, along with some iced osmanthus teas. After discount the total was $30 which wasn't a bad deal. Food is tasty and decent quality, though rather small portioned. The beef cheek was tender, though I would've preferred it in more of a "ragu" style rather than in chunks. I'm not sure why shiitake mushrooms were used - it didn't go quite so well. The pasta was apparently house made and quite nice. Chicken leg was well seasoned and tasty but potatoes were under-seasoned. Overall not bad but without the Entertainer discount, I don't think it would've been worth he price.

This cafe is spacious and has a nice decor and has self service free flow of ice water.What I like is that I can have buy-1-get-1-free for the mains with the Entertainer app here, which means it's only $20 plus for 2 pax. The food quality is okay but the serving of the rosti could be more. The fries are thin and crispy and the type that can get quite addictive.

The coffee is 4-star but the food is miserable so 3 star it is. The place is crowded on weekends and you can leave your name and contact number if you wish to wait for one. They will call you once a table frees up. On weekdays it gets crowded during lunch time but it is not horribly noisy that you cannot hear yourself think. The place decor is typical of so many others with a bit of industrial look and with wooden furnishings. Still a nice place for a cup of coffee, but not necessary a comfortable place to chill with a book. The food menu looks appetizing, unfortunately the sandwich I had was pathetic (see pics). There was so little meat that you could count the small pieces dotting the bread. No wonder I thought I was just eating two slices of bread. Maybe it was a one- off time but I did not go back to try again.

I've been in here a few times, always on my way to see a movie at The Cathay. Why? For me, it's all about the beer. They usually have 2 taps of Archipelago's small batch beer, which is a perfect pre- (or post-) movie drink. The desserts are good, too. I love their sticky date pudding. And I've been told that their coffee is quite nice...It's been popular every time I've been there, so it gets a bit noisy for my taste. But I'm an old guy, so consider the source. ;-)

Edit: deleted a star because a $8 cup of iced latte seriously should not be that tiny! I guess I'm paying for this little dainty sprig of flowers in an empty lemonade jar on my table. I'd rather head to Starbucks right across next time I think. Came here to chill for a few hours before a movie, and loved the experience! Can't speak to the food which some other reviews comment negatively on, but I'll be back next time for coffee & to chat with friends. The ambiance and design is the hipster/woody style and I loved it - tables are placed a comfortable distance away, and the staff don't make you feel uncomfortable for just whiling away a few hours here. They have free wifi & iced water & many tables. It's the type of cafe I've seen at more inaccessible places like Tiong Bahru and Tanjong Pagar, so I'm very glad this is so close to a major MRT station! We ordered 1 for 1 iced cooler promotion ($5 for both), honey cabana & osmanthus. Both were served in mason jars & looked very thin and watery but quite tasty and light! Very refreshing. Also shared brownies, a popular item on the menu according to the friendly staff, which were delicious ($6.50). I was craving a coffee so I also ordered an iced latte ($8), which came with a scoop of vanilla ice cream inside. I was a little disappointed about the size of this - it's a small glass maybe 8oz? (Def smaller than the Tall at Starbucks). But the coffee was strong and good. The baked goods at the counter (not in the refrigerater) are freshly homemade: selections included Thai milk tea cake, brownies, citrus loaf, and they looked very good!!

Definitely a nice spot for refueling or hang out at the Cathy and much better than the restaurants downstairs, Assembly Ground is right next to Assembly Store, which happens to be a neat men's store.  I stopped by for lunch after some shopping and was pleasantly surprised by a very nice lunch set.  For $15, I was able to enjoy a nice cauliflower veloute, a sandwich or pasta, french fries, a small salad, and a iced tea!  Although it's available only on weekdays and there are no substitutions for coffee, it's a great deal, when even a single a la carte sandwich in Toa Payoh can easily cost $14.  I went with the tuna salad sandwich, and while it wasn't revolutionary I definitely enjoyed the lunch set as a whole and went back for some espresso, which was just perfect.  I bet the place gets packed on weekends and in the evenings, but it's also a nice spot for a quiet weekday lunch or coffee as well!

* Last Order at 9pm, do note that cash register will be closed so meaning not even cakes can be ordered.Ordered Smoked Duck Pasta ($17-18)It's done very simply with a medley of vegetables and the duck of course. I didnt quite enjoy the dish(could do with more garlic and seasoning) but my partner enjoyed my leftovers.My group shared Truffle Fries which was more satisfying than the above. The cafe offers a variety of cakes and tarts though the menu doesnt state so.The takeback of this visit would be if you order a burger, it comes with a free pint! Do check with the server on the validity of the promo.

Chic cafe in a half dead mall.They had a 1 for 1 lunch promo for Mondays, choice of pasta or pizza. We ordered a Beef Chilli Fettuccine and a Spicy Sausage and Bacon. The Spicy Sausage pasta was delicious and did not taste spicy at all. The beef Chilli on the hand was just okay. Its a partial service eatery, you have to place your order at the cashier and they will serve your dishes. You can help yourself to some water at the far end of the cafe.Lovely ambience to chill with friends. The promotion makes it affordable to dine there, without the promotion not quite sure if it's worth it.

The ambience is all good; really nice place to hang out with friends.Staff was really patient while my friend and I worked our way through the menu + decide on which cake to get. Price is pretty reasonable. Didn't get to try the coffee that everyone seems to rave about as we were not up for caffeine, but the facilities/coffee machine looks amazing + barista seems professional even with our drinks (camomile honey lemon tea + green tea latte that comes with a scoop of vanilla ice cream).Can't stop popping the pop corn chicken and the assembly brunch's cheesy potato layer is simply addictive. Definitely recommend for people who just wanna chill in a café on a lazy afternoon.

Brought my daughter here today for lunch. We had the portobello burger n spicy sausage pasta. Both are below average.  The pasta particular tasted like instant noodle throw in few slices of beacon n sausage.  The service also was lousy. This is my first time here n probably last time too.
Nice chocolate drink. Noisy place. Expensive mains. Serving so-so lar. Martini Lychee did not give any martini kick at all.

Its a was a girls night out gathering on a Friday Night. It was a fun night catching up with friends and gossiping.Timbre has a nice outdoor ambience where you can let your hair down and enjoy the band, beer and food.Love the pizza they serve and the variety which you an mix and match. The duck pizza is simply too delicious and i simply fall in love with it.It is located near the town area and is hiding in a secluded area with a mini carpark. There is a big carpark located beside it so do not worry about the carpark space.Two thumps up for the relaxing ambience and a awesome band.I will definitely visit this place again.

The best chill out location that holds dearly in my heart. Spent many special occasions and moments here, and with the dopest local band, Goodfellas!Goodfellas played for the longest here at Timbre Substation, and they engaged with the audiences perfectly! (No time for awkwardness man!) Customers can always dedicate songs via SMS, convenient, and you will be sure they read it out. (Seriously there are many other places still using paper and pen for dedication, hello?)Food here is awesome!Signature duck pizza, thin crust, topped with crispy crackers and special sauce!Seafood pizza, good for sharing too!Menu are also updated with new selection of pizza. Now we have green curry pizza and Goodfellas pizza! Dope!Greedy and spoilt for choice can always top up a few bucks for a half and half (choose 2 types of pizzas!)Drinks are normal I would say, your basic beers, cocktails, house pours, spirits, wines.It's my personal favourite chill out place - good food, awesome resident band, alcohol!
Pretty good liveband and pizza. Only bad thing is ventilation is very bad, I was perspiring throughout the whole night.

Pretty much the drinking hole for nearby SMU business students because of the location.It's packed to the brim especially on Fridays and weekends, but sometimes even mid-week too. It's a winning formula: beer, pizza, snacky food and good live music. Pity I don't come too often because of the queue and the fact that it's so frequently standing room only. If it wasn't so warm, I might, but it's part of the attraction I guess!

Good wings and live music nightly. But be ready to talk over the booming tunes.Pizzas are average, some fusion combos that don't really work for me (Peking duck pizza??). Most of the food are forgettable. Don't bother with cocktails here, you can never go wrong with beer though. Service is a little slow and hard to get a hold of. There's always a line on weekends (including Fridays) so buffer at least 20-30 mins waiting in line if you don't have a reservation, or on nights when they don't take reservations.

Good food and good music - don't think you can ask for much more!It's always fully packed on the weekends and even some weekdays so do make a reservation in advance - they don't hold tables for very long either so you've got to get there on time. They don't however take reservations on friday nights, and their Arts House Outlet doesn't take reservations for saturday nights either. Can be abit of a hassle going down only to find it packed, but there are lots of alternative venues that you can walk to at Boat Quay from the Arts House Outlet. Don't like how they don't take reservations, makes it hard to plan for a gathering - its probably the biggest pull back for me.Different bands play every night - so do check out the Timbre website to check out when your favourite band is playing, and what time they start.  It can get a little warm as the venues aren't airconditioned, and I've had an attack by mosquitoes at the Substation outlet - perhaps its the location up on the hill? But I'll surely be bringing some mosquito repellent with me the next time I go there!

This place is lovely to unwind after the hustle bustle of school (for those who are studying at SMU) or for those who would like some good acoustic music to chill to. Their specialty wings are to die for with the crisp exterior, sweet and sour sauce and tender succulent meat. Also worth trying is their duck pizza! I really crave this on some days as it has the right amount of sweet sauce, duck, crispy crackers (not really sure what they call it - but it sure is tasty and crackle sin your mouth) and all served on a thinly crusted pizza. All this downed with a pint of good beer, is simply delightful.

This is the first Timbre I went to back when I was still a teenager, and it's still my favourite Timbre! The atmosphere here is just fantastic, with trees popping out in the middle of the venue, a big stage for performers, and great ambient lighting.You can get some decent pizza here, including the mouth-watering duck flavour. I also like the spicy seafood pizza. Also try the chicken wings.The best part is of course chatting with friends over beer.But once the bands start to play, the music gets really loud so chatting is out of the question. Stick around and listen to the local bands; some of them are really good!But if you come after 6.30pm, be prepared to queue.

So I went there yesterday for dinner--seafood aglio olio with no discernible garlic or chilli flavours, and no calamari? Perish the thought! Though the prawns are very good and I ordered the wrong thing anyway--what you want are the pizzas and the chicken wings. There's a goodly selection of drinks (cocktails, bottled beers etc) and the live music comes on later in the evening so get your talking done before the bands start.

Talking about quality Cze Char, there is always a queue outside Kok Sen Coffeeshop. They have been serving the usual Cze Char Dishes for about 50 years serving good dishes to family. They are one of those who have been listed under the Michelin Guide months ago.If you are tourist and going to Kok Sen, be prepared that this is not a upscale Chinese restaurant but a typical Singapore Coffee Shop place. In the event that the restaurant may be full, you might be asked to dine in the backlane, just beside a small road.If you have looked through the Menu, there were quite a number of noodles dishes with big prawns under the recommendation. However, we decided to go for plain bowls of rice at $0.70 per bowl to pair with our Cze Char Dishes.One of the recommended dishes will be the Claypot Yong Tau Foo. It tasted special to me with special gravy and stuffing in the Yong Tau Foo. Stuffing consist of meat and seafood which stands out from the mainstream ones from YTF Stall and these married well with the sweet addictive gravy.Claypot Yong Tau Foo 巧手三宝煲 - $15 (Small)Sweet and Sour Pork was better than the average but not the best we had eaten. The general taste of sweet sourness was there and the meat of the pork was significant when we bite down the meat unlike some other places, we were short changed by replacing more fats that meat in the dish.Sweet & Sour Pork 酸甜咕酪肉 - $13 (Small)When asked what to order, their staff recommended us to their Sambal Deep Fried Fish Tail. It was the expensive of all our dishes ordered but we had no regrets ordering this for its taste was outstanding and more than our expectations.Sambal Deep Fried Fish Tail 叁巴油鱼尾 - $53 (Market Price)The deep fried fish was fragrant. The spiciness neutralized with the sweetness of the fish tail and together with the thickness of the flesh, I would say the dish was very well executed. Besides Chilli, this Sambal dish was elevated with onions and even cut of pineapples.They accept reservation for at least 6 pax. Though it is an old school Coffeeshop place, I am quite impressed by their efficiency in serving food. Not only that, prices are friendly if compared to the quality of food.

Excellent place for Hokkien style cuisine. Had chili shrimp, Kung poa frog logs, Tofu and egg, water spinach, and beef with onion. Everything was full of flavor! The frog legs were in a clay pot with fragrant chilis. The shrimp chili had silky flat noodles in it. The water spinach was mixed with a delicious sambal. The wait staff was friendly and they have air conditioning.

Classic Singaporean restaurant. The peanut paste fried chicken is incredible. The Brinjal Claypot with Prawns was rich and flavourful. Cheap and incredible street-side Singaporean food. A notch above hawker stalls and a real gem.

After a year of walking by, crowd watching and drooling over what everyone is eating, we finally had the opportunity to try Kok Sen Restaurant, a local Tze Char restaurant that have had glowing recommendations, even recently receiving a Bib Gourmand recommendation in Singapore's Michelin guide. We were surprised at the queue considering we arrived around 5.45pm. Good thing was, the queue didn't take too long, about 10-15 mins but we were parked at the back ally of the restaurant, which was fine by us as it brought an even older feel to an already old restaurant. The menu is pretty extensive as well, with 98 dishes ranging from meats, eggs, vegetables and  seafood. Being our first time here, we had to go with their recommended / blog worthy dishes. Poached Chinese Spinach with Assorted Eggs ($11 or $14) Recommended as one of their must try dishes, the spinach didn't disappoint. Being one of my personal must haves at any Chinese restaurant, Kok Sen does it as perfect as is gets. The spinach was not overcooked, still bright green with a bit of a crunch, which the stock complimented the dish perfectly. Not too salty with the taste of the salted eggs gently infused in and the fried whole garlic adding a bit of a punch, it was really a very well balanced dish. Claypot Yong Tau Foo ($14, $21, or $28)Another well balanced and well conceived dish although I would recommend not ordering it if you were not a brinjal / eggplant fan. It comes with 3 varieties of Yong Tau Foo. Toufu, Capsicum and Eggplant, 3 pieces each. The tofu was nice and soft while the capsicum had a very good punch. But what made this dish special was the stuffing. Unlike regular Yong Tau Foo that uses purely fish paste for the filling, the ones here had a nice blend of fish and prawns, giving it an elevated sweetness that complimented the mildly salty yet very fragrant sauce. A must have with rice. Bittergourd Braised Pork Ribs Black Bean Sauce ($14, $21, $28)The bittergourd was in this dish was braised beautifully with the black bean sauce. It was soft yet juicy with a slight bitterness that complimented the black bean sauce wonderfully well. The pork ribs were very good too, juicy and tender. The only draw back is that they chopped the ribs to very small pieces which was a little disappointing. That and there were bits of bone shards you had to be careful of. Prawn Paste Chicken ($12, $24) One of the best Prawn Paste Chicken (Har Jiong Gai) I've ever had. The prawn past was fragrant without being overpowering. The chicken was juicy and tender and it wasn't overly oily. Key note: it was nearly a whole chicken chopped so you don't get beautiful whole chicken wings but bits and pieces with the bones still attached, which I did like because the bones always have a lot of flavour. Might not appeal to all because not everyone enjoys going through bones the way I do. Overall, I really liked the dishes here. They weren't overly salty and had no or minimal MSG (I am quite sensitive to msg so the fact my body didn't ache after the meal showed that they barely used it if any at all). Despite being a very busy and popular restaurant, there's still something very home cooked about their food which was very nice. We'll definitely be back to try some of their other recommended dishes, like the claypot prawn horfun which was highly recommended as well.

Love at first taste. A friend recommended this very local resto to me some months ago but I never made it here until today. And thank god I did because I tasted the yummiest noodles ever for the first time today.I wouldn't be able to describe their signature big prawn rice noodles as well as it tasted - a brown sauce, kinda spicy and meaty. The noodles were flat and wide silky stuff. The shrimp was fresh and juicy. Think of a horfun x1000000 of wow factor. The shrimp paste chicken was delish. Small bites. Could be one of the better ones in Singapore. It ain't got anything on Ice Cold Beer's but was still noteworthy. Fried eggs were just alright and nothing to rave about. Would order the butter calamari the next time here. Man, I can't wait for dinner tomorrow. It will be here.

One of the best Zhi char places in Singapore. The old guy still manages the place with his son. I can't stress how much I love going to this place. Consistently good. And doesn't break the bank. Must try: Egg Fu Yong (or Furong). It's a deceptive dish that isn't too easy to perfect. And theirs is perfection. Awesome wok hei (heat). Delicious. We fought over it like a bunch of survivors in Hunger Games cos guess what?! We WERE hungry!

After reading some totally awesome reviews about this place, I'm afraid I was a tad disappointed by their food, service and prices.Their food is alright... nothing fancy to get me back again. I ordered the big prawn hor fun and Big prawn mee soup. Tasted similar with a minimum size and cost of $14-$15 per plate or bowl.All I remember was that it was a LOT of prawns. Was even feeling a bit "jelak" after eating so many!If you had to choose one of those, go for the hor fun. It's not bad but quite expensive. The service here was little rude but it's quite the norm with old coffeeshop workers or owners in this industry in our tiny island city. Get used to it! Hahah..Would I recommend it? Well... if you haven't been before and happen to be around the area... sure why not? If you have to travel quite the distance (more than 20mins) just give it a MISS! You won't be kicking yourself and still be able to go home and sleep well....I ASSURE YOU. ;)3.0 STARS

We ordered the prawn hor fun, soup spinach and the shrimp paste fried chicken.  They have a big menu but it's pretty standard dishes.   Unfortunately,  we couldn't order the chicken specials and they ran out of the tofu pot.  It's aite if your around,  but I wouldn't make a special trip just for this place.

Was going to be in SGH area so thought of some C&G (cheap and good) for dinner.  So as usual checked it out on Yelp for this zhi char style restaurant.  Got to say it did not disappoint.  Food came out as described.  Best of all it is not oily.  Note this is within ERP and parking can be a real pain.  I was lucky to get a spot as i came in early for dinner at 5:30pm otherwise i think it will be a problem finding parking.

I join the many people below me to proclaim Kok sen as one of the most consistent/tastiest cze chars around. However, instead of the big prawn noodles and sang her mee ( I believe Wah eke serves better ), I'm more impressed by the consistent good dishes with good wokhei and taste that they dish out. Dishes to note: Fried fish head with black bean sauce and bittergourd. crispy fried fish pieces drenched in a tasty, addictive black bean sauce. Life is Good indeed.Yong tau foo - Amazing fried pieces with their own homemade fish+prawn paste. Add in the sauce and some rice and you'll be on your way to culinary heaven.金龙鸡- golden dragon chicken in direct English translation. The same delicious fish prawn paste wrapped with delicious crispy chicken skin. However, the owner can sometimes get carried away with the msg, leaving me very very parched after meals. Ask the owner to lay off the msg if you want. The food will still taste as great!

im in love.you're simply e best, better than all e rest better than any noods or prawn I've ever tasted I'm stuck on e plate, I savor every sauce there is tear us apart no, no, baby, I would rather be starved - *sings to e tune of 'simply e best' - tina turner* BIG PRAWN horfun... so good i licked up every drop on e plate.  cant believed it took me so long to find this gem.

It is ok. I guess for the ultra hip Keong Siak, this is probably the most affordable.Come early for dinner though. When we sat down for 8pm Saturday dinner, they have already sold out of their famed chicken and and frog legs.Hor fun has a good wok hei. Veggies in fermented beancurd is way too salty. Black bean pork ribs and bitter gourd is ok, not the best out there. Sliced fish with chilli is decent.Price point - the four dishes cost us less than $100.

The food is very affordable, albeit a little salty. I don't think people would complain about the food or price.The service though, is Terrible. I'm never going back. To start off, they tried to squeeze 13 people around a small table. And succeeded, but it was very uncomfortable, and "13" is clearly an inauspicious number.

Even if you don't speak a word of Chinese, just remember these two syllables: Dai Har. Dai Har is the holy grail of Kok Sen, it is what causes the sun to rise from the east; it causes the first flower to bloom in spring; it is why the machu pichu has so many steps. I promise you a mind blowing experience. So remember, Dai Har in its numerous variation (Hor Fun -my personal favorite, Vermicelli soup, Ginger and Leek stir fry etc.) is all you need. Oh yeah, the claypot yong tau fu is smashing too. Don't forget to get that ;)

One dish: Thin Rice vermicelli with Big Prawn. Now say it in cantonese. Dai Har Siew Mai. That's the one dish that matters. Think Fish Soup Vermicelli, but this one has big prawns with lots of roe in the soup and thin "bee hoon" and aced with chilli padi.Ah. Perfect for the wet season.

Is it blasphemy if I consider the beef hor fun here better than Tong Ah's? Sure, they probably use more meat tenderiser than I'd care to look into, but it's SO GOOD. The black bean gravy is such a flavour explosion, coating the noodles to perfection.If you think I'm singing too much of a love song, you got to come by and try it out for yourself.Of course they have loads of other things for you to eat, but first things first... get the beef hor fun.

The first time I went to Kok Sen was entirely by luck and was the first week I arrived in Singapore.  We just had a few rounds of drinks at Vida Vino across the street and was craving some real hot food.  Then we saw Kok Sen on the opposite side of Keong Saik Road.  The food was typical cz char fare but they were all well executed, esp. the stir-fried.   I went back last week.  It was a Wednesday night but the place was packed with people. However, turnover was quite fast so we got a table after 10 mins.  I have to say the quality was pretty consistent and the stir-fried dishes are really good. I agree with one of the prior reviews, that the dishes have good "wok-hei" which I don't really know how to translate exactly but it means capturing the good "chi" from the wok.  To have good "wok-hei", you need superb stir-frying skills with good control of temperature and intensity of the stove fire.  We had the big prawn bee-hoon, the soup was so full of prawn flavor it's like a prawn juice, I guess umami is the word for this.  We also had the pork steamed with preserved prawn paste. This can be a bit salty on its own, but the way we Cantos eat it is to down each little piece of pork with plain rice.  However, I must warn you that preserved prawn paste is not for everyone given its very strong aroma (kind of like salted fish) but if you like it it's paradise.  Their harcheung chicken is also very well done - crispy and flavorful. Again the stir-fried veggies were well executed, another evidence of the superb stir-fry skill of the chef.  The place is not fancy at all but serves good old home-cooked meals, which is an increasingly rare find on keong saik road.

The menu here was pretty extensive and reading thru other people's reviews, we tried some of their favourites:Onion Bhaji - my kids attacked this dish as its a starter. They loved it so much they even ate their deep fried curry leaves that was in it! Hubby said this was like extreme Muruku. Onion strips with Muruku coating! Must eat there, fresh and crispy!Butter Chicken - buttery and creamy and just delightful. My girl was practically drinking the sauce! Mutton Tikka - they didn't have it on their menu but this is a FAVOURITE dish of my hubby's and their chef very generously said yes. So they made that dish specially for him. It was also another hit with my children. Even I was impressed. I have tried many others and theirs was really one of the better ones. Rogan Josh - lamb chunks cooked in spicy curry. I swear mutton is not the easiest meat to handle and they do it right! And the curry sauces are seriously distinct from each other but still oh-so-yummy!!!Aloo Gobi - I was slightly disappointed when I saw their it was quite dry with no sauce. But the taste just knocked my socks off. Seriously one of the best Aloo Gobi I have eaten. I could finish bowls of this!Chicken Biryani - this was served in this deceptively small bowl with lovely spiced rice and tenderly cooked chicken chunks. My girls LOVED the chicken in this dish. And after many spoons of rice was eaten, the bowl still looked kinda half full!! Hub and I was so full after we finished the rice but no regrets there. Butter and Garlic Naans - this was another great dish. We ordered 2 first and then had to top up with another naan. Evident that my girls were just packing the naans away!!!We are seriously fans of this very understated eatery now. The service is swift and very sincere.

The one thing I immediately learned when moving abroad was to immediately find your own comfort food, and I've been delighted to find Tandoori Corner in Balestier to serve as my refuge for those moments I just need Indian food.They do not by any means deliver their food on that "home cooked" taste, it is still very much restaurant-esque with heaps of butter and oil, but suffice to say they are delicious and consistent with their taste delivery.My go-to's, depending on my mood, range from their yellow punjabi daal, to butter chicken, rogan josh, or malai chicken with garlic naan.I usually opt to take out as I don't think I'll ever adjust to this Singapore heat and they do not have indoor seating or aircon, but their service is quick, responsive, and you're welcome to take a seat (I always choose to sit by the fan!) while your food is prepared. I'd definitely pay them a visit if you're in the area.

We live around Balestier. This is our regular Indian go-to and deliveroo option for nights we want something spicy, comforting and something we know is good.This place never fails us. Some of our favourites dishes/ must-try's:Chicken Briyani - This is so, so flavourful! Tandoori Chicken - Mint sauce is dellllissshhh.Butter Chicken - A classic! Daal Tadka - So creamy and comforting Vegetable Samosas - The tamarind sauce that comes with is greeeeat.Aloo Gobhi - Such a simple dish, but done really well. Enjoy!

In general, I'm not a big fan of eating outdoors, but Tandoori Corner is definitely worth dealing with the heat and humidity for some really good Indian food.  I have been here twice for lunch and I have been really impressed with how flavorful and balanced the food tastes, without being overly spicy.  The chicken tikka plater is a great sampler with succulent chicekn and some sides, such as dhal, rice, paneer, and naan.  It's a great set which includes a drink all for $12.  The briyani was also very good.  The rice was fresh and not dry at all, seasoned perfectly and again the chicken was outstanding with a generous portion.  I also loved the fact that they use boneless and skinless chicken, so that's another big plus :).

We got Punjab Dhal (lentil soup), tandoori chicken and garlic and plain naan and samosa. All so delicious! We will make this place our regular once a week spot. I don't give 5 starts but this place deserves it.

This is our go-to place for Indian food in our neighborhood. (Ooh look at me and my fancy rhymes!)I love Indian food, but my husband? Not so much. However, he doesn't mind the dishes here. They've won us over with their butter chicken: big chunks of tandoori chicken in a creamy, not spicy tomato sauce. Mmm! If we're really hungry, we add in an order of butter naan (because if we're going to eat a "buttered" main, we might as well go big or go home!) As for their other dishes, the chicken tikka masala is very solid, and I thought their rogan josh was pretty good too (a bit spicy, though.) Note that they are located in the corner of Balestier Plaza, with outdoor seating only. The service is friendly and prompt. We've been here when it rains, and the staff is pretty good at moving the tables and chairs a bit further in to ensure nothing gets wet. Also, if it's busy, they always manage to pull a table out of nowhere and set it up for you. So far, we've never made reservations and we've been lucky to get a table each time. I do find it a bit pricy for a restaurant that is outdoor seating only, but the quality of the food makes up for it. The portions are just right, as well.Solid choice for Indian food if you're in the Balestier area!P.S. They do have a TV inside the small bar area, but you can't really hear it if you're outside.

Terrific tandoori and naan, try the lamb chops if you have any taste buds at all. They'll blow you away. I'm pretty close to Little India but the food here is good enough that I usually end up going here instead. Friendly service and they always manage to find a table, even when it's full.

I just got back from a week-long trip in New Delhi. For those who don't know me, I'm not the biggest Indian Cuisine fan in the world. However, based on my latest gastronomic experience in India, I can safely conclude that this Indian shop is the REAL DEAL. Not only is this restaurant better than any restaurant I tried in the Motherland, but also the chance of getting Delhi belly is zero. A true win-win for sure. My favorites at this restaurant are the (i) Butter chicken, (ii) Chicken Tikka masala and (iii) butter naan. One has to wonder why one would need to go to Delhi, when you have this shop in Balestier. Two words: Taj Mahal. :D

Being an habitué of travel to India, I was pleased to find a North Indian restaurant in my neighbourhood. You always know the food is going to be authentic when they not only have Kingfisher beer on the menu, but also Kingfisher Strong. Tandoori Corner did not disappoint. The food was excellent. I greatly enjoyed the murgh malai tikka, fish tikka and their assortment of naans. The tikka dishes were note-worthy, and the accompanying mint sauce was as authentic as you can get. I was instantly transported to my favourite spot in Delhi! It certainly is pricey in comparison to other eating places in Balestier. We paid slightly over S$40 for two. It was, however, a real treat and a nice change from the usual fare in Balestier. My only real gripe about this place is the set-up. Situated next to a clinic in Balestier Plaza, there is no indoor sitting space and the tables have been placed along the corridors of the neighbourhood mall. Not very picturesque at all.

This restaurant was recommended by friends and we decided to check it out on Saturday evening.  The restaurant is pretty basic, with tables set up outside the restaurant.
