While staying in Little India we would swing by here frequently for breakfast and mid-day snacks. The roti prata stall was good and the owners are awesome. Tried a masala dosa, appam with orange sugar, and much more but those were the highlights. Masala dosa was unreal. So good.

Here'a one-stop shop (or market) for your food and clothes need in Little India.There's the coffee shop and wet market on the first floor and the clothes and tailoring on the second floor. I come here usually to get my indian costume and accessories and I'd usually bring friends and family to get theirs too. If you're looking for an affordable sari, punjabi suit or lengha and the accompanying accessories, then the 2nd floor is the only place you need to go! There's also a good range of men's indian costumes here from the casual to the elaborate.I got my sari blouse tailor-made here at one of the tailors for only $28. I also got a punjabi suit for $40 and got it tailored to fit me better just next door to the shop for only $8!The coffee shop downstairs has a good selection of indian food next to the wet market and a row of chinese food on the other side.Final verdict: Great buys for Indian costumes and great stop for your grocery and meal too!

India Village or Town or whatever it is called is like Chinatown in San Fran, but it is all Indian.  Incense wafting through the air, crowded, narrow streets, and in the middle the Tekka Center.  Stall 254 has the best prata.  I had regular, cheese, and then chocolate.  The line tells the story of the quality of food here.  Watch the chef work his magic.  Love India town Tekka Center. Ginger hot tea in a small glass mug is amazing, which is tea mixed with ginger, honey, and milk.  Really good meals for less than 3 dollars.  There is a muslim influence on the food as well, so happy to try the different foods.  People just sit at your table in front of you when crowded, so be sure to take pictures of the strange looking man staring you down as you sip on your tea, like I did.  The only bad part is that the restrooms are disgusting, if you can find one, and you have money to pay for the exclusive ride.  Each stall also has a rating for cleanliness.  I only stuck to A ratings and there are very few of these, so keep that in mind.  Tekka Center is right next to the MRT, so it is easy to get there.

Tekka Centre is a Hawker Center near the Little India MRT station. This center has a lot of food stalls to choose from. The levels of cleanliness from A to D were clearly visible for each stall. Definitely go for Level A and B stalls to prevent from getting sick from poor hygiene stalls. My family and I went here twice and this is a breakdown of their food: The mango lassi was not as creamy or as aromatic as I remembered it to be on my first visit here. But, it was vindicated on my second visit. Man oh man. Sweet, fragrant mango. It was so good. The mutton masala was spicy and flavorful and went well with garlic naan.Chicken tikka masala was ok. It didn't really have as much flavor as the mutton. The chicken tandoori was juicy and had a nice bbq taste. But, still not as good as Naseeb in Houston. The fish biryani here was good. The fish was moist and flaky. Lots of curry seasoning. The rice was fluffy deliciousness as well. Indonesian food was great here too. The Ayam Penyet was probably one of the best things I've eaten here. The chicken was fried perfectly and covered in a thick coat of chili sauce. It was so good. I would come again for just this (and mango lassi of course). Overall, I liked my experience here. If you want to get your Indian food fix, with a side of Indonesian, Malay, and Chinese food, look no further than Tekka Centre. Look at the attached pictures for my recommendations on which stalls to get what type of food.

Excellent indian briyani here by bff, locals stays here all their life and indian friend. Chicken briyani at $6, with egg and a cha, the cripsy papadoom. Value for $ and tasty. Better than usual becuase:1. The biryani rice is all yellow, no uneven rice spread like other seller. All evenly cooked. 2. Chicken curry drumsticks is so tender like it has been steam. Usually eating chicken with plastic spoons and fork would render it broken but their curry chicken drumstick is so tender that it just melt in your mouth. Must try if you like biryani and value for $$$$* One thing to note : The hawker centre is rather dirty especially during peak hour and at night when crowded , so just eat and go.
Wow, a huge variety of Indian food and other hawkers. The prices are pretty low and there's plenty of options to appease anyone! A definite place to check out if you are in Singapore.

Wow, this place has literally anything Indian you want to get, from food to clothes to flowers and fruits and veggies to meat and seafood. It is an experience not to be missed and the food center has some amazing food stalls and upstairs a great little antique stall packed full of really cool items.

This rather large building can be a little difficult getting into, especially since the Little India MRT station doesn't open directly into it (which meant we ended up getting a bit wet as we wandered around looking for the entrance). There are two main levels, one of them housing a huge food court, and the upper leven housing a large market that sells quite a lot of fabric. The two times that I have been to Singapore I have wandered around here, especially to look at the fabrics on display, but also to grab something to eat. The thing that I found really disappointing is that the food court is basically an enlarged version of your typical hawker centre, and like many of them simply has a random selection of stalls, which means that they aren't exclusively Indian. That really annoyed me because the main reason I came to Little India was to have Indian food, and in particular curry - a dish that I had a lot of trouble finding.

Great intro to the Singapore Indian hawker stall scene.  Got my table, reserved it with tissue bag (bought for 1 SD from someone walking around), noted the table number and went wild.  Soon all sorts of food started coming!Can't beat the mutton biryani, fish ball soup and the Hiananesse Chicken with various sundry drinks.Cheap and tasty!

We were headed to Little India after visiting Chinatown and Maxwell Centre, but briefly stopped by the hawker area. It feels slightly less "upscale" compared to the other hawker centres, but I like the fact that there is a handwashing station right next to the tables. There are plenty of food options here, but we just opted for something quick: prawn noodles and duck and rice. Overall, good and cheap. Next time I visit, I will definitely try the Indian food, as well as explore the ground level food market.

Good food in the hawker food area - the vade, biryanis, teh halias, and even the prawn noodles (545 Whampoa) Great produce in the wet market area - Chia's for vegetables and herbs that Cold Storage would charge you an arm and leg for (they have everything!); Joe's Butchery for above average cuts of meats (even tripe and osso bucco). Fruits. Eggs. Top notch quality. Follow the sound of the jazz music for the best vegetable shopping experience on this island (at Chia's vegetables, at the back of the store).Cash only.

3.5 got a quick whampoa prawn noodles with soup to start, love the crunchy pork skin and garlic bits in otherwise simple prep.  come here for biryani and other indian dishes. quick egg and onion roti with lamb sauce makes for an inexpensive quick snack

Great place to eat in Little India. Plenty of choices, even Chinese food to my greatest surprise! In terms of Indian food, which I'm always craving form, I was amazed by the quality of the meals for such low prices. I tried the famous pratta stall and it reminded me of my grandma's Mauritian rotis (highest compliment I could give). I also loved the chendol and the chicken tikka. All of these for $5.The place itself is like any kind of food courts, decently comfy and clean. Not enough trash bins though.I definitely need to go back to try more food!

Yea... I LOVE THE TEKKA MARKET!!!!I mean this is one stop shop for fruit, veg, fish, chicken, shark, and who knows what else is in there!  The produce are very reasonably priced and you can get loads of wonderful veg that you cant find in most stores.  and what you would pay for a small bag in Jasons you can get more than a basket!my favorite part is that when i get done with finding my produce i can get some amazing naan and curry from the hawker stalls.  remember bring cash for everything 1) because it is cheap 2) because i have no idea who takes cardsnote that this place gets busy and parking can be a pain so it is easier to take the train, assuming you don't buy too much :)

Home to Singapore's largest indoor wet market, expect to see anything from black chickens to butchers violently chopping up slabs of goat meat to lush roma tomatoes. Fresh produce and variety both guaranteed.You'll also find a big coffeeshop on the ground floor and many other shops on the second floor residing in Tekka Market. Lots of good Indian food stalls to try out, but there are also Chinese and Malay stalls if for some reason, you don't feel like eating briyani. Shops on the second floor are just as colourful. Most sell ethnic Indian clothes that range from simple to elaborate, but there are also tailors, hardware shops and even an antique store! Once I was there with family, mum was admiring a sleeveless salwaar kameez on display outside an apparel shop. Sensing her interest and noticing that she wears the tudung, the staff suggested using the dupatta as sleeves. There was a tailor just next door, and she told us that her neighbour could sew them up within half an hour. Excellent idea! Mum was very pleased with her new outfit.

My new regular hangout: briyani + teh halia has become my regular lunchtime formula as of late!Initially ventured here in search of Teh Halia and this place has since become home to 2 of the best cups of Teh Halia I've ever tasted!Maya Mohan - 2 stalls in Tekka Market, both equally good. The tea was fragrant and flavourful, and they certainly weren't stingy when it came to the ginger essence. In contrast, EVERYTHING else tastes weak and diluted. A must-have at Tekka Market. Get the hot version- the ice just melts way too fast in the cold one, leaving the tea tasting too diluted.AR Rahman - just as nice, though the ginger essence isn't as strong, but otherwise ALMOST as good as Maya Mohan.

Lots of options here, although vegetarian is limited...  there were veggie places, but just very few of them...  tried a few different things from different vendors and everything was fab :-)Great street food, great prices and definitely worth a visit - we'll be going back soon :-)

My mum drags me to Tekka Market every Christmas eve, and there we get everything she needs for all the cooking that happens over the next 48 hours.So take note, this review is regarding the wet market part of Tekka Market, not the hawker side. There're some of the best vegetable/produce sellers I've seen in Singapore. Fresh herbs, vegetables, fruits, everything and anything. There're butchers, (we always end up buying mutton, meat, bones, and marrow), seafood sellers, poultry sellers...I mean, this here is a good and proper wet market, so expect strong smells, wet floors, and things to be a little sticky. But considering I end up going back every year? Trust me when I say it's still pretty worth it.

Really nice shop on Bencoolen near Middle road with quite a following of young office workers at lunchtime. I was lucky enough to snag a small table indoors on this hot steamy Friday.  Alfresco is an option.   I was able to walk here from the Intercontinental hotel in 10 mins tops.  The menu is a mixture of Thai, Chinese and Japanese.  The lunch special was a crazy 6.90 Sing (about 4.90 usd today) and most of the young office workers seemed to be doing just that.  I had too much of an appetite for only that today, so  I ordered off the ala carte menu where there were plenty of veg options for yours truly. I selected kai lan with garlic sauce, black olive fried rice and tofu with bean sprouts which was just enough.  I didn't find any of the options crazy spicy (like Thai Express!) and the olive rice might even be described as plain tasting albeit delicious.  Next time I'll add some chili and soy sauce me thinks.In any event the entire bill came to 24 Sing including my lime juice. A very nice bargain all in all.  I'd say a non-ravenous couple could eat here for well under what I paid for my massive lunch samplings. I asked the owner how long she had been in business there and she indicated 5 years. I'll be back. --Enjoy

A pretty okay small food shop. More Thai than Japanese. Pad thai came in a smaller-than-expected serving so if you like more pad thai, order it in the larger size ($9.90) instead of the small size ($6.90). The broccoli was well cooked too. This place probably does well because of all the NAFA students about.

Went to this place since I always visit the Thai restaurant next to this (Thai Gold) and thought why not try something different. Overall the food was decent, nothing fantastic to comment on. Couldn't really tell the "Japanese" part of the dishes. Price is affordable and appropriate. Not a bad choice if next door is full or closed.

This is a review of a Sunday afternoon solo lunch at Zenso.I was running errands in the neighbourhood.  I was hungry and had a hankerin' for some Thai food.  I knew there were some Thai places in Sunshine Plaza and so I headed over.  I randomly selected Zenso.I was quickly seated.  The restaurant was not very busy.The ambiance is very basic and functional.The service was good but it was not overly attentive.  The staff was polite but not friendly or talkative.It wasn't too long before I had ordered and my food had arrived.Thai Basil Chicken - This was a pretty decent rendition of the dish.  The chicken could have been a little more tender.  There could have been a little more sizzle pop to the flavours.  But, it was enjoyable.  I certainly ate it all.  The rice was well prepared but a little cold.tinyurl.com/cvl7xxmOverall, if you are in the immediate area, it is a decent option for a quick lunch.  But there are certainly better options near by.  There are even better Thai options very very close-by.  There is little reason for me to consider returning.  Everything was just ok and nothing really stood out about Zenso.

The unfortunately disappointing shop of the trio here, despite it looking the freshest and brightest one, but I guess that is the disease of our generation (sorta) - sacrificing proper quality for a flattering exterior...I had the standard thai fare - pad thai, pineapple rice - I don't like to be too adventurous when I'm assessing the standard of a place, and sadly this just didn't cut it for me, especially in the light of its cheaper and much more flavoursome neighbours.I can't quite put a finger on what's wrong with it , but there just wasn't that special quality in their dishes that would compel me to come back. It's more or less what I'd expect from a thai shop in a food court, and not much more. A pretty decent thai iced tea though!

Met up with some mates for dinner and one of them suggested a Thai place at Sunshine Plaza but unfortunately it was packed! So we searched for alternatives along the same aisle and chanced upon Zenso. It has a rather dim ambience so we thought it could be a nice cozy dinner hangout. The restaurant serves Thai and Japanese food. We went straight for the Thai menu since we've been craving it. Was too hungry to look at the menu in detail, we decided to go with the set meal for 4. It came with olive rice, kang kong, sweet & sour fish, beef thai salad, tom yum soup, thai iced tea and mango rice pudding. You have two choices for each 'course' of dishes, you can pick one - those I've listed were our choices - other choices include pineapple rice, prawn salad, lemongrass tea, etc...This set that serves 4 people costs $45.80.The food was nothing to shout about but we were starving so I guessed at first bite, everyone whispered some token praises but once the meal was complete, we realized we've had better thai food elsewhere and if we compared it to the standard thai fare like Thai Express - we all agreed that we'd much preferred Thai Express!The positives: The beef salad was pretty refreshing, The Thai Iced Tea was delicious except there was too much ice! There was no service charge or GST which was pretty awesome.The negatives: They served us the rice last. All the dishes were on the table and we were kinda twiddling our fingers in hunger waiting for the main dish - THE RICE!Food portion for 4 people could be bigger. The dessert portion was very measly, a little stingy on the coconut sauce, we asked for a top-up!Final verdict: Zenso is not so zen after all....

Zenso is a quaint shop at Sunshine Plaza that serves Thai-Japanese cuisine. They offer both Thai and Japanese food and not a fusion of the 2, which would be interesting. Zenso serves Japanese Bento sets and Thai dishes like Tom Yum Soup, Green Mango Salad, Green Curry and Mango Sticky Rice. I only stumbled upon Zenso because the other eateries nearby were too crowded. Looking through the menu, I found the dishes really affordable and decided to give it a try. I ordered the Tori Teriyaki Rice Bento, which is grilled chicken with teriyaki sauce. The Rice Bento came with Japanese rice, teriyaki chicken, coleslaw and fruits. For $6.90, that was pretty worth it. There was nothing special about the chicken though, and it was even slightly dry. I could not finish the rice because there was no sauce and it tasted too plain. I doubt I would return again, although the food here is cheap. There are better eateries around that would grant more satisfaction.

Cultural relevant - Singaporean cuisine in very sweet  old conservation bldg. within a block of Little India.  Refreshing cocktail- nice adaptation of a margarita.  And at the end: Truly Huge Chocolate Slice = delicious.  And then walk around Little India.  Been back twice - worth the trip just for that chocolate cake.

Popped by here for a lazy Saturday lunch, and I felt the food was just okay.Nothing fantastic, and slightly pricey, though I understand costs are rising these days (inflation, guys). The Itek Tim (duck soup) was way too salty - perhaps they could have washed the salted vegetables a bit more? The century egg tofu sauce was too dilute (too little century egg), but what really got me were the raw salted egg yolk bits, which stuck to my teeth and were cumbersome to remove. It was a really pretty dish though.The lamb shank rendang was really good though - I thought it was the highlight of the meal for me. The prawn paste pork, yeah, it was meh. Oh the desserts, the durian cake was a rip-off, and on the light side. I prefer my durian cakes heavy as durian IS heavy.Would I return? Maybe. To give it a second go and order things I didn't try.

Lovely interior!!! Definitely has nice ambiance and decor but I personally think this place is overrated. As a fan of Peranakan food, my expectation for Peranakan restaurant (albeit fusion) is pretty high.We had both overly salted prawn pork prata with keluak and babi pongteh. I couldn't taste the prawn at all though. Babi pongteh would be excellent if they could tone down their salt seasoning just a little bit because the meat was already perfect. Pumpkin soup was decent, edible but not fantastic. Was supposed to go with youtiao but they ran out of it so settled with baguette which is not a good combo actually.Durian cake was the only thing that's above average. They gave generous real durian on two layers.Oh and pandan lemongrass drink was really good and perfect for humid afternoon. So refreshing.On a side note, I noticed the restaurant was dominated by female customers, I think most probably because the food portions were quite tiny. So one star for decor, one star for durian, one star for the lemongrass drink!I don't think I'll be returning. No, wait, maybe just for the drink and durian cake.

Hey you can go to Desker Road for something other the usual eh eh, ifyouknoworrimean. Lovely establishment that does mod Sin cuisine. Nice and fragrant ambience - lemongrass. Mmm. Friendly staff, great service. Now the food. Of note is the buah keluak and prawn prata small bites for sharing. Buah keluak is awesome delicious and this does not disappoint. I wonder if they just went down the road and got some prata from the prata man. Probably not, but I think they should. Signature chocolate cake is decent, and comes swimming in a sea of salted caramel.

Love this spot and I'm thankful to Michelle M. and whoever the Yelper was that posted the picture of the PRAWN & PORK BUAH KELUAK ON PRATA which is one of those few plates around the world that totally made me close my eyes and savor it. Also the Rainbow Cheesecake is the best cheesecake I've ever eaten in my life - and I used to live and eat for a living in the home of cheesecake - NYC.Nearly every dish that I've tried here is a 5+ star taste, all of it feeling like a first-class home cooked meal. The staff is all extremely friendly and helpful and the setting is well-done in this Little India spot.As mentioned above, it is a must to order the Prawn & Pork Buah Keluak on Prata and both the Rainbow Cheesecake or the Durian cake (or any of their desserts really).Other items I recommend:- Lemongrass and pandan tea - Do it iced if you need something refreshing. Very flavorful!- Honeydew Saketini - I've never had as well done a sake cocktail with two flavors that go so well together as fresh honeydew melon and nigori sake. I think I gulped this in two sips!!!! Very light!- Ah Gong Fried Chicken & Ah Ma Noodles - This hit the spot. Homemade noodles and fried chicken - can't go any better than that.- Coconut Affogato - If you aren't feeling cake, try this. I already love Affogatos (vanilla ice cream with a shot of espresso) but doing it with Coconut ice cream is like that windows shattering in your head when you find your favorite dessert can actually be better. Very well done!They have a solid lunch special for a great value which I'd highly recommend either casually with friends, family or on a nice intimate date. They serve lunch until 3:30pm too so you have a lot of time to make it happen!

All their mains were just average. My party ordered the babi pongteh, kong ba bao, vermicille salad, duck+pear salad and Zhu burger. To be honest, nothing really impressive. For desserts, the DURIAN CAKE was the bomb. They are very generous with durian flesh + cream on two layers of very soft sponge cake. The rainbow cheesecake was a complete BLEAH though. It was hard and no cheese fragrance. I don't think I'll come back =/

Tucked away in a historically known notorious area, this little eatery is a breathe of fresh air. Lovely deco brings you away from the bustling roads. Yummy food. Good ambiance. Not very expensive. Really loving the food and the environment. A definitely must try is the cod and seafood chowder. The Barbi Ponteh was really good as well. They say that the durian cake is good but we over ordered so we couldn't have anymore. Food proportion was value for money as well. :)

PRAWN & PORK BUAH KELUAK ON PRATA is over rated and pricey, Try at your own risk. Babi pongteh will taste better if it's not that salty. Pumpkin soup was alright too, nothing to shout about. 3 stars given perosnally mainly because of friendly staffs, nice decor, refreeshing drink- lemon grass pandan, good durian cake.

What an amazing experience at CreatureS. I happened to hear about this place and went ahead and looked at their website. I had a good feeling I would enjoy visiting, so Cristina and I decided to take a metro to Creature's spot. As we walked past, I was hoping to not miss it, but quickly noticed the cool door and rosemary herbs growing in front of the window. I then looked at the sign and seen "CreatureS." We walked into the restaurant and immediately greeted by the waitress, then shown to a table. I already knew what I wanted, so I quickly ordered a bottle of wine, which was reasonable in price compared to other in the city. I then ordered an appetizer of Asian fries, which were thin potato fries served with kaffir lime mayonnaise and we devoured these. As a main course we ordered the Ah Gong fried chicken and Ah Ma noodles which is a crispy leg of chicken dipped in a garam masala crust, and served with chinchalok mayonnaise and la-mein tossed in shallot and light soy. We also ordered the Zhu burger, which is a pork patty marinated with Xo congna. Amazing!!! As desert we shared a scoop of lemongrass & ginger ice cream. I must say, visiting this place made be fall in love with Singapore. I know I am coming back again and bringing some friends with me too.

This place was a good find!  Beware when ordering, sometimes the tablet doesn't register your order - Make sure you double check with the server to ensure it went through.  The half chicken is definitely worth the money and the sautéed mushrooms were amazing!

So been to several other outlets of this French sounding named restaurant. The first time years ago had lumps and lumps of un-melted soup granules ( like those you see in cup-a-soup). At least this shop served without those granules. Overall the soup was salty.The roasted chicken was tender and moist, but the white sauce was rather bland. Probably compared to the salty soup.Ordered side of curly fries and the buttered rice. The rice was good but at 2.50 for a small cup was rather expensive.The dessert creme bulee, the egg contents was like 2 egg tarts but sells for the price of a dozen.Overall rather expensive for a "cheap" French style food.BTW, found no reference of this restaurant chain in France.

Wow, this is what makes a chicken a chicken!  haha, loved it since the first time I visited!The roast chicken is cooked well and the meat is still so tender, made so much tastier with their signature sauce!  Nom Nom Nom... I enjoyed it until the last bit.I tried their Roast Chicken with the signature Mushroom sauce, the special limited edition (during CNY) Mandarin Orange sauce, and their tangy sweet Cranberry sauce.  All three are AWESTRUCK-YUMMY!!!  And I figured that many others might have posted the photos of the shroom & cranberry sauce ones, I posted the photo of the limited edition Mandarin Orange sauce during my visit last time in CNY.  Oh...how I wish they will repeat this very special orderagain!  It was perfect!  XDBut hey, the other sauce and dish they have are exceptionally good as well, so I am still a fan of this French chicken!  Just one comment tho, they should give a bit more of those green leaves on the plate.  "More Green, please!"  Tried the Escargot, Mushroom soup, Sauted wild Mushroom too, and I enjoyed them as well.  And, Last but no least,  there's a reason why people say, "There's always room for DESSERT!" (ahem)  Yes.  ze' TIRAMISU.I'm done for. Love it.  Totally.  Wow. ahahahhaOh yes, and the Creme brulee, is ok.I choose T-I-R-A-M-I-S-U.  Yeah.Overall, worth a visit!

My first time in Singapore and I was trying to eat locally, but after a few days I really needed something simple and familiar. Enter their base entree the roasted chicken with a mushroom sauce and steamed vegetables. The steamed veggies were just average but we're simple and just what I needed. The chicken was absolutely moist and the sauce was just right. I tried the "on special" lemon sauce on my second visit and it was just ok.The service was average but they always said "Bonjour" when a new group came in which was slightly annoying. Guess its there thing.

Smoked duck salad with a tangy citrusy dressing was the highlight of our dishes ordered. Can't go much wrong with duck and orange!Lamb shank was alright. Meat was falling off the bone but wasn't flavoursome enough. Brown gravy that accompanied it was meh.Escargot - well cooked, not rubbery.

After months of wishing and hankering I finally managed to get my bum down to the French seats of Poulet!Queue was long, journey was hard. We waited with rumbling stomachs, but Lady Luck was on our side and we got a seat (mainly because we came as a pair)As I sat and waited for my food, I had this sudden familiar feeling. Like I've been to this restaurant before.And yes I think I have. It feels like an upmarket kenny rogers or a French astons.Sitting next to the walkway didn't help too, as people kept gawking at my meal and probably judging me as I'm a messy eater. Note to self, sit in boothI chose the french onion soup and Poulet d cranberry - chicken doused in cranberry brown sauce and Dijon mustard. The french soup is better than the average soups you would meet. Nice and plenty of onions ...was I being too much as I  craved for melted cheese on top of my soup? And came the chicken.chicken was nice and tender, the gravy was the usual brown sauce with the cranberry.I'm not gonna rave much nor knock it down. Its alright.The price isn't extravagant. The chicken was good and enough for 2 (I ordered half mind you)I still think Charlie Ts chickens are better though.

I should have not gone to this place with my French colleague.  Why?  She said, the food isn't authentic so in my head, I was eating a mediocre food and didn't think my brain worked well to ingest it well.  Alright, that's what I think so it won't sound as bad.  She and I order a bunch of things to share and it really wasn't all that great.  She eventually took me to her place and cooked the same dish.  Then I knew what it's supposed to really taste like.  Yeah, not going back again.

Felt healthy eating the signature chicken dish. The white sauce complemented the half chicken really well. Came to Poulet with two other friends and we all ordered the same thing. I came late but my friends who were queuing waited an hour for the dinner. Fortunately, the dishes were served promptly after we were seated. For 15.80 a pop, this is really inexpensive French food. Will come again to try the other dishes!

Came by this place on a Monday night to celebrate a friend's birthday. Surprisingly, there were quite a few people, which is testament to how good they are.The concept here is that you get a card which records what you choose to drink from the wine machines. I quite like the concept, as you get to try a bunch of things, though why do they charge for a taste... :(Food here is good and competent. Nothing game-changing, just good food and good wine. The Amex platinum card has a 50% for two diners which makes this place quite value for money. Without the card, I'm not sure I would come again.

Our reservation was for 9:45 on a Saturday. We were told last order was at 10pm whereas when we were making reservation through Chope it gave us slots up to 10:15pm, so that didn't make sense. Any way, there were barely any people. We had to order from an iPad with no suggestions, help, recommendations. We ordered a large cold cuts platter which came with only two types of cheese and the waiter brought the bread basket afterwards and the oil, vinegar and butter later than that. We shared the truffle gnocchi between us which was served on a flat plate and had terrible texture and lacked flavor. It was covered in watery gravy which was hard to scoop out for the flat plate. No Parmesan or fresh ground pepper were offered. Looked like they just wanted to close up for the night. We had high expectations but quite disappointed.The place looked like it had potential but sadly failed.

Napoleon is our favorite lunch spot on Telok Ayer. We have not had food this well prepared and presented in Singapore outside of a fine dining establishment.It's clear that this place turns into a big wine bar party at night because things are always a little askew during lunch. No matter, the chef is awesome and the staff are pleasant. I recommend the foie gras starter and tenderloin entree. There a few value priced wines as well along with higher end selections. Along with a la carte dining, lunch includes three tiers of set menus if you are inclined.Check out the wall of plaques parodying famous actors dressed as Napoleon complete with witty thoughts and reflections on alcohol.Will be back as often as I am able.

Unfortunately no photos as I was famished and inhaled the food. The Place:Nice cosy decor, small restaurant, nicely decorated. Seats a bit close together for a romantic dinner, but regardless of that the ipad menus ruin any remaining ounce of romance anyway. Did I mention I hate ipad menus?The back of the restaurant held the kitchen, which was viewable through the big glass window. This is great if you have a nice kitchen and have something interesting to show, not so great if your chefs can be seen playing with their phones or microwaving food. The Food:Despite my misgivings about the kitchen, the food was actually pretty tasty. I had poached salmon with carrot purée, my partner had seared tuna. My salmon was nicely cooked. I usually like salmon rare in the middle but this poached salmon managed to retain its moistness. The carrot purée and (what was a bit like) ratatouille weren't bad either - despite the carrot purée coming out of a plastic container. The tuna was ok. It was blue in the middle as its meant to be, however it really lacked any flavour. There was no char or grill flavour to the fish. A bit disappointing also that it was served with deep fried potato wedges rather than proper roasted potatoes. Wedges seem a bit out of place for a restaurant which is trying to be refined. The Good:- Tasty food- good service- reasonable prices- extensive menu - it's in the Entertainer appThe Less Good:- my plate was chipped and broken. Unforgivable. What if I had cut myself on it?- microwaved foodOverall I'd recommend This place and would come back...but I'd use the entertainer app.

The food here is very good.Came for a business lunch and had the 2 course set lunch for $25. You can choose a starter and main and a drink. Unfortunately I couldn't take pictures of the food as I didn't want to look like a freak during the meeting.The coq au vin main dish I had was fantastic. The chicken was tender and tasty, the presentation is quite nice also. The really unique aspect of this restaurant/wine bar is their tech setup. They have an iPad mini at every table. Our table had like 3 or 4 of them. You place all your orders via the iPad. They have a pretty intuitive program to make ordering a breeze.They also give you a wine card so that you can go up and get yourself a glass of wine and have it keep tabs on this RFID card so you can settle later. I've seen a similar concept at a wine venue in SF before.As a tech geek, love how they are using technology to be different. I'm hoping one day I can come eat here and never see or talk to another human being in the process. (I'm kidding).

First time coming here, the place isn't that big so it's pretty intimate. The set lunch I ordered was definitely above what I expected! Portions aren't too big but quality was excellent! The prawn salad I had, the prawns were crunchy and had a smokey flavour! My calamari carbonara was excellent with a dash of truffle oil used as design on my plate. When I tasted it and found out it was truffle oil.. I wonder why it wasn't IN my dish! Lol... Don't waste the truffle oil for plating purposes only la! I quicky scoop it up and put inside my dish sia... yummm!Good and prompt service. I shall be back one day for dinner... Maybe this time with a date perhaps? ;)

Very ordinary food.Granted we were not hungry and only walked over for some light bites and wine. The wine dispenser is interesting but I just want my wine to be served.We tried two cheeses and the Brie and Comte tasted just like supermarket cheeses. Also tried the beef tatare which was also nothing mind blowing.I would go if there are no other options in the hood. But in this area, you are kind of spoilt for choice.

Solid spot for a weeknight dinner!Thanks to my visit here, I learned a few things about Singapore and life in general:1) I can't read Malay for shit. "Telok Ayer" is pronounced something along the lines of "teh-low ah-yay". Special thanks to the cabbie who dropped this knowledge on me and my colleague as we took a cab from the office to Napoleon! 2) An automatic wine dispenser is a must in my next house. (Miguel, are you taking note of this?)I came here for a double date with one of my super cool colleagues, and it was a good time. I ordered their carbonara, which was amazing (and in hindsight, I'm now realizing why I don't fit into my jeans anymore.) Although I can't remember what everyone else ordered, I do remember them being satisfied with it.Going back to the second thing I learned, Napoleon has this really fancy wine dispenser machine that theoretically allows you to sample all 32 of their wines. I say "theoretically" because each sample does cost you a few dollars, and you don't need to have a bill for over $100 just for tastings, do you? How do they know what you've tried? Well, you get this nifty card that you swipe and then you get the option of pressing 3 different buttons that range from a tasting to a full glass of wine. Then, through some voodoo magic, it somehow gets added to your bill at the end of the night!Definitely a convenient spot in CBD for a casual sit down dinner, with a good menu and hipster lighting (if you're into that stuff.) Worth giving a shot if you're in the area and looking for European fare.

Food - burrata cheese salad is simply out of this world.Wine - a little flat, order a bottle instead in my opinion. The experience of getting wine from the dispenser is pretty fun though.Service - this is where Napoleon Food & Wine Bar fell a little flat. Out of our large party of guests, 3 people were given back the wrong credit cards to bring home. That's 10% of our party size. There could have been a lot more checks put in, such as signature checks or referring to the card in your hand and greeting your customers by name - these measures would have prevented such a disastrous mistake from occurring.

love the concept that you can taste any wine, YOURSELF.  can you image a bar that actually treats you like an adult?!?!?!  they give you a card and let you pour a taste and then your own wine, it is like being at home but with a way better selection.  the staff was excellent and knew there stuff about wine.  so why only 4 stars???  they have an abundance of french wine, which is not my favorite, however i was able to find some wine i enjoyed.  i cant wait to come back and try the cheese and meat plates and some more wine.

This month's Friday's after Five was held at Napoleon. I thought hey affordable wines + partial self-service so we don't have to wait around for tipple + affordable food = winning combination.Surprise surprise, we ended up drinking more cocktails than wine. The mixologist was eager to make drinks that each person was happy with and he used fresh fruit where possible. I'd only ask that the tea be brewed fresh instead of a concentrate. I did manage to try a glass of wine off the enomatic machine and unfortunately, it tasted more sour than the "fruity" notes that were promised. The $8 serving was also quite small, so I felt like I got better value at the bar. Food wise, we tried the calamari cabonara, shrimp and avocado salad and the sous vide steak. The salad was quite refreshing and I loved the grill-kissed shrimp. If only the avocado slices were more generous and there could have been a party on my plate. The Calamari cabonara was essentially a plate of strips of calamari in cream sauce and while that sounds quite heavy, it was rather delicious. The squid is 'rubbery' in a good way and you feel like you're eating a punchy ang moh mee pok. Finally the steak and mash was, how should I put it, gone in 8 minutes with all the sauce mopped up.Everyone had a great time I think and the food and drinks didn't burn a hole in our pockets. The owners were a little antsy about our party as half the people were an hour late and we had booked the entire bar. I guess that's fair considering it's a small, new business but really guys when I bring a party I bring it.
Great wine bar on a pretty little street! Great place to hangout after work and enjoy a bottle or wine or two. The Chablis was gorgeous. Note: french wine lovers only
great lunch sets, huge portion and love the ambience in here.

They say that Geylang has some of the best food in Singapore, and Little Vietnam is representative of one of those. It's surprising how difficult it is to find good and cheap Vietnamese food in Singapore considering how close it is to Vietnam. Even the Vietnamese food all the way in the Bay Area is often better and cheaper.Little Vietnam is the only saving grace. Fresh, quality ingredients and authentic-tasting Vietnamese food at reasonable prices (currently no GST or service charge) makes this one of my favorite haunts to frequent. They have some unique Vietnamese dishes that can't be found anywhere else.They have a good selection of salads like papaya salad and peanut salad. The banh xeo and claypot fish were very delicious as well. They also had some great drinks like the passionfruit juice and vietnamese coffee. You can order to your heart's content and not feel guilty about burning a hole in your wallet or clogging your arteries.

This place gets so crazy busy that it is better to come early if you do not want to wait in line.Not sure why the long line though. The food is ok, but nothing spectacular. It falls into the category of "I don't mind eating it but I won't think about returning". We were a big group and we tried a variety of dishes. Apart from the pho, the bun, both fresh and fried spring rolls (fried ones are better), we also tried the carrot cake (like a plainer version of our local white carrot cake), quails (4 tiny birds for $15 but tasty with some ice cold beers), cockles, gong gong, etc.On a breezy evening, it is nicer to sit outside where you get the evening breeze (plus some traffic smoke). There's parking in the building itself.

Anthony P is so right about this place.  Indeed a little Vietnam in Singapore.  Place was packed even when we got here at 7:30pm.  Pho is wonderful with excellent broth and medium rare beef.  Prices are reasonable service efficient.  Hits for us were the bbq quail, carrot cake, cane prawn, pho the misses were the boil fish, cabbage chicken salad.  Again all in all a good recommendation and a new found place for pho at least for us.
We have been here a few times. Wish we had discovered the place earlier. Legit Viet food and you don't have to go down to Joo Chiat
Food is good. Service is excellent. If want to pick, it will be the price. It's quite expensive.

Finally got my mala fix here. Delicious and tasted just like the spicy dishes we ate when we lived in Beijing. The chicken was tender and I loved all the different veggie options we could add to the pot. Definitely would go back.

Craving for hot pot? Fat Bird offers a distinctive dining experience in this aspect, treating you to braised chicken simmering in generous amounts of delicious sauce. It's very much like a steamboat, with the main difference being that your soup base is dark sauce with a customisable spiciness level: mild, medium, and hot. You can order a host of side dishes such as enoki mushrooms and lotus root, and these will be added to your hot pot upon serving.Since Fat Bird comes from the same people who gave us the unique and tantalising food at Chong Qing Grilled Fish, we anticipated that the spiciness of the soup would be above normal levels, and so we opted for the mild level. The choice turned out to be the right one, for even this mild version sent us fetching for cups of Jia Jia Liang Teh!The interior of the restaurant provides a cosy setting in which you could talk for hours over the bubbling pot of soft, tender chicken. A definite choice when thinking about where to head for dinner with a large group of friends!

This restaurant has the same owners as Chong Qing Grilled Fish, which pretty much assured me of the high standards there. Fat Bird's house specialties include the Chicken Hotpot and Spicy and Fragrant Pork Rib Pot where you can pick your own level of spiciness. Feeling greedy that day, I decided on ordering both the house specialties - spicy kampong chicken hot pot and spicy pork rib pot. I know, both dishes were spicy and were asking for it. The chicken hotpot was phenomenal. The chicken was smooth, tender and had so much flavor concealed within. The spicy broth provided the needed kick. The pork ribs were tender too and probably had been stewed prior to that. The portions were rather large and the hotpots were served on top of small gas stove to keep warm throughout, which was a considerate gesture.

Restaurant is located in a very creative setting- former church in old British barracks in the super hot Dempsey area. The food is good, the service is great and the prices are very reasonable in general. I'll be back for brunch!
I went here for a friend's birthday party. The food was excellent and the space was nice.

This is my first time at white rabbit. Heard allot about it and wanted to give it a try. We had the 4 course dinner. The location is great. At a chapel. Lighting and stain glass made this a very pretty restaurant. Unfortunately the chapel was also an echo chamber, so it was a very noisy environment and frankly spoilt the ambience. Not a great place for an intimate evening. They should install sound dampeners to sort it out. Service was attentive and very good. The food was also excellent. Taste and presentation was all superb. The goose liver came with apple, apple sauce, micro greens and a rich balsamic vinegar. Perfectly balanced to the rich liver. For mains we had the beef short rib that had been slow cooked for 36 hours. Fork tender and incredible flavor. A really good dish.  Mother had the Dover sole. A decent choice, but it came slightly overcooked. Dessert was a deconstructed cheesecake and crepe Suzette. The cheesecake was unusual. Not your typical heavy cake. The cheese was whipped and therefore very light. It came with a raspberry ice cream which went very well. The crepe Suzette was also good, though it was a tad thick and as such had insufficient sauce. Nonetheless it was decent. Overall a very nice dinner. Cost wise, pricy but worth it. Recommended.

I came here for brunch once or twice and was immediately struck by how nice the place was - it's in a lovely chapel and the interior decor is just perfect for a brunchy setting.Before you start your meal you will probably get served up some breads and take that to fill your tummy before the mains come as it could take a while if the place is packed.I ordered the eggs benedict which I thought was really good, it's topped with salmon and the eggs are really big so there's a lot of lovely yolk which comes gushing out once you bite into the egg.I guess that whatever you order will turn out pretty decent, but to me the best thing about the place is the ambience rather than the food. I hear that if you come here during sunset it's even more gorgeous, as the sun sets and its fading rays shine through the stained glass windows.

3 of us went there just for drinks at 7:30pm on the last Sunday of 2014 and had the whole bar area to ourselves. Very pleased to find Monkey47 on the list and it tasted as good as expected. Also had a glass of Havana 7 which was yummy! And had a Kiwi cocktail which was ok. Extra star is for the gorgeous church space. Finished our drinks and walked up the hill to JumboSeafood for dinner.

The food is not the best in Singapore but the place is just nice and cosy so I love bringing guests there.  It is quite relaxed that you can enjoy a long meal with your friends while having decent food.I've been here for both brunch and dinner and their menu selection is quite ok.  For lunch I had the lobster omelette which was a good serving of lobster and a side of truffle fries.  Their truffles fries is served with some shaved truffles and not just sprinkled with truffle oil unlike other restaurants.  For dessert, we had the bread pudding which was quite good but the serving was huge -- good for at least 4 people.Lastly, there is ample parking...

While most people would recommend the White Rabbit as an ideal brunch locale, given its leafy surroundings in Dempsey, I'd say go for lunch there instead. Parking is free and what better way to beat the crowd and enjoy a nice little lunch before heading back into the cubicle for another couple more hours of soul-draining work! The lunch sets on offer are decently priced and taste pretty good as well, a very good value for money combo. What's more service is very efficient and the fact that many haven't thought of the White Rabbit as a place for lunch makes it more attractive (to me at least).

*This review is purely on a Halloween Party held at the restaurant's outdoor bar area and the restaurant's weekend brunch menu.*I was club-hopping on my Halloween night-out ... and found my way to The White Rabbit. It was holding its annual Halloween party, with this year's theme being The Superstition Ball. Seriously, this place is so mad awesome. The whole place is divided into an indoor restaurant (which is more relevant to the second part of this review on its brunch) and an outdoor area. The outdoor area called the Rabbit Hole has a sheltered portion with a full bar and a garden area reminiscent of a cloister. Splendid architectural concept for people to weave seamlessly between the dance floor to groove to the DJ music and the 'cloister' for a cozy chat. Drinks are on a slightly pricey end (I think I paid $21 for my raspberry mojito which was not alcoholic enough ...). But the music was so good - don't expect Top40 hits here ... but an upbeat electrifying remix of hip-hop/classics/cheese/trance. I would definitely be back here for more of its theme parties or even on a usual night-out!So on its brunch menu! Where should I start? The restaurant is a remodeled chapel and with its Victorian-style furniture, its timeless elegance could not be more accentuated. The early afternoon sunlight filtered into the restaurant through the stained glass, suffusing the place with a romantic atmosphere.All the servers were clad in smart white uniform (think the white rabbit from Alice in Wonderland) - and the service was impeccable, besides a slight slip - one of the servers accidentally served us the wrong dish ... but she was quick to realise so (oh well ... but the dish she brought up to us was so obviously waffles not brioche french toast, as introduced by her). Water was refilled very promptly and the manager checked on us to make sure that everything was good.The food - oh man, where should I start again? A White Rabbit's brunch regular brought me here and according to him, the restaurant's signature brunch dishes were the Eggs Benedict and Brioche French Toast. We got a serving of Eggs Benedict each and split the French Toast (the only way to resolve the savoury-or-sweet-brunch-contention).Eggs Benedict with salmon: The poached eggs could be more runny, to create a more volcanic effect upon rupture. Otherwise, the hollandaise sauce was quite good with an adequate zesty punch! The smoked salmon was fresh. The English muffin was nicely toasted, moist in the inside and packed by a crunchy exterior. I am a massive Eggs Benedict fan (having tried tonnes of them in Europe and the States) ... this is premium Eggs Benedict I would say. The side salad (fresh greens tossed in Balsamic Vinegar) was so good as well ... a perfect light complement to the more flavourful Eggs Benedict.Brioche French Toast: The mango bits on top of the French toast were some pockets of bomb! Sweet, but not sickly sweet - that's the WHOLE point of having FRUITS on french toast - they have to be sweet (not sour), but not overly sweet to steal the show from the french toast. Peanut butter and jam were sandwiched within the pleasantly caramelised brioche ... and with the maple syrup (above average, but not so much of a bomb) drizzled over the toast ... I was sent to cloud nine.I enjoyed my brunch experience here tremendously - I am so sure that I would be back here again!Also, for the non-drivers and anti-cabbing peeps, there is a cobbled path, cutting across the grass field (across the road from the restaurant), which is a short-cut to the nearest bus stop (quite a few buses come here). Dempsey Hill is so not that inaccessible after all.I am now a massive White Rabbit fan. *Hops*

Dining experience here is incredible. Though the food and service is seriously lacking, admittedly it was still an enjoyable experience; mainly due to the majestic ambiance. I was simply in awe of the surroundings, making the dinner a very relaxing and enjoyably romantic moment with wifey. Don't mind paying more just to have a memorable moment.

I havent actually eaten in White Rabbit, Ive only been here for drinks. My experience was pleasant enough. The place used to be an old church which they converted to a restaurant and bar. An intersesting concept. The acoustics are pretty bad and it can get pretty noisy inside. However the bar outside, the Rabbit Hole, is really quaint and chill. A nice place to hang out. Drinks are what you would expect from a place in Dempsey--good but pricey. Overall a nice place to chill for a drink.
Fancy place for a meal in Singapore. It's a old church they have converted into a restaurant. Very interesting decor and nicefood as well. It's a good place for a romantic meal or a celebration.

Located in Demsey is the White Rabbit. It has a rather decent sized parking lot which is free of charge for customers. The White Rabbit is more of an upscale fine dining place you would take someone to celebrate a special meal with. It is also a beautifully restored 1930s Ebenezer chapel!The White Rabbit resides in a restored old chapel along the stretch of Dempsey Hill. The historical establishment itself is very captivating in creating a unique 'Alice in Wonderland' concept of The White Rabbit, attempting to bring you to another world. There's a very cute outdoor dining area lined with lounge chairs. The staff explained that they were setting up a wedding the next door. I can definitely see this place being used for weddings. I am glad that they managed to preserve the stained glass from when this was a place of worship. The atmosphere in the chapel was peaceful and romantic with ceiling lights as well very powerful air conditioning systems. So much so, that they staff offered us ladies, scarves or even warm water instead of cold water.1. Truffle Mac and Cheese with mushrooms $16++Though this is an appetizer portion. It had alot of mac and cheese and thus, became very filling quickly. The amount of truffle added to the mac and cheese was very significant and you could smell and taste it. They were generous with the mushrooms as well! The texture of the cheese was warm enough to enjoy and yet stick all the macaroni together.There was also bread service. I picked tomato basil bread, and since the bread is all freshly baked in house. The bread was piping hot and extremely crisp to begin with. The provided butter melted immediately once I applied it into the bread. 2. Deconstructed Cheese Cake $18++This was an interesting dessert. The wait staff asked me to mix up everything on the plate as there was graham crumble, blueberry sorbet and pop rocks all layered one on top of the other. The cream cheese wasn't too sweet or sour. The pop rock popped in your mouth in every mouthful. It was definitely a surprise for me. I enjoyed that the graham crackers were crumbles instead of a hard crust, that you would find in any typical cheesecake. This way, you could enjoy the graham crackers bit by bit.3. Chocolate Fondant $16++The chocolate fondant consisted of a caramel core lava cake with fruits and banana and rum ice cream. The lava cake wasn't moist on the exterior, but rather it was bread crust like. On the inside, was a small pocket of caramel that flowed out like liquid gold! The banana and rum ice cream was full of creamy goodness. I guess to compliment all the sweet stuff, all the fruits provided were sour?All in all, a very beautiful place to spend time with your loved ones. The food and the ambience are both top notch!

Typical brunch place. Their truffle Mac and cheese was absolutely heavenly. I've been meaning to eat here for a while, and I'm so glad we finally came here! It was most certainly an enjoyable experience. The place was really quiet, and quaint. Love the fact that it kept the original structure of the church! The boyfriend and I are thinking of hosting our reception here; only set back is that it seats 120pax max, which isn't enough to hold all our guests!

Although I had my doubts about coming here because of all the mixed reviews, I had a really enjoyable dinner!Service:Our waitress was very welcoming and our servers were very attentive. When they offered us complementary bread they even came back to ask if we wanted seconds.I really liked their TOMATO BASIL BREAD which was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft and warm on the inside. The bits of tomato and basil reminded me of pizza bread. Food: TRUFFLED MAC & CHEESE WITH MUSHROOM - highly recommend**We asked for it to be served as a starter and it was delicious!! Probably my favorite dish of the night.ALASKAN KING CRAB TAGLIATELLE - I ordered the appetizer size and the portion was pretty filling. I thought the dish itself was satisfactory. I liked how the sauce was light and the bits of crab made the dish more flavorful. Personally, I would have wanted more bits of crab but it probably wasn't as much since I ordered the appetizer portion. The pasta was also a little harder than I would have personally liked. MUSHROOM RAVIOLI -I didn't try it but my friend said she enjoyed it!Decor:It's understandable as to why so many people compliment this restaurant. The interior decor is breathtaking!! The abundance of candles and dim lighting makes for a very romantic atmosphere. The bar which is located outside on the patio (the rabbit hole) is also thoughtfully furnished. It's a very cute area. At night, they light up their walkway leading to the bar which adds to the whole romantic vibe.  Plus it's also perfect for taking photos.

One of my favorite restaurants in Singapore! The chapel setting is beautiful and creates a peaceful ambiance despite a full dining room. I have yet to be disappointed by the food, but I especially enjoy the roasted black truffle chicken (come early, the supply does run out) and the truffle mac and cheese. Definitely order the crepes suzette for a table-side preparation. The drinks are also delicious and should be popular for gin lovers, given the relationship The Rabbit Hole. Aside from the the food, the service consistently been wonderful!

We had gone for the set lunch at the White Rabbit. As always, the place is enchanting because it was an old church. The stained coloured glass is always nice to stare at if you would like to avoid some conversation with whoever you are having a meal with. HahahaThe appetizer was nothing to shout out about as I had a salad printemps and a few of the rest had the salad nicoise. I had the pork collar, which I think was quite a fatty piece of meat. I wouldn't recommend this to any of my girlfriends seriously. A few of us had the seabass that came in a pot and wrapped in plastic bag, which was interesting. I think they also say that the seabass taste good.The side dishes we have ordered, apart from the set lunch were good, especially the truffled mac and cheese. The portion was really tiny. A portion could serve 3 people, I believe.  We also ordered grilled asparagus and fries which were average in my opinion. It is definitely a lovely ambience for a date night or even just a girls' night out sort of place.

The ambience is nice but didn't like the overall experience. The serving size is actually tiny, I got a fish main and wasn't impressed. Definitely overpriced. And the service was really bad. We asked for ketchup with the fries and the server got chilli sauce, 3 times!! We kept saying we asked for ketchup and they would go back and bring chilli sauce, 3 times. Just insane.

Firstly, 3 stars is an average of the overall experience at white rabbit.4 stars - the food is delicious, however overpriced. the drinks are amazing, I highly recommend trying their gin and tonic, but be warned it's displayed as a girly drink here.1 star - the service for some reason is not top notch. after asking for a pen to help them divide the bill up exactly for those paying with credit cards, and giving the pen back, the guy asked for his pen back. It's just a pen dude, come on. Even if I were to take it, what's the big deal? I wouldn't. It's just a pen. 5 stars - the venue really is amazing. It's just a shame the service can't live up to the food and venue. I really wouldn't mind paying more for food if the service was superb. I think that's one thing Singapore needs to work on, the customer service. For some reason, they're a little Chinese in the service sense where they won't take the time to make sure the customer is satisfied. They just get things done and that's it k thanks bye. No thank you.

I was very excited to have lunch at The White Rabbit. The setting is lovely. I went with several ladies for lunch on a Friday. The lunch set offers a two or a three course option. I chose the two course option. I started with the scallops. The scallops were absolute perfection. They were in a delicious sauce that was thick and rich. I should have ordered two orders of scallops and that probably would have been a perfect meal. I selected the pork belly as my main course. I was rather disappointed in it. It was fairly flavourless and way too fatty. The White Rabbit staff was attentive and kind. We had a large group and they did everything they could to accommodate us comfortably. I am not sure whether or not I will be back. I don't feel like anything was amazing enough to draw me back. However, if you are in Singapore, I do recommend trying it, if nothing else for the lovely setting.

First, I had made an error and made the reservation for the wrong evening.  I know.   I know.  It isn't easy to do but I did it.They did not have an issue and still seated us right away.  Luckily, the restaurant was not packed that evening.The service was actually impeccable throughout the entire meal.  It was professional.  It was polite.  It was timely.  The servers were there when you needed them but they were not constantly interrupting the meal.The room is a very impressive and commanding room.   The transformation from church to restaurant has really worked.If service and ambiance were the only factors, this would have been a four or even five star experience.In the end though, food is the primary factor.  There were some weaknesses here.  Unfortunately, the key one was with my main dish and it was quite severe.The Bread - I have to say the bread was amazing.  I chose the baguette.   My friend selected another type of roll.  I loved mine.  She loved hers.  It left us begging for more and we were obliged.tinyurl.com/8wrabfeBurrata and Tomatoes - The burrata was creamy goodness.  Unfortunately, the tomatoes were overly acidic and lacked any sweetness.tinyurl.com/9qncbhjTagliatelle w Alaskan king crab, kombu - My friend ordered the tagliatelle.  She really enjoyed it.  First, she simply ate all of the crab.  Then she ate the pasta.  i thought she was going to lick the plate.tinyurl.com/9y9rgg7Butler's Steak - First, the steak in butler's steak is basically roast beef.  As we learn from our mothers, it isn't hard to overcook it and end up with a very dry piece of meat.  That is what happened with by butler's steak at White Rabbit.I must also add; I love and I mean love bone marrow.  But, there was just a "unique" flavor with the bone-marrow.  In this case, unique does not mean enjoyable.  At least, it wasn't enjoyable to me.i did enjoy the vegetables.tinyurl.com/8jtpk97I basically just toughed my way through the main.If I ever return, I am going to share the Côte de Boeuf.with someone.  It is sliced table side.  it is 1 kilogram.  It was served at a table adjacent to ours and it looked delicious.Overall, White Rabbit is an amazing space with extremely good service.  But, I can not overlook the fact that my main course was difficult to eat.  As for returning, I wouldn't say definitely no.  But there are so many other restaurants to try.  In Singapore, for the most part, a restaurant only gets one shot to make an impression and get it right.(additional note: we took a walk around "the rabbit hole".  this is the bar in back.  it looked like a lovely spot to have a glass of wine or cocktail.)

possibly the most beautifully gorgeous place to brunch, lunch, or wine and dine in singapore. this is my first return to the white rabbit after a visit years ago, though not from lack of want. it's as lovely as ever, with decent food and a wonderful ambience.prices aren't cheap, but the cooking is acceptable - and really, you're here for the overall experience, which they excel at.the brunch menu is small but serviceable, with easy egg dishes and more involved ones like potato rosti with smoked salmon. I particularly enjoyed the latter - smoked salmon can so often be more salt than flavor, but not here. it was served a sizeable portion, with a heartiness I normally only associate with hot-smoked salmon (which I love, incidentally).the steak with eggs was pretty good too, with our beef done perfectly medium rare and pink and topped with two perfectly done sunny-side-ups.but if you're in the mood for something heartier, they also have a more lunch-type section with things like a proper beef burger (slightly over-minced (which leads to a mushier, less chunky patty, though still acceptable) and a salad nicoise with not-too-salty anchovies and colourful salad leaves.mind you, I say heartier in the sense of flavor rather than any indication of size. the portions here vary from small to reasonable, so don't be expecting anything remotely close to belly-busting.we finished with the waffles, since their rather famous white chocolate souffle wasn't available - this is possibly the only dish I'd steer clear of, seeing as how it was both anemic and biscuit-like (these really should be contrary adjectives, seeing how the first indicates lack of cooking, and the latter indicates rather too much). the only saving grace were the tart berries and ice cream. go for the affogato instead, which has a scoop of great ice cream over a satisfyingly bitter shot of espresso.service is pretty hit-and-miss. we waited a goodly amount of time for our food to arrive, so the portions did seem paltry at arrival - but it's otherwise friendly when you can get it. prices are commensurate with the venue rather than dish size, and so don't expect anything cheap - but come at least to see the place, and bask in the whole posh brunchness of the place.

I'm a little hazy on the details: I remember a warm spinach salad that was decent, a flurry of other appetisers that the table had to share, and then the huge mouth-watering grilled Wagyu Cote de Boeuf which, even when shared among four, seemed a daunting task.But I was most blown away by the chapel. It was resplendent with the setting sun shining lazily through the stained glass windows. Resting on the chapel seats, we felt like some reverence was demanded of us in such a beautiful scene.Would definitely love to visit again for date night with just the hubby.

I used to come here for lunch when I was working at Dempsey and the one thing I liked was that the place is usually empty during lunch. Parking is free for those who drive and there are lunch sets on offer that are really value for money. Also, the times I was dining there, I noticed a couple of people having business meetings as well, so you can consider that if you meet clients regularly. The food is pretty good and service is quite attentive as well.

Lovely ambiance in the old church building, I love the metalwork and stained glass decor. Brunch was decent, though not much in terms of choice. The Carbonara, English Fry Up and Poached eggs were quite good, wouldn't bother with the Maine Lobster Omelette which was pretty disappointing though.For sweet stuff, you have to get the crepe suzette (Grand Marnier and Crepes) just for the fact they they prepare it live right next to your table. The hot orange smell is delectable, and the final orangey-Marnier sauce goes with everything. Waffles are good and crispy too if a little dry as there's not enough syrup.Beware of mosquitoes though, I got bites just walking over from my car!

Went there for New Year's Eve Count down celebration. Plus 1. The restaurant is housed in a church house. Pretty cool.2. The Party was held at the restaurant's outdoor bar area. Nice area. 3. Had a photo booth for the event. Minus 1. There is limited parking space (so do come early) 2. The garden space was nicely decorated for the evening but they should definitely add more flooring or pavement if they wanted to add a sofa in the middle of the grass patch for guests to sit on. We had to walk across the muddy grass. 3. There's tons of mosquitoes there and I didn't notice till I got home that I had so many bites :( Service - Ok. Given that it was new years eve and they were all so busy (I think they deserve a pass even though we had our drinks cleared before we finished them and had to ask several times before we got our new ones)

Love burgers - and love Carl's Jr, because they're the freshest there is of the hamburger chains.I was chuffed about finding it in VivoCity and went right ahead to get an early dinner. The guy at the counter looked very stern and I pondered over the idea of walking away as I'd had the kind of day where you want to be treated nicely.However, I stayed. Only to find out that the gentleman at the counter was actually real nice. So, note to self, appearances are really often misleading. I ordered and got a number plate for my order to be put out on the table. Shortly after finding a seat I got my order from a lovely, smiley elderly gentleman. I then found a choice of free salsas and jalapeños at the same counter where you'll find the drinks machine. The burger was just right, juicy with fresh salad - something that you'll never find at McD. All in all a very satisfying burger meal if you are looking for fast food :-)

I'd heard about this place but have never actually been to one, namely because they don't exist in Australia (as is the case with a number of American chains). Honestly, I really didn't like it. Basically it is another one of the many fastfood burger chains that pretty much dominate the restaurant scene (though that seems to be changing for the better). The burgers weren't all that crash, and the chips were pretty average as well. Sure, they have bottomless soft drink, but once again it is soft drink, and I'm really not a fan of soft drink. In the end this is one of those places if you have seen one then you have seen them all.

My favorite fast food chain in Singapore!!Honestly, I am considering to give them 4 stars but it fails my 4-star test: would I go out of my way to eat here? Not really but I love it!! However, I feel that 4 stars for a cookie cutter fast food chain is over the top as they there is little real cooking involved, they just follow the corporate guidelines.But in Carls Jr case these corporate guidelines result in something super yummy, this is definitely one of my guilty pleasures and whenever I am at Vivocity (or Jurong Point) I am tempted to get a Thickburger and fries.What makes them better than Burger King or Mikey D's? First of all: the size of the burger, it is not a tiny affair , a meal at Carl's Jr always fills me up to the rim. Secondly: the quality of the burger, arguably there are better gourmet burgers available throughout Singapore but for fast food this is as good as it gets. I can really taste the grilled flavor. Thirdly and certainly in no means last: the condiment bar and soda fountain, they offer free flow salsa (both chunky and smooth), jalapeños and sauces. The only thing I am missing is ranch -but I eat ranch with everything so it might just be me who wants ranch*! The free flow soda fountain offers a wide selection of drinks way more than other chains.I love the super messy burger and fries drenched with salsa and jalapeños so three stars and major thumbs up!!*DISCOVERY OF THE DAY: you can ask for ranch when ordering and they'll hand you a tub of ranch for free!

Pretty sure no one needs to read a review for Carl's Jr. but here goes anyway. Maybe this review will save a life. Or at least save someone from a bad decision. Zero stars if I could. Carl's Jr. I used to love you but now you suck. Big time. I paid a premium for your dry cardboard burger. Do yourself a favour and go to McDonald's instead. At least you know what you're getting and you save money.

I ordered the portobello mushroom burger, and I shudder at the cost. The burger was a lot worse than I remembered - I think the quality must have backtracked a fair bit. The patty was overly greasy, and there was a lot less mushroom than I remembered.I don't eat much fast food, and this burger reminded me why. 'Nuff said.

Pricey Quality for a fast food chain.Good quality and excellent taste. Lots of condiments and friendly staff. Above average pricing for burgers. Bigger sized burgers then average. The fries is pretty good compared to the usual fast food culprits.The patties are grilled, and a bit more moisture then McD, less charred then BK. The lettuce is probably fresher compared to the fast food joints but it could be due to timing of the day of the meal. Will I return. Yes.Photos? Probably not. The meals comes wrapped and not really displayed for instagrammers.

Guilty pleasure but somehow I associate VivoCity with Carl's Jr and end up grabbing a burger here more times than I care to admit.I don't remember them having fried zucchini in the past as I believe I've asked the cashiers before only to blank stares. They have them on the menu now and will even happily upgrade your fries to zucchinis as part of the combo meal for only $1.60 or something reasonable. It even comes with ranch dressing. Fried zucchini and ranch dressing go together like peanut butter and jelly, kaya and toast...who came up with this brilliant combination? Carl's Jr? If so, I praise you sir Carl.

amazingly, I found the quality similar but loses the star b/c of the ultra-expensiveness!yes i get it, it's not like beef grows on trees here...but boy, $15 for a combo for their special meat!! i get this 33% cheaper lol.but the spaceness really wows me here, plenty of seating, and feels hip to be here.  even despite how expensive real estate it is in asia, these guys sure don't miss a beat.

Been having the Korean food cravings lately so I decided to drop by here on a Saturday after seeing the storefront a few days before. The interior design is welcoming and the wall decorations are inviting. My mother and I were quickly seated and were each given a menu to look over. Since I was craving for Ddukbokki (rice cake), I ordered that as well as Yuzu as beverage.The waitress placed 4 side dishes on our table - sugar coated ikan bilis, kimchi, spicy octopus/jellyfish (unsure) and black beans. The black beans were good. It has a little sweet taste to it - honey was probably added.My dish came around 10 minutes after the order was taken. The first plunge using my metal spoon was the rice cake with the spicy sauce on top. The rice cake was stringy and chewy. I have been craving this texture for awhile ever since I got back from Los Angeles. Been missing the rice cake at Koreatown Galleria's food court. Besides that, the sauce was spicy, sweet and tangy at the same time. On the plate of Ddukbokki, there were glass noodle (was surprised to see it inside as it is normally used to do jap chae) and korean cabbage with fish cakes. All I can say is that I will definitely be back for more. This is the closest taste to the one I had in L.A. Price wise, it is considered pricy but worth for the ingredients as well as the right spicy sauce taste. Will be back for other dishes as well as this dish I love :)Tried the dolsot bimbimbap (vegetarian). The ingredients are fresh and the portion was right. As it is served on a hot plate, the bottom of the rice is crispy. You would need to mix the ingredients, rice and chilli sauce before the steamy effect goes out. Probably will be much better with beef slices :)

We decided to eat here after movie as there was no queue. Most restaurants were having queues during dinner time. Iced water was not served.Saba & Samguebsal (S$15.80++)Grilled pork belly, chicken sausage, and mackerel with sauce. Served with rice and soup.The pork belly was tough here although it was thinly sliced. The mackerel was a tab dry.Japchae (S$7.80++)Stir-fried glass noodles and vegetables in soy sauce seasoning.The fried noodles looked a tab plain although it was flavourful.Banchan :Gamja Jorim (Soy Braised Potatoes )Myulchi Bokkeum (Stir-fried Anchovies)Kongnamul-muchim (Marinated Bean Sprouts)Kimchi Not much choice when your dining partner refused to have anything spicy. Not sure why, but the kimchi tasted a tab off here with a kind of sour taste.

It offers 4 free flow sides/appetizers. It was so-so but I think it's kimchi is not bad and is rather crunchy. Tried it's Kimchi soup with rice and was quite impressed by the flavour; is so savory leaves you wanting more. Even as I was sweating eating it, I had a hard time finishing it because of its portions. It's so appetizing I just kept going! Free flow water at no cost does help in this aspect. Another dish we tried was the Ginseng soup. The soup may be a bit bland but because it's portions were so huge and there are actually rice underneath the soup (a bit like porridge or is it already porridge?), couldn't imagine anyone finishing it with a heavier flavour. However you can definitely taste and eat the Ginseng added to it and is a nice healthier choice. Choices in the menu is a little bit limited to me. After all it's just a small joint in the Plaza Sing shopping mall. Prices are before GST and service charges added to it. Service is not very responsive. I requested something twice and it wasn't given until I asked for the third time! When they served the dishes, they forgotten about the utensils! Sometimes I do hope Singapore eateries lump the prices together with the service charge so that I will not grumble paying for it.

Can you believe it? This is the only decent Korean restaurant in Plaza Singapura!! And by what I've had, this is somewhere where I would go to if I were desperately craving Korean food and needed a quick fix.We went to Manna Story with the thought of having Budae Jiggae. We were seated at the two-persons table near the entrance. As we were carrying lots of bags and it was rather cramp, we were asked to move to a two-person couch seat. I noticed that the couple at the table next to me ordered something similar and the plug that was used to power the hot pot was used. We placed our order and the waitress asked us if it would be okay if our food was kitchen-cooked as there was no more plug to power our hot pot.
