Had their luncheon meat fries and they were fried beautifully with a serving of nancho cheese chips.They have dart machines in the bar as well so dart fanatics, dart your night away.For fellow Yelpers and Yelp Elites, do write a review and get a free luncheon meat fries on ur next visit. Do check with the staff on this promotion!

If you're planning to organize your company event here, this place is a one star only.Food - good and sufficient for the flowService - actually a 1 star service. Food was served very late, 12.50pm when my company event supposed to start at 12pm!! Totally unacceptable! The owner appeared really "chin chai" (anyhow attitude), and agrees to everything prior to the event, but failed to deliver.Location - your PowerPoint slides can flash on to their big wall in stage, yes, but in fact it's day time and there will be light entering the entire bar which makes your visibility of details on screen really low. Although there are TV screens available, but they are not compatible to the laptop and is unable to screen your PowerPoint slides. Here comes the issue. The owner actually mentioned that you can flash your PowerPoint slides prior to your event. That's cheating!Price - expensive and not value for money.Overall experience was bad for a corporate event.No doubt, it's an ok location to hang out with your friends. But if you cannot handle a corporate event, please stop advertising for it, or find someone who is capable of doing it professionally. I can only say, the boss is just a pub owner, not a professional event organizer trained.
Love this place for the music and delicious luncheon fries ! Good for group gatherings and party night out.

This is the place to go if you are looking to listen to original music in Singapore. Almost all the bars and clubs in the country play cover songs but Hood is one place that's looking to break that mould. And more power to them I say! What kind of a country has so much talent but has so little platforms for it's musicians?Opened by musicians for musicians and music lovers, this place has just moved over from their old location at Keong Saik road. The ambience is friendly and casual. The bands that play here differ in terms of music styles and even languages. I've heard full out canto bands, hard rock bands, metal bands, easy listening and singer songwriter stuff here too. Original music is played on Saturdays so that would be my day to visit. I might go down with ear plugs. It might get loud.Outdoor smoking area available andyou can bring your brews out too. great for an indoor drinking hole.

I'd never been to the old place at Keong Saik, and I'd be poorer for it. But hey their new digs at Bugis+ = awesome! Even better: the new line up of live bands that they host pretty much every day of the week.Shirlyn and the UnXpected now play here as well as many other awesome local live bands. It's awesome.

Wohooo this place rocks!! While it seems like a new place on the cinema level in Bugis + (formally Illuma), Hood have been around for a while. They used to be located in a cosy spot in keong saik street. A relocation with a bigger fit out, bigger bar and now a food menu, the Hood I've always loved just got better. Drink prices are reasonable, the live bands great, food wise the hot dogs are the biggest and tastiest in Singapore for sure.They have been really clever with their choice of location. It was fantastic to pop in for a drink and a hot dog, before going to the cinema on the same floor before returning for more drinks and a chilled out Saturday evening. Cool tunes, great food and great live music, highly recommend a visit to Hood. It has just got a whole lot bigger and better!!

Just order the butter chicken and whatever naan you fancy.It's delish.For dessert, there's this mango sorbet thingy that's served in a tiny lil brown claypot. Awesome stuff. Definitely worthwhile to forgo Udders for dessert.

This is a review of lunch with a colleague at Chat Masala.My colleague suggested Chat Masala for one of our lunches.tinyurl.com/bc55xzoThe ambiance is relatively basic but has a modern feel with clean lines. The tone of grey selected provides a cool feel to the room.tinyurl.com/b9ve3ngOn this day, the restaurant was almost entirely empty.  I have a feeling they do much of their business for dinner.  Their food and service are certainly of the quality level of a dinner destination.The service was friendly, professional, polite and timely.  This was the case through-out the meal.The food ranged from very good to extremely foodtinyurl.com/atdrs7pSamosa and Pakora - These were the appetizers.  Both were very good.  They were crispy and flavourful,  The filling for the samosas was just right, tender with near perfect seasonings.  Both dishes were very well presented.tinyurl.com/ath8udxtinyurl.com/bau2jq9Fruity Naan/Garlic Naan - The naan was fresh and tasty.  I had never tried fruit naan.  It actually kind of reminded me of my mom's fruit cake.  Their naan was very good.  I thought the garlic naan could have used just a tad more garlic though.tinyurl.com/avy7g37Rogan Gosh - This was a very well prepared lamb dish.  It is one of the best rogan gosh's I've had recently.  The spices really came together,  The lamb was well prepared.  This was an all around nice dish.tinyurl.com/aktm6g4Chicken Masala - What's not to like about tender pieces of chicken in a wonderfully flavoured sauce.  I wish there had been just a tad more chicken.  It would have made it a little fairer in the sharing of the dish.  But outside of that, this was a extremely good Chicken Masala.  The spice blend was so nicely balanced.tinyurl.com/a6vxc5bPilaf Rice  - This was very good rice.  It may have been just a tad bit on the dry side but the way it came together more than made up for this.  This was another dish with a very appetizing presentation.tinyurl.com/ay9cvcxReceipt ($61.50)This is not your average lunch and it doesn't come with an average lunch price-tag.  But I think the food was well worth it and I would not have an issue paying  the same price again for the same food.  Plus, we ordered two apps, two naans, two mains, rice, and beverages. But, at around $15 per, this is near the high end for mains in Indian restaurants.tinyurl.com/bg5any9Overall - A nice space, very good service, and great food all come together for a very enjoyable lunch.  Chat Masala could also easily make it as a choice for dinner with friends or a casual date.  When it comes down to it, every dish they served was well presented and, more importantly, tasted wonderful.

Yum!This is as good as how North Indian food gets. While it is not cheap, you do get quality and taste. Fresh naans, savory rich butter chicken, yummy fish appetizer.If you are going to consume an obscene amount of calories, at least make sure the calories are worth it.

OH DAT NAAN. Them be delicious naan. I don't know how to make naan unfortunately, so I'm coming here for those tasty tasty flatbreads. If you like naan, come get some here. But of course that's not the only thing that's good here. I'm going to tell you to have the Kerala meen curry. It sounds funny, and it's certainly a mean curry - generous chunks of mackerel in a piquant gravy. Then there's the eggplant strips. I've loved almost every rendition kathirikai pachadi I've ever tasted, and this is pretty damn awesome. A deep reddish paste with eggplant strips... cooked in, and smothered in this sauce that is at first sweet, then after two bites, fiery, but oh so delicious... aiyah just come and eat lah.

This place is expensive. There, I've got the bad bit out. And aside from the high price point, I love Chat Masala. The decor is tasteful and soothing, and the service is top notch. Even the cutlery is of good quality - heavy and wrought into a pretty design. The menu is great, and I'll go for the usual fish masala, butter chicken, aloo gobi and palek paneer together with a stack of naans. The fish is moist and juicy, butter chicken creamy, and aloo gobi mildly spicy and the palek paneer finger licking good. The naans are biggish, crisp and fluffy, and everything is great - even the biggish slivers of ginger sabotaging some of the dishes - until I receive the bill. Then my heart constricts a little, but I willingly part with the dough because I'm happily stuffed.

Elegantly decorated with dim lighting, Chat Masala exudes the slightly expensive, charming neighbourhood specialty restaurant vibe. With many North and South Indian dishes from the more famous such as tandoori to the less well-known, the menu caters to all kinds of people of all ages. For those who are not as good with spice, the butter chicken is creamy and delicious which comes with the perfect sauce to go with the variety of naans offered. For dessert, the carrot cake is quite unlike many carrot cakes I've tried in Singapore and served delightfully warm. The mango kulfi is also highly recommended, a small home-made pot of ice-cream that is undoubtedly sinful.The service is also exceptional. We are always greeted warmly and there is a cozy feeling that is a result of the combination of beautiful decor, homely dishes and a friendly atmosphere. It is a lovely place to have lunch or dinner with friends or family and you will probably want to be back for more.

My first taste of butter chicken was here and it has been at least 6 years since I first patronised. Chat Masala is a family favourite, and it pleases everyone in my very big family ranging from 5 years only to 50 years old. The food here is good and that's the least of it. With a charming interior of organza curtains to partition the washrooms form the main dining area, Chat Masala is cozy and easily noticeable from the main road. The menu has expanded over the years, but only to the patrons' benefits. The Mamma Mia Mussels are a great dish to share, with a great balance of heat, sweetness and savouriness. The fish vadais are good; soft filling with chunks of fish with a crusty batter that can't seem to keep you away from taking another and another. Also, if you are wary about the vegetable dishes, and do look spinach and cheese, you have to try Palak Paneer, my all time favourite done right here at Chat Masala. The spinach is creamy and well seasoned, without a raw taste to it, and the cottage cheese is soft with a slight chew, going very well with pilaf rice if you like your rice flavourful as well.Finish off with their mango kulfi, thick, rich and creamy, you may just need a partner-in-crime to polish that little undaunting pot of ice cream.

I am quite a fan of North Indian food, so when my friend recommended for us to come here for dinner, I immediately jumped at the opportunity.The entire place has a very nice décor and ambience. Service was prompt, and we managed to grab a seat and made our orders quickly. Some of the food that we ordered included Chicken Masala, Fish Masala, Fish Briyani, Masala Tea and probably some others that I forgot. The briyani was nice, but I thought that the texture of the rice was not what I had liked. Oh, we also had butter chicken, and I thought that the gravy was really addictive! It's just too bad that the chicken was a little tough; I would have given it top marks if the chicken had been a little more tender. The naan here is amazing though; it's warm and fluffy, but crispy at the bottom. Simply perfect.Overall, this is a decent place to have North Indian food, but to be honest I've had better experiences elsewhere.

This is a great place to stop in for a beer.  They have a great selection of Japanese craft beer in bottles and on-tap.  The tap selection rotates frequently to keep things fresh.  Their selection of food is also good.  The service is also great as they are very helpful with both the beer and food menu and look to get you seated no matter how busy.  The staff are knowledgeable of everything on the menu.

After much yelping and froing where to have dinner we somehow ended up choosing this place. Jumped off the MRT and despite the madness and mayhem of busy Somerset 313 and its surrounding malls, we were able to get a table after a short wait. This was a plus as I don't do long waits. There is not a lot of ambience here with the hustle and flow of the passing throng. However, it is made up for by a fantastic selection of beers from Japan. Some by bigger breweries and some by tiny craft breweries that I had neither seen or heard of previously. Japanese bar food was available on the menu, and the Yakitori and fried chicken was a welcome addition to the beers.

Japanese craft beer? Yes please! Given how much care Japanese people put into their work - this has got to be good, right? There's a long extensive menu with a lot of interesting beers from Japan. Some are very traditional beers (i.e. there's nothing special - although they're good) but there are some that are truly unique. A beer brewed from rice? You can't tell me you've tried that anywhere else!It's in a great location as well, great patio in a busy neighbourhood that's easily accessible.  Beers are about $13 a bottle from what I remember, and I think they have specials as well. If you're a beer fan, I definitely recommend this place.

Japanese craft beer specialist - there's a whole menu's worth of interesting beers here that you don't often or see at all at other spots!The draft beers are tasty - I had the local brew - Jungle Beer Tropical Wheat Mango & Orange... perhaps not for the purists but I like the slightly fruity/sweetness that this beer had. The Hitachino Nest ales were also tasty, and have the cutest owl logo.Food was decent - I wouldn't order the kaarage chicken again cause it was rather fatty for my liking, but we ordered the Hibiki set (12 yakitori sticks!) that was pretty filling for my party of 4. Interesting black peppery sauce it came with. We also ordered the Mozarella-Tomato yakitori, and I liked the mozarella.I like the ambience of the place in the sheltered outdoor area of 313, it's been raining so it was nice and cool and not too crowded or loud so conversation was easy.

Japanese craft beer and vegetarian curry rice, a wonderful unity of booze and food. I come here for the espresso stout since they sell it cheaper than other places I've been to that serve this beer, plus they have other really unique beers like a new one I'll be trying soon which has coriander and bonito fish flakes. I was weirded out for sure when I saw the description but the waiter assured me that it doesn't taste fishy at all. He explained it was a new craft beer only for summer. It's so strange and unique, I just HAVE to try it.

This place is a relatively new addition to the spade of bars in the somerset area. If you want to avoid the loud music and crowd at emerald hill, this is your kinda place to have a beer with some peace. Great for dates if you actually want to talk to your date. The main attraction of this place is the variety of japanese craft beers it houses. On top of it, they also offer a spread of sake, some wine, and a full bar. There's a beer for everyone here, from their taps of sapporo, jungle beer to hitachino white ale and pale. I prefer this place wayy better than it's next door neighbor Brotzeit.

we went for some drinks on a sunday funday.  it was a little warm since it was outside and not a lot of fans.  i tried the beer flight and i only enjoyed 1 of the 4 beers a friend also had a flight and she liked 2 of the 4.  I cant speak for the other parts since we only had a drink.

Great location, great beer, great food. Great, all-around. I am no Japanese beer connoisseur but they had quite a selection (and a great HH price for Asahi for beer newbies like me!).They have an extensive beer menu and while its not the cheapest, you can find all kinds of interesting niche craft beers. They also have quite a large food menu. They say they're known for their yakitori, which I didn't have a chance to try. We ordered off of the lunch menu, which is in the $15 range and includes a full set of soup with a salad. I had their curry rice with karaage chicken and it was the best curry rice I've had in the city so far.As far as I could tell, they only had outdoor seating so it might not be the best place when it is pouring outside or if you need to cool off from the heat. Still, its nice and breezy and it allows you to do a good bit of people-watching. It is located right outside of the western entrance to the Somerset313 building, next to the German restaurant.

Offering people watching up the wazoo, JiBiru is a top notch spot to sample some cracking Japanese craft beers, sit under the Big Ass Fans™, and just watch the world go by.Located behind the busy Orchard Road shopping area, and within earshot of the MRT entrance makes this thoroughfare busy as a bee.Grab a bucket or two, or a craft draft, and settle in for a gawk and a talk!
Average bar - only worth going to because of the general Somerset outdoor bar atmosphere.

This something as unusual as a place specializing in mainly Japanese craft beer and the selection is pretty great. I have explored some of these beers while in Japan but the craft beer trend was jot as strong when I was there so many of the ones on offer here were new to me. They are also thoroughly described in the beer list and the staff are knowledgeable so really impressed by that. Prices are perhaps a bit on the steep side but the happy hour is pretty good (at least if before 6pm).They also have some Japanese whiskey and sake as well as some beer from other countries and some ciders so most people should be able to find something to drink here. Of course they also serve food and it is good and simple Japanese food. I sampled several of the dishes and it is good solid Japanese food, my favorite was the curry but I would not come for the food but rather the beer selection and I may or may not have some food. The locations is central, right by Somerset tube in the mall 313@Somerset.

As a travelling beer snob I was super pumped to find a place like this on vacation.  If you want to get your hands on some awesome Japanese microbrews look no further.It was pretty packed on a Friday night but I was able to find a corner of a table, and I was surprised by the selection of beers.  The beers were all great, lots of varieties, styles and microbrews.  Most beers are bottled so if you are a fan of draught beer than you will be disappointed.My two issues are: 1) the beer menu was organized loosely by brewery and not by style, they are not cross-referenced anywhere so you have to flip through a lot of pages to narrow down decisions, beer snobs like to see styles of beers grouped together. 2) Food was not at the level of the beers, beers were 5 stars, food was 3 stars, sorry but I am use to yakitori style foods that make you want to stay, eat and drink moore.If you down with beer, this is the place.  Bring your wallet though, this is in one the pricey areas of Singapore.

My fav to grab a beer place in town currently. I like their Japanese craft beer and Jap fried chicken. Minus one as it can get rather humid sitting out there.You may call them in advance to ask whether their tv is showing the sports channel you would like to watch as well. :)

Five stars because their selection of Japanese craft beers is fantastic. In their selection is Shigakogen IPA, among the best (best beer for me) in the world. Their yakitori isn't half bad either (and reasonably priced). The location isn't going to please everyone, but it is good for people watching.

JiBiru Craft Beer & Yakitori Bar maybe one of my favourite place on earth!More than 40 Japanese beers from microbreweries available in drafts or bottles! Selection of beers that I can only dream of back home. And paired with yakitori from Saitama region north of Tokyo with sauces directly imported from Hibiki yakitori restaurants of Higashi-Matsuyama. I know what I want to order... I want one of those Hitachino Draft serves in Weizenbier glass with that cute owl logo! I Unfortunately they were out of Red Rice Ale or the Amber Ale. Hitachino Nest Dai Dai IPA ended up being the drink of the evening!We also ordered Edamame and Yakitori which were both really good. So many beers I want to try. Just wish they have 3 oz samplers options or I should get more people to come drinking with me next time! Come before 6 pm for the best deal $10 VS $15 after 8 pm!! I should have started drinking much much early! You know who can resist specials?I am dreaming of a taste of Hitachino Nest XH (8%) A robust Belgian style Brown Ale made with extra malt and hops and matured in Shochu casks for over 6 months. I wonder how this will taste like!or Kinshachi Matcha Draft (Green Tea Beer)or....Until next time!

Those who have met me know my love towards craft beers and most of the places that serve them. I'm usually an instant fan and seeing a review of such places below 4 stars usually means I've finally become annoyed enough to provide feedback via a review.It's definitely not my first time here but my previous experiences did not have service issues because I happened to be there during off-peak "happy hour" before the main crowd comes in. While it was far from packed tonight, the lapse in service became quite evident.I stopped by with Gold Elite Nik T. and Sweet Elite Linda L. for a beer and a good conversation after our dinner with Cindy L. and Ning.*******10 minutes to get our order in.5 minutes for Linda L. to receive her order.15 minutes of chatting without anything else arriving.5 minutes before we got someone's attention and to find out that they RAN OUT of our orders...and we were never informed about it.Nik T. looked at his watch and decided to downsize from 500 ml to 300 ml. We both ordered something else that they said was available.15 minutes of chatting without anything else arriving.5 minutes before we got someone's attention again and NOW found out that they CAN'T serve the new draft due to fizzy issues with the keg...and offered a ton of apologies.Nik T. downsized all the way and decided to go dry while I finally settled for the same drink as Linda L. It arrived in less than 5 minutes.Linda L.'s drink became warm while she waited for ours to arrive. Nik T. ended up leaving with just a sip of hers. I ended up having one instead of going dry like Nik T. so that Linda L. didn't end up having a brew herself.BUT WAIT...if that wasn't enough to end the night, our bill...was wrong. We were billed for our initial order. Gold Elite couldn't take it anymore...and gave immediate feedback. I just smiled...said it was okay...and got ready to review this place.*******Thankfully, I waited a bit...and managed to justify in my mind that they deserved 3 stars at least for their product. But seriously, their staff needs some training yeah? This isn't a Kopitiam...and even then, Kopitiams don't pull this kind of crap.Yelp 100: 20/100

JiBiru specializes in Japanese beers, and they have the most extensive selection I have seen outside of Japan.  Actually, even i Japan I'm not sure if there are many places that carry 60 Japanese craft beers in bottles plus 5 on draft.  Anyway, they have a sampler of 4 beers on draft (all from Hitachino) which is the way to go if you would like to try a few.  I'm not the biggest fan of HItachino though (except for their espresso stout), so for me it was just ok.  Their selection by the bottle was better though.   I tried an Imperial IPA from Minoh, which was a great example of the style - strong, bitter, and full of flavor with an ABV of 9%. I could drink it all the time, except for the fact that it's so hot here, and that the pub is outdoors, with very little cooling.  They also carry some nice craft beers from the world including some of my faves (Rogue, La Trappe, etc) as well as sake, whiskey and shochu.  JiBiru also specializes in yakitori, and the chicken skewer I had was very tasty - perfectly cooked chicken with just the right amount of char and with a sauce that wasn't overly salty or sweet.   The one thing that could improve here is the service though.  With the number of people working here, I found the service to be strangely inattentive or rather focused on one table only  Maybe they were celebs?  No idea, but in any case, JiBiru is a great place to see what Japanese craft breweries are doing these days with some tasty food to boot.
I've only been here for lunch - didn't even know this was a beer place. Their lunches are quite OK quality-price wise. A bit noisy but this is the Somerset shopping area.

This place helped me realize how good the craft beer scene in Japan was becoming. Hitichino Nest and Yona Yona are the highlights, but there's a lot to choose from. They also have some local stuff (Jungle Beer, usually on draft), and on my last trip I noticed an improving selection of craft beer in bottles from Australia, Europe, and the U.S. Prices are reasonable:  normally $11-$15, but a little cheaper during their 2-tiered happy hour (before 6, and 6-8). It's also a nice, mellow, breezy place to chill out. In contrast, Brotzeit next door is always a little chaotic. Access is great for the MRT crowd. It's just a few steps outside of Somerset.

Ji-Biru offers a good range of Japanese imported beers. Some of these beers cannot even be found in the Japanese supermarkets around! One of our favorites is the chocolate bottled beer, but it comes in only seasonally. It has a really nice packaging, like what you expect to get on a Japanese beer. This little bar started along with the starting of the mall, and has since updated its menu with a good amount of food items, and expanded the choice of imported beer. This I think is a really good sign for any business, having business owners are willing to progress and make changes for the consumers. I guess they have figured out that Singaporeans still like to munch while drinking. However on the downside, the staff are not very attentive. They will not attend to you until you go and take a seat yourself, from several of my personal experiences. Perhaps it is their style of service, but I cannot really get used to it. Environment wise, I actually like the open atmosphere. That's when I can do my favorite activity - people watching! Perfect spot to chill and watch people as they walk along.
Love the amazing choice of beers. I got cheeky and tried some outlandish chocolate beer which wasn't great. Overall the happy hour is great and it's a great place to experiment with new drinks.

Like other places over here, Kinki is about the view and the ambience. Where it's a step ahead of its competitors would be its menu. "Ginger and Cumkuat capirinha" sounds fantabulous right. Unfortunately it's beauty was in name only. Watered down overpriced drinks and inattentive staff means  I wont be coming back.

It's a pretty decent place for after-work drinks as it's located right smack in the center of the CBD. The ambience at the rooftop bar is very chill and you get a great view of the Marina Bay area if you get a seat at the edge.Food-wise, I felt the sushi was decent, but if you really like good quality sushi please go elsewhere. It's more bar-food sushi than anything else.Loved their Kinki specials (drinks) though. They were really good! I can't really remember what I ordered but I remember wanting to order more and more.

Kinki is my favorite place for sushi in Singapore for quiet some time now.I like the quality of almost any dish and the service has always been very good and accompanied with a smile. :)One of my favs to order is sashimi and you can bet it is again one of the best I ever had here in Singapore. The price for food is in the upper range which is being compensated by the quality. The environment is nice so far or maybe I have just been lucky. I'm not into the pretentious places and so far Kinki this is not the case at all during my visits.The setup of this venue is ideal be it for a lunch or dinner, meeting or date.I'm not big on drinking a lot when eating sushi however they have a bar there which by itself is worth visiting as well. The pricing is ok, all in ~18$ for a drink.Enjoy ~ !!-s

I have been off Japanese food for a while after a bout of food poisoning but I've slowly been trying to get back into it not least in celebration of my husband finishing his samurai computer game.  Did I mention I'm married to a nerd? What better place to reintroduce my tongue to Japanese than the uber-swanky new Japanese restaurant Kinki.  The place is decorated with koi acrylic floor paintings, Oishinbo inspired food portraits on the walls, and very low furniture making it seems futuristic and modern. Also the view is breathtaking.I had the edamame (salted to perfection), vegetable tempura (best I've ever had), and pomegranate miso black cod while my companions stuck mostly to sushi.  The sashimi we saw coming out of the kitchen made me drool by the way.  All of the food was spectacular and obviously was washed down with sake.  I would just caution that the miso was just barely cooked which I'm sure is the method de jour but I am just barely adult enough to handle undercooked fish.  Stick with the raw stuff if this bothers you too.  The sushi I was able to sneak off my husband's plate was fun and inventive and really tasty.At present the clientele is mostly older business gentleman. I suggest we turn this around and make it a haunt for the younger foodie crowd.  You won't be disappointed.

This is for the roof top bar only. Great view of the waterfront and of MBS, great happy hour, great crowd, great location. What more can you ask for. We had the fried chicken and it was crispy and delightful, albeit a bit expensive.

Utterly Disappointed - i had the worst Singapore dining experience here the other night. Sorry to say this as Kinki has a cool vibe and a nice rooftop where i've taken guests in the past. I thought the staff was poorly trained and the dine-in policies bizarre and inflexible. Suffice to say, I wont be going back.I attended my friends birthday party at Kinki where she reserved a table for 20 from 6 - 9 PM. My partner and I arrived about 1 hour late and at that time the table (for 14) that was given to us was over-packed already. We noticed that the table for four next to our large party was available and I asked to sit there so we could be close to the birthday party. We were told by the wait-staff that the table was reserved. Ok no issues, we were only 2 people and didnt want to take up the larger table so we asked to sit at a 2 person table in the vicinity of the party. Again, that table was reserved. We then approached the manager and told them of our situation: we had a party for 20 but were seated in a 14 person table but we arrived late and the wait staff wont let us sit at the tables nearby. So how?The manager let us know at that point that the entire restaurant was booked for the night. Perplexed, I looked around the restaurant of (im estimating) 30 tables and only 8 of them were occupied. As we were with the large birthday party, i inquired if could eat quickly at any one of the reserved tables before the parties arrived and was told that we could not as the tables were reserved. I then asked what time the people were coming for their reservation for the tables near the birthday party and were told that she didnt know. Then I asked since they didnt know, if we could eat and if the party came, they could be seated at another one of the 15 open two seater tables. Again, I got the "cannot sir". I asked her "so you are telling me that we are here for a birthday party already eating, you have 75% of your restaurant unoccupied and you are not letting us eat". The only reply i got was sorry the restaurant is reserved. I thought this was odd, and we were left awkwardly hovering near the birthday party table for about 10 minutes while they hurriedly finished eating. At that point we were told by the birthday girl that we had a reservation upstairs at the bar and that they had some bar snacks that we could eat. We hovered and waited for critical mass to finish eating and headed up stairs to the open air bar area. Despite a reservation for 20, Kinki gave us a table to seat 4 but was in the corner so we had some standing room only spots. We ordered a few bottles with all the mixers and ice buckets so there was little room for us to order food to eat. I asked the bar wait-staff, if we could sit at the table next to ours so that we could order some bar food to eat. Again, that table was reserved. Looking around there was our party of 18-20, and about 8 other people in the rooftop bar area and about 15 open tables. I asked the wait staff what time the table was reserved for and he said 10pm. Looking down at my watch, it was only 8 so i asked him to give us the seat for 30 mins so we could quickly eat and then we would go back to the original table. He said, sorry the table was reserved and walked away. However, he then came back a few minutes later and nicely said okay we could site there for an hour. Another wait-staff took our order and being vegetarian I ordered the Vegetarian Okonomiyaki. He told me that the Okonomiyaki was not available. There weren't many vegetarian bar snack options so I asked if i could order from the restaurant menu. "No, you cannot". I asked where the bar snacks were being prepared and he answered "the restaurant downstairs". Odd... I told him nevermind and that I ordered a drink. When he came to bring my drink he apologized and told me that the Okonomiyaki was available so I confirmed the Okonomiyaki order.The vegetarian Okonomiyaki was brought out abut 30 mins later and it wasnt Okonomiyaki looking at all. It was mayonaise atop toasted bread but wasnt bad tasting until I bit into something that tasted like chicken. At this point i was about to lose my sh*t. I asked my meat eating friends if it tasted like chicken and 2 out of 3 agreed. I approached the wait staff and  told them annoyingly that they had served me meat on a vegetarian dish. The wait-staff shook his head violently and flapped his arms up and said looking even more annoyed than me, "that was vegetarian". They sent another wait-staff who confirmed that it was mozzarella cheese. I never really knew mozzarella cheese and chicken could be so easily confused and let my friends eat the rest of my dish. No dinner for me after 3 hours of trying, thanks Kinki!

Take the lift to the top of Customs House and you'll be greeted by Kinki's bar on the roof top .This trendy place is yuppie paradise. I really like the vibes, as it reminds me of another painfully trendy place in London called Aqua Kyoto. I come here with colleagues after work sometimes. It's a good spot for post-work and farewell drinks. The drinks are OK-ish price wise (a Gin & Tonic costs around $12+++ I think) . I suppose you can expect to pay a little more for the ambience, etc.As Kinki is an open roof top bar, it can get a little warm on some nights. They do have fans etc. to alleviate the warmness though. It's usually busy and crowded. They play good music which sometimes veers on excessively loud to me (maybe I'm getting old?), so expect to do more shouting than talking.

This place closes at 11.30pm - even on the eve of public holidays! This is what I've learnt when I visited the bar on such a night at 10.30pm. I really liked the roof top concept though and would love to go back and check more of it out. I've also heard good things about the music at the bar. However the closing of the bar at 11.30 is quite the downer, seeing how popular it is with the working crowd. We had to leave to go to Overeasy nearby because of that.The location also overlooks our beautiful Singapore skyline and buildings. The drinks are priced higher than normal but not that astronomical. What I really liked is the vibe and crowd.
Service wasn't great but 1 for 1 happy hour is not bad and the view is good. Chill atmosphere but a little cramped in my opinion. Nice place to meet people though

Kinki is one of my favourite places for a date. It's the perfect balance between casual and chi-chi, yet also trendy with a great vibe with good service and a view of the water.Food : Ooh I love the foie gras and scallop sushi! Totally melts in my mouth. Also really like the wagyu aburi sushi, salmon belly aburi sushi, unagi and anago sushi as well as the botan ebi and uni aburi sushi ... all pretty tasty! We also really like the momotaro tomato with ginger dressing and snow crab, organic tofu and century egg with ponzu sauce and ginger. The grilled black cod marinated in Kinki pomegranate-honey miso served with braised gobo and scallions is supposed to be a Kinki specialty, but we thought it was just so-so. The wagyu ribeye cooked over cast iron seasoned with truffle sauce was pretty good as was the pan seared kurobuta pork belly served with Kinki's spicy sesame sauce. We were not impressed by the Kinki okonomiyaki, i.e. a Japanese styled pizza of Hokkaido scallops, prawns,apple wood smoked bacon, sweet onions and mozzarella. Kinki doesn't have a wide selection of desserts so we tried the most exotic sounding one i.e. the Oreo Sesame, which is black sesame ice-cream blended with Oreo cookies. Predictably it was a bit too sweet and heavy.Ambience : Love it love it love itService : Pleasant, welcoming and efficientPrices are a bit steep but the fusion sushi is great.

Graced with one of the sexiest views of Singapore, this aptly named venue is a happy hour haven for post-stressed bevvie mavens!The best tables are almost always booked out. So getting here early ensures you'll get a good use of them before the reservees show up (and sometimes they don't). Best bang for buckets are the Kronenbourg 1664. All iced up you'll be knocking these puppies back whilst you drink in that view and soak up those tasty tunes.This is a bi-monthly stop and it never fails to entertain and delight.The one downside is the toilets are a slow elevator ride away. However, if your wallet is fat the sushi/sashimi located on the same floor is as sexy as the name suggests, so you can always relocate post happy hour tipple!

Visited both the bar and restaurant. Very overpriced for above average food, sub standard ambience and staff. We were by the window and it really wasn't that great. Portions are small so you'll need to order quite a bit. Thankfully I had good company or it would be a 1* experience.

My review is for the rooftop bar. The view is nice but the service is poor. I booked a table for 12 in advance and when we got there on time, half of it was given to another group. When we asked, the waiters were rude and said this was it. Later the other group told us they were given our table and would leave in 30 mins an so we eventually got the table and weren't crammed. The service is super slow, they just ignore you while you try to order. Isn't worth going to for the service, many better options available in Singapore with similar views and price range.
Excellent view, great folks and very helpful.Reasonably price.  Get there early for good seating

Overall, this is a good meet up place for casual drinks coz of its central location, good views of the bay and the price of the drinks, there's one for one during happy hour (albeit heavily watered down I suspect).But if you decide to go there, you need to be mindful of all the other imperfections - service was slow and choppy.  During our 4 hours there we had three orders of food and the average waiting time is 40 mins, which is pretty long considering we only ordered snacks like sushi and hand rolls. They have left out certain items in our order until we checked and the food was just ok.  I would say go for the location and the view but nothing more.

My review is solely for the Bar and not the restaurant as I think the restaurant is ehh...for the exorbitant prices you have to pay for good sushi/sashimi.Kinki's Rooftop Bar is just out of this world! In my view, it's the best after-work / happy hour bar in Singapore. Friday nights are simply packed. First off, it's got an amazing view of Marina Bay Sands. Second, they play some fun catchy 80s tunes to get the party going (which brings me back to my old stomping grounds in Murray Hill, NYC)! Third, the drinks are relatively cheap, albeit watered down and/or measured, as is most alcoholic drinks in Singapore (ugh!). Fourth, the crowds are good looking expat working professionals (very few, if any, locals to be found).To conclude, I give this place 5-stars for the atmosphere, but more importantly it's the place where I've met so many of my Singaporean based friends, since moving to this country three yrs ago. I liked it so much that I had my 28th birthday party here!

Despite the name this place doesnt exude sex...well that depends on the amount of alcohol consumed. But anyways I will touch upon the restaurant and bar separately.   I went to the restaurant for my birthday and I would say it was very good. The food is a but pricey for the amount given but the quality is great. I LOVED the tai carpaccio and truffle rib eye. Also loved the spicy edamame. It had tons of flavor. I consider the sushi to be so so and not really worth the price.  There are plenty of better dishes and the okonomiyaki is not like the japanese varitey at all but is really just a pizza ( but its still good).  I wouldnt come for great japanese food but its dishes are inventive and pretty good with a few misses.The bar above is a really fun spot. I love the atmosphere, the view of the bay, the open air, etc. They also have these great miso pork nachos that are awesome.  Its fun and lively and a great spot to preparty or just hang out for the night.  Its just as good a view as the lantern but half the price.  Definitely on my go to spot for showing friends around singapore

Kinki the restaurant = 3 stars Kinki the rooftop bar = 4 starsYou can find me, my husband, yuppie expats, and all the trendy Singaporeans that work in CBD at Kinki's rooftop on Friday evenings. I always roll in after happy hour, when the DJ is letting that beat rock, all the tables are taken, and the crowd is collectively cheering that it's the freakin' weekend.Drink prices are steep (for me... because Maker's Mark on the rocks = $18) but I put up with it. As other reviewers mentioned, it can get pretty warm, and the mega fans they have don't help that much unless you stand in front of them. Every time I'm there, they seem to play some super weird background videos of people getting tattoos. Anyone else notice that?! Does it annoy you as much as it annoys me?!Despite this, I've met some great gal pals here, and yes, we still keep in touch. As for the guys, I'm married, but I can say that a lot of them seem like eligible bachelors so if you're in the market for one, this would be a nice place to start!As for the restaurant, I've dined here (drunk) and all I can remember is that the sashimi was good quality, the portions were small, and the price kind of put a dent in our wallet... so maybe next time I'll be smarter and go to McDonald's instead, haha.

Come here when you are looking for a place to chill with nice view and serves alcohol. It gets very crowded at night though, so naturally it will get very noisy as well. You will have to put an extra effort to hear on what the other person is saying even when he/she is sitting right across you.Not recommending this place as your first date or business meeting venue. Portion-wise the food at this place typically is very tiny. However you could count on that the chef will decorate your meal to make it look very appetizing. Pretty food, pretty view.Last but not least, they do take reservations.

I was contemplating to rate this place with either 3 or 4 stars.There are PROS and CONS:Pros:1. Nice awesome view if you're lucky enough to get window seat2. Small but elegant setting3. Good quality food and fresh sashimi4. Fusion modern Japanese dishes Cons:1. Unfriendly staff 2. A little bit noisy due to small space3. Overpriced4. Tiny portionBest menu so far:Beef tataki (pan seared sliced beef)Tofu steakSeasonal sanma sashimi with ponzu sauce*I personally wouldn't order sashimi because it's overpriced and nothing special about it at this restaurant. However I think if you do eat meat, beef is always a good choice here. :DI'll be coming back to try other things soon! I'll keep you guys posted!Tip:If you don't wanna break your bank, try not to go for a dinner here when you're really starving.
Service was frustratingly slow and the food overpriced for what you get...

I've been here a couple of times for lunch with friends. Their set lunches, though not cheap, offer good quality food at reasonable prices. We had the nori crusted spicy salmon for $30 which came with a salad, miso soup, rice and mochi dessert. The salmon was of a generous serving, cooked perfectly moist and tender. The mochi dessert is always the highlight of my meal because it's delightfully chewy and fragrant - I wish they'd provide 2 pieces instead of 1 every time. I do find the price of $5 for tea a tad exorbitant but you're paying for a nice view with a relaxing ambience. It can get crowded at lunch if you're in a big group so make reservations on Chope.

I've eaten here many times and even had my 32nd birthday dinner here.  I am crazy for the Spicy Hachimitshu!!  It's like a cucumber martini infused with wasabi.  The sashimi is pretty darn fresh too.  Caution: Extremely pricey menu

Don't let the name mislead you, this restaurant sells good Japanese nosh and good cocktails, and nothing sleazy. The great food will be sure to hit your unami spot. If you are down with a friend, be sure to order a cocktail each. Their mixes are delicious. I will recommend the Ume Mojito.Be sure also to get the Tai Carpaccio, a platter of thinly sliced Snapper topped with truffle sauce and shio konbu. Ok let's skip the fanciful words and read this: fresh sashimi with flavourful truffle = a clear winner. The Pork Belly with Truffle was melt-in-your-mouth lovely and left a aromatic aftertaste swirling in your mouth with the shaved truffle. Plus, indulge in the Fresh Sashimi Platter (with Maguro, Amaebi, Hotate, Hirame, Hamachi and Sake) which features fresh cuts of plump meat, no scrimping there.A word of advice, be down there when you are feeling ready to spend and order without looking at the price list. Also, be sure to grab seats near the wide windows so you can dine with the view of the city skyline.

Kinki is overpriced, in my opinion. However it's worth checking out if you go for their weekday lunch sets! I got the executive sashimi set for $46. The set came with miso soup, rice, pickles, a fresh salad and a mochi dessert. The strawberry cream mochi wasn't anything great, and the green tea mochi also had a cream and red bean paste within, but I thought the best one was the simple peanut mochi that had no filling.The rice was just normal white rice, so if you want Japanese rice, they charge you more for it. This seems rather outrageous, if you ask me. It's a legitimate japanese restaurant, so they should be serving proper japanese rice! The miso soup was average, salad was very fresh and crisp, but the cream mochi was too creamy so I didn't enjoy it. The sashimi was very fresh though! It was pretty good quality, and there was a wide variety. They have 2 pieces of each type, and one sweet prawn. They even give you 2 pieces of the fatty tuna and scallops, which are pretty premium.The service staff aren't friendly, but they are efficient at filling up your green tea cups and clearing your plates, but they're a miserable looking bunch with nary a smile for anyone.The other saving grace is the view you get overlooking the bay and their chic interior. I really love the strange but interesting light made of black cords and bare light bulbs arranged to look like a chandelier on a low ceiling. Save it for a special lunch date or business lunch meeting, I suppose, but I find that it isn't great value for money here.

This place was LEGEND...wait for it...DARY! The view from the roof top bar was phenomenal and though service could have been a tad bit better the food downstairs was amazing (and that's coming from someone who really isn't a seafood fan)! We had platter after platter of some of the best sushi and seafood I have ever had. Definitely try the hot dynamite maki (my personal fave) and the hirame carpaccio. Can't wait to go back!

Boon Tong Kee (or more affectionately known as boons) is one of the more famous chicken rice shops in Singapore. Chicken is velvety and the rice is fragrant without being too oily. Drizzle copious amounts of black sauce, wallop a large amount of chili on the side, and you have heaven staring at you on a plate. The best thing about this outlet of Boon Tong Kee is its location. Sitting right on busy River Valley Road, the outlet is the perfect post clubbing spot - especially because it opens till pretty late too. I think I have stumbled into the restaurant at 4 am before, and they were still willing to serve me (I might be wrong though; everything was pretty much a haze). Yummy, comforting food at 4 in the morning - what more can you expect from a restaurant?

I feel that Boon Tong Kee has been unfairly slighted by 'foodie hippies' that criticize this place just because it has been commercially successful. Despite opening up branches here & there, and having that super-LOL TV advertisement (not sure if it's really aired or just viewable in their own TV inside their restaurant), I feel that Boon Tong Kee has not sacrificed its quality.I've been frequenting this River Valley branch for a decade now and the quality has always remained consistent. It is, admittedly, not the best chicken rice in Singapore but it's close to my house and opens up till late, which is certainly a huge plus point.Aside from the chicken rice, I love to order the deep fried boneless chicken feet. Served with some sweet Thai chilli sauce, it perfectly complements the rice.A small tip: They don't serve the ginger/garlic mix if you don't ask for it.

It is not the best chicken rice I have ever had, but it is convenient when I do want some chicken rice in a more comfortable air-conditioned seating area. The white chicken tastes good, with their potent chilies. What a pity that this restaurant does not serve chicken rice soup, which is complementary in other chicken rice stalls & restaurants. You would have known that their mini fried tofu that comes with wasabi sauce is great like a snack or side dish. Another dish that I like over here is the spinach with 3 different types of eggs. I would say they have a not too bad rendition of this dish that I really like. Apart from the queueing at times and sharing of tables, I wouldn't mind coming here more for my dinner fix. ;)

A wandering sage once said, "I'm crazy for chicken rice!"since those wise words were spoken, I've lived my life striving for the ideals represented by that quote. and it is in that spirit that now I must deliver this heavy message: Boon Tong Kee is only ok.since emotions are sure to fly high at this declaration of mediocrity against this populist favorite, let me break this down as objectively and deliberately as possible:chicken (dark meat) - the dark meat was delicious, but then again it's dark meat, which is always delicious. one thing that sets Boon Tong Kee apart is that the meat has been deboned, excepting the leg. that's a huge plus for this lazy ABC.chicken (white meat) - drier than expected, this was a bit of a let down as it looks perfect, but is clearly not as tender as my front runner for chicken rice and baseline for comparisons, Tian Tianchicken (skin) - not gelatinous enough, this was also a disappointment. whereas the skin on tian tian is good enough to eat on it's own and gets even better when eaten with the meat, the skin here definitely adds to the meat flavor and texture but can not stand on its own. chicken rice - very aromatic and flarvorful without being oily, and they even serve it in a pyramid. I was quite happy with the quality of the rice here, but i would have to give a slight edge to Tian Tian, who's rice is slightly more fragrant and has better texture as well.other factors - no chicken innards is a "no good" from me. the place is air conditioned which is a huge plus relative to typical hawker center fare.

Boon Tong Kee is a perennial. And a perennial near-delight. Their staple chicken rice dish is tasty, the sauces just about right. The poached chicken is typically juicy, though if like me you don't fancy a super strong chicken flavor, the chicken breast is better - ask for only that. BTK's rice is great, full of flavor and with a hint of pandan that makes it quite special. The real gem are the sauces - BTK's trademark red chili sauce and the sweeter brown (Hoisin?) as also the fresh ginger paste make for the magical Singapore chicken rice taste - each on its own, or in any combination with the chicken and the rice! Yes, freely mix n match what is on your plate - for an equally delightful result do what you may!It is the average service, erratic stocking of even chicken, and a mediocre set of alternatives that take away a star from this rating. And 5-star Hainanese next door has slipped in this count too, so you're left with a choice between two quite good but no longer superlative eateries if you want chicken rice. Still, a reliable, enjoyable outlet with atypically long hours for a good plate of chicken rice, night or day.

Perhaps Oscar Wilde is right and the only thing worse than being talked about is not being talked about. In which case, Boon Tong Kee must be pretty damn pleased. I think it's safe to say by now that this chicken rice is nothing if not controversial. There are people out there who swear by it and contend that it is the best in Singapore. There are also people out there who will scream until they're blue in the face that it's terrible and best avoided.Such is the perennial issue of chicken rice in Singapore.I'm going to tread the middle path. I think the chicken rice here is pretty good. It's not the best chicken rice I've had in Singapore, but nor is it the worst. Would I eat here repeatedly? Sure. It's accessible and open late. Service is slightly transactional but works fine. But if you're on a chicken rice tour in Singapore and have the luxury of time allowing you to hit up multiple places - then give BTK a shot. Maybe it isn't the best but the name and the fame would indicate you should at least try it once. Right?

I would have given BTK 5 stars in the past. BTK has always been one of our favorites so needless to say we must eat it on this trip. Thing is, they posted the opening time as 11.30 but it wasn't open when we got there. We did a little shopping at Great World City and the place was already pretty filled when we came back. We ordered the chicken rice for two, deep fried tofu, prawn roll and kang kong belacan. I sometimes forget how the food in Asia is right sized. The chicken portion looked pretty small to me. Still tastes just as good, nevertheless. The kangkong belacan is pretty good. Husband pointed out that they don't give soup? We still enjoyed the food but the bill was pretty hefty for the amount of food we got, with the drinks and extra rice etc, we paid like a little over $50. Sorry BTK, love the food but can't afford to eat like this every time. We went to get some at the hawker centre the next time we wanted chicken rice.

Definitely the best chicken rice in Singapore -- sometimes referred to as steamed chicken or white chicken.  Tender, juicy and flavorful --- they serve it with the sweet dark soy sauce and chili sauce but I ask for the ginger sauce which gives it another layer of flavor.  For the perfect bite, you should have on your fork the rice, chicken dipped into the three sauces and a small piece of cilantro.  They don't take reservations so try to arrive when they open at 12nn.The other dish which is a must try is the "Raw Fish" --- its their version of ceviche but the fish is not marinated in vinegar only but a mixture of sesame oil, vinegar, soy, and cilantro.  Aromatic and flavorful.Other dishes that are good are the fried bean curd, cereal prawn, green bean in XO sauce (warning this is spicy!), and if you want to be adventurous -- the battered boneless chicken feet.

A friend brought me to Boon Tong Kee here in Singapore and I must say, this was definitely the best Hainanese Chicken Rice I've ever had.I've tried the dish in Toronto, and at various food courts and hawker centers in Singapore - but this restaurant had the smoothest, tastiest steamed chicken I've ever had the pleasure of trying.Between the 4 of us, we ordered a half chicken order, with rice and an additional dish of Fried French Beans and Scallops with Spicy XO Sauce. Each dish, from the chicken, to the flavourful rice to the crisp and delicious beans / scallops, was enjoyable.I've since introduced it to coworkers who have shared their appreciation for Boon Tong Kee. Highly Recommended!

Maybe once, a very long time ago, Boon Tong Kee had acceptable chicken rice. But I no longer remember those days.To be fair, the chicken rice itself is okay. The rice is nice but oily. The chicken is okay but really oily. It's just that everything else about the BTK experience is so expensive, and so meh. Other than the chicken rice, everything is meh and not that great. The chicken rice itself is quite expensive comparatively and also okay only lah.So... for a late night post-clubbing chicken rice fix, I much prefer Five Star chicken rice next door, which is cheaper and tastier.
Expensive but the quality of their food is fantastic. Succulent chicken meat. Fragrant and tasty rice. Please do try the fried tofu!

Most chicken rice lovers know of Boon Tong Kee - but, not because it is the best. Standards have dropped quite a fair bit since I first ate here when I was 17. The last time I had it for supper, the chicken was practically swimming in oil and no longer as tender I remembered it to be. The rice was fragrant and well done, I have no fuss about that. Chilli and ginger dips deserve a mention for giving a good kick to the meal.The best thing about the River Valley branch is that it opens till late, like post-clubbing late - fantastic for odd cravings at night.

BTK at RV does a pretty decent steamed chicken but the roast chicken errs on the dry side. The rice is OK but have had better elsewhere. The fried tofu is pretty good but the sweet and sour pork is quite disappointing .. one of our orders came a tad under cooked! The good thing is that they're open till pretty late but you definitely pay a lot extra for that!

Been living in this area for nearly five years now. Come here for supper at least two to three times a week. High quality of food is very very consistent. There was never a bad day in this place. I leave this place happy and fully satisfied Everytime and have NEVER been disappointed even once. This restaurant is a well-oiled and superbly managed and executed business. If they are selling stocks, I will definitely buy. Favorite dish is roasted chicken which gets sold out very fast. Must come in afternoon or reserve.

One of SG's most famous chicken rice restaurant. They have multiple branches across the city - my personal favorites are the classic Balestier and River Valley outlets. Although pricier than your typical hawker fare chicken rice, the chicken rice here are really good / worthy of its name. Chicken meat is juicy, rice has a fragrant smell, sauces a good complement. We also like their fried tofu appetizer and three egg spinach. Definitely a place to bring out-of-town visitors to try the city-state's famous dish
I went there for the chicken rice..taste good!! Good place for family to eat dinner togetherCONCLUSION = RECOMMENDED!!

Quick service during lunch time with comfortable seating and air conditioning!My friend and I ordered the half hainanese chicken with two plates of rice. Returned the appetizers. The entire experience was fuss free. The food was decent. Nothing to rave about, but it wasnt bad either. I'd say it was sufficient to satisfy my chicken rice craving for someone who hasnt been home for a year!

Had the chicken and rice with kai lan . I was pleasantly surprised. Roasted chicken was nice and hot with a little bit of crispiness and I really enjoyed the flavor of the chicken rice. Would definitely try again. It seemed a little expensive though, 1/2 chicken, 2 rice and veggie came out to 40$+

Don't know what the fuss is about, this place is perennially crowded. Went there for lunch and ordered their famous chicken rice. Rice was cold, chicken was barely warm either. Very little sauce as well. Prices are cheap, but you get much better Chicken rice even in Portland!! Many many more options in SP so give this one a miss.

This place is open late, and who doesn't like a place that is open late, sure they might not have the best chicken rice but they are open to the whee hours of the night.  Fighting jetlag, and you are hungry, this place is open.  It is pricier than most places, but when it is 130am and you want some chicken and rice, this place is open.

This is just another overrated chain that is too commercialized and had lost its flavor. There was no soup. Service staff impatient. Honestly this is just a place to scalp tourists. (If you are reading this before coming to Singapore, you can find better chicken rice in Clementi and Chinatown) 2 bucks for wet towels and a little more for appetizers, which is just Chinese braised nuts.Chicken Rice has almost attained a cult status in local context. Please improve service and food quality I'll promise to go back and try it.

I love the chicken rice here because they prepare the chicken rice well, it's not busy, the servers are friendly and the spicy sauce is great! I really like boon tong kee because of it's ambiance and because the chicken rice is sooo good. I really don't have a complaint about this restaurant and i think boon tong kee is really good!

This restaurant is not an honest establishment. It seems to belong to the same Boon Tong Kee group of restaurants but per Ah Leong (the Manager), it serves "higher class" food made from "premium" ingredients compared to the Ang Mo Kio branch, which is supposed to be the "lower class" version.I ordered some take away via phone and was attended to by Ah Leong. He took my order of Salad Prawns (which price was indicated as SGD15.00 on their online website).When I picked up my order of prawns, the restaurant charged me SGD42.80 (not including GST yet) for 1 order of Salad Prawns. I was flabbergasted as it was thrice the price that was listed online! When I questioned Ah Leong, he claimed that the price indicated online was meant for the Ang Mo Kio branch and that the prawns used at River Valley was far superior than that used in AMK, thus costing thrice the price.He was very aggressive and said that if I could not afford it, I could request for a refund and was extremely vocal about it, attracting attention from other customers. I was embarrassed, paid and left in a huff.I was surprised yet again when I returned home and opened my box of prawns because there were only 5 pieces of prawns, each no more the length of my little finger, coated with layers of flour. That means that each prawn costs about SGD9.00. By the way, the prawns were tasteless and in no way considered "premium".It is unbelievable how such unethical establishments still last in Singapore. Definitely not recommended as you will definitely feel cheated after dining there.

First time to have this white chicken in Singapore. SGD13 for half a chicken with out the rice. The rice is separate.This place has no napkins. They set out wet towels that is not free. They charge you $2.00 per wet towel. Take note that the appetizers they give you is not complimentary. They charge for that too.Over all the experience was blah.Chicken was just ok.

4 stars for the food, but I would say it is really expensive here.$20 for 6 pieces of fried pork? Crazy. Hainanese chicken was tasty and pretty good. Worth it if you want to try it at a place that makes it well.

There are many popular places in Singapore that are famous for their Hainanese chicken and Boon Tong Kee is one of them.Hainanese chicken comes in two version (roasted/boiled) and Boon Tong Kee serves both. We had half roasted and half boiled Hainanese chicken. Both was nice with moist succulent chicken meat, but the roasted had a slight crispy skin. But if I was to choose a favourite then it has to be the boiled version.Although Boon Tong Kee is popular for their Hainanese chicken, I found there are many other dishes that are also nice. One of these dish is the crispy cereal prawns and one I do recommend to order. The prawns were massive and were definitely jumbo prawn. It was messy to eat but it was delicious. I actually thought this was the highlight of my our meal.

What sort of chicken rice place doesn't serve soup with the chicken rice? Why don't they give ginger unless you ask? Is it deliberate that they make you ask for more chili instead of having it on the table so you can help yourself? And their chili isn't even that good. Quite simply put, this branch of Boon Tong Kee seems to be more for the tourists. It's great that the staff speak English because my mother doesn't speak Mandarin and we're quite sick of how people assume that everyone speaks Mandarin. No they don't. That all being said, the breast meat is dry, there isn't that delicious layer of congealed chicken oil beneath the skin, and they don't serve soup. I have no idea why I ever liked coming here for chicken rice, but trust me, from now on, I'm going next door to Five Star.If you do end up here for whatever reason though, order the crispy tofu. That stuff IS THE SHIZZ.

I used to go to the Boon Tong Kee on River Valley Road and get take-out chicken rice late at night because they operate till 4 am and I lived just down River Valley Road when I first moved to Singapore.  In terms of chicken rice, there are cheaper options of the same quality (if not better) such as Five Star (next door) or Tian Tian but I find that their chicken rice is pretty good and the quality is consistent.  I also like the chilli sauce and their take-out packaging is very nice and neat.So last week, when I picked up my family from Changi and we were looking for a lunch place, I decided to go to Boon Tong Kee.  It's close to my apartment, is air conditioned and serves good local dish.  I did think about taking them to Tian Tian but with all the luggage and stuff I don't think it's a good idea to line up in the hawker center.  This was the first time I dined in the shop.  The aunties there are very friendly but they are extremely good at up-selling.  We were not sure about what else to order apart from chicken rice and the auntie suggested cereal prawn which is their specialty and so I said ok.When the cereal prawn arrived they looked humongous (like the size of my hand) and I quickly checked the price on the menu, WOW it's SGD42 (the most expensive cereal prawn I ever had).  To be fair, the prawns are of good quality and the four of us had 2 prawns each so it wasn't that bad and we were ok with the higher price.  The prawn dish ended up being the most expensive item of our meal, more than all our chicken rice and vegetable added together.  We were also really stuffed as we probably over-ordered. So, do be careful when you order and check the prices so you know what you are getting yourself into!  That said, my everyone was very happy about the chicken rice.
Great food. Kind host. Great atmosphere. I only wish I had taken photos before jumping into the food :-)

This place is incredibly overpriced and disappointing. The margaritas taste like there is no alcohol at all. We had a waiter that invariably pointed us towards the most expensive things on the menu. Our meal for three was over $500.The Mexican chocolate dessert was decent though.Paul has a review which is currently "not recommended" that says it all better than I could. I would have given this two stars if I didn't think it was so overrated at present.

Grasshoppers in my food! why???First off, this is a restaurant with great decor in a beautiful setting within Chijmes. Major points for that. Service was good too, no issues here and found the staff to be pleasant. Overall the food was tasty too. Not the best tasting ever but on food taste merits, would be worth another visit. What bothered me most was the fact that they put grasshoppers in my order of Guacamole. I respect that grasshopper is found in Mexican food as a delicacy but if you are going to put bugs in the guacamole, please disclose that on the menu before I drop $18 on it. The menu clearly says: Guacamole - Pico de Gallo, Tortilla Chips $18. Why would i expect to have grasshoppers in my Guac if it was advertised as "Guacamole, Pico de Gallo and chips"? When we questioned the wait staff, their answer was "because it's Mexican food".I'm from California where we eat our fair share of Cali-Mex and I've never had or heard of grasshoppers in Guacamole. I understand it's a real thing, and that's totally cool, but friggin' disclose that REALLY important ingredient on the menu!I also got the Chicken Mole dish ($34). It was comprised of a chicken breast dropped into Mole sauce. They didnt even bother to put sauce over the chicken, let alone slow cook it, mix it or marinate it. Literally just chicken dropped into sauce accompanied by Chinese/Thai style rice...We also got the corn on the cob. I was expecting some Nacho Libre style corn with the white sauce and spice. We got baby corn on the cob instead. I must admit that the donuts that came with the corn were the bomb. those were extremely yummyWhile the atmosphere was cool, we felt the food preparation was very underwhelming and expensive!

We had a late dinner here on a Thursday evening.Chijmes is generally not the place where you'd want to go for a quiet, peaceful dinner, and boy was the place busy for what naive me thought was the end of a regular working day. The operators of the various eateries at Chijmes seem to be engaged in a fierce competition of who can play music loudest as part of their campaign to astroturf maximum amounts of fun to the venue, and the result is that in most venues you hear the soundtracks of at least three other places plus live music and can generally not hear each other talk. Unless of course, you scream at each other and add to the overall cacophony. Not exactly romantic.Yes, you could argue that if you're a claustrophobic, crowds- and noise adverse kinda fellow, you should just stay away from Chijmes altogether. Point taken. But if you now are one such fellow, and happen to get stuck there hungry and desperate, then maybe... After some wandering we were relieved to find that El Mero Mero had a nice, non crowded back room where the music of the other eateries was not quite as audible and we could discern the beat of what came out of their proper loudspeakers, and better even, we could actually talk to each other, one or those totally underrated activities it seems these days, where a 'fun night out' often gets equated with blood coming out of your ears on the cab ride home.So, long story short, they get points for a bit of good old fashioned privacy and peace in an otherwise rather caustic, crowded environment. But now to the stuff that matters: The staff was friendly and attentive, we got taken care of promptly. But do double check the bill before you pay - we had an extra dish on ours and almost didn't notice.The interior is nice and cosy, the usual interior designed eatery experience, old bookshelves with Mexican sounding books and the works. Not exactly a fireworks of novel ideas, but providing a good ambience for some nice enjoying of foods.They feature a small selection of Mexican beers, the usual suspects, but also smaller breweries I never heard of before. The usual north of $10 beer prices are to be expected in a place like this. We're supposed to be sober at the office tomorrow, after all. If you want to get hammered for cheap, surely there's a kopitiam nearby.I went with the carnitas tacos, and they seemed just about right, like what I remember they were from the taco trucks in LA. Except, of course, the ones from the truck were $2.50 apiece, while here three are SGD 26. It may sound shocking, but I'd almost say that's an acceptable bonus for foreign food, and a peaceful ambience.All in all, a not un-recommendable experience. Not the most uniquely original place in the world, but you can't really blame anyone for not experimenting too much in a locale where rents surely must be astronomical. So, give them a chance, and they get three stars, which is to say: good, but not awesome.

Ok, so I went there 3 times, before, and last night was the only time I ate there!Previously, the prices scared me away. I mean, for mexican food, it's expensive, and how premium can the dishes be, using the traditional ingredients?It was in all honesty, a little bit of fusion, like 20%, and the portions were just perfect, but it was expensive. The only exceptional dish was the chocolate dessert, but most places do it well.I really don't know what to say. It's in a premium place, and it's commanding palatial prices, but the food is essentially mexican, which is as basic a cuisine as possible, and then it tries to be fusion-ish.I've no reason to return.

One of our Singapore faves and we often bring guests. Proper classic margaritas and a couple of other interesting cocktails (one that is something like a mango lychee habanero martini) service is consistently friendly and knowledgeable. Orlando always participates in service and says hello. The El Mero Mero ceviche (ceviche served in a Bloody Mary mix) is a light, tangy must - have starter. We've tried most of the tacos. The fish are hands down my fave. These serves are on the small side but perfect if you had starters and might want to share dessert. Skip the dense, doughy churros. Totally have the pecan pie, tdf .

Ambience was nice, really trendy with an open kitchen.  Highlight of the meal was prob the appetizers: guac and chips, salsa, and grilled baby corn (REALLY good). But $16 for guac that doesn't have any special is pretty pricey.  The beef burrito and the vegetarian & carnitas tacos were mediocre. We ordered four desserts (chocolate, rice pudding, pecan pie, pineapple) but the only good one was the braised pineapple. Service was ok, nothing good or bad stood out. We most likely won't go back for Mexican.

I don't know why this has so few stars but I really like this Mexican restaurant. My future sister-in-law is Mexican and like from Mexico herself and she was the one who brought me here first. They have very good tequila cocktails and I love their food! She says the chicken mole is super authentic. I came back a second time with another friend of mine from USC before we went to bible study and we had three different tacos each - one beef, one chicken, and one fish. I highly recommend the beef and chicken. The staff recommended the fish. I am a beef and chicken kind of person, not really into seafood, but we devoured all 3. I remember it was on the pricey side and the restaurant was not super full, but we went for an early dinner 6pm and the first time I came for Sunday brunch before I had to fly off. More packed on Sunday. Less packed at 6pm. But I like this place and I'll go back with people that can afford a little more to pay for the ambience and the food.

We wanted to seek out a great Mexican restaurant and found it we think we had! We started with:Guacamole - chunky yet creamy that went superbly with the red and original nachos. It was Taco Tuesday today so we whacked only the taco list! We ordered:Kurobuta Pork "Al Pastor" - caramelised slice of pineapple with strips of pork. I found the pork rather mild in flavour and quite Asian tasting. Ok tacos. Roasted Dorper Lamb - burnt chunks of onions and other wonderful something with slices of grilled lamb. This one is very good!!! Grilled Free-Range Chicken - spicy popcorns are added in this taco but not that you can taste it. The grilled chicken chunks were really good! Not as good as the lamb but very good still. NZ Angus Beef Tenderloin - this! THIS was the star of the night! The seared slices of beef were SO good!! Biting into the burnt fats were just flavour bursting in the mouth! Wow wow wow!!! I could eat this everyday and twice in Sunday!Excellent meal and service is good! Definitely a come-back-for-more place!!

Long overdue update to my previous review! I was last here years ago.Overall: 4 stars with the Entertainer App deal, 3 stars without because it is Pricey. If you have the app, definitely try this place out. My 3 friends LOVED the place. If you don't have the app, I'm on the fence. Go if you're absolutely craving good Mexican food and want something fancier-looking. Else go for Belmonte Latin Foods.We paid $75 for 4 mains thanks to the app! The waitress said we could use the promotion for anything (including appetizers and desserts) below $30. Portions are decent - 4 mains for 3 of us (our last friend had already eaten) was too much, although I wonder if 4 mains for 4 people might have been too little. Probably about right if you're not huge eaters.Grilled Wild Fish Tacos ($28) - 4 starsPretty solid good fish tacos.Creamy Green Enchiladas (Tiger prawn) ($28) - 3 starsMy friend loved the enchilada sauce, although I thought there weren't enough prawns and the (corn?) taste of the enchiladas was a bit too strong.NZ Angus Beef Burrito ($29) - 3 starsDIdn't have much of this as I was pretty full by then. Nothing special, and the beef was a bit tough but the dish was cold by then.Roasted Poblano Pepper ($26) - 3.5 starsWe loved that it was stuffed with grilled corn! Expensive dish for a pepper though.Unfortunately I'm not as much in awe on my second visit, and I suppose it's because I've tried Belmonte Latin Foods (another plug for this humble down-to-earth and reasonably priced cafe). So I'm not jumping at the next opportunity to return. But if you're in the area, want fine-dining Mexican food for a fancy date, want something different from your usual food-truck burrito and taco, or have the Entertainer App, hit up El Mero Mero.
The food was decent and the atmosphere was great. We had the tacos and octopus, and enjoyed our meal.Worth a visit for good Mexican!

Worst food ever. $18 for something they call a cerviche that is not only non edible and a massive ripoff. Avoid this place look the plague.Can I give this place zero stars? Or negative stars?Just look at the pic of the cerviche..Worst place ever.

Was initially hesitant to try this place after reading the bad reviews but some folks in our party wanted to try so off we went. I was surprised by the food quality -- the tacos were excellent, ceviche was good and desserts not too bad. Despite the empty restaurant and many waitstaff and front of house folks milling around, service was dismal. The waitstaff could not speak English, had trouble keeping orders correct (wrong food served). Not sure that I will be back as tons of other food options around.

Mostly Mexican favorites dressed up to cater to the high-end crowd, with "high-end" prices to match.El Mero Mero replaces Señor Taco and is owned by the same guys. In the open kitchen, I saw that the restaurant came decked with the latest in high end cooking equipment. Josper Grill ($30,000)? Check. Sous vide machine? Check. Vertical spit for the Al pastor grilled meat?
