This venue always have a queue waiting except a certain timing. Do see the food photos and you will know how appetizing their food are.

I ordered the sho yu ramen, with an extra egg. The pork was very tender and flavorful. The soup base was tasty but a bit too salty. Overall, it was a good ramen bowl for the price. However, I was a bit deceived by the noodles, which were a bit "hard".My friend ordered pork cheeks which were amazing. They literally melt in your mouth.The atmosphere is okay, very noisy but expected in Singapore. There are some seats outside but it's very hot.

friend: "hey, have you heard of hokkaido ramen santouka at mitsuwa market place in torrance? wanna go? but must take bus, ok?" me: "where's that? huh, must take bus there ah?? sure good or not???"friend: "world best bah!!!"me: "ok lor, if you say so."and that was back in 2007, when i first started yelping in the USofA.memories of that first bowl of tokusen toroniku shio ramen, despite it being in a food court setting, was forever etched in my mind.a big shout out to my "friend" who, for privacy reasons, wish to remain anonymous.fast forward to the future(present) and many time zones later, hokkaido ramen santouka finally made it's debut in sg at the central with crazy fanfare and snaking queues! and when it opened it's second outlet at cuppage terrace, some sanity prevailed and this outlet became my current go to joint instead.why here?firstly, a big plus is that i never had to wait for a table. secondly, they close at 12am from Mo-Sa with last orders at 11.30pm. i have once walked in at 11.31pm and they still accepted me!:)thirdly, the presence of a more japanese clientele and their smatterings of the language plus ecstatic slurping is sexy to me. fourth, the presence of an outdoor seating option for al fresco dining is appealing on those cool, windy, romantic nights.what here?just remember, tokusen toroniku shio ramen!ok, that sounds a little too linguistically challenging.how about just remember "CHOICE PORK RAMEN"?!yup, that's what they call it!what i like about this is particular ramen is that the toppings are served separately.this enables you to get a sip of the pure, salt infused, 20 hours simmered, never boiled but kept at optimal temperature, collagen rich, melted marrow and fatty creamy, broth before the toppings permeate the unadulterated taste.you can then choose to add what you like, into your ramen, when you like it.ah, the power of choice!:)but eventually everything, save the pickled plum, finds it's way into my ramen matrix as if to balance the healthy diet equation.if any deserves to be singled out for special mention, the slices of pork cheek definitely ranks top.it is the ONE.it is the special ONE.it is what kama otoro is to tuna, rare, rich and resplendently tender.the noodles are never soggy, always springy.so slurp it, like you mean it and become the choral symphony of a ramen orchestra!

Thanks to ippudo orchard being full, I grit my teeth to try santouka again after the bad taste and trauma Indonesian santouka has managed to fuck up the ramen. Thank god I tried santouka again. I ordered the shio classic ramen and everything is perfect: al-dente noodle, fresh tasty soup, melt-in-your-mouth chasiu, perfectly soft-boiled tamago, Reminiscence of that first time I had santouka in San Diego, California. Will be back again when I have a craving for Hokkaido ramen.

A good substitute for those who are addicted to Ichiran Ramen; though, Santouka can be too generous with the salt at times.Price-wise, it's also not the most affordable ramen one can get out there. But overall, a good, tasty ramen.

The Char Siu Ramen (Miso) is one of the must tries. The char siu portion is generous and the ramen tasted great!The Tokusen Toroniku Ramen (Shoyu), which is roasted pork cheeks ramen. A first taste of the ramen without mixing the ingredients felt great. Definitely, mixing the ingredients made the ramen much nicer. The Spain Iberico pork cheeks were full on flavour and smooth. The ramen tasted smooth and springy. A definite must try if you are here, and the servings are generous too!A recommended place for ramen and one of the best ramen restaurants in Singapore as voted by numerous websites and blogs, I personally feel the same that this place truly deserves to be one of the tops. Must come!

I'm not too sure i like this ramen and having had it twice, i would say, it's really just okay. I was intrigued by the chicken broth option since I tend to find pork too thick at times. When I had it though, it wasn't spectacular, and certainly the soup was warm instead of hot. My friend had the pork with a spicy mince meat added, it was okay as well. I liked the spice but the soup was too gelatinous. With the increasing amen joints invading this small nation, i'm not sure santouka would be my pick if not for sheer convenience of proximity.

Met a motley bunch for lunch last week, and we found ourselves in Somerset, looking for Japanese food. A hot tip told us to head to Cuppage Terrace, and Ramen Santouka was the first to greet us (well not physically, because it's a shop, not human, and... oh nevermind). Now I'd heard of the place before, so in view of the other options (Indian, Greek, Indian, zi char, closed izakaya, closed ramen by Nantsuttei in OG!!!) I suppose Santouka was an easy pick.Hungry people order fast, and thank goodness for that, because they were 30 minutes from the end of lunch hours - closed kitchens and I don't do well together.Highlights? Pork cheek is STELLAR. Get it. I didn't order it, but I should have. I pinched a good couple of slices of a buddy anyway (see what I did there? I pinched the cheek? hahah... oh nevermind). I was a-hankering for tsukemen for some reason, and it was pretty good, except the soup wasn't very hot. And when you're dipping cold noodles in semi-warm soup... it gets cold quick. To qualify the temperature though, there s a page in the menu about why the soup temperature has to be just so.Other than that, the lack of functioning air-conditioning needs to be addressed. I promise you, I can sweat it out with the next glutton at a hawker centre of your choosing, but I don't know if I was meant to do the same in this restaurant. The presence of the box-fan provided some relief, but was it meant to be there in the first place?Parting words? Pork cheek. Get it.
I think santouka and ippudo are the best ramen stores in Sing. The noodle soup and specially grilled pork are second to non.

I didn't think much of this place when I had my salad with soup and sandwich shortly after it opened. I thought it was a wannabe following the success of Saladstop several years ago when there were just not many salad places. Fast forward to this week. I wanted some fresh veggies and this was the only option then. I am glad I gave it another try. The menu has been tweaked and there are more varieties in what's available. Plus I found the yummy toppings which i like - mushrooms and beets. Besides the regular salad with the cold deli or protein, you can also order hot protein for your salad. It may look confusing but it is quite easy to choose what you want. You can also add the soup and sandwich to your salad. As this is part of Cedele, you can be sure the soup will be good, likewise for the bread.

This s an awesome salad chain in the heart of Orchard. For $12, you get a mixed of romaine lettuce and pasta/rice, choose 2 proteins and 4 greens and either an iced tea or orange juice.The pasta and rice selection are delicious, always a plus for someone who tries to eat healthy yet still want some carbs choices.The proteins are great. There are the heavily marinated mushrooms, the cheese, smoked salmon, sausages, chicken and tuna to choose from. The greens are not too shabby, I would say. However, I have quite a tough time to choose them because I personally don't eat quite a few greens, thus leaving me with options like edamame, braised brinjals, red beans, olives, nuts, eggs.  There are  also broccoli, corns, beetroots, sprouts, cherry tomatoes, etc. For $13, you can have a bowl of salad and a soup. It is a good deal, only in Singapore.

Salads are fresh and delicious, prices are affordable,  and I really love their sandwiches despite them being small. Aside from their very average soups, there's nothing lacking. Full marks! 5 stars given for:+ price + taste+ service+ ambience/cleanliness + revisitability

Ok I have always loved eating here coz they used to serve big portions and u can request for two salad dressings ....but recently what happened to the salad portions? To be fair, They do try to help customers by maintaining the price but visibly reduced veggies and even prawns are down to 3 as one staff explained politely, " management directives..." Ok... Depending on staff , some are friendly and accommodating but others are....meh... Not very consistent.

My favourite place to grab something delicious and healthy in Singapore! It's fast, its affordable, and you can load up on loads of veggies - the portions are huge! The one thing that I've always felt was missing from Singapore was a good ol' salad bar and low and behold - one has now been presented to us!I actually come here on the way to work or whatever just to get a salad. Sometimes I'll drive down with the family to grab salads and then go home again if theres no food in the house (and we're all being a bunch of lazy people .. but really just for the fact that their salads taste a lot better than what we would make haha).Would definitely recommend toss & turn if you're in the orchard area. There are now quite a few 'salad bars' but this is definitely my favourite with taste, options, flavour and portion size. It's a winner!

Toss & Turn by Cedele should be a fairly new concept, so new that even their service staff had trouble articulating the various sets that we tried ordering!Dont get me wrong, the food is pretty good and the concept of sandwiches, soups and salads is great. Plus the fact that it's be Cedele, you can be sure that quality of the food is awesome as well and it's really great!However, the number of sets are somewhat too many, it confused not just the consumers but also the service staff. A mix of small/half sandwiches plus large/full size soup vs the other way round and not forgetting throwing salad into the whole combo, it's not easy to grasp that quickly.Because of that, the order process became a struggle. As everyone queued along the "canteen" line, the wait took a little long as most customers had to clarify the sets and details of the order with the service staff. Perhaps giving it a little more time, things will get more familiar.
Rude cashier man will make you lose your appetite. Decent food, by Singapore standards.

We came here on a Friday night and they were out of almost all their toppings for the custom salad. In exchange, they let us pick another protein, but could only have 1 topping (instead of 2 protein and 4 toppings). Well, not that I really minded, but seriously, shouldnt they have stocked up their ingredients in preparation for the weekend crowd? Mind boggling.Anyhow, serving portion here, especially for the salad, is VERY generous. I shared a full sized salad with my girlfriend before gym, and we were both decently filled. They have a half portion salad too, but for more than half the price. Not sure how the Math works. But hey, I'd recommend just taking away the remaining of your salad if you can't finish it. Makes another meal :)

I really wanted a salad for dinner and was thankful that this is close by to work. A regular salad for $9 and you get 1 salad base, 2 deli/protein and 2 veggie/crunchies. I was delighted to see them offer smoked salmon (generous rolls) and shrimp so i chose those but my other favorite beetroot was in the same category so i couldn't have that - bummer. Choices in general were not that many and the self serve salad dressings were not that exciting in variety too( i think it was just 5). in short, I'm just spoiled by what Salad Stop offers at almost the same price. Unless I'm craving for smoked salmon or shrimp, i don't believe I'll be at Toss & Turn much. I must however mention there is deal going on now and it's a full sandwich with either a small side of soup or salad for $12.90; the shrimp avocado with spicy sauce sandwich actually looks quite yummy.

Love the huge portion. A mountain of healthy ingredients for $9.90! You can choose a salad base (vege/cous cous), 2 proteins and 2 others. Their salmon and edemame are safe choices! Sometimes the vege is abit tough to bite. Oh By Friday night, they run out of a lot of ingredients... :/ Pretty hard to get a seat as well since it's such a small store.

What a steal!The portion is huge and the food itself is very delicious. They also made ordering quite a breeze with very clear pricing and instructions. Base (greens/pasta/couscous) + 2 proteins (salmon/shrimps/mushrooms) + 4 toppings (beans,etc.). This is a complete different experience from Saladstop - limited free toppings and the proteins are always too pricey. I do hope Cedele opens more of this salad bar.

My to-go-place for a quick lunch/dinner.$9 for a huge salad/cous-cous/rice/pasta base (you could to half-leaves-half-couscous which I always do), two protein choice (e.g. egg frittata/ roast chicken / peppered prawns) and two veg/beans choices (e.g. raisins / carrots / edamame / corn). You could add any amount of seeds/nuts to your salad from the dressing/nuts counter. I would normally have half of the regular salad for lunch/dinner and keep the other half for my next meal.I always feel that $9 is a steal. Long lines always during dining hours. But the waitstaff are really efficient and so the lines move quickly. I really really hope that Cedele will open up a few more Toss & Turn eateries around the island. The other salad places are way too over-priced.

I have lived in Singapore approximately three weeks and have already eaten here three times! I love it! As a very health conscious eater and an American who has yet to learn the ins and outs of more local fair, this is my "safe go to" when I am out and about. I always get the same thing: mixed salad with chicken breast and walnuts, edamame, red beans, broccoli and red bell pepper with plum sesame dressing. I feel like the portion is really generous. Ingredients are fresh and tasty. It slightly reminds me of a spot in the US, Salata. However, Salata allows unlimited toppings of fruits and veggies. Oh the glory! Nothing will ever be that great, but this is a fine substitute while I am residing in Singapore.

Best value place to grab a healthy lunch. HUGE portion of healthy goodness for 9 bucks! Makes me feel salad stop has been ripping me off lol The only con is it gets real busy around lunch time, the queue can be really long and finding a place to sit is quite a challenge
Good salads... food appears to be fresh...  tasty salads and interesting dressings...

My husband and I went to Park for the first time a few days ago with our two young daughters, and we were all happily surprised. It is rare that we can find a restaurant that fills all of our requirements, as my husband is vegan and the kids and I are vegetarian (not to mention the fact that our kids are picky eaters!). However, it was a home run for all of us! The kids loved the truffle fries and the truffle macaroni and cheese, as well as the juice; I enjoyed the fantastic caprese salad, and my husband enjoyed a grilled vegetable sandwich. The location is great, the wine and beer prices were reasonable and the atmosphere was very pleasant. We will definitely be back again, though we live rather far away near Bedok Reservoir. I wish they would open another location close to us! However, in the meantime, we will keep making the trip over as the food and atmosphere are worth it.
Yummy duck salad with quiona! Loved everything about it. Anqi's duck confit was really tasty too!

Came here about 6pm on Friday- we were addressed as we walked up and told that they didn't currently have any available seating despite the fact that I could openly see three empty tables. Sure- maybe they were reserved... but we weren't even asked for a name. Honestly felt like we weren't "good enough" or something for them. Disgusted at the lack of service. Will not be back.

Consistently good coffee and good food can be found here at Park. Truffle Mac and cheese is quite good, complex cheese flavor and strong dose of truffle oil. The food in general is not too exciting in terms of concept, but what they have are well executed and delicious through Park's own interpretations. Portions are always substantial and good value for money.  My own and family favourites are the spam chips and truffle fries for sharing, omega 3 salad for some greens, the burgers- Thai chicken, vegetarian and Park burger (with the blue cheese is good!), Mac and cheese.

(P)ark is a brand new pub-bistro setup on the site of the old Holland Village carpark.  You will recognize the huge old rain tree that was in front of Starbucks.  It's still there.  It's just a part of a big grassy park now, called Holland Village Park, sited over where the carpark used to to be.  In this small park, sits (P)ark.It's a pleasant enough place and easy enough to find in Holland Village to be an awesome meeting place to hang out before heading out for dinner or more serious drinks.Holland Village has become a very neat hub for dining, spa/beauty and pubs.  Conveniently accessible via the Circle Line (Holland Village) and surrounded by bus stops.(P)ark is all steel and glass and as I alluded to in my tip, a pretty jewel box when lit up at night.  Other than the location, it holds it's own by being quite serviceable with nice outdoor seating (covered) and a reasonable drinks menu, although truth be told there are a dozen other watering holes in Holland V to choose from which have menus just as and in most cases more extensive than (P)ark's.Worth a stop by in you're in Holland V to catch the vibe of the place, and a good vibe it is too.  I love you, Holland V!  You rock!

Had the Park Blue Cheese burger,  Stout Pork Ribs and Omega 3 Salad with the missus. Everything was excellent. The salad was especially yummy. The burger was as good as the omakase burger I had the previous week.. Except I couldn't finish the buns on this one. Ribs were very nicely marinated (in Guinness Stout no less!) and came in a very generous portion. We could barely finish everything and had a tub of fries left over. Worth a second visit to try their other items..

PARK is a nice little new gastropub in HV.  They have a pretty straight forward menu that serves up good and interesting food.  The atmosphere is nice and relaxed. The food was well made and good.  I thought it was very good actually considering it was such a casual atmosphere.  I had a seafood salad.  The dressing was a little bland but its more a matter of personal choice. I also had a chicken breast with pureed spinach that was pretty tasty.  I like that the chicken wasnt over cooked and dry.  They have a great menu and I definitely have to go back for the truffle mac and cheese.  The service was great and the staff were really friendly.  Definitely much better food than most the bars in HV.  I think its my new go to spot in HV for drinks and food.

This is the only place I've seen where you can get a few pitchers of beer served in a giant table-top Eiffel Tower. The beer itself was very light and almost sweet, as if it had a hint of champagne in it. The location was very crowded, which made it difficult to get a seat. Most of our group had to stand on the outside edge of the bar.
Only dined here once. Food was surprisingly good and i loved the Eiffel Tower-:)

It all began when I saw the long line outside a Japanese restaurant at St. Mark's Place in NYC. As Singapore has taught me, a queue must mean something's good for the taking, so I joined it for an hour-long wait in the blistering New York winter and was rewarded with a steaming bowl of springy noodles with chashu that has been cooked so long in broth that it melts like butter in my mouth. This was Ippudo New York.A year later, I heard Ippudo was coming to Singapore, and was insanely happy. Even though it wasn't nearly the same, and the chashu here was not as mind-blowing, the rich broth of the red bowl and the same springy noodles convinced me to order kaedama (additional order of noodles to add to your remaining soup). My husband, who often has half a bowl of soup left over in his ramen bowls, polished off the whole bowl of splendid broth.6 months later, I completed my homage when I went to Roppongi Hill's Ippudo in Tokyo. This was the ultimate chashu shrine and which all Ippudos aspire to be I think.While the wait staff at Ippudo Mandarin Gallery attempt the same level of enthusiasm as their counterparts in Tokyo, I am reserving my fifth star for when their chashu attains the same melting quality. This beats Tonkotsu King I feel, but then again, perhaps my feelings towards Ippudo are heavily influenced by my experiences in all three countries.

Update: When I wrote my first Ippudo review, I actually haven't been there for months, maybe a year in fact. For some reason, a couple of weeks ago I decided to give it another go and to my pleasant surprise, Ippudo has improved. One of the reason why I disliked Ippudo was that their ramen broth was always lukewarm by the time it got to the table. But now, it's much hotter and this really matters. You can also choose the hardness of the noodle now, which is another important factor.Ippudo, you're back on my go-to list.

we got introduced to ippudo through one of our friends who raved about the pork bun.. i'd skip it here since the meat it cut pretty thin and it was just mainly sauce on a bun.. nevertheless.. if you do come here.. get the ramen... it's pretty damn good.. pricy for a bowl of noodles.. but it's definitely quality stuff.. the broth is truly flavorful
Great, and unlike the NY location which is the single most yelp reviewed restaurant in that city, there is rarely a line.

I haven't tried the Ippudo in NYC or in Japan, although I wish otherwise. I will, one day. For now the Ippudo in Singapore opened to amazing fanfare. They were, I think, one of the first superstar ramen places to set up shop here.I like the ramen enough. All of it. I just don't love it the way I love Nantsuttei.

Years ago, I would never have thought of eating at Mandarin Gallery but in the past two years, more and more restaurants and cafes have been opening up and gaining popularity, using the expensive, upper-class feel of the area to complement their fine cuisine. However, I was not too fond of the ambience at Ippudo with loud music playing in the background, a stark contrast to the other quieter and more relaxing restaurants in the building. The tonkotsu ramen, though, I really liked. The soup was good enough to drink. The noodles were springy in texture while the pork belly was soft and decadent. The egg was also cooked just nice with a slight runny yolk. The normal ramen costs $16 while the egg added an additional $3, but was well worth it. The sides, on the other hand, was less outstanding. I did not really like the rather tough gyoza and though the shrimp mayo was rather good, it wasn't quite worth the $13 for 4 shrimps. Ippudo is slightly pricey with an average meal costing about $25 to $30 with drinks, but the ramen lives up to its reputation. The biggest thing putting me off though is the queue which goes round a table inside the small restaurant and out of the restaurant, and groups with 3 or more people will not be seated until everyone is present. If you go there, try the Sakura flower tea for a more unique tea experience!

This is one of my favourite ramen places because the deco of red plush seats is amazing and so is the delightful array of ramen types you can choose from. The broth does not disappoint and you can even choose the tanginess of your noodles and strength of your broth. Their sides and desserts are pretty good too.The only drawback is that this place seems to draw long lines. The last 2 times we were there we had to queue for half an hour, and the waitstaff refused to seat us until all our guests have arrived.

Ippudo came to Singapore with much fanfare, but I'm sad to say that it doesn't really live up to the hype. I'm not saying it isn't good, it's definitely one of my top few choices if I were to have ramen, but it's not in my top 2. Having been to an Ippudo outlet in Japan before in Yokohama, I'd say the only similarities between them are the long snaking queues. When it comes to the ramen, the portions and condiments found in Ippudo here pale in comparison. Taste wise, I can honestly say it is very close, say 85% to what I had in Japan. The service staff here are decent but compared to the ones at Santouka, pale in comparison. However, for people who may not find Santouka to their liking, or for those who are new to ramen, Ippudo would be a very good choice to begin the foray into the world of ramen. Just don't bring them to Ajisen to skew their views of what ramen should be!
Absolutely fantastic, top of the line ramen. Just delicious and deeply flavorful.

The ramen broth is above average, and the noodles come perfectly cooked. I would have given it a four, but the side dishes were maybe the same standard as any normal japanese restaurant. Also, it is super packed and crowded, which is really not a turnoff for me if the food is outstanding, but in this case, not worth it.

My second time at Ippudo and yes the ramen is REALLY good, however after this visit I did leave wondering if it was THAT good considering the 40 minute queue and the $70 bill for two... That's a lot of dosh for some noodles! Granted, we also ordered some very over priced limonata and a gyoza to share, but still... I found myself questioning whether the quality/price ratio was in order. I had the poor belly ramen with the seasoned egg, and yes, the meat is tender and the egg was perfectly soft boiled, but I did find the noodles rather salty. You choose the texture of your noodle and I can't say I found much of a difference between my boyfriend's firm and my soft! You can pay a few dollars to have your noodles replenished if you have enough soup left in the bowl. This is always tempting when placing your initial order but we manage to reign it in by the time we have slurped up our bowls. The service is Japanese friendly, with the welcoming "moshy moshy" being yelled out left right and centre. Service is also efficient - good when you're waiting (and willing that waiting line to go faster), but leaves you feeling a little short changed when you've eaten your $35 meal in about 15 minutes! Jury is out, I might go back for a third time, but I probably should try out one of the many other ramen options out there first!

Instead waiting on lines outside in NY, you'll probably better going here if you get a chance. Yes, you'll still have to wait in the same long line, but inside a nice air-conditioned mall. So far the best ramen that I've tried. Ordered the akamaru chashu with extra tamago - definitely worth the long wait! The interior itself if very hip and modern, almost like a lounge.

The ramen is awesome, and the pork buns are to-die-for with soft succulent meat. Gyoza is so-so but looks popular. However, they are slightly more pricey compared to other ramen shops like Marutama Ramen. However, my biggest beef is the queue, be prepared to wait around 45 mins if you go there at peak hours during dinner and lunch

To date, this is my favorite ramen in Singapore! The noodles, the soup, the egg and the chashu... the best combination I can ask for! My usual order is usually the Shiromaru Tamago (Ippudo Original Tonkotsu with flavored egg). Also, I like the interior of the shop. It's simple and cozy, which is really a great place to have a good meal and catch up with some old friends. The staffs are usually quite attentive as well, overall attributing a positive dining experience. On the downside, I really hate the queue sometimes. The queue can get really long at the weekends and during dinner hours. So to avoid frustration, just avoid those times. Last but not least, complete the ramen meal with a delicious and light sakura flower pot tea! This is a must-have for me whenever I visit Ippudo as well. The first time I tried it, I liked it already. It's enough to share with a friend, but for some reason or another, they do not allow refill for the pot. Enough said. Oishii!!!

By far the most authentic and best Ramen in Singapore! The endless queue speaks for itself. Ippudo strictly does not do take away as they believe the ramen quality will be compromised. There are million options to choose from but mainly they are broken up into spicy and non spicy, miso or chashu base. Ask your server for a recommendation if you're unsure. With every ramen tasting this good, you won't have to worry about your choice. Bite-size gyozas are also a good add on to have with your meal. Fir drinks do give the Aranchiata Rossa and Choya mix a shot, a truly refreshing drink that will tingle your senses!

I used to live in New York City, and Ippudo was my drug on weekends. I'm used to lining up for hours just to get into this joint. This particular outlet serves really awesome Hakata style ramen in a chic building in the middle of Orchard Road. Fancy a power lunch? Ippudo. Fancy a spot of tea? Ippudo. Fancy waiting 1h for a seat for dinner? Ippudo. I must say that the pork buns don't taste as good as the ones in NY. But pork belly? Who can say no?!?!?!?

Ippudo has been one of the most talked about ramen places every since it opened in Singapore and the queue that never fails to form outside the restaurant is testament to its reputation. However, I do not think that the standard of food served here lives up to its reputation (and the hype). The ambience is nothing special either, and can get a little too noisy at times. I had the char siew ramen. The broth I had was overly salty, and left me very thirsty for a very long time after. Too much MSG i suppose. What I liked most about my dish was the egg as it was cooked perfectly, hard boiled on the outside yet a little wet at the yolk. Other than that, its your average ramen place, just a little more expensive and a lot more crowded.

What to say? I'm a huge huge fan of ippudo. Whenever i think of ramen now, i will think of ippudo. Love the texture of the noodle. I always order the hard version for the ramen.Not fogetting to mention my love for spicy shrimp mayo. The mayo really goes well with the freshly fried shrimp. 4 in a plate is definitely not going to satisfy me enough.Lastly, please go early to avoid the queue. Even during weekdays, it will be super crowded.

Is it the best ramen in Singapore?  Maybe, maybe not, but Ippudo is now one of my favorite ramen places here and it makes some of the best ramen broths anywhere. The central location and beautiful, open design in Mandarin Gallery also add to a great vibe here.Food:The ramen is the star here, but it's not just about the noodles (I liked the thinner texture here), but the combination of broth and toppings (the charsiu is nice and tender).  The broth here is intense, rich, and well flavored.  I had the seasonal variety with black miso, a touch of garlic oil and spicy oil. That broth is worth the trip.The pork buns are WAY too hyped up here.  I tried those as well as the shrimp buns and was completely underwhelmed.  The buns are tender as is the meat, but there isn't much flavor in the meat.  The shrimp were also small and the batter was way too thick.   There is no wait if you are here before 12 pm on a weekday.  I haven't/have no desire to experience a weekend wait but there is a decent bar and waiting area if you have to wait.

This Japanese Restaurant is tucked in nicely in Mandarin Gallery - pretty chi chi - but it's quality and menu is worth checking out. The quality of their noodles is amazing - fresh and their Ramen portions are huge. I had the Sesame Salad the last time I was there - and it was fresh, healthy and really really yummmyyyyyyyy.What I Love: Their authentic Japanese fare. Their dumplings were amazing. I had the Salad which I returned to have another time, as well.What I Don't Love: Their prices. They are pretty steep - though their food is yummmy. A starter, green tea and a main would set you back $30, at least. I spent $27 on my last visit. They also do not seat you until your whole party is there - thus, my friends had to wait 45 mins - though, a reservation was made. That wasn't fun.

The good: Best ramen in Singapore (forget what the self appointed "ramen heads" say). Atmosphere is good, service is on the ball.  The bad: Always packed. Probably the longest line aside from Astons (god only knows why people queue there). The ugly: Many people stick their noses up because of its chain restaurant feel/reputation. I say good food is good food, regardless of how many outlets there are.  I don't need an "authentic" experience to appreciate good food.

Overrated. The restaurant banks on its name being big in Japan--and charges an extraordinary amount of money. We paid $75 each (also had beer and appetizers), which is ridiculous -- this is ramen.The ramen tasted good, but was not worth the money. There was nothing special and there are lots of other ramen restaurants that can be had for half price (Ramen Champion, etc). Don't believe the hype.

blahh, nothing nearly as good as the NYC one, nope, not the ambiance, not the ramen nor the pork buns (which are my fav at Ippudo NY). Food there taste and look like a more expensive fast food ramen joint. Or maybe now that I live in Asia, my expectation for good Jap restaurant has raised, or maybe they are just a fast food ramen joint.

Came to Ippudo with a couple of colleagues last week. I was interested in trying this location out, as my only other experience at Ippudo was the one in New York with my girlfriend. I had high regards for Ippudo based on my experience in NYC, but sadly, I must believe that the experience I had here in Singapore did not meet that expectation.We arrived to a queue of about 2-3 tables ahead of us. We arrived around 8PM and it seemed to be a good time to come, as tables were turning over.We managed to secure our own table (there appeared to be options for a more communal, big table experience too.I ordered the Shiromaru Special - that included an egg, bamboo shoots and cubed pork, served on a side plate. Generally the ramen was nice and firm, and the broth was rich. I would've appreciated if they had actually served the special, with the extras IN the ramem - as they tasted cold when left on the side plate.I've sought out many ramen places in my (short) lifetime thus far, and while Ippudo ranks in the upper half, it definitely isn't the best I've had. Wouldn't feel bad recommending it to someone if they enjoy ramen.

1. Shoyu ramen- Nice crunchy noodles- Good broth, light and not too heavy. Perfect for those who prefer clear soup rather than a thick, creamy broth.2. Love the egg tamargo! - So used to having my tamargo cold and placed on top a shushi but Ippudo's take on the hot tamargo has changed my stereotype of it being a solely cold dish. Definitely like it hot better now (not many japanese restaurants serve it this way). - Their tamargo is like an omelette but slightly sweeter. However, the only downside is the 1-2 hour queue :( definitely not worth the long wait. I recommending going during odd hours like 3pm (no queue).

Tried the gyoza, the spicy black ramen and the akamaru ramen.  The gyoza were excellent, nicely cooked and still piping hot when they were served.The spicy black seemed to be a seasonal dish - it was peppery, spicy and full of flavor!The akamaru was miso based and a bit peppery but overall much more subtle.We arrived bang at noon so no wait...the place was full by 1230 so I would try and get there on the early side to avoid a log wait.

Very crowded but worth the wait in line. Ordered the original ramen with the whole shebang, its one of the best ramen i've had in Singapore. Also ordered the pork bun which is good for starter. They also have umeshu cocktail which i would try it next time.

Extending my review from NYC on Ippudo. Simply AMAZING!!!!   As it is ranked one of the top five in Japan, it lives up to its expectation...in NYC, Japan and now in Singapore. Queue is always long so be sure you get there early and don't forget to try the original ramen they have

If you have been to Japan ippudo, you will very much prefer the Ippudo in mandarin gallery. The taste is richer and the noodle is tangy. This shop isn't easy to locate for first timer but one can easily spot the queue on the level 3 of the shopping mall.Service is good and you will get to choose different types of soup and noodle as well as the side dish to go by. You will not be disappointed with the char siew and soup, as the quality is well managed. However the price is on the high side and I would recommend this as one of the best ramen shop in town .Interior design is great with a woody touch, giving patrons a homely feeling, but keep in mind the close proximity between tables and the long queues might not make this an ideal place to chill out.

I like that ippudo always has a seasonal menu serving up special seasonable ramen.My standard order though, is the Spicy tonkotsu ramen with egg. Tonkotsu broth with spicy miso which adds a kick to the otherwise very thick soup. Noodle portions are pretty small, but you can order an extra serving of noodles.The line is very long, so definitely go early to avoid the wait!

I visited Ippudo for the first time last week and had a pleasant experience. I was expecting a line but was surprised so see only one party ahead of me. Then again, it was past 2pm on a Sunday.I ordered a bowl of Karaka-men spicy tonkatsu and a calpis soda. The food was delicious as expected and I'm sure there are ramen experts out there who are better equipped to provide a concise review on the food. However, I just just wanted to mention that my positive experience would not have been complete without the fine service at Ippudo. The staff were friendly (without being overbearing and annoying), polite and attentive, all of which are as common as a minister taking the MRT ;) Congratulations to Ippudo Singapore- I will make it a point to return soon.

My basis for trying out Ippudo is because it's the biggest ramen brand in the world. I had read about the Akamaru Shin-Aji "Modern Tonkatsu" ramen and came here prepared to order it. Perhaps my expectations had been too hyped up. I was expecting an out-of-this-world broth that would blow my mind and scream "umami"! Reality: Very good though nothing incredible. The broth was a tad too oily for my liking and not as flavorful as advertised. I ordered the special so it came with ajitsuke-tamago (flavored egg), char siew cubes and bamboo shoots. I personally prefer my ramen eggs to be on the slightly runny side and the yolk in this one was 75% hardened. The char siew slices that came in the ramen itself was fantastic (soft and flavorful), but the cubes were a a little too dry and hardened. It's hard to get bamboo shoots wrong so I finished all of that. I don't care much for ramen noodles themselves, so I won't comment on the texture or quality. Overall, I'd say Ippudo is a dependable brand of ramen. I'd compare it to Starbucks maybe - decent and consistent but not memorable. Just like how if you really wanted a special kind of coffee you'd go to a family-owned café, if you really a special bowl of ramen, you'd go for those hole-in-the-wall places, ideally run entirely by Japanese staff.

I used to love this place- I'd get the Akamaru, sometimes with a side of stuffed chicken wings (which was surprisingly good). I dragged my parents here quite a few times! But I began to realize the soup is way too thick, salty and tasty for me, and it's just become not worth the wait. I prefer Ramen Keisuke at orchid hotel, Marutama, etc to this. The taste is very similar to the original branch in New York and one in Malaysia, though, so props to that I suppose!

So...this is the faaaaaamous Ramen that is worth queuing an hour for huh? Well, if you're able to slide in at 4:30PM, you'll be treated to no queue and pretty much have your pick of the tables. Located on the 4th of Mandarin Gallery, it follows suit with the mall's equally pricey options. Their regular ramen starts from $15, not including Singapore's ++ Syndrome (7% GST + 10% Service Charge)I really like the fact that they ask for your noodle texture preference - soft, medium or hard! I dunno about you, but I'm pretty picky about enjoying my noodles al dente. Medium texture is perfect for that! To be honest, the taste of the ramen itself is probably only worth about 3 stars. The broth is incredibly rich and borderline too fatty & oily. The portions are probably not worth the price but hey, you're technically paying for the brand! The real standout is actually the char siu pork - so flavourful and tender! The extra star goes out to the staff who were super sweet that day. I accidentally left my camera at the table and they actually came out of the restaurant to try and find me. After I realised what had happened, I went back and they had kept my camera safely at the front counter for me. Really appreciated that gesture and it was one of those rare instances that I didn't mind the extra service charge one bit!

Love the rich tonkotsu broth, it's definitely done right, on the thicker side full of umami goodness. The chashu is also very flavorful. My favorite is the spicy tonkotsu ramen! The price is one of the highest I've ever paid for a bowl of ramen though, and you'd have to add on the egg for some of the items on the menu. The appetizers are very tasty, I recommend the wings. A good treat every now and then!

While the broth is a hearty and soothing highlight to the dishes here, I don't find the overall experience to be much better than any other high-end ramen place. I recommend the pan-fried gyoza for an appetizer. The spicy version of the traditional soup was preferred over the original, although the broth was great for both. Oddly, the higher-priced spicy soup comes with no meat in it (well there were some tiny slivered pieces of fat, but not anything you could reasonably call meat), while I was expecting those large medallions of pork that come in most ramen bowls. At $18-25 a bowl, a good broth alone just doesn't cut it. Furthermore, the dining area is quite loud because the entire staff shouts at everyone who walks in the door. It's one thing to greet people at the door, like many Japanese restaurants do, but this is like an uproar of indistinguishable noise that continues throughout your meal.

My favorite ramen in Singapore. I first tried it in Mandarin Orchard 4-5 years ago, then I went to another branch recently I think it's this one. And I always go for the one that has the black garlic in the broth. Yummy! But don't eat here too much because it's got a lot of fat in the broth, but that's also what makes it good I think. I also like their gyoza.

We got here when it opened (to avoid the long wait since they don't take reservations...I think for weekends especially). There was no wait, but by the time we finished, there was definitely a long line! Moving from NY with the extremely, long-wait but delicious Ippudo there and having tried the disappointing no-wait Ippudo Tao in SG, I wanted to give the main SG Ippudo a chance. I ordered the Akamaru Tamago and the pork bun. The ramen was very good and definitely redeemed my thoughts about Ippudo in Singapore. The pork bun was a bit underwhelming having tried the pork belly buns in NY...perhaps it was because the NY ones were pork belly instead of just pork...the fat really must've made the difference haha.I would definitely come back at an odd time to avoid the wait again. This is probably not the best ramen but it's up there. The service was attentive and my water was always being re-filled (I love when I don't have to flag down someone to re-fill water!).

When I still lived in the states, I went to Ippudo everytime I visited new york. I was so excited when I found out that they opened a branch here in Singapore! Imagine my excitement and my high expectation when I came to their branch in Orchard road. Though the place has always been crowded, the service is really good - at least at the time I came there. The waiter/waitress are very attentive when taking my orders and when making recommendation to my friend who is not familiar with Ippudo before. I ordered tonkotsu and the pork bun. They were as good as I remember. Will I go back again? Definitely. I could pretty much say that so far Ippudo is the only ramen restaurant where I get my ramen craving fix in Singapore.
Long lines during lunch time but not as good as the one in Japan. Too salty and noodle was overcooked. Still rich broth and quite authentic compared to other ramen places run by Singaporean owners.

I headed to Ippudo  by chance, was around the area when my friends and I were craving for ramen for dinner. Since it was somewhere that many people have been talking about, we decided to try it for ourselves.I had their spicy char siew ramen. The broth was nicely rich and was comforting to drink. Ramen cooked al dente. Char siew was well-done. Essentially, a decent bowl of ramen which most will enjoy. But I didn't quite get the oomph I needed from the bowl.My friends say that their egg is the best dish on the menu. I might need to return to figure that one out. I'll say, trying it for the sake of trying?

While it is not the most impressive but it carried the title of being an authentic Japan noodle!this is my 2nd visit: despite it is a busy day of its 33rd anniversary celebration, it offered real cheap pricing of 3.30+ for per bowl of Ramen, it didn't cut cost or scrimp and save its ingredient, it is still the world-renowned ippudo standard!Hence I round it up to a 4 star, even though it is a 3.4-3.5

Famous for its ramen.Have not been here for a Long time.No queue at 12.30 p.m. on a Saturday but it was full by about 1 p.m. Shiromaru SpecialIPPUDO's original creamy tonkotsu broth served with thin and straight noodles, pork belly & pork loin, bean sprout, black fungus and spring onion. A classic Hakata-style ramen.Selection of noodles: soft, medium, hard or very hard.Love the ramen but am not so sure about the char siew or the 3 layered pork which I didn't find to be tender.Goma Kyuri - crunchy Japanese cucumber with home-made sesame dressing - refreshing.Renkon chips - crispy & tasty lotus root chips - nice & crispy.Beef tataki- well-marbled prime beef slices, pan-seared and served with tangy soy sauce - good.Lemon soda - a non-alcoholic cocktail made with fresh lemons and mint leaves - refreshing.

Quite disappointing, to be honest. While the noodles are OK, the broth seems to lack the flavour of some other ramen places. A lot more expensive than standard ramen joints, I'm not sure what the price premium is for.

Truth be told, the ramen is nice. Hardness of ramen good, not too hard nor mushy. Char-Siew is soft and tender. Soup broth is thick and tasty. So would I go back again? Not quite sure. I mean, I had nothing going wrong with the meal. There was no queue going in, service was good, food arrived swiftly, food is tasty, bill was settled quickly. So what's wrong with me? I supposed it's the up-market feel that maketh my lunch to be more expensive that I was willing to pay for.

I lived in Japan for quite some time, and I have traveled around the world a bit so for me it's quite hard to eat something "not entirely local" in a different country from where the food was invented. I love ramen, so going at Ippudo was a bit of a challenge under certain points of view, but being in Singapore I take less risks than eating ramen in Europe for example. Anyhow, Ippudo ramen is very close to the real deal, tonkotsu soup is rich and tasty, ramen are perfectly made, no complaints there.Only note of demerit is the fake Japanese atmosphere, where everyone shouts in Japanese welcome phrases but know no real Japanese language apart from those lines. Then again, it's all part of the atmosphere so it doesn't really matter in the end...

I'm personally not a huge ramen fan but Ippudo's dishes were as authentic as it could be. You can choose the texture of noodles (soft, medium, hard) for each ramen and customize the toppings. We also ordered the cucumber appetizer that my friend recommended and we're glad we ordered it as it was a good refresher from the creamy ramen broth. Peak hour is from 6:30pm- 8pm so go early if you want to beat the line. Would recommend it for casual dining!

This is my comfort food for Saturday brunch if I felt like having something soupy.This is my comfort food for weekdays' dinner if I felt like having something spicy & soupy. This is my comfort food on weekends' afternoon after a hangover. This is my comfort food on a rainy day.

Like usual, for hakata style ramen, Ippudo is still the king. The ramen is excellent like usual and service is fast and attentive (came during late after lunch hours). Can't go wrong with Ippudo with its ramen.

YUM. This is the best ramen I had during my stay in Singapore! I have eaten ramen in Japan and this was pretty close! The opportunity to customize your meal is great. The broth was delicious and so were the cucumbers and the gyoza!

The ramen noodles are good, no doubt about it. The broth is rich, perhaps too rich. As an appetizer,  I love the lotus root chips.I'm not giving 4 or 5 stars because they don't refill teapots, and won't serve hot water either. As a restaurant in a tea-drinking country serving food of another tea-drinking country, this is just unacceptable. One pot (probably just 600 ml) costs $6. Not cheap!

Service staff was quite short with us, emphasizing their need to get everyone out over the customer's experience. Despite the place listing an 11pm closing time, they stop taking side dish orders at ~9pm and ramen at 1020pm. The ramen was only average despite the $20+ price tag. This was my second time here and unimpressed with the food, service and pricing, I will not be returning.

Brunetti's is a fancy European style breakfast place/cafe located in the Tanglin Shopping Mall. Big you're in the mood for some kind of egg based breakfast or a quick coffee and a pastry, this place will take care of your craving.I tried the macaroons and they come in a wide range of flavors.  I tried the salted caramel, tiramisu, and vanilla macaroons.  All big winners.  I had reservations about coming here because they're a bit pricy (around $2.25/m'rooon) but they ab-soul-utely to die for).Will definitely get some more these before I leave SIngapore.

Brunetti is located in Tanglin mall with an entrance from outside as well.  More of a lunch and dessert place than dinner. Lunch options are ok I think the stars of the show are the desserts and pastries as well as the gelato.  My favorites are the cronuts, oh so good.  The macrons are tasty too!

The food is nothing to write home about - extremely average: no special innovation, not memorable flavours - but the menu offers a decent selection of bistro-type dishes: pastas, salads, pizzas, fish&chips, one burger, sandwiches. Friendly staff, whose main task is to bring the dishes and drinks to your table after you have ordered and paid at the cashier.

Went there for late lunch. They have indoor and outdoor seating, and you have to order food at the counter and they will serve it to you later. The cafe latte was good, seafood aglio olio was averagely okay, the mussels (only 2) were pathetically small and it cost $21.

Overall, is another Italian.  Gelato is nice.  Food is average Italian food.  But remember this is not a restaurant, so the food is more for lunch rather than dinner.ジェラートは普通に美味しいのですが、食事は極普通の平均的なお店です。パスタ、ピザ、量は多めですし、味も悪くはありません。ただ、特別にここに行くということはなく、イタリアンを食べたいなら近くのFORUMにあるBenjaminをオススメします。

My first trip here was just for their cookies which were quite decent. On my next trip I picked up pastries (a selection of tarts etc) which were ok but not amazing. On my third trip i was craving croissants which despite looking nice are awful. They taste like the recipe used oil instead of butter. I'd give anything in that display case a wide berth. We sat down to breakfast here today and while they had as many staff as they had customers no one seemed to be able to figure out how to serve anyone. The kitchen forgot our order twice, sent out the wrong thing an hour later and somehow re-made it in 10 minutes. Even by Singapore standards the service was exceptionally poor. There are so many great new bakeries in town now. I think it's time for this one to move on.

I wasn't too enthusiastic when my friend initially suggested going to brunetti for desserts. I had doubts about an Australian cafe trying to be Italian. Something about that just didn't seem to impress. However, their display of colourful and beautifully decorated desserts got me pretty excited the moment I stepped in. I was very impressed with the macaroons. The Rose flavoured macaroon was very impressive and one of the best i've had in Singapore. Its texture was just right, crisp on the outside yet soft on the inside, melting in my mouth. The flavour was pretty strong but not over powering. I also had the yuzu macaron which was rather unique.I tried their Passion cake, and liked the smooth velvety texture of the chocolate mousse that was infused with raspberries but found it a bit too heavy after a while. I had a flat white there and while it was not the best, it was pretty decent. Overall, I think they are pretty good for their macarons but do not set your expectations too high for their other offerings.

Everyone got very excited when Brunetti officially set foot into Singapore. And I got influenced too, especially since friends who've returned from Aussie kept selling it to me as if they've got a share invested. Perhaps it was the lack of Australian kangaroos or something, Brunetti was okay but it wasn't WOOTS. I like the layout of the place, it immediately leads your eyes to the vibrant display in the long counter. The coffee was good, the pastries were mostly fluffy and sweet, the gelato - don't bother, and service was decent. One negative was that there was no proper queue for ordering - you have to get the attention of the waiters behind counters yourself. So it might become a problem during peak hours - customers have to either 'target' waiters or hang around like a lost lamb. And short people might have to jump a bit.It was a cool and relaxing environment, sitting outside was very airy, pretty good for chatting with a group of friends or if you just want to quiet chillax by yourself.

If you've been to Melbourne, you've probably seen a number of Brunetti outlets in and around town. Well, this branch is the only outlet in Singapore. It's a combination of, pasty shop, gelato shop, coffee joint and sandwich bar all rolled into one. A lot about the outlet is very Melbourne-esque, from the pastries on display, to the coffee, to the ambience.My experience though, was a little hit and miss. Their lattes well good but the pastries were a little inconsistent. I was greeted by a wide selection of pastries and I settled for the Lemon Tart and New York Cheesecake. While I enjoyed the cheesecake, the lemon tart was disappointing.Despite this, I think I might be going back to give their breakfast a try sometime soon.
Yes, the decor is nice, but that's about it.Neither the staff nor the prices are friendly, and the products are average.

Italian style cafe that people familiar with Melbourne will know. They have a great range of cakes and desserts, but their best sweet stuff would be their gelato I think! Definitely try the hazelnut gelato. Everything on the menu is on the pricey side though. Tried having lunch for the first time (their Club Sandwich) and it was pretty good! Would give this place 4 stars if it weren't so pricey

I was at Brunetti after dinner one night, and got rather excited over their selection. The pastries reminded me of Italy, a variety of tiny biscuits and mouthwatering pastries were on display and it was difficult to pick which to buy. The gelato however, was a lot less inspiring. The names were fancy but the way the server described it, it sounded like they simply mixed delicious foods into an ice-cream base, such as Ferrero Rocher for the hazelnut chocolate. Perhaps it was the way he had described it that made it sound extremely uncreative, but as it was closing time and he seemed rather impatient, I decided to just order two scoops for the sake of it. The pastries were variably good and not very memorable, but it was much better than the gelato that I ordered. I've definitely tasted far better gelato in Singapore and I regretted my choice instantly. Next time I'm in the area, I will probably be back to try more of their pastries to be able to get a better gauge, and sit down and have a drink.

Brunetti at Tanglin Mall recently replaced Oomphaticos. Walk by and it will be hard not to resist all the goodies and ice cream displayed in the café. Pastries are pretty good, but a little too sweet for my taste. Everything I have ever tried here, from the cakes to the cookies have been really, really sweet. They have sandwiches and pizza. Ive tried the pizza which was alright, but really bready. I have also had the breakfast here which was probably the best food I have had here. Try the truffled scrambled eggs. Coffee is also a plus point here. They have an old Italian man as the barista, he is super friendly and funny.

We came here for brunch and loved the setting - it was designed just like a cafe in Italy. You really feel like you're transported to some town in Italy as the waiters banter to each other in Italian. It was affordable at about $12 a set and the portions were just right. I had nothing to complain about - save for the fact there were so many delicious goodies that I was just spoilt for choice! Do not come to this place if you are trying to diet! Just looking at those pretty pastries make my mouth water. The pastries are slightly more expensive though - at about $3-$5 for a small sized one, to $7-$9 for larger sized ones. They also make a mean cuppa coffee so be sure to try it!

If you've stayed in Melbourne long enough, you would know that Brunetti is not the best place to have your cuppa or cakes for that matter. The only people that actually frequent it in Melbourne are foreign students which explains why it seems to be all the hype here in Singapore. A place trying desperately to be Italian with pretty looking cakes. Other than that both coffee and cakes are average. Nothing distinct, a sad representation of Melbourne, but definitely a much better experience than Starbucks or Coffee Bean.

Nice pub right in the middle of Clarke Quay to grab a whiskey and people watch. Interestingly enough, they have a minimum age for the interior area. To add to that, the minimum age is different for male versus female. *mind blown*Nice assortment of whiskey selection, but don't expect anything rare. Like all of the drinking establishments around Singapore, prices are going to be fairly steep for a stiff drink. Service is good and the staff kept the drinks flowing pretty well all night. They had a live band here playing pretty good cover of top 40s plus some classics. Pretty good vibes and there were a few ladies dancing, but most of the action seems to be next door at one of the adjacent clubs.

My first time at Highlander. Not impressed. I'm not sure what's the standard rate for beers in Singapore during non Happy hours but $17 for a Corona on Thur night? That's pretty damn steep.There was a live band which wasnt that great. Then again, we sat outside so maybe thats why the audio wasnt good. I did like that they had a TV screen which projected the band performance indoors though :)Service was slow too. Pretty sure there are some better bars around!

Wow - Loads of fun on a Sunday night.  Lovely live music, friendly people, and good atmosphere.  The service was fast and friendly.  They kept the drinks coming.  Drinking can be expensive, but beers run about $15-$20S.  Be careful where you sit if you want to see the show and dancing.  There are several view obstructions in the bar.  Watching the crowd can be half the fun.  Get a good seat.When I was there, lots of people shared tables up front.  Even in the back, it is hard to talk.  Try sitting at the tables outside...very nice.

Located in a pretty happening plaza in Clarke Quay. There's lots of lights and modern looking buildings in the area. I stopped by on a weekend night to go drink with some Singaporean friends.The bar was pretty busy but the hostess put us on a small table outside immediately.There's some kind of promotion going on with Guinness, but it was very confusing because a Guinness girl would come up to us and only take orders for Guinness, then relay the order to the bar. Except for that we already had a waitress so those orders were ignored and we had to go through our normal waitress again. Huh? What exactly is going on here?There was a live band, which was alright. You could see them displayed on video screens outside. I heard some other band while I was going to the restroom, but they were TERRIBLE. I'm not sure whether it was the same band or the band from the neighboring bar which had a shared bathroom.I got a ginger beer cocktail which was alright. As always, alcohol in Singapore is pricey, I think mine was somewhere right under $20. Service is slow and it's hard to grab their attention. I think there is better in Singapore!

Touted as a Scottish pub, the most Scottish aspects of this place are the extensive whiskey list and the kilts worn by the staff.  I must say, however, that my experience with Highlander was pretty positive. The pub grub was delicious, albeit being expensive and marred with small portions. We had the Kobe Beef Burger and Whiskey Prawns, and enjoyed both immensely. The resident band was playing that night, and, while they were certainly not playing music I would normally enjoy (i.e., Evanescence!), they were great performers and their high energy was infectious. By half past eleven, the dance floor was filling up and the atmosphere transformed into party mode. As with most watering holes in Clarke Quay, expect to pay premium prices for the booze and food. Also, Clarke Quay is not always the most conducive place for a casual night-out, what with the hoards of bar-hoppers brushing against your table as they move along to the next stop, and the loud music coming from the surrounding nightspots. It is certainly fun, but you have to be in the mood for a riotous time.

Probably the only place in Singapore you can find Haggis being served, Highlander is unique in that both the food and drinks on offer are great. The selection of malted whisky is quite comprehensive and they also happen to have a very nice selection of Kentucky bourbons, something you don't really see much of here in Singapore. The food is great and you should really try their shepherd's pie, which is served piping hot and filled with chunky meat fillings. Service was friendly and very brisk, you don't have to really wait long for your drinks to arrive, even when there's a large crowd.

Ive put off this review for a loooong time because I insist on giving this place a second, third chances because i love the theme and live band thing they have going on but to be completely honest... This place has one of the worst service staff teams I have ever experienced in singapore. Time and time again I have been served by black-faced waitresses who toss menus at me and seem to have an attitude if I dare ask a question about the menu. The second time I ever came here, i ordered a dozen kamikaze shots to share with two others.. I shot six shots one after another (because they weren't strong I downed them like juice). Six shots in 15 mins should be lethal, I felt nothing. Drinks are pretty watered down if you order anything that isnt straight up.Dont get wrong though, the live band is pretty good and the manager is very sweet. But my goodness, dear waitresses please smile and be a bit more hospitable.  One star for the band and one star for the atmosphere.
This is my least favorite bar in Clarke Quay. The product is super expensive, the service is rude, and the menu is very limited. Only noobs go here.

Everyone's got their guilty pleasures. For Anthony Bourdain, it's plastic cheese. For my father, it's corny crime paperbacks. And for me, it's Highlander in Clarke Quay.I mean, theoretically, this place should activate my gag reflex immediately. It's prime Clarke Quay real estate and going here on a Saturday night is a little like having a ringside seat at a vomiting competition.But, for the same reasons, it's a pretty great vantage point to see carnage comparable to a monster truck derby. And it has the added benefit of an ample smoking area and a really good whisky list.So sometimes, when I'm bored, and it's late on a weekend, and all the usual options just seem too much trouble... I'll come to Highlander, sit and chat with friends over a good single malt and watch modern society at its absolute worst. Bliss.

Nice patio area for people watching. There's a good view of the center of Clark Quay and the water show. Service was good. The music inside was really loud- I could barely think! Menu looked good but we only drank here :) Good scotch selection. One of our group ordered a bourbon and coke but received a vodka coke. Pretty big mistake.

Came here for drinks and live music the other night. The entire experience was meh. The drinks were expensive and the music wasn't fantastic - just radio hits delivered in a squeaky voice. The crowd was mostly made up of foreigners. I probably won't be back.

Four Koreans brought me here. It was very authentic. We had to wait for 45 minutes to get a table.They had a lot of our favorite foods. The mixed pancake appetizer was very impressive. Many different types of snacks and they were all excellent and remind me of the same things in Seoul. The mushroom bulgogi was a high point, although you need to make sure you stir it before the meat gets cooked and sticks together. The Makgolli and plum wine were great.Some people also like the interior because it has a Korean motif, but I think the food is really the reason to go here.
Absolutely delicious meal and value for money! All the dishes we ordered are so wonderful we want to b back here again! Come on Thursday for their freshly flown rice wines!

I thought the food was ok, but probably not worth the price tag if you go for dinner. They have lunch specials. The side dishes were meh and a bit disappointing, but the main dishes we tried were not bad. The agujjim and the kimchi stew we ordered were very generous in portion and filling for our party of 3. Probably not a good place for a big group as seating is limited. I recommend you make reservations ahead.

I was craving for bibimbap and chance upon this place.Came here with my church buddies and we decided to go for Tteokbokki even though we wanted to try a number of dishes. The Tteokbokki wasn't what I expected - I was thinking of Korean Rice Cakes served in a plate with spicy sauce, fish cakes and some spring onions on top. It was actually in Budae Jjigae (Army Based Stew) style. There were a number of ingredients inside and you have to wait for it to cook on a portable gas stove.Price wise, if there is three or more sharing this dish, it was pretty reasonable. The portion was right for the three of us. The interior was pretty spacious too. Service wise was excellent. Upon stepping inside the restaurant, the waiters/waitresses greeted us and guided us to our seatings. While leaving the restaurant, you could grab some Korean candies along the way too. Overall, it was pretty good and my friends and I enjoyed our time there. :)

We wandered into Todamgol during prime dinner hour one Thursday and got the last table available.  While we were glad to score a table since subsequent dining hopefuls were relegated to waiting outside, the table was awkwardly placed by the door and the servers had to constantly lean over our chairs to pass and clear plates for the table next to ours.We thoroughly enjoyed the famed seafood pancake, but at $28, we felt it was pretty expensive.  The redeeming factor came in the form of the 5 free small plates that our waitress was happy to refill for us.  We particularly enjoyed the butter potato and carrot small plate.We also ordered the kimchi soup with spam ($30), but this was less palatable for us than the pancake.  We would not order this again.PARTING THOUGHT: The lunch deals looked very good and very reasonable.  We may be back for lunch.

Disclaimer...being a Korean dude although I am from the US, I am very selective about my Korean food and since I prefer authentic Korean food over westernized or fusion, please consider this when reading my review.This place is awesome~~~~  I come here quite often with my co-workers and sometimes with my friends and this is one of the better Korean restaurants in Singapore.  Then why not 5-star?  Because there are handful number of items that aren't that good.  They might want to consider modifying their menu.  And sometimes, the serving size is very small.  Love their o-deng, kimchi pancakes, seafood pancakes and this weird thing that has squid, pork and some other ingredient in it all meshed together in some hot chili sauce.  Definitely my new favorite thing to have.  Another downside...ban-chan (small dishes) needs to have more variety.  Still love more than half of them though :)

LOVE THE FOOD. Okay so there are lotsa Korean places in SG, but my gawd this was the best bin bim bap EVERRRRRR. First off, it surprised me like crazy cuz it came in a large steel bowl, and the rice...i really dont know how to describe it, but its some goddamn amazball rice. The dish also came with lotsa other lil veggies that don't come with regular binbimbaps. loved it so much. it was also a huge portion for SGD20 and i was holding my tummy out the door. my friends got some meat stuff, but i really didn't pay attention as the binbimbap was just too amazing. i still can't get over that rice. when i mixed up all of my veggies with the rice (this is a regular practice for binbimbaps) - the rice sorta clumped up into little balls....IT WAS JUST SO GOOD.In addition, we got lotsa lil free side dishes that came along. while most korean places offer the lil dishes for free, i never take them for granted, given how some places in SG still charge for WATER!!!!! damnation! anyway - go and try this place. it also happens to be in a great neighborhood with lotsa other bars/restaurants. please try the binbimbap - you won't regret it.

We popped into Todamgol for lunch on a rainy day, and I'm glad we did. It's a but of a crapshoot picking a Korean restaurant on Tanjong Pagar because there are so many of them there, and it's possible that some of the others are even better, but I was pretty happy with Todamgol. We had the lunch set, which just a ridiculous amount of food, and tons of variety. There must have been at least 10 different dishes, not counting the kimchi and other banchan, and all of them were good. We also got an extra side of kimchi pajeon, which was another winner. I wish I could describe the dishes in more detail, but I was in such a massive food coma afterwards that it's all a little hazy now. I'm going back soon, so will try to write an update then.
Lunch was great - for 12 dollars one could a bibinba or stir fried beef with rice and 6 assorted pickles. Thank you for being open on a public holiday when everyone else was in bed!

Where else can you watch ponies trot by as you enjoy brunch? In a lovely little cottage-like house with wooden beams and everything else that makes it feel like a modern ranch, Riders cafe is as laid back as brunching can get. If you take a sanity leave day from work, this is where you should come to get away from it all. Eggs benedict, smoked salmon and pancakes next to horses, the world might be alright again.It's a little out of the way, best if you drive, or else it might be a pain getting in and home.

A non-airconditioned place which is great for brunch. Do get there by car/taxi though, as it is relatively unaccessible otherwise. I love the lush greenery this place is set in, and how it is housed near horse stables. The eggs benedict here with salmon is pretty good -  the portions were not that generous but sufficient. Do remember to make reservations if you want your date to be impressed.

One of my favorite brunch places because of the excellent food and view they have, I am quite sad to find that more and more people know about this place. That's because then it gets really crowded and the quality of the food/service might be affected as well. However, barring that, yes I would recommend this place since I last had it because their brunch was really delicious. It was wholesome, yummy eggs and sausages with the usual other sides. An iced coffee while watching some horses gallop by is nice as well.Prices were also reasonable if I don't recall wrongly.Getting there however will require a car. Otherwise it is too much of a hassle to travel in and out of the place. Reservations are definitely required because it is super popular with the expats and locals alike.

Excluded location tucked away in Fairway Drive near the Singapore Turf Club. Rocked up on a Saturday for brunch one weekend. I didn't have a booking, and Im not too sure if they take brunch bookings, though had to wait for a wee bit to get a table on the verandah. No air con in this place, though they have done well to make sure it quite comfortable and airy. Straight forward comforting food here, think shepherd's pie, beef burger, eggs ben etc etc. Well priced items, freshly squeezed orange juice always wins extra brownie points in my books. Had the shepherd's pie which was ok, would of gone down better if it was perhaps made in the classical way with mince lamb as opposed to braising diced lamb.  Service, at least the young girl who served or table had to be one of the cheeriest I've had in Singapore.

Pan fried snapper ($26++ = $31) - 3 starsSmall portion, and the "creamed kale" turned out to be one kale leaf... when I asked they said the "kale is in the sauce." Snapper was cooked excellently but then ended up being too salty at the end.Service was also really slow, it took our food a good 20-30 min to arrive. We sat by the window and be aware it smells like manure. However it was a cool night and overall very pleasant and the waiters and waitresses were very accommodating and friendly!We paid $15 each using the Entertainer app so I can't complain.

Good food. Nice ambience. The service staff are efficient, informative and accommodating. The food is a decent standard - value for money. Hope they will have more variety in the choices of food available for after Brunch Hours. Place is ideal for a private event.

One of my favorite brunch places in Singapore! I always have trouble deciding between the crab omelet and the Blackstone Benedict, but the best part of the meal: the molten lava chocolate cake. Rather indulgent for breakfast, but it's worth it! I especially love being able to enjoy brunch while watching the horses.

We went to Riders on a Saturday for brunch and it was packed. We overheard the staff saying that the waiting time was about half an hour. Fortunately, we'd made a reservation, so we practically sailed right past the waiting line. I like the atmosphere of the cafe. It was open, inviting and bustling with activity. Perfect place for people-watching. We were seated on the balcony facing the stables. My initial concern was about the smell, but it was unnoticeable. We had the corned beef croquettes, Riders Burger, and homemade sausages with creme fraiche scrambled eggs. The croquettes were good - the crispy, golden brown breadcrumbs gave way to creamy potatoes with the occasional chewy beef bits. The corned beef offered a pleasant pop of flavour that accented the mild potato taste. They were truly enjoyable to eat. The portion was generous too. I expected maybe two pieces of croquettes but there were four - more than enough for a starter. The Riders Burger was all about the beef. The other ingredients were reminciscent of Burger King's Western Whopper, but they were all overwhelmed by the beef. This burger would be perfect for meat lovers.I chose the homemade sausages and creme fraiche scrambled eggs because they came with a leek and potato rosti. Unfortunately they looked better than they tasted. The hollandaise sauce was the best part of the dish. The scrambled eggs were fluffy and creamy, but for the most part tasteless, but that was ok as we had salt and pepper at our table. The rosti was, strangely, creamy. It was essentially fried mashed potato and leek. There was a mild taste of leek on the fried surface, but that was overpowered by the flavourless mush that was underneath. Next to the mild flavours of the eggs and mush, the sausage tasted too strong, which shocks the taste buds. I dipped most of what I could in the hollandaise to get some flavour, but there was barely a spoonful of it to begin with. The food may have been slightly disappointing, but the service was excellent. The crew was attentive and proactive, and we could really tell that they were properly trained to provide high-level service. For that, kudos to the staff AND the owner/management of Riders Cafe for caring. Service really contributes half, if not more, to customer experience and satisfaction. For this, I would definitely go back to Riders (and order other things on the menu instead).

It is definitely advisable to make reservations at least 1 day in advance (they don't take same day booking) as it is still full house at Riders Cafe on weekends. They do take walk in customers but likely you just have to wait for at least 30 minutes or more. It is not so bad as you get to gaze at the lush greenery, clear blue sky (if it is not raining) and listen to the neighing and clopping of horses every time they are led back into the stables. Quite enjoyable as it is not a common sight in this concrete jungle.Being my 2nd visit in a span of a few years, I am glad the food is still as good. We shared the pacific benedict and brioche french toast with bananas. They were excellent. Quite a generous serving of swimmer crab meat with nicely poached eggs and spinach and shrimp hollandaise (couldn't taste the shrimp) sauce. Something different from the usual egg benedict or eggs royale. The soft brioche made a perfect french toast. Loved the grilled banana caramelized with a thin layer of sugar, crispy bacon and maple syrup. The cafe mocha was also decent. Being a full house, service was a bit slow but not as bad as some places. There is no air conditioning throughout, except for the washrooms below stairs, adding to the charm of a rustic setting with fresh air coming in through the verandah. Note: You need a car or taxi to get to the restaurant.

Riders Cafe is one of the earlier brunch spots which was so popular that reservations have to be placed in advance. Fortunately and coincidentally, there was a table cancellation when I called on the previous day of visit and so we did not have much problems securing seats.
