This long conveyor belt were filled with salmon when i first arrived, the variety was improving around 10 mins later.The sushi were okay, werent that fresh, and i wish there are more variety

Well. It is $1.50 per plate and you definitely get what you pay for. The sushi aren't anything special - just plain, cold raw/ smoked fish on rice. Nevertheless, it still satisfies a poor man's craving for sushi! I suggest you steer far, far away from their desserts though, especially their cheesecakes as their "Japanese chefs" have clearly not yet perfected the art of cheesecake-making.

First time at Chili's even though it was everywhere in the US. Here in SG Chili's is quite hip and very busy, there's even a line when we were leaving at 7:30pm. Enjoyable place with tasty drinks and good snacks. I had more than enough alcohol from sharing a jug of sunrise magaritas ($42.90). Nachos with guacamole were thoughtfully covered with cheese - very neat and unlike the typical Mexican pile of cheese and sauces. The guacamole needs more work and salt, but tased ok with sour cream and tomatoes. Cheese curds was not melted enough for me. Also batter was quite salty. Service can definitely be improved. Will be back with the right crowd. #latergram #chilissg #drinks #drklingeats

I've been to this outlet on a few occasions and I've decided that the burgers should be skipped.I stopped by here hoping to enjoy a hearty meal before heading to my next meeting. I ordered from their lunch specials, and chose a Caesar salad and double cheese burger. The salad was fine, but the cheeseburger, though cheesy, had dry patties. The fries were also not fresh, as they were more chewy than crisp. For $18.75, you're better off just going to Burger King or McDonald's for something that costs a quarter of the price and would probably taste better. The only good thing about the lunch specials is that the soda refills are free; none of that $1-extra-to-top-up funny business.However, their baby back ribs and other Tex-Mex dishes appear okay. But if you're in the Clarke Quay area, I'd rather you visit some of the other restaurants in the upper levels of Central Mall for better chances of satisfying grub.

This Chili's is located right in a central area near bus stops and the MRT. It is in a prime position and was even quite busy at the off-peak 3-5pm period. Unfortunately, they have very few people staffed to run the large dining area. Thus, things can be a bit slow and you definitely have to grab someone to get any attention. Otherwise, the food is as good as any Chili's I've been to. The chips and salsa are always a good choice, as their tortillas are paper thin and crispy. The fajitas are one of the classic choices as well and may be enough for two to share unless you have a big appetite. If you know what to expect from a Chili's and want to have it, then you should not be disappointed by this location.

The food is of ok portions and ok taste but with a slightly above average price. We were sitting at these tall tables at the back where the air condition is very cold so we shifted our tables. One of the waitresses chided us for moving the tables without their permission. After which we were afraid to say anything back or to feedback for fear that waiters or waitresses spit in our food. Gosh, why do we have to endure bad service and non-ethical behaviour in our F&B world? I will never visit there again. There are other places that served better food and provides better services.

Oh Chili's, why can't I quit you?Perhaps it's your glorious chips, ethereally thin and perfectly crispy with more salt than I ever need to eat in one sitting... Truly the most perfect tortilla chips in Singapore, perhaps the world!Perhaps it's the curiously appealing, Tex Mex / Asian fusion Southwest Spring Rolls... With the completely unnecessary, but totally appropriate ranch doing sauce?Perhaps it's just remembering the good old days in college, hanging out at Chili's where my friends worked, milking the free refills and bottomless chips and occasional free dessert.Most likely it's the amalgamation of all of these things that makes Chili's a guilty sentimental pleasure.  One thing's for sure... I'll not be quitting it anytime soon!PARTING THOUGHT: bring your passion card and save 10% off your bill!
It is a 2.5 stars for me. Docked half star for price. Standard American fare that seems overpriced.My quesadillas were $20 at lunch.

Chili's is one of my favourite places for Tex-Mex cuisine. And ribs! Because we regularly hit up the original branch at Tanglin Mall, comparisons between that and its sister outlet at The Central were inevitably drawn when we dined there last weekend.Service differs, the Tanglin Mall one being better staffed, with more efficient service, whereas the staff at Clarke Quay were a little more frazzled and bumbling. Food, too, was a little lackluster at Clarke Quay compared to the commendable grub at Tanglin Mall. Clearly, the standards between the branches are inconsistent; I'll probably stick to the Tanglin Mall branch.We had:1) Beef Chili ($12.50): This was a little charred compared to the ones at Tanglin Mall, like someone left it on the burner a tad too long. Still a decent starter nonetheless.2) Chicken Enchilada Soup ($9.90): subtly spiced, and really lovely, if a bit stingy on the chicken chunks.3) Bacon Ranch Quesadillas ($24.90): these were a little anaemic, and significantly less generous with the fillings than at Tanglin Mall.4) Mango Chile Chicken ($19.90): wholesome, healthy, and delicious. The chicken was very nicely done, moist, flavourful and tender.5) Grilled Chicken Fajitas ($27.90): one of the highlights. Succulent chicken, thoroughly marinated, and imbued with an aromatic smoky accent.6) Classic BBQ Baby Back Ribs ($40.90 for full rack): outstanding as usual, hearty, flavoursome to the bone, fantastically burnished, with meat that was so tender it was practically fall-off-the-bone. This was served with excellent homestyle fries and a disappointingly dry skillet macaroni & cheese

Chili's, like Tony Roma's and Outback, and "those types of places" are really just as advertised. Hearty, fairly affordable American fare for the masses. And while dinner here is a perfectly average affair of typical choices at typical prices, I do appreciate Chili's as somewhere near my clients that I can grab a quick lunch.For between $16-18 dollars you can get a half portion of soup, and a half portion of salad, or a sandwich, including a free flow drink. That's... decent. It's a nice change of pace when you're sick of eating the same thing from the area around the office everryyyyday. I can confidently say I'll go back, once in a while. It's nowhere I'd 'recommend to a friend', or visit because it's a special occasion, but in a way it's a like McDonald's for grown-ups. Simple, stable, kinda fast food that doesn't make for any surprises.We all need something familiar every once in a while!

I've always gone to the Tanglin location, but this time I was down getting a dependant pass at RiverWalk and decided to stop in for a rare weekday lunch with my wife. This Chili's is really nice, it's very bright and open with a wall of glass, feels much newer than the Tanglin location. The food is standard Chili's food, if you don't know, this is casual American food with a tex-mex twist, but still a full varied menu of choices. I have always enjoyed Chili's food since I worked in one over fifteen years ago. The menu has changed a lot over the years and some favorites have left (I will always miss you Smoked Turkey Sandwich) but many new items have been added to round out the selection. My favorite feature of Singapore Chili's is the unlimited drink refills, that really takes me home to the US.I was very pleased to see the Weekday lunch break promotion starting at $12.90 you get a starter, a main and a free flow drink. While the portions are a bit smaller, a few less fries, smaller main salad, at SGD12.90 this is a fantastic deal.The food took a bit long to come out for a lunch promotion in a fairly empty restaurant, but overall very good experience.

as-you'd-expect - which is to say, good for simple, filling meals - at this american tex-mex chain outlet at the central in clarke quay. let's cut to the chase: this isn't gourmet, and it's not trying to be. it's full-on american diner-steakhouse type food served in large portions, and it (almost singlehandedly, actually) fills a niche gap in the singapore dining scene that I think many of us didn't know existed.it's casual dining in a large space with very-american-style diner booth seats, incredibly enthusiastic staff, and a boisterous atmosphere that lends best to loud gatherings (impression fostered also by their myriad alcohol promotions) - but all that aside, this place has a killer banbread pudding: one of the best, most satisfying non-chocolate puddings I've had in a while.in a food scene dominated by open kitchens manned by skinny tight-trousered intensely-styled chefs, this establishment feels a little out of place. at best, it's esoteric; at most-impolite, it's probably best described as crass. but.. that's not necessarily as bad as it sounds, and not a bad thing neither. it's (lack of supposed) pedigree is visible in the cheese-encrusted steaks and cheese-surrounded most-things-else - but it's fun, you know.I wouldn't dress up to come here (and you don't need to, either), but if your friends appreciate a loud place to indulge in margharitas and too-much food - this would be my best recommendation.the gist of it: you really should come here for as americanesque a meal as you're likely to get in singapore. the food is decent, and the prices aren't cheap - but the portion sizes give it huge value (especially if you consider that the same money would bring you tapas-type servings in hippie places), and coming with a large group of friends will mean a good time.or just come for margharitas and their dessert - I've heard great things about that chocolate cake too.
i always go back here. i just love the food and their service :) bottomless tostada and veggie quesadilla and the classic nachos are a few of my fave. :)

I find myself here every now and then because I teach dance around the area. I almost always sit at the bar area to order my buffalo chicken salad or lunch special. I've been watching the Winter Olympics and they put it on the tv for me. Nice folks that work here for the most part. The food is ok. I think the lunch special for $9 is a decent deal because you can get a small BLT, small salad, and small fries - perfect amount of food for lunch with variety and includes a drink too.

Ambitious place that challenges big-name neighbours (Starbucks, Coffee Bean, etc) and sells more than coffee and tea: salads, semi-serious b'fasts (eg. waffles with fresh fruits, eggs benedict), as well as 4 kinds of beer and food (eg. linguine with clams, smoked joint, deep fried pork cubes). May not attract many customers from Orchard Towers next door; those may prefer mee sua in the basement or greasy quesadillas with mojitos at Señor Taco anyway.

Cute place to get some work done. Pretty quiet with some chill music on a lazy Monday Labour Day. There's free wi-fi with facebook check-in or filling out a form (pretty straightforward once you connect). Too bad the outlets were few and far between though. The internet speed was pretty decent although it started out a bit slow. The A/C was wayyy too cold though, so unfortunately I had to bounce after about 2 hrs. My hairs were standing on end!
Had great coffee from here almost everyday. Usually ordered with Sumatran beans for a more local flavor. Really really good
Best coffee in Orchard, on a quiet side street. Good seating options, nice place to chill. Looks pricey, but cups are gigantic!

Great coffee with many variations of the latte -- piccolo, Gibraltar, cappuccino etc. also variants of drip/brew coffee. Watch out -- the latte is a huge cup of coffee. Too milky for me. Gibraltar hits just the right spot. They don't offer decaf like many other proper cafes, most frustratingly. Eggs and toast at $6, with butter and jam, is an affordable option compared to $16 similar breakfasts down Orchard Road. Bonus points to Jewel for offering vegemite if you prefer it.

Ordered a flat white ($6) and pain au chocolate ($3) for breakfast before my Japanese class at Delfi Orchard. The coffee was unlike anything I've ever tasted and was brilliant. Smooth yet strong, I savoured every single drop of it. It went well with the pastry although the latter was just a tad too sweet.

They are one of the few speciality coffee shops in the area.  Very fresh and all beans have dates.  They don't have full body kind, but that's alright other beans are also good.Thanks for opening here.  You are awesome!こちらでは少ないスペシャリティコーヒーのお店です。ここで焼いているわけではありませんが、ストレートコーヒーをちゃんと焼いた日付を記して販売しています。日本のように苦めの焼き方はしてませんが、十分美味しいです。お値段もお手頃で、いいお店ですね。2015/11

I love Italian food but I rarely eat Italian in Singapore as I find that most places overpriced and overrated food. Gattopardo is an exception: I still find it on the pricey side but the food was quite good.On a Monday evening the restaurant was relatively quiet but there was quite a lot of staff present. The service was ok: friendly and prompt but nothing special.I was pleasantly surprised that, even though I only ordered a main, they gave me a complimentary amuse bouche and sourdough & focaccia bread. The bread was a rare gem, I find it amazingly hard to get decent bread here and this bread was on point!The Taglioloni with sea urchin & bottarga sauce looked like a small-ish portion when it arrived but looks can be deceiving: I finished every single drop but was super full afterwards and passed on dessert. This pasta dish was very good, the briny taste of the sea urchin combined with the delicate flavor of good quality pasta and a hint of parsley made this into a winner.One of the better Italian restaurants in Singapore, will go again to try other dishes if I have the opportunity.

After hearing rave reviews from my foodie friend, we decided to use the Entertainer App to try this place. We ordered:Mains:- Zuppa (seafood stew)- Tonarelli (squid ink with mussels and pistachio pesto)Starters:- Burrata- Octopus Overall the starters were excellent, if not a little pricey relative to the portion sizes (ie very small). However there's not a lot of cooking involved with the burrata it has to be said. The mains were a bit more underwhelming. Zuppa was generous with seafood, but lacked and flavour or seasoning. Truth be told it's probably something most decent home chefs could cook themselves. The squid ink tonarelli was quite nice, with excellent bite to the pasta. Mussels were fat and sweet. Pistachio pesto was interesting...but overall it tasted rather like a Thai dish. (By the way there's a fair bit of Asian influence in the menu here).Service was very average, and they lose a star because of it.  It didn't start well when they didn't have our reservation. Wait staff had zero personality or warmth. We sat for a very long time with empty/dirty plates on our table, and had to ask a waiter for the dessert menu after we gave up waiting. Our waters were not topped up a single time during our meal. These sound like petty gripes, but really if you're meant to be a quality establishment then the entire experience should be top notch. I would return to try the food nonetheless, and lower my expectations for service.

DELICIOUS, oh-so-good italiano (more specifically, sicilian) dining at this small, cozy little restaurant along tras street. this reivew is a long time coming, given that I ate here during my birthday (six months ago, hello!), but it's a goodie (even if it is also an oldie now).we got a delightful little corner table on the ground floor - sunlight streaming in, in full view of the bricked facade of the kitchen. attention is a little spotty, in a relaxed sort of manner - they certainly can move quickly, as they did with the table next to ours that was clearly there for a swift lunch.I was impressed with first dish of salad - it was rather beautiful with the colors of the orange and red cabbage, and the flavors were perky and fresh with the endive and sweet cooked prawn strewn throughout. the dressing is light and clean, with a measured use of olive oil that keeps everything crisp and cool.and then our mains arrived - and boy, were they good. first, the zuppa di pesce 'gattopardo', the house special of seafood stew was served in a rustic pot with all the intensity you'd have expected in a bisque. if you get this, I think you'll be just as surprised as we were at the amount of seafood in there, and how tenderly all the different types of fish were cooked.and for something to sop the stew up, a risone con polipo brasato e midollo di bue, which is italian for grain-shaped pasta cooked with firm octopus and bone marrow. I think bone marrow is one of those modern, fancy ingredients that you see almost too often, and which I almost always avoid for its fatty oiliness - but here, it worked with the orzo to create a silky, lovely pasta. and I haven't even mentioned the tasty, deep flavors of the pasta sauce, or the firm octopus (which is one of my favorite seafoods ever).we finished with two desserts (but of course - the fiance understands my need for sweets). and while I have to say I'm not in general a fan of italian desserts, seeing as how many are basically constructions of cream or semifreddo, but these were really satisfying.the millefoglie was a mille-feuille with puff pastry layers encasing chocolate and caramel mousse-creams, and it all reads really sweet until you realise that the unique comopnents of vanilla oil and smoked sea salt really bring that something special to the dish.we also took the signature semifreddo di lino of nougat parfait with an almond sauce - you might not typically like whipped cream (real here, of course!) but it does bring a mild counterpoint to the sweet semifreddo and balances things out.I'm really bad with compliments, but we might have had our best meal this year here.

I'm no italian food foodie expert but Gattopardo is worth a mention regardless. The pasta, albeit a tad on the pricey end, was sublime and the service even better. We had their tagliolini with uni and homemade spaghetti in a tomato seafood sauce, both were excellent. Each table is presented with complimentary hors d'oeuvres both to begin and end the meal which is definitely something you don't see often anymore unless you're at a michelin. Highly recommend this place for those looking to celebrate a special occasion.

Food and service are excellent! I had the mussels to start and they were ridiculously good, next I had the wagyu steak and let me tell you...it was literally melt in your mouth and the jus which accompanied it was oh so good! The tiramisu dessert was a huge disappointment though but everything was good :)

This is a review of a dinner at Gattopardo Italian Grill and Pizzabar.First, I must say that the service here was spectacular.  They were attentive, professional, and polite.  As far as a fine dining experience, this exemplifies what I expect in service.  Each time we needed something, someone appeared.After my dining companion complimented the dessert and her meal, the chef even came out to the  table.Next, the ambiance is beautiful.  This is for the al fresco area.  The tables are well spaced.  It is a wonderful veranda.  It has a feel of being on vacation.However, you may have noticed I've only given three stars.  Unfortunately, the food was simply inconsistent.  As I stated, my friend really enjoyed her main and dessert.  Other portions of the meal simply did not stack up.  For the most part, each dish was presented very well.Tomato Soup - This was a complimentary chilled tomato soup.  Generally, I am not a fan of chilled soups.  I found this one quite refreshing.  My friend did not.  She pretty much ignored it.Prosciutto di Parma Pio Tosini e Burrata di Andria (24 Months Aged Parma Ham "Pio Tosini" with Burrata Cheese)This was so very good.  The saltiness of the prosciutto with the creaminess of the buratta just came together so well.tinyurl.com/bzwc79kMozzarella di Bufala e Cuore di Bue (Buffalo Mozzarella Cheese with Italian "Ox Heart" Tomatoes and Fresh Salad)And yes, if you are thinking a meal with Burrata and Mozzarella is pretty decadent, you are right, it is.  The mozzarella itself was too die for.  It was so creamy.  However, the tomatoes were run of the mill.  They were overly acidic and lacked the sweetness I would desire in a dish like this.tinyurl.com/bbflph9Linguine alle Vongola Gigante  (Linguine with Japanese Surf Clams in White Wine Sauce) - This was my companions entree. It was quite good.  The pasta was cooked perfectly and the seafood was obviously very fresh.tinyurl.com/arszvfcTagine di Pollo con Harissa e Couscous (Free Range Chicken Tagine with Harissa and Couscous)Unfortunately, this was my main.  For me, it was mostly inedible.  The way the chicken had been reconstituted or stuffed led to a bland and overly grainy dish.  I would think harrissa would keep any dish from being bland; but not in this case.  The couscous was very dense and retained a lot of water.tinyurl.com/bcu2ev9Frutti e Sorbetti (Fresh Seasonal Fruits and Homemade Sorbets)I did not have dessert.  My dining companion loved her sorbets and fruit.  She just kept raving about it.  That being said, we did have a bottle and a half of very good red wine.  At that point, she may have raved about a snickers bar.Overall, if my main course had been enjoyable, this would have been the type of experience that defines fine dining.  The service was impeccable.  The ambiance was resort like.  At times, the food demonstrated flashes that met my expectations.  However, when a dinner is going to come in at over $500 for two, it really has to meet all marks.  Unfortunately, Gattopardo did not.

Pizza is one of my favourite things to have and the pizzas at Gattopardo are as authentic as they can get. Having tried 8 out of the 20 types of pizza available, I must say that it's only a matter of time before I go through all. And I have not been disappointed so far. The ambience of the restaurant, especially the al fresco areas are breathtakingly beautiful, and make for a wonderful experience of dining under the stars. While they don't only serve pizzas, bear in mind that they're more known for their seafood and pastas, which are very traditional Sicillian.

2 Blur Guys is a relatively new burger shop set up in Orchid Hotel. Its concept is simple - a stripped down quick meal place which serves quality food at reasonable prices. The menu is simple - there's a list of less than 10 burgers to choose from, and each burger comes with a side of potato salad and greens. Portions aren't massive, but they're pretty filling. 2 Blur Guys also serves desserts such as brownies and ice cream. The restaurant is nothing fancy, but it serves as a functional place to grab dinner at with friends.

This burger joint is a solid 3.Came here for an early lunch and it was already beginning to get busy as we rolled in.The burger was cooked to medium rare and was quite juicy, and it was a good overall bun-to-pattie ratio, which made for a good experience. I had the prime beef with streaky bacon, which looked to be the best burg on the menu, but unfortunately they snuck some sort of truffle flavour in there (can we stop with that nonsense already???) and there wasn't a good burger sauce to give it a better taste (anything would have helped - BBQ, Tomato, Mustard).So whilst they have the cooking down, they need to work on the construction of the burger somewhat.The handful of wedges was a bit meagre and the wait for the food was on the extreme-side. However as there is only 2 guys, that's probably part of the experience, and with it being Singapore, service is never on the awesome-side.

Eat Until "Blur"Oh, the humble hamburger. How it's evolved from a meat patty, melted cheese between a toasted sesame bun to a level that's..... gourmet worthy. We love a good burger bar and was gutted when discovering that Mojo Burps, one of if not our favorite burger joint, had closed. Since than, we've given a few other places a shot without much satisfaction, UNTIL NOW!We decided to do a takeaway because we've seen just how saucy their burgers can get and decided we should do a takeaway to avoid messing ourselves in public. The Wife had the Prime Beef Burger with Foie Gras while I went with a more Non-traditional, smoked salmon burger. Prime Beef with Foie Gras ($24.95)OMG. First the basics. The bun was nicely toasted and thanks to the Foie Gras, the top bun was flavored with the Foie Gras oil, which soaked in every bit of flavour it had to offer. The patty was a spot on. An inch thick patty, well seasoned and perfectly cooked (we had ours medium rare). The patty had a great fat to meat ratio, ensuring that it didn't taste dry or chewy. Consistency of the mince was good as well, avoiding any portion of clumpy meat or overly mushed mince. The results? An extremely juicy patty that constantly dropped juices down the side of our mouths. The Foie Gras was pretty generous, with 2 thick slices, which added richness to the burger. Though not the highest quality of Foie Gras, they were still pretty good. The cheese was perfectly melted while the relish used added a nice sour kick to the burger, helping to cut the richness of the burger. Smoke Salmon Burger ($12.50)I was expecting maybe 6 slices of salmon, max, with tons of avocado. Turns out, it was the complete opposite!The smoked salmon was folded into a one inch thick patty while the avocado was a thin layer between salmon and bun. It was a smoke salmon lovers delight! Only thing I wished was for more avocado and more sauce and you could barely taste it over the salmon. It did need that bit of sourness to help cut the powerful taste of the salmon. Also, it did feel a little strange either smoked salmon between a burger bun, might have been  more "traditional" between a bagel but hey, It still tasted good but I have zero complains with the generosity. Every order also comes as a set, which comes with a drink, salad and awesome wedges with cheese sauce. Hands down for now, this is my favourite burger joint. It may not be the most price friendly restaurant but it's definitely worth it.

Came here with two church mates as one of them wanted to try out burgers for dinner around 7.00 pm on a Saturday. Located walkable distance from Tanjong Pagar MRT and next to famous ramen chains. After exploring the menu, I decided to order Prime Beef with Streaky Bacon. Yes, I am a fan of bacons. And Gruyere cheese sounds unfamiliar. For the beverage, I asked one of the staffs whether the ice lemon tea was homemade and when she answered it was, I ordered that.Price wise here was a bit steep. For the meal, you can either get the wedges for the price listed on the menu or add-on for other side dishes. I decided to try truffle fries with the burger.For the home made ice lemon tea, it is highly recommended. But unfortunately they placed too much ice cubes inside the glass that lost its taste after 20 or so minutes. Could probably ask them for less ice. For the truffle fries, it was good if consumed before 10 minutes. Unfortunately I left them out in the air for long and they turned soggy even though the truffle fries were of thin cuts. For the beef patty, I ordered it medium rare as that is what I normally choose for burgers. Sadly it was not as juicy as other Yelpers had mentioned. The bacon was chewy to my liking and the buns were nicely baked. Store wise, it is not so spacious and could only contain maximum 15 customers. So to avoid the crowds, you might need to come earlier. Portion was reasonable and it did satisfy my hunger.

OH MYYYY GOD!  This burger is owwzaammmm!  I wonder why I didn't know about this place earlier, tho I came there several time.  The place is quite small, but the ambience is rather nice.  Ordered the #1 Prime Beef Burger & I love how they cook my medium rare beef, it was just perfect and juicy all the way until the last bite! Yum.. every order come with garden green salad and wedges potato topped with gruyere cheese (the type of cheese which I'm not sure how to spell it, but anyway it goes so well with the wedges potatoes :)If you don't like wedges, you can change it with truffle fries (add $2.50) or french fries (add $1.50) - but in my opinion, wedges potato is da'bez!  And come try their homemade ice lemon tea, super fresh and tangy-sweet, such a perfect lemon tea I've ever tried so far! ahahah.And  not forgetting the very friendly staff, who even notice my need before I asked - when the tabasco was finished in our table and I was still pouring the last drop, the staff came to my table and offered me a new bottel of tabasco!  Wow, very very good service!  i am impressed - and stomach is happy!  Will come back and I might try their salmon avocado burger  =D

I've been introduced to this place a couple and came a couple of times already because I'm drawn to their pulled pork burger. They have nice dessert, but the basic burger is already food for my soul! I've tried a couple of places around this area, but this place still wins hands down. Sure you have to wait a bit, the guys are really trying their best (and they're not slow, mind you) to serve. Friendly staff, and patient (even though my colleague and I took so long to decide on our drink choice).Hope people would give service staff a break with their negativity because a smile to them makes their day too!

I've always walked past this place but have never gone in as the place looked small and cramped. This time, my hungry friends had traipsed down the entire Tanjong Pagar Road on a Friday, and with every establishment full (I kid you not), we ended up here as this was the only place with seats, which isn't always a good sign. We were however pleasantly surprised at the burgers! The beef patties were suitably thick and juicy! Flavorful!! The burgers/patties aren't large, so if you are looking for something substantial, these aren't. nonetheless, these burgers were still satisfying! The portobello one seemed nice (my friend's order) and I would go back to try this one. The truffle fries were good too, although I found the smell to be a little overpowering. Haha! One side note, the salad was a little oily, which was strange. We sat outside, so thankfully it didn't feel cramped. Will go back!!

The portobello burger is amazing! The patty was juicy and everything was just so yummy. The place is kinda small and you will smell like burgers after eating there. If you're looking to hang out with a group of friends at the place, try to make a reservation before heading there. Only two guys are working to make and serve the burgers, try to be patient and its definitely worth the wait!

The best burger in Singapore... where is the six star rating? When I asked for a medium rare burger, I finally got what I had never gotten in this city-state, a medium rare burger. The finishing was perfect, from the bread to the meat to the greens served with it. The fries were amazing too, and the mayo with the fries and the burger was to die for. I'm not one to like mayo very much, but this one, this one is something different. Had a pecan pie for dessert which is quite nice, and the beer selection is quite affordable and varied. I honestly wish I could write more, but I don't want to waste any of your time while you read this review instead of going and having the best burger here. You'll thank me for it!
The bun is good but not grilled inside, the meat is OK but not grilled enough on the outside, the sauce is good but there is too much of it.OK burger ...

Two Blur Guys definitely has the best burger I've tried so far in Singapore.  Back in NYC, this burger would fit right in.It's a small, cozy burger shop, with limited seating and a warm and welcoming staff.  There is one primary waitress and one burger chef.  We noticed that our burgers were made with extreme care, and after we ate, the burger chef was very focused on making sure we enjoyed our burgers.  The burgers come with a small scoop of potato salad and a side salad of greens with a delicious balsamic glaze.We wrapped up the meal with the apple pie, and it was tasty, but I can't help wishing it was served hot with a scoop of apple pie on the side :)PARTING THOUGHT: We'll continue on our Singapore burger quest, but so far, we're quite happy to have found a winner!

They don't serve water here--only bottled water and an assortment of soft drinks.  My biggest pet-peeve for a restaurant. Oh, that and adding $1 for water. Really, do I need to pay $1 extra for tap water? I'm just borrowing the glass!Other than that, I def. do recommend the burgers here. They're not the big, fat ones at Billy Bombers, but they will fix that burger craving. The beef patties are meaty and seasoned well! I especially fell in love with the balsamic vinaigrette in the side salad, so much that I offered to purchase the bottle off them (They said no :[).Great little joint for some mean (portion-controlled) burgers!

The burgers here are very good - the beef patties are thick and juicy and the bun is also very good. I had my burger medium well and it came out perfectly cooked, while my wife's was medium and slightly more pink in the middle. Love it when a restaurant knows how to cook their meats.The venue is very small and non-descript. I've walked past this place MANY times without as much noticing it. It looks like a bakery from the outside b/c they display their pies and desserts prominently. There's not much seating so get there during an off hour or do take away. They really need to put a BIG picture of their juicy hamburger on the storefront to attract more folks.We also shared the lemon curd tart which was awesome, worth trying.I only give them 4 stars b/c they do not serve fries and their version of ketchup is a translucent gelatinous pink sweet goo that I couldn't get into. Next time I'll bring fries and ketchup from McDonald's to complement their satisfying burger!

For someone who generally stays away from burgers, I really dig the ones here. I ordered the Prime Beef Burger which came with a side of leafy greens and a tiny mountain of potato salad. The beef patty was thick, juicy and well-seasoned. Definitely not fast food material. I saw the cook meticulously grill the beef patty as she toasted the buns, take out the buns and slap on the patty and a slice of gruyère, stick the whole thing back into the oven and finally, keep a watchful eye for the buns to turn a nice golden brown and the cheese to melt just right.The burger here is surely a product of love, love that goes all the way down to my tummy tum tums.

Apart from the other reviews, this small burger bar also does quiches and quick bites to go, which they will heat up for you. The mushroom quiche I got tasted good, but it was a little small and I scoffed it down quickly.I came here on a Friday afternoon around 4pm so it was really empty. Staff were a little bit lacklustre in their service attitude, but otherwise the place looked quite appealing and I wouldn't mind dropping by for a full meal if I'm ever around the area.
Order the burger without relish and mayo. Otherwise the burger is disgusting. Without those two, a medium burger tastes legit.

I came here today for a spur of the moment lunch plan with a friend. As soon as we walked in we were seated. Unfortunately, it was in a cramped little corner. We ordered our food and though it came rather quickly, I wouldn't say it was the best. It was overloaded with truffle mayo and the meat was two soft and crumbled out of the burger. The bread ended up getting soggy because how juicy the burger was. All in all... I have a coupon for this place from pickatsg but I don't think I'll be using it. #disappointed

With just four tables in a tiny space, Two Blur Guys isn't trying very hard perhaps in this newly competitive Duxton/Tanjong Pagar area (Soooo many good things to eat around here), but maybe it doesn't have to. I come to Duxton a lot and frequently walk over to the Orchid Hotel to eat at Teppei or Tonkotsu King. So I was pleasantly surprised to see this tiny space along the Tanjong Pagar stretch.I wish they did more marketing, or maybe it's good that they didn't, because when I started to hear friends excitedly discuss the burgers and desserts here I was intrigued enough to go check it out. There's a small selection of interesting (mostly Aussie) beers and wines, and the cakes and tarts like the Lamington are good.Alas I have been too full from ramen usually to ever eat a full meal here, but I'm going to check out the burgers next time especially now that I've found out that Singapore's elusive food extraordinaire Jimmy Chok is involved here in some way or other.

New kid on the block serving North Indian cuisine nestled between a couple of coffeeshops in the middle of nowhere in Sembawang.I was told the chefs used to work at high-end places such as Raffles Hotel. Explains why the food quality is close to that served at the other pricier places around town. I enjoyed the butter chicken, fish tikka and the Rogan Josh (lamb curry). One thing to note is that the interpretations of the dishes are skewed a little towards western palates, with the spice level on the lower end of the scale and more tomato in the lamb curry. (As you know, Chicken Tikka Masala hails from the UK, not the sub-continent)I rounded out the evening with a mango kulfi (ice cream), though I wished more dessert choices were available (It was either this or the gulab jamun). This is more of a casual dining eatery, I saw a couple of families celebrating birthdays here. Prices are reasonable and don't cost you an arm and a leg. Now, if only if was not so out of the way, I'd not hesitate to make my way back here.

A Wonderful family-run Indian Restaurant located in Sembawang rd, of all places. My wife and I and fellow Yelper, Ricky, and his wife came here after spending an hour or so at the River Safari. We were looking for a place to eat while we waited for the Night Safari to open.Yes, food options at the zoo are quite limited, so why not take a quick can ride/uber to the nearest food centre? Do it!The food at Sher is fantastic. Everything from the butter chicken to the aloo gobi to the butter and garlic naan to the palak paneer was top notch. Pretty generic words, I know... However, I'd consider Cher to be my 2nd favorite Indian restaurant in SG. The owner is a pretty cool chap as well. If you have trouble choosing dishes, feel free to ask him his recommendation. You can't miss him.

We had a hankering for Indian food and visited Sher again. Yet again we just left it the owner to bring us something to eat with the caveat it had to include the fish tikka!  Mushroom Kukuri and a Melai kebab followed and all were up to the standard set with fish tikka. Our San Miguel's were followed by a great Margarita. Place looked to be busy with a nice mix of locals and expats.
The food was great, we had butter chicken, 2 Naans and a chicken Biryani and all were great.  The price was also very reasonable for a good North Indian restaurant.  I'll definitely visit again

We're staying in this area and looking for something to eat late at night on a Friday evening. The whole area in general was busy and buzzing, full of young people. Really good vibe. We had fish and chips and the food was fresh and good. After our meal we walked around further and there's so many places to eat. On hind sight I would have liked to have gone to a different restaurant just to try the different local dishes. Don't get me wrong, the food was good, but their menu options I could have gotten at home.

Visited on a Friday afternoon at 3pm. Service was great.  Ordered the house white wine and received a healthy pour for $10++.   Most places would serve a smaller amount for more money.   I also ordered the battered cod fish and chips which were fresh and nice portions.  The chips were crisp and not over cooked.  I would highly recommend the location.

This restaurant is nothing compared to the real thing.The food is expensive (e.g. SGD16.00 for 4 prawns - each the size of my ring finger) and the texture of the seafood is murky/slimy/soft. Taste is slightly above average but nothing to talk about. Staff is rather attentive but not open to feedback and defensive upon comments. Bought Groupon Vouchers for the Lobster deal but was utterly disappointed with how it tasted (virtually no taste whatsoever) and the lobster flesh was tough. Ordered the mussels and clams but the meat was the size of a Singapore Five Cent Coin.Just terrible experience. Won't ever head back.

Apart from the decor channelling the laid back, carefree vibe of Freo, Perth, there's nothing else that I really like about Fremantle Seafood Market. Their Sunday brunch menu looks more Japanese than Aussie to me with its spread of king fish Hamachi, yellow fin tuna, chilled shrimps, half-shell scallops and mussels with lemon cocktail sauce.The ingredients are fresh, and there are certain stand outs like the squid tempura and soft shell crab. But had i known it would be so Japanese-centric, with all the sashimi, I'd have skipped it and gone somewhere else instead.

Its a big shame that they call themselves Fremantle Seafood Market but the food there is NOTHING like seafood from Fremantle. I ordered a few things. Seafood and clam chowder, oysters kilpatrick and fish and chips (cod and john dory).The clam chowder was an ok start to dinner. The oysters were average at best. But I could not believe it when I received my fish and chips. I was practically eating batter the entire time. The fish was pathetic.Never again will I go back.

Sunday lunch = $70 for two peopleI spent three years working at a seafood restaurant in Fremantle, so think I am qualified to write a review of this place. We came around 1pm on a sunny Sunday, as I have always wanted to try this. It got a fairly mediocre review from the Business Times, but then most Western restaurants do. Started with the jug of Heineken ($34.13) which is the usual Singaporean style of price gouging on beer. Moved on and ordered the Seafood Bucket ($28.25) which was well presented in a metal bucket and piled high with fried items. Unfortunately, most of it was chips, the fish was a relatively small piece and not a quality filet. The oysters were decent, but you could taste that they were either frozen or leftovers from Friday. There were also a mussel or two, some squid and I think a scallop. Disappointing because if you get this dish right, it is the perfect meal to share.Also ordered the bread basket ($8.24) and I am not sure how you can make bread taste so average, get some flavour! As you will see from flipping over the menu, this restaurant is owned locally. They have probably been to Freo on a recon mission and mimicked it here, the difference is that the seafood restaurants get really fresh items, and you do not need to drench them in batter to make them taste better. Lastly, your prices in the menu should reflect GST and service charge - anything less is cheating.

I remember the first time my dad took us to The Ship in Penang! It was really in a ship and there's a unique charm about dining in a ship with English style cooking. We don't exactly have a ship in middle of the city but  the ambience is enough to bring back those memories. The food also follows the traditional English style starting with soup and bread with butter. We had pumpkin soup today which was yummy. We ordered the lobster special with grilled pork chop served with potatoes and vegetables. The lobster was excellent, we will definitely order the whole lobster next time. The pork chop although not the juiciest I've tasted, was nicely seasoned. The potatoes! I don't usually comment about sides but the potatoes were good and for the vegetables you have steamed carrots and broccoli, buttered and lightly salted, again very satisfying traditional style. We finish off with a cup of coffee and mango pudding + sago dessert. The portion size is nice for a light dinner for my 4yr and the both of us. When my carnivorous inner self emerges however, the set is all mine. On our previous visit, I had the half spring chicken and the wife had the salmon, both gave us smiles to return!Service is good but it gets busy when traffic peaks so your mileage may vary.

Service was disappointing. I was on crutches and waiting for receptionist to get off the phone. A group came along and she promptly sat them down. They had a reservation but so did I ! They are losing a star because of this. Truly disappointed.So I don't understand why I was ignored. I don't expect to be served first just because I was on crutches but to have my queue cut by the receptionist is just way too much. It also took forever to get the attention of the service staff after my Friend arrived after me.Fried fish noodles in milky soup with vegetables and tomato - still good although I think it was better before the renovation.Chicken chop with cheese, tomato paste, potato, broccoli and carrots - a tad saltish.

It is always crowded, so you definitely need a reservation, especially for lunch. It can be an hour wait if you do not have reservation. Or you may be asked if you can finish your meal in an hour if you pop by without calling. It is THAT busy. I see mostly older folks, families as well as office crowd on weekday lunch time. The lunch set is quite value for money and it is available 7 days a week, and it is different every day. The only thing that is constant on the lunch set menu is the fried fish noodle soup. And that is absolutely my favorite dish. For $12.90++ you get the fried fish noodle soup, choice of drink (coffee, tea or iced lemon tea) and dessert of the day. Quite a good deal, I think. The soup is creamy milky (reminded me a bit of campbellis mushroom soup), with thick bee hoon (you can request for thin bee hoon), slices of tomato, ginger and salted vegetable (I found a strip). The fried fish fillet is on a separate plate so its retain its crispiness though it hardens when cold). The Hainanese chicken rice is only available on Thursday and it is not a big deal. The soup is much better as it is filled with old winter melon, wolfberries, fungus and stuff. I would imagine the steak to be of similar quality as Jack's Place or maybe Hot Tomato and Shashlik. Oxtail stew is available on Wednesday and Friday for the set lunch though it is also available in the a la carte menu too. Prime rib is also available on Friday for $39.90++For a bit of old school nostalgic Western food, The Ship is the place to be.
Very packed during lunch on Wednesday. Most people orders the fried chicken and oxtail stew. Loved the food

This restaurant has the air of nostalgia but sadly the food doesn't seem as good as I remember it.This restaurant is very quaint it wasn't considered so but now that decor has changed over the years, The Ship's retro decor really gives you the feeling that you've entered a time warp that rewinds 15 years.I've eaten here twice in the past year and I have to say, the food (western cuisine) is really average. I find it to be actually kinda pricey for it's quality. The restaurant has a nice vibe and the staff it's friendly, I hate to say it, but apart from the novel 80s vibe, food wise it's really not that good.

It's located at Shaw Centre, orchard road. Even though the location is not convenient, the shop interior design and food will be worth the travelling. The authentic woody design and street lamps give a very down to earth feeling, slowing the tempo of the hectic work life in Singapore. Most do not know ,  food to try is the fried fish soup noodle (which cannot be found on the menu!). The soup is perfectly brewed and filling and the fish is definitely something for you to visit again. Its crispy, crunchy and juicy. Certainly an economical place to hang out and dine.Do note that the fish soup noodle gets sold out easily so do call and check if they still serve before going, especially during the evening time!

The Ship, a truly nostalgic experience for 90's generation yet again. This used to be the go to place for myself and my dad when we wanted to have steak. You could say at that time, The Ship was one notch above Jack's place. The better choices of steak here usually comes sizzling on a hot plate which risks overcooking so be sure to dig in fast. Food standards have definitely fallen over the years or rather the wide availability of steak now has set a higher standards for my tastebuds. Either way the Ship is worth a visit just for old times sake! AHOY!

We had 11 people, so we got a private room. The food was very good but expensive. It seems like it caters to tourists. It was fun to eat family style as it allowed us to try a lot of different items. Good food but expensive and they charge you for everything including the peanuts and wet wipes for after you have eaten the crab. Go to Chinatown for great food at a much lower cost.

Out of the branches, the outdoor seating in Jumbo Dempsey is beautiful. Brought a friend visiting Singapore few weeks ago and we couldn't have asked for a better atmosphere/seating. With guests, D and I always get:-the award winning Chilli crab/black pepper crab + dozen (or more) bread-Deshelled prawn with salad cream in golden nest, or deshelled wasabi prawn. -Scallop wrapped in Yam Ring-Steamed bamboo clam with minced garlic and some fried ricetook off one star bc while the waiters were generally honest at this branch, the chilli crab came with basically no chilli. We were done after dipping our breads into it for a bit. Usually, there is so much chilli leftover that I end up taking it away and eating it with rice next day for lunch. Disappointing, but the great atmosphere and the other dishes made up for it. Make sure to make reservations early! for visitors, i also recommend No Signboard in Esplanade bc of the beautiful view of marina bay sands and raffles place, though you have to keep alert NOT to get ripped off by the greedy waiters.

Chilli crab!!! My brother is a huge aficionado and avers that they have the best. Also, bf's family friend also swears by the chilli crab at this particular outlet of Jumbo Seafood, apparently. Although, I have to say, Forture Seafood along Bkt Timah Rd does a pretty gd rendition (and their mantous are to die for, really) for cheaper. Not as nice ambience there though.Soon hock in soy sauce was fresh and delicious!Spinach beancurd with spinach/three types of mushrooms (enoki/shimeji/shiitake, I think) was delicious too!Roast chicken, mm.Black pepper venison, very tender!Kai lan in garlic, normal.HK mee, pretty gd too! Nice al dente/bite to the noodles, crunchy prawn, shredded cabbage and bean sprouts.Yam paste dessert and mango pudding were pretty gd!Can't comment on prices as this was a treat. But Jumbo card holders get 20% off ala carte and 10% off set menus. They also sell the chilli crab paste should you wish to try making your own chilli crab at home!

jumbo is consistently good. their food is always tasty and well prepared, although probably not the best. their chilli crab and pepper crab are both excellent. the pepper crab is very peppery which i love. the chilli crab sauce is fantastic and such a great pairing with their mantous. i had the cereal prawns this time, and got them without the shell because i'm lazy. unfortunately they just didn't taste that great. not sure if it was this particular jumbo, or if it was because of the lack of shell. i love the razor clams dish, but they were out the time i came here.drunken prawns are also excellent.

If this was a normal dining experience, I'd really rate JUMBO Seafood at Dempsey only three stars. BUT. As a JUMBO privilege card member, I got 20% off our a la carte orders, AND 50% off the fresh crabs. Yes, you read that right. HALF PRICE off the Chili crab and Pepper and Spiced Salt crab that we ordered. So for that awesome value, I'm adding a star. Dinner was a pretty last minute decision; we only realised that the voucher for 50% off crabs was only valid for April on the 29th of April... so at 8pm we frantically tried calling the Dempsey branch because it was the most central for all of us. As expected of a busy restaurant there was no answer... so we went online and Chope-d our seats. SCORE.Got there, and as we ordered, we were a little disappointed. They'd run out of a few drinks, and didn't have anymore pork ribs. So we ordered two crabs, their scallops wrapped in yam, black-pepper venison, baby kai lan fried with garlic and mantou.I won't talk about the crabs, since everyone does, but I highly recommend the scallops wrapped in yam. The yam is light, crispy, and sweet. While a little overpowering for the scallops, they're still very enjoyable and actually quite addictive. The black-pepper venison was also a pleasant surprise. The black pepper sauce was incredibly rich, fragrant, and really stole the show. We were mopping it up with the mantou instead of using it on the Chili crab. It was THAT GOOD!So all that food, with some drinks... at $50 a head? I MEAN COME ON! That's definitely worth one star right there. I'm just looking forward to the 50% off fresh lobster month. :D

Walked here post-drinks@WhiteRabbit down the hill. 3 of us had the signature chilli crabs, 2 baskets of fried mantaus and kailan cooked w garlic. Everything was tasty but my fav crabs (in this type of setting) is still Malaysia's FattyCrab in PJ. Extra star is for the airy patio seating.

I've never seen chilli crab advertised so aggressively! Ask any local about Jumbo Seafood and the association with chilli crab comes to mind. Besides chilli crabs, Jumbo does serve up a decent black pepper and salted egg version. Order a side of chinese buns to go with your crab instead of rice! Located in Dempsey, this is a great place to enjoy a taste of local flavor before heading off to any wine bar in the vicinity to enjoy a relaxing glass of wine under the lush greenery and foliage.

Jumbo Seafood at Dempsey is a great family restaurant. The seafood is always fresh and well cooked. I've been here several times, all reasonably satisfying experience. The service is prompt but not on the polite-side. The staff are mostly Chinese-speaking and do not understand a lot of English, which for some, myself included, makes it very difficult to give a simple order.The interior is nothing great, following their corporate colours, and themes. If you've been to one, they're just about the same as the rest without a hint of uniqueness. Jumbo about the biggest player in Singapore's seafood market, just about every local has been there! They've definitely built a big name for themselves, and for that they have my respect.Generally a place for family or co-workers, it is a great place for a reunion and even a company dinner.Mon - Sat, 12:00 pm - 9:00 pmSunday, Closed

Nice food, but a few items were not available.  You definitely need a reservation and basically full every night.  Black pepper crab probably best in town and prices are reasonable if you have the Jumbo privilege card.

Jumbo Seagood is one of the stalwarts of seafood dining in Singapore. It is famous for its chili crabs - the gravy is thick and luscious. Order a side of fried mantous (little buns) to dip into the gravy, and you're guaranteed to leave feeling satisfied! Other dishes which are good include the ever ubiquitous cereal prawns and black pepper crabs. The Dempsey outlet in particular has a rather nice atmosphere. It has a decidedly more upmarket feel than the other Jumbo outlets - this could also be due to the fact that it's one of the newer stores. Bring your tourist friends to Jumbo for a seafood dinner, and I'm pretty sure they'll have a good impression of Singapore (:

This place was superb. The food options were very great as it had lots of seafood to choose. We chose the feature dish of jumbo chili crab. We ordered two type of buns: fried and steamed to dip into the chili crab sauce. We also ordered the scallops, it was great! The service was wonderful as it provided with all the tools to avoid the mess that it requires to eat crabs. The tools were: plastic cover for your belongings, plastic bag for your phone, cover for your clothes, and many more. We also ordered fried shrimps,veggies, meegoreng, and many more. It was an awesome experience!

Delicious seafood close to the city! This location is most easily reached by car, so I would suggest driving or grabbing a ride as it's situated in the heart of the Dempsey estate. It's a great place to bring out of town guests as the air conditioning and upscale decor are pleasing and comfortable, compared to its seaside location which can be tricky when it's rainy.

Chilli crab: 80$ for 900g of Chilli crabService: 3/5 no complaints, just that staff do what is required of them only....nothing moreTaste: given many of these crabs are flown in from Sri Lanka, I'd recommend trying this in places like Ministry of Crab or Far Crab in Sri Lanka. Preferred dining experience & taste at Ministry. Repeat: no

I like to come her for "atas" seafood. For those of you are not familiar with Singlish, atas means "high class", "boujee". I do like this location of Jumbo, its more convenient than going all the way to East Coast. There is both indoor and outdoor seating. Personally, I hate sitting outdoors because the mosquitos start feeding on me! Nothing is worst than going for dinner and leaving with lots of mosquito bites.TIP: if you mosquitos love you, and you have to sit outside, wear long pants. And spray insect repellent if needed. This is not 100% fool proof, but it will help a little, thus enabling you to enjoy your meal more.Everyone loves eating chili crab here. I personally enjoy eating black pepper crab here. It is quite spicy! Be prepared to get your hands all dirty- but that is part of the experience! Don't worry, there are finger bowls as well as bathrooms for you to wash your hands.The food here is excellent. Some of the usual dishes I like to order are:-sambal kang kong-Hong Kong style steamed soon hok -Deep fried yam with scallop-Fried Rice and Fried Hor Fun Overall, a great place for seafood!

On a nice breezy night, this is a great Jumbo outlet to have dinner at.Jumbo remains my go-to for chilli crab, and I'm glad I was able to take my mother here to finally show her the wonderfulness that is Singapore chilli crab.Unfortunately they ran out of live prawn when we visited so the drunken prawn was unavailable. We ordered the cereal prawn instead and it didn't disappoint!In addition to the normal chilli crab and fried buns, we also got their seafood fried rice. Delicious as usual.Definitely make a reservation for dinner or weekends as far in advance as possible, as this place books very easily.

2nd visit this year, totally love it. Good food and good atmosphere. The outdoor seat is cooling but still will advice to avoid when the day are too hot.If you prefer indoor aircon seats, please make a reservation before visit. (You can use chops to make reservation as well)We ordered fried baby squid, salted eye prawns, egg fried rice, chili crab and scallop with yam ring. For me Jumbo serve the best chili crab among other major seafood chain, the sauce taste are balance and fried/steam mantou is a must eat with the chili crab sauce. Aaaaa is like heaven.

The 4 of us ordered 1 chilli crab which I thought was very good. It was not too spicy so that it went well with the Man Tau. The crab meat was nice and firm and filled the claws, indicating freshness and a high turn over. Some places the crabs have been sitting around a long time starving!The prawns cooked with salted egg yoke was good, but the dish was small. I liked the tofu cooked with broccoli and mushroom. Overall it was a very pleasant meal.

Another example of an expats staffed restaurant surpassing Singapore in service.  Singapore desperately needs to follow this restaurant's example of fine dining.  (Really Singapore you don't have to tolerate being so poorly served within a restaurant - wake up). A small entrance bar- good bar service.  Two dining rooms with plentiful, capable wait staff.  It's good Italian (not inspiring) with an attentive wait staff.  The place has an excellent wine menu.  If you can afford it - dne here.

You're always guaranteed to have a pleasant experience here. Excellent food and very good service in an elegant atmosphere. For starters, I recommend splitting the 'Dream' (S188++) with a partner: so decadent but how delicious - cold angel hair pasta with prawn, oyster, scallop, uni and caviar! Having the dish on your own would be too rich for most people. Classical dishes like osso bucco and veal milanesa are prepared to perfection here; the former melts in your mouth, the latter is juicy with very light 'batter'. Pricey, but still cheaper than the top Japanese restaurants!

We dropped in as most of the eateries in our neighbourhood had closed for business by 9:30 pm - Garibaldi seems to be one of very few places open late.The staff was very friendly and courteous, we were asked to have a drink in the bar area whilst a table was set for us.When our table was ready we were taken to the main dining area which has a very calming atmosphere, with white and light coloured wood being predominant - complete with curtains to draw out the outside noises and lights. Our waiter introduced us to the set-menu, five courses with coffee, all truffle-themed for 188 S$ per person. It sounded great but we did not want to eat all that much - and spend a little less on dinner.We decided to go with half a dozen oysters (Australia & NZ), shared a scallop/white truffles pasta starter and had pan roasted sea bass with vegetables as main.The food was delicious, the oysters fresh and very tasty, the pasta with scallops cooked to perfection and with the fresh truffle shavings just divine.The fish had a nice crispy skin and the meat was just perfect both in terms of texture and flavour.We had chosen a Sauvignon blanc/Semillon from Australia to go with the food, which was lovely and at 88 S$ one of the cheapest choices on the extensive and expensive wine list. We found that the wine in general was overpriced but since we hadn't splurged on food for some time we decided to treat us to it - this however being the reason for 4 stars instead of five, as it really blew us away.Service was very good and professional, and consistent throughout which has become somewhat of a rarity these days, unfortunately.This place is perfect if a celebration is in order - actually there were two local parties celebrating a birthday complete with cake and candles :-).We will certainly be back some day for their excellent Italian food (the executive chef is Italian) and perfect service.

Great food and service, and not really expensive for Singapore prices if you stay away from the caviar :) I had the lobster linguine which was exquisite, really a full whole lobster. $68++ Also ordered the antipasti set, which gives you a sampling of 6 different appetizers. $38++ My partner had the carbonara penne, which was also very good. Authentic cheese and real high quality smoked bacon (not your ordinary kind) I think the lunch set menu is also really reasonable, I think something around $40 and looks like a good deal.

I went there during the Restaurant Week on 1 Nov. This is the only restaurant that live up to my expectation during this Restaurant Week experience. They really prepared their best though we were paying half the price of their normal menu.Black Ink Fettuccine was on the menu that night. It was well executed :)

What a gem.  Pretty high end Italian place.  Pretty formal old school cooking.  The portions were pretty good sized.  The staff is responsive, the food fast, and very good.  I had the lamb...very good tasting.  However, it left my stomach upset.  It might have been how rich the food was, or how rare the meat was served.Wine list is great here is you have the money to spend.  Lots of good wines to try for any group.We had to ask for the bill.  Service was not attentive at times.

A fancy place with 5-star service and delicious Italian food? Yup, that's exactly what this place is! From the moment we entered, we were greeted with a jovial waiter and a complimentary plate of cheese and olives as we waited for our table to be ready. Just a few minutes later we were guided to our table and sent a complimentary appetizer and some of the best bread I've ever had. I had the fettuccini pomodoro and my husband had the veal and mushroom ravioli. We really enjoyed both and though we won't be coming here all the time (it's a bit expensive), this spot is perfect for a romantic night out.

Restaurant week dinner -appetizer. Fois gras with fusion flacked that didn't work. Pineapple compote and pandan chiffon cake bits should not appear with fois.  +tagliatelle duck ragu. Not bad. Big portion. Expected a bit more al debate+roasted cod. V nice-dessert was an afterthought. Strange flavor combo. -decor reminds me of higher end ikea. Too modern Not sure if I'd return even if I know the chef

Garibaldi is one of my favorites. It's pricy so I don't go as often as I would like. But the food has always been very good and the service friendly and professional. This evening we decided to go with the executive dinner. 5 courses with a beautiful prosecco as an aperitif. The food was excellent as usual with new flavor combinations that were fantastic. Highly recommended for special occasions or to impress a special person.

Came here for my Birthday and had a great time! Have always known that they were famous for their food - but I've never really got the chance to come. Am glad I kept it for my Birthday!What I Loved: The decor is nice. Service is really good too. We sat at the bar area - at one of the tables - as we wanted to have drinks and finger food. The staff paid quite a lot of attention to us. I ordered an Apricot Brandy & 7-Up which was great. For our finger food, we got the Bruschetta al Pomodoro & Calamari. My fave was the dessert, Tortino Caldo al Cioccolato ($18), Molten Lava Chocolate Cake with Hazelnut Gelato & Raspberry Coulis.What I Don't Love: The prices are pretty rough though. Just finger food, 3-4 drinks & dessert came up to like $138? But it's a pretty high end place so that's expected.

Pour quoi does Garibaldi even exist? Especially when competition is rife with Gunther's down the street? Well, I went one day as Gunther's was fully reserved and AMEX concierge suggested Garibaldi. The place was 3/4 full on a Friday night.Food  was lackluster. Perhaps because my taste buds are not evolved enough? I can't even remember what I ate! Service was polite, swift and sterile, albeit lacking a touch of attentiveness that is expected.

This Italian restaurant is good, but oh-so-pricey.  We enjoyed the dishes we had, extremely authentic, but small portions. The also have a huge selection of wines by the half bottles which is much appreciated and their free bread is good.But when the bill came, it was around the same price as Mozza, and it just didn't blow us away, so I think I'll head to Marina Bay Sands next time.

Garibaldi is known as one of Singapore's finest Italian restaurant and it is believable with its elegant façade and fine dining setting. The menu entices people with its authentic Italian cuisine and ingredients that have been imported from Italy. I tried 2 dishes there, both of which I am very satisfied with - Osso Buco Con Risotto (braised veal shank with saffron risotto) and Linguine with Crabmeat and Vodka Sauce. The spaghetti was marvelous, proving the high standards of this Italian restaurant as the pasta was cooked to al dente and tossed in a flavorsome tomato-based sauce with a touch of alcohol. The Osso Buco Con Risotto stole the show, with the braised veal shank so tender and succulent. The creamy and rich risotto perfectly complemented the savory veal. The standards of this restaurant are heightened by its impeccable service. The staff was warm and friendly, and not to say attentive and accommodating when taking our orders.

Fine Italian dining. Sophisticated dishes in a modern European ambience. I had the linguine with sea urchin - absolutely divine in its blend of favors, creaminess from the uni. The crackling pork was also wonderful.  Portions are small, but that's normal for high end European dining. Impressive wine list.  But - it's expensive, as the other reviewers note. Expect to pay $250-300 per person including good wines.

High-end modern Italian food which is yummy .  Excellent service and nice ambience.  On the pricey side. Good for groups and romantic dates.  Value for money lunch sets options available for weekday.   My duck ragout pasta was fabulous!

E-Sarn is hands down the best Thai place myself and my family have ever gone to. Our Thai friends introduced us 6 years ago (which just proves how authentic and good it MUST be!) and we've been going regularly ever since. We bring all our guests and visitors, and they all agree on how wonderful E-Sarn is!The service is wonderful and friendly, and extremely fast! As soon as we order, it's almost at our table instantaneously.Our favourite dishes are the sun-dried pork, clear tom yam seafood soup, fish cakes, cha om (thai vegetable omelette) as well as the mango salad, and have become our regulars when we pay our visits. We've never found another Thai restaurant in Singapore that tops E-Sarn, and honestly, that's fine, as we love E-Sarn and would not trade it for anything!

Good place for Thai food. Nice restaurant setting and location if you want to get away from crowded shopping malls. Located just across the road from pasir Panjang mrt station. Two girlfriends and I shared a large pad thai, minced chicken with chili and omelette with minced pork. The pad thai has the right amount of gravy and taste. The minced chicken came in a decent portion and was not too spicy. The star was the omelette which was super crispy and addictive. My friend also enjoyed the coconut drink. It's a pity that the mango desserts were not available during our visit.

This restaurant is managed by a team of Thai staffs so the food is expected to be good.My most recent trip was on Monday with my husband and a friend of mine. We initially ordered the green curry, grilled pork salad and stir fried kang kong. However, after seeing how tiny the portions were, my husband quickly added another order of basil minced pork.Green curry looked more yellow than green but it tasted pretty good. Kang kong was ok. It was fresh with the spicy kick. Grilled pork salad: I think the taste is altered to cater to the numerous expats living in the area. Typical Thai salads, or "yum", usually have strong sour and spicy taste. However the dish is rather mild (and also lacks the aromatic crushed rice bits).Minced pork and basil: I'm utterly disappointed with this dish. It doesn't look anything like a basil minced pork. It's more like the chef accidentally threw in an entire bottle of Chilli paste. Ironically, the dish doesn't come with much basil. I highly recommend that they change the name of this dish to stir fried minced pork with Chilli paste. The 4 items, 2 Thai ice teas, and 3 rice portions cost us 75 dollar. I don't remember it being so costly but I guess that's because it's been quite some time since I last came here. That said, it will be another long while before I come back here again. It's too painful to part with my money knowing that there are better and cheaper places to visit.

I really like this restaurant. It has been my go to place for Thai restaurant.I like all the food that we ordered. The grilled pork is very tasty, the fried fish with green chili is crunchy. The gai lan is good. The green curry & tom yum are good as well. Food is overall very satisfying. Minus one star for being so far down south and a little on the pricey end for Thai food. For the price I paid for 5 dishes ($150), you may fly a return flight on budget airline when it is on sale to BKK. Hahaha It is also a place that is frequented by many expats. I didn't know Pasir Panjang is quite popular with the expats.

Good food though inconsistent of late. Very poor value at their much increased prices. Tiny portions - large salad is enough for a nibble for 2. And service remains poor. Pity this erstwhile gem is slipping fast.
Love e-sarn, delivers every time. (And I come here every other week)Little pricy but worth it!
Great set lunches. Worth your money, but there may be a queue.The cooks are all Thai, so it is really authentic Thai food. i love the olive fried rice.:)

Try their herb salad and Thai vegetable omelette cha om! You don't get them in most other Thai restaurants and they are unique & delish. The other dishes are good too. More expensive than Thai Express (unless you get the lunch special or bento) yet worth it.

Definitely a fan! Other outlets are at Ridgewood, Thomson, Tanjong Katong and Robertson Quay and now there is also one close to my office!!Well close...it's actually a 10 minute walk from the nearest MRT station through a blistering heat. Then most of the time I get there, there is only a place outside for me to sit. Most people leave office around 12 for lunch in the neighboring offices, meaning they arrive there at 12:15-12:30, that's when the place start to get packed. For a reason though, because the food is just so good! E-sarn never fails to let me know if I grave for pad thai or green curry (although I don't really know what the figs are doing inside the curry and none of my collegues seem to eat them as well). They have a good set lunch menu for 7.90, see picture! Service is fast as well. The mango sticky rice with icecream on top is just heaven, but the same price as the set menu all together so take note. All together, great place to have lunch, but beat the crowd!

Who could resist the aroma of a freshly bake dough coming out from the oven and not getting hold of them? The sight of it was enough to make me hyperventilate, let alone tasting one.It as probably 6-months ago since I last had my bun from Maison Kayser at Scotts Square. They have never failed to draw crowds despite the fact that they are anchoring at the basement of a smaller but prestigious mall. Prior to its opening last December, it was one of the most anticipated bakery by many eager Singaporeans. I admitted being one - so sheepish.Their butter croissant has always be a big draw. As they baked in batches to allow the bread to taste its best (given the high humidity level in Singapore, the crust gets softened pretty fast), luck plays a big part in determining if I manage to bring one home today. It was far better than striking lottery, to me.Today, I am not in my lady luck - I missed the batch of croissants. The fella who has gotten the last piece, must be gloating now. Not feeling worst, I have still have other consolations to pick from.Recalling what I had on my last two visits, I chose an array of sweet bread which tasted almost new to me.Pain Aux Pommes - The bun had a very faint sweetness arising from the honey. Its shell was undeniably crusty with a chewy dough. It was visibly filled with large apple chunks, stodgy and a tad sour. The walnut adds a good nutty flavor to the rustic bun.The Orange - Not sure if I read the tag correctly at the counter, "earl grey with orange peels". I sniffed none of the earl grey scent but the bread was baked using dark rye flour - nutty and doughy. I have always been attracted to chewy European-styled bread; this was the show stopper among all, which I bagged today. Generous amount of orange peels were seen everywhere, candied but still contained its natural citrus flavor. Marvelous!Pain Aux Yuzu - Didn't know that I had this yuzu bun until I read my previous blog! So this was my second attempt? And it had the same consistency! I adored the crumble yet the center was soft. The sweetness in the dough was prominent but natural. The yuzu peels were seen scattered evenly which gave a good lemony taste. I am still loving it.
This is a cute, small French-style bakery/cafe in the basement of the Scotts Square building. A good place for a post-dinner pastry and coffee.

A better than average bakery in the basement?  Yes!  Despite the German sounding name, Maison Kayser is from Japan and their products fill a nice niche that is richer than local bakers yet lighter than traditional European bakeries.  After reading the other reviews, I really should have gotten a baguette.  But I was able to try some croissants, eclairs, and cakes so I can definitely comment on those ;).  Their almond croissant was excellent.  Really.  Not sure if I like theirs over Paul's but in any case, it's damn good.  I wish I could say the same about the cakes.  Most were ok, but nothing really stood out.  However, their best seller, the lemon tart, is excellent.  Great flavor and a lovely tart altogether.  The yuzu eclair however, was a fail.  Overall, a very nice choice for bakery in an unlikely place.
It's all about the chausson au pommes. Croissant was legendary also.

This place has the best bred I tasted so far in Singapore! Better than most boulangeries in France. I love it. Although because of the weather you tend to lose the crispiness quite quickly.  Advise: put it in the over a few minutes before eating if it stayed out a few hours.We had a croque monsieur, mushroom soup and hand and cheese sandwich.Everything was quite good, very simple but good.Ham and cheese may not appeal to the asian crownd as the baguette bred is quite crispy and hard on the outside but it is authentic.

We had lunch here on a Sunday. This is the second time we have been for a Sunday lunch and have not experienced the queues mentioned in other reviews of this place. So the good news first. The food is very good. The menu is fairly simple but non the worse for it. Soups have been very tasty with the bread basket with six different kinds of bread. Not sure if the breads with fruit in go so well with soup but they are nonetheless very tasty. The jambon and fromage baguette was very good. Not too much mustard and the cheese and the ham both had good flavour. Apart from running out of Coke while we were there the flavored teas Nd coffee also lived up to expectations. Now the not so good. Simply put the service is poor. It is certainly not for the lack of staff with 3 to 4 people serving a relatively small number of tables excluding the staff behind the counter. However no one takes responsibility for set tables with the result that no one is responsible for your food and drinks coming out quickly. Our drinks finally arrived just as the food was finished. The staff need to take responsibility for set tables otherwise nothing will improve. As mentioned accurately in another review. They should change to self service and save on the staff costs. It really is a shame as the food and drink make this a worthy stop.

The best bakery in Singapore hands down. I've been waiting for Maison Kayser to enter Singapore ever since I read about it in a manga. Without a doubt, the main attraction is the buttery smooth crossiant that makes just having one only impossible. Snaking queues are a common sight in the day so the best time to go and try it would be in the evening, as I found out when I visited. Service is brisk and the staff are well-informed on the various types of bread on offer and can advice you on just what you require.
