Pricewise, I was pretty amazed that for such high quality breads, what you're paying for is downright cheap and inexpensive. They have a small cafe where you can dine in and have coffee as well. Being in the basement does cost the cafe a little bit of the allure of a glamourous bakery, but the bread more than makes up for it.
For the crusty baguettes alone, I give 5 stars. For baguettes so good, I am happy just munching them on their own. Anything else on it is just a bonus.

I tried the almond croissant but was not impressed, but Mum really likes the orange breads. Definitely prefer the version at Tiong Bahru Bakery. The coffee is alright though not mindblowing.This place is always filled with tai tai types, not surprisingly given its location and type of stores. Service is friendly and helpful.

All the breads and pastries I've had from Maison Kayser have been really satisfying. It's on the more expensive side as far as bakeries go, but I think it's worth it. Even though it's a chain, I'd still say they do one of the best baguettes in Singapore.

Best croissants in Singapore. Slightly crispy on the outside and smooth inside. Not as oily-feeling as Tiong Bahru Bakery's and doesn't deflate like Paul's. However, I find several of its other breads a bit too hard.
still happy with the baguette, however..they've stopped selling ananas coco :(

Decent selection and ambience for a hotel buffet. Rise is baby-friendly to boot for family gatherings. Check out their daily specials. I came on Seafood night which is a Tuesday I believe. That works out great for me since I do like to feast on all things from the sea. Starting out with sashimi, oysters, scallops, mussels, crab legs, and octopus from the raw bar, it was the perfect way to start the gluttonous meal when paired with Mediterranean mezze and fresh salad. A variety of global cuisine in the hot section including local faves like black pepper crab and roast duck to Indian Kerela fish curry to Spanish paella and slices of prime rib. All decent but not necessarily memorable. I stuck with the raw bar more. Some desserts to cap off the meal. I was unimpressed with the pastries but thankfully the  fresh fruits like mango and dragon fruit plus zesty sorbets ended the meal on the right note. Service was attentive and friendly. Asked to be seated deeper inside the restaurant if the night is a romantic affair as it's dimmer and away from the tourists visiting MBS. Also believe there are discounts if you are part of the rewards program.

Average buffet breakfast, typical to what to be expected from a 5 Star hotel breakfast.They have two omelette stations. They have an Asian station and an international station. I got all of my food from the international station. They also have pastry station for all of the sweet stuff. It got crowded after 8am but not overly crowded given that the seating place is really big. They open at 6:30am and close at 10:30am. Marina bay has 3 other breakfast buffet restaurants I believe not sure if they serve different food.

I passed by Rise many times but it never occurred to me to dine there until recently. As it was still within the 15 days of Chinese New Year, the price went up by $10 because they were serving some CNY dishes. Errrr....the only CNY dishes I saw was a plate of yusheng in the salad section and 3 types of snacks in the dessert section (prawn rolls, kueh bangkit and something else). There was a wide variety of dishes with many sections - Asian, Indian, Western, pasta station, salad, cold cut appetizer, cold seafood, Japanese, soup and bread, dessert plus cheese and fresh juices. I love the Western dishes - braised veal cheeks so soft and tender it melted in the mouth. Rigatoni was cheesy and rich. Broccoli au gratin was equally good. The giant red snapper was very fresh and the meat was not too tough. The beef cubes in the Chinese section was a bit tough, especially when compared to the veal cheeks. But the broccoli and mushrooms were big and juicy. There was a honeycomb with honey dripping. Love this. The other place I have seen this was at Swiss Cafe at Swissotel the Stamford for morning breakfast. The juices (apple, orange and mango) were ok, but I preferred the fresh juices at 10 at Claymore (apple, orange, grapefruit and pineapple). The selection of cheese and freshly baked bread/rolls were very tempting. Olive roll, sundried tomato...shallot bread...yum. For the Japanese section, there was cold soba, some sushi which did not look very appetizing. The sashimi (tuna and salmon) was fresh and good. The cold seafood include crabs, prawns, mussels, clams, the usual suspects. I like the cold meat section with smoked salmon and seafood terrine. There were also smoked trout and other fish and cold cuts. The rojak was also pretty good with crispy you tiao. There were 2 local soup dishes which were made to order - laksa and fish ball noodles. Did not try those so could not comment on that. Desserts - the cakes were good, looked like what you could get at SweetSpot, the dessert coffee place in MBS. What blew me away was the warm stuff - sticky toffee pudding, chocolate souffle and bread and butter pudding. The bread and butter pudding was  the highlight. It was moist and sweet with a surprise dark chocolate base at the bottom. Topped with vanilla sauce, it was sublime. I had the rum and raisin ice cream to go with the pudding and it was generously laced with rum. As the place is pretty big with high glass ceiling, you do not feel hemmed in at all. The only "drawback" would be the sunlight if you dislike being in the sun. Otherwise it is a bright and airy place, nice for a lunch date.

Kudos for the food varieties. Colour and texture looks appetising but unfortunately it is too dry from my perspective. Sashimi looks beautiful but it is not as fresh and chewy as it looks. Main dish wise I'm disappointed. With the 1 for 1 voucher it is is worth to try I guess..Next, dessert. Mochi is chewy but the inside is not appetising. I tried a few dealer and I think the small plate of creme brûlée is the most appetising. The pudding like cocktail is good too with longan, blueberry and strawberry. Gelato sorbet - mango and strawberry is good too. Overall I still into the desserts here than the main course.Parking- you can park at the hotel or the shoppes area. For the shoppes parking, park at the central and walk to the left and left till you see the MRT sign and follow the sign board towards the hotel. It is in Tower 1. Open space concept that you can hardly miss. Bon appetit!

Been here on multiple occasions so I will break it down accordingly.1. Breakfast - plethora of options.As it is the complimentary option that comes with staying in a regular MBS room, this place is super crowded in the mornings! I don't know about everyone else, but the last thing I like in the mornings are ravenous individuals shoving me to get ahead in line for food.Sky on 57 has less options but makes for a more dignified experience, IMHO.2. Late night supper - for late night munchies. It serves up a decently extensive dessert/food menu past midnight. Not gourmet, but does the job when you are hungry and stranded on the island known as MBS.3. Drinks - now, this deserves 4 stars at least! Good selection, bartender was knowledgeable enough.

Avoid this buffet for breakfast. Its zoo like, packed with hotel guests who have it included in their stay; seems this is the only choice breakfast venue. Think 15 people deep lines. If you do go, get there before 8am.

Great pizza--some toppings are off ...like, who would ever put meatballs on pizza, other than my American wife? :-). You can see from their brick oven from Naples that they are serious!  Consistently good service, at least at lunch in the weekends (never been here at night...)

The Quattro formaggia is the best we tried of 3 different types. It's not a bad place at all. Just that we have tasted better. Prices seem reasonable especially because of the location. Service is very good.
Visited this place and enjoyed the food as well as ambiance. The customer service was great.

Of all the ripoff places in Singapore, this one takes the pizza!The Caprese was laughable, only 3 little pieces of store-bought mozzarella and small tomatoes... Not impressed.The pizzas couldn't be smaller and they could not be stingier with the ingredients. The Meatball pizza came with 5 tiny pieces of some sort of meat concoction at $23!!!Horrible place... and the manager? Nowhere to be found on a Saturday afternoon... and it shows! Spend your $$$ somewhere else!

Was prepared to spend a decent many of money there. Was going to get 2 or 3 pizzas (all over $20 each) and some wine. Then they have the audacity to say they will charge us for Singapore tap water per person.  First time we were there they didn't seem to charge for a simple galas on tap water. We left just on principle only.  There are a number other pizza places around that treat their customers much better.

Originally from Brooklyn, I was very excited to see Motorino arrive in Singapore, as it doesn't hurt to have another fine pizza joint.  And in terms of the pies, Motorino definitely delivers, but there are a few other parts of the dining experience that could be better.  The actual pie is 12 inches so it's good for one hungry person.  The crust is definitely amazing, and I really enjoyed the quality of ingredients.  It's a bit different from Mozza in the sense that there is more sauce, and I really enjoyed my version with sweet sausage, mozarella, and mushrooms.  What could be better?  For starters, it's very warm inside.  Even warmer than outside.  I know there is a massive oven inside, but still, it's quite uncomfortable (tip: there is a fan by one table which is where I would sit).  Secondly, it's next to the Butcher Club which apparently has a live DJ (at least on the Saturday night), so it was quite loud...not as loud as Attica, but it would be difficult to carry on a conversation.  So overall, while Motorino has some fine pies, I found it not very comfortable in terms of a restaurant.

Pretty Christmas decorations that welcome us on our way up the stairs. Even the chairs get dressed up with Santa hats!Great selection of Beer (try the Green Monster Beer!), Great Band, Great Ambience (but it can get a little loud at times when they raise the volume of the music). Great place to celebrate friend's birthday, you can order dessert and get the staff to personalize the plate with the word "Happy Birthday", you can also dedicate birthday song via the band.

I've been coming here for about 4 years, mainly for the beers and the outdoor setting. Staff are attentive and the beers are fine with a wide variety. But last Friday, 3 of us met there around 6:30pm. We sat outside near the water feature...I hadn't been back in about 6 months. I noticed how old and tired the place was looking. Nothing has changed outside in 3 years. If anything, service to the outdoor area has gone backwards since the closure of the outside serving station. Beers came in a good order from the inside bar, but the pizzas took an eternity from the kitchen. The Parma ham pizza was passable, but the meat lovers pizza was epically horrible...cardboard base with tomato sauce, topped with ground beef and BBQ sauce drizzled on top with unidentifiable cheese globbed here and there. A sicky sweet awful conglomeration...No pepperoni, no salami, no onions, no herbs...nothing. Avoid eating pizzas here at all costs. And please, spend some money on the outdoor area. Would have given just 1 star for the beers, but credit to staff that the toilets are clean and well serviced.
Ehhhh. Food was not great and not a lot of vegetarian options. The green beer is fun and light!

It is ok. It is a microbrewery. The fun beer is the green monster which looks luminously green but tastes like a normal beer.I find the beers here just ok, noting to rave about. Never tried any food here before.The place is nice for a quiet chill with friends as it is big, great for groups, nice on a balmy evening when it is not too humid. And yeah, free parking too!

Good beer........the extra star is for the beer, otherwise my rating would be TWO stars.  You can order a sampler set and taste the different beers before ordering a pint.  I was surprised with the lime wheat, very tasty and refreshing.  Food was edible and not memorable.  A bit overpriced for what you were getting.  Ordered the Baby Chili Squid, over cooked and basically eating crumbs of breading, did not eat.  Also ordered fish and chips, chips were good and dusted with a lovely seasoning and fish was okay.  Now for the service.  Seated by the hostess who did not appear to like her job.  She took our initial drink order and later our food order, 15 minutes later.  The food was served in a timely manner.  However, the service not so great.  When I was in need malt vinager and condiments, I had to flag some one down and each attempt was ignored by wait staff.  When I finally got the hostess' attention, I made my request, but again had to wait, in the mean time my food is becoming cold.  She finally  brought a sweet balsamic vinagerette dressing.  When I commented on the balasmic vinagrette dress I was served, the hostess responded rudely, "You asked for vinager and this is what we have."  After making a second request for vinager to a second waitress who promptly and apologetically brought me white wine vinager, which at this point I gave up asking.  Who serves fish & chips and does NOT have malt vinager?  Attempts at getting the wait staff attention is very difficult.   Make sure you make all your requests before they leave your table.GOOD beerOKAY food - a bit overpriced HORRENDOUS service - so far the worst service
Good location,  great selection of microbrew beers, very decent food for a brew house, good place to chill with friends, can get noisy but you are at a brew house after all.

This is a review of a short stop at RedDot Brewhouse for a industry related event.i recently attended a work event here.  There were about 20 of us,   We took up two tables.The staff was very friendly and attentive.  They were constantly there pouring beers and insuring orders were taken.I like the indoor/outdoor feel of the space.  It is very airy.  The place has a very relaxed mood.tinyurl.com/agh94vkThe beer was decent but doesn't really rank with amazing micro-brews.I would certainly consider to RedDot again.  I think it is a good spot for groups.

A nice bar with an alfresco vibe. There was a live band playing really chilled out tunes which set a beautiful relaxed atmosphere under the stars. RedDot brews their own brand of beers, with a taste test available so do test out before you get it, as we were recommended a sweet beer with passion fruit notes, but after tasting I was thankful I didn't get stuck with it in the end. One unfortunate thing that happened, as we were sitting beneath the trees, some gross unidentifiable semi-liquid stuff fell on my friend which kind of dampened the experience there, but this is probably and hopefully an unfortunate isolated case.

Much like the bigger red dot we're all living on, how much you like Reddot Brewhouse really depends on what you're expecting and what you're looking for.Don't expect: amazing fancy complex beers, or excellent service, or delicious satisfying mains.The service in particular, can be absolutely atrocious on some days.  Nope. Don't expect any of that.Instead, expect what you'd expect of a casual pub with a good band.Affordable, good (but not amazing) beer. Some interesting brews, and generally it all goes down easy.Great bar snacks and finger food. Their spicy wings pack a REAL KICK so don't go in cocky. The wedges and other snacks and eats are all perfectly decent. Nothing inedible, nothing gross. I found their Vongole HORRIBLE though, so I'd definitely give that a miss. Previous experiences have established that their other mains are also 'just decent', so generally I recommend eating dinner somewhere else first (and there are so, so many options in the Dempsey area so there's no excuse) and then going to chill out and have beers at Reddot after.The live bands they bring in are alright too. While not always the best singers in the place, they always work hard to engage the crowd, have little gameshow type things, (we won a free beer tower!), and generally really help up the fun factor.So like I said at the start. Don't go to Reddot looking to be disappointed. Go with low expectations, a high threshold for beer, and with friends you want to laugh with. That's the secret sauce.

Went here for dinner early on a Saturday evening. Our party of 4 didn't have a reservation, but luckily we were able to get seated right away.The menu has a good variety of pub grub and pastas, with average prices for Dempsey Hill. I wanted to order a pizza but apparently it wasn't available. I think the waitress mentioned something about pizzas only being served later in the evening? Either way, I was peeved about that, so I ended up not ordering. My husband ordered a seafood pasta of sorts and it was alright, nothing to Yelp about. Our friend's date got the fish and chips, and it also looked decent.However, the service was good, as the place was packed but I don't remember any long waits. Also, they were nice enough to let us move to the smoking area on the patio after the staff dried everything off (I don't know why they weren't prepared for the daily rainstorms we have!)What I really enjoyed was the live music. The first act of the evening was pretty good, 2 guys doing an acoustic act, singing an alternative music set. However, I really liked the second act- a man and woman who just sang with a keyboard. They sounded amazing! Loved their focus on top 40 hits.Overall, not a place to go out of your way for, but good spot for casually hanging out with friends or starting the night out. Also, the only place I know where you can have green beer year round, as opposed to only on St. Paddy's day. :)
We tucked in for one drink and enjoyed the flavor. The bartender was really friendly. The area is way too touristy for me and I don't think I'd like to eat here but it wasn't bad for grabbing a pint.

Nothing special. Just a microbrewery that serves surprisingly mainstream tasting beer. It's a pretty decent place to hang out if you do not mind staff with mediocre service that know NOTHING about their beers. Can do a lot better.

My friend took me to Chili's for their molten lava cake which I heard is one of the best in town. They are also famous for grilled baby ribs and their fried chicken. I love the ribs because it falls off nicely from the bone and oh the sauce they glazed the ribs with is simply mouthwatering. Their fried chicken is quite moist.. not as dry as some fried chickens are.. and very tender as well. Ambiance here is also quite lovely.

Wasn't super hungry and had a fire-grilled Corn Guacamole with nachos and my hubby had chili as starters. The guacamole dip was ok, I found it slightly on the bland side. The chili wasn't very good either. In fact, I find Botak Jones made better chili, compared to theirs.  Hubby ordered a pulled pork sandwich which was actually delicious!! The pork was tender and flavourful! Very good indeed!!The kids ordered Mac & Cheese which was not bad. Corn on the cob was also nicely buttered and grilled. The cheeseburger and fries were ok, nothing to shout about. Not likely to return unless no other makan choices.

Yesterday was our first visit to Universal Studios Singapore, and as it was my husband's birthday month, we received a voucher from RWS Invites offering a free main with a meal set purchased. We purchased two full racks of baby back ribs, cheese fries and a lemonade for ourselves and three children. The portions are generous - we could not finish all the ribs! Both ribs came with a whole ear of buttered corn on the cob and a side of fries. The waiter was friendly and the glass of lemonade was refilled regularly, twice upon request.However, our middle child removed his expander retainers, placed them on the table during the meal and forgot to wear them again. We even returned to the restaurant to use the restrooms as the table was being cleared, but were not stopped to retrieve them. Perhaps this is because someone else cleared the table than our waiter who would have recognized us. In any case, we remembered less than an hour later and returned to the restaurant looking for them, but were told that they were not located. They said they will call us if they find them. I really hope they will find them for us, but it's been over 12 hours already without word. We even stopped by again in the evening and were told that they hadn't found anything yet. One of the staff even proposed that perhaps our child had taken them and left them elsewhere, but that was not true because we were all at the table when he removed them and he did not leave his seat until the end of the meal. Losing these retainers has made this our singularly most expensive meal ever.
Considering that this is Chilis in Singapore it won't like the USA, but it wasn't a bad example.  It work.

I've been to this particular Chili's restaurant many times before and each time I go, I thoroughly enjoy my meal. I usually have the fajitas or the burger. My absolute favourite is the Mushroom Jack Fajita. The sizzling hotplate appears with marinated grilled chicken covered in mushrooms, bacon, onions and cheese. It looks and smells good enough to eat on its own without the wrap, but the fresh tomatoes, guacamole, lettuce and sour cream adds a delightfully refreshing touch when everything is combined in a wrap. There is almost something sacred about eating an indulgent meal as such with your hands that makes it taste even better, and that is accomplished quite neatly with a wrap. I would also recommend the sides like the chips and cheese fries that make perfect sharing dishes.The staff have always been rather pleasant to us, so service is not something I'd complain about. Also, the most of the drinks are refilled for free. I go to Chili's almost every time I go to Resorts World Sentosa, and I won't hesitate to go again.

We decided to eat here after a day at Universal City. Food was good albeit a little pricy compared to the US Chili's restaurants. As is the norm for chain store eating places in Singapore the customer service was sketchy at best. We were brought to our table and after several minutes of waiting had to request that a server come and take our order. Guess it has to do with tips being included in the price. They don't seem to care if you come in or not.

Menu is standard American, but the served items don't match. 'Big-mouth burgers' came looking gross (gray, like they were steam-cooked) with them a quartered burger rather than grilled (confirmed by manager, using 'ctx oven'). Boneless chicken things were dry and unappetizing too.Overall, from what we ordered, this is name-only Chilli's.

Love our experience eating here this time. We got table right away and our waiter are very tentative. She always refilled our ice tea when its low. we ordered beef fajitas (big portion and delish), steak and cheese quasadia ( delish also), beef chilli soup (the best chilli ever), warm brownies sunday with vanilla ice cream (big and full of yummyness. The brownies r amazingly soft in the inside). Will be eating here again for sure

SSB has been making news for their hip concepts (an actual standing only outlet in Marina Bay Link Mall and the group also owns Tanuki Raw at Orchard Central) and reinvented sushi rolls such as the American and Rockstar Sushi Rolls. Price-wise, it is not exactly cheap but they do have some pretty affordable lunch sets and I tried out the Shake Batayaki Bento Set ($22++).The set consisted of a Salad, Miso Soup, 8 Slices of Sashimi (2 Salmon, 1 Yellowtail, 1 Swordfish, 1 Tako, 1 Akagai and 2 Tuna), Grilled Salmon with Butter Sauce, Grilled Mackerel, Japanese Rice and 2 Slices of Watermelon. The best part of the meal was the sashimi and miso soup, which were respectively fresh and belly-warming good. I especially loved the Yellowtail and Salmon Sashimi, though some slices were a little small. The grilled salmon on the other hand, while decently cooked, was doused with an overly-buttery and sweet sauce that made it hard on the palate, especially in the theme of Japanese Cuisine. While I do not usually enjoy grilled mackerels, I found the version at SSB to be delicious, albeit a little salty, and much preferred it to the salmon.For the full review and pictures visit voraciousappetite.wordpr…

I know most people come here for the unbeatable Monday prices where a portion of salmon sashimi goes for SGD 3, a small glass of sake for SGD 1 and an Asahi for SGD 5. However, it gets pretty crazy on Monday nights and I, for one, really don't need that sort of incentive to visit Standing Sushi Bar. The menu is excellent, and I tend to order loads of other things besides the salmon sashimi.Some of my favourites include the grilled tiger prawn, bacon moriawase and shime saba sushi. Their salads are excellent, too, and their kyuri wakame is a real treat. Definitely my favourite spot for sushi at the moment. Despite the name, people don't stand at this sushi bar, although that was the concept they started out with. So if you're going on Monday, don't forget to make reservations!

If you're a salmon sashimi fan, come here on monday nights for their $3 salmon sashimi deal (5 slices). There's also sake shots for $1 and $5 Asahi beer, umeshu, and wine. It's quite a steal! But you have to make reservations though because monday nights are sure to be packed.I came here with a few mates for this promotion solely so we gobbled up the salmon sashimi almost endlessly - they were generous cuts and tasted fresh. We also had the seared salmon roll (yes we are crazy about salmon). The salmon almost melts in your mouth, it was too addictive, we had to order another plate!We stuffed ourselves with salmon to try other dishes, although the extensive menu looked really tempting. Maybe next time when there isn't cheap salmon sashimi to distract us.By the way, don't worry about having to stand while enjoying your sushi, there are tables and seats all round the restaurant. The name was probably a homage to the concept of serving busy professionals who are always on the go. You can however, find standing sushi bars in Japan.Final verdict: Outstanding sushi bar!

3.5* but closer to 3*Came here (opens at 6pm) after visiting the art museum on Fri. The food was fresh, so it's okay raw, but the cooked fish tasted very flat. I had the sanma, and while it wasn't bad, it was pretty blah. My friend had some mackerel in his bento, and it was pretty horrible, so I guess I can't complain since mine could have been worse, eh? :PWe also tried the fried salmon head, and it was also okay, but nothing extraordinary. A tad salty and dry-ish. But it seemed deep fried, so I guess it was meant to be that way.Also, the staff kept bugging us to take our orders. Hello? If we say give us another 5min, give us at least another 5min. Not bug us everyone minute for our order! Maybe it was because the place wasn't completely filled, and I did notice it was always a different server, so maybe it was just bad co-ordination. Still, it was annoying. Also, my set was served in a weird manner, i.e. the soup was right in the middle of the tray, first row facing me. Still, the price was okay, neither cheap nor expensive. It seems it's cheaper on Mondays, so maybe if I went then, I'd throw in another half star for being cheap.So I'd say this is just another average sushi bar. Nothing extraordinary.

The food here is pretty much a collection of ups and downs.I ordered the sake (or salmon. i have no idea what on earth they call it shake) batayaki bento set. It consists of 2 slices each of salmon & tuna sashimi, 1 slice each of an assortment of sashimi, grilled salmon with butter sauce, grilled mackerel, miso soup and 2 slices of watermelon. Pretty good for a $20 price tag.Lets break it down: The highlight of the set was the sashimi - it was really fresh and the quality was decent so I enjoyed most of it, especially the ika (squid), which they had a unique preparation. It lasted until i hit the maguro (tuna), which was on first sight pretty unappetizing with its dull color. Don't get me wrong, the tuna was fresh, but the taste was just that of cheap crap you won't want to see in a sushi bar. The grilled salmon was fine, the miso soup was good, but the watermelon and the grilled mackerel is rubbish.My experience was shared by my dinner companions too which felt that some things are good while others are nothing short of bad.Despite it all, I find the counter food is pretty good while the kitchen food require much more straightening up. I think this place has the potential of a good sushi bar if 2 things happen: the purveyor look out not only for freshness, but also quality and; the kitchen learns to properly season and cook their dishes.

For food and sashimi quality, it's a bit on the pricey side. Very crowded and not the most comfortable for a sit-down dinner/date night (hence the name), but the queue moves fast. I'd recommend going on days when they have specials. Sunday you have significant discounts on Donburi's. Monday night is Salmon night. Tuesday is half off sashimi and cheap beer, and Wednesday it's 50% off their rolls. If you check in on yelp, you get one free shot-glass of sake. Not a lot, but in this town where drinking is expensive, I'll take what I can get!

Average sushi, intimate setting, half priced Tuesdays. I think that says it all. Menu favorites are the white tuna (shiromaguro, albacore), karaage and beer. Did I mention you should only go here on Tuesdays.

sa-shi-mi!I think I'm over sushi. My eating partner and I were debating this over the endless devouring of "special rolls". Wouldn't it be great just to have the protein without the rice...We both looked at each other and exclaimed "sa-shi-mi!" with our best Japanese gameshow winner facial expressions!Nevermind that the entire packed-out restaurant stopped what they were all doing to stare at us for a solid 20 seconds. We just smiled. No embarrassments here, we were in our element.All we wanted was salmon... and my friend introduced me to something I'd never tried before, the salmon toro... or for the lay person, salmon belly. Yes it's the tenderer - fattier - tastier version of its standard salmon sake sashimi sibling; and it is so oishi!Standing sushi bar has deals, but I suspect if it didn't have them it would still be fairly busy. Where I think they go wrong is by having a menu trying to be everything, when really they should stick to the one thing they do well, and improve it until it is amazing... I'm talking of course about the sashimi.Would I come here again? Probably, on a discount day, when invited by a friend. Otherwise? probably not.

Meh. The sushi is not impressive. They have different promotions each day. I went on a Wednesday and it was 50% off their specialty rolls. They only have two pages dedicated to their specialty rolls, so the choices were extremely limiting. I tried the "all salmon all the time" roll and the "eel dragon" roll. The "all salmon all the time" roll had seared salmon over salmon sashimi and avocado. This roll was disappointing. There was some mysterious sauce on top of this roll that had a lemon flavor to it. It did not compliment the salmon at all. The eel dragon roll consisted of tempura and eel. This roll tasted a lot better but was still mediocre. The size of the rolls were actually  tiny as well. But these rolls were 50%, so it only cost $8 SGD for the salmon roll and $10 SGD for the eel dragon roll. FYI, the free glass of sake when you check-in on yelp is just a small shot cup of sake!

Pretty decent sushi rolls for the price! Good place to share sashimi platters and specialty rolls. There are also weekday promotions, which are really worth it. Just a warning that you will smell like raw fish after having a meal at the place.
Sushi was good.  Just not good enough to justify the price, and everything was too small for the price.  Might be better if I had caught a happy hour.

Came here after a look-see at the Singapore Art Museum. I went in about 1330, when lunch was nearly over. Service was prompt and polite, but the food was lacklustre.I had the sushi set lunch (it's really hard to eat clean in Singapore), which had 7 pieces of sushi, a salad, some pickles, a small serving of plain udon in broth, and two slices of watermelon for $20++. While it looks like great value, I doubt I would come here again, for the food.The sushi was smaller than what you normally get outside, not that I'm complaining, but it might take some getting used to. It was so-so, nothing to shout about. The udon was over-cooked and mushy; mediocre, I would say. I would say the watermelon was the best part of the meal. I read through the other reviews for this place, and people come here for the promos. I highly doubt I would come here for any promo - I think supermarket sushi and sashimi are better (try Takashimaya's Cold Storage sushi). I wouldn't call crappy sushi and everything else at a very low price, value.Plus: They take Amex.
I came here back in May and so I can't quite remember everything I had, but I remember loving every bit of it. A great sushi restaurant that is far superior to the Marina mall one.

Standing Sushi Bar is pretty awesome with its promotions I have to say.I went down last Monday to check it out. $3 for a 5pc Salmon Sashimi helping - ordered 6 portions of those between me and a friend. Only thing we noticed is that the Sashimi could've been colder. Not a fan of the chef removing the salmon with his bare hands either.. but I assume his hands are clean since I did not get a stomach ache after. Lol.A friend asked me to try the Seared Salmon Roll and it was good too.Overall exp was good. But it got really crowded at about 730pm and thats when service went down. I think they are really under staffed and missed my orders a few times.I had a glass of 1dollar sake to wash it all down at the end with my hot green tea.What I noticed is that it is a little bit expensive if not for the promos. The prices on the menu did shock me a little.I'll still return though if I get another salmon sashimi craving! Bon Apetite!

While Standing Sushi seems to offer a great value, everything in my bento set was off.  For a little over $20, I got 8 pieces of sashimi, salmon cooked in butter, grilled mackeral, rice, miso soup and watermelon.  Let's go through them in order.  The sashimi was a mix of everything from salmon and yellowtail to octopus and clam.  While the salmon was decent, there was one piece of yellowtail that was definitely off. Fortunately, I was ok afterwards, but still it was nasty.  While the portions for the salmon and mackeral were generous, the butter had a funky taste and totally overwhelmed the salmon and the mackeral was dry to the point that it was tough.  The miso soup also had some very non-traditional veggies, which just didn't belong.  Given the options, I would spend a bit more, and eat a bit less at a number of better places nearby.

Chose to eat here as it was nearby another place I had to go and I regretted. Food wasn't particularly cheap, quality was very very mediocre. My garlic fried rice smelt of margarine butter instead of normal butter which was super disappointing. The natto sushi wasn't fresh and the natto tasted strongly of metal container, while the sushi was wrapped in seaweed that's not fresh. It wasn't even crunchy anymore and almost like rubber. Basically not impressive place at all, I could get better sushi at a better price at supermarkets like NTUC fair price.

Went on a Wed night with 50% off sushi rolls. Larger parties have to wait longer to be seated  -- better if you're one or two persons.This place isn't going to win any awards -- it's sushi. I ordered from the sushi roll menu, of course, and there were about 6 choices (not too many.) However, both rolls were large with a good amount of fish,, and not too much rice. The rolls were tasty (I just kept to the sale items.)I wouldn't go out of my way for this place, but if I crave cheap sushi, this is a good place to go to.

$3 for a plate of sashimi? Sounded too good to be true - virtually unheard of in our dog-eat-dog, kiasu world - I decided to check it out with my mum to see if there were any 'surprises'...There were! But of the sensuous, silky smooth, thick-cut kind... On Mondays (yes Mondays only), you get 5 long and hefty pieces of expertly prepared and cut salmon... They tasted very, very fresh and my mum and I shared 4 orders. No regrets here!We also went ahead, and abused the $5-a-flask of sake deal they had. The sake was deliciously warm, heating you up from the inside after the chill-ish salmon cooled you down. Mum went ahead and ordered the Fermented Soya Beans ($5), a good serving of anti-oxidant-filled, life-prolonging, sticky tasteless clumps, with wasabi and an egg yolk on top.Wasn't meant to taste good, but we enjoyed it anyway.The Grilled Eel ($16) was a little overpriced, but the freshness and tenderness of the flesh it offered to us (BBQed right on the spot in front of us!) made us forget about the price tag (cha-ching!). Mumsy & I will definitely be back... this is a gem that's above all the Japanese chains that served everything in a croquette, deep-fried, and it should be cherished.

The night museum is back, my friends and I decided to check out this year's installation and one of the stops were at 8QSAM. After walking around 8QSAM, we were kinda of hungry and decided to try out the Standing Sushi Bar.It was rather late at night and they did not have any cooked food but only sushi and sashimi plus drinks. Interestingly, they have some special items to mark the event. It is called the Night Owl Maki and apparently it has a dash of red bull added to it. Well, we weren't too adventurous to try that but decided to stick to sashimi. We ordered the sashimi platter and some maki rolls together with the plum wine drinks that were on promotion, its good!  I heard that they have cheap sushi nights too.

Please check out my blog (on my profile) for photos :)I went on a Thursday because Standing Sushi Bar (SSB) has a promotion on mondays and thursdays for Salmon sashimi. It's 5 for $3 which is such a steal because sashimi elsewhere is much pricier, like 5 for $8.Anyway, my partner and I ordered 5 sets = 15 slices, but we ended up adding 2 more sets so we had 21 slices altogether. Is that a lot?? Hahaha idk but we really love eating salmon sashimi and SSB's salmon sashimi quality is not that impressive. But for the price it's definitely worth it!!Also tried the yakiniku don set meal, which comes with beef and saba fish, and sashimi of its own. It was $20, not very worth it considering that the fish was a really small piece, and the sashimi wasn't that fresh.Also had some of their speciality rolls and I can't remember the names but I'm quite sure we had one called Puff the Magic Dragon? It was quite yummy but overpriced if you ask me: $18.90.Overall our experience was alright cos we made a reservation and didn't have to wait. Service was also quite prompt! Be warned: without reservation the queue is quite long. Reservations also have to be made more than one week in advance.Anyway we probably won't return because it's kinda overrated :( other than the sashimi madness promotion everything else is overpriced. The price would've been acceptable if the quality was better but that's not the case. But this is my personal opinion because most of my friends are avid fans of SSB! Does anyone agree with me? Hahaha.Please check out my blog (on my profile) for photos :)

Seriously the Monday madness is insanely good. $3 fo 5 pcs of Salmon Sashimi (it's not super premium, decent enough but for that price are you complaining!?), $5 asahi beer and $1 sake!It's not a standing joint anymore - at least in the evening while I was there, with tables and chairs laid out like a normal eating spot. The counter gives you great view and immediate access to the sashimi and grilled skewer stuff, but the high stools and squeezy space aren't the most comfortable place to sit.Decent food, not that much cheaper than your typical Japanese food restaurant in Singapore but the Monday madness and 15% standard chartered discounts are pretty decent... plus the free glass of Sake if you check in on Yelp there! =)

Fabulous! Gunther's *modern french* dining certainly lives up to its name. I had Gunther's when it first opened a long time ago & i'm glad to be back again tonight. Signature dishes:Angel hair pasta with caviar. Back then this signature dish was all the rage and it still tastes just as good. Light & heavy flavors at the same time to match perfectly with a nice champagne.The foie gras with crushed almonds & hibiscus sauce is a classic & it's return to the menu is a welcome return. Again, light & heavy flavors will match with a nice burgundy or red. Apple tart is not in the photos i uploaded but it is another must try dish. Light flaky crunchy crust matches very well with a light apple filling that won't overwhelm your stomach but is a very welcome end to one's meal & palette. Today's dishes that i had that were memorable... actually they were all great!Onion cheese gratin - a very french influenced dish using onion, the texture & sweetness of the onion is brought out nicely. Langoustine meuniere - full of prawn flavor yet it is very very light. It is sliced very thinly so the gamey taste of raw prawn is not overpowering but its sweetness is brought out, nicely balanced with the cream & caviar.Carabinero gambas prawn - Gunther's is very capable to do a sharing portion for 2 tonight. The 2 spoonfuls of tomato & slightly spicy rice is full of flavor. The prawn is cooked just right with some tasty roe. It's head & brains is cooked to perfection! Pork Belly & Coquille Pasta - Very large portions for sharing. The pork belly is very fulfilling, comforting & satisfying to one's belly. The sauce would match well with a margaux or burgundy! I was feeling very full at this point BUT dessert beckons!For dessert, crepe suzette that was also shared between me & my guest. Gunther's staff will put on a nice show to flambe the crepe's in front of you. The orange sauce is tangy served with an equally tasy ice cream & light crepes that is nicely burnt in a few places. Ambience:Gunther's decor is very simple but its ambience is quite quiet & there are not many tables that adds to the exclusivity of dining here. This is a nice place for a romantic dinner for two.Price: Special's & seasonal items can be quite expensive but given that gunther's is willing to do sharing portions & some dishes are large portions, at least one's belly will not go hungry after the meal. As always, lunch is the best time to go for value for money. Monday's & tuesday are corkage free which adds tremendously to gunther's value. Service:The ratio of servers to each table is approximately 1 to 1-2 tables depending on how booked Gunther's is. Every staff is friendly and willing to explain anything. I recommend Mogish who is a long time staff to take good care you. Overall: Gunther's has been fabulous. My guest was equally delighted. Each dish is a nice gastronomical surprise & a nice refresh of memories from my first dining experience at gunther's. I will return soon! Thanks chef & team!!!

Gunther's is one of the best French restaurants in Singapore. Located in the middle of the shophouses, next to its sister restaurant Garibaldi Italian Restaurant & Bar, another equally well known restaurant. Although the restaurant is quite high end with its equally expensive priced menu, it offers quite a reasonable priced 3 course lunch set at $38++ which is available on weekday.The restaurant is decorated in grey with paintings and dim lights around which gives an elegant setting. Besides the usual menu, the staff also make his offers on what is in season by using a "daily special cart". Today there is vegetables from Japan, lamb, wagyu beef, and assorted seafood such king crab, scallop. But the one which holds everyone's attention is the truffle. Even when covers in a glass cover, one can easily smells the earthy pungent smell.Before starting the meal, one is served with hot towel to wipe with. One is served with a pipping warm mini buguette and butter to start the meal. Though the bread looks hard, it is quite crispy and soft to texture.For today's lunch set, there is 3 choices for starter : Farmer's salad, Clear vegetable soup, and Braised Portobello mushroom, sunny side up egg. Braised Portobello mushroom, sunny side up eggThe mushroom is quite well flavoured.Next is the main which also comes with 3 choices : Gunther's Creation (seafood pasta), Braised lamb stew, Leffe beer, and Charcoal grilled Wagyu steak (additional S$20++).Cold Angel hair pasta, Oscietra caviar ($60++)However I decide to go with the staff's recommendation to topup $40++ more to change the main course to the restaurant's signature cold pasta dish. It is quite popular which could be found in most tables. Refreshing cold and smells great of truffle which makes one high before eating.The last course is the dessert which also comes with 3 choices : Dessert of the Day (Pineapple Panna Cotta), Cheese Platter (additional S$10++), and Fine apple tart "à la dragées", Havana rum raisin ice cream (additional S$8++).Fine apple tart "à la dragées", Havana rum raisin ice cream ($25++)The apple tart is different from the traditional apple tart. It looks more like a flat pizza. Thin slices of soft caramelised apple on a very thin base. Crunchy and crispy on the outside. The ice cream is rich and creamy. Pairing the cold ice cream and the warm apple tart together is quite a yummy combination.Lastly there is coffee or tea and Petit fours to end the meal with.The coffee is quite rich with a slight bitter and chocolaty taste. I have it with just milk and without sugar. It is just nice to balance with the sweetness from the dessert and petit fours. The petit fours consists of Financier, Canele, Wafer and chocolate. I like the canel, which has a soft and tender custard center with a dark, thick caramelized crust.Overall the food is quite delicious. The place is packed even it is a weekday lunch time. Although the restaurant is busy, its Chef Gunther still make an effort to visit the tables.

Came here three years ago for our anniversary and after a great time here, we recently revisited when my mom was in town again. This time around, there was NO set menu- it's all a la carte, with an exception of $250/person chef's degustation "surprise" menu which we opted for. We weren't disappointed, and their signature caviar pasta still lingers in my palette and memory days after our visit. But I'm not sure if it justified the high price tag ($880 for 3 pax). D and I thought it was a bit pricey for its location and mundane decor (small room with not much decor and no view) and were a bit annoyed that it only offered one set menu or nothing at all and having to go a la carte, as we like the surprises of set courses in fine dining. In comparison, Les Amis offers courses in the range of $150~250 and Jaan $190~$299, which also has sophisticated and lovely decor and an amazing view, respectively, as an added plus.Service was great as always, and every dish was delish (with an exception to truffle that we thought lacked much flavor) so no regrets. But not sure if we'd return again.

No matter where I am, I always have this thing about Lunch Specials! Gunther's Modern French Cuisine is one of the Top 20 restaurants in The Miele Guide with Set Dinner Menu at a price tag of SPD$ 128++. The SPD$38++ lunch set menu for sure sounded like a bargain.Purvis Street where Gunther's located is quite interesting. The business/restaurants here has this mix of the different cuisine of traditional VS modern, new VS old, local VS international. The co existence of all these restaurants is just how Singapore is as a whole.Gunther's is smallish with just a handful of tables so reservations is highly recommended.There are a couple of choices for Appetizer and Main, and  I decided on the following:Green Asparagus with Ravioli Foie Gras - I just could not resist when I saw foie gras on the menu. The sauce really complimented the Foie Gras as I cleaned my dish with the warm baguette. The asparagus was cooked perfectly with just the right crunch.Oven roasted cod, béarnaise sauce - I found it is just OK, average the most. The Tempura vegetables lack the crispness and off the fryer freshness. Dessert of the Day - Earl Grey Pudding - which is really really good! Light, Smooth and with just the right amount of sweetness!Followed by Petite Four and ended with a cappuccino.The Chef also gave me a taste of their Cold Angel Hair Pasta with Oscietra Caviar - All I can say is CAVIAR! This suppose to be their signature appetizer and I have to say it is Excellent!! Refreshing and light and  Truffle Oil!! CAVIAR!!Services is attentive and professional. Great Food! Great Value! Lunch Specials ROCKS!

Went for set lunch. Gunther's creation for the day was braised beef cheek, paired with pureed potatoes and a sliver of corn, and it was succulent. The cauliflower appetizer with purple mustard and a strip of bacon came together nicely and the flavors complimented each other well - the mild sweetness of the cauliflower with the smoky saltiness of the bacon and bitterness of the mustard. Chocolate ice cream came with creme anglaise and three segments of mandarin. The apple tart seemed German, flat and shaped like a pizza slice with carmelized sugar on top with rum raisin ice cream on the side.Epic.Also, it is a legitimately fancy restaurant. I felt underdressed in jeans.

I have heard rave reviews about Gunther's for a very long time. The name just keep on coming across my ears for years; but for some reason, I just never ended up there. We're not completely sure what made us go there, but we decided to go there to celebrate our 2nd anniversary.I had the truffle soup for my starter and it was up to standard. It was creatively served with pumpkin veloute; I think they match well. Le wife had "Floating island of champignons de Paris" which is basically consomme, with thinly sliced mushrooms. It was disappointing tbh. The dish was completely lacking and just too plain.The second course was the star of the night. I had the scampi carpaccio, cream, caviar and it just blew my mind. I'm a fan of a simple-dish-done-well and this dish was executed to perfection. The ingredients were fresh and the cream compliments the caviar perfectly without overpowering it. Le wife had what I think was their signature dish, the cold angel hair with caviar. It's not a unique dish, but again, the execution was spot on.The third dish was decent. I'm a big fan of prawn so I decided to go for the carabinero gambas, which is basically those red prawns from the Mediterranean Sea. It was not the best one that I've ever had, but it was still ok. It was slightly overcooked for me, and there was some tomato risotto that just felt out of place. Le wife had bamboo clam with black truffle.The main course was another dish that I love. We shared the roasted rack of pata negra pig. At first bites, I thought it was just a mediocre pork chop. But the after taste of the pork was just superb, I feel like this is a very deep and mature dish that you just can't stop eating. Heck, I even took 1/2 of my wife's pork!The dessert was also great. We shared the apple tart a la dragees. It's a very thin and crispy apple pie. It was a little bit too sweet to my taste, but it didn't stop me from finishing them.Overall, I'd definitely be back to Gunther's. I heard they have a great lunch deal but even without it, a future visit to Gunther's is imminent.

I had friends and business associates visiting from Beijing and London. I planned to host them for dinner.  There would be at least 8 and possibly 10 of us.Three of the upmarket restaurants that I contacted insisted that a party of 8 or more must all order an agreed set dinner!  I was astounded to hear that a high dollar restaurant could not be bothered to take individual orders from my guests.One restaurant did agree to take my request for individualized service to their general manager for consideration but I told them not to bother. If a decision to give a customer and each of his guests what they wanted to eat required top manager approval then I was obviously talking to the wrong restaurant.I took a chance and hosted the dinner at Gunther's. We spent about 3 hours and about S$2,500 in Gunther's.  Not only did I consider the money well spent, I considered it a bargain.Everyone got exactly what they wanted and was extremely pleased with the quality of the food, the ambience and the attentive service.You can't go wrong with Gunther's. There are not enough upmarket restaurants in Singapore where you can get a fantastic meal served by friendly staff who are happy to meet your requests rather than insisting that you confine your expectations to the limits of their policies.Fortunately for the more demanding Singaporeans, there are still restaurants like Gunther's.All five stars were fully earned.

Gunther's is a French restaurant that cannot be missed. The elegant ambience of the restaurant and exemplary service makes you feel pampered, while the good fare feels like a treat. The restaurant is located at the central area of City Hall and Bugis, which is accessible and convenient. This restaurant has merited positive reviews for its angel hair pasta, so I had to try one of those. I ordered the Cold Angel Hair Pasta with Oscietra Caviar and was not disappointed. The pasta was cooked to al dente and seasoned generously with truffle oil, and finally topped with Oscietra Caviar. The amazing flavor of the seasoning coupled with the bounciness of the pasta made it a satisfying dish. For dessert, the Canele from the Petit four was outstanding. It is a bite-sized snack in perfect proportions, and is crispy on the outside and chewy inside; a good finale to the meal.
Easily my favoritest high-end restaurant in Singapore! Suggestion: order the fresh seafood.. the dead-eyed fish may seem slightly scary, but I promise that you will not regret splurging on this :)

Divine food.  From start to finish, each dish brings its best flavor out of the ingredients and very well thought through taste.  Apple tarte is a must - make sure you share, the portion was huge.  Great for date night, special occasion and corporate dinners.
I enjoyed the set lunch at Gunther's. The food was good and the service, professional. Nothing to complain about! I really would like to try the Cold Angel Hair Pasta with Oscietra Caviar next.
Fresh food! Grilled fish is better than steaks. My 3rd or 4th time here, will definitely comeback again!

Sunday lunch, waited 15 minutes for someone to offer us water and menusWhen questioning the specials he had no idea what they came with ... brought my main course whilst I was eating my appetizer....had the lamb shank which was ok, had the rigatoni with ragu which was good....the service throughout was disappointing

Culina is fresh European bistro food served in a clean, white, and cozy space.The oysters were full and fresh.The burrata smooth and creamy.Charcuterie salty, smooth, and rich.Everything was cooked in a way that brought out its natural flavors.The fish and chips was so simple yet delicious. The mussels and rack of lamb were also cooked and seasoned just right. (The lamb came with a side of roasted tomatoes and peppers that literally melted in your mouth. I'm still confused how they made that happen.)The place was buzzing for Sunday afternoon lunch. Salads and sandwiches are $20+. Mains $30+. Certainly not cheap, but eating here reminded me WHY food can cost this much in the first place - you're paying for a meal that you enjoy in the simplest and fullest understanding of the word.The deli made for a fun wander-through as you waited for your food, though it felt a bit small - probably to make room for the dining space. The place was chock full of wonderful, wondrous imported gourmet things. If I ever run into anyone seeking a thoughtful gift - I'll direct the kind soul to Culina.

I really liked their steak here. But, a little pricey for just a steak. However, the burnt sections of the steak where they grill it tastes very good for some reason, it's like they grilled it on cedar wood or some sort of wood that makes it have that smokey taste.We paired this steak with Chilean wine. So they sell wine in the supermarket, but they charge you corkage if you buy from the supermarket. If you buy from the menu, no corkage. Weird right?And the cheese is good - they have a variety of cheese.Dessert we shared sticky toffee pudding and apple pie - both were good too.I would recommend coming here if you can get reservations. It's a nice place to have dinner, indoors, because I can't stand the weather in Singapore...

This place has a novel concept where deli and restaurant merge as one. Culina produces reasonably good quality food. A recent change in chef has meant we miss some of the ways some dishes are prepared but still, we think this place is great to sit, people watch while enjoying steak, pasta or the like which are all cooked well.What disappointed me and caused me to score it one star is the service. While Culina has the basics and generally their floor staff cannot be faulted, they clearly lack a competent sommelier and an empowered assistant manager. For a place that serves wine, it is intolerable to not have someone who can provide sound advice on wine on their standard list and the wine in their deli section. It is also intolerable to not have someone who understands customer relationship management and to make the executive decisions in this space when a customer is complaining about a legitimate issue.Last night, we ordered our regular favorite bottle of wine from their store which we paid corkage for on top of the deli pricing. On tasting, it was badly heat damaged. We raised the concern and the assistant manager decided to stand firm and insisted it was not heat damaged. She pushed the fact that the whole batch has been sitting here and there is nothing wrong with it.I won't pretend to assume I am an expert but in my 20 years, I know when wine is heat damaged or not. We have had this same bottle of wine on many occasions here in Culina prior to last night. Same year. Same vintage. It WAS perfect.She offered to decant and we eventually opened a second bottle. Also heat damaged. In the end, we paid for the bottle but hardly touched the wine still sitting in the decanter and the first glass she poured it in. She never offered any form of apology or suggested to replace the wine with another vintage despite this.This place used to be a staple for us for steak and wine. It is now off the list until someone informs us a competent sommelier is in place. Or a competent manager. Preferably both.

Its a great gourmet supermarket with an attached bistro to it. You can find a lot of hard-to-get items at most supermarkets here ranging from bread, herbs, drinks to fresh produce. I like to come here and browse around before heading to the bistro to grab a quick bite. Most of the times I go for the sandwiches. Most of the staff working here are very polite and will help you look for what you need without any fuss.

Culina is a gourmet restaurant located at Dempsey Road. They serve excellent bread and wine. But this had a lot of people in an uproar. I heard from a very upset friend that they apparently have a corkage charge if wine is consumed on the premises. I usually just blindly pay my bill, but could you say way to capitalize much?Besides from that my personal experience aside, I've only heard good things about this restaurant. It's a fantastic place for a Sunday lunch, or a lunch anytime at all. Great place to sit down with you buddies for some quality bonding. Generally I am very happy with this restaurant. It has this consistency that I can always depend on.Opening HoursMon-Sat: 9am - 8pm Sun & PH: 9am - 6pm

This review is solely for the boutique/grocery.I was excited to visit this place, as I love to cook Italian food and I can never seem to find quality ingredients for Italian cooking at my nearby grocery stores.They had a good selection of balsamic vinegars and olive oils, and they range from affordable to ridiculously high end. I didn't see any bottled tomato sauce, which surprised me. (I guess I'll head across the street to Jones the Grocer for that, as they have a nice selection there.) Their produce and bread selection is small, but everything looked fresh. It seems they put more of a focus on their wines and their butchery.I guess I had my hopes a bit too high, as I felt the store overall was lacking. I think it's because it's in a small space, and it's simply a "gourmet" grocer - gourmet in a VERY broad sense, as it doesn't focus on a specific cuisine. Still, I lust after their high end stuff and once I start working, I might treat myself to a few items from here. :) I don't think this will be my go-to spot for fancy shmancy shenanigans, but if I'm in the area wouldn't hesitate to drop by.
Fun little grocery store that carries hard to get Italian ingredients (Singapore).Has a little cafe and bar. Food is tasty and they turned a decent steak sandwich.

Culina Dempsey is the best gourmet food store in Singapore by a long long way. Fantastic products from all around the world, a great selection of beef, mainly from Australia and New Zealand, they also sell dry aged beef, which I can't think of anyone else in Singapore who is selling this incredible product, worth every cent!! Amazing fresh air flown vegetables, from France, Holland and Australia, will inspire anyone looking at whipping up a fantastic dinner. Their customer service team is awesome, product knowledge is very astute and they are always very friendly and helpful. Add a bistro with great food and you'll find yourself grabbing a basket full of goodies for the kitchen at home, and sitting down for lunch! Steak sandwich and croque monsuire are both very very good, simple dishes executed well with great produce.  Will and always will be a regular customer of this store.

One word. Oysters. These are the freshest oysters I've had in Singapore. The Perle Banche and the other variety that belongs to the creamy category. They were fresh, big, sweet and amazing. Topped with the Tetsuya sauce which was like a miracle sauce for oysters, these oysters are unparalleled. Their homemade gnocchi with duck ragout was an excellent dish as well. Everything I had here was pretty tasty, except the spaghetti with crabmeat. Crabmeat was clumpy and soft and the pasta was overcooked. For a complete review on it, visit my blog (address under my profile). Thanks!
Great bistro. Try the waygu Blackmore steak or Oyster. Good wine selection. Excellent hangout during the weekend!

Now this is a difficult one to categorize: it is partly restaurant but also partly high-end and expensive delicatessen. Today, I bought Bleu de Gex and Reblochon and lamb prosciutto. There is a great choice of wines from different countries (no Alsace found though), exclusive vegetables (the small artichokes looked delicious), French type bread and cheeses.The restaurant was completely full  but that is typical here for a Sunday at lunch time. I had a frisée with vinaigrette,croutons and baked fat lard with a poached egg, and the only comment I can give is that it was too much frisée (a curly slightly bitter salad, not sure how that translates).I saw my neighbor had salmon trout on a risotto that looked good as well. Definitely a nice place for brunch on a sunny Sunday. Friendly service (no service charge).

Make a reservation if you can; although the restraint is rather large, it was ill and people were waiting outside for a table. The service is excellent here, but try to bring someone who speaks mandarin with you. The cuisine is your typical southern Chinese food, but there are special dishes like mei fan and frogs legs. It was my first time trying gross legs... they were good though. The texture was almost like fish, but it tasted and looked like chicken... sorta. Idk, you just have to try it! The duck was maybe my favorite dish. Mei fan was interesting.... but I'm not really a fan of Chinese sausages, especially liver sausage. For dessert, we had the fried ice cream and Malay cake. Both were good. The dishes come out one by one, so expect to spend a few hours eating here. They also have a large wine list and don't have a corkage fee. All the tables in our area had wine and they are very accommodating with the glasses. Jade palace is centrally located, relatively cheap parking and great service.

Reliably excellent. Run by two brothers from Hong Kong, serving pretty authentic Cantonese food. Importantly, they haven't over-expanded (only one outlet) so quality is pretty consistent. I've been here quite a few times, recommend the dim sum for lunch and for dinner, the beef brisket and bamboo clams are excellent.Doesn't charge corkage and has proper glassware - hence a regular spot for people who bring their own wine. Good wine selection in-house too as reasonable prices.Likely to come back here many times!

Jade Palace is an interesting dining experience - it boasts a very Asian menu paired with a large selection of European wine. The atmosphere is nothing special - the decor and furniture is dated. However, the food is really what we are here for so let's talk about that :The food was a little hit and miss. The hits were the fried frogs legs ($55) and the durian mochi ($6). The frog legs were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. For a fried dish it was not oily at all and was pleasantly fragrant. The durian mochi had the perfect mochi texture - soft and chewy with a generous serving of fresh durian on the inside. I  would come back on the merits of these two dishes alone. Other honorable mentions included the siew yok and the salted egg squid.Everything else was subpar. If you're having dinner here feel free to skip 1. Soup of the day (bland and boring)2. Century egg (average)3. Fish maw soup (taste was below average and servings of fish maw were fishy and cut into tiny pieces)4. Steamed garoupa (not bad but definitely can get better elsewhere especially for the price)All in all I had a pretty mixed experience given that some dishes were just amazing while some were below average. I would definitely caution everyone to pick from the menu carefully!
Great place for dim sum lunch. And surprisingly good and attentive service..... Hard to get in the weekends, make a reservation ahead of time or bounce! :-)

Had a range of dishes for dinner for 20 people in a private dining room. All the dishes were great, fried tofu, fried pork squares, fried bamboo shoots, succulent scallop and broccoli, delicate chicken and celery, chili Alaskan crab, proven fried rice, sizzling chicken and shallots in oyster sauce, etc.  This is one of my favorite Chinese/seafood restaurant, the set up may not look trendy or ultramodern, but the food is really good and the service is great!

Was here for lunch before and thought it was pretty good.   So finally booked for my mothet-in-law's bday.   Even got a whole peking duck for the occasion.   Unfortunately the duck was just not up to par.  The skin was a little too dark and does not have the crunch.   The wrap that came with the duck was just too doughy and un-refinely done.   What was puzzling is it came with cucumber??!! seriously? Anyway the duck so huge we also had the duck meat fried with scallions.   Also ordered Naibai and gosh it was over cooked and limpy.   Got a $25 a pop sharks fin and for some reason it was orangy in color.   Taste was ok and generous with the fin but unfortunately does not come close to the value u pay.   Beef sauteed with garlic was ok just nothing special.  Mango pudding came without evaporated milk and we have to remind them before they bring it out.   What was most annoying was they are on a 2 shift dinning so they were eager to get u out of the door fast!!  The take away is if you want sub-par food with no cockage this be the place to come.  But if you want quality food and impeccable service wahlok is far better.

It's my dad's new favorite place for Chinese cuisine. In fact, he loves it so much he wants to throw his birthday party here (in a few weeks time). It was packed to the brim the last time I went there. Maybe there's something in this place that I am missing out on? I am indifferent to the food here. Some hits (the usually suspects) and some misses. Nothing out of the ordinary for me. Matches up to most Chinese restaurants I've dined at previously. 1. Sharkfin with crab meat - $25 - Meh. Had better. 2. Peking duck - $38 - LOVE IT!!! I might be biased. Crispy duck skin rolled in a soft-taco like wrap. Add some savory-sweet sauce and throw in spring onions. Simple but amazingly delicious invention. 3. Squid with salted egg yolk - Ok. Ironically, the salted egg was too salty. The squid is a tad bit too oily for my liking. Not very much like the western calamari I had hoped for. 4. Yellow fish (fried) x3 - $30 - I didn't really like it. I felt that the its fishy taste was not musk well and it was presented as a whole fish. No deco. Just a fish staring back at you. Don't get me wrong, I like beef/fish as much as the person but just because I do doesn't mean that I want to see that cow's/fish's face staring back at me... on my plate.  5. Luffa with Fungus - Good. 6. Scallop with fried rice - $39 - Ok. Overpriced though? Not much scallops. Rice for 30+++???7. Daily Soup - Good. A chinese herb based soup but it was savory not bitter  (kinda reminds me of the cantonese soups that my grandmother makes). 8. Mango & Sago - LOVE IT!!! This was so freaking good. A pity the portions were so tiny. It came served in a rock glass. Only 1/4 was filled with the mango goodness. The mango slides were sweet & fresh. 9. Chinese herbal pudding - Good. A tad bit on the bitter side but you have the option of dousing it in honey. 10. Lime Ice cream - Meh. Boring. It's basically a scoop of sobert or ice-cream (I can't remember) soaked in a green color liquid with a few topping of nata de coco. 11. Lamb chop with garlic - $27 - Interesting cooking style. They chose to fry the lamb chops and it was done quite well too. Well marinated but as with most lamb dish it has a distinct lamb smell which I don't really like. Worth a try for those who like lamb. Service - Good Ambiance - Typical chinese restaurant. Very practical :) Nothing fancy. They do have some fish tanks out at the fron though where customers can see where their fresh catch is derived from. Nothing pretty. Just fish tanks.

been here many times for lunch and dinner.always so crowded that it's best to make a reservation.very friendly and efficient service staff.good dim sum.the usual suspects are all of good standards.for starters:excellent cold crab.cooked well and kept at right temperature.vinegar garlic sauce for dipping.kurobuta char siew is fatty and tender.grilled pork collar, nice marbling.pork floss sprinkled on crispy strips of egg plant is yums.crispy squid tentacles, not many places does this well.for mains:kai lan fried with liver and chinese sausages is a must if you cant get their lap mei fan.crunchy stalks of kai lan made ever so tasty with delicious sausage slices.i always ask for a mix of two sausages, as i like the rich liver ones but the normal chinese ones adds sweetness and texture.if the lap mei fan is available order it for a full whack of the different preserved wax meats!for dessert:durian mocchi, real creamy durian meat contained in bite size soft melt in your mouth mocchi.mango pudding with real bits of mango and no artificial taste.p.s. if you need the bathroom, they do have their own located within the restaurant.

From the outside, Jade Palace Seafood Restaurant does not look like much. However, it has a strong following of regulars given its consistently delicious food. The claypot rice, in particular, is one of the best around town IMO. They also have one of the most impressive selection of wines among the Chinese restaurants in town. BYO is also allowed.

CM-PB or Contemporary Melting Pot & Bar lives up to its name as it offers quite a range of dishes, both western and local (fusion) as well as plenty of drinks.  They even have sushi although I haven't tried it yet.  What I have had so far has been decent, but nothing has wowed me.  I've been here 3 times with a group, as it's a fave with my office.  The thin crust pizza is always a good bet for sharing, as is the burrata and prosciutto salad.  The burger is also quite good although at $28, it seems a bit pricey and if you add an egg, then it's $32.  The tomato crab pasta however was not as good as some of the other versions I have had in this town, e.g. latteria mozzarella in Duxton.  The beer selection could also be better - Kronenbourg on draft and a few predictable choices by the bottle didn't win me over.  Overall, it's a nice setting, especially outdoors, and it's a good choice for groups, and perhaps some light bites and basic drinks.  But not really for fine dining or drinks.

Restaurant location is great- in red hot Dempsey area. Food was mediocre; our dessert (mine was date pudding) was tasteless and uninspired. The service is lame- the waitstaff really needs to go through retraining. That bunch of teenagers...wow.

I enjoy sitting al fresco on a cool evening, chilling with friends with a cold beer in hand and good live music (songs from the millennium and my era!). The food here is quite decent - the black pepper crab pasta is quite tasty though might be a bit much if you're eating it on its own. The pizza was quite decent - I liked the wagyu beef with sweet onions and mushrooms, and the calamari and chips with truffle mash also quite yummy.Food is a little bit pricier at about $25++ for mains, but I would come back here again. Free parking at Dempsey (whee!) - there's a larger carpark hidden behind if you can't get any lots at the main carpark, plus I love the ambiance of this place.

I came here looking for more bites after a meal and was tempted into their desserts as well as truffle fries calling out my name. I know it is also a popular place for their drinks (love their mojitos!) and was pleasantly surprised to see that they offer breakfast options too. Mark this down for your next Sunday dining spot.The strawberry shortcake is paired with yuzu in its execution, consisting of a scone like cake infused with yuzu and paired with a raspberry-yuzu sorbet. Very interesting combination of flavours and the sweet and fragrant notes of both fruits paired together worked for me. It's sort of like a twist to the popular strawberry-orange flavours.The truffle fries are really good, I liked that their fries were thicker but not too chunky so you have a good amount of crispy and soft potato inside. The truffle oil was really fragrant and the shaved parmesan cheese added a great salty tinge to the flavours and bite. This one is really good!I've head many more of their dishes way back when they first opened and was impressed. Will go back just to try them all again and properly document them!

CM-PB | Contemporary Melting-Pot Bar, I love the name of this place. It is crafty and humorous at the same time. This place is kinda like a café/bar/bistro that mainly attracts people that are looking to relax, chill out and just have a good time. This restaurant embraces the all-in-one concept, being a great place to bring family for breakfast and branch and even experiencing happy hours last until 9pm with your buddies. For the weekend breakfast, children will have free cereal. The truffle fries are another thing to definitely come for, some say there are even the closest contenders to P.S cafés.This restaurant must be tried out personally; you won't ever get the full taste just by reading reviews, viewing photos, and hearing opinions about. It is all fusion there, you get some really interesting stuff.

I've been here twice, both times on Friday night and it was packed, so a reservation might be wise. Both times I sat outdoors and it has a casual and lively vibe (if at times it felt like it was teeming with slightly too many people). I love the mussels with Parma Ham Cream and my friends are fans of the mussels with Tom Yum. These are the two things we order whenever we go. At $30 for a big pot, we got one each and were left stuffed. There is a live band that plays music inside, and they're pretty decent, so that's a nice accompaniment to dinner. I'd say that because of the noise level and the crowd, it's the kind of place you head to with friends and not a first date.The only cons about the place is that it is slightly on the pricey side, getting a cab is a bitch if you don't drive and it's a little out of the way.Otherwise, if you're looking for somewhere laid-back on a Friday night, this might be an option.

In 2011, I used to frequent CM-PB at least once a week. It's no longer the default hangout of my friends and I, but it still remains one of our favorite places to go to. They serve good and affordable food and drinks without being pretentious and the staff are warm and friendly. What I love most about CM-PB is that it is comfortable for any occasion. We would bring our laptops (free wifi and power plugs!) and work there all day (it's relatively quiet before dinner). It's also good for any meal. My favorite dishes include the black pepper crab aglio olio, wagyu beef chili and lobster and crab "tacos" (note: they are actually dips with nachos). Their waffles and burgers are also popular among my friends. I haven't found any item on the menu that I did not like. It's also great for after dinner drinks. I love their ginger fizz, old fashioned mojitos and lychee mojitos. The bartenders are also very obliging with drink requests. One of my favorite cocktails came out of asking for something with lychee and choya. CM-PB is also a favorite for pre-gaming nights. Umm, our favorite bartender, has given us 10 free shots on more than one of our pre-clubbing stops there. They used to have good live music too (especially when 53A was still playing there). I don't go for the live music anymore but the bands are usually enjoyable. There are huge pluses for being regulars too! CM-PB gave me a massive bag of presents when I was there on my birthday, which included speakers, skin care, a tote bag, and more. Also, CM-PB gives out free soup at around midnight.

Another one of Dempsey's gems, CM-PB is a hip and chic joint that offers decently priced drinks and food for the young and trendy crowd. Surrounded by the lush greenery, CM-PB is a very conducive environment for short getaways from the concrete jungle that is Singapore. The all day breakfast option is decent and much better than the international and local menu and there's a live band performing during happy hours. Depending on your preference, it's much more airy to sit in the al fresco section then to remain cooped up indoors. They also have a complimentary "Soup of the Night", which is a fairly nice touch, as we found out about during our last visit there.
