I'm a little fastidious about this - so everything ended up getting a dip through a bowl of hot tea.we'd return more frequently if the dishes were less oil-slippery, the meat less fatty - as it is, there are cze char places out there with a lighter hand in cooking, and similarly expert flavors. so, this place, I'm going to deem as divisive - I certainly can't begrudge the flavors here, and the cooking style could be right up your alley.reservations definitely needed, and it's a good place for family. if you find eating next to the carpark (with parking cars and the sometimes whiff of exhaust) uninteresting - make sure you let them know when you call.

Plate after plate after plate! Whew! I left here with a food baby! Not only was it packed but the food was phenomenal. Especially the sashimi. We had tempura, shrimp, soup, sushi, sashimi and nigiri. I can't forget sake! We had 3 bottles! What a great experience! We sat at the sushi bar and ate like glutenous kings. Located near the famous Dempsey rd. This place has extremely fresh options and was beautifully prepared.Not so humbly submitted,Michael C.

Had dinner here with a couple of friends on a Friday night, and the bill came up to about $45 per person, after taxes. For a Japanese buffet in Singapore, this is quite cheap!I found the food here surprisingly good, and sashimi here is fresh and thickly sliced. They are not stingy, but you will have to be very specific with your orders. Everything else like tempura and grilled items are the same standard as what you will find at Sushi Tei. For what you pay, really, this place is a bargain. Service is very iffy here, and they are quite under-staffed, but you can't ask for too much when you're not paying top dollar for reasonably acceptable food. Do book in advance because this place gets PACKED! Dinner starts at 8pm, no earlier, no later, and there will be a crowd waiting outside.Would return.

Still $44.73 (or $38++) for the buffet. The food here was as good as any other Jap food I've ever eaten (note though that I'm not a connoisseur and I don't go around eating at Tokyo Michelin restaurants). You go NTUC buy sashimi oso $95 per kg aredi. So if you got big belly, confirm can eat enough to cover the price. Remark: Much less crowded than when I last came in 2013 - possibly because of the recent sashimi scare. Which is good if you are not a typical Hamji-porean, because less crowded means prompter and better service.

Buffet dinner with good friends to celebrate the quick recovery of one of the close friend. Supremely lucky to get a table at such short notice as someone cancelled their reservations. Ikoi has a good spread of yummies as always. You know this because on a Tues night, the restaurant is PACKED!Ate too much food and loved these very much: 1) Chawanmushi - for a buffet item, it really good. It's got a good size piece of chicken and half a crabstick. The egg is soft and tasty too. As good as the ones I make at home. 2) Fried Fishcake with Cheese - its really the normal Fishcake with a hole in the middle and the melted cheese together with the fried-ness. Nice! 3) Salmon Sashimi - generous, fresh thick slices of salmon yummies. You order by the slices so that awesome! 4) Teriyaki Salmon - they grill the salmon pieces till nicely charred on the edges and the thick teriyaki sauce is a great accompaniment for the taste. There were many dishes I enjoyed but I couldn't remembered exactly how much I have eaten. It worked out to be about $40 per pax and it's $40 well spent!
Great quality Sashimi even though it's a buffet. One of the best Japanese buffets in Singapore

The number one gripe I have about Ikoi is that it appears too run down! And it's always packed! But if that doesn't bother you, then you're in for a good time, especially if you're a sashimi lover! Think free flow of swordfish, salmon, yellowtail, tuna, snapper and octopus. That's the reason why this place is always packed. You definitely get your money's worth from this buffet. There's a wide range and Japanese dishes with the glaring omission of unagi which is surprising. You can skip the rest of the filler dishes like fried chicken wings and focus on the important stuff - sashimi. And for the prices they charge, its really a steal!

This is a great japanese buffet to enjoy with a big group of friends. You order your food with the wait staff - and you tend to get carried away ordering for a buffet - sharing the load of stuff you ordered with your friends is one of the best things ever. For less than $40, you can get free flow of your favourite sashimis (mine is swordfish and salmon), tempura, tofu dishes, fried rice, soba noodles, and best of all Shishamo (or some would call 'pregnant fish'). You can't get shishamo at your regular sakae sushi outlets so when you find it at a buffet, it's hard to restrain yourself from ordering a dozen of it to share with the table!Like others say, this is a very busy place, always packed so make sure to book way in advance, you won't regret it!

I think one has to keep in mind the price paid for a verdict of Ikoi. With tax and service charges all in, you usually pay under $50 and for that amount, I think Ikoi is pretty stellar.This place is always packed so don't stroll in and expect a seat - give them a ring a week earlier to arrange a booking. This buffet is a-la-carte style and the variety is decent enough for you to be a little bewildered about what to order. A must-try (over and again) is the sashimi. Salmon, yellow-tail, tuna, octopus, hamachi - eat your fill. The tempura is also well-done with a light batter coating fresh vegetables and crunchy prawns.What I like about the vibe of this restaurant is how it isn't too posh looking - the interior is modest but exudes a nice sense of familiarity. Space is a little tight but the hustle and bustle about is actually what adds to the experience.

Had their Japanese buffet lunch for $35 a pax. Given the huge number of Mediacorp celebrities that have apparently endorsed this restaurant, I was expecting something extraordinary. The restuarant itself had a humble feel to it - nothing too formal. It does a good job of recreating the traditional Japanese restaraunt atmosphere - for the seats on the side, you can even take off your shoes to sit cross-legged, Japanese style. Even the Wordart emblazoned on the menus can be nicely disarming - a nice, if unintentional touch. Sashimi was great and came in many varieties. I enjoyed the salmon, although the tuna itself was not that fresh (neither does it give the choice of parts). Compared to other Japanese buffets I've had, however, I found the variety lacking. They did not have the assorted vegetable tempura, not the baked scallops or bacon rolls I've been spoilt by. Nonetheless, the dishes they did have - chawanmushi, karage chicken, shishamo and tempura - did not dissappoint. Come here for a good meal, but leave your expectations at the door.

Ikoi Japanese restaurant is one of the few a la carte Japanese buffet restaurants in Singapore. It is highly popular, with reservations having to be made 2 weeks in advance in order to dine in Ikoi. Walk-ins are difficult to fulfill as they are usually full house. Even if walk-ins are accepted, one might be allocated counter seats which are not very conducive for over the dinner chatter.At $33++, Ikoi is one of the better Japanese buffets for it's excellent quality. Sashimi is fresh and the tempura are fried well. One of my favorites that is quite well done is the grilled shishamo and tebasaki (chicken midwing joint). In large groups of more than 8 people, customers will be able to dine in a private room with waitresses waiting to take your orders. The menu also comes in at an astounding 80+ items.Overall, I would describe it as a pleasant setting with good food. While not all the items on the menu are of the best standards (I don't expect them to specialize in every dish), all dishes are of good standards. Protip: Call and make a reservation at least 2 weeks before the lunch/dinner appointment. It is that popular!P.S. Parking will be in the underground carpark in Hotel Miramar.

While waiting for my friend to be done with work, decided to come here as her office was located opposite this store.Came here the second time before writing in this review. The first time I came, I had savory bread - Bacon Focaccia. It looked good on the display section and it was even better after they used the oven to heat it up. It was also filling and I just had one piece of that for dinner. When I was about to leave, I bought the lemon meringue. It wasn't as good as I thought it will be as I consumed it hours later. The second time I came, I had the Raspberry Croissant. The server also heat it up before serving. I asked for a to go bag (brown bag) so that I am able to taste the croissant in bites instead of using fork and knife. The raspberry filling was so amazing. On top of the croissant there were powdered sugar and almond which made it sweet and crunchy. The texture of the flakes was just done perfectly. Service was excellent. The servers will repeat the order of what you are getting one more time for accuracy. They also greet you upon entering this cafe. Every time I come here, people also started to rush inside here to buy other kinds of breads or pastries. They also serve main courses as well as soups. Definitely a good place to hang out during the rainy days or during tea time. Will be back for more soon :)

I was staying down the road and craving some food in the evening, but I felt too lazy to walk far or actually sit down at a restaurant, so I happened upon Bread & Hearth. I had asked for something that they didn't have because it was so close to closing time, so I chose a ham and cheese bread and a focaccia instead. They were delicious! They warmed up the food for me to take back to my hotel, and I also got a free croissant because I had bought 2 breads. Everything was absolutely delicious and the service was prompt and friendly.

Small cafe that bakes a wide variety of bread every day. I tried the croissant  (plain), the baguette, and an Americano. All were tasty, but I would say the baguette was most impressive especially because I had it when it had just come out of the oven  (still warm)! Seating here is limited and the tables and stools are small. Best for solo or duo seating.  Terrible place to come with a large group.The employees were very friendly and helpful and I liked their music selection too. Would come back again next time I'm in the area!

Almond croissant ($3.50) - 2.5 starsI suppose I was eating it right after lunch... But honestly it was nothing special - not much almond filling. They even warmed it up. Probably wouldn't get it again.Ambience - 3 starsClean but tables are small. I got my croissant to go.
Lovely bakery. I'm definitely smitten by their pain au chocolate. Sandwiches are decent, burger is overrated. The show stoppers are what they pull out of the oven.

This is a nice little pastry shop in Chinatown. After something for breakfast, we wandered in to see lots of different types of pastries and bread. I chose to have the croque Monsieur which was pre made and they warmed up. This was really nice and tasty. The coffee was a bit too much for me (and I like strong coffee) so after a few sips I left the rest. Friendly staff and great food.

Raspberry croissant is buttery, crunchy and not too sweet with the light raspberry filling. I thought it was delicious. You can smell the baked goods from a few steps away. The place is small and cozy, does have a feel of a bakery with tables so it's easy to grab a fresh pastry or bread with a coffee and enjoy the ambiance in air con.

You have my heart at baked anything, and i can never say no to freshly baked breads, pastries, cakes, you name it. It's the smell of butter and sugar probably, both of which i cannot resist and that resulted in a shopping spree when i stumbled into Bread and Hearth, a new artisanal bakery in the Keong Saik/ Chinatown/ Ann Siang area. Bread and Hearth prides themselves with using pure butter and quality ingredient. There is absolutely no shortening used, as highlighted by the friendly staff. French Normandy butter and flour goes into making these quality pastries.The Matcha Orange is a bread roll with a nice matcha fragrance and the flavor is lifted by the refreshing chunky orange peel. The Honey Chocolate bread ($3) was porous and very bouncy. Even though it said Honey Chocolat, it wasn't sweet at all and it actually had a salty taste. That said, i still like how it was flavored nicely with the dark chocolate chip bits. Do add some honey to it after you toast it. I swear it's divine.The Bacon Focaccia ($6.50) is exactly that kinda bread that i'd want for a breakfast. The fragrance was taunting me during work the whole afternoon and i finally succumbed to my weakness and took several bites and boy was it satisfying. It's the perfect savory snack. I would eat the foccacia even if it didn't have bacon on it. The Cream Cheese Sesame ($2.80) turned out to be a sweet treat instead of a savory one! Think dense creamy cheese with a nice sweet pastry crust peppered with smokey sesame seeds. Yummy! Another must try is the Bostock which is more than 50% cake i swear. Bread and Hearth also does sandwiches and coffee and they do have a nice enough spot for lunch/tea.

Cute little bakery that has all sorts of pastries and sandwiches.  I had a very good croissant sandwich and vanilla latte - it was teeny tiny and coat $7 but I enjoyed it and bought another a few days later.

I have only tried the almond croissant, sliced bread and latte here but this three items have won me over! I cannot wait to try the other pastries at bread and hearth. And a bonus, the staff here are super helpful and nice!

Haven't been here for years.My Husband recommended to the then Editor of Makansutra years ago. Then they received 3 chopsticks and became so popular that when we went one day, the soup was not hot. Turned us off and never went back for years.It's gone upmarket in price. Used to be about $8 for a deluxe bowl. Today big prawns with 2 small whole Australian abalone is $15 per bowl. I prefer the good old days when the abalone was sliced. Hard to bite through a thick abalone. Still good but I don't think the soup is as good as it was years ago. Not as thick. It is strictly self-service even though she only had one bowl to serve at 3 p.m. It's good but no longer a die die must eat to me.

Saw my friend post about this place on Facebook so I brought my parents here for lunch on a Saturday. Good thing we got here a little before 2pm. I didn't know that they sell out of stuff. When we got there they only had 3 items on the menu left. We ordered the prawn with scallop and the prawn with pig tail for $6 each. You place your order, get a number and wait for your number to be called to collect your noodles. The noodles really didn't disappoint. I got the dry kway teow mee. Both the noodles and broth were delicious. The downside for me was the location, it's a little hard to get to where I live. It was also raining heavily the day we came here. You're pretty much trapped if you're caught without an umbrella. But definitely worth making a trip!
Been here many times my overseas friend love it he can it 2 bowls as for me I think is too crowded and hot and over price but their service is good and orderly queue number I like it.

I've been going to this store for about a decade. My family loves to eat black chicken/turtle soup at nearby Ser Seng, which I was not a big fan of. I took a walk once, found this stall, and just fell in love with it.I'm not a big fan of soup, especially noodles in soup (with the exception of ramen), so I always go for the dry version here. I like heavy food and tbh, the noodles here is very greasy, oily, saucy and combine it with the fried onion that soaks up all of that, it's the perfect recipe for a guilty pleasure. I also get the pig's tail, intestine and ribs alongside my prawn. CHOLESTEROL LEVEL OVER 9000!!!On a bad side note though, I noticed that their quality dropped a level or two during my last visit. I haven't been there for some time, and was looking forward to some good prawn mee but was left disappointed. I hope it was just a blip and I'll definitely go again.A tip: The uncle that cooks at night uses more sauce/oil/spice than the auntie who cooks in the afternoon. And this place opens up till late, a great supper spot!

Was brought here by my boss when I was still working in the Ubi vicinity. The whole company used to troop out for a prawn mee fix once every two weeks - or, every time someone's craving got the better of that.I always think the soup is really pretty much what determines if the prawn noodles will be good. Here the broth is obviously created from good stock that has been painstakingly brewed for hours. The prawns are always fresh (and huge) with that nice crunch that comes with being well-cooked. Add on their signature chilli powder for spiciness with a slight hint of garlic.The only issue I have is with the lunchtime crowd. Pick a less common hour to enjoy and to avoid standing in the torturous sun, ready to pounce on the next available seat
I hope that I have come on a bad day because in terms of soup, this is no better than any 3.50 in any coffee shop. Soup was diluted and salty . No way i will pay 5.50 for such standard.

This is one of the most popular prawn noodle places in town. For $4, you get 3 deshelled but head-on prawns which is certainly a joy to those who hate peeling their prawns.  The prawns were indeed fresh, but it is about the same quality as the half-sliced prawns you get ordinarily at prawn stores - so don't expect the prawn quality to be on par with those prawns fresh out of the net. The noodles was not bad, quite a nice texture - delicious but not fantastic. The chilli sauce lacks punch and could be slightly more salty. The best part of this store is that it opens 24 hours a day!

I was extremely excited to try a Spanish Tapas Bar in Singapore to reminisce on my amazing experience in Barcelona, Spain. Obviously I knew that the experience and food wouldn't be the same or as authentic, and probably a bit overpriced because Octapas is located in the tourist central of Clarke Quay. First off, we made a reservation for a Wednesday night dinner for our friend's birthday. They accidentally gave away our table inside where the live music played (which was not good music anyways) and shifted us outside. At least it was shaded and not too hot outside. We ordered a few tapas and a paella that supposedly fed 4 people. Throughout the course of our dining experience with Octapas, our party progressively became more and more dissatisfied.My extremely small plate of S$12 Champinones al Ajilo (Mushrooms with Garlic) was drenched in oil and salt. I had to chug my entire cup of water while eating it. And, when I asked for more water - it took forever to get the waiter's attention and we had to ask repeatedly (3 times) to get my refill. And, our bland Valenciana (Meat & Seafood) Paella was $60 and finally came after about 45-50 minutes. This dish is supposed to serve 4 people, but it was extremely small, overcooked, and had an awful cardboard taste. There wasn't much meat (chorizos) or seafood either!  Also, our $15 Caipirinha cocktails were extremely sweet and barely had any alcohol in it.  Save your time and money by going somewhere else! I would've rather eaten snacks or a Bao at 7-Eleven.

Octapas is a cleverly named tapas bar on the bank of the historical Singapore River, along Clarke Quay. Right next to the Read Bridge (pre-party central), Octapas offers indoor as well as outdoor seating to its patrons. Most nights, live music can be found at this quaint yet vibrant joint, and you can sip an ice cold beverage of your choice as you watch tourist-laden bumboats float by. The menu offers simple Spanish fare, some items more traditional than others, but all of it tasty and satisfying. They also have a happy hour, for those who want to eat out on the cheap - always a bonus in my book! Service can be hit or miss, which is unfortunate, but not uncommon in such touristy areas. Though in my opinion, the food is well worth the occasional frosty waitress. Try the garlic bread, chorizo, meatballs, bacon wrapped prawns, chicken in cream sauce, and croquettes.Buen provecho!

Incredibly nice location and some very good food options and choices for the vegetarians too!! Service is decent and a seat by the water front just does it!! I will surely go back here again sometime with friends

Every time I go running along the marina, I see Octapas.  It's cute sign, clever name, and location are all so alluring that we decided to check it out.  First disappointment, the menu.  It is not tapas.  None of our favorite spanish tapas: bacon wrapped dates, cheese stuffed peppers, etc. were on the menu.  We should have left at this point, but we didn't.Second disappointment, the disco ball that started up immediately after we placed our order.  We were in the mood for something casual and low key, and did not anticipate the disco ball which felt so NOT Spanish (albeit fitting for Clark Quay).Third disappointment, the food.  It was just not good.Lastly, everyone else mentioned, service is terrible.I was literally angry by the time we left.  Poor food, poor ambiance, poor service.  Why waste your money?

Honestly, there are much better options in Clark Quay other than this one.I went with my friend to have a girl's night out. We ordered Paella to share and we were told that we have to wait for 30 mins so the waitress recommended that we order tapas as well. As we are already starving, we ordered beef and calamares. Lo and behold, paella came like 10 mins later. While we were eating, the waitress came over and told us that they need to send back the paella as this was for the other table (good for 4) and not for 2.Ok, so they take back the paella to the kitchen to do what again? Add more and serve to another table? And then she came back and said its okay like we owe her. I wanted to call the manager and talk to them about this unacceptable quality of service but was there to catch up and spend quality time with a friend so I didn't bother anymore.We ended up paying $120 for a mediocre food and utterly lousy service.Really not worth it!

I went with a group of five and we were seated at the one table large enough to accommodate us. This is a nice place for a traveling group, since the tapas format allows for the sharing of several small dishes. We shared the chorizo, garlic shrimp, garlic bread, vegetable bruschetta, and paella. The vegetable bruschetta and chorizo were the best dishes. The paella was mediocre and needed a lot more spice. The portion sizes were appropriate. They also served good mixed drinks, such as a mojito. There was also a live band setting up, which began playing towards the end of the meal. Thankfully, it consisted of a pleasant soft female singer rather than the rowdy ear-destroying over-amped guitar music that typical bar bands chuck at diners.

We came here during happy hour to refresh ourselves from the outside swelter. Half off Sangrias were tasty and affordable.We got the shrimp tapas which were amazing and came in a metal dish of olive oil and garlic. Tasted great but is also twice what you would pay for comparable tapas in the states and seemed an expensive food option compared to other area foods. Although I give the food and drinks top marks I found it overpriced.
food is ok, taste is ok - even hot dishes are not hot. Service was good, spend 130$ for a wine and some tapas

I am going to keep this short and simple.*Awful array of dishes*Awful setting which is not appropriate for children(Personal opinion)*Awful,sluty and unskilled waiters*Awful waiting times*Awful food compared to the extremely steep price

Love the food and excellent service. Fusion of Italian and Malay traditional taste. They say you can judge how a good a place is by its salad; and here...the salad is perfect!Place can be a little cramp but service is prompt.

This is a value-for money food joint that serves fusion western makan with good taste. We had* Ayam Bakar - which to me is essentially fancy satay on a plate. It has the raw onions (slices), ketupat (cut into smaller pieces and satay sauce spooned over the meat. I found the sauce a tad too sweet and the chicken chunks not as tender as I would like it. Not bad but not a dish I would order again. * Arrabiatta Prawn Pasta - I originally wanted marinara sauce with Chilli padi. The lady at the counter looked at me funny and asked, "So you want Arrabiatta sauce yah?" Heh, I trusted her and yes, it was spicy tomato sauce. I found the pasta a tad TOO al dente but the prawns were large and fresh and beautifully grilled! Very happy with the pasta overall. * Truffle Fries - daughter insisted on having this and the serving is a large serving of hand cut fries with generous mix of truffle bits and slices to give the whole pot of fries adequate taste. * T-Jar - their version of tiramisu. Theirs is not with sponge cake but a denser chocolate cake. The jar is a pretty substantial size and one jar was enough for my family of 3. They have other very tempting mains that I don't have enough stomach space for which I wanna try the next time. The

Love this halal Eatery at Bali Lane. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the food served were very good. The only dish we didn't quite take to was the ribeye steak as the garlic butter affected the taste of the beef.

This kind of place reminds me of saveur, good quality food for a cheap price. Why a 3 star? Well there are small things that overall lowered the experience a bit. First the tables are awful. They are very light and wobbly which makes you feel like your eating during an earthquake. Add to the fact that the tables are really dirty. Maybe I'm ocd but there is a good portion of dust and food crumbs accumulated on the second bar. Then the water I was given had some kind of food crumb floating around. HmmmmOn the food, the ayam bakar is nice but they serve it with cold cubes of compressed tasteless rice(ok I suppose this is the traditional way to make but don't like). It's better to just leave that out. The cremoso which is a carbonara says there is egg yolk. When we asked the waiter he didn't see understand what we are asking which is if it's mixed in the sauce. He took the dish and returned with the same dish. Some places have the egg yolk on top(Concetto). It's good. It's very good. But actually Concetto does it better. You order and pay at the counter which is ok since they don't charge gst and service fees. I still think I would return back to try other things. I hope the venue is upgraded by then.

A new cafe opened just last month, 'Krave Cafe' is definitely a place to reckon with! Small yet cozy, it fits around 9 small tables. Apparently run by a local celebrity Chef Sufiyan and friend, Chef Helmi. Both the chefs were there when we lunched in. Honestly, I could not recognise their faces since admittedly, I do not follow Malay celebrities/shows. Sorry, chefs! It was my colleague who pointed them out. I'm impressed that they were quite friendly. Coming to the food, I must say, whatever I've tasted were just tip-top fabulous! It was my colleague's 2nd time dining there and she insisted that I try that place out. The place was quite full when we reached there. What impressed me next was how fast we were served. Noted that none of us ordered a big course meal, since we just ordered some fried snacks and desserts. We ordered the Chempedak Creme Brulee, Mars Attack and the fried Otah-Tah. The creme brulee was nice. Each serving has one chunk of Chempedak flesh inside. I just thought that it would have tasted even better if it was sweeter. But my colleague thought it was just right. *shrugs* To each their own, eh? 'Mars Attack' was served in a cup of halved bars of Mars chocolates, battered and dipped fried, served with vanilla ice-cream. Nice! I liked it. Too bad they didn't do it with Snickers bars instead. Always preferred those to Mars. Coming to the Otah-Tah... bloody hell! On my first bite, I finally understood why I was coerced into coming to this place. They were marvelous! For you locals, you know what 'Otah-Otah' is, no? Well, these were dipped in a specially seasoned batter and fried to perfection. I was hooked. They served them with a small serving of mayonnaise. You can easily ask for chili sauce if you prefer that instead.All I can say is that next time, I will definitely not refuse an invite to this cafe again.

The chicken rice is very good, maybe comparable to Tian Tian. We had 1.5 chicken, a fishhead claypot, tofu claypot, pork chop, kangkong, sweet potato leaves. Very satisfied group of 13 people.The portion is decent, the service is quick. The servers is the usual coffeeshop standards but they serve good food at great value.

I prefer the chicken rice here when in this area, maybe because it serves roast chicken. The pricing (I think $4 for individual serve) is similar to those at food court but the portion is way bigger as it comes in 2 layers of meat on a plate. You get a miserly amount in food court. The chicken is flavorful and the breast meat is not that dry. The chili sauce is quite spicy so go sparingly on it. The grated ginger sauce is just ginger with no scallions or chopped green onions in it. The service is typical of coffee shop - efficient and brusque. There are other dishes available but I have yet to try any.

I've been here several times over the past decade yet I've never had the Hainanese pork chop. Big mistake! It was so tasty we ordered a second serving! Besides the pork chop, we also had the chicken rice, eggplant with salted fish, kailan and hei zhor (minced meat roll). They were good but not outstanding to specially return. The bill came to about $50 for 4 persons.

Situated along the shop houses of Purvis Street, Chin Chin Eating House facade is one of the most humble looking among her neighbouring modern eateries. Astounded by the crowd during dinner time, we walked into the eating place and tried to grab a seat. Lo and behold, there was a table for 2, just nice!Besides having good pork chop, they do sell Haianese Chicken Rice, Claypot Mutton Soup which I believe had been drawing the hordes thus its full house on a saturday night. The restaurant interior was simple and decent with hanging ceiling fans at each sector above. Chinese Lanterns were seen hanging from the florescent lights too.Haianese Pork Chop, being one of its Must Try on their Menu had been awarded for its Best Food for 2011 and 2012.It's not quite frequent we come across this dish on the menu moreover it had won the award. Having prepared similar dish, I would say that it was quite good but not really what I would expected. The dish was served with few pototoes wedes and boiled green peas with a bowl of tomato gravy.The piece of lean meat was fried to golden brown with crumbs coated evenly at its exterior. It was cut into smaller portions equally and was served.Braised Ee Mee tasted better than average. It's black braised sauce was aromatic and noodles was generously drenched, a little more would have the gravy overflowed.Having tried only 2 dishes, I would definitely be back for more when chance come!Total amount spend for 2 with drinks: $30

This seems like a popular place and got good ratings so we brought our visitor here.  The chicken is pretty good, but I also can't say it's a lot better than any of the other equally well known chicken rice places.  Personally I prefer the chicken rice at Tian Tian or Boon Tong Kee but I have not tried the roast chicken though so perhaps that's better?One of their signature dishes is the Hainanese pork chop but I found that to be just ok - the meat is a bit dry and I prefer it to be thicker and more succulent.  Other dishes like stir fried kangkung are ok but nothing special.  Prices are pretty cheap so definitely a good value for money.
Very Very good...I love the garlic chili and crushed ginger on the table. Great food...but not cheap.
Came all the way for the chicken rice and mutton soup but the mutton soup was already sold out. First time here and it was really one of the best chicken rice I've had. Would definitely come back!!

The Hainanese chicken rice is deliciuous, which is better than Yet Con (tho my fav is still Tian Tian :P) Half a chicken is good for 2 person. And each of us ordered a dish of chicken oil rice, which is lovely too. However, the Hainanese veggie is so-so, too watery and salty.

Best items were the chicken rice and the hainanese pork chop (like Japanese pork cutlet). Other items I did not care for. Make your own dipping sauce before meal begins. Bring your own napkins and wet wipes as there are none at this economy restaurant.

Chin Chin Eating House has been my go-to place for fast and convenient zichar and chicken rice since young. This place is what a zichar place is like - hot, crowded, noisy and big tables with lazy susans in their middle. A typical local eatery with no airs about it and where people can just come and have a good meal at any time of the day.Other than the chicken rice and chicken that are must-trys, I will recommend their pork chop and chap chye. If you are a tourist and want to try local food, get out of Raffles Hotel and walk one street down to Chin Chin Eating House!

Tried this place several months ago and made a point of returning because it was so good. Not sure why chicken rice isn't on their (rather extensive) menu, but that's the dish to get. Perfect tenderness and flavor, a great broth to accompany it, and the chili/ginger are so good that I get an upset stomach every time (in the best way possible - watch your spice levels, people). Right up there with Tian Tian at Maxwell.
OK food. Terrible service. No one could speak Engilsh, the wait staff ignored people they thought couldn't speak Chinese. Never going again.

Purvis street used to house many European families which had Hainanese chefs working for them so I'm not surprised that it is a known haunt for the best Hainanese food in town.Get the Hainanese pork chops - sweet ketchup sauce drenching crispy pork cutlet is the ultimate comfort food that reminds one of childhood meals by the grandmother. I even like that crinkle-cut fries are stir-fried into the dish too. Super old school!I've yet to try more Hainanese dishes from here but it is a safe bet if you're looking to go good old traditional!

Along the stretch of shophouse restaurants at Purvis Street, this stall has old chicken rice seller Yet Con Restaurant to compete with, but Chin Chin Eating House has nothing to worry about. In a traditional local coffee shop setting, Chin Chin Eating House sure looks like it goes way back. Studying in a nearby school, Chin Chin is an eating haunt for my friends and I. The dishes that we regularly order include chicken rice, Hainanese pork chops, Hainanese chap chye and claypot beancurd. The chicken rice has an authentic taste to it, and the chicken is blanched in cold water after cooking, making the skin smooth and the texture of the meat tender. Afterwhich, the chicken is served in a flavorful and aromatic sauce. The Hainanese pork chops here are passable but if you want a better version, try the one at Yet Con just across the street.My favorite dish at Chin Chin has to be the Chap Chye. The vegetables are fresh and crunchy and the sauce is the deal breaker. The sauce has a special oomph to it, which is provided by the dried cuttlefish strips I guess.

They've gone from dingy hole in the wall to a comfy, contemporary, casual eatery. But the food is consistently good and reasonably priced. The Henghwa cuisine boasts a lot of seafood so anything with seafood is a must try. The drunken cockles are the bomb - literally and metaphorically. It's loaded with garlic so if you're on a date and feeling dainty this ain't a dish to order. I love the lor mee and the noodles - the broth for the lor mee is tasty from the lard and shallots, with a super silky, decadent mouth feel. the noodles are loaded with clams and pork belly, delish. The braised bittergourd is another winner although I wish they'd remove the seeds - it's not so elegant to be spitting out seeds in a restaurant. Another of my favs is the stuffed pig intestine where the intestine is folded in on itself and braised to tender savoury perfection.

After this eatery near me got a Michelin star, I just had to come for lunch, given I live super close by this place!I had the pork intestines, fried yam (taro), garlic cockles, and the lor mee. The pork intestines came with a heating underneath, which continues to cook them as you eat, and while they were really interesting and dare I say, intricate (they were rolled into each other, making a very compressed intestine "sausage" of sorts), they could have been cooked a bit longer, to make them softer. They were however, well-cleaned and tasty still.The garlic cockles were absolutely delicious. They were not as raw as I expected them to be, with the sharpness of the garlic gone, yet still raw and delicious (what sorcery is this?). I polished them off in minutes!The star dish has to be the fried taro. So simple, yet difficult to execute. The taro is specially sourced from somewhere (my memory evades me), and is powdery (not crunchy), and each morsel is coated with a thin, crispy layer of sugar that crunches. Just the thought of it makes my mouth water...The lor mee, I am not a fan of. It was plain and while I think the sweetness of the seafood (clams, prawns etc) was meant to shine through, I had to flavor it with copious amounts of their in-house chilli (very delicious btw). I don't think noodles should be drowned in excessive amounts of chilli, delicious as it may be. That's definitely a pass for me.Would I come back? Absolutely.

Lured by the Michelin star sparkle and desire for great Chinese food, myself and a few Chinese friends visited Pu Tien. We opted for the set menu for four - sure, a tired uninspiring choice - with the taro on the side.After resisting an aggressive up sell to order more courses, the fantastic starters (radish was fantastic) arrived. The tofu soup was fantastic - the broth was rich and delicious. The taro was curious - a tough crunchy exterior, but near melt in the mouth texture. On the downside, the fried pork was the same you'd find in any Chinese place. The Yellow Croaker and Lor Mee were not bad - but nothing special. Overall, the meal and service were pleasant. Maybe we ordered badly and maybe the (well advertised) Michelin star created high expectations. But hey, a good evening - although I wont rush back.

This is an elegant place to have a family meal. They hv free valet service so don't worry about parking. The staff are helpful and friendly. The menu is extensive. You will not be able to try everything in one seating. I can't think of any dish that's not delicious.

Pu Tien sells quite a few dishes that are actually pretty unique.. and being Chinese myself, I thought I have already seen nearly all the Chinese dishes there are to see. Boy, I was so wrong when I came here to eat. I expected the usual prawns, sweet and sour pork and all that but here.... I have never ever heard of these dishes before. It was a real eye opener. I like Pu Tien's snacks.. instead of giving us braised peanuts to munch on while waiting for the dishes to be served, we got some kind of awesome fried seaweed thingie with another dish of preserved chilled vegetables (I am so sorry, I really have NO idea what these dishes are called...) When the main dishes arrive, they may look "HUH?" but they are delicious. The only dish out of all of them that I can name are the fried fish which my grandma cooks at home. The rest, I'll be struggling to tell you what they are named, but if you order it and I happen to be at the table, I'll be able to yell out "OHHH THAT ONE IS DELICIOUS." So do pop by Pu Tien and try out their food, it's really quite different from the other chinese restaurants.

The mothership is purportedly the best of all the branches, and I agree. But taking into consideration the horrendous traffic and parking woes of this Kitchener Road original, I'd much rather head to the town-based branches for convenience.The secret to loving Putien's brand of humble, peasant fare lies with their awesome chilli sauce, which goes with just about everything. It's really where the magic is, and no wonder Putien now bottles this for sale in the open market.We had:1) Steamed Live Seabass ($39.20 for 800 gm at $4.90 per 100gm): done perfectly, with soft flaky flesh complemented by the delicate soy sauce.2) Homemade Beancurd ($9.90) with wobbly strips of silky beancurd, black mushrooms, sugar snap peas, and carrots, swimming in a sumptuous oyster sauce gravy: simple and comforting. A must-try here.3) Stewed Spinach in Superior Stock ($12.90) flecked with century and salted egg: mild and creamy. 4) Seaweed with Beancurd and Crabmeat Thick Soup ($13.90): wonderfully nuanced and balanced. A must-try.  5) Fried Heng Hwa Bee Hoon ($8.90): infused with a collagen-rich stock of pork bone and old hens' bones, and dappled with clams, prawns, pork belly, beancurd, mushrooms, cabbage, kailan, and seaweed. Scrumptious with oodles of that awesome chilli sauce. A must-try.6) Mazu Mee Sua ($8.90) - done in the style of their lor mee, and simmered in a milky pork bone broth, with pork belly, clams and prawns, eggs, mushrooms, snow peas, seaweed, and peanuts: After growing up eating mee sua exclusively as 'sick-food', I much rather have the lor mee instea

One of my neighborhood favorites. My go-to dish here is the baby kailan with bean curd skin, which is both healthy and tasty. They also make these delicious shredded pork buns. The pork comes sautéed in a sweet sauce with onions, and is served with these fantastic toasty sesame buns that I think are actually deep fried. They're kind of like donuts that you slice open and stuff with the shredded pork. As a nice added touch, they give you a pair of thin plastic gloves with these so you don't get your fingers all greasy in the process.Definitely also try their spice mum, a homemade chili sauce that is really fresh and spicy. It goes great with everything and they sell it by the jar, so a lot of our friends and relatives back in the U.S. demand this whenever we make a trip home.

Have been coming here for family meals for more than 6 years and in this span of time they have struck gold and managed to expand considerably. Now you can get your fix of Pu Tien at many other shopping malls (of which I am not too sure of because I stay loyal to this outlet). The specialty here is in Heng Hwa cuisine which obviously got me a little befuddled when I first heard of it because it is not all that common in Singapore. Heng Hwa cuisine originates from Fujian in China which intrigued me because I am teochew by descent and that means my grandparents came from Fujian too. Okay, never mind, that was a confusing digression.The thing I like about Heng Hwa cuisine is that it is similar to Teochew food in that it is light and flavourful. Here are a couple of things you should try at Putien (though most of the menu is well up to standard). The drunken cockles topped with the sharp taste of garlic and wine marinade makes a good start to a meal. Have the flavourful and soft braised intestines if you aren't irked by entrails. Sweet bamboo herb prawns will also make an excellently succulent choice. And of course, your Heng Hwa meal will not be complete without a plate of stir-fried mee sua that will give you a good load of carbs without being overly filling.

The flagship Pu Tien in Little India was originally a scruffy little no-name place. Discovering it at the time was like landing on a pot of gold. It was cheap and very good, with Chinese favourites that are at once familiar and interesting (because it specializes in Heng Hwa cuisine, which has that effect on me where I know it but not really because I'm also part Fujianese but not Henghwa).I'm happy to say that even after expanding like crazy -- it now has branches all over Singapore and even in Malaysia -- the food is still good. The prices have gone slightly more upmarket too, along with the decor. The decor clearly aspires towards one of the higher end Chinese restaurant empires. But the food and service are still down-home good. I like the homemade beancurd, all the seafood dishes (esp the clams and bamboo prawns). The lor mee and mee sua are very good too. When the season is right and they have razor clams, you must order it.

This place is affordable and has a very nice setting. The prawns here are juicy and succulent. And the vegetables and typical dishes you added had a very local/homecooked flavour about it. The Pu Tien Chi fun or lor mee are great staples to have. Do also try the Bamboo Herbal prawns. The Celery Tofu soup tastes great and refreshing too, normally I hate celeries, but the celery in this soup is so well-cooked that the raw taste of it is gone. They have set menus at $168++ for 4, which is rather value for money since they provide premium seafood such as abalone. If you would like something more affordable, there's the set at $108++ and includes steamed sea bass and deep fried pork ribs. My aunts and uncles who are very traditional swear by this place, and I agree with their choice.

Senmi is a sashimi/sushi joint.We ordered California lobster roll and sashimi on rice.Both were good for the price but price for large Asahi was $9. Too much?Order through i-Pad at each table. Human servers.Service was efficient and polite.I'd come back again.

Blech... I expected more from a sushi place in a Japanese specialty store, I should have known by the fact that the place was very quiet on a Friday night.On a positive note: I was seated immediately and ordering through the ipad system was easy. The food was served almost instantaneously so it was good for the quick bite I was looking for.Unfortunately I was also looking for something tasty and the quality of the sushi was below par. The sushi in my neighbourhood supermarket is of better quality quite honestly.The only thing which makes me not give it a lower rating is that some of the offerings on the menu looked quite inventive and were not your average sushi, but the fact that I walked past Sushi Express (who serve 2$ sushi) on my way back and regretted not going there says enough!

Did an uber takeout with senmi sushi, Chirashi Don ($20.81) and Flamed Salmon Salad ($8.61) to be exact. The sashimi pieces were chunky and fresh, so was their rice lol. Would give a 3 half star for their dons, though did expect something more  judging from the number of stars and reviews they've gotten on Google. Flamed salmon salad (soury) was nice too, but isn't something uniquely different from other restaurants. Delivery and preparation was relatively fast around 30-35 minutes.

3.5 Decent sushi restaurant located inside the Emporium Shokuhin market! Japanese sushi restaurants in Singapore are either decently priced and so low in quality that you'd rather not eat it, or super expensive and awesome. except that the super expensive restaurants import the fish directly from Japan (and proudly boast about it) which D and I freak out and avoid at all costs...  so we've been looking for decent sushi places to eat on a normal day out. and Senmi sushi satisfies just that. Senmi sushi is not cheap, yet not so expensive, at around $19 each for chirashi and rolls- and the sushi is fresh and delicious. the restaurant ambiance is clean and inviting, being that it's located inside a recently opened new market. We got the seared salmon roll and the regular Chirashi bowl, which was fitting for two but Chirashi bowl was a bit on the smaller side. There's a chirashi bowl for 2~3 pax @ $35 option which we heard was great, will try next time!

I had gone to Gyuu before, and had some vouchers, so we decided to try a new place.  Opted for sushi as everything should be fresh and website photos kph great.  I'd say, for the price they charge, it really wasn't anything spectacular.  We ordered a cucumber furikake appetizer. This was good  ( but really couldn't go wrong with this dish). We ordered a thick cut chirashi Don, but it wasn't thick cut. Normal thin cut sashimi. I ordered a bluefin tuna temaki.  Usually temakis are a nice round cone, sure its usualky filled with more rice than fish, this....was a flat small cucumber sliced filled nori roll with some rice and a sprinkle of fish. Which i personally do not see it being worth the 6.80 price tag. Overall, the experience did not meet our expectations. I don't mind paying for something, as long as its good and as described in the menu. The emporium has many other restaurants, so I'd say go try the other ones out first....
Been here several times. The Chirashi don and Sushi are very good. The sashimi was good in my previous visits but at our visit it wasn't as fresh. Still worth coming back though.

Not going to this place again until there is a significant change... Made a booking before going. Online menu looks really tempting and the prices does not seem all that bad at that time... The place was rather empty when we arrived. Granted that it was a weekday and we were slightly early. Ordered via the ipad on the table (never a fan of ordering this way...), and food came quickly enough. The onsen tamago was decent (though this may be the reason for my vomiting after dinner... Or maybe that was due to the $6.80 single oyster... It will remain a mystery....). Temaki were a bit sad.... Flat piece of folded nori was presented... "Thick cut" chirachi was abit-less-than-normal slices of sashimi... Spicy tuna roll was passable... Dinner for 3 was about $100. Thank goodness voucher reduced it to $60. But we had to look for another place for our second dinner because we left the restaurant very unsatisfied and generally unhappy. ... Thank goodness dinner no.2 that night turned out good

Simple, fresh sushi place. The sashimi is great. Being Singapore, the prices are ridiculous... (On that note, the rolls look good value for money, though have not tried any of them so can't speak to how they are). The venue is simple, casual, exactly as you would expect from a place that is attached to a supermarket!  Likely to be back, for a casual lunch.

This sushi joint is part of Emporium Shokuhin, a new gourmet supermarket with 7 restaurants, a takeaway sushi section and a very hyped up bunch of seafood tanks and steak room. My colleagues and I were pretty darn excited about a Japanese market opening near our office, since the Suntec/Millenia/Marina Sq area is pretty much the dead zone for value (read value, not affordable, since that doesn't exist in the vicinity) meals for lunch. Unfortunately, we got a little too excited and were brought down to earth quickly at our visit to the sushi bar last week.Senmi Sushi IS located in a supermarket and high end as it may be, I do expect *some* value . We ordered the chirashi and wagyu beef roll, which are the specialties and I thought the former was mediocre. The chirashi came with fairly standard fish, portions that left us wondering where we should get some mee pok afterwards, and at a price tag that was a little lofty. I didn't mind the lack of variety as much as I minded the portions because honey, there ain't nothing worse than under-feeding a hungry office worker with only an hour to spare. The beef roll scored way better on the value card, with some delicious slices of beef wrapped around a shrimp tempura roll and covered in some mystery sauce with crunchy crumbs. Again at about $18 (if I recall correctly), you were getting what you paid for. My advice is to stick with Teppei at Millennia Walk, where you get a humongous bowl of Kaisendon for about $17 and they creatively offer a salad option if you're on a no-carb diet. There's also a restaurant in Purvis St that does a very generous $25 bowl but I find the slices too thick and jelat. Besides the food, I liked the decor (a calming zen aesthetic) but that was about it. We came during their opening week so the front of house was really disorganized. The restaurant has a long sushi bar and a row of tables that were, well, long. Since most office folk eat in 2's, every table had enough space for 2-4 more people but  was underutilized, so there was a long line of people watching empty table space. We were initially seated at the sushi bar, which has iPad's for every 2 people. However, the waiter thought it was necessary to consolidate our order on one iPad and turned the other one off, so we all had to take turns moving to the seat with the glorious functioning iPad to place our orders. The face -palm-worth use of technology was made worse by the fact that every iPad (at the counter and tables) was connected to a cable on the wall that was about 15cm long. So be warned, you're gonna get really chummy with your colleagues while trying to peruse the menu and order at this sushi joint. Lastly, our orders (which if you notice was mostly raw) took almost an hour to get to us and it was only after we asked about them that they magically appeared within seconds.Not a fun opening week experience but if you're desperate (and you probably are) for a change of scene with sushi, this is it. Just uh, save a couple of bucks for mee pok afterwards because you will be hungry. Or just eat the takeaway sushi in the emporium itself.

I would've given this place s five star rating if their menu is more descriptive of what's inside of each dish.To conclude our Singapore trip, we decided to have a quick dinner close to the hotel. So we stopped by Asia Grand. The restaurant does look grand, and omg they didn't skimp on AC!! It's 90 degrees outside, and they blasted AC inside the restaurant making it feel like it's in the 50s!! Since its so cold inside, we've decided to order some soup to warm up. My soup was pretty good ( I ordered the fish soup with tofu); however, my hubby's soup had some mysterious ingredients that's not listed on the menu. Since he's allergic to shellfish and those ingredients look like shellfish, we decided to not chance it. The waitress told us that we can't return the soup as they already made it. Well, that's not acceptable. In the end, they didn't charge us for it, but we did need to put up a fight for it.Other than that, the meal was very good. Food was tasty and service was good. I recommend the chicken steamed with yellow wine, salt and pepper ribs.

Decent to slightly above average dim sum restaurant located within the City Hall/ Bras Basah / Bugis area. You can't miss the restaurant as it is located right across the iconic Raffles Hotel (North Bridge Road side)  and in the same building as The Loof - the rooftop bar everyone is raving about. We made reservation 2 weeks in advance just because we have a big group and to ensure we have a table secured for us during the peak brunch / lunch period on a Saturday. Kudos to the team - the table was set up nicely when we reached and the service was prompt. We browsed through the extensive menu and picked a few dim sum staples like har kow, siew mai, liu sar pao, cheong fun and etc. All were decent, nothing spectacular, the standard you would expect from a chinese restuarant. Since chinese new year is just around the corner, we ordered a big plate of  salmon "yu sheng", a raw fish salad to toss in good fortune for the upcoming lunar new year. The 'Yu sheng" priced at $88 for the big portion was very overpriced looking at the portion and the very thin slices of salmon (2 small plates with 5 to 6 slices/plate) while the rest are just pickled vegetables and crackers. I would pay $50 max but to charge this exorbitant price just because it's in high demand now is just absurd. Lucky, to  balance things out, Asia Grand do have peking duck promotion ($38 whole duck) and each table is only entitled for single order. We ordered the peking duck as well and it was good. Whole duck was brought to our table where the restaurant captain did her magic, carving the crispy skin and then wrapped in thin crepe to be eaten with hoisin sauce. Delicious!  The remaining of the duck meat can either be eaten as it is or you can request the kitchen to cook it the way you desire (with noodles or porridge, each with different surcharge, of course)For dessert, we had red bean pancake ("wor peng") and glutinous rice ball (mochi) with black sesame filling. Overall, we paid a total bill of $370 to be shared among  13 of us. Asia Grand definitely needs to live up to its expectation and maintain the food standard looking at the tight competition within that area - Wah Lok at Carlton Hotel and Royal China at Raffles Hotel. As at now, I am still not "very" convince with the overall dining experience hence the 3 star. COME BACK, I MUST!

This is a respectable established Chinese restaurant. I've been here a few times for family dinner and a few business lunches. The service is professional and experienced.My most recent meal here was a CNY lunch and these are some of the dishes:1) Yusheng. Nicely balanced seasoning. Fresh veg. I really liked the fried salmon skin that was really light and crispy. They DID use some salmon sashimi despite the recent raw fish scare. The crispy crackers were very crunchy and in copious amounts - always a highlight for me to have generous crackers.2) The fish maw super soup - light and not gluey. Some more expensive menus I've had recently seem to have a more gluey consistency which is really too heavy for a lunch with so many courses. This was not bad and quite a lot of fish maw in it but not that special in terms of the soup flavour. Could be a bit more intense.3) Fried pippa duck. Nice crispy bits but some parts of the meat were a little chewy. I had limited stomach space so I left those.4) Fresh prawns in superior stock with tung hoon. Super yummy and tasty! Prawns were fresh and firm. The tung hoon was bouncy and full of flavour like it had absorbed the sauce.5) Abalone - I've had so much abalone the past few weeks at places like Jade, Summer Palace and Szechuan Court repeatedly. This is no worse in quality. Although a slightly smaller size but the other places are more pricey. It was tender and tasty. The sauce was tasty. The broccoli it came with was a bit boring.6) The fish was kinda muddy. We all commented that it was obviously freshwater fish but really the aftertaste was too strong. Disappointing.7) The glutinous fried rice. This was ok only for me. But to be fair, I was really full at this point.8) I enjoyed dessert. Red bean with mandarin peel and a sesame paste glutinous dumpling.I liked that they brought the nian gao straight in the steamers to the table. They had put the fine peanut and icing sugar mixture on the side to serve since one of our group was allergic to nuts. The nian gao was really very smooth and tender and actually stretched a lot when we were picking it up. Usually it would be rolled in the nuts so not their fault. It was quite mild tasting but the texture was really soft.

My family has been a regular at Asia Grand Restaurant for many years. The owners of the restaurant used to work for Tsui Hang Village in Asia Hotel many years ago (must have been at least 10-15 years) and my parents have always been loyal patrons.Asia Grand is your typical better-than-Crystal-Jade Chinese restaurant serving decent ala-carte dim sum for lunch and cantonese style cuisine for dinner. The pricing here is fair, not super high end but not extremely affordable either. Great for family dinners on special occasions!I love the peking duck here as the skin is always nicely sliced and wrapped with the egg skin. When my parents are in the mood to splurg, I also enjoy the geoduck clam/ lobster sashimi/ steamboat. Otherwise, food here can never go wrong, although standards may vary depending on the number of customers/ how crowded the restaurant is.

I am a huge dimsum aficionado and it is often regretful that one can only procure good dimsum at dingy places (eg 126 Web Dou Sik) or nicer places (St Regis). I refuse to comment on Crystal Jade as my earlier statement excludes seemingly mass-produced dimsum.Asia Grand is similar to Jing; it bridges the gap between low-end and pricey. It is a middle ground meal that you will feel comfortable bringing clients of a certain profile to, or a family dinner etc. Make sure you order the liu sha pao - it was the best I have had for awhile. The golden molten was glorious.

An established brand name when it comes to dim sum and chinese cuisine in general, I have had the chance to dine here a couple of times, but somehow i don't think the food is that great. The suckling pig has some sort of a smell that you can still taste, like they didn't clean it properly, which made eating it unpleasant. So you might want to give that a miss. The dim sum menu is really just average, and even sub-par on certain dishes. Long queues are fairly common here so its always good to make a reservation should you want to dine here in large groups.

Review's for dim sum - no complaints at all. Pretty crowded so be sure to make reservations. Come to think of it, I didn't think their specials were that spectacular, so I'd recommend to keep to the staples.

Love the food and service staff at this place. I've been quite a regular here. The Peking duck is way better than imperial treasure IMO. Every dish is rather unique. The managers will arrange your Menu according to your budget and all the dishes are rally well done. Must tries are the Peking duck, xo noodles, pork belly appetizer and many many more.

Attracts a lot of business meetings due to its location. Food is quite decent i.e. above averge but given the price (high side) and average ambiance and service, I wouldn't make this my favourite makan place; but still worthy of my consideration.

We took a chance and went without reservations and since it was early and a weekday, were able to get a table.  First time in this place and its your typical Chinese restaurant.  We ordered the usual fares of dimsum: hakaw, pork suimai and they were all tasty.  The carrot cake was delicious.  The disappointing dish was the roast pork -- it had a certain smell and taste from pork that is not so fresh.  So I don't understand the hype -- it's good but not fantastic.  My friend says that on weekends, they push you to finish your dining in 45mins.

it is the weekend! which means it is brunch - and here is a good place to get a decent one, even if more than a little far out. this rustic little cafe is unpretentious (pretty rare in the recent crop of cafes), and it serves up an averagely-decent brunch menu that spans american brunch classics to local delights.most of us started off on the western side of the menu - mostly average fixins' - their poached eggs are probably the most notable thing on the menu.they make an appearance in most of the breakfast dishes, and each is a neat parcel of cooked white and flowing yolk - good execution, but it might have helped more if the sauces and flavors had just as much care.the local specialties were rather a hit-and-miss. a hit with a very lemak mee siam that was served with a poached egg - you will want to eat this hot because it quickly loses its charm as it cools - and a terrible miss with the nasi lemak, which came with another one of those poached eggs. the rice had barely any flavor, the chicken impressive-looking but barely seasoned and a tad dry - this dish was pretty dismal.I also think that poached egg on the rice smacks a little of trying-too-hard - there's something to be said about the texture of a golden fried egg with a runny yolk and the texture it brings to the dish.but I got pretty lucky with my main of grilled saba (mackerel) drizzled with a sticky soy glaze on baby spinach. definitely not the sort of thing I expected in this sort of place, but nothing to complain about since it worked very well. the mackerel was oily and savory, the baby spinach crisp and green, and that glaze a sweet-savory counterpoint.it works for this place that its kitschy, in a good almost-believably-local way, without any of the pretentiousness in the hipster-hangouts we see these days. the food is decent, though not quite worth traveling for without a car - I suggest it only if driving and looking for a cute little place to sit on the weekend.

Ate here with the yelp crew and was expecting something delicious but definitely left unsatisfied and worse, hungry.  I think the restaurant does a good job with the decor and food presentation but I just wasn't impressed with the food.  We tried most of all the things on the breakfast menu and it was just eh..  Maybe bc I'm used to American brunch places that are huge and delicious (referring to NYC and LA only) but yeah.. Will not go back..

Was looking for a petfriendly cafe in West to bring my dog, and found this gem!My parents were really taken by this quaint place!I do recommend to try the meesiam (which may seem like a strange choice for cafe food), but the portion was really generous, & the broth was really tasty!The ondeh ondeh cake is pretty good too! The toasted coconut bits really made the cake!

Tucked away in a corner of a residential street, I wouldn't know about the existence of this cafe if my friend didn't introduce it to me. Business is quite good during lunch time and I would guess that most customers specially make their way here. Since it's not in a mall or upscale location, I expected the prices to be lower but it was comparable to mid range restaurants. I had duck confit which was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. I would have preferred it to come with a less creamy sauce. Portion and taste are fine so if you are tired of chain restaurants, give this a chance!

Nice ambiance. Pricy quality.Lamb shank $28. Well grilled with moist insides and slight crisped on the edge. Chewy yet flavourful. I don't like the fats though it adds to the taste. I don't mind the redness.Beef Sirloin $28. Medium rare. Good balance of greens and fries. The fries is the surprise. I will remember the fries. As for the steak, it's pretty good. Nothing memorable, on the positive side.Ambiance like this on the west side neighbourhood is a nice find.

When I first saw W39.. Located next to KFC... It looked so cute and bloo!!! :) i had heard great comments about their cakes so I decided to try their rainbow cake at $6.80+ it's reasonably priced even though.. Anyone who can bake will tell you that's still overpriced.. Nonetheless... The buttercream wasn't too buttery and the cake was light. The colours were pretty too :) we had a side of chicken wings which tasted and smelt just like the har jiong kai which you get at a tze char at 2 times more than what the tze char stall would charge you for.. Nonetheless I would recommend you to checkout other places for wings and you can def try their apple crumble pie :) delicious and a  generous serving with a dollop of ice cream! :)
The food is decent. They have an onde-onde cake that is not bad. And prices are ok. I have never left upset but I have also never left completely wow'd by anything here either.

i put off writing this review just to see if i still feel as strongly as i did, about this place, after a cooling off period.it's been more than a month now and i think it is safe to say i'm not clouded by any impulsive verbal diarrhoea.firstly, finding this place is a challenge.even for a former west sider junkie like me.fortunately, i was cabbing it and even though the taxi driver knew of the road, he still brought me on a tour of the colourfully named roads, kuning(yellow), merah(red) before arriving at puteh(white).if you are driving, your safest bet will be parking at clementi stadium.limited parking in front of w39 is available and if you do like to take a risk at parking illegally, do have a word with marcus before you do so.it was packed to the brim on an august saturday afternoon.thankfully, we secured a reservation and were seated within.decor was pleasant enough but i'm forever wary of style over substance.staff were not the most experienced but they tried.upon the recommendation of their staff and the fact the brunch menu exclaimed it as a local favourite! nasi lemak with roasted spice chicken leg, that was what i ordered.when it arrived, the fleeting moments of it's decent looks gave way to an inner flaw that is hard to overlook.salt or the lack thereof.yes, most times people complain about their food being overly salty but today the oldest, most ubiquitous food seasoning was missing?did someone forget about it?but not only was the coconut rice lacking in salt, the coconut milk was way watered down resulting in a tastelessly bland, overly wet and not so lemak rice.sure, you could ask for more of their homemade sambal but again that is mere window dressing.nasi lemak rice has to be palatable enough for you to eat it on it's own.next the chicken leg, best described as a powdery turmeric mess.again, did salt go AWOL?after just one bite, all you want is to wash it away with their decent coffee.mind you, their nasi lemak is priced at $12.50, so the benchmark should be set so much the higher, no?and guess what? they interestingly use nicely poached eggs for most of their dishes.but guess what, i'm not a fan of poached eggs!:(give me oily fried eggs with runny yolks, anytime, for my nasi lemak, please!seeing how i only recently scored me the maverick badge, here is a 2 star rating in hope you can score yours too!:)

was in search for the next big rainbow cake in singapore that drove (well rather by Mr SBS uncle) me here. Cakes look pretty on the shelves that screams 'eat me'. so i did. ordered the rainbow cake and red velvet. remember how many say not to be just a pretty face but have substance? sadly this place just has a pretty face when it comes to dessert and coffee. i have to admit the sponge cake used in the rainbow and red velvet cake is light and not that sweet but the cream... OMG. tooooo sweet and too much. ordered a latte to go with me cakes but sadly I had better coffee. i'm not picky with my coffee and even I can say its meh... sooo for coffee lovers I would recommend you trying something else insteadi have to admit the service here is good and attentive. they just have to up a notch on the desserts and drinks to make this a good chill out place.i can't comment on the savories for i had none of it this time but I doubt i'll ever come back and try - looking at the reviews. however, this is a good place to come once and see the pretty cakes. overall, its a good attempt at a cafe but needs more work to reach memorable. Gambatte W39!
Relaxing ambient. Simple decoration. Food was quite good but seems to be in a higher price range for this kind of restaurant.

Drawn by the siren call of the Yelp Saturday Brunch Club, hordes of hungry hungry Yelpers descended on W39 for a good balance of 'ang moh' brunch options and some local choices. Now, I've have rated W39 3 stars. I enjoyed the mee siam although it was atypical (much too rich and creamy, though the poached egg was a fascinating take), and while it might not become my go-to place when I have a mee siam craving, I definitely wouldn't mind ordering it again. The Eggs Benedict was well put together, my only complaint is that it was TINY. I could have had three of 'em. The Honey Lemon was way way too sweet, but once the ice started melting, it wasn't so bad.BUT. For everyone else at the table, I could tell that W39 felt a lot more 2-starry than 3. (And if you'll refer to Jerilyn's review, you'll get further evidence why.)The Nasi Lemak that one of the other Yelpers ordered was... very underwhelming and the small size of the Hearty Breakfast, well okay it wasn't small, just not HEARTY (full caps intended). The rice for the nasi lemak was under seasoned and the paninis were awfully small. Small niggling issues here and there that really undercut the place standing out amongst the increasing number of brunchy cafes popping up in Singapore.My conclusion after our visit? An Eggs Benedict and Mee Siam are just enough to feed one, and if that's all you order, you'll have a pretty good meal.If you stray off that path that I have painstakingly cleared for you though, don't blame me when you find yourself in a minefield of mediocrity.

The only cafe/resturant I've found in West Coast that comes close to an Australian style coffee shop. Coffee was good and they have a decent range of meals and snacks on the menu. It has great customer service which can be hard to find in Singapore.

W39 is the brainchild of 2 Eastie sisters and this cheerful blue and yellow spot is actually both a bistro and a bakery and that only means 1 thing for me-brunch.I wouldn't have gone out of my way for brunch in the West if not for an appointment in the area. Sorry westies, you're not gonna be seeing more food posts from the western part of Singers.My Mocha tasted more like regular latte. Where is ze chocolate??! Meh-ish latte at best. Very diluted. Thankfully I've lowered my expectation so I wasn't overly disappointed. Don't go expecting anything artisan.Hearty Breakfast ($13.50) is a greedy and lazy girl's best option. Well, first and foremost, it has everything. It's quite hard to screw up an American breakfast since everything is kinda outsourced. The scrambled eggs were a little overdone for my liking. The best part was the toast (i think it's brioche) with its airy texture. Salted butter would be welcomed anytime. I originally opted for a Brie Parma Ham Panini (or was it a Croque Madame) but i was tempted by the Braised Pork Cheeks Gruyere Panini (S$13) that the neighboring table ordered. The mouthwatering scent was too good that i had to change my order immediately! Boy was I glad i did!The panini was stellar with the slightly crusty shell and dense and moist center. Pork cheeks were tender and flavorful and the sandwich had a perfect meat-gravy-bread ratio. The taste of the meat was rather strong but i'm a carnivore so i don't care. Besides, it was balanced by the savory gravy and the light sweetness of the bread.If you're looking for something lighter, the assortment of cakes, breads and pastries should not disappoint (i base that on my review of their breads).

This was good. They had great white beer and crab cakes and salad. The tenderloin steak was also great, but it was too bloody when I had asked for medium. Sauce that came with the tenderloin was good. They let me substitute mashed potatoes instead of fries.

Have been hearing quite a bit about this place but have been feeling lazy to trek down to the West to try it out. Well, finally I did and I wasn't disappointed at all.Was a short bus ride away from Clementi or JE MRT Station. On first sight, the place reminded me of my area at Serangoon Gardens with the cafe nestled snugly among  residential houses. Was quite crowded on a rainy Sunday evening where most people were there for dinner; isn't it a testament to how good a place is if it is filled on a raining Sunday evening? The interior was filled to the brim and so was the exterior.We weren't there for dinner but vowed to try their mains the next time around as it looked so good from what we saw at our neighboring diners' tables. Ordered a chocolate cake (forgotten the exact name but have a look at my picture) and the texture was gooey, melty and is a chocolate maven's piece of heaven - a must try. The coffee wasn't the best but was passable.Loved the atmosphere! Wished I knew of this place while I was at NUS as it would definitely be on my hang-out list!

Heard about the crowd here on weekends so I was a little concerned about coming here on a Sunday night. The place wasn't too hard to find from the nearby bus stop (you might have parking problems if you're driving though!) and the ambience was decent. There are lots of nostalgic stuff laid all over the place which makes the overall ambience quite cosy - albeit a little forced, as another Yelper mentioned in his review. Having gone down mainly for dessert. A friend and I ordered a flat white, the crunchie hazelnut and a tiramisu to share among us. I take pride in my coffee and I can honestly say the flat white was nothing special - a little too flat (pun unintended) actually. The crunchie hazelnut and the tiramisu looked great and I thought it would at least make up for the disappointing coffee. I was wrong. The crunchie hazelnut had an overwhelming taste of fresh cream that made it far too sweet for both our tastes. The tiramisu came with a serving of espresso - which was something I had never seen before, and for good reason. Without the espresso, the tiramisu tasted entirely of marscapone. Even with the espresso poured in, it still felt pretty... off. I couldnt taste any kahlua liqour in the tiramisu with or without the espresso, which to me, sealed the deal as one of the poorest tiramisus I've had. If you want a good tiramisu, try out Kith Cafe at Park Mall - it's far better. The place was also quite noisy, so if you're looking for a quiet place to hang out with friends or loved ones, take note. I didnt try any of the food items, but the lamb ribs and wagyu burgers other people were eating looked quite appetitizing.  But then again, so were the desserts we ordered.Not coming back to this place again. At least the service here was something worth mentioning.

Came here with the Singapore Yelp Brunch Club and while I loved meeting fellow yelpers, W39 was well, ehhhh. It's 2.5 stars (but not quite 3) in my opinion. Let's just say, the concept is good but the execution just well, kinda sucked, for lack of a better word.Food: I got the Hearty Breakfast, and wasn't the least impressed (especially because I was at Arbite the weekend before, and they, they do a mean hearty breakfast - but more on that in another review!) the portions in general just seemed small all around (except for the local options) which would be fine if it tasted amazing but everything just seemed subpar. I also tried bites of the Mee Siam and the Ham & Cheese Panini. The Ham & Cheese Panini definitely tasted kind of like something I could've done myself, however, the Mee Siam was probably the best thing there in my opinion. It was hearty, with a nice sweet flavor to it. I enjoyed that the most. We also got the Honey Lemon Ice Tea which tasted like someone spilled half the jar of honey into. Did they?! Ambience: Like I said, great concept, horrible execution. They try to be "cute" with the cute nautical theme and selling old candies we grew up with but it just seems kind of copied. The seating inside is limited and pretty cramped and the service was alright. All in all, we left happy to have met everyone but not so happy with the food. Not horrible but really nothing special.
A lovely corner boutique cafe that serves good food and desserts! A lovely place for lunch and weekend pig out. Also good for small events and celebrations

W39 was just kind of average. Worth a visit if you just want a chill out spot with a nice decor. But not a place I would return to.The service was earnest and polite but quite inefficient. Granted that I did not try the food, I really cannot comment on any dish in particular. But when I checked out what the other diners were having, none of them screamed or even said 'EAT ME!!!' And the coffee was decent but really not worth the fifteen minute wait for it.But if you are bent on trying an average brunch place, it could be wise to reserve a table, as W39 was quite crowded on a Saturday afternoon.
