Guzman Y Gomez finally opens for business, in the west side of Singapore.During the opening, they gave out free burritos for an afternoon with a live mariachi band playing. The line was extremely long but moved rather quickly, I got my burrito in 20 minutes.It's similar to Chipotle, fast food tex-mexy type burritos and tacos. It's okay not mindblowing, but the good part is that they're consistent. (extra star for that) It's good now that they are in a convenient location outside the central business district (CBD).3-stars. Overall consistency and that free burrito bribed me into giving another 1-star.

I was excited with this place opened near me. I've tried them in Perth, Australia and really liked it there.Maybe it's opening pains, but it's just not the same. The ingredients aren't super fresh, and the meats were a little too salty.Those with kids beware - smoke from the nearby smokers' hangout will permeate into the al fresco dining area.

Pulled pork mini burrito ($8.40) - 3 starsI really like that they offer mini burritos! Won't be getting the whole wheat tortilla the next time - the flavor just didn't quite fit in. The pork and beans were just okay. Not too dry, but the flavors could be better. The rice definitely has room for improvement - it could use better spices.

Always a good place to grab a quick bite. My kids enjoy it too. The frozen lemonade is too sweet and I do wish they would hv a garbage can so that people can throw away their garbage. Love the biodegradable plates & cutlery.

Decent Mexican place with a variety of options. The outside seating area is prettier than the inside and the fans are enough to beat the heat. The burrito can be filling after a while so you might find it more enjoyable to have a small burrito and pair with sides like nachos. My friend opted for 2 quesadillas instead which looked rather small for a proper meal. My preference is the burrito bowl. The fish is surprisingly good- very fresh in big portions. The guacamole is also well prepared.

disclaimer: i am a big fan of chipotle mexican grill!the idea of having mexican food at a stone's throw away from my abode was so exhilarating! of course i have to give it a try asap and my first impression was, "my! what a small shop front they have." their cashier counter was basically 3 steps away from the automatic glass door. the lady at the counter must have known it's not that easy to be staring at a steep menu board for long so she very quickly offered me the paper menu. I chose the spicy grilled steak with regular rice and a side of gucamole. she asked if i wanted sour cream. not being too keen about it, i replied, "just a little." she said, "sorry, we don't do just a little...it's additional 50 cents." that's when the first wave of missing Chipotle came crashing over me. i already accepted the fact I had to pay additional $2 for my guac and also they don't have corn as an ingredient in the bowl so I didn't think I want to splurge anymore for my $13 meal. Quickly i ended my order before i could do anything else stupid like ordering an additional side of churros with chocolate dip. My order was ready in less than 5 minutes and i was happy to find that they offer chipotle medium hot sauce at the condiment table; there were also sliced Jalapeño and diced red onion plus 2 other kind of sauces. It was a good 30 minutes before i could eat and the bowl stayed pretty warm in the eco friendly to-go container. Another nice touch was the melted cheese on the rice but the real saving grace was the hot sauce I picked up on the way out. the sauce really gave the other wise regular tasting bowl its kick. if you like black beans then you will be happy to know they are very generous with their beans. i ran out of rice faster than i could eat the beans. By now i am completely missing Chipotle like crazy.Thanks Guzman and Gomez for offering me a decent bowl of mexican food. it doesn't completely satisfy me but I am glad you are in my life for now.

It's ok. it's just ok. the burrito is a decent size, chock full of rice and beans, but the pulled pork was neither spicy (as advertised) nor particularly tasty. they have a nice salsa bar where you can load up on salsa and all the onions and cilantro/coriander your heart desires.
No shame. Queued for the free burrito during their opening.Beef was decent and juicy. The fish, I had lacked seasoning.However, I would recommend coming back for a hearty bite.

Yummy! Tried it for the first time and I must say I'm already a big fan. Had the pan seared barramundi burrito bowl with smoke chipotle sauce and extra guac. There is just so much flavour and spice in one bowl, which blended well together. Though the portion isn't huge, its enough to keep me satisfied. I'm glad that I'm able to find a similar version of Chipotle in Singapore!
This is nice. Close enough to to chipotle imo. So much meat stuck on my teeth. Tonight I'm a t rex.

Food is fine.. It's Tex Mex, not hard to get it right. But the state of the property when visiting BEFORE the lunch rush at 11:53 am was an embarrassment . Floors are filthy, table tops filthy, waitresses uniform was covered with food as well. 4 thumbs down for cleanliness

As a Californian from a Mexican family, I really started to miss tacos and burritos. I decided to explore every Mexican food place in Singapore(been here for over 2 months) and this is by far the best food for price. The burritos taste almost identical to Chipotle in the states, the tacos are really really good, and the quesadillas are delicious(my favorite).  You can also get jarritos(Mexican Soda) and a pretty good guacamole. If you're from cali or want some really good tacos/quesadillas I would definitely recommend this place. The burritos are just ok in my opinion(just like chipotle).

4 stars for a mexican place in Singapore - if this place was in America, it would be 3 stars.  It's the closest thing to Chipotle in taste, but not price.  I love their steak burrito and steak burrito bowl.  If you dont have the biggest appetite, definitely go for the mini burrito.

I really like Guzman and regularly go here for lunch (I work across the street), but it can get pricey. My favorite order is the burrito bowl and ask them to add guac and switch out for brown rice. I would avoid the lines around noon on weekdays and pretty much any time on weekends.

I paid a visit to the new branch at Star Vista, enticed by a free burrito flyer handed out at the mrt station. But when I got there shortly after 5, I was turned away by staff saying that the promo ended at 5. No end time was indicated on the flyer and the staff  acknowledged that but still said the promo was over. Talk about false advertising! !! I told her to tell the manager that this was wrong but she casually dismissed me (the staff were having some kind of celebration and totally ignoring the customers) so I have zero confidence that she will pass my feedback. Hence I decided to post this.

The crowds at Hong Lim Complex FC can get insane, and it pays to go there a little early for the good stuff. Found this place upstairs and towards the middle of the unusually shaped hawker centre. They serve char kway teow and that is all. $3 for the standard serving, $1 extra for more cockles, 50c for more egg. The cook had just finished the last batch when I arrived, so I got to watch him work, and he is a master at it.He deserves 9.5/10 for the food, but I had to round down for the lack of sliced pork. Otherwise, everything was fantastic and delicious. If you are in the area, stand in line, watch the master work, then savor his art.

Get the extra egg and cockles! You deserve it after waiting on the line. The closest thing to Penang char kway teow that I've ever found in Singapore, imho. The addition of the crispy pork nicely disguised in all the mess in the plate was definitely genius!

I hardly eat char kway teow and the one that is stuck in my memory is from the early 90s when I was still a kid and the price was $1 a plate (slowly creeping up to $1.20, $1.50, $2 etc). On this trip back to Singapore I made it a quest to find a good char kway teow and this plate was pretty awesome. It has lots of hums (cockles) and bits of crispy pork lard. It is not too wet or dry. Unfortunately it does not have much of a wok hei flavor. Plus there is no lup cheong (Chinese sausage). But this is definitely a wow if you are a cockle lover. The queue is not very long at 1030am on weekdays, maybe about 10-15 mins wait.

Is this what they called the best in Singapore??? Totally soggy and all clumps together. Cannot taste any fried taste, more like boiled only. The Long queue probably due to the good amount for the price. For the amount, one more star.Overly rated. Not worth the wait. Cannot even tastes the pork cracklings. No Chinese sausages Nor fish cake.

A bit of redemption on our most recent visit here for a place that is well-known for their fried kway teow, but failed to impress us the first time around. Same crazy line at the hawker center, same guy behind the wok, but something different I tasted this time around. Pork cracklins! I'm pretty positive this is something new added as I think I would have remembered tasting it before. Overall, the fried kway teow was quite delicious and didn't have that fishy aroma I remembered last time even though the cockles were aplenty in our dishes. The line was definitely worth it this go around.

Add cockles for $1 sgdFried  kway teow mee $3 sgdThe noodle was good but saturated too much in sauceThe cockles were ok but not quiet fresh tasting completely Open 6am to 4pmLocated in food court upstairs Singapore hawker masters 2010 winnerRecommend to bring cash and napkins

The secret is the pork lard.One of the best, not the best. I like this version of sweet char kway tiao for the longest time. And the secret is the crunchy pork lard. The chilli can be better so that keeps me from giving the fifth Star.Eat it when it's hot, that's the best flavor!

Value for price? Amazing! For $3 you get a medium-sized portion of tasty fried kway teow. You will have to wait for around 30-40 minutes during the lunch hour, but it is worth it. The stall is sort of hit or miss in terms of the portion size, but generally you get enough for a small-ish lunch--I was certainly satisfied. If you're with a group send multiple people out to scout for seating while you wait in line. The stall aunty will come down the line to collect your order and payment and you will pick up your portions immediately as you get to the front of the line.
Very good char kuey teow. Good char on the noodles , lots of garlic - tasty indeed. A good serving of cockles for those who like it.

due to some serious jetlag, me and justin b. were wide awake early in the morning and since Outram Park opens at 6am, we were there first thing for a breakfast of fried kway teow haha. at about $2-3 USD, this is a great value for a great meal. there was absolutely no line at 6am and we actually might have been the first customers of the day haha. the noodles are cooked fresh for you and it was a delicious way to start my day. lots of good flavors and texture to this dish - you've got some crunch, diff types of noodles, and a slight spice kick. so good!

Breakfast of champions: char tway teow with teh o'ais limau. I am totally addicted to char kway teow and eat as much of it as I can when I'm Singapore or Malaysia, so I was pretty excited that I could get some of the good stuff as early as 6am. Filled with delicious crunchy pork lard and rice noodles, it's not exactly a healthy start to the day, but damn it's good. I came early in the day and it wasn't too busy, so the kway teow mee was served fast and fresh for just $3. I shared it with my partner and with the heat that had already kicked in, was enough to keep us going until lunch (though I could have easily smashed one to myself without hesitation!).The cockles are very fishy, so if that isn't your thing I would recommend ordering without it. We opted for extra chilli and it was well spiced. Definitely a dish I will be missing at home and having been to Penang the day after this visit, can say it's right up there as one of the better noodle dishes I had on this trip.

Definitely the best char kway teow in Singapore. I usually avoid going 11:30am to 2:30pm. The wait time is crazy.Very simple. Cockles, noodles, bean sprouts, lots of garlic and lard. No Chinese sausage or fish cakes. I get mine with $2 extra cockles, fried white with extra chili.RTE whenever I'm in Singapore.

so where do you get char kway teow at 6am in the morning?here la!truth be told, i've not had a plate of char kway teow for ages!but somehow, army food just makes you crave what you cant get inside.since it's early in the morning, there isnt a queue.order, pay and be seated.they will deliver to your table even though it says self-service, i guess only when they arent busy.my previous complains about them is that their version tends to be too dry.but today it was very much to my liking.together with nicely cooked(not under and not over) cockles(albeit a little small).every now and then you also get a delightful crunch of crispy pork lard!breakfast of champions?

This is hands down, the BEST char kway teow you can get in Singapore. It's almost an institution and you cannot say you've had char kway teow until you have eaten here. Waiting times can get insane, especially during lunch hour, and waits of up to 45mins are really common. The old chef is a master at what he does, and he cooks it non-stop till the crowds begin to dissipate near the end of lunch hour before taking a break and closing. The pricing is insane as well, for the incredible standard of the char kway teow served - $3 for the standard serving, $1 extra for more cockles, 50c for more egg. Guaranteed to leave you wanting more.

First time I've ever tried char kway teow. Quite delicious. I got mine with spice which made this dish extra special. You can choose to have your dish with or without cockles (blood clams). I did both. Cockles have a very potent taste. Too potent... and I generally love extreme tastes. This preparation includes small bits of crispy pork skin for even more kick. Enjoy!

It's one of the best if not the best Char Kway Teow in Singapore.  It's done the Singapore style i.e. a bit wet.  The cockles is done just right ..... al dente!  Long queue is to be expected but definitely less than an hour.  Very affordable pricing.  A $3 plate is usually sufficient for me!

I'm a huge fan of char kway tiao; it's no doubt really sinful but I just can't resist the smooth pieces of kway tiao and the pork lard. The char kway teow here was moist but not overly greasy. Just the right amount of sweet dark sauce to accent the savoriness, yet not overpowering it, and plenty of wok hei. Finally, the spicy chili gave this simple hawker dish just that bit of oomph. The Ingredients included the usual beansprouts, cockles, fish cake and pork lard. Most notable was, of course, the succulent cockles and ultra-crispy pork lard. Overall, definitely one of the best char kway tiao that I have eaten, and no doubt very highly recommended!

Soooooo tasty. Best Char Kway Teow in the country, for realz. Long lines during lunch. You'll be hard-pressed to find a table anywhere, but take it to go and huddle in some park around just gobble up the goodness. Just do it

They make ok burgers...the patty is a tad dry and a little bland. But the sauce and cheese does make the Burger taste overall ok. Their burgers warrant a 3-star rating. The service by the manager gets the 4th star. I didn't get his name but he made sure our dinner party of 9 was well taken care of. That really made my mum feel good as the meal was her birthday celebration.

For all the years I lived in LA, I never went to or even heard or 25 degrees and now I understand why. There are probably much better burger joints around, like Umami Burger, Father's Office or my personal fave, In-N-Out!That being said, we are in Singapore, where we have none of the above and burgers are generally overpriced. So how does 25 degrees stack up? The #1, which consists of patty, bacon, gorgonzola, caramelised onions and arugula, is quite tasty and sizeable for $14. However, I take issue with the bun to patty ratio. It is too big compared and you can barely fit the burger in your mouth. I usually end up having my burger topless. If their bun was better proportioned, Id give it one more star. The fries and onion rings are pretty good ($5 each or you can order a mix for the same price). The tuna fish burger (#4) was nasty. Really fishy and bland.Once you add in the beer and fries/onion rings, the bill for one person is close to $40.Id come during lunch: burger + fries for $12. The burger patty is a little smaller than the a la carte one, but it's lunch! From 11am-3pmThey also have a decent happy hour from 3-7pm,with certain beers and cocktails discounted, and 1-for-1 specials on certain food itemsIt is also open late, so if you're craving a burger and beer at 1am (and dont Mickey-Ds) this is your place.

This gives me the burger sads :(25 Degrees is a chain that I first tried in Bangkok (it's annexed to the Pullman G Hotel), and I had a fairly good experience there. However, the one thing I do remember was the bun to burger ratio being completely off - and that was definitely the case here.I had the #2 at this location and it was just too much bun. Unfortunately it also was very unwieldy and sogged straight through so I basically had to eat the burger with a knife and fork. Whenever that happens, the burger experience has failed, and it needs to go back to the drawing board to be retooled.I feel like there is potential here, but the bun overload is not working - they need to figure that out first, and then work on building in a better taste profile overall for the burger. Mine was overdone also.At this stage I wouldn't return unless someone told me they've changed the menu/management.
One of the better burger places in town. No1 is good with bacon. No2 is meaty and meat lovers will like it. Good choice for those with sweet tooth. Just hope the service timing is improved.

It's a great concept - burger and beers! Opens late too! Decent fries and onion rings, good service and pretty tasty burgers but... and this is a huge BUT. Our burgers had dry and overdone patties which is a huge letdown for a specialty burger place. :(((

So I'm staying at G Hotel in SG and they have a 25 Degrees downstars.  Being a little jetlag I wanted something to eat and in my room is a flyer for this restaurant, so I went down and figured I'd have some onion rings and ordered them and I just wanted water.  The place only had two others inside when I ordered.  How long could it take?  5 minutes max?  So while I'm waiting a group of 3 come in and ordered beer, fries and bugers.  They got their beers, OK I get that.  They got their fries. Where's my onion rings right?  My order was in before they even ordered anything at all.  Then their bugers came out and I thought it was a little odd.  Well one guy opens up his buger and I see an onion ring on top of his buger patty and I say to myself WTF!  So, I grabbed my bag and walked out.   I'd normally would call for the manager and complain but instead I hope the owners read this review instead!   This is the first time in over a decade that I have walked out because of being so unhappy about service!

Man the place is pack at 10:30am on a Friday??!!   Seems like nobody works here?   The noise level can be a little high but fortunately i got a slight ear infection so got bit of muffle ear.   Otherwise a nice utilitarian cafe.   Food again was wonderful even though place waa busy service was still good.

Brunch place in Bukit Timah. Had the signature mushroom on toast here and it did not disappoint. I got a huge slice of sourdough bread with an overflow of mushroom in white wine cream sauce topped with parmesan cheese. The dish was creamy, rich and delicious. The mushroom texture really goes well with the texture and creaminess of the sauce. While it could easily be too rich / heavy to be enjoyable beyond a few bites, this wasn't the case. I managed to finish the whole dish despite not being a fan of super creamy stuff. The only letdown is probably the bread which was a bit chewy to begin with and gets worse over time as it becomes too soggy from the creaminess of the mushroom. My friend had their other famous dish - the pancake - which was fluffy and as sinfully good. Would recommend checking it out.

The cafe was walking distance from the MRT station and opened from Tuesday to Sunday 8am to 7pm. While there was no 10% service charge, there was a 7% GST charge in the bill. Pay as you order at the counter. Low & Slow Pulled Pork (S$20+)Braised pulled pork, scrambled eggs , streaky bacon , arugula served on sourdoughThe serving was huge. The pulled pork was topped with curry like sauce, quite tender and savoury but a tab too salty on its own. The bacon was a tab salty too. The scrambled eggs was creamy. The arugula was lightly dressed. The sourdough was soft which I like best.White Cold Brew (S$7+)Recommended to have the drink  without ice cubes so that one can taste the chocolatey notes more easily. Although it was non sweeten, it was not bitter in taste.Overall the food was not bad. The crowd started to come in at around 9am, so best came early.

Pleasantly surprised by this gem of a coffeehouse. I visited twice and both times found the place quite crowded, which is a great sign! I expected more of a coffeehouse vibe but it was definitely more of a mix of that and a restaurant - some people are doing work on their laptops and some people are eating some damn good looking food. You even sometimes need to be seated by a hostess as if it is a restaurant, but you order at the counter.The attitudes of the staff is beyond friendly and I love it. They love being there and it makes me love to be there too. The coffee is good and they have much variety which keeps it fun.Highly recommend if you are in the area and need a lively place to be to yourself, catch up with friends or even have a meeting.
Great coffees, tasty dishes, lovely ambience, friendly service.  Keep up the good work, Atlas!

I passed this newly opened cafe a few times already but it was always super busy during weekends so when I had opportunity to go for brunch on a Friday, I decided to give this place a try. When I entered I was a bit wary as the place oozes a hipster atmosphere which to me often translates into average quality food against a premium price, you pay for the stylish environment, not for the food: WRONG, this is not what Atlas is about! The food is great and the price point is more than acceptable.Atmosphere: as mentioned this place has a relaxing hipster vibe, it's very instagram worthy, I am not a good photographer so I did not capture this in my pictures but google some pictures and you'll see what I mean. The service is friendly and punctual.Food: The menu had many interesting and healthy looking dishes but I decided to go for a brunch-style dish, I had the Creamy Mushrooms on Sourdough  with scrambled eggs and Italian pork sausages. This could potentially go wrong in so many ways: chewy canned mushrooms, overcooked scrambled eggs and dry sausages but it was fantastic! The creamed shimeiji mushrooms are tasty, they provide a nice touch of unami to the dish and the sausages are juicy but the real stars are the sourdough and the scrambled eggs. The sourdough toast was perfect: good crust and one of the better tasting breads I had here in Singapore, the eggs were fluffy and light yet creamy, yum!Food part II: since I was hungry and greedy, we ordered next to our main dish a Maple Strawberry Pancake to share between two people. Once I had the Mushrooms & eggs on toast, I kinda regretted I'd ordered more as I was quite full and more than satisfied. More so, when the pancake arrived I feared it would be dry and bland as it looked thick. Wong again!! Whilst we both just really enjoyed our mains, we wolfed down the pancake like we hadn't eaten in ages! It is really delicious, the combo of fresh strawberries and the moist pancake is just great. The people next to us ordered the Caramelized banana pancakes with ice cream which looked absolutely delicious too (but I don't eat bananas so not for me).Price: I was pleasantly surprised to learn that our total check for two coffees and three mains (two savory dishes and one sweet to share) was similar to what I am used to pay for a typical weekend brunch for two in this neighborhood (around 50$). Prices are nett here, GST and service charge included. Additionally, they offer large jugs of ice water without charge!I'm coming again? 100% sure, their counter had cupcakes and cheese cake which looked very tempting and the I can see myself craving their dishes in the future! Since it is a new opening I hope they can keep this standard up.

Pros: It's a stone's throw away from Botanic Gardens MRT station, and there's a bus stop right in front of Atlas Coffeehouse, making it a convenient cafe to visit for those residing in the West.  The truffle fries aren't too pricey for local cafe standards ($8++), and the portion size is good for sharing among 2-3 persons. The flakes of cheese scattered on top of the fries is delicious! I also like how there are window seats and plenty of sunlight comes into the cafe. Their black, matte, industrial-looking stools are also surprisingly, quite comfy. And if you're a fan of white marble tables, there are plenty of those in this cafe. Their service also isn't too shabby.Finally, their peppermint tea tastes superb, so do give it a try! Cons: The truffle fries are a little on the greasy side, and I found this to be the case on both my first and second visit to Atlas Coffeehouse. On my second visit, the fries definitely tasted hard and crusty. I'm however, still a loyalist to PS. Cafe's truffle fries, as they are more consistent and fresh, as compared to Atlas Coffeehouse's. The cafe is quite popular and can get quite crowded, even on weekday afternoons.
Waffles arrived brown and over cooked. Mixed berry compote is too sweet. Overpriced cafe and not worth it.

I was here from around 2 - 4pm and it was so crowded!! There was thankfully enough space to sit down but the acoustics of the place meant that it got very noisy very fast! Apparently something is going to be done about that soon so hopefully it won't be as noisy in the future.It's a bit confusing to find, well for me it was, because I thought it was on Duke's Road itself, but actually it's in a building right next to it instead! Duke's Road itself has a lot of houses and no coffee shops.. heh...I tried their Ice Toffee Latte which even though it comes with a scoop of ice cream, you can ask for less syrup, which I'm not sure if it made a huge difference in taste with mine, but it was still very nice. Sort of like a more "adult" milkshake? It was quite rich and filling, so not ideal if all you want is a coffee. Their Atlas Signature Pancake was AMAZING. I've never seen a pancake before that looked like a literal cake made in a pan. It was so fluffy and had the right texture and moistness to it, but it was also about ONE INCH THICK. YEAH. ONE INCH THICK. It had a scoop of homemade ice cream as well as crunchy maple syrup cereal bits and bananas. I really think this is something to share with 2 people, unless you're really hungry and just want a sweet meal.. But even then, it's pretty massive as far as I'm concerned.Although it's a bit out of the way for me, I'm definitely going to remember this place if I'm in the area again!! Might even get to try some of the savory dishes for a change too.

Love the coffee and small local shop vibe! Waffles are great too! Hidden along the bukit timah area, just before you reach the stretch with many schools, sits this adorable cafe! Make reservations on chope before you head there for brunch on the weekend, it's already busy by 9! The wooden tables and minimalist designed serving  plates are awesome! Make your order at the cashier when you've decided but otherwise, don't bother with self-service. The servers don't get too pleased when you try to help yourself. Several notable items I've tried:Nitro brew - not too acidic, smooth, good for patrons who enjoy coffee but have gastric problemsBerries waffle - love love love this. Great crisp and chew to waffle. Berries compote is a great balance of sour and sweet. Definitely a YES. Banana pancake - it's more like a sponge cake than pancake. The cornflakes are awesome but why are they soaked in syrup? The dish was too sweet for me. Hash - excuse me this is mashed potato not hash. Hash needs to cast iron pan to get its crust there's no crust in this hash. Flavors wise it was not bad. The sausage was delicious! Scrambled eggs - just get it! Great moist and delicious. Huge portion! Truffle fries - thin crispy fries with generous serving of Parmesan cheese. No truffle taste though. The cheese was nice I'll be back if I'm in the area but I probably won't travel the way here to have brunch

I dropped by on a Wednesday afternoon to meet a few acquaintances for a late lunch and loved the chilled out vibes of the place. It can be slightly hard to find but it is otherwise just a short walk from Botanic Gardens MRT.We ordered lattes all round and everyone agreed that the coffee was pretty decent. They had a large range of coffee so it was a pity we all had the same thing. Also a point of note, free water. I had the salmon soba noodles which came with glazed salmon and a fried egg. The egg was cooked well and the salmon was in my opinion, well-marinated. Did not get to try the waffles which looked really tantalising. Definitely worth a repeat visit.

A nice place for coffee and eats, that gets super packed.  The space is very modern and cool and...noisy?  With concrete floors and high ceilings, this place does get loud, but it's still a very pleasant space with lots of light, large tables and friendly staff.  I had a very solid latte here, and food also looked quite good and also with some healthier options, although I didn't try any this time.   But as it's close to our church, it's good to know that there is more than just MCD around!

Friendly service! I missed out on their special combination and they are willing to change my order. I'm so grateful. There's sufficient staff to meet customers' needs as the crowd builds up during lunch time. Food is yummy and fast service. So glad that Yelp provided this option for me. Enjoy!
Really cool place. Can order entire meal from an iPad. Cash only. Affordable. Don't get the egg rolls - they're not good. Red curry is fantastic, beef is a bit chewy though.
Was not feeling the best so came here for some rice. Outstanding. Will come back later in the week when I am feeling better and give it a true test. Sure it will be great.

I used to visit Jai Thai at Katong for lunch when I worked in that area. After changing jobs, I really miss their Pineapple rice sets that comes with a generous serving of other sides at a total cost of $8.90++.The restaurant serve authentic thai food and it's really a delight to indulge. Another one of my favourite is their tapioca dessert which fortunately did not run out the evening I was there. The tapioca was sweet and warm with a generous amount of coconut milk.With Purvis Street near my current work place, I should be coming back again soon!

Value for money this food. I've tried the one at clover and this is my first time here :) it was a very hot day and the red ruby drink is an absolute treat. Although I would order it will less ice, else it would be like an ice kachang. The pad Thai at $5 is a steal! It's so delicious and big enough to share!

If you want something spicy, affordable and delicious.. Jai Thai is the place for you.They have an all day set menu ($12 and below). I am quite partial to their green curry rice set which comes with a bowl of rice, a bowl of green curry filled with ingredients, traditional Thai dessert of the day and a cup of drink. If you have a bigger stomach, you can try their pineapple rice set which comes with a plate of pineapple rice and a sample platter of their green curry, one spring roll, one pandan chicken, sweet and spicy fish. It also comes with their dessert of the day and a cup of drink. For the price you pay, I'll say it's worth it. Their pandan chicken well, it's amazing. I love it. It's $2 a piece but hey, it's pretty big. Do give Jai Thai a try if you are around the Purvis Street area!

Prawn cakes/fish cakes are a must for a starter.Followed by green curry, phad si euww. All the food here is pretty affordable, but also small portion, so just have to order more to fill up :) I didn't think the pineapple fried rice was any good. You could give it a try and let me know what you think though. I will come back to try other dishes.

My other go-to Thai place in Singapore and it is really near my office. I eat here during lunch and always order ala carte. I get that most office folks dig the set lunches which come in these flower shaped platters, but I prefer ordering 3-4 dishes (portions are more than adequate) with friends and it works out to about the same price. Food here is pretty close to what you'd get in Thailand.The fish and prawn cakes here are handmade and fried fresh, just like at Joe's Thai. The tom yam soup is authentic and therefore searingly spicy. Even for someone who comes from a line of chili kings & queens, Jai Thai sometimes gives me a stomach ache afterwards from the spiciness so I usually ask them to tone it down a bit. I also like the steamed tofu with basil chicken, which is a different take on the usual Thai basil chicken. Their prawn tung hoon (which is one of my barometers of a good Thai cook, along with beef soup and fried duck) is darn good too. Basically, I haven't found any dish that wasn't to my liking. Prices are ridiculously cheap but don't tell the restaurant that. Service is hit or miss and if you reach there any later than 12.30pm on a weekday and aren't willing to share a table, go look somewhere else because this place is always packed.

A personal favourite :) go quite a lot after work. Decent good cheap Thai food that is pretty authentic! I like the green curry, the fried rice with basil leaves, the Kai Lan and many others. mylifeinsin.com/2013/01/…

Craving for Thai food after class one day, I decided to head down to a Jai Thai outlet at Purvis Street since it was nearby. My friends had good reviews about the place, saying the food there was good and cheap so I agreed to give it a try. I ordered the Phad Thai since it is a Thai dish that can determine the standard of a good Thai restaurant. The dish was so fragrant that I could smell it the moment they brought it out of the kitchen. To my surprise, the Phad Thai was flavorful and fulfilling. The dash of lime balanced the sweetness of the dish and made it perfect. Also, it was not dry like how most Thai restaurants do it, so it was really palatable. The prawns were fresh, crunchy and succulent, while the little bits of egg were really tasty. The service was good, as the staff was warm and hospitable. I would probably go back again whenever I need a quick fix for a Thai food craving.

Nice hole in the wall with great food. I liked that is added some spice to my life. I love that you order like a sushi menu. Great prices considering a Singapore sling at the raffles long bar next door is 30 sing and is less then 2 blocks away. And the food was amazing. Great pad Thai and spring rolls.

For my money it's one of the best Thai restaurants in town - a (really) extensive menu, great tasting food, and relatively cheap prices in a clean, casual environment.  My favorite dishes are the fish cakes, tofu with basil chicken, and pandan chicken.  The tamarind prawns are also a fave.  I haven't had a dish here that didn't taste good.

This place is pretentious and overcrowded with people people watching and being watched in return. There, I got that off my chest. That said, the Prohibition Long Island Iced Tea Party is potent as heck, and the main reason I keep coming back. Not for the Bay Prawn Capellini, nor the risotto, lovingly referred to as bee hoon and mui fan by my fans-of-kopitiam friends. Not even the star truffle fries can detract from the booze. It comes in a Chinese tea pot, separate from the soda, which lets you adjust how strong you wish for it to be. And very strong is the way we like it. Granted, it's meant for three or four, but the two of us down it like sky juice. We always leave in a good mood and as a result, keep coming back.

House has been around for awhile now and they've really set themselves apart from the competition with creative marketing and interesting decor. I really give credit to the Spa Esprit group for always having fun and creative ideas in all their ventures. I was here in the late afternoon on a Saturday, with one aim only: to try the pearl barley salad, an item on House's new menu. I was initially informed by a waiter that they were no longer serving lunch at that hour. That is, no food at all, except for fries and pizza from a separate menu. I was so disappointed! I noted however that the next table was given the lunch menu when they were seated shortly after us. With an undefeated, must-have-my-salad attitude, I asked another waiter if I could still order food. Perhaps this waiter felt my desperation or was persuaded by my earnest plea. He responded in the affirmative and I quickly placed my order for taro truffle fries and pearl barley salad, as well as a bottle of san pellegrino, beer and a carrot, celery, juice (obviously my dining partner and I have extreme preferences for food).The pearl barley salad was a tad expensive at S$15 and S$3 extra for grilled chicken. The serving size was big but essentially the dish was lettuce, crispy quinoa and barley. I can't imagine ordering this salad without the grilled chicken as it would have been too plain. However, I enjoyed the salad as it was clean and very light. I could eat the entire huge plate of salad easily. Will come back to House again for this, as I'm a sucker for light and simple but tasty salads. Also, having barley and crispy quinoa in a salad is just genius and I don't think I can get this anywhere else.The truffle taro fries were predictably good and quite reasonable at S$7 for a huge serving. These were crazily addictive - no complaints. I would have rated House with 4 stars except that the service was somewhat of a let down. The servers were not attentive and were often chatting amongst themselves or behind the bar or crowding around in a group, instead of looking out to assist customers. The wait was long for everything and it was hard getting the attention of the servers. Not to mention the inconsistent position taken when I first arrived at the restaurant. Why was I informed that I could not have food from the lunch menu by one person, and otherwise by another person? The first waiter didn't even bother to try and check with the kitchen if I could order from the lunch menu. When I told him/her I wanted to order the salad, he/she (can't recall which), adamantly informed me that lunch was over. I often saw food and drinks waiting at the bar for servers to bring them to the tables. It's like the customers are waiting for the food and the food is waiting to be served to the customers, while the servers are standing around doing goodness knows what. Well, I'll probably still be back as I like the variety in the menu - healthy choices and comfort food all at the same place. Easy and free parking is a plus too. Will be back, but hopefully the service will improve. Also, isn't it just silly not to serve your full menu throughout the day, at least on weekends?! Most establishments even serve all day breakfasts on weekends, surely a big restaurant like House can afford to do so as well. And it's not like they suffer from lack of customers on weekends - the place was full when I was there at around 4 pm on Saturday.

Great place to taste Spa Esprit Group's food all in one place, a nice setting as well right in Dempsey facing the lush greenery. I would say that the food is a little pricey but all for good reason, great taste and great location. I've always enjoyed the chinese stewed fatty pork bun so when I saw an upscale version of it on the House menu, i had to try it. The best part about this version is the fatty pork is served piping hot in a mini pot, well marinated in a spicy dark sauce along with fresh buns on the side for you to stuff with how ever many slices of pork you wish. This dish also comes with a side of sweet potato fries almost like strips and light on the palette. If you're in the mood for something light, try their signature Tau Sar Pau instead with Asian red tea, there is a set meal going on for that if I remember correctly. Either way just sit back and enjoy Dempsey!

I'm a fan! House is a hip joint located on Dempsey Hill. You take stairs down to the restaurant (so be careful of how much alcohol you consume because you will have to climb those stairs again when you leave)!The interior is very chic with rustic and modern elements. Their menu adds perfectly to their branding and offers fare that is a fusion of Asian and American. The menu is Paleo-friendly (as long as you have steel will power). I started with a mixed berry gin fizz ($19), which was sweet and so refreshing that I ended up ordering another (which is why I forewarn about the stairs when leaving). We totally cheated by starting with the mustard chili fries ($9) and the pumpkin hazelnut fries ($12). They have about 6 varieties of different fries and they all look awesome, so it was a tough call! I ordered the blackened snapper with quinoa, kale and sweet peas ($25), as did the other two at my table. It was cooked perfectly and the medley of vegetables complimented it perfectly. The service was prompt and polite. They were excellent about bussing the table and refilling drinks, which is sometimes hard to find in Singapore. I really enjoyed our meal and will be back. I'm rating them 4.5 out of 5 stars because the prices were a bit high for what it was, but we'll definitely be back.

The last time I came for brunch was many years ago. So I thought I would walk down memory lane this weekend and come back for brunch. They used to have the loveliest breakfast menu. My Favourite is the seven layer pancakes. They still serve pancakes which I apparently ordered. Boy was I disappointed! It's dry and far from fluffy. My Husband ordered a duck confit eggs Benedict. It was a let down too. They are famous for the fries. So we ordered truffle fries; it was the best thing that was served on our table. And it wasn't even prepared fresh. We could tell it that the shoestring was frozen. I expected more from this acclaimed hidden gem.Expensive and food doesn't complement the price. I regret picking this spot over P.S cafe that weekend.

This place is very hard to find! We booked a table for two on a Sunday morning for brunch and we had the paella, tuna salad, and truffle taro fries.The paella was meh, the ahi tuna salad was a teriyaki-ish tuna stirfried with a lot of oil, and laid on top of a bed of garden greens. I expected my salad to be a nice, clean salad with raw tuna. What I got was a bit of an oily shock for me. Let's just say I didn't finish my salad.Now, this place is supposed to be famous for their fries. I do love taro, and taro AND truffle oil TOGETHER? Disappointment. The taro fries were cut way too thin - matchstick-like, and after being absolutely deep-fried and crunchy, the delicate taro flavor doesn't quite come through. I was just crunching through very fried sticks with a mild truffle flavor. I think the fries could have been cut thicker, so that the powdery texture of the taro and flavor could be tasted.The best part of this place is their juices. They have a good range of expensive, but tasty mix of vegetable and fruit juices.I would not come back again. Not even if it was free.

I was nicely surprised by House.  The menus were a bit annoying, but the food was really good.  The pumpkin salad was 90% pumpkin and 10% salad, so mis-named.  But it was delicious!  Also the fried seed cheese I would order again.  For mains I had the fish croquettas.  While I was disappointed my brunch mates would have to wait for my meal to cook the wait was not unreasonable and our starters kept us happy.  The pricing is standard Singapore 18-25 brunch menu fare.  Lastly, the group tried 2 desserts, the flourless chocolate cake was exactly  what you are looking for, dense, moist, delicious and chocolatey, and we got a fruity pinapple passion cake which tasted light and airy with a feeling of spring.  Coffees are standard.  I would go back once every 6 months or so.

3.5 stars. Came here for the unlimited buffet style high tea. It's a bit hard to find for a visitor like myself. It's not at the 8 block, you need to go further back until you see the sign that says House.The decor of this place is really nice and cute! And the food is laid out in a really beautiful manner. I may have stained a couple of books that were placed open near the food though, oops.While overall there aren't that many items that make you go WOW, most of the items are pretty good. The overall experience of having an unlimited amount of pretty tasty teatime snacks arranged in really decorative ways is pretty awesome. I wish there were more heat lamps though, most things got cold very fast.Tea comes with high tea, so we got the mango tea, which was pretty good.Items that stood out:Truffle mushrooms - So goodCheese spreads and crackers - Decent selectionFries were pretty good, but how they brought them out made no sense. They came in sparsely restocked cups with tons of ketchup and 3 fries. Then finally like 1 hour later a giant batch of fries only came outDeviled eggs were really goodOther various items that I remember:Flat pizzas - Pretty creative, but very varied in how crispy the bread part was. Also was not very warm.Spinach tart thing - Pretty good, but is a little too spinachy. It just tasted like.. green. I think the spinach flavor could be cut by something else.Various cakes and pies and pastries - Pretty good I guessSalad - eh. The pickled fish was a bit grossOverall left extremely full and pretty satisfied.

My second time here, this time, we were here to work. Unfortunately, unlike Jones the grocer, House does not provide free wifi, so we had to do tethering instead :( Also, the lighting isnt as great as Jones, so I guess it really is a better place for social gatherings rather than working.We ordered an Asian slider to share and absolutely loved the taro fries. I think the trick was truffle oil :/ It started to get really oily at the end so that felt really sinful, but the fries were REALLY GOOD. The asian slider was basically just kong bah pao. Decent too!Prices are slightly higher, but I guess this is pretty normal Dempsey range!Will probably only be back here for food.

Meh. Typical place that doesn't offer any flexibility to make slight changes on your dish even if you are willing to pay the charges. Can I substitute the salad with fries? No.. Can I just change the sweet potato fries to taro fries? Why of course not.. Price is a bit steep for what it is.

I enjoy visiting House at Dempsey - something about the concrete interior and high ceilings... it's a nice place to chill out with friends for brunch.My BFF swears by their truffle fries served in their metal tins, which are quite moreish. The Asian Sliders is really just braised pork and buns, but they do it quite well. The usual western mini-hamburger type sliders are also quite good. The brunch menu's eggs benedict/free form eggs are my usual order when I'm here, and while the 7-layer pancake sounds like a lot to stomach, it's actually only about 2-full pancakes, as it looks like a slice of crepe cake rather than 7 full pancakes. It's chockfull of fruits and cream though, yum.I love the way their menus present their food, done up to look like a faux lifestyle newsletter, excellent food photography is always so enticing!

The restaurant was situated around a nice green scenery which gave the place an open and natural vibe. I got a feel that each table and set of chairs were individually handpicked for the decor and no 2 sets were of the same design, which meant they put effort into selecting the decor.The food however took quite awhile to reach our table and we were already hungry by the time it got here. The dish that i ordered was the Moroccan spiced baby half chicken with sautéed fennel and taro fries. Sounds nice but the chicken meat was really dry and not tender at all, and the taro fries had no taste to it and was a little hard.The truffle fries are what stands out for me. Crispy with truffle fragrance, they were the best thing I had that day to save the meal. I would not go back there as it is kind of out of the way and food was not that fantastic.

This is a review of dinner at House.First up, when we first arrived, they did not have our reservation.  I showed them the reservation confirmation email from reserveit.sg   I am not sure why it was an issue.  The restaurant was less than half fullAfter asking us to sit at little sidebar and wait, they came back and said they could seat us.I really like the room.  It is open and airy.  It is also eclectic.  The tables are mostly independently selected and it creates a home-like feel.   While the tables are individually selected, I am not sure how careful the process was.  It certainly was, at times, form over function.  Our table (along with others) had a medal bar at the base.  This meant it was difficult to find a comfortable place for your feet.  Plus, for ladies with open toed shoes, it creates quite the hazard.Beyond the reservations hiccup, the service was pretty good.  it was attentive and timely.There were a couple of menu issues.  They did not have the bottle of wine I initially selected and they did not have the corn on the cob.  I had actually been looking forward to trying their corn.The food was inconsistent ranging from very  good to poor.Bread Medley with Chunky Dips - The breads and dip appetizer was pretty good.  I will note though that I've had better bread served for free at numerous restaurants.  The dips were relatively tasty but a very good olive oil and balsamic would have been just as nice.  tinyurl.com/9nm2ozjtinyurl.com/9fwak2tPrawns - These were quite nice.  The seasoning was done well.  it provided a nice basic foundation while allowing the taste of the prawns to shine through.  The prawns were very tender.tinyurl.com/9foa5wm Sliders with truffled aioli - The sliders were the stars of the meal, hands-down.  They were cooked to a perfect medium rare.  The beef was obviously of high quality.  The buns were soft.  These little sliders rocked the house and are reason enough alone to return to House.They look rather ordinary but they are oh so good. I will also note that they are served with a bunch of fries and sweet potato fries.  it is listed as a main.  I think this is a mistake.  I think they should serve them individually as appetizers.  We certainly ordered them as an appetizer.  But we were stuck with a ton of relatively good fries and not so good sweet potato fries.  The sweet potatoes were an epic fail.  I have no idea why they decided to bread them before frying them.  If they want to contact me, I will tell them step by step how to make really great sweet potato fries.  Because their way is simply not working.tinyurl.com/9bbktqbtinyurl.com/993qhbaHouse Rib-Eye Steak - My dinner companion ordered this.  She really enjoyed it.  I tried it.  i placed it at the level I expect from second tier steak house chains like Stuart Anderson's Black Angus.  But, it fell well short of what I expect from top-notch steak houses.  It was a reasonable cut but it was not overly tender.  It did not have the grainy fat that I expect from a rib-eye.tinyurl.com/9noe87xJamaican Jerk Pork Tenderloin - Then there was the greatest disappointment of the meal.  I knew it was a bit of a risky choice.  After-all, we are quite a ways from the Caribbean.  First, there was nothing Jamaican about this dish.  Second, there was nothing even resembling a jerk sauce.  It is obvious the chef has never had a real jerk sauce before.  Honestly though, I could have easily forgiven shortcoming in authenticity.  But, the pork was bone dry.  It was difficult to swallow.  Rule #1 of cooking pork is to keep it moist.  I ate most of it.  I will note that the presentation was quite pretty.  There was lots of color.  Unfortunately, there wasn't any real flavor with that color.tinyurl.com/8mgnlrwOverall, it is a beautiful room, the staff is friendly, and the flow of the meal was managed well.  There were some gaps with the reservation and missing menu items.  The food was wildly inconsistent.  For the sliders, I will return though.  If not for the sliders, this would have probably been a two star review.

Upon arriving at the cafe, the host didn't tend to us nor tell us to wait, he was busy chatting away in his phone.When he finally attended to us, he took a long time looking for our reservation and gave us a seat right under the blazing sun even when we requested to be seated inside where it was vacant.The menus for the beverages came in an overused gross soiled condition. Sure printing a new piece of menu doesn't cost too much.When our drinks came, our dear waiter got our orders mixed up. The prices of the place are way overpriced for a corporate chain trying to cash in on the hipster trend. To be far the food tasted decent but not worth the price as it didn't come with good service.To sum up this review, eat your food before going to the men's toilet as it absolutely stinks.

Most high tea in Singapore are on weekends and public holidays, it is rather 'rare' to find a weekday high tea buffet.  House@Dempsey chooses to be different, they have their high tea buffet "Vintage Tea Party" only on thursdays and fridays. I have been to many high tea buffets but this is probably one of the better high tea buffets. There are huge spread of items to choose from but they come in different "batches". One word of advice, don't stuff yourself silly to what you see on the buffet table, pace yourself for the varieties. In fact, the recent visit, I realized that some of the more interesting items, came out towards the end of the buffet hours. Aside from their high tea buffet, some of my favorites here are their Big Breakfast Skinny Pizza, Truffle Fries, Tiffin Punch's, and their version of Long Island Ice Tea. Great place to chill with friends or even have corporate offset meetings.
The fries and fresh squeezed juices are nice.  The beinget was raw and uncooked on the inside.  The pizza was terrible.  Nice place to hang out, but I didn't find the food good

I love the warm, welcoming feeling of this place! The service staff were attentive and made the experience there a pretty good one. I was only there for dessert and hence can only comment so much on their foods. It turned out that having desserts here was a brilliant choice as their warm strawberry shortcake was absolutely divine!My friend and I got their warm strawberry shortcake (a known house specialty) and the blackforest cake, along with a pot of white rose tea. While the blackforest cake was decent, with a generous serving of kirsch spiked cherries embedded in it, the strawberry shortcake stole the show with its warm, moist and hearty goodness. The natural strawberry flavour was present in every bite and the vanilla sauce that was served to accompany it made it a heavenly treat. The tea went well with the cakes! Very fragrant and heart-warming. Loved it!

Tired of the concrete jungle and you need to escape to somewhere peaceful and quiet? Why not try House? Nestled in the forest of Dempsey Hill, the former British military barracks has been converted into a trendy and somewhat whimsical dining place. Ample parking at Dempsey hill has made this place wonderful easy to visit during the packed lunch hour. Especially if you want to avoid the ERP zones and crowded carparks in the city! You definitely have to give the Barracks Good ole Halibut Fish n Chips, Black Pepper Linguine, Squid ink paella a try. If you're just feeling peckish, their amazing truffle fries would do just fine! Check out their Vintage themed high tea that's available on Thursdays and Friday from 3pm onwards that serves a range of both sweet and savoury bites.

I like the creativity that goes into establishments like House, turning what was essentially a former office in a barrack (my uncle used to work here) into a restaurant. Yes, there is an air of silly brunching snootiness to the restaurant, but that can be said of most restaurants in Dempsey. Yes, the prices here can leave you balking, but I take it as payment for rent and free parking. The food here is quite simply...inconsistent, which is something I've experienced at other yuppy joints. That doesn't make things ok. They make really good sweet potato and truffles fries, but really, it's not rocket science to sprinkle truffle salt and market an ingredient that is as ubiquitous on menus these days as oh forbid, foie gras. They do a really good prawn capellini, but it really depends on your luck. On my most recent visit two Sundays ago, I waited half an hour for my pasta and it arrived bone dry. No funky Asian stock with al dente noodles. Just a really dry noodle cake. I sent back my order asking the waiter if the chef could add some stock . No one got back to me about my dish. Instead I waited another half hour before the waiter returned with a newly cooked capellini (I'm sorry but isn't it logical to ask your customer if they'd like to wait half an hour for a dish you screwed up?) and remarked, "let us know if there's anything wrong with it".No apologies. Ok.If by chance you're patient enough after an hour, an order of sliders may just show up. Again, with a waiter anxious to shove it on your table without any apologies. It will turn up dry despite your request for medium rare sliders. The sauce you were asked to choose doesn't come, so you basically eat a sauce-less burger. Add to that of course, coffee orders that show up later than the food, requests to check on the kitchen met with waiters running away as quickly as possible.If there's a lesson in restaurant management gone wrong, Gordon Ramsay has a winning episode here. Waiters are assigned to deliver drinks or food, not care for your table. The kitchen sections seem to work out of concert, not giving a crap about whether 2 diners get their french toast while the other 2 receive their food up to an hour later (and that's me being nice with time estimation). As someone hoping to do justice to the state of food quality and service in this country, I'm speaking with my wallet. You couldn't pay me to step foot in this restaurant again. Not even with pau, pasta, truffles or heck, Ryan Gosling busing my table.

I've been here several times but had a different experience each time. Somehow the service standard is really inconsistent, thank goodness the food is not that bad.Most recently, I came here for dinner. We had a party of 5 and ordered a fair share of starters, sides and mains. We would've ordered dessert too, if not for the poor service.So our orders were placed, and our salads and three different types of fries (curry, sweet potato and carrot fennel) arrived in a decent amount of time. We were famished so we finished everything really quickly. The only exception was the carrot fries.... it's like a weird tempura carrot and it's too soggy. I wouldn't even consider it a healthier option because come on, it's deep fried how healthy can that be?? Not worth the calories.Everything started to go downhill from here. We waited at least 45 minutes to an hour for our mains to arrive. We kept checking with the staff but we got increasingly more impatient because they seemed to have done nothing to help our situation.Finally, a waitress told us that she had placed the orders for our starters first, and she decided to only place the orders for our mains after we finished our starters...... I guess that's an acceptable reason but still, it wouldn't take 45 minutes to prepare our mains, especially when the neighboring tables all got served though they were seated much later than us!!I accept their reason but I'm very disappointed that they did not show sincerity in their apology. The long wait for our mains really killed our appetite, and the entire dinner was ruined because nobody apologized for the long wait.I really doubt I'll return anytime soon. Their food is alright but maybe it's better to come on weekdays when it is less crowded.In terms of food, I think quite a few things are overpriced. Their truffle fries are really good though, and so are their thin-crust pizzas.Please check out my blog (on my profile) for more!

I really like the setting here. The outdoor patio facing the trees is really quiet and relaxing on a nice evening. The food is hit and miss. It's one of those places in Singapore that has gone to great lengths to appear to be western but is missing the mark on a lot of the menu items and hasn't quite got the hang of service. Really you just shouldn't try to make a substitution or ask for something on the side. The confusion will take up half your evening.  That said we've still managed to have some nice times here.  As others have mentioned, the desserts and drinks are the stand-out menu items. I'm not a fan of their "pizza" experiment so I'd give that a miss.

This place is really cute - the furniture is a bit mixy-and-matchy - giving it a really welcoming feel. This place is known for it's pizzas. Although I personally thought my order was barely alright (spinach and egg pizza) - my friends really liked their orders. I was sort of giving up on this place when we all shared the pear cake, fudge cake, and also the lemon cheesecake, all of which were super great and awesome.I'd go back again just for the desserts =)

great brunch place and a very cool spot to eat and lounge in general. spanish baked eggs - hearty, tasty and loved the bread and small skillet it came inthe club - SO stinking good! the bacon was crispy and the amount of chicken was sizable. i would come back for this again and again.pate - was only ok, i prefer my pate to be creamier. however, i liked that they have a wide variety of cured meats to choose from and i'm very curious about their other options. all in all, really enjoyed it and one of the few places i've had a good western meal.

Situated right at the entrance with beautiful people sitting and eating, there must be something special about this place! I wanna look beautiful too and boy, I wanna look cool. Luckily there's space and they're opened till 10pm. It's expensive wanting to sit here and look cool.. I gave the coffee a miss because I'm not shelling out 9 bucks for coffee I'm unsure of. The food is good.. Expensive but...you are paying for location to be seen. And it isn't that bad.. The food I mean. Had the papardalle pasta ($24)with slow roasted beef cheeks, stewed in a ragout style and little kales and mushrooms. The atmosphere is seen to be seen and somebody needs to tell them they need to equalize their music.. Too dang sharp to hang out there now :( They offer lots of variety in snacks and coffee. Would I come back? Nah.. Not really. To hang out with friends yeah I could.

Located upstairs on the 2nd FL of another sleek shopping complex around the area, this was a pleasant spot to wind away in. The lighting is a cool soft-hue but sufficient and the shelves have a neat organized array of stuff.I had a quest of looking for different chai to try around the island and I was able to check this one off of my very non-solid list, lol. It was mentioned that it's made in-house so those are always curious to me... It was a nice chai latte and also had nice presentation from the simple art and the popsicle stick laid on top with some sort of spice dashed on it for taste (cinnamon, nutmeg... not sure, could also be the chai powder). Whatever it was, I just dumped it in, stirred it up and drank it. Perhaps like anything with powder, it's best enjoyed warm and regularly stirred, 'else you swallow clumps waiting for you at the end. ;) Anywho, this was a nice subtle--if not lacking--chai latte. I probably should've checked about cinnamon and nutmeg [and sugar], which I always enjoy mixed in.Staff was good and felt welcoming.The chairs at the window bar, where I sat, are sort of neat molded wood stool types. The backrest has a height adjustment but the wing nut screwed on wanted Hulk strength to loosen... ;/ These types of wood chairs are SO comfy with the right setting.

Sunday brunch, the holy grail of the weekends. If you're looking for a well-located place, this is it! Ride the escalator located outside of Mandarin Gallery (on the side nearer to H&M) and you're magically transported right to The Providore's doorstep. Definitely magical because once you step through those doors, you leave the humidity of Singapore's weather outside - which was what we were looking for on a really sunny and warm Sunday afternoon. We were quickly seated as there was no queue and relatively little patrons when we arrived - there was a queue when we left, so my advice is to really get there a little earlier though the accepted is a late Sunday brunch. All I have to say is the early bird catches the worm! Service was quick as well - we ordered drinks first, and subsequently they actually came round thrice to ask if we were ready to order food! Iced Latte as usual for me, while the partner had a Musk Earl Grey Tea. The iced latte was nothing to shout about, it's just habit that I have my morning coffee. The musk earl grey tea smelt divine and tasted great as well - earl grey tea served with slices of citrus (lime, lemon and orange slices to be exact). After much deliberation, I ordered the Lobster Mac and Cheese - it was yummy, but overall a disappointment. While the lobster and pasta tasted great in the cheese sauce, it was cheese sauce. My standards of great mac and cheese start and end with the macaroni being engulfed in gooey cheesy goodness. This one lacked that, the cream sauce was thin with a hint of blue cheese - a more creamy rather than cheesy version of what would've been perfect because the sauce really tasted awesome. The partner had the Ham and Cheese Toastie, which was totally awesome - made me regret not ordering the steak sandwich instead because of a ham and cheese could be elevated like that, I would really loved to have tried what they could do with steak and bread. Unfortunately, we probably will not be back here unless a twist of fate brings us back to The Providore - he found this place for brunch at 3am in the morning through Google and glad to say, he decided on his dish based on photos posted by fellow Yelpers! Overall, it was a good experience with speedy service but I wouldn't be back here again for brunch - maybe to buy alcohol as they have a selection of wines and spirits that aren't frequently seen around.

More of a cafe than a restaurant but with restaurant prices. I suppose the location is nice and it does have a nice balcony overlooking orchard. The pasta was a bit watery. It just missed an opportunity. It needs to be thicker or richer in some way. Salad was ok and no complaints. I would come back to try their coffee and dessert as I like the venue as a cafe. Not so impressed with the food so far. Actually their meats and cheeses look nice as they have a deli corner.  The service is so so. They forgot our water and give us another table's bill.

I am a fan, the food is excellent and healthy. It is a tad expensive but I would not expect otherwise given the quality and location of this place. A random find that I warmly recommend to those who love simple and high quality meals and olive oil.

Terrible service.We got there at about 10:20p. They said we have to finish by 10:40p.But in reality, they close at 11p. I guess they just wanted us out of their hair.We ordered the Lemon Meringue cake, Cookies and Cream Cheesecake, Rocky Road, and Chocolate ice cream cookie. The only item that was nice was the Rocky Road. The Lemon Meringue cake was alright. but the cookies and cream cheesecake was horrible. it was very bland. we didn't think they used oreo for the crumbs. not sure what it was. some knock-off oreo maybe? chocolate ice cream cookie was non-descript. the ice cream was very bland.
If you crave for refreshment coffee and some sweet treat, this place is recommended. Coffee was nice, flavoury, not too acid. Ambience was nice, good service. I like their cakes and ice cream too

The Iced Cappuccino is disappointing. The coffee was bland as the taste of the coffee was not strong, even the milk taste wasn't apparent. The Flat White's blend came from Toby's Estate, so you know what to expect. Great coffee! The Roasted New Potatoes with Rosemary and Romesco Sauce was well sauteed and roasted to perfection, its enough to be eaten on its own. Have it, however, with the Romesco sauce for a mild spicy and tangy taste. The Spatchcock Chicken is a chicken that had their backbone removed so that it can be flattened before roasting it with lemon & thyme, garlic & shallots, verjus & Creme Fraiche sauce. This resulted in a crispy skin and each piece of chicken tasting juicy and flavourful. It is one that must be ordered here! The Red Velvet Cake had disappointed a bit. The cake did not crumble easily, the taste of the cake were alright, but the taste of butter/cheese was in near absence in the cream used. Nonetheless, the quantity was enough to delight both of us.
Great brunch food with a view of Orchard's hustle and bustle.  Service is a bit hectic, though, and it can get a bit hot sitting outside.

This place is just around the corner from the office, so an obvious choice. It is a nice place to sit: you see the tout-Singapore parading by - or at least part of it. One must say that the serving staff is very friendly (although when I asked what time it was, one gave me the Philippines time ;) Not cheap but this is not a cheap location. Count about 16 S$ for a sandwich. The quality is variable: I had a few times the cheese/ham sandwich which is quite good - a bit better than a croque monsieur. A few days ago, I had the slow baked salmon sandwich which unfortunately was veeeery slow (a group of local women may have been the reason). But it also tasted poor: the tapenade was barely noticeable, the salmon had no taste and the other things - what were they again?

I went here twice.  I feel their food is better than jones n they serves decent cuppa. I really like their muesli w yogurt, n I've tried their portobello mushroom w sourdough bread which the bread is not to my liking. I also tried their red velvet cake which is dissapointing
Well, service is terrible, food is limited, beverages are abundant, and prices are astronomical for the lack of care and ambience.  No love given, no love received!

This place looks nice from the outside. The Providore charges more and gives you less than the competition that it is so obviously copying.  Case in point: $12.50 (!!!) for two (of the smallest I've ever seen)  eggs on ONE slice of (insufficiently) toasted bread that is cut twice to look like two pieces.  An insidious move that fools no one.The BLT was tiny and overpriced. We have way too many better choices for the same fare better executed, as the other reviewer mentioned. Good review, Irene was overly generous about them not being able to, as she says, muck up breakfast. For some, Toast can be a difficult thing to master.

The menu looks delicious and was full of promise, but my dinner here fell flat.  We had the lobster mac and cheese, tuna tartare, choux buns, mackerel crostini, beetroot and goat cheese, and stuffed pork.  The flavors for the most part were there and the presentation was good, but nearly everything was overcooked (with the exception of the beet which was cut too thick and not quite roasted long enough) - the lobster in the mac and cheese, the mackerel on the crostini, and the pecorino stuffed pork were overcooked and really dry.  Decent service by Singapore standards.  I also took a peek at the desserts and they really didn't look up to snuff - too rough around the edges and not appealing at all.  If I had to choose between here or Foodology for some western small plates, I'd pick Foodology by a mile - better value, more extensive menu, and better execution.  That said, I'm willing to give them another try once they worked out the kinks.  Breakfast looks promising and should be more difficult to muck up.

I know I know...this place is good for its peking duck! But not everyone is in love with duck, just like me... So I had to order its roasted chicken.. Verdict is: It's damn fuckin good, the meats are roasted to perfection, very juicy and succulent... They also provide additional spiced salt on the side for you to sprinkle on top of your chicken! The skin is also heavenly crispy, very nice texture and the saltiness is just right! However, other than roasted duck or chicken, other food menu just taste mediocre and bland (probably because they promote low sodium diet??! So could be either good or bad depends on individual..)Hint: might need to reserve due to high popularity among locals and expats (both for table and roasted chicken/duck..no kidding)...

My family & I go to this restaurant because of their famous dish, Peking Duck & most of their customers, just like us, usually order one whole duck :):):) The roasted duck skin is crispy, not greasy & the skin is not thick at all. Really worth your calories . The balance of the duck meat - we usually ask the Chef to fry it with Ee fu noodles together with mushroom. And then, we will add black vinegar to it. So yummy.......Another yummy dish is their soup. The Chef uses superior broth for the soup. They boil their soup for hours & we can taste the sweetness of it. Very worth dining in this restaurant.

The Peking duck is really good here and I wouls definitely recommend it. But I do suggest that you book the table in advance and also reserve the duck. You don't want to turn up at your table and be told no duck left!The Peking duck is served three ways with a chef displaying his duck cutting skills. The first serving is the duck skin which you dip in sugar. The duck skin was crispy and we hardly noticed any fat on it.The second serving is the duck meat which we wrapped in pancake, with cucumbers, spring onions and hoi sin sauce.The third and final serving is the one where you can choose how you would like the remaining duck meat to be cooked. For an additional charge, we choice the remaining duck meat stir fry with noodles. I actaully prefer this over the lettuce wrap which you usually find in most the restaurants I have had Peking duck.Peking duck is an intereating dish because it is clever how one duck can create three different dishes!

one of my favorite restaurants, from possibly my favorite group of restaurants in singapore - I associate the imperial treasure line of restaurants (referring to the higher echelons here) with reliable, delicious, traditional cooking in sleek, modern environs and I haven't been let down by a meal here before.it's one of my family's regular haunts for dimsum or a good dinner, and the eponymous dish is glisteningly shiny and crisp, the meat tender and really rather juicy. they slice off the skin with some of the best parts of the duck for you to dip in sugar (sounds weird, but tastes great), before the thicker, more substantial slices arrive to be wrapped in thin egg skins with slivers of cucumber and spring onion.you then have the choice to take your duck sliced and eaten neat, or to have it cooked up (there's a surcharge for this latter option). it commonly goes into a noodle stir-fry, but we like it chopped up and salt-and-peppered into garlicky, bony chunks. it's not an option if you a. don't like garlic or b. don't like bones, but the kitchen's probably expert enough to cater to your choice.we finished with a sweet heavy-on-the-plum sauce pork rib that was very fatty (but therefore also very juicy) in a sauce that was possibly too sweet, and some cleansing greens topped with mushrooms.it's good food - and for such a lovely, sleek restaurant, prices aren't too expensive. the restaurants at the higher price points in the imperial treasure group all make fantastic options for great chinese food, at qualities you'd usually associate with the old-school, venerated hotel chinese restaurants (that have price points to match).

I come here for my Peking duck fix! The duck here is superb, with a thin, crispy, flavorful skin that doesn't have too much fat. The meat is also tender, and the skins that you wrap it up in are wonderfully thin, so it does not detract from the taste.You ate asked to eat the skin dipped in a bit of sugar first, as that's how it was traditionally eaten in the past. After that you move on to have the duck in the wrap. The dark sauce is thick and sweet, but not overly so.At $68 for a whole duck, it's pretty good value for a nice dinner. You definitely have to make reservations and order it in advance as they have a limited number of ducks, so walk-ins normally won't be entertained. I went on a Friday evening and all the tables were booked out. We were also asked to vacate our table by a certain time for the next customers.We also tried the roasted suckling pig and it was fantastic. The skin was thin and crispy, not too much fat, and after you are done, they chop up the rest of the pig for you.The ambience is that of a typical Chinese restaurant, and the whole place has been done up very nicely. Service is fast and efficient, but the place does get a bit manic when it's busy. Great place for family dinners to impress the parents! :)

Yay! I like this place. Mostly consistently good food (a couple duds I will point out later). I've been to this branch twice, once for a company dinner and today for dim sum with family!Peking duck - order in advance! $68 for whole duck. And $10 for add on stir fry meat, or meat in noodle/rice, or lettuce wraps. We had the lettuce wraps the first time and weren't particularly enamoured with it. Today we had the duck meat stir fried in black pepper sauce (the way the AMAZING black pepper beef is done), that was pretty gd but not as good as the beef! The black pepper beef is to die for. Seriously. It melts in your mouth. Oh, also, it's spicy :) Just a warning.Dim sum here is fairly reasonable, about $4+-$6+ per basket of dim sum. Goodies first:1. Har gao - 4 plump juicy ones nested inside, thin enough skin, bouncy prawns ($5)2. Crispy prawn rice roll - Cheong fan with almost a tempura type of prawn inside, served with the soy sauce on the side so it doesn't get soggy ($6) - this I first had in Hong Kong and so really doesn't match up to that version, but was still pretty gd. My bro's favourite dish!3. Normal prawn rice roll - delicious! thin skin and yummy sauce. $5.504. Carrot cake - chunks of radish inside! $4.20 for 3 pcs. nice pan fry. Mom liked it.5. Liu sha bao - this was rated as one of the top five in Singapore by Daniel Ang (food blogger), I thought it was pretty gd but wasn't all that amazed by it..
