Again, I have to emphasize that nothing was bad about the meal, and perhaps we were just expecting a little more and it did not satisfy.

Buko Nero has a casual upscale vibe which bodes well for good, honest Italian food. And I heard that the chef/owner is Italian so I got my hopes up. Unfortunately I found the experience to be underwhelming. They had a hamachi carpaccio as a special appetizer that sounded interesting. None of the other specials grabbed me so I ordered the risotto entre off the main menu. I really liked the concept of the hamachi, but the delivery was stunted by the hamachi itself. There was more than a bit of a funk to it; definitely not sashimi-grade so it should not have been served raw. And the risotto was flat. I'm a sucker for a good risotto, but this one failed on every level. The rice was chewy, almost crunchy and there was no umami. Overall just bland a chalky. I've heard good things about Buko Nero so perhaps I just order the wrong things. Maybe I should have asked for more guidance from the nice hostess, but I don't think I'll be back to find out.

Gorgeous food, excellent service and nice ambience.  The chef is creative, thoughtful and detail to attention.  The set dinner is great value for money and the daily special is fantastic.  Excellent for date night or group dinner.  Will be back!

One of the secret addresses in Singapore - although I'm not sure why: is it because of its size or its interesting fusion cuisine? It certainly is tiny (can only accommodate 20 people at the same time) and has an interesting fusion menu that combines South Asian and Italian cuisine. Impossible to get a table without reservation before 9 PM. The interior is modern - white being the primary color, and the service very personal (all in the family).Some combinations are interesting.

Seriously this place has one of the best crispy and thick waffles I have ever eaten! When I placed my order, the waiter came to tell me it would take at least 15 minutes. I ordered a sour plum soda $3 + $1 for iced. It tasted good to me, my mother had expected it to be a bit sweeter.Rum and Raisin Waffles $9++When it was served to me, it looked so brown, I had wondered if it was burnt, but it didn't smell burnt. The ice cream tasted strong of alcohol, there were raisins in the ice cream and in almost every pocketed square of the waffle as well! The waffle was so crispy and because it was a very thick waffle, it was still fluffy on the inside. Even my mother compliment the waffle, and she rarely has great things to say about waffles, considering she made waffles for breakfast just yesterday.All in all, they serve a variety of food and I will be back to try more main course and definitely for more waffles!

Heard that the food was good so I came to try it, but left disappointed.Waffles were soggy, meat wasn't well seasoned and didn't taste like much inside.Food was expensive. No air-con. No free tap water and cash only.Seriously, restaurant prices for a hawker experience... don't bother.

Sometimes it's really hard to find a nice place for dinner in the neighbourhood that has a good ambiance and also open till late. Bliss Restaurant may not serve the best food around, but it certainly has a nice chilling atmosphere for you to sit and enjoy a nice supper or late night drink with a good friend.I never knew the Community Centres can be so hip until I visited Bliss Restaurant at Cheng San CC. The food was so-so but the environment is pretty good. Besides the "hu" and the "hah" from the guys in the basketball court doing taekwando or other activities, it's actually pretty enjoyable. You can choose from the alfresco outdoor dinning (it can get rather dim so you may not really be able to see what you are eating) or the indoor dinning (for those who cannot live without aircon).They also have an interesting selection of alcohol from beer to wines and even cocktails. For some sweet bites, the selection of desserts is still decent but of course, not comparable to a town restaurant.The price is economical and overall experience. Wouldnt mind hanging out there again soon.

Bliss used to be at Punggol Park and it served the residents in the area very well. Waterfront dining by the pond was awesome. That's till it got taken over by Wild Oats. :( Nevertheless, we managed to hunt it down at Cheng San Community Center. It's quite a chill place if you stay on till late, which we did, with our bottle of Moscato. The drinks list is pretty extensive, like it was at Punggol Park. The service is more attentive now that the space is smaller and brighter (the servers can finally see our faces). Beer, cocktails, wines etc are available along with Western mains and snacks and desserts.We had some finger food which were not too bad. In my alcoholic state, i could hardly remember what i ate but i vaguely remember the cheese fries which were quite good and chicken wings maybe? The mud pie wasn't too shady as well.In all, not a bad place to get decent food and wine at affordable prices.

A new found place to have a glass or two beer. It is located in a community center near to Ang Mo Kio MRT. The restaurant offers quite a variety of alcohol drinks besides the usual western menu. Something special in a neighbourhood.What we like about the place is that it offers alcohol at a reasonable price and not crowded. The pace there is slow and you can enjoy the night sitting there. Another good thing is that it is easily accessible, out of safety concern. we can take public transport back after in take of alcohol.Never had the chance to try any main dish there. But from observation, serving are quite big but serving time is quite slow. We ordered fries to go along with the beer. Beer took some time to be serve and fries took even longer. It was serve after we are half through our beer. But what's the hurry when you are at a slow pace place. Totally acceptable

Located within Cheng San Community Center, Bliss restaurant is an alfresco-themed restaurant serving western food. Their menu presents quite a standard selection of western food - grilled chicken, steak, pastas, fish.I ordered their grilled chicken and sausage, priced at $18.90 before GST. The presentation of the dish was pretty well done. However, the taste was normal: nothing good nor bad about the dish. After main course, my friends and I ordered some of their desserts: Choke on Choc and a Banana split. When it came, the portion was humongous. One can literally choke on the amount of ice cream served. We left the restaurant barely able to finish the desserts.I would say that their desserts were pretty good, but the main course meals were a bit on the expensive end, considering the quality of food. Service was slow, even for a a relatively empty restaurant. I recommend Bliss restaurant for some after meal desserts.

As part of a large Community Club, Bliss Restaurant is hard to miss. With both an air-conditioned interior and an open-air exterior complete with candles perfect for chilling out with a drink alone or with friends, Bliss can accomodate a huge crowd. The food offered is reasonably tasty, with standard western fare like pasta and meat dishes. Their finger food stands out as awesome tidbits to share with friends and family. However, the selection of alcohol Bliss Restaurant offers makes one almost spoilt for choice. Picking your poison and pairing it with the proper dishes elevates the flavours and amplifies the experience.

I've not done a review in ages but this bar is worth the time. I can see from other reviews that it is good for other stuff as well (breakfast, high tea etc) but this bar scores well for ambience, its drinks and attentive service. My girlfriend and I had the Lord Kane and Tea Time cocktails, which were relatively refreshing with a decent kick. Perhaps the only kink to mention would be the range of drinks available. If they had more choices, it would be perfect.

I had heard about this place a few times, and I was fortunate that my Amex card allowed me a 20% discount menu-wide here, so I thought to pop by to try the place.They have a good list of cocktails here, and I can't remember what I had to drink, but they were strong and hit the spot (I mostly drink gin cocktails). We also ordered oysters, which were a steal (a dozen at $36 I think), though I do wish they had green tabasco. The oysters also came beautifully presented, which I really love.The convenient location in a hotel and the dark vibes at night make it a nice location for a date, as seen by a few canoodling couples on a Friday night. It does get busy at prime times, you may want to make a reservation.

Anti:dote is one of my favorite bars in Singapore. To me it ranks higher than some others which are on the prestigious World Best Bars list but each to their own. This review is for the evening bar, I've never experienced their seemingly popular high tea.I like to sit at the bar, which is beautifully lit and watch the bartender craft their cocktails. I have tried several cocktails from their menu but after a few visits I have decided that their Old Fashioned with Diplomatico rum is one of my favourite drinks ever.The oysters are decently priced (for a bar in Singapore) and are of good quality. Actually, most food on the menu is a very good match with their drinks. Another fave of mine are the cod croquettes and surprisingly I love the olives which come complimentary.Summarized: Atmosphere: A+, Service: A+, Drinks: A+, Food: A+Recommended!

Their lobster roll with caviar on the charcoal bun was pretty good. I like the ambience and the location. I would go back for their afternoon tea except it's not served everyday only on Fridays which is annoying ( hence the 4 stars!)

At the lobby of Fairmont Singapore, there is this restaurant called Anti:dote well known for its bar. But do you know it also served tea set?The restaurant offers 2 types of tea sets : The Anti:dote Tea and The Oriental Tea which costs $45++, and comes with a choice of tea from a selection of TWG tea. Both tea sets are similar except that The Anti:dote Tea has The Anti:dote black truffle scrambled eggs, while The Oriental Tea serves a selection of steamed and fried Hong Kong Dim Sum. There is also Children Tea set ($15) but need to pre-order in advance.For tea,Tibetan Secret An exclusive green and black blendAs dramatic and uplifting as the Himalayan plains, this remarkable delicate TWG black tea is blended with sweet fruits and spicy overtones to soothe and revive the spirit.It tastes slightly gingery spicy.Holiday In ParisAn exclusive white blendRare Yin Zhen and sweet vanilla have been blended as an ode to a leisurely promenade along the cobblestone streets of Paris. Nard and wild flowers decorate this cup with their crisp, floral flavour and leave a heady, perfumed aftertaste.It tastes rather light with a slight flowery taste.For The Anti:dote Tea set,The Anti:dote black truffle scrambled eggs is served in black colored egg shell look alike cup, with soldiers by the side. The scrambled eggs smell of truffle and tastes creamy and rich.For The Oriental Tea set,There is pan fried carrot cake which looks slightly over fried as it is a bit too char. The inside is a bit too soft. There is also the fried shrimp fritter which is filled with juicy shrimps. Have it with the delicious chilli sauce.For steamed, there is Siew Mai topped with a piece of juicy scallop.The tea set is beautifully served in box with 3 layers of drawers with different items in each drawer.From the bottom drawer, there is Butter Cookies, Homemade Strawberry Jam, Devonshire Clotted Cream, and Lemon Curd. The butter cookie is melt in the mouth with a milk powder taste.In the middle drawer, there is the pipping Warm Raisin and Candied Ginger Scones. The ginger scone is not overpowered by the ginger, just a hint of it. It tastes very nice with just the rich clotted cream and slightly tangy lemon curd.In the top drawer, there is Smoked salmon, lemon and dill cream cheese, ikura roe,Boston lobster roll, confit lemon, chervil,Iberico ham quiche, mozzarella, black truffle,Confit duck rillette, foie gras terrine, pickled onions, and Coronation curried chicken, apple.Surprisingly my favourite item here turns out to be the plain looking quiche which quite a nice taste of the truffle.On top of the drawer, there is Strawberry gateau,Limoncino Napoleon,Cappuccino comtessa,Framboise lychee macaron,Red cherry rose ball,Karukera chocolate mirror tart,Chocolate pralines, andChocolate-dipped strawberry.Unlike the usual macarons with over the top sweetness, the one here is not too sweet with a melt in the mouth texture.Overall the tea set is quite tasty and pretty looking. The armchair is quite comfy and roomy. Service is not bad with the staffs checking on us from time to time. Remember to check out the unisex restroom before leaving. It has a rather interesting 2-in-1 Dyson tap. Besides being a tap, it's also a dryer.

Came for a nightcap on a Friday. Service was pretty fast and attentive. Good variety of cocktails - I recommend the Corpse Reviver, which is gin- and absinthe-based. Interior is nice, but a little too brightly lit for a bar. It has that odd smell that every hotel uses, so overall it feels a little too sanitised, if that makes any sense. As far as hotel bars go, I thought this was pretty impressive. 3.5 stars.

Went during what happened to be Singapore cocktail week.  They had a guest bartender from Speak Low the world famous bar, which was cool.  He made some killer cocktails.  The small plates they have on the menu were just ok though, and service was actually pretty bad.

no speakeasy here, just pure intoxication under broad daylight!a big thanks to carolyn, as it was her free cocktail week wristbands that brought me here in the first place!having been to 28 hong kong street just the night before, the comparative experience was like night versus day.and anti:dote might well become my next deadly sin!love the decor, opulent yet inviting.with space for the single alcoholic, the lovey dovey pair and communal AA group!even though the dress code is supposed to be smart casual, i have not been turned away nor frowned upon judgmentally despite not meeting that criteria. their staff from the greets to the bartenders to the servers were all very polite, attentive, knowledgeable and professional.the bartenders in particular were very chatty.friendly banter constantly interjected between their busy shaking schedules.the cocktail week menu's milk punch was an interesting concoction.cognac based, milk whey, orange and coriander.i was initially apprehensive about the coriander but luckily it was just the most subtle hint of it.milk whey gave the cocktail a shot of milkiness without overly clouding the drink.whisky lovers like myself and yenny took to this drink like fish to water.i went back the next night and had the sherry cobbler.oloroso sherry, bourbon, homemade falernum and lime juice.this had a nice tropical feel and just sipping it, instantly teleported me to the beach.the free flow crisps and wasabi peanuts were so addictive and made me crave for more drinks!but here is where you need to pause for a cause and peruse their bar bites menu.the list reads like poetry.i need to eat, one of each!and you will definitely find one that satiates.if not, then just salivate watching others partake.the perfect antidote for hunger!p.s. if you really need free wifi, pm me for the secret code.

Sit by the bar. The bartender is cute, funny and totally knowledgeable. I had the sour plum pisco which tasted exactly like the dried sour plums. Sweet, salty and sour.  Totally refreshing on a hot summer evening. There are plenty of cocktails at hotel bar prices to choose from. But hey most cocktail places are about $25++ per drink anyway. What's fabulous however is the snacks of olives in brine and chips. Shamelessly asked for double servings. Definitely a YES!

A poster child for unwitting bad customer service. They can't even get the morning coffee and pastry special right. The deal only applies if you take it to go. If you want enjoy it right there and then you get anxiety filled looks as if you're breaking some major rule. In some case you're reminded that you actually can't enjoy your coffee and pastry there. Just awful. Their obsession with following "the rule" makes for a terrible experience where you truly feel unwanted. Forget this place and go to Starbucks.

Hotel bars are getting a revamp these days (finally) and we headed to Anti:dote for their innovative tapas and reinterpreted classic cocktails crafted with premium spirits and house made bitters, liqueurs and sodas.Anti:dote's cocktail menu offers ten mixed drinks ($23), each classified by its potency and refreshing flavor. These drinks are made from artisanal pours of rum, vodka, rye whisky and gin balanced with fruits and spices, mostly of which from the hotel's own garden.Corpse Reviver #2 with level 4 potency and refreshingness. This would revive any corpse. A seemingly healthy drink with beet, rosemary, honey, lemon and tequila- Blood of Dillinger. There are about 24 items from the Tapas menu which is served till 10.30pm. We were fortunate to make the last order!The Crisp parmesan pizza ($12) is a must order at Anti:dote. This minute cracker is made of parmesan crust with dollops of flavorful pesto and powdered tomato as its based. Topping it off, you have the olive oil caviar, melty cheese snow and micro basil. Hearty pizza flavors in a small bite. Lovely! Crisp anchovy sticks with garlic aioli ($8) are the perfect snack to go with drinks and by that i mean cider but cocktails can do too! I love the salty and buttery puff sticks and also that strong and pungent garlic aioli.The Caramelised foie gras and vinegar glazed leeks on crisp puff pastry ($18) were little sweet morsels, kinda too sweet for my liking and there was quite a fair bit of leek/onion glaze. I could do with a slightly more seared/cooked foie gras but that's a personal preference.We could smell the Black Truffle Bao ($20) before we could see them. For a hotel bar, i must say the bao (Steamed Bun) skin was done very nicely and it had a nice fluffy bounce to it. It was nice seeing sliced Perigord black truffle but somehow the taste of the truffle didn't come through. Perhaps it was the strong flavors of the veal cheek and caramelized shallot with Madeira that overpowered it. The foie gras in the bao might as well have been a piece of tofu because it didn't give the bun any flavor at all.  We would have gone for more items if we weren't so stuffed. Other must tries are the 2-hour braised short rib ($18), clam sphere ($14) and the Paleta iberico de bellota done tomato shabu shabu style ($18).

Overall a greay place to be for high tea.  Fortunately they had the truffle egg back so that was enjoyable.   Presentation, food and service were all good can tell from my bettet half reaction especially to the jewelry box.

Well, it happens, but it seems that this is one of those places that Yelp and I are going to disagree. It is not that the service was bad, it's just that I am not a huge fan of these flash hotel bars - which is what this is. Fortunately it was one of the bars that Yelp recommended to me that was actually open, and I must say that the name intrigued me, but when I walked around the corner and discovered that it was a part of this really fancy hotel my eyes literally rolled. Still, it was my intention to step in here for a drink. The seating wasn't the best. Okay, they did have some lounge areas, and you can sit at the bar, but there were these other odd things that you sort of leaned against - I really don't like leaning against things when having a beer, I like to sit down. However, they had a pretty decent selection, not the usual stuff that you find at most bars, so I do give it points for that.

The reviews for Anti:dote are confusing, as it appears that people are reviewing everything from breakfast to tea to cocktails.  So to be clear, my experience with the establishment has been solely as a guest of the bar, which has been superb on every visit.  Starting with the space, I love the modern décor and clear bar table.  The cocktail list is both creative and traditional, and even the traditional cocktails can have an interesting twist, like a spray of Chartreuse on the glass for the Tuxedo.  There is a very nice selection of Whiskey, not the most extensive but well-thought out.  After reading an article on the Whist cocktail in the New York Times, I requested one here, and the bar tender actually put together 3 versions using a different sweet vermouth, which was genius and also really showed what a difference one ingredient can make.  There are also some interesting tonics, which are made in house, but I tend to stick to old school drinks.  The food is also a nice surprise, being light and modern.  The parmesan pizza had a crust which was the parmesan, so it's basically a delicate frico with pesto and other toppings (careful - they break easily).  The octopus skewers were also very good, as was the aged iberico ham.  I have never stayed at the Fairmont here, but one does not need to be a guest to appreciate the quality of the drinks, food and service here.

The frog here's cooked JUST enough that it maintains more the texture of a firm-fleshed whitefish than of a chicken - which is great! It's snappy and tastes very fresh, despite the fact that they don't have the frogs lined up in tanks outside like the other establishments in the area. I have mixed feelings about this - I do feel like we should confront the fact that our porridge requires murder, so the uncomfortableness I feel when I see the frogs in the tank is a plus for me.I got my frog - just one - 'dry chili' style, which is still pretty wet-sauced. This is nice because the sauce bleeds into the porridge and gives it some flavor.

This place has a huuuge seating area and for good reason. It's famous for its frog leg porridge, so popular that it's now a chain in Malaysia, China, Taiwan, and Indonesia.We were actually looking for a small snack, so we ordered a small claypot ginger spring onion frog instead of porridge. It was very flavorful, albiet a bit salty without rice. The pieces of frog were quite decently sized, and very springy and fresh. It's definitely not that dirt cheap street food though, and ran ~S$9 for a small claypot with about 4-5 large pieces. The guy taking our order was a bit strange, constantly trying to upsell us to get a large even though we insisted that we already ate dinner and were just having a quick snack...It wasn't really a quick snack though, because of course they cook everything fresh to order, so we were anxiously waiting for about 15-20 minutes while everyone else around us seemed to be getting served their food! Next time gotta try the actual porridge...

My to go to frog porridge place every time I am back in Singapore. My absolute favorite. Best paired with oyster egg from the stall beside and the beef kway teow from across the street. You can just sit and order and they will bring all of it to ur table. Love the spicy version with porridge and I usually get the large size for 2. :)
Not cheap, but it's my grandpa's favorite frog legs! The sauce is very flavorful and I can have porridge with the sauce only, and be completely happy.

Good balance of flavour and taste.The porridge is cantonese style, like congee, with ginger! Add the sauce it taste heavenly.The frog are fresh, but somehow it lack a certain oomph. Without the black sauce it's just taste like chicken.

I've been here twice now and I'm not sure if my expectations for frog porridge are high (and why should they be?) or if my memories of frog porridge are long lost dreams instead of real life experiences. Lor 9 specializes in two flavors, dry chili and ginger spring onion. The latter was definitely on the sweeter side, with a gooey caramelized glaze. Out of the two, I enjoyed the dry chili more--the gooey caramel sauce was an overkill. The consistency of the plain porridge hits the target. It's not too watery, overcooked, but nice and thick! Similar to the frog, it comes in a piping hot clay pot! Plain porridge is an additional cost at $2. Tip: Order some beef hor fun across the street. They'll bring the dish across the street to where you are sitting. Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Leg Porridge will not do the same.

One of the better frog porridge. I like the dried chili but the ginger & green onion is good too.For the uninitiated, the frog are live in a cage. They're killed just before cooking. So they're very fresh. You get the whole frog, not just the legs.Give them a try. I think they opened a branch in Bukit Timah.

The only time I've ever eaten frog legs was last Easter in Paris, smothered in butter and cream sauce.  So when my friends in Singapore asked if I wanted some frog legs, I said, sure, why not.This was an interesting combo of frog legs cooked in a clay pot and then served with rice porridge.  I said I didn't like spice, so they ordered a plain one for me, and a spicy one for the others.  The frog legs came in a sweet sauce that was nice as it soaked into the rice porridge.A bit strange for dinner though, because the only times I've eaten rice porridge in the past was either:1) when I was sick and my mother made it for me when I was little, or2) after a night of clubbing the O.C. with Vietnamese-Chinese Americans, and we ate it with steamed fish to rehydrate after a night of drinking and partying.The most interesting thing for me is that we didn't actually eat at this establishment.  We happened to be eating at the Beef Kway Teow across the street, and then one guy ran over to place our order, and then they served us at the table for the other other restaurant.  I guess this is common here, but I've never heard of anything like that before.

This is a review of lunch from the Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Leg Porridge stall.We actually headed to Geylang for lunch because a colleague wanted to take me to a different stall that is across the street from here.  We discovered that it is closed on Mondays during the daytime.So, we decided to hit up Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Leg Porridge for some frog's legs.The ambiance is what it is; you do not go here for a white table cloth and a waiter serenading the table.  You go to get great food.  tinyurl.com/b2od8roI would not call the staff friendly.  Ok, I would not even call them hospitable.  But, once again, that is not why we were there.  We just wanted some fantastic frog's legs and we got them.We did order the porridge.  We just ordered the frog's lefs straight  up with some rice on the side.We ordered two types.Dried Chili & Ginger Spring Onion.  They were both very good.  I preferred the dried chili ones though.  I liked the heat.  Eating frog's legs always reminds me of eating chicken wings.  These were no different.  They were delicious saucy messes.  I enjoyed every bite.  The soup in each was also provided a tasty treat.Dried Chili Frog's Legstinyurl.com/a6axd42Ginger Spring Onion Frog's Legstinyurl.com/bkeh384Ignore the surly attendant.  Ignore the general disarray.  Enjoy the tasty frog's legs!

I love eating it with their hot piping porridge. Love both the ginger onion and the kungpao versions. The meat is always served just perfectly cooked, and not overcooked like in some places.Even if you are not a frog leg fan, there are oyster omelette and the famed beef horfun from across the street.plus, you get the usual Geylang parking woes s bonus.

I've had better in Japan of course but so far in Singapore this may be my favorite ramen. It's a cool vibe with indoor and outdoor seating. Reasonable prices. Good lunch and early evening specials. Definitely worth a visit if staying close by.
Decent ramen with good broth in the Tanjong Pagar area. The chasu wasn't super impressive but the broth was. I tried the black sesame ramen which I found to be unique.

Ok so Tonkotsu King has silly long queues so we gave this a shot and was pleasantly surprised. Friendly attentive service, high quality pork broth which has character. The pickles were excellent.The large portion with eveything in (pork, egg, nori) was particularly satisfying.
I think the waiter and the cook are from Japan (at least the water is), so the ramen is surprisingly decent. The restaurant is cozy and small. Very nice dining experience here.

This is a Michelin bib gourmand Turkish restaurant near Arab street. Their hummus with their special breads are the highlight of the place. I would NOT recommend the chicken kabob, it tasted like leftover chicken.I definitely will be coming back quite often just for a hummus and bread snack. One of the best hummus I've ever had and the bread is soft and fluffy!Great ambiance if you come by in the evening and the tables are set outside along the street.

So-so kebabs with asianized-sauce, disappointing dessert. Perhaps I ordered the wrong menu items?The sigara borek is pretty good - think fried Turkish spring rolls with cheese filling. The karisik kebab (mixed kebab plate) was next. Although the meats (lamb, chicken, ground beef) were grilled well, they came smothered with an asian-like brown sauce and accompanied by stir fried broccoli and cauliflower (!). Don't get me wrong, it tastes good but I don't think it's authentic.Sadly, the künefe was also disappointing. The kadaif pastry (noodly phyllo dough) was left too long over the fire and was pretty charred when it came to the table (see photo). Too much of the element with atomic number 6 isn't my idea of a good time.Eh, so there's this row of Turkish restaurants along Bussorah St leading up to the Sultan Mosque, all in competition with one another. The menus were mindbogglingly extensive and restaurants were filled with tourists. Had to pick one restaurant to try. Decided to come here as the menu items looked pretty authentic, but I guess I was wrong. I don't claim to be Turkish food expert, but I've lived with a couple of Turkish roommates and was educated on the food and how to make a mean pot of Turkish coffee. I'm sure Singaporean stomachs can digest the authentic stuff. Off to try the next restaurant along the row.

Sometimes you wander around the Kampong Glam area wanting to have some authentic middle eastern food but alas, some of them do not serve alcohol! Alaturka is the place to go for some really good turkish cuisine and still have a cool glass/bottle of beer to go with it. (Alaturka sectioned their restaurant into 2 areas where those who would like to order alcohol can sit in the other section, away from the main restaurant where they strictly do not serve alcohol.)If you want to truly enjoy a hearty turkish meal here, I would advise to come with a few more friends. This is because the serving is rather generous and between 2 pax, it may be challenging to order a variety.Some staple that will ALWAYS be on my table, regardless of whether Im there with only 2 pax or more, are the HUMMUS and one of their huge platter for two that has a combination of different types of kebabs. The hummus is really smooth and the amount of olive oil is just right in my opinion, thus it not too wet nor too dry. The bread that comes along with it is also exceptionally delicious. It's definitely a great complement to the hummus.As for the platter, it would have been more ideal to share between three to four light eaters as it comes with a whole lot of different types of protein such as chicken, beef and lamb and a serving of veg and rice. The gravy is slightly salty thus the rice (buttery on its own) is a great side to neutralise the saltiness of the dish.To round up the meal, a pot of the hot turkish apple tea will surely do the trick. Slightly sour while rich in it's apple fragrance and sweetness, I simply love the taste of it. Will definitely introduce it to my friends. :)

Been here many times today was an ultimate surprise.   Quality of the food was absolutely horrible.   Apparently the chef was not around so some in the kitchen is not doing a good job.   Humus of all thing came in sticky like peanut butter.   It was not smooth and creamy as it was before.   had a grilled platter and everthing was burnt and dried up.   worst thing is the food was cold!! how is that even Michelin standard.   i will give then one more chance hopefully they get it right if not i am gone for good.

Great to have something different in Singapore...We really enjoyed the hummus, the halloumi and the lava bread as well as the barbecued fish in garlic and lemon sauce - yummy!Would definitely recommend and will be coming back :-)

What I love: The food & ambiance is great. The place is small, a little narrow and tables are close together - but it has a nice homey feel. The food is yummmmy! Rice and Kebabs are my fave, the Adana Kebab, and their traditional Turkish bread, the Sarmusatli & Ekmek. There are not too many Turkish places at Arab Street, so it really does stand out.MUST HAVES: The Musaka, eggplant & lamb stew, Omg, I'm like literally aching for one now. Hahahaha. The Ali Nazik is yummy too.Desserts: Baklava and Kunefe is REALLY REALLY yummy here! Especially the Kunefe!What I don't love: Prices. It's quite a pricey place. But the food is good. It's an average of $18-25 per pax, just for the mains. So, if you're getting a starter, main, drink and dessert, it would range from $30-35 per pax. So, it's pricier than other places in Arab Street. But it's a nice and romantic place - great for a date.

This is my go to place for Turkish Kebabs & Middle eastern fare in Singapore. The apple tea (hot) is terrific & their breads are fantastic, fresh & rather delicious. The kebab platter or rack of lamb, beyti kebab, shish tawouk or adana kebab are my go to options when it comes to ordering food. Also order in a portion of their Baba Khanoush (egg plant tip) and some Lavache if you're in the mood for some piping crispy hot bread! The service is attentive, cheerful & take good care of you (small gestures such as immediately topping up your glass of water matter). They also held on to my hat for 2 months & returned it to me when I visited them next. A great place for a quiet dinner with a small group of friends. Make sure you have a reservation if you go on the weekends.
Asianised with funny bbq/tomato sweet sauces, broccoli and cauliflower side dishes and very expense for what it offers (and what it does not)There is always a first time and off went mine.

There are lots of places to get kebabs in the Kampong Glam area, but of all the various Middle Eastern food places to eat, Alaturka is probably my favourite place to have kebabs and hummus. The menu is quite extensive, and the food is quite consistent, if a little bit pricey. Bring your friends along, this is where you want to share your food!I particularly love having a nice hot teapot of Turkish Apple tea when I have my meal, no matter how hot it is. The apple taste is nice and strong and the tea is so flavourful, really yummy! The coffee is served the thick Turkish style if that's what you like.

Delicious Turkish food off Arab street. Personally I loved their chicken or lamb beytti, but recently they changed from grounding the meat to serving it whole. It was more moist and delicious when ground. The hummus is great and has delicious bread, I just always want more for how much humus you get :). The babbaganoush, yes my spelling needs help there, is mediocre. Just not as flavorful as I like. Finally, the dolmas need more rice at the very least. I also prefer it with ground beef as well. Definitely recommend though if you are in Singapore and craving middle eastern food.

We ordered the lamb and cheese Turkish pizza but they served us the chicken and cheese one instead. To their credit, they offered to replace it but my dining companion didn't want to waste food. The chicken one wasn't great, we couldn't finish it. The portion was just too large, and it didn't taste particularly special. The chicken kebab was good though, juicy and flavorful. Wish this serving could be made larger and the pizza serving made smaller.

This was a spur of the moment choice as we explored the Kampong Glam, Arab Street and Haji Lane area close to Bugis in Singapore. The area outside the restaurant is pedestrianized and on a Saturday early evening, there was a live band playing right outside this restaurant. The entire area has a very unique and eclectic feel to it, so we decided to forego a trip to the Usual Suspects of Singapore restaurants in the city itself, and try Derwish. We were seated very quickly inside what is quite a small restaurant, although there appears to be additional seating areas upstairs. We ordered a lamb pide after plucking up the courage to ask the people at the table next to us what it was they were eating. Yes, I know some might consider this rude, but it looked too good to pass up. The salad was a simple tomato and cucumber salad chopped up with some fresh warm cheese. The lamb pide was simply wonderful. For those unfamiliar with the dish, as we were, it is like a thinner Calzone pizza with a spicy minced lamb and cheese filling. It was the star of the show. Both dishes arrived very efficiently which became the watch word for the level of service throughout the meal. The staff really busted a gut keeping up with the demand from hungry customers. Most of the time it remained efficient, but we did notice two tables who waited forever for their drinks despite asking at least twice. The mixed kebab was tasty, but the sauce that the meat was in was little bland for my taste, the minced lamb, lamb chop and chicken breast pieces all tasted very good, but the chicken wing was a bit lacking in flavor. The Turkish coffee we ordered was strong and as you consumed it the consistency changed to a much thicker mud like. Our lack of experience in eating Turkish food, may come through in the review, but overall we gave it four stars with one off for the inconsistent level of the service, despite the wait staff working so hard.

Came here through a recommendation of a friend's friend on a public holiday. Surprisingly wasn't too crowded even though we arrived there at about 6pm.Parking around here will be the street parkings where parking coupons are essential.This restaurant comprises of indoor and outdoor seating. We were given choices on the seating arrangement. After minutes of looking over the menu, we decided to get a mix of kebabs, hummus and bread and Künefe (see description of what this dish entails through Jeannie's review). For the drink, I ordered a glass of Turkish Apple tea.The hummus and bread arrived first. Was a little salty but the texture was well-pureed. It definitely satisfied my tastebuds and kept on scooping for more even though there were no bread left. The kebabs. It has pita bread at the bottom and on the middle was a layer of rice pilaf (not too fond of) and three types of meat (lamb, beef and chicken - either on a skewer or not). The meat was pretty tender and the spices made it tastier. It was definitely on the pricier end but it is worth a try.The Künefe was special. First time trying this dish out. The first look it reminded me of the crunchy noodles. First bite, it was delightful in the mouth and the crunchiness of this dish made me continue to dig in. A must try dish here.The apple tea wasn't too special. It was fruity and not too sweet. The three of us paid approximately $75 for the three dishes and three drinks. Was a little pricy but somehow we were satisfied with the dishes. :)

NOTE: This review is only for the künefe.Had a turkish food craving, so I went around looking for this dessert. I've had some pretty good renditions of the dish outside Singapore and simply had to find it somewhere.Forget baklava - Künefe is a dish made of cheese and lots of sugar syrup sandwiched between 2 layers of baked kadayif, the noodle-like phyllo dough that looks like fried bee hoon. When done right, it's one of the best desserts.The version at this restaurant came with a generous serving of cream around the pastry, and it was heavenly. The kadayif was crispy without being overly soggy with the syrup. Freshness-wise I guess it's okay, considering we're 5000 miles away from the Bosphorus Strait.But at $9 per serving, perhaps you should bring a friend to share it with. Tar-powing (packing) the leftovers doesn't do it justice. Will be back for my sugar high sometime.

Came here for anniversary dinner w the bf! :) He had a coupon from Bliss or something of that sort, entitled us to an appetizer, a lavash bread, mixed kebab, chicken (or lamb) stew, and a dessert.Some of the food was pretty good, other dishes I found a bit on the salty side, so it's really more of a 3.5 than a 3. Bf thought that the saltiness was probably offset by the carbs (i.e. bread/rice), I guess that's true but I'd have preferred less salt still! Nevertheless, would recommend lavash bread and kunefe dessert!Appetizer - babagannus! $7.50 (yes.. I seem to have been on a roasted eggplant spree) - this one apparently was more descriptive in the menu - capsicum, crushed red peppers, butter (i bet there was a substantial amount!), mixed with a touch of garlic with homemade yogurt. This was not bad, definitely had more flavour than Cafe Le Caire. I thought it was a bit on the salty side too though. And the portion seemed a little small! Cool that there were some chunks of eggplant. Bread that came with it was so-so, quite thick but not that warm/crisp on the outside.Lavash Bread - awesome!!! $4 or so I think, can't remember exactly. Huge puff of happiness :) Came warm and toasty fresh out of the kiln (I'm guessing). Black and white sesame seeds lavishly sprinkled atop, crisp bottom (cracker-like). Patlican Musakka - Mediterranean stew $22 (chose chicken, don't like lamb that much) w eggplant and potatoes (the eggplant was really gd! potatoes not bad too, tender), topped w cheese and baked in a claypot. There was some sort of a tomato-ish sauce, which was kind of salty.. Very umami though! It was pretty nice to spoon the stew onto the lavash bread.Mixed kebab platter - 2 beef kebabs (fairly tender); 2 chicken kebabs (also pretty tender, but a bit salty!); 1 chicken wing & small drumstick (same, tender but a bit salty); 1 lamb chop (REALLY tender! amazing..) and one sausage-like thing that I'm not sure if it was made of minced lamb/chicken/beef. Came with rice and some sort of a tomatoey sauce as well (tasted different from the sauce in the stew). The rice that came with the stew and platter was pretty good.Dessert!! Chose the kunefe :) YUM! $9. Shredded wheat, fresh cream cheese and honey syrup, with tring pastry. [this is copied directly from the menu, no idea what 'tring pastry' is, guess it was "string" haha.] Anyway, I guess it must've been baked cos the top was browned and crispy, mm! Cream cheese sauce surrounding the pastry was not sweet (surprised me, I thought it was like a vanilla sauce or something), went really well with the pastry threads/honey inside. Words just fail to describe how awesome/interesting it was. We had to make a conscious effort not to finish the whole thing, given how full we already were from all the food before!Service was pretty good. Oh, we had a turkish apple tea as well - that was really sweet.. We had to ask them to add more water. Also, bf noted that it seemed like they had tea bags sitting at the back - begs the question whether their "freshly brewed" tea is really from the leaves, or just tea bags? Hmm. Ah well.

I personally find it challenging to find a nice halal restaurant with nice ambience, great food and good value in town for a good team lunch sometimes. How glad I was to have the recent team lunch at Derwish! Cos we made reservations for 14 pax, we were directed to the room upstairs (I see it sort of like an overflow room) instead of the usual seating at level one. Because there werent anyone else upstairs except for our team, it's as if we were given the royal treatment of a lavishly decorated room and dedicated service staff. :PAnyway, the food is really great in such a setting cos we could order a variety for communal sharing. Dishes such as the mixed kebab, the kofte and even the pizza were great. Too bad I cant share any photos cos my Hp got reset and I lost the images but the presentation of the meal is pretty cool as they use really nice engraved plates and utensils.Overall a great dinning experience. The only thing that got us a little nervous (since we were having lunch and dont have the luxury of time) was time management as the food do take quite some time to arrive. We tried to avoid the situation by pre-ordering some side dishes when we made our reservations but those also came quite slowly.If you are in a hurry, this may not be the best place but given ample time to just chill and relax with friends and family, the experience should not disappoint.

We used to come here quite often, but a recent visit was a complete disappointment and crossed it off the list for good. Size of portions shrank by probably half. The kofte with cheese dish was runny like a soup. The waiting staff used to bring syrup separately from the mint tea. No more of that.I should really have trusted the recent reviews here before heading over. Sadly, one more once-decent restaurant now has become yet another tourist trap.

Arab street has become one of my favourite areas in Singapore. From the famous mosque in the background, to the many folks enjoying shisha in their hookah at nights, it is definitely a site to see if  you're living or visiting in Singapore. There are plenty of food options as well, and I decided to stop at Derwish because of their ambience and the fact that they had a decent amount of visitors at the time. I sat at a cool table, and waited for our server. There was obviously only 1 person serving at the time, and he looked overwhelmed. I had to wave him down. If I wouldn't have waved him down, he probably would have never taken me or my wife's order. After placing our order for food, drinks and shisha, I sat back and relaxed. Well, that relaxation came to a halt since our server decided to move us to another table. Something about no smoking there. Okay, that's fine. He moved us to an awkward table that didn't seem clean and the area seemed to smell funny. Well, after 5 minutes of trying to relax, he stopped by and asked if I would move... AGAIN. If I wasn't patient that evening, I would have told him to screw the order and left for another establishment. But I was calm and I moved again (mostly because I felt bad for the guy since he was the only one that seemed to be working).The food was okay, the shisha was the wrong flavour, and the only saving grace was the strawberry smoothie. After our experience, let's say I don't plan on ever returning to this place and I don't recommend anyone to visit either.

Came here last weekend for dinner and I actually was trying to get a table at Sufi, but they are under renovation now, so I was directed here. This and Sufi, and 2 other places come under the same management. But the menu is different from Sufi, though they are both Turkish restaurants. The options are pretty standard - but not really the same. They don't have Doners here.What I Love: I really liked their decor - it had a very Turkish / Mediterranean feel to it - and the ornate walls and cutlery really did transport you to another place. I loved the menu - the visual; aesthetics of the place is pretty nice - pretty lamps everywhere. The ambiance is pretty nice, it's bustling, staff running around - was pretty cool. It felt alive, and there was character about the place. The food was very tasty! Sorta like Sufi. Ordered the Sucuk Pide (starter), which was yummmmmy. A eggplant starter, Saksuka, which I ordered more Lavash bread for. And a Iskandar. Everything we ordered was yummy. It's quite a comprehensive menu.What I Don't Love: Service is a bit slow here. And the staff could be a bit more observant. So, gotta get their attention quite a bit!

What horrible food. We had the Moussaka and the Turkish pizza. The moussaka had an overdose of canned tomatoes and the pizza was bland beyond belief.We ended off with some Baklava and apple tea. The baklava came right out of a box, the apple tea was the only thing that I was happy spending $58 dollars about.The ambience is nice and the owners are friendly. But the atrocious food will never ever see me going back there again.

Ended up here with a guest after we strolled Haji Lane and Arab Street. We were super hungry and looking for something yummy and filling. They didn't have much seating so we were seated by the kitchen across from the main location in what seems like an extension across the road... It was weird. Anyways, we ordered our food and it was pretty boring. It didn't seem fresh. The hummus wasn't finely puréed (it was kind of like crunchy peanut butter) ... The entire experience I could have done without. I don't think I'll be coming here again.

OK food, but good luck getting any service whatsoever!  Forget ordering extra bread with your hummus (which BTW comes with four minuscule slices of bread) ...ah, but check your bill, we order extra bread multiple times, it never came, but somehow two orders of it made it to the bill!  Ridiculous... :-s

4-star hookah bar. 2-star restaurant. Derwish sits on a walking mall with a nice view of the Sultan mosque. As such it is an idyllic spot to relax and have a nice hookah smoke (until the 2016 ban). We love Turkish food, but the restaurant scene in the Arab district is quite disappointing. The cold meze and fresh breads are really the only things you want to order around here. Dinner for two with drinks came to S$75.

Appetizers are delicious. For a place with such a small menu, I had high expectations of the steak. It came medium when I ordered medium rare and overall was ok, nothing special. Ambiance of restaurant is nice.

There's really only one reason to visit L`entrecote. And that's for their awesome steak and fries. Everything else doesn't matter! Conveniently located and wonderfully furnished, you almost feel like in you're in Paris, thanks to the ambience and service afforded. Perfect for either lunch or dinner with friends or on a date, the steaks on offer are tender and juicy and proof that wagyu isn't the only choice when it comes to having grilled meat. The appetizers are very French, with a variety of escargots, pate's and terrines on offer so you might want to give that a miss if they aren't very familiar to you.

A great place for steak and fries, highly recommended for a chill dinner with friends. It is located among the shophouses at the duxton area, so do keep an eye out or you might miss it. Inside, it has this unique ambiance which kinda feel like those french bistro. The staff were all warm and cheerful which I do really appreciate (it's becoming uncommon these days). The menu is simplistic, with some chouce of appetisers, desserts and beverages to go along and the steak and fries as the main highlight. I had the onion soup which was sweet and fragrant (liked it very much). The steak and fries were also great with great attention paid to the doneness of the steak. Most restaurants tend to serve the steak in one slab and that's it, leaving you with uneven doneness. Here, they took a different approach and instead separated it into 3 servings, ensuring perfect doneness as per requested and you would get warm food throughout the meal. The sauce was rich without being too overpowering. Perhaps it is also good to note that the fries are free-flow, though i found the initial serving was already very generous (But hey, fries is love fries is life). Overall, this is a highly recommended place for steaks if you happen to be in the area. An advice that i would give to fellow readers (and a suggestion to the restaurant perhaps) is to avoid coming in at peak dinner time since the place is really cramped and gets rather echoey when crowded.

Average French bistro. We ordered their famous steak frites which was ok. The fries were quite good but the steak was pretty much uninspiring - something you may expect when you order steak from a general western restaurant not a place focused on its steak. We also ordered escargot which was also quite average... House red wine is ok.  Overall, a bit pricey and not really worth it given the mediocrity of the food

As a carnivore and french fries addict, this is my place to go to meet both cravings. You get a piece of beef which you select if you want Rare, medium rare or well done, they write the selection on the table and shortly you receive your meal. Salad with walnuts and dressing, then the beef and all you can eat fries. Everytime I have gone, they also serve a mini glass of the house wine. This Bistro also has dessert options and appetizers. We have tried their cheese appetizer, which was amazing (if you love cheese ^_^)If you have a craving for a simple yet fullfilling dish, stop by the restaurant in Tanjong Pagar. it is also on a cute cobblestone alley.

We had no idea where to eat on our last night in Singapore and relied on some guys we met at a bar. So many restaurants close on Sunday nights. We weren't looking for French, but L'Entrecôte Bistro on Duxton Hill was open. It's basically 1 restaurant split into two next to each other but with different menus. We chose the Annex. The food was excellent. My Oven Baked Bone Marrow with Guérande sea salt and grilled buttered Poilâne bread satisfied my months long craving! I basically licked and sucked that bone LOL. A friend ordered sardines and it was served in its tin...very cute.I also ate 2 fresh shucked oysters from Ireland, then stuffed myself with a perfectly cooked medium rare entrecôte steak served wth French fries and walnut green salad. I don't recall the French wine we had, and they have a beautiful modern wine cellar to house their stock. Our waiters were nice and friendly.It was really a great, relaxing evening after so much hustle and bustle around Singapore.

We went to Duxton Hill wanting to go to Prawn Star which seems closed now, and ended up here.It is a nice 'French style' bistro type restaurant that serves French fare like cold cut and cheese platters, steak frites, mussels etcWe had a cold Salmon platter and the steak & fries.The salmon portion was on the small side but ok, the steak frites was quite large, with the steak already cut in strips which was great for eating, and amazing fries to go with it. The sauce on the steak was good however I would've preferred it on the side as I like medium-rare with just a bit of salt best. The meat was ok but I have had better, especially for the price (32,50 S$), but that's S'pore.For dessert I chose a tarte tatin which would have scared a French person off as it was huge, with a tarte being normally flat, and the base was very heavy shortbread. It tasted nice though and the sour cream that came with it was perfect.Staff was very friendly and service oriented - we would come back to try their Saturday brunch, but not necessarily for dinner as it is rather expensive, in general, especially when there are so many great "local" places to explore.

I waited here for 20 mins on a Friday evening at 8pm for a seat as they don't take reservations (major minus). I have to say I don't love the steak and fries, especially the half-rate sauce. Free flow fries don't appeal to me, because I don't love fries, and the first portion was way too much for me. The salad that came with the steak had a dressing that had too much vinegar for my taste. When it comes to my salad dressing, I guess less is more for me.So me and a girlfriend had:Homemade Duck Foie Gras TerrineOven Baked Beef MarrowSteak and fries x 2Profiteroles to shareThe terrine was horrible, and it was mostly butter, so avoid it if you come here. The beef marrow was out-of-this-world, and I wish they'd offer a jumbo portion of it. It's just beef bones cut into two with melting marrow inside, to spread on bread. Terribly sinful, but so simple, and so delicious. Our dessert - profiteroles, were drenched in chocolate syrup and ice cream; pretty standard fare and an easy combination that can't go wrong.Would I come here again? Probably not. It wasn't exactly cheap, and there are a few places that do steak better than this.

Wouldn't recommend. Steak has a salsbury like sauce which tastes a little like canned soup or boulion beef cube stock reduction with lots of pepper. The fries are as good as mcdonalds, but cost considerably more,  Sigh.

This is the kind of place for the lazy people who dont really like to be bothered with choosing your main course - there's only one main course here -- 2 portions of steak and fries!The only thing you might want to think about is - the doneness of your steak. :)For those who cannot resist the need to pick and choose, you have a selection of appetisers and desserts to choose from. Some signature to look out for, escargots for appetisers and the caramel cake with vanilla ice cream for desserts. The caramel cake is like the caramel version of the chocolate lava cake with the caramel oozing from the centre upon cutting.Great atmosphere, nice service. A fantastic hipster joint for those who have a few more dollars to spare. Would have been a five star if one could make reservations but you gotta queue for your tables! Guess that's part of the experience!

Dining in Duxton always make me feel like I am not in Singapore.No reservation, no frills, just good old steak plus fries. While it is not my favorite cut of steak (dry-aged filet mignon is my weakness), this is a decent piece of meat. Just do not come expecting the quality of a traditional NYC steakhouse.I still prefer my steak served simply medium rare, no sauce. Though the gravy is nice, I believe you do not need any bit of sauce on good meat.

Alright, if you feel like steak frites (and you really must feel like that, because there is nothing else on the menu...) The only choice is the size of the steak, regular or XL--which is really the normal size for a steakhouse. Ok service, overall.

After hearing about this place from so many people, my husband and I decided to check it out with a few friends. To start, we waited over 30 min for a table inside (which wasn't too bad as we were enjoying some lovely wine in their patio) when we finally signaled the hostess and asked what was taking so long she promptly ushered us inside and gave us a dinner menu which consisted of 1 item....steak and fries. Being a steak lover I was overjoyed and ordered the steak and decided on the escargot as an appetizer. The escargot were absolutely divine....and the wine was magnificent! The main course when it arrived looked good although a bit watery. It was perfectly done to my likeness but that was it....the flavor and sauce were a huge disappointment :(I couldn't understand what all the hype with the steaks was about!!!! The sauce was watery and to be quite honest not very well done which was a shame because it ruined the great cut of meat. It was a complete waste! It was as if they were trying to mask the flavor of the actual meat by loading it on with a strong green runny sauce. When paying premium price for a steak at a high end restaurant, the expectation is to get a juicy melt in your mouth succulent piece of meat full of flavor but here it was just meat slathered with runny sauce. See a well done steak on its own doesn't even need any sauce let alone be smothered in one. Overall, the ambiance is nice, the place is clean (although a bit too crowded...not enough room and too many tables) the wine and appetizers are great but if you're looking for a good steak...your better off making it yourself at home for a fraction of the price.

Want to experience dining at cramped rustic Parisian bistro, this is the place to be. Le Entrecot packed its customers like sardines. Dining here doesn't allow you much privacy. The tables are so closed to each other, you can literally hear the next table's conversation.Well, one thing for sure. You don't have to think too hard what you want to eat for main as they only have 1 thing on the item and that is Steak and Frites. But with that said, you will have a tough time deciding what appetizers and desserts you would like to complete the meal cos there are too many selections to choose from.

Despite the cramped atmosphere and the fact that the waiter literally has to pull the table away so you can step out to use the restroom, L'entrecote is a great place for what its best known for:  Steak & Fries. Cooked to your liking and served in two portions with unlimited fries the steak is juicy, soft, and full of flavour. What makes L'entrecote different? THE SAUCE. Extremely delicious and simple, the sauce is the real treat here and I'm willing to bet will go with almost anything. I recommend ordering an extra side of it, there just never seems to be enough!The location is beautiful and very quiet, perfect for a romantic night out

I LOVE this place. The food is simple, unpretentious and good. Of course, the steak is perfect. Served in two separate portions to keep it warm. It's the only main course on the menu. Order the house wine to go with it. But what doesn't get enough credit, in my opinion, is the amazingly good appetizers and desserts. The roasted bone marrow is a must order, and the waffles are fantastic too.

I've been to this place twice and I will surely comeback.Reasons why?1. Duxton Hill is a nice area to hang out after work or go on a date2. L'entrecote reminds me of the cafe's i've been in Paris. It has a nice and cozy ambiance3. Steak and Fries is great considering that you pay only $30! generous portions indeedCome here for a date or just chill with your girlfriends. Its a nice place kick off a Friday night!

Has only 1 main to choose from - a delectable steak and fries which they recommend you get in medium rare. Make sure you enjoy it with their secret sauce!You can choose your starters and desserts though - the escargots were quite tasty and I love the sauce it came with, went really well with the bread. Their signature dessert is a caramel lava cake of sorts which takes 15 mins to prepare but well worth the wait.Small place and can be a bit cramped and noisy when full, but perfectly pleasant once the crowds thin.

Do you like fries? Sure you do, or have had McDonald's before = then you must come here. Otherwise,  All: Don't bother washing your hair coming here; Ladies, Asians, or Me: Do not come here when the state of your skin ain't exactly at it's peak, or x - 7 days before your period etc. And otherwise, stare at yourself against that giant mirror staring at you and remind yourself how after all these fries that you are and still beautiful.

We had high expectations when we went there lately. Food was okay but nothing special from our point of view, just ok. The service lacks some friendliness and the personal touch. The location is of course nice but inside, the tables are placed to close to each other. For a romantic dinner probably not the best precondition. Overall ok but there are many other places I would try first before coming back.

The steak & fries are a must-have. Best part is while you're enjoying it, the waitress surprises you with a second serving, and then asks if you want more fries.Great atmosphere (although slightly cramp), courteous staff. They don't take reservations; first come first serve.

at the end of our visit to santos's island. we had lunch here. so many selection to choose from. we had hong kong noodles soup with lots of veggies, indonesian chicken and rice with the best samba tumis i ever taste, indonesia's chicken bbq, red bean peanut kachang, tu tu kueh, mango mango kachang and different varieties of fresh cut fruits.

Run of the mill food court. Basic versions of dishes. Lots of people because it's affordable and quick. Used plates and cups were not cleared in time. Patrons standing everywhere waiting for an available seat.

One word for the whole place: overpriced. Does that mean you should not eat here? Not necessarily. Options in Vivocity are generally not cheap. More affordable options are either non-air conditioned or super crowded. At least the food here is good. I tried the prawn noodles with soup. The amount of ingredients was decent and the soup was delicious. My friend had roasted duck rice and added roasted pork. The duck was tender but the pork was full of fat so avoid if it's not your kind of thing. There are also rave reviews about the mixed vegetables and Chinese handmade noodle stalls. Just don't get a shock when you find yourself paying $7 and upwards for a dish.

Mmm I like this place. This was my first experience dining on Singaporean cuisine. My friend and I spent the morning at Senotsa, which has a shuttle that connects to this place. We chose Food Republic since there are a million different options so you get a lot of variety depending on what you feel like eating. Lots of traditional local dishes for very cheap prices! We had the wanton noodles and hokkien prawn mee for lunch. Everyone is sold in small-large sizes which is cool. Ahh so yummy! I loved the wanton noodles and the hokkien prawn was quite good as well. They sell desserts on carts that are pushed around (reminded me of dim sum style) though you can also go to one of the stalls. For dessert, we had soursop ice and ice kacang, yum yum. Loved the soursop--it was the first time I've ever tried it.Basically, my Singaporean friend described this place as a hawker with AC. It has a bunch of different stalls selling different types of food, and then you just grab a seat. It was pretty crowded when we went around 1pm, but as we walked toward the back, there was a lot of empty seating. So if you go, be sure to walk around to the back if the front area is too filled. So much yummy food for a decent price (Though still higher than hawker of course) but then again you're paying a little bit more for the AC and comfort, so I think it's worth it. From the tourist perspective, it's a great opportunity to try a lot of Singaporean foods.tldr; great place great food, def worth going to if you happen to be in Vivocity.

This food court has a bit of old feel to it. Making you feel like your outside but it has air con! I had a Mini Seafood Hotpot (steamboat) (under $ 6.00SD) - this is a really nice and filling meal to share if you want a light lunch or if your hungry to eat all of it on your own. Not spicy at all the soup is very creamy  full of flavour of the sea. You get quite alot of prawn meatballs and fish that has been deep fried and into the broth. Also lots of chinese cabbage too. Add another ($2sd) you can have a choice of variety of noodles to compliment the dish from wheat noodles to flat rice noodles. The sauce on the right is fish sauce with hint of chilli and sauce on the left is chilli but with a hint of sour lime.

i love how they make cheap eats not look and feel cheap. The dark wood interiors with the chinese red lantern is a nice touch.All you want to taste, eat and feel are housed here.Very busy but you can always grab a seat.Great for families or  big parties.

One of those upclass-tity food courts.Every dish is probably $2 to $4 more pricey. Quality depends on luck, unless you have had previous experiences with specific stalls.I prefer the Indonesian stall, and grilled chicken is my repeat order. Unpretentious, and it taste like grilled chicken with a sweet shallot oinion-y fragrance. It meat is moist, the rice is fluffy, but the sides are average. The soup, hmmm.... probably to rinse your utensils.
Prawn kuay tiao with Pork Ribs is nice. The pork ribs is not really tender but flavourful. Soup is thick and tasty!!!

Food Republic at Vivocity is one of the few places I will be willing to go to at a drop of a hat because of the awesome variety of food it has to offer here. I personally find this place better than the Wisma one. I find it ironic that hawker style food were demolished over the years and now we are desperately trying to recreate the same ambiance our grandparents and parents had in the 40s/50s/60s... with bright lights, less stuffiness and air con. But oh well, Gen X and Y kids like me were sold by the ambiance because when we were born here, these places seems to cease to exit already (Perhaps the only 'authentic' one left is the one along China Town road). I love Jessie's Rojak here. She has a black and white version of rojak with vegan options. The ba chor mee here is also nice. Frankly, I come here more for the rojak because she serves adequate rojak sauce to go with it. If you ask me to compare, I'll say her rojak is on par with the Hoover Road Rojak store at Whampoa food center sans the long queue at her store. But that is in my opinion lah. So do give her rojak a try when you are there, it's situated next to the BBQ chicken wing store.. she should be there reading a newspaper or a magazine when you walked by her store.
Good food court with tons of local eats. Love the Hokkien Mee, Pie Ti, Rojak etc. It's always crowded but there're seats deep in the food court. Reasonable prices too

Food was ok here.  Yes, it might appear more easy to order and find food there, because it all is more organized than other hawker centers, but on the other hand does feel less authentic plus the food reply was below the average I was used for other places. Now with these places being even more expensive, I don't see a particular reason to go there once agai

Food Republic is one of my favorite food courts because they often have a good selection of tasty local food. It is quite appropriate to introduce your foreign friends to some of the local selection of food at a relatively inexpensive and air conditioned environment. But one thing that I dislike about this specific Food Republic outlet is the layout. Sure, it is spacious and has ample seats to deal with large crowds at VivoCity on weekends, but the layout of the stalls is pretty far apart and confusing. You may find yourself walking in rounds if you are not familiar with the place or is going there for the first time. Overall, it is still a clean and comfortable environment to have a quick meal at.

An interesting takes on a food court, recreating the old world charm of Singapore in the 40s/50s/60s with aged wooden beams and benches. old-school looking pushcarts and decoration. I like this particular Food republic for its good collection of quality stalls. Xin Sheng Ngoh Hiong is one of them, and a branch of Sergeant chicken rice, as well as the popular Heng Hwa restaurant, Putien.  Food starts from $4 at most stalls. Soy bean drink and you tiao, the Korean food stall, and sotong mee stall are also very decent.

So this food courts has everything you can ask for in Asian food and the braised short rib bun is the first thing you see as soon as you walk toward the flowery sign and a must have. you get 3 for 5 and this super tend, juicy pork rib is served is a bun just like peking duck and it a great start to your meal. I tried the hainanese roasted chicken with rice. Yummy, totally simple dish that just celebrates the tenderness and sweetness of chicken with a dash of fresh ginger sauce. my Hubby and his brother was sold on a special at the next door stall which was 6.50 for 2 meats and their Indo chicken and Fish was so tasty. I was surprise how much I like the Fish as it has a little crisp skin and tender inside, not to sweet or salty. The end my wonderful lunch I had to get a fried dough or you tao with soy milk. That was so good that I had to get another order to go.

I can confidently say Food Republic is one of the better food courts in Singapore. Despite higher prices, the food selection is generous and flavorful. My favorite picks would be the Nasi Lemak/Padang store at the entrance and the Dim Sum restaurant within the food court. The great thing about the Nasi Padang stall here is the good sized chicken drumsticks, be it the deep fried or curry version! If you're game for dessert, give the tu tu kueh a try! The sweetness of the coconut shavings and the texture of the velvety flour is an absolute winner!

No kidding. Each slice of duck has a thick layer of fat under the skin. But the flavour... oh so good! On the few occasions I had it, the skin was crispy and the fresh, juicy and tasty, with a flavour close to goose, Irish ducks are indeed more flavourful than the Malaysian ones we usually get here.

This is more like Imperial Treasure and Crystal Jade Kitchen fare rather than a proper Chinese restaurant with only dishes to order. So this is quite a do-able meal if you are not here with a big group or are dining alone. The difference will be a smaller menu as the focus is on the duck. The only meat available - duck, roast pork and char siew. Then you get the dim sum options with the usual suspects of siew mai, har gow, cheong fun etc. The rice and noodle dishes highlight will be with the roast duck. Congee is also available. I had the highly recommended black pepper duck bun which was nice. It was very saucy and while it was tasty, I felt the black pepper overpowered the duck flavor. The duck noodle was excellent. The noodle had a bite to it and when mixed with the sauce and chili was delicious. The duck had a rich taste due to the fattiness. I removed the layer of fat from the crispy skin. Unfortunately the skin was not crispy all the way. The duck was tender at some part and a bit drier on others so it was not consistent. Overall it was a good meal and I would come back again as it has more than just duck. A good option when you do not want to go to Crystal Jade or Imperial Treasure. The prices are decent too, slightly lower than the Noodle Place in 313 Somerset.

Before today I had only ordered takeaway char siew which was nice and tender but expensive @ $15.90 for 11 small slices. Not sure that it was worth it.  I had also ordered the black pepper duck buns (all good - moist, tender duck, soft bun - except maybe a bit too much of the black pepper). Even for takeaway orders, the staff were a confused lot and what I would call 'cannot make it'.Today I had a late lunch in the restaurant. By the way, they have taken additional space (see photo). No crowd so service was much better than before. Staff was friendly.Had duck noodles and warm barley.  Duck was tender, skin not crispy at all. I had to remove the fat but alas the skin came off too. Barley was not even warm. Waiters and Waitresses in Singapore food outlets have a problem understanding 'hot', 'warm' & 'luke warm'.So my conclusion is that it is not 'die, die must eat'.

This Fat Duck is NOT for the skinny hearted.I've recently been seeing a lot of people try this place out and I knew, if it was good, would make the perfect Sunday brunch. We're happy we got here around 10.15am as the queue really started to pick up around 10.45 -11.00 am.First impressions... Service was a little slow. With only one main server taking orders, another 2-3 waitresses were running about getting the restaurant ready, turning on the tele which showcasing how their signature ducks are bred etc. After getting our seats... We noticed a huge amount of filth on their floor. Not a very good second impression. Used tissue paper and crumbs on the floor, clearly they weren't ready to open. We decided to ignore all that and concentrate on what we were here for, their famous duck.  Signature London Roast Duck ($12.80) $12.80 for an entire leg (drum and thigh) is pretty decent and comparable to the prices you get at imperial treasure or crystal jade. The skin itself was so wonderfully crispy, while the meat was juicy and tender. The health conscious maybe not be a fat of the thick layer of fat under the skin but hey, that's what they're known for.  London Roast Duck Rice ($7.80)We decided to ask for the breast this time around and we were not disappointed. Just as tender as the leg, the duck rice gave a good portion of meat along with a generous portion of fluffy white rice. Very very good. Signature Black Pepper Duck Bun ($4.80) Similar to a Bolo Bun, the top of the bun has a nice, sweet,  crunchy crust while the inside was filled with succulent duck, cooked with a tasty black pepper sauce (almost a hybrid between a char Siew and black pepper filling).It was such a delight the have!Pig Liver Congee ($7.50)Breaking away from an all duck brunch, we decided to order a Pig Liver Congee and see if it truly is a worthy challenger to Crystal Jade's crown. The texture was perfectly smooth and a worthy rival to many of the top Cantonese style porridge a in Singapore.The taste however fell a little short. It's not as "porky" or tasty in comparison while the liver was a little over poached. Will try the century egg Porridge next to see how it measures up. Overall, I'm giving this place a 4* solely based on food. Their manager or owner still seemed a bit lost while and looked drastically under staffed and not prepared for the flood of patrons and the cleanliness leaves a lot to be desired. But at a month old, I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt and hopefully they will be able to stabilize the ship and really give the other Chinese restaurants a run for their money. But for duck's sake, please try the duck!b

The duck, the roast pork, the char siew was drenched in sauce making the london fat duck experience a soggy one. The sauces are overly sweet too. The duck has some flavour, some fat under the slighly crispy skin but because of the sauce, the crispiness of the skin is very much diminished. The roast pork was cold & not crispy at all with or without any sauce. The char siew leaves much to be desired, tasting overly sweet, overly charred like candy & not like barbequed pork. The rest of the dishes ordered siew mai, wanton in soup, xiao long bao are decent but also not very tasty. To compare the roast duck, char siew & roast pork, imperial treasure peking duck or crystal jade or even the local hawker stalls serves much better food! I do not recommend london fat duck.

Go eat the duck! You can have dim sum or noodles or congee or whatever but you should just order a serving of duck and eat that. The duck is moist, delicious and fatty. Mmm. Don't go with the kind of friend who eats meat and leaves the skin behind. On second thought, do - more skin for you!Char siew had a yummy sweet glaze and was very good. With super chow tar bits at the end. Not the greatest char siew in the world but pretty darn good. Go early for lunch - before 1230 - and you probably won't have to wait much.

With all the rave about the "Wagyu of Duck", I decided to try it out for myself. Let's start with the food. To be honest, the duck tasted pretty average to me. I personally prefer their Char Siew better than the Roasted Duck (and my girlfriends agreed too). Besides that, the rest of the dishes are alright. I won't say it's fantastic or like out-of-this-world. But if you do head down and try, do try their Duck Bun and Egg Tarts. That I recommend. Be warned though. With the expected waiting time (since they just opened and everyone wants a piece of their duck), the place was a little messy and chaotic. The plus point for them for our night there is the lovely wait-staff who was assisting us (just that one nice auntie) and that the food came almost instantaneously.Now, I can say "I've been there, done that."

Ok why pay a premium here when you can easily get a whole roast duck at hawker centres for say SGD 25-30? Before we proceed, a duck here will cost you about SGD 50 after GST.If you don't already know, they do import their ducks from Ireland, which probably adds to the cost. But how different is it?
