Breakfast remains to be decent but I feel that it's bordering on the decline.The menu used to be interesting and imaginative. Now it's mediocre and boring. Portions are small and like other Yelpers have mentioned, it's overpriced. Never once when I came did the chef or the owners who are sometimes at the premises asked the diners if they are happy with the food.The joint is not often full. Hence instead of texting away on their phones or having a smoke, it pays to ask the customers what they thought of the food if they wish to cultivate repeat business. The staff is often very friendly and cheerful. I do miss the long hair girl with the braces. She's the sunshine of the lot. I used to recommend the Little Diner but I doubt the joint is barely keeping up its former glory. It's now just a restaurant trying to make money. Not returning.

This is one of the best places for brunch. The food is delicious and service is good too. This was my second visit to this place in 6 weeks. Both times we had a lovely meal.The eggs are amazing no matter what you order. We tried the omelette, croque madame, poached eggs. pastas are delicious too. We tried the aglio olio and Mac and cheese. I absolutely loved the french toast and double chocolate milkshake as well.Would definitely visit again.

This place has a great vibe and the staff are awesomely friendly.I went for a Saturday brunch, which means two things. Coffee, and RED VELVET PANCAKES.The coffee was aiight. The Red Velvet Pancakes... unfortunately didn't quite live up to the expectations of my friends that love this place. I can see how the pancakes would be in in theory, except when I ordered them they were a little undercooked. Undercooked pancakes taste of soggy flour/batter and really no amount of cream cheese or syrup is going to cover that up.That said, my date's Eggs Benedict was pretty good though a little on the small side portion-wise and we were left wondering if we should order more or head somewhere else. In the end we decided to head somewhere else for a burger, but funnily enough I'd stlll be very willing to try Little Diner again just because the service was so friendly.Good people and good service save any dining experience, and I think this was no different. The team there deserve a second chance!

My pan seared sea bass with kalamata olives, cherry tomatoes (6 of them) and mashed potatoes was not bad, but I recall it being somewhat oily (this is from 2 months ago). My friend loves their fried chicken, and the bits that I tried were certainly pretty good!

UHHHHHH.... First of all, the mac and cheese was overrated and considering we came here primarily for the mac and cheese we were a bit disappointed. It just felt like it was missing something and none of us (a party of four) could figure out what it was lacking. The steak sandwich and truffle fries were pretty good so that's what the stars are for. Don't order the mac and cheese... It will disappoint!

The naïveté of the interior (plaster wave meets bats!), pleasantly pleasant staff, a fun reading menu with no grammatical or spelling errors and an enthusiastic owner (we assume) gave us some reason to look forward to our meal. First sign of trouble was the plating of all the dishes. Token salads, stacked and skewered food looked like compensation of some sort and turned out to be the case.I did note some rather inspired moments on my plate. I did like the fries and the coleslaw that came with my dish, but to serve fried chicken looking and tasting burnt was quite beguiling. I even finished it. Limpid, supplier-style Oreo Cheese cake was not and remained half eaten. A friend's pork chop looked robust but was an unexpected star anise party-in-our-mouths. We were left unsure about that. His apple crumble on the other hand held no surprises, but in a good way.I suggest the owner take a long, hard look at rivals on the market and see what they deliver against what they promise. Right now the output of the kitchen can't cash the cheques. Could have been acceptable in the 90's. Not anymore, not at this price point.I would suggest to lose the gimmicks and get some basics right. Otherwise a great location for a diner. I wish them all the best and hope they keep working at it.

The good: Location (for me) and throughout my meal I was attended to quite frequently, including a hi from the owner/manager. My items came out fast, which was a testament given the place was packed (98% locals, not that it matters). The bad: Not terrible, but the food wasn't great. My eggs benedict came out with 1 thin slice of ham on each, and one of the eggs wasn't cooked thoroughly. The hollandaise sauce was runny and forgettable, about the only thing holding it together was the muffin (acceptable) and the ground pepper that was sprinkled on top (table side, nice touch). My latte was tasty (hard to get that wrong) but too small. The ugly: Unfortunately, it's another Frankenstein restaurant that doesn't have it's own identity. Even the decor screams outdated (there was Halloween decorations still up almost a month after) and there were design concepts that I've seen around town. Not all is lost, but there is still much left to be desired.

If only the food looked as good as the decor. And that's why I always say that you can't judge the quality of a restaurant by its looks alone.  Touted to be one of the go-to places for brunch, we were not in luck when we decided to pay the place a visit. Perhaps it was due to the unusually large crowd that had showed up while we were there. Service was inattentive and fleeting and wait times were horribly long. We got our orders messed up at twice and they actually placed the wrong orders for us. When the food we ordered arrived, it was disappointingly lackluster and middling at best. The burger I had was all mashy and seemed a tad undercooked and my girlfriend's eggs were all runny and messy, nothing like what she had ordered. I wouldn't mind giving the place a second try, but it will be some time for us to forget the madness.

I wanted to like this place for 3 reasons:1) There are very few affordable brunch places near my home that serve mind blowing food and don't require advance reservations.2) It's called the "Little Diner"3) I saw red velvet pancakes and french toast and immediately thought of the Griddle Cafe on Sunset Blvd (yelp.com.sg/biz/griddle-…)So what happened when  I ate there on Saturday afternoon?Service was great by East Coast standards, so I guess it fits with the New York theme. We (let's call him R) certainly appreciated the server checking up on us and serving water quickly when we got seated. +1 for using those umm... jar-mug thingies that the man and I used to use in college. We ordered the red velvet pancakes and eggs benedict and well, both dishes were kind of meh. My first reaction to the pancakes was wow that's a small stack. A small, thin-looking stack of pancakes that goes in-line with the "Little" in "Little Diner" I guess. I mean that's all I can really say about a stack of pancakes I ate in about 5 mouthfuls. It had some flavor to it but certainly wasn't the rich, dessert-like, thick and fluffy pancakes I was hoping for. The cream cheese frosting was on the side and didn't really taste like cream cheese (or at least what I'd associate with say a cream cheese frosting on cupcakes) and looked kinda awkward, as was the small swivel of cream. However, I must say the side of bacon was very, very well done. Super crisp, bubbling with oil, perfect. The eggs benedict that R ordered because of the honey ham in it was a benedict in name. The muffin was kind of tough and somehow the eggs and ham and hollandaise just didn't meld together and work. We've had some really insane benedict's at  Choupinette, Rider's and the Porch cafe in Bali and this version just didn't, quite, cut it.Bottom line, I'm checking this place off as tried and visited but am unlikely to return. It reminds me of the gastropub down the road - passable food and cool decor, but not enough to make me return again and again. For the price I'm paying I'm sticking with the stalwarts in the neighborhood, even if it means more effort on my part in making reservations.

Some New Yorkers hot-favorite, no doubt. It rocks the island the day it made its debut here, choosing to open at 8pm in the evening and attracting its fans to queue as early as 7pm for the opening special goodies bags. I wasn't one of 'em but was hoping to pay an opening visit if only they have started their business in the morning.Didn't had a chance to drop by Orchard Central until lately. I normally wouldn't walked to the far end of Orchard Road unless there's a good reason to. And today, I had a valid one - Brunch at Dean & DeLuca.Traveled up via the snake-long elevator has been such a breeze, of course, provided the weather is in your favor. Yes, it has been kind today - cooling with slightest dark clouds shadowing me. 2 snake-ladders up and this sleek-looking Dean & DeLuca stood in front of me as I entered the mall on 4th floor.From afar, I am attracted by the elegant marble-tiled bread counter & ham & cheese station. The store offers quite a good varieties of breads but I still didn't understand the reason that these were from Maison Kayser, Bread Project, Baker & Cook's oven and some others. It makes more sense to me if I get to savor the home-made ones than having to buy a loaf at Dean & Deluca , that was baked by others. Skipping the bread counter, I walked into the groceries section. Famed for its luxurious groceries, I wouldn't say the range has been extensive but are definitely some high quality breed by far. Some of the seasonings on the rack can be seen available at three-sixty supermarket at Ion Orchard, even before we get one at our own backyard. These items don't come cheap and a teeny D&D carrier bag (8cm x 8cm) will cost you S$15.00! But if you are looking some some great gourmet seasonings, wine, olive oil, truffle salts, even some gold/silver flakes for your cake decor, this place is it! Mind you, the gold flakes cost about S$125, probably make a luxurious topping on that Christmas frosting or so.The dining area looks bright but the table-to-table space appears cramped. The wait staffs are mostly green horns (looks wondering) to me, many a times, you will need to wave for service. The cafe comes with a self-service concept. You would need to order/pay your food at the front counter and collect your beverages at the drinks counter. The staff will serve your food when it's ready which takes about 10-15mins during peak hours. While I was there, I overheard diners complaining on wrong orders and the long wait for the food, so please check your orders with the wait staffs or when it fails to arrive.The All-day-breakfast selection written on the blackboard was limited. I had The Belgian Stack - was dainty and makes me feel so princessy sweet. The deep waffle pockets were filled with organic maple syrup and a dollop of vanilla ice-cream. The batter cake was baked to light crisp on the outer with a rich buttery center. Served with berries and chocolate sauce - the most conventional way. I could only comment that it was overpriced given its portion. For S$21+, I could get a more hearty breakfast to fill my day.The other breakfast I have tried - American Country Breakfast for S$22+. This was a lackluster! The most classic dish but the worst I have ever tasted. Nothing lived up to D&D's except for the pork sausage which has a blasting sausage skin and flavorful pork fillings. They failed in their scrambled eggs which was cooked dry and too coagulated. Sautéed mushroom a tad ordinary while the bacon strips were too soft and layers of fats seen 'raw' instead of charred crisp. However, the harsh brown was house-made I presumed. Unlike the mass produced 'McDonald's' version; this big mashed potato ball with bits of ham embedded, was tasteless. I only figured it out at the end of the meal, that this was the harsh brown D&D refers to, in their dish description. Was it me who's slow to find the association? Anyway, I regretted having American Country breakfast, but I wish I could have more choices when the hot-favorite Brioche French Toasts was sold out for the day.It was not a very enjoyable brunch that I have expected on D&D. I could get a more delectable breakfast at Wild Honey with the bill. A S$55 for 2 - the amount I could get a scrumptious meal. Now that I have tried D&D - be it for service or on food; I gladly discovered that I won't be back at the cafe but probably the gourmet hall delights me more.

Terrible. Over-hyped. Ridiculous and a waste of time, really. This place should wake up their idea and realize this is not New York so they should stop the New York attitude.We pay a good 70 bucks on 2 x coffee and breakfast and all we got was bad nasty new york snob attitude from the staff. shame on you! Food was nothing special. Pastries are from mason kayser and other good bakeries in Singapore. I really don't see the point of this place...

The service is unapologetically terrible. Despite the place being half filled, the servers managed to:1. interpret our table 22 as 21, despite the table sign present.2. bungle our orders and send another table's orders to us. Thrice.Food's not that great. Sure, the portions are big. I had the portobello cheese burger and green juice. What's the point of having a nice juicy burger and piling fries in the same bowl? The fries are going to slide to the bottom, soak in burger juice and get soggy, no? My friend had the chicken breast and a side of salad, and she complained that the chicken breast was too tough and dry, and the salad overpowering with vinegar dressing. I think my favorite part of D&D was the roasted onion ketchup.

It's been almost a month since this NY deli set up shop in Orchard Central but they're still plagued by sub-par service standards. My friends and I dropped by on a Thursday afternoon after a movie and were able to get a table easily. I guess the hype has finally settled down a couple notches. We placed our orders which were served shortly except for one - the portobello cheese burger. 30 minutes had gone by before my friend went to the counter to check on her order. It wasn't till another 10 minutes later that her burger finally arrived. We asked about the long waiting time despite the lack of a crowd and all the staff could tell us was that "sometimes the counter has a lot of burger orders". Needless to say we were disappointed by the level of service. I had the Brioche French Toast with Salted Caramel Bananas and Berries which was delightful but a tad too sweet. The Portobello Cheese Burger arrived medium well with overdone fries on the side but the mushrooms delicious. The grocery shelves definitely caught our attention but sadly it's all ingredients we can only dream of using in the kitchen.

Finally made it back to Dean & Deluca after several months and had been wanting to eat brunch/lunch here. I loved Dean & Deluca in Soho for their groceries, amazing bakery, tea, and coffees. Also their prepared food section is yum too. This Dean & Deluca in Singapore is the sterile and paired down version of the store in Soho. Of course its going to be overpriced b/c its all imported. But their iced Americano coffee is decent and the lox on my toasted bagel was delicious! Wasn't too big a fan of the scrambled eggs in the bagel with my lox though. It was mushy. Will probably try something else next time. I do like their pasta sauces though and used to get them all the time in New York so it reminds me of my past life.

Dean and DeLuca was a nice quiet place to kick up one's feet and take a load off.  I have walked into the NYC store and this is definitely not the same.  I ordered a chocolate croissant and a lychee New York soda.  The croissant was ok but the soda was a little too sweet.  Service is great but nothing to write home about.

Dean and Delucca is a little taste of home while I was in Singapore or traveling in general (where they have outlets, like St. Helena, Japan and Thailand). That being said, this outlet is pretty good.They have a good selection of yummy hot food entrees and side orders. And their dessert selection is always good especially when I'm not quite sure what I'm craving. I like their lemon tart. Their rainbow cake feels like a Singapore classic too.

Dean & Deluca. A more upscale cafe. A brand name. The good. Location is easy as they are now located on the ground floor. Plenty of seats and everything looks and feels high quality. The bad. The espresso? Mmm so so. The beans taste ok but it's taste as if it's made from a bialetti not an espresso machine. You can compare to Joe and dough just across to taste a proper extraction. (Best franchise espresso IMO)Also, no wifi?Anywho, I'm still glad this popped up as every cafe will be maxed out on the weekends in this area. I suppose this place can be good for a homesick New Yorker. What I really want is Joe and dough espresso with Henri Charpentier dessert in this venue setting...Update: decided to try the dessert on another visit. The strawberry rhubarb. I think potential to be good. Potential meaning when she asked to heat it up , she microwaved it rather than the proper reheating machine which maybe the "crumble" dessert is a a mush dessert.

Dropped by Dean & Deluca for a quick lunch with my boyfriend. I've had their rainbow cake before last year which I quite liked, so I was looking forward to trying out their more savory food. I had the orzo salad and the mozzarella salmon quiche, whilst my boyfriend had the bacon and egg burger. We both had the mango lassi The quiche was OK - I felt that it was lacking the punch to make it a delicious quiche. I also felt it was rather dry and too crumbly. I quite liked the orzo salad but again, I felt like there would be other places that served even more delicious dishes. My boyfriend, however, seemed to love his bacon and egg burger and even claimed it was only slightly below par with his mom's cafe burgers, which is a pretty big compliment. The mango lassi was way too sweet to my liking, but I've always been a person who prefers subtly sweet treats. Service was not bad, the staff were cheerful and friendly. Dean and Deluca is a pricey pricey place for a restaurant that serves mediocre food. Perhaps their other dishes might be better though.

I was told the pancakes (flap jacks on the menu) were to die for and that I must head over to Dean & DeLuca to try. I finally made my way there for brunch over the Chinese New Year break. It was early at 11+ am and there were not many diners then. There was a stack of buttermilk pancakes (4) topped with heavy cream and berries. It came with a small serving of maple syrup (not sure if it was real 100% maple as I could not smell the maple at all). Presentation was pretty and the portion was huge, maybe to justify the price (think it was $18). The pancake was thick and fluffy with the taste of buttermilk which was nice and a bit salty on its own. Add a dollop of the sweet cream and it was perfect on its own. I did not need to add the syrup, except when the cream ran out. After polishing off half the stack, I was quite sick of it, so it would be best to share this dish. I would say the pancakes were nice, but not enough to want to make me go back again anytime soon. I think the highlight was the heavy sweet cream.
Decent food but there is still room for service to improve. Staff is unfriendly and seems to be reluctant when we add additional requests on the food and drink.

Massively overpriced, edible-ish canteen food in a drab location. No ice water or free water of any kind is served, so you have to buy drinks - and they are in the $8 range. The roast beef is quite good. The chicken "burrito" was just boiled chicken in a wrap with a pile of fries, admittedly enough calories for two but without much in the way of taste. The pastries are a bit dry, they'd be OK for a mall in the heartlands. Considering the amount of choice around Orchard, I don't understand why there are so many customers. I'm guessing Palate membership? Because that's the one reason to go - 50% off most things, bringing the price slightly below what is normal for what is served. For example, their burger goes from $24 to $12, about 10% more than the delicious EwF downstairs; and at $9, the roast beef becomes the cheapest steak in the area.The location is unfortunate. I'm sure they thought it was premium, and the side next to the escalators is alright if completely empty, but the side past the lift is straight out of the Harkonnen stronghold in Dune (the 1984 movie) - surrounded on all sides by either a massive drop, or industrial walls several floors high, with bad lighting and a bit too much AC, sitting on rickety metal chairs and Starbucks-style tables. It might look better once the works are finished; part of the issue is that one side of the sitting area where food is served is a construction wall.

So after hearing so much about Dean & DeLuca, I finally went down to try it... and was sorely disappointed. Perhaps there was too much hype around it, but even if I tempered my expectations a little, the overall experience there left me with a bad taste in my mouth.I ordered a coffee and a lox, which is smoked salmon on bagel. And since Dean & DeLuca is from NY, I kind of expected the bagel to be at least decent. It was not. The bagel was too hard and dry, and chewing through it took far too much effort. It did not fare well in taste either. What was worse, the smoked salmon didn't taste fresh. And it came in a large portion on top of my bagel. Normally, I would never ever complain about getting a large portion of smoked salmon... but it kind of felt like the salmon was going to be off, so they just wanted to be rid of it. The coffee there comes in a large disposable paper cup. It was so weak I could barely taste the coffee. My friend's tart tasted like cardboard and we couldn't even be bothered finishing it. Considering the prices they charge here, and how everything is meant to be gourmet, it's shocking.To add insult to injury, the service here really sucked. The staff were very unhelpful, and even when I asked for things, I either got ignored, or they just sullenly pointed in a general direction. Lastly, I really hated sitting under those awful bright fluorescent bulbs with the slight flicker. It gave me a headache after a while. We left the cheap tables and uncomfortable chairs behind in the dead space that is Dean & DeLuca.Hated it here. Truly.

Came here for desserts one evening just before their last orders at 9.30pm (the restaurant closes at 10) so there was no problem getting a table. A friend and I shared a cherry tart and a tart with a chocolate and coffee filling. While the tart fillings were delicious, both the tarts had a rather soggy crust, as if they had been stored at the counter for days. I've heard negative reviews of their breads too. Most of the pastries and bread sold at Dean and Deluca come from Baker & Cook, a gourmet bakery at Hillcrest Road. The problem with outsourcing your food is the compromise on freshness, which is very obvious the moment you bite into their pastries. I've heard that their mains and brunch menu is pretty good, so I'll be back to give that a try!

Ordered the 2 eggs w ciabatta toast and added bacon. You get a choice between scrambled or sunny and I chose scrambled. Eggs were amazing but the toast was extremely disappointing. Soggy from the eggs being stacked. Bacon wasn't as cooked as I would've liked. I ordered the house brew which was good. Not too acidic. Staff however were nice and friendly.

If there's only 1 thing you gotta eat at Dean & Deluca, try their French Toast which is made from 2 1-inch buttery brioche bread which is coated with caramel and caramelized, topped with vanilla ice cream, bananas and some berries. Love that powered sugar coating. This is fantastic dessert food or make it breakfast if you have a sweet tooth. Don't worry, it's not as sweet as it looks. The ice cream kinda neutralizes things a little.The Eggs Ben however was disappointing. Even though jamon iberico was used, the flavors didn't gel together. Hollandaise sauce was watery and bland. Eggs were overcooked at first and they redid it. The sun dried tomato bread just didn't go with the whole get up at all. It was bland and felt a little stale. Definitely not the best I've tried.The iced mocha is great though. Love the caffeine and chocolate packed drink. I can't stop ordering it.If you are not hungry, just order some tart from Baker and Cook or perhaps a Quiche from Mayson Keyser. Both were decent if not good.

I went because I remember D&D from my time in New York where I occasionally bought something. Main reason: I was thinking of a great sandwich and I was out of balsamic vinegar. I went to sit down, but nobody came. Although there are several mm.. not waiters (although for once, the term would have been appropriate) - staff hanging around, they didn't seem to be interested. So I went up to the counter where I learnt that yes, this is where I had to order. I looked up at the options, didn't see sandwiches, and chose 'king mushroom & bacon quiche'. What I go in the end was a slice of some sort of sweet crumble dough filled sparsely with a vaguely quiche-like substance. Pretty awful. The expresso came without sugar or spoon: you also have to go and get that yourself.Altogether a poor experience. In the end I didn't even want to buy anything there.

incredibly disappointing and wholly vapid food - even after tempered expectations - at the dean & deluca cafe in orchard central. I've been to their pretty shop - with highly magnified prices - before, read the dismal reviews everywhere on the blogosphere - and I still went because I was drawn to an image I saw online of their pancakes. it was a regrettable experience, and one that's made me feel quite a bit foolish.the pancakes seemed commercially pre-made and were rather stodgy, and the smoked salmon sandwich with scrambled eggs terribly salty. we left wholly disappointed - and it was a pretty expensive meal, especially for what we got - and so the emptiness of the cafe even at dinnertime (yes, I like breakfast for dinner) is rather justified. pretty place, pretty food, terrible taste - perhaps you might be better off going for their cheese counter or charcuterie and doing a takeaway with all their gourmet products. just steer clear of the food.

There was so much hype about this New York deli coming to Singapore, so I wasn't sure I wanted to head there in the opening weeks where there were bound to be hordes of people checking out the new hip hangout.Still the crowd was not too bad on the Thursday night that I visited. I tried the Iberico Eggs (my poached eggs were a tad too cooked, boo, but the rest of it was pretty good) and the Portobello Cheese Burger (yummy and tender meat, huge portion). Not sure if it was where my table was but that aircon was COLD.After that filling meal, it's nice to be able to browse through the grocery section and look at all the lovely, lovely stuff I will never be able to afford. I foresee many window shopping trips here in the future, or perhaps splurging on a D&D mug so I can remind myself to aspire towards being able to afford a lifestyle like this!

I don't really like the bistro here as everything is overpriced. No doubt the food is decent, but I cannot accept the fact that there's a lot of stuff we have to self service even after paying so much. The saving grace of Dean & Deluca for me is the gourmet market that carries a good variety of foodstuffs and produce that you don't see in supermarkets here. The goods here also make great gifts, thanks to the nice packaging they come in as well!

I was at Dean and Deluca with a bunch of friends on a Friday evening. It was a challenge getting a seat/table but I suppose that's the way it is anywhere along Orchard on a Friday night. It was a delightful experience browsing through the shelves of grocery items and kitchenware in the shop but the prices of stuff there are slightly overpriced. They had a cheese and meat counter that carried imported European cheeses and the likes. I was there mainly for a chill hang-out session with friends so we didn't get any of their main meals. I had their blueberry cheesecake and sour cherry tart, as well as a green tea latte to go along. The blueberry cheesecake was enjoyable, not stunning but definitely above average. I liked their sour cherry tart quite a bit, tangy and fruity, it was very satisfying!My main complain is that the service was pretty slow. I was in the queue waiting to place my order for a good 20minutes. Overall, Dean and Deluca is a chic new hangout that serves decent desserts. Nothing mindblowing but it is a pretty aesthetically appealing place, offering a little bit of posh grocery shopping too.

I lived in New York for a good 8 years and never frequented Dean and Deluca. However, I don't know if it's because I secretly miss New York, or because I am easily distracted by shiny things, but this D&D location had some sort of hold over me and just pulled me in.I was tempted to try their bistro for lunch, but then the prices were a turn off. If I recall correctly, it was about $28 for a cheeseburger, yet almost the same price for a caprese sandwich. How could a mozzarella cheese, basil and tomato sandwich cost as much as something with meat? Does the mozzarella come from a unicorn? I'm a bit confused how their pricing works.The store is very nice, and has lots of tempting things to buy. I ended up getting a $25 bottle of vodka sauce. It tastes okay, but nothing special.What I didn't like was that I had to wait in the same line as the people ordering food to pay for my vodka sauce. They had other cash registers throughout the store, why couldn't someone ring me up there? Overall, nice place to browse, and maybe have a cookie or some coffee, but that's about it.
Note to Dean & Deluca: You can't advertise a "classic Reuben" and deliver a sandwich with chipotle sauce. I feel cheated.

I've been here twice and I enjoyed it. Gashouse Egg is their specialty and I strongly recommend you to try it if it's your first visit. It's like egg in the hole, bread toasted till crispy but the yolk is not overcooked. I'm in love with their bacon jam on the side.Coffee is definitely the selling point here.I tried their choc croissant during my second visit. It was good. And because I couldn't forget my love for their bacon jam, I requested for the jam on the side (add $2). I know it sounds weird but the savoury jam actually went well with the sweet croissant.Be warned that this place is always very crowded on weekends!

Recently the cafe had updated its menu with new items such as XL crispy chicken burger and Furikake Mushroom pasta. Order was taken at counter with only cash and NETS payment accepted.Sriracha Pork Belly Burger ($15)served with sweet potato friesThe pork belly was fatty with a texture similar to soft bone, although I was expecting a melt in a mouth fatty part with a crispy crust. The burger was not as spicy as expected. It was not messy to eat the burger. The fries was lacking of crispiness.Coffee Soda ($6) It was a glass of soda, accompanied with a glass of espresso. Just add the espresso into the soda before drinking. It tasted like soda drink with a coffee aftertaste. Quite refreshing for a hot day.
Pretty good coffee and desserts. Brunch is legitimately good as well, especially the maple bacon. Hard to find a seat on weekends.

Most people come here for the Gashouse Eggs but the Croissants are excellent as well. I tried the basic croissant which comes toasted warm with a side of their homemade jam and butter. The croissant was large and flakey, but not too buttery. It was so good that I devoured it before taking a picture. I'll definitely have to come back to try the coffee next time!They also have some outdoor seating which includes a few hanging coves, which I found perfect for reading. Sitting outside is a nice alternative if you want a bit of peace and quiet. Most of their tables are in the shade, so it's not too hot on a typical day. L
Try the croissants too! Feels like I am back in Australia. A hidden gem with the coffee and the food. The price is not super expensive also. Typical cafe prices.

One Man Coffee is tucked away in Crust's shop, using the venue during the day before it gets transformed into a pizza bar at night. Nice ambience, not too noisy for a lazy Sunday morning, and very affordable prices (average $10 as opposed to the $15 average in other cafes).Tried the Gashouse Eggs ($10) and Brioche French Toast with Berry Compote, Candied Walnuts & Fresh Cream ($10). The Gashouse Eggs seemed like a Croque Monsieur, satisfactory, though slightly on the greasy side. Egg could be runnier as well, though the bacon jam on the side was interesting.The French Toast was perfect, not too sweet, crisp on the outside and fluffy on the inside. Thoroughly enjoyed it.

I am not in the habit of awarding five stars for a single dish as I normally feel that it requires more than that but trying the French toast with caramelized bananas and salty caramel is just great. I will return just for that. It is perfectly fluffy, not overly sweet and feels fresh. The big brekkie is also very good but it does pale in comparison to the French toast but as I seldom come here alone I will force anyone going with me to share a Big Brekkie and the French toast with me (just a fair warning if I ever suggest going here with you).The coffee is nicely made, perfect execution on all the espresso based beverages. Unfortunately no filters but can head down the road to Pacamara for that. The service has also been very friendly and they managed the packed place rather well. Worth mentioning is that it shares the space with a pizza place so in the evenings it transforms into a pizza place. Never tried the pizzas there but it does make the setting feel a bit strange but nice with some variety from all the other similarly looking places.

The bacon in the big brekkie is to die for. The eggs are perfect and the sweet dressing on the greens are great combinations to go with a cuppa. The atmosphere is calm and relaxing for a Sunday brunch.

I've been rather hardworking for the past couple of weeks in checking out the cafes. Well I must say that Instagram has been most helpful in keeping me updated with the prettiest cafés on the block and that kinda led me to One Man Coffee, a hole in the wall that shares their shop front with Crust gourmet Pizza Bar along Upper Thomson Road. Sip on the Melbournian Axil Coffee Roaster beans pulled by Sarah Jane (formerly from Immigrants) or E-gene (who pulled his way around MEL). Coffee is little acidic with medium finish. My latte wasn't quite full bodied or milky though. While it's not quite my style, it was sufficient in packing a punch to last me through my afternoon meeting. Coffee is priced between $3 to $6.50. OMC also stocks B.A.O's pastries. I simply love Christophe's croissants, well the French makes the best croissants! The Chocolate pain is also amazing. Get them to heat it up for that crispy flakiness. Better still, have them with honey ham and melted cheese ($6). Cakes are also available and I was seduced by a Salted Caramel Banana Cake.For something a little more than sweets, OMC does all-day-breakfast with a lean but mean menu, all of which come out of a pizza oven! Talk about easy to make but delicious food here! Love the description of the Gashouse Egg aka Toad in hole aka Egg-in-the-bread-with-the-hole-in-the-middle ($10). It's more of a snack I feel. I really do have a monster appetite for breakfast food. The dish is really simple, they really do just make a hole in the fluffy brioche, crack an egg in, top with cheese and into the oven it goes. Almost a croque madame.Really there's no need to be fancy for brekkie when the ingredients are good (hello ooooozy yolk). What's special is that bacon jam which is smoky, meaty and sweet. I could do with a thick layer of that in the toast anytime. Satisfying flavors, a little dry on the edges, not so satisfying portion but that helps save space for other food. The Broiche French Toast ($10) is another popular item and it looked freaking amazing with the homemade berry compote, candied walnuts and fresh cream. Of course the dust of sugary white completes the instagram worthy picture. OMC is a great alternative to the super packed Habitat Coffee which I failed to visit TWICE! Well I guess I'll just have to explore the rest of the Thomson cafés until Habitat becomes less crowded. Anyhoo, great vibe at One Man Coffee but do go early or be prepared to wait as well due to the extremely small space.

I came here a couple months back with a friend and boy do they really need to improve on service. Seating done by a list is not extremely effective if you have a maitre'd who is easily pushed around. Granted it was a Saturday afternoon and from what I've heard (they're always packed), I felt that it should have been made clear that there was a waiting list for seating. Numerous parties after me all sat down at the same seats and were told of their policy and had to get up soon after. Would slapping a reserve sign on the table be so hard? On to coffee, we had a cappuccino and long black, the milk wasn't frothed well, and the long black was just the darkest point of my life to say the least. Last but not least, everyone around was ordering the french toast, so maybe you might have better luck with that than the coffee?

Sorry... I've had to dock a star. I enjoyed this place for coffee and went back to try a brunch on a Saturday. It was crowded, and the staff weren't very on the ball when it came to seating waiting customers. Tables were cleared but waiting customers were still left waiting... Tried the Big Brekkie and it was OK. The eggs were purportedly 60 degree eggs but I'm pretty sure mine were over cooked and too firm.

I stay really nearby and have heard of it before so I decided to try today. This coffee shop's name should be Wobble coffee instead. The tables outside are all wobbling. The wooden plate of food is also wobbling. The Big Breakie is not that fantastic. I like the one slide of bread though. Havent tried the coffee yet ( ya i know. It's such a shame)  I will come back just for the coffee one day

The good: High quality ingredients. Good ikan billis, nicely cooked onsen egg, tasty fish cake and quality noodles. You can tell a lot of care has gone into the food, and It's a nice place with a comfortable ambience. The combo meals are also pretty good value. The Less Good:All the above can't make up for lack of flavour. Unfortunately the broth of the House Special Pan Mee lacked flavour, and so did the noodles themselves. The same for the hot Chilli pan Mee. Very little flavour, and could've done with a light toss in some pork oil, or the drippings from the mince pork topping. The Chilli comes in a tiny container, which I thought was a bit stingy but turned out to be plenty. It was very spicy indeed!Overall a bit disappointing but I'd come back for the Sarawak Laksa (which I saw too late, after I'd placed my order!) and Kolo Mee.

This is the closest thing I have to the kin kin chilli pan Mee frm KL! Even the original Kin kin which now resides in Singapore is no where close to the KL kin kin! At about $9.20 for a set meal which comes with a small side and drink of your choice. The noodles is soft and not too dry, the egg is done perfectly to be mixed coating every bit of noodle. The bowl that they use is huge and it doesn't look like much but I have to say I'm very full after having finished it. A bit expensive for a bowl of noodles when I compare it to KL, but who am I kidding?! You can hardly get anything cheap in Singapore these days. But the question is, "does it hit the spot when I can't have the kin kin dried chilli pan Mee in Singapore?" YES DEFINITELY!!They should offer some soup to accompany it though. 4.0 STARS

Face to face ban mian is really not that fantastic, I will recommend the dry ban mian at tpy lor 5 hawker centre (blk 75? If I remember correctly ) which opens till 3-4 am. Although it is not the best I tasted but I'm pretty sure the next time you have ban mian craving, kin kin and face to face will not pop up in your mind ever.The positive thing is that the Sarawak noodle taste pretty ok, much better than the ban mian here.

This is a somewhat new noodle bar in City Square Mall, serving a plethora of Malaysian-style noodles. The place is clean and renovated nicely. I got the traditional Sarawak noodle set. The pork was quite good, and the noodles were quite al dente, and tossed with the egg, made it moderately tasty. I just don't understand why they give such a miserly portion of their chilli, which is in a tiny plastic container. They should put the chilli in self-serve containers on their tables.

Came here approximately at 5+pm on a Tuesday evening.It was pretty empty at that time. Only two tables were occupied (one occupied by the owner herself). And another corner seat was filled with another person with a laptop. Managed to get a corner seat too so I was able to re-pack the things I bought earlier.Had always wanted to try their hot and spicy pan mee and their wantons. Ordered that with three musketeers (lime, lemon, kumquat?) - pretty refreshing mix of sour and salty beverage.I left the noodles in the open for awhile before eating it as I was busy doing other stuffs. Managed to take a nice shot of it. Tried the wanton but it wasn't flavorful. The skin was crispy but the two small bite wantons probably lack of pepper and salt. The noodle was stuck together (like a lump) when I was about to consume it. On the side, there is a plastic container of the "spicy mix" to add flavors to the existing ingredients - flat noodles, poached egg, minced meat, fried anchovies and shreds of spring onions (not sure). But somehow the flavors were there. The meat was soft. The noodles were chewy and the anchovies gave a crunch and salty after taste to add to the noodles.The environment is definitely conducive for studying or doing admin work if you are on the go. I stayed here for awhile and decided to try the longan Ribena drink. Wasn't too impressive on that. Will be back again to try their other noodle and appetizer options ;)

Nice theming  for a noodle shop. Walls  decorated with wood carving and umbrella. The environment completes with thick wooden table and chairs, a cool air con and piped in music. This gives a nice rustic feeling bringing you back to yesteryear. Well may be not the music.It's a quick service concept but delivers the food to you. With limited number of choices, ordering was quickly taken. The cashier seems knowledgeable but did a small mistake but was corrected quickly. Overall the staff was friendly. Noodle dishes description was put up on a large menu board behind the counter much like that of a fast food restaurant. May be it is mimicking that as the food arrived quickly.Ordered the house special pan noodle value meal. The deal came with noodle, 2 wings and a drink. The noodle came with some minced meat , greens and an egg. The ikan billis (anchovies) came at the side along with a sambal chilli paste in a tub. The side dish of chicken wings came in the same long dish. Not sure if it was supposed to dump the anchovies and sambal into the soup, but I didn't. The egg looked good and I eat it alone, but it was rather cold. The soup was bland, it may be because I did not mix in the condiments. The noodle was cooked well and soft but not soggy mostly because the whole bowl was lukewarm.The 2 wings were pre-prepared so the skin was not as crispy as it would be. It was like only 1 and half wing as one of the wing was less than half the size of the other wing. Other side dishes available was fried won ton and cheese ball. The drink was honey lemon that tasted a tad salty hopefully from the 2 slices of lemon and not from some where else. At least the drink was cold with ice.Overall value wise, you pay for the environment. The noodle, side and drink itself should not command such a price as you can get better noodle and fried wings elsewhere. But then it is a restaurant in a shopping center that is  considered downtown, so price is somewhat cheaper than say at an orchard road eateries.

I'm a huge huge fan of KL kin kin chili pan mee (used to love the one at mcpherson but it sucks now), and so when I saw that there was another one in another area I decided to check it out. But I was very disappointed! I was craving it so badly and had such high expectation! I guess trying this place for the first time would be a 50/50 shot anyway considering the reviews. But I was close by and I figured well it can't be that bad. Yeah it was that bad. SO, STAY AWAY!!!!!! Absolutely terrible and super bland. I thought I needed more chili to enhance the flavorless pan mee but adding chili did not help at all. My bf and I had ordered the Sarawak noodle and Chili pan mee. The chili had no kick and flavorless, it's just like a plain boring dried chili; so different from how it's supposed to taste like originally in KL. The price is actually very high for a (not so delish) bowl of noodle so it's quite ridiculous however it's acceptable if the taste is mind-blowing. I heard the chef is from Ipoh well I guess he needs to visit KL and recreate his recipe again otherwise he won't have any repeat customer which is sad as I see a potential in him. Sadly I won't be back as of now. Hope it gets better in time.

Don't think there's anything new I can add that previous reviewers have not already mentioned. Good effort on the part of the restaurant, and the noodles and the ingredients are decent. The onsen egg is done just right. However, the flavor itself was lacking, and no amount of side dressings can make up for that. Also, this place does not take credit cards. For a nice eatery charging more than $10 in a shopping mall, that just shows a lack of concern for customer convenience.

Having tried the Nandos in Australia and London, I have high standards for this chain. It is disappointing that Singapore has decided to market it as a proper restaurant rather than the fast food/casual dining concept overseas. The Katong branch was disappointing with the chicken too dry and flavours lacking, but upon hearing good things about the Bugis Junction branch, I decided to give it another shot. The chicken comes in various flavours ranging from mild to extra hot, and my usual order of extra hot  piece chicken with peri peri chips was a very good comparison to the ones I've had in Australia. The meat was succulent, even with breast meat, and the peri peri sauce was flavourful and sufficient. The peri peri chips were good too, although more peri peri salt wouldn't have hurt. Overall, I the food was good, but unfortunately, at the end of the day it's still much better overseas and cheaper too.
Good food. The starter came with the main dish. Friendly staff. Liked music and atmosphere.

Walking past Nando's was always accompanied by a glimpse of mouth-watering chicken glistening in its famous peri-peri sauce. Food-wise, the chicken pita I ordered was average with nothing much to rave about. In fact, the chicken was on the dry side instead of the juicy chunks I was expecting. However, its mild peri-peri sauce deserved a thumbs up. The balance of herbs mixed with just the right amount of spiciness was perfect as an accompaniment to alleviate the filling of the pita. Each bite of the veggies has a lingering smokey aftertaste that leaves you craving for another bite. Although not the best i've had, Nando's is worth a try as a quick fix for cravings for smokey flavours. But do take note that service levels at the JCube branch are not quite satisfactory. The branch was severely understaffed and somewhat not attentive. Waving frantically when they looked vaguely in our direction was probably the only way to get their attention. Definitely not the most ideal, but forgivable for a heartland mall I guess.

Maybe we came on a rare good night and have the blissful ignorance of not having visited their apparently cheaper and better overseas locations, but we had an awesome, filling meal here for about $60. The chicken was well seasoned and flavorful. The chicken breast slices that came with the salad were perfect compared to the half chicken which was a little on the burnt side. The mashed sweet potatoes, corn on the cob, and salad were all excellent. My girlfriend said it was now one of her favorite restaurant at the end of the meal.
Good veggie wrap, nice, moist, juicy veggies and of course the Cora hot peri peri sauce! Very average on the hummus and pita, wouldn't order that again.

If you've had Nando's in Australia, you would know they are famous for their grilled chicken with peri-peri sauce. In Singapore you can find the exact same offering however at a much higher price. Nando's over here offers table service but with poor standards service and guess what, water is chargeable! The chicken here in Singapore is really dry and under seasoned. Honestly it gives first timers a bad impression of a brand that actually serves up really good grilled chicken!

Shanghai Dumpling aka Xiao Long Bao.  For years I've been seeing people declare that the best Xiao Long Bao is from Din Tai Fung.  Unfortunately, there are no Din Tai Fungs in Hawaii.  Apparently, Din Tai Fung seems to be all over the place in Singapore.  I think I saw at least 4 while out there.  This review is for the one at The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands.  During our first visit at this mall, the crowd waiting outside of Din Tai Fung was crazy.  I would estimate at least 50 people waiting.  So we passed on eating there are we thought it would be an hour wait at a minimum.  A couple of days later, we're back at the mall and my brother tells us to try it.  Again, there was a huge crowd waiting outside.  We're quoted a 20 minute wait... not too bad.... Unbelievably, I think the wait was closer to 15 minutes!  These guys are totally on it and they are fast.  (While you're waiting they give you a sheet that you can start marking off your order choices.  I'm sure this cuts down on time as a result.) We had the Xiao Long Bao (of course!)  It was excellent.  The juices inside were still liquid and not reabsorbed like all the other dim sum places.  Perfect!To be honest, the rest of the drunken chicken, spinach dumplings, etc. were as expected. Everything came out hot, delicious and freshly made.  Service was excellent.  It was a great lunch and if you go, do not be deterred by the crowds outside.

Honestly, this was my first experience of dumplings and I don't think I've been missing much. Maybe I'm not a dumpling fan or maybe this place just wasn't good. Who knows? What I do know is that a lot of the dishes on our table were dirty so we had to ask the staff to please give us clean ones... And for someone who is pretty much a germaphobe... That, alone, makes me not want to come here again.

Was a busy Saturday night and had family down from overseas so we headed to MBS. After waking around for half an hour we decide on Din Tai Fung and we were glad we chose it. Really good food..with the beef brisket being the best of them all! The dim sums especially the prawn ones were mouth watering and chili wantons were another great surprise! Service was good and attentive and thy were pleasant even though we were the last to leave and it was late.
Din Tai Fung is coming to Orange County!!!!!!!!!!!!!!   Near Sears where the Rain Forest Cafe used to be -----  I can't wait!!!!!!

I love all Din Tai Fung no matter where they are... this one is extra great because they have a wine list.  get some dumplings and enjoy great food.  i always take out of town guests and they love it!

This place is always recommended by everyone for places to eat in Singapore and with good reason! The soup dumplings here are the best, and they have so many varieties. It's always packed and a little overrated but so delicious, you have to come here at least once if you're ever in town. My favorite was the truffle soup dumplings even though my friends say it's not worth it. To me, it was! YUM!

How to view Din Tai Fung? Sort of the McDonald's and Starbucks. It's not bad at all but it's a safe backup as it's in many cities. Is it the best Xiao long bao? In sg I am not sure. Compared to China it's way below. Well below but I'm still glad it exists. I would say you are paying for a nice clean environment with clean ingredients. Clean=not as tasty. The venue. Casual. Lots of kids and families. The staff. Pretty good. Working hard.

A good place to slurp down some ramen or to eat dim sum. Beware that it is a fast-food style place, you will wait a few minutes outside and fill in your order form, and then get the food delivered to your table.The dim sum is actually pretty good so I would happily be back. Prices are a tad high for the type of place and service but not excessive. I was kinda divided between 3 and 4 to be honest.

I think because of the location the wait time here is always going to be an issue. We only had to wait about 15 minutes but during that time we had a order sheet and a menu so we could get a jump start on what we wanted to nosh on. The standard pork XLB and fried rice with egg and prawns are something we order every time. I also recommend the pork wontons in black vinegar with chili paste. Service here was not as good but it was also crazy busy. I would have to flag people down for refills or additions to our order.

This branch is inside Sands, among all the luxurious brands. I feel the price is higher than the other branches. Their xiao long bao is best for its skin, very thin and delicate, but the flavor is not so good, nor the meat inside. i like paradize dynasty more for its flavor but their skins are also thicker. Ding tai fung now also does the truffle flavor like paradise dynasty. i still like their hong you chao shou, but the Taipei HQ is so much better and spicier than this branch. Other side dishes such as veggies are okay but not very special.

Having been to DTF Stateside, I was interested to see how one in Singapore compared. It did not disappoint.The wait is pretty considerable, but given that it was in the Shoppes at MBS I expected a decent amount of people to be waiting. As with everything else in Singapore, the queue was orderly and the complete opposite of what goes on Stateside.Once seated though, the food was more than well worth the wait (also helps that you can select what you want to eat ahead of time while waiting). We did not go home hungry. Ordering what I typically get in the US (pork xiao long bao & shrimp shumai) was a good starting point to compare - consistently great. What surprised me were some of the menu items I hadn't seen yet (and needed to try). The pork and chili crab dumplings were amazing. But the truffle dumpling was absolutely phenomenal. Not sure if it was just from the amount of food eaten, but this place made me happy. It was like a rush of dopamine/serotonin/endorphins just flooded my system. Amazing, phenomenal comfort food wrapped in little pillow-y pieces of dough.

I don't want to say all Din Tai Fung chains are the same, because they're not. Wait time, service, attention to detail, promptness, and taste all seem to have some slight differences- this specific one is very keen on efficient customer service. This DTF does not have proper AC. It's very stuffy inside. Aside from that, there's nothing really to complain about. The place is managed well- take a number, walk MBS around for 45-60 minutes, come back, and get seated. Maybe a 30 minute wait for your orders to arrive. Like every other worldwide DTF location, you can gawk at the kitchen workers making the dumplings through the window. I still have an appreciation for the level of detail that goes into each individual dumpling, but I do not distinguish these XLB's or dumplings to be better or worse than the other DTF's I've been to. My main local DTF is in Bellevue, WA (USA), and it has one noticeable difference. The kitchen workers speak Spanish to one another, as opposed to Mandarin! !jajaja! (that's Spanish for laughter)But yeah, I'm DTF for some Din Tai Fung.

鼎泰丰 Din Tai Fung A big Thank You to my bestie from high school for taking me here for lunch!!Thanks to her quick thinking too, she got a seat around noon before I arrived. I could see people started coming in here for lunch and there was already a wait outside the restaurant. FOOD 4/5Din Tai Fung 鼎泰丰 is famous for their xiao long bao, it's also my favorite dish to order from here. I could just eat xiao long bao and nothing else. However, we girls ordered the followings:1) Xiao Long Bao 5/5*It's Din Tai Fung's famous signature rendition of the traditional steamed dumplings. The dumplings here consist of juicy meat fillings wrapped in melt-in-your-mouth paper thin skin. Each dumpling is supposed to be made with a minimum of 18 exquisite folds. Personally, xiao long bao the best at Din Tai Fung 鼎泰丰 ;)2) Sliced Duck in Crispy Spring Onion Pastry 3/5*The smoked duck inside the crispy pastry did nothing to me. I actually really dislike this dish among all the dishes we ordered. I do like the crispy spring onion pastry though. 3) Fried Rice with Shrimps & Eggs 5/5*The fried rice was so fragrant with the eggs and it was a simple rice dish yet it was really delicious. The fried rice was not loaded with heavy seasonings so the ingredients really shine through. Shrimps tasted fresh.4) Deep-Fried Specially Marinated Pork Chop 4/5*The boneless pork chop was well marinated and very tender. I like it but it did not blow my socks off. Meaning? I may not order this again in future. I would still recommend this dish though. 5) Mango Pudding 4/5*Again, this mango pudding was very good. It was not the best I had (maybe it had to do with the consistency)but it was the only dessert I would order here. I could see real pieces of mangoes inside, the pudding was sweet and I did not detect anything artificial. *rating out of 5AMBIENCE 4/5There is nothing intimate at any Din Tai Fung 鼎泰丰. It is for families and friends. I have no complaints about the ambience. Lively or noisy. I just concentrate on eating :PSERVICE 4/5The staffs who brought our food were all so nice and polite. Hard to get a staff's attention, my friend needed to order more food. I felt for her. Lol!! I never like to wave or wave frantically to staffs for their attention. Hmmm.. for some reason, i think I like the DTF's location at Orchard better.

Except for the xiao long bao, the dim sum dishes at Din Tai Fung are a bit boring for me, and the other dishes not that varied compared to Cantonese restaurants. However, it is extremely reliable in spite of the rapid expansion of the chain. Service at this outlet is better than the average.

This location was an excellent and easy meal from our hotel (the Marina Bay Sands). We ordered the pork dumplings, the vegetable dumplings, a pork black truffle dumpling, a yam bao, and a veggie bao. We also ordered a bottle of Fiji water and some hot green tea. Service was fast and friendly. The pork dumplings were SO yummy. The veggie were also good (a good option for a vegetarian). The veggie bao was the same filling as the veggie dumplings, so not interesting and my vegetarian fiancé says the dumplings were better. The pork black truffle dumpling was delicious, but I'm not sure it's SGD$5 each delicious. :-) We totally enjoyed our experience here! We would definitely come back.

Alas, my first experience at Din Tai Fung, where they supposedly serve the best xiao long bao in the world! But unfortunately, my verdict is that they're a little overrated. The dumpling skin was very thin and delicate, yet sturdy, and the pork inside was delicious, juicy, and succulent, but the soup could have been more flavorful. The steamed chili crabs filled buns, another one of DTF's specialty items, were very filling. The crabmeat had a bit of mild heat that didn't linger because the fluffy bun helped soothe the spicy sensation quickly. Despite the restaurant not at full capacity around 11am on a Saturday, the service felt a little slow but were kind nonetheless. My first experience at a DTF was more than satisfactory, and I would dine at the other international branches if I get the chance.

It's definitely way better than the average mall food. We felt like it was a real restaurant, not just another place on the food court. The food was good, with lots of options at good prices and the service was fast.

My family and I came here at the earlier side of lunch, and did not have to wait long. I highly approved of  their efficient "take a number" system, where they assign you a number and give you a menu to fill out while you wait.While the service initially was a bit slow, we really enjoyed our meal once the food started coming out. We all shared an assortment of steamed dumplings and buns and a bowl of dumpling noodle soup - all of which were awesome! The meal favorites for me were the pork, chicken, and vegetable dumplings. That being said, nothing we ordered was disliked. You can't go wrong at this place!
Why do people queue to be squashed elbow to elbow next to strangers to eat waffles while listening to next table conversations. Totally pretentious. So hipster I can't breathe.

I dont think these reviews need to be too long? This place is fit for purpose as a neighbourhood coffee joint, and if I lived around the corner I'd probably drop in for a coffee ever so often. Otherwise, better for kids with its friendly pricing or only as a second best option.

Another cafe tucked away in a neighborhood. Ambience is whimsical and nice. The decor is pretty sweet, especially the clear roof ceiling at the back of the cafe, the fairy lights and the adobe walls. Came here twice on a weekend night and a morning. There was already a crowd so we had to queue a little. Tried their breakfast menus as well as their deserts. Both were good, but nothing great in my books. Price is reasonable of course due to the quiet location.I have to commend their staff, particularly a male staff wearing black frame glasses, couldn't get his name. Excellent service, always with a smile and cheery attitude! Also orders were quick.Would definitely come back again, likely shooting for non-peak times again.Not sure if we caught a one-off experience but the quick service was a plus.

Visited Wimbly Lu a couple of times has made me a fan of this place. Love the carbonara with bacon, the creamy white sauce taste homemade, poached egg is well-cooked, spaghetti is Q, portion is just right. Love the waffle with chocolate ice cream. The waffle may look simple and plain, but that's the beauty of it. It is perfectly crisp on the outside and soft and airy on the inside. Goes really well with a scoop of chocolate ice cream. One of the best waffle I've ever had.Love the hot chocolate (70% dark chocolate). Rich and creamy and taste like a bar of dark chocolate.  Love the chicken nuggets. Crispy on the outside and juicy and tender on the inside. Overall, service and ambience is good, menu is well categorized for easy ordering. Just hope that they show a list of food photos on the menu so that those who has not been there before, know what to expect and order from the menu.
We had the Ethel's Blackout Cake. Kinda Nice.

Love the ambience. Drinks were well made, specially like the iced chocolate and mocha drink. One of the staff was really friendly and nice. However, i find most of them pretty inexperienced. They had 4 choices for 'soup of the day' which really should be soups of the day. We had the mushroom soup and it was quite pleasant. Beef cottage pie was not available so we thought of going for more desserts since there was a rave about it here.Waffle is a must; come early for it so that waiting time won't be long. When asked what was "eton mess", the staff said "choc cake", and what was "blackout", she said "choc cake". Could have been a little more specific and professional in this. In the end she recommended the blackout which was a total disappointment because it's just a very moist chocolate cake.Price is on the high. For the service and the quantity of food (the $5 chicken nugget comes with literally 5 piece of chicken karaage), i will only return if i am seriously craving for waffles. Else, nah.

Wimbly Lu is all about chocolate. Period.A rising star in a little hideout, Jalan Riang, it's really not that difficult to find with the cute red and white vintage beetle parked right in front of the shop. You might actually have better luck locating the Cafe than an empty parking lot!My fave there gotta be their Rootbeer Cake.Who in the world will think that rootbeer infused chocolate cake would taste so good! With a scope of vanilla ice cream, the combination is just like a regular rootbeer float just that instead of drinking, you are actually eating it.The salted caramel truffle has a touch of chocolate bitterness that fuses with the sweet and salty caramel. Rich and tantalising, it's a really cool chocolate treat! If you can't get enough of the chocolate, try their chocolate molten lava cake. There's seriously more "molten chocolate" than cake in this dessert. Havent had the chance to try their savoury dishes but their desserts are definitely good enough for me. ;)

Until now, I still do not know why this place is so popular. Ironically, the desserts did not impress even though Wimbly Lu is famous for them.   The Hazelnut Butterscotch Blondie ($4.50) was too dry and chalky with rancid untoasted nuts though the butterscotch sauce was rich and sweet. I don't understand the logic of molten lava cakes  $6without ice cream or creme anglaise sauce but I know some do. The version here is very rich, dense and luckily not too sweet. However, the cake texture was still dry as compared to Domino's or Morgansfield.   The Chocolate Tofu Cake $6 did not taste anything of tofu but I guessed the ingredient blended into the mousse did help to give it a smooth, creamy texture. However, the biscuit base was stale and not crunchy as described by the staff.   With a crisp texture and some even noted a resemblance with cereal taste, the signature waffles with one scoop ice cream ($8.50) was the better ones that day. I wonder if the salted caramel ice cream came from Salted Caramel at Upp Thomson though. But it was too small a scoop for the size of the waffles.Mediocre Cheese Toast Melts which can be skipped Another recommended item was the Chocolate Root Beer Cake $6. Think layers of root-beer-infused ganache intersecting with chocolate sponge. I like chocolate and root beer. But the combination of both tasted strange.Blackout Cake $6Bottomline, a cafe that is simply over-rated. Perhaps it is crowded because the seats are limited. My companions were generous to comment that the ambience was good, for instance the settings such as the red bricks tiled wall and lightings. But I tend to ignore ambience and focus on the food. Given the substandard quality of the chocolate desserts, I would not fancy a return.

Tucked away coffee shop in the Serangoon suburb.  All the locals hangout here on the weekend.  The chocolate, the cakes and the savouries are of superb quality.  They make a proper flatwhites which is hard to find in Singapore.  Service can get patchy as they get busy during the weekend.  They also showcase their decorating cakes which is very entertaining for children.  Recommended esp if you are in that area.

Love the space, reminded me a lot of NYC with the exposed brick wall, longish shop space, glass roof that lets the sun in.Coffee - much too weak. Can't taste the coffee at all.Brownie - like that it is rich and not sweet, but it was a tad dry.Truffles - nice to see them making them fresh in the shop. $2 each for assorted favors. But we didn't like any if the 3 favors that we tried (salted caramel, dark chocolate, bailey's). The chocolate taste is just not decadent enough and it doesn't feel like premium chocolate.I would go if I am in the area looking for a nice place to catch up with friends, but nothing to write home about.

The ambiance is great.  Wimbly Lu  has a very pretty, serene vintage feel. However, the food ranged from average (at best) to disappointing. But we loved the ambiance so much that the food didn't really mattered all that much after awhile. I would recommend you stick with the "safer" choices then sit back, relax & enjoy the place. Read a book. It's a beautiful way to spend a lazy sunday afternoon :) The food (desserts) 1. Root beer cake - We saw many tables order this + It was highly instagramed + It was a chef's choice... so we went against our gut feeling (which was warning us that root-beer & chocolate will probably taste weird) and order it. Sadly, our guts were right! This tasted pretty strange! I am a fan of root beer and chocolate. But not both together. Lesson learnt. 2. Waffles with salted caramel ice cream & toffee sauce - Since we went for a risky choice with #1, we decided opt for a safer choice with the waffles which was not bad. Average. Safe. Expected. My only complain was the toffee sauce which tasted nothing like the sticky, rich brown toffee sauce I expected. This was a translucent, honey colored liquid which tasted more like a cheap syrup than toffee! The salted caramel ice cream was also more salty than I'd prefer. 3. Honey lemon - Ok4 Scones - A good safe choice. Served with cream and jam... just the way I like my scones :) Service - Great.

The interior reminded me of the castle of Edinburgh with the exposed brick walls and natural light from the ceiling. Very vintage and yet homey. There are little nooks and crannies to be explored such as the kids section under the stairs. I think it's the perfect corner to take off your inhibitions along with your shoes and sit cross legged on the mat. You can do that while enjoying a yummylicious dessert.There's quite a selection of sweets but Wimbly Lu place quite a large emphasis on their chocolates. Caught sight of the Root Beer Float Cake, which has a slice of moist chocolate fudge cake soaked in root beer and ice cream and good ol' choc fudge. It's a dessert in a dessert! I don't know why this didn't appear on my table but then again it's really lousy judgement on my part for letting S do the ordering. :P Heard that this is pretty awesome. I think it's only $6.50.Skip the mains, go for desserts straight.
Great dessert place, ordered the banoffee pie, carrot cake, blackout cake and molten lava cake. Highly recommend the banoffee pie. Cakes here are as good as you expect them to be.

"Just go for the desserts, skip the real food."That's what I heard about Wimbly Lu. Well what happened was we had dinner at Fat Cat, and then we hopped over to Wimbly for desserts! A friend on Instagram also recommended their Orange Flour-less Cake, and someone said their Waffles are good. My neighbour told me about their molten lava cake and smores pie, which is then what we ordered. Chocolate overload!The molten lava cake was not as sweet as I expected though, which is good. Still gave me a sugar high (ok perhaps it was the smores pie) but the chocolate quality is detectable to be better than average. With the smores pie, it is a layer of granola crushed bits, with a huge chunk of chocolate, and molten marshmellows. Super decadent. super sweet.The place itself is very whimsical and nice. I really liked the decor, especially the ceiling fairy lights and the adobe walls. It was quite packed on a Sunday night as people lined up to sit for some coffee and desserts. The noise level is a bit high, but that's expected.

I heard good things, so I went... and ehhh I think it was all right.First impressions are GREAT. It's a BEAUTIFUL shop - vintage VW Beetle out front, great shopfront, and stepping in, you see the dark brown brickwork, and the greenhouse-style roof at the back... it's pretty gorgeous.Menu-wise one should remember that this is a chocolate shop. I wouldn't look at anything else, especially if the store itself says so. I've had a friend rave about their spicy hot chocolate (and he's a dude, so it must be pretty good). I... liked it, but I didn't think it was all that.The gang and I had a raft of other desserts too, and I was particularly looking forward to the clafoutis - cherries in a chocolate tart? Heck Yeah! When it came though... it was kinda thin and dry; perhaps their interpretation was a little different?This spot gives me a "style over substance" feel, but when so many friends are in love with it, I'll have to give it another try. And hope they've fixed the clafoutis.

I love this place, they make the most awesome desserts. Try their home made ice cream with waffles, it's probably as good as it gets anywhere else in Singapore. There's also a great ambience to chill out with friends.However, on weekends, do note that if your party is small you may get shifted around as larger parties come in and they need you to give up your seat. Didn't happen to me but the waiter did give advance notice in case it happened.

Located at Jalan Riang, Wimbly Lu was certainly a hard place to find for someone who did not know the area well. It is perhaps easier to identify their adorably vintage signature car parked outside which is quite hard to miss. I was brought there by a friend who had raved about the place and their waffles.The place was not big but very cosy and comfortable, with quite a nice homely feel to it. We went there in the day but I was told by my friend that it was gorgeous at night with the lights and an open area so I would have to go again to witness it for myself. The staff were extremely pleasant with huge smiles and an ever-ready attitude, which made it a very delightful experience indeed. The happiness of the staff seemed to be rather infectious as it made me feel rather happy too despite the rain outside.I ordered a chicken baked rice which seemed to be more of an eastern take on chicken baked rice, without the creaminess that most baked rice dishes have. In fact, there was no sauce, and it was simply a slightly sweet chicken and mushroom rice, reminiscent of claypot rice, baked with a layer of cheese that was likely some form of cream cheese instead of the usual cheddar or mozarella. Although it was not the best baked rice I've had, it was quite an interesting take on chicken baked rice and went rather well together as a whole. We also had their famous waffles with cinnamon icecream, and though the ice-cream was far too grainy, the waffles were wonderfully fluffy on the outside and crispy on the inside.With the stellar service I received and yummy waffles, I would be more than glad to go back again to verify if it is indeed as lovely as my friend had described at night.

I dropped by Wimbly Lu one evening with the parents as I was craving some sort of a chocolate cake. As I live around the area, wimbly lu was probably the closest cafe for me to get a nice cup of coffee and cake. I have heard raving reviews about the place from some friends who have been there a couple of times. My parents were familiar with the area so we found the cafe quite easily. However, I believe it might be pretty difficult for most people to get there by foot as it is located in the private housing estate quite a distance from the nearest MRT station (Serangoon MRT). The cafe is easily identifiable by their signature red car parked outside. The decor of the place is lovely, and great attention is put into the display pieces and ornaments placed around. Walking in, antique looking shelves line the wall, giving the place a touch of vintage. The rustic red bricked wall on one side, coupled with the beautiful lighting gave the place a homely, yet romantic atmosphere. I had their Rootbeer cake, which essentially was a piece of dark chocolate cake infused with root beer, topped with a chocolate root beer syrup and served with vanilla ice-cream. The chocolate cake was alright, and I could taste the hint of root beer with each mouthful. However, the chocolate did not come through sufficiently, which was pretty disappointing as what can be worse in a chocolate cake than not tasting the chocolate. That said, the chocolate syrup was divine. The chocolate was thick, but not too heavy, and the root beer flavour combined with it brilliantly. The vanilla ice-cream was slightly icy, but otherwise went well with the cake. I also had a flat white, which was pretty good!The service at Wimbly Lu was brilliant. The service staff were attentive and patient, answering my questions about their various desserts. Overall, this cafe is a pretty awesome find and I will definitely be back to try more of their offerings (especially their waffles, which I heard is pretty good).

really good desserts at this small store in a surprisingly hipster part of serangoon - I live near the area and never knew this place even existed (except for all the posts floating about the blogosphere on this place and its cajun neighbour). I didn't really know what to expect, actually - I tried to come with tempered expectations in case it didn't actually live up to the hype - but came away liking it quite a bit.it's a small space (so be prepared to wait), but gorgeously furnished in kitschy retrovintage furnishings and what I feel is rather old-school american - which also leads me to ask: have you also noticed that hipster places in singapore take on a vintage persona from history that never quite happened to us? I feel like this place could fit in fantastically in seattle, but here seems a little like an isolated microcosm of american fifties-style coffee shops.and the food? pretty good, really. we had two waffles  - both of which came warm, crisp outside with soft insides. I think this ought to be a sure-order; it's a rather large portion as well. we also had a bread pudding - served with crème anglaise - as well as a still molten chocolate lava cake. I think the latter was more impressive - the chocolate was sufficiently darkwell-worth a return, and especially so after dinner at the fat cat.

Just based on the butter crab dish itself, I would come back countless times. The other dish that I would order is crab bathed in creamy less buttery soup with some udon like noodles.The only two things I don't like is that one rude person who took my order and sounded like I owed him a great amount of money and the waiting time. But who am I kidding here? Everywhere with good food needs to wait. So the next time I go, I hope that that guy won't be there to take my order.Current medium (which is the large) crab over at Mellbenn is about $80 per crab. Tell me where else would have tasty butter crab and I will hunt it down.

Get ready to get your fingers dirty for some delicious seafood!This is a great place, but a bit out of the way from the MRT Stations. You would have to take the Red North South Line to Ang Mo Kio, and either have a long walk or hail a taxicab. But, the location is prime because of the large space.Be prepared to wait though. There are usually long lines here, and a group of 10 of us had to queue for about 45-55 minutes. Pick up a menu, and prepare to order while waiting in line so the wait for your food will not take as long once you are seated.We ordered 2 small chili crabs, 2 small butter crabs, 1 medium Signature Crab Soup Bee Hoon (Noodle Soup), Jia Mantao (Fried Buns - which are great for dipping in the chili or butter sauce), and stirred fried vegetables.
