This was the perfect amount for 10 of us!Having tried a lot of seafood from all over the world from Maine Lobster to Scandinavian Salmon to Hawker Centres across Singapore, this has definitely been one of the freshest and most tasty seafood experiences I have had. We ended up pay about $33 Singaporean dollars per person, which is not bad at all!The wait is long, but it is worth it!
The best buttered and pepper crab i have tasted in singapore. Bit pricey but all worth-it.

Mellben used to be one of my favourite crab places. I still like it, although the prices have gone up substantially as they got more famous. Where they used to be one stall in a kopitiam, they are now the entire kopitiam (which got revamped to look more restaurant-like, adorned with decorated crab shells on the walls.. quite cute). The prices are significantly more expensive now.The crab bee hoon soup is still excellent, rich and delicious as always. The creamy butter crab still has the tasty sauce that few other stalls can replicate. I also like the Playboy Chicken (feng liu ji) which is what people here would usually call Thai-style lemon chicken, except it's better and comes with a beautiful sauce. I still like it, but it's become harder to justify coming back here as often as I used to, just because of how expensive it has become.

crab crab crab. i love crab.that is why i love melben. it soothes the inner crab cravings.crab bee hoon, butter crab, chili crab, its ALL good. this is THE place to go if you have some way of transporting yourself out into the Heartland.

I love the food here. This is where you can get one of the best seafood in the heartlands, at heartland prices (or close).Chilli crab, pepper crab, etc... but the most amazing dish that I like is the Cream crab! Of course their signature crab bee hoon is fantastic here too.The only drawback is the wait times. You have to wait around 1-2 hours, depending on which date and time you go. We went during dinner on a Saturday, and my poor friend had to stand in a long snaking line for almost 2 hours.Will I return? Yes!

One of my favorite places for crabs! Their food is always so good whenever I go. And it's amazing how long the queue is!! The downside is they don't take reservation but luckily the queue moves quite fast. I just hope they are not going to get more expensive than they already are.

Utterly absolutely amazing. I'm hard pressed to think of a better place to get a crab fix. This place was so highly adorned by my fellow crab-worshipping friends, yet I was an unbeliever for the longest time - for this I repent!!!We shared a huge butter crab, chilli crab and a bowl of crab bee hoon (with a whole crab in it of course). Everything was absolutely stunning. The least overwhelming one was probably the chilli crab, mostly because this is a taste you could get from your Jumbos and Long Beaches and the chilli sauce isn't particularly special. The butter crab, on the other hand, was soooo to die for. It was tastefully sweet, and perfectly buttery. Think about the best butter prawns you've had in your life, and think of that taste in a bottle. Now open that bottle and pour that insane goodness all over this beautifully fat steamed crab, throw on some curry leaves and you've got a plate of perfection before you. I confess to underestimating the power of the crab bee hoon. When my friends proposed to order that, I was going all "huh, noodles at a crab place - really?" But how incredibly wrong I was. The broth was sooo sedap and rich with the fragrance of the crab cooked in it. It is also very milky and makes a perfect accompaniment to the noodles, or just as a soup on its own. It's so good that it makes the crab in it a little underwhelming. It was ultimately still really good steamed crab, but I spent most of my time slurping the soup with noodles and digging into the butter crab instead.One warning though: be ready to queue for so so long. Bring a stool, bring a fan, bring a book, bring a friend. We went really early at 530pm and were fortunate to only have to wait in line for about 40 minutes, but a friend of mine once spent 3 hours in line on a weekday night, so...brace yourself!

Ok, as most things go, they used to be better. Now they have done some renovation and looks like a real restaurant rather than a tze-char restaurant on a HDB void deck. Good or bad, it depends on your preference.I only come for the crab beehoon soup and it is still the best around. It is like the best sliced fish beehoon that you have tried, only that it's made with crab. so it's sweeter and thicker. Yums. We typically cleaned the entire claypot.Have not tried any other crab dishes here.Not sure if it is that common or only common here, but they post photos of customers who leave without paying. I guess as a form of public shaming? Weird...kind of...

After being on my list of places to check out for ages, a few of us went down to Mellben AMK to try their famous crab bee hoon on Mothers Day 2012. Firstly, the queue is always large, others here seem to think you can get through quickly at certain hours, but not anywhere near dinner. We arrived at 7:15pm, were seated at 8:30pm and the food arrived after 9pm.But when it does arrive, it is well worth the wait. The menu does not have prices listed, which is terrible, so prices may be slightly off. The first to arrive was the tofu combination ($7.80) which was a dozen or so fried tofu squares, some broccoli, two shelled prawns and two scallops. Quite average.Next up was the famous fried crab bee hoon ($55). We were lucky to get a female crab with lots of roe, and the whole dish is out of this world awesome. Not an incredibly secret list of ingredients, it should be easy to replicate this at home.Finally, the last dish was butter crab ($55) which I would never have ordered normally, except I read the comments on HGW and honestly believe in the wisdom of crowds. Very awesome dish, the sauce was thick, buttery, had a hint of chili and went perfect with the crab.So the positives were to be expected, the crabs are fantastic, and well worth the trek to AMK. Their are a few suggestions I have:* put prices on the menus. Yes, I know seafood is at market price, but even the veges on the menu are not priced. It is great that service charge + GST are included, but everyone should do this.* the tofu combination is below par* take credit cards and lose the whole no 100% guarantee crap - no-one advertises their terrible customer service

When my colleagues discovered that I'm a crab lover, they whisked me away to Mellben over the weekend. It was at a kopitiam in one of the HDB estates in Ang Mo Kio; the environment was bustling and filled with hungry customers. The Mellben signboard hung high and proud on top of the shop. There was no price list for us to reference, it was just talking to the person who took orders and praying it all won't be too wallet-busting. The range for crabs is generally $50 - $60, depending on market price. We had the chili crab with the fried buns for dips. The gravy was sweet with generous pools of eggs, the claws were full of juicy crab meat, but other than that, it wasn't very memorable, especially for the money that was spent. Crabs are already good to begin with and I've tasted better ones elsewhere.Be prepared for long queues during peak periods.

my mouth still waters thinking about this chili crab temple.  had 4 types including bee hoon which had an amazing milky broth, black pepper, and butter shared among four.  the mantou are perfect for soaking up the chili crab sauce.  "finger licking good" should be applied here!  and bring some extra packs of napkins.back again for more crab -- choose large for the chili crab, medium bee hoon for 4.  also had the shrimp in curry sauce, lemongrass, very nice.  add some veggies

This is my favorite haunt for crabs. Simply because they have the best crabs in town! Unfortunately, the rest of the food items are just a-okay, so I usually only eat crabs when I'm here. One of those places that again has long lines. Doesn't matter if you'd made a reservations, you still have to queue up to some extent. The good thing is that it is worth the wait. My absolute favorite is the butter crab. The sauce is sweet, savory and a little spicy all at the same time. And the crabs are so sweet and meaty! :) I've never tried the salted egg yolk flavor but it looks good as well. The chili crab is pretty good, and the crab vermicelli soup is very good as well.

I went there for dinner with my family. I love their crab with the chilli sauce and claypot crab the bee hoon soup..taste so good. The place was quite hot because there is no air conditioner and u can get sweaty. The cereal prawn is also good!! During the weekend or dinner time the queue can take up from 30 minutes to 1 hour.CONCLUSION = RECOMMENDED!!!

Two things to order- crab bee hoon soup in claypot- butter crab- ok maybe add fried buns (mantou)You can skip the rest. You are only here for the crabs, nothing but crabs. The bad is the long wait, averaging 1-2 hours, though it seemed like the wait is more 45-60 mins now. Even at 9pm on a Thursday night, the line was still there. It only disappeared at 930pm. You are warned. Make reservations though they do not take it during the 15 days of Chinese New Year. Now why the crabs? The crab bee hoon soup is just very tasty. The taste is similar to the fish bee hoon soup but this is sweeter and tastier. The butter crab is to die for. The butter cream is so tasty and perfect to dip the mantou in. We had 3 crabs for 5 persons and it was just nice.

Finally visited Mellben after YEARS of everyone telling me that we should go. Firstly, make reservations. If not, you'll wait for a long time. Even with reservations, you have to wait! Secondly, know that this place is pricy. If you're having crabs, be prepared to drop a good dime here. Estimate about $90 for a medium crab--good for 2 or 3, I think.We got the butter crab and crab bee hoon. Crab bee hoon is the classic dish here and everyone gets it. It is very good. Add more soup and bee hoon; it is worth it. The butter crab is good too, and has a more heavy flavor and is also very creamy. Both were delicious. The crabs are fresh and the meat is plentiful and succulent. After all, you're paying good money for these crabs.The other side orders are good too. We got rojak chicken, tofu with pork floss and mushrooms, and salted egg pork ribs. The salted egg pork ribs were not very meaty, unfortunately. Come here for crabs. The crabs are so good. It would have been 5 stars if it weren't so pricey, were less touristy and had a better reservation/queue system.

As everyone knows this is the best spot for crabs in Singapore. Well this was the only spot I visited due to the amount of time I had here.  You can get crab cooked in different ways, but the most popular is the chili crab.   And the fried mon taos seem to be popular and used to soak up the sauces. And don't be like me trying to muscle through some of the crab pieces.  I ended up slicing my finger pretty bad.  Ask for a cracker or something to get into it.  We ordered way too much food, but my cousins wanted to try as much as we could since it was our last night.  The food was bomb, but the price is super expensive.  I think the total came out to about 350 USD for the 4 of us.  We didnt make reservations but we only waited about 20 minutes for a table.  Highly recommend you to try out if visiting Singapore.  Just make sure you dont eat and jet, they have cameras and pictures of ppl who've done it before - lmao

Apparently this is where all the locals go! Great seafood!It's not a fancy restaurant, there's no AC, but the food is delicious. We had all things seafood! Cereal prawn,  kang kong, two crabs (one salted egg-yum! and the crab beehoon with the soup noodles). Get here early, or expect a long queue!Everything is freshly cooked so it takes a little while as well for your food to be served.

This is one of the place you had to go when you are craving for crabs.This is my 2nd visit here and I really love the way they cook the crabs here. This outlet which I went is located at Ang Mo Kio, it is just located right below a HDB. I went to this place on 2 separate occasion and it's always bustling with people. There's a huge carpark located infront of the restaurant and fret not there's plenty of car lot. But try to avoid popping by during dinner time as this is a residential area so car lot might be limited.We order quite a number of dish that night and it was a treat by a friend therefore I can't state the bill for the meal. 1) Signature Crab Beehoon Soup 5/5This is a must to try, the broth make you go drooling and it's so flavourful as the beehoon and crab is cook together. I always ask for extra portion of soup as it's really very good.2) Salted Egg yolk Crab 4/5Anything cook with salted egg yolk is always so yummy. The crab is coated with salted egg yolk and the flavour just blend in so well which keep your finger locking good3) Butter Crab 4/5Oh my, the mantou really goes well with the butter sauce and the children keep dipping into the sauce with their mantou and crab. I think this really tells you how good it is. 4) Cereal Prawn 4/5This is one of my all time favourite, love the fragrant smell of the cereal and Prawn. They just simply blend in and the Prawn is so crunchy.If you ever pop by here, pls order their signature crab beehoon soup. Trust me it's really very very good.

We brought our overseas guests here on a rainy saturday evening. Have warned them about the snaky q as we did not make any reservations, but it wasnt that bad actually, perhaps because of the rain.We were seated down after about 15 mins & our food arrived 15 mins later. We had the crab with bee hoon soup, butter crab & chilli crab with fried mantous (dough). For drinks we had the fresh coconut ($5) each. Our guests love this place & declare it as the most delicious crab they have ever eaten in Sg. In their 1 week trip here, they have tried at least 5 different places for crabs.The place is full of tourists & locals. Price is stated clearly & size of the crabs. Check out the  wall of fame in the restaurant. This place is not air conditioned. 5 of us shared 3 small crabs.

Mellben is located under a HDB block in Ang Mo Kio but because this restaurant been featured in some travel magazine this restaurant always pack with tourist. So my suggestion will be make an effort to call and make a reservation 1 day before.They are famous for their crab, the most famous dish will be the crab beehoon (rice noodles) soup. So you will see almost each table will have this dish. The soup are very nice have a strong taste of crab freshness, if you want more soup you may request for a bowl or two, but they charge for each bowl or soup.I also recommend that you try the butter and salted egg crab. You might want to skip the chili crab, personally I find it don't taste as good as lots of other restaurant in Singapore.The only problem I have with this restaurant is no Aircon, so get ready to sweat when enjoy those yummylious crab.

The crab bee hoon soup was pretty bomb. Wish they had cracked more of the crab shell for us though. Also cereal prawns are a must order. Black pepper crab was pretty large and legit. No wait at all since we got there a few minutes after they opened at 5pm. Interesting that they have a policy that states meat is not guaranteed in the crab -- what?! So what am I paying $70-100 for then?! Luckily we had meat in our crab. Price was not as bad as I was expecting. Only $37pp for a table of 7 and we were pretty stuffed.

*4.5 stars*Love this place! About a 15 min walk from Ang Mo Kio mrt but worth the trek. Officially my go-to place when I have out-of-town visitors that need to try some chili crab. The crabs are so meaty here and I learned to request for the male ones because the claws are bigger! For those who think it's a hassle to eat crab and don't usually think it's worth the effort, this place will change your mind =) I've also tried their famous crab bee hoon that comes in a claypot and actually like this better so if you have enough people, try both flavors.Making reservations is also highly recommended.

My friend insisted that this was the best place to get chili crab. I don't often eat it seeing as it's so intense so I trusted her opinion. SHE WAS SO RIGHT. HOLY CRAP. Honestly you shouldn't really order anything else except chili crab and mantou. We however were quite hungry so in addition to our mountain of mantou and 2 chili crabs, we also got the salted egg yolk green beans which were a perfect 'starter' before the main event. I'm drooling just thinking about how good it was...

Mellben Mellben Mellben... How can anyone not like the seafood and their signature Crab Soup Bee Hoon?!?!?!?! The soup is just right in flavor and with the huge crab soaked in it, it's truly heavenly. Of course other must try dishes include their deep fried prawns cooked with oatmeal, chilli crab (you can ask for less spicy for those who cant take the heat, like me!) and fried dough fritters.For a good seafood indulgence, please make your way here.Do remember make reservation if you don't wanna wait too long in the queue!Oh oh, something that I thought was hilarious yet cool. If you head to the loo at the restaurant, don't forget to check out the photos that they have put up of various people who tried their luck in getting a "free meal". All victims have their faces caught on tape and their pictures are plastered all over the sink area. How shameful!! Tsk tsk tsk.

Delicious creamy butter crabs! It was worth the 1 hour wait... With 4 drinks and 2 plates of fried mantou(each plate had 10 mantous) and a crab bee hoon, it cost us $144. Split by 4 people it wasn't too bad and we were bloated!!! I couldn't eat anymore! There was so much crab roe!! It was delicious!!! But so high in cholesterol! :( otherwise I would've eaten it all!! The butter crab sauce is perfect for dipping the mantou in! I was tempted to ask if they just sell me the sauce! Would totally just eat the sauce with plain white rice! The crab bee hoon though it was supposed to be bee hoon portions for 2 people, 4 of us barely managed to finish it. We were a party of 3 girls and 1 guy. The soup is delicious, although I could sense a great deal of MSG in the soup! But still worth the wait!! We came at 7pm and waited an hour for a table. We came on a Tuesday night!

Best crab bee hoon and butter crab in Singapore!!Having been away from Singapore for long periods at a time, this is one place I always crave for. The crab bee hoon is super flavorful with the broth having a strong sweetness from the crab. The butter crab is heavenly and always leaves me licking my fingers. The wait here is VERY long, even on rainy weekdays so definitely do come early. The place is pretty hard to get to via MRT so you gotta drive or cab or bus here.You still have to wait for about an hour for take out because they cook your order on the spot and it takes about an hour for the crab bee hoon to be ready!Trust me, the wait is worth it.

Haven't been here in 2 years, but came here today to satisfy my wife's sweet tooth. She had the black sesame yoghurt with azuki bean, and I had the original pancake. Not sure if standard has dropped or my taste has matured, but not as amazing as I remembered.Furthermore, waited 35mins for the yoghurt, and 45mins for the pancake. Still, good variety of food, desserts and drinks at reasonable prices. Would consider coming back if it's not too crowded.

Well well well.. Another Japanese french Fusion Restaurant. Along with the dolce tokyo, ma maison etc.... It seems like everyone one is trying to ride on the whole jap-french and now korean-french cafe/bakery.We've walked past this place plenty of times before, always wondering if it's worth a try and finally... We decided to give it a shot. First impression ...not too bad.... Place had the type of decor I liked, warm woods with metal and Edison bulbs. Menu is simple enough, pasta, rice and their renown soufflés (which I unfortunately didn't get the chance to try). Instead, we went for a mixed seafood in squid ink rice, clam chowder and tried a matcha ice cream in iced matcha latte. First up, the clam chowder. First glance, nice presentation but chowder looks very light and "liquidity". Upon tasting, just as I expected, instant and mixed in with the bare minimum of what makes a clam chowder. I counted maybe 3 clams at most while the potatoes were still crunchy. I don't think I've ever had crunchy potatoes in a chowder before. Carrots were barely there and the entire chowder didn't taste so much a chowder as it did a plain soup. No distinct seafood or clam flavours. Next up came the matcha. The latte itself was decent enough while the ice cream was a little sweet eaten in its own. Mixed in with the matcha and it was much much better. Lastly, the rice. For once, a dish that looked very similar to its poster and menu. The Dish looked appetizing enough, with the rice nicely coated in squid ink and the egg they put on top looking extremely appetizing. Now I'm no expert in cooking, but, I do know that squid ink is very delicate. Over or undercook it and you'll be left with a pungent rancid after taste. Dish came with a decent portion of rice with about 4 pieces of squid, 3 shrimps (those peeled frozen ones you get at a supermarket) and 3 mini scallops (the kind you find on top of a sushi). Overall, it tastes really good. Well seasoned with the egg bringing balance and really tying the dish together. Now... I would have given this place a 4* rating based on the rice alone but 4 main factors hanged all that. 1) An underwhelming clam chowder 2) the sheer size and cost of the drink. It was $8.00 for something slightly bigger than a large tea cup. 3) the overall price of this place. 3 dishes for $40+ is not value for money and if I'm going to compare it to other places that serve me seafood in a pan than you're better off at fish and co or Manhattan fish market where you get a bigger bang for your buck.4) while leaving the place, a staff tried squeezing by me and banged into me accidentally. That's fine but a word of sorry would be nice. That's the problem with our service industry isn't it? Maybe my rating will increase once I try the popular soufflés and french toast but until then, this place is forgettable.

I can't say much for the rest of their offerings since I only had the Miam Miam spaghetti. First impression was: dang, hot mess!The pro? Every spoonful/ forkful of spaghetti yielded a different taste because of the different combination of ingredients. However, it still looked messy. Still, I'm all for trading aesthetics for taste. Light butter coating the spaghetti combined with sautéed vegetables and sliced sausages, topped with an egg. It was definitely a satisfying meal, but until I've tried more of their offerings.... I wouldn't know, maybe this could have been the cherry on the cake?

Another Hoshino? Maybe? Maybe not. The Miam Miam Spaghetti was our favourite.  Like a typical Japanese wafu pasta, the cream is kept to a minimum or literally non existent. But when French butter, onion, shoyu and some secret broth is reduced in a right way and tossed with sausages, spinach and bacon, the dish  ($16.80++)  turned out brilliant, better than it should be for what went into it. Interestingly, the Riz Noir ($16.50++) which resembled a Spanish squid ink paella, is made with Hokkaido's top grade ika sumi powder. The grains had a delectable firm chewy bites and garlicky flavour, though the scrambled eggs were far from the soft runny Japanese style omelette. Meanwhile, it was the opposite situation for the Souffle de Nuage ($17.50++); slightly clumpy glutinous rice-like tomato grains that are cleverly masqueraded beneath the golden and cheesy tasting whipped eggs. For the sweets, french toasts  ($10.80++) with their irresistible buttery aroma are probably the best morning call one like to receive but these stiff, slightly dry brioche deprived of the moist eggy flavour seems to lack a bit of that charm.Matcha desserts such as matcha parfait  ($11.80++)  or matcha souffle ($11.80++) are made with top grade matcha powder from Japan but unfortunately the taste did not come forth. However, the Varlhona chocolate soufflé ($13.80++) was excellent. Though it did not rise tall and high as I imagined, this dense baked chocolate dessert has a delicious molten center achieved by precise execution of oven time and the bonus drizzle of chocolate sauce on top. Do place the order early as it takes up to 20-25 minutes to prepare.

I keep calling it Niam Niam.... Instead of miam miam.I think baby talk never escaped me*.Anyway, I've been here 3 times and I keep ordering the same food.The Niam ..no wait the miam miam spaghetti and the arrabiatta Awesome possums. The spaghettis are really good. Came in huge plates and huge servings. No problem for me. I am getting good at clearing mah fooooooooood So much so that I ordered a valhorna choc souffle.Came pipping hot. In had to wait a few minutes before I could gorge it down my mouth. I'm glad I chose patience instead of a burnt tongue. Velvety and smooth and not to sinful ( can it be?) Oh so  Soft in the centre! The coffee is also a must have. Hand dripped and its good. Oh so good. Muddy and earthy just how I like it*kinda like nom nom

First. This is a cheap place so the $$$$ rating is wrong. It's mostly pastas and soufflés. To be honest the non dessert soufflés is just so so. It's so weird when they just put a half hotdog twice inside. It's like the chef chopped his finger off and just left it inside. The pastas really shine more. I can imagine the dessert soufflés are nice. Croque Monsieur is so so. An average experience.

When it comes to French Toast, the most talked about one currently has got to be Miam Miam. With all the raving going on, I had to check it out for myself and French toast for dinner is always a good idea in Ms Skinnyfat's food world.Miam Miam is a French-Japanese cafe and they serve the usual Fusion Japanese cafe stuff e.g. pasta, baked rice, soufflé, matcha latte and of course french toast. Knowing that they do not take reservations, we made it down early to the Bugis Junction outlet on a Friday evening and an empty restaurant welcomed us (but not for long).Drinks first, the Iced Matcha Latte with Softee ($8.80) was actually pretty decent. Great green tea flavor with a milky flavor, though I still prefer the intensity of Nana's Green Tea.Iced Earl Grey with Softtee ($6.80) was bleah. The tea was too weak and the softee lacked in the cream department. Take note that water is charged at 50 cents a cup.Gave the other savory dishes a try as well. The Riz Noir ($15.80) is a Squid Ink Black Rice and Scrambled Omu Egg. The portion was surprisingly small though. A rather disappointing dish that lacked in smokiness. The rice while moist was also on the salty end. Eggs were nicely done though.The Miam Miam Spaghetti ($15.80) was typically Japanese with a light savory sauce made from French butter, shoyu and some secret sauce. Well, looking at the ingredients (processed sausage, bacon, some vegetables and mushrooms and a soft boiled egg), it seemed like a randomly thrown together plate of home cooked noodles and indeed it tasted kinda like that as well. Not to say that it's not nice but i would expect better ingredients. If you are a fan of saucy food, then the Riz Au Curry ($15.50) would be for you. Sweetish rich Japanese curry with soft rice, minced meat (almost non-existent) pork sausages, broccoli cheese and egg. Everything kinda drowned in the curry. The flavor of the curry was alright but maybe just go easy on the sauce?Now the redeeming grace of Miam Miam would be their desserts and there are pancakes, souffles and parfaits. Honestly, there's one thing that you definitely should order and that's the French Toast.Disappointing mains aside, the French Toast ($9.80) was every bit as good as everyone promised. Soft fluffy brioche cubes that had the texture of clouds. They're paired with the thoroughly whipped heavy cream, it is close to clotted cream but lighter in taste (but sweeter) and texture. Absolutely delicious with the smoky maple syrup. I would have drenched the toast with it but there wasn't enough. Have this as a main course instead!Matcha Souffle ($10.80) was undercooked and very wet inside. The texture is that of whipped raw egg whites that are pandan flavored. I could hardly taste any matcha. The Chocolate Molleaux Dessert ($9.80) fared better with the rich chocolate taste though i found it on the cakey end. The softee was too icy and lacked in vanilla. That said, i wouldn't mind having this again.Conclusion, Miam Miam is better for its sweets. The mains will fill you up but you wouldn't be quite satisfied. Maybe the pasta is alright. I don't know. But as for me, i'll stick with the French Toast and Matcha Latte for now.
Food was delicious. Don't order any of their coffee, especially Cafe Au Lait, no taste of coffee only milk. Service very bad.

This is the best restaurant-on-the-fly experience... ever. I work a block away from Alt. Pizza and have been walking past the restaurant everyday, skeptical and all since, um, when you work in the doldrums known as Suntec City everything looks bad, overpriced or both. Hello only 3 bars for after work drinks, $0.70/pc yong tau foo and the crankiest front-of-house staff at the ONLY salad bar in the vicinity? Yup it's that crappy.Anyway, my colleague and I decided to try Alt. Pizza after a long lunchtime meeting. We were starving, it looked empty, cheerful and held the possibility of good food.The order chits were simple i.e. you fill in what you want and hand it to the waiter, and they served iced water free. The average pizza is about 1.5x the size of your face and costs $12-16, which is ah-mazing value for Singapore, let alone an office area. Let me just talk about the pizza for a second. Wow. Thin crust, quickly oven crisped, fresh ingredients, nothing processed and the most insane cheese (I ordered the Free Bird) topped my lovely pie. I kept declaring that I would return again with the dude while chomping down my entire pizza. Yes, I ate the whole thing by myself. I also shared the spinach salad with my colleague and it had the lightest but sufficient dressing and some crushed nuts.I'll probably be eating at Alt. Pizza again, tomorrow. I need to eat every starter on the menu and have some of those craft beers. If you work in the area, PLEASE DON'T COME HERE. I don't want to have to queue up for insanely delicious and affordable pizza. Kthxbye.
Pretty good. Not too greasy. The chese was good. Often I find good cheese lacking in Singapore.

It's a high energy, well put together place. Pizzeria, Craft beer, wings & burger what more one can ask for! And all of it is decently priced. The food we had; Pizza & Wings w blue cheese sauce were pretty good not outstanding, but the craft beer was excellent and also rest of the elements came together so well have to rate it a 5, worth a repeat visit..

Best pizza in Singapore. Quality is good, prices are reasonable, location is convenient.  Wine and craft beer choices are decent, with wallet-friendly price tags. What is there not to like? We've been a couple of times, and have introduced colleagues and friends over, who have also been impressed. Only if it could offer some sort of referral discount!
Absolute disappointment. The artichoke dip was over cooked, the pizza tasted... well it was not good. My husband had high hopes and we agreed not to order here again.

Needed some pizza and decided to find a place nearby. I'm a fussy pizza eater - the crust is the base so it's really one of the most important components. We ordered the old fashioned (so a margarita but they added some dried oregano and basil) however they cooked the basil instead of garnishing it fresh before serving. My pizza dough was over baked - total crisp and edges don't even spring back. Sauce was too sweet, couldn't taste the natural flavour of tomatoes and they put too much on. Cheese of standard quality. Overall, wouldn't go back unless kids are super hungry and can't manage to get to another pizza joint. Must say, service is good.
The crust is exquisite.  But... A bit on the salty side lately.  Had a salad that was almost inedible from salt.Still... That crust.

Spoilt for food choices at Suntec and was googling for something we've not tried before and Alt Pizza popped up. Decided to be adventurous and came by to try their pizzas after hearing the good reviews. Hubby and I shared the:Crispy Calamari Fritti - I appreciated the fact that they used real squid rings and not the processed mashed-up-grub that some places pass off as seafood rings. The batter was nice and crispy as its name says but we found it a tad too salty. Other than that, very nice size to share before your own pizzas. Buffalo Bill - hubby liked it quite a bit with the blue cheese taste adequately lacing the pizza. Generous amount of roasted chicken breast meat all over too. Truffle Shuffle - if you like the taste and smell of truffle and this pizza shouts your name. Like my hubby's pizza, generous amount of funnel sausages and roasted mushrooms and onions makes every bite a delight. The interior decor just screams young and hip! Not to mention their colourful and zany pizza box designs!! This pizza place is gonna give other established pizza places a run for their money. The others better watch out for this one.

we found this place as we were looking for something around suntec which would be fast and simple. reviews said thin crust and voted top pizza place in singapore, so we thought of giving it a try. we had the truffle shuffle and Idaho fries. the fries are generously covered in cheese and the pizza was great. not sure if it was cause of the aroma of the truffle oil or if we were hungry..but it was good. for drinks I ordered the blood orange soda and my friend had their gingerella drink. both are from a new Zealand company..but both were good. I went another day and tried two other pizzas. they weren't bad...but my top choice was still the truffle shuffle. and I preferred the white sauce based ones.... either way..I'd say it's worth a visit. they seem to take a lot of delivery orders cause we see their delivery men going in and out...plus ppl from Uber eats coming in to collect orders.

Been wanting to try this place as quite a few yelp friends told me that it was pretty good. Hence I came here with a friend who loves pizza as well on a Monday noon.This place is located at Exit C of the Promenade MRT station. You would have to turn to the left and keep on walking till you see the Alt. on the right hand side. Was not difficult to find but I decided to ask one of the security guards for direction as it was almost lunch break for most office workers. We were greeted by a staff upon entering this brightly colored place and since it was not as crowded yet, we were able to select our seating arrangements. Prior to coming here, I did my research on what to get beforehand and quickly ordered the food items below to avoid the long waiting time for the dishes.1) Truffle Shuffle Pizza - as many of you might notice, I am a fan of truffles (oil or mushrooms). Decided to head for this to have a "lighter meal". The pizza came in 6 slices so my friend and I decided to split into 3 slices each. The pizza was interestingly thinner yet fluffy at the same time. The ingredients were combined perfectly. The cheese that was spread on the pizza were stringy and chewy to my liking. The fennel sausage were cut into too small pieces that I can hardly taste. The temperature of the pizza was not too warm when served that both my friend and I could straightaway bite on it after taking pictures. Do try the chilli oil or the chilli flakes. Tried both of them and I prefer the chilli oil. Your hands will be greasy after using the oil but fear not. This place offer a wet napkin at no cost.2) Alt. Wings - come with bbq sauce or blue cheese sauce. This dish was not entirely made of wings but it has drumsticks too. This reminds me of the buffalo wings I had in the U.S. Pretty flavorful without condiments. I also tried it with the bbq sauce and the blue cheese sauce. I prefer the blue cheese sauce over the bbq sauce. Service was pretty quick. This place also offers some light bites, salads, burgers and DIY pizzas. Pricing wise it is pretty reasonable and this place gets crowded pretty quickly. Definitely a good addition to Suntec City Mall.

Alt pizza offers deliciously thin wood-fired pizza at an affordable price. The pizzas are quite personal size, and shareable among groups. I ordered the Lean & Green pizza and the Truffle Shuffle pizza to share with a friend. Both were tasty, with all of the individual ingredients having a distinct taste. I would most definitely return here to try the other options, and will likely opt for the Truffle Shuffle again in the future. Ambiance is quite casual with plenty of seating. They also have a free loyalty program where you can get 1 free pizza after buying 10 pizzas.

I've never had such terrible service ever. Each time I tried to make eye contact with a server or raise my hand they would ignore me or look away. Okay?? Hello, if you didn't want to have human interaction don't work as a waiter. I ate here for a large group for my friends goodbye dinner. We tried to reserve a spot in advance cause 15 people is quite a bit. Well turns out for a group that large you need of minimum of 25 sgd PER PERSON. That's a bit high for our budget and when each pizza is about 20~ and we've got a ton of tiny asian girls who aren't going to eat all 6 pieces it's not going to happen. So instead my friend went there an hour and half earlier to claim our table.As for the food - Yeah it's pretty good, but honestly the service was so terrible that I didn't care much for the food. Try the:+ Truffle Shuffle+ Bacon Fries

Alt Pizza is quite simply a fantastic place to get Pizza in the Suntec City area. I'm still wondering how I missed this place given that my workplace is only a few blocks away. Thanks to the Yelp app for helping my wife (and me) find this hidden gem! The menu is all about Pizza (specifically, individual 11-inch pizzas). Half/Half pizzas with different ingredients are a no-no.  I ordered the Truffle Suffle - White sauce, parmesan, mozza, white truffle oil, roasted mushrooms and onions, fennel sausage, while my wife ordered the Hangover - organic tomato sauce, mozzarella, pepperoni, fennel sausage, roasted onions and parmesan. After the first bite of my pizza, I could not help but think how similar it was to Extra Virgin's Mushroom Bianco, also a truffle infused Pizza. My wife's pizza the Hangover tasted eerily similar to Extra Virgin's Spotted Pig. After doing some research online, I discovered that Chef and owner, Matthew White, came from Extra Virgin Pizza to start Alt Pizza. No Wonder!  Given this discovery, why not have a Pizza throw-down (an ode to Bobby flay) review: Alt Pizza vs. Extra VirginAlt's Truffle Suffle vs. Extra Virgin's Mushroom Bianco:- Sorry, Alt Pizza, Extra Virgin takes the cake with this one. Extra Virgin's Mushroom Bianco has a roasted mushroom and onion mix that melts in your mouth. Alt's mushroom and onion has the taste, but doesn't deliver the same satisfaction.  Alt's Hangover vs. Extra Virgin Spotted Pig- Alt's Hangover is the clear winner in this one. My issue with the Spotted Pig is that I feel the pork sausage overpowers the other ingredients and doesn't fuse together like Alt's Hangover. Alt's Hangover is a perfect combination of all the flavours mentioned all of the above. In short, the ingredients mesh well together an mouthwatering taste. I think comparing Alt Pizza to Extra Virgin is really unfair. It is a testament how good both Pizza joints really are. Extra Virgin's pizzas cost a little more, $20-$25 a pie vs Alt Pizza's of $12-$18. Alt Pizza menu is quite limited relative to that of Extra Virgin (Extra Virgin Menu includes Pasta and other cool side dishes like oven baked clams, etc). To conclude, this is a must try establishment in the Suntec City Area.

Wow!!!Walked over from Bugis for biz lunch and lucky I had the hotel umbrella- it poured on the way over... Arggggh!In any event, I finally found ALT (no thanks to bad directions to building 3 instead of 4) and what a pleasant surprise.   Well worth the walk in the rain.  Yep!The place was packed for lunch.  A good sign for sure. One orders up their own pizza and drink on the order pads provided and in 10 minutes I had my custom pizza.  No cheese, NY style thin crust, tomato sauce and lots of fresh roasted veggies I picked from the list.  The pies are 11 inches and just right for 1 hungry person!  Prices are reasonable.  Had a great  blood orange soda- my wife's favorite.  Thank you, ALT!  You've restored my faith that there's great pizza outside of NYC and Italia...I'll be back.  "Mangia!"

Mediocre pizza at best although the ingredients sounded promising:  wagyu short rib meatball?! hickory smoked bbq sauce?!  How can you go wrong?  I'll tell you how.  You make it in a hurry and fail to load up like other pics in the reviews show.Perhaps my pizza was a one-off case.The only saving grace from my experience was the Red Hook ale they had.  It's a pleasant surprise when a joint in Singapore features a brewery located in Seattle.I had this on my first night in my numerous trips to Singapore so maybe I was too tired and cranky to give it a fair chance.  I walked over in a zombie like state and walked back to my room with the pizza and the beer.  But I'd like to think it could have been better.

I look towards the weekends with anticipation because that's when I typically pig out! Hehe... The bf and I chanced upon a pizza joint called "alt pizza" at Suntec and decided to try. We found the Food choices on the menu quite interesting. There were a good selection of starters, pizza options, drinks. But most of all the prices looked very affordable and won't break a bank.Our order for the evening:1. Kale and green apple salad - I have never had kale before and wanted to try it, as I have heard, watched and read so much about it in the media. I was pleasantly surprised that the salad was awesome! I loved the fact that the honey dijon dressing didn't drench the vege! In fact the dressing complemented the slightly bitter aftertaste of the kale. Definitely a must try!2. Crispy calamari - The calamari were definitely fresh and succulent. They were each wrapped in a thin crusty batter and paired with some seafoody garlicky type of aioli. Pretty awesome! 3. Buffalo bill pizza- So onward came the supposed highlight of the evening. After all this is a pizza joint right? It's thin crusted, slightly spicy pizza with bacon and chicken breast. To be honest, the pizza felt soggy and we would have preferred if it was crispier. I was definitely slightly disappointed! Taste wise it was a tad salty for my liking and at certain bites I actually tasted some flour in my mouth.After dinner I figured out that perhaps "alt pizza" could be the short form of "alternative". I am not sure, I didn't do much research about this place. But if I were to compare along side some of the pizza joints in town? It's probably in-between Pizza Hut and Skinny pizza. But then what can I say the prices are superbly competitive, these guys are pretty smart... I am sure you will definitely find quite a fair bit of youngsters coming in. My bf and I took a good look around the restaurant, we were right! Will I come back here another time? Probably not, not because they are bad, it's just that I'd rather waste my calories on on other better pizza joints out there, ie. Mozza Pizzeria at MBS.
Good pizza with fresh ingredients. Throwback music choices too. One of my new fave pizzas now.

Best pizza in Singapore by far. Visited Alt Pizza a number of times. Their pizza surprisingly doesn't leave you with an incredibly heavy stomach like many other pizzas (even if you eat a whole one). Their wait staff and pizza makers are friendly and full of smiles.I did the Old School which is a margarita pizza equivalent. I don't know how to describe it, it tasted much better than any other I've ever had.The other time I visited, I went with their meat lovers pizza (don't remember the name) and this one also they nailed. Solid spot to get a beer and fresh pizza. Great setting on the outside of Suntec and awesome menu. I heard the burger is actually really good too!Highly recommend!
Best pizza for the price. Period. We come back almost every week. The 400 degrees, truffle shuffle are favorites. Try it! You won't be disappointed.

What a tasty new find by the office! I had the kale and apple salad which was delicious, albeit a tad pricey at $12. The truffle shuffle pizza was also a winner in my books, I ordered this without the Parmesan and it was perfect. The mozzarella and mushrooms are such a great flavor combination.

At Alt Pizza, you've got to take charge and know what you want.They've got their specialty pizzas, and to be honest, most of the combinations sounded very weird. They sometimes do specials if you order their specialty pizza, and they were running a great deal when we went there (2 specialty pizzas + 2 starters for $45). But none of the specialty pizzas appealed to us, so we built our own pizzas. It ended up being a $3-$5 more for each pizza than if we had gotten specialty pizzas, but we got exactly what we wanted.For cheeses, they've got at least 5 different choices -- regular mozzarella, blue cheese, manchego, parmesan, goat cheese are some that I remember. You can put prosciutto, wagyu meatballs, fennel sausage on your pizza. The combinations are great, the only thing that I miss is an egg.The pizzas are thin, done true Italian style. Some places in Singapore charge $25 for the pizza that I ordered for $15 -- so all in all, a very good value.  We ordered 1 pizza each,and it was plenty of food. I think 2 people could share 1 pizza and 1 starter, but then you'd have to fight over which pizza to get.Alt Pizza is OUTSIDE of the Suntec mall (if you're walking inside the mall, you won't find the entrance.) There's plenty of signs, but go outside to the taxi stand outside of the Suntec tower and look around.

This place had so much potential! Alas the seating positions were not too ideal. Another table also switched places. The smokiness of the kitchen fills the seating area and the music was a tad too loud. The fan was blowing from don't-know-where and it makes you feel like you're in some hawker centre with serviettes falling around on the floor. The redeeming peripheral is the napkin which allows you to clean your hands so you could hold and embrace into your burger. We ordered the wagyu burger. There is the party option and the shabu option. It's sad that their one for one promotion doesn't even allow you to have one patty and one shabu at the same time, ceteris paribus. Kind of inflexible imo. Anyways burger patty was juicy and good for medium rare and the medium well was well roasted with charred parts on top. The sweet onions and two slices of tomato didn't seem to overpower the meaty beef patty. Fries was upgradable to truffle fries or sweet potato fries for only $1.50! Usual fries was alright albeit a little too salty. Truffle fries was good and servings was generous. Oh how I wish this place was more perfect in user comfort. Service was also mediocre.... the food had potential and I really the next time it'd be better.

Venue and location is nice. Price is not expensive at all imo for this venue. I think that the burger was ok. Tried the classic at 13sgd. There are definitely better burgers but it's ok for the price. One red flag that I for any burger place is when they don't ask how you want it cooked so I know it's gonna be average. The beer hmm I felt tasted a bit watered down. I suppose they make most of the profit from alcohol sold as it's a nice place to hang out. Roasted veggies is meh. Cole slaw is meh.

The wildfire seems to be a perfect name for this place - wild for the setting and the loud music, fire for the light underneath these burgers. The setting for this place is definitely more of a classic pub vibe with a lot of loud music pumped in, which means despite the high tables that are great for gathering with people, I don't really see this place as a good location for catching up with people you haven't seen in a while. Service was really mediocre. When they were serving us, they were nice and polite when they were helping us, but were extremely inattentive which was honestly off putting. One of the waitress tried to keep our menus before we ordered which made us feel unwelcomed. In addition when we were done with the meal, I couldn't wave down a single server to get the bill or even clean our plates as they seemed more interested standing by the bar chatting with one another. The food on the other hand actually made me decide to give this place a 3 star instead of a 1 star based on the service. I ordered the classic burger, which was grilled to perfection - juicy and tender with a slight char on the edges. The brioche bun was the perfect compliment to the meat, and the fries were seasoned properly. They also had a large variety of craft beers that seemed interesting but I didn't get to try it due to having a follow up appointment afterwards. 5 stars on the burger, but 1 star on the service, which means if you hear down for a good meal, brace yourself for inattentive service and long waits to just get the check.

Naked burger ($13++) - 2.5 starsI hated the bun - it was way too soft. I guess it was a toasted brioche. The patty had too much fat in it and the vegetables were a bit sorry. Unremarkable.Truffle fries - 4 starsThese were good! Stole some from my friend. Add $1 to change the fries in your set.

I have to say the have a good location and nice outdoor seating. The music is up beat and fun. The prices are high. I paid S$30 for a Chili Con Carn burger and a small coke. The burger was supposed to be angus beef. Well this was a bad choice.The burger looked great.But tasted like flavorless meat that fell apart when you bit into it. I don't recommend this restaurant to anyone who loves burgers...
I ate a sandwich with cheese there which was delicious, and the perfect size for a sandwich, they also don't skimp on the cheese. They have free wifi which is a nice bonus.

The cheesesteak here is mediocre. The beef tasted like it'd just been cooked and there was neither the flair of the grill nor any fragrance - it tasted like it'd just been boiled and then put inside the bun. Although it was oozing cheese there was almost no onion inside.The chicken coney hot dog was a bit better. There was quite a lot of coney sauce but it was made of chicken so it didn't taste exactly right. It was better than A&W Indonesia's pathetic and limp chicken coney sauce though. The sausage was okay - better than normal chicken sausages in Singapore (what is called "hot dog", is filled with questionable material and is really soft). In fact it was similar to the Ikea hot dog sausage. Strangely it was cut in two and fully wrapped with paper which made it very messy when opened.The first batch of fries were good - well fried, with bite and with enough cheese on top. Unfortunately the  second batch were slightly underdone - some fries were slightly undercooked and/or not crispy enough.The mushroom soup was mediocre. It was a bit watery and tasted like there was mushroom oil or essence inside. It didn't taste generic - which was good - but it wasn't quite hot enough.The coleslaw was weird, tasting raw and underdressed. Also, strangely, it was marked as a dessert.
Sandwich + cheese = happiness. Why's not to like?! My kids love it here. Because their cheese is covered with cheese too!!!

Toa Payoh has a nice selection of local food, but for Western fare, not so much.  Therefore, I was very surprised and excited to see a cheese steak place near the office.  Having lived in Philly for  3 years, I had some high expectations coming here, so perhaps this explains the 3 stars.  For starters, I would say the bread was actually the closest to D'ambrosio's that I have had in SG so far.  Soft but not too soft and the perfect size for a sandwich.  But if I look at the cheese (way too much) and onions (way too little), the balance was not there.  For about $3 more, you can get a set which includes a drink and cheese fries, which were quite good.  But at the end of the meal, I felt like I had way too much processed cheese :).  Overall, Yellow Submarine falls short on the executtion a bit, but the results are still pretty tasty and the value is there.

I'm a carnivore and nothing makes me happier than a combination of thin juicy slices of premium beef with gravy, topped with melted American cheese and sauteed onions sandwiched in a bread roll.  The latest option to satisfy this Philly Cheesesteak craving in Singapore is the Yellow Submarines, a cheery and happy spot located in the Toa Payoh heartland. The Yellow Submarine Classic (S$6.90) is a tasty sub no doubt with high quality Australian sirloin steak being used in this one. The cheese sauce also had me swooning and i wished there was more of that in my sub (i gave feedback that they should provide a side portion of cheese sauce for all who wants more heh). The bun was also faultless with its crusty exterior and toasted  buttery interior.  Here comes the but.. and only because i'm too accustomed to the real deal. The meat was a little too thickly sliced and hence it lacked in the juice department. The large onion chunks (a fixture in all their subs) were too Asian styled for my liking. Philly cheesesteaks have long strands of sauteed, caramelized onions, not chunky pieces. And why the ketchup? Now that definitely doesn't belong in a Philly cheesesteak. Thankfully the ketchup taste wasn't too overpowering. I'm not saying it is no good, it's just not authentic Americano. I cannot express how crazy i am about Yellow Submarines' cheese sauce. Made from a blend of several cheeses, this heavily guarded secret recipe is a sure winner. You gotta make your sub a meal with the Torpedo fries and a drink for an additional $3. I say this is certainly one of the best tasting cheese fries in Singapore. Desserts don't fare as well here ($2.80 each). Again, everything was toned down for the Asian palate. Food should educate, not accommodate and this whole 'catered to Asian taste' thingy is sure pissing me off (i'm . The cheesecake was very milky and soft, though lacking in the richness of the cheese. The brownie was dry and not chocolatey enough.Overall, i did enjoy my meal at the Yellow Submarines. The fries are sufficient for me to visit again soon. Do hope some changes will be made to un-Asian-fy the subs. More cheese would definitely be awesome.

Crispy fries that were soft on the inside. Great with the cheese dip! Coleslaw came with raisins which was a nice change from the usual. The beef cheese steak was not too bad, though it didn't come with the oozy cheese a philly would have. I'd be giving the classic yellow submarine a try instead the next time. Cute dining concept, happy to see they have an outlet in Bugis too.

This place does live up to the hype! I got here right when it opened at 11 and got right in with no wait. I ordered the #1 noodles dry and an extra order of fish ball soup. The soup was so flavorful but still maintained a light flavor. The noodles were very good as well but I do think the reviews are right that the chili makes the dish. This is also very cheap as everything is under $10. The only issue is that this is so far that you spend $20 on taxi fare which is double the price of the meal. I also got takeaway but it wasn't as good...still good but the soup tastes different.

Rare night without the kids and decided to try some spicy noodles. Getting here - they have limited street parking but it's easier to just park at the HDB parking lots nearby and walk over, not far. They have pictures of what they serve so it's easy to figure out what you would like. As greedy people, hubby and I had our noodle bowl and an extra bowl of soup with their jumbo fishballs to share. I love the idea of a nicely poached egg in my noodles, waiting for me to break it over my noodles. As its called Chilli noodles, then must do it justice and lace my noodles with the good stuff. As other reviewers had cautioned, their Chilli packs a punch and go easy if you're unsure. They leave jars of Chilli on your table so you can raise the spice level any time you want. From the first mouthful, I am hooked! Hook, line and sinker! Done! It's AMAZING. I actually lack the vocab to tell you why I love it. I only know I need to tabao some more back so I can eat it again the next day (which I did, while it wasn't as good as fresh, it was still pretty darn awesome). I am definitely a fan. I need to pay the noodle stall homage often from now on!

I love the signature noodles! I have gone there twice within 2 weeks. The queue on Saturday is quite manageable and it helps to have a sign outside indicating customers are to share tables during peak periods. That also means the staff is on hand to make sure customers wait outside (with order chit and menu) and will assign tables to those in line as and when seats are available. The process is quite fast, and food is served within 5-10 minutes after ordering. They must have streamlined the nightmarish long waits during the first few months after opening.I think the sweet spot for less people will be after the usual lunch time and before the dinner rush. Be warned people may start to stream in after 4pm for early dinner though. It probably makes sense since they close at 8pm and last order is at 730pm or so. The noodles is different from the usual noodles in Singapore. It is al dente and chewy, giving more bite to the noodles. I like that you can adjust the level of spiciness in your noodles since you get to add the amount of chili. It can get really spicy so do it slowly. I added 4-5 spoonfuls of the chili the first time and that almost burnt my tongue. The chili looked harmless but it packed a punch. The 2nd visit, I just added 2 spoonfuls and it was just nice.The noodles is just so good with the crispy ikan bilis, minced meat, meat balls and perfectly soft boiled egg. Order a bowl of handmade fish ball soup for the huge fish ball which has real fish taste (and meat probably) unlike those machine factory made fish ball which tastes more of starch filler than fish meat. I am not a fish ball fan or connoisseur but this is really good. Sweet, soft, bouncy and salty. The bean sheet with fish ball and meat ball soup can be skipped unless you really want the bean sheet. The bean sheet is so-so. This is a place I can go dine at all the time. There is street parking but it may be better to park at the URA car park further away and just walk over. Otherwise there are a bus stop and MRT (Tai Seng) nearby.

First thing came to my mind when I ate this was: comfort food. That kind of taste you'll miss when you are far from home. It's simple yet delicious.I ordered their signature noodles. No fancy ingredients. Just minced pork, ikan bilis, poached egg, fried onions and meatballs in the noodle bowl. These complement each other. Since their shop name is Kin Kin CHILLI Pan Mee, no one should ever leave this place without ever trying their chilli. Spicy and stir fried(my guess)  till fragrant. Goes very well with the noodles with a kick of spiciness. My friend and I went on a Saturday afternoon and had to share table. The place was filled. Other than us, there were only a couple of people waiting. Food came quite fast too. Our food came around 5 minutes later after we ordered. This place is definitely for those truly like their noodles instead of chilling out.

My colleague introduced this place to me for lunch  and it's a lil Cosy air conditioned restaurant. The noodles start at $5. Do not underestimate these noodles. They are delicious and yes I know I should be sentenced to jail for not liking chilli but the noodles still taste awesome even without chilli. I know I know I'm missing out on life. But it's still super good without chilli! Although, now I'm inclined to know what the real one in KL tastes like! There was so much fried onions and ikan bills, minced meat which added so much flavour to the noodles! 3 meatballs and the egg to add some oooomph! To the dish :) gotta come back here for more awesomeness!

AS GOOD AS THE ORIGINAL! I would give this place 5 stars if not for the crazy wait.Kin Kin Chili Pan Mee is the first stop on my itinerary whenever I visit KL- the last time was in November 2013 and I'd been having a craving as of late so this opening couldn't have been more timely. And judging from the number of articles/facebook shares this got when it first opened, it seems that quite a few of my friends share my fervent cravings for this place too.Came here on a weekday afternoon and there was a pretty long queue outside, though not as bad as expected. Perhaps about 20 meters? You're queuing at the corridor along a row of shophouses, it's sheltered and not too bad.The restaurant itself is air-conditioned and way cleaner than the original stall in Malaysia. BUT service is a lot slower. We were given a standard menu with about 10 items to choose from (most people just pick their Signature noodles) and an ordering chit which we had to fill in and then bring to the counter and pay. For some reason just the queue to submit the chit and pay took quite long (about 25mins) - according to my dining companion, it was because everyone in the queue was trying to add this and that to their meals and coming up with all sorts of funky special orders. Gosh.So after paying, we expected our noodles to come pretty quickly. My friend joked that it would be a one-hour wait. Shortly after we said that, the couple next to us (we were all made to share tables) asked the waiter about their order and I overheard that they had arrived about an hour before we did and my face turned pale as I realised that MY FRIEND WAS NOT JOKING. Or rather, he was joking but it turned out to be true. T_TAnyway we didn't wait for 1 hour for our noodles. We waited ONE AND A HALF HOURS. Which made it about 3pm by the time we actually got our food... which was really really good and as good as the original and a must-try but you know what, the thought of waiting 2 hours for it again just makes me balk. Honestly I have no idea why it took so long, considering how standard the order was. But then again we saw a bunch of people doing takeaways of 10, 20 bowls so that could have been the reason.Will return, but not so soon... perhaps when the hype finally dies down.It was quite difficult to find legit parking around the area and we resorted to slightly illegal means (luckily we didn't get a ticket!). Seems quite troublesome to get to without a car too.

The noodle and ingredients are great. Especially the fish ball and the hot chilli. I would have given it 5-star if the soup have more depth to match the quality of the rest. Still one of my favourite noodle place.

Recently opening their Singapore branch with much hype 2 months ago (to the extent of having to queue up to 2-3 hours just for the food on their first few days), Restoran Kin Kin is a popular restaurant in KL specializing in their chilli pan mee.Besides having the original pan mee and other types of you mian, they also have soups.The Signature Dry Chilli Pan Mee ($5) looks like an ordinary dry ban mian when it was served out, but after mixing the chilli paste that is provided on the table, it's not hard to see why this is one of the favourites here. The chilli, while not being overly spicy, brought out the flavour in the ban mian after mixing the minced meat, ikan bilis, poached egg, fried onions and meatballs. It tasted like a dry ramen you can get in a Japanese restaurant, except that this is more flavourful, more filling, less dry and definitely more spicier (but less spicier than other types of noodles).The chilli that is responsible for the great tasting pan mee.As the hype for this place becomes more manageable, it is now easier to have a meal here (be it for lunch or for dinner, dine-in or takeaway). Given that this place is around the MacPherson / Tai Seng area, this place will be filled with the lunch crowd!

The chilli is very good but without the chilli it is as tasteless. Fishball is fresh and big and tender. Too pricey for the portion and ingredient. Soup is tasteless and they only give a few leaves of vegetable. Though my girl likes Clam Pan Mee soup. In my opinion, not worth the value.

Finally made it to kin kin pan mee! I have been meaning to make my way here to try the famous noodles but the thought of a long queue has put me off for awhile. After trying it, I can say that it is really delicious and definitely worth a try. The signature noodles is the bomb! It's a superb combination of al dente noodles, egg, ikan bilis and minced meat. Yum yum! Just talking about it is making me hungry again....
Not the same as the KinKin in KL cause the mee is different. But other than that its brilliant :)

I LOVE THIS PLACE SO MUCH!If i dont come here for awhile, i start missing the remdang beef salad. I can't describe why it's so good. It just is. The fresh ingredients definitely doesn't hurt, and the super friendly owner.Bonus point as they are never busy during dinner. For lunch it's a different story I heard!

Healthy, fast, with a sense of humor. What's not to like?This is a great takeaway spot if you're looking for something healthy. I wasn't in the mood for meat so I went with their veggie wrap, which had miso tofu in it.I thought that the tofu wouldn't have any taste, but wow, I was wrong! It definitely had some good spice and flavour to it. In addition to the greens, the added achar and nuts gave the wrap some good texture and an extra boost in energy.The chef (and I will assume owner) is very jovial and knows all his regular customers by name. He's good with small talk, so don't be afraid to strike up a conversation with him as he's preparing your food!

Lock me up and throw away the key!Dining here turned my colleague and I into petty criminals. So engrossed were we in our lunchtime rant-a-thon that we neglected to pay after eating.We only realised this fact upon returning to our office. A solid 5+ minute walk from this establishment.Once our crime-spree registered in our brains, we were both instantly wracked with full body pangs of guilt and embarrassment, quickly followed by engaging in a long walk of shame back to the eatery.Re-arriving, with guilt-ridden faces, we bowed our thieving heads in an act of ultimate contrition hoping to assuage the owner into letting us off lightly.We proffered our payment and our sincerest apologies in good faith as we looked to escape a long stint behind bars in a federal pound-me-in-the-4ss prison (thanks office space).To our delight we discovered that the owner/operator is actually Captain Cool from the ice planet Chillax. He found our tale of woe and misdemeanour hilarious and amusing and deemed our prodigal return a clear act of good faith. Restoring our smiles to our faces and the freedom to return to his fantastic little world of food again.I had the special which today was Wagyu beef, and I chose to wrap it in a shroud of wholemeal and assorted greens. The taste? Anything that tastes this good should be a crime!The price? A steal! (Actually it is quite spendy @ $16 but I would gladly pay it again).This place lives up to its name, simple and humble food done good. Just remember to pay your bill when you leave ;)
Really good food with generous servings of meat, but it's a tiny space and really stuffy inside. Strictly for takeout only!

Came here for the first time today, absolutely incredible! Lovely service, convenient location, simple and well thought out menu! I had a veggie wrap and it was to die for! Vegetarian food can be bland or boring - but this exceeded every expectation! Yum! Will be making this my regular lunch joint!

Meat and Green is in a small space in Boat Quay that is good for lunch. There is limited seating inside and a few street side tables in front, but it's convenient food for take-away, too. The owner, Akil, is always there making sure that everything is of high quality. The vegetables are fresh and the wraps are piled with meat. I'd recommend the pulled pork. Delicious and satisfying! They have some interesting bottled soft drinks in the cooler, and a limited selection of ciders and beer (Tuatara on the crafty side). It's pretty quiet in the evening, which makes it a good option if you are in the area and you want to find a quiet place to chill on an otherwise busy street.

Overall, I'm rather satisfied with my meal here. The two star rating really is because it's not my first choice for forking out $22-24 for a main course. The price point simply doesn't make sense for a place that looks like a simple cafe. If this place was a little fancier, I would give it another star. The chilli crab linguine was good - the tomato sauce had just the right amount of spiciness to it and there was plenty of shredded crab meat to accompany the pasta. However, I found myself having too much crabmeat and sauce remaining (which honestly isn't a bad thing considering that it reflects well that there's more than enough of the important ingredient - crab). So Marmalade Pantry, please don't reduce the amount of crabmeat/sauce (you're doing great justice to the price of the dish), just give more pasta (which I'm sure costs you nothing) and doing so will only impress your customers considering the large portion of the dish. The mushroom risotto was creamy and definitely "truffly". There was just the right amount of mushroom in each bite. The done-ness of the rice was just right too. I was initially hesitant about ordering the dish because I've read that the portion is small, but as a girl, I think it just managed to hit the "satisfied" level. I found the cupcake we ordered okay, but my friend raved about it. So perhaps I didn't think much about the cupcake because I've been spoiled with the best cupcakes names in the US, and this one just failed to impress compared to them.The ginger pudding was soft and warm, and the caramel ice cream that accompanied it was clearly speckled with vanilla. I would order it again.All in all, I would be willing to visit Marmalade Pantry again and would also order these items again if I had to eat here.

There seems to be a lack of chic food places at Ion, so I always end up at Marmalade Pantry. Went there again for dinner this time, and I had a wonderful meal!The service was really prompt, especially this waiter with a cool haircut who was really enthusiastic and warm, and made us feel very comfortable.My boyfriend had the Crabmeat Linguine, which was good! I felt like it was too watery though, and I maintain that the best crabmeat linguine pasta I've ever had was elsewhere... (see my blog on my profile)... but it was still delicious by normal standards. It has an abundance of real actual crabmeat and not like faux crab or crabsticks so it's still worth it for the price at $24.(The previous time I came here, I tried the Seared Scallop Linguine ($24) and it was super delicious! The crabmeat one is tomato-based, but this one is more like a broth and it's quite savory? I kinda prefer this more cos I like special pastas that I can't get elsewhere!) The milkshake was good but also too watery for me... hahaha oops what's with me not liking watery food?? The best cookies and cream milkshake we've had is also from elsewhere (check my blog) but Marmalade Pantry's is pretty good!So I had the Pantry Club ($20) sandwich which was reaaaally good. I think when my food came my boyfriend's eyes popped, you know like Popeye when he sees his girlfriend or something. It's quite a simple chicken ham egg sandwich but it just looks so appealing!! It also comes with a side of like... healthy vegetable chips? I really love them!!! Of course I couldn't finish it (there were 4 mini sandwiches) and my boyfriend got to eat one :) score for him!Finally, we shared a Caramelized Pear and Salted Caramel Bread Pudding for dessert! The bread pudding is wrapped in some kind of crispy filo puff and okay wow it was so yummy!!! It went perfectly with the ice cream and the salted caramel sauce - perfectly sweet and salty at the same time.So maybe that's why I keep coming back to Marmalade Pantry, because for the price we get a good meal! The portions are big enough for people with small appetites to share. Their desserts are also good so this place is good for tea with friends too :)Please check out my blog (on my profile) for photos! :)

With its accessible location and sufficiently wide menu which caters to all day dining, it is no surprise why marmalade pantry is perpetually crowded (even on a weekday afternoon). Service is good and fast, the waitstaff are great at taking orders and the food doesn't take too long to come. I also like that since its not in a confined space, the noise level is kept very low and you can actually hold a conversation no matter how crowded it gets.I'm a risotto freak and usually not hard to please, but I found the mushroom risotto here a tad too salty for my liking. It was served in a good portion, there were plenty of mushrooms in there, and the grains were cooked to al-dente perfection. I think it would have been just fine without the cheese. I've also tried several of their cupcakes, and found them to be pretty decent. The cake has just the right moisture to hold it together, but at the same time is not too dense.This is a perfect place if you want to have a good dinner at a fairly reasonable price!

In terms of food, ION has a very limited selection. The Marmalade Pantry offers bistro style dining including all day branch to cater to weekend shoppers. A main to try would definitely be the crabmeat linguine, served with a generous portion of crabmeat, pine nuts and just the right amount of chilli to add some spice to the dish. If you're looking for a healthy alternative, do give the king salmon and soba a go. To end the meal, do try one of their famous cupcakes, the red velvet is a crowd favorite with a deep red color, cream cheese and coconut shavings.

good, better-than-average bistro food at this branch of the yummy-mummy chain in the ion shopping mall. the food is pretty decent, the prices competitive for the area, and there aren't much better options around for a place to sit down and have some cake and tea.it's pretty flabbergasting to realize that though the orchard road precinct is hangout-de-rigueur for most people on the weekends, and so ought to (and does) have a slew of eateries, there really isn't much to eat around there, just a whole lot of overly expensive sit-down places or trendy takeaway options. this place remains my fall-back option when I'm out with the girlfriends, and has been since I first visited their palais renaissance outlet nearly five years ago.the food may not be spectacularly surprising, but it is reliable and very enjoyable. the menu runs the gamut of european-fusion-ish bistro dishes: easy brunch food, salads and sandwiches, proper entrées and pud. I tend to come here for brunch or tea, and so the menu does me well - don't come expecting a formal dinner service here, it ain't that sort place.truth be told though,  my constant visits are for their sweets. they have the same sort of style as the p.s. cafe chain (and both do a mean sticky date pudding). I got to try something new this time: their caramelized pear and salted caramel bread pudding. doesn't that sound fantastic! and it really was intriguing - two rectangular slabs of bread pudding wrapped with filo, baked to a pale golden, and topped with a scoop of delicious vanilla ice cream. the filo was a little floury - I think it could have been baked a little longer, or brushed with an egg wash - but I'm quibbling: that bare drizzle of salted caramel on the plate was just the right accent to the pud - it was a great way to finish the meal.

Marmalade Pantry at ION is a really convenient place for lunch in Orchard or catching up over a cupcake or three. Food : LOVE the chilli crab linguine with pine nuts. I've tried this dish at other restaurants but Marmalade Pantry still does the best version. The portion is just right and it's not too spicy, while the pine nuts add a nice texture to the al dente linguine with generous helpings of crab meat. Being partial to seafood, the lighter option of crab Caesar salad with parmesan and pine nuts was also pretty good! I personally like the William Pear and Limonata cupcakes for dessert while some friends love MP's sticky date and toffee pudding with vanilla ice cream. Good selection of bites for afternoon tea.Ambience : Casual chi-chi and one of those yuppie / tai-tai go-to places for teaService : Hit and miss. We've been there when the service staff behave as if they couldn't care less for our business, but there have also been occasions where our wait staff was really pleasant and efficient. Your experience really depends on the waiter serving you.Unfortunately Marmalade Pantry does the best version of the chilli crab linguine in Singapore despite its slightly steep pricing and sketchy service, so I go when the craving hits.

The food is average but this is one of the few places in Singapore that is open for brunch if you are looking for western food.For my last visit, I ordered the Smoked Salmon Salad so I was a bit surprised when it arrived looking like a salmon wrap.  Inside were a few spinach and supposedly fresh fennel but I really could not taste the anis flavor.  Though expectation was not met, the taste was still ok.My friend ordered the mushroom risotto and I guess it was ok as she didn't complain.For dessert, we shared the Elvis cupcake which is basically a banana cupcake with peanut butter cream frosting.  It was quite good but very rich -- its the size of a mini-cupcake and we did not get to finish it!The service was good -- the staff were attentive refilling our water glasses and asking if we wanted more coffee.  So I was a but surprised to see the bad reviews on the service.  But then I was there for brunch at 1030am --- so when we began our meal, only a few tables were occupied.  But the service was good until we left at 12nn and it was a Sunday so the place was quite full by around 1130.

The best thing about the Marmalade Pantry is their cupcakes. The food is decent enough, although pretty pricey for a main dish. Portions are not huge, but I guess thats good if you want to have dessert. Do not try the high tea. Not worth it. And not good at all. Back to the cupcakes. With the trend of cupcakes finally picking up in Singapore, Id have to say that Marmalade Pantry still holds the title for the best so far. The cupcakes are bigger than other places here. The flavors are awesome. My favorite is the Elvis cupcake-- chocolate, banana and peanut butter. Amazing. I also really like the coconut with cream cheese frosting and sprinkles. Come for the cupcakes.

A favourite of tai-tais, as the food is good and you can occasionally see your shopping girlfriends walking by. Unfortunately, the food can be inconsistent  - strangely enough, even the dressings for salads, refreshing one day and meh the next. Pricey for what it is, but not so much after you've been to Chanel or Cartier.
