I mean, ok, I thought gentrification in Tiong Bahru is bad but it's not all that bad.  I love the storefront with the large square communal table where people just sit there going on about their own business.  It's not air-conditioned but usually there is a nice breeze.  It's good for people watching on weekends since a tonne of visitors come to Tiong Bahru and Yong Siak street is their no. 1 destination.  Besides, what's better than sitting there being immersed in the smell of warm butter?I have bought their cupcakes and they are pretty good.  A whole range of flavors to choose from and not too sweet.  Besides cup cakes, they also sell cakes but I have yet to try, they all look too big for one person.  There are also other peculiar home goods on offer here, as well as cook books, which I don't think are a whole lot practical or necessary but nevertheless interesting to look at. This is a place that leaves a memory on your senses.  As I am writing I can recall the warm breeze brushing on my skin and the aroma of sugar and butter.

A great treat to the neighbourhood. I've followed Vanessa from Holland V to Tiong Bahru and even to some of her pop-ups. She has been consistently fabulous at her baking. She keeps things simple and in this day and age, it's the most welcoming approach to bakeries. While her HV store is small and cosy, this is welcoming and enticing. I love the wide space and benches. The counter space allows us to stand in front and ponder. Her selection as always, spoils us like an only child in the family. I am always drawn to a salted caramel or special of the day. A new old favourite is earl grey lavender cuppie. An old because I always had it in USA but never in Singapore. Thank you for bringing it here. Have yet to attend her events. Plain Vanilla has a line up of events through out the month so pop over to their facebook for more details.
There is nothing plain about Plain Vanilla.  Delicious baked items as well as a small assortment of home goods and a nice covered patio makes for a nice break from the midday heat and humidity.

Great ambiance and decent coffee however we were not at all impressed with the pastries / cakes we ordered. Blueberry cake was overloaded with sugar it was all you can taste. Too bad the food wasn't better because it is a nice venue to hang out for awhile

I ordered the Dark Chocolate Ganache and a Raspberry Pink Lemonade for a meal closer. Loved the lemonade. The cupcake was fine. Not a fan of the crispy texture but the cupcake could use a little moistness. I would want to try the Red Velvet next time.

This is my first time here at this restaurant and it blown my mind away. Firstly the boss would stand outside and invite you in, followed by seating. The salad bar is really extensive and there are so many food. Please do not take too many salad bar and wait for the meat to come. The meat would be serve first round, all kinds of meat and following they would come slowly to let you eat slowly. There are just so many meat that I could not describe all but please do try their duck confetti, chicken knuckle, beef chunk and most importantly the grilled pineapple! For the price you are paying the meat are all exclusive and really hard to find in Singapore yet you are able to taste it here. Recommended!

It has been a while the last time I dined here. And I'm talking about years and years ago when I was still in the University. So the very fact that the restaurant still packs the house to this day is testimony to something. We were a party of 9 tonight and the meats just came by swift and furious. They are certainly not stingy with their cuts and the servers will often joke with us diners here and again, which really makes the dining experience great.They have many different servings of meat and I enjoyed 90% of all served! I love how the grilling brought out the natural taste of the meats. Each of us had our personal favourite cuts so I'm confident to say you can definitely find something you will go gaga over. I, personally' enjoy "Top Side" slices very much. And I forgot to mention that they have a salad bar that features about 20 items of delectable vegetables and pasta too!!! I loved their coleslaw and caramelised onions most! I could easily make a meal out of JUST the salad bar! But it's was a really tough choice to decide between more meat or more vegetables? So I just ate more BOTH!I had to roll out of the restaurant after the wonderful meal! Will definitely go back!

Authentic and overall good value for money for S$47++, but you gotta pace yourself. 4-stars relative to other places in Singapore, but in all honesty, not that great and 2-3 stars if compared to other places outside the country.The cuts of meat in Brazil do not correspond directly to the ones you are familiar with. (i.e. the dotted lines on the cow are drawn differently). The picanha (aka top sirloin cap) is the most prized of Brazilian meat cuts, and that's the one cut that is done decently here, so you should grab more pieces when the passador brings it around to the table. Choose a piece that's slightly rarer.The meat cuts are of slightly lower quality, they lack flavour and are sometimes way overcooked and dry. I couldn't tell if they were using a real wood fire or gas. Exotic stuff like chicken liver and chicken hearts are also served, which I appreciated. There were other items like lamb, grilled pineapple (abacaxi), sausages. They also had other non-brazilian offerings like roast duck (?!). The cheese bread (pao de queijo) was also average-tasting and were not spherical. They looked like they were baked in a cupcake pan.Service however, is very good and attentive. Your plates are changed quickly, and some of the waiters are actually Brazilian.I've eaten at other churrascarias around the United States and also some of the good places in Sao Paulo and Rio. In comparison, this place stacks up as 2 to 3-stars compared to other churrascarias outside the country. But there are very few players in this space in Singapore, so this will have to do.

This churrascaria has been around for many years, and I've been coming here since I've been really young to celebrate birthdays. The salad bar is pretty extensive, but it always takes me so much self discipline not to take too much in preparation for the meaty meal to come. This place serves up a buffet, except that the servers come to your table with the meat and cuts you a slice if you want. I love love the beef, fish and the pineapple. The Bahia Cooler here is the best. Must order! And definitely make a reservation!

Prepare to starve yourself before making a reservation at this buffet style BBQ place. There is a salad bar with about 12 different cold dishes, but don't fill your plate too quickly! I made the embarrassing decision to get everything which only resulted in a sheepish request for a fresh plate to replace my overflowing one. Food wastage is never a good thing! Especially when every single meat was delicious. Service is quick, efficient and all round excellent with super attentive staff. My lazy bum self was delighted that you didn't even need to move from your seat after the initial trip to the salad bar. Waiters would come round continuously with various meats kebab style, and slice it straight onto your plates. Must try dishes would be their rump beef, smoked duck, and BBQ-ed pineapple. Try asking for the burnt portions - its warm, sweet with the charcoal fragrance locked in it, really unexpectedly yummy! $47++ per person for a Saturday night dinner, reservations are encouraged!

This is a replacement review for one that mysteriously disappeared.This is a review of a large (30+) team dinner that I hosted at Brazil Churrasco.The staff was very friendly and helpful.  Most importantly though, they kept the meat and drinks coming our way.First, as with most Brazilian steakhouses, this place is about meat.  Lots of meat and lots of different kinds of meat.  There is a salad/food bar but make no mistake about it, you go to Brazil Churassco to load up on proteins, beef, pork, lamb, chicken, duck, etc..  The meat was cooked well.  They use a lot of seasonings and there some great flavours along the way.  This is no place for a vegetarian.There was a steady flow of different meats and the team was up to the task.  As with most of these, some of the better, more exotic, expensive meats come later in the process.  So, if your appetite is a bit light, you might want to hold off on some of the earlier rounds.I do think it is a great experience for a larger group.  It is fun (and sometimes surprising) to see who can keep going and who drops out along the way.Overall - This was a fun dining experience.  I would certainly go again.  But I would want it to be another group event.  If you need a place for a party (and there will be no vegetarians), I suggest giving Brazil Churassco a shot.   You will be well fed and I think you will have a great time(ps - this is one of the few reviews i will post without photos.)

Neighbourhood restaurant with top standardsThere are so many good things about Brazil Churrasco:1. It's in the 'hood, which means the service is warm, welcoming and you feel like you're family2. The meats are top notch - you'll never feel shortchanged at the quality of the cuts3. Lovely fresh salad bar items to help you get over meat guilt4. Potent cocktails5. The just-right rhythm of the buffet as the passadors come to your table bearing skewers of meatBrazil Churrasco has been delighting customers since 1994; I remember heading there as a JC student in 1996 as a treat for the end of exams. Dining back there just a couple weeks ago, I have to commend them on keeping standards high. The restaurant decor is homey, not tired or slick, just a nice shade of comfortable, and the cuts range from beef hump to rump to ribeye, as well as chicken, fish, ham, lamb and more. At $46 all you can eat, the price is right for a monthly red meat treat that rivals some of the steak restaurants in town.

This is probably one of the oldest Churrascaria restuarants in Singapore and the food quality is still good. This is a place for meat lovers and carnivores. This place dish out meats, meats and more meats. This is a typical churrascaria restaurant where the Passadores (the meat servers)  would bring around skewkers of BBQ meats and walk around the restaurants dishing out the meats on the diner's plate.  They served a rather expensive range of bbq items such as beef topside, beep rump, tenderloin, ham, chicken hearts, livers, lamb, smoked duck, pineapple, sausages, fish and much more.  It also have a salad station for those looking for some fibre to accompany the meaty meal.  Personally, I love the beef topside, rump, lamb and smoked duck.Comparative to other churrascaria in Singapore, I prefer the variety and quality of meats here. Oh yes, and I love the mini cheese buns that serve prior to the start of dinner.  Oh yes. Don't forget to order a glass of refreshing caipirinha to accompany the meal.

In a country full of restaurants operated by amateurs, this place is a welcome change.  The staff here were friendly, well trained, and attentive. The meats were good (great variety served to your table) and the sides (self served buffet style at a bar) were all tasty.  Comfortable, casual, and warm atmosphere.  We had a party of 6 and all left happy and content. Since it is all you care to eat, you will most likely leave very full.  Pace yourselves!  Will go back soon.

Be warned! This place is strictly for serious meat lovers-:)They serve a wide variety of meat, marinated and grilled (South American style) to perfection. Ambiance is nice, quite and romantic and service is friendly. Pleasent dining experience enought to fill you apettite for meat for a month.

Good overall Churrascaria.   I was thrilled to find it after a long day of biking.    The Picahna was very good.  The other beef cuts were average.   The mutton was a little too gamey.   Overall selection ( I think they said 14 cuts) was average.    Service was very good and pleasant.

I can only assume that the people giving positive reviews of this place are the owners because the food is legitimately among the worst meals I've ever had in my life. Putting aside the gimmick of eating in the dark, which is fun and different for a few minutes, a restaurant still needs to sell food that people want to eat, and this food is objectionable. Anyone who has a food allergy - don't even try eating here. Went in a group with a few allergies and vegetarians - almost everyone ate something they weren't supposed to and in one case narrowly avoided a trip to the hospital. The visually impaired staff that work here are great. That's the only positive thing I can say about the place. Other than that, I can only pray that you never are forced to eat here.

Have you all dine in the dark before? We all heard a fair bit about the concept of dining in the total darkness, haven't we? I think NOX need no further introduction.NOX is located along the shop houses of beach road occupying 2 level of shop space.The service staff welcomed us into the lounge and gave us a drink menu to choose upon. The moment I sat down, the plushy sofa seat reminds me of Gold Class Cinema lounge, quite similar in a sense. Servers explained there is no food menu to choose from, rather there is a secret menu at $88++ per pax that consists of 12 dishes spreaded into 3 courses, appetizers, mains and desserts. Restaurant menu will be change every 6 - 8 weeks and should you have any dietary preference, e.g. vegetarian, please highlight to them.MocktailA citrus combination of orange with a bittersweet finishing taste from a pomelo. Its more sour than sweet per say with grapefruit, lemon juice, simple syrup and Grenadine that give a tart and sweet flavour to the naturally sour fruit.Grapefruit Spritz - $14The zesty and minty flavours make this quencher such refreshing. Out of 3 drinks tasted, I rate this the best. Ingredients were close to other drinks with passionfruit, simple syrup, lemon juice, lime juice, fresh mint leave and ginger ale.Virgin Passionfruit Julep - $14Being described as not the ordinary strawberry milkshake, it really make me wonder how does it taste like. Drink was milky pink served with little ice cubes and a strawberry. It was more of sweet and less of the sour taste with fresh milk, vanilla syrup, simple syrup, lemon juice and Amaretto Almond Syrup.Strawberry Shaker - $14StartersWe were served with the starters with a vegetarian on the left and 2 mini cones on the right for the non vegetarians. The fried vegetarian had a pleasant scent of truffle oil smell and looks good with its creaming sauce at its base.Starters for the non vegetarian was miniature. Raw salmon was served in the tip of the ice cream cone biscuit added with caviar. The presentation which depicts some plants on the soil had totally taken me away.Before Proceeding into the darknessWe was told not to bring any of our belongings to the dining area and had them kept in the given lockers, not even our handphones or watches with illumination / glow in the dark function. Instagrammers, sorry! For those who needs to go toilet, its best to have the "passage" clear before entering into the darkness.Entering the DarknessWe were quite excited while the door to the dining area swung open and we were greeted by the service staff. Have you wonder how to walk up a flight of steep stairs in total darkness? Well, we conquered the first stage by having 1 hand tapping to each other shoulder in a line and walk up the stair and into the dining.Dining in the darknessIt all started with uneasiness, getting ourselves up at the dining area. When we reached our table, we were led to the back of the chair and have to figure ourselves to take a seat under the clear instructions of course. We were briefed to locate our cutleries (spoon and fork) and the position to place our drinking glass on the table. With every course served, we was told to lean backwards to our chair as these visually impact servers placed the dishes onto our table accurately. Each course consist of 4 dishes served in a wooden tray and placed in a "t" shape. The rule to dine is to start with the dish nearest to ourselves at the "6" needle base on a analog clock and go clockwise.It was a challenge as well as fun locating the dish and place our spoon correctly into our mouth without dropping off the food, afterall this was my 1st time ever dining under such environment. I vividly remembered that our appetizers consist of rocket salad, foie gras, fried calamari, chick peas, lentils etc. While the mains were duck confit, wagyu beef cubes, cod fish. Meat was tender and tasty. Desserts was lava chocolate, popcorn ice cream, lemon sorbet and strudel. Finishing the mealWe stood up and walk a few meters on the carpeted ground using the same "tapping shoulder method" in a line before heading back to the stairs. Luckily the stairs were dimly lit and we could see and walk down under the shades of light. As we proceed back to the lounge, our eyes were tired and as though we had just woke up.We were told to fill up a questionaire to recall and guess what we had eaten. After which, the person in charge will come with an ipad, showing the pictures and naming out the 12 dishes we had. We were surprised by our guesses as it really gave our taste buds a good test.ConclusionAll in all, it was a good 1.5 hours session of experiencing the life of a visually impact human, coping with darkness in their moves. We took our 5 senses daily for granted and being in such environment really gave us a good reminder of how lucky we are to be able to see, h

Not sure if they do this to help you identify the meals, but I found the food was really drenched in sauces, and not very subtle at all. Overall it was an interesting novelty experience but at upwards of $100 per person you expect a lot better, I don't think I can recommend it on the food alone. Very cheap tableware and uncomfortable furniture used as well.

Came here during a visit in Singapore as this was one of the top things to do. While making a reservation here, I didn't see any pricing on the menu so I kind of came here blindsided, not knowing how much we would spend. The experience itself was different. Everything is pitch dark. Not something my husband and I would try again, but it was definitely an experience. I think that what's upsetting is that our tiny courses came up to almost $200. If I had known that, I'd probably wouldn't have tried this restaurant. We could've hand good steak and overall, good food for that amount. If you got the money to spare, then try it. If not, it own't kill to skip this experience.

Very cool and enlightening dining experience. The downstairs staff are so friendly and professional as are the waitstaff.  The waitstaff are your guides who help you walk up the stairs into the pitch black dining room, help explain where all your utensils, food, etc. are and also help you with anything you need. You really do make a "transfer of trust" to your guide, and this in itself is a very illuminating experience. As for the food, very unique! At $78 per person it does seem a bit steep, but they do serve quality food and it is fun to try and guess what you are eating. There are three courses, but each course comes with 4 different dishes (which also means 4 different desserts, a big plus if you have a sweet tooth like me) so a lot of food to try and my husband and I were definitely full afterwards.  Eating in the dark also raises your other senses so I could hear everything very clearly, and relying on just your taste to experience food is definitely very different from when you can clearly see what you are eating (and maybe even unconsciously judge food just based on the appearance).I was also trying to be extremely careful not to knock anything off the table. I am normally a bit of a messy eater so eating in the dark didn't help that, and I did end up with some chunks of food on my lap ;) The menu changes every month and a half, keeping the novelty and surprise alive. We would definitely return! They can also accommodate different dietary requirements. One of the highlights was at the end of the meal when they take you back downstairs and you write down what you think each dish consisted of and they reveal what it actually was and also show you the pictures of each dish. It was quite surprising and funny to see how wrong we were on some dishes and satisfying when you are right.  The hostess pointed out an interesting trend about how what you end up guessing right typically indicates what type of cuisine or food you normally eat. For example, most of the food I guessed right was geared towards veggies, seafood, etc. but my most inaccurate guesses were the meat dishes. All in all, my husband and I had a very wonderful time at Nox - Dine in the Dark, and it was a novel and enlightening dining activity to experience with each other.

A very unique dining experience and something you have to try at least once. You will enjoy a total of 12 dishes per person from the mystery menu and they were all really good. The waiters are all blind and the service they provide in the complete dark dining room is truly amazing. After the meal you will get to guess what dishes you had before they reveal pictures of the food. We had a blast and will definitely be going back!

Really enjoyed the dining in the dark experience, as it was a complete novelty although more than a little disorientating... We definitely spent a lot more time 'thinking' about and concentrating on the food we were eating, which made me realize how much I rush through my everyday eating experiences. It also did make my boyfriend and I giggle quite a bit as we tried 'toasting' in the dark as well as pouring water. Unfortunately I haven't given the restaurant more stars because I think it is overpriced for what it is. The 3-course menu is $88++ per person, add wine pairings (3 'small' glasses including a sickly sweet moscato at the end), plus 2 cocktails (as you spend 30 minutes in the bar prior to your dinner seating) and our bill was just shy of $370... Eek!!! Rather extravagant for a meal that I would call 'good' but definitely not 'fantastic'. I did like the quiz side of things at the end...something I was convinced was fish, then possibly chicken, turned out to be duck... and then they had one complete curve ball in there as well. Apparently they change the menu every 5-6 weeks so you don't have to worry about repetitive meals... having said that, I think this is something great to do once in your life but I wouldn't feel the need to return. My other suggestion? Update the music! It was like a 90s cocktail bar...

One of my best birthday dinners! In a time where social media and mobile phones are the way to communicate this place embraces the concept of good old conversation. Had a lovely night with my husband who surprised me by taking me here. We were served by visually impaired service staff who were simply amazing and the notion of having to use your senses like touch, smell, taste and hearing to enjoy your meal and company is really mind blowing and needed in today's world! Food was good too and the best part was the 'quiz' at the end of the meal!!

When my friends first spoke about trying out this restaurant,  it sounded really interesting although the inital idea of dining in the dark sounds rather daunting. We decided to take the plunge and met up for an early christmas dinner at NOX. We were very excited about this dinner and we prep ourselves that this would probably be one of our messiest dinner. Well, we were glad that we proved ourselves wrong as we left the restaurant as clean as when we got there. :) This got to be the most interesting restaurant concept that I have been though the price is a little steep. The tasting menu is good (The chef was previously from Ember and Private Affairs)  but what stands out from other restaurants is that this dining concept teaches us a life lesson on appreciating the finest things in life without sight.  Having "surrendered" our phones and any light illuminating gadgets to the lockers provided within the restaurant prior to the dinner service, it is back to the good old school conversation that is sorely missed. Finally,  a gathering without having the camera to grace our food before we partake our meals and also  no distraction of Facebook, what's app and another other social media to distract us. Not to forget that the guide who is visually impaired did a great job with the dinner service.  He taught us how we can navigate around our new found surrounding and making us feel 'at home'. He shared with us how he turned visually impaired yet he is still very optimistic about life. We spent most of the time pacing ourselves with our friends and guessing the ingredients and dishes since there is a "pop quiz" at the end of the dinner.  We looked forward to moment where the hostess revealing the "secret" dishes. We were very excited that we got 70% of the dishes correct! :)It is not a restaurant that I would visit everyday but it is definitely a good experience and I do encourage everyone to check out this place at least once to see a different side of life.

Food was good (you'd expect that at this price).  Service was slow (full house on a Saturday night).  We went as a group and sort of became an annoyance to the dinner date table next to us.  It is a fascinating business model and you gain tremendous appreciation, but not sure it is a restaurant to "repeat".  Fun to try in a group (quietly) if you have not dined in the dark!

You can do much better than this place if you explore Singapore.  The stalls are boring from my perspective, after seeing the rest of Singapore.  It is on the expensive side as well.  If you enjoy bland, safe, and food the locals leave to the tourists, then this is your zone.

I only ever come here for the shiok maki at the Japanese stall. For the uninitiated, that's an unagi and avocado roll wrapped in seared salmon and topped with roe and creamy mayo sauce. Normally I hate mayo but this one doesn't taste gross. Expensive and your arteries will likely protest but they can stand to shut up once in a while.

let's say you want to be inside, (full AC), experience the fancy mall-like food court rather than outdoor older hawker centre, don't mind successful franchises, then a food republic food court will feel safe and easy.  sure more expensive, but singaporeans take food seriously -- where else will you find food courts upstairs and downstairs in the same mall?  and even separate kopitiams.  therefore with more discriminating eaters, even the chains are better.  I say try both here and the hawker centres.

Found this place when I had an extreme craving for Xiao Long Bao (XLB) and went to Din Tai Fung.  Prior to arriving I found myself immersed by plenty of aroma that made me question if I were in Foodie Heaven.  How jealous I am that a food court like this does not exist in California.If I could copy and paste this paradigm to where I live, I would become a millionaire because there will be an interminable demand for food like this from where I come from.Also, in the center of this chaos of amazing food, there's a woman quietly selling these amazing tutu coconut or peanut steamed cakes.  I bought 5 for 3.50Sing$.OMG they were sooooo good!I'm coming back here tomorrow and the next day before I go home and cry because I won't be able to walk to this place.

Food Republic at Wisma Atria has renovated and it is even better now.I will say skip the other ethnic food and stick to local food. The safer way to tell which stall is good will be by how long the line is.I only tried the food twice since the renovation. But based on what I had, I liked the Yu Kee Yong Tau Foo very much. I have always like this brand and only had it at Bishan outlet and the old food court at Orchard Emerald. So I am very happy it is available here.The items are standard, different from the other yong tau foo stalls, with 5 pieces of tofu and fish ball/fish cake and the noodles are topped with minced meat. I like the set which includes a side of kang kong drizzled with fermented bean curd. So yummy. The soup is also very sweet and tasty.The mee pok stall is also different with fish maw in it. It is not the best bak chor mee but it is decent. Good choice for Orchard Road. The or luak (oyster omelette) was also nice, especially the chili. Skip the Korean ginseng chicken soup which was very bland.Currently there is a 10% discount if you show your passion card.

With a recent revamp, Food Republic did a good job at changing the mix at the Wisma Atria location. The company also runs Food Opera at ION Orchard, and the food court at Isetan. They complement one another well, and local workers can navigate among the three without feeling bored. Don't know why the sushi and teppanyaki counters are there, since Japan Food Town is literally next door and so much better (also pricier).
Ordered Japanese food at Goen. Black udon & W-Katsu Curry Rice. Ok taste. But when you are hungry, that's another story.

A good place to visit when you can't really decided what you want to eat, just because this food court give you a variety from la-mian, fish soup to BBQ Chicken Wings Love the chicken/pork cutlet noodles here. You should always go for double cutlet upsize because only additional $0.50 more.

Say you want cheap but you're a little too intimidated for a full immersion experience at the hawker centers? Start at Food Republic. It's a food court with stalls representing food from all over Asia. We tried several stalls and the Hainanese chicken rice, the Indian stand, and the avocado ice were all really, really good. The options are seemingly endless and everything is clean, with lots of corners for finding a seat. The decor is of course not legit, but it's still super cute.  Only caveat - there are no napkins.

For those who want a slightly upmarket hawker centre experience and with air conditioning - Food Republic at the Wisma Atria shopping centre on Orchard Road. I have been to this food court numerous times in the past few years and have had good experiences on all occasions. Expect to pay higher prices than hawker centres but it is a sophisticated atmosphere.Of note, the stall selling fish bee hoon soup has a very good soup base, better than many other such vendors across the city. The special prawn noodle served in a bamboo leaf from the wok stall is also very good. The charcoal chicken wing stall is also very popular as they grill the chicken wings basically to order.The Yong Tau Food stall is good value with a minimum of 6 pieces. Get it with some noodles or rice and you have a substantial meal for 2 people.There are ladies pushing carts around with various drinks so you can just get your food and sit down and not worry about going to the drink stall.There are plenty of tables/seats and there is also a few 'hidden' areas if the main areas look like they are full - just head towards the far corners and look for the signs for 'more seating'.

One common thread that Singapore has are the numerous food courts.  You can't walk more than 50 yards before you see a sign blaring "food----".  This being our last night in Singapore we wanted a sit down place and order off a menu.  We walked around but it was one food court after another.  We finally bit the bullet and settled on this one.  This food court is more appealing as it's located on the fourth level as opposed to some other ones tucked away in the basement.  After circling around I settled on stall #06   Pork rib noodle soup $6.50 SGD and prawns $3.00 SGD added on.  Tasty broth.No more food courts for me!

If you find yourself shopping in Wisma Atria and you felt the need to grab something to eat, then head off to the Food Republic at the 4th level. You will be welcomed by a variety of cuisines and sometimes an overwhelming crowd. I try to come here for lunch around 11am to beat the usual lunch crowd. Queue's are shorter, and more seats to choose from. My favorite is the fish stall where they serve a variety of ways of cooking fish-deep fried and soup. I tried the deep fried dory twice and it was just ok but when I had the soup dish, it's the constant thing that I order every time I'm here. Also, when it comes to beverages, I don't need to come up to the drinks kiosk, I can just wait for auntie to pass by with her cart of refreshing drinks. One time when I was trying to veer away from the usual lime juice that I order, auntie was really helpful in suggesting other drinks and I opted for the lychee-just to try something new.When you come here, and it happens to be crowded, remember to look for more seats through those corridors and not just settle on the seats you see. Chances are, you might end up a window seat with a great view of Orchard road.

The newly renovated food court at Wisma Atria Level 4 is finally open to public about a month ago! The folks from the Breadtalk Group really know how to make a difference with their food courts - which gives them such an edge above the rest. Each food court has a theme - though most of it relates to our Singaporean heritage, there are some subtle differences. For the most famous Food Republic (and probably with the most expensive rent) it is all back to basics of our Singaporean food roots with the revamp this time round and they have decorated it with all types of vintage items from our past which gives it a really nostalgic flavour and makes it distinctly Singaporean, even if some of the stalls in there hail from different countries and serve other cuisines. It is after all our heritage to have a mishmash of everything. There is a total of 23 stalls, 3 mini restaurants and 1 kiosk. How's that for spoilt for choice? I need to eat at this food court whenever I am in town next time and not bother thinking about restaurants.I would recommend that you make a beeline for their Odeon Beef Noodles - where my favorite is the dry noodles that comes with soup that packs a punch. Otherwise there is always the safe choice of Thye Hong Hokkien noodles which made this branch famous in the first place when it first opened. People are still queuing to this date, which is good. Their Indonesian Padang stall also has rather hefty meals that is sure to fill up a hungry person or 10.

This place is pretty, the food is okay, but the extra dollars we're forking out for the slightly fancier packaging just affects the foundations of 'hawker food'. I would steer clear of the nasi padang and 'economic' rice if I were you - you could pay up to $6.50 for a $3.50 meal you could usually get at your hawker centre!The only stall (if they are allowed to be called that) that I patronise often is the Rojak Vendor, which serves up a great Rojak! The ingredients are fresh, a little cold, but it enhances the experience (Cold Rojak... now that's an idea!). Besides that, I'd recommend a train ride to Tanjong Pagar or Tiong Bahru for a more wholesome experience.

It's got everything for everyone. It's priced right especially for being right next to the ion high end shopping malls. I ate at salt and pepper and had a hot dish with salmon and chicken and egg for 10 bills.  It was great. Old ladies walk around and sell u drinks off the carts from water to fruit drinks.

Definitely one of the best food courts on Orchard. Would definitely recommend the Vietnamese (awesome Pho and Bun Thit) and Indian stalls. What makes this food court good is the variety of stalls, nice atmosphere, lots of available tables and the option to go to the sushi, teppaniyaki or Din Tai Fung restaurants which are on the same floor for something a bit fancier !

Great selection and great value for the price. I wouldn't call this a relaxing dining experience but if you're looking for a place to satisfy your hunger at a good price then this is a good choice.It's noisy, chaotic and sometimes very crowded but the food is very good.Make sure to bring your own napkins - no one provides or sells any.

Pleaseeee go somewhere else.  Bad service (got our order wrong), bland and tasteless crab (seriously...?!), and expensive!  The only, only reason to go maybe is if you're hosting an out of towner from the US or some far flung corner away from our Singapore, you can bring them here to impress over the skyline of Singapore.  But honestly, the food will just not hold up.  Avoid!

You know things are going to roll downhill when the waitress tells you the only crabs available are Irish brown crabs; this is after we've arrived at the restaurant at 6.45pm, imagine we had a later booking. Maybe they sold out all the Sri Lankan crabs by lunch time or maybe I look like a tourist and don't know any better. It only gets worse when she tells you that the only way to get both Chilli crab & the Pepper crab is to order the Alaskan King crab at $200 /kg with a minimum size of 2kg. Are you kidding me? As we had guests from out of town and they had heard the must try dish for Singapore was Chilli Crab, we persevered. Although I never heard of out 'national' dish known as Singapore Chili Alaskan King crab. We skipped the White Pepper option and stuck with the Brown crab, hoping other dishes could make up for the rest of the meal. Next, add the cereal prawns de-shelled please. But our request was denied as she said the restaurant doesn't de-shell the regular prawns. We would need to order King prawns if we wanted them de-shelled. Seriously?There's really very little else worth reviewing after this. The Chilli Crab had hardly any meat. We paid $128 for lots of egg and chilli sauce. The King Prawns weren't de-shelled. All 6 dishes we ordered arrived within 10 minutes from start to finish. It's as if the cooking staff just wanted to get everything out as fast as they could. Later when we ordered more fried mantou, since we had so much sauce, they arrived a minute after ordering, barely warm and definitely not just fried. Someone is making these in big batches and leaving them in a tray until someone orders them. The final straw came when we found out the price for coconuts. They were $9.90 each and that was hard to swallow. Maybe this is a tourist trap. If you venture to this establishment, be prepared to be taken advantage of. It is their cash cow and they are prepared to milk you for as much as they can get away with. You've been warned. This is a tourist trap.

You are paying for the location.  Can't beat right off the Marina.  We tried the chili crab it was pricey and okay not very meaty.   The bowl was mainly full of sauce.  The noodle dish was good.   They do charge for tap water, peanuts and the wet wipes.  We were afraid to ask for extra napkins!    But after paying for the meal the worse was the ladies room.  We had to use the public ladies room around the restaurant.  The smell was horrific!

Would have to disagree with the previous reviewer on this place. The food is always consistently good here and much more reasonably priced compared to say palm beach seafood a stone's throw away at one Fullerton. Granted service can be a bit erratic when the place is packed on weekends but it is my go to for quick dinners before and after performances at esplanade because the dishes always arrive promptly and they're often delicious. The signature homemade bean curd is the bomb - there's an extra flourish to it cos they add deepfried dried prawns which gives each bite a little umami burst of saltiness. The spinach in broth is good too with a very tasty stock. Among the other zichar staples to order are the salted fish fried rice and coffee pork ribs. And the bill won't give you sticker shock (if you don't order pricey seasonal seafood lah). I've had wonderful filling dinners here at between $25 - $40 a head. This place is a classic lah. Haven't forgotten its neighbourhood roots despite the posh setting.

Just terrible. Worst meal for the money. Actually this would've been a bad meal if it was 10% of the final bill. Service is aggressively resentful delivered with chili and white pepper attitude. Food at the average hawker stand is better quality by a mile. Also, I challenge any Yelper to try the Sri Lankan crab. I'll save you the suspense - you won't try it because it's never available. The worst, as expensive as this place is, it looks like a dive and you get nickel and dimed for the privilege: water $3 for 4, peanuts you didn't order $2, extra wet napkins $3...etc. This place is a disgrace and the owners and staff should be ashamed.

Please don't waste your money here. Ordered some food, service was terrible because the guy came and was like I'm a part time here I can't answer any questions, there was fish scale in our hor fun dish, coconut not fresh, pork ribs tasted funky, squid tasted fishy not fresh like in other restaurants, just avoid this overpriced place for any occasion. Ugh.

Chilli crab, 6 mantau, 1 signature tofu, 1 beer, 1 tea $200. Hardly good value when the chilli sauce is not even nice. The tofu was quite good, though pricy. Atmosphere was the highlight with live music by the water, pretty light and cool breeze. Overall disappointing value.

No signboard chain is good in general, but this one probably has the worst rep out of all.  We usually come here when bringing guests from other countries due to its perfect location in Esplanade with beautiful views of both Marina bay sands and Fullerton hotels. If you look like an expat, or look like you are with clients, or you just look easily deceivable in general, beware and be warned. You will order a crab dish and get charged $1000 (including GST and service charge) while the Singaporean locals sitting beside you get charged $100.  When you order chilli crab, one of the main dishes to get here, they will ask if you'd like an Alaskan one (and not the typical sri lankan one) without quoting the price. the menu shows no price but a mere "market price" statement. The difference between the two is that Alaskan crab comes out to about $600 per dish, while the Sri Lankan crab comes out to approx. $50~80. If there is this much price difference between the two, i think a moral restaurant would and should state the price when asking a customer whether they want the "other (expensive) kind." However, on the few times I came here with a company, I realized the waiter actually avoided in answering (or acting like he didn't hear) our question on how much per g an Alaskan crab it is and hoped that the "stupid rich expat" would just nod and agree away on ordering Alaskan.We've tried both Alaksan and Sri Lankan due to companies many times not being able to forthright ask its price in front of clients, and there really really isn't much difference in taste to warrant the $900 difference.  No signboard, you're so rich already. Get your morals straight and stop acting like a restaurant in a third world country ripping off your own customers.

Among all the big chili crabs places, No Signboard was my favorite. Emphasis on the "WAS" because I think they deliberately offer the Alaskan Snow crabs without telling you that it is 3x more expensive. Our usual bill in this restaurant is $35-50 per head depending how big the group. Last year, I was entertaining some tourists and suggested the place. They went and (ordered) ahead of me -- I just told them to order the chili crabs and white pepper crabs. We were shocked when our bill came and it was $1500+ for 10 pax. When we checked the bill, the Alaskan Snow crabs was the reason. I was told that the waitress said that the usual crabs were not available so they offered the Snow crabs --- without mentioning that they were 3x the price.Last Tuesday, I was back there for a team business dinner and my Chinese-speaking officemates ordered -- so I couldn't make what they were ordering. When my boss got the bill, it was $2400 for 16 pax --- and again it was because of the Snow crabs. Don't get me wrong, I'm ok spending $150 for a meal IF its worth it. I can get very good chili crabs in other restaurants at $30 without feeling duped.

My family & I love this restaurant & also known as Golden Spoon. Die die must try their famous signature dish, crab with bee hoon soup. The soup is so tasty & the crab is fresh. Their appetiser - deep fried oyster roll with mayo is delicious, too. We love their fresh fish & vegetables & as if we're dining in one of the good restaurants in Hongkong. Noticed lots of expatriates dining in this restaurant. The boss told me that he has lots of dining places & Red House Seafood is one of them. Prices are reasonable. This restaurant is always packed & so is their car-park lots. Worth your calories.

A classic tze char restaurant with competent food and reasonable prices to boot. Tried their signature crab bee hoon and it was on point. Crab was big and fresh and fleshy. The stock was robust with wok hei and the bee hoon soaked them all up. The coffee pork ribs were very aromatic and well marinated and the HK steam fish (we took soon hock) was fresh and steamed just nice. Service was fast and polite.

It's been a while since I've been here. I stayed away after hearing news that the chef was different, but came back cos apparently he's back. The crab beehoon was still good. I liked the gravy A LOT. Some must orders: crispy squid and their crispy tofu. Both were standout dishes that got everyone in my party fighting for thirds. Haha

A fairly typical Chinese restaurant serving up the usual dishes, the one reason why I keep going back to Golden Spoon is for their crabs, specifically their Crab Bee Hoon. Located in the heart of Tiong Bahru, near the market, parking is relatively easy as there are a lot of lots to be found just in front of the restaurant. The only issues I have are with the staff, who don't really seem to understand you, so patience is definitely required. One thing to note when dining, especially when you're going for the signature Crab Beehoon, is that the later you go, the higher the chances are that you'll end up with only the larger crabs left. Meaning if you're planning on going on a date, its best to get there early to choose a smaller crab or you'll end up like me having a 1.8kg crab to share with my friend, which honestly, is a little too big!

Great crab bee hoon. Although I have to admit, I haven't had crab bee hoon anywhere else, I can't imagine it being any better than this anywhere else. Another hidden gem is the cereal tofu - think cereal prawns, but with less cholesterol. Chunks of egg tofu coated in garlicky corn flakes and deep fried, but the kicker is the sweet pumpkin sauce underneath. You don't get that with the prawns, and it's great. I just found out that this isn't even on the menu anymore, but they'll still make it if you ask.

Another one of my local favorites. The chilli crab is really good here, and is the mee goreng. I also tend to order the famous crab bee hoon, but for me it's slightly inconsistent- sometimes good, sometimes not memorable. The drunken prawns are another of my favorite orders here, and my wife, loves them. The broth is strong, and the prawns very fresh. The pumpkin sauce tofu is also delicious. There is much more seating outside than inside, and sometimes the fact that it is right in the car park might be irksome. Once, during the the height of CNY, they set up a tented area next to their restaurant, and the breeze was very welcome there. Also, BYOB is free. Highly recommended.

Update based on a visit a few weeks ago: the crab bee hoon unfortunately lacked a rich crab flavor.  The crab itself was tender and sweet, but the bee hoon was lacking salt or something.  The cereal tofu is also now an off menu item.  It is still one of the best dishes here (my out of town friend agreed)!

I didn't go into this place expecting super authentic Mexican I mean after all it's called super loco and it's in a super touristy area in Singapore. So perhaps adjusting expectations before going helps the experience. We went during happy hour for $9 frozen margaritas and these were strong enough. I prefer margaritas on the rocks but not available for happy hour. Advised that the dishes were meant for sharing family style so for 8 of us we got 4 dishes and chips and salsa. In America each dish woulda been a portion for one but that is bc we are fat Americans. It was plenty of food and it actually tasted really good. Had the chicken enchiladas and the steak both of which were flavorful. The salsa that came with the chips isn't really my favorite kind - more smoky rather than fresh but went nicely with the drinks. The setting is fun and it didn't rain and their fans are powerful enough to feel like a cooling night breeze. Overall attentive service and a fun night to hang with other friends who had to leave for the airport early. I certainly wouldn't have chosen to go here just bc the name but my friends did and I'm glad we did. I think the dishes were expensive - like high 20s to low 30s but I'm getting used to these types of prices. I suppose it's about the same for tourists that end up hanging around Times Square. I mean what else do u expect but jacked up prices and mediocre food? So when I get pretty decent food like I did here I'll just be happy and not sweat the high prices.

Decent Mexican food. Tacos are really good. I'm from San Diego and I know what a good taco is.However , food is super expensive and nothing special to justify the price. Might as well walk over to Clark quay and get your Mexican food there.Additionally I just came here for breakfast and wanted to order the breakfast burrito... I asked to have the black beans on the side....not the most egregious of requests....but they could not do it. The server (very nice by the way) explained that it was already in the burrito and could not be taken out. Which made me question...am I ordering a pre made burrito??? For $19? What am I paying for? I should just go to 7 eleven. It's was the strangest thing .

I agree with previous reviews, the portions are so small and expensive. A single taco is $11. Nothing about the taco justifies that price. It's small (six inches) and basic. The garnishing is simply shredded cabbage and some sauce, the cheapest fixings possible. There's no sight of any kind of onion or tomatoes.That said, the grilled corn sprinkled with cheese is really good. I don't remember the price of that item, but that's probably why I liked it so much.The margarita jug is a rip off. It's not a jug, it's a slim carafe. $59 for six short glasses. Yes, that's cheaper than if you ordered six separate margaritas, but barely.The servers are nice. Okay, you get one point there.

DINNER: - tacos al pastor ($13)- quesadilla de Pollo ($16)- gingerale ($7)FOOD: The food is a deserving 3/5, as both dishes were very well seasoned. The tacos are served on single tortillas with a small portion of al pastor, couple pieces of grilled pinapple, and salsa Verde. Each taco is a couple bites. The only issue with the dish was the overcooked meat, which tells me they don't prepare the al pastor on a revolving spicket as its traditionally done. It had ok flavor, but was dry and tough. Quesadilla was average at best, and lacked cheese. No stringy, oozey, goodness here. Food is better here than at their sister restaurant, Lucha Loco.AMBIANCE: Decoration is well done. Comfortable, relatable, but elevated enough to host a date or set group dinner. It has the markings of a Baja taqueria without actually putting you there. I only wish it were a bit brighter. I sat inside, and found it hard to see what I was eating. Probably not an issue if seated outside. PRICE: It's expensive for dinner, because the portions are so small. My bill for one totaled $37.50 and I could've eaten a couple more tacos ($11-$16 each). OVERALL: Come for drinks + late night eats. It's not a bad place to visit, and could be very fun. Stop by with a group later in the evening to grab drinks and share a few small dishes.
The food was bad and the service was horrible. I do not recommend wasting your money at Super Loco. I am sure any other Mexican restaurant in Singapore is better than this place.
Super cute but pricey! The drinks are strong and the menu sounds very tasty. I will come back for snacks one day. It looks really nice for a chill out sunday with friends. Nothing pretentious.

Decent Mexican, love the pineapple in my salsa.If you've read my 200+ reviews on Yelp, I've eaten at some fancy expensive restaurants and nevertheless have found the food to be of value. Either on the quality per dollar or quantity per dollar ratio or both.Super loco is unbelievably expensive.There is a dearth of Mexican options in Singapore and they are milking the expat pocket for what it's worth. I especially disliked how the "tequila cart" came round and the servers "didn't know how much each shot costs" yet pressured my whole table into buying them. It sounds silly but you'll understand when you're there. It was $16 each, which is Pangaea type pricing while drinking said shot next to a kid watching Aladdin on his iPad. The food portions, as with lucha loco, are pathetically small. You could eat better and be full at other super atas street food joints like Ippudo down the road. Unless you are craving tacos epicly like I was craving chwee kuay in the middle of Virginia, or your boss paid you a really good bonus and Hermes ran out of Birkins for you to buy, skip Super Loco.

I went back and fourth between 3 and 4 stars on this one.  The service here was abismal, we could not get someone to take our order or attend to us, but as I'm new to Singapore it seems like maybe I'm asking for more service that is to be expected.  In any case, the food was great!  The masa huarache is a must try, great flavor, as was the tostadita de garbanzo.  These really tasted good.  The tacos were good, but expected.  My boyfriend and I also ordered quesadilla which never came, so they offered us a tequila shot instead since we were full and ready to head out anyways.  This was a nice touch.  Speaking of drinks, the margarita did not impress.    I will definitely come back for the Huarache and stick to a corona and it will be a nice dinner :)
This place is pretty nice I think. 3.5 star. The food is not pricey imo, especially in this location. We tried several ceviches and many of the tacos and all were nice.

Each bite delivers explosive bursts of flavor....tantalizing your tastebuds with hints of sweet, spicy, and tangy...hitting you with one after the other.,.and the harmonious flow of textures and freshness in each dish! Pure genius (the main reason I love Mexican cuisine). The crab appetizer, taco's, chicken quesadilla, sirloin, and let's not forget the drinks...all are top notch! Go now before it's too late and this place like so many others starts lacking in the "umph" that made it great.

I really don't understand the low rating for this place, I know it's expensive, but so is everywhere else. Fish tacos and chorizo tacos are delicious, the drinks are strong, and the churros are damn good. Had 2 tacos, a margarita, and churros and that was plenty to fill me up. I'm a hardcore taco fan and would definitely recommend this place. Food, drinks, atmosphere, all great. I'll give 4 stars because yes, it's expensive.

the tacos are great!  I can't get over the experience we had there.  the service was some of the worst i have ever had in Singapore.  we could not get a drink from our server despite being next to the bar, so i would just go to the bartender and get them since he was quicker.  somehow they messed up our order (I rec'd the wrong quesadilla) and then forgot a dish. our friends sent back their salad  2 times and the people next to them sent back their quesadilla 3 times since it was the wrong one.I would take this as a bad night and they're still working out the kinks as it's a new place.going forward i might stop in for a taco and a beer, but I am not going to stay long, especially if the service doesn't get any better.

Ok all please forgive me, I am writing this for Americans that are accustomed to Mexican food.  While the favors are ok, the quantities are un acceptable, the menu is small,  the price for taste, quantity is something to be ashamed of.  I have actually thought about going to confession after this meal as I feel guilty for going.  That being said if you not used to good Mexican food and are used to over priced fare, you just might enjoy it, just know that even a run down Taco Bell provides better value.
It's just bad, food is bad, service is bad and price is bad.  All up bad.  Had the chef even eaten a real Mexican food? Ugh, never would I ever come here again.

This is a quick review:Positives + good food+ good locationConsiderations- forgetful service- rude maitre d (hostesses)- devilishly small portions (those labelled large might be good for almost one person)

If youve been to lucha loco then you know what youre getting yourself into.  This is the younger drunk sister to lucha loco.  Its set in the robertson quay area near the gallery hotel.  If you like lucha loco you'll like it here. If you hate the expensive food at lucha loco you'll hate it here.  The menu is almost exactly the same which was a disappointment.  I love the food but I thought they would try something new.  They added a couple new menu items but its pretty much the same, as is the drink menu.  Its fine because I love the food anyways. This is more of a casual bar atmosphere than lucha loco. More of a casual drinking atmosphere to grab some small bites.  I gave it 4 stars because in spite of the prices I really like the food and atmosphere.  It was successful for a reason.  The service was on par for singapore which means not stellar but it can be worse for sure.  Our server was available but not overly attentive.  Expect to pay what you'd pay at lucha loco.  The drinks arent cheap but until the powers that be realize that taxing the crap out of alcohol doesnt actually work in making people drink less, the drinks will still be expensive here.

Ambience was decent; has a very chill vibe, and it helps that it's next to the river so the whole setting was quite casual. Perhaps taking note of the previous feedback, the service we we experienced was extremely fast, and their staff were friendly. Food was pretty good! My favorite dish by far was the blue crab tostaditas! Price point is definitely on the higher end, probably because of the location as well. With that said, I think a lot of people on yelp are complaining because they're not used to paying for a single taco (I've been to a few restaurants that charge by per taco overseas). The only disappointing thing, for me, was dessert. Their churros were a little bit overdone, and my husband didn't really like the rice icecream.

Well I saw that this place was located close to my hotel. It was a great location but the place had no WiFi to check into Yelp with.I had a desire to grab some tacos for the night. Looked at the menu and ordered two beef and two Chicken.Plus ordered a side of chips and guacamole dip.Well normal Mexican food restaurants don't usually charge separate for a small helping of chips, and charge for salsa. But this place does. Since the salsa and Guacamole were the same price I went for the Guacamole $5 Singapore dollars and $5 Singapore dollars for the small bowl of chips.I also ordered a margarita.Well I got the bland chips and the blandest guacamole ever. Was really expecting more flavor. My tacos were then brought to me and there was not a shred of cheese on them. But the instead put red cabbage. Well I tried the beef. It was a bland, watery mess. I was so disappointed. So then I asked again for my drink. It was brought out and to my surprise was just a nasty looking lemon slice on a glass of margarita on the rocks. Tasted it and was again disappointed. Well moved to the chicken taco, and Wow, disappointment number 4!!! Tastes like eating a paper taco with cabbage. No cilantro in sight. No spices, or hot sauces to add. Just a lot of money and a disappointed stomach. Asked for my check and left after paying S$10 for on beef taco and S$8 for the chicken. S$16 for the margarita, and S$10 for the chips and guacamole.The Resturant at least took off the two tacos I didn't eat. I highly discourage anyone eating here, unless you like high priced bland food...

I obviously was not expecting authentic Mexican food in Singapore but was hoping for something decent. I loved the decor, the music, the ambiance. Service was great throughout. The concept of the place is great, but I'm sorry the food did not live up to the price they are asking for for each dish.The beginning of the meal was not too bad with the tostaditas - wishing they just made tostadas, that were regular sized instead of the topping too heavy for the tostadita.The tacos were not bad. The poblano taco needing a lot of help in the seasoning department. The lamb al pastor and the lengua tacos were not bad. The baja was quite flavourful.The churros to end our meal was a disappointment. It was more like a crispy biscuit. Yes they were crispy throughout. Was it overcooked? Overfried? Not sure but it was not doughy or chewy on the inside and we felt let down.I feel like this place is worth 2 stars only but I'll only take 2 stars off for food and value. I'm sorry that I can't recommend a place that charges 5 times more than what it's actually worth.

This might be the biggest disappointment in all of Singapore. Pretty unbelievable how much hype this place got and how poorly it delivered. I guess they know their audience well, since people keep packing the place in. Perhaps it's tourists or nearby residents who want tacos but can't be bothered to venture farther than 10 minutes to get decent kormex at Vatos. Save your time and money and go someplace else. Nothing on their menu tasted well, and I'm not even going to complain about the price. The food is bland and even the tortillas don't want to be there since they fall apart before even getting picked up off the plate. Sad. They have beer and creative cocktails, so that and the river location save them from a one star ranking.

Super Loco is a Mexican place (same owners as Lucha Loco) located alongside Robertson Quay. It has a very colorful look and design and it does look as if it is a fun place to hang out at. In a sense it is also as they serve some pretty decent Mexican food. We sampled several different tacos and they were all good but everything does however feel slightly like a rip off as prices are too high for what they are serving.I was also (like some other reviewers) asking for some changes to the dish but that was not possible which also seems to suggest they are perhaps not making the food (or that they are just unwilling to do much for their customers). Service was very disinterested as well, one of these places where the staff are more interested in talking to each other, checking their phones or fixing nails and/or make-up. We had to waive at people several times to be able to place an order and when finished it was the same thing trying to pay (and the place was not even half-full)So food was decent but over-priced and we did not really feel that welcome so will not return any time soon.

Great atmosphere, but the food is pricey and not really that Mexican.  The tree enchiladas with no other extras like beans, rice, etc. was SGD 26, about twice what it should be.  It was also extremely spicey, not very Mexican.  Interestly, no burritos and only one enchilada choice.  Might be better with the tacos that looked good. Probably wouldn't return, although I did have a brunch here before and decided to try again.

If you like overpriced, inauthentic Mexican food served by disinterested staff, this is the place for you. Some of the worst 'Mexican' food I've had in Asia. Clearly, the owners don't know the food. Will definitely not be back.I think they call it Super Loco because you would be  Super Crazy to come back and eat here.

I am very wary of Mexican restaurants outside México, since I've had so many dreadful experiences with horrible food labelled as "Mexican". My general rule is: if a restaurant has neon signs, cacti, sombreros, skulls, and a stereotypical name including words such as "tequila", "amigo", "fiesta", "loco", "señor" or "latino", that is definitely a place to avoid. So, anyone could understand why I was reluctant to visit a place called "Super Loco".Reading the menu quickly dispelled my fears: no burritos, no nachos, no chimichangas, no fajitas, no chilli con carne, no "taco meat" (whatever that is). Instead, they have proper corn flour tortillas and also several welcome surprises with ingredients such as axiote, huitlacoche and pibil pulled pork. There is fairly good variety of tequila and mezcal, some very good brands included, and even explain the difference between tequila and mezcal. When it came to taste, Super Loco delivered. I had a huitlacoche quesadilla, with more mushrooms than huitlacoche but was still good. I also tried a red snapper taco which had a very nice touch of axiote, and a very nice mango ceviche. I was glad to have some of those nearly tasteless but fresh Mexican beers we like so much, rather overpriced. The only thing I did not like was the habanero sauce since it was, in fact, mayonnaise and that ruined the habanero taste. Overall, it was a good meal. It was also overpriced, though.The obvious question is if the place is "truly" Mexican, whatever that means. I could tell the owners are not Mexican, some slight misspellings on the menu gave them away. However, it is clear they have done their homework properly. The menu states they travelled to Mexico City and the Pacific Coast to do research on street food, and that explains Super Loco's good taste. It is a very good take on Mexican street food. It's true, maybe it's not exactly as it is in México (purists sure will say that), but it has the proper essence. The fact that they don't stick lime wedges on your beer makes them more Mexican than many other joints I've visited elsewhere.

Love the food but be wary of the prices. I'm a big fan of Mexican food. Super Loco delivers HOWEVER beware, prices are steep. A single taco could equal a meal elsewhere. A single Elote is enough to burn pockets. So order with caution! Prices aside, food was incredible. Flavours were spot on and service was great. Ambience was fun and vibrant. I'm a big fan of ceviche and man do I love their combinations. Their tortilla chips are super addictive and the hot sauces are so flavourful you hardly notice the spice. Elote was simply awesome and tacos were delicious. However the portions leave a lot to be desired. Remember to leave space for cocktails as they have a pretty extensive list. I understand that Super Loco is situated in an expat area and prices are suited to the clients there but I feel that for the amount of food they serve, the prices are unreasonable. Not for every dish but for most. I'd love to return as much as I can but the prices are simply far too high. Amazing food. High prices. Worth a try for a true Mexican food lover.

Not the cheapest place in town but I find Singapore can be expensive anyway for eating out.Came here as it caters to gluten free. They do corn tortillas and there is lots of choice for what you can have which was a big plus.So, fab chips and guacamole. Salsa was ok but not as good as the guac. This was a decent portion that two of us shared.Tortillas good (portions of two) but small so you need another couple to fill the gap. We ordered pork tortillas then little small (4) portion mini crab things which were tasty. Mexican was normally always a cheap meal but not so much here so be warned. Desserts again offer gf options - not wow but ok enough. Great margaritas.Service was so-so. Solid 3*.

If you're a fan of Lucha Loco, you ought to know she's got a hot new sister at Robertson Quay that everyone's checking out.I met her over the weekend, and I must say she's got a colourful personality. I admire her taste in furniture and her keen eye for decor. Her taste in music is top notch, as she bobs her head to club-like Tanjong Beach Club-esque tunes. And my, can she cook up a storm. For starters, her salsa is pretty good but her guac isn't as good as mine. (And I'm not saying that 'cause I'm jealous. I make a meaaaaan guac!) Her elotes (which is roasted corn smothered in sauce and sprinkled with cheese and chives) are probably one of the best snacks I've had in a while. I also loved one of her tuna appetizers, though I forgot what it's called. Although I'm an only child, I do understand that people hate it when you compare them to their sibling. But I gotta say that Senorita Super is just like her sister in the sense that she charges outrageous prices for a single taco.* However, I couldn't help but see if it was worth it at all. I ordered the one with chorizo, but was disappointed that it was more shredded meat than ground chorizo itself. So overall, I'm giving her a 3.5. Don't get me wrong, she's a cool friend and I'm thinking all my other friends will like hanging out with her, but she's just really high maintenance considering she enjoys the finer things in life. Maybe we'll just hang out once in a while over margaritas and elotes. --*That did not sound right but whatever leave me alone.
Well, don't sit at the bar, service is pretty poor as you have a team waiting on you..... Nobody in charge and nobody to blame.Food was ok, but 4 of the 5 drinks they advertised, they didn't have.

The day before I visited Super Loco I was told that it was currently the hottest thing in town. Digging around on the internet I found out it was run by a couple of Aussies who consulted chef Jason Jones (of Mamasita fame) on the menu. Being from Melbourne and having lined up at Mamasita on a number of occasions to eat tacos like every other hipster in town, I figured it was worth checking out.We arrived early (6pm) on a Saturday night and got a table right away. In the hour that followed the restaurant filled up with all sorts of groups - families out the front, dates on the the smaller tables and groups of friends gearing up for a big night on the larger high-topped tables at the back. The Margaritas were good, the salsa and chips were excellent though I baulked when I saw the meagre portion of guacamole that was served with them. We then ordered the famous Elotes, a Mamasita staple, which I declared would be the test for how well they had interpreted Jason Jones' menu. Flavour wise they were spot on - sweet, spicy, sour and salty but for some reason they were cold when we ate them as if they'd sat for far too long after being grilled. Perhaps this is an interpretation suited to the Singapore climate but I'm not sure it's for the better.The tuna things* were great, the chunks of fish generous and the dressing really well balanced. I'm sad they whisked the plate away before we could scoop up the slaw that they came sitting on. They would have been a nice addition to the top of them. *I can't remember what these were called!The Mexican truffle quesadilla were also terrific. Hot, melty with cheese and stuffed full of mushrooms. Compared with the tacos (ranging in price from $8 to $12!) they felt like one of the better value items. I tried the snapper taco. It was okay though at $8 I was kind of expecting the flavours to blow my mind. They didn't. While certainly not a cheep night out, a visit to Super Loco is a fun one.  Choose your menu items wisely and consider the cocktail jugs as a way to maximise your cash.

The pricey and high maintenance sibling of Lucha Loco. (As Michelle M aptly put it)This is the new up and coming spot on Robertson Quay, decked in blinking neon, blaring music and similar lucha libre decor. The line is long even on a weekday. The menu is very close to the one at Lucha Loco, and so are the exorbitant prices. For the premium pricing, I was underwhelmed by the food. I went for the elotes (mexican grilled corn), a couple of tacos, a chile relleno and the huitlacoche quesadilla. The chile relleno tasted rather tired and bland. The huitlacoche quesadilla didn't contain any huitlacoche, they substituted with a couple of mushrooms and corn. Maybe Singaporeans aren't ready for the real thing. (Huitlacoche, plainly speaking, is mouldy fungus infected corn, i.e. an acquired taste) Their tacos were a little better, but not particularly authentic. Also, $8 for half a ear of corn?! You have gotta be kidding me. Again, it's Mexican street food! Tacos cost between US$2-4, S$8-12 is daylight robbery at around 4-5 times the cost. I've eaten at many a food truck and hole-in-the-wall type places south of the border, I know what I'm talking about.Adios, better Mexican food and pricing can be found elsewhere in Singapore.

As the new kid on the block of robertson quay, Super Loco sure has stirred up a lot of buzz among my group of friends. Frustrated for not being able to get a reservation here for friday or saturday night at a good time for the past two weeks (calling on a wednesday on the same week is not early enough), i finally headed down on a sunday night. Even at 6:30pm the place was already packed.Overall I think their food was tasty. i enjoyed my meal, and this place has got their ambience correct for that trendy place with dim dim light (the older couple next to our table made me smile when they used their iphone light to look at the menu) but what ultimately made me knock off one star is the price to portion ratio. It baffles me that $11-13 per taco is just for ONE single 6" taco. The flautas were $18 for two regular sized rolls, and the quesadilla was also $18 for tiny pieces. Churros were $12 for 5 pieces. The elotes was as tasty as everyone gushed, but it's $8 for half a cob of corn.I think if the prices were 20% less, it would have made more sense. But then again, in a country where $22-28 cocktail has become a norm, i guess this is the price to pay for glam-ed up street food?The drinks on the other hand, is pretty averagely priced at $15-18. The margaritas were pretty tasty!

Is it time for brunch?If so, this is one of my new favorite places for brunch.  It's by the water, but not too hot, and has such fab options for a casual meal.  Reservations for groups can easily be made over email (gotta love it when you don't need to call!) Also, who doesn't like Mexican food right?The FoodThere's a nice variety of bites for the kiddos and adults.  We started with the esquites - grilled corn with a healthy dose of spice and lime mayo.  It packed a nice kick and was a great, semi-healthy side/starter.  The Mexico Grande was a great variety of options including avocado toast, bacon, eggs, and baked beans.  Everything was seasoned well with an ode to savory Mexican flavors. The sweetcorn fritters were nice and crispy with a little sweetness and paired well with the salty smoked salmon. My little one LOVED her berry smoothie and I felt pretty great letting her go wild with the smoothie because it was full of almond milk, coconut water, and agave nectar.  It's great when restaurants present sugar-free, healthy options.  But when you want the sugar, look no further than the crispy, sweet churros.  Fried dough and chocolate sauce - does it get better than this?The verdict?I'd definitely return.  The ambiance is chill and it's a nice, family friendly option.  This is more of a Californian Mexican style type of restaurant, but in a good way.  I'm just thinking of my next smoothie there...

Have heard much about this place and as this is my first time here, what I heard didn't disappoint. The ambiance and atmosphere was vibrant and the food scrumptious. The soft shell chilli crab spaghetti was a little spicy for me but the Suki beef rice bowl was done just right with the right amount of sauce, and the beef, tender. For drinks, the Hulk, which was a concoction of green Apple, ginger and honey and the Tropical Dream, of mango and raspberry was perfect compliment to the meal.

This place is a work hanger built into a restaurant.  It's a very cool concept. The food is reasonable priced for Singapore. Plates were a good sized.  Chicken was a full breast.  Garlic bread was crispy and good.  I like the ambiance. It's a good place to come and chill. Have. Coffee and small bite or a meal. Fried Cauliflower very good.  Lemoned iced tea very strong. Coffee looks good too. (Didn't try it though. So that's off what I saw being served.) We would come back and eat here.

The drinks/ coffee are good but the food is terrible! I ordered the Salmon Mentaiko pasta which was a chef's recommendation. I love mentaiko everything but this $19.90 pasta was fishy, bland and tasteless all at the same time. It was definitely cooked by someone who could not care less. Even Whampoa Market/ Pastamania serves better food. My partner ordered a fish and chips and beware! It comes with fish bones! You are only paying for the ambience. What a shame.

The craze for this hipster,instaworthy cafe has died down.But the food remains satisfying!My colleagues and I had-All day breakfast - Fish & Chips- Seafood Pasta- Grilled Chicken - Taco Platter The portions were generous, the only downside was that the chicken lacked seasoning. I would definitely order F&C again, feeling blessed as I had 3 awesome F&C from different places this year! (TICM and Workbench!) Wheeler's has a large serving mayo for those who like to splatter their fish with! Fries are plentiful too, it's the kind of fries that are still delish even it's not piping hot. It was a hearty meal overall.The ambience of the place has an industrial chic vibe going on, the signature blue doors, high ceilings are unseaworthy. * Weekday Set Lunch $19.90 for selected mains with soup or salad and a drink.*Water is self serving, I really dislike food establishments that charge for water!

Great ambience with wide spaces - something hard-pressed to find in Singapore. Food range is surprising wide. Love the food choices we made although the poached egg is still far from world standards. The coffee is good. A glance at the drinks list reveals another surprisingly wide range of whiskeys, cocktails and beers. A bit hidden from the main road but a definite gem if you are looking to chill in a unique and cool environment amidst good beverages and decent food

I am a strong supporter of bicycles as a mean of transport, and I sometimes miss those Sundays back home when they close some main avenues so we can cycle just for recreation. No wonder any kind of place devoted to cyclists will always catch my attention.Wheeler's Yard is on a quiet area in the border between Whampoa and Toa Payoh. The restaurant is inside a spacious industrial warehouse, sharing the massive space with a bicycle shop and self-labeled atelier. In a time of crammed cafes and confined restaurants dubbed as "intimate", the high ceilings and massive tables of the restaurant are a delight. The whole place is a vintage paradise, highly appealing to architectural restoration enthusiasts. They basically kept as much as they could from the original warehouse and made the restaurant and atelier fit in there, creating a vast place with a warm atmosphere, ideal for groups and sharing.The menu is varied, with some Japanese inspiration and local ingredients. I had a nicely done pan-seared snapper served in a small pool of fragrant mushroom stock. It was not spectacular, but the flavours were wisely balanced. My wife had a sous vide chicken, which was juicy and fairly tasty. We also had the truffle fries, which we liked a lot. They have a small, careful selection of local craft beers at reasonable prices.
