Another plus is they don't impose service charge, since the place actually works on a self service basis. The food prices are not those of a self-service place, though.All in all, Wheeler's Yard works as a retreat from the race of the chase. It feels ideal for a quiet afternoon in Whampoa (which is quiet enough itself). I can imagine myself arriving there after a long and tiring urban cycle ride. Yeah, that's going on my list.

Wheeler's Yard is my go-to place during the weekday if I need a place to complete work or do some readings. The high ceilings and spacious arrangement doesn't give a claustrophobic feeling. Best thing is, I don't need to sit elbow to elbow with people and fit for a good cup of coffee. The servers pretty much leave you alone most of the time so don't expect service here. It's something that I don't mind when I prefer to just concentrate on my laptop and my readings. Food wise- the fries are a must-try. My friend and I made a mistake of ordering our mains AND fries. The portion is so huge that even on its own, the two of us could not have finished it. The big breakfast set is rather big also. However, the price did leave a huge hole in my pocket. Overall, good place you want to have some quality time with friends or by yourself.

Wheeler's Yard, you surprise me.Your concept is too cool for school. You are a bike shop, a pop up bar, and an air conditioned cafe all in one. I love how you picked up on today's industrial decor trend and morphed your huge warehouse to house all three concepts.I'm not a bike rider, so I can't comment on your sweet looking bikes, but I am an eater and drinker, so I will give you my 2 cents on that! Your calamari is a great starter; LOVE the sauce it's drenched in though the squid was a bit too chewy at times. Your Caesar salad is my second favourite in Singapore (next to, you guessed it, Salad Stop's haha.) I love how you give me those cute little cookies to go with my coffee, and how I have a good choice of ciders if I'm in the mood for one.And how can I say no to the easily accessible pitchers of ice water, some which are displayed on the back of a bike?I normally decide to cool down in your air conditioned cafe, where I enjoy listening to your awesome pop playlist. I love how I spot neighbours of all ages hanging out here and in the al fresco dining area too. Basically, you know how to appeal to the local community, and you're doing it all right. And hey, you're even willing to serve not-cool-enough people like myself with a smile, so you get all the stars for that!

Being a cyclist from the moment I heard of this place I was intrigued. My first thought when I walked in was that it is awesome and very Melbourne...The coffee was good and definitely a stop point after my morning ridesIt definitely had the potential to be a 4 star food experience. Unfortunately we had to send back our burger because the meat was sloppy red raw! So we sent it back and the next one was really good and fresh, which is why I think this place still has potential and  just needs to ask how you want your burger done.

What a find!In what feels like the middle of nowhere, Wheeler's Yard doesn't look like much from the street. A big blue door on front of a warehouse doesn't hint at what's behind... but the people standing in front of it madly taking selfies indicates that perhaps something interesting is going on inside.Walk down the side alley and through a big open door and you suddenly realise that this place is choc-full with people drinking coffee and eating brunch. I'm not talking just a dozen people, but a hundred, maybe more! There's two areas to sit. Behind the glass doors, you might be lucky to score a seat on the big communal table where you can read magazines and relax in AC comfort. Outside there's more seating and also the view of the bicycle workshop where you can buy a funky bike or bring yours to be serviced. I spied some cute kids helmets sporting animal faces, and only wished they came in big-kid sizes!We stopped in for drinks only - there's coffee and tea, interesting soft drinks and also a small selection of beers. But many visitors were sharing piles of fries, sweets and brunchy items that looked appetising.It's great to see that the entrepreneurial F&B world is alive and kicking here in Singapore and if Wheeler's Yard is a sign of more fun things to come, then it's safe to say that Singaporeans have a lot to look forward to when it comes to innovative venues.

I was frankly pretty disappointed with the visit. The ambience and layout are really fun and the place looks like it ought to be great. Sadly, the food was only so-so. We went for Sunday brunch and between everyone at the table sampled quite a few items on the menu. I had the Ultimate Beef Yard burger and my wife had the Big Breakfast. My burger was slightly undercooked and VERY greasy and the fries (which I had heard good things about) were dry and overcooked. The breakfast items were rather bland as well. Prices (as mentioned in other reviews) are not cheap and frankly very inflated for the quality. The place is fun to visit and I suspect that's what you pay for. It is family friendly but very, very noisy for lunch on a Sunday - don't expect any intimate conversation. I think this is a low 3 star rating due only to the quirky fun atmosphere but I would not return for the food.

I went to Wheeler's Yard yesterday evening with my partner and the first impression was very good. Nestled within an industrial warehouse, it's like a hidden gem that's waiting to be uncovered. The ambience within the cafe is certainly unique - with its high ceiling, warm lighting and consistent bicycle theme. It felt like a place where one could relax and chat with friends for hours. The food and drinks were definitely pricey, especially considering the location and the fact that everything is self-service. We were there too early for dinner, so we ordered a bowl of truffle fries to share ($14.90, i think).The truffle fries were AMAZING. The moment the bowl was set on the table in front of me, I was hit by the aroma of truffles. That was when I knew this was going to be an experience to remember. The fries were hot and crispy and the chef was definitely liberal with the truffle oil and grated cheese. The portion was just right for 2 people, and we polished it off in no time. The truffle aroma stayed with us for the rest of the night, even through dinner. I'm still gushing over it. We'll definitely go back again.

A place like this exists in Singapore, holy schnikes! Texas barnyard meets Novena hustle & bustle. At the onset, when you first lay your eyes on this beauty, you begin to wonder, "this place looks out of place doesn't it?" You walk inside this pimped out barnyard and you concur, "this place is really out of place!" But I guess, that is part of the charm of Wheelers Yard, a huge pimped out warehouse located in a quiet street corner of Novena with neighborhood Aunties and Uncles as regular customers.Inside this proverbial barn is a restaurant, bike shop, a pop-up bar/cider stand, and what I swear is a stage concert. Literally, the place can turned into anything the owner desires.  In terms of the food, the Fried Calamari dipped in black sweet sauce is a MUST try. I know I sound like a broken record that this and that is the Best in Singapore. But, why not, I'll say it again, the Best Calamari dish in Singapore. The Calamari portions are huge, even for Singapore and the Sauce was well... the bomb diggitty. The Prawn Aglio Olio, which I seem to try at every restaurant, was good, but doesn't compare to Starker down the road. I didn't try the bbq ribs, but I might as well have had it since my fellow communal seating partner was gorging himself right next to me. Based on his reaction after every bite, it must have been good or at least worth the consideration.  Overall, Wheelers Yard is a MUST SEE cafe and truly embodies the creativity of Singapore and its people.

I found a review online that mentioned the Ribeye steak was worth a shot! Steak in a cafe didn't seem like the natural option but none of the other items on the menu impressed me much so I decided to go for it! What's the worst that could happen? $27 wasted and a sad face. Boy! Was I glad I decided to take the path less travelled! The Ribeye steak was delicious (I had it medium done)! Unfortunately, the same cannot be said about their burgers! My friend asked the cashier, "what's good here?"She replied, "up to you lor"Unsatisfied with the answer I chimed in, "but what would you recommend?"She asked, "the burger" He decided to go with her recommendation but we weren't impressed. The meat was subpar. It tasted kinda chewy and over marinated... kinda like cheap sausage meat grounded into a patty? Either she has poor taste or she gave him really bad information. Coffee-wise, I really didn't think that they were as good as Nylon etc. Passable but it wasn't impressive.Service was also rather slow that day. My steak came out on time but my friends' food didn't. Ambiance-wise, Wheeler is unbeatable! A beautiful hipster cafe! I love the concept and the deco. Not so much the location and the parking. There's barely enough lots to fit 5% of the customers. They only have 4 lots out front. All 4 were taken when we arrived. Plus, the remote location (an industrial like area) didn't really help because it wasn't very accessible via public transportation so I wished they had more parking space!
Really nice place.. Great coffee and good brunch items on the menu. Strongly recommended to visit on a weekday as Saturdays and Sundays tend to sometimes get a bit busy.

The hype over the locality of this place, an industrial space functioning both as a bike atelier and a cafe at the same time, Wheeler's Yard is a place where you can get unique bicycles while also having western food items and drinks!The food menu is rather extensive here.And the drinks menu! Rather simple.The Latte ($5) tasted ok with the right amount of milk added. Nothing too great.The Big Breakfast ($14.90) is served with a wholemeal bread toast, scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, hashbrown & garden salad. This is way better than the coffee although not overwhelming as well. The toast was rather nicely toasted and crusty. The scrambled eggs are nice. The bacon is great. The sausages and the hashbrown are average. The garden salad is also not too bad. In overall, this could have been better.If you live or is around the Balestier area, this place should be considered to have your meal (for its ambience; do not expect too much from the food and drinks)

So there's food and coffee here but that's not what I'm talking about (if you must know, its ok).  But the bike shop here is fantastic!  Custom builds from Taiwan.  Amazing little accessories.  Bamboo fenders!  And a smart and enthusiastic staff with a strong love for all things bike.  Ya...I get it...it's about as hipster as you can get but they know how to throw down for reals.

Super friendly service, good happy hour prices ($5 for a half pint). Interior is all over the place - is it a restaurant? a bar? a darts place? Menu similar - Thai, Indian, Japanese?! Could use a little focus. I guess it's part of the charm. Lots of uncles inside.

Had a Saturday dinner at this place with a friend. Purposely came here for their special dish, pitan maki. Basically it is a sushi rolls topped with their special made century egg sauce. It is good, and I enjoyed it very much. I ordered other food like unagi kabayaki and sukiyaki beef as well. However, I would not recommend the unagi and sukiyaki, the unagi taste cheap and the sukiyaki was tasteless. They have wide spread of variety from Japanese to Thai, but lack of focus and signature food. Well, it is a good place for a beer and some snack food though.

I remember walking into this restaurant last year with a bunch of friends, browsed the menu and then left. "Jack of all trades, master of none" is probably the best description of the food they are trying to do here. From THAI to JAPANESE to ASIAN-FUSION to WESTERN - we were actually tired of reading all the description in the almost 30-page thick menu. If you're here, just ask the waitress for recommendations.  Fast forward to last night, my friend suggested we go MAD NEST for dinner and trust me, I was very reluctant to go. She's into the arts and craft scene here in Singapore and apparently there is a "Flower Exhibition" going on at the restaurant. Little did I know that MAD NEST host art exhibition every other month and it's all displayed on their wall. For this season, its a collaboration of local florists and photographer where beautiful bouquet of flowers were created and photos were taken (think Kinfolk, Cereal style) and all the photos are on sale (if you want to buy). Coming from a photographer's point of view, the photos are pretty rad. At one corner of the restaurant, there's a display of small edible microgreens in small pots. We got to know you can be part of the "ADOPT A PLANT" programme where you can pay any amount you want and take back a jar (which consist of soil, seed and fertilizer you just need to water them) and grow your own plant from the jar at home! All the donation will go towards the Nature Society of Singapore. I think this is a very good initiative on sustainability. Now, moving on to food. As usual, I was totally confused and we leave it to the waitress for recommendations. Eve (the waitress) was very friendly and helpful and suggested a couple of "best sellers" . For starters, we ordered  fried squid with salted egg yolk and 2 temaki (sushi). The volcano hand roll was pretty good and the salted egg yolk squid decent. For mains (all shared), we ordered seafood fried rice, stir fried long beans, and steamed fish thai style. Fish was particularly good, very fresh and executed perfectly. You have to order if you happen to come. All the dishes come in medium sized portion so it's good to order a couple and share among a few people. In total, we ordered 6 items with no drinks and paid $95 total. No doubt the price is very reasonable and the food was pretty ok, I walked out of the restaurant still feeling ............. confused.

Been here a couple of times . Good beers. The Jap food, good couple of items, skip the ramen though. Thai and Indian food is definitely above average so do give it a go. $2 for white rice?Reckon I just cut my carbs in that case. Service, Oh the service.Let's put it this way.I stand a better chance getting hit by a car standing in the middle of the road than to get a simple glass of water the first time I ask for it. By far my record was 13mins and after 3 attempts before I decided to walk up to the bar with the glass to get water. It just get ignored the moment the wait staff acknowledge your request for water. For that, kinda struggle to give it any better.

What kind of food can one find here? There's Japanese, All-Day Brunch, Italian-Asian, Northern Indian and tapas. Nice spacious indoor dining, with art pieces decorating its walls.We tried Oiishi Maki, Sashimi Moriawase San Shu, Mad Nest Wings, Mad Nest Breakfast, Old Bay Frites and Chili Crab pasta. Food was good, and the wings and fries came with their own dips. The wings were well marinated and flavourful. Oiishi maki was tasty because it had many ingredients such as avocado, unagi, salmon, tobiko in/on it. The Chili Crab sauce was refreshing, and the pasta was not undercooked. Liked the brioche in the Breakfast set. Tasty with good texture. The bacon would be better if it was crispy, or softer. Happy hour till 8pm, and a jug of Stella Artois goes for $25+. There's a mounted TV screen outside the restaurant, so diners at the al-fresco area could watch football or whatever sports that's on that day. Have seen people with pets at its outdoor seating area.Service crew are mostly young and ernest.

Having passed by Mad Nest so many times (I live nearby), I was determined to give it a shot. I loved what they had done with the space. It's very modern and clean, with art pieces on the walls that are also for sale, and a large al fresco area. A glance at their menu proved to be rather intimidating. There's just a little too much going on in that restaurant, and I'm not sure if I want to have tapas dishes with Indian curries or sushi - just saying.In the end, I settled for trying their brunch. I arrived one early afternoon and ordered the Eggs Oscar ($16) - crabmeat and asparagus with poached eggs, cheese and hollandaise sauce with an English muffin. It was really good! I really loved the flavours that came together in that brunch dish, although I have to say, the portion was kind of small.I tried my friend's order of the smoked salmon & spinach eggs benedict ($16), but it was somewhat disappointing. There was so little salmon on it you couldn't really taste it at all.The coffee here is weak and not worth making a trip down for, if you're into coffee. On the plus side, they do have an extensive drinks menu of cocktails, shooters, liquers, whiskeys, japanese sakes, ciders, beers and wines though.

Standing out from its neighbours, Mad Nest at East Coast is a chic bar eatery that serves up a smattering of cuisines from Northern Indian grub, Spanish tapas, Japanese fare and also brunch items. The first time we went there, we thought it was actually a Japanese restaurant, thanks to the bottles of sake on display and its décor is quite Japanese as well. The food is pretty decent and affordable, but so far, what we've seen was that more people are coming for after work drinks rather than dining. The locale is quite and parking is fairly easy, seeing as how most of the neighbours don't really draw large crowds. There's ample space, but the al fresco areas don't have any shelter so all it takes is a sudden downpour to spoil your night out.

1. French toast - It came cold. Would have preferred it hot. Otherwise, it was nice. The fruit and nuts mix at the side complimented it well and the toast was thick and soft inside. - Love butter slice that came with it. The waiter said it was imported from uruguay but he failed to spell the butter's brand name correctly (he said it was spelled "Canerbroule" but that name had 0 hits on google - anyone knows what it's proper spelling is?) 2. Ice cappuccino- Average. Service - Good. It was rather empty when we headed there at noon on a sunday. There were only 2 tables (including us). Ambiance - Good. Only thing is that I could not get any internet reception inside the restaurant which was a bumper! I suspect it was those thick concrete walls that blocked the internet signals.

If it looks like a Japanese restaurant, chances are, it is. Mad Nest however, doesn't seem to stick to that line of thought. Since we were there when they were about to close, we didn't really get a chance to try out most of their mains, just whatever they had that didn't take too long to prepare. But based on that alone, I have to say its interesting enough to make me want to come back. And with a large and spacious al fresco area that allows smoking, I've got to admit I'm quite sold on the concept of it all. Going through their menu, you'll find smattering of cuisines that range from Northern Indian, tapas, Japanese and even brunch items. Getting here is convenient and parking is just a minute's walk away. Rain however, is bad news for al fresco diners as there's no shelter at all in sight.

Generous portions, chicken breast is smooth and juicy, and really flavourful. Vegetables and char siew are pretty good, but not really standouts. Quick, friendly service and reasonable prices. Maybe the only negative is the lack of variety on the menu (or the lack of a menu at all), but that's probably the only reason they can serve so fast.To get a table, you'll probably have to come before 630pm for dinner on weekends. There's a long queue for takeaway orders too. Overall, this is way better than Hawker Chan's (also in Toa Payoh).

It's different. It's rich in flavour. It's old in ways of preparation. You can actually taste how things used to be back then.This chicken rice is class. No frills, just like how they used to make'em in the old days.  Nothing superbly spectacular about it as a whole but you can tell that it's something special.It's a slightly above average plate of chicken rice that gets you there for sure. But there's something about that taste that brings you back to olden days Singapore food. The star however does not lie in the rice or noodles or chilli, the chicken is definitely one of the softest and most moist I've ever eaten!The sauce is uber thick but a tad starchy. It had a slight herbal flavour to it which made it fragrant. This is definitely a very unique alternative to your everyday normal plate of chicken rice. I do for see myself coming back again just for that soft sweet chicken.P.S - Things are a little bit more to the sweet side than salty here I noticed.3.2 STARS

Sweet, sweet, chicken rice. The sauce is the magic in this hard to pronounce restaurant. LEE FUN NAM KEE (combination of founder's and his wife's surnames). Now don't forget that because this is where you will experience the sweetest chicken rice sauce ever. The brown sauce that comes with the soya sauce chicken is thick and starchy and so flavourful. You can mix the chicken with the chicken rice and you're set, your meal is complete. If you're not easily satisfied, there are the standard veggies that you can order as a side, the veggies - Kai Lan, comes with sinful pieces of pork lard. YUMMEH. The price of the dishes are higher than your usual chicken rice in the kopitiam but this is a semi-restaurant leh, so the price is not that bad la. The restaurant is always crowded on meal times, both weekdays and weekends. Do make your bookings beforehand.

Lee Fun Nam Kee is a reminder that there's more than one way of preparing your chicken rice. I personally like the "normal" Hainanese version, i.e. plain "white" boiled. However, this restaurant, in addition to serving it plain, also offers an awesome soy sauce version. The thick and sweet gravy is poured over the chopped chicken before serving with chicken rice. The rice is slightly oily and very fragrant (which is how chicken rice should be). It's so good that you can just eat it on its own.This restaurant is also highly recommended if you are looking for a nostalgic taste from the 1960s. The restaurant began as a food stall in the old Toa Payoh Lorong 4 food centre in 1966 before moving to its current location.

I am a huge chicken rice fan....lee fun serves really juicy and tender chicken and sesame oil chicken, perfectly executed. The rice is also really fragrant with lotsa chicken flavor. The only problem is the quality of the rice can be variable, and I have had better rice at other chicken rice places. But overall this chicken rice joint is legit and a must try

Have long been meaning to come check out this place! It has 2 of my loves, fish and soup!We ordered their 10 pax set dinner for $288 and it had:Coral trout steamboat - very fresh and sweet meat. Free flow of soup too. I'm really just happy with this fish soup and white rice. Homemade Tofu - very well executed dish. Tofu is soft in the inside and crispy on the outside. Sauce is also delicious!Asparagus with Scallop and Sea Cucumbery in XO Sauce - I love the slight spice that goes with the freshness of the scallop and the vegetable. Golden Roast - this roast chicken is not bad. Claypot Pork Belly with Salted Eggs - this is really a Claypot of goodness! I can't see the salted eggs but every mouthful is damn good!Prawns with sweet spicy Sauce - also not bad. Choice of Mango jelly or turtle shell jelly 龟苓膏  for dessert - nothing very special but a nice end to an awesome meal!Will definitely bring the extended family back to let them have a feast here too!

Visited Balestier and Killiney road outlets.For the steamboat, would gave 4 stars for Balestier outlet due to the great tasting soup stock. The 3 stars was given because we felt that there were more fish bone parts than fish meat in the steamboat. The same goes for the Killiney road outlet except the soup stock was not as tasteful as the one in Balestier road.  The way steamboat is serve in this restaurant chain, one does not know what one gets until the dish comes to the table and one starts eating.However, the Killiney road outlet is more spacious than the one in Balestier.I would hesitate to patronise these restaurants on a regular basis.

Zichar dishes were average - 2.5 stars.Fish steamboat - 4.5 starsWith the thick bee hoon, it tasted like really good fish bee hoon soup! I didn't pay though so it might be expensive for what it's worth. The Holland Village XO fish bee hoon might be comparable.Mango pudding - 2 starsToo sweet.Guiling gao - 2.5 starsGood texture but wish it was served with honey. They gave what looked like a sugar syrup.

Fish steamboat is the signature dish here. There are 3 choices of fish:For medium size (recommended for 3 to 4 persons)- Badang - Quite common in many fish soup places $40- Garoupa - This is good and meaty but has some bones when filleted. Bigger chunks that flake $50- Pomfret - Sweet and even texture $60We took the Garoupa. The dish was a good portion and can also be shared with 5 persons. It comes with quite a lot of vegetables inside and some pieces of yam. The soup was really thick and flavourful and the steamboat kept everything piping hot even after the fire had gone out. It's a complete meal with some rice. It was served with their garlic chilli sauce which is quite spicy but really tasty.We ordered some other dishes and really liked the hae cho (prawn rolls). The Indonesian style claypot $13 was quite unctuous but seemed quite fatty as well with lots of skin. Simple stir fried veg was a generous portion for medium $11.
This place is an institution.  They could not be bothered if ratings were bad.  Since day one i knew of please wonderful msg laden steamboat it has gotten more prosperous so something must be right.

This place can get rather crowded and your clothes might stink afterwards. Hence, do not wash your hair before visiting this place or I suggest you may wanna go to the salon after.It is a great venue for family dinner. You may already know that they are famous from the  celebrity-lined wall, however I have not seen any of them in the restaurant. The charcoal-fueled fish steamboat never fail to lift up the family gathering.  They have 3 types of fish to choose from, pomfret, garoupa and batang (boneless). Always choose  the amount of fish +1 more than the number of people you have because portion is rather small or I am a big eater. The soup is souperlicious! I really like the milky salty taste of it. That is the highlight.As for the side dishes, they are all not too bad. You may want to order them, but the highlight is definitely the fish steamboat.  Also, this is definitely a cheaper alternative compared to Imperial Treasure steamboat for their fish feasting.

The red garoupa hotpot ($35 for 2) itself was quite tasty. Don't get me wrong. But the whole experience just felt underwhelming. By the way, for those not in the know, it isn't actually a "steamboat" you expect in hotpot restaurant where you cook raw food. The dish comes boiling and the ingredients are already cooked when it's presented at the table. I've had this dish at their rival over at Serangoon Road twice before. I remember the soup over there being tastier. But we also ordered other dishes here like hei cho, sambal kang kong and prawn paste chicken wings. All were good but not outstanding. The chicken was particularly tasty. The whole meal for two ended up totaling $80. Felt like a rip off when I saw that we were charged for things like rice (it must be a cultural thing as I've not encountered additional payment for unlimited rice refills in any other country), soup refills (clearly a hidden cost because there's no way anybody would not ask for a refill since the first serving is a pathetic amount based on the shallowness of the pot), chrysanthemum leaves which you add into the soup and paper napkins. The waitress didn't have the initiative to inform that the leaves were an additional cost when she asked if I wanted them (the hotpot already comes with cabbage). Which I guess is typical "service" in Singapore. The "soup refill" and chrysanthemum leaves (a small plate of tatty looking vegetables) was $6.

My parents are regulars of Whampoa Food Street Keng... they are so regular here that they can even go up to the counter and go "Is Ah Keng (the owner) here? Say Hi for us!" And if he is around, he will come by our table and have a short chat with my parents. If you do come by here, do order their trademark Fish Head Steamboat. I love the soup in the steamboat. Another trademark dish is their hot-plate tofu, prawn-paste chicken, roast chicken, coffee ribs, their cereal prawns and salted egg prawns. Do go down before 6.30pm as that is where the place hits the full house.. so getting a table will be quite difficult after that time.
Excellent food! Fish broth is so good - I've become a regular. Always full of people - recommend a reservation or go after peak hours

Located near at the whampoa wet market, this place might be difficult to find for people who don't stay in this vicinity. The shop opens from 5pm onwards till 9 :30 pm and you will realize the food market is relatively empty except for this stall and the drink stall.The food served is fish head steamboat and the cooking method is very authentic, using charcoal to heat the soup. The soup is very rich and you will realize the owner uses a lot of anchovies to cook it. The fish is tender and soft. Do try their duck wings, it is braised in an awesome gravy which does well with it. The meat is cooked to perfection and soft.However the waiting time gets longer if you reach after 6 pm, you can wait for 1 hour, it is that popular.

i find the fish head soup expensive. we ordered a small 3-4 to share. It was $60. When the soup was served. We counted there were only about 10 pieces of fish. Really? Did they made a mistake by giving us a small 1-2 to share?  Will not be back. Over priced.

I drove down this road almost every weekday for the past two years, but never once looked in. Last week, mum goes, "hey let's eat at this steamboat place in Whampoa", and I'm like, "What? Where?"Yeah, there's a signboard up front, but it really doesn't look like much... until you see the queues. With an S. The night we went the queue stretched from the foot of the stairs (the small, simple lower floor is JUST A DECOY - there's so many more seats UPSTAIRS) to a snakey line along the main road.Before you let that deter you, have patience. When you finally get to it, the steamboat soup makes it all worthwhile. they cook some of the freshest fish I've ever been served, and the flavours are so clean and simple, you'll wonder why new-age/fusion-y restaurants mess with tastes.Oh and before I forget - the steamboat comes to you with charcoal inside, which is as old-timey as you can get! Hipsters will kill themselves to get in.
expensive. bad service. the food was below average. they forgot our drinks. when i asked for help the reply was 'what do you want' not how can i help or yes sir...really crap..

Located along ophir road, this restaurant is a great hang out place for lunch, dinner or after work happy hours. The restaurant has 2 areas where you can chill, the outdoor and the indoor. Outdoor will be along the alley which is nicely decorated with graffiti. In addition, they have long sofas to accommodate large group of peopleThe drinks are affordable during the happy hours, the food they served are delicious too, especially the cheese finger stick. It definitely goes well with the booze. During lunch hours, do try their curry chicken and fish and chip. The chicken is soft and tender, together with the thick curry gravy, heavenly.Great place with nice music at the background, certainly a place worth visiting after work.

Down to earth, extremely casual bar located right at the entrance of Arab Street, Blu Jaz is the perfect combination of sheesha, beer and bands. The bar expands up 3 floors and across to another building. On a cool weekend evening, its often hard to find a table, both outside and in. They often host themed nights such as 90's RNB which are buzzing till late.The food is mediocre unless paired with some alcohol to amplify the taste, my personal favorite are the Balls of Fire. The sheesha is quite good and reasonably priced with a selection of flavors to boot. Drinks are also reasonably priced and there is something for everyone.The facilities are weirdly located almost inside the kitchen but are kept relatively clean. All in all a fun time with the right crowd.

I used to come here quite a fair bit because they do have a decent selection of beers at rather reasonable prices for Singapore. From time to time, a live jazz band plays on the 2nd floor. The place was rather "underground", used to be set apart from your more commercial offerings, but of late it has gotten rather popular with the locals and expats. Hardly a place for a relaxing evening these days. But they still serve decent food and beers, I would still come if I can find somewhere to sit. Do make a reservation beforehand if you intend to be there on a Friday night.

Blu Jazz is a nice, casual bar to chill out at in Haji Lane. They have three levels, all with different things at each place. The downstairs has a nice outdoor area and they serve food. Upstairs is a bar, and during the weekends it becomes a more club-y area, with a dj and dancefloor. The food here is alright, nothing to write home about. Drink prices are pretty good. The weekends here can be fun. They have different themed nights and djs. A pretty cool crowd here too.

Blu Jazz has its nights. It's located just slightly off once hip Haji Lane, and is a 3 story restaurant/bar with alfresco and indoor seating. Drinks are okay - not the cheapest but not out of this world either. Blu Jazz tends to be filled with tourists and foreigners who just moved to Singapore, with the latter often searching for an 'authentic' Singapore experience. Perhaps because of the crowd, Blu Jazz can sometimes feel fake and off-putting, but hey, when the crowd is right, Blu Jazz can be pretty awesome.

Met up with some friends for drinks here and was very pleasantly surprised. I wasn't expecting Kampong Glam to have any bars -- this is the Muslim quarter after all! -- much less a funky bar like this that looks like it's been transported straight out of Melbourne or Berlin. This bar is cool and hip, mildly grungy, edging on the side of hipster but not quite there (thankfully). Nearby Haji Lane and the narrow laneways around it are chock full of street art and graffiti, so I felt like I was definitely back in Melbourne.The place is in an old house (mansion?) with pretty shutters on the windows and outdoor seating in the laneway to the side of it. Inside, it's an explosion of colour and Moroccan lamps, crazy mirrors, and a faintly Middle-Eastern-on-acid vibe. Whatever, it works. There's a huge stage and often live music here. When we went, it wasn't jazz music -- I think it was more rock, but I don't actually remember because we wanted to have a conversation so we chose to sit outside.We went on a weekday night and it was PACKED. They barely managed to squeeze our group of 5 in. They weren't serving full meals, just bar snacks, and we didn't order any so I can't comment on the food. Drinks didn't seem any cheaper or more expensive than in other parts of Singapore, and they serve massive Tiger Beer towers here (our group of 5 shared one and it was plenty of beer!)Staff was super-friendly in spite of how busy the place was. There was a veritable monsoon while we were there, and staff were quick to rush out and crank up the roof cover thingie so we wouldn't get soaked.I noticed that this place was way more popular with Westerners (either tourists or expat workers, I don't know) than with local Chinese-Singaporeans or Indian-Singaporeans. I'm not sure why, but that's what I noticed.Definitely recommend checking this place out if you like the cool, hip, unpretentious types of drinking holes, especially for live music.

Great place to chill with a beer and friends and see local artist perform,  has a funky chill vibe going on.  I love to see people step up and play or sing with the bands, have seen some super talented people rock out!

The jazz performance we saw was VERY good. They have a great band that played when we went, however, their drinks are very weak. I ordered a Pina Colada, which was pretty much just a smoothie. The other drinks my friends ordered were also weak. The place wasn't packed, so I was surprised that they weren't paying attention to our table. I would go back to try to food and listen to the jazz, but I don't think I would get any drinks there again.

Great place to hangout at night! We came here on a weekly basis and I will always order chicken shawarma, I love their cocktails, and reasonable price for beer as well! Now I moved to the state i sometimes miss blue jazz and their fun ambient!

Very pleasantly surprised. Ordered the grilled salmon and it was perfectly prepared. And it came with the crack...you know the skin that was perfectly crispy. The sauce with capers was nice as well and finished with mash and grilled veggies. Really who could complain with that. Ok even the house vino was pretty good. The Pinot noir from New Zealand. Aussies please do not hold that against me as I did marry an Aussie after all. The music is a bonus.

Blu Jaz Cafe is just terrific! It has got something for everyone. 5 stars, baby!* star -Great hipster, Indie vibe, in a cool location. Good food, music, drink, lots of seating...hookah* star -excellent bar/ drinks...bar on all three floors, yay!* star -entertainment-live music, dj, dance club, comedy club. Depending     on floor/day. (Check website calendar) * star -good middle eastern food.* star -professional as well as personable staffBlu Jaz Cafe -one if the best times in Singapore!

Miguel and I stopped by Blu Jaz during our crazy staycation with our friend, this time checking out the dance club on the second level. If you like to dance to American hip hop and reggaeton*, this is the place for you!We were disappointed in the indie music at Kyo, and the non-dancing groups at Trace, so after paying our $10 cover at Blu Jaz, we were happy to see that the dance floor was crowded with people ACTUALLY DANCING and the music was awesome!To echo Miguel's review, the place IS slightly run down, but when it's dark and you're just there to take shots and dance, I'm hoping ambiance is the last thing on your mind. Friday night here was a ton of fun for me. I wouldn't hesitate to return again!--*Admit it, you like reggaeton when you're drunk!

There is only one word to describe Blu Jaz: FUN! The first floor is where some of the best Jazz talent from around the world strut their stuff. I'm, particularly, a huge fan of the band Fuze Collective headed by vocalist Fendi Sahid. Fendi is one of the few artists based in Asia that has a voice that oozes with Soul... So rare to find in this part of the world. In fact, as good as the Jazz artists / Jazz bands we would hear from the Dirty South, USA. Fuze Collective performs on Saturday Night, so if you're free, be sure to check them out.If Jazz isn't your thing, there is a fantastic night club on the second floor. The cover charge is $10 and is well worth the price of admission. During my last visit, on a Friday night, DJ was jamming it up with Reggaeton. Who knew, they play Reggaeton in Singapore, but they do at Blu Jazz! I found myself reminiscing my college years in New York City. I give this place four stars. The music fantastic. However, the facilities are a little run-down. Additionally, there is not a lot of room for patrons to hear music on the first floor. In short, Come early! By far the best place to hear great music in Singapore.

The venue is colorful and it's got some life. The music though... Could've been more groovy. Those who've been here a couple times say the music is either a hit or a miss. I guess I came on a miss-y night? The DJs probably rotate? The live drummer was awesome though. Definitely was feeling his beat. If the second floor is too busy for ordering drinks, walk on up to the third floor where it's a bit emptier (or at least that was the condition on Friday 11pm-ish). The bartender will give you one on one attention and prepare your drinks in a blink. In addition there's a smoking area on the second floor.

Located right in front of Haji Lane, Blue Jaz is the place to be if you are looking for something indie/underground. Personally, I come to this place for the food. I love their grilled fish and their balls of fire which are minced chicken rolled into balls. Occasionally, they do hold dubstep nights so anti-fans of dubstep, do take note on which days they are holding this and steer clear of the second floor. Other than that, it's a great place to chill out with friends and chit chat.. oh and to smoke some shisha too!

I first came here when it was a small little Cafe - but now it's this huge place, with the upstairs bar, then, there's the third floor and the downstairs restaurant. I prefer the downstairs area - as it's by the road - you get to people watch, and it's pretty fun.What I Love: It's good a good selection of finger food and drinks. And the music upstairs isn't that bad either.What I don't Love: It's become so crowded and full, that service is a bit slow. Prices are a little steep too - compared to the other establishments in the area. The food too, isn't all that great. It's basic finger food. I mean, it's not exactly memorable. I like the place - due to the great times I've had with my friends there. But I could do that elsewhere. For the price, I would rather eat elsewhere.

I heard a lot of good things about Haji Lane's night life so when a friend from the states was in town, we decided to check it out on a late Saturday night. We strolled around at 11pm and I was a bit disappointed. I think I was expecting something like Lan Kwai Fong (LKF) in Hong Kong where people are just dancing in the streets with music blasting from every storefront.We heard Blu Jaz was a cool venue and were seated pretty promptly on what seemed to be a busy night. Ordered a few mixed drinks (gin and tonic, vodka tonic, etc) and we seriously couldn't taste any alcohol in any of our drinks. They're reasonably priced at $10-12 but I'd rather pay more for a stiffer drink.The hookah (shisha) was fun - we had the mint flavored stuff. There was a live jazz band playing indoors (we were seated right outside) so that added some great ambiance. There was also a video projection of a DJ spinning upstairs in the club that looked pretty happening. We tried to check it out but with a $10 cover at close to closing time, we decided not to waste our money.Overall a fun place for a really chill night.

Every city has a place like Blu Jaz: really cool at first when they started. Then everyone felt the same way and it got unbearable in some way or other. Blu Jaz is that place in Singapore.To be fair, the music, DJs and indie events they hold here on the second and third floors are always good fun.It's just that the bar/cafe... it's exploded, and in the process it's lost something we once loved about it. The casual and intimate vibes about this eclectically decorated place were its star attractions. Now that hundreds of people feel the same way, you can rarely get a table or hear anybody when they're talking. Service has become brusque and impersonal.No fault of theirs. It's a tricky thing to be this popular. The food, which used to be pretty acceptable at its price range (mid-range), is no longer so.I still want to love it, I still want to go every time, but I can never get a damned table. These days I just go to the better bar/restaurant *behind*, that they also own... even when Piedra Negra gets crowded, at least you can stand/sit in the streets.

I love this place cause it's really casual and a good place to just catch up with friends for some food and drinks. The prices are mid range but worth it for the portion that you get. It gets really hard to get a table in the evenings and weekends but they usually try and find a way to accommodate you. The place is open for lunch and dinner and the one dish I like best is the Beef Lasagne. It's amazing. The sauce that's in the lasagne is so good. It's piping hot when it comes out and you will definitely be wanting more after you finish it. What else is good is the Balls of Fire and the Zing Wings. You can also have Sisha here and the price is about the same as the other places around Arab street. Overall this place is great for a casual night out with friends.

Not really one of my favourites, it is nevertheless a great place to hang out for casual drinks and an easy meal with friends. It's not excessively priced, although the food tends to be pretty average.They got really popular and it's always packed, resulting in an odd expansion of the venue. Whilst the shophouses they occupy are atmospheric and nicely done up, they've also got a sequence of unsightly tables lined up along the pavement. Not really the best seats in the house, but this is where you usually end up if you arrive later in the evening and all the other seating options have been taken up.

Nice place to relax and socialize with friends. Food and drinks are cheaper than Clarke Quay but normal standard. Sometimes the live music can get loud. Shisha also available and the Balls of Fire (small chicken fried balls) are good but are not consistent in taste and can get salty some times. If you are in the mood let your hair loose on the dance floor above. Entry to the dance floor is free.

This place is a gem, since I don't particularly go to Greenwood Ave much as it is rather 'ulu'. I didn't expect that within the same stretch of shophouses, there are at least 3 different Italian restaurants. However, Fratini caught my attention as she has a no menu restriction. Everything will be chosen by chef Gabriel and all you need to do is totell him what you don't or can't eat. Lunch started off with very tasty appetisers. The prawn is sauteed with pumpkin puree and avocado mash. I could eat more than a portion of this. The scallop with cheese was satiating. Presentation was good. The main pasta was al dente. I would say that all the food was from the range of good to very good. The set lunch is at $45++ which is reasonable. I will definitely be back again. I would like to have some crayfish the next time I am here. :)

This an absolute gem of a restaurant. There is no menu and the owner goes round to each table to see what your likes/dislikes are and if you have any allergies. He also recommends wine and they certainly have an amazing selection. The food was excellent. It has been a while since I've had such a good meal and it really was like being in Italy. First and second courses are a selection of fish and meat dishes. Each is just a mouthful or two but fantastically prepared. The last main dish is an individually prepared pasta, we could see from the other tables that none of the dishes were exactly the same. Dessert was a small selection of tasty treats, again no more than a mouthful or two. Despite each dish being quite small we were perfectly full by the end of dinner. All of the staff were fantastic and the atmosphere is nice and cosy, I actually forgot I was in Singapore as it was so much like being in Europe!Not a cheap evening but well worth it for a special occasion; I will definitely be back!

It seems like sharing plates was the theme for all my birthday meals this weekend. I had dinner at Bar-roque Grill the night before with 6 family members while tonight's dinner at Fratini was with 5 of my childhood friends. Though the French and Italians will probably snuff at anyone comparing their "pride of my mama's table" cooking, I will.I thought Fratini offered a way more enjoyable, bang for your buck, well paced and homely meal. Before you say well hey, isn't Bar-roque going for more of a fine dining angle? I'd say if the chef "plumbs his roots", serves "large familial portions" and his mum's apple pie is a star dessert, we're talking bout the same concept here and modern Alsace vs. Pescara cooking becomes a discussion on semantics and style for the chefs.First on the food, I liked that Fratini offered almost 10 dishes (I lost count) that had different textures (roasted, fried, grilled) and flavor combinations. My favorites were the roast pork, which was like an Italian siew yoke, braised beef cheek with black lentils - common cheap cut at a lot of restaurants these days but Fratini's was braised well enough that it *melted* in my mouth. The fried squid was a winner too but then again welding a fryer isn't a standout skill at this level. All our dishes came just as we were finishing the last and the waiter introduced each one, which was great pacing.In contrast, while the grilled octopus at Bar -roque was unique, the seafood and meat platters we ordered kinda ran into each other texture and flavor wise. The seafood pan for example comes with a delicious broth for you to spoon over the fish et al, but its essentially one flavor and a stew. The meat board had a very well grilled ribeye but again, all the meats were from the oven so it wasn't interesting. Our plates were also served with long wait times in between which was cited by all my family members as a killjoy. I mention these things because if you're gunning for a sharing plates concept, people either need to be worshiping your grill skillz (for a roast/grill platter) or be wowed by the different flavors/textures to warrant sharing their plate with 5 others in a fork battle. Otherwise I would just order my own dish to my liking.I felt Fratini was a lot less pretentious though he maintained a how do you put it...semi-fine dining level of service and presentation like Bar-roque. We saw chef Fratini and his wife almost 4x during our meal, which really made us feel taken care of and this goes for other tables too. At Bar-roque we had an Aussie waiter who explained our menu well (though with a bit of sass "oh you need to order the duck 4 days in advance. Not to rub it in but the table next to yours has done that"), service was just proficient and unobtrusive; then  the pace dropped significantly after the starters.Lastly in terms of value, you get very well fed at Fratini for $70/head. I don't like to count change at restaurants but at Bar-roque I paid almost $100/head ex wine and we were "full" from alot less food because we had to wait so long between dishes. So I will definitely be returning to Fratini many times more and maybe next time, score seats inside the restaurant.

A small restaurant helmed by a husband and wife team, who are both warm and friendly without being intrusive. There is no menu, but they will ask for, and accommodate, requests if you have allergies or medical conditions once you are seated. Many types of seafood were featured during the meal, all very fresh and well-executed. The panna cotta is probably one of the best I have had locally. We had an excellent time and will definitely be back.

Fratini is a lovely place. Everyone is so incredibly friendly and helpful, they make you feel at home before you even sit down. And of course, the food is excellent. We had the tasting set, I lose count of how many dishes there were. They just kept coming. We had an incredible prawn in passion fruit, fried baby squid, veal, mackerel, roast pork, chicken and mozzarella, seafood tagliatelle... And I'm not kidding, that's just to name a few. We also had a really nice bottle of organic chianti, highly recommended. Will definitely be back!

Interesting dishes. My fav is the spaghetti that kind of look like mee-poh. Al dente and soaked up the yummy seafood broth! Dessert was really good too. Apparently they change their menu everyday so that customers can go back often, but spaghetti is always on their menu. Yay!

Spent my new years eve here. Great ambience, great music, awesome artworks, fantastic burgers is all what makes this joint so special. Price is a little bit more than burgers out there but you pay that little extra for all that extra perks.Witty burger names, delicious burgers and fresh tasting salads makes me wanna come back.

I came here on a Thursday night with a group of friends looking for some good burgers and a chill place to hang out. Potato Head Folk was that and so much more. The decor is amazing and the vibe is 1930s casual.. add in some of the best burgers ever and you have one helluva place! I had the kids burger (dizzy rascal), a bit of the  burning man, some cracka lacka corn, and house fries. The dizzy rascal was just the perfect thing for me. Tasty and not too meaty. I had a bite of the burning man and it had a real spicy kick to it. The corn.... well, it was definitely "cracka lacka" flavorful. The fries were the only that were boring... but whatever. You can't win them all. I'll definitely be coming here again though!

The best burger I have had thus far in Singapore!  Far better than a burger from Omakase in 3 major ways: 1). The bun is not soggy; 2). The beef was perfectly cooked - nice pink Medium; and 3). You could taste the bacon, as the slices were thick and smoky.  Naughty fries were also like a meal in itself.  The fries were interesting shaped - like long thin slices, and topped with chili beef and a spicy béarnaise sauce.  Awesome.   Now for what I didn't care for - the room, which looked like a tea room and not really my style.  And do not order their home made cola - it tastes nothing like cola.  But they have some beers and decent wines which go far better with the burgers so we shifted strategies.  Definitely go upstairs to the bar -1939.  Not sure if I should be breaking this into another review, but they definitely have a nice selection of booze and wines and their cocktails are solid.   The Brooklyn was spot on - not too sweet, and they did a perfectly solid version of an old fashioned with Rittenhouse 100 rye.  So far, in the uber competitive burger world in Singapore, Potato Head is my fave - far better than Omakase or db Bistro.

Finally! After so much talk about Potato Head, I've managed to pull a decent excuse off my exercise regimen to come savour the burgers here.... and fries *ahem*.My friend and I came on a Sunday evening, and the good thing is that the place was not crowded; it was easy enough to get a seat. The problem is that it is located in Keong Saik, which means parking is always a problem. Hence, you can get a seat, but most of the time you're not gonna find parking.Tried: Rambo and the Burning Man burgers. They are very delicious, although I wish they were bigger. The buns are baked from whole meal, making this a little more healthy compared to the sin I'll be ingesting.- The Rambo burger is mutton/lamb, which they managed to mask over the gamey taste with lots of spices and I believe... a blue-cheese kinda sauce? I might be wrong, but it sure tasted like it. The combination of the sauces and spices sure gave it a pretty unique taste.- The Burning Man, now we're talking. A nice slice of beef patty well grilled with mayo and ketchup, topped with Californian jalapenos to spice up the taste. It was good. However, the burning man's jalapenos has some serious zing into it, which was fine for me but not for my friend... you have been warned!- Also tried the Naughty Fries, which are basically fresh but soggy potato chips slathered with a generous dashing of cheese sauce and beef chili (the Mexican kind). It literally was one of the best cheese fries I had so far.Rants: Wish the burgers could be bigger. The sizes of these burgers remind me of what you can get from MacDonald's (no not the big mac). That's the reason why I had two burgers instead of just one. And the prices of each burger is kind of expensive ranging in the $20s, without any side dishes or fries or salads etc.. Burgers are tasty, but the pricing still leaves a bitter taste. You have been warned!Raves: The whimsical theme of the décor leaves a nice chill-out location if you're into these kind of things. Food is very tasty and makes u craving for more! Oh the top floor has a nice rooftop bar which oversees much of Keong Saik.

Anyone who rates these burgers less than 5 stars has their head firmly inserted in their ass. I've eaten burgers from Singapore to San Juan, from Stockholm to Santiago, and this is a delicious burger. I had the burning man. Extensive cocktail menu which was delicious. Only comment would be that the fries are pretty average and could certainly be improved. Other than that, shut up and eat your burger. It's 5 kinds of delicious.

on a cool night, this is a good place to have drinks on the rooftop.  my friend came during the weekend before and said it was packed, but on a tues, we were able to get a table.  we each got a calypso cocktail, which made us feel like we were on an island.  deliciously refreshing.

Okay, I get it.I've never been to Potato Head in Bali, so I guess I'm missing out. But Potato Head Folk in SG definitely has that trendiness factor that you can't ignore. Keong Saik Road address? Check. Renovated shophouse? Check. The "You're not cool enough to be here" vibe? Check.I still wouldn't wait 2 hours to get in, but if you have the opportunity/luxury to visit before peak times, I will admit that it is quite a lovely experience.I started out in the lounge ("Studio 1939"), and it's totally my kind of bar. It's one of those spots that makes you wish you could chill there all day and make it your office. The backlit bar is really cool, the decor is pleasing to the eye, and the cocktails are strong (but expensive.)Then I transferred to the second floor ("Three Buns Burgers & Cocktails") where the food was being served. It seems like the theme here is upscale pub grub and fun cocktails. I tried the Baby Huey, and it was a messy, juicy, and sweet burger. Maybe a little too sweet. Like BBQ sauce sweet + a little more sugar than normal. I enjoyed their American pop culture reference cocktail names like "Mary J Blige", "Kris Cross", and "Gin and Juice" (laid back- with my mind on my money and my money on my mind!)Not sure how long they'll be able to sustain this buzz, but it's definitely a spot you should check out if you have a chance. Their music choices are actually pretty good (mix of old school and American rap) and any selfie taken here and uploaded on Instagram/Facebook will make the rest of your friends say, "BO JIO!"

From the people who brought us Potato Head Club in Jakarta and Bali, comes the smaller, quainter "folkier" version here in Singapore. I like the multi-level venue that offers a different experience depending on the mood you're in.On the bottom, it's a casual outdoor spot where you can take away a burger or scoff it there and then. Past the charming door hosts and up the quirky stairwell painted by Melbourne artist David Bromley, you'll come to the dining area where Burgers and fun pre-mixed cocktails are the order of the day. The staff here are delightful, making recommendations and having a bit of fun with customers. I love their colourful shirts and great attitudes. The burger I tried was pretty bloody delicious, though a little soggy on the bottom by the time I got through eating it. Next time I'd skip the sauces as not only do they create the soggy bun, but they add unnecessary sweetness for this savoury lover.One level up and behind a big black door is a colonial feeling cocktail lounge. Here it's about serious cocktails, both the old school and the modern classics as well as some Potato Head creations. I settled on a Martini and loved the glassware and the delightful handkerchief-like placemat it was sat on. If downstairs is for the young at heart, this space is for proper grown ups... or those of us who like to at least pretend we are.Up one more level and there's a rooftop bar. We didn't experience this as it was a scorching day and I felt as if my face might melt off. On a cool evening, this might just be the pick of the bunch. Guess I'll just have to make another visit, right?

Love the ambiance and the quirky interior. My cocktail, truffle fries and chicken burger were on point, even if my tinder date wasn't. The darkness of the restaurant helped to mask the awkwardness. I'll be back with better company!

Was here for the September instalment of the Yelp brunch. I'd picked this place as it promised good food in an interesting location, and the decors (designed by some Australian guy with a fear of flying...) had been much hyped about.Good things first: The decor was really quite impressive. We were seated at the Three Buns restaurant (second floor) and blue floral designs decorated the walls with artfully mismatched furniture and quirky statues, lending a whimsical vibe to the area. Most guests are seated in comfy-looking couches surrounding low tables, but our group of 14 got the large communal dining table in the middle of the room. The stairwell featured checkered tiles and more interesting statues/paintings, and the bar on the third floor reminded me of a 1900s Gentleman's bar- dark woods, heavy furniture, the most amazing collection of liquor in bottles of every kind. It was amazing and one could really appreciate the planning put into the design of this place.HOWEVER, the food was just ok. Yes, this is a burger joint, but we were a bit disappointed that they didn't really have any decent alternatives for those who were craving something else. I mean, usually there would be at least 2 sides which could pass off as a decent meal on its own? But anyway, most of us tried the Baby Huey (beef patty), Honky Tonk (chicken), 4 stories (double beef patty)... The verdict was that the Honky Tonk was the best due to the excellent pairing of the buttermilk chicken fillet and tangy coleslaw. We tried the Naughty Fries (potato spuds with salsa and a hell lot of parsley) and Sticky Date pudding too. My fries were alright, luckily not as bad as the one that Natalie had. The Sticky Date pudding was good but the portion was TINY for $8.Bad things last: The service was pushy and hurried. We had a reservation from 1230-1430, and while we did take SOME time to order, there was this guy who kept on rushing us and telling us that we had to get out by 2pm... He must have said it at least 4 times in 10 minutes. (Turned out that they got the timing wrong, we left before 1430 anyway) Yes, I know that you're popular, yes, I know that you have tables to turn, but it could have been conveyed in a less authoritative tone. I'm not sure if they even apologised after we informed them that they had gotten the end-time of our reservation wrong.Would I come back? Maybe... But a return visit isn't near the top of my agenda now.

I'm updating my review since I went back a second time for food.Previous reviews are spot on. The food is way too expensive. I spent $20 for a tiny burger. It would be a different story if this was Potato Head in Bali where you're captive in one club without other food options, but there are plenty of nearby eateries where you could get better bang for your buck. And the fries? Meh. They're not even fries. The food did not impress me one bit.I still regard the decor as top-notch and the rooftop area is still one of the best al fresco dining areas in Singapore.

Burger was spot on for flavor. I typically choose a burger with cheddar, bacon and bbq sauce. The Smokin BBoy delivered on it. However, the price at $18 is pretty outrageous. Especially because the burger is only 120g. Naughty fries are pretty delicious but are 10$. So a $30 burger and chips set. The rooftop garden is really nice for conversation and atmosphere. 3* for value. 4* for taste. 4* for ambiance.
Was here with a friend and spent $70 for 2 drinks, 2 burgers and fries. The naughty fries are on the spicy side, get your ice water ready! Recommend to order Da Cheese Master burger!

Such a cute kitschy place. Love the decor. Love the rooftop tiki bar. The feel was perfect despite the heat. What's not great? The crappy drinks they call cocktails. My Siak Daiquiri tasted like detergent. At $25 a pop, I expected a decent drink. Something refreshing. It was just full of syrup, stingy with the alcohol and just a bad taste altogether. I was bummed because it's such a lovely looking place. So I gave it a chance and asked if I could change my drink because I absolutely hated this dishwater. The server refused saying it was just probably not to my liking and they couldn't help if I don't like it. They would however add more yuzu syrup to make it taste better. I appreciated that gesture but I did not appreciate her reasoning. Some people sitting next to me overheard our conversation and told me this happened to them earlier too and they were told nothing could be done. So they left most of their drinks untouched. What a pity. Everyone just writes it off as bad customer service in Singapore. But I say, it's a top down issue. If the management don't educate and empower their staff, service staff will never bother to make savvy decisions on their feet. Until then... Drink up your lousy drink!

One of the best burgers I have had in Singapore only because I haven't been able to find a half decent burger around. We had the Burning Man ($24) - the burger in itself had an overpowering taste of the Jalapeno relish. The bun was nothing special - it neither reduced or enhanced the taste. Left me needing a huge bottle of ice water to wash down the taste.Honkey Tonk ($18) - the chicken was done impeccably well. Was crisp, tender and moist. Again, the bun was just a filler. Personally, not a fan of chicken burgers but the execution of this was pretty good. Likely to go back for this one.Finished off with a Sticky Icky Wicky ($8) - was moist and was not too sweet. Coupled with the fresh cream topping, it was nice and balanced and easy on the palate. The ambience was great. The entire Duxton Hill area has a nice vibe to it and I loved the setting of the entire place. However, the service was really bad. From the girl at the counter who was in an extremely sour mood, to our server who cold shouldered us the whole night.

*Great environment, but the food, while very tasty, is expensive for small portions*Invited a group of friends to join me for a casual dinner, and we all agreed that while the food here was really tasty, warm and full of flavor, the portions were far too small to justify the big price tag.  The cheapest burger, ~$15, was the kiddy burger, and the most expensive one was the $35 truffle burger.  Most of the other burgers ranged from $20-$25.It's strange because since the burger join is so close to a few different bus stops and MRT stops, it's easy to get to, and the atmosphere is great.  Chill music, nice wallpapering and overall a nice environment to go with friends or for a casual date.I'd love to give this place a 5-star review for their tasty burgers, but the food just isn't worth the prices they charge.
Great atmosphere and staff, always a pleasure to come here. It's the place to have one more drink after a nice meal. Perfect location.

Food is just alright for all the hype that this place is getting. I would recommend the naughty fries but that's about it. Decent variety of burger. Tried baby Huey and honky tonk. Both are just alright. Service is not prompt and it's hard to get the waiters' attention. Maybe they are just busy. Roof top bar has a good vibe but considering the food/ price/ service I probably won't be back.

Went to Potato Head for cocktail week 2016 and once the staff finally pointed us to the proper bar where we could order the drinks, everything went smoothely.  The bartender made some solid cocktails and we feasted on fries in a relaxed 3rd floor atmosphere.  It is amazing how different the floor ambiances were.  I will go back for the rooftop bar scene and a tastey burger down on the bottom floor restaurant.

5 for ambiance and 3 for food. So I gave it a 4. One of the more creative and interesting places to eat, drink and just hang out. I love the feel of the place.  I read and heard the service is bad and that they almost seemed bored.. but I have been there a few times and always had very good service and they were very attentive. I like that they take a different approach to food and drink menu and what they serve. Not typical Singapore where everything is essential the same..However, the execution of the food was just ok. I had the burning man burger which was spicy (which is great) but not alot of flavour and too much bun. Had the home made soda which was not all the good, but i like they don't go traditional. . But overall a great place to hang and I will go back.

Really wish they would bring over the same menu as they have in Bali and not just burgers! Still though this place is a gorgeous venue with good vibes on weekends to entertain friends with decent variety (albeit super pricey) of drinks...just be sure to eat somewhere else first!

LOVE the ambience and drinks at Potato Head. We went on a Saturday night for drinks on the rooftop (4th floor). There are all together four floors, each has different vibes and functions.  The rooftop felt like a tiki bar with cool décor - hanging lights, wired sculptures of animals, etc. They were playing reggae music which is great for the scene. It was pretty packed when we were there (11pm-1am) but you can definitely find standing room.The drinks are AMAZING but also pricy. Cocktails average about $25. They take their cocktail making super seriously! Our favs are Calypso, Zombie, and Age of Sage. Excellent rum selections too.We didn't get any food but will definitely be back for more.

Something for everyone! Great venue with three themed floors that serve delicious burgers and drinks.  The rooftop is beautiful at night and the Studio Lounge is fun and unique. There is a wide selection of cocktails, many of which are included in happy hour specials, and although the wine selection is small, it offers great choices. We tried and loved tyhe Krabby Patty, James Brown and Rambo burgers.

Recommended.  And for once a great recommendation.  Not very hungry for lunch but I had the Baby Huey burger and couldn't stop eating until it was all gone, then I proceeded to eat all the fries.  And they aren't just ordinary fries - they have béarnaise sauce and beef chili on them.  The drinks i though were weak and not very interesting - more thought went into the description than the ingredients.  The ambience is a bit confusing, I think they were going for English fantasy garden but it just felt a little crowded and dusty.

Alas, I had heard great things about the burgers and was sorely disappointed. Their sister restaurant in Bali is much better. I ordered the sliders and they just didn't deliver for me. I left hungry bc the server wanted me to take advantage of the happy hour deals, but that wasn't enough for me. And, they were very underwhelming sliders. I walked up all the levels, and the rooftop was entirely too hot. I ate on the third level and had people just eyeing me to leave my table, which I graciously chewed and drank slower just for them. There are so many more great places to go in the city.
Really like this place,  the vibe is cool a bit loud though so not a place for a quiet dinner.  Burgers are tasty, the buns are good as well. The crack a lacka corn wow this is good!!!

If you have heard the news way back about Tong Ah Coffee House, you could have knew that the one talking over the shop space would be Potato Head Folk.Potato Head Folk creates a whimsical environment with its furnishing spanning across 4 floors in the hertitage building of Chinatown.At the first level along the passage way, you can see the workings in the kitchen and perhaps smell the good food that they are preparing. They are called the Three Buns with a space serving gourmet bugers and cocktails, also for taking aways.Stairways between the levels are all hand painted with murals and hanging with art pieces.On the third level where we dine in the lounge bar as the dining room in level 2 was fully reserved. Atmosphere is definitely better if you are in the search for vintage seating, leather couches to chill and have catch up conversations with friends over for some snacks and cocktails.If you enjoy alfresco dining, head up to their rooftop setting where you grab a good dining environment with herb around.Their artisanal buns were freshly baked by local baker daily. Even their sauces, pickles and garnishes were made by their own chef with love. Priding their food with best quality prime beef and lamb from Australia as well as UK, be rest assure to sit back and enjoy the burgers. Do not be too shy to request how you want your patty to be done, be in medium or well done. Even if you are looking for different diet like protein style, they can provide patties to be wrap in lettuce instead of the buns.Baby Huey - $18The toasted demi brioche buns was airy and light, sandwiching 120g of prime beef patty together wtih cheese, lettuce, 'Notorious T.O.M. sauce', pickles & spiced mayo. Yummy!Baby Huey - $18Fun Boy Three was classified as burger of the month. With its name after the 80's pop band, grab it when you see it as they won't be in the menu for long.Fun Boy Three -$25This rich gourmet burger features 120g aged beef patty, roasted portobello mushroom, garlic, miso butter, smoked cheese, double ketchup, truffle aioli in toasted demi brioche bun. If you were to asked me to choose 1 between the 2 burgers, I would give this more voteFun Three Boy - $25Just 2 burgers with nothing else in our orders cost us about $55 in total which we thought was hefty to our pockets. If you don't mind splurging once a while for quality burgers, these gourmet burgers are actually good. However, do remember to make a reservation before heading down to avoid disappointment

A really gorgeous interior and a fun rooftop if you can manage to survive the Singapore heat (or get lucky enough to go on a 'breezy' night).In all reality, the drinks and food are quite overpriced. I've only had their bucket of beers because it's the most decently priced item on their menu, but if you were to come here without money to blow, it's to enjoy the rooftop with good company in a really loud atmosphere. Start your night here and venture off somewhere else.

Great service, great view, great food Got the chicken burger and that wasn't too fantastic, we also ordered the angus burger was was really really nicely doneFries were great too Cocktails were sweet and slightly weak but great nevertheless for a nice drink Got a rooftop seat and the ambience deserves a thumbs up Though the climb up to the roof could be tiring for some

I came here for the September YUBE, and our organizer kindly made a table reservation for us, which the waitstaff bungled up, and told us we had to leave by 2pm, when in fact, the reservation was made specifically till 230pm. Very unprofessional - really ought to do their homework.Aside from that glitch, everything service related was great.This place is beautiful and very Instagram-worthy. We didn't go to the ground floor, but Three Buns, which is the second storey, thankfully, air-conditioned. I don't think the ground floor is fit for eating fried, greasy things, for lunch.I got a Honky Tonk burger (chikennnn), and Nik T got the Four Floors burger (moooo). We got em to slice our burgers half and half, and boy I'm glad we did so, because I was going to order a Four Floors too.Four Floors was essentially two 100gm beef patties, instead of their usual 1 x 150gm beef patty. There was nothing memorable about the burger, despite the double cheese, triple onions, "Notorious TOM" sauce, and miso mayo on brioche. They didn't ask how we wanted our burgers, which was kind of strange. Our burgers came medium rare and pink, which is how I like em, but who knows? Someone else might like well done.Honky Tonk was the better of the two burgers. Buttermilk fried chikn patty, a very delish and tart coleslaw, hot sauce, miso mayo on a sesame seed bun. Did I like it? Yes. Was it better than Four Floors? Yes, sometimes less is more. The coleslaw made its presence felt, which made the burger very refreshing, despite the fried chkn. I have noticed that that tend to slather sauces on the burger buns, making the buns very soggy. We shared a Naughty Fries (bearnaise and beef chilli on fries), and I felt that it was especially naughty, given that the potatoes they used were probably green. My first bite into a Naughty Fry made me wince because of the sour and bitter. I tried a couple of other pieces, and some pieces, on and off, had that taste. Not cool. Meh.I had a Tom Collins to drink, and WHOA! It was strong, which was good, and made me laugh a lot. I didn't like that they used paper straws. Very annoying, as halfway through my drink, my straw went soft. Nobody likes hard things that go soft.Would I come back here again? Maybe for drinks.

Da Cheese Master ($21 incl. GST and service) - 3.5 starsGood but it's not quite $21-good given that the burgers aren't big and don't come with anything on the side. The beef patty was moist and there was an option for a wholemeal bun, but I couldn't quite taste the whole wheat.Ambience - 4 starsCute, and we stayed around to chat after lunch. I'd come here with a group, not just for the food.Service - 3.5 starsI've heard bad things about the service. This time, the waiter wasn't too friendly when taking our order but as the crowd thinned he warmed up, so perhaps customers were being demanding.

Extremely hip and extremely pricey burgers and drinks in the former Tong Ah (東亞) Eating House building. Now owned by guys that started the Potato Head Beach Club, kaya toast is nowhere to be found on the menu. I found the burgers pretty good even by American standards, with the brioche bun suitably soft, the beef cooked medium-rare and paired with a sauce that tasted like siracha and Tabasco combined. I was particularly amused by the names given to the burgers like "Burning Man", "Rambo" and "James Brown". The "naughty fries" are basically an interesting rendition of chilli cheese fries. The building is located at the intersection of Keong Saik Road and Teck Lim Road. It consists of 3 floors and the rooftop bar. The kitchen on the 1st, the restaurant is on the 2nd, the lounge (Studio 1939) on the 3rd and the rooftop bar right above.Formerly a red light district, the Keong Saik area is rapidly gentrifying, the next hip 'hood. I used to occasionally stop here to enjoy a kopi and very good kaya toast at this corner, and watch the world go by. In the evenings, they used to serve pretty decent "zhi char". (Kaya toast and zhi char have moved 50m away, see other review)I was particularly impressed by the restoration, attention to detail, and lighting of conservation building's facade, highlighting the 1930s art deco motifs. The restored spiral staircase inside also makes a good photo. It is said that the owner of Tong Ah Eating House sold the building for a cool S$8 million. That explains the high cost to enjoy my burger in a restored conservation shophouse. Burgers are now where I used to enjoy a kopi and a kaya toast or two. I do miss the old days, but a good beef burger is also definitely welcomed.

We came here in a group of 11 with reservations made. The food (mostly burgers) on level 2 (Three Buns) was good but not worth the price.
