I thought I knew the Tiong Bahru neighborhood like the back of my hand after living here for a year, but obviously I am wrong - I forgot about Cheng's.  My first visit here was more than 2 years ago when I first visited the Tiong Bahru neighborhood and before the big wave of gentrification.  I remember the space looks less modern and more like any yong tofu or kopitiam in the hood.  Now it looks completely modernised to match the rest of yong siak street.  We went for dinner with friends who live closeby.  Food is home-style hainanese. We had the omlette, ginger chicken, steamed pork and broccoli.  Everything was good.  I particularly enjoyed the ginger chicken which is deep fried chicken with a sweet and sour seasoning, the chicken is juicy and sweet and I actually prefer this over the usual hainanese pork chop.  The steamed pork is just plain steam pork with a sour vinegar based sauce, very tasty as well.  They also serve home baked cakes and cookies but we were too full after the meal.  Great place for some hearty home cooking.

I've never heard about this store before but when I ate here for a first time, I fell in love with the pork cutlet with curry and steamed white rice. After that meal, I've become a regular customer ever since and actually, I've never tried anything else from this place. I'd recommend this to anyone who likes Japanese katsu curry with pork cutlet. This version of the dish floors many other Japanese diners I've eaten in.  The pork cutlet is crispy, the serving is generous and it's deliciously prepared, served separately, the curry has a bit of a kick and tastes very much 'home made'. Situated on the ground level, this place is particularly serene for lunch or brunch. The surrounding greenery in the old tiong bahru neighborhoods adds a flavour of nostalgia. I keep telling myself I should try the other dishes but i never do!

I was trying to make online reservation for dinner on 13th January but the website indicated N/A. I then called few times but transferred to auto voice machine. After few attempts finally a lady answered my call and made the reservation for us.  Went earlier than our schedule time and received a warm welcome from hostess. The food was delicious but some servers need more polishing in terms of talking to guests and body language, One server was pouring my glass with water while talking to another waiter at the other side. Some waitress are very attentive and polite while others seems to be blind when I was raising my hand to get their attention to Ask for water while my partner was coughing. Nice view and food but service needs a lift.

It was the mom in law's birthday and the missus wanted to treat her to a luxurious Sunday brunch. if you have ever tried looking for a good Sunday brunch, most of the recommendations are for hotel buffets. but if you, like the missus, are not fans of buffets because you simply do not eat enough to make it worth your while, then you will have trouble.That's when we discovered that Level33 serves Sunday roast - the wonderful English tradition of pubs serving Roast and other food on Sundays that still lingers fondly in my memory of England. Sunday brunch at Level33 had a quiet expensive bustle with mostly rich customers on the 33rd level of the marina bay financial centre. The view is quite spectacular but nothing compared to MBS or One Altitude of course. the food was decent for its price. it's handcrafted beers were ok but we had better. To be honest it was one of those places we would go once to experience it and see what the fuss is about and probably never go back again. But the girls had fun playing tourist and taking photos on the outdoor balcony. you will also get an entertaining, but not necessarily pleasant, view of scantily clad residents walking around Marina Bay Residences.
The view is spectacular of Marina Bay up here.  Only came for a drink and the view so couldn't say anything about the food. Nice atmosphere for a date.  I would come back.

amazing amazing views.  that fancy hotel with the pool on the roof really looks cool with your eyeballs and also in pictures.  also the servers were very accommodating.  we had reservations for 8 pm, showed up at 6pm, they seated us and never rushed us out.  service was attentive enough.  happy hour prices on their beers before 8pm - 300 mL and 500 mL sizes available.  beers were fine, i'm not much of a beer drinker but the happy hour prices seemed reasonable enough for singapore and also kinda a schwanky place.  it was filled with banker type looking people, a very ny looking scene but not too loud at all.  the food was actually pretty tasty, the lamb shoulder was super tender, flaked off the bone, had some really gigantic baby corns and i think shishito peppers and came with 5 sauces.  yeah it's a 100 bucks but it's a lot of food, 5 of us shared.  got two sides the leeks - which are difficult to slice and the cabbage which was many different leaves of leafy vegetable (i.e. one brussel sprout leaf) but actually super tasty and flavorful.  we also had the ploughman's board for two which had enough meat for 4 and the beef tartar.  i am told the beef tartar was good.  it reminded me too much of the walking dead so i couldn't eat it.  overall seemed like a classy place, beautiful views and they didn't rush us out.  we spent like 3.5 hours there.

4- stars for the view....minus one for the food/drinks/price.I was only here for drinks. Heard enough bad reviews about the food for me to waste any calories here. It's a microbrewery and the beers are ok. nothing mind-blowing.Snag a table outdoor in the evening, and you will wow any guest that you bring there. Of all the rooftop bars surrounding the Bay, I think this place has the best view. Come in the evening and you can watch the sunset and the changing colors across the entire city. Enjoy!

LeVel33 claims the distinction of being the highest brewery at least in Singapore if not the world. The beer is actually very good including their seasonal brews. It is definitely a sign of the increasing popularity of micro and nano-breweries popping up in Singapore. If you head here for happy hour you can find the beer of your choice for a reasonable price and get a seat outside for the spectacular views of Marina Bay, the Singapore Flyer and the ArtScience Museum. Definitely worth a visit!

There was no way we could resist a visit to a brewery 33 stories above Singapore. The views are most definitely worth the visit. Possibly even better than at MBS, because you get to see the enormous building in all its glory, as well as its surrounds. As for the place itself? The beer is expensive and extremely bland. I'd take a Tiger over the offerings here for a fraction of the price. The food is just as bad, if not worse. Super expensive pub-fare, very bland. Honestly, all of this is to be expected. This place is all about the wow factor and they are hardly the first restaurant to capitalise on the tourist trade! We enjoyed our visit as a must-stop on our list and were happy to pay for the beer as the price of entry.

The Food - We had the Vday set meal so I am not sure if all the items listed here are on the regular menu. 1. Starters: - Fresh rolls with 3 different types of butter (love butter!!!)- Scallop (my favorite) & pork belly - Foie gras (excellent & Normally, I don't like this dish but this one was good. Whatever else I write will be an understatement for foie gras lovers so I'll stop here. 2. Mains: - Overall, quite disappointing especially after the spectacular starters. I have a feeling that this place excels in its niche - starters/finger food/desserts & (of course) cocktails/beers. However, not in their mains.  - The pan fried sea bass had a fishy smell that was not musk well which really irks me. Another big downer was that the fillet had so much small-annoying-hard-to-see bones in it. Beware! It was a chore to debone it and isn't worth the effort because it wasn't even that tasty to begin with. - Beef. I ordered mine medium-well. A precarious task because as most restaurants do not do this well. It comes often comes out over cooked (well-done). Level 33 was no exception. Also, they topped the steak with a strong cheese (melted on top of it) which really overpowered the flavor of the steak. The steak sauce was great but they gave too little of it, and whilst I tried to ration my meat to sauce ratio carefully in the end the sauce ran out before the meat. 3. Desserts: - Chocolate lava cake - Good! I love who they balanced out the sweetness of the chocolate with sea salt and cream cheese at the side. - Mascarpone - Great!!! even though they got our order wrong! We were suppose to have the banana dessert (whatever that was, it was recommended by our server) but this was excellent! I am a big fan of mascarpone so I might be biased. If you like cheesey-sweet treats like me, this one is definitely for you! 4. Drinks: - Excellent. I am not a big fan of beer. In fact, I NEVER order it. However, this microbrewery has changed my opinion. All their cocktails are beer based (I believe) and they were sooo good (with the exception of the stout. I am still, and forever will be NOT A FAN OF STOUT. The bitterness puts me off.) Even the plain beer alone is good. It has a really light taste, even lighter than Heikien.- Paris - Love x2! Very sweet though. - Blond mojito - Love x3. My favorite drink. - Beer - Love- Unknown stout cocktail with berries - Cannot Love, because of my predisposition to be biased against stout!!! The bf thought it was ok though. The Service - Good. The waiter was kind enough to throw in 2 free drinks. The first because I hinted it looked good. The second because our desserts took 45min to come. - Really appreciated their effort to be efficient. - They had a pre-set the dining table with a rose & a box of chocolates so definitely good news for the guys. Half the work has already been done for you. The View- It was AWESOME. Overlooking the entire marina bay :) How singapore has grown. I feel old already! - It's a bit chilly up there so definitely bring a jacket along. Overall: Will definitely be back here again with friends to grab a cocktail & snack on some starters.

I like to come to L33 occasionally for a drink or microbrew to relax and hang out for a while. It's okay and I find it kinda fancy how they for example serve a Gin Tonic with a mini bottle of Hendricks on a small board. That plus the check surely let's you get big eyes haha. But I guess it's ok. L33 has a nice view, the service is nothing special but then again there are not many places in SG where I find service to be excellent.I like their Executive Lunch when I'm into the Lunch thing every now and then. The quality is consistent. Due to it's location at the MBFC (Marina Bay Financial Center) this is a typical ExPat and Business Folk hangout as I experienced, convenient for a quick bite and drink in between or after work.Pay it a visit and get the picture! :)Cheers-s
How much fun was this! It was a bit windy when we were up there but I loved taking the elevator up and then having a good IPA on the patio. We didn't eat--just sipped and enjoyed the view.
The ambiance is on point complimenting the great view. Very chic! Food is good but slightly overpriced for what it actually is. Service can be improved.
Went just around 7 to wait for sunset. Lovely view but with prices to match. Definitely must check it out though!

The best view in the city, better than the Marina Bay Sands, mostly because you get to see the Sands from here. The beer is solid and the waiter ensured we paired our flight with just the right appetizers. Its called beer dining on the menu and we tried it all pretty much, my favorite thing was the rillettes trio, the beef was so good, and the beers cleansed my palette so well, keeping me eating the entire $110 worth of apps. But even if you just want to stop for one beer and the view its worth it. The staff was very welcoming at every level. I wish I worked in this building. Thank you level33

5 Stars for the view, 3.5 stars for the food.  These views over Marina Bay from the outdoor patio are amazing.  Definitely worth the price of admission.I dined here with colleagues from work and had a fun time and a good meal.  The meal was not spectacular but it was tasty.  The views from atop Singapore are the reason to dine here.The wine selection is fairly good, I found several bottles of French wine that met the needs of our group nicely.  The wine list mostly consists of Australian wine which you would expect in this area of the world.I would come back again for a leisurely dinner with colleagues to take in the great views.

They have gotten some selections of beer, thought it is over priced for the view that you get - nothing outstanding in terms of selections either. Their food doesn't taste good at all - I have tried their platter, lamb, and pork and all of them were big disappointment.It's just conveniently located and thus I brought my leadership team and customer a few times, but a few visits have proven that it's not really a place to go for food. Atmosphere and the view are what you are paying the high price.

This is my favorite go to spot for a view in Singapore.  You can get a great view of the light show at the Marina Bay Sands as well as the Gardens by the Bay.  The service is top notch. the best anywhere in Singapore.  I have been to some of the high end restaurants here and this place is A+++ on staff.  Food is always fresh and well presented.  Menu changes a bit but we always go for the Steak Tartare.  Just the best here. They brew their own beer, but you can also get the usual suspects of Tiger and Heineken.  I prefer their owne brew as its always tasty.  Do make reservations as the staff will give you the best spot in the house.  I am not a regular, but I do come as much as I can!  Way better than the other high dining, drinking spots in the area.
Love this place. The beer is average but the food, service, and views are all top-notch. I especially recommend the Sunday Roast - amazing Yorkshire pud!

This resto has the best view in singapore, better than one altitude and kudeta marina bay sands. Best time to come here is sunset time around 7-7.30pm to see the sunset and changing color of the sky and buildings. 5 stars for the view, always bring visitors to visit this place to enjoy the view with snacking and beer Food is mediocre, i would rate 2.5 stars for the food, it would be excellent if they can improve their food so it will match with the best view resto and have a great food as wellBeer - i love wheat beer, they house brew beers

Being at the Marina Bay Financial Centre, you can probably guess the type of crowd that congregates here - there's lots of groups of bankers coming straight from work, which gives the place a very smart atmosphere and you'd probably feel out of place (but not unwelcome) in more casual attire. The atmosphere was buzzing, and the view is outstanding.The craft beer here isn't anything to write home about - I ordered five samplers of ale and was a bit disappointed in the lack of diversity in the flavours between the ales. They're very conservative flavours, and the ales will be enjoyable by most. Hailing from the UK, though, I might be being a bit harsh compared to the selection I enjoy there.We interacted with at least three waitresses/waiters, and the I have to say, the service was absolutely phenomenal. They must have taken recent criticism of the other yelpers into account! The wait staff did a great job of helping us order the right amount for our party size and making sure the meals came on time. The food was great, but boy do you pay for it! It's overpriced, for sure, but it is pretty decent. The view is fantastic, and Level33 is definitely a great place to bring visiting friends to get a wonderful sunset view of the bay. Will I be visiting again for dinner without guests? Not really, as the price doesn't really justify the quality of the food to me.That said - the pre-8pm $13 for 500ml is a pretty good deal, so I'd highly recommend you visit for a drink, the view, and the ambience, at least.
food was average and expensive. Nice view over Marina bay...overall a good spot to grab beer with colleagues on Friday evening, not recommended for dinner.

Mid 30's international traveler walking around town with camera gear, hungry and thirsty. Went to Level 33Took Private ElevatorReceptionist didn't acknowledge me at all. Went to the balcony myself. No table so I stood in a clear section to look at the view. First thing waiter said to me when he saw me is "No Tripod" to take photos. I ask for a menu.Menu never came. I left with my camera, my tripod and my American Express.Went to a food center in China TownPigged outWent back to the hotel. Writing a review. GREAT VIEW from the balcony tho. Make sure you dress up.Don't bring your camera gear and act all touristy. LOLIt is a fancy place, but unfortunately too fancy for me...

I'm a fan of this place for the amazing views. Definitely a cool spot to take a significant other on a romantic date or to impress clients at a business lunch/dinner.To be honest, I don't remember the food being bad at all. It's been a while since I last dined here but I thought the food was alright, the views spectacular.The service... hmmm again I don't remember how it was, but it wasn't anything horrible.Finally, the price. I don't remember b/c it was a work function, ha. This is a totally useless review. Go for the views!!!!

What a great view! You can see across Marina Bay and all the shiny lit up buildings that Singapore is famous for. I met up with a decently large group of friends here with a reservation for 2 tables outside. We tried to get moved to a smoking spot because we saw some were free, but they said it was all taken, so my friends were not able to have their cigars.The spot is very chic and modern. There's an elevator within the financial building that goes directly to the venue.We got the craft beer sampler, with 5 samples of their own beers, then got more based on what we liked. Overall, the beers were alright. I liked the blond. I did not like the stout or the mixed stout with the pale ale, which they said was one of the beers. Lots of color but not much flavor. I know Singapore has high alcohol taxes, but you think for like $20 the beer would be better than that.Anyways, a nice hangout spot, if a bit expensive. It does get a little windy up there.

A pretty awesome view, in fact one of my favorites in Singapore without requiring a cover charge. While a dinner here is pricy and I have only tried it once (was delicious). The drinks are very reasonably priced and their own craft beer and craft beer cocktails are well worth the visit. Sometimes the balcony gets rather crowded but usually you can get a table after 20-30 minute wait or can always enjoy the view and come back inside for drinks. Overall I highly recommend to visit here. In terms of food - I had the steak + shrimp combo dish and it was well prepared and presented though expensive!

We came here for dinner and it was pretty unmemorable. The food that is. The view is awesome though. I would suggest to come here for a drink or two. Grab a table outside and enjoy the sunset.Bar food is decent. The mains are very average, not worth the price. Also the layout of the restaurant section is quite bad. Diners seated towards the window or middle could be hemmed in when it is full as all the chairs are back to back when seated, leaving no space for people to pass through. Not sure if that layout has changed now.
Very nice view of the city. Nice range of in house freshly brewed beers that go well with bite plates of sliders.Good value for money lunch buffet as well.

LeVel33 is currently the World's Highest Urban Craft-brewery.  Enjoy a full food menu, craft beers, and/or crafted beer cocktails, with an amazing view of the Marina Bay and city skyline.  They also have a wine selection.  The restaurant has an awesome modern vibe, with warm wood tones.  A reservation is highly recommended to secure a spot here.  When you enter the large Financial Center building head to tower 1.  There will be a desk at the base of the elevators were you confirm your reservation and they will give you admittance to the elevator that heads straight to the restaurant.  The elevator will take you up 33 floors quickly (my ears popped). The doors open directly into the restaurant were you will be greeted by the smell of brewing beer.Their crafted brews are of European heritage and made using state-of-the-art technology by SALM & Co Gmbh. They have a 33.1 Blond Lager, 33.15 India Pale Ale, 33.3 Stout, 33.4 House Porter and 33.9 Wheat Beer, with seasonal brews on the menu.  You can see the beautiful copper kettles, and silver beer vats as you walk throughout the space.  You can order a beer paddle which gives you a 0.1 litre taster of five LeVeL33 craft brews (of your choice from the options available).  This is a perfect amount for sharing.  The seasonal Golden ale was the table favorite.  The other beers were OK.  Very 1 dimensional.  Lacked character or flavor.  Had a single flavor profile which made it pair well within their beer cocktails.  Their beer cocktails are unique and tasty.  I would highly recommend them as the way to go here for the price. The food menu highlights European classics with a twist. The food was GREAT.  Out of the sides our table favorite was the pumpkin.  The broccolini, corn, and heirloom tomato were also tasty.  The starters are also good.  The Ploughman's board was the best.  The seafood medley was OK.  I would definitely suggest the ploughman's board as the cured meats were addictively tasty.  I loved the crostini and rye bread that they came with.  Be sure to save room for the mains!Our table had a mix of different mains.  From fish, to the different options of gnocchi, to the Beef & Reef, and grilled meats.  Everything was cooked to perfection. The chevre gnocchi was OK, the original gnocchi was better.  The Beef and Reef was pricey, but good.  It is quite the show as they bring out the lobster and throw it in a pot of boiling water for a minute.  The meat cut like butter.  Amazing flavors and large portions.  You will leave full.  The prices are high. This would be a place for special occasions.  You pay for tasty food and excellent views.  Unfortunately, the beer wasn't great, but if you stick to beer cocktails or their other selection of drinks you will be OK.  With the large price tag you want to ensure you are getting something great.The service was friendly and prompt for Singapore.  .

We have the ultra lounge, Singapore has the sky bar or rooftop bar.Quintessential to the culture these bars are located on the top floors of office buildings.  They showcase incredible views of the city with both indoor and coveted outdoor seats.  Pricey mixed drinks and upscale bar food satisfy the up-and-coming youth and the well established alike.Level 33 has it all including incredible craft beer brewed on site.  The beer has a strong European influence. More classic malts and hops result in a cleaner, more restrained aroma and flavor than the in your face American style.On this visit, a very British style IPA. Extremely refreshing finishing only slightly better. Extremely clean on the palate. The stout, dark and brooding with excellent roasted grain notes and a sweet finish. Finally the wheat beer, very German in flavor. Unfiltered, beautiful citrus and banana notes, finishing sour.  Basically any of these beers could be bottled and sold as European. They're that good.All beer served in 0.3 L or 0.5 L pours.Note: prices increase on all drinks after 20:00.  Think of it as a nighttime view charge.Sadly no food sampled. I could not get my dining companion to eat the kangaroo or a dish called pig and snails.Excellent, proper service.Located in CBD, MBFC T1, 33rd floor.  Look for its separate elevator. Reservations recommended. It gets busy by 18:00.Note: despite how busy the taxi stand is,  it is incredibly difficult to hail a taxi.  Be sure to use Grab.And essential experience while visiting Singapore.

The place is located in Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower One, with its one dedicated lift. It has a specular view overlooking the Marina Bay area. It also offer interesting choices of beer, but I did not try the beer on this visit. They offer set menu during lunch time. There is a buffer starter with choices of salads, pasta, cheeses, smoked salmon. Desserts are also part of the buffet. Not great but adequate. I chose the fish and chips for main course. The fish was quite 'skinny' and somewhat tough and dry. The chips are large sized ones. Between 3 or 4 stars; decided to be on a generous side, as the ambient is quite good and the view is appealing.

My old co worker took us here.  The view alone is worth the visit. Lots of unique beers that they brew themselves.  I didn't try the food here but the view is breathtaking of Marina Bay. Definitely check it out!

I think this hits the sweet spot in terms of value for money and views of the singapore skyline. Has the worlds highest craft brewery which might sound a bit gimmicky but the beer is pretty good and if you get in before 8 its not even that expensive (~8-9 SGD). The view is staggeringly good, if you don't have a table, order a beer and head outside and enjoy the cold brew while you have the entire SP sklyline as a backdrop.

Honestly the best view of Singapore I've seen since my time living here. Yes drinks are 'pricey' --$13.33 for half liter, but with the incredible view outdoors (and my conversion of the prices to USD) it's completely worth it. My boyfriend and I came for drinks on a Friday around 6- no reservation and of course no seated table, but we managed to get a standing table right next to the viewpoint on a pleasant evening. Their beers were delicious and you can easily watch the gardens by the bay and marina bay light shows in the evening. Decided to get some appetizers to pick on while drinking- the lamb chops were relatively good, but the chicken winglets were not worth the cost. Great atmosphere- can't wait to return to try their pumpkin beer.

Views are fabulous. I went during the afternoon and sat outside. The beer price was not any more expensive than anywhere else but the view was phenomenal. I ordered the pork belly which was good but not great. I found it interesting they make the beer in full view (and full smell) behind the bar. As anyone knows who's brewed their own, that sh&t smells nasty and they kept the door to exterior open most likely for that reason. I would absolutely recommend this place for a date night or a beer aficionado. I only had the IPA which could have been a little hoppier but it was still tasty.

Been here a couple of times to unwind after work. They labelled themselves as the "world highest urban craft brewery" and man, actually the view up here is splendid! Take the inside seats facing outdoors, as it's really not that chill after all staying outdoors in this 365 summer Singapore.I chanced upon a post by a friend on the Saturday brunch buffet and decided to give it a try for my big boy's birthday. It's a minimalist brunch compared to the hotels buffet we usually come across, which I like about it as the selection is small but great individually! We made reservation through a 3rd party app, and the staff called to confirm my reservation the day before. On Saturday itself, we were held up by some errands on the morning which we called to delay our reservations twice, and the staff responded positively to our request and I'm truly thankful for that!The selection are very clear in 1 small confined area. Cold selection, hot selection, cheese, soup, desserts. That's all we've got. There's nothing international about the Saturday brunch. Cold selection includes salami, some seafood, salad. Hot selection includes foei gras, mini eggs ben, mini blue cheese quiche tartlets, roast beef, sausages, and 2 more dishes I couldn't recall. Desserts and cheeses are cluttered at one corner. Well, I'll pass the soup next time. Soup served on that day was a tomato relish sort of soup (well it's not labelled), and it tasted super salty which I stopped after 2 mouthfuls. There's also a selection of bread which you can choose to go with it. Apart from the soup, I love how all the rest are served so nicely.The highlight of the brunch is definitely their craft beers, beer cocktails, and special beer cocktails of the month! It's your a hardcore beer drinker, you can opt to top it up for the "beer buffet" version from the normal buffet price of $58++. Alternatively, you can order the beer separately. For a brewery, buffet and beer combination is definitely the way to go!One of the nays will probably go to the service. Staff do not give you much attention and you just gotta try your best to wave hard, or go up to them. My plates are not cleared promptly, neither was my water filled. I don't know if it's the privacy time which they are trying to give us, or they simply don't care. However, they are not rude la, still can make it.Finally, the view up here is a true win! We enjoyed the lovely view over brunch, which makes our Saturday slow paced and relaxed. They also live up to their name as a brewery for the tasty draft they served! It was an enjoyable weekend brunch which I'll be back again.

LeVeL33 has no cover charge like 1-Altitude and in my opinion, offers better views of MBS/Marina Bay, but does not offer 360 degree views of the city.  I personally preferred this chill spot over 1-Altitude.LeVeL33 specializes in craft beers, but I opted for a girly drink instead.  I ordered a skyline (gin, blueberry stuff, ginger beer, mint) which the bartender generously gave me for free for my birthday - he didn't even check my passport!  It was actually quite delicious and you couldn't taste the alcohol at all - perfect girly drink.Drinks here are pretty pricey at $20-30/pp for your craft beer and cocktails.  Unfortunately, I didn't try the food so I can't comment on that.Overall, I enjoyed the vibe and views of this lounge - definitely a good place for a fun and chill, but classy late evening.(They close pretty early, like midnight on the weekday)

Ticking off the rooftop bars, we headed here largely because they have their own on-premise brewery. We managed to get a table (but no seats) at the balcony, ordered some snacks, and sampled their wares. Their own brew beers are good, on a par with some of the better craft beers I've tried, and whilst a little pricey due to the location it wasn't extortionate.Our food was good, a mix of sausage, hummus, and bread, and the service was top notch, very attentive and friendly.Obviously the view is the main attraction, it's one of the better views available, but I'd definitely go back to try the full menu.

Just wow!  Take the direct elevator up.  Sunday they run a great brunch.Views from this place are unbeatable.  Good crowd and unique beer brewed on site.  Note to self:  Try the peppered  chocolate fondant....looks awesome!

Spectacular view! You can see the whole of Singapore from up here! The wine selection is amazing! The scallops were delicious! We went for a office event and the entire atmosphere was fun! The service was a bit slow but they made it up with the amazing food!

nice, chill place to hang out with a glass of wine - and have a dessert (or two). this local microbrewery is pretty top-of-its-class, with a view up on its place on the thirty-third floor (the name's a no-brainer, really), with a good selection of food and drinks, a good mix of standing and sit-down space - and it feels pretty cozy, even with the throngs of people that come here post-work.I'd like to talk about their desserts too (a proper meal here is still a pending to-do) - and in particular, this interpretation of a sticky date pudding with triangular block of cake topped with a fig compote and goat's cheese caramel. it's a subtly sweet cake that plays up to the sharp savoriness of the goat's cheese (which isn't something I usually eat, but this was properly moderated), and the soft vanilla ice cream on the side.very pretty, very modern, and a well-portioned plate of enough sweet to sate without cloying.I've also tried their fondant previously, and it's pretty good too - but I'm working my way up to the assiette, which is a two-person platter of dessert. I could really do with one right now.p.s. it's a nice view outside, but too damn hot. I'll stick with the aircon.

Here's an alternative place to view enjoy the beautiful Singapore skyline without having to push and shove against too many people. While it's best to book for the outdoor seat, you should be able to get a standing table after 9PM. Service is usually great as well!They have a variety of beer to choose from. If you can't decide, order the sampling set first. I haven't tried their food nor their cocktails, but they look decent.

Posted this in the Da Paolo Pizzabar by accident. That's a different outlet. Refer to my other review below - those items were better!Blackforest cake ($8.80) - 3.5 starsThe alcohol taste is strong but pretty flavorless - enough to give me a hint of headache for nothing. I liked the cherries, but there's too much cream and too little cake - and it's the sort of cream that's tasteless and greasy. Not many cherries inside.Tiramisu - 4 starsVegetable salad ($12) - 3.5 starsGood.Vegetable lasagna ($11.50) - 3.5 starsGood!Smoked salmon pizza ($8) - 1 starWay too salty!

The coffee and baked goods are very good. The cream crodo (I think that's what it's called?) is a cronut covered in sugar and filled with cream. It is a very good, albeit not healthy, piece. The caffe latte is also very good. The salmon and horseradish sandwich had a bit too much horseradish but it was by no means a bad sandwich. Overall, a very good place to drop in for breakfast, brunch, or a snack. Also a good place to get some work done.

I have been looking for a nice cafe to read books on the weekends, and feel like I have found a perfect spot. Gastronomic offers a wide selection of drinks, pastries, and food with plenty of comfortable seating both inside and out. I would definitely come back again!

I love this place! Reminds me of Larchmont Wine and Cheese in Los Angeles but slightly better. Great sandwiches and coffee! Highly recommend this place for a brunch or lunch! Friendly staff.. I was recommended the roast beef sandwich, got half and it's quite huge. Got a latte. Delish. Show you pics :)

Part of the Da Paolo group, this bistro is located on a quiet street in a residential area. It's more relaxing than the main holland village stretch, and quiet idyllic.I had a sandwich and a cottage pie. Everything was freshly baked on the day itself, and my sandwich came stuffed full of goodness. The bread was crisp on the outside an still warm, while the cottage pie was very hearty and tasty. Still, it wasn't anything to shout about. Like it's coffee. And I'd have to be really hard pressed to make my way all the way here just for pizzas or breads.Ambience wise, it's nothing really special. The chairs aren't too comfortable and it's got a very limited seating capacity. Definitely no good for large groups. Still it's clean and cheerful, ad the glass front lets in the afternoon sun.The large colourful meringues caught my eye but I did not get any as I was stuffed from my "snack". I'll definitely be back to try them if I'm in the neighbourhood!

I am an incredibly regular consumer of desserts at this Da Paolo. If you've never had a dessert box (in the self-serve fridge), I suggest you don't. Everything in that fridge is delicious, made of high quality ingredients, relatively good value on a $/g basis and packed in a convenient albeit non-environmentally friendly container.Despite attempts to contain my greed, my partner and I religiously eat 2 desserts every week. I like all the chocolate cake permutations, especially the giant $8 slice of chocolate & vanilla sponge. I also love the lemon tart sans the sweet frosting on top. He likes the dragon role and tiramisu (if you want to prevent addiction, DON'T touch this pick me up!).If you live in the area and need a quality dessert fix to go with your video ez DVD rental for the night, Da Paolo is it.

Best ciabatta in town, hands down. This upmarket Italian deli is very consistent and I have come to rely on them for last minute dinner party details often rushing in for some grilled veggies and cheeses. The desserts in the fridge might look modest in their little plastic tubs but don't be fooled by appearances. The hazelnut crunch cake is perfection and they do a damn fine tiramisu. Skip the cupcakes. They store them open air with the air con blowing over them so they are dry dry dry. If you get there first thing in the morning have a fresh doughnut or croissant and an espresso.

I've been coming here for years to buy the slices of pizza or pre-cooked food (that you can just take home and heat up, like the lasagnas). In a now competitive deli scene, it now stands out as being okay. But not great. There's also gelato. Which is also okay. The Da Paolo group really needs to step it up, they're no longer in the prime position they were at, at their peak!

This place is a life-saver, especially their ciabatta, marinated artichokes, and pesto sauce. I think it is also one of the cheaper places to buy Parmegiano Reggiano, although nothing in Singapore beats stuffing an entire checked bag with groceries in Rome.

This is my cheat sheet when I need to prepare dinner and I have no time or energy to muster. Located in the tranquil neighborhood of Chip Bee Gardens, Gastronomia has a decent selection of pasta sauces, antipasto, mains and pizzas that you can just grab and go. Probably won't be the meal of a lifetime and isn't exactly the most economical solution to your laziness but one has to make do with shortfalls. The salmon pizza with pesto is a great choice to accompany beers during game night. If you are have about 15 minutes to spare and put in a tad more 'effort', get some tagliatelle and arrabaitta sauce to put together in the kitchen later on. Sauces tend to have little ingredients though, so stop by the Cold Storage across the road to grab something to spice it up if you will. If it is a hot day out there, have a scoop of gelato before you make your way home - it's nice enough to put you in a better mood.

I give this place 4 stars, cos it's always there when I need it :) Croissants, donuts for breakfast, delicious sandwhiches for lunch and pre-cooked food for dinner. They have a whole fridge stacked with choclate desserts, my favorite the flourless chocolate cake and the peanut chocolate cake which is basically the same as eating 15 snickers. Staff is very friendly as well. Coffee is a bit watery so i always get the capucino or espresso.

Gastronomia is a solid location for a quiet peaceful lunch spot in the Holland Village area for a nice sandwich. I have definitely come here for a peaceful solitary lunch on more than a few occasions. My favorite is the sausages with caramelized onions on crispy ciabatta bread. Its delicious. I always get the half sandwich because the portion is huge. My mother is a fan of their chocolate cakes.

Whenever I'm asked by friends about where should they go to get good desserts, I always recommend them to go to Da Paolo Gastronomia. I have seriously liked everything that came out of their cake cooler so far and I can't decide which is the second best after the Tiramisu because they are all so darn good.

My mother and my best friend love crabs, so very often I end up eating with my mother, my best friend, and her husband at places that specialise or feature crabs.JUMBO. More recently, Happy Crab. And this actually was the meal that inspired me to bring my best friend to Happy Crab... because this place really let us down.We had high hopes because I had heard good things... so when we arrived we discovered they had a buy three get one free offer. DING. Four of us. FOUR CRABS. Done.Chilli. Pepper. Fresh steamed. And Bee hoon soup. We had all four of their preparation styles. We also had their chili marinated top shell starter that was SUPER GENEROUS in terms of portion size, and a nice, spicy starter. Only I had to eat most of it because top shell wasn't too popular with the rest of the people at the table. A single portion shared amongst 6-8 people would be ideal though. It'd really whet your appetite.The crabs. Now the bee hoon soup was... average, the fresh steamed incredibly unmemorable, the chili a bit too sweet, but the pepper was quite delicious. Not quite Eng Seng at Joo Chiat level, but good. Why was it so disappointing though?a) Temperature: some of the crab pieces were actually a little cold. It seemed like all the crabs had been pre-cooked and then they're reheated and tossed in whichever sauce you order it in. b) Freshness: the crabs didn't come across as very fresh. The flesh had that slightly mushy, waterlogged texture that comes from freezing, and it was especially noticeable in the legs where the meat was really almost unpleasant. One of the crabs we had, I think the steamed one, also had a rather unpleasant smell of... ammonia. It tasted okay, still sweet, and a little mushy, but it smelled really unpleasant.Overall, the value was okay, but when I eat crabs, it's all about freshness. I'm sticking to Happy Crab at Pahang Street.yelp.com.sg/biz/happy-cr…At least there the crabs are super fresh.

When in Singapore you MUST get crab. Well, unless you're deathly allergic, then maybe not. But for everyone else, Chili Crab is a must. I was told a story that Singapore is green because it apparently looks like a crab and a brown crab is an unhealthy crab so they decided to plant many trees to make it a green crab. It's alive!I think I missed some of the parts to that story, but nevertheless, crab is a really important part of Singapore for all tourists. It's not too hard to find places that serve Chili Crab and they're usually swarming with tourists. Crab is also super expensive but I figured it was worth the splurge as long as I could get a review out of the trip.I decided to go to Mama Kong's because it was recommended to me by a Singaporean friend. I had tried to go last year and was turned away because I didn't have a reservation. I wasn't about to make the same mistake this time and booked a reservation for 5pm -- table for one!The restaurant is small with seating both indoors and outdoors, It's a clean, sit down restaurant with a cozy vibe. Very different from the Chili Crab places about a block away. Reservations were made online and they have a rewards program, but since I don't live here I didn't sign up. I had had Chili Crab before at a tourist trap and it was awesome so I was expecting good things.The Black Pepper crab is "The Original" crab that is most recommended here. I was told it was spicy so I decided to get the classic Red Chilli (spelling it how it's spelled on the menu) instead. It's advertised as your basic Chili Crab, but Mama Kong's style. Both crabs were priced at $50 ($36.67 USD), so it didn't make a difference in terms of budget. Again, crab is always expensive in Singapore. It's probably possible to find cheaper crab, though.I was parched and got an apple juice, as well. It was $6 ($4.40 USD) and it literally tasted like apple juice, so I wouldn't say this was special by any means. It was definitely over priced but whatever, I needed something to drink and Mama Kong's didn't have a special drink that I was dying to try.The apple juice came first, followed by the Chili Crab shortly after. The crab was huge and I also ordered Fried Mantou for $3 ($2.20 USD) which is commonly served with Chili Crab. The Fried Mantou were so good! They were a bit heavy for me so I didn't eat all of them, but while they may have been unhealthy, they were also very delicious. I dipped the bread into the Chili sauce and enjoyed.The crab came pre-cracked. They have a de-shelling service but I didn't need it. I made piles of crab meat on the small plate they provided. I then put the meat onto the big spoon and scooped some Chili Sauce. The crab meat was juicy and there was a decent amount. The Chili sauce was sweet with a strong kick. I don't like spice so it was borderline too much for me, but I was pretty happy overall. It didn't go too well with the apple juice, though. Next time, I'll opt for a water.The restaurant was pretty empty while I was there but it's probably because I got there so early. The waiters asked to take a photo of me and gave me a copy with my check. The service was good and every one was super nice.I think Mama Kong's is a great place to go if you're looking for Chili Crab and you want a nice, cozy ambience. However, the actual quality of the crab was similar to that of the crab I've had a tourist traps and the crab overall was a bit too pricey for what it was. Plus, the $6 apple juice really threw me off.TOTAL COST: $70.05 ($51.38 USD)34 Mosque StSingaporeThis review is copy and pasted from my blog of solo travels and solo reviews.

What to do in Singapore if not eating their famous chili crab? We tried to find a place that is far from the limelights but still do good chili crab, and the answer was right there in our own neighborhood ( we stayed in Chinatown ). Momma Kong's was just a few walks away from our hotel and it looked pretty decent joint, a small-ish one but with good reviews, so we went in. We didn't take the package (you should if you're a big eater, we found out later that the package for two people is really good deal), but we ordered one crab each, the black pepper and the chili one and a set of steamed mantou to wipe all those delicious crab broth away.The crabs were super delicious and we were super happy. I had problems with cracking the claws but the staff spotted it right away and helped with it. My boyfriend who never had such large crab experience before also dove right in without any problem. My chili crab was perfect with the perfect amount of burn and the black pepper was super delicious. The bill came at around 75 dollars or so, so it was almost the same price with the package ( I believe the package is without drinks, and alcohol is quite pricey in Singapore) and we had beers, so if you think you can eat a lot, go for the package.I would definitely go back to this place if I had time next time. I am still thinking about the chili crab these days....and do book a table online, they can be a bit busy!

As today marks my one year anniversary of living in the little red dot I will review my favorite place to eat one of Singapore's signature dishes: Crab!I've tried Jumbo, No Signboard & Longbeach but this is the place I take all my visiting friends to eat crab. Momma Kong's might not have the "authentic" feel of No Signboard in Geylang or the history of Longbeach but their service is great, the staff is super friendly so it means that I don't have to deal with the grumpy, non-English speaking, "I don't wanna serve filipino helpers" auntie to enjoy my crab fix.The crab dishes are on par or even better than the previously mentioned restaurants and I love their mantou, they must have the prettiest and fluffiest mantou of all.Except for the chili crab, I've tried also tried the crab beehoon & pepper crab which are all good but my favorite is the steamed crab: this fantastic dish displays the freshness and glory of crab in all it's simplicity. Yes, simplicity is the ultimate form of sophistication!Highly recommended!**Additional bonus points are granted for the fact that they offer to de-shell your crab (for 15$ a pop) so little bananas like me don't need to get their fingers dirty.

I wanted to try chilli crab during my visit to Singapore, it being the national dish of the country and all. I wasn't really sure where to go. Lonely Planet actually recommended this place and it wasn't too far from where I was staying in Chinatown. This restaurant also has a new modern look to it, compared to some of the other places on the same street. And the staff is really young. I was seated outside (which was disappointing cuz it's hot outside and there are mosquitos!), but I didn't have a reservation and they recommend that you do that in advance. They offer a lot on the menu - not just crab, but stingray and other plates as well. I ordered the chilli crab cuz that's what I came for. I added on the steamed mantou too, since everybody recommended getting that to dip into the chilli sauce. The crab was delicious! Some of the tastiest crab I've ever had. And the sauce was really good. It was spicy and had a nice kick to it, but it wasn't overly spicy. Really good flavor. They provide you with a crab cracker tool, a little bucket, a little silver stick to help you scoop out more meat, and a moist towelette. All the things you could possibly need. More towelettes and napkins would've been nice though (I had to dig into my own supply; bring your own moist towelettes/wet tissues with you if you can! Eating chilli crab is messy!). They also charged for the moist towelette. And they charged me for the little fish side dish they gave me, which I hardly touched. Overall, delicious chilli crab! Yum!

A charming place specializing in Sri Lankan crabs. The price was very reasonable- $48 for one crab with a variety of cooking methods. They even offer deshelling service at $15 per crab! Haha. The cereal crayfish almost stole the limelight from the crabs. In contrast, the stir fried kai lan was disappointing so maybe skip that. The crab soup with bee hoon absorbed the essence of the ingredients. Highly recommended dish! At the end of the meal, the staff even took a photo for us and gave us an instant Polaroid photo!

Momma Kongs serves delicious chili crab for people who prefer to avoid giants to the likes of Jumbo seafood. Food quality is good, and setting very clean. They also take reservations and come around to take a photo for every table--including a complimentary  printout on your way out (a nice touch) Prices here are not cheap, yet I felt there were areas I was under served. For example, MK does not offer bibs for guests, a crucial element as we are expected to peel our own crabs. For you to get it peeled, MK charges $15 extra per crab.

I enjoy a good dining experience and who I can only presume was the owner or manager of Moma Kongs delivered this, he had a really people personality too him when taking our order, ensuring he got photos of all the diners for his patrons for his ever growing marque, etc.Staying in China town and wanting to enjoy chili crab a simple still away this seemed out best choice, best of all they took booking which made it the top of my list.We had the three crab offering a big task for two people, we chose the chili and black pepper and were recommended the butter to even out the flavors; best of all for us tourists they offered de-shelling service at a small(ish) extra so I could concentrate on eating an enjoying (sorry to any purists out there)It went without saying that I found all the crabs enjoyable though I do not profess to be an expert at these things... The drinks menu was sufficiently stocked for a cantina style restaurant.As you can tell I would recommend. This to other tourists like myself who want a simple and approachable way to enjoy one of Singapore's most famous dishes!

The chili crab was amazing as were the side breads. The sides were fresh and spicy. And the whole thing was about $50-60 a person total. A great deal for this quality seafood. It's a small restaurant not great for large groups but I'd definitely recommended over more expensive places like jumbo for small groups of 2-4 people. We went twice in the week we were there

Two little wolves went into Momma Kong's for date night and had a thrillingly messy time.  Huff: Most of the time, it can be challenging for a duo, however dynamic, to take on two Sri Lankan crabs, but at Momma Kong's, the crabs are around 600 grams, so it can be done!Puff: While the crabs are good, none of them are the best versions of each that you'll ever have, but the bee hoon and the butter are among my favorites at Momma Kong's.Huff: The Ikan Bilis starter is nice too, tends to be spicy, so order mild if you can't take the heat!Puff: Can't go wrong with the garlic prawns either!  Tender and flavorful!And I'll blow your house down!  The most magnificent thing at Momma Kong's is the fried buns...golden brown, gratuitously crispy and simply perfect for soaking up every drop of butter or chili sauce!  Truly the best fried buns this little wolf has ever had, and I've had my share! PARTING THOUGHT: bring a trio and order the special: 3 crabs (any style) for $118

I would say: it's crap.The only reason we stopped here was to have a quick drink and perhaps a quick snack. We opted for the fried chicken chunks and fried calamari, not such an adventurous choice I admit. The tonic water I ordered came garnished with a nice stick of cucumber (as often seen in Gin and Tonic). I nibbled on that one first only vaguely registering something odd. The I began to sip the drink and I realised it actually was a Gin and Tonic, even though I can still hear the waiter say: 'one tonic water'. Quickly fixed. No hassle later with the check. The crispy chicken chunks weren't very crispy nor very chunky. They were actually not nice at all!When we ordered I thought the calamari wouldn't be nice but it turned out those actually were nice. More like thin and crispy  tempura than a thick layer of tasteless batter. I realise this place specialised in crab (which I haven't tasted here), but I was not very pleased with their other offerings.

Crab Crab CrabWe booked in here ahead of time after searching the internet and finding out you could pay extra to have the crab de-shelled.  BONUS!!  I hate de-shelling.We arrived early for our booking, but they happily seated us.  Not long after, the restaurant was full.Undecided, we opted for 3 crabs (between 2 of us).  Red Chilli Crab, Black Pepper Crab and Butter Crab. With a side of greeen vegies.  The waiter recommended we also get the steamed and fried buns.  As the meals arrived, we were able to sit back and eat the crab without having to de-shell. Dipping the buns in the sauce to get a hit of flavour.I think we did well to clear most of the crab.  De-shelliing is $10 extra per crab (Oct-2014) but well worth it in my opinion.I would come back here on my next visit.

One of many live music spots in Clarke Quay, The Pump Room differentiates a little with having a couple of their own brews. I enjoyed the Golden Ale and the IPA plus there's a buy-one-get-one-free happy hour special. Otherwise drinks can be expensive especially if you're not drinking alcohol. Bottled water for example is $12. Drink the beer. It's cheaper and they're pretty legit brews. We sat outside on a cool night so didn't really listen to the live bad but the bits I heard was decent. Overall a decent watering hole for happy hour. And from Sunday-Thursday, happy hour goes through 10pm.

This place screams of a tourist trap, but since we were both tired of walking and we wanted to enjoy the picturesque Clarke Quay in Singapore, so we settled for a beer. This place boasts its own brewery, although like pretty much everywhere in Southeast Asia, beer (especially craft beer) isn't their strongest point. The price level reflects their tourist trap, or that because it's generally expensive to drink alcohol in this state-city. Not really worth a visit, unless you're here for the view, or for other touristic reasons.

I actually really wanted to like the bar, I really did, and the reason that I give it three stars is because I want to give credit where credit is due. First of all awesome music and awesome atmosphere. Secondly it is a microbrew and the beer that I had was nothing short of delicious (if you can use that word to describe a beer). However, the reason that it is not getting anymore than a three was become of the over zealous waiter. He was terrible. First of all I had no choice so to where I wanted to sit, and secondly he did not understand the concept of 'I only want one beer' - but it was happy hour, two for the price of one - yes, but I only want one beer. However, great beer, and I would give it another go, but watch out for the zealous staff (or go with somebody who will drink that other beer).

Unfortunately, I find this place a little bit too expensive for what it is. The food isn't anything to shout about, yet you can expect to pay SGD 25 and above for a main course. The drinks are expensive as well, and if you're looking to let loose and have a couple more drinks than usual, it's going to cost you here. I am not a big fan of the whole concept of transitioning from bar/restaurant to hopping club with live music as the night progresses. I certainly wasn't expecting that, and it started getting a bit too rowdy and crowded for my liking and we had to leave for a place that'd be more conducive for conversation.
$55 for three glasses of a beer they made?!!?!?!?! It's not like it was imported from Belgium or anything. An awesome live band with a transvestite front-person was the saving grace.

Lots of beers to choose from, which is great. I think they brew their own as well, which I will have to try sometime. Anyway, GREAT MUSIC....the new band is very lively and a lot of people were dancing...like, the dance floor was packed. Super easy to get to as well...we drove and parked in the parking garage nearby, but the MRT lets out very close by as well. If you're looking for a place to party with good, cold beer and a solid band, I think this is among the best in Clark Quay.

Impressed with this place! They have buffet lunch and a la carte dinner, and buffet dinner on holidays. Live music starts at 8 pm every night.The Papdi Chaat (indian taco) was sooo delicious and my favorite with flavours of mint, yogurt, and tamarind.We got the Tandoori Milawat that has a few pieces of 4 kinds of tandoori grills - chicken tikka, fish tikka, prawn, and kebab. It was great to try different kinds.The Aloo Gobi (cauliflower and potatoes) was kind of mushy and could've tasted better.The Chicken Makhanwala (butter chicken) was perfect with the naan bread.If you like bread, the bread basket was perfect! Plain and garlic naan, roomali roti (thin chappati-yum!), and tandoori parantha (also yum!)We tried the Jal Jeera to drink and it was very different and not something I would recommend. Can't go wrong with the Mango Lassi though.Unfortunately we were disappointed with the service. It could've been much better for the price we pay. Servers didn't clear our table or refill our waters. Most were chatting and standing around.We went for dinner this time but would love to try the lunch buffet next time.

I had a splendid time at Shahi Maharani. In my context I feel that this place is lush and posh.I had Chicken Makhanwala, Palak Paneer and Bengali Fish Curry with my Garlic and Butter naan. They are flavorful and delicious. I would prolly order 1 gravy dish in future. I had so much gravy that added complexity to the naan. LOL!As I was sitting at my table, I noticed a lot of hot plate being served out. And I was intrigued by the smell and flavour that I had to just ask the service crew what it was. Tandoori Paneer, the crew explained to me it's cottage cheese and peppers laced with a creamy marinade. The service was excellent n warming.
It is known as one of the best restaurants in Singapore and definitely lives up to the reputation. The service is great and the food is even better. Try the kulfi sampler for sure!

Shahi MaharaniStaff seated us but did not bring menus until we asked. Failed! They are losing a star for lack of service.Salt lassi - goodLong cracker - good but a tad saltishAppetiser - Pakora - vegetable (it is actually white onions within)Garlic nann & plain nann & cherry naan (sweetish & surprisingly nice)Tikki masala chicken - Nice; a wet fish food for those who don't like their food too dryOkra - nice and crunchy with onionsGrilled prawns - sliced open and easy to cut - tastes good tooTandoori chicken - quite nice and tender Somehow the food was better when catered by a Friend. Probably it is because she knows what to order.Music was too loud and 2 of us ended up having headaches. At one point the mike went berserk. I would rather they do without the Indian music and singing.

Our main course was the chicken tikki masala. Although a bit heavy on the onion, the tandoori chicken was tender and flavorful. The sauce was a scintillating collection of spices that excite the tongue. It worked well atop the sesame naan and vegetable stuffed naan. Note that each table also gets a crispy spiced wafer basket to start, which includes some tasty mint/pickle paste. The service was pretty good. There are several roaming staff members who fulfill different roles and work together to cover the tables. The ambiance in the dining room is most pleasant. It is quiet and decorated with an intricate gold/brown Indian theme. After 8pm, there was a small group playing live ambient music composed of subtle drumming, wind instruments, and light vocals. The flavors were great and the environment was soothing. While the prices are on the high side, this remains a good place for a wonderful Indian meal.

This place offers a very good value for money weekday buffet promotion where 2 people can eat for ~S$35. Food is good and ambience is pleasant.Food is good overall but nothing extra ordinary with a standard north indian restaurant menu. Prices are a bit on the high side for the location but still affordable.

Serious contender for the number 1 spot for Nasi Lemak. Every single dish is awesome. Chicken wings are mega awesome, simple, clean fried deep but doesn't feel yucky oily. This is one of the few places you feel clean after eating. I would say this is the elevated, a little more premium kind of nasi lemak. Its even suitable for a weekend family dinner if you get what I mean. Again, 5 stars for the good food, clean environment, and just a wonderful place to eat Nasi Lemak at. Detailed review:Rice - fluffy and grainy. Not soggy and meshed up at all. Very good. Cross cut cucumbers - thank you for the love. Chilli - above average but does not mix too well with the rice at times.Chicken wings - awesome! Dry and very crunchy on the outside. Juicy and succulent on the inside. Just how I like it. Sides - all good and what it should be. (Nghoh hiong and heh Joh is a little disappointing though.) Lon Tong is a absolute delight especially when mixed in with the chili. Queue - 10-15 mins. Saturday night still able to get seats.There's a sink for you to wash your hands after eating those wings. Must be the cleanest coffee shop in Singapore and sets an example! This has to be mentioned!

This spot is unassuming as they come. It's cafeteria style food, right...and then you take a bite of the coconut milk-infused rice...and then it's basically game over from there. You dab at the chili sauce, to find that the flavors mingle perfectly with the rice- so you mix the rest of your chili into the rest of your mound of rice. Then you bite into the crispy fried chicken. What a texture contrast to complement the creamy heat you've just concocted before. Juicy and crispy- matched with creamy heat- wow. Two crispy fried tofu rolls stuffed with water chestnuts and a bit of ground pork and wood ear mushrooms completes this wallop of a meal to my taste buds. I finish off the meal with a cold barley drink- not very sweet, just enough to help cool of the residual heat from the chili. I'm down for the count.  And fat. And happy.  Oh, and this was my second meal after an already solid meal across the street at Heng Long. Simplicity and excellence in food can be so beautifully tasty....

My 1000th review is dedicated to my favourite nasi lemak place in Singapore!The perfect combo for me is: rice, fried chicken wing, luncheon meat (Spam), fried egg, ikan bilis, string bean, eggplant, and yes to chilli. Total damage is $7.30 + more fat for my muffin top. I regret nothing every time.If it's your first time, definitely choose the fried chicken as it never disappoints. Always juicy, with the crispiest skin that is the most beautiful shade of golden brown I've ever seen.Don't let the queue deter you. Also, pay attention once you are the 4th or 5th person in the queue, as that's when they begin taking your order- and they are rapid fire quick.Add in a lime juice from the nearby drink stall to complete the meal. You're welcome.

I can seriously imagine Daym Drops coming to Ponggol Nasi Lemak, ordering some of that seriously fine Fried Chicken for "take away" and heading back to his car where he does of one of his well-known YouTube videos showing off his initial reaction after the first bite! Yep, my reaction was the same reaction he had when he took that very first bite out of a Five Guys Burger. The fried chicken at this Nasi Lemak is literally just to die for (cholesterol anyone?). The skin is crispy, and the meat has that great oily finish. The coconut rice is super fragrant and the side offerings are top-notch. In terms of the side offerings, go for the green beans and egg. Aside from the Chicken, my favorite is the serving of Sambal that the auntie puts on once the dish is served. I'm not sure, if the Sambal here is specially made or comes from the regular supermarket, but I find it very tasty, but not overly powering spicy like other sambals I've tried. The mix of fried chicken, coconut rice and a tinge of Sambal is just heavenly.Lines are long, a lot longer than I'd like, but as any Singaporean / local would know: a stall with a long line, is usually a stall that is very good. Punggol Nasi Lemak is no exception to the rule!

Finally! I had the foresight to arrive 15 minutes before opening (5:15) and man was that a smart move. 5:30 and the queue was already wrapped around the corner. I went with another yelpers recommendation and got the luncheon meat and the chicken thigh. I also added lady fingers and French beans to counterbalance the fry fest. Everything was so good. The chicken was  cooked perfectly so that with every bite you could hear this delicious crunch. I might have to double up next time. The sambal was a little tame but kicked up the flavor level with a mild spice and slight sweetness that mixed pleasantly with the coconut rice. I can't wait to go back and try everything they have to offer. Yummmm
I like going to this place for a quick dinner. There is always a line up, but it goes pretty fast. The rice and chicken wing are so good!

There is always long queue everytime I visit this place, large variety of food but price might be on the high side despite its nice display. Ordered some ikan bilis , otah , fish fillet and chicken to go along with the rice , price has risen a lot from a mere 6$ to 8$-9$. I think the price has increased tremendously from the past and food quality has really dropped. Apart from that i would not want to queue for such a long time for that kind of quality and price. The green rice was average (used to be better), not really the grainy type that i like to eat. Chicken wings was pretty normal as well, nothing fantastic about it.The queue can sometimes reach the main road and that is madness. Overall i would not waste time queuing for expensive and low quality food. Maybe if they improved on their food quality will i go back to patronize them again.

The nasi lemak here is pretty good albeit  a little on the pricey side. The rice has that nice fragrant coconut flavour and the sambal is sweet and not overpowering. The chicken wings are crispy on the outside, tender and moist on the inside. The otahs are flavourful and really good. The only problem is that the servings sit a little toward the small side. I'm not sure if one serving is enough to fill you up if you're rather hungry. Nevertheless, its good food!

I must say, being raised in the US, I didn't even know what Nasi Lemak was until I moved to Singapore for work.  And I didn't like it one bit until I tried this place (fortunately, I live few blocks away) and ever since I came here, I have been a big fan.  Is it really that good?  You should see a long-ass line every night and there are at least 20-30 people waiting to get the best Nasi Lemak I have ever had.  Highly recommend!

The line that forms from 6pm till the early hours of the morning are testament to the quality of the nasi lemak here.  Perhaps because the two vital parts of the nasi lemak - the chilli and the ikan billis here are done differently from elsewhere and are just so darn addictive. On top of them serving excellent nasi lemak in the traditional sense, they also offer a range of other dishes that you can choose from (very much like a mixed rice store in a way where you pick the dishes that you want to accompany the fragrant coconut rice) - from deep fried chicken wings to fish cake, fish, squid, eggplant, eggs, and a wide variety of other vegetables.  With the wide variety of dishes, it'll be hard pressed to find someone who isn't able to have an enjoyable meal here. The portions are however tiny,and their nasi lemak is pretty pricey! Very clean for a road side / hawker store though, even the toilets are kept clean - I was pretty impressed.

Having been a fan of the original Punggol Nasi lemak for years, I can say that while this one isn't bad, it does still somehow disappoint. The rice, for starters, isn't as fragrant, and sometimes is a bit greasy. The rice portion also seems smaller.The chicken wing here is still good, and so are the other vegetable or rice dishes. But I feel less satisfied with the overall experience as it just doesn't seem like good value to pay so much for a meal that isn't that filling.Parking around here is a right pain in the proverbial... I'd come here later at night rather than around dinner time. The traffic here also does get pretty congested during the peak hours in the evening. I've witnessed accidents on this stretch 3 times already, no kidding.The place is clean and brightly lit, but I do prefer the food from the original stall. Can't really put my finger on what's wrong exactly, but the everything just feels that little bit off kilter.

While there are 2 branches you can choose to go to satisfy your nasi lemak cravings, I prefer the one at Tanjong Katong, simply because its bright, relatively new and clean!  To me, it has the best chinese style nasi lemak with the home-made otah and awesome chilli sauce creating the perfect blend. Add in a fried chicken wing, some long beans, a fried sunny side up egg and some ikan bilis and you have the perfect meal for you. ]However, parking is a nightmare around the area since it draws a huge crowd all the time. You can either park at the public carpark across the road (the entrance is next to the petrol kiosk opposite) or park along on either side of the road since it has no markings.

I love Chinese style nasi lemak, and I suspect many others too, after that immensely popular Holland Village drama on Channel 8. This place is bright and airy, and incredibly crowded. The queues are ridiculously long, so much so that there are lines to mark out the direction for queueing. Parking is terrible, as the Tanjong Katong stretch is jam packed with eateries. I do find this place incredibly expensive though; a takeaway box can cost up to as much as $6 depending on the sort of ingredients one chooses. Yes, the rice is fragrant, chili has enough kick, chicken wing crispy but still, is a bit too steep for frequent stopovers. Heck, the place isn't even air-conditioned!

Nasi Lemak is one of the staples of Singaporean food and that's probably why its so popular. It's pretty common to see a long queue forming up during the evening and especially later at night, when most of us head out for supper. This branch located in the east, has a fairly decent amount of seating though parking can be a hassle as most of the time, you'll find cars either parked there or the nearby carparks full, which means a longer waiting time. What I usually do is to go there, queue up, order take away and proceed to somewhere else to indulge myself with the deliciously fragrant nasi lemak.

The first Ippudo bar in the world (or so Google tells me), from one of the most popular ramen chains in Asia. While that pedigree sounds good, it's food was acceptable at best.I'll just comment on items of note since most of the items were nothing to write home about. I ordered the summer special duck tsukemen - I thought the lime they provided really gave it a nice refreshing touch. However, they also served the ramen with 3 greasy pieces of grilled leek (unsure why they needed that much oil) and smoked duck (was hoping for seared duck). The ramen was enormous though, so if you're carb loading, it's perfect!I really liked the spicy potato salad which was surprisingly awesome with the slightly spicy meat sauce. The fried eggplant sandwich with meat sauce was also pretty decent.There was no line on a Sunday evening but I'm not sure how crowded they get. There's a small selection of sake and the usual ramen suspects. I might only return for the potato salad but I can make that myself so... Would I really do that?

There was bar area next the main dining area. As the outlet was currently having a $9.90++ promotion for its Extra Rich Tonkotsu Ramen to celebrate its 7th anniversary in Singapore, the place was packed. The turnover was fast and I got a table almost immediately. Ice water was free here. Extra Rich Tonkotsu Ramen ($9.90++)Served with chopped spring onions and 2 slices of cha shu. The cha shu was rather thin and the texture still have not reached the melt in the mouth stage and had a bit of porky taste. The soup seem to have watered down to suit the local's tastebud. The ramen was done just nice to my liking.Crispy Corn ($6++)Lightly-battered deep-fried corn-on-the-cob, sprinkled with smoked paprika powder for a burst of different flavours.It looked coated in a rather plain batter, but it tasted addicitive with a Maggie like flavours, filling the mouth with umami taste. Can't help having one after one although the corns tend to stick between the teeth.Chashu Tsukune Bun ($4++)Juicy minced pork patty accompined with crisp lettuce and mayo in freshly steamed bun.It was served pipping hot. Could not taste the mayo in it, but the patty was surprisingly good, even when it was minced very finely. The texture was buttery, melt in the mouth. I wish I could eat another piece.Overall the food was not bad. Service was fast.

I was inclined to giving this Ippudo at Shaw a 4 stars but on my way out the chefs/staffs in the kitchen simply raised my rating to a 5 :D haha!! How? They said thank you in Japanese and I smiled and nodded at them. I suddenly realized they did not just say it like many places do while those staffs were working away not even looking at the customers. I do not need a robot or robots saying "Arigato gozaimasu". Maybe these staffs really said thank you for the sake of saying but they must be darn good actors. And one of them is quite cute I must say, haha.So my experience at Ippudo at Shaw...I love Ippudo located in Ginza, Tokyo very much. The staffs were nice and the ramen was excellent. The gyoza was perfect. At Ippudo in Ginza, those complimentary little snacks/appetizers were placed on the table. Here, the staff gave them in a container divided by two compartments to customer. I have no complaints about that, I do not eat them. They were too spicy for me. I am sorry but I have to compare this location to the one located at Ginza. I do like the ambience here at this Ippudo but I love the one at Ginza even more. It was a lot more cozy there. I ordered the small sized Shiromaru ($12) on the lunch set and added the Tamago egg (+$3). I asked the staff if the Shiromaru came with chashu (pork slice) cos if not I would add the extra chashu (+$5). She said the bowl of ramen came with two slices of chashu. I like ok, two would be good for me so I did not add extra meat.When my ramen came, I only saw one slice of meat :( Thank goodness it was a good size of meat. The thing about me is I can't have no meat so I will not be reviewing any salad place for that reason. The gyoza were good, slightly edged out those at Santouka.I am pretty sure I would be coming back to Ippudo in Singapore very soon. Glad I got a chance to try out Ippudo here and finally crossed out one of the "a place must visit" on my list.

Had ramen at their Mandarin Gallery outlet once and wasn't impressed.Though I'd try it one more time at their Shaw Centre outlet.Given fried garlic, sesame seeds and Chilli flakes to add to taste.Bonito Tonkotsu (ramen) medium texture - 2 strips of thinly sliced 3-layered pork, some crunchy bamboo shoots and thin noodles. Can choose texture of noodles - soft, medium or hard. Soup was a bit rich but at least it was piping hot.Side orders: egg and satsuma age (fish cake) - comes in a soup. Soup was not hot!Fish cake was soft which is not to my liking.Iced green tea - not free.Verdict: No big deal.

We usually visit the one in mandarin gallery but decided to try out the one in shaw because we were in the areaThe "feel" is quite similar to that in New York, in the sense that there's an actual bar adjacent to the dining area, something the one in mandarin gallery doesn't have. The menu is slightly limited in ramen choice, and it didn't have my favorite Karakanen ramen. It, however, boasted more creative appetizers such as the soft shell crab and beef tartar, which was amazing. Did not particularly like their spin on the tonkasu ramen with the "Singapore" flavors because it tasted like black pepper crab sauce. I wanted japfood! Other than that, it was really good. Quite pleased with the appetizers!

Okay, I have to admit I've never tried the original Ippudo in Japan, but was mighty impressed with the one in KL, perhaps it was the very favourable exchange rate at that time. Have to say, food wise, here in Shaw Centre, the ramen (I had the one that was exclusively available at this branch only, each branch has its own exclusive ramen) was good, but not the crazy good that I would queue 1 hour for (and I've actually done that before). Just good. No extra stars for this part. But the service, oh boy the service, TOP notch! My bad I didn't get the waiter's name. It's probably the best service I've gotten since returning from the States. At one point, I even caught myself wondering if this guy was working extra hard for his tip. He anticipated our next moves with ease, upsold me an extra portion of ramen (kaedama? Good value for only $1), convinced my son to try a dessert. This guy was smooth, all whilst making us feel comfortable and well looked after. He alone has garnered this pace the 4th star. So, I will come back again, only as long as my unidentified waiter is still there. If he's gone, I'm gone. On wandering with my quest for the perfect ramen in Singapore.

Ippudo is definitely  my favorite ramen in the world.The broth is delicious and flavorful and the noodles are so thin and really good. The service is fantastic and the ambiance it great. I really like Ippudo and I hope they keep doing what there doing!

Actually Ramen at Ippudo is pretty good.  Been to the Mandarin outlet twice and got to say the turn off the level of noise.  Got to say the shaw outlet is far better apart from the family with usually noisy kids :).  Staff here are extremely motivated and works well for customers.  The gyoza here are really good.  Not oily and skin is thin.  All in all a good experience.
