However, I am very shocked that this happened to us because my family has had other Indian food at hawker centres/ food court/ kopitiams before and we were ok (being Singaporeans, we do consume a fair portion of Indian food so I am not sure why this happened). Anyways, this spice intolerance did put a damper on my overall experience. Definitely do beware, definitely not for weak to normal stomachs. For the taste, I think we can definitely find a better place without incurring the unsavory consequences of the aftermath...

Always consistent, satisfying Indian tandoor and moreIt's one of the longest-serving Indian restaurants (I understand that the owners of this particular hotel are Indian) since 1985, and you can bet they know what they are doing. The tandoor items come out succulent and singed to perfection, with the marinade well penetrated into the meat/vegetable. The lobster is a bit pricey, but go for anything else including chicken, mushrooms or prawn, and you'll be just as satisfied. The chefs work in a glass-fronted open kitchen, so you can see your dishes being prepared. A Sunday buffet is perenially popular, and helps ease first-timers into the various dishes available. The well-dressed waiters are mainly male, and pretty charming/chatty as they work - a mark of confidence. The setting includes a fountain in the middle of the seating area and lovely detailing of an Indian palace. There are plenty of choices of booth seats but we recommend the 2 tables in front of the tandoor kitchen - truly fascinating to watch the chefs at work.

Tandoor has awesome decor and a great ambiance. However we felt a little bit hustled by the waiter. The food here is very expensive and does not seem commensurate with the quality that high-priced food comes with. The jaljeera was worth the s$10 we paid for it.
Matcha green tea really does taste premium, tastes great after a meal. Second time getting dessert here after trying it yesterday, i wish we had something like this in the states.

I'm totally addicted to Nana's. My faves are the matcha latte, hojicha latte, matcha soft serve, and matcha anmitsu.  The matcha dishes have always have an intense rich matcha flavor which I love, and their desserts aren't too sweet. Minus one star bc service can be spotty, depends on who you get. There are a couple of super nice waiters but some kinda have an attitude.

Arrived at about 6+pm on a weekday and was surprised to see it fairly empty. The friendly servers showed me to a table.I ordered a July's special of black sesame iced latte with mochi, a scoop of azuki (mashed Japanese red bean) and whipped cream, while waiting for my friends to arrive. The latte had the lovely and subtle flavour of black sesame (it's good for hair!), the mochi was chewy and the azuki was just right. The whipped cream seemed out of place though. I would order the drink again.Subsequently I ordered a Hamburg rice set. The vegetables were enough to satisfy my fiber intake for dinner - 2 cubes of eggplant (nicely cooked to the way I like it), a thick strip each of red and yellow capsicum, grated radish and lettuce, with a tangy dressing!The Hamburg was cooked medium well (only very slightly pink, but cooked enough for me as I don't like raw food). It was flavorful too. The millet rice did its job to provide carbs for the day.I requested for warm water and was provided with one. Pity it wasn't refilled when I finished it.

The food here isn't excellent. (If you must, try the sukiyaki udon which my friend gets every time she's here.)But the dessert is excellent. In particular, the green tea ice cream, and the more unique hoji ice cream.No one knows about the hoji (oven roasted tea) ice cream. But it's the real gem, because where else do you find hoji ice cream in the first place, and good hoji ice cream in the second place??You can't just order the hoji ice cream as is, though. So what I normally do is get a cold matcha (green tea) latte and add a spoon of hoji ice cream on top for S$2 more. The two flavours are both good, and complement each other (when you are tired of one, get a taste of the other). If you're feeling indulgent, get the matcha float and add a scoop of hoji ice cream.I have tried the hoji ice cream in a cold hoji latte, but that is way too much hoji for one person. I have also tried it on top of the azuki (red bean) latte, but the tastes are both way too "heaty" in a bad way.Oh nana's green tea, would you consider making your hoji ice cream a differentiator from all the other green tea places, and allow me to get the hoji ice cream on its own, or in a cone by itself take-away? I promise I would bring so many more people here if you did that, because it would be so much more affordable and I would be able to convince so many more people to take a shot.If you're going to follow the crowd though, just get the matcha shiratama parfait like everyone else, and share it with a friend. It may be incredibly difficult to get the side profile of the parfait all in one scoop, and it may have cornflakes that become half-mushy if you don't eat them fast enough, and it may be mediocre in its a-bit-of-everything approach, but hey; have it your way.

I was not feeling that well when we went shopping at Plaza Singapura. All I wanted was something to calm my stomach. We stumbled upon Nana's and it was just what the doctor ordered. I don't even remember which hot matcha green tea I selected, but it was very good and I drank the whole pot. I also don't remember exactly what type of udon I ordered! Maybe Sukiyaki Udon? It was nothing special, but it had pork, mushrooms and tofu. See my photo; maybe you can tell me LOL. It wasn't anything special, but this is a tea and snack place, not a ramen house. The restaurant is clean, modern and opens to the mall. The food appears from I-don't-know-where, and oddly you pay your bill at the cashier across the corridor.

For lunch - 2 stars for the chicken cutlet curry. Set lunch for $16.35 incl GST includes a meal, soup and a drink.The good1. I thought the curry was tastier than Coco Ichibanya's.The bad1. The curry came coagulated - there was a thick film on top. Not appetizing.2. The rice was mushy! Disappointing.3. The chicken had too much fat.4. Not enough pickles to go with the meal5. Expensive once you include the service charge.Go for dessert rather than lunch.

This place is matcha lover's heaven! They have a wide array of matcha and hojicha drink and dessert selection that satisfy those with a sweet tooth and anyone who just wants good tea. I love how their drinks can be opted to be either cold or hot, and you can also choose to have thin matcha, in which case, the sugar syrup will come on the side so you can add it according to your taste! My personal favorite is the thin matcha float, which is a cold matcha drink with a scoop of green tea ice-cream! The drink itself isn't sweet because it has no sugar added, but I like it because when the green tea ice-cream melts, it makes it the perfect sweetness! Their drinks and desserts are instagram-worthy so if you're into instagram, get your phones ready ;)I would give this place a 5 star but because the place seemed understaff and you can't make substitutions for the drinks (i.e. trading the mochi in for the jelly) unless you top-up, I gave it a 4 star. Note: Free wifi but you have to ask the staff for the password!

I first heard of Nana's Green Tea when I was travelling in Shanghai, and decided to give the Plaza Singapura branch a try. For green tea, I must say that is is pretty pricey. $8 for a cup of green tea with ice cream? Hmm... not so sure.To be fair though, I gotta say that the tea was definitely very good and I love the soft serve ice cream.I ordered the Hoji tea (roasted green tea) while my friend had the normal green tea. The hoji tea was slightly less sweet, although I think I would have preferred the normal one (sweeter!)I'm not sure I'd pay $8 for just the green tea, but I guess it was worth it since we spent a couple of hours in the afternoon there just sitting and chatting, so perhaps its more for the venue than just for the drink!

Nama chocolate is so delicious. Green tea on the outside and green tea chocolate on the inside. Green tea ice cream. Corn flakes. Matcha powder. Vanilla ice cream. Green tea jelly pieces on the bottom. This dessert was really unique to me and I would definitely come back for more. I'm actually craving it right now! I can't say for the other things on the menu since I've only tried the matcha nama chocolate parfait. The downside is that it's pretty pricey at $10.60 USD.

This is more of a dessert place. You can come in for dinner too but don't expect much except for a few selections of udon and dons. I had the salmon don and my partner had one of the udons. They actually mix the ginger with the salmon (which was sliced really thinly) so it wasn't very convenient separating the two. They were all pink in colour. They added sesame to the rice and you are given some sauce to pour over the rice and some wasabi on the side. Overall I thought it was mediocre.The best thing about this place is the matcha float though. The green tea ice cream in it is really gao. Lol. I also tried the hot matcha in a bowl (ala wabi sabi style). Its just a small amount but is really thick and quite bitter. Desserts go at about 7 or 8 bucks.Would have given this place a higher rating but the food selection is too limited and could have been better!

As the bubble tea appeal dies down a little and I look for different after-meal options to satisfy my sweet tooth, Nana's Green Tea comes into my life at the perfect timing. I might be in love with the Matcha drinks here. I love that they don't taste artificial/instant. I love the richness, creaminess of the drink without it being an overkill. I loved that it wasn't too sweet and had just the right consistency to it and I love love loved that it's like dessert in a cup (with green tea ice cream, red bean and mochi balls in your matcha if you like)Probably one of the best matcha green tea dessert drinks I've had. Of course, this review is based solely on their desserts and not their hot food. But really, it's more of a after-dinner dessert place anyways in my opinion.

Nana and your green tea, where have you been all my life?I've poo-poo-ed this place for a bit now. I mean... the name... but when the Girlfriend and a pal suggested giving this place a go after dinner, I thought it was a perfect excuse. Eh not my idea right, so I had no choice but to try it. I think I was secretly excited. Okay, not so secretly now.Anyhow, for our post-dinner treat, we picked both matcha parfaits. Eh real matcha okay!? I overheard someone gushing about how it comes straight from Kyoto, so I was quite impressed. And then they appear. And I was pretty excited to dig in. Picture this: dark green matcha at the bottom, with kanten jelly, followed by a layer of vanilla/milk soft serve, and then cornflakes (brilliant!) and then matcha ice cream. Then depending if you ordered the cake or mochi, you'd have that as well, and a scoop of adzuki. Typing that just made me want to go back and eat it. Go see the pictures. Every layer is genius, and it all tasted amazing. I'm writing like an idiot now, because I'm just thinking of going back and having another all by myself.

We came here because it was full house at the other Japanese restaurants in Plaza Singapura. The menu looked promising. I had the salmon and tuna chirashi don. It was quite awful as the fish tasted like smoked salmon and tuna instead of being deliciously raw. The cooked stuff was much better, likewise for the sushi. I like the beef sushi. It seemed like almost every table ordered the parfait so we had some to try. We had both green tea and hojicha versions. They were ok but I think I prefer the version served at Sun with Moon Japanese Dining at Wheelock. The corn flakes here were bigger and harder which made it harder to melt in the mouth after crunching on them. I guess I am also not a big fan of jelly so it did not do anything for me. I just left them alone. I do like the red bean paste. So maybe I should order the simpler dessert of just green tea ice cream with red bean paste. There are some not too bad food items so I guess it all depends on what you order.

I have passed this place countless of times thinking it's a cafe serving desserts and green tea so I never really bothered popping by for dinner until last night when my friends cajoled me into eating there. I arrived a little late and had a late lunch of brioche with caramel, bananas & nuts (btw worst brioche ever! by Jimmy Monkey's but that's a story for another review). By the time I got there, my friends were feasting on some lovely Beef Don, Salmon & Tuna Don and a bowl of Something Udon. It looks like the friend who had the Udon had already polished up her proteins so couldn't guess what she ordered. They looked satisfied so I decided to go ahead and try something too.I ordered the Chicken Teriyaki Don. It came with a poached egg. Its runny yolk went fantastically with the savory Teriyaki sauce and sticky japanese rice. Yummy! Although the Teriyaki Chicken meat itself was only mediocre. Next we moved on to desserts. We order 2 matcha ice-creams. Almost every dessert/drink on the menu was matcha flavored. 1) The first was served with matcha ice cream, red bean paste, white mochi, on a bed of kanten jelly. The kanten jelly was light and refreshing. Not artificially sweet but true to its green tea flavor. Some would say it's blend and tasteless in comparison to ice-cream and paste but I sort of liked it. It was a refreshing break from its sweeter counterparts. 2) The second desert we ordered was almost identical to the first in that it had all the ingredients of the former except with 3 additions -  cornflakes, vanilla ice-cream and whipped cream. It was a beautiful parfait! I only wished they had laden it all with more green tea ice-cream instead of the vanilla. The vanilla ice-cream was disappointingly sweet! It sort of reminded me of the softies you can get at Mac's for 50 cents. Lastly, the drinks. The iced matcha drink was so-so. I liked that it wasn't ridiculously sweet and artificially flavored. I know some bubble tea shop (like Gong Cha) use cheap, knock-off green tea essence that taste more like a jasmine flower dipped in sugar than actual green tea. However, Nana's green tea wasn't as mind-blowing as it's name would imply. It wasn't bad either. It was just ok. For a place that inserts "green tea" into its name you would come to except that their green tea will knock your socks off but it didn't. It was rather ordinary. Overall, this place is worth a shot :) If you're in PS and looking for japanese rice/noodles and a good bowl of matcha ice-cream why not pop by? It's taste pretty healthy too so your belly will love you for it.

we tried this because it was recommended by a friend. It didn't disappoint. 3 of us ordered 3 different dish, mine was fresh seaweed with udon, which i think was good and delish and healthy too. my other friend ordered the chicken karaage and she said it was good too. the other one ordered some sort of salad (i thought the serving was small) which, she also said was not bad.  we contemplated if we're going to order dessert coz it was a bit pricey. When we finally gave in, we ordered the kanten jelly with soft vanilla ice cream, motchi and red bean, it was definitely worth it.  For the ambiance, it was ok, interior and design was something new to us. Will come back here and definitely recommend it to other friends.

I'm a fan of their green tea desserts. Ok, I'm a fan of any thing green tea but their price is a bit steep for the dessert.Matcha Latte (S$7) was creamy, smooth and full of the rich goodness of Green Tea.Will indulge once in a while but would go for cheaper alternatives elsewhere.Couldn't say much of the service as it was subpar.

For those whose tastebuds are attuned to the over-sweetened Starbucks latte or mass-produced green tea milk, the Matcha Latte ($7) would not be your cuppa of drink. But I liked this brew as it did not go crazy with sugar. It was slightly bitter and milky, with a dark green suspension of foam sitting above the liquid.From the chilled drinks selection, the Matcha Slushy Shiratama ($9-above pic) is a matcha slushy topped with matcha ice cream and mochi. It might be good to allow the ice crystals to thaw before enjoying the "slurry" texture or your taste buds may be too numbed to taste anything. Alternatively, go straight for the Matcha Shiratama Float ($9) which is similar but more of a milkshake than a frozen drink.Like any other cafe, Nana green tea also serves savoury food such as sushi rolls, rice bowls and udons. The Salmon Cream Sauce Udon ($14.80) came with firm chewy udon swimming in a pool of soupy cream. I always wished there were more sauce for carbonara-style pasta but not this time as the amount was more than sufficient. Had one-third left after pasta was done. The best dish of the day was none other than their specialty matcha desserts--Parfaits. Like many others, I am often guilty of comparing Japanese food in Singapore to those in Japan. But the huge parfaits here were pure decadence, and admittedly better than Kyo Hayashi.Starting from a brownie-like green tea cake that looked like this cake from Japan, the red bean paste and delicate whipped cream, I conquered happily into matcha and vanilla ice cream, colliding occasionally with crunchy cornflakes. Stranded in sweetness, there was no end so to speak, until I reached the bottom of kanten jelly with matcha syrup. Every ingredient was fresh, especially the chewy kanten jelly that was unlike factory-made lego blocks.I personally prefer  the Houjicha Parfait $13.80 as the roasted nutty flavors intensified with every spoonful. Similar to the previous parfait but drenched in houjicha syrup and topped with houjicha chocolate gateaux, this dark brown dessert might be less eye-catching but equally stellar. Overall,  Nana's Green Tea excels in what it specializes; and that is green tea drinks and desserts. Their Uji Premium Matcha has an adult taste suitable for those who wish to sip an authentic pot of bitter brew. And for those who can't resist having sweets to end their meal, the giant Parfaits here cannot be missed.

We ordered a matcha dessert, matcha anmitsu (well, actually I would've been more in favour of the parfaits but those looked too gigantic! perhaps tsujuru is a better choice for that).Here is what is in a matcha anmitsu ($8.80) - matcha ice cream, red bean paste (chunky! yay), white mochi, on a bed of kanten jelly (apparently Japanese traditional healthy jelly - kind of like konnyaku but without the same bite to it and not much taste). There were also some random soy beans (I think, they were somewhat salty). Little pitcher of brown sugar syrup (REALLY sweet) came with it. The matcha ice cream was pretty good! But it wasn't melting (or we were eating it too fast), so were left with a lot of kanten jelly (which really tasted healthy.. hence the pitcher of syrup came in handy) and those random soy beans. Red bean paste was also pretty good, not too sweet. I guess the balance of ingredients wasn't quite there for me. I bet their parfait is pretty good though!

For full reviews and more pictures visit my blog.The No. 1 Japanese Cafe Nana's Green Tea has set up shop in Plaza Singapura to serve you all the delicious versions of the green drink. This is the first Nana's Green Tea Café outlet outside of Japan. Lucky us! The zen decor is a modern twist on the traditional tea ceremony space. Even though the space is very open, the use of the suspended wooden frames as table setting cleverly creates a private environment for the diners.All green tea leaves served in the Café are imported from Kyoto only, which is the most famous production center of Matcha. I love the intense fragrance of the green tea latte and how the aroma lingers on the tongue after a long sip. Best still, top it up with Matcha ice cream for a happy buzz. For the fat conscious, there's the thin version (no milk and sugar). Or go for the Hoji-Cha variation, a roasted green tea that has a smoky, slightly caramelised flavor. A whole range of hot japanese tea is also available.Other than the teas and desserts, Nana also provides a substantial food menu, the largest among all the Nana outlets. Salmon Carpaccio ($8.80) is one of my favs here. Just look at those thick buttery slabs drizzled with a light sesame and citrus dressing. It's really more sashimi than carpaccio. From the hot section, I enjoyed the Locomoko Don ($15.80). This is a juicy and tender Japanese Hamburg over Japanese rice. Absolutely hearty and well flavored. The tomato bbq sauce is a little on the sharp side but overall it is very appetizing. Lunch set is now available and there's a giveaway on my blog. Read more there!

I guess everyone knows what a cafe is in our modern era. By definition, it means a place for light snacks, along with coffee and tea. But because our mind has been propelled to move faster than we could handle in this new century, sometimes we grey out the terms and inject some vibrancy which we thought it'd better exhibit a work of pure genius. The same can turn disastrous when the culinary artistry try to transform the old-school to something fashionable, in hope to woo the palate of many. I still prefer the former class of food- that comes with authenticity - unadulterated by our inquisitiveness. It may be boring to some, but not when the new-age food starts to dribble its identity away with less remarkable in taste, to make matter worst.I should have read the word "CAFE" with a deeper understanding before stepping into Nana's instead of allowing my grouchy stomach to takeover my intelligence. Nana's Green Tea is indeed a place for light snacks, or rather, a moment of dessert indulgence to be more specific. This homegrown Japanese cafe that aims to spread the tea culture to the natives has since expanded regionally -  Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore. The cafe layout is similar to the ones in Japan done up with a clean and brightly-lit atmosphere, sharing the compound with Skinny Pizza. I was less impressed with the service in the cafe, often having to wave for service yet missed their attention many a times. The staffs - mostly young individuals are polite nevertheless. Somewhat inexperience, there was a spill over incident by a staff at one table, the unfortunate lady ended up with a soiled dress. Service level requires great attention here.I am glad that I needn't wave for a menu as it was given to me when they walked me to the table. Flicking the menu, those Matcha, Hoji, Chocolate, Berries parfaits are plain irresistible even on 2-D and you risk a heart contraction if you try peep at your neighbour's.While I watched the ladies digging into the tall towering sweets, I am struggling with my bowl of Chicken Nanban Don. The savoury course coincides with the candied nature of the main cast in the eatery. The Japanese is better known for their preference for lighter fare and sweet tasting over spicy variations, and so I have to reason out along the same line. The rice - stickier and mushy - unlike the texture of any sushi rice was seen cushioning the battered chicken fillet - sliced - losing its crisp. Instead of savoury, the fried item taste sweet under the dollop of tartar sauce but mimic the "Thousand island" cousin. I see it as a calorie-laden dish, less healthy sort though the fresh lettuce shavings did exchange for some good, along with a spoonful of sweet corn kernels at the side. When something doesn't warrant any special culinary skills to put together but requires a hefty $13.80, I start to question their valuation alongside the pricing method.I am a big fan of Matcha Latte and always get my fixes at the invincible green "twin-tailed siren" counter, in soy and 25% sweetened. Not missing on any, I get one at Nana's since it is famed for using good quality green tea. I opt for my regular hot brew but not the soy concoction. It arrived unsweetened, with a sugar stick to add, which was perfect for me - a control freak when comes to food. I like it sterile and so I refused to add flavour to it. To certain extend, the potion gave a sharp but soothing Matcha flavour as I inhaled its scent in the extract. The dark greenish hue mirrors the one at Starbucks but the latter has a creamier texture and is less pricey. The miserable ounces I had today was way overpriced at S$7. It comes with a taller glass when you ordered a cold, not giving the extra ml but to hold the ice cubes that made up the larger content now.The hot savory selection was somewhat narrow with a few options on Don, Udon and a few sushi rolls but the sweets made up 2/3 of the menu. So, this place is truly for the sweet-toothed but only those who are fans of the great antioxidant - Matcha. Yes, this is the hallmark of the eatery and be mindful before you make your visit.I left the cafe without a parfait since I had a bowl of "sweetened" don, without the slightest regret. Not sure if I will return any sooner, if I do, the reason has to be a much smaller price tag following my appraisal.

The dining room was full (with no line, we were told it would be 15 minutes wait, which must be some kind of policy). We got the thin maccha drink which has no milk or sugar in it except we got the one with soft serve ice cream on top. We asked for no ice after we had paid and they complied. I liked the drink. My date thought it wasn't sweet enough though. I would recommend drinking it without mixing it so you taste the sugar from the soft serve. Either way I don't think i would pay $8 for it again to take away.

Being from the US and actually having an aversion to chain restaurants I should have known better than to attempt to visit this establishment.  While guests of the Mandarin Oriental, we had made dinner reservations at another restaurant in the hotel and wanted to grab a drink at the Morton's Bar prior to dinner.  Huge mistake.  The way their staff made me feel was probably the way Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman felt when she tried to purchase clothing on Rodeo Drive, and I look/act nothing like a trashy hooker.  If you want to feel snubbed or treated with disrespect you should definitely go to the Morton's Bar, they are exceptional at that. Cheers.

Feels like the real deal compared to the US.  The meat in my opinion falls a bit short, but that's more or less because of the laws around dry-aged, bone in meat not allowed for in Singapore.  Australian beef just does not compare.  Never tried the happy hour.  Only have heard good things.

Visited the place on Sunday for brunch. Compared to its next door crowded buffet restaurant, the place was surprisingly quiet with just 4 other tables of couple. We were showed to a roomy booth table, where the staff pulled out the table for us to be seated. Looked through the menu, we decided on the 3-course Sunday Lunch Set Menu (S$98++).After placing order, we were served its signature Onion Bread and butter. The huge bun was pipping hot and fluffy.For AppetizerBaked Five Onion Soup (ala carte price S$29++)It was served in a small cup with melted cheese toast on top. The soup was more salty side but great to dip the bread with.Chopped House Salad (ala carte price S$28++)It may not looked much, but the flavours were great. Just take of note of the strong flavoured goat cheese.For Entree8.5oz Filet Mignon with Asparagus and Mashed Potatoes (ala carte price S$101++/ 8oz)Went with the staff's recommendation of medium rare. Opt to serve with mustard and brown sauce, plus sour cream for the mash on the side. The meat was done just right without too raw or too tough. The mash was delicious with bits of potato in it.Center-Cut Prime Ribeye (Topup S$30++) (ala carte price S$118++/ 16oz)Went with the staff's recommendation of medium. The meat serving was double of the filet mignon.  Opt to serve with brown sauce, plus sour cream for the mash on the side. The meat was done just right without too raw or too tough. The texture was smoother compared to the filet mignon, but the serving was too huge for a female like me. The end part was a tab too chewy than preferred.For DessertMorton's Legendary Hot Chocolate Cake (Topup S$10++) (ala carte price S$36++)The molten chocolate cake was served hot, topped with raspberries and a scoop of vanilla ice cream by the side. Soft crumbling crust, encasing the hot molten chocolate inside. Sinfully rich pairing with the cold ice cream.Key Lime Pie (ala carte price S$26++)Served with a slice of lime and a pile of whipped cream.I was too full to have a mouth of it. The staff kindly packed it up for takeaway.

Morton's is one of my happy places, I was more than thrilled that my friends agreed to go there for my birthday.The whole night was just perfect, Morton's in Singapore can definitely keep up with the branches in the US. The steaks and seafood are just on point, they are perfectly cooked and of very good quality.The cocktails are also comparable to those in the US, unlike in most Singaporean bars & restaurants it is not a watered down jobbie, it is a full strength Martini. The wine we had was excellent (but $$$!).Another nice touch is that they had (like in the US) the menu personalized and offered a complimentary souffle plus a printed out picture for me to take home. In general, the service was very good throughout the night.Morton's complimented the great company of my friends perfectly, I felt so spoiled and happy. The only downside was the price: it is certainly not cheap and is still more expensive than their US counterparts but it is well worth it in my opinion. Will go back if another special occassion comes up.

Order- 1/2 doz oyster in their shells, 6 oz center cut filet mignon and I sampled the center cut ribeye (all steaks done medium rare). We had the lava cake as dessert.The colour on all steaks were nice and I personally felt the portion size of the ribeye was huge! Still, it was a good night out - good quality steak but I'm not certain it's the best steak I could get for the price it commands.

My first visit at Morton's steakhouse was an extremely good experience!Planned a birthday celebration for a big boy, and started off dinner with pre dinner drinks by Morton's bar in the evening. Morton's bar happy hour every evening from 5pm - 7pm, with free flow steak sliders with any drinks purchased, and selected martinis at $15.95.I ordered a chocolate mortini and the big boy for himself a cosmopolitan. The chocolate mortini taste fabulous with a thick layer of chocolate which settles at the bottom of the martini glass. We also helped ourselves with a couple of steak sliders (2 mouthfuls worth) which are so succulent and good!We moved on to dinner at the restaurant.We love the setting and service of the restaurant, private yet intimate, and dark romantic and comfortable set up. We had sufficient introduction and great service from the staff who made us feel comfortable throughout our whole dining experience.We ordered a chilled Morton's Prime Ocean Platter, a 12oz centre cut filet mignon (add enhancement of a slab of black truffle butter), and button mushroom only (as recommended by the waitress) for sharing. The sweet gesture by the chef, separate the 12oz filet mignon to 2 equal portions for us. (Look at it on a cost saving perspective..)Received a complimentary small soufflé for the birthday boy, and a lovely birthday song by the staff. To sum up the night, the staff helped us take and developed a photo for souvenir.Concluded that Morton's is not only known for its steak, the ocean platter is also fresh and worth the mention! Steak is perfectly medium rare by the chef, and it should not go without a good glass of red wine.We had a great dining experience with good food, drinks and service at the restaurant and will definitely pop by again in future!

Visit umakemehungry website for more detailsNestled in the heart of Marina Bay area, Mandarin Oriental housed a legendary steakhouse, Morton's. It is located at 4th storey of the hotel, just opposite one of the popular buffet lines, Melt-The World Cafe.The exterior of Morton's was a classic looking American steakhouse with wood panels as its background and its reputable name shining brightly under the warm orange lightings.  Dining in Morton was really a good experience with its elegant interiors and service was impeccable with special needs well attended. Furthermore they were quite detailed with little actions well taken care of and make us felt close to heart.We were presented with a hand decorated birthday card with our photo instantly printed which was a pleasant surprise to the birthday guy, making the event a memorable one in Morton's !Overall, everything was good. My only gripe was that Photography was a challenge as the place was dimly lit. Nevertheless, this had create a very good atmosphere especially for special occassions. I would highly recommend this place if one is seeking for a good steak dinner, service and ambience.

I am not ashamed to say that this is my first time at Morton's Steakhouse, despite their legendary status among my beef-oholic friends. Their price tag is also equally legendary.Excited yet apprehensive about the quality of the steak and the size of the hole it will burn in my pocket, I accepted my partner's invitation to have dinner with him at Morton's.A few things sorely lacking in most F&B establishments in Singapore is the quality of service provided. At Morton's, you can expect the best, personalised service ever (Well, comparable to Black Swan, I would say).Stepping foot into Mandarin Oriental (Morton's is at Level 4), I gave 2 thumbs up to the antiquated-like settings with deep maroon and brass finishing. Somehow in my mind's eye, I always have this vision that good steakhouses will have these kind of furnishings. Anyway, I digress.The two waitresses greeted me with a warm smile and without hesitation I mentioned that my friend is already inside. To which, they confirmed my friend's name and one of them walked me to my table. The self-independent woman in me wanted to decline for her to walk me to my table but she was walking too purposefully for me to stop her. I spotted my partner in one the booths and he gave me a mischievous smile. We reached the table and next thing I knew, the waitress pull out the table with effortless Herculean strength to let me in. Wow. I guess this is part of their service to diners who sit at the booths which I feel was adequate for one person to slide in, slowly.Having checked out their menu online, I was still undecided on what to order so we decided to seek the recommendations of our waiter. He gamely and cheerfully recommended me a Center-Cut Fillet Mignon 8oz as he felt that the 12oz onwards would be too huge for me - if only he knew of my appetite for beef, having ate 2 Jack's Place steak in one sitting! For my partner, he recommended the Chilean Seabass Fillet a La Nage. We ordered the cream spinach after our waiter commented that the sauteed spinach and mushrooms are meh.The crowd was picking up by that time and I was impressed when our food came in record time. Verdict:1. Center-Cut Fillet Mignon - I was singing praises with every gentle slice of beef that I savoured - "Wow, very soft, melts in your mouth. This is good." - to the point my partner was highly amused. The 8oz would be more than sufficient to most ladies, but not to me. Almost to the point where I was tempted to order another one! Served simply on a white plate, the steak oozed flavourful spoonfuls of beef juice!2. Creamed Spinach -  The dish looks overwhelming at first sight but it goes well with my steak as I had no sides on my plate. The delicious butter-filled aroma that it exudes is simply appetizing. Though it is 'creamed', it is light and easy on the palette.3. Chilean Seabass Fillet a La Nage -  Fresh, that's one word to describe the fish. The portion is somewhat larger then what most steakhouses would serve but we are not complaining. The sauce may seem a bit too light for those who are used to creamy, buttery sauce but I feel that it acts as an excellent foil to bring out the freshness of the fish. 4. Key Lime Pie - This tops my list as the best ever, dethroning the Key Lime Pie at PS Cafe. Light and tangy with just the right amount of sweetness, this is a good choice for a desert. Best savoured with after-dinner tea (without milk).The manager stopped by our table to chat and check on our satisfaction and though I usually dislike chatting with the staff during my meal, I was infected by his good sense of humor and charm.Would I return again? Hell, yes! On special occasions though..Service: 5/5Humor of staff 6/5Food: 5/5Price: 3/5 (only because it would burn a huge hole in your pocket if you start craving for the Fillet Mignon 8oz every two weeks!)

Everyone is just so friendly at mandarin oriental. That's why I love staying at this hotel everywhere I go. Staff at mortons too are just as proper and sweet. Their cocktails at happy hour too just make that smile bigger on your face. Free steak sarnies too from 5-7pm. You know how a medium rare steak is so juicy? A slice of that is sandwiched by two soft buns and slathered in a horseradish cream. Oh so gooood!!! The chocotinis are the best in town too. Those steak sandwiches and one cocktail will fill you up too. Writing this review just makes me wish for Monday happy hour to come :p

My steak- medium rare was perfectly cooked, I was impressed because it was so good. We ordered tuna tacos to share as our appetizer and they were delicious too. I think my mouth just gave my stomach a high five.  Oh, and the service was excellente

Morton's used to serve some of the best steaks in town at a mid-to-high end price point. The food is still good and service is very good by Singapore standards, but perhaps not as good as before since Lawry's took over. Had lunch recently during a conference, which may or may not explain our experience. Even with a very full house, we got hot cups of lobster bisque and good bread (though we had to ask for it). Our sirloin steaks came at the right doneness but everyone had quite different sized cuts, which is strange for a restaurant that I used to think was very consistent. I would also have liked a bit more charring on my steak but that tends to be done best on a filet mignon. We had cheesecakes for dessert and as always, there were no complaints there.I am willing to give Morton's the benefit of doubt as this restaurant has historically been a great experience at dinner. Will be back sometime to see if things have really changed.

Morton's is a steakhouse from USA that is really famous for the kind of service that they deliver to customers. Think the service from there have definitely been built up in the Singapore chain. When we walked into this particular restaurant, we were served immediately and brought to our seats in a jiffy. A waitress then came to our table and presented to us the different cuts of beef which was an eye opener.The menu was then passed to us and we decided to order the new York cut and ribeye steak which did not disappoint us at all. We tried the molten chocolate cake as well which was pretty normal, not really glorious or anything was hoping for the wow factor.One thing that we should not have tried is the Caesar salad, with only grated parmesan cheese and croutons on it and really over priced. I have had better Caesar salads with bacon bits and eggs topped on top of the vegetables. Overall a good experience if you know what to order from the start.

This is my go to place for steak in Singapore. There is a consistency to the food quality and service standards offered at Morton's. I guess every individual would have their own experiences but I personally have never had a bad meal at Morton's before. Their crab cakes and chocolate lava cakes are also my absolute favourites! Dining at Morton's has become an annual tradition for birthdays and anniversaries. I've tried other steakhouses such as Cut, Chris Ruth, Wooloomooloo etc. some were pretty good as well but so far none comes close to Morton's in my opinion. Its good value for money.Also try getting in the bar during happy hour for the martini and free flow mini steak sandwiches!

Morton's is a good choice for a leisure meal and happy hour drinks. It proved to be consistent in service, pricing & quality.In terms of the actual steakhouse function of it I have to say that Morton's is a good 'run of the mill' chain restaurant for the better and the evil. The better being the aforementioned pro arguments: I never had bad service here, I never had bad food here and I find the prices to be reasonable for a good steak. The negative part of any larger scale chain restaurant is that it is generic, not outside the box. Meaning Morton's won't give you the unique experience as Cut would do however it is within a totally different price bracket so not fair to judge it by that.A solid 4 star establishment!

I have been very fortunate to make a stop in Morton's at the Oriental whenever I am in Singapore (which has been about once a year for the past 10 years), and each time has been great. The Vibe is exactly how a Morton's should be and the people who work their are awesome.After eating here (this was my first time to a Morton's), I figured I would visit the locations in San Francisco and San Jose, but was completely let down. Maybe the Morton's in the USA should take a lesson from this location on how to offer good service. Anyways, You guys rock!!

We usually come here for the happy hour where martinis go for a song (relatively) and there's free flow of steak sandwiches to go around. However we decided to check it out properly this time. Love the onion bread. The steaks are great although the portions are ginormous! The crabcakes are to die for and so is the chocolate lava cake.Intimate and cosy. Good place for a celebratory dinner.

Singapore sadly doesnt have great steakhouses, only good ones.If you're used to Lugar's in Brooklyn or Goodmans/Hawksmoore in London, you'll be  disappointed with Mortons.But given the few other options on this island, Morton's is worth going to. Its expensive, and somewhat dark inside. The steak is good.

Steaks make me happy, and when I know I'm headed to Morton's, my heart leaps.Begin either at The Bar at Morton's perched midway up the winding stairway with $12 Martinis or head straight to the restaurant for appetisers. The complimentary onion bread is quite something, I can never have enough of it. But you must leave space for the crab cake. We usually order it to share (begrudgingly) but if budget is not an issue, do yourself a favour and have one on your own. I listen obligatorily to the server's repertoire as they roll the meat cart around, explaining and pointing to the various cuts in a well-rehearsed manner, and managing to stifle a giggle when they pick up the lobster with its claws flailing about. However, when it comes to the steak selection, I only have eyes for the marbled US aged black angus ribeye ($97, moderately huge, we ordered one to split).   Morton's always gets medium exactly right, so no ribeyes of mine ever go to waste, and the marbling means I get delicious melting fat to go along with well-seared, pink-in-the-middle king of all steaks. Add a side of asparagus if you must have your vegetables.Looking for an excuse to go back again! Reservations are a must.

It used to be good. The last visit in Nov 2012 saw many changes to the staff and food quality/presentation and size. Had food poisoning after eating oysters on half shells. The double porterhouse tastes different too. Won't be visiting it for a long time.

Wow. Just wow. I didn't know I had to go to Singapore for amazing southern cooking! And I am from Texas. Stopped here on our way to the theatre inside the mall, it wasn't very packed so we decided to try it. Service was amazing! The only place i was able to find southern "sweet tea". The menu was very unique and it worried me to try some of it but it was ALL delicious. It's a must if you want to get out of norm in Asia.

Decided to come here for lunch as it was of the few restaurants that was not crowded. Deviled Eggs ($14++)dill, chives, smoked trout roeSlightly salty but appetizing.Skillet Cornbread ($8++)vermont sharp cheddar cheese, bacon, jalapeno, honey butterIt was soft and moist, with a salty cheesy top.Chicken 'N" Watermelon "N" Waffles ($45++)honey hot sauce, chilled spiced watermelonvermont sharp cheddar cheese waffle, bourbon maple syrupIt smelt very delicious when served. But the taste was pretty average and the meat of the drumstick was rather dark. Frozen chicken with injures?  The watermelon had a minty taste. The waffle looked kind of dry, although the cheese taste was nice. I kind of wish for a huge piece of butter on the waffle.

Definitely not your granny's Southern cookin'; high-end with high prices to match!This restaurant is by the same people that operate Yardbird in South Beach Miami. (Miami? That's a little too far South) The menu had almost all the Southern favorites I used to eat regularly when I lived in Atlanta. Fried chicken, collard greens, biscuits, cornbread, shrimp n grits, fried green tomatoes.  The chicken and waffles were good, with the waffles fluffy and the chicken mostly crispy on the outside, tender and juicy on the inside (except for 1-2 pieces that were a bit dry). I was particularly impressed by the fried green tomato blt, basically a re-imagined appetizer of fried green tomato slices with pork belly and cheese slathered on top. The peach cobbler had a crisp crust and nice balance of cinnamon and vanilla. It takes 25 mins to get out of the kitchen but I felt it was worth waiting for. Everything was really a high-end restaurant take on traditional dishes, immaculately plated and great service and presentation.The only menu items I didn't see were fried okra and pecan pie. Prices were also rather high, S$45 for the fried chicken n waffles, and S$25 for the peach cobbler. Definitely not your everyday dinner hangout spot.We're pretty far away from the Mason-Dixon line, but I think I found a place to get familiar favorites. 3.5 stars due to the dry chicken and the elevated prices, 4 stars for the good service.

Wow! I am so happy this place is in Singapore! It's exactly what I've been craving. I believe it's done by the same guy who did Yardbird in Miami (near my hometown!).  Look it up, it's famous and has won many awards. We ordered: the fried chicken, collard greens and hot fluffy buttery biscuits. Yummmm....No, this place was not cheap. The chicken was a whopping 35$$$! But in my humble opinion it was worth it. It has a nice thin crispy coating and when you dip the pieces in the accompanying hot sauce and...BAM! An explosion of true southern home flavors are flooding my tastebuds. The biscuits were pretty good. I would give them a 4.5 out 5. They could have been a little more fluffy but that's really just a small complaint because they were still pretty delicious.Collard greens are so hard to get right but these guys nailed it. The flavor and texture are spot on, spicy, vinegar and a little bit of sweetness. Soooo good. I will eat here every chance I get and I can't recommend them more if you want to try or are craving southern American cooking in Singapore (even at a super high price).  Oh and the service was too notch. Super fast, really friendly and eager to help us. Way to go guys!!! Love this place!

Recommended by the Sands concierge service, hot and new. I am glad that I was there. I just squeezed myself out from the travel revolution held in the Sands Expo; eagerly looking for a place to settle down so I could go through the package details. It's a nice decent restaurant and it's not hard to tell by looking at how the host and hostess suited up. I was led to my table after got my name (I didn't have any reservation, it is solely for the purpose of greeting me and to make me feel respected). The waiter who attended to me was very polite and well trained who knows the menu very well. After found out the portion and the wine list, I decided to have the crab cake egg Benedict with a glass of Chardonnay. Trust me, the crab cake is simply awesome. It's not like some of the restaurants make the crab cake with 80% of batter and only 20% of crab meat. This one is opposite, you could get a mouthful of crab meats, so fresh and so yummy and the egg Benedict is perfectly done. It is heavenly delicious when you mix the egg yolk with the lemon hollandaise sauce ... mmmm..... Well, back to the reality ... time to settle the bill. The crab cake cost $30, while the Chardonnay is $25... not cheap but worth it.

A new restaurant to the Shoppes at Marina Bay and a welcome addition. My girlfriend and I have been two weekends in a row now and are very impressed with the food. The menu pricing seems a bit off, as the Swine Burger is one of the cheaper menu offerings at $26, while a plate of chicken and waffles rings in at $45. The burger was all around fantastic--a mix of short-rib, chuck, and brisket, topped with pork belly--and is one of the best burgers you can find in Singapore. The fried chicken is excellent as well, and the macaroni and cheese is a must try.The only disappointment to speak of was dessert. We tried the Mississippi Mud Pie Flower Pot, which was quite small and just OK. At $18, it was hardly worth it, and I would be reluctant to try any of their other desserts, which all seem to hover around that same price point.Lastly, the service during both of our visits was very friendly. We will certainly be back for more!
I love this restaurant ! Used to go when I lived in Miami and I am sooooo glad it has finally arrived in Singapore.

Super strange place that can't decided if it wants to be a cafe, bar, pub or restaurant. Stopped in for a coffee and a Pimm's. Coffee was a little weak, think it came from a machine.Decor very disjointed, nearly tripped on the huge carpet on the floor. Overall, just a strange experience.

This place definitely has my heart sentimentally because it's part my nickname, part a university haunt when I was studying nearby. This was a go-to place for one of my girlfriends and I after class because we loved their unique salad dressing - however, that was a few years ago and that dish has since retired, along with their service.I had initially planned to go to another restaurant for drinks after a long day out in Sentosa but it was very unfortunately closed for renovation - I headed here because it was something familiar, and because they had Archipelago beer plus some pretty okay Happy Hour prices. A pint will set you back $11 (before 3pm) / $13 (3pm onwards, third tier of pricing applicable but I can't remember exactly how much it was) during their Happy Hour - but that's about all the awesome there is to this place already. Service here is very slow - for some reason their 4 - 5 waiters/waitress were all lingering in the al fresco area, leaving the indoor seating devoid of people. Thus, trying to get attention from them is pretty hard. After ordering a beer for myself and tea for the partner, it took about 15 mins for both to come. I subsequently ordered truffle fries which took another 30 mins to come - they had actually forgotten my order when I asked again, and had almost no truffle taste which was disappointing. Trying to get the bill took another 10 mins to get the waiter's attention - which was sad because the indoor seating had filled up. I would understand if service is lax when we were one of the two tables that were used inside, but by the time we left, the indoor seating was 60% - 70% full, and there were still no waiters stationed within the indoor area for guests to call if required. I would therefore recommend sitting in the al fresco area if the weather is not too hot - you'd probably get better/faster service there.

Been here several times. Beer is excellent and fresh - Archipelago. Ordered the Ale - dark and nice. The food - got the "bar bites" - Shish Toaruk - very nice presentation and excellent taste !! The source was spicy to the exact point. The Mrs. had the regular portobello which was, as always, very good. All in all nice food, great beer, helpful a quick staff.

Over-priced and subpar foodWe came here for dinner this evening and left really disappointed. Service was subpar and the standard of food dropped drastically from when they first opened a couple of years ago. My BF and I wanted wholesome healthy fish mains this evening, so we ordered the salmon and pan-seared barramundi. When the salmon arrived it was sitting on what looked like melted cheese on heavy cream, with roasted potatoes soaked in the fatty creamy sauce. The sauce was so darn oily that I felt queasy after eating the dish. More importantly the salmon tasted soft and mushy vs soft and firm. The barramundi on the other hand was well cooked and fresh. However the risotto that was supposed to complement the fish was ultra bland. Overall, pretty bad and over-priced food experience! Did I mention? I actually had diarrhea when I got home. Needless to say, we will not be going back! :(

The first time Missus and I went to Queen and Mangosteen was a Friday night. we were looking for a chill place for cold beer and hot food late at 9-10pm. we walked into Q&M and thought it was deserted but as we walked to the back of the joint, we were hit by the crowd, noise and lack of service and left in horror.We gave Q&M a second chance one late afternoon and discovered an entirely different side of the gastropub that was quite charming. The place was quiet with a few tables of idle tourists who were enjoying a cold beer on a hot afternoon facing Sentosa with a wonderful waterfront view. it was entirely resort like and a perfect romantic and cozy ambience. Its menu had classic Brit pub food like guinness pie, mini burgers, etc. happy hour promotions are also relatively worthwhile. So what's the catch? Tiny tiny food portion that cost an arm and leg. definitely a downer for people looking for value for money.

Went here for the happy hour with a friend. Service needs improvement. The waiter was just walking aimlessly that makes it difficult to get his attention. When he did take our order he had to come back twice to check what we ordered which is basically two drinks and truffle fries. Lousy service!

I've always liked the name of this restaurant, I'm happy to say, I've finally dined here and it was good. This is an English pub with some Asian fusion, which makes it tastier than regular boring British grub.Well, it was my Finnish friend's idea to dine here before his flight home. I have only eaten here once, but I would surely come back. The dishes that I had for dinner were the Thai Spicy minced beef served with corn chips and sour cream, Roasted rack of lamb with rosemary potatoes, asparagus and mint yoghurt plus two bottles of Thatcher's green goblin cider.The lamb was delicious and tender tender. Very nicely done. The minced beef dip with chips was very interesting and very declicious... this has chilli padi in it and combined with sour cream and chips. It's a hard decision, but I think the corn chip minced beef dish was the star of my meal. A nice view of sentosa if you sit outside. A memorable dining experience.

Pricy outfit, and I suspect patrons are paying more for the nice view and decor than anything else. Food is ho hum, slanted more towards high end pub grub. The duck rillette is pretty good, but nothing else stands out. Fisherman's Pie, fish and chips are all run of the mill items that are easily located elsewhere. Beer is good, I guess, but only because of the extensive Archipelago range that you'd be hard pressed to find anywhere else.
Home-cooked food style. Reasonable price. Tasty. Fast service.Always come here for "fast food".All home-cooked. Traditional teochew fare.

Been here since the dawn of civilization :).  Sadly the standard have gone from bad to worst.  Ok prices are reasonable and one good news is younger staff are taking over.  Perhaps was just there at the wrong time 6:20 on a Friday?

The food is fresh and it gets crowded after 6pm. Many people will drop by either to dine in or take out.Being a half Teochew, I will say the fare is common in my home and maybe that is why growing up, we usually do not dine out at Teochew porridge place. This is probably the 3rd or 4th time in my life that I have actually ate in such a place. I would say it is good wholesome food which is very familiar to home. So if you or your family hardly cook, then this place is a Godsend. But if you get such food at home all the time, it is not impressive, and you definitely will think twice about spending $20 for 2 persons for a plate of fish, mei cai kou rou, 2 meat fishballs, cold tofu, braised tofu and hard boiled eggs.

We picked up a friend from the airport, and we were hankering for some comfort food... and suddenly, a brainwave - TEOCHEW PORRIDGE.Now everyone has their regular spots, and mine is currently the not-so-convenient Beo Crecsent, so after sent the fella home for a shower, we hunted down the nearest one with a decent rep, and this was it.Looks pretty impressive from the outside - they have two shops side by side okay!? - and when we sauntered in, I was impressed by the clientele (lots of old people), and the counter looked pretty massive, even from a distance. As I walked up to order, the authentic experience kicked in: the uncle spoke to me in Teochew, and I had no idea what was going on. I gingerly started in my stuttering Chinese, with the occasional Hokkien (I know, wrong dialect, but that's as close as I can get), and then the girlfriend came to the rescue; she of Teochew origins (on her mother's side), with the brave and direct pointing and nodding. If only I'd known...To be honest, the selection didn't look so hot, and maybe it was the unfamiliarity, or maybe it was just full of stuff that I didn't eat - I'm not Teochew at all, so this is my usual palate/cuisine.In any case, we over-ordered the pre-requisite amount that we do, and while the food was all tasty, I couldn't help but have a longing for my Beo - and I felt like I was cheating on my food! Horrible feeling, let me tell you, but it was what it was.Glad to say I've tried this one, but my heart belongs to another.
My to-go-to teochew porridge place. You will be spoilt for choice with the wide variety of dishes to choice from.

I LOVE teochew porridge. I can't say this enough but I think this passion was probably cultivated from years of sitting around the dining table, with a whole spread of dishes before me - my chopsticks hovering mid-air, uncertain what to to add to my steaming hot bowl of porridge.My family shifts their loyalty every few years from one Teochew porridge stall to another for some strange reason that I am not let in on. And for the past two years, it's been Ah Seah. It's quite hard to review the the dishes at this stall because there are just too many of them. Expect the usual fare of fresh steamed fish, duck simmered in dark sauce and soft cabbage stew - they do it quite like how a grandmother would make them, and that's a thumbs up. Bring a whole group along, that's the best (and possibly the only) way to get the most out of having Teochew porridge.

We tried out the Bangkok jam in Singapura plaza, and it was good. Our two dishes were brought to us after just 10 minutes, as Well as our drinks. We took the vegi pad Thai and the vegi coconut sauce spaghetti. Both portions were not really large and the flavours of the spaghetti were so so. Our Tea's were at huge. We sar their for an hour just to finish our tea.

Food here is at most average but the long waiting time is why they lost one star with me. We ordered:* Spaghetti with Prawn in Tomyam coconut sauce - I thought this kinda sound strange but there were more than 2 reviewers who mentioned it as good so I thought we'll try. My gut was right, the sauce was coconut-y and Tomyam-y but the concoction just doesn't kick it. Sad  * Olive Rice - after a long wait, we hungrily ate it up and liked it. * Mixed Grill - this was great. The chicken and beef slices were nicely charred with right amount of BBQ taste. The sotong was also done just nicely without making it into rubber. Unlikely to return as the wait doesn't warrant the taste of food.

A Steaming Pot of GoodnessBangkok Jam has been one of my preferred "commercial" Thai restaurants to visit but it's been a while since I was back. We happened to be looking around for dinner at Plaza Singapura when we stumbled upon their Steamboat Buffet! Being an avid fan of steamboats and having the Gf suddenly agreeable too (she's not a big fan of steamboat), I had to take the chance to give t a try and I had no regrets. Soup BaseUnlike other steamboat speciality restaurants, there isn't anything overly fancy about their soup based here. No laksa, collagen or magic dust, just a simple selection of chicken, pork, red Tom yum or clear Tom yum. We decided on the clear Tom yum since, according to them, was the less spicier option. It was a really good soup base. Fragrant, sour, sweet, without being overly spicy, it tasted like a really heart warming bowl on Tom yum soup, which was refreshing as compared to some other places that use Tom yum stock cubes. The Ingredients Don't expect an extremely wide variety of ingredients here too. There's enough to keep you satisfied but there isn't the usual suspects like hot dogs and luncheon meats and in terms of seafood, there's only the option of baby octopuses, Cuttlefish and Dory. The soup does come with 3 fairly large prawns though, which was a bit of a bonus. What they do have here may be limited but very good ingredients. The pork and beef were good and the beef and pork balls were good too. There's also the option of stick noodles (those used thai boat noodles) and glass noodles, which made the whole experience very thai. Plus PointsThe free flow drinks. They don't believe in charging you for soft drinks or water. Instead, they've included a free flow of ice lemon tea, lemongrass tea and the ever popular thai iced tea. They do have desserts available but that's at a separate charge though. OverallDefinitely worth the try. What they lack in quantity they certainly make up with quality and if you like yourself a nice boiling pot of good Tom yum than this it definitely your cup or pot of tea.

The first time I patronised this chain, the food was really good.Inevitably, though, the curse of food in Singapore (especially for chains) hit and quality plummeted.The noodles I got were haphazardly fried and had no wok flavour at all. And the prawns had way too much sodium bicarbonate.This place is expensive too.Stay away at all costs!(the Caramel Thai Tea Blend was a pretty good ice blended version of Thai iced tea, but it hardly made up for the awful meal)

Service is bad! We waited for 30 mins before the food is served. And we had to approach the staffs twice just to get some water. And my friend and I asked for a plate and they only gave us a small plate (10cm diameter) and refused to give a normal size plate. According to the manager, the normal size plate only given if we order rice. Oh Gosh!! We just asked for an empty plate... The food was okay... But the service was really sucks ... I will NOT go there anymore.

My friend had a wriggling live worm on her basil pork rice. Server waived off her dish and offered to change mine as I had the beef.Not sure if the salad was too fresh that worms were on it or was it  a hygiene issue. The side dishes weren't too fanastic, the fish cakes seem to be made from paste and could have had more flavours.Overall, there's room for improvement.

Okay, having had incredible Thai food in Bangkok 20 days ago I was missing it, and my Aunty suggested this place. Our usual Thai hangout is either Sabai, or Folks Collective, so that should give you an idea of our benchmark.Food was ok. How badly can you screw up a coconut curry and meat dish?It wasn't good value either. The portions were what you'd expect in Thailand, and the salt and oil were probably what you'd expect in Singapore! Too much!It's a decent effort, but half-hearted, and wasteful at best.The service was ok. Our mango salad was serves way too sour and the mango was too raw. My Aunty (who loves Thai food) couldn't even eat it, and we asked to change to another dish, and was not charged. Not bad, but that kind of thing seems the norm at this place. Subpar food with cheesy decor.I'd spend my money at Sabai and Folks Collective.....or cook Thai better anyday!Don't bother with this place.

I didn't have too high expectations going to this place, but I was starving so ducked in. It was an average meal and alright for the price. I could easily see this being a joint I go to for a quick feed in Dhoby Ghaut. Oh and the other half (girlfriend) wanted me to mention there was a ton of garlic in our meals. Quite a bit too much! Overall alright food for a good price.

I'm about as badass as a napping puppy.  So coming into this restaurant and being seated at the edge of a balcony overlooking the other floors of Plaza Singapura, I had high expectations for my meal to be quite the thrilling experience.I mean, the name of this restaurant is called Bangkok Jam.  That sounds pretty intense, already.  And the decor is adorable: full of traffic signs, stoplights, telephone poles and wires, Metro/MRT maps, and street lamps.  Even before ordering, I was already starting to get an adrenaline rush after being reminded of the anxiety that is Los Angeles traffic.Now, I don't know why people have been complaining about poor service--it must have been early growing pains.  We were seated promptly, received our menus quickly, and were served drinks rather rapidly as well.  The staff was attentive, but not bothersome.  If anything, the staff and their service helped assuage any anxiety I was feeling from my fear of heights.  One of the people at a neighboring table even changed her order after picking at her food, and their server was still very accommodating.I had gone with my roommate, who ordered their seafood pad thai.  I ordered their egg noodle with bacon and crab pieces (didn't know that was a Thai dish o.O), which was marked as a special in their menu.  It seemed that we didn't receive a large portion for the amount we each paid (S$11.90), but upon mixing the noodles, the food seemed to expand and it looked like we were both going to be satiated as opposed to slightly-less-than-famished.Her dish had a hint of smoke, which tasted good, although not very Thai authentic.  She said she really enjoyed it, but had had better Thai food before.I, on the other hand, had no idea what a ride I was in for.While I agreed with my roommate that my dish didn't taste very Thai authentic, initial impressions had me puzzled as to what it actually did taste like:  It didn't taste like either crab or bacon, but rather, just egg noodles.  It did taste good, but wasn't too much different than any other fried noodles found at a Hawker center.  Where was the thrilling experience everything had been leading up to?Then, I spied a tiny cup with Thai chili oil and lime(?) juice that came with my noodles.  Feeling courageous (or badass, if you will), I poured it in and mixed my noodles thoroughly.  My roommate had a bite of mine and said it tasted good, so I got a huge forkful of noodles and eagerly shoved it in my mouth.And immediately screamed.Not loudly enough to make our neighbors turn, though.  They seemed to be thoroughly enjoying scarfing down their noodles and the changed order.My roommate looked at me, alarmed.  She knew I was a chronic victim of wasabi/chili overdose, and thought I had poured the spicy oil with a little too much gusto.  When she asked me what was wrong, I could barely answer.Not because the food was spicy.  But because I had accidentally eaten an ENTIRE raw garlic clove that had somehow stowed away in my bite of noodles.  And because I was, at the moment, quickly dying.I scarfed down my noodles to chase the garlic I had just ingested.  And then half a liter of water.  People must have thought this was the first meal I had eaten in a month, with the speed at which I was eating.  Unfortunately, since my taste buds had been sufficiently obliterated by that shocker of a first bite, I could only taste garlic afterwards.  I can only presume that the dish tasted better with the oil mixed in, since everything usually tastes better with more fat.  (Cue Paula Deen.)Bangkok Jam was definitely a... rigorous experience.  I just wish the chef would dice his aromatics more finely.  Now excuse me as I look for an army of vampires to slay with my breath.

Exactly why does this place exist, and WHY is there a crowd? (I have figured out the answer to the latter, but yet to ascertain the former).The waiting time is terrible, turn around time is slow, extremely short staffed (3 waiters serving the entire floor). Food portions are minuscule, quality is substandard. The only saving grace is the dessert - red ruby coconut ice cream was GREAT. Then again, if you slather sugar on anything, the chances of it failing is low. Prices are not justifiable for the quality of food. Psh - NEXTTT.

The food is a combination of good and bad. The Pad Thai and yellow curry was very very good but the cashew chicken and soft shell crab salad were these deep fried monstrosities and the olive rice was actually average.Overall just another Thai place! The service was pretty average as well, getting the full order needed a couple of reminders. Tables which were vacated by other patrons lay uncleared forever until unless another group of customers required the table, pretty depressing actually for someone who had such tables in their line of sight..
My favorite Thai food in Singapore.  My wife is from Singapore and I look forward to having Bangkok jam every summer.  Mostly the food in Singapore is horrible but this place is a gem

I won't repeat what others have said about the unique nature of this place. If you have not been here before, you should!Dinner prices can however be a bit steep. Lunch sets are however pretty good value, so I'll be back more often for that!As for the food, the pics speak for themselves!

Tucked away behind Hua Bee's Mee Pok, you can find the entrance to Bincho near the carpark and the rubbish bins. The menus are hung on the wall in the form of chalkboards. Besides the a-la carte items, there are 3 options for yakitori sets, all priced between $60-$120. Some of the pieces of the tori zukushi set were delicious - the assorted appetizer, chicken liver, tsukune with egg yolk, and soft bone karaage stands out. However the rest of the food in the set were bland and underwhelming. But to me personally the star of the night was the garlic pork (a-la carte). The meat was well seasoned, crispy on the outside and the garlic complimented the pork really well. We also ordered grilled squid from the a-la carte menu, but it was very chewy. While I think my meal at Bincho was overall satisfying, I found the price to be too steep for the amount and quality of food we were getting. It was more like a been-there-done-that experience, and I don't think I'll be coming back for their food. However they do have a pretty impressive list of Japanese sake and I'll probably return for that. 3.5 stars.

This is among the easiest reviews I've had to give 5 stars to. Bincho is an incredible find and excellent experience from the moment you find the place to walk in its back door all the way until signing the check and heading out. The food and cocktails both are extremely great.My girlfriend and I made a Chope reservation to check this place out on a weekday night. We heard about Bincho through the shoutout from Singapore Airlines in their in flight magazine for SG50 and knew we needed to check out this hidden yakitori spot. You find a very nondescript corner of a building with a sign that says to go in through the back of the building where you walk in to what looks like a small tunnel. Since we were having dinner, we walked past the lounge/bar area and sat at the counter, bracing ourselves for some solid yakitori.We went ahead with the Bincho yakitori tasting menu which included:1) An appetizer platter (chicken liver pate with baguette, octopus tentacle with some veggies, and some prawn dish), 2) Assorted Sashimi (salmon, tuna and snapper)3) Soup that you drink then eat its ingredients from the pot (included some fish, a prawn and chicken), 4) Chicken yakitori platter (neck, wing, breast and thigh), 5) Choice of lamb, fish or waygu beef skewered, 6) Japanese tomato 7) Tsukune Don - Chicken patty with rice and egg 8) Seasonal fruits which is japanese peach and grape. We shared one of those tastings then ordered 3 items off their a la carte - kinki fish, veggie platter and these yams convered with pork (looks like mini hot dogs) called Red Monnyaku Kurrabuta Roll. THIS KURRABUTA ROLL WAS ONE OF THE GREATEST DISHES I'VE TASTED HERE IN SINGAPORE. Insanely good, we devoured these in record time. Highly recommend you order that one and the veggies too. Kinki fish was great although it has many bones to pick through.Only thing I wish for is that they use the yakitori sticks for all of the meats they serve. That's usually my favorite thing about any yakitori place, even the Michelin starred ones around the world. For the cocktails, we ordered the Yuzu, Sake, Gin one which was light, refreshing and really nice. The one that really hits the spot is their Mangosteen Cinnamon cocktail which also has vodka. It tastes like a spiked apple cider drink, extremely easy to drink.Service is impeccable, ambiance is very New York/underground Tokyo feel and the food is excellent. I would highly recommend coming here on a date or to impress someone. I for sure will be coming back again and and again.

Food here is pretty tasty. It is at par with izakaya food in Japan--however, price wise, it's whack. $18 for one tsukune is ludicrous. I just don't get it. I've patronized this place twice, but doubt I will be back again.

I went for Sunday lunch and got here 30 minutes before they opened the waiter let me hangout at a table using their wifi until they were ready to serve. The food was great! I got the ramen which came as a multi-course meal. Excellent service and great food.

Having lived in Tokyo for several years and eaten all kinds of delicious Japanese cuisine, I am always skeptical of trying it abroad but, Bincho did not disappoint. Their Tsukune and Yakitori is delicious, the ambiance is cool and the presentation is unique. The bar is also diverse with many Japanese microbrews, sake and even an all-you-can-drink beer deal on Sundays. I guess the one difference between Tokyo and Bincho is the price. Be prepared to pay $50-100 dollars to get full, but this is expected as a good Yakitori restaurant is rather rare in Singapore and this place rocks!

Wow this place is so cool! I felt like a spy coming here!Imagine walking through a plain coffee shop, past uncles having their kopi-o and smoking cigarettes at the entrance, and reaching confidently for the hidden door at the back before entering a secret lair full of cool people having Japanese food...Except that we weren't sufficiently IN THE KNOW, so we walked past this place maybe 3 times while looking puzzedly at our phones ("Google Maps says we're HERE but WHERE IS IT?!?!") to the amusement of said uncles, and peered into the coffeeshop to see a very normal-looking place, and finally walked to the back alley to open a nondescript metal door which led us to a dark lair of high tables and chairs and a bar filled with alcohol bottles with kanji on them.Clue: Use Google Maps. Then enter the coffee shop with the green door. And push the green door INSIDE the coffee shopAnyway. We were here for the lunch set which was a really great deal. Sets start at $25 before tax and go up to $40+, but you get a drink, a starter (of 2 chicken drumsticks), another starter (of chicken skin salad which was oh-so-yummy), your main and then dessert (mochi or ice cream).They recommended the chicken dishes (it's a yakitori restaurant afterall) but because we were greedy, we had the ikura negitoro (salmon roll, chopped tuna belly with chives) and yakitori sets to share. Portions were reasonable (actually I was already filling up quite a bit before the main came but there's always more room for good food...) and the service was really attentive.Ikura negitoro - ingredients were fresh and good, though it could be a bit underwhelming if just for one. Afterall, there's not much texture in a negitoro don (besides soft and mushy) I'm so glad we decided to share this instead of me having it all to myself.Yakitori - the slices of chicken were moist and tender, I loved the grilled skin as well. And it looks damn good on photos in case you want to make your friends jelly. (HI IM IN THIS COOL PLACE WITH AWESOME FOOD AND YOU'RE NOT, is what I sent to my boyfriend in Brunei)The restaurant is divided into 2 areas, 1 dark and claustrophobic (and you're all sitting at 1 side of the table, facing the bar, but not AT the bar, because there's an alley between you and the bar counter) and 1 bright and airy with a nice view of the chefs grilling the yakitori. You know which one to choose.(Btw I now know where the cool entrance is and I will be using it for my next visit)

I cannot praise this place high enough, deciding to walk and take the back streets too our destination I had started to loose faith we were heading anywhere, and when we followed the small sign out the back down an alley I was dubious...Thankfully you open the door on the coolest sake bar in town and are able to grab a drink of one if their more unique cocktails or select from the bar menu.Choosing to be seated at the counter we were able to watch chef carefully and lovingly plate each dish Nd he was equally interested in our reactions to his delicious dishes.Our waitress was knowledgeable and together we agreed in a compromise of a share omake and a few special dishes from the regular menu which ended up being a little too much food but never got to the point if welling pained.Our drinks were constantly topped up and the staff matched sake perfectly to our meals, perhaps too much so since I did slightly over indulge.While prices were consistent or cheaper than Australia I imagine this could be somewhat more expensive then people realise though on my opinion it represents true value offering such care from the staff and craftsmanship from the chef.

Back in singapore. So I've tried Bincho again.Once again, the food was delicious and interesting.  I tried pufferfish skin as well as tuna eye. Things I never get to try.The sashimi was delicious and the yakatori flavoursome.Each to e I come to singapore, this is where I will come.

Wow never have I disagreed with Yelp more than on this one. Bincho looks wonderful. It's set up in an old Tiong Bahru coffee shop, has been retrofitted with many bells & whistles and yet manages to keep the romantic old school vibe while still providing a comfortable modern dining experience. That is a big achievement. Unfortunately that is where the achievements end.My dining partner and I went for their two omakase-style sets (Bincho & Fuji) that were semi-delineated on their chalkboard menu while leaving some room for the chef to make decisions.
