The homemade jelly was a nice touch though! Service was pretty good... we were lucky to arrive at 1140 and be seated immediately, but come any later and be prepared for a 20-30 minute wait. I think I'll be back, but hope they keep tinkering with the formula!

Despite the price tag and what I thought would be too hipster to be good, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food at The Coconut Club! Of course, I still thought it was utterly overpriced, but for a nice restaurant in Club Street with a/c and yummy food? Aiight, I'll pay for it.I went on a Friday night and got a seat right away which is a nice change for Club Street that's always bustling and with people spilling onto the street. Service was fairly prompt, and it would have been nice to have the specials on the board instead of me having to ask if the menu was all there is to it and then the server then filling in the gaps on their specials of the day.I ordered the nasi lemak (of course) and the sayur lemak (which is apparently the less creamy version of sayur lodeh - it certainly tasted that way too) which was one of the specials. The nasi lemak came out looking delicious! The rice was coconut-y and fragrant, the egg was a nice oozy crisp, the ikan bilis was fried without being too hard, the chilli was a little too much on the spicy side (and just not as delicious as the one at Adam Road) and the chicken was glorious. The chicken was a full thigh and drumstick, was marinated in this delicious marinade (lots of local herbs - lemongrass and the like) and fried to juicy perfection. Yum. The sayur lemak had a really good broth - possibly ikan bilis? I made the unfortunate mistake of mixing all the chilli into it and ended up sniffling my way through my meal although it was really quite delicious. Although they also serve alcohol, my dining companion and I both got the lemongrass tea which was serviceable.This was all-in-all a very satisfying meal, and although I might still return to Adam Road for my nasi lemak fix (at a much lower price point too), I wouldn't say no to anyone asking me to get nasi lemak if I were ever in the Club Street area.

The Case of the Confused Fast Food. Now... I don't normally write reviews about fast food joints. Not because they're not good or creative but well.... It's because they're fast food outlets. They should taste the same everywhere? Right?I couldn't help but write this because of the "rebranding", if you could call it that, that MOS burger is trying to do. It's not uncommon either. In recent years, we've seen McDonald's launch McCafe, KFC having KFC cafe, so it comes as little surprise that another fast food outlets decides to join the fray. MOS café, newly rebranded, offering desserts and some new innovative burgers like the Wagyu Tower or the Osaka yaki rice burger, the Tortilla salad, vegetable smoothies, all items not found at other MOS outlets. They even had mock displays of their food at the entrance, all nicely presented on plates and looking pretty good. Even a look at their website is impressive, "MOS Café was conceptualised as a FLAGSHIP CAFE that caters to the LIFESTYLE of our consumers....... Driven by a "FRESH" CONCEPT - using lots of fresh vegetables and fruits. The menu is made up of ORIGINAL Café items as well as items CAREFULLY CURATED from the MOS burger menu". Sounds exciting. However, upon reaching the entrance of the restaurant, with exception to the huge "MOS Café" sign, nothing much has changed. It still looks like a MOS burger, the seats still look the same, no cozy sofa corners and still filled with booth seats. The ordering counter looked the same and even the uniform was the same (at least McCafe took the effort to give the barista's a different outfit).  But well.... We decided to give it a shot. Once ordering, it was clearly confirmed to me that... It was nothing but a sad rebranding attempt and an even desperately gimmicky attempt to make themselves look and sound updated.Firstly, I get the same number tag I get at MOS burger. Fair enough. Than came my cups in a regular mos burger paper cup. No change there. But when our orders came, the all too familiar basket appeared. In it were our burgers and fries. What happened to all the nicely played burgers you were promoting by the window? Why was everything still wrapped? I don't deny it.. I felt cheated. Anyway... On to the food. I won't spend too much time on the regular items as I'm sure we're pretty familiar with those. Osaka Yaki burger. Now this looked good... In picture and on display. Of course I'm not expecting it to look the same when served, especially not since its in a wrapper. Taste wise.... Decent. However, I am left with figuring out what I actually ate. While the image showed a nice layer of egg, fried seafood patty topped with bonito flakes, I could only make the egg out in the burger itself. I'm still trying to figure out the protein they gave. Was it fish? Prawns? No clue. Unfortunately, the project they embarked on fell pretty much on its face.Don't get me wrong, I love MOS burger, but, in terms of this being a flagship concept and a cafe? It's more a MOS burger doing cosplay on a budget than it is actually being a MOS Cafe.

I was going for 5 stars but you "DO NOT SERVE DIET/LIGHT COKE"?!? W.T.H.I loved you man. Loved you since I was a teen. Back in the days when Britney released her first hit single. I longed for your rice burgers when I moved to Australia and then Canada/America. Now I'm back here I wanted to rekindle our love. But when you told me you didn't have diet/light Coke, you spat right into my mouth. And to top it off, you did not allow me to pay using my credit card. Not. Cool. Bra. Not. Cool.From 5 to 3 and now 1. Why? Well as I went over to trash my wrappers and return the tray I saw you emptying the tea from the dispenser - it was closing time and you were draining different teas into one bucket. So I asked, even though I know it's not typically refillable, "hey mind pouring me some? I did buy a whole last cup of unsweetened ice tea". "No refilling". "But you're pouring them away right?". No answer and you just looked away.Service. Matters. Douche.

This is a delightful place to have brunch.I would like to thank the staff for keeping and returning my sister's handphone. They made sure that they were returning to the rightful owner. This shows how thoughtful they manage the cafe. Good job keep it up!

Matcha Latte - a new drink from Mos Burger.The color looks too tempting not to try. Well, it is good for a fast food standard. I like the light matcha taste and aroma. I did not add sugar so it is just right for me.

A better choice among fast food chains? Come to Mos Burger. It is a Japanese fast food chain and there are a few in Singapore. The first chains I tried was at west mall and isetan Scotts but those stores closed down. I was browsing on what's to eat at raffles city and I was delighted to find mos burger here.Personally I am into ebi rice burger but that changed after I had allergy breakouts after eating shellfish. So looking at what's on their advertisements, I spotted salmon rice burger. All I can say is you keep wanting for more if you eat it. The salmon was cooked perfectly with the sauce on top and covered with rice buns. Yum...Service is extremely fast at this chain even though the workers are mostly elderly. You can get your order within 2-3 minutes if you do take away. Depending on what time you stop by, you might be able to find seats. I tried two chains : one near to clementi mall and the other in Ang mo kio and I still love this chain. This is the healthier choice of burgers if you consistently think about calories. YAY to Mos Burger!!

WORST MOS BURGER I've ever had.I got the pork with rice buns and the rice was overcooked and really dried up and hard to chew. The hokkaido ice cream was unflavourful. The only thing that's worth coming for is their corn soup made from powder. Highly disappointed with this location in Singapore. The one i had in Taiwan was way better.

Well this was disappointing. I wanted to try a cheap, uniquely Asian burger, and what I got was a cheap, uniquely bad burger. Bland patty, and the sauce was like a poorly made mild chili. Also, I understand that this is a fast food establishment, but that doesn't mean yelling at your customer when they ask if credit cards are accepted is warranted.

I like coming here for their fries and scallops. Their burgers are nice too. Have always been a fan of Mos Burger - for their swift service, friendly disposition, great menu and options. You can get your tea less sweet, or get Barbecue sauce, etc. I love that they serve stuff in a tray and you take it out of the paper bags, etc.What I Love: Their Rice Burgers are yummmmmy. I've had the beef and chicken ones. If you want something light, then skip the Rice Burgers. They are a reasonable size - but once you have them, you'll realize that it is pretty filling. Their yummy fries and deep-fried scallops are to die for. And their nuggets. Really does beat McDonald's. And their mayo.... yum!!!What I Don't Love: Their soup. It's nothing special. And their prices! A few stuff added up together and it's like $8-$10....

This is not my first time here but I do like going to MOS whenever I'm in Asia.  This time wasn't as good as the last time I was here or the other chains.  I had the seafood rice burger, beef rice burger and a korean beef burger.

Located at the basement of raffles cityBurger to try, Chicken Teriyaki burger and if you are watching your calorie, you can request to deskin the chicken before served. The chicken is well marinated in the teriyaki sauce.I would suggest to go with the potato croquette side dish. The plain croquette tastes much better than the curry flavoured. However the reason for visiting Mos Burger  is the milk tea. The milk tea is very rich and well balanced.As compared to other fast food store, Mos burger definitely has its own unique selling point and dishes but the price might be on the high side given the quantity served.

You can hardly go wrong with Japanese fast food! The flavors from the rice burgers here are just fantastic. The two rice burger to try for me would definitely be the beef slice rice burger and the ebi burger. If you're looking for something on the side, give the deep friend mussels a go, a great tasting alternative to the usual chicken nuggets.  For drinks, do try the milk tea, you can't go wrong with that! Meals are a little more expensive than your regular fast food joints but for the quality of food you're getting, I think it's well worth it!

standout indian food in the grastronomic wunderland that is katong - I don't usually come to this area because it's a little far out of my reach, but the many good reviews of this place were too great a draw to resist. and they live up to it - indian food made modern, really in the style of masala zone in london, which I haven't yet seen in singapore - I would say this is food that admittedly might play more to the mainstream consumer's idea of indian rather than traditional fare, but it doesn't detract from the pleasure of eating here, and judging from the clientele in this place - it might not be wholly unauthentic either.you do pay for the experience though - prices are much higher than what you'd see at other indian joints, though merely on par with other new cafés/bistros. service is a little absent-minded sometimes - though this only happened with one of their waitresses - but the food is well good, and well worth coming back for.

Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant Indian restaurant in East Coast area. I always get excited to see Indian restaurants get recognition.It's good and definitely hits the Indian food craving. It looks like they have a significant service issue since there are many Yelpers mentioning it, but I was lucky since the restaurant was mostly empty when I was there. I was the only one getting food so service was alright.I ordered the following:1) Papdi Chaat - It was good, not the best but definitely good.2) Butter Chicken - Hit the spot. Again, its good but doesn't stand out compared to other restaurants in SG.3) Plain Naan - Excellent Naan4) Sweet Lassi - Pretty bad. Maybe the yogurt was already spoilt.Lunch was decently priced. Although I don't understand the reason for Michelin's recognition here, I would come back for lunch if I was craving Indian and was around the East Coast area.

Zaffron Kitchen was pretty good Indian fare. Sure, the iPad ordering substitutes for friendly service, but the food comes out fast.The Tandoori (and meats generally) were fantastic. Succulent, high quality and tender. The Biryanis were a bit of a miss - still good, but not great. The Butter Chicken was silky smooth and the Naan were reasonable.6 people plus 2 bottles of wine worked out to be $50 each - which, by Singapore standards, is still kinda pricy.

Been here many times especially when we are in an indian cuisine fever. I would have gladly given a 4 star but today we discover there is no free flow of water!!!  Now that is a BAD chicken tikka for the management.  Otherwise we had our usual package chicken tikka, garlic naan, mutton curry, two types of rice and a mixed veg curry.  Finishing of with teh terik and were happy as usual.as usual they are understaff :).   patience is key here.   clearing table is slow.   getting out teas after meals takes 15 minutes. Nov 20th '16Back again for an Indian fix.  Unfortunately this time round instead of the service staff being a mess the kitchen too was a mess.  Post putting in my order at 7:40pm there were at least 4 tables waiting for their food.  In fact one table with a party of 8 walked out.  Come on management wake up!!!  Get a hold of your wonderful business before it get hold of you!

This was my first time trying "actual" Indian food and i'm not disappointed. Our order:I came here with my mum for lunch and we ordered 2 set meals - available now weekdays from 1130am - 2pm, if i remember correctly. I got the Tandoori Naan set which included 2 pieces of chicken; naan; biryani rice and the sauces + curryMum got the Vegetarian naan set which had basically the same things except for the chickenTaste:Tandoori Naan Set:The chicken was coated in some yummy goodness (i actually don't know what it was marinated int) which tasted ahmazing. To my surprise, it wasn't really spicy as I thought it would be - how stereotypical of me!The naan was hot when it was served and tasted absolutely spectacularBiryani - i've never had biryani before but according to my mum, it was one of the best ones she's had and trust me, she's pretty picky about her food. Yoghurt - this was one of the "sauces" (not sure if that's the correct term) in the set and i really liked itCurry - ahaha i personally found this a tad spicy but nevertheless it was superbAs for the Vegetarian naan set, once again, mum said it was the best.Portion:We were initially a bit skeptical to order 2 sets because we though it'd come out huge, however, the portion was just enough for one person.Service:Because it was our first time there and it was my first time trying Indian cuisine, I didn't really know what to order. The waiter tried recommending some things to me but I didn't quite grasp what he was trying to say... Nevertheless, service was fast and the staff were friendlyPrice:This place is definitely a bit pricey and is not one of the places you'll visit every day. However, for the food served, it's definitely worth it.Overall, I really enjoyed my first real Indian cuisine of my lifeeee and i've fallen in love with Indian food... hehe :))OH AND SET MEAL CAME WITH A DRINK!

I think Zaffron has heard our cries, because I found the service here was insanely fast and incredibly friendly. Loved loved loved the atmosphere. Chill and buzzy.The chicken tikka starter was unreal. In comparison, the chana masala (chickpeas) and mutton rogan josh were just ok - good, but not *amazing*. I also couldn't stop dipping everything in the the mint chutney. Amazing.Will almost definitely be coming again for the good food and great vibe.

This is a 3.5 for me, but because I do like the food, I'll give it a four.Don't get me wrong- I like Zaffron Kitchen's branding. Their ambiance is great, they have iPad menus that are easy to navigate and work, and it's kid-friendly. Their service could use a little more work, though.The first time we came here, it took almost half an hour for our food to arrive. The second time, I was one of the first to arrive for lunch and it took a little under 20 minutes. To echo the other reviews, the servers are a bit distant, but I get it- you don't need to remind me where I am.I was surprised about their naan lunch sets- it lives up to it's name as it comes with 4 large pieces of fluffy naan! Very filling. I also liked all the sides that came with it, and my butter chicken hit the spot. If you're looking for a good veggie side, their aloo gobi is my favourite!Service may not be the best, but I know I'll be back.

I hate to sound like a broken record, but I second my fellow Yelpers that Zaffron has excellent food, but service / food delivery is poor. Thanks to the Yelp app, via Check-in, I discovered that it took 27 min! for the food to be served. Fortunately, it was the entire order, which consisted of Butter Naan, butter Chicken, Basmati rice and aloo gobi. When the attendant delivered the food, we didn't have any utensils at the table and had to kindly ask the diners/table next to us for their unused set. (Hint: the service staff should've done this for us). Despite it's suspect service, Zaffron delivers excellent Indian Cuisine within a modern restaurant exterior. The butter chicken was definitely my favorite dish of the ones I ordered. Not as good as my favorite North Indian restaurant in Novena, but good nonetheless. The sauce was thicker and darker in colour and a tad less sweet. Overall, Zaffron delivers 4-star food with 2-3 star service. If you are craving for great Indian good in the Katong area, but are happy to wait just a little longer than normal for food, then Zaffron is an excellent choice!

We tried out this restaurant as my daughter wanted to give us a treat. We checked out Yelp and reviews were mixed, generally stating that the food was good but the service poor. Nonetheless we decided to give it a try. True to form the food, northern Indian style WAS good. All dishes we tried were very nice except the nan which was a little tough. The portions are larger than expected. We were impressed. The restaurant is child friendly with a little play area. Very casual atmosphere, perfect for a family dinner. Service was good. We had the fortune of interacting with the restaurant manager Dinesh. He was very service oriented and we had a pleasant chat. I suspect that previous reviews had them working on improving service and it has seemed to work. We noticed that the other staff provided service with a smile, though there is still some way to go on in that while they did serve well it did not seem genuine. They need to do a little polishing. A credible performance. Perhaps in time Dinesh's example and training will rub off on them. We had a great evening and the cost of a full meal was about $30 per person. Very affordable. I will be back.

The food is great, but I'm leaving it at 3 stars because twice I've had really bad service and it spoilt the whole experience. Long queues, forgotten orders, rude waiters and such. Other reviews cite good experiences though, so maybe I just caught them at a bad time or something. Anyway. If you're vegetarian most Indian places are full of options and Zaffron is no different. My favs are the Tandoori Gobi or the Tandoori Mushrooms. In the curries section, their Dhal Mahkani is probably the best I've tried anywhere. Ever. Their naan is pretty spectacular as well, but the curries go really well with rice, so it's a tricky decision. I'd say go with lots of friends and order lots of things. What really adds to the experience is the presentation of the food, which is pretty and quite stylish. The waiters aprons also have clever food-based slogans on them which is fun to read. Do make a reservation as it's quite crowded usually, and every time I walk past at dinner time there's a long queue. There's also a play area for children which looks like so much fun I've always been tempted to sneak in. Also, popcorn machine!

The Zaffron Kitchen had a décor and ambience that doesn't seem to resemble an Indian restaurant, but perhaps more of a usual European restaurant. Anyway, we sat down quickly and ordered our food because we were rather hungry. The service here was prompt with smiling waitresses.We tried a few of their dishes such as the fish kebab, chicken tikka, butter chicken, chicken biryani and chicken chettinad. The chicken chettinad was very spicy and I really liked the taste. We dipped the naan into the curry and it was simply perfect. The chicken was also very tender and the meat came apart easily. The chicken tikka was another of our favorites. There was a distinct and nice grilled flavor to the chicken, and the meat was succulent and tender.Overall, we had a great Indian meal here and would definitely be back.

What can I say that hasn't already been said. I have been coming here since early 2011, even had a birthday dinner here for my daughter with the extended family. For my group meal the service was good, for most other meals the service was awful, the food has always been good. The service has been improving, they have chosen to go the route of self ordering iPads and decreasing the actual staff to guest interaction. This technique has worked well to improve the "Service."The food has always been very good, it has been what has kept people coming back, their front Tandoor churns out good smoky tasting food including Naans and Daal Makhani.Aside from the food, the real draw is the family friendly atmosphere with a kids play area in the back, including a play house and even children sized sinks and toilets. Although, now that I think about it, the staff is just as indifferent to the kids as they are to everyone. The food quality will reward you for returning, the kids area will let you enjoy the food, and the staff seem to be getting trained to stay away!

Last time I will be coming to this place. Waiters/servers look as if they don't want to make any eye contacts to sit you, give you the menu, take orders or anything customers want to do. If this was the US, they would be getting that infamous $0.20 tip.

Refined Indian cuisine, but most dishes are very heavy. Don't expect to be productive at work after having lunch at Zaffron Kitchen. Very nice ambience. Too many aircon units can make the place uncomfortably cold, however the staff are willing to adjust it.I experienced both very good and very slow, inattentive service where it can take 15 minutes to receive the bill. Food is consistently good, not the service.

Zaffron is a relative newcomer to the buzzy eatery lined stretch of Katong. It's unpretentious and serves up authentic North and South Indian food. It's not much of a stretch to say that almost all the items on the menu are hits. The butter chicken is a must try - succulent meat swathed with gravy, fish masala is fork tender, and the naans are great. My group did find the Kashmiri naan a little unusual though, as it didn't quite go with the rest of our savory items. The kulfi was interesting, though some detected a hint of cardamon, and it did not agree to those who were averse to the spice. Due to the popularity of the restaurant, service can be a little spotty. The decor is very pretty though, and there's a play corner for kids to busy themselves at. The A/C is very cold, but happily, the service is warm. If you can catch the servers' attention, that is.

Classic chain seafood restaurant, now more accessible since it is near the city. Thus you see lots of business dining tables.Long Beach claims that they invented the black pepper crab. It's an overall crowd pleaser. The rest of the classic seafood dishes are all available: deep fried baby squids (it was a tad too sweet the night we ate), steamed bamboo clams with garlic and vermicelli, fried mee goreng (nice and spicy). And if you are there with overseas guests, they can also try lots of local desserts like durian pudding. All set in a floating bowl of dry ice for added effect. Cheap thrill, I know, but it's tacky local!Plus, free parking at dempsey!Tip: If you prefer black pepper crab to chilli crab, but like the chilli crab gravy.....For S$6, you can get a bowl of chilli crab gravy (without the crab, but the full works with runny egg, etc) that you dip with mantou. Best of both crab-worlds.

One of my favorite places for seafood. The steamed garoupa and pepper crab is really good. If you find the black pepper crab too spicy, go for the white pepper. I would rate this restaurant higher if the service was better. Parking is also a problem.

Visited again. If even possible, the food, especially the black pepper crab is even BETTER! The manager, David Ng informed us that CNN had rated the crab one of the 50 foods you must eat in the world before you die. Totally agree. It would be criminal to come to Singapore and not experience this.

Long Beach has been around since god knows when - and there is nothing negative about that.  I remember coming here many, many times when I was younger for those huge raucous family dinners where we would occupy two tables and leave only after we have littered the tabletop with heaps of crab and prawn shells. Pretty standard Chinese seafood fare here. The thick chilli crab gravy is fantastically fragrant and a perfect dip for a deep fried mantou. Another dish I really like is the drunken prawns. The preparation of the dish is a tad disturbing though - they dump the live prawns into the broth in front of you and you may have to watch it shiver and jump in the throes of death. Not for the faint-hearted. Another famous dish here is the black pepper crab but it is a little too sweet for my liking.One thing that I have grown to appreciate about Long Beach is that it is such a typical Chinese restaurant - impatient and boisterous waitresses, a dish of peanuts of a complimentary appetizer and dubious looking chinese tea that tastes pretty much just like hot water.

When I think of crabs, especially chilli crabs, there's only one place that comes to mind - Long Beach Seafood!The name alone tells you what to expect, and having been around for the longest time, is one of the places you know you can trust to have a great time. I've been here since young and the standards have always remained consistent. Bookings are essential if you want to sit indoors where there's air-conditioning, if not, you'll find the al fresco areas rather breezy as well. It's not just their crabs that are awesome, they also have other delicious items on the menu like bamboo clams, fried duck, hor fun with a very good 'wok hei', mee goreng and the Alaskan white pepper crab. Their desserts are rather good as well, do be sure to try their durian pudding. Its one of the best they have, but unfortunately, it depends on your luck as they don't have it all the time!

Outstanding in every way!   The service was attentive, food was outstanding and setting was beautiful. We had some all time great dishes: razor clams steamed in garlic, pepper crab, and a soup with an amazing broth and fish ball (fluffy and not dense).   Dessert was coconut ice cream with mangos.  It was the perfect end of a great meal. We were brought there by some friends who live in Singapore.  They are foodies and we were appreciative!

The reported home of pepper crab, one of my all time favorite dishes. Big noisy and un-airconditioned. Cold tiger beer accompanies the outstanding food. But be prepared for the price - the simple food court atmosphere belies the high cost - especially for the chile and pepper crabs which were about $50 apiece.

This location tends to attract a lot of tourists, and for that reason I didn't go there with the highest expectations, but I had a very good time there. The butter crab was absolutely delectable, with soft, sweet, buttery, finger-licking, lip-smacking, rich gooey goodness everywhere. The razor clams are much bigger than I've gotten elsewhere on the island, and were absolutely worth the premium price. Very fresh, sweet, tender, yet with a good amount of chew, and a great garlicky sauce. The sea bass in thai sauce was average but not bad. Otak was pretty good, tofu with house special sauce not a big standout but still popular with the table. All in all, a good meal!

the chili crab here is delicious.  i don't even remember what else i ate, but i just remember drinking the chili crab sauce when we finished the crab.  if i had known it was completely made of lard, i would have probably refrained.

Long Beach failed miserably today. We were able to get an outside table at the last minute of CNY Eve. However they served us frozen Alaskan King Crab! The manager confirmed it and apologised but by no reasons should they have compromised quality in the interest of more business. We've been coming here for over 7 years not looking forward to come back. No more trust.

Dempsey is quite hard to get to, if you don't have a car. Luckily, my friend drove me here and the parking lot was completely full and hard to find a spot to park. Garlic steamed clam with fun see - it reminds me of those good ones that i had in HK, though it wasn't as good as HK, but still decent. Black pepper crab - very tasty, good flavor, i don't normally eat crabs, but this one didn't get me stomachache because the pepper warms up my stomach. the crab is relatively easy to open and eat. Dessert with flames/ice - it's a special mango dessert from this shop, i don't recall it was free of charge or we paid. obviously i didn't pay for the meal LOL    it was very sweet for me but nicely looking! I tried Jumbo seafood, it was not nearly as good as this one.

Been coming here for more than a decade. Long beach has the best pepper crab hands down.... after eating and sampling pepper crabs round the island, Long Beach really has the best tasting pepper crabs around.This round, we ordered white pepper Alaskan snow crab. The huge Alaskan crabs were cooked to perfection, in a buttery creamy pepper sauce. The chilli crabs are tasty but i would recommend the pepper crabs. Other dishes tasted great but didnt taste as savory as their signature pepper crab which they invented.I gave them 5 stars for their fantastic pepper crabs that never fails to satisfy.

I didn't think it was so expensive as for dollars mark. The food is great and vegetables are cooked in nice way, sea food is awesome.  Should try and see.個人的には好きな部類に入る中華です。野菜も一品料理も美味しく、たまに行きます。海鮮料理が上手なので、貝や蟹もオススメです。2015/11
Must visit resto in singapore The black pepper crab is a must! Try durian dessert  or glutinous rice with ice cream as well

My friend and I came here because we had heard that the crab here is pretty amazing.We ordered the "chicken with fruit sauce" as an appetizer, and we also ordered chili crab and black pepper crab. The chili crab came with some fried buns, which complemented the chili crab nicely. They added some texture and also helped cool us down when the chili got too spicy for us (it rarely did, though; the chili in chili crab really hasn't seemed that spicy so far). I LOVED the chili because it was so rich and creamy, while my friend loved the taste of the black pepper. We ended up devouring the crabs quickly, thoroughly enjoying this meal.We highly suggest this place if you're in town and looking for some chili or black pepper crab!

The most disappointing Long Beach location yet.  The restaurant seems run-down and dirty, and the service questionable. I asked for paper napkins (not the wet ones) and the man returned with paper towels he rolled out from the bathroom. wth? this place sticks out like a sore thumb in midst the plethora of good/classy restaurants in the Dempsey area.  For seafood in the Dempsey area, go to the Jumbo Seafood instead!

Brought 2 friends visiting from the states and shared the $168 set menu which included quite a few dishes. More than enough food for 4 people. We started with a live prawn dish with broccoli that was quite good, and also some chicken wings (who doesn't love deep fried chicken wings, mmm).The black pepper crab came out next and the table went silent with everyone enjoying the deliciousness. We added a chili crab to our order so that we can get a taste of both and we all liked the black pepper crab better. The veggie dish and noodles were quite good also, rounded out with a dessert (some kind of warm taro paste, yum).As newbies all dining here for the first time, we didn't know we could ask for bibs, gloves, and scissors for the crab! When we saw the tables next to us with these awesome amenities, we were very sad as we just didn't know to ask.The weird thing about this restaurant is they have pictures of scantily clad women on the napkin covers and menus which makes the place seem very cheap and sleazy... I thought that was quite weird. Also weird are the beer girls. When you order beer, they pour for you. These girls wear Tiger outfits which consists of a very short one piece miniskirt dress thingy. Again, makes the place feel cheap and weird and not a respectable restaurant. I don't get it.Still, the food was all around good enough to get 4 stars and not 3.

Went here for a dinner with a group from work.  Perfectly acceptable from that perspective - got a nice private room, ordered from one of the set menus with a million courses.  All of the food was good and served family style.  I will say the roast chicken was phenomenal - the skin was super-crispy (like duck) and the meat perfectly cooked.I wouldn't come here on my own looking for an authentic Singaporean food experience  though.  It's a tourist place.

I've been coming here with my boyfriend to only order CHILLI CRAB, *hyperventilating right now* the deliiiiicous razor clams and steamed buns. We needed no duck, fish or whatnots. Just the Chilli crab and its friends to go along with. So first we ordered the razor clams as our appetizer, it was so yummy. It had glass noodles with finely diced garlic ontop. The garlic was quite a lot (which I like), accompanied with the yummy sauce. Everything was just so mouth-watering. After that came along the.. Chilli crab ta-daaa!!! It was so darn good- the sauce is only a little spicy for me because I take spice pretty good.. So so savory. We eat that with the steamed buns. When the crab meat is all gone, we tend to just keep eating by dipping the buns in the chilli crab sauce. Deffinitely will keep paying a visit hehe but I need to refrain myself for going every darn weekend since the chilli crab is such a high caloric food haha.

Been here numerous times...whenever we want to introduce out-of-towners to chili crab, we come here. Once we brought a friend to Jumbo and were duly disappointed. The branch on East Coast is probably slightly better in terms of freshness, but this one is much more convenient. Plus you can have a drink in one of the bars & pubs at Dempsey afterwards. You have to order the fried mantou to go with the chili sauce. Soak it all up! A friend took the remaining sauce home and made a nice pasta the next day.   In addition to the crab, I'd also recommend the crispy duck and the Thai-style steamed fish. The duck especially is one of the best I've had anywhere. Crispy, chewy, meaty, and packed with flavor. I can gnaw on its bones! Service and ambience are so-so, and it's on the expensive side. But still the best chili crab in Singapore in my opinion.

I prefer long beach (Vivo and East Coast) location better than the Jumbo's and no signboard restaurants for their chili and black pepper crabs.  Service has gotten a lot friendlier over the years as well.  Popular with locals and tourists for chili crabs.  I am just reviewing the crabs...i haven't a lot of the other items except for vegs, soup, etc....usually go for the crabs!

I love this place. OK, decor, ambiance... can do better.But the crab is great. I love the black pepper crab and the sauce of the chilli crab. I prefer this to Jumbo, especially with regards to the chilli crab.I love the pitchers of beer... nice with the crab.

Chili crab is to die for...it's amazing, I can just take shower in that sauce! It was so good and amazing. Blacked pepper crab was...okay. I think chili crab was must have if you must choose. I also had some beef dish and noodle but I was just so mesmerized by chili crab I almost forgot...yes they were as good but...chili crab! Must have chili crab!!Location is closed to a mall (like everything else in Singapore), free parking right by. Waiters were very friendly and attentive.

I must admit that the only reason why I wanted to go to Singapore was for the food. Particularly Singaporean chili crab because nowhere else can I get this thick flavorful pot of meaty crab.My friend who frequents Singapore told me we should go here and so we did. I decided to wear a white top and shorts because it was pretty hot and humid even in December in SG. If you're reading this, don't make the same mistake.We got there at 5:30pm and there were only 3 tables that were occupied and the hostess was still deliberating if they had a table for us - ummm...the place is practically empty! She told us she can give us a table but we have to be done by 7pm - WTF? You should tell your server and kitchen staff to hurry up then.We weren't even offered bibs after placing our order. We got chili crab, fried mantou, and tofu. We got to cracking the crab and sure enough it landed on my white top and my legs! Then, that's when they us bibs! Too late for that.The food is good. The mantou was good for soaking up the sauce. There are hundreds of seafood restaurants in SG that serve chili crabs - go there.

Long Beach Seafood at Dempsey is a great place to sample Singapore's variations of the crab dish. I had their chance to taste black pepper, salted egg, and chilli crabs in addition to the crab beehoon. Although my favorite is the black pepper crab, all variations were impeccable. Food is 5 stars. The service at their Dempsey location also deserves 5 stars. The staff was attentive; although we didn't feel that we were being watched, as soon as we needed something, the staff appeared to our table. The staff also offered to de-shell the crabs. The decor at the location was upscale. The utensils were new and the table cloth clean. Long beach at Dempsey offers a refined singaporean crab experience. If you prefer a more casual atmosphere, their Long Beach branch is not as formal while the food is as good.

It's all about fingering the crabs baby!You cannot say you've been to Singapore if you have not tried their amazing seafood. More specifically the iconic Singapore chili crab.A perfectly steamed from live mud crab (Samoan crab to Hawaii Yeeps) claws the size of your hand.  Shell cracked then basted in a fresh chili sauce, fragrant herbs, a touch of sugar, and thickened by eggs.  Messy to eat (wear your bib or be prepared to toss your shirt) but so tasty. The warming but not thermonuclear chili flavor, draws out the natural sweetness of the crab. The meat itself, very firm in texture, closer to lobster that crab.  A side of montou (deep fried sweet buns) the perfect accompaniment to mop up the delicious sauce. Heck, they even provide a bowl and spoon so you do not let any of the delicious sauce go to waste, it's filled with the female crab eggs after all..Do not pass on the black pepper crab.  Invented by Long Beach Seafood, outstanding.  The same mud crab, perfectly steamed, shells cracked, but this time sautéed in very finely ground, copious quantities of black pepper.  The dry roasted pepper corns, very spicy, aromatic, with no bitter or acrid flavors. It works even better at bringing out the sweetness of the  crab.  Outstanding.Add a few additional fresh seafood dishes to round out the meal. The razor clam, ordered by the piece, steamed in a gentle soy garlic sauce and topped with vermicelli and crispy garlic is exceptional. The clams, well cleaned and perfectly cooked display and oceanic sweetness and texture of an abalone more than a clam.Crunchy deep-fried prawns cooked from live with freshly fried garlic also amazing. The restaurant knows how to tease the sweetness out of the best seafood.  This prawn dish can be ordered with or without the shell.Note: crab dishes can be done with the traditional mud crab, Australian Crystal crab, or Alaskan King crab though why mess with tradition. Market price by the kilo. 1 kg minimum.What to drink? Tiger beer of course.Service is extremely efficient but always with a smile.  It is surprising that there are no accidents in the hectic dining room with servers rushing between tables.Advance booking required at all locations. Use the website.  Indoor and outdoor seating.  Despite the heat, dine outdoors so the food doesn't cool too quickly.Although the food sounds humble, seafood is rarely inexpensive. This dinner for two inclusive of four beers, tax, and service exceeded $250 SGD. it was worth every penny.I truly cannot wait to get back to fingering one of my favorite crabs of all time

This is my favorite place in Singapore to get chilli crab - mainly because they make each batch fresh and from scratch, and the sauce is always rich, satisfying and with a nice balance between sweet, spicy, sour and savory. If you're lucky, they'll have enormous crabs available which are the absolute best!!! They cost a pretty penny but it's so worth it when you can dunk that giant claw in all the delicious chilli crab sauce. The sauce is so good, I eat it with everything - the crab, additional prawns that I order on the side, mantou (steamed or fried buns, I prefer steamed), mee goreng. If there's a lot leftover, I even take it home to toss with pasta the next day.They do good seafood overall - I've had good experiences with their steamed clams (bamboo clams or pacific clams), prawns (the drunken or steamed ones are my favorite), baby squid (fried in a sweet black sauce that I love), geoduck (expensive but yummy). They also have some good vegetable sides and I really like the mee goreng. Especially when you can eat the mee goreng with the remaining chilli crab sauce. Yum.Because I don't eat crabs in any other style, I consistently come back just for the chilli crabs which are truly the best thing available here. I've had chilli crab in many other restaurants and none of them come close to what Long Beach offers at Dempsey. I've found that their standards can be a little inconsistent in other outlets but Dempsey has always been consistently delicious! Service is great too - you can get plastic gloves and bibs to protect your clothes and hands when handling all that seafood. It just makes the entire experience more pleasant (and it's also great when you don't go home with chilli crab sauce all over your top).

MUST GO! Your life isn't complete without going to Long Beach Seafood when you're in Singapore.My husband and I were skeptical about going out of the way for this restaurant. We were staying at the Mandarin Oriental in Marina Bay. Getting to Dempsey Hill was a hassle and there are so many other good food options closer to us. Still a local coworker insisted that we try Long Beach Seafood... And thus the journey to great food began...Public transit was a hassle. We took the green line on the MRT (train) to Commonwealth then took the 105 bus to Opp Pierce. From there, we walked across a pedestrian bridge, across a lawn, up a hill, thru a construction zone, passed several parking areas and VOILA! We finally arrived. Somehow we ended up in the back of the restaurant? The really nice wait staff ushered us to the front. *whew*Instead of testing our luck at picking random things on the menu, we went with a pre-selected dinner menu. The meal for 2 people cost $148 SGD (which was about $110 USD). Razor clams hadn't been delivered as a result of bad weather... So instead, they gave us some other clams as substitutes but prepared the same way as the razor clams. These were the best clams I've ever had. The clams were stuffed with garlic glass noodles and clam meat. There was also a light soy sauce that complimented the dish. The savory dish was light, flavorful, and left you wishing for more!Up next was the leek flower blossom. I never had this before but it was so very delicious! The leek flower blossom was cooked but still had a nice crunch. Again, it was a very light dish even though it appeared to be stir-fried or sautéed. The main dish was the black pepper crab. This was a life changing experience! The black pepper sauce was thick, flavorful, and spicy! It complimented the huge chucks of crab meat we dig out of the claws. Not only did was this finger licking good, I almost kicked my plate clean!!! I seriously had to go wash my hands and face after this yummy dish.We also had the flat rice noodles with "la la King" sauce, which was a thick gravy sauce with clams and topped with crispy friend wontons. The flavor of this dish was very subtle and elegant.Lastly, we had an amazing dessert of pudding with ice cream and a mango sauce. No words could possibly describe light and yummy this dish was. You'll just have to go try it for yourself!The wait staff was so very kind and attentive. We never had to ask for anything bc they were always a step ahead of us. Our waiter even called a taxi for us to get back to our hotel.The restaurant was also very clean. The food/restaurant standards in Singapore should be commended.

wow, this was awesome. messy, spicy crab but so worth it. we drank wine but this is definitely  a place you want to drink lots of cold beer. service was great. didn't seem like a touristy place at all. my only complaint is how expensive it is. the crab and all the sides we had were great, but I wish it could have been a more reasonable price. oh well, everything in SG is expensive. I'd go back.

Try the Chilli crab. Its gravy was on the sweet side, perfect if downed with fried buns.I was also impressed with their lala horfun, you could taste the wok hay and they gave it a crispy twist. Try it!

There is always this danger of one being an elitist. I could just imagine how the skew of stars would change from an positive curve to a bell curve or even a negative curve. However, I guess I just become one when the price tag reaches a certain point. After all, being in business, I always believe that paying a certain price comes with a certain expectation.Here at Long Beach (Singapore, not California - where the term usually conjures up memories), I will have to be somewhat of an elitist after witnessing my aunt drop down a stash of cash to pay for a dinner welcoming my fiance to Singapore.So Pepper Crab originated here aye? Well, I can believe that is the case as I continued to fight through the sweat pouring out them pores so that my tongue could continue it tonguegasmic tour of the seafood that is provided here.Yet, thing is...that was all that was the splendor this place had to provide. Freaking crabs.Everything else on the menu (with the exception of the fried chicken - which isn't even seafood) was bland and boring at best. I wanted to say I hated everything else BUT let's be honest, the aunt was showing much love to us...and wanted to bring us the "best" as a show of love and welcome.She definitely was a WIN.This restaurant, however, was bordering on a FAIL.Eat pepper crab...and tell the rest of the seafood choices to get a life.Yelp 100: 28/100

A good experience here in general. While we found the dishes pricey, they were well worth it. The drunken prawns and the steamed crab were the two dishes this seafood lover enjoyed most. My only gripe is service. Granted, it was a busy evening, but I didnt like the feeling of being rushed throughout my order. Overall a good meal, would go back on occasion for a celebratory meal perhaps

Was taken here on a public holiday for lunch. We arrived at 2pm so we didn't have to make reservations, but they close the cashier at 3pm so we were hurried to pay for our meal. Apart from that, service here was pleasant and attentive.We had the goose wings, braised duck, spinach with 3 eggs, and jellied pork trotters. The pork trotters were cold and smooth, with a generous amount of meat and skin within, but not much fat, which is good. It came paired with a mild but moreish chili sauce.The goose wings came in the same sauce as the braised duck, and I got a bit tired of that. I was loathe to deal with the wing bones so I ate more of the duck. The braised duck came with a garlic chili sauce, and the gravy spooned on rice makes it a very home-style meal. The duck comes with tofu underneath, so one doesn't get meat overload. The spinach with eggs was done well, but it was too much for the both of us. The eggs were cut in perfect squares - loved the attention to detail.I finished off with dessert; yam paste. The yam paste here isn't the greasy pork lard version, but instead is a mound of taro, with a slice of pumpkin on top, and a light sugar syrup drenching the dessert. Not heavy enough for my palate, but still delish. I expect most grandmothers would be agreeable to this place for family meals. Yum!

Serving up some really authentic Teochew cuisine (or so my relatives say), this restaurant is part of the Jumbo Group franchise so expect slightly higher prices. I'd reserve it for a nice family occasion as this restaurant has a great tablecloth banquet-style setting. You do get a 20% discount for being a Jumbo member though. The final bill (~S$30pp) was not unreasonable considering we were all stuffed with leftovers.I liked that they start off each meal with traditional teochew tea as a palette cleanser, which really sets the mood for the rest of the meal. Unfortunately their signature braised duck was sold out when we arrived, so we ordered the braised chicken instead, which was still quite delicious. We also ordered other signature Teochew dishes, shrimp ball (虾枣) and liver roll (肝花), and the latter was surprisingly very tasty! Each person should have two pieces -- the first to whet the tongue, the second to fully savor it. We also ordered the traditional dried scallop and vegetables, which was a thumbs up! Fried yam is also of course a must. For dessert, they have the classic Or Nee (芋泥) or yam paste with ginko nut and pumpkin, which was well-balanced and not too sweet.Like a typical Chinese restaurant, don't expect much of service; don't hesitate to the wait staff whenever you need something.

This is a place for Teochew food and you can see many families or towkays (businessmen/big bosses) dining here.There are only two dishes which I really like over here - oyster omelette and the yam paste with pumpkin dessert. The other dishes are quite standard or typical of such restaurants. Good old Teochew food. The cold crabs are nice but I prefer the version at Asia Grand. The fried yam stick coated with sugar was also pretty good. The fried ee mian to dip with sugar was somewhat of an acquired taste. I did not really fancy it. Likewise for the seafood fried vermicelli, I thought it was a bit heavy on the Maggi sauce seasoning. This is under the Jumbo group, so if you have the Jumbo card, you can get some discount. Service is spotty. Some days they are good and on other days they can be quite slow and lackluster. But as with old school Chinese restaurants, you are not really there for the service, you are there for the food.

interesting enough everyone raved about the oyster omelette at this restaurant but i just didn't get what they described. my plate of oyster omelette was quite charred and the oysters were miserably small and hard to find in the dish. A family member having eaten this dish before on his first visit raised his concern about the lack of quality of this dish but only to be faced with a very cold reaction from the manager on duty. the manager on duty turned and faced another table even before our conversation was over. His aloof attitude was not appreciated and maybe it would work better if he switches to the entertainment industry since that kind of bad boy attitude garner more fans in the world than do anything for hungry people at a Teochew restaurant.but i do want to praise the older lady servers who were attending to our table. they did their best and really was genuine in wanting to provide good quality service. they were the ones more concerned that our dish of lobster e-fu noodle was never served and still unseen even after 15 minutes of the second notification. There's one dish that i really enjoyed. it was the cold crab. fresh and sweet; each crab was $30. the lobster e-fu noodle that finally showed up after we cut the birthday cake and had desserts was pretty good; the lobster was fresh and succulent. the price tag for that dish was $138. just a note: there is no parking validation.there are private function rooms for use if you have an event, complete with karaoke systems.
Pro: - Karaoke in private rooms, great for bonding - Suckling pig- Braised duck- Interesting appetizer platterCon:- Pricy?

Food was great but service  standard dropped. The place seems understaffed and it's only saving grace is the taste of the dishes. However this dinning experience was really unpleasant as they said they sold out of many items on the menu.The service staff seems a little disgruntled and it really ruined my dinner. Really disappointing

Pre-order the suckling pig. It is the best suckling pig in town now! They serve it roasted in savory Chinese spices, and they actually remove the layer of fat and serve up only the crispy skin with a thin piece of succulent meat under it. How's that for a healthier version of roasted suckling pig! Yummmmmm.....The rest of the teochew dishes are all generally good. The fermented bean steamed chicken is a great, succulent and flavorful. Their rendition of pomegranate chicken is actually served steamed, with a medley of chopped vegetables and sea cucumber cutely wrapped. I would give it a 4.5 stars, but since it is CNY, 5 stars it shall be.Jumbo members get 10% off, and reservations necessary! Make one pronto and go eat some pig.

Chui Huay Lim Teochew Restaurant is pretty posh and the place is nicely decorated, keeping its oriental character while fitting it into the sleekness of modern beauty. Being somewhat a fine-dining restaurant, the prices of the foods are quite high. I do not mind paying high prices for good food but the food at Chui Huay Lim were pretty mediocre. I guess I expected more for the price I was paying so the food was quite disappointing to me. Service was dismal. The staff were pretty rude, and some did not even understand English. They were also very slow and we ended up having to cancel some orders because they took way too long to serve the food to the table.We got the braised duck, which was not bad but not great either. The clay pot tofu we ordered was drenched in gravy that was way too starchy. We also got a serving of black pepper beef which was tasty but again, not impressive.Overall, I find Chui Huay Lim Teochew Restaurant is pretty overpriced. While the decor depicts a fine-dining restaurant, their food betrays their identity, and that is quite a pity.

Very surprised it's run by the Jumbo group - it's so clean!!! Service was also excellent, even if impersonal. The food was good, although not very filling. Loved the tea at the start (I'm not sure what it was but it was divine - my grandma called it "gongfu cha") and the pu-er they refilled was good too.assorted appetizers (so-so, had jellyfish, duck and tofu in soy sauce, ngoh hiang and something else I can't remember), prawn (bad... the sauce just didn't work for me),shark's fin (good - lots of dried scallops and crab inside!),roasted suckling pig (very good - very crispy skin!)steamed fish (so-so, the soup I like to drink at the end was quite sour)mushroom abalone and veggies (good - imo cannot go wrong)fried noodles (so-so, not too salty, and there were fresh scallops)yam paste (I have never liked yam paste :P but  others said it was good)shou tao (nice filling, but too much skin)fruits were standard watermelon honeydew appleI have no idea what the dishes were exactly though because I wasn't the one who ordered (grandma's birthday). Still, I found the course better than most dining establishments overall and everything was fresh. Great for large group get togethers too.And I must repeat how clean it was (relatively speaking). Chinese restaurants are usually dirty to some extent, so I was in a bit of a shock :P

Chui Huay Lim Teochew Cuisine is Jumbo Group's first foray into fine dining. A lot of research has been done before they set up this establishment and it shows. I was told that the management went to several well known Teochew restaurants before coming up with the concept and menu, and the result is great!Food : Steamed pomfret, hee peow (fish maw) soup and orh nee are de rigeur orders when in a Teochew restaurant and we are nothing if not ardent followers of foodie tradition. The pomfret was fresh and steamed to perfection. Soaked in a light tasty broth with hints of tomato, mushroom and ginger, it was excellent. The fish maw soup with crab meat was tasty and rich in flavour, a great substitute for sharks fin soup. We were feeling festive and so we also got the Teochew style roasted suckling pig ... pre-order recommended. We had heard it was one of the restaurant's specialties and for good reason! The crackling was crisp and the pork wasn't too greasy. The cold crabs were quite good too and we really liked the orh nee. The texture of the yam was just right and it wasn't too heavy and cloying. With the addition of pumpkin and gingko nuts, it was the perfect ending to a Teochew meal.Ambience : Modern Chinese decor, very clean layout.Service : Prompt and friendlyGood for business lunches and family celebrations. Jumbo members get 20% off.

The chicken meat was beautifully grilled where the outer skin had a nice charred taste and the meat inside was still moist and tasty. Depending on your order, they will have a special sauce glaze over their meat. With my colleague, we both ordered a whole chicken and 3 sides:3 Beans Salad - tangy dressing over 3 types of beans, the red kidney beans, chickpeas and yellow beans. I also like the slices of onions and capsicum thrown in. Coleslaw - rich and creamy and slightly tangy, the vegetables used were also fresh. Grilled Vegetables - sliced vegetables that had that nicely grilled taste. A great side dish that is light and tasty.Service, while friendly, is a tad slow. The food also takes a while to arrive so may not good to eat here if you're in a rush.

I would love to give no stars for Nando's but I guess the minimum one star is fine. I walked by this place and it looked interesting. I was seated quickly but no one came by to take my order. I waited for more than 25 mins and servers looked at me and walked away. I gave up and left and no one asked me for how my meal was. The poor service is absolutely a game changer for me. In Singapore one is made to pay for service charge whether or not service was good or bad. Don't eat here if you can avoid it.

This is not a place you go for good service. This is a place you go for great, comparatively cheap grilled chicken. The Portuguese salad with chicken is my favorite because the slices of chicken that come with it are better seasoned and easier to eat than the larger chicken pieces like the half chicken. All of the fino sides are awesome. I usually order them all.

I've been back a few times now to this location and the service has been consistently poor, slow, and neglectful, even with an empty dining room. They are always understaffed, with for instance one cook and one host who moves back and forth between recruiting outside and (barely) waiting tables inside. Meanwhile, it seems two or three people are always hiding behind the register doing nothing. I don't even bother ordering the famous free flow lemon tea here, since it is extremely difficult to get it refilled even once. Don't bother waiting for your bill as you're unlikely to receive it. Just proceed directly to the register and pay there. If fortunate, you will see your server twice (order and initial receipt of food) without hunting someone down. I highly recommend the Nando's in Malaysia, as they have had great service and food. This location simply doesn't live up to the Nando's name and gives a bad impression of the franchise.

Nandos ..... Hmm i heard about this place a few years back  ...... In Perth itself i saw  this restaurant located near the central train station but did not try it back than.If you read my review you will know the reason why??My friend introduced me to this and i was like ..... what's that .... only chicken served .... You sure its nice ....After much debating with my friend i decided to order the 1/2 chicken thigh. We are chatting while waiting for the food to be served .The serving of food is alittle slow ... Ta da ..... i have my 1st mouthful of the chicken. Its so juicy and tender and caught me off guard.... it really taste nice and i had try all the different peri peri sauce.Its worth the money spend ya .......

4* but docking one for poor service.Never had Nando's before, but my friend said they have it in a few places and it's cheaper abroad (big surprise hah).The wedges were really good. Like, super good, I'm not sure if they sprinkled stuff on top but it was really yummy. I think I may have liked it more than the chicken, which was great too.So next, I really did enjoy the extra hot platter - the chicken was far better than I thought it would be. Really flavourful and the skin was crispy in just the way I liked it. You get two sides with the platter, although we had 3. The previously mentioned yummy wedges was one of them. We also had some spinach. I enjoyed it, although it was a tad sour and probably had more spicy sauce mixed inside. As the previous reviewer has mentioned, service was pretty appalling from the start to the end... and it wasn't even super crowded! No communication from the staff (we didn't even know they were seating us because the staff just walked past without a word, expecting us to magically understand we were to follow), they forgot to get our water after saying they would, couldn't settle the bill when we wanted to = wasting our time... it's as bad as it could get for inattentiveness. I shudder to think what it would be like on a busy day!

Your typical Nando's fare, which is a good thing if you're a franchise. It's the same Nando's you'll find in other parts of the world, no better, no worse, maybe a bit more expensive. If you're a fan of the infamous Nando's Peri Peri chicken, then don't worry, you'll get your fix here. For new-comers, just stick with the Peri-Peri chicken, and get the cinnamon sweet potatoes as a side. You can thank me later.

This is my first Nando's experience and wow, the chicken pretty good I got to say. But that is about it.I had the Extra Hot Full Platter for 3 with Wedges, Spinach, Corn on the Cob and Spicy Rice as the sides. I can't complain about the chicken as it wasn't dried out and seasoned well. Wedges were awesome with the sauces; Spinach was too much like preserved veggies for my liking; Corn was meh and; Spicy Rice isn't even worth mentioning.Service was pretty mediocre as they were never attentive and all crowded around the kitchen area. This kind of got on my nerves after requiring their attention for 4 times and having to wait a long while for each. Good thing the chicken is awesome enough to turn things around for me.

If you need a quick bite and like spicy chicken, then Nando's is the place to be. If you're looking for atmosphere, excellent service, and incredible food, you'll have to look around. It isn't that the food is bad or the servers inept, it is just that Nando's falls solidly within the 'average to  barely-above-average' chain restaurant. If I was the owner, I might give the staff some extra training in customer service, because we had a problem with our bill once and they seemed skeptical, and I felt as if I had to prove to several staff members that the mistake was on their end. Either way, decent food if you're in need of a quick meal.

The chicken was tasty, as expected and I liked the roasted cinnamon sweet potatoes. But that's about it.The service however was poor. Very slow - not because they were understaffed but because the staff didn't seem to take the initiative to serve tables. They were either chatting away or standing listlessly outside the restaurant, without being attentive to the diners. I had to call out for service several times. What was even more aggravating was that when we finally got a waitress' attention to take our order, she came by, then told us to wait for "a while", and then quickly disappeared. She then resumed her place outside the restaurant and we were again left hanging, waiting to order. What's up with that? It took maybe 5-7 minutes before we got the attention of another waitress to take our order.This outlet suffers from badly trained and disinterested staff.  I also don't agree with the prices.

Wanted to come here for lunch on a Friday. First in queue, multiple tables free, we were completely ignored by staff for a good 10 minutes. The place was about 2/3s full, and waiters were busy attending already seated guests. It seemed like they'd rather not have us because it would have meant even more work. We walked away. Grossly understaffed. Maybe in less busy times an option.

The burger bar is located in the middle of a row of shophouses. The place looks small. Although there is no aircon, I could feel the wind blowing from outside. The staff is quite friendly and takes my order from my table without me going to the counter. Payment is made after having the meal.PORTO POLO (BERG $14.5/Small $11.5)Grilled Chicken in Spicy Portuguese Marinade, Lettuce, Tomato, Red Onion, Cheddar Cheese, Homemade Peri-Peri Sauce & Aioli.Through the staff's recommendation, I order this burger. It looks huge. It tastes quite spicy and the patty is a bit dry to me. I could not finish it although I have not eaten whole day.BERGS Homemade Lemonade ($4)The lemonade is quite refreshing. Just nice to cool down during a hot afternoon.Overall the food is not bad. Service is great. There is no much crowd around during the sunday afternoon.

For me, this place is above average because of the size of the burgers. But tastewise, I'd give it slightly above average. It wasn't excellent because the beef patty just wasn't all that great. It's hard to describe, the texture to me seemed dry and "rubbery". Could be that it's a leaner cut of beef. I like the Bergs sauce, which I can best describe as a teriyaki, BBQ, onion blended glaze. The Haji Land location is one of three with the other two located in Amoy St. & East Coast Road. Note: operating day/hours vary by location. Beer and wine on the menu too. Be warned, their Bergs-sized burgers are huge!

Gave Bergs another shot, this time at the Arab Street venue. Nice and cozy little hole in the wall on a bustling and touristy Arab Street.Our burgers were tasty and well done, definitely hit the spot for our burger craving.There's a $4 option to add chips to your burger along with a drink (ice lemon tea or lemonade). Both drinks are ultra-sugary but the lemonade a little less so.Bergs beef burger patties have a unique seasoning that I can't quite pinpoint. It's not your typical burger but it's tasty nonetheless.Other pluses to eating at Bergs - they have a washroom stocked with nice paper towels to dry your hands which is loads better than using a hawker washroom only to come out with dripping wet hands b/c a certain someone hasn't picked up the habit of carrying around a hanky or tissues.They also have napkins here that they give out generously, another plus for the reason stated above.It's not gourmet but I'm easy to please. Napkins and a place to sit? You're good in my books!

I ordered the small Miss Piggy burger, which I thought was quite big. It was more like a regular-sized burger I'm used to back in the States. You can add $5 to your burger and get fries and a drink (iced tea or lemonade). I thought the burger was ok although I wouldn't consider it gourmet. The service was really good.

checked out this place on a 3pm on a saturday. awesome location at haji lane, perfect for people watching if you sit outside. inside, it had a really chill feel and is a nice spot to meet up with a group of friends for some beer and rowdy catch-up. noticed that they have a happy hour from 5-8, where beer bottles go as low as $6, so i can see it doing just that. the menu was pretty interesting and they had a number of decent veggie options. burgers come in two sizes; small and burgs (big) and hover around $10-$15 bucks, with the option of chips and a drink for +$4. they even offer a 3 (mini) burger sample for $15, for the indecisive lot. i went with the bergs miss piggy ($14.50, beef pattie, bacon, lettuce, tomato, red onion, aioli, bergs sauce & edam cheese) and was quite excited to sink in since it looked pretty damn good. sadly, i was underwhelmed. the meat was totally anemic and lacked a nice chew and sauce was SO sweet. like i get sweet bbq sauce, but this was just kind of ick. also, the bacon tasted kind of weird. i mean, i finished the thing, but i definitely would not be back for another, unless one of their veggie burgers fares a lot better. the only redeeming thing was how if you join their fanclub on facebook, they'll knock 15% off your bill. but i guess, for that price, i was hoping for something better.

Located in an alley way behind Ophir Road/Beach Road, this place serves awesome Aussie burgers. By awesome Aussie, I mean thick patties, hamburger buns don't fall apart, and the toppings are very good.  It's a fun place where the menu is interesting and they server burgers in paper bags rather than plates. Kind of different. I got the Bailout Burger, which is a Greek burger with feta cheese. You can get a lamb burger, burgers with bacon and pineapple, and if you don't like what's on their menu, you can add whatever toppings you want. They have very thick steak fries.The place is open to the outside, so there's no aircon. They served us free water, always a plus. Prices are inclusive of GST, so it's quite reasonable.

Walking around trying to think of what to eat for dinner, my husband pointed to this tiny shop. I was beyond tired and agreed. So we line up, I order our food and wanted to find in, alas all the seats were taken and no one seemed to care that we had a 3year old in tow who needed to be fed. We too our food to go but couldn't find anywhere around Paragon that would be suitable to sit and eat a take away meal. As we wondered around we made our way back to Tori-Q and woohoo, there was a spare spot. So we squished in, my 6'4" husband, daughter and I. I was adamant that our meal would by now be lacklustre due to being carted around, but I was wrong. Everything was tasty, I particular the chicken balls. My husband had to go back for a second round of those!So food - awesome; service - great; ambiance - poor. But still gets 4 stars!

A fairly decent and quick meal if you happen to walk by. I do think their serving sizes could be a bit larger for their chicken box offerings, and the ladies taking your order shedding a smile wouldn't hurt.The chicken meatballs are probably the best aspect of the meal. Overall, satisfying, but nothing I'd generally crave or go out of my way for.

Some things are ridiculously priced - $1.30 for 1 fried shrimp? Craziness.The chicken balls are pretty yummy, the chicken kabob is decent, the chicken wontons are decent. Overall not a bad snack or meal if you add rice.
Yummy!Decently priced!Great Choices!EAT UP! by itself or a bento :)

Always yummy! For a quick bite in between hop by Tori-Q and enjoy the flavor!Be it either the Tsukune (which is widely known as chicken balls in the decent version) or even the full Yakitori you will not be disappointed.The items here are well priced and I never had a bad dish. I would recommend though you stick to the chicken dishes as those tend to be better in my opinion. I had a couple pork varieties and barely got them off the skewer.Enjoy! Num num...-s :)

Tori-Q is great for a quick bite when one has neither the time nor effort to sit down for a full yakitori meal. I love the tsukune (chicken meatballs) and the chicken ... the kawa (chicken skin) is amazingly crisp ... I used to wonder who would buy chicken skin until I tried it ... and I was sold! The ebi is not bad as well ... the pork is a tad on the tough side so I generally prefer the chicken options. The sauce has gotten a bit too sweet for me so I usually opt to have my yakitori without. If you are feeling really hungry, opt for the bento box option with rice, it's a pretty good deal!Service is generally friendly and efficient.

If you're in Paragon and looking for a budget bite, Tori-Q is your answer. Basically Tori-Q offers "lunch boxes" comprising of steamed Japanese rice, 4 yakitori sticks and a side of pickles. Favorites include, bacon wrapped asparagus and chicken with green peppers. These yakitori sticks are made freshly throughout the day which you can observe through their class kitchen at every outlet. More of a take-away place than a sit in. Think of it as Japanese fast food if you will!

fantastic seafood and zi char at this casual chinese restaurant nearish the singapore expo - really, it's rather out of the way (for us), but it's now become my family's go-to place for crabs and the like, and well-worth travelling to. the place has been packed to the rafters even by early evening (we popped here on two consecutive sundays because it was so good) - but the prices are reasonable, the food is absolutely commendably executed, and service is both sincere and quick.having spent a few years away, I've gained newfound appreciation for places like this one - where you can viably decide not to cook and pay a little more for a balanced meal: this isn't really an option you often get in london - not such variety at equivalent prices, anyway.the food here is great - and it draws large crowds despite occupying two shop spaces in an obscure location, so I recommend reservations, and also that you head down for a spot of great seafood no matter where you are. it beats those too-crowded options at the east coast - you know which ones I mean - in price, service and quality.

Food standard fluctuates. Same dish can be delicious but bland on another visit. Lower your expectations and enjoy whatever is served.Wasabi prawns lack the heat.Nai bai claypot is unimpressive.KL hokkien mee is nothing to shout about.Crystal hor fun is almost tasteless.Salted egg crab is ok this visit. Very fresh.Deep fried prawns in beancurd skin is nice and fresh.Hotplate otah is nice.Tong po rou could be softer.Sambal kang kong is nice.

My friends and I were on a quest for crabs and we googled for new places that we haven't checked out and read about this place call Big Eater Seafood. We decided to check it out as none of us have been there although it seemed to be a popular seafood restaurant in Simpang Bedok. They are super packed and even provide valet services as parking is limited here.I am very intrique by the wall of crab shells graffti that their customers have left behind. Tucked away in the east, we tried some of their popular dishes like the salted egg crabs and the KL hokkein mee, pretty yummy and we were not disappointed. Definitely worth coming back and checking out their other dishes. I love how the management at this chain restaurants name their chain stores pretty catchy. This particular one is call big eater seafood, they have the other outlets by the name of Grand Eater  and Master Crab.

Standard orders here are 1 x chili crab, 1 x salted egg yolk crab, 1 vegetable dish, and the not to be missed KL hokkien mee. BE is unusual in the sense that it's a largish, airy restaurant; quite unlike the crowded and claustrophobic settings with grumpy aunties that seem to be the norm at other seafood places. And surprisingly, the service is actually good. The aunties are friendly, and it's easy to catch their attention for advice (are we ordering too much??) and extra drinks. The crabs are firm and fresh, though the experts will tell you not to order when the moon is full or something like that. The salted egg yolk crab is better than the chili, while he KL hokkien mee is a happy heart attack on a plate; a mess of black stringy noodles and liberally sprinkled with lard. Oh so good. Prices are ok, and have been correspondingly adjusted for inflation, much to the the dismay of customers. There's valet parking too, which is a good option due to limited lots.

These days the trend is an increase in price with a decrease in nice. Unfortunately, the trend has hit Big Eater. While they still serve up a mean salted egg crab, the rest of the menu leaves a lot to be desired.  The seafood they served previously used to be one of the freshest around. The crabs were meaty and juicy, but these days they seem to have gotten considerably smaller.Bad points aside, the dried chilli frog is pretty decent, along with their signature KL hokkien mee. These are worth trying but I doubt its going to be enough to warrant a second visit.

Big Eater is popular seafood restaurant near Simpang Bedok. It is constantly packed with people, especially on weekends. I love their Malaysia styled fried Hokkien Mee (dark sauce!!!). On some days, the noodles seem to be too overloaded with lard. But usually, it should be fine. They are also known for their Seafood Crystal Horfun, which is cooked with generous portions of fresh seafood. The deep fried beancurd skin is also worth a try! Fresh seafood wrapped with beancurd skin. Although sometimes the wait can really be long (be prepared to wait up to 20 minutes on packed days!), I like that the seafood they use is really fresh and they give generous portions. Last but not least, I think they need to space out the place a little more. It can get really noisy when the restaurant's packed with people.

Big eater is a very popular eatery that services Chinese, Zi Char, Fujian, Seafood,  and Cantonese food. It is a corner store that takes up 2 units. The chili crab is delicious and so is the hokkien mee. Against my will I have been dragged here several times, but the food doesn't stop to surprise me. What erks me about this restaurant is the congestion and noise. They obviously are maximizing space with the amounts of tables set up. I wouldn't say much about the atmosphere, I wouldn't even give it more than one star, but the real reason why this place is so packed is because of the quality of the food.The service is constantly busy and is a task just trying to waive one down. The prices are reasonable, very satisfactory for the great food they serve!

For the experience itself, this is a pretty nice area to stop by after you're done with the Singapore Flyer. Situated right under the Flyer, this entire area is located on the first floor. Modeled similar to a hawker centre, you'll see different food stalls lined up. Prices here are a wee bit higher than the usual stalls at other hawker centers. For the food options, there is a huge array of typical Singaporean dishes, some Indonesian food, Chinese and desserts. For food, I tried the laksa (prawn noodle soup) and found it quite lack luster.
