Much like everyone else, I come here for the dry specialty meesua.The noodles are coated with this oil, chili and vinegar dressing, then topped with minced pork, sliced pork, ikan bilis and fresh lettuce. Served with a bowl of simple broth.It's delicious and open 24/7 except Sunday, which means its perfect for a late supper after drinks. There isn't much else to say except that you HAVE to try this dish. A true delicacy at only $4/bowl.

BK eating house saved my tummy more then once while I was in SG.It was located right across from where I was staying.Because of the late night hours... I was able to come here in the middle of the night and fill up on cheap eats. Everything from kaya toast and teh, noodles and rice dishes and lime juice. This place is popular with the locals and I can see why.Thank you BKEH for my numerous meals here!

Extremely cheap place to eat. I was surprised by how cheap the food was and the amount of food they gave me. You could probably buy one of everything and still have money left over! Can't really comment on the sanitary conditions but seemed safe enough to eat. Feel free to sit with some random strangers. They won't mind.

Yes. Mee sua. Yes. Mmm. We always went here after a night out and were never disappointed. I get mine without cockles and easy on the vinegar. My friends always ordered extra noodles and meat. We haven't tried the other stalls and we never really needed to. The mee sua is a beast.

I absolutely love the mee sua here. I haven't tried anything else but it deserves four stars on the strength of the mee sua alone. The noodles are brilliant, the sauce is spicy, the fishballs are standard and the pork is delicious. Eat the mee sua, you won't regret it.
I've went to the Park Mall branch some time ago. Ambience was good. but pricing for the menu was quite expensive in my opinion, expensive for tea time. don't think i would visit again

Kith is a cute, cozy place on the quieter side of Robertson Quay .  It's one of those places I'd been meaning to try for years, literally, and I finally got round to it about about 2 months ago - this tells you I've got quite a backlog of reviews!Kith offers a decent selection of food (ranging from biccies to small bites to traditional full breakfasts and to sandwiches) at reasonable price points, e.g. $10 for a sandwich.  Our table only tried several simple food items like the smoked salmon sandwich, brioche with yogurt and strawberries, and a tuna + green apple toastie.  Even simple dishes can sometimes go awry, but I'm happy to report that all these items were well executed and presented.Where I felt a bit let down was in the coffee department.  I'd heard a lot about Kith's coffee and had been tremendously looking forward to trying it.  However, the coffee was disappointingly average.  I'd certainly put places like Toby's Estate and Smitten above Kith in the coffee stakes.Still, Kith is a pleasant place that's hard to dislike.  It's a comfortable place which is family-friendly, pet-friendly and offers ample people watching opportunities.  If I lived in RQ, I'd be happy to call it my local.

Quirky little cafe by the river (canal?). I like how it's hidden from everything else, like a little sanctuary.Brunch sets and coffee here are average but the laid back atmosphere makes up for it. Salads and juices are great, the first time I visited Kith, I wanted something more than what was offer on the blackboard so I asked if I could request for a specific salad. I was in luck because the person who would soon say yes was none other than lady boss Jane herself.So I had a ginger grilled chicken salad with baby spinach, wild rocket, japanese cucumber and cherry tomatoes, and have had it again every time I return. It tastes awesome.Perfect for a lazy weekend.

If you like your food home-made style, then you should check this place out. A good time to go would be during breakfast so you can try out the toast and homed strawberry jam that is quite good actually. Coffee on the other hand, was just average and nothing to shout about. The place is quite stuffy so don't come overdressed or you'll be perspiring throughout your meal, which is never good.

Kith Café is an awesome hole in the wall along the Singapore River. It actually recently just expanded but before was literally a tiny little space frequented by the River Valley neighborhood. Staff is super friendly and the food is simple but very satisfying. Go for their breakfast which is served with the best toast in Singapore and home-made strawberry jam. Their coffee is pretty great too. Try the Kith macchiato, which is espresso, chocolate, topped with a marshmallow. They recently expanded to a bigger space, in the same location. Have lunch outdoors facing the Singapore River. They also just opened a new branch in Park Mall, serving dinner as well.

Paired with the glistening surface of the Singapore River and the occasional bumbleboat whizzing by, a sip of ice-cold liquefied Nutella blended with nuttily fragrant hazelnut ice cream over at Kith Café is the rest-stop for winners after a day-long poach at flea markets at Clarke Quay. Drink it before it melts - it is good to the very last drop!

Kith is the little cafe with outdoor seating right along the river to the west of the Martin Road bridge.  This is a favorite of congregations of expat wives with black spandex leggings walking their dogs.  Their brunch-y fare hits the spot - especially the smoothies - but don't expect huge portions.  The atmosphere is homey, friendly and sweet.  A nice place to meet friends, especially on weekdays when it's not as crowded as on the weekends.
Love the bfast in here w the view n services are great too. Its still my fave plcs to go for bfast among all 3 outlets that they have in sg.

A great little cafe down at Rob Quay. This place is always swelling with people, no matter what day of the week and once you have been in there it is evident why. Great coffee, fresh, tasty simple food and mouth watering fruit juices every time. Service with a smile is guaranteed. I've eaten many of their meals in the past and each time they have been delicious.

Right along the river...walking difference from severalHotels..we were at four points and found it handy..prices are pretty reasonable by Singapore standards...latte was really good...I had a bacon egg and cheese toast sandwich and it was only $6 and it was really good...wish they were open earlier for us jet lagged folks.

I stopped by here when wandering from Clarke Quay towards Robertson Quay when the hunger and heat got the better of me and I just had to stop somewhere. I saw Kith and recalled that I had been at their other location by Dhoby Ghaut and did not find it horrible so I was up for giving it a shot (and to be honest at this point I would probably even have given McDonalds a chance). Kith has a pretty relaxed setting at a corner of a house with some shade but it does not really have any seats inside so even if it is shaded it is still fairly warm.I had some pretty decent pasta with a pretty good flat white while S went for a toastie and a freshly pressed juice. Neither of these were anything special but more what one can expect and prices are a bit higher than I would like to pay but then it is Robertson Quay after all so perhaps to be expected. I have since been a few more times and they are in a sense reliable, there has so far never been anything amazing nor anything really disappointing. It can tend to get a bit too noisy around as many families with children appear to like to come here and at least when I have been there it has been the type of people who do not feel like telling their kids to behave and take it easy so if that disturbs you it may not be the best place.

I was looking for a simple place to grab a quick bite of breakfast before I continued my exploration of Singapore, and I had walked past here the day before so I decided to check it out. I must say that it wasn't really the best place that I had visited here in Singapore, but then again you can't always expect to strike it lucky when exploring a new city. Okay, I do have to say that the staff were pretty good, but when I looked at the menu there really wasn't anything all that appealing. The place was pretty small, so all of the seats were outside, and while their coffee was okay, it wasn't the best. Mind you, the locals seem to quite like the place since there were always people gathering around here (usually mums with their strollers). However if I am ever back this way I'd probably give this place a miss.

Excited to try the place. Woke early on a Sunday morning and looking for spot nearby to "break" my fast. I was happy to see that this cafe opened early and served simple breakfast that I'm looking for. Initial impressions are that the spot gets a lot of recurring business which is always a good sign.I ordered a pretty standard breakfast that I would fix at home in the states. Eggs, bacon and some wheat toast. They also had fresh juice, I had the watermelon. For lack of a better word, it was homey. Just what I was looking for. It wasn't anything extraordinary but the cafe gave me enough to want to come back and try out the specials. It looks like people were very keen on the Kith Coffee, so I need to come back and get that. I love the neighborhoody feel and the friendly service. I'll definitely come back and will be making this part of my breakfast go to places.

I feel this cafe has good food potential and was certainly recommend. Coffee is quite strong which I do enjoy. My chocolate crossaint was great and partners mango smoothly delicious. However the bacon, egg, tomato toastie I felt was a little lack luster. What really let this place down was the speed of service. It took us 30mins to get the toastie and crossaint, which we needed to ask for as a reminder. Also be prepared to sit outdoor or take away. As there is no indoor seating.

I've been coming here for so long..sometimes you forget to highlight a place because it's always there. What I like about Kith is that it's kinda cute and quirky, it's always sincere and honest..and that reflects in the coffee, food and service.It operates out of a tiny space but they expand quite a bit outside. The tables and chairs are built for small people (luckily I'm one) but many tall expatriates seem to squeeze in comfortably (kid in tow). I personally think the old location was prettier inside..more seating but the new location is less food-fumey and has more shade so I think overall it's better.The food is simple and straightforward but there are little touches of brilliance. Love their white bread in the big brek always nicely toasted and love the homely strawberry jam - it really looks like someone spent all day cooking it on the hearth.Free wifi - always a nice bonus.Prices for the big brek and coffee are attractive. I've had the toastie several times for a lighter bite and it's very simple but it's served nice and hot with a tart apple salad on the side.The coffee is not the best but it's usually a nice to good cup..at $3.80 it's worth it. If you get a cup that's over-extracted and bitter, give your feedback to the staff. I think they will hasten to replace it.

Kith is definitely my favorite brunch spot at Robertson Quay. It's cozy, the coffee's good and food is great - especially for the price.It's right down the street from where I live. So when I need some down-time to myself on the weekend, i'd head down here with a good book for a cup of latte and sandwiches. If the weather is nice you can people-watch by the river while enjoying your meal too! Love!On to the food - I usually get one of their sandwiches. It's easy no frills sandwich and cheap for what it is - they're priced at $8,$10 and $15. My favorite is the smoked salmon one for $10.I've had their big breakfast too and it's relatively cheap for about $15-16. It's a proper breakfast. Their mini toasties are good for if you don't feel like having any of the above but still want something to nibble on.Coffee is excellent.The only down side is, seating is mostly outdoors and there are no A/C, which can be downright unbearable when it's especially hot in Singapore

Given that I had low expectations for this place, I was pretty impressed with the food and service. We were a group of four and though it was just, we were seated in a matter of a few minutes. I ordered a cheese pizza and pineapple ginger juice and my husband ordered some roast beef wrap thing. Both were pretty good (not to-die-for but not bad) and the juice was quite refreshing.

Who love Mondays? Well I do 'cos I'm having lunch at kith's cafe. A little Monday pick-me-up lunch of Spaghetti Meatballs and Flat White makes my Monday that much sweeter. My first time here, I was abit disappointed that the place was a bit small (no seating inside) but managed to get a seat outside, facing the river. However, since it was a Monday, there wasn't much crowd save for the odd Caucasian couple with kids, Caucasian yuppies and a few passer-bys getting some takeaway coffee. The view was good - luckily the sky was overcast and the weather was cool; I can't imagine what it would be like if it is a hot sunny day!  Food was ok but coffee gets my nod of approval! I drank one cup and got another one to take back to the office. Will definitely drop by again - but not on weekends!

This is always a stop for us along our walk. Great place to see friendly and smiling people. Breakfast is our favorite time here. However, lunch is delicious as well. Great coffee, and all at reasonable prices. Favorite stopping point for me on my frequent walks/jogs

The interior is very small- a couple of bar seats, and a long bench for a large group. Furnishing is pretty spartan, the legs of the bar and chairs reminds me of book stacks. Feels pretty much like an old classroom with the blackboard as well. The 'alfresco dining' is in fact a couple of tables and chairs/stools scattered along the corridor. Fits very much into the home and patio concept. I can see how the residents are drawn to this little spot.Breakfast food is a must have (if i have my way that is). I would also insist on all day breakfast too. We were there for tea so we didn't try the food.Kith's scone looks pretty but tastes crappy and it got worse as the temperature dropped. The texture is almost cardboard-ish and dry. It was only a little better with the.. wait for it... WHIPPED cream (oh how i hate it when they serve whipped instead of clotted). The jam was kinda weird with the watery texture. It looks like it was curdled and then defrosted. Anyway, just avoid the scone at all cost.Drinks are good though.

Friendly service, good food, reasonable prices (for Singapore) and litle unexpected added touches like apples with the toastie that turn this suburban corner cafe from ordinary to extraordinary¡!! Highly recommended but you'll need to beat off the joggers and mums with bubs to find a seat on a sunny day...

A good advantage of staying relative near town is the accessibility to all these little cafes that are sprucing up in town. Kith Cafe has become one of my usual brunch places on the weekends to grab a quick bite with "free" parking. My typical brunch there would be their hotdog and a glass of  lychee watermelon iced blended. Kith Cafe is very popular with expat families and increasingly popular with the locals too.  Great place for informal group gathering and even playdates for the kids. It can be quite chaos  on weekends with kids and pets around.  Well, its one of the very few cafes that is both kids and pets friendly. Recently, my husband and I brought my 8 months old baby girl along to have brunch. She loves to sit and watch the older kids play. I think she must be wishing that she is old enough to join in the fun. Great place to people watch by the river too!

In all honesty, i can't see why theres so much hype about this place? probably cos of its indie concept and the fact that it appeared on Monocle.The tables and chairs were pathetic and tiny. The view... well by the canal (wouldn't really call it a river tho it connects to the Singapore River)Coffee was decent, but the toastie I had was terrible. I ordered a egg and ham toastie. it was very homemade style, which wasn't quite what i was looking for. Worst part of the toastie was that the scrambled eggs inside was definitely cooked eons ago and was too dry. more like a scrambled egg bits.Kitchen looked make-shift, small and dirty.

I thought the coffee here was excellent. I also had the toast with Jam for breakfast. The bread wasn't great, but the jam appeared to be homemade and was quite good although they don't really give you enough of it to cover the giant pieces of bread. On this weekend, the place looked like an expat daycare center because of all the toddlers running around--that could be a positive or negative depending on your point of view but just be aware. Plenty of seating outside though and a nice place to have a cup of joe.

Another addition to the brunch places popping up all over the city, Kith café is located along Robertson Quay and provides expats, families and yuppies with good coffee and sandwiches. On weekends, Kith is generally crowded unless you come a little later in the afternoon. I usually order an unsweetened iced coffee and a cheese and bacon toastie (I love the little apple slices they provide on the side to temper the savouriness of the toastie with crunchy sweetness). Sitting outside along the sidewalk with a newspaper and coffee at hand is a great way to spend a peaceful Sunday.

We walked with our dog close to three miles from Tangling Mall along Orchard road, through Ft. Canning park, down to Clarke Quay and finally Robertson Quay. Having the dog with us limited the places we could eat at but then we found Kith. They were happy to let us sit outside with him, even providing water for him. We ordered the smoked salmon sandwich and the steak sandwich. We also ordered the pineapple and ginger drinks. The service was prompt and friendly. The drinks were cold and refreshing, never having tasted pineapple and ginger before. The sandwiches were very tasty, the steak getting the slight edge over the smoked salmon. The side order of bacon for the dog was tasty enough that a couple of pieces did not make it to the intended customer. All in all it was a good experience, we will be back.

Truly enjoyed Sunday brunch at the Edge... I liked how the food was fresh and plentiful, a wide selection so you're not at a loss for choice. The quality and the service was great. It seems that a lot of people are more interested in drinking than eating but that also meant our glasses were always topped up and we didn't have to fight or queue for the popular items as you would at other buffets. Don't recall how much it was as my friends took me out but I would definitely recommend if you are looking for value for money and a more classy buffet.
The spread at Edge definitely trumped the one at Rise. I really enjoyed the waffle counter because, 1) waffles, 2) they made it fresh! So it came out hot and toasty.Good ambience, and good wine.

So this is going to be my shortest review ever ! I think everybody's heard enough about the food and the spread and the ambience already. And I'm not going to disagree with any of the other reviews about the edge, because the food, the spread and the ambience are just as good as everybody says it is. I just want to say something about service leadership at edge. In reviewing the service at the edge, I will say one thing: the team in charge of service wants you to have a seamlessly extraordinary experience. In fact, I'll go one better and  say that they seem to take it personally!Here's just one example. We ordered a dish of curried chicken that was part of buffet but off their usual menu. This didn't arrive, and it truly wasn't a big deal given all the food  we didn't end up trying; just not humanly possible or healthy to in my opinion.  The concierge not satisfied with more than just the usual apologies,  made sure to leave us with a small token of appreciation. It certainly cost them next to nothing but bought my admiration and loyalty forever. Service at this level may be something that is usual stateside, but so very unusual in Singapore and so very refreshing to see!!   There will be those who point to the less than responsive service of the floor staff, but I'm happy to overlook it if the service leadership team is so committed to good service that they take it personally.  If this is the attitude of leadership, slow service staff and another practical details will work themselves out over time.  I will continue to give them my custom as long as that is the case!  Kudos concierge team at edge!!

Been here around 5 times as my family loves this buffet. The quality and variety of the food is consistent. Decent food with a variety of the usual-seafood, dim sum on certain days, various Singaporean dishes including laksa, chicken rice and other foods that can be found over Singapore. Despite the raving reviews, I found myself kinda disappointed with the spread-nothing much exciting or special that made it worth its price. What makes this worth a trip would be the dessert bar, filled with ice cream, more than 10 types of cakes, pudding and all including meringues, crème brulee, pandan cake, nyonya kueh, waffles and more. The service is good but not exceptional. Overall, this buffet might appeal to those hungry for specific types of food in mind and are particular about the quality. Not a personal favourite but probably worth a try if you're in the vicinity or staying at the hotel

wow, what a crazy good buffet. came here a few times when having meetings in the Pan Pacific.so many stations! lots of fresh seafood, shellfish and sushi. soups, italian food, asian noodles, fresh fruit and an amazing dessert stop that was like a pastry, chocolate and ice cream store all rolled into one

This is a nice international buffet located inside the Pan Pacific Hotel (near Suntec) on the 3rd floor. The food quality is generally quite good and there are tons of different options, like Indian, Japanese, Western, seafood, and local foods. The Indian dishes were a bit too salty on my visit, but the seafood (lobster, crab) was great. My favorite dish was the wagyu beef, which I recommend highly. This was a dinner visit, but I have also attended the breakfast buffet, which has a great variety of selections. It is pretty safe to go at any time of day. Also, while buffets are generally not associated with quality food in the US, you should not be turned away from this place. It is a classy and tasty buffet. Although there is plenty of seating space, it can fill up, so it is safer to make a reservation a day or two in advance. We visited on new year's eve and the staff members were very energetic. There were also different dining options for the holiday, so you may want to check on the different offerings based on when you plan to visit.
Exceptional and tasty. Really enjoyed the selection and the food was quite delicious. My only qualm is the juice bar. Where's the fresh squeezed anything??

The food was good, don't get me wrong, but I'm rating this place 3 stars because I think it lacks value. I think there was way too much food to try, and not enough tummy space. If you are looking for a good spread for dessert, this is not your place. It's more of a main course kind of place.I came here for dinner. They had an impressive spread of seafood, including lobsters. There was an array of Indian foods, which were quite good, and Chinese food (I liked the soup), Western styled dishes, and grill etc. I can't quite remember everything. Everything was cooked well. My only issue is that you can try maybe one bite of half the items, and you're done with dinner. I think I would have been happier with a smaller spread with a smaller price tag.Lastly, we came here for work with a guest. Their credit card machine was not working, and they asked us to wait a little while they rebooted. We ended up waiting for 30 min, which was really embarrassing. I think they should have let us pay at the next door restaurant, or use the credit card machine at the reception. Given the size of the bill, there was no way we could have carried enough cash to pay for it, but that way the only option we were given for payment.-------------Update: March 25, 2017We are doing a buffet tour of Singapore, and came back to the Edge for lunch last weekend. Lunch price was $48, but we used a UOB credit card for a 20% discount. I think they have restructured the buffet because I recall it used to be more expensive (although I checked during the holidays, so there might have been additional charges). I believe the addition of local delights means that the food is cheaper to make, so they were able to reduce the price and still please the crowd. I was here for dinner the last time, so I can't tell exactly what was changed because of the meal, and what was changed to deal with the price. The grill station is gone. They had a teh tarik station. There was a pizza station, a pasta station, kueh pie ti station, Indian, and local/Chinese station. There was chilled seafood (mussels and prawns), and sashimi. There was a fried banana station, and maybe a kaya toast station (although I didn't see anyone get it), and a bunch of local kuehs at another station. Yeah, they definitely replaced a few things.The dessert station is improved since the last time I was here. I particularly liked their ice cream -- they had 5 flavors. There was a yuzu sorbet, a blueberry yogurt, Thai milk tea, and matcha, and I can't remember the last one. I didn't like the yuzu. The blueberry yogurt was okay. I liked their Thai milk tea ice cream. The waffles were pre-made, and red velvet flavored only. I skipped that. The cakes didn't blow my mind. They had a bunch of kuehs, and Portuguese egg tarts.  With the change in the variety of food, I think the buffet is now better value (less variety, but also lower priced). I think the quality of the food wasn't spectacular, but acceptable. I might bump this to 3.5 stars.

the food was decent. I don't think it was outstanding in any of the criteria we judge buffets by: quantity, quality, variety, and service - but it's good enough to return to, just to differentiate itself from the main players (to my mind: melt, the line, and straits kitchen).they have the usual roundup of local food, japanese sushi and sashimi (the latter is good and very generous - ask for the salmon belly, which is available via request and not on display). the cold seafood seems serviceable (they have oysters and crab legs, which I know many people are into), but my favorite was definitely the prime roast - pink, tender, and full of flavour. pity they don't serve au jus.I also want to warn you that their so-named barbecue is in fact an indoor table-top grill, where you place your orders for various cuts of meat. not what I'd named a barbecue (and I'll refrain from judging this insidious clever marketing) - and also not very good. highly by-passable.there's a good spread of dessert, with a chocolate fountain, artisan-looking chocolates, and pretty cakes. skip the waffles though - anaemic, and rather biscuity, these are serviceable only with the ice cream.not bad enough to warn against - but if you're into stuffing your face, I'd recommend you to melt (still my favorite) and the line (which is an oldie but decent-ee).

Lovely selecting of breakfast foods from across the globe. A little disappointed the Sashimi/Sushi station has disappeared recently, but none the less, still a good start to the day (if you can control yourself from overeating!).

This place is definitely a must try for buffet hunters. Highly recommended:i) widest spread of food in Singaporeii) fresh seafoodiii) tasty foodiv) competitively pricedCan't go wrong if you are a big eater.

The Edge had a pretty well-displayed buffet. The salads were fresh ave they had a nice selection of Western, Chinese, Malay and classic Singaporean.  The service staff were also friendly and very quick, which is less common in Singapore.

This place is the bomb!  Cuisine after cuisine after cuisine. The breakfast layout is insane. Staff friendly and courteous. Cooks are friendly and listen to what you want and how to prepare your eggs. This is the best buffet type setup I have ever seen in my life. The food is pretty delicious as well. Of you can get here you need to check this out!!

If you are thinking of pampering yourself this Valentine's day, Caffe B might be the place for you. This Japanese-Italian restaurant sits a distance away from most celebrity chef restaurants , providing a quiet ambience though one might take some time to be used to the dimly lit brown .The set meal of five courses is based on the Groupon voucher and not all items are available on the ala carte menu. The following is an excerpt of that day.We loved the very nourishingly sweet Japanese pumpkin soup with tomato, with the nutty aroma from the roasted walnuts topped with a piece of fried basilFor the main, I believed our choice of the Argentinian Beef Tenderloin with Marsala (red wine) Reduction was a right one out of the three choices including salmon and risotto. The purple and white pom douchesse are the two spiral shaped things if you can spot them in the picture. They are seasoned mashed potato mixed with egg, squeezed out from a piping bag then baked till golden.Just look at how pink the meat is and you can imagine the tender of the beef was. The meat sat on top of spinach puree next to a sauteed radicchio trevigano, a vegetable which resembled purple cabbage to me. Squid Ink Uni Pasta is a signature ala carte dish which truly stood out from the usual squid ink dishes as the tangy tomato cream balanced the unique smell of the Uni which some people might be afraid of. The Japanese eggplant was sliced into rounds was plain on its own naturally but a perfect match when eaten with the pasta.Service was courteous while not too friendly since a distance is kept to give some personal space to diners especially since most customers that night were couples. Anyway, there is still something that grapples me. In Japan, I've heard of B-class restaurants, whose names are relative to A-class Michelin restaurants but it does not mean that the food is not good. It just implies that such places are more down-to-earth eateries, serving delicious cuisine with inexpensive prices. Could that be why Caffe B is called Caffe B ? :)

Honestly, I don't know what happened to this restaurant.  Surely something has gone wrong.  I'll leave how wrong the decor is  e side I want to focus on the food review.  I went for the set lunch with colleagues and was told that grilled chicken salad was replaced with salmon salad.  Fine, no problem, instead I get a few leaves of lettuce with what is more of a potato salad with a tiny bit of salmon crumble. The main course was tomato risotto, which only looked like a bottom of the pot congee with very poor presentation.  (Please see the pic). Wagyu strip loin was cut horribly and despite requesting 'rare' it came out as 'medium'.   For the dessert, it was a strange combination of red bean, berry and cream which none of us had more than half a bite.  The service was awful with very snide hostess.  Wine we ordered was forgotten, even though only two tables were occupied, one being us.  Rushing us to clear the table at 1:30pm at the end.  Glassware was from Ikea and decor was just horrendous with mix of Italian rustic, modern and Japanese.  It could be soooooooo much better but clearly nobody from the management cares.  Sad.

After failing to get a a table at Mozza, we swung by Caffe B, as we were still in the mood for Italian, and we were very glad that we did!  Billing itself as Japanese Italian, the Japanese influences were subtle, with perhaps the strongest being in the beautiful presentation of the dishes.  We stopped by during lunch, and one of the best values is the $25 3 course lunch set, which included a beautiful chicken and mizuna salad, a choice of entree and a rice pudding.  On our visit, we could choose from wagyu rump, pan seared sea bass or risotto.  We tried both the wagyu and sea bass, and both were excellent.  We also tried the pappardelle with a rich meat ragu and a lighter spahghetti pomodoro which my daughter loved.  Our table also shared a lovely pizza with sausage, broccolini, and mozzarella cheese which was also very good.  Overall, I found the food quality excellent - and in most cases while Mozza and Pizzeria Mozza might be a hair better, Caffe B is a much better value.  The pizza was definitely one of the best I have had in Singapore, and both pastas were excellent with a good sized portion.  The ambiance is also quite nice - quiet and elegant with excellent service throughout.  Definitely a great value, and a nice find among the dining options at MBS!

Nice atmosphere but the food was just mediocre for the price.We got the course meal - for its price, it should have been presented much better and taste should have been better.Overall Verdict: 3Taste: 3Amount: 3Price: 3Atmosphere: 4
Pasta is freshly made .. Try the Japanese bolognaise .. For tomato based lovers .. Fruit Flambé is the highlight of the dessert menu ... This place has a quiet and cosy ambience .

Caffé B is an Italian fine dining restaurant and bar that offers diners the best of Italian tradition, style and cuisine - topped with an exceptional dedication to service. The restaurant is also spread across two floors with a 30-seater bar along the Marina Bay Sand Waterfront Dining promenade.For the first-timers who are new to bar culture, Caffé B recommends that you start off by finding out your preferred base for alcohol drinks before working your way around and they hope that you'll eventually end up loving the forgotten classics which are the purest way to enjoy the spirits.My friend picked a Dirty Martini to taste, of which I took a sip. Dirty Martinis have a saltiness picked from the olives soaked in the drink while delivery in crisp, sharp taste from the alcohol. Interesting to finally taste a classic often pictured in vintage ads and movies.The sweet-toothed in me was enticed by their selection of Ice Cream cocktails of which I picked the Straight Flush - Vodka, lychee liqueur, fresh strawberries and vanilla ice cream sounded like my kind of thing. True enough, it was very much a fun drink because it was so palatable.

The "fine" in this fine dining outlet is the same as in fine print, so don't expect big portions. Food wise, its pretty generic tastiing which really doesn't deserve the price. The few nice dishes are probably the lamb, which was surprisingly good and encrusted with mystery delicious stuff, and the lobster pasta thing. If you want good, decent food, head to db bistro instead. The service staff is pretty nice though, i think that having to deal with my sister is a bit of a trial by fire for service staff, and they did pretty well i think.

Had heard friends rave about Caffé B so decided to check it out for one of my birthday dinners. Always a big fan of modern fusion cuisine, so was quite looking forward to the experience.Food : K and I went for the wagyu beef carpaccio which was good but not amazing. H went for the foie gras degustion, essentially foie gras done three different ways; a foie gras lollipop sprinkled liberally with walnuts much resembling that of a Magnum ice cream, pan fried foie gras in filo pastry and a foie gras mousse tartlet. Interesting presentation but H commented it was again, not amazing. For the mains I went for the Boston lobster with yuzu citrus butter sauce ... commendable but nothing to shout about. K had the lamb rack while H had the Kurobuta black pork loin. Both agreed it was not bad, but nothing to write home about. What we really liked though were the desserts; I went for the lemon sorbet with vodka and prosecco, which left me feeling really high and happy! The boys had the hazelnut tart which they loved as well.Ambience : Not bad ... a lot of mirrors and chandeliersService : Decent

If you somehow enjoy fusion food - Japanese and Italian in this instance, then you'd probably enjoy Caffe B. Helmed by a Japanese chef, the offerings are relatively well-done, considering the fusion doesn't always bode well. My favourite so far has to be the live boston lobster linguine which was done perfectly al dente and was so flavourful that I left nothing on the plate. Service is very prompt and efficient, no doubt thanks to the ever watchful maitre'd and prices aren't really sky high. With the choice of an al fresco, indoor or a bay front bar seating, Caffe B is the perfect place to have a romantic dinner, or a nice family gathering.

This is like two different restaurants. The lunch buffet is good (although nothing to scream about) and reasonably priced, even during weekends. At dinner, the food is more sophisticated, but prices are quite extravagant, overall resulting in poor value. I find that if you want an upscale Indian meal, Rang Mahal is way, way better (more refined and innovative cooking, not just gimmicky; and more pro-active service). Alternatively, Song of India and Punjab Grill also serve better food. Otherwise, if you just want an old-fashioned but very satisfying North Indian meal, then there are many choices in Singapore at a fraction of the price of dinner here: the Curry Culture, Tandoor at Holiday Inn Orchard, or even Kebabs and Curries at Mustafa Centre!!

Yantra is an upscale Indian restaurant in Tanglin mall.  They have an amazing Indian buffet for lunch for 25 Sing.  The food is delish.  Dinner takes on a more elegant setting and the dishes are masterpieces of taste tantalizing dishes.  Service is very attentive.

I went with a group to the lunch buffet. It was very pretty the way it was laid out, but something was just missing with the food. The chicken was tasty, but there was a mushroom soup I was not quite fond of. There were some very yummy sweet potatoes that had been given a lot of love...slow roasted and had smoked paprika added which had caramelized during roasting. Their cocktails looked fabulous as even the non alcoholic drinks were pretty dressed up. I'd give the place another shot for dinner.

Yantra is an very high priced Indian restaurant that I would not recommend unless you are looking for a new spot to try out. What makes this review odd to me is that I had two completely different dining experiences in the same dinner...I started out with a very high enjoyment of the restaurant followed by what I thought was totally abysmal.I was joining my friend for a dinner and knew she would be late so went ahead and started myself. The setting is beautiful in what is a pretty ugly and boring Tanglin Mall. I came in without reservation on a Tuesday evening around 6:45 PM and was seated by the friendly hostess at a nice corner table. My waiter was named Raju who was a total rockstar, very cool, prompt and attentive throughout.I was starving and went ahead and ordered the following: 1) Chair Chaat ($16) - Uniquely presented Indian street food snack placed on wooden chairs. Delicious and fun! Great way to start.2) Paneer lal merch ($29) - If you like paneer tikka (Indian fluffy cheese cooked in the tandoor oven) this is a solid choice. You can taste the unique flavors of the tandoor and they also top it with a light masala sauce of some sort. 3) Chicken Tikka Makhani ($40) - Yes, that's a $40 dish. I was craving my usual butter chicken so I got it. White meat chicken tikka in a tomato paste curry. It was great and hit the spot but as other Yelpers have pointed out, it doesn't have anything particularly special compared to some other marquee Indian restaurants in Singapore. But if you are craving this dish as much as I do, it was good.4) Plain naan - Good and did its job.5) Raita - Yogurt with veggies and herbs that I use to put on rice to combat any heavy spice from curries. The raita is very well made here!For a starting drink, I was curious about the Watermelon and Rose Martini which was made with chunks of watermelon, Belvedere vodka and rose water. A bit strange that they don't strain the ice but I figure because they want you to enjoy the fresh watermelon chunks?Service and food up to this point was incredible and I was ready to give it 5 stars on Yelp. I would highly recommend you order the above at the very least if you are looking for a good meal. However, that's about when my friend joined in and everything turned bad.The restaurant seated a few more tables and Raju began serving the others while we were with one of the other waiters who wasn't as attentive.She ordered the following:1) Tandoori Avocado ($32) - cool concept except it was awful. The masala spices tasted nice but it completely contrasts the rich texture of the avocado which just tasted bad. We both felt ripped off on this.2) Ganderi Kabob ($28) - Looks better than it tastes. I had an identical plate on my recent trip to Vietnam which was a fraction of the price with 500 times better flavor and texture.3) Sugarcane sorbet ($12) - The absolute WORST sorbet I've ever had in my life. Seriously, who puts masala powder on top of a sorbet? It also tasted more like a faint ginger than anything else. Understandably, sugarcane doesn't have much of a flavor but why do they even have this on the menu? It has a cool dry ice presentation but otherwise...Horrible.4) Cheena Payesh ($20) - Think of Ras Malai indian dessert except they ruin it by including diced strawberries and cheapen it by serving it in a cheap looking martini glass.Lastly, they have a bit of an odd cocktail menu since 90% of their drinks have Indian spices in them which is strange. My friend had the Indian Mojito which she liked - refreshing masala cocktail. I ordered the Mango Gimlet thinking they use fresh mango puree but rather they use something that is green and disgusting.I want to commend Indian restaurants that try and push the boundaries for what is usually a typical and predictable kind of experience but to say that some dishes were just awful is a totally new thing for me. I love Hemant Oberoi restaurants in India but this one is not one I would at all recommend for a nice Indian food night out. It's a great setting but I can't stand feeling ripped off, and I've only felt this way at a few restaurants around the world.

I'll give Yantra four stars for the food, but was slightly put off by the wait staff trying to talk us out of ordering dal because we refused to order naan or rice.  Interesting that they think dal can't be eaten without a plateful of carbs.  So much that they would rather convince a customer to not spend money on their food.  Loved the raita, that's a scoop of heaven right there is what that is!  Truly the best I've ever tasted.   The roasted eggplant is definitely worth going back for and we will if I can convince my better half to get past the decor he believes he paid for.   Oh, and we did end up ordering the dal too which was on par with what we've tried in other Indian restaurants.  Quite a romantic place to go for a Friday night, but deceiving in how expensive it is.   The cost caught us by surprise because of the location being in old Tanglin Mall.   Perhaps because Marketplace is an anchor tenant, which may bring in a lot of expats, which further means jack up the prices and apply the white tax folks.

Probably the best Indian buffet in town. That sentence does not really do justice to Yantra's buffet. Hidden away in one the corners of Tanglin Mall is Yantra. Not a place to eat at every day, but if you have visitors and want to show them some great Indian food, then try Yantra.I can only comment on the weekend buffet, which is pricier, but has different free flow options. The choice of food is really very good. The main trick is not to overdo the appetizers and leave room for the entrees. One tip is to bypass the rice. Amongst the appetizers, for me the tandoori mushroom stand out for flavor. Entrees include many lamb, chicken and vegetarian dishes each cooked with the same consistent care and attention as the others. The staff will also bring you some appetizers made in front of everyone by one of the chef's. Very tasty. Pricy yes, but a great place to eat good Indian food if you have the stomach and the wallet.

Its always difficult for me to come to terms to pay high price for an Indian curry because all restaurants (except Song of India) use the same cream, heavy curry base, same cuts of chicken and thus, taste quite similar. I like the decor but I never feel like paying premium prices for the interior decoration - I rather go to a museum for that.The buffet seems value for money but as a previous reviewer mentioned, meats are monotone. For me its just another Indian restaurant with premium being charged for hanging some expensive paintings on their walls.

Tucked away at the end of Tanglin Mall (street level coming in from Starbucks or Traders Hotel side, not Taxi Stand level) is Yantra. It looks posh and quiet. Either most people overlook this place or think it is too expensive. They are not wrong. The location is not the greatest as it is not easily visible from both the inside and outside. The a la carte dishes are very pricey. Mains and entrees start from $20 to $50 or more. Fortunately they do a lunch buffet on weekdays and weekends which make it very affordable to try and dine. I went on a Thursday and the lunch buffet was $19++ which is value for money. The quality of the Indian food is excellent and the ambience and decor are classy, understated elegance, making it almost a fine dining destination. The dishes available when I was there (what I can remember):It serves 3 kinds of rice - briyani (chicken and vegetarian) and plain white rice. There are 2 tandoori dishes (prawns and chicken - pretty tender and moist, much better than most places which are often dry and hard).There is a decent variety of relishes and chutneys, including regular raita and tomato/vegetable raita). The curries and vegetables (okras, paneer, broccoli cheese...) are equally tasty. Plain naans are brought to your table. Dessert - carrot pudding, rice pudding, gulab jamun and fresh fruits. As Indian desserts go, they are generally very sweet and these are no exception. That said, I am pretty much blown away as a tiny bit goes a long way and the sweetness becomes just nice. The gulab jamun is kept warm in a pot and it is soft and light and moist. Service is also excellent. The water glass was topped up constantly without having to be asked. I would definitely want to go back again, but likely for the lunch as dinner will be too expensive since most people will order several dishes to share.

Probably the  best palak paneer in Singapore --- you can tell from the color and the texture that it is so fresh -- bright green and light and not at all oily... but the other dishes are so-so.Low lights were the garfa tikki which are patties of garbanzos (chick peas) and fava beans -- it was dry and was bordering flavorless.  Also avoid the vegetable samosas --- which is surprising for an Indian restaurant to miss.  The pastry of the samosas was too thick and dry so the ratio between the filling and pastry was off... too little filling.   Then the filling also lacked flavor so it was like cardboard. The butter chicken was delicious but then so many other Indian restaurants can do butter chicken very well at half the price.  The same goes with the mango kulfi -- it was good but I have had better.The prawns cooked in a tandoor was tender and cooked well but lacked the garlic and anise flavor as described in the menu.  So if your guests are more on presentation and does not have such a discriminating palate, you can take them here since they make an effort on presentation.  The prawns are flambeed table side, then the kulfi is served on dry ice.  So some folks are easily impressed with those...
For 25 bucks...the lunch buffet was ok.  I was hoping for more...or at least that I wouldn't have to keep asking for more bread and water.

What's the best way to get over too many bowls of loudmouth soup the night before? A big bowl of Ramen soup from Suzuki today!This place is off the charts good and one of my favourite Ramen in Singapore!It's cash only, steers towards the expensive end of the market (it's on Circular Road no less) and at lunch times it's packed to the gills with guys and gals. Even with these challenges it's an easy one to recommend because the experience makes it all worthwhile.The menu is heavily customisable and you get some good options to go with. I almost always go the 5x spicy for that super kick, and salty because we are in the business of curing last night's mistakes. If you're a big eater you can plump for an egg and extra char siew to tide you over...Still hungry? There's help-yourself potato salad and a bowl of hard boiled eggs on the table to bang into your broth.If that doesn't satiate your hangriness then you shoulda gone the gyozas for starters - better luck next time rookie!

Had to check it off the ramen list, and I'm glad to report it was worth it. Pretty close to Tonkotsu King in taste and presentation, so you kinda know what you're getting here. Rich, tasty broth, and thin noodles (i'm a fan - no udon for me) mean simple satisfaction in a bowl.Learn this lesson though: go early. REALLY early. I was there at 1205 and already there was a queue eight people deep. Made me wonder how early these people snuck off work.

Crazy lines at lunch time, so either come very early or very late.The ramen here is very thin. Thus, they have a tendency to get soggy if you are a slow eater. I ordered mine harder and it still retained a bite at the end of the meal. I presume any order softer than that may result in soft noodles towards the end.Broth is flavorful. On first bite, it doesn't come across as being too salty. Thumbs up for that. However towards the end, it did.The standard serving only comes with one slice of pork, but you do get to choose whether you want belly or pork loin. So it is great for the health conscious.Free flow of hard boiled eggs at every table and more free condiments like rice, cabbage, etc.I would eat it but I don't crave it.Cash only.

Pretty legit ramen joint in Boat Quay, popular with the office crowd.Had lunch here today and there was no queue at noon or during our meal, most likely due to folks still out of the office on the Monday after a 4-day CNY weekend. Perhaps the popularity has waned a bit, not sure.Kudos for all the free flow rice, seasoned bean sprouts, hard boiled eggs, and mashed potatoes along with busting out two types of Tobasco sauce without prompting.The place is cash only and you jot down your order on a paper order form giving your preference for noodle firmness, broth flavor strength, level of oily-ness, etc then pay at the front register before finding a seat.The spot seems popular with expat Japanese workers in the area which is always a good sign.Def worth a visit and I look forward to returning for lunch again soon.

So I got this ramen kick. Every day had to have one, tried many places but this one is my Favorite. Flavours are bold, make sure you get amber broth, limited to 10 bowls per day only. Service and ambience is fair. The only downside is cash only and the order forms can be a bit confusing for a first timer.

Fresh Ramen with all of your special order fix-ins is GREATER THAN Dehyrdrated ramen from the grocery store.Came here on a Wednesday night around 8PM. The restaurant was full -but no line from what I could tell.  Each dinner gets to select his/her own soup noodle base + special order fix-ins (e.g extra meat, extra toppings, flavored soft-boiled egg, etc). If you're still not full from all of the noodles and yummy broth, then you can get your fill from the all-you-can eat shredded cabbage + dressing  and/or rice that your little tummy desires.  If you leave not feeling satisfied (and perhaps with some spots of soup splattered on your clothes), then shame on you!

Soup is thick and flavorful enough - Just how I like it. Char siew needs improvement though as it is quite difficult to chew, Recommendation is to get the Pure white special because you get 4 char siew and 1 flavored egg for only $13.00. Would be nice if they can add dipping noodles to their menu.

This is a dinky little ramen place smack right diagonal from my yoga studio, and what better way to nullify a hot sweaty workout than stuffing my face with carbs? RBS specialises in Tonkatsu ramen, with choices of white (original), red (spicy), black (squid ink), tsukemen (dipping noodles) or fish flakes. I opted for the white, and aside from the customisation available - taste, flavoured oil, noodle hardness etc, you can also partake in the hard boiled eggs and bean sprouts available. Hm, isn't that quite similar to a certain ramen place at Orchid Hotel, your though bubble visualises. Yes, but RBS manages to one up them by providing jugs of iced tea, fried pork lard and fragrant garlic chips at each table! That's pretty ingenious I think! And in addition, there's complimentary free flow of rice and shredded cabbage with homemade dressing to go with your remaining soup too, which makes this joint even more of a win.Taste test: I went with the white Tonkotsu and the soup base was thick and flavourful without being too oily as most ramen places are wont to do. Sure, a lighter touch is very much tweaked to Singaporean tastes, but hey, that's how I like it. The noodles are on the thin side, so I chose to have them hard (they also have a "harder" option) as I was pretty sure they'd get soggy in no time. And they did, so I'll opt for harder on my next visit. The char siew slice was thin, and I was a bit disappointed at that, but it was deliciously tender. What a crafty ploy to get customers to opt for the extra char siew version, but then again, it works! Extra char siew next visit it is. In addition, they also put in a kicker of a really cute Japanese chef - great eye candy and he's got the girls' votes. Er. Have I mentioned that I'll be going back?

Tried this breakfast joint recently as it rated highly on Yelp. Not everything is good on the menu as we found out soon enough how dissappointing their waffles (Canadian Bfast) were. I'll stick to the European (Eggs Benedict) or English (Scrambled Eggs and Sausage) for now. S$80 for 2? That's quite abit for breakfast.

Most sets cost around $20. The menu looks interesting with breakfast inspired by all parts of the world. I had the Tunisian breakfast set served in a pan - I loved the seasoning used, and how it looked. You pay at the counter before getting your set. Prepare for a long wait though, as this place is always crowded. More importantly, i liked the cosy cafe setting with nice sofa chairs. What I disliked is the queue!

My wife and I had breakfast here on a Monday morning, and loved it. The service, food and atmosphere were all great. The food is quite expensive, but for a schmancy breakfast spot in downtown Singapore, that's to be expected. One thing I really liked was that both of our entrees came out together. In Singapore it is very common for different people at the same table to be served minutes apart, which is a major faux pas in decent restaurants all over the world. My Bloody Mary could have been spicier and had another splash of vodka, but it was still good, and a great compliment to my eggs bennie and fruit.

Chops for ambience and location but food is rather overpriced for the quality. Had the Santa Fe and the Brittany, both of which were served at room temperature. Would have been nice for the food to have been served warmed. In any case, I suspect we're paying for the rent here. Could be better...

How can breakfasts be so expensive? Singaporeans must really love their breakfasts to pay these prices. I skipped the breakfast items (so cannot comment on them, and therefore, I suppose I shouldn't judge the pricing, as the breakfast items could be really crazy good) and ordered a "chicken salad chop chop" or something with an equally silly name. Possibly "chop chop chicken salad"??Anyway, the salad is NOT like a salad at all. Firstly, there were no greens. Ok, fine, there was some lettuce in the salad. But the lettuce was coated in some brown coloured seasoning (curry powder? no idea). In fact, the entire bowl of "salad" was one single colour - brown! Definitely not appetizing and not the fresh, healthy bowl of salad I was expecting. However, having said that, the salad tasted fine and I grew to like the crunchy crackers in the salad. So much for trying to have a healthy meal. In a bid to keep up with my attempt to have a healthy meal, I ordered the mixed beetroot juice - this was expensive, but not too bad, quite tasty and was freshly squeezed, of course.Service was slow. Our glasses of water were not topped up. I'm not used to paying such sky high prices for breakfast food and won't be coming back. It's not like the food I had was that great, or the service, that good. In fact, everything was pretty average to me, down to the ambience. Only advantage I suppose would be the location, although to me, I'd very much prefer a relaxing, quieter cafe to have my breakfast at.

Holiday weekend and we walked to Wild Honey to get a change of pace from The Line at Shangri La. The hostess stand had an iPad where we checked in digitally and received texts regarding the status of our table. The wait time was estimated at 45-60 minutes and we waited only 40 minutes. We walked around the mall and did some shopping to pass the time more quickly, which was a nice change of pace to lingering around the entrance. We received a call when our table was ready and were greeted by a friendly gentleman apologizing for how crazy it was, but we weren't concerned at all because it was a holiday weekend. We were seated at the round counter and quickly greeted and put in drink orders - iced coffee. The menu had a lot of variety and offered meals from many regions around the world. I chose the Tunisian, which was chorizo and eggs in a tomato based sauce, with two hearty pieces of toast and a cucumber and tomato salad. It was incredibly tasty but not very filling since my Paleo lifestyle doesn't allow me to consume grains. My hubby tried the special - duck confit potato hash topped with poached eggs and hollandaise. It was also very good. We topped off our meals with the berries, but passed on the yogurt. The service was good. The menu is a little limited if you're paleo, but it's not too hard to make it work. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and I was a fan of the music selection, which would fit into the "coffee house" genre. Overall, we were very pleased and will be back.

Wild Honey at Scotts Square is a vast improvement on its sister outlet at Mandarin Gallery. For starters, there's a lot more space and a wider variety on its menu, and we can finally make reservations online instead of having to wake up at the crack of dawn on a weekend to queue for a table.Food : The best eggs Benedict I've had in Singapore. We shared the Tunisian, the Scandinavian, the European, the English, the Australian and I Love New York amongst us so that we could all get a taste of the different breakfast sets. The coffees were well made and a couple of us tried this Banoffee drink which was mad yummy! Being a ravenous lot, we also shared a bread basket while waiting for our breakfast sets to arrive. We particularly liked the croissant, evident in the fact we almost came to blows over the sole croissant in the basket. The homemade jams and honey too, were the perfect complement to the bread basket. If we hadn't wanted to save some stomach space for our breakfast sets, we would have ordered one more! The most difficult decision you will face at Wild Honey is deciding which breakfast set to order, but whichever you decide, rest assured they are all equally tasty in their own indigenous way.Ambience : Love the mosaic tiles on the floor and the airy feel of the restaurant. The dark wood works well with the colorful furniture and drapes. Overall, the atmosphere is bustling yet comfortable, and is a great place to people watch on weekends. We like!Service : Can be a bit sketchy if one is sitting outside on the verandah. It is practically impossible to get service after the server takes our initial order, and the wait staff inside the restaurant are too busy to pay us any attention. If you can get their attention however, they are perfectly pleasant.Perfect if they can improve service standards. Prices are a bit steep for brunch but at least the large portions compensate somewhat. Reservations for weekend brunch at prime time absolutely necessary at least a week in advance.

Decent food but way overpriced.  I had the Spanish Hash which was tasty, and my wife had the English breakfast.  She also had a donut and coffee.  She was disappointed that the breakfast came with toasted brioche but no jam or marmalade.  Overall bill was $70...ouch.

I went to Wild Honey with my SO for a special occasion brunch. It is AMAZING! I got the eggs with smoked fish. They had gluten free bread that was actually so good that I was afraid it wasn't actually gluten free. The hot chocolate was ridiculous with the housemade marshmellow. WH also had the only Bloody Mary that I've had in Singapore so far that was actually good. Overall, I wish my stomach could have fit more in it cause it was all so delicious. My only complaint is it was very pricey. It's definitely not something we could do regularly as it was over $100 for the two of us.
Good eggs Benedict.

Wild Honey @ Mandarin GalleryWild Honey dared to be different by serving all day breakfasts - even for dinner.  Totally against the grain but it works! With queues even at dinner time, expect to wait 15-30 mins for a table. Service is mediocre, the staff aren't exceptionally cheerful (or efficient) for that matter, but you're really here for the atmosphere - plush cosy chairs in little corners, dim lights and a strong cinnamon-y sweet scent. Love how the dishes are named after different cities / areas - one of my favourites is the 'Belgian', fluffly waffles with grilled mango and blueberries.  An instant hit for my sweet tooth - beware though, it IS sweet and may not go down well as a main for dinner.  Perhaps better to share as a desert :)

Sad to say, Wild Honey was an over-hyped and over rated restaurant for me. A couple of old friends suggested dinner there to try out their 'must-try' all day brunches, and it was on the list of 'trendy cafes in Singapore' that we've heard so much about. We weren't allowed to make reservations, and despite arriving super early after rushing down from work, I couldn't get seated to ensure 4 of my other friends had seats either, which was quite disappointing service. So there I was waiting alone outside while the restaurant slowly filled up, to the point where by the time all my friends arrived, we had to be seated at a table for 4, with an additional chair squeezed in. The food was greatly talked about, so we went all out and got a banana toffee milkshake that came served in a colour and shape that was honestly that of doo-doo. It tasted cloying and overly artificial, and the drink slowly congealed into a paste towards the end of the meal - not tasty at all! We ordered several different pancakes from their all day brunch menu that they were famous for, and the top choice was the Norwegian pancakes, that came with smoked salmon on scone like breads. This was average at best, with the accompanying sauce a bit too sour for my taste since it just made the eggs taste sour and the salmon taste bad. 2 stars at most for just having a good ambience in the restaurant.

This is one of my favourite brunch places for a few reasons: its accessible(for me) smack in town, the service and food quality is consistent, wide range of  menu, cosy ambience, delicious smoothies. The downside is the price (well its in Orchard road, what do you expect), some dishes aren't too fantastic (e.g. Mexican), some of the portions are too small for my liking in relation to the price. Also you can't make a reservation for the mandarin gallery branch, although this is not a problem for the Scott's branch.In conclusion: not perfect but always a reliable place to go for brunch. I'm still waiting for the seats out on the patio!

We have been coming to Wild Honey since this branch opened and are pretty much regulars on the patio at opening on Sundays.  It helps that one of our friends has a baby but the rest of us are just naturally early risers.  I've tried most of the menu and would say my ideal meal is the European with a side of Brazilian bread and a Queen Bee.  The dishes are all named after a geographic location but are pretty imaginative from there. The European is their take on eggs Benedict: seriously thick brioche with parma ham and poached eggs.  The brazilian bread is this cheesy little roll thing, amazing. And the queen bee is a honey grapefruit mocktail.  Yum.Other highlights of the menu are the Tunisian and the English.  Enjoy breakfast!

A beautiful breakfast parlor in the heart of Orchard road has been the talk of the town since its opening. The beeline at its 1st outlet; Mandarin Gallery, has become a common sight. Due to the limited seats, many find it frustrating to wait. The restaurant did excite me but not the queue. I wouldn't brave myself to Wild Honey until its 2nd outlet at Scott's Square becomes operational; there - I have gotten my most important meal of the day fixed without having to wait, any time of the day.    Serving an array of breakfast dishes; distinguished by country that ranges from English, European, Belgian, Canadian,Tunisian to Japanese et cetra. While many raved about European - eggs Benedict; I heart English instead.The portion has been massive; it can feed 2 ladies with small appetite. Routinely, I would portion the plate unless I declared a NO dessert and could leave the place without any. What have been so enjoyable in the plate are those juicy pork meat cased in its crispy sausage skin. They are perfectly grilled without drying out and loosing their flavour. The toasted brioche is more provocative - rich in taste with a strong buttery note. Slightly fluffy yet crumbly in some parts. While the briny bacons compliment well with the bread, the scrambled eggs add moist and even-out the saltiness in the former. When waffles becomes unavailable, I will make good with a stack of pancake - Canadian. These thick fermented round flapjacks are doubled in size; 3s are somewhat excessive - sharing is more ideal. I am particularly fond of its texture - very light yet with some volume. They are relatively moist but not dampish. For a savory note, nibble on the bacons along with the cake. Otherwise, top it up either with maple syrup or homemade jam - the morning becomes more angelic.

Empty restaurant in the haze but they refuse to make even minor modifications to menu items. Avoid if you have any dietary restrictions at all. Ordered a pitcher of "extra spicy" bloody maries and they were bland but for being exceedingly salty.

The only good thing about wild honey is the wide variety of food. The service is terrible. My friend made a reservation for her birthday and we were kept waiting for an extremely long time. The hostess was continuously rude and bitter about our requests to be seated. In addition, the chef is incapable of accommodating to simple modifications of a dish. Later, hair was found in a dish and certain items on the menu were unavailable.

I had a great, albeit somewhat expensive experience here. In between my friend's church wedding and wedding dinner reception next door at the Hyatt, i managed to meet another friend for coffee here (talk about multitasking; gotta keep the schedule going when you're visiting for only 2.5 weeks). I had a delicious, strong serving of French Press coffee- really, it reminded me of Blue Bottle Coffee in SF- strong and luxurious. Also had a serving of the Apple cobbler ala mode. Delish. It's definitely overpriced, but i look forward to checking out their brunch or dinner service when i visit again

Breakfast done in a odd seating and difficult service routine - not the worst breakfast in Singapore but the facility is more for a family reunion than a breakfast.  Coffee is cold and pricey.  The wait and amount of strollers is disturbing.  Don't the helpers know how to cook an omelet and toast?

Dining here costs a lot - at least $50 a head. And that's just for breakfast! However, if you're willing to splurge, then there is no problems dining here. The service is excellent and they only use the freshest ingredients. I mainly come here to sample their worldwide breakfast menu, as there are quite a few varieties available rather than the boring standard breakfast. The ambience is really nice and conducive to have breakfast with friends, or even alone.

Delicious. Best breakfast I've had in a loooong time. Great portion sizes. Very popular place, can't linger without a reservation. The European breakfast was amazing. The hubby had the English breakfast and rated it.

Best breakfast/brunch restaurant there is!They have all kinds of breakfast: Spanish with chorizo, the classic English breakfast which comprise of bacon eggs and baked beans, Tunisian breakfast, salmon, and so on. The portion is very filling. I went for English breakfast, which was very good. I will definitely go for Spanish next time!

Nice selection of western style breakfast food. I ordered the Santa fe which is two fried eggs sitting on top of two folded tortillas with some pico de gallo and tiny bits of avocado mixed in. (If you are from the south west region of the us or CA you are probably laughing at this type of presentation and mere the idea of eating tortillas with a fork and knife!)My husband ordered the Norwegian which looked very nice too. Ironically, it was served with slices of avocado. (When was the last time you had avocado in Norway?)We also had a raspberry smoothie that was essentially raspberry puree and ice blended together and served in a martini glass. Nice presentation but the flavor was fairly bland.Topped off with hot herbal and black teas served in mini french press pots.I'd go here again, but I'm curious to see other brunch spots as well.

I believe most people are familiar with the fantastic range of all day breakfasts available at the Wild Honey. But due to the smaller set up in the Mandarin Gallery outlet, seating is limited and it is on a first come first serve on-site queue basis, no reservations allowed.But guess what, at the Scotts Square branch, not only is the restaurant bigger, you can actually make reservations! No need to queue and you are guaranteed a table when you arrive! As this outlet is also larger, you wont have the issue of tables being too close to the next so you have more privacy when dining. Not only that, for those who love the Wild Honey Concept so much, you can actually reserve their terrace for private parties!One thing to note though, due to the mall operating hours, this outlet closes slightly earlier than other regular restaurants not within a mall so do go early to maximise your dining experience.Cant wait to go for my breakfast during dinner time again soon! :)

Another great breakfast option in Singapore! I had the Canadian which was 3 perfectly fluffy pancakes, maple syrup, fruit compote and candied bacon. Absolutely delicious and just the right size. My fellow diners (breakfasters?) had the Flinders Street and the Corsican. Both looked excellent and were well received. You definitely need to be book, we were there on a Wednesday at 10:00am and it was pretty full. I also wouldn't recommend it with small children, it's definitely more of an adult breakfast joint!Didn't really enjoy the coffee though but realising that coffee is pretty personal I could make do.

This place was FANTASTIC!!! We came on Easter Sunday and it was a great atmosphere and it's very reasonable in price. My husband had the European and I had the coconut waffles. Both were excellent. We also ordered sausages and Canadian bacon. Again, simply amazing. We will definitely be back!!

Wild Honey has the best Eggs Benedict in Singapore. Two perfectly poached eggs, sauteed mushrooms and prosciutto on toasted homemade brioche and hollandaise sauce. This has to be my favorite dish of all time. I always end up ordering this even though i always say i wanna try something new. Anyway, i think that the Mandarin Gallery branch does it better? Somehow the bread is over toasted and was too crunchy. Pretty dry. :(The Wild Mocha Dolce is my poison. This is intensely sweet but packs in some serious caffeine. I always get super high after drinking this. Friends know not to feed me with too much coffee/tea because i'd be bouncing off the walls. I also love the scones at WH. For tea, i like to have their cranberry scone with a cuppa of hot mocha dolce. This has to be one of the better scones in town. I'd put it in the same category as Foster's (another of my favorite). The exterior is crispy and the middle is dense and moist. I'll gently coat it with a thin layer of butter and sprinkle sea salt flakes on it- my very own version of salted butter (because WH doesn't provide salted ones). Yummy! And their fresh compote of berries to go with it. Perfecto.I would be hanging out at the SS branch more often for the following reasons1. Wider desserts selectionAccording to the manager, the kitchen at SS is 3 times bigger than that at MG. Therefore, more space to make pastries! I tried the sour cherry strudel when i was there recently (not fantastic) and they also have more tea cakes and stuff. :) I'll be sure to try more desserts soon.2. More breathing space! I always felt that the MG store was really claustrophobic! In fact, the entire MG feels that way. I feel like i can easily touch the ceiling (ok i exaggerate). Also, because of the small size of the place, i do feel like i can't stay on for too long even though i just wanna chill out with my book sometimes. Scotts is more airy and there's more natural light hence the relaxed ambience. So if you haven't tried WH (quite impossible IMO), do head on down. All day breakfast means that you never have to wake up early! As for me, ADB FTW!

Expensive but worth it. We had an amazing brunch ordering the Portobello Road and the European breakfast. The eggs were poached to perfection and the coffees were perfect. I was actually struggling to finish my meal given it's size. We arrived around 11am on a Sunday and only bar seating was available. This was fine. It is near a hotel so you get many international travellers here having a leisurely breakfast. Fantastic atmosphere and décor. Definitely on the pricey brunch end.

brunch as good as the states! lord, let me tell you, me and brunch have a long, intimate history together and our relationship has been a little bit on the rocks since coming to singapore. don't get me wrong, there's brunch places here but a truly good brunch consists of eggs, eggs, meat, carb and eggs and a very good bloody mary. wild honey does not disappoint!tunisian - delicious! a lot of spice, great portion and just love the brioche that comes with it. i would come back for this dish alone.breakfast sandwich - huge! delicious ciabatta placed on top of a mountain of eggs and meat. i got this with a side of pork sausage, all good. the teas here are great too and the decor is beautiful. officially my new go-to brunch joint.
Food was excellent and presentation was of a high quality. Unfortunately, the hostess was being dismissive towards us

A business cum social meeting was the occassion and Wild Honey was chosen as the venue. I must say from the get-go, its popularity is warranted. Location wise it is the most convenient to get to - minutes away from Orchard MRT station, with bus stops closeby and the Grand Hyatt taxi stand at your disposal next door - it was a breeze getting there.Without the foresight of making a reservation, we were told it would be a half an hour wait at 11.30am on a Sunday, during which we decided to have coffee in the basement below. Their technologically advanced waiting list system was impressive. A few taps on the iPad located at their entrance, I was 7th in line and I received a call on my mobile, informing to choose if I would be there immediately or needed at 10 minute extension. A 'service' I was particularly fond of.Jumpin right in, we were seated outdoors (you can indicate preferences on the iPad), and it being my first time, I took about 5-7 minutes to decide what I wanted whilst we were served water and the orange juice I ordered (Which was fresh, not too sour, good job once again). I decided on the 'Scandinavian', which is grilled salmon fillet on potato rosti, chargrilled asparagus & homemade Hollandaise sauce. It was right on the money,  approximate $25 bucks if I recall correctly. Salmon was grilled to perfection and the rosti was crispy (I am used to it being less crispy, but it clearly said 'crisp rosti' on the menu so I guess it was done right). Do note it takes about 15-20 minutes to prepare, so if you feel like having this, get your order out right as you are seated.  My friend ordered the 'Norwegian' which consisted avocado, grilled asparagus spears, two perfectly poached eggs wrapped with imported Norwegian smoked salmon, homemade Hollandaise & salmon pearls on a whole-wheat brioche. It looked fantastic, and he isn't too expressive about food but just gave me a thumbs up and a sigh of satisfaction when he was done.Definitely coming back here for more. Service was great, a little too crowded for my liking but then again, Singapore is getting that way and perhaps making reservations in advance would save you unnecessary delays. Another great brunch menu checked off my list!

The food here is good, but I don't think it's worth the prices they serve them at. Although the atmosphere and the service was really great. It's a nice "I feel fancy today" kind of a place... But definitely not coming back here anytime soon. Still on the hunt for a regular brunch spot. Mainly breakfast and brunch place that serves brunch cocktails. Decent food and large servings but extremely pricey.
This place often stays quiet at meal times when Coffee Academics downstairs is full. Portions are large, but the food is really nothing to write home about.

Who can say no to all day breakfast? Prices here seem a little on the high side but portions are comparatively larger. The food was decent, and I did enjoy my spanish hash, but it didnt wow me. I guess I'm paying more for the ambience, the comfortable seats and the strong AC. Great place for a meetup with friends where food isnt the focus.

Late lunch.. found this place inside the Scott Plaza. Surprisingly, it's almost full house at 3pm+. Ordered a cold brew single origin. It was actually quite good, even slightly better than Starbucks and far better than TCC. And the price is reasonable $5.50. I ordered the all day breakfast, Scandinavian. Salmon wrapped with asparagus, on top of deep fried thin hash brown (I hope I got it right), drizzled with hollandaise dressing. Sadly, I didn't like it. Not at all. Especially I didn't know what to do with the tomatoes. The deep fried "nest" made of hash brown was very tough and oily, I was slightly worry about it flew out of my plate when I cut it with knife. That would be embarrassing. I didn't finish the main, I thus ordered a brownie with vanilla ice cream. Not bad! Good for sharing. Too much for one person.
