The place was almost empty, hardly surprising really, we waited ages to be attended, one of the main courses turned up at the same time as the starter, it looked absolutely nothing like the image on the menu - the menu shows a pot full of colour, texture, seafood......what you actually got was a pot of slop. The food is bland, tasteless and ridiculously expensive for a third rate eating house in a shopping mall. Avoid at all costs, if you want good asian food, there are so many other places to choose from. There were 4 of us eating, one of us was sick before she left the mall, another still has a tummy bug.....awful awful, awful......

As its name suggests, Bali Thai offers a unique fusion Balinese and Thai cuisines. The setting is slick and contemporary, with modern Thai and Balinese décor along with plastic chairs. The restaurant serves Thai dishes such as Thai Fish Cakes, Seafood Tom Yum Soup, Phad Thai, Pineapple Rice and Mango Sticky Rice, and Indonesian dishes like Tahu Telur, Chicken Paggang and Fried Red Snapper. The Tom Yum soup did not taste authentic enough, as it had a sweeter hint to it than usual. Dry and slightly bland, the Chicken Paggang was disappointing as well. The only dish I was all right with was the Phad Thai, and even so, it was not great.  I guess I would drop by a restaurant that specializes in each separate cuisine the next time I have cravings for Thai or Indonesian food, as it seems more authentic and reliable.

Woken up at 2:30 am in the morning by the room next door blasting effing Selena Gomez and Rihanna.  Ooh na na, what's my name...?  I have a few names in mind for you...Anyway, rather than kicking their door down, I decided that my energy would be better spent searching for some grubs, since I had roughly 5~6 hours to go until proper breakfast time.  Sin Hoi Sai was one of the few places that open past 3:30 am in this quiet little area of Singapore, and as far as I could tell, Selena/Rihanna haters were welcomed.Menu selection were listed on the lighted boards above the restaurant.  I went with the Indonesia chicken and baby Gai Lan since I recalled that both of those had pretty solid mentions.The veggie came first, and it was solid with a nice garlic flavor.  Texture was crunchy and that slight bitterness that I like in Gai Lan really came through.  The Indonesian chicken came with a bit too much breading for my preference.  The taste was also a bit too salty for me.  When I looked at all the menu selection again, I realized that pretty much of the chicken options were pretty much breaded...  They had shrimp and fish available that appear to have no breading, perhaps those would have fared better...Well, next time I get woken up by RiRi, I will certainly keep that in mind...

I was in Singapore and my friends who lives here brought me out to this place. They did the ordering so I can't recall the names of everything ordered. I know we had the chili crabs, gailan, baby clams, eggplants, and fried chicken. Everything tasted really good! I felt like an insider eating here.

This place is fine, but pricier than I would have liked. We paid about $270 for 11 people. The food tends to be a tad salty. My biggest gripe about this place was that they charged $2 per person for tea, and never once changed the leaves in the pot. This means, we paid $22 for one pot of chrysanthemum tea--that's outrageous and disgusting. Had it been 2 or 3 pots of tea, fine. But one pot of tea that gets topped up with only water? $22 is way way way too much! We ordered everything sized large, but some of the dishes were impressively small for a 'large size'.We ordered:Chaipo Tofu--OK. Tofu quite soft. Chaipo not crispy though.Guinness Pork Ribs--Very small portion. There was not enough pork ribs for everyone to have a single piece on their own. Tastes very good though, but portions were too small. Not worth it!Cereal Prawn--The prawns were a little overcooked and dry. Cereal topping was not bad, but there were not that much cereal topping.Salted Egg Squid--Very good! Squid was overcook and slightly chewy.Yam Ring--OK. A bit salty.Har Cheong Gai--Good and crispy!Thai Style Chicken--Good! Folks liked this dish.Sambal Kangkong--Very salty.Garlic Huang Di Cai--Very salty.Stir Fried Lala--Not as good as it was touted to be. Lots of shells that didn't have any meat in them.Sun Moon Hor Fun--Very impressive with raw egg on top, but taste like regular horfun or pad see ew. Not very special.Sap Gam Hor Fun--Not bad, but not that much wokhei flavor.Mee Goreng--Too spicy for a lot of us.
Our favorite east coast eatery introduced by a buddy who bailed for vietnam! Marmite chicken and salted fish fried rice. Nuff said

Rule No. 1: Do not follow the crowd in Singapore when choosing a restaurant. I live down the street and often see this place packed in the evenings, more so than the Five Star Chicken Rice place next door. So one evening we decided to give it a try and it was probably the last time we'd ever go there. Dishes we ordered: garlic baby kailan, three-cup chicken and garlic stir-fry clams. What was brought over to the table was half cooked kailan with some visibly blackened leaves, overly sweet three-cup chicken and very gooey stir-fry clams. We couldn't finish them. It was completely uninspired cooking, and these materials deserved a lot more tender, loving care. Service wasn't bad, which was probably the saving grace.

Sin Hoi Sai Eating House - If I lived anywhere closer to the East, I am guessing I would be here a lot more than I'd be willing to admit. In a tight group of 8 friends, 7 of them live pretty close to Sin Hoi, and these 7 congregate here for dinner at least 2-3 times a week.On the few occassions I've been here, service has been excellent, also in part due to the fact that my friends are regulars. They swiftly take your order for beverages, leave, bring them to your table and collect your food orders while they are at it. On weekends this place does get crowded, so avoid peak dinner timings, or be prepared to wait for a table and for your food orders to be served.We have a few favourites, I'll list them out - do be certain to give them a try! We love going for their sambal char siew fried rice, prepared with an adequate amount of spice and served in a portion good for 1 person. We swear by their Indonesian chicken dish, a slightly tangy crispy chicken dish where the fried chicken is glazed with a light, spicy gravy and onions. Being chicken fans, we almost always have to have their hot plate chilli ginger chicken as well - a bowl of it dropped right on to the hot plate at your table so it's sizzling and all the more enjoyable when had with the fried rice. The few other favourites include their baby kailan in oyster sauce, crispy noodles, fried salad you tiao, sambal kang kong and prawn paste chicken. Their menu is expansive, and I wouldn't say that the food here is inexpensive, but given it's prime location and good quality, you pay for what you get. (I spend an average of $10 - 15 here including soft drinks and food shared with about 4-5 friends). I would definitely have to come back here many more times to try everything else on their menu. Lucky I have friends who are regulars.

standard tze char. nothing fancy. Pricing is a little high, I thought,  but then this is Katong.I love san-lou horfun. This place's not bad, but still lacking that elusive wok-hei flavor.The marmite chicken - I had better marmite dishes. I love marmite and the salty-bitterness of it all. The marmite flavor is not enough for me. (then again, for people who doesn't quite like the taste of marmite, they like this dish as it is more subtle). Also didn't like that the portion came mainly with chicken breast pieces only. I will eat there if I am around the neighborhood. but nothing to hike the distance for.

Having supper here is always the best way to cap a night of partying off. The explosion of tastes from the awesome Sambal Beef Fried Rice is always a good way to wake yourself up from that drunken night that almost ended with you in an alcohol coma. A plate of prawn paste chicken on the side should help with that burnt tongue from the sambal. Yup, do beware. It's spicy!The operating hours are from 5pm to 4am however, they do start washing the place at about 345am so try to get there and place your orders by 330am. There are lots of parking lots within walking distance at Chapel Road, Chapel Close, Cheow Keng Road or Lor Stangee however, it can get quite busy at dinner time because of the many restaurants in the vicinity. Late nights, are never a problem.I'm there at least 3 times a week and I really hope to bump into you folk soon. See ya!

Known for its seafood and extensive ways in which fried rice and noodles can be served, Sin Hoi Sai is a secret gem for vegetarians too. It isn't on the menu, but there are a number of dishes cooked with mock meat that you can choose from, as well as customisable options from the regular menu. Just ask! Highly recommended is the Indonesian Chicken. which always manages to fool even the most meaty of meat-eaters. It goes great with fried rice, which you can ask for with only veggies (instead of meat) and tofu (instead of egg, if you're vegan). Go green with Garlic Kang Kong, a veg-friendly alternative to Sin Hoi Sai's Sambal Kang Kong. Just those 3 dishes and you're set; that's pretty much all I order every time I'm there, which is pretty often :) It's also cool for enjoying some beer before or after a big night out partying!

My mum is in love with this eating house, and then she made us all fall in love with the awesome hor fun and sambal kangkong. There is a charred fried flavour that the chinese call "wok hey" with the hor fun and they have concocted a really solid sambal  for their vegetables. Prices are really reasonable, for a family dinner with 4-5 dishes, we would probbly pay $60- $70. It can get really crowded and noisy over the weekends. So if you're starving maybe it's not so good an option to go for dinner on a weekend.

Thai restaurant in Singapore with several branches. Authentic Thai food at very affordable prices. Been here a few times when I crave Thai food. Curries, veggie dishes and Pad Thai are pretty good safe bets. Basil chicken a bit salty. Their Thai milk tea is very sweet though. Portion is a bit small - would recommend ordering a lot of dishes to share / sample.

2 of us queued up just before the outlet was opened for business. Yet we were treated like invisible. The rude woman just waved and the staff showed the 3 of them to a table, bypassing us. When I proceed indoor to take the last table, the staff made us to take the outdoor table which was pretty hot given it was noon time and there was no fan blowing outside whereas indoor there's fans on. Reason given that we were 2 persons, whereas the other groups got 3 persons. What kind of treatment was this! Yet when I was paying I could spot guys of 2 taking the tables for 4 indoor.Bad experience!Don't come here for small groups!

Decent Prices for Average Food. There's something about Thai food that captivates everyone. Whether it's the over the top, burn your mouth off chilli or that combination of flavours that evokes all your senses at once, Thai food never fails to warm your heart and make you crave for more. Being a regular at Holland Village, we've seen the super long queues for Nakhon Kitchen and it's always made us wonder just how good the food is. We finally had the chance to try when, amazingly, there were less than 10 people in the queue. Waiting time was around 15 mins considering that most people had wanted to sit indoors instead of outside in the sweltering hit. Having a few favourite thai joints, we had to try some of our favourites. Tom Ka Chicken Soup ($6) Unlike most people who go on the search for the best Tom Yum soup, I love my Tom Ka. I love myself a god Tom yum but Tom Ka elevates that sour tanginess with the rich, smooth, sweetness of the coconut milk. There's was a good portion of chicken and mushroom and while it offered that tangy kick, it was a little light on the coconut milk. While it gave it that milky colour, the sweetness and richness of the coconut milk didn't shine through as much. Pineapple Curry with Mussels ($8)The one thing I admire about thai curries is their ability to use fresh fruits into their curry, adding that extra level of sweetness to compliment to spiciness and sourness. The curry here was pretty nice, thicker than I expected but really spicy and Because of that spiciness, it didn't really do much for the mussels. While the mussels were large and fresh, they didn't add a lot of flavour into the curry and vice versa. Maybe because there were only 5 mussels. Ironically, when I took the dish home, added in some coconut milk and cooked it with fish, it turned out to be a very good fish curry. Stir fried Kai Lan with mushrooms ($6)Kai Lan was not overcooked, which was nice. Mushroom, sliced, were juicy but the overall dish was just a bit too salty for me. I love the use of thai oyster sauce in vegetables, I use it a lot too in mine but this was just too heavy on the sauce. Thai Iced Tea ($3)This had to be the biggest let down for me. At $3, it was probably the most diluted or weak thai iced tea I've had. Overall, the food was decent but at the prices, I could see why they were so popular. Unfortunately for me, it really felt like the crowds were there more for the price than for how good the food actually is. For me, I'd still rather pay a little more and stick to my favourite Thai restaurants.

Ok, not the best Thai food in the world, but probably the best value-for-your-money Thai food in Singapore. There's usually a queue here for dinner, even late into a weekday evening around 9pm, so just prepare yourself. They serve authentic Thai food including all the classics and a killer sticky mango rice dessert. The prices are very affordable for a serviced restaurant with seating and free napkins, and they don't have GST or service charge! My only qualm is the pork floss on top of the pineapple fried rice, which seems like a very Singaporean-style of preparation. Still, save yourself from the food court, Black Canyon, or Thai Express and eat at Nakhon next time you have a craving! I believe there's three locations throughout Singapore.

Came here with the recommendation of a friend who loves Thai food. He said that I may have to queue. I get suspicious whenever there's queue outside a restaurant in Singapore. Nevertheless, I gave it a shot. Arrived 10 minutes earlier as I don't believe in queueing for food. Order was taken and the nice lady told me with a smile that once the store it's opened, we will be served promptly. Very nice.Ordered Tom Yam soup, $6 and my favorite Phad Thai $5. The restaurant was half full 2 minutes after opening. Food arrived pretty quickly. Dug into Phad Thai and the soup. My heart sank. Why is it so sweet? The Phad Thai appeared to have a big bunch of sugar in it. Like wise for the soup. I have made both dishes at home and it can taste good without the sugar load. I looked around me and I can see patrons tucking enthusiastically into the sugar bin. For the easy on the pocket prices, I can see why it's so popular.Came here a second time and was hoping it will be better. The green curry chicken is horrible. It's frozen chicken and paste at best.

I'm only gradually getting used to waiting in line for food and typically I am not amused by a long line but WOW, this was worth the wait: this is the best Thai food I've had outside Thailand and it is super affordable!I came here on a Tuesday evening and it was the only place in Holland V which had a long line but I decided to give it a go anyway.  Good thing the line moved fast but we still had to wait for 45 mins but as it was not very hot outside, we enjoyed people watching. Also, it gave me enough time to extensively study the menu and decide what to get. A bonus is also that after a while they took our order whilst still being in line so once we got to our seats our food was served super fast.The atmosphere in the restaurant was great, it was obviously super busy but not in an annoying "full cantine" type of way, it was just bustling and when seated outside you could still enjoy the live music from Bar Bar Black Sheep across the street. I actually like that they use fans instead of aircon, this creates a cozier environment instead of a sterile place. The staff was very helpful which was unexpected since they were so busy.And then the food... Super delicious! We had the Shrimp Tom Yum soup, I am typically not a Tom Yum fan but this was super yummy (sorry for the bad pun).Since my dining companion preferred not to go for spicy dishes (except for the Tom Yum soup which had quite a kick), we went for the spring rolls, chicken in pandan leaves, green curry and pad thai. All of these dishes were fantastic, they tasted clean and had the right balance.I was in a pretty good mood when the check arrived as I noticed that there was no service or gst added. 27$ for two persons, what a bargain!Will I go again? You bet! Who doesn't love cheap, delicious food and good service?
Busy, they don't take credit cards and they forget your order... food's pretty good though! I loved the mango salad

An authentic Thai makan place. Their food are really good.....often orders their Basil pork (spicy and right amount of sweetness), stir-fried squid in yellow curry, kang Kong and of course, tom yam soup.Get prepare to perspire with the spice & freshly hot cook food.Oh yes, I always order the Fanta Green, it something that Singapore use to have long time ago..Bon Apertit...

The queue at this place is incredible. We arrived at 11:45am but the place only opens at noon sharp. We started the queue and soon there were quite a number of people behind us. Once the shutters open, everyone shuffled in and each waiter got assigned to a table. The service was very prompt without any compromise on quality of the food. The pandan chicken and prawn cakes were the highlight among our dishes. I felt that the Pad Thai did not have the wok hei smell. The prawns in the tom yum soup were big and fresh. The lemongrass drinks were also very refreshing as only the fans were switched on but not the air con.

This hole-in-the-wall, hawker-center like restaurant (no AC, outdoors) has one of the best, authentic and CHEAP Thai food ever. Not the freshest and best quality ingredients in dishes as the ones in expensive thai joints, such as Patara at Tanglin Mall, but it's authentic as you can get, as the ones you'd eat in a normal restaurant in Thailand. We frequent this place as it's near our home, and love that we can order 7~8 dishes without breaking the bank. and the portions are pretty great. The line forms out the door at 5:30pm when it's opened for dinner as any other cheap and great for value dining in Sing, so come early to avoid queue. Must gets: (all around $5~8/dish)-Pandan Leaf Chicken. Tasty and plump chicken, wrapped in the leaf!-pineapple fried rice-shrimp pad thai-tom yum soup. portion is great and delicious-Basil minced pork. D loved it as it's full of flavor. -Green Curry-thai ice teaso-so's:-Mango sticky rice: mango is expectedly not as sweet as the ones you'd try in Thailand, but we expected more from the rice. the rice was hard and tasteless.-cereal shrimp. a bit soggy and not worth getting it here. better to spend more and get the perfectly cooked one at Jumbo or No signboard!

Great taste good value and prompt service.This is those well run small restaurants that keeps its customers returning for the great taste and good value.We ordered five dishes; Tom yum, green curry, stir fried asparagus, pandan leave chicken and pineapple rice.The green curry is a winner for me, always my favorite and this place got it right. The prawn were fresh, and the curry is rich with a nice aroma of coconut, basil, and the long beans and fig were crunchy. The stir fried asparagus is a surprise, a good balance of garlic brought out the sweetness of the asparagus, the carrots is probably there to add color, but the prawns here is probably frozen thawed type. Pandan leaf chicken is a biggest pleasant surprise of all, very tender like otah, chicken chunks soft. A definite repeat order.Tom yum is well prepared. Good balance of spicy and sour, and seafood prawn and squid is fresh, I don't normally order Tom yum on my own, but this dish is good enough for me to try.I would not order the pineapple rice next time round. No comments on the taste but I do think white rice will bring out the tastes of the above dishes better.
Standard just constantly dropping and they obviously play very loud Thai music so as to deter customers from staying longer than normal.

I was pleasantly surprised to find Nakhon Kitchen in my neighborhood so I decided to go there with my parents. we went on a Saturday evening around 6pm and found ourselves behind a long line of people. we eventually sat down after 35 mins of waiting; orders were taken while we were in line so it helped speed up the serving of dishes. we ordered olive fried rice, pandan leaf chicken, seafood tom yum with coconut milk, whole red fish thai style, kang kong belachan, mango salad, and cereal prawn. i really enjoyed all the dishes and as other reviews have said, the pandan leaf chicken was very good. i was excited about the cereal prawn because it was only $12 for quite a huge portion (based on what i saw on other tables before i ordered). the prawns didnt fail me and they were pretty big, fresh and succulent. i did however think that the cereal was lacking a little in taste when compared to what they serve at the zhi char stalls. for all that, including a mango glutinous rice to go and a coconut drink as well as a glass of lemon grass drink, we paid $67 and took home enough food for lunch next day. this place is certainly value for money! i would definitely go again!

Great tasting thai food! The line gets pretty long during dinner time, but the good thing is that they take your order while you are in line. When you get seated, your food is handed to you quickly. I love the pad thai here, probably the best I have tasted in Singapore so far. Also I recommend trying the green tea here!
Great thai place with authentic dishes and drinks. They have a good selection and their prices are really affordable ! Greatly recommended ! Come early as the place is always crowded

My friend who lives in the area told me there are two types of people who eat here: Tourists, and people with hangovers. Even so, the broth they serve here lives up to the hype. We had a side of salted vegetable (just okay), and also a pork belly dish in a stone pot that was pretty tasty.  While I wouldn't mind coming back, it wouldn't be the first place I came to when going to Singapore.

The outlet was newly opened and located in quite hidden location at the level 2 of the shopping centre. Menu and wet tissue was served after I was showed to a table. One could reject the wet tissue as it is chargeable. The condiments such as sliced chilli, dark soya sauce, light soya sauce, chilli sauce can be found at the divider by the table. There was also a teapot and hot water from the tap on the divider to brew tea. There was a pail available for the bones.Pork Ribs Soup ($7)Served in a traditional rooster bowl with 2 ribs and garlic.The pork ribs was quite tender. The soup was peppery. The soup was refillable. A staff would go around with a kettle to refill the soup. Throughout the meal, the staff refilled twice for me without being reminded.Braised Chicken Feet with Beancurd Skin ($4)The chicken feet was very tender and melt in the mouth. The beancurd skin was not bad too.Mee Sua ($2.50)Its texture was quite smooth and light.Do take note of your table when making payment at the cashier. By the way there was a 7% GST and 1% service charge on the bill. Staffs were friendly and service was fast.

Good food, hate having to pay 20¢ for each wet tissue that they put on our tables, or 30¢ for dry tissue paper. For real. You're rich and have franchises overseas. Stop being so petty please. Service is ehh... but I can't help but feel like the taste of the soup in this branch is inferior to the one across from Central in Clarke Quay. Maybe it's just me.

Relatively new branch of Song Fa that I would recommend people to go to instead of the original stall (the one at New Bridge Road). It is much roomier than the New Bridge while still offering same quality (you know, they don't suffer from the degraded quality that is common as restaurants expand)Onto the food. They serve Bak Kut Teh (duh) in the style that I prefer. The soup is peppery and one could definitely taste that the broth came from hours of boiling pork bones. On top of that, they do have unlimited broth refills, so don't be sad if you're running out of the delicious soup, they would refill it for free. On top of that, there are other side dishes, which are common offerings in most BKT stall. The side dishes are all fine but I think the dough fritters deserves a special mention. Their dough fritters are crispy without being oily, which complements the soup very well. Another thing that one may want to note, they serve 2 kinds of tea. One is the common teabags and the other one is the traditional chinese tea (complete with all the chinese tea set, you know the one with the small cups).

I've only ever been to the old location at Rifle Range. The new set up is much bigger and yet they've somehow manage to keep the ambience cosy. Service is still as excellent as I remember. We had the squid ink pasta and the lobster midweek special. Perfection complete with the bruschetta and beef carpaccio. Definitely a must visit for anyone craving good authentic Italian. P.S. Tuesday's ladies night and you can a free glass of proseco with your main!

Some hits and misses, but definitely outrageously expensive.Food-wise, the pasta is above average, but the price is definitely way far above average. I was wowed by the squid ink fettuccini, excited by the grilled octopus tentacle, bored by the beef ravioli and utterly disappointed by the bread sticks. (For the record, the breadsticks were crusty, hard and far too dry)Service is exceptionally attentive and professional, and possibly one of the best experiences I've had dining in Singapore. It's the kind of place you can bring someone on a first date. (And leave crying when you are handed the check)My wallet is now begging me for mercy. Kinda explains the Ferrari parked outside (which I'm told, belong to the owner of the restaurant).

This is a review of a dinner date at Ristorante da Valentino.This was a very pleasant dining experience.  The entire experience (service, ambiance, menu) represent classic Italian dining.From the moment you are greeted, the staff is pleasant, professional, and informative.  Out of my entire experience at Valentino, the service is what stands out the most.Our "Captain" was obviously an experienced professional server.  He was consistently there.  He was very engaging.  He was very informative with the menu and what to expect.  I love the table side portioning of the appetizers.  It just adds a touch of sophistication and personalization to the experience.The ambiance is relatively classic fine dining.  It is large open space.  There are sporadic tchotchkes that add touches of charm along the way.The food ranged from flawed to excellent.  The starters were fantastic.  The squid pasta dish was amazing.  For some reason, each of our mains were disappointing.  My dinner date was very dissatisfied with her main.Ciabatta Bread - This was very good.  It was warm with a mild flavour and there was a very nice dipping oil for it.  (I am going to note here.  This was presented as complimentary bread but it is not.  They charge $6.50 for it.  I expect this in lesser restaurants in Singapore.  I do not expect it in a dining experience that is going to run over the $500 mark.  They simply do not need to stoop to this level.)  tinyurl.com/m6kuebpBurrata with tomatoes - This was simply a plate of heaven.  The creamy warm burrata.  The tomatoes had a light sweetness.  The small bit of ham for additional saltiness.  Even the greens worked to add some additional texture and a peppery bite. The dish was brought to the table as a complete dish.  Our "captain" then cut and portioned the dish.tinyurl.com/lw6gmyuGrilled Octopus Tentacle - This was so very good. The octopus was tender.  There was a soft smokiness from the searing.  It was just delicious.This dish was also brought to the table whole and then portioned table-side.tinyurl.com/md55gcnSquid Ink Fettuccini with crab meat - This was our selection for a pasta course.  This was rich and creamy goodness.  I think I finished my portion in two minutes.  I have never wielded a pasta spoon with such speed and grace.  The crab was buttery.  The pasta was perfectly prepared. The sauce was silky.  The squid ink was perfectly restrained.tinyurl.com/lf3v7jwManzo Gorgonzola (steak with bleu cheese) - This was my main course.  This was a basic and neatly presented dish.  Unfortunately, I did not like it very much.  It came down to the beef.  I simply did not enjoy the flavour of the meat.  It was cooked to a perfect medium rare.  I just didn't enjoy the way it tasted.  I also thought the bleu cheese would play a stronger role in the flavour  profile.  The sides were basic and lacked imagination.tinyurl.com/m9ypje6Sirloin with foie gras - My dinner companion selected this item from the evening's specials.  She did not enjoy it. Primarily, she stated the rosemary was dominating the entire flavour of the dish.  This is an easy mistake to make when using fresh rosemary.  She did not eat very much of her main course.I do not have a photo of this dish.Lemon Sorbet - This was her dessert.  It was elegantly presented using the frozen rind of a lemon.  She seemed to enjoy it.  I did not try it.  tinyurl.com/mofovkoSalame Cioccolat - This was a chocolate cookie dish with ice cream.  I found it to be an average chocolate dish.   It's chocolate.  So, it was good.  But, it was not anything special.  I also found the hardness of the cookies made it a little challenging to eat.tinyurl.com/mrwj9snReceipt (Dinner for two): $530.00tinyurl.com/lh3256aOverall - I do think this was a very enjoyable experience.  I can't say enough great things about the service.  The ambiance is classic fine dining.  The menu is diverse.  It all fits so well together.  The food had some extreme high points (starters through  pasta course).  However, the main courses fell a little short and this is the reason I am only providing a four star review.  I would not hesitate to return. I also think it an excellent option for a special dinner.

My first visit was when they were a small cozy outfit at Rifle Range. Came back last weekend for dinner at their new home at Turf City. Food was still excellent. Still impressed by their aged beef served on a wooden board (didn't get the dish name). Lightly seasoned, moist and so tender. Mouth watering delicious. Go for the lightly charred parts and I reckon you will remember the taste for a long time. Desserts: they don't do trolley service anymore what a shame. Don't let that stop you from going up to the display to see what's available. The panna cotta is an absolute must try. Flawless service. Attentive and personable. What can I say- I love this place!

There aren't many Italian restaurants in Singapore that serve such wonderfulHomely food. The service is often top notch. A tip would be to order the specials such as the buffalo mozza or the grilled octupus leg. This is quite a pricey restaurant though.
The more other Italian places I go to in Singapore, the more overpriced I think this is. I prefer Trattoria Lafiandra, Bella Pasta, and Cicheti.

I wasn't quite as blown away as everyone else at Valentino, so feel free to take my review with a pinch of salt. I went there to celebrate a friend's birthday. We got the private room, everything was pre-ordered, and there was plenty of food to go around.First off, the service was excellent. We had a person assigned to our room, he was friendly, helpful, and was always able to get us whatever we needed (plates, condiments, etc.). He was also very friendly, and in fact the entire team was. It was a very warm, personable dining experience, and I cannot fault the service at all. Food wise, the antipasti was good... borderline great. We had some grilled vegetables, marinated mushrooms, ham, the usual basically and it was all of good quality. I just wasn't blown away because that's really the minimum you expect now of a respectable Italian restaurant. I actually found the pastas very mediocre. We had a vegetarian Aglio Olio and a ricotta and spinach cannellon. Neither were spectacular, both were just good. The mains of fish and pork were also unspectacular. Good but so uneventful that I just remember being satisfied, but unimpressed. Maybe they just didn't suit my palate, maybe we just ordered the wrong things.I'd would come back even if I only rated it 3 stars because maybe I just didn't order the right items. At least, that MUST be the case if everyone else rates them so highly.

Still my favourite Italian restaurant in this country. Yes, I like it more than the higher end Italian restaurants.It's moved to a new location on Turf Club Road (sadness). Its original Jalan Bingka/Rifle Range location was perfect, because it was so hidden away. It still maintains the sense of hiddenaway-ness, even with larger space at Turf Club Road.Diners who have been going to Valentino for a long time will fondly remember the living room and how it was such an integral part of the entire Valentino experience. This restaurant was never atas or fancy -- it was warm, homely, and made you happy with the great food from the great family that made it. Chef Valentino cooks with his mother Alma. It's beautiful.The food is still good, still very authentic, and sometimes it seems like various family members will just spring up and go to cook you something... and that's good! "Try my mama's lemon tart!" When someone enthusiastically wants you to try his mother's desserts, you must.I have been eating here for a long time and.. I love everything. Especially the squid ink pasta. I love all the risottos, and all the mains, and all the appetizers... I love everything here. Most of all I love the warmth of this family and the amazing place they've built together. Truly a gem of the west.

Valentinos is small family run Italian restaurant here in Singapore. Having visited Italy, I would say this place is the most authentic you can get here on the island. Amazing food and even more amazing Italian hospitality. The staff (all family) go out of their way to talk to you and make you feel welcome. You feel as though you are entering their home for a meal.Food is fantastic and very authentic. A must try is the burata mozzaralla served with tomatoes. Its flown in straight from Italy and is amazing. Try their desserts as well, all made by the daughter, Perla.

Ristorante da Valentino is a truly italian restaurant. Maybe the only really italian restaurant in Singapore, very authentic. It is run by a family, who is very warm and after all these years they work just as hard for you to make you happy. When you celebrate a birthday here the whole family comes out and sing for you. And this is while they don't have to do that because they already made their money, visible from the ferrari's outside. The food is amazing, fresh and intense. Italian cuisine at it's best. Simple dishes with high quality ingredients prepared perfectly. My favorite is the mozzarella and the truffel pasta's. Their desserts are made by Perla, who also has a store at the Taka basement.

This place serves the most delicious italian food I can find in Singapore. Very authentic, very home-style. The decor is beautiful, very old-school Italian with a touch of modern art. They have a nice patio and herb garden that they are still working on, but the interior of the place is already sufficient to leave an impression, with an eclectic display of various vintage appliances, photographs of various parts of Italy, and salmon colored tablecloths (which I never thought could work...anywhere.). If you plan on coming here, please plan on paying around 100 per pax. The mains are around 20-50 dollars, but you have to pay for bread ($5.50) and my mixed berries cheesecake was 16 bucks. A glass of pinot grigio was 20 bucks, go figure. I guess I'm used to homestyle italian restaurants back in southern california where they offer free bread and offer a free dessert on your birthday....Anywho, the food was delectable. We had the burrata with cherry tomatoes and greens, and the burrata was very milky and fresh and was a delight to eat. The tomatoes were from Sicily and very ripe and sweet. We had the fried anchovies too, which is a Roman specialty, and it was comparable to that served in Roma. My squid ink fettucine with crabmeat in a creamy tomato sauce was a tad too creamy for me, although the flavor was very good and the crabmeat was very sweet. I really enjoyed the gnocchi in gorganzola sauce. The gnocchi was like soft pillows of pleasure and definitely home made. I would come back just for the gnocchi. My mixed berry cheesecake was very light, fluffy and just the right amount of sweetness. One of the better desserts I've had in a while. In general, a good place to splurge at for a special occasion.

Tried out this place on a review by a fellow helper. One detail, it is on the 5th floor of the Takashimaya shopping center.I ordered the scallop mentaiyaki and the Kaisen chirashi don for lunch. The don was pretty good except for the tuna and salmon which were a little fibrous. This meant it wasn't the best cut of fish or it was not prepped properly. Overall it was a very tasty dish. As for the scallop it was sliced very thin and tasted amazing with a mildly spicy mayonnaise and some truffle (I think) oil. I does come across a little greasy. Other than that the dishes were very good for about US$33.

If you are craving for the ultimate aburi chirashi bowl, you are at the right spot. This is a must try. Fresh and thick slices of sashimi, torched just enough to release the omega three goodness, coating the rice below, this is literally a bowl of heaven if I can only imagine. Their other dishes are also very competent and all rather reasonably priced. Make a reservation to avoid long queues.

The place brought back a fond memory. It's funny sometimes to think that everyone seems to have moved on, while I got stuck in time and resist to grow up. I stepped in right at 9pm when they took the last order. I opted for the torched sashimi over rice, same as last time- at $26, it's a big bowl full of fatty pieces. Though anti-carb, I cannot stop eating the rice as it's the right texture and almost bouncy on my teeth. Also, the sashimi was so fatty- I had to use the rice to balance. ;) Imagine how satisfying it was.. Now, I am ready for my midnight flight home. ;p Until next time..

The Sushi Bar is a few steps away from Sushi Tei but how people still pick Sushi Tei over The Sushi Bar is a mystery to me. Only explanation could be that they do not know there is sushi heaven behind the corner.The place was packed on a Thursday night around 7 pm, but we managed to get a seat right away. Overall, the service was super quick and food appeared almost instantly.I will join the choir and sing praise for their kaisen chirashi don: it really is as amazing as you read in the reviews (and the reviews of their other location). The fish was amazing, the slices were thick and super fresh. I had trouble finishing the normal size don (granted I had a late and rather big lunch) which is a first!Highly recommended!

Came here a few weeks back with my friends, who were having a massive craving for some sushi. Although located quite centrally (in Taka), I had a difficult time looking for the shop as it was tucked away in a corner. We were quite early, and didn't have to wait too long for a table, so that was good! (Though I've heard it can get pretty crowded, so do try to go early!)The service was a disappointment; the waitstaff was less than attentive, and my friend had to get her own water, after asking for it a couple of times. The food however, was their saving grace. I loved their salmon aburi roll & the sauce they put in their sirloin steak; it was a nice balance of sweet and salty, and acidic. It was also reasonably priced!Would definitely recommend this place if you're okay with substandard service.

I truly regret not trying this place earlier! Yes I've heard about this place also having one of the most worth it chirashi sets at a good price. Well... Everyone was right! As seen on Yelp, I went for the popular items right away - the scallop mentaiko carpaccio to share, I had the premium chirashi and my friend being a smaller eater had the normal chirashi. The premium chirashi even came with uni inside with big and plump ikura! Everything was generally very fresh, however the prawn was a bit slimy and strong tasting to be absolutely honest. Everything else was to expectation and a little above, given the great feedback all over the Internet. One thing about this place that really stuck out was their stuff which are aburi-ied (flame torched) ! Anything that they flame torched wasn't just for show. It really does bring out that extra flavour! They seemed like masters at it. Even down to the scallop mentaiko carpaccio! That smokey flavour.... I miss it already!They seem to have a chirashi bowl that is all aburi (torched on one side and raw behind)! I absolutely can't wait to go back and try that! I'm giving this outlet 4.2 out of 5 stars! Would have been slightly higher if it weren't for that lousy prawn! ;)

This branch of the sushi bar offers more seating and a larger menu. Service, however, is brusque and sullen. The aburi salmon roll they are famous for is flavourful at first bite. The dollops of mayo on top lends it sweetness and creaminess, with a touch of saltiness that accentuates the other flavours. However, once you remove the dollop of mayo on top, the roll itself is extremely average. Though fatty and plump, the salmon itself is not particularly flavourful. The filling of avocado and crab stick and lean maguro don't contribute much in terms of flavour too. So I would say the star of the dish is the mayo! :)  There are better quality sushi options out there at a similar price point.

I'm a huge fan of The Sushi Bar at Far East Plaza, so I was pretty psyched when I heard they were opening up another location down the road at Ngee Ann City.  In some sense, this location is even better than the original. Blasphemy, I know!  I find that the food selection here is a lot more extensive than the original. The Aburi Kaisen Chirashi Don, which in my view, is the STAR dish of this restaurant, is not available at the original location, from what I remember. Second, the Ngee Ann City space is far larger and has much more of a restaurant feel than the hole-in-the-wall experience at the original location. Third, the queue is a tad bit shorter.  In any event, the aburi dishes are the real winners of The Sushi Bar, separateing them from every other sushi restaurant in Singapore. I'm not familiar with the term "aburi", but from what I understand, it is essentially grilled/torched raw fish. The Sushi Bar has perfected the art of torching high quality sushi, leaving the edges burnt with the inside nice and raw. Simply, an awesome combination. In short, depending on whether you fancy chirashi or sushi, you should order either the Aburi Kaisen Chirashi Don, Salmon Aburi Roll or both!

My first time trying The Sushi Bar chain and it was a splendid experience indeed. This branch is pretty new, hence I'm the first reviewer. The queue was pretty long and told that we had to wait for 30 mins (on saturday night about 6:40pm) but we only waited for 18 mins. Woohoo!Anyway, we ordered their two kinda signature dishes:1. Aburi Kaisen Chirashi Don $26.9This is basically the main attraction and the star of the night! The combination of torched fishes with fresh glistening pearls a.k.a ikura is just perfect! Don't forget the rice is magical too! Toppings are generous with fresh grated wasabi and sliced ginger!2. Salmon Aburi Roll $15.9Raw salmon rolled with crabstick & avocado and topped with torched salmon! Double salmons attack! Great for salmon lovers! And two non signature dishes but very delicious as well:1. Teba Gyoza @$3.5 but no minimum orderAs good as I thought it'd be! Yes, you might have guessed it, it's actually chicken wing stuffed with gyoza fillings. Creatively delicious! Me love!2. Amaebi Karaage $6.9I always love Japanese sweet prawn sashimi and The Sushi Bar definitely nails the fried version.The ambiance is pretty nice, sophisticated decor and spacious area. Perfect for casual dining whether with a date or family. It is well hidden and located at the ngee ann city (behind serenity restaurant). Price wise, I think it's very reasonable too. I'll be back.

The sashimi is fresh and thick. The kitchen shows creativity, but some dishes are good (e.g. pitan tofu, or the daikon salad which looks like a mini yusheng and tastes ok if you don't mix the awful sweet pink stuff), while others are terrible (e.g. wafu spaghetti, amaebi karaage, scallop mentaitaki cut so thinly it breaks). The portions are minuscule, so you could end up spending $70 per head before being full. At least here, they take some credit cards (not Amex), whereas the original Sushi Bar outlet at Far East Plaza (which is cheaper) only takes cash. At this price level, with minimalist service, you'd be better off going to Ginza Kuroson Takashimaya on 3/F for much better ambience and better food. People will mourn the disappearance of mid-price, varied Japanese eateries at Nghee Ann City, like Sushi Tei or Ichiban Boshi. Now, for reasonably-priced Jap, you have to go to the basement lah!

My second visit at the Ngee Ann outlet for dinner. The place was relatively empty when I arrived around 645pm but by 730pm, a queue had formed. I had tried to make reservations but couldn't get through the line. The restaurant will only seat you if everyone is present. I had the aburi kaisen chirashi don for $27. The seafood was fresh and perfectly seared. My only grouse was that the rice could be seasoned better and a larger portion of rice provided because the amount of seafood overwhelmed the carbs. I guess that is a happy problem to have.

I was craving tapas, and found this place online for the unlimited weekend brunch ($38++ without sangria, menu here don-quijote-restaurants.…). I went there with my dad around 1pm on a rainy Saturday afternoon after making reservations. It was fun and the food was pretty good! We tried almost everything, since we are typical Singaporeans at a buffet haha. We split our order into 3-4 separate times, and the servers were quick and friendly. Sometimes I feel awkward for ordering a lot at a la carte buffet places, but definitely not here. Each dish is small with maybe 4-5 pieces. My favorites were *the gazpacho (very refreshing and tomatoey and each portion is in a little jug to be downed in 1-2 mouthfuls- I ordered maybe 5 of them)*the oven-baked eggplant in a casserole (this is literally an entire eggplant cut into half. delicious and chewy!!)*garlic fried shrimp (I LOVE the garlic taste, it had those fried bits too that were so delicious. Each order had maybe 8+ small shrimp)*asparagus rolled in bacon (what's not to like about asparagus and bacon!). The crab, scallop and avocado dip was also solid - I loved how it wasn't overly creamy or strong, and I could taste the little crab & scallop pieces. Strangely enough my dad was a huge fan of the scrambled eggs and ordered another portion. They seemed to resemble chinese-style scrambled eggs but were dry and fluffy. The chicken wings, meatballs, shrimp, etc were okay. Nothing wrong but nothing super impressive either. For desert, we tried both the orange cheesecake and the bread and butter: my dad loved the subtle citrus flavor of the orange cheesecake. I was pretty full by that time and they just tasted okay. 4 stars because I've had better tapas: the dishes were good but not mouthwateringly delicious. It's a great way to sample many dishes though, since tapas can get pretty expensive if you order individually. The Dempsey Hill area is really nice, albeit a little confusing - we drove around for a bit before finding Don Quijote, nestled further inside with a carpark right in front. The restaurant itself was a little dark, and there were around 2-3 other tables filled then. It had a very chill vibe - we, and the other tables, stayed for a few hours just eating and chatting. I'd love to come back to try their paella sometime, especially after reading the other Yelp reviews!

As a European, I love this place. Yes, it is at Dempsey Hill, which is an expat playground and despised by some because of that and the slightly higher price point of most places but after being in Singapore for some months, there are some days that I miss my home and this seems to hit all the right spots during one of those days.To clarify, I am not Spanish but I've spend many months as a young professional in Spain where I was involved in a project and whilst I disliked this project I found some comfort in the food and the warm culture and Don Quijote offers the same type of comfort. When browsing the menu, we asked the super friendly waiter (local, not Spanish and none of the staff speak Spanish) what paella size he would recommend for 2 and he told us that a small would do. So we settled for a small Paella Valenciana, a bottle of San Pelligrino (which is actually Italian but I consider that a detail) and two glasses of Sangria. I also appreciated that they ask you how you want the rice of your paella cooked.The paella is definitely a recommendation, it was fragrant and the rice was done perfectly (we asked for al dente). The typical crusty bits stuck to the pan made it a pleasure to scrape out every grain of rice. I was not super hungry so the small was enough to feed two people but I did find the portion on the smaller side and would recommend to add some tapas to make it a complete meal for two.Another big feature of Don Quijote is their outside seating, as it is located in Dempsey, it feels like you have escaped Singapore. After sunset, it has a cozy vibe, I really enjoyed sitting out there sipping the Sangria which by the way is not too special, average at best, but is a decent size glass so the atmosphere and amount of alcohol resulted me being in a forgiving mood.Would I return? Yes, I enjoyed the paella, liked the atmosphere outside and thought it was reasonably priced for Dempsey.

Made reservations through Chope for Don Quijote's Sunday tapas brunch. 1st star* Really liked their location within a leafy outdoor mall in the plush Dempsey Hill neighborhood. Another plus...lots of free parking. Dining room was beautifully decorated and low lit beautifully. Whomever designed this room did a great job. 2nd star* Although the staff and I had a little bit of a language barrier;they gave me tons of attention and absolutely fantastic service.  Once I understood the menu and the ordering process, a full hour of yummy Sangrias and tapas dishes just kept coming. Really some of the best service I have had dining out on Singapore! 3rd star* The quality of food, the quantity of food, and the presentation were all top notch. The seafood was good but it was the meat dishes that were outstanding. Well, Except for the meatballs. They were moist enough but really, really bland. One miss out of twenty five dishes, that's pretty good!4th star* The never ending Sangrias here were so good. I have been to Spain, sat on the Ramblas, pounding down pitchers of Sangrias. I know Sangrias...Don Quijote's makes a freakin great red Sangria. The white was good, the sparkling wine, better, but stick to the red for a taste of the real deal.The location, the staff, the food, the Sangrias, make this restaurant a most definite must return!

I'm not sure why others have low ratings, but it is always full and I love the food there.  All meals are good.  It's only that they have less waitresses so the service may not be as good as you expect.大好きなスペイン料理のお店です。明らかに美味いですね。パエリアも言えばきちんと追加レモンをくれるし、全般的に美味しいです。唯一、店員が少ないのでサービスはイマイチかもしれません。後らお値段もそこそこ行きますが、味がいいのでオケーです。ぜひお試しを。2015/11

This is a review of a dinner at Don Quijote.  It is a tapas restaurant in Dempsey.The ambiance is relatively basic.  It was a comfortable room.  However, that is about it.The service was inconsistent. At times, it was attentive.  At others, it seemed to disappear.  The staff was friendly and professional.   When my friend asked to have the prawns in the paella peeled, they obliged.   Maybe not quickly, but they obliged.  The food ranged from below average to very good.Pa am Tomaquet (Spanish ham with tomatoes on bread) - This was one of my favorite dishes here.  The ham was quite good.  While the bread and tomatoes were simple, they did work well in complimenting the Spanish ham.tinyurl.com/bfqwjrbCalameres Fritos (Fried Calamari) - This was probably my favorite dish of the meal.  It was served fresh from the fryer.  The breading was crispy and had a nice flavor without masking the natural flavor of the calamari.  The calamari was cooked perfectly.  It was very tender.tinyurl.com/ayou4kkPatatas Bravas - These were basic patatas bravas.  The potatoes were slightly overcooked though.  This made them a little dry.  The sauce was right out of the typical patatas bravas sauce recipe book.  Overall, a mediocre interpretation of a classic tapas dish.tinyurl.com/ax44ogjCamarones la Plancha (Garlic Prawns) - I love garlic.  I really do.  But, when having garlic prawns, I still want to taste the prawns. In their version, the only distinct flavor was garlic, garlic, and more garlic.tinyurl.com/ajpflyzPinchos Morunos con Salsa Chumichurri (Beef Skewers w sauce) - As with a number of the dishes here, this dish was well presented.  When it first arrived at the table, I was thinking "wow, this is going to be good".  Alas, after my first bite, my hopes were dashed.  This was barely edible.  The meat was covered in way to much oil.  There was a very strong flavor of overcooked oil.  It went mostly uneaten.tinyurl.com/a5abc2rPaella Especial - First, once again, this was a beautifully presented dish.  However, the seafood lacked that fresh out of the water taste I expect from a paella.  Plus, the rice was simply clumpy.  Despite the looks, this was not a very good paella.tinyurl.com/bj4xkupOverall - The service was here and there.  The quality of the food was all over the map.  There is nothing particularly special about the ambiance.  This is simply not a tapas restaurant that I can recommend.

Great place at the Dempsey Hill. The tapas are all very nice. Jamon - we have chosen the cheaper one which is nice enough. Sangria - got a choice of white, red and virgin and all the good. Ox-Tail - slow cooked with chicken peas, the meat is so soft and cant get enough only having one piece for each of us! Paella - Medium is good for 3 to share. We have ordered the seafood one which the prawn, mussel etc. are fresh. What else.... the squid! 3 choices of cooking - battered / olive oil / with its own ink. We have chosen the last one which turns out to be an excellent dish..! Yummy !

Had a birthday dinner here recently and Don Quijote did not disappoint. Located in the bustling centre of Dempsey Hill, this place is mostly frequented by families and large groups of friends. Which makes perfect sense since the menu is mostly made up of tapas and dishes for sharing. Since it was large group of us (more than 10 people), we ordered many tapas and paellas to share. All the tapas were good, but the most memorable for me was the Garlic Mixed Mushroom which we ordered a second serving of. Note that the servings are pretty small. I would say that each tapas portion is meant only for about 3-4 people. We ordered both the vegetarian and valencia (chicken and seafood) paella. Ingredients were generous for both, but most of us preferred the vegetarian version. We ordered a few jugs of sangria, both red and white, but the red was the more popular option by far!The service was excellent. I brought a birthday cake and the staff was immediately very helpful with storing the cake and later bringing it out at the appropriate moment. Will definitely be back!

This is my favorite Spanish place in Singapore. I followed them over from Lorong Kilat to their current location at Dempsey. The restaurant is very cosy and the service is friendly as well. I've tried quite a couple of dishes from their mains and tapas menu. The calamari is a must order for me. The nicely batter fresh squid comes with a special orange tar tar sauce. I can't remember what's that really. Maybe it's a garlic aioli. The garlic gambas (prawns) are also very fresh and succulent. I love their paella which is done on the spot. Order this once you get there and start with other tapas while your rice is being prepared. Thumbs up for the squid ink paella. If you don't like your rice al dente, you can request for it to be cooked a little longer. Their al dente is a little on the cooked side.There are the red and white sangria available here. 1 glass to give you the giggles and 2 to remove your inhibitions. Enjoy!

Over the years, Don Quijote has had more than its fair share of bad publicity, but it appears they've weathered negative reports of bad service, lackluster food, and Donoghue v Stevenson-type lapses. Their half-a-decade tenure in the brutal F&B scene, where Spanish restaurants are a dime and dozen these days, is evident of their staying power, and their loyal following. Tbh, Don Quijote isn't the most outstanding or exciting of Spanish restaurants, but like that trusty beat-up Toyota Corolla, the fare here is hearty, rustic, and solid.  Still, Don Quijote is excellent in their treatment of seafood, so best to focus your orders on their seafood-based tapas.We had:1) Gambas Al Ajillo ($18): get the live prawns, as opposed to the regular prawns. Purportedly sweeter, these were lipsmackingly good.Highly recommended.2) Grilled Squid ($16): absolutely fantastic. Brilliantly cooked, with a smoky accent, this was a must-try.3) Chipiron ($15): perfectly tender baby squid cooked in its own ink, wonderfully nuanced.4) Tacos de Lomo al Queso Azul ($21) - tenderloin beef cubes with blue cheese dressing: The beef was cooked very well, and sauce refined, but even that couldn't mask the gamey taste of the beef.5) Paella Especial ($53 for small): commendable, but a tad forgettable. That said, the seafood was very nicely treated, and swimmingly fresh.6) Churros ($16): Delicious, these were crunchy on the outside, moist and chewy on the inside

I liked this restaurant a lot. Was there with a crowd and it was fun passing all the dishes around. I thought the paella selection was good and very tasty. Pasta was just right and the cream sauce not too heavy. Wine selection was adequate and the cocktails good enough. The service--and we had two three-year-olds at the table--was understanding and on top of things. It's not five-star because it isn't fine dining, but it's great for a fun casual evening out. Bring the family and order some sangria!

Awesome service and managers; found us a nice corner table and took great care of us with good advice.  Great tapas (splurge for the expensive ones like the shrimp and beef - they are worth it).  Good house wines - all in, a nice chill environ to get a small plate and have a glass of wine.

Don Quijote bears repeat visits, and indeed, I haven't been disappointed at either instance. The interior is dim and cosy, and if you're the sort who likes to take photos of food, sorry, this place is going to elicit some curses from you. We ordered a load of tapas to share, and I thought the most unusual pick was the crab and scallop dip with toasties. Then again, you shouldn't miss out on the regulars as well, such as garlic shrimp, fried battered calamari, paella and the standard patatas bravas. If you can splurge, go for the Jamon Iberico - it's unbelievable how flavorful a few slivers of cured Spanish ham can get; a veritable samba on your palate. A jug or two of sangria wouldn't be too out of place here, but save some space for desserts as there are rather interesting items on the menu - notably the fried milk! It comes crispy on the outside and silky smooth on the inside; a weird kind of yum. Everything adds up quite steeply, and I remember my credit card smoking a little post dinner.
Tried calling earlier at 6pm to make a reservation but no answer...walked in and got a table.

Was in the mood for Tapas one night and stumbled upon Don Quijote after reading a few reviews online.The tapas were pretty decent, not the best I've had in Singapore but they were okay. The chorizo, garlic shrimp,  and other standard tapas were as expected, so its a good place to go if you're just looking for the basics.The Paella though was awful, overcooked and tasted as though it had been sitting out for hours before it was reheated.What was worse was the service. The waiters hardly understood what we were saying, were incredibly slow in bringing out our order and had the hardest time splitting the check between two credit cards. They even came back after 30 minutes of failed attempts and said they didn't know how to do it and asked us to just use one.Overall the meal was just average, so I don't recommend coming here unless you're truly out of options or if everything else is closed.

I'll have to start Ive never been here for dinner. I've only been to the brunch. Now that being said its not a bad deal for the free flow sangria, wine and beer.  The sangria is not very potent though.  They have a wide mix but I wouldnt say the quality is anything stellar.  The pasta tastes good, the crab dip is ok, the meatballs are ok but nothing really STANDS out.  Its fun just to go eat and drink with some friends but I dont find myself craving it or anything.  For $57 per person for the free flow your basically paying for the alcohol.
Please do not waste your time.  The apps are mediocre.  Paella really sub-par.  All for a very unreasonable price.  What a disappointment.

One of the fanciest Thai restaurants I've ever been to. Very posh interior, excellent service in an old British barracks type building. Food is very tasty and relatively authentic, although not particularly spicy. Good for date nights.

There are reasons I love this restaurant.1) Thai dancers dance throughout the restaurant. It's transportive.2) The grounds are like a spa. Very special.3) The interior décor was stunning.4) The food is not pretentious and was quite delicious.5) I just appreciated very casual food that's overdressed. Allows me to dress up and be comfortable with my friends and my wallet.6) Reasonable.

We went to Jim Thompson on our way to Changi as we were craving for Thai. The setting of this restaurant is just awesome - a quiet place full of trees with a tropical look and feel. The moment you walk towards the entrance of the restaurant, you are greeted by women in traditional Thai costumes. It's a great feeling of being in Thailand. The ambience of the restaurant is just fantastic. They have a vegetarian menu for folks like me - that's just fabulous.  We ordered coconut water to quench our thirst, what a way to get refreshed quickly!  It's served in the coconut and they even give you a spoon to scoop out the soft coconut flesh to eat once you are done drinking the water. We had the green curry, cashew tofu, fried rice and regular rice. Everything was delicious. We didn't have room for dessert. The service was out of the world.  Even though the restaurant was a tad bit expensive, it's totally worth it.  Great place to chill and unwind with great food. Highly recommended!

I had a tough time choosing between 3 and 4 stars for the Jim Thompson Thai restaurant on Dempsey Hill. They'd officially get 3.5 for me. I called in advance to make a reservation for 6 the day before and my husband requested outside seating.We got there and the architecture of the building reminded me a lot of the Jim Thompson museum in Bangkok. We were seated outside and got to watch 3 women dressed in Thai garb dance the whole evening. It was a little warm out and the patio did not have fans, so if you overheat easily (especially when noshing on spicy Thai food), I recommend grabbing a table inside.The drinks were good, but a little pricey at approximately $24 each. The mojitos were wonderful and so was the Jim Thompson Cooler. My husband and I started out with the Chef's Special Appetizer ($32) and it came with chicken satay, tiger prawns, crab spring rolls, marinated grilled beef rolls, and minced chicken salad. Sauces were brought out for all and they were delicious. We were actually able to order brown rice here in order to try to stick to our Paleo lifestyle. The rice was very earthy, a bit crunchy and delicious with the green curry and beef. We also got the half rotisserie Thai chicken ($26), which was cooked perfectly. In addition to this, we got the morning glory vegetable ($14) for the table. The food was excellent, and the service was friendly. They did get a little swamped shortly after we got there and we did have to ask for our second round of drinks a few times. The ambiance was lovely, and the food was good. If you're looking for a nice restaurant for a special occasion, this is a great choice.

I think this restaurant must be surviving on foreign travelers that are having it recommended by Hotel Concierges. While our appetizer was good, my stir fry was the worst Thai food I have ever have. There was absolutely zero flavor/spice. I was extremely disappointed. For the price and the recommendation from the hotel I had high expectations and was I disappointed. While the restaurant has a beautiful interior I don't go to a restaurant for the interior I go for the food. If you want Thai food go elsewhere, eat better and for less.

This is probably the fanciest Thai restaurant I've ever been to in my life. What I like about Thai is that you don't need to spend much to experience great food, but hey, there's nothing wrong with splurging every now and then (or so I keep telling myself!)Jim Thompson sets the tone immediately when you arrive. As it's outside Dempsey Hill, it's a bit more secluded, which gives off this feeling of being personally invited to someone's beautiful black and white home. At the entrance, there are ladies dressed in traditional Thai clothing that greet you in Thai, complete with the slight bow and palms pressed together. Walking inside, the decor was quite opulent. Nice silk decorations (after all... this is Jim Thompson we're talking about), occasional live music, and a beautiful bar.I dined here with my husband and his auntie, and we chose 2 curries, Pad Thai, and a veggie side dish. We all thought everything was well done. I thoroughly enjoyed my beef Mussaman curry (as it wasn't spicy) and the red curry with grapes blew me away. I thought the grapes would be weird (what can I say, sometimes my tastes are like that of a 5 year old) but it added sweetness that complemented the savoury curry very well. And the Pad Thai? Absolutely wonderful, it's one of the best Pad Thai's we've had outside Thailand! The crowd on a weekday night was majority expats, and it seemed like a lot of business meetings were going down. It's definitely a place to file under "Special Occasion", "Important Business Meeting", or "I'm Feeling Generous, Let Me Invite My Favourite CM Michelle To Jim Thompson Just Because".

Been a frequent traveler to Bangkok and tried many local Thai dishes , this place is really "OK" for the choices of food and can be better . Superb ambience and good to bring your guest over . Overpriced Thai food but if you are seeking to impress , why not ...

One of the best thai food ever. Fine dining. Almost every dish is nice. The price on average is about $50/ head but it is definately worth Try. Location is hard to find but better to take a taxi there
Nice ambience, a good place to bring tourists for a romanticized view of Thailand. Service is good but everything on the menu is so-so, watered down flavors for non-thai food aficionados.  Pricey too

Good thai resto, authentic though pricey, 2 people eating with 3 dishes and 1 dessert cost me sgd144. The food is really good though, i love the tom kha and dessert as usual mango sticky rice is always the best one
Love this place, the decor is beautiful,  food is delish. Service is excellent sometimes and at other times not so.

There is a fantastically crafted Thai touch to the Jim Thompson at Dempsey Hill. In terms of its interior design it truly embraces the art of Thai fabrics, materials and styles. The Thai cuisine is definitive, each dish is immaculately made, from presentation to tastes. It is delectable.The atmosphere is serene and the staff are well trained and very polite. They are prompt and always making sure everything is in its right order.I personally was very impressed by this place. From the general aesthetics, the service, to the food. You will find great variety on the menu, serving you more than 80 classic Thai dishes, including appetizers, spicy salads, soups, curries, main dishes, seafood, barbeque, noodles, desserts and more.The prices are high (you will spend around 30- 120 dollars), but the ambiance makes up for it.The building is beautifully historic, definitely a must try, at least once!

awesome!  one of the best meals I have had in Singapore and the best service.  Went with two vegetarians and a guy that only eats veg and  seafood. no problem lots of choice to cater to all.   service super polite. super fast.  food and drinks fresh and tasty.  the people I went with have eaten literally all over the world and they loved it and are going back again.  I would not say cheap but good value for the quality.  if that wasn't enough some lovely Thai traditional dance also while you eat.  won't be my be my last time.

I had heard so much about Jim Thompson and was extremely excited to finally try it out. Imagine my disappointment. The food was bland, boring and unbelievably over priced. I would never recommend this restaurant and am appalled by the number of people that actually think this is good food.We ordered the 3 person starter with Spring Rolls, Chicken Wings, Pomelo Salad and Prawn Cakes. At $44 dollars this was the worst decision of the evening. There was no spice, no flavor and no salt at all. Everything was deep fried to a point where that's all you could taste. We had the Green Curry & Red Curry with beef, equally unimaginative, and a Pad Thai that was cold and tasteless.The three of us spent $284-- infuriatingly expensive for a miserable meal.

Nice ambience, and lovely colonial building, but the food at Jim Thompson is lackluster, far from authentic, and depressingly watered down. Notwithstanding the abysmal fare, the restaurant was still a full-house on a mid-week evening. Packed with business-types.We had:1) Goong Hom Sabai ($20): mushy prawns swaddled in a rice paper and yellow egg noodles, and deep-fried to oblivion. The tasty plummy chilli dip did little to save the overdone appetizer.2) Khao Phad Nam Lieb ($20) - rice fried with black olives and minced chicken, sided by raw shallots, lime dice, cashews, and chillis: one of two dishes that actually passed muster, this had a good amount of flavour and char.3) Gaeng Panang Neau ($24) - panang curry with Australian beef tenderloin, coconut cream, and crushed peanuts: the other commendable dish, but it would have been better served piping hot, instead of tepid.4) Phad Grapow Gai ($22) - stir-fried minced chicken with straw mushrooms, garlic, birds eye chilli, and holy basil: should have been punchy but it was disappointingly vapid.5) Pla Ga Pong Daeng Thod Gra Tiem ($22) - deep-fried red snapper fillets blanketed in an gooey garlic sauce: let down by the less than sparkling fresh fish. The muddy taste of the fish overwhelmed the lovely sauce

Valentine's Day lunch. The ambience was very nice, so was service. But I must say the food was pretty average. It's a personal value proposition whether $80 per person all-in for buffet lunch is fair. I don't thin so...

I will admit I went in with very low expectations as I had just come back from a week in Thailand and was used to very spicy authentic Thai food. I thought this would be bland and expat-oriented. Let me tell you that I was actually quite pleasantly surprised. I quite liked it! Lots of choice (oddly including some western fare) but for example the papaya salad had the proper level of heat. I enjoyed the chicken curry and various starters and the sides of vegetables and the coconut rice for dessert. Check out my blog post, I was there with friends for their birthdays. 88$++ for brunch for 3h on the weekend, including freeflow prosecco, I think it was 58$ for the food with soft drinksmylifeinsin.com/2013/10/…

If you ever need a place to take a client or a business partner to a beautiful looking restaurant that won't break the bank, Jim Thompson is your place! Nestled in the jungle of Dempsey Hill, this restaurant almost seems like an an oasis among the scores of beautiful trees that line the restaurant. I went for dinner with my wife and my aunt visiting from Hong Kong. We were greeted by thai dancers strutting their stuff to traditional thai music, not to mention, the all too familiar words of "Sawadee ka." The decor within the restaurant is sublime. It's probably best to see the pictures to see what I mean. This restaurant oozes with "expat" appeal and is evident by the restaurant's patrons.  I, for one, like to go to Thai restaurants where there are a lot of Thais in order to personally certify the restaurant food's authenticity. Although Thai patrons were few and far between, the food, nonetheless, was very good and authentic.   Our order included Pad Thai, Beef Mussaman Curry and a veggie Thai Dish. The Pad Thai was the best I've had in Singapore. It's probably because Pad Thai is the THE expat dish of Thailand and this dish has to be a hit in order for this restaurant to bring its target demographic. As for the Mussaman Curry, I second my wife when she says it wasn't too spicy. My only compliant about the restaurant, believe it or not, is the ridiculously small portion white rice they give. :D Overall, the restaurant is just beautiful and the food is a sure fire winner. Personally, I would not pay these lofty prices for Thai Food, as there are so many great Thai options in Singapore and with Thailand a short place ride away, but the ambiance, experience and the backdrop of Dempsey Hill is all built into the price!

This is a beautiful restaurant, and the food is equally match the decor. The service is also top notch, including the price. This restaurant experience is worth the splurge now and then.Overall most of the dishes that I had eaten are deliciously cooked, beautifully presente, and authentically Thai.

When I was young, my Father used to take me here to enjoy succulent Chicken Rice which I would ask for more bowls for rice. My record so far is 4 bowls of rice and 2 plates of steamed chicken at one shot, that was how hungry I was at that time. Fast forward to recent times, the quality of Chicken rice has dropped to a standard that I can hardly believe. I find the quality these days is no better than some of the food stores at Hawker centres. Why should I pay more when I can get cheaper price from else where? I been to this branch a couple of times, and frankly I am also less than impressed with the service. Signs of impatience and mood swing (seems to me) when some of the stuff served my friends and I. One positive note about this place is that they sell other dishes as well, not bad but to be honest, I only come here for the chicken rice and sadly the standard has dropped. Overall, I am disappointed with the quality but I will still come back to try the other dishes. With the opening of the Beauty World MRT station, business should be better.

Busy restaurant with standard food . Not really a MUST HAVE. Nevertheless they are serving traditional Chinese food. Seen much better elsewhere. Below the line, it is too expensive for a good course. Sorry , but one  try and last try.

How much you like this Boon Tong Kee outlet depends very much on what type of diner you are- whether you're dining in, taking away, or doing a drive-thru (yes, they actually have that!).I especially like the drive-thru service. I live about 5 mins away, so I usually call in advance to place my order. It takes about 10 minutes for the food to get ready, and they will ask you for your car plate number. The welcome counter doubles up as the drive through counter- the food prepared for drive-thru takeaways are placed on chairs there with receipts indicating your car plate number. The only thing left for you to do is to drive through the lane (enter from Cheong Chin Nam side because its one-way), roll your windows down, pay, and go. I always try to give exact because the cashier counter is all the way inside the restaurant to prevent holding up traffic.Dining in is not too bad as well. Even though the place is pretty small, its quite ridiculously overstaffed- I don't know if I appreciate that many people looking at me when I eat. Having said that, service is especially efficient, and its always a plus to be able to have hot food before you. There also isn't usually a problem looking for a seat, even though their chairs are not very comfortable and they use a kind of leathery-plastic to cover their tables and that kind of freaks me out.What I dislike is the taking away service. Because of the popularity of the drive-thru, take aways (by yourself) can mean you have to wait for as long as half an hour- they cant afford to let the cars hold up, so they will almost always prepare the food first. Also, they are extremely short staffed for those who are actually to handle food, so while you have many people at your service as a sit-in diner, as a take-out customer you have very little choice but to wait for the orders before you to clear up before you can even place your order. Once they take your order though, they pod gets served pretty fast.The standard of the chicken here is pretty good- but a little known dish which happens to be my favorite is the deep fried tofu. Somehow they manage to fry it in a way that doesn't make it appear toooo sinful.. though I'm sure it is. The batter is crisp, thin, the tofu is silky smooth and the portion is just right.

I did not grow up in Singapore and therefore was not familiar with the name of the resto. But my cousin brought us to this place for dinner so I came without any expectation. Now, we're all Malaysians (well one is now a Singaporean), six of us, half all their lives, the other half very well travelled but our palate is still genuine Malaysian/Singaporean. The food here is definitely not average as the 3 stars overall suggest, neither is it a top restaurant for the Hainanese-chicken-rice-plus-zhichar category. Most of what we ordered were delish, especially the fried tofu. The rice was magnificent but feels a little too oily. The service was so-so, and the ambience was average. The price of six-dish dinner was acceptable but the drawback was "no American Express". Bah. I'd give you 3.5 stars if I could, but I couldn't.
