Four felt a little less unfair than 3 stars but BTK you really need to lift up your game man!

How did Boon Tong Kee get so famous? All their branches are the same: mediocre, overpriced, terrible chicken rice.It's not terrible, sorry -- it's still edible.But oh so mediocre.The only saving grace is most of their outlets are open really late, esp the river valley one. This one till 1 am, but still.. Even among the late night after-partying chicken rice places, BTK could not even hold a candle to.. say, Five Star. Not even close.

The only time I come to Boon Tong Kee is after a night of partying. There are always plenty of seats, and even if you have to wait, it won't take too long unless you're in a really big group.I have to say the chicken rice here is really fragrant and moist, but it is served in a strange little pyramid. I suspect the reason for that is to hide how little rice you're actually getting. The chicken itself is tender and tasty. They are famous for the white chicken, and even though I normally prefer roast chicken, I don't mind the chicken here. However, i do find the jelly bits quite gross and normally pick them out.The chilli here is nothing to shout about though. I think the chilli is what makes a chicken rice dish exceptional.I do like their other dishes, such as the fried tofu, and the fishballs with minced meat. The tofu has a nice silken texture and isn't too oily even though it's deep fried. I  especially love the fish-meat balls that explode in your mouth. Watch out for the hot soup that comes squirting out. i have burnt myself and squirted it at friends (by accident of course) several times already.I do think the food here is overpriced, but the food has always been consistent. The ambience here is nothing special, but the service is fast and efficient.

This restaurant is definitely famous for its chicken rice. Some may find it too premium for a plate of chicken rice where you can actually find any stalls to serve just as good. However, this stall does not only serve chicken rice and the other dishes should be given credits as well.Some of the dishes to recommend are the crab meat soup , which taste rich and great in texture, the fried tofu , one of the signature dish tastes awesome, the tofu is smooth and the crust is crispy. Wonderful combination.A point of worry as mentioned at the start is that the crowd at restaurant is unusually thin..I suppose the higher than expected pricing of the dishes has something to do with it.

A craving for Japanese food led my friends and I to Ginza Bairin one fine afternoon. As I felt like having something soup, I went for the spicy tonkotsu ramen. It was really rather spicy which was quite a good twist from usual non-spicy ramen, but the soup base was disappointingly bland. There was a lot of noodles, although there could probably be more ingredients. The service was extremely fast and there wasn't much to complain about. I would go back again probably to try their katsudon which they're more famous for, definitely not for the ramen.

Ginza Bairin is located at B4 basement at Ion Orchard. I love the Ginza Bairin in Tokyo. The one here is very different in terms of the decor and ambience. The Ginza Bairin is cozy and warmth. I know I know, I kept overusing the word "cozy", but I really really like cozy places. Perhaps the Ginza Bairin Singapore has a bit of a almost fast food feel, or maybe it was just the lightings. Not sure why there were so many white/bright lightings in many places in Singapore; my face looked sickly greenish once in a grocery store. It was hideous!!The staffs here were always nice but the staffs at Ginza Bairin in Tokyo were nice and warmth. Ginza Bairin is famous for tonkatsu which is fried Japanese pork cutlet. The tonkatsu here was always crispy, tender and juicy during my visits there. Ginza Bairin is definitely for people who love tonkatsu!!

Recently the causal Japanese restaurant has re-opened after been closed for upgrading. The restaurant is known for its deep fried pork cutlet. There is 50% off the items in the menu for the first 3 days. However the well-known sandwiches and side dishes are not available during the promotion period. Although there is a lot of people queuing up for the promotion, one can find a seat easily as food is served quite fast and the turnover is fast too.After making payment at the cashier, one would be given a number tag where food will be served to you at your table.Tonteki (pork steak) ($22)Served with Gonzalez bairin's special sauce, pickles and deep fried garlic slices. Plus a bowl of miso soup. The dish is one of the new dishes in the new menu. The meat is juicy and goes well with the wasabi like sauce. However the garlic slices are not crispy and texture too chewy.Ton Kara ($2.50)Available in 3 types : pork, chicken and chicken wing. Battered with Bairin's way of battering, then cooked with CONFIT cooking method which involves cooking the meat in its own fat.The pork version is too fatty with the thick layers of fat, while the chicken version is too salty. The chicken wing fares slightly better.Overall the food is average with improvements needed. Service is not bad with staffs clearing the tables swiftly.

Know I was supposed to eat their tonkatsu here but the karaage curry udon called out to me and got that instead. It was $16.00 inclusive of 7% GST, I didn't think it was worth that price for something I could get fast food version in Japan or event at a food court here in Singapore. The tonkatsu costs around $21-25; not worth the price either. The price probably is to cover up rent in ION orchard; but definitely not the quality of the food. Karaage usually comes in small pieces but ginza bairin chose to have them large - too big in my opinion. Had a hard time biting off the chicken to fit my mouth; even tore the roof of my mouth in the process...

A favorite place for curry rice and tonkatsu. The materials are mostly from Japan and price is reasonable compared to other Tonkatsu stores in Singapore. I always go with Tonkatsu or Curry rice there. Order Kurobuta (black pig) tonkatsu, the meat is more juicy.

Located in basement 4 food court of ION Mall. The set up does not offer the cozy feeling that you normally have in its home country.  Didn't realise I should order first before seating until got a polite (but nothing warm) reminder from the waiter.  The black pig pork curry was quite presentable, with well fried and juicy hamburger and thick and tasty curry.  The portion was just right.

This restaurant is nice when you want to have a quick Tonkatsu meal at a descent price.I ordered the Tonkatsu set (the 140g Kurobuta of course hehehe) that came with rice, cabbage and miso soup. The price of my meal with an iced green tea came up to SGD 22 (which is reasonable for a good Tonkatsu in Singapore). Plus don't forget that the set comes with unlimited rice, cabbage and soup. All you have to do is ask a waiter what you would like and he will bring it to your table. That's pretty awesome because I love eating lots of cabbage with sesame dressing together with the Tonkatsu!! :-)Restaurant: It's really just a place where you eat and leave. It's more a "canteen" style restaurant so don't expect a nice, quiet and cozy venue ;)Service: The service is just okay... It's really the minimum but it's fine for this kind of establishment. Basically, all the waiters do is serve your meal and clean your table when you leave. Don't forget that you must order before sitting!! I saw a few people waiting to order until they noticed people sat holding a number... The waiters don't bother telling you how it works unless you ask (which is what I did).Food: The Tonkatsu was nice with a crispy crust and cooked well keeping the juiciness of the pork. I will definitely go back for it.

Very well fried Iberian pork Tonkatsu with fresh and crisp cabbage and addictive dipping sauces for both. The Japanese rice was fluffy and provided the necessary carbs for the day. I enjoyed the meal very much!

Yay I'm a fan!I was so psyched when Ginza Bairin first opened (yeah how many of yooz have been coming here for this long huh?) as it was well marketed as one of the big brands for tonkatsu in Japan.I was here within 3 weeks of it opening (okay that's not that fast) and I've been a fan ever since. The pork is (usually) crispy, flavourful, and the portions are pretty decent. It's a wee bit pricy, but I'm usually quite full wen I'm done so I'm not really complaining.The curry's good, not amazing, but I particularly always like the tonkatsu-don with egg. It's a sloppy mess, but damn is it a delicious sloppy mess.It's not the fanciest of places, nor the cheapest of places, but it's a simple no-frills option that I often turn to when I'm stumped on where to eat. And thankfully, it hasn't let me down yet.

Considering that it's in prime area at ION Orchard, you would expect it to be pricey. Some tradeoffs have been done to keep a cap on price, which result in the place looking more like a canteen than a restaurant. Place was rather empty for a weekday night at 7pm. Slowly but surely the crowds turned up after 8pm.Knowing that pork cutlets were their speciality, I went for the Special Katsudon ($15 after 10% JPassport discount). It came with a runny egg that I gleefully burst and mixed into the rice. Verdict, it was as good and savory as the ones I had in Japan. Definitely worth an occasional visit when I miss authentic Japanese food.

Fried food. Frieeeeeed foooooood.Love that stuff--the pork is juicy, the breading crisp, the portions generous. They do have a black pig special that is on limited quantities every day, but I think the regular is good enough for you to save your money for dessert elsewhere!

This restaurant seemed to have the best queue to join if you're in ION on a weekend night looking for Japanese food. We asked the waitress if we had to find a seat before we joined the queue, she said, 'It's okay, we'll find the seats for you, just queue and order first'. So we did. Turns out after we ordered we were given a number tag and had to find our own seats. Not much of a problem though - there were visibly empty seats.The food took some time to come but it was impressive. The crispy batter that is. It was extravagantly crunchy and wrapped the meat well without being oily. The cheese croquette... Sigh, was a disappointment. The crisps was thick and the potato too, which left little room for the cheese inside. It was a sad patronising smear of cheese. For $3+ per croquette, I'd definitely not buy it again.

Tonkatsu that is perfectly crispy and succulent meat is not one thing you can find easily here in Singapore. Used to be being disappointed at the poor imitations that local stalls offer, I almost gave up hope of ever finding some decent here in Singapore.Luckily, there's Ginza Bairin. Introduced by my girlfriend, I have to say I was sold the first time I tried it. They have a choice of normal or Kurobuta (black pig) to choose from and I went with the normal option. A set meal costs about $18, pretty pricey for something relatively simple, but after my first encounter, I guess you could say the price is worth it. In addition to the tonkatsu, there is a variety of other dishes on offer as well, but if you ask me, I'd say go for the normal tonkatsu. They definitely won't disappoint.

Located at the basement of Ion Orchard beside the food kiosks, Ginza Bairin doesn't really scream out to you, and if you're not looking for it, its relatively easy to pass it as just another Mos Burger or Japanese fast food joint. While I'm not particularly a big fan of tonkatsu, I have to say that Ginza Bairin does satisfy my cravings with the more than decent offering. The tonkatsu is not too oily and deep fried while retaining the succulent and juicy meat and you always get a good crunch. The variety on offer is really comprehensive so it is always good to take a look at the menu before ordering or you'll definitely hold up the queue.

OK I confess, I've been here 4 times, and every time, I order the SAME thing. I'm not sure what it is about this place that keeps me coming back. Perhaps it's the fact that there never seems to be a queue, it's open quite late (I go at around 9pm on weekdays) and the food is quite delicious.  The only issue I have with it is that it's somewhat on the pricey side so I always have to debate if I want to spend close to $20 on a fast-food type meal. I spend around $17 per meal when I get the Croquette Curry Cheese set and an iced green tea. The Croquette Curry Cheese set... mmmm... yummy, though I suspect not very Japanese fare of fried potato / cheese and curry with rice and soup. Being the carb lover that I am, what's not to love??My friend is in love with their Ebi Fry set - she has also ordered this many, many times and it costs around $18. According to her, it's delicious, so that may be worth trying out also. I'll definitely head back here to sample their other dishes.

I had a discount voucher from Perx and decided to use it for my dinner. at 8:30pm the line at Ginza Bairin was long and even though the place was fully packed, people just kept coming. since it was crowded and i was on my own, i asked for take away. to my dismay, no ramen on the to go menu. sadness so i ordered the unagi don (i forgot the actual name of the dish) - eel and egg on rice. it didn't help when the lady got my order wrong. the kitchen staff came out to clarify and she still got it wrong. it took her about 2 customers later to clarify with me then she asked me to pay the difference in price for the wrong order she put in - by this time i had already waited 10 mins. thank goodness the rice was tasty even though it was like 45 mins later that i got to eat. next time i would choose a better time to eat there.

Was surprised to see this famous Japanese chain in orchard ion. I made it a point to try the Katsu which I had in Tokyo and the taste was really similar. No frills and tasty Katsu was what drew me to their chain in Tokyo and this new outlet in Singapore did not disappoint. Great place to have Fried breaded Japanese style pork

Ginza Barin was my frequent choice for dinner after work because the portions are big and the food is pretty decent. The tonkatsu has always been pretty much up to standard - the deep fried breaded pork fillets are not too oily and the meat is usually still tender enough. Recently, I took to the Ebi Fry set -3 huge battered (but succulent) prawns served up with steaming rice accompanied by delicious tartar sauce. But, I won't be going back anytime soon because I had a horrible experience  the last time around. Got berated by a service staff when I requested for a second serving of tartar sauce - apparently it is only ethical to put up this request after you have licked up every last bit of the sauce that is on your plate. Wow. I was flabbergasted considering I had about two dips worth of sauce left. Left a horrible aftertaste so don't patronise this place if you are one who enjoys your food and would like a little more sauce from time to time.
Very good!! Always crisp and tasty katsu. Their fried oyster and cheese stuffed pork katsu are both extras I must always order. Another big plus is they open pretty late.
I'm deducting a point for refusing to take my order at 9:50pm when their website says they close at 10:30, and for refusing to serve tap water.
Customer service non existant. The only response we got is, "order what you like as what I recommend does not matter."No pleasure in dining.
Their full American breakfast is nice and it's a great place to hang and yak!!!

3.5 starsA goal of mine is to start using the buses more often so I can get to know Singapore a little better. After hopping off the bus and walking allllll the way up Dempsey Hill, I decided to reward myself by indulging in lunch at Jones. (Okay, walking up Dempsey Hill wasn't that bad, but come on, I should get some recognition for not driving or taking a cab out here!) I ordered the leg ham and gruyere cheese sandwich, with zucchini, tomato chutney, and apples. Sounds different and amazing, right?! Well, I was slightly disappointed. I found the sandwich to be a bit small and overpriced. I felt the ham just tasted like ham, the gruyere just like regular cheese, the tomato chutney was sweet but that's it, and the zucchini and apple portion was lacking. Basically, nothing really stood out and the flavors didn't seem to combine well. It was served with a small salad on the side, but I wish it had dressing on it. I did like the bread, as it was toasted perfectly.After paying my check, I decided to look at some of their grocery items. I love how they had a lot of Italian goods like bottled tomato sauces and dried pastas - I've been striking out on finding good Italian restaurants here so I'm always looking for quality ingredients to make my own Italian meals. The cheese room looked amazing but I was a bit intimidated by it. I also loved all the exotic teas they offered.Overall, so-so experience at the cafe, but totally loving their merchandise. This seems like the place to be on the weekends, so I wouldn't be surprised if I ended up here again. Looking forward to my next visit!

Jones the Grocer is very comparable to any of the nicer specialty markets in the US, i.e. Whole Foods, Dean and DeLuca, Jimbo's Naturally.  I came across Jones after doing a search for smoked paprika in Singapore, it's been challenging finding the things we can so easily find back home in the States.  I had never heard of it before and discovered they are actually an Australian chain, which I found interesting and also really thought their website was nicely designed.  There are several locations in Singapore, I went to the one located in Dempsey Hill.    They have a good selection of spices and in addition to finding the smoked paprika I purchased some really nice artichoke hearts, pasta imported from Italy, bruchetta paste, and Estrella Damm beer.  I did not try their cafe, but all the pastries and baked goods looked delicious and I bet their espresso is wonderful.  They also had an extensive collection of books/cookbooks, a nice cheese selection, as well as quite a bit of tea.If you are looking for a store to stock up on pantry items Jones the Grocer is definitely a great place to start.
Good food, indifferent to borderline rude service, and free flies provided with indoor seating.

This was the original upmarket grocer before D&D came to town, and its chillax nature up on Dempsey Hill I think makes it that much more appealing. The FnB isn't the cheapest, but I love their choice of desserts, including the nougat and rocky road which for some reason is not available at the Mandarin Gallery outlet.There's an airconditioned cheese room and quite a good cheese platter available, plus lots of fancy pricey grocer food to gawk at while you're here. While evenings and brunch times find it quite packed, weekday afternoons are really not crowded at all and its nice to just take your things up here to have a cuppa and unwind.Also cool: FREE WIFI (which is what I'm using to write this review now) FTW.

Jones at Dempsey is a café and specialty food store from Australia. The food here is decent enough, not the most extensive menu though. Best to come here for brunch and breakfast. During lunch they have sandwhiches, salads and main courses. The sandwiches are alright, but honestly they are very stingy with their portions. Desserts here are nothing to write home about, they could definitely do much better. One plus is the free wifi, which makes it a nice place to chill in the Dempsey area.

Jones the Grocer is of course more than just a gourmet grocery store. They offer a unique mix of cafe and european fusion cuisine with everything from steak to cheese platters. The food tends to be a bit on the pricey side but nothing is too extravagant or over priced. The cold cuts and seafood are extremely fresh best eaten when paired with something from their extensive cheese cellar.Their range of products is extremely diverse & unique although sometimes a bit over priced. A good place to come in for a glass of wine and cheese or a cup of coffee over a nice novel on a quiet weekday afternoon.

Expensive expensive expensive is all I can say and this is said with relation to the tiny portions. A side order of sausages comes cut up in a bowl, not even the slightest effort to garnish, rather disappointing for an add-on that cost a bomb. Jones the Grocer was and still is to many a novelty. One drink to try though would be the citrus infused iced Earl Grey. Bergamot is relaxing and the citrus infusion pairs well and adds an extra kick to the refreshing cooler. If I do remember correctly, Jones also serves a good club or BLT sandwich. Not the best place for brunch but definitely a nice place to spend relaxing weekends!

Venue 5/5 great ambiance and atmosphere with clean and well-maintained venue, always appreciated. The place is spacious indoor as well as outdoor. Service 5/5 attentive and helpful service throughout. Food 4.5/5we ordered pork ribs that comes with grilled corn and mashed potato, and it is as good as it can get. You can slice through the meat with just the weight of the knife and it melts in the mouth. The mashed potato is very fresh and goes well with the meat, no additional sauce needed. Can't really comment about the corn aside it being fresh since I don't like corn. The next food is prawn risotto which is first class, although I am not a fan of el-dente rice, therefore it is not as enjoyable as it could, but I appreciate the food prep and quality itself. The sauce is perfect, flavorful but not too much, the prawns are fresh and prepped excellently. I give an overall score of 4.5/5 because I haven't tried other options that will make me a regular yet, but will try since it is a nice place to hang out and chill while enjoying a good food and wine. A bit pricey but reasonable with the food quality offered.

Perfect if you're into the uppity type of thing. The prices are parallel to pretentious brunch in the US in a NYC restaurant. While well lit with large windows and filled with imported foods, Jones lacks the flavor and excitement to me that the rest of Singapore does. Have your $9 SGD tea with your $22 SGD brunch with the ex-pats if you will, but if you are visiting Sing and not a local, you're not missing anything by passing on to the next food adventure.

jones the grocer is back in the game! They have streamlined and refined their concept to continue bringing us gourmet and quality food recognised, with a greater emphasis on promoting healthy eating and lifestyle. The airy Dempsey outlet is pretty much the same. Other than housing Singapore's first walk-in cheese room (with over 100 varieties), a large artisanal retail outfit, and bakery, jones has now added a brand new butcher's corner by Swiss Butchery as well. Have a meal here and then bring another meal (or 2) home!We started with the Cheese & Charcuterie board (3 items $35, 5 items $45, 7 items $55, additional items $8). This is served with truffle honey, jones olive oils, jones Egyptian dukkah and a selection of jones artisanal bread. I can't go on about how good the Stilton Blue was with the truffle honey. UMAMI. I would also add the smoked duck breast and some other cured meats to the mix.If you're not sure what to pair your cheeses with, don't fret. The on-site cheese experts would help you with that. There are also suggested accompaniments placed together with the different types of cheeses on the shelves so you can always pick them out yourself. A starter that is the equivalent of a main course is the Oriental Crispy Duck ($26) which is a pan fried duck confit served on a bed of mesclun salad tossed with shimeji mushroom, Russet potato, cherry tomatoes, and tossed in a plum dressing. Somehow the salad stole the thunder from the duck, which was simply a protein accompaniment that is rather characterless. jones Classic Wagyu Burger With Truffle Fries ($26) is the bomb. Resistance is futile. How can anyone say no to this juicy 120g 100% Australian wagyu beef patty with crispy bacon?! Of course, the various condiments layer on the flavors perfectly- melted gruyere cheese, truffle mayo, bois boudran sauce, pickles, hot English mustard, and caramelized onions. They even make their own fluffy brioche bun which held the stack perfectly. I also had to tell them to take away the fries, if not i would not be able to taste the rest of the food with my limited stomach space. The Asparagus Risotto ($24) was a creamy soft herb risotto with fresh asparagus, Taleggio and rana padano with black truffle oil. Expect this to be very very filling. I couldn't take more than 3 spoonfuls of this as it was rather cheesy, though bland. An enjoyable pasta was the Spicy Seafood Aglio Olio ($28), which was piquant and full of garlic. This dry pasta could do with a larger variety of seafood actually as it was mostly prawns (not that i mind but it did say that it's a seafood pasta). I wouldn't mind finishing a plate of this actually, but i thought the prawns were too powdery.Grilled BBQ Chicken ($26) was succulent and juicy, though pretty standard. The BBQ sauce had a nice hint of apple, which i thought was rather refreshing. That creamy and buttery garlic mash and minty coleslaw were kinda heavy for the dish. So i have found the best Warm Sticky Date Pudding ($15) in Singapore. Seriously this cake was buttery and moist and that salted caramel sauce was the bomb, especially with that rich vanilla bean ice cream. Any dessert after this just couldn't compare. Of course, if you're looking for something small, the freshly baked breads, pastries, and cakes would satisfy your tastebuds. All jones breads are organic and they only use premium ingredients here. So yes, welcome back, jones the grocer now!

Another one of my favourite breakfast/brunch go-to's. Friendly staff and a cute atmosphere. Food will come out so fast! They have interesting drinks on their menus such as a charcoal latte. Their English breakfast is probably one of the best attempts in Singapore. It is a nice place to go for a quiet morning breakfast. Never too busy
Decaf soy latte ($6.50) - 3.5 starsDecent! Pricy but I hardly see decaf soy lattes.Multi grain bread ($7) - 4.5 stars
Great service and delicious food. The outdoor seats are pretty chill, great for those who would like to dine outside. Service is attentive and friendly. Enjoyed having brunch there.

I'm ok with this place.First time was 5 years ago. It was much more packed. Ok coffee. And had a sandwich or something but they must have changed the menu since. Nice place to chill at the time. More people around, it was busy but staff was attentive.Second time. We went on a lazy Saturday, wanted a place to drink tea. Ordered some cheese and went to the deli to buy ham because the waiter said it's cheaper to do that so we did. Food is good, but service is a little off. I had to get the menus myself. Kept having to ask the waiters to get our orders or get water, etc. I don't like flies/insects in general and there were a lot hovering by the bread maybe because of the cheese smell also. But anyway I would go just to buy some meets and cheese to take away. Won't go back to stay and eat.

Being totally honest here, I'm not the biggest fan of the food. It's ok. But the main reason to come here would be the ambience.This is a dream brunch place to take the family to just because its so pretty! The lighting, sun shine streaming in and the white making it really so wonderful. Running around here looking at the beautiful products while waiting for the food to arrive is a must. I literally love looking at packing and unique brands and thats what this place is all about.My mum and I couldn't find anything we wanted to eat for lunch here but we would definitely recommend it for a breakfast/brunch place with the family or friends!

Coffee & cake time after lunch. Food knick knacks and sweet things abound. The coffees and hot chocolates came by. Good for us. chocolate was not too hot & not too sweet. Price was ok. We liked the ambience of a larder, kitchen counter and bakery all in one. With the slight air or organised grocery shop chaos. Some how works for tropical Singapore. Neat, tidy, works but cluttered in an ordered sort of a way. Wah! can do lah!

A refreshing place to peruse and explore.The pumpkin, feta, and arugula salad was super simple and fresh. I'd order it again in a heartbeat. Will probably be back when I'm in a more cheese-inquiring mood. (If you're a cheese person, just stepping in that cheese room is like instant therapy for the soul) ;)

Came here for afternoon tea with a friend, but mainly because we were both trying to work.Loved the fact that there was free (and decently fast) wifi, as well as power supply (though not at every table). Makes working out of a cafe so much more convenient :)My friend really loves the ginger ale, but I didn't enjoy it as much since I'm not a fan of ginger. I wanted ice tea, which they dont serve - only ice lemon tea (sweetened) :/ Went with Earl Grey Tea, cant go wrong with that!Had a good time working there. Will be back again to work!

I like the grocery more than the food served. The yummy real ginger ale, the different salts and oils, the wafer-thin crackers.And did I mention the totally awesome cheese room? Get in, freeze yourself, taste some cheese, buy some home, get fat, die happy.

free parking.free wifi.a good start.can be real crowded on weekends.ended up seated at the bar counter.the bar stools look like they have seen better days!we ordered an earl grey tea and a mixed carrot and orange juice.the juice came sans ice which i guess means you get more juice for your $6.50.but the ratio of carrot to orange was on the high side.we tried a plate of duck rillette with sliced baguette, pickled onions and gherkin.the baguette came cold and chewy.the duck rillette was tasty and with a good dollop of duck fat attached.the mini gherkins was sharp and tart to cut through the fattiness.the onions were really nice and sweet.their brunch menu is available till 5pm just for the late risers.service can be spotty.

I love coming to the Dempsey outlet of Jones the Grocer on weekdays when I'm around town and have a couple of hours to spare. It's not very crowded in the afternoons so its the perfect place to do some reading, or have a good catch up with a girlfriend. The staff are very chilled, attentive and ready to take your order when you're ready, but know how to give you your space to just relax. Really one of those rare places with a great atmosphere where you can escape from the bustling city.The food is good, they have a big range of cakes, slices, cheeses, breads and desserts to choose from - so you'll really be spoilt for choice. Coffee is excellent too - and very consistent, I've never been disappointed here.  And to top it off, I really like how they include the gst and service tax into their menus - I think everywhere in Singapore should do that! It makes our lives a lot easier when you need to split the bill.

Keng Eng Kee Seafood was recommended by a local.  We were fortunate to have gotten a table at the air conditioned section.Food was great including The black Pepper Crab and the Egg Yolk flavored Crab.A Spinach dish with Duck Egg Yolk was delicious.My eye opener for this meal is the Cereal Shrimp.  Crunchy, Toasty, Umami cereal covering a generous sized Shrimp.  After all the Shrimp was eaten, the Cereal was delicious eaten by itself.  At the suggestion of my friend, I ate some more of the Cereal with the sauce that was used to flavor the Egg Yolk flavored Crab.  A singular great taste treat.Great local place with fair prices.

This is where the locals go and it is amazing! There are long lines especially on weekends but it's worth it. I tried their chili crab, a few vegetable dishes, butter cereal prawn, fried rice, and noodles.everything was very good but BUTTER CEREAL PRAWN. TO DIE FOR.Please get it if you are going to keng eng kee.  YOU WILL NOT REGRET :p

This was definitely one of the highlight of recent trip - everything was good. Chili crab, blacked pepper crab, noodle, beef...list goes on. It's outdoor table type place more of hawker and doesn't break your bank. Waiter was very friendly and took great care of us. There's also a taxi stand and parking lot, very convenient to get around.

Dude! First off we went here for the famous Singapore Chili Crab but the Black Pepper Crab stole the show! It was fantastic! First off, It was HUGE and the flavor was amazing. We had some other dishes as well but I can't remember what they were because of how good the crab was. A friend of mine who is a chef working in Singapore took us around to the places he thought were the best and this place did not disappoint. The owner and his son even came out with a bottle of Remy (not on the menu) and took a couple of shots with us. After the shots they left the bottle for us to enjoy at our leisure. Talk about excellent customer service! I was a little under the weather but still enjoyed myself. I' love to go back healthy with an empty stomach!Not so humbly submitted,Michael C.

I've heard lots of good things about Keng Eng Kee (KEK) Seafood in Bukit Merah and decided to give it a try along with a family birthday celebration. It was easy to make a phone reservation just a day before, but do call earlier if you have firmed up plans, to ensure air-con availability.  1.  Salted Egg Crab $70/kg *highly recommended*Crabs seem to command better prices that rare minerals like gold or diamonds! It was just 2 years ago when 1kg of crabs cost $50, but nevertheless, these Indian crabs are fleshy. The salted egg sauce was so good, you know it's real salted egg and not the powered artificial salted egg, due to the graininess of the sauce. Not to mention, the taste. Sadly, KEK does no serve fried mantous, only the steamed mantous at $1 per piece. In the background of this photo, you can see 2 mantous, they're pretty big but I would still prefer to dip fried mantous into the sauce. The crab tasted reasonably fresh, but I felt that the chef had fried the crab for too long, resulting in the meat being stuck to parts of the shell.2. Ming Zhu Roll *highly recommended*This mingzhu roll is definitely a worthy cause to visit KEK. With salted egg right in the middle, this is so pretty and yet delicious. This dish came straight to our table within 2 minutes of ordering. I was confused if this order belonged to another table, but the staff insisted it was for us. The batter is light and crispy. The mushrooms were juicy and added alot of flavour.3. Fried Hor Fun $5/$8 *highly recommended*Probably their number 1 seller is their fried hor fun. Served with a raw egg. This dish is one of a kind, the wok hei can be subtly picked up by you sense of smell, but the taste of the wok hei is so vivid to your tastebud! The egg helps to make the hor fun wet, and when we ordered both a $5 and a $8 portion, we felt that they gave the same amount of ingredients, with 1 egg in each dish. Maybe they gave us more noodles, but we couldn't see the difference.There's prawns, lup cheong (chinese sausage), squids and some slices of fish mixed into the delicious and fragrant fried hor fun. I definitely want to come back to KEK seafood for this!4. Fried Prawn Paste ChickenA family favourite that we usually order at every zi char, tasted rather ordinary here at KEK. The pieces were quite small and wasn't quite what we expected since the other dishes had set our expectations much higher. Skip this and also skip the hot plate tofu, it was bland and a waste of $10.5. Coffee Pork Ribs *highly recommended*The coffee pork ribs were so addictive. The meat was boneless and tender. The coffee sauce wasn't too sweet or over powering. The meat had a tad sweetness and chewiness in every bite. The coffee sauce was the bomb!Overall : A great place for a family meal. It cost us $180 including drinks for 7 adults.

The only dish that really was a hit for us was their signature noodles.  The fried eggyolk fish skin was good too.  But the real reason for us be here was the eggyolk crabs.  Unfortunately they were way to eggy and by the 2nd shot at eating you already feel overwhelmed and choked up.  Also their signature fried tofu we just simply did not get what the fuss is about and did not even finish it.  All in all ok but i would not drive 28km RT for it.

We went on a night before CNY and the Coffeeshop was jammed packed with tables all within and all around the Coffeeshop. Lucky I called to reserve 2 tables for my family, else I don't think you can walk in with seats for us 17 pax. We ordered many dishes and mostly, they were good! All flavours were a little on the salty side but all enjoyable!Dishes that are great: Moonlight Horfun -

I came to KEK once several years ago without realizing how big of a following this restaurant has. In a typical coffeeshop setting, it didn't look anymore impressive than any other tze char stall. However, one of my friends had told me KEK was one of his favourite "go to" tze char so I made a point to revisit. This time around, with my family to celebrate a birthday.  Alas, 3 days before the actual event, we couldn't book the aircon rooms. But luckily for us, it was a cool night and it was fine sitting outdoors.We ordered  quite a bit of their popular dishes - chili crab with mantou, salted egg yolk crab, 3-egg spinach, prawn paste chicken, mixed platter of fried appetizers, coffee ribs, moonlight horfun.  Most impressive was the moon light hor fun HANDS DOWN.  $8 for a medium portion gave us a large plate enough for 6 full bowls or 7 slightly less-full bowls.  The horfun was full of wok hei, full of lardy flavouring agents like lard cubes, lap cheong and seafood (fish slices, prawns and squid rings).  Was very very satisfying and luckily we didn't have extras for I would have walloped them all (bad for waistline!).The rest of the food was good but nothing extraordinary.  The biggest let down was the famed salted egg yolk crab. The sauce was paltry, but most importantly, the crab was overcooked and the meat stuck onto the crab :(  The chili crab fared better. While not particularly impressive, the sauce was eggy and morish enough to down a couple of pillow soft flower twist mantou  (these deserves a highlight - they were so soft!). Note there is no fried mantous here.  All these dishes for merely $207 with change!  We even had leftovers to pack up.

affectionately known as KEK.the parking can be a nightmare but with the improved ERP parking system, it seems easier to get a lot.be careful not to park in the red lots though, they look tempting but are only reserved for season parking.reservations these days is essential especially on weekends.else be prepared to eat closer to 9pm where the crowd tide ebbs.of course i will always prefer the air con comfort of their shop house unit. the toilets in there are also way cleaner.alternatively, their outdoor seating is very spacious, as they take up the entire coffee shop at night and is cooling enough with awning and fans strategically located.the ambiance is that of a zi char place and service was fast in general.especially in relation to the number of people waiting to be fed.i was a guest, so left all the ordering to the in-the-know regulars here.first up was the yuen choy(spinach like) in superior broth and the winner was the generous amounts of crispy tasty ikan bilis embellished on it.next was the deep fried tofu topped with a minced pork saucy mixture with chye po(preserved veg) and chilli.the entire slab of of tofu has a nice golden brown hue, a smooth silky white finish together with a complexity in taste from the minced mixture.another winner.their signature ming zhu rolls was next.crispy bean curd skin stuffed with salted egg, ham, prawns and lots of mushrooms served with a sweet mayo dip.the ratio of mushrooms needs to be toned down in order not to drown out the rest of the ingredients.simple quick fried nai bai in garlic is always a hit with me.the white rice they served was sadly, overly wet and mushy.good thing i'm not a fan of this carbo evil.the seafood fried rice however was much better.i guess they used the drier overnight rice for this.individual tasty morsels of wok hei coated goodness.the marmite pork was ok but i prefer marmite chicken better.then suddenly it was as if our meal ended.all the dishes headed our way, always landed on the tables to the left and right of us.it was like an intermission at an exciting play, unwelcomed and ill timed.a regular was eventually send to check and magically regular service was back.the clay pot liver was a hit with me.not too many do it well.i hate them overcooked but they taste evil if uncooked.shallots, spring onions, thinly sliced ginger and black sauce complimented the liver slivers.lastly, two types of crabs completed our feast.both crabs were very well cooked.the flesh firm and sweet.the temperature control of the wok heat was perfect.both the black pepper and the salted egg yolk sauces were just the right consistency.neither too dry nor too wet.and evenly coated through and through.there's no other way to eat crabs except getting your hands dirty and the crabs here are definitely worth your effort.additionally, the claws were nicely cracked giving you quicker access to it's plump flesh.no finger bowls but the tap and soap method is available.

Keng Eng Kee (Kek) is a tze char store tucked in the Alexandra Village which have both aircon and non aircon dining area.  The aircon dining gets snaps up first so be sure to make reservation. The food is reasonably priced and the dishes are above average. There are some hit and miss on the dishes here but one of the must try would be the chef special "Mingzhu Roll". It is deep-fried bean curd bag stuffed with a rich assortment of ingredients like prawns, salted egg york, ham and parsley. This dish is the store speciality and you can't find it elsewhere.
..OMG I thot all salted egg crab taste like salted egg crab, but this one is amazing . Den ofcos you have to try t HorFun, believe me it's unbelievable..Service is wonderful too They speak English
Remember to make reservations a few days in advance! If you like pork liver, be sure to order the claypot spring onion liver... I think it's the single best dish on offer.

Ming Zhu juan/roll. Try it once, so you can say you've had it. It's got Chinese ham. How's it different? I can't say...but it's certainly an experience trying to cram ham, salted egg, mushroom, and that special Chinese ham.Other than that, it does the classic things well, I suppose. A tasty Jiu Gao soup, spinach with very generous amount of crispy ikan bilis, and hae chor and har cheong gai were all well received, and disappeared into our bellies without much comment.Interestingly, our party of 6 also had something called Yue Liang He Fen, which translates moonlight hor fun? I hear it's called that because the raw eggs they crack over the hor fun give the noodles a delightfully smooth texture and glossy sheen... but that's what I hear.Its good food, and was relatively affordable, but I'm not sure why they are SO crowded! Maybe I need to go with a veteran to see what the famous dishes are.

I went here with my Singaporean friends and they did all the ordering.  And I think all were flavorful and cooked well.The Ming Zou rolls I think is their best seller, quite delicious.  We had the chili crabs, pepper crabs and salted egg crabs and the best one was the salted egg crabs.  I also recommend the fried battered squid, the roast chicken and the leafy vegetables with eggs.  Both the marmite pork and chicken were good -- don't worry, if you are not a marmite fan, the marmite flavor was not very strong.  Everyone raved about the liver dish but I am not a liver fan so I cannot comment myself.The service was good and quick.  Am just not sure if the ordering will be easy if I was not with chinese speaking folks.  I hope their menus have photos!I have been here twice for dinner but both at very odd times -- at 5pm and another at 930pm -- so the parking was quite easy.  If you come early, I suggest booking a table inside the air conditioned room so its not too hot.  If you are doing a late dinner, then its ok to sit outside.

Buckwheat ale was the highlight for me. The food wasn't bad - it was served with honesty and generosity but with a little less finesse than one would have hoped. The caramelised onion quiche was well made and the greek salad fresh. The ploughman's sandwich was a real tummy filler, just like one would expect back in the UK!I would like to see this place stay as its a rather unusual location and relatively off the beaten track unless of course one lives nearby. I am only giving it 3 stars as it feels somewhat overpriced... clearly targetting the expat market.
Service is really very slow, waited 40mins for a simple branch meal. Flood is so not satisfying, total regret for wasting time and calories in this restaurant.

Excellent British Pub Food - we had roast pork belly (crispy skin!) and beef cheeks (tender as it melts in your mouth).  A little pricy for the east coast location - but really a treat if you live close by and want something british and nostalgic.  They even have rabbit pie!!!

This review is based off of their breakfast as I have not had a chance to try their dinner menu yet.  We have been here several times now and each time not just the food but also quality have been top notch. The lady who makes the lattes has some kind of magic touch. They are creamy, frothy and make us feel like we are somewhere in Europe.  We come with our one year old who can be a little rambunctious at times and everyone has a lot of patience, it's great. I usually opt for some kind of scrambled eggs while hubs gets the avocado toast. Eggs are softly cooked each time and the avocado is super fresh and exactly ripe. They also have a guest chef who prepares special items for brunch and dinner but we are always too early to try. I think one dish is huevos rancheros and it looked awesome. Oh and they also have the best music playing in the morning a little bit of new wave, disco and some funk. Definitely recommend it if you're in the area.Update:The last few visits have been off due to the service. There are some excellent people here but you're only as strong as your weakest link... Even my order for food was lackluster and I was really bummed that this is where we chose to have Mother's Day brunch. Unfortunately this place is just inconsistent. You're taking a risk if you dine here. Hopefully you'll go on a good day but I wouldn't choose this place if you're expecting anything special.
Week days. Wait staff could use some training the juniors.  I'm gonna stick to Sunday roast. It's dam good.

This is one of those rare situations where I disagree with the current Yelp rating.I'm new to the 'hood, and I decided to give Rabbit Carrot Gun a try as Miguel was raving about their breakfast. When we arrived, we were greeted by Richard, the lovely owner. He was very chatty and made us laugh quite easily, so I had this feeling that a good experience was coming up.After perusing the menu, we called Richard over. I had questions about the juices, and he was very honest ("Oh, the second one? That's just a fancy name for apple juice!") I ended up choosing the Ruddy and Ready, which is their take on the classic ABC juice.I ordered the French toast upon the recommendation of Miguel, while he tried the special, which was an omelet with a local twist. I loved my French toast, as it was light, there was a generous side of maple syrup, and the portion was perfect for me. The berry compote really made the dish! Miguel's special was a well-executed savoury dish; good to know they can add in local flavours competently.As it's now 2015, I encourage everyone to stop by and check out what they're doing here. With Richard now managing the restaurant most of the time, the staff here is well trained and his presence just makes the place feel very neighbourhood-y and lovely. If you have the pleasure of meeting Richard when you visit, you'll know what I mean.

Wanted to feed some of my Brit pals some grub from their home and this place came up in the trawling the internet.Many of us had the Sunday Roast (or at least the meal that came closest to that) and it was at best so so only. The meat cut was slightly dry and not very flavourful if not for the sauce. The sides were also ok only. The meal was not cheap thus I thought it was not really value for money. Not likely to return though...

I'm seriously calling out all the Yelpers for their reviews of this restaurant. This brunch spot is downright AMAZING! From the food to the ambience to service. All great. The Breakfast menu is top-notch. The French Toast served with maple syrup & berry compote was Wow! I like my French Toast a little soft, likely due to slow cooking. However, this French toast was doused with egg cinnamon and dark sugar mix. Who knew French toast could be mixed with anything other than butter. The berry compote is a nice touch, adding that sweetness that so many of us crave in the morning. I know I mentioned that Suprette had an amazing French toast, Rabbit Carrot Gun just may be a little better! The other dish worth a try is the omelette with sugar cured prawns and topped with sweet Malaysian Sambal. The owner, Richard, dared me to try this dish and said to me that if I didn't like it, it would be on the house. Let's just say, I didn't get my money back. :D Kudos to Rabbit Carrot Gun for delivering a traditional western meal with an South East Asian twist! I'm dreaming of it already, as I write this review.My only knock on this restaurant was the flat white. It was just that, flat... There is some seriously some good competition nearby, ie Group Therapy Cafe etc, so I can't blame them. In terms of ambience, who can beat an open space on the corner of the bustling street of East Coast Road. Best of all, this spot has a neighborhood feel to it, which brings me back to my days of living in Brooklyn, NY. I would argue that this one shop turned the fortunes of Joo Chiat / Katong into the next new hip neighborhood. This resto oozes what this neighborhood can become.In terms of service, maybe I was a little spoiled since we were served by the gregarious and welcoming owner, Richard. However, I've been here once before on a weekday morning and thought the staff was courteous and prompt.Overall, one of my favorite brunch places on the Red Dot, if not my favorite. I can't speak on behalf of the other reviews, which were written eons ago, but this place has surely improved since those were written. Keep it up guys!

Had dinner last night here, after stumbling around the block while waiting for our movie. Finally we decided to dine here, coz ( i think is the owner, a big western guy) come approach to greet us. I had rib eye steak; it was bit too thin and meat bit hard for my taste, the potato gratin also bit dry. Hubby had saussage, it was ok. We had choco lava with ice cream as a dessert, was ok too.Ambience was nice and warm, service good and fast. But i wont come back for their rib eye.

A quaint place in the middle of Katong, its quirky name was the first thing that inspired my friend and I to give it a try. The food was slightly underwhelming, with the exception of its crisp fries. The fries were definitely a huge plus. We tried the Eggs Benedict and the Gourmet Beef Burger. For lack of a better description, both were distinctly average. The eggs were done alright but could have been fluffier. The beef was not really juicy as well.Coffee was not too bad though and you could drop by here just for a cuppa if you feel like it. Skipping the breakfast will not be a loss though.

Had the Beef Wellington which was rather underwhelming, the beef was kind of bland and the puff pastry was raw. However, the staff was kind enough to re-bake it for me, but the beef became over done and the pastry was still kind of raw. The staff are attentive and nice, but the food is quite bad.My friend had the Beetroot salad and it was extremely blend as well. Wouldn't suggest it, but the drink menu is comprehensive.
One of the best places to have good food. It was fresh, friendly and most important, tasty. Would certainly recommend for a relaxed and appetising food.

This used to be my Famous 49 Laksa shop, and still retains the retro blue mosiac tiles so don't begrudge me for being a little angsty upon my visit. No more lemak goodness *wipes tear*Anyhow. You know how when you hit up Boat Quay at night and will be left wondering if you've fallen into a rabbit hole and ended up down under? Or visit a hot pot restaurant and ended up at the birthplace of your forefathers? Similar experience here; only two tables of us natives and the rest a hodge podge of globalisation. We ordered up the lamb shank, sausages and a bottle of Odd Socks Shiraz-Cab-Merlot to share. Food was one dimensional and bland overall, and the lamb while tender, had barely any flavour to it. The sausage had tiny bits of apple, and the bubble and squeak that came with it had an interesting textureIf you're sitting inside, seating leaves much to be desired as tables are situated uncomfortably close to each other. It's a challenge to inhale deeply before squeezing past the neighbouring table, and you're always faced with the dilemma of whether to have your ass or crotch possibly brush against your neighbour's arm. Decisions, decisions. Product knowledge seems a little off. The lady on my left ordered a glass of red, the exact same blend as us. However, the waitstaff referred to it as Old Socks rather than Odd Socks, in that "Ma'am did you order a glass of Old Socks?" and "Excuse me, here's your Old Socks." How do I know this? Blame it on the close proximity of the tables. The table on my right had a bit of a sticky situation when the couple's mains arrived before their side of wedges. The guy went ahead to devour his steak, which looked more like a skinny sirloin than 120 day grain fed rib eye, and the lady just didn't want to touch her chow till the spuds arrived. They arrived after having had to check with the waitstaff twice, by which time the dude was more than half done with his steak. How do I know this? Again, blame it on the close proximity of the tables. More of a miss than hit here, sorry.

This café is nestled under a beautifully restored shop house, at the corner of East Coast Road, where the famous 49 Tanjong Katong Laksa used to be. Rabbit's unique name is actually inspired by our popular childhood game 'Rock, Paper, Scissors'!This café is set up by Richard Huggins, former regional sales director of Microsoft Advertising and English chef Jane Glascow of The Pantry at Loewen Gardens. I highly recommend you to drive here as this place is quite inaccessible. Parking lots are available along Ceylon Road or Marshall Road. Forget about taking the MRT! The 'nearest' MRT Station (Dakota or Paya Lebar) would take you 25 minutes to walk!The entire place is very hip and informal. The interior is filled with black and white photographs and retro-looking artworks. Coupled by the antique furniture collection and 'traditional' floor tiles, it certainly felt quite homely.I visited this café on a weekday afternoon and the place was very quiet and empty. What I disliked the most was the lack of air-conditioning. Since the café is open to the street, it's quite hot and humid, especially in the afternoon. I felt that the seats were arranged too closely to each other, which made me feel uncomfortable.I later found out that their only business isn't just a café - they also have beautifully re-furbished suites for travellers to stay in. Directly above the cafe lies the Rabbit Retreat - three luxuriously furnished rooms for travellers to explore a different side of Singapore.I find the food here very expensive. Appetizers can go up to $16.50! Besides, food takes forever to come. There were a total of 4 customers (including us) but it took almost 20 minutes for our pastas to arrive.My friend had their Prawn Aglio Olio ($16.90). Pasta and spinach tasted pretty good - it's chewy and not too salty. Also, prawns tasted very fresh.I went for the Beetroot Pasta ($16.90). It tasted sweet and goes really well with the lump of yogurt! The only drawback is that the portion is slightly small and to pay such a high price for it, not value for money!I would say Rabbit Carrot Gun is a decent place for catching up with friends over a good meal and for people watching. Service was pretty good. All of them were quite friendly and helpful. However, the high prices will surely deter me from coming back anytime soon!

Pretty quiet for a Sunday evening dinner much different from a Saturday lunch crowd that we saw.  By quiet I mean really quiet like 20 percent capacity.  Certainly no need for a reservation and I wonder why.  We sort of had cold feet on whether we should even bother going in and tempted do a burger two doors down but braved it anyway.  The food finally came...ordered the salmon, steak and the sausages.  Food was pretty good actually.  For starters they did not over cook the salmon.  The apple sausages were nice with just enough fat and pork.  The mash that came with the salmon and sausage was light and smooth.  They got a medium rare steak right too.  Only issue is on a value for money they get a 2 out of 5.  Certainly a salmon with mash and local naibi will not cost you $28 and another 10 bucks that be at fine dinning level main course.  That is a high profit margin there.  Ambience wise it was a little dimly lit and the Airconditioning has no effect.  I suppose if you want more customers they should brighten the place up perhaps able to attract more customers.  Overall service was not too bad just perhaps things are a little slower so they tend to be slower?  Has the apple crumple and toffe pudding.  Not bad but wish they got more ice cream.  Unfortunately the toffee pudding could not beat the one at pinique at taka.

Great looking place to hang out and people watch.  The food was indifferent.  I was indignant because I ordered the 40 dollar steak and got a lump of gristle.  Drinks were ok.  Coffee of decent quality.

Very noisy place, as it is open to the street. Somehow the ambience and the prices don't match. Attentive service. Food OK, but nothing exciting. Pricey.Good attempt to extract money from the growing expat community in Katong/Joo Chiat in the former location of Famous 49 Katong Laksa.

Tapas were about 20 a plate, we had fried squid (can't go wrong with that), bacon and asparagus (can't go wrong too), and ham (can't go wrong too). We had the seafood paella, which was decent, only real grouse I have is that the prawns were mushy (not fresh), and then churros for dessert.I really to want to complain about my strawberry sangria - I have not had a more stupid drink. There was strawberry pulp in the drink - yum, and then there were tiny pieces of citrus with the peel floating in my drink. I had to fish out the citrus pieces with a spoon, then drink my drink so I could enjoy my drink. Not a very smart bartender.Service was okay, but my companion was asked if he'd like a refill of his beer, and the refill never came.

I was in a bit of a dilemma reviewing this place because I went with 2 vegetarians and one person that didn't eat pork so I couldn't really try all the stuff I wanted. But the bottom line was I found it to be way over priced for what you get. I'll start with the atmosphere. It was nice, comfortable, cozy and sterile in a mall restaurant sort of way.  The service was ok. Not that friendly but they were attentive and did their job.  The food had some ok and some misses.  The hard part is there was a lot that looked good but I didnt try any of it.  The brussel spouts were ok and garlicky.  The best dish by far was the vegetarian paella which had nice flavor.  The worst was the pan con tomate the literally was just bread with crushed tomatoes spread on it. It really lacked flavor and wasnt what we were expecting at all.  The oxtail stew was tasty but way over priced considering it had 2 pieces of oxtail in it.  Another thing that annoyed me was that they charged everyone for tap water.  People were drinking and eating food but they were kind of snobby when people asked for tap water.  Given how expensive everything on the menu is you just get the feeling they are trying to scam you. It just didnt feel like a friendly place.  Maybe it was just a bad night. Maybe if I had gone with other carnivores it would have been better.  Really the menu looks great but in the end it felt flat. Meh.

I had the Cochinillo Asado (roasted suckling pig) that mummy booked ahead of time. The manager approaches the table with only a plate and proceeded to cut the whole pig with it - yes it's that's crispy, that's what he's trying to say.Not only was the skin ridiculously delicious and crispy ("su pok pok" as the lady serving my siew yok in a Chinese restaurant would say), the flesh was surprisingly tender, very different from Chinese suckling pigs. I was in awe.The grilled calamari is also true to the authentic Spanish of cooking very good seafood: as little seasoning as possible so you can taste the ocean. Paella was very good as well with great soccarat (the slightly burnt crust of rice), something that eludes most paellas I've had.I didn't foot the bill for this one and so didn't feel the pinch, if any. But the food is pretty good, if not one of the best, as far as the local Spanish scene goes, so I'd probably willingly shell out the money.

To my husband, he refers to this restaurant as KFP. Well, why so? He loves their crispy pork knuckle and feels that it has the taste similar to that of KFC Chicken. haha...By far, this place dishes out pretty decent spanish food.  They have quite an extensive drinks and food menu.  I love their tapas, paella and sangria selections. On the whole, the food is pretty good but comes with a rather hefty price tag too.

Went there for the nth time today and was very disappointed. Food was stale, service below par. Walked away feeling very disappointed and will surely not be going back here again anytime soon. To serve stale food is a crime in my view for any restaurant.. Anyway, done with this place for good now.
Poor effort to pass off as a Spanish restaurant - food was too inconsistent  ... The calamari was good but Avoid the whitebait and fried egg... Sangria was watered down...

Decent, semi-authentic and WAY too overpriced Spanish food. This place has bombarded us with email ads in the past weeks and we finally decided to try when we went to Vivo city. Their tapas are expensive (mostly around $20) and of tiny portions. We shared four between the 2 of us and went away hungry. As for the taste, it was alright but nothing to shout about. The "grilled Spanish squid" was the biggest disappointment--it tastes like greased rubber. The mushroom in olive oil & garlic and the roasted potatoes are good, but honestly, how could one go wrong on those? The roasted peper stuffed with minced beef was nice too, although I don't think it's particularly Spanish (nor are the rest). We were sitting at the patio, facing the bay & Sentosa. It was breezy and pleasant. Service was commendable as well. But the price is really ridiculously high given the quality & portion of its food.

Despite the anonymous setting that faces the south portion of VivoCity, there's no doubt of the quality and presentation of the food at this established with good service and serves of the best tapas and paellas in Singapore at a reasonable price. The menu has standard tapas fare, with most priced at ($12). Calamares a la plancha is a must try on the list with the tender pieces of grilled squid served in a rich balsamic sauce, sweetly tempered with cherry tomatoes and finely sliced asparagus. Something else to try on the list is albóndigas ($12) which features beef meatballs in a tangy tomato sauce. For mains, we got the paella valenciana ($40) which is no doubt one of the better Paellas i've had in Singapore. It comprises of saffron, chicken, Spanish chorizo, tiger prawns, squid, half shell mussels and is well mixed with rice. The generous portion is for 2 but 3 can share it too with other side dishes.

Serenity hardly sounds like the name of a Spanish restaurant so it didn't cross our minds to have Spanish food until we happened to be in the vicinity for a late dinner pre-midnight movie.The staff manning the reception looked friendly and welcoming so we decided to take a chance, and were pleasantly surprised when upon perusal of the menu, realised that several of the dishes including the recommended paella and salmon papillote were amongst those in the Singapore's Top 100 Signature Dish Awards.Food : We got the seafood soup which was pretty good, rather generously filled with fish, mussels and prawns. Instead of the signature chicken and chorizo paella, we went for the seafood paella instead, which was also one of chef's recommendations. Both were commendable. We also tried the iberico ham and the churros, both of which were fairly average.Service : The staff were fairly eager to please but being seemingly filled with inexperienced students, weren't very up to scratch. Pleasant enough though.Ambience : Not too bad, we sat inside but we could still hear the live band and singer quite well without it being noisy and intrusive to the point that we couldn't hold a conversation.Definitely will return if I have a craving for Spanish cuisine. We wanna try the sea bass baked in salt and many other dishes! :)

I was in vicinity and wanted to treat myself to some spanish tapas for lunch, then I found Serenity. The menu was really alluring, I might have gone abit overboard for a lunch for one.I had the gazpacho as a starter - gazpacho is a cold tomato soup, its a common spanish appetizer. It was refreshing but also surprisingly slightly filling after awhile, I could taste the fullness of the tomato and the freshness of the cucumbers. You won't like it if you don't like cold dishes coz it comes really cold.For my tapas spread I had the grilled squid drowned in olive oil and the fried cheese. The grilled squid was simple but lovely. The fried cheese was my favourite. So sinfully good - it was nicely crusted on the outside and once you put your knife or fork through it, you can immediately see the gooey cheese inside - heavenly!Final verdict: I had an enjoyable solo lunch here in serenity (in all sense of the word, coz I was there on a weekday afternoon, there was no crowd) but I also took quite a hit on the wallet, it was quite hefty for a meal for one! Might only come back if I'm coming with a group or someone else is treating!

I love the ambience that this place has created very nice to chill out and relax. The food though was not what i expected for the price i paid, quality was pretty normal. I went in a large group of 10 people and most of us ordered drinks, but they wanted to charge us for those who did not order drinks and wanted a glass of plain water instead which was ridiculous judging from the fact that we were paying more than $40 per head for our meal.Some of the food that were still edible were the ham and melon, paella, fideua (pasta that is cooked like paella), baked fish in salt and sangria. Definitely need to do your homework to research on the menu items before you decide on what to eat for your lunch or dinner.The service rendered there was really bad as well, we waited for about 5 minutes before we were served and it was not really crowded at that point of time. I did not like the layout of the stall as it made the place look cramped and messy, the walls and spaces were curvy but the tables used were of square shape totally did not match each other. Will not go back if i can help it, i think pastamania serves much better food with a cheaper price.

The wait to even get the servers attention was absolutely horrendous especially if you're seated alfresco. That itself was a major turn off for me and if you're looking for authentic Spanish fare, this is definitely not the place to be. One of the tapas includes bacon wrapped asparagus which is more like a Japanese Yakitori dish which you could easily get for $2 or less at Tori -Q.  The next big let down was the much hyped about Paella, it was so dry and flaky. I honestly don't know how a good paella should be but if that is it then I guess I am not a fan of paella in the first place. Really disappointing service and exuberant prices! Most of all, pretty far from authentic!

Love this place with the secretive entrance. It's one of those rare places on orchard road that's not too crowded. They have a selection of finger food and small portions of ramen and rice. I had the karaage rice and the uma uma ramen. Both were pretty good. The drinks are little pricey. I had the zombie cocktail and it was pretty good. The bartender is nice and if you could name a drink, he could make it for you.

The good:  Louis, Louis, Louis.  I didn't want to like you, especially after hearing so many glowing reviews about you and your drinks.  I told myself that your drinks couldn't be that good, that you can't be that nice, I dismissed it all for biased hype (which it usually is).  Several days later, I'm fantasizing about my next visit as if I just had a fling with Victoria Secret model.  I lost myself for a bit there...      The bad:  Based strictly on drinks, I have nothing bad to say.  Louis nailed it every time, introducing me to familiar libations with a twist.  Each cocktail came with a story about the spirits used and how he's looking to improve the drinks even further.  A true bartender, in every sense of the word (I think there are like  5 senses, or something like that).  Consistently accessible, never lurking, completely professional and welcoming.  I ordered off the menu, only hinting a preference here and there.  Dude read my mind...and my soul.  Ok, this review is getting to be a bit too much, let's just cut to the ugly.     The ugly:  This place is cool...for now.  Has a few hidden doors that make for a surprise entrance or ninja bomb exit.  Next door is a high end Japanese restaurant that brings all the yaya papaya Japanese clients to the yard.  Above is a ramen spot that will, without a doubt, satisfy a bits and nibbles appetite.  Music was loungy, like my grandfather would have said turn it up loungy (my friend made several comments about falling asleep because of it, although it could have been my stories).  Because of the close restaurant link, location and decor, I don't see it ever being a "hot" spot.  It would be pretty sub-par if you had to stand or wait to order, but should you go when there is space at the bar I think you'll enjoy your cocktail adventure as much as I did.  It's a scary thought though when 1 bartender makes up the majority of the experience, so lets just hope the Horse's Mouth can keep Louis around for awhile.  If not, I'll follow the pied bartender wherever he may go.
not so much for the food but the super good cocktails @ bar downstairs. love the concoctions

One of the better mixologist bars I've been to. I've been here twice, and it's been outstanding every time.I couldn't describe what I had, because every drink is slightly different, but the Sophie/Sophia is really amazing. Please order that, and make a booking if you come here on a Friday night.And don't get a shock when you get the bill. I think it's 25++ per drink. Worth every damned penny.

Nice hidden place, with really friendly and knowledgeable bartenders. Drinks are made with care - you can usually go bespoke and they'll make you whatever you like. Interior is a little dated though, and prices a little expensive for what you get. Quite a cool casual place, good space for a chill night of conversations.

You definitely pay for the ambiance here, but it's worth it once in a while. Secret entrance is a bonus. Cocktails have a Japanese twist, but will cost you 25++. The Sloe 'n Steady was my kind of drink, citrusy and refreshing without tasting too much of alcohol. Mockup on whiskey is about 2x, and there are only a few wines that are sold by the glass.

Purely rating based on Food.  I say this would be a good place for your snack.  But if you are looking to really fill up your belly with them snacks errrrr.....that would not be a good idea.  Ambience and service all good.  And yes indeed a little on the pricey side.  So really drinks and snacks don't do what we did trying to fullfill our dinner with snacks :).

The place is located in a hidden place where one can enter through Uma Uma Ramen which is located above it. The place is dimly lighted, so it is quite difficult to take a good picture here. Although there is not much customers, I am showed to a counter seat. The counter is packed with 2 loud groups, while the tables only has a quiet couple at one end. Bushi Tonkotsu Ramen ($19++)Bonito flakes, chasiu, white onions, bamboo shoots, egg, lime & red gingerI am told that the lime is used to kill off the strong fishy taste, although it does not make much of a different in the soup. The lime is given in a slice instead of a wedge, so it is quite difficult to squeeze out any juice. As the aircon is quite strong the dish turns cold very fast. The dish tastes quite average.Bespoke Cocktail ($25)It is a mixture of Diplomatico Añejo rum, pineapple juice, passion fruit and almond. Tastes not bad, except that I have gone through a terrible experience with the staffs when ordering the drink. I have thought that I have ordered but it never comes. The billing of the drink is not what I expected.Overall poor service from the staffs. Food is average.

After so many missed opportunities, I finally made it out to Horse's Mouth! This is a fun bar to enter, at least if you do it through Uma Uma Ramen. Walk in, wave at the staff and say you're going downstairs, press the button that's slightly hidden on the side of the wall, watch as the black door just swooshes open, and descend to the basement where all the liquor is!In the past, walking in on a Friday night was impossible as they'd be fully booked, so I made sure to make a reservation this time. But surprisingly it was very quiet this time around. Was it because it was Deepavali earlier in the week and everyone went on holiday? Or could it be because Louis, the bartender everyone talks about, moved to L'Aiglon on Neil Road? Or are locals over the trend of speakeasies and subterranean bars?Whatever it was, I was just happy to finally get a seat. The decor is really neat and since there are no windows, it's just one of those watering holes that lets you lose yourself in your drink.The menu had a lot to offer, and they can also do bespoke cocktails as well. I ordered the Czech Connection, and although I can't list all the ingredients in it, just know it was stiff enough and was a nice way to start the weekend.Though you can get bar bites, I love how you can still order off Uma Uma's menu. (This also helps in saving some $$$ as The Horse's Mouth is more high end.) Hooray for getting affordable ramen and rice dishes along with cocktails!We arrived around 7, and even by 8:30 or so the bar wasn't filled up too much. Hopefully this isn't a bad sign, but hey, if you've been meaning to check this place out, perhaps now's the time!

Love this place! Been here a few times for drinks, and thoroughly enjoyed it and the company. Finally tried the ramen here and it's surprisingly delicious! I tried the truffle ramen and hubby tried the garlic ramen. My brother and friend first introduced me to this place because of the Bloody Mary and the waiter, but I think the waiters have changed since I'm not sure. Anyway, highly recommend for a chill place! Good Japanese whiskey here too, and other cocktails :)

Love the space.Not to impress with my cocktails that night. Perhaps because Louis, the master, was not in. They were mostly too weak and nothing too impressive. But the service was great, the space brilliant, the food yummy. I guess that is good enough for me to want to return.

This stunning cocktail bar is a hidden gem and well worth writing home about.We shared some fun banter with the friendly guys behind the bar, as well as some great tips on sourcing some local food gems. The cocktails? Some of the best I've had not just in Singapore, but ever. I couldn't tell you exactly what I had, because in each case I ordered off menu and let the boys do their thing after hinting at a few ingredients that float my boat. They nailed it every time. We only spent three nights in Singapore, but came here on two of them!

Friendly guys behind the bar, felt very comfortable with the Japanese minimalist surroundings and atmosphere. These guys are perfectionist and I had a lot of pleasure tasting the product of their labour. They describe them selves not as a speakeasy though in my opinion it comes pretty close.

Along with Jigger & Pony, Horse's Mouth is my other major pick for cocktails in Singapore. Bartender Louis is well-versed in the art of the stir & shake and provides pretty great conversation to boot. Pro-tip: ask him why he hates the Moscow Mule cocktail.The usual applies here: a menu exists but one need not be limited by it. Just tell Louis what you feel like drinking and he'll cook something up for you. I recommend their whiskey sour and also suggest you look at their bourbon & rye options. Willett Rye in particular is an excellent choice.You can also get ramen from Uma Uma, which is a pretty solid option for late night grub. The place is small so book ahead on weekends or walk in and sit at the bar on weeknights. My only complaint: early closing time of 12am.

Ok - I'm not that much of a drinker or going to bars every weekend. I do enjoy a drink or two every once in a while with good friends. I was looking for a place to go after teaching my dance class with my friends for my birthday drinks and found this place searching through Yelp. (Thanks Yelp!)We took a while to find the entrance for this place - we went through a dark door through Uma Uma Ramen even though the restaurant was closed the door was surprisingly still open and we found our way downstairs to Horse's Mouth. What a pleasant and beautiful surprise! The place is impeccably designed. Very Classy. My small group was seated immediately and we ordered amazing specialty cocktails. For once in my life, I was able to order a Cosmopolitan (I'm allergic to Cranberries) because they make it with Pomegranate juice. It was delicious! My second drink was also delicious and I told the bartender, Louis that I wanted something fruity, fizzy, and with rum in it. The drinks here are strong but also go down easy. Drinks in Singapore ain't cheap, and too many bars serve them watered down. This bar doesn't serve their drinks watered down and the concoctions are original. Very nice bartender as well. He kept coming over and talking to us. Great place to bring a group of friends for some drinks and conversation. :-) Definitely had a fun night. I will be coming back here.
