If you're thinking about desserts for presents on occasions like birthdays or holidays, Pique Nique probably will win some points for presentation. Upon tasting the cakes, they didn't fare that badly either! Only thing is that they can be a little pricey (think $6-8 for a slice, on par with places like Canele).Service on the weekday afternoon was relatively fast and fuss-free, and the staff seemed cheerful and willing to attend to my requests.

Coming across another one on the list of dessert places by chef pang, I was pretty interested to give it a shot. It is an American themed restaurant serving burgers, fries and shakes, as well as an extensive list of desserts. A bunch of friends and I dropped by for lunch one afternoon. The place was nicely decorated, slightly casual with a nice chilled-out vibe and a dreamy ambience. I ordered a burger and was pretty disappointed with it. The bun was soggy and kinda oily, and the patty was dry and blend. The fries were ok, but nothing to shout about. I had a taste of my friend's Mac 'n' Cheese and that was pretty yummy, comfort food material. The egg benedict another friend had was not too bad either. Well, I guess I was just unlucky with the burger. I had a couple of macarons to end the meal and ordered a pistachio, red velvet and salty caramel. While the texture of the macarons were really good, they were a little too sweet. I wouldn't exactly call it pretty either, as the colours were way too bright. I've heard great things about their cupcakes and I guess I may return to try it out if I am around the area.

I went to Pique Nique with a friend for a snack. I love the decor of this place. However, I find the service here a bit lacking.. took us quite a while to get the attention of the waiting staff. My salad came and I love how generous they were with the amount of chicken..however the lemon dressing did not sit too well with me. My friend ordered their iced chocolate which I have sampled and it was good, that is something I will order if I should go back again. Oh and their desserts, I have to try it one day as well.

I had rather high hopes for Pique Nique, opened by Chef Pang of Antoinette and Canele previously, and its American-style food and desserts. I have not actually had an opportunity to try the food there but have been there a few times for desserts at tea time. As expected, it was a stylish place with pretty food that you'd want to stare at all day. The general feeling of the place is very different from Antoinette just as high street fashion is different from high end. The service is casual, perhaps not the friendliest but not a turn-off either. I ventured to try their cupcakes, after being told that they were really good. I have to admit I was a little disappointed. I first tried the red velvet cupcake which looked disturbingly bright and lacked any hint of cocoa, and violet cupcake which had a very interesting dropped sticking out at the top. They weren't bad, although the amount of sugar could be reduced a little, but lacked uniqueness in taste and a more multi-faceted flavour beyond sugary sweet. Also, it was a lot more dense than I like my cupcakes to be with a thick layer of cream. I very much preferred the violet cupcake, which is actually somewhat of a berries confiture filling and a simple twist to the traditional vanilla cupcake. I've also tried their very American Whoopie Pie. It was interesting, and definitely not a macaroon, but I'm not crazy about it.Cupcakes are about $5 each and cakes are about $8, so while it is not exactly an expensive dessert place compared to many of such similar Western cafes around, I wouldn't exactly be craving for it or returning too often.

Although the decor of this place is cute, the food is really super meh. Nothing stood out and my basic breakfast meal was beyond ordinary. We also tried the red velvet cake, since some reviews recommended it, but it wasn't good at all. It was dry with hard frosting....

It is difficult to find a café in town that serves decent food at affordable prices, but Pique Nique is one such café. It is an American-themed café that serves all-day breakfast, desserts and pastries. It has a rather pleasing ambience, with princessy seats. Having dined there twice, I have had one good experience and another disappointing one. The Eggs Benedict was passable and came in a large portion. The poached eggs were cooked right, fully cooked on the outside but with a runny yolk. The hollandaise sauce was rich and buttery. The omelette was a miss, since it was overcooked and far too ordinary. Seeing that they had Whoopie Pies on display was a pleasant surprise. Whoopie pies are like American versions of macarons and the difference is that whoopie pies have a chewier and more cake-like texture than crispy macaron shells. Pique Nique is one of the rare few places that sells this snack.

Possessing unique décor and staff dress code, Pique Nique takes one away from the hustle and bustle of Takashimaya into a little sanctuary to rest your soul after a hard day of shopping. Although pricey and with seemingly small portions, their array of finger foods, burgers and meats team up with a quaint selection of beverages and desserts to soothe both soles, souls and voracious appetites very well. With staff that are willing to go the extra mile and ensuring service with a smile, Pique Nique is a perfect place to recoup while you strategize your next romp around the vast shopping centre that is Takashimaya.

I visited the branch at the recently opened J-Cube in Jurong East a couple of weeks ago. Initially I was rather impressed at the decor and set up of the cafe; there was a little raised platform with 2 tables that seats 4 people each in the center of the cafe. This platform was covered in fake grass and had a distinct picnic feel to it. The rest of the seats consisted of an endearing medley of ottomans, armchairs and wooden rickety chairs. Service was a tad slow for my liking, with a perpetual sour face on their staff - not cute! We had the Chilli Fries, which was one of the tastier ones I've tried. The sauce wasn't as thick, meaning we didn't have to fight over scraping our fries on the leftover sauce. The Sticky Date Pudding was great too, but it didn't come with the scoop of ice cream - we had to order it separately. The price was ok only because we shared 3 dishes among 4 people - I would not recommend going there with an empty stomach as their pricing is definitely not worth the heartland mall location nor quality of food! It was nice place to have a short afternoon chat, but then again there are many nicer places. Would not be going back again soon!

it's a small, open cafe that doesn't seem very crowded at the moment, and while I remember they had a glass counter of cake and the like, nothing really seems to have stood out - but then again I wouldn't have gotten anything else seeing as the words sticky pudding were on the menu.it's a small portion of cake and a drizzle of sauce alongside a scoop of bean-speckled vanilla ice cream. not the best or the most innovative (this goes to artichoke for the moment), but it was well-warmed and moist, and not too sweet. a decent rendition, really.photos here: andmorefood.wordpress.co…

My daily coffee fix - I cannot believe that I waited so long to tell the world about their amazing coffee and service :)Thanks to Jewel, I became an absolute coffee snob. Their baristas are true experts, their coffee beans carefully selected - and you can pick from two coffee bean choices every day - with the coffee itself being pure velvety, strong goodness.Ask for the stamp card if it is not automatically given to you, as you'll get a free coffee once your card is full.The staff is cheerful and seems to love what they're doing. Food is quite good - I've had pasta, bacon & egg muffin and a ham & cheese melt before.My current crush is their Red Velvet latte, which is an absolute revelation that I don't know how to live without anymore. Good for them, tricky for me ;)

Excellent single origin coffee spot. Jewel offers a couple of bean choices for your coffee order. Today I enjoyed a flat white with beans from Las Brumas El Salvador's 60 hectare fertile farm located on the Santa Ana Volcano. If you need something to pad your coffee, there is also a good selection of pastries, pasta and sandwiches. Also, if you want to learn more about the art and passion of "cupping" (coffee tasting), sign up for one if their free coffee cupping sessions.

Nice little coffee place right in the heart of CBD. Good place to grab a coffee and work, there is quite a crowd around so seating might be a bit tricky. I liked the coffee they used for the latte, very strong chocolaty flavors.

I like Jewel, it's around the corner from my office, the people are friendly, and the coffee is STRONG!  The only downside is that they don't make flavored lattees, only the regular kind.  The muffins are excellent and the prices are decent!  I also like the outdoor tables, which are perfect for a client meeting, or quick catch up.  Or in my case, provides a quick escape from the office in the middle of the day.  Great choice!

This is one of two Jewel outlets in Singapore. The other one is on Rangoon Road and this smaller one is on Shenton Way in the CBD. Not surprisingly the guests and feel of the places differ a lot. This is more the go to place for a caffeine fix or a quick lunch for all the people slaving away in the CBD and unfortunately that also impacts the service here as it often feels rushed, not that friendly and occasionally the quality of the coffee is not at the level I am expecting here. That said the coffee is usually good and there is at least two beans to choose from and several different brew methods. I try to come after morning rush but before the lunch rush as the quality of the coffee is usually better when they have more time for it. The seating is limited indoors but there are some tables outside where it is fine to hang out for longer periods of time. The food is very much something that can be skipped. There are so many better options to get your stomach filled around here. Still it is a pretty safe bet for a cup of coffee when in the CBD although I would personally rather head to the New Black for filter coffee and 6 oz Espresso for espresso based beverages but this is also good.

I hardly return to cafes in Singapore but I have been a huuuggee fan of Jewel Coffee since I join my gym. I'd like to say that our cafe scene in Singapore is good, but in all honesty it's only cafes like Jewel that make it good. Their coffee and the standard of their coffee is a benchmark. I've been to both their outlets and not only is the coffee good but the food at Rangoon Rd is pretty awesome as well. Forgive their small outlet in CBD, it's obviously catered for take & go but I'm guessing that it's the only way they can sustain the high rental in the area. When somebody ask me which is my favorite cafe in Singapore, Jewel is usually the first name that pops into my head.

Coffee - I'd recommend the Gibraltar. I'm a personal fan of their Sumatran beans.Food - I thought maybe I was hungry the first time I went hence it tasted so good. Made a return journey, just as pleased. Sausages and tomatoes hit the spot.Service - friendly and unobtrusive. Both times I was there working on my laptop and never made to feel that I was "taking up space". Seating was adequate, the al fresco area is always nice to people watch.

A haven for coffee lovers in the CDB, Jewel coffee is doing some interesting things with single origin coffees, and with different brewing methods. Espresso - the volume was perfect, with a medium dark crema. The dominant flavour in the shot is citrus - but it's a shot where the astringency is very evident - as much a sensation as a flavour, an intense hit of citrus that awakens your taste buds, with an aftertaste that fades out slowly. The mouthfeel has some syrupy elements, but not overwhelmingly so either. The choice of single origin beans is a nice touch - when I visited, beans from Costa Rica and El Salvador were being served. Each has distinct tasting notes, however I found that the citrus elements were dominant in each. This is an intensely floral shot, and may not be to everyone's tastes. I'll never complain about single origin coffees on a menu - it's a sign of how far coffee culture has come, and it directly benefits the farmers who grow the beans in question. However, it could be a good idea to have one strong citrus single origin and one robust, earthy and less floral single origin paired with each other. The cappuccino that I ordered came with smooth foam that complemented, rather than drowned out, the underlying coffee flavour. The layer of microbubbles added the required smooth mouthfeel, while allowing the coffee flavour to dominate. The layer of foam and serving size were just as they should be, ensuring that this was separate and distinct from a latte. The latte art, and contrast of light on medium dark foam, was a welcome touch.There is a good selection of drinks on the menu, with Chemex, V60, Syphon and Iced coffees available also. It's a good coffee choice for anyone working in the Shenton Way area, however it is slightly more expensive, with an espresso priced at $4.20.

My go to coffee joint whenever i'm in the area. The ambiance is nothing fancy, but the coffee is probably the 2nd best I've had in Singapore (pm me if you want the first), and I drink a lot of coffee! Try the flat white, Melbourne style and with velvety microfoam. They also usually have at least 2 selections of beans to choose from.

I'm fortunate enough to have Jewel right around the corner from my office. I've been going to these guys on-and-off for over a year and while I'm not there on a daily basis I can attest to their coffee being of fairly reliable quality.Jewel offer only single origin coffee on their espresso machine. I think this is overkill as there's nothing wrong with a good blend but the origins they have on offer (they usually have two to choose from) are normally pretty good.Cafe owners passionate about coffee usually find it difficult to find service staff in SIngapore that can match them in knowledge and obsession, which usually affects the quality of the service. But the service quality at Jewel has definitely improved dramatically since I first started coming here which is very heartening to see.My only gripe about the place is that it's obviously set up more to cater to the take-away office crowd (of which I am also part) than the drink-in coffee drinker. This is evidenced by their lack of seating inside the shop itself (they have a sizeable al fresco area), their use of bar-stools and the self service set up. While I understand why a business owner would employ self service, I'm just not a fan. I don't like juggling two coffees while opening a door. It's a recipe for disaster if you're as clumsy as I am.Bottom line though, these guys serve some of the best coffee in Singapore and their sandwiches are pretty good also. Give it a shot.

My favorite coffee joint in the CBD area. It's a little bit on the pricier side, but the coffee is worth it and you can get a punch card and earn a free drink after 9 drinks. I personally love the flat white ($6) and the iced mocha ($7.50).

Gourmet coffee shops are becoming a trend around the island, especially in the financial and business districts - perhaps owing to the fact that people work hard in Singapore and caffeine is in demand. This shop is known to serve double shots for all its cups of coffee. You get to choose your preferred beans while their chalk boards teach you a thing or two about brewing coffee. It's a great place to have a quick meeting or to catch up with a friend. Unfortunately the indoor, air-conditioned area is small so you may have to sit outside when it is busy. I had a cafe latte for $5.80 that was really strong and kept me going till 2am that night.

First visit. Had a Gibraltar. For coffee lovers who like their joe slightly bitter with an astringent quality, this is for you. Decaf lovers this is not your place. My fav latte is still at Liberty. I applaud SG for offering so many decent cafe options!

i finally got a flat white whilst here in singapore.  i miss them so much from my london days, b/c they are hard to find in the states (or, impossible, rather).the coffees here are expensive, and if you want soy, it's an extra $1!  however, you do get to choose the type of bean you want.  i chose a brazilian bean today, b/c it had chocolate and caramel notes, and i was not disappointed!  the other choice was sumatran, so my indonesian cowkr got that one and liked it as well.

Over hyped. Over crowded, over priced. Spent 140$ for two crabs. Their signature crab and chilly crab. Chilly crab was sweet and ketchupy tasting. Crab quality was not bad but not worth the wait and money. Better off at jumbo ECP if you want the touristy thing.

Let's see... how do we summarize our dinner at Melben? Yum. Yum. Yum. Let's just jump straight to the crabs. First time having salted egg yolk crab for me and I think I just found a new favorite preparation for crab. The savory salted egg yolk elevates this fried crab dish and brings out the sweetness of the crab. I just wanted to gather the crab roe and salted egg yolk to make a "crabonara" sauce to throw with some pasta. The crab with tung hoon dish had a nice fragrance and this peppery preparation of crab was truly delicious too. As before the crab is incredibly sweet and nicely counterpointed by the black pepper. Lastly, the crab bee hoon soup was just sublime. I could drink that sweet and savory broth for days on end. Honestly can't remember too much about this crab because the broth was just that good. All in all, we had a nice variety of crab preparations and they were all yummy in their own unique ways. You would think other dishes would suffer when you are known for one thing, which in Melben's case is crab, but their other dishes are pretty decent too. From the garlic veggies to salt and pepper pork chops to the cuttlefish youtiao, the dishes were pretty pretty tasty although relegated to playing back up to the crabs. My aunt called ahead to reserve a table and our crabs and I think y'all should too. As everyone has mentioned, you need to come early otherwise you're out of luck. Or as I would like to think, feeling really crabby for the rest of the night.

CRAB. apparently is a "MUST EAT" when in singapore. & That's exactly what I did... 2 days in a row... Mellben Seafood was the 2nd day. And it did not disappoint! The food did not. The service was definitely just frustrating and straight up terrible. But, I was very excited to try this place because the Foodporn show on clicknetwork (youtube channel) did a segment on their shimmering sand crab and salted egg chicken drumstick lollipop! There are two locations apparently. This one in tou payoh (sp?) and another one. This one is located across from a food hawker center. Currently, there is construction going on so the front of the restaurant might be hidden from the street view so you'll have to tell your taxi driver to drop you off at the side with the numbers "211" on. Basically, go inside the carpark and after you pass the gate, turn left..? and there should be a durian stand in the front. Now, don't be expecting some fancy high end restaurant with Air conditioning okay. This place is where LOCALS singaporeans go so the food better be bomb but that also means that the place is going to be pretty much kind of like a hole in the wall. & it kind of was. The restaurant was a bit tiny inside so they kind of expanded out to the courtyard where a few tables were set. Smaller tables are inside the store, cooled by basic fans. We had a table reserved out in the courtyard because our party was originally bigger than 6. It was so hot and ratchet outside seriously. and it was dark too. They had one or two street lights but they didn't help much. Since they're known for two tyypes of crab: the braised beehon style and the butter style, We got both ! Yay for two crabs for one meal! Def. get crab. It was soooo fresh and delicious. The hardest part about eating crab will always be taking the shells off. & that will always be a pain in the ass but that's what makes the crab meat even tastier. Be sure to dip the meat in the sauce so that you're not eating some tasteless crap. I wanted to also try shimmering sand crab but it would have been way too many food for just a party of 6 haha. We also ordered the salted egg chicken drumstick lollipop, which was da bomb!! Def get that! Some other dishes were the tofu with enoki mushrooms. steamed fish, green veggies, and pork spareribs. Pretty much over ordered! So, all the food were pretty yummy! My favorites were the crabs and the chicken lollipop. And also, the coconut juice here is fresh and yummy as well! Their dishes have different sizes you can order from small, medium, and large. Now, onto the disappointing part of the experience: the SERVICE! It was definitely a bust!! My grandma and I had arrived before the rest of the party. I was told to tell the host the reservation information. I don't know if speaking ACTUAL ENGLISH, not SINGAPOREAN English, is considered to be a bad thing or what... but when I spoke English to the girl, she treated me like crap! She just pointed to a table out in the courtyard and simply said, "that's your table." Okay, like can you actually walk us over there. Wtf. Anyway, onto the rest of the evening. We sat there for the longest time and NO ONE came to check up on us. I repeat, NO ONE. Not even to ask if we wanted water. or Even if we were ready to order for that matter. Granted, the rest of the party hadn't arrived yet, but still. When everyone arrived and we were ready to order, none of the servers cared to check on us. My cousin had to basically flag down the waiter who was taking the orders of the adjacent table. All throughout dining, every time we needed something, we had to be prepared to wait forever until they noticed us. It was definitely frustrating. If they're that understaffed, you'd think the management would hire more people or at least train these people to be more efficient. Food was delicious. Service sucked. Decor sucked. Prepare to have drops of sweat roll down your face as you're going at it on that crab claw.

Honestly the food here is good. Of course it's not cheap but not crazy-Jumbo prices either. The items that we're oh-so-good were:1) Crab in Broth - we paid for extra Beehoon and soup and it's super worth it! The broth was thick with favour and the crab, tho not huge, was fresh. The flesh came apart nicely  and easily. Indication of freshness to me. Easily best dish of the night. 2) Guinness Pork Ribs - very well marinated ribs with excellent taste. Doesn't taste like Guinness at all. Very very tasty dish. 3) Broccoli with Beancurd Skin & Mushrooms - it's essentially a very simple dish but don't very very nice!4) Creamy Butter prawns - it's really prawn in thick salted eggs sauce. What's NOT to like?! Large fresh prawns in savory sauce! Makes you wanna scoop up all that sauce after you're done with the prawns. Other dishes are decent but the above of special mention worthy. Will be back again. :)

The Toa Payoh branch of one of the better known crab establishments in Singapore. This branch opened when the original Mellben surged in popularity. Prices have risen over the years but it is still a decent place with a good variety of crab and seafood dishes.Mellben is mostly famous for crab bee hoon, a whole crab served in a fragrant, flavourful milky soup with thick rice noodles. Their chilli crab is also good, although not the star of the show.However, the menu has since expanded to encompass a multitude of crab dishes, the latest of which is "Shimmering Sand Crab" (jin sha crab). This is crab deep fried and smothered in a sauce made from salted egg. Absolutely finger lickin' good.The queue is as equally long as the outlet in Ang Mo Kio so arrive early with ample amounts of patience. The wait can stretch to 1 hour. (I found myself browsing the durians next door while waiting) Depending on the supplier and season, they also tend to run out of crab, so being early is also important. One good thing, they also accept VISA! :)Skip the other overpriced crab restaurants in the city. Toa Payoh is where it's at.Footnote to non-locals: BTW, this is not your frou-frou white tablecloth atas seafood restaurant. You sit outside with no AC, on plastic chairs and service is brusque. You're here for the food, no?

Again dinner here cause my friend recommendation. It was  a nice kinda hawker food. The noodle crab very yummy, love its soup! The green vegie was nice. And pepper crab was so so. Recommended for group at leadt 4 ppl.

With all the rave about this restaurant, I invited my family to celebrate my birthday at this restaurant. My experience was a disappointing one where the food was not as expected. We ordered the Bee Hoon Crab Soup and Chilli Crab accompanied with some other Cze Char dish. The dishes were nothing fantastic. As for crab, they were very big in size. The claw was as big as person closed palm.  Sauce of Chili Crab was too watery and crab meat was not fresh enough. The total cost of the meal come up to around $200 plus which was considered expensive. Overall, I will not go back to this restaurant again

Right smack in the middle of a coffee shop in Toa Payoh is a branch of the ever famous Melben Crab. I was quite excited to try it out since it's been long established as one of the best and most authentic crab restaurants in Singapore. My first impression was ultimately chaos since there was no visible system to queuing to have our orders taken, and even with their staff desperately trying to get some order into the system, I still encountered the unpleasant experience of having several families jump the queue ahead of us. Couple this with a growling tummy and you get a very grumpy patron wanting food fast. HOWEVER, the food took forever to be served, and I hated how they served the rice first, with 3 dishes being served one by one - as if we were attending a 8 course wedding dinner! The rice was cold by the time the first dish of bamboo clams was served, and we had to actually stop eating the rice while waiting for the veggies to be served. The crab, which finally came last, was served after our rice bowls were empty - big fail! But to their credit, the Butter Crab we ordered was delicious, with huge chunks of fresh meat coming off cleanly from the shells. Their fried mantous (buns) were amazing dipped into the butter sauce as well.

We have eaten here several times over the last two years. It is usually the special place to take friends when they come to Singapore. You have to get here early. It opens at 5pm so be there by 5pm. Any later and get ready for a wait.During our latest visit last night, we ordered Mongolian prawns, steamed Grouper Hong Kong style and White Pepper Crab. Some Kai Lan and Asparagus and some seafood Fried Rice completed the order. Service was actually pretty quick, even though they advised us it would be a thirty minute wait for the food. The vegetables and seafood Fried Rice arrived first, the garlic in the Kai Lan and the Asparagus helping add some flavor, while the asparagus had just the right amount of crunch when you bit into it. The seafood fried rice was OK, but not spectacular. Does anyone know if seafood fried rice is spectacular anywhere?  I thought not. Anyway, next up we're the Mongolian Prawns. Only five on the plate which would have been fine, apart from the fact there were four of us. This meant a fight to the finish for the last prawn. All were big and juicy with the Mongolian sauce having good spicy flavor. Next up should have been the White Pepper crab, but actually turned out to be Black pepper Crab. No problem it was still great despite the mix up. The steamed grouper was last, serviced up Hong Kong style in a soy, ginger and garlic sauce. This was the star of the show, the fish was very tender, falling off the bones, with a really delicate flavor not overpowered by the soy, garlic and ginger sauce. Many napkins later, four of us sat back covered in crab shrapnel and surveyed the scene before us.  We had done justice to all of the food and swore we would be coming back soon.

Affordable, authentic and delicious. Since I popped in here with some girlfriends I've brought at least 2 other groups of friends on other occasions and recommended Big Mama to many! I love the budae jigae - chock full of ingredients, and I love that it's quite spicy with a strong kimchi taste. I've unfortunately tried other places in SG where it tastes incredibly watered down, or just like instant ramen. Love the rice cakes too. The best part of korean restaurants are the unlimited banchan, and we especially loved the japchae (!). Any restaurant that serves japchae as an appetizer almost certainly becomes a favorite. I've also tried the kimchi seafood pancake here, and it's huge and shareable between 3-4 people if you're having it as a side. I loved how it was filled with squid and other seafood too, and also thick enough. The ambiance is not the main star here, but at least I didn't emerge smelling of korean barbecue as some places lead to. I actually really like the lively, chatty atmosphere. Service is also prompt. Reservations are required perhaps a week in advance if you'd like to eat at prime dining time (eg 7pm). We ended up only getting a 8pm reservations & had drinks & fries at another joint down the road. It's walking distance from Tiong Bahru MRT and not difficult to find at all

So my friend recommended this place for the 8 of us to indulge in some casual dining and to chill out, and the signature dish, the Dakgalbi, which is charged at $18/pax. Basically it's this giant stew-like pot of korean rice cakes, vegetables and chicken that they cook on the spot (or at least they show you that it's cooked on the spot), and yes it's really good! Disclaimer: Unfortunately, I'm no Korean and neither have I stepped onto that island before so I can't tell whether it is authentic. Nevertheless, the soup/gravy was relatively spicy (I'm a relatively light spicy eater) but it tasted good. The chicken meat was succulent and the rice cakes were chewy - again, I don't know what should authentic cakes taste like, but I definitely liked the chewy texture. We also got the Suyuk, but I felt that it was relatively expensive. It's basically strips of pork belly served with thin slices of cucumber, radish and beansprouts and 2 types of sauces. And you eat the pork belly with 1 condiment and 1 sauce. Well, if you want to kill your curiosity or if you want to see how a traditional Korean food looks like you can try it, but I don't think it's that value for money.Overall, there was 7 of us actually eating, and we paid about $30~ per person and we got away relatively full. So that's the price range you are looking at. But we sat there for around 2 hours (oops :X) This would be a good guide. Note: Water and Korean sides are free flow! (yay!)Bigmama offers a nice, casual ambience and we felt like we could talk alot without disturbing the other customers. The staff is friendly and service was nice. However, during the busy period, the wait-staff might be a bit lag, but that was fine.This shop is conveniently located, and is a mere 5-10 minute stroll from Tiong Bahru MRT. We went there on a Wednesday night at 6.30pm and it got pretty crowded by 7-8pm. Do reserve if you want to come in that timing because I'd noticed walk-in customers getting turned away because of lack of space.Good news: I just found they have a website so you can take a look at the menu before going bigmama.sg/#!tiong-barhu… (nope, I'm not paid to share this)Overall, I would like to bring other people to try this readily accessible, yet good food.

After the Biopolis branch opened, I was never deprived of their seafood pancake again. Their bbq pork was so good, we ordered 2nds. For dinner, this branch almost guarantees seats cos the office crowd wudda gotten their fix over lunch. The atmosphere is very different compared to the Kim Tian branch, more upclass versus the latter's family-restaurant feel. Recommended for a group of 3-6 so you can order more items to share!
Pro:- Pretty unique Korean dishes- Rice wine was pretty decentCon：- Long queue- Ambience is virtually non-existent

Came here for a birthday celebration with my mates. We ordered lots of stuff, but I'm not a fan of spicy food, so I only had a taste of the kimchi stuff that they ordered. The dishes were indeed very spicy! Fortunately the restaurant offered to make a vegetarian pancake for me when we asked. How lovely! The vegetarian pancake was quite appetising and I was quite pleased with it.

I finally tried Big Mama's Dak Galbi at Tiong Bahru! For a Tuesday night and they are fully occupied, that's impressive. We had to wait half an hour for a table. We ordered the Dak Galbi which tastes really so so if you have been to Korea and had Yu Ga Chicken Galbi. Of course, the cold weather in Seoul helps as well. We ordered 2 sets for 3 girls to share. It was sufficient if you are not a big eater as the portion is small and they have very little other side dishes added in such as the rice cake and vegetables. However, for the big eaters, do not worry. You may request to add rice at almost the end of your dakgalbi for them to fry with the red sauce and seaweed!!! The seaweed helps to make the fried rice tastes soooo much better I must say! The rice was the life saver or else I would have to go McDonalds afterwards! Hah Another this, sukyu was at best, 3 star as it is thinly sliced and has the sour sauce and spicy sauce to dip in. Makgeoli was undoubtedly good! Service is good. But, 3 star is given as it is like a home-cooked meal served in a restaurant. However, I will come back to try other dishes or as and when I crave for dakgalbi.

As a Korean-American looking for familiar Korean comfort food, this is the place to go.  Sorry to say, it's been hard to find decently-priced, authentic Korean food in Singapore. So Bigmama is a favorite go-to restaurant. Their dakgalbi is flavourful and perfect for a rainy day.  It gets really busy, so make sure to make reservations.  If you have a spontaneous craving for it, your best bet is to drop in for a lunch there (definitely not dinner).  It's so good, you'll probably ending up over-eating and regretting your life..but that's not always a bad thing =P
Good Dakgalbi. The fried rice they made in the pan after the chicken was nearly finished was truly excellent. My Korean and non-Korean friends seem to agree that this place is good.

(Read in "The Most Interesting Man In The World's" voice) I don't always eat Korean food, but when I do, I prefer Big Mama.No seriously though, this is probably the only Korean restaurant I can think of that I've been to in Singapore! I only come here for lunch when my colleagues have a Korean craving, and it gets the job done. Located on Kim Tian Road, I would say it's about a 5-7 minute walk from the Tiong Bahru MRT.It's been a while since I've eaten here, so I can't recall the exact dishes that we normally order. All I remember is that they are the ones that can be shared between 3-4 people. What I thought was unique was that some of the shared dishes are served in one of those pans attached to hot plate. At least the food will never be cold! Last time I ordered a la carte and tried the beef bulgogi; it tasted perfectly fine to me. All the extra fixins that usually come with a Korean meal (like kimchi and those glass noodles) are also all okay.There's not much in terms of ambiance here, and the TV will most likely be showing some random Korean TV show. However, this is a good spot to check out with friends, as most of the tables cater to groups. Since I don't eat a lot of Korean food, I don't have anything to compare it to, so for now it's just a-ok.

First Korean restaurant we tried in Singapore due to overwhelming recommendations by Singaporean bloggers. We were disappointed. The suyuk was edible. The banchans were semi edible. The jeon was overcooked and greasy. We didn't try the dakgalbi that people seem to enjoy, but I'm guessing we probably wouldn't like it. The flavors are more local than Korean, which works well for the local clientele but it was not what we were looking for.

I dragged a group of friends to Big Mama's after reading a review on it on a famous food blog (maybe Lady Iron Chef) and had a very mediocre experience there. I can definitely say that this is not the best Korean food in Singapore, nor is it authentic (I have had a ton of Korean food in NY/LA).  It's good, but not fight the crowds, drool at the corner of your mouth good (not by a long shot).Make reservations on a weekend because it gets really crowded here full of large groups.  I guess most of these diners prefer home style Korean cooking, because there are fewer grilled options here.  The most popular dishes here are the soups, dak galbi (chicken with cabbage and rice cakes), and the sliced pork belly.  The pajun (pancake) was crispy and passable and the kimchee fried rice had nice bits of kimchee.  The dak galbi is the best dish of the dishes I've tried and while it had many more ingredients than traditional dak galbi, it is hearty and satisfying.  The sliced pork belly is ok and comes with different types of pickles.  The odd thing is that the waiter insisted on choosing our pork and sides and put it on our plates.  The panchan consisted of good kimchee, spinach, bean sprouts, potato salad, and a salted fish.The prices for the meat and portions can be a little high at S$25+, but it is within the range for typical Singaporean Korean food prices.  I'm craving Korean food, but likely will try a few more places before coming back here. Next!

Dakgalbi!! Spicy chicken, cabbage, rice cake, sweet potato matchsticks cooked in a bbq pan thing. I really wanted to try this since I didn't get a chance to while in Seoul. I would've liked it to be spicier, but my family liked it well enough. $15/pax, 2 person min. order. Highly recommend the option of adding $3/bowl of rice to be fried with the remaining 10% of the ingredients after you're mostly done eating the main dish (chicken etc). They add some seaweed/sesame oil (i bet, that's why it's so delicious)/pickles in the same pan and cook the rice with the remaining ingredients. SO good.. We only ordered one bowl of rice to be added and it was plenty! $18 grilled mackerel was delicious, very juicy. My brother says it was so good because it was fresh fish! Nice spicy/vinegarish dipping sauce to go with.Seafood pancake ($15) - AWESOME. Really crisp and thin, kind of like a pizza. Didn't have that much seafood though, that I could make out. Same dipping sauce as mackerel, also yummm.Side dishes - jap chae (korean vermicelli); kimchi; lotus root in some creamy sesame dressing (yum!); ikan bilis (expected it to be sweeter, this one was kind of salty - family loved it though!); spinach (just steamed or something); some sort of jelly in light chilli (yum too! very light)It was a little hard to get the attention of the servers, they were pretty busy running around. Reservations must be made for wkend! Good Korean food and for good prices :)

This is good Korean food for Singapore, this is as authentic as it can possibly get (so far). The reason im giving it a four is bc its the best ive had so far in singapore. If this were in LA or Korea, 2 or 3 at best. I had the jjambong and it was below average but the banchan (side dishes), pork, and tofu soup were good. But let me tell you, the portions are tiny. I know most SG people are rather skinny but the portion of pork (for $25) seemed like a rip off. I think its a strange concept for me on how expensive korean food is here bc it literally should have costed half of what we normally pay for. But, i cant complain. Im in a different country where the majority of people here arent korean so you gotta deliver to the masses. My hunt continues to find the best tasting jjambong here!
Cheap, good and authentic. There's a reason why you can't grab seats when you walk in. Book in advance. Walkable distance from Tiong Bahru Mrt. The free flow side dishes are to die for. Haha!

This place is seriously underrated. Their charsiew and sio bak are damn awesome and are right up there with the big boys. I only say this as they aren't your usual household name when it comes to roast meats but hey definitely should be!The charsiew has a good balance of caramelised fat and meat. He gives me 2 kinds of charsiew. One more lean and another with the more caramelised note. The internationally charred bits of skin of the charsiew actually held a crunch.The sio bak is by far the BEST I've had in singapore. I dare put my name on the line for this one. The crackling, meat and fat are just crispy HEAVEN in your mouth. Out of all of Singapore... none can match the price and quality of this stall. It's mad.4.9/5 STARS
Sadly standard have dropped but the attitude the same - bad.  Condiments ginger water chilli water :)

This place is really a heaven-sent for meat lovers! Their char siew just feels so thick and the bite is just right. Not too dry, not too wet but juicy enough to wake up your senses of indulgence. The roasted pork is also made just fine, so fine. The crispy part and the fatty part and the meaty part just work out so well in your mouth. Unbelievable and indescribable.I didn't get to try the chicken and duck but I heard they are most famous for their duck. Just by trying the two meats above already lets them deserve the highest rating. I look forward to trying their duck and update this review but what a splendid meal of meat over here! Come on all carnivores, over here!

I'm going to cry, this place is SOOOO good. The name Nan Xiang Chicken Rice is misleading because this stall specializes in Roast Pork and Roast Duck.Let me start and end with the Roast Pork. WOW, I mean wow! It's got three layers of heaven: (i) juicy inside, (ii) marbled fatty area  and (iii) a crunchy skin. However, what separates this Char Siew vs. others is that the skin has got a serious Smokey Finish. The best part of all, the smokey flavour sticks in your mouth up until you eventually brush your teeth! :D   Be sure to bring your mints, if you plan to go out on a date afterwards. Word of Advice: To best enjoy the roast pork, DO NOT put any sauce on top. It will dilute the flavor. However, be sure to ask the uncle to put sauce on top of the rice. The separation of rice with sauce and the roast pork is just a perfect complement.  Lines are obviously long, Locals already know this little secret. The Uncle is as cool as cucumber and has this air of confidence that "yeah, i'm the man and what I'm serving you is the da bomb diggity!"    Badda bing Badda boom and there you have it. The best Roast Pork on the Red Dot bar none!

I wish I could give them 6 stars. This place is so freaking awesome!  Whenever you have the urge to gorge on meat then this should be your go to spot. Soft succulent pork belly with the perfect crispy skin, tender and juice chicken, and bursting with flavor char Siew! Yum yum yum! I wish it wasn't so close to my house because the temptation is real! The rice is delish too! They tend to run out early (sometimes before 1:30!) so if you don't live/work in the area it can be a real pain in the butt if you miss it. Give it a try and I promise it's worth the risk!

I was hungry, and running late for a meeting in the area, so I thought I'd stop here for a quick lunch... And my decision was made easier by the fact that there wasn't anything in the coffee shop to eat at 2pm, save the very last bits of char siew, siew yoke and some chicken breast... So I got a plate of char siew + siew yoke rice, and sat down to wolf it down.Fate intervened of course, and uncle had generously slapped on my plate some rough cut meats, liberally marbled with soft, juicy fat. As I took a second to admire his handiwork before shovelling it into my now ravenous mouth-hole, I realised the beauty in what lay before me - the rough cut meant he did not stinge on razor-thin slivers, and the chunkier segments offered more bite and flavour, so I could really experience the char in his char siew.Though I did savour each tasty morsel, it was gone too soon, and all I had left was the simple soup to end what was a very tasty meal for just three dollars. Who'd thought you could find such a gem?

I tapaoed this home and ate it three hours later for supper.The roast pork/charsiew tastes good even when cold. There's like three layers though not to be confused with the three-layered pork (San chen rou) which has a middle layer of pure fats.This charsiew is awesome and it's almost an art to see the stall owner finely slice the meat in front of you, then drizzle it with some sauce and pack it up for you.Now I know why the reviews of this place is so positive. Tried the chicken rice like 5 years ago, but kinda forgot how it tastes. Will come back again for chicken rice add charsiew/roast pork!

This is a review of a lunch with a colleague at Nan Xiang Chicken Rice.tinyurl.com/cfer3ssWe were planning on going to a different spot.  But when we arrived, we changed our mind.  My colleague knew of Nan Xiang Chicken Rice and suggested we go there.The staff was terse but professional.The space is neat and clean enough.  It certainly will not send anyone running.tinyurl.com/d7hsfnoNan Xiang is reallyabout the food.  In that, they deliver.  Boy, do they deliver!Chicken rice with roast pork and char siew - This was a very tasty plate of food.  It was all good. The chicken, the roast pork, the char siew - mmm mmm good.  The rice was perfectly prepared.  The chicken was so tender.  Then you get the saltiness of the pork.  Needless to say, we left nothing on the plate.tinyurl.com/cvlw6qvI did not pay for this meal.  Great food, free food - You can't beat that.  The lime juice from the nearby stall was quite good and quite large.tinyurl.com/d53kzcoOverall - If you just want some really good chicken rice with some pork, then this is the place.  It is worth a little trip to visit.

One of the best roast chicken in Singapore - not dry but juicy. I love the roast pork as well - it is crisp and marbled with enough fat.I usually order the chicken and the roast pork but even the char siew is good but there is only this much space in my stomach :)

While this place is an institution here, I haven't been until recently, for lunch. They make a great show of everything - the salad, the cutting of the meat, the yorkshire pudding... I really like the lobster tails starters, and everything was generally good. The prime rib was so juicy and large, I felt so guilty eating one by myself, which I nevertheless shamelessly finished.I do like this place, and liked my window seat! I do feel a little funny that my friend's vegetables on his steak were skewered on little forks suspended over his plate. I also feel a little funny that this place has a lot of pomp. Good place to impress a girl, I spose. (haha) Decent food.Oh, we also had the house-branded wine, which was okay as far as generic wines go.

Service not so good for price you pay. Service in HK Location amazing. The waitress make spinning salad , stand on tippy toes when pouring dressing is the best , food great. But I go for the salad show. I had a dude make my salad in Singapore last night. Not cool at all. I won't be going back to Singapore location anytime soon.

A cut above the rest.Lawry's The Prime Rib, what more can be said about it. Since opening its doors in 1999, Lawry's has been THE go to place for prime ribs in Singapore. With its English style setting (ironic considering the restaurant started in Beverly Hills), it's wait staff dressed immaculately and of course, it's iconic silver cart, Lawry's has attracted thousands, maybe millions, of hungry carnivores looking to get a dosage of their prized, USDA, 21 day aged Prime ribs. However, with tons of Steak houses like Wolfgang Puck's Cut, the much more affordable Aston's and the rise of restaurants like The Prime Society and independent restaurant's like Cocotte,  the question remains..... Is Lawry's really still a cut above the rest? If you're looking for a good generous slice of meat done different from anywhere else than... Yes. We've seen how steaks are done at most restaurants. In a pan, on a grill, all beautifully seasoned and seared off in perfect 200g cuts of sirloin or ribeye but till date, no one quite does it like Lawry's (at least i don't think so). The menu at Lawry's (lunch menu) is fairly simple. No 50 item menu, just a few selections for each course, but be warned, their prime rib lunch which comes with a salad, mash and Yorkshire pudding is more than enough for a meal. This round however, we decided to go for the Festive cut. 220g of their renown prime rib, served with an additional side. We did however thought we'd give their appetizer a shot since it was only for a $19++ top up. Pan Seared Hokkaido Scallop and Shrimp. This was a very beautifully presented plate. Very different from the one you'll get with your ribs. However, sad to say, the presentation was more beautiful than the dish itself. The Shrimp was over cooked and slightly on the rubbery side while the scallop, which was nicely cooked, was very "stringy" (apologies for the lack of a better word). It was hard to cut through and chew and while you could tell it was cooked well, the knife somehow wouldn't slice through smoothly as you'd expect when eating scallops. What bothered me most about the dish though was the mango salsa that came with it. While it was a mango and strawberry salsa, it was very very sweet. The mango had cancelled out all forms of acidity from the strawberry and what you were left with was a salsa that was neither vibrant or complimented the seafood above it very well. So much so that all natural sweetness that should have be showcased by the prawns and scallops, was lost in the salsa.Signature Spinning Bowl SaladWell.... I've honestly had better salads. While it's a decent salad, it certainly didn't blow my mind and really tasted... Well... Rather ordinary. Plus point? The croutons are great! Festive Cut Prime RibsThere's no doubt in my mind that the quality of the meat has changed. While it's still delicious and tender, the meat wasn't as melt in your mouth tender as it was when I first tried it a few years ago. The vast difference in the tenderness between a medium and medium rare was very obvious. That said, it was still a good piece of meat to have. While the meat was good, the sides that it came with sort of bothered me. Mashed Potatoes, a little too starchy and heavy for my liking. Buttered Peas (for myself)As good as buttered peas can get. Peas were decently sweet and nice buttered. Creamed Spinach (for the Gf)Very thick and very rich, just the way spinach should be done. However, flavour? A little flat. You get a heavy dose of cream but don't get any depth in flavour, be it salt or a tinge of acidity to balance it out. Yorkshire PuddingPlus Point? It's HUGE! But, that's about it. Having spent most of my holidays in England thanks to having family there, I've spent my entire childhood enjoying restaurant and home made Yorkshire pudding. However, this Yorkshire pudding sort of misses the spot for me. My aunt uses lard to coat the strays to ensure it crisps without burning but there was that prominent burnt taste in the puddings here. While the overall texture is still nice, the flavour just misses the mark for me (maybe it's because I've been spoiled by the original home made versions). Overall, this is a very tough call for me to make. I still rate the meat a 5 but some of the other dishes didn't quite hit the mark for me. Will still give the restaurant a 4 because of the ambience, the meat, the showmanship. The only qualm I have is, whether Lawry's needs to modernize. While the meat is still good, the way it's served on a plate and the overall feel of the restaurant does somehow feel comfortable yet dated, if that makes any sense.

It took me a while, a long while, before I finally tried Lawry's. It has always been on my list but somehow I never made it there till recently for its 15th Anniversary celebration. A friend was enamored with the special dinner menu and as he was leaving Singapore soon, we made it a leaving do. I think many people dine at Lawry's for special occasion as the pricing is a bit on the high side. There were a few birthday celebrations when we were there. We were also given a complimentary slice of cake together with picture taking (print given on the spot with the soft copy being emailed a few days later) as I mentioned it was a farewell dinner. That was really nice and a good way to remember the occasion.The dinner set menu includes - King Salmon Gravlax- Spinning Bowl Salad- Hokkaido Scallop Vol-Au-Vent- Roasted Prime Beef Ribs - Chocolate SurpriseI liked how the salad was served with a chilled salad fork. The coolness made the salad very refreshing even though the veggies were quite ordinary.The beef was medium and fabulously pink. I had the creamed spinach which was nice but not mind blowing. The yorkshire pudding was fantastic, fluffy inside and crisp outside. I believed they made it right before serving it. The dessert was good too. The salmon and scallop were nice but not that memorable. I would go back just for the prime ribs. That is after all their specialty. The place has a lush yet cozy feel. A bit of the old world charm with its wood paneling and carpet. It is not so intimidating quiet that you feel strange talking nor is it very noisy that you feel like you are in a fish market. It is indeed a fine place for a special occasion.

This place is full of comic factors. It's like dining in a theme park. For reals. Me and the missus walked past the restaurant and I made the casual comment about the fact that I've never tried this restaurant before and then we decided to check out the menu and vibes. The fact that it looks straight out of the 80s was probably the sole comic factor that lured us in. We thought it would be funny. It turned out to be hilarious indeed, and then a little sad. Almost fell off my chair as soon as we were seated, when I saw how they dressed their waitresses in chambermaid uniforms. I mean.. Seriously??!!! Surely it's against some HR policy or Moral and Ethics Code of the restaurant association?!! It was both funny and sad at the same time. We ordered roast beef and steak. It comes with salad. But they didn't tell us that the salad comes with the chambermaid preparing it in front of you with a little dance number. I mean... It's intense. Me and the missus had to channel all our willpower to stop ourselves from laughing out loud. It was hard. Surely this restaurant belongs in Disneyland or something. Surely. The food? It felt like food that you get in a Hard Rock Hotel, or on a cruise. Which to be honest is super aligned and on brand to the vibes of this place. So you can say it's authentic and brand consistent cuts across all touch points. Only problem is that they position themselves as a premium prime rib place, and at a price point to match. They should completely target the cruise dining scene. They'll be big.

If its USDA Prime Rib you crave, you can come here.Most people order the Lawry's Cut or English Cut, that comes with the salad and other extras. For Singaporean appetites, English Cut is adequate unless you're a carnivore who craves more meat. The "performance" of food preparation and faux "english dining room" decor is the novelty here, where the waitresses are dressed in tacky uniforms, they spin and toss your salad in a large metal bowl, and a guy dressed as a "chef" with a fake medal hung around his neck rolls the prime rib out to your table and carves your serving of meat infront of you. Service staff are well trained and very attentive.I've tasted salads better elsewhere, and the "special" seasoned salt is the same thing stocked on the shelves at the grocery for US$1.99. The USDA Prime Rib is decently good, but not mind-blowingly amazing.Unfortunately, Lawrys is extremely pricey here, and I have no idea why. The meat is good, as in US$40 good, but not SGD$120 good. You're better off stepping into Lawrys in Vegas or LA instead.

Yay Lawry's in Singapore! Again, totally overpriced in comparison to the one in LA- Lawry's cut in LA i believe is around $38, here it's around $80 per cut. But I came here for my birthday lunch and mine was complementary! and the service, food quality and portion was just as great. Lawry's is more of a fine dining here- while back in LA it's more casual family dining. Lawry's cut plus the spinning salad never disappoints.

This is one of my favourite restaurants in Singapore - it's pricey, though, so my family tends to go there for special occasions. I pretty much always order the same thing when I get to Lawry's: a California cut, with creamed spinach on the side. Between the salad, the prime rib and the side, I'm always guaranteed to be completely full up and pretty much unable to squeeze in dessert!I'm not sure if these are only for "members" (or people who signed up for the mailing list) of Lawry's, but if they find out that it's your birthday you get a free trifle with candles and the staff sing you a birthday song. It's fun (if it's not you they're singing at) and also quite embarrassing (if it's you they are all singing at and everyone turns to look). Hehe.

LOVE THIS SO MUCH. You will find many places in Singapore and all around the world professing to do the 'best steak ever' (hello Hawksmoor), but I have found no where to be as reliable as this in serving up a quality cut. Admittedly, I have only ever had the Lawry's Cut, but that's mostly because I have never found any reasons to get anything else. The Lawry's Cut comes with a side of salad in a spinning bowl, which is as much a highlight for me as the steak itself. The whole meal is served to you via a little cart, even the salad, and it never ceases to fascinate me how that spinning mechanism can be so simple, yet so elegant, and then mix the salad so perfectly. The croutons are as crunchy as you would want it to be. Best salad ever. Following the salad, prepare for the most glorious cart of meat to be pushed in, and choose wisely. Have it medium-rare, or medium at most. I have decided as a personal guideline that the more expensive the steak, the more rare I should have it (without going to extremes), reason being that fancy places tend to take pride in the freshness of the meat, so you want to be able to taste as much of that as you can get. The serving is sizable - even for the meat lover I am, this plate was a challenge to clean up - and the meat practically melts in your mouth. This finest specimen will come accompanied by the smoothest Idadho mash and a wonderfully prepared Yorkshire pudding to cap off a terrifically English feel to the experience. Worth every single penny.

Lawry's has been around in Singapore for quite a while. The boyfriend and I have been walking past it when it was in Paragon going "One fine day, we shall come here and eat." True enough, we eventually did go there and eat on our anniversary. Firstly, the ambiance of the place is classy. We got a seat by the window side which was lovely. Our first course was the spinning salad, which was supposedly their signature dish. A waitress dressed in a maid outfit rolls a trolley to the side of your table and does a sad little dance while spinning the salad bowl in ice and tossed the salad. I personally feel, other than that dance.. there is nothing quite special about the salad. Our main course came soon after, the chef rolled a trolley to our table and slices the beef in front of you. Cream spinach, corn and mash potatoes were served on the side. Yorkshire Pudding was also served for you to eat it with the gravy. So here's the verdict, the beef was ok. But the Yorkshire Pudding was lovely! I had like two servings of that because it was good. I am not a big fan of greens but at Lawry's I surprised myself by finishing all the cream spinach. All in all, Lawry's is lovely for the ambiance, great service and well.. alright food. It is worth a visit at least once in a blue moon.

Lawry's belongs to a famous chain of prime rib steakhouses in the states and a must try for prime rib lovers out there. The Singapore joint isn't as good as the ones in the United States or even Hong Kong but i would still give it a 4 star rating because there aren't any really good prime rib places in Singapore. Overall satisfying but not an over the top experience.
Went there after xmas, ordered the festive cut, medium, finished everything in the plate. No room for desert.
Their Lawry's prime rib is really good. Service is great if it's not a busy night. Their sides are pretty decebt too.

Easily one of the best steakhouses in Singapore ,  Lawry's the Prime Rib is the to-go place should you crave meat and want to impress your client or date. That's if cash isn't an issue. While it may be pricey, I've never been disappointed once considering the number of times I've been there. The service remains impeccable as always and while there's a slight change in decor ever since they shifted over to Mandarin Gallery, the food remains spot on. Newcomers to Lawry's should give their signature Prime Rib Dinner set a go and request for the Lawry's Cut (250g of the most popular cut). But please remember, if you're going to have steak, make sure you have it at least medium-rare, or you won't get to enjoy the lovely steaks as they should be!

Very nice ambience. Great service. Food is good. Roast beef is sliced according to your preference. Medium should be the most cooked you should request.  Beef could be a little more tender. Suppose to be USDA Prime and aged, but I have had better. Nonetheless the flavor was excellent. For starters we had the crab cake. Good but then in have had the best in Chicago. So could have had less filler. Crust a little hard, but I'm being picky. The brownie desert was very good. I'd pass on the trifle. No flavor of rum at all.  Price is on the high side. Overall a very nice experience and would return for a special occasion or with a special someone.

A trip to Japan has it drawbacks for me: after being spoiled with the most awesome food whilst being there, I suffer from serious Japanese food cravings after returning from Japan for quite a while. So I went to search for a sashimi fix and found this restaurant at the nearby Dempsey Hill.For a Friday evening it was suspiciously empty but this allowed me to get a prime seat at their  bar which has a very tempting display of fresh seafood. Also, the service was quick and correct since there was a lot of waitstaff available.As the oysters were recommended on social media, I went for two oysters, a chirashi with a selection of sashimi and deep fried shrimp. Obviously I paired it with a jug of sake to make the feast complete. The food was of good quality and I was pleased with my sake (which the waitress helped me pick) so I managed to satisfy my craving.Is it as good as in Japan? No, but it was one of the better mid range Japanese I had in Singapore, I will certainly return when I want to treat myself to decent Japanese food.

Overall the food was pretty good but don't think it's worth the price. The two of us spent 100 bucks per person getting the following things:1. oyster with yuzu sauce. My favorite dish of the night. The yuzu sauce with zesty lemon goes perfectly with those oysters2. Chawanmushi. I always have a soft spot for steamed egg, and they do it pretty well here.3. A sashimi platter for two of about 14 pieces. The fish was okay, not super impressed.4. some shishito pepper and shitake mushroom yakitori. I like the shishito pepper really charred but they don't cook it to that extent. And you can't possibly mess up shitake mushroom?5. Green tea icecream. Don't think it's homemade, tastes pretty standard.Again, it wasn't a bad meal but you can get more bang for the buck elsewhere.

For full reviews and pictures, visit my blog,Heard from my friends that it's not easy to get a table at the Far East Shopping Center outlet, which is quite booked but no such issues with the one at Dempsey. If you like your sashimi and Aburi sushi, this is really a place to visit. Love the buttery and smooth texture of the fish, indicative of fresh and not frozen fishes. They are served with freshly grated wasabi, which IMO is a indicator of a quality Japanese restaurant. Oyster lovers would be glad to know that the ones served here are ginormous. The mini course or the bento set is really value for money considering the amount and quality of food. Perfect for sharing (for 2) with an additional side dish. Highlight of the meal has got to be the Aburi platter. The meat was simply sublime and each piece was drizzled in a different cream/miso sauce. Perfect torching technique as i've previously highlighted in my Kaiho Sushi review. The kita-komachi rice, one of the best rice in Japan, accompanies the fish, adding that light vinegarish and sweet dimension. The little charred spots bring in some smokiness too.

Rakuichi Japanese Restaurant prides itself as one of the most authentic Japanese restaurant in Singapore. Speaking to the manager he mentioned to me how the cuisine only uses the best quality and freshest ingredients, of course imported from Japan. I don't know whether it was the way he described the ingredients, but when the food came, the taste of authenticity and freshness were definitely there. It was delicious. The atmosphere was quiet and relaxed, it's a great place to be silent and enjoy a good meal.It is one of the older establishments situated at Dempsey. The parking obviously is great, and the atmosphere somewhat like Robertson quay, is very much so westernised.There is a wide selection to choose from, it may be a little pricey, but definitely worth it.

Located at a quiet corner of Dempsey hill, Rakuichi is a good place to sit outdoors with plenty of sake and yakitori. And there are smoking tables available! Inside, you have a choice of seating at the sushi bar counter or on traditional Japanese dining rooms (the type where you sit on the floor) or normal tables, depending on the mood of the group you're with. The set dinners are reasonably priced and look really delicious though  have not had the chance to try their lunch or dinner sets yet. Price wise, it is slightly on the high side at around $40 -$60 per person. OCBC credit card owners get to enjoy 10% off, so make sure you make full use of it!

I first came across the outlet at Far East, which was tucked away and imposible to find unless you know it's there! Since then I have become a fan (especially of their sushi) and one day decided to try their outlet at Dempsey.Well,... let's just say that I still prefer the outlet at Far East.

Now - I'm not a big fan of Japanese food (yeah I know, how is that possible). But I've been to quite a few Jap restaurants thanks to friends who are more than enthusiastic about Jap food. Rakuichi is a pleasant restaurant. Decor-wise, it doesn't differ very much from the typical Jap restaurant. The food's good though. The aburi sushi scores with its good looks - distinct morsels of yummy-looking sushi. Every piece was tasty, right down to the humble tamago. Only minor gripe is that the chefs were a little too heavy handed with the unagi sauce.   The sashimi was fresh. I liked the wasabi. The grilled beef and beef tongue skewers were surprisingly tasty. Assorted sushi we ordered were all about there. Deserts and desert selection were nothing to shout about though.I didn't pay for dinner (thanks LF!) so not too sure about prices. From what I remembered of the menu, prices were pretty decent. Staff were polite.Guys - if you are inclined towards washing your hands after using the toilet (I know many of you don't), be gentle on the soap dispenser.  A press and soap spurted all over my right sleeve, which took quite a bit of dabbing with paper towels to partially remove. On the plus side, I did exit the toilet smelling fresher than when I entered...
Authentic Japanese restaurant.  Very friendly wait staff.  Wide menu selection.  Sushi bar. Reasonable tariff.

Went there on a Saturday morning around 11am in an obvious attempt to avoid the crowd. Evidently, pretty much everyone else had the same bright idea. Victor's Kitchen opens at 1030am, and by the time we got there, it was packed to the brim with couples and families.Food: The glutinous rice with chicken and sausage was excellent. And this is coming from someone who's not a big fan of carbs. Really liked the zhar leung (i.e. fried doughstick in rice roll), was pretty much the closest we've had to Hong Kong fare. The har gau and siew mai were so-so, not exceptional. The carrot cake with XO sauce was unusual but not exceptional, and the custard buns were just so-so. The mango pomelo sago's pretty good. The iced milk tea though, was absolutely kickass. Victor's Kitchen is the ONLY place which serves iced milk tea identical to the famous stocking iced milk tea in Hong Kong's Fa Yuen Street.Ambience: For a relatively ghetto hole in the wall dim sum joint, it's acceptable. Service: Pretty decent, they try to do their best given the crowds. And I love being surrounded by authentic Cantonese speaking wait staff. This is the real deal.They close around 10pm so it's a decent place for a bite after work if one gets off late.

We stopped by here just as it was closing and begged the staff to let us da bao some custard buns. They did, and it was awesome. Best custard buns in town. Exploding with buttery sweet hot lava. Enjoy with caution!

The siew mai was tasty, as were the har gau. The golden egg yolk lava buns (liu sha bao) were alright, but a bit too oily. Wouldn't eat them again.Service was terrible, though, almost like they felt they were too good for us. Ordering was an ordeal and food arrived slowly.

A great find and so reminiscent of Hong Kong's cha chan tang. You can find the first location at Sunshine Plaza to be full always. At least now there is no long queue waiting for seats! Prepared fresh daily, they have my favourite milk tea, rice rolls and steamed milk! Now I need not have to take a flight to satisfy my dimsum pangsI've tried almost all they have on their menu. Everything is good. Must haves: siew mai, har kow, cheong fun, steamed pork ribs, yam cake and the salted egg custard buns.

What an interesting place to eat at.  It is located at the Sunshine City Plaza.  The owners are very friendly and speak mainly Cantonese but we were able to get by with Mandarin haha.  We tried the siu mai, xiao long bao, golden egg yolk lava bun, and golden crispy yam bun.  Everything was so good and fresh!

Hmm. Good if you are in the area and just don't to wait on a line. Personally I'd rather go to swee choon for dirty or Tim ho for clean. I don't think this place is much cheaper than a better dim sum place.
Dirty, delicious dim sum. Go ahead and wait in line. It goes fast because no one wants to loiter there.

I love this place for the food. I hate the queue and I hate the fact that they are squeezing people in to max capacity. This happened in particular the last time I was there. The tables and chairs are already on the small side (for someone bigger in size than your average Asian girl). Long tables which can generally sit to a squeeze of 8, they decide to fit 10. Not very impress with this. However, food wise, yes, they serve a delicious salted egg lava bun, great chicken feet, Cheung fun too. Coffee, tea, coffee tea mix all good (drinks abit on the pricy side). So go early, go for the experience of you have not been to those tiny places in Hong Kong, good food, but be prepared to be pushed, asked to move, asked to sit a bit off, loads of excuse me (if you are lucky, otherwise just be prepared to have an uncomfortable sitting experience while enjoying good food).

Thanks to my colleagues, I was introduced to this dim sum place. You work around City Hall area and the chance of enjoying authentic dim sum that's affordable yet awesome is not something that's easily achieved.Thus I was extremely happy to walk in to this tiny shop, squeeze into some tight spaced tables to enjoy some really delicious dim sum, sharing my table with other strangers who equally enjoy their meal.If you have heard stories about scary aunty, they are true. But they are ok, just smile and remind yourself that nothing can be worse than having to work in a tiny shop like this one for long hours in a hot kitchen. Anyway, scary aunty aside, the food is superb! Love the carrot cake (XO SAUCE, yo!), love the liu sha bao, love the pork rib rice, love the glutinous rice (wrapped in leaf), love the prawn dumpling, love the fried beancurd skin...i Love everything...I cant wait to go back again!!

To do: find real authentic dim sum Status: checked. Yes, din tai fung doesn't disappoint. But as I develop taste for Asian food, living in Singapore I get greedy and crave for something beyond. So while on the look out for good dim sum that hasn't been all fancied-up by us expats, came across quite a few posts on this place. Then our office move happened and found myself working only ~10 minutes walk away from here. So it finally happened. Food was great. My Chinese friend approved its authenticity and way above-par taste (and even over-ate -- this is someone who DOES NOT over-eat.) * Egg tarts (4/5) were really good. Very fluffy & light with crisp crust on the outside. *Siew Mai's (3/5) were okay. I definitely had better ones before. Didn't particularly find them flavorful. * Har gao (4/5) -- yes! The shrimp meats were thick & tangy. Enough said. * Spinach & Prawn dumplings(3.5/5) also had good shrimp meat inside & had stickiness and juice that went well together. But would've liked it better if there was a bit less skin of the dumpling. * Chee-chong fun with Charsiew (3.5/5) was decent as well. Now that I think about it, perhaps I don't like the dumpling skin-like things too much in general. * Carrot cake, I can't say much about because I am not a fan to begin with. So will refrain from commenting. * Spicy sauce chicken claws (a.k.a. chicken feet) (4.5/5) was a wow! I've heard many things about how it has lots of collagen and all & tried several times, but one bite was enough for each of those. But this time, it was different. The sauce was just the right spiciness with really delicious flavor. Best chicken feet I've had so far. I will definitely order this again. * Steamed spare ribs with black bean sauce (4.5/5) was another win. Well-steamed to the right level of tanginess, just the right amount of flavor that brings out the taste of the rib, while not being bland. Loved it. * Golden "Bo Lo" Char Siew Butter Buns (4/5) were very tasty. Crips on the outside, filled with rich char siew fillings on the inside. But to me, it was a bit too saucy. Still good, but a bit more meat and less sauce would've hit the golden balance. * Double-boiled egg white with fresh milk and almond juice (2.5/5) was okay. Too much almond taste for a double-boiled egg. * Golden Egg Yolk Lava Buns (3.5/5) -- supposedly the most popular dish here -- didn't impress me too much. Expected the inside to be a bit more rich gooey liquid fullness but didn't really happen. The mixture didn't seem to be very well mixed. Still decent.  I will be trying Charsiew Baos and some porridge the next time I go. Service is not bad, but the food doesn't come out too fast either. (Having heard of the long queue, I went pretty early-- a bit before noon -- but the food still came out rather slow and came in a staggered manner, not in any particular oder. Perhaps my personal preference but I like my dimsums to just come all at once for me to gawk at the variety and steaminess all together.) But let's just think that that's how fresh the dimsums are? as they are made to order? The ambiance is not somewhere you'd just walk by and be invited to go in. But I think it's part of the authentic experience. So I loved it and would definitely be bringing my friends here.

First time here. The food was alright. Prawn dumpling was good. We had to wait really long  porridge and the staff told us that they only had 2 people working in the kitchen. So prepare yourself to wait.

I don't really understand all the praise and rave about this place. it's not bad, and actually, the food is just as you'd expect it to be considering the style of the eatery - just that my expectations were raised what with so many people citing this as some sort of powerhouse. but at least it didn't cost too much, eh?I think this might possibly be what's known as proper hong kong style - with a spartan piece of white paper to mark your orders from. drinks come in old school pyrex and glass dishes, and the dimsum arrive in weathered bamboo steams - all of which elicit a sort of rusticity amidst the old-school decor.queues start ridiculously early and long - so that when the doors opened, all the tables were occupied. how much madness is that?!but anyway, it's all as it looks: coffee-shop style dimsum, and pretty far removed from any refined sensibilities. I expect you're really expecting some sort of verdict on the famed liushabaos (those salted egg yolk custard lava buns) and those were pretty disappointing. it was very oily, with much of the fat having separated from the paste, and it didn't really ooze (not even with a less-than-gently squeeze). flavor-wise, I think it could have done with a bit more salt.the menu is small, but it's cheap, and it's rather like those eateries you get in old-town malaysia or hong kong. I'm not sure a revisit is in my future - I'd rather spend a bit more and get better quality - but it's a decent option in the future, though definitely un-rave-worthy.

I have heard some reviews online about this stall so decided to try it out for myself, since i am such a dim sum fanatic. When i arrived it was just as people commented 'small, tiny place'. Did wait awhile to find a seat and had to call the waitress a few times to get the order chit. Aside from these, the food was not bad. I decided to try the summer milk tea which sounded yummy, indeed it was. However i thought that it was quite expensive $3 for a cup of tea, it was akin to buying a cup of Koi bubble tea with pearls. Next we tried the highly acclaimed items such as the siew mai, custard bun, king prawn dumpling and hong kong style pan fried chee chiong fun (rice roll). The siew mai was really good with actual crab roe on top of it and it was flavourful, juicy and succulent. The custard bun was really smooth and creamy and went well with the texture of the fluffy bun.The dumpling was a giveaway as for that price, the amount of filling given was really worth it. The succulent skin was so thin yet maintained a bouncy and chewy feel and alot of filling was wrapped into that skin, it was as if it was going to burst anytime. Next came the hong kong style chee chiong fun and it was interesting i must say. Have never tried anything like it, crispy on the outside but soft and chewy on the inside, yummy. The service there however was not really good, they seemed to favour westerners more than us. Overall a good experience with some misses.

I must admit, having heard and read about the dim sum at Victor's Kitchen, I arrived with a level of expectation that they didn't quite match.
