The selling point at Victor's might be its authenticity in its owners  - they sound like they hail from Hong Kong - and their drinks - the closest you'll get to HK milk tea. Prices are decent but I thought the food was just okay.We had the usual fare: har gau, siew mai, shrimp chang fen, beancurd skin with pork stuffing, steamed carrot cake and custard buns. Nothing to shout about, I've had far better dim sum. They forgot our order of the you tiao chang fen or there was some mix-up. It was so busy and chaotic that we didn't bother to ask them.The real highlights of the meal were the drinks. Iced milk tea - hot tea served in a plastic cup in a bowl of ice cubes so the tea isn't diluted when the ice melts. Pretty novel idea and the tea is close to what you get at cha chan ting's in HK. We saw the auntie pounding the lemon slices too when she made the iced lemon tea, one of the better homemade versions I've tried.Come for the experience, if you're looking for a piece of Hong Kong in Singapore.

I've heard a lot of people raving about this place and how authentic it's dim sum is so I went there with really high expectations. I would say it's ok but I honestly did not find it too special and the price is not that cheap if you consider how crammed the place is and the general comfort level.  So people told me their egg yolk bun (liu sha bao) is the signature dish but I think you find similar quality ones in any of the imperial treasures or crystal jade dim sum restaurants.  I also don't think some of the items are that fresh, pretty sure it's not freshly made at the site because it's a bit too hard (esp. the char siu puff pastry).  One thing I like is their HK style milk tea which is quite authentic.  As a person with over 30 years of dim sum eating experience, I would say this is definitely not the most authentic dim sum in Singapore, there are better places at reasonable prices.  It's also not a place where you can hang out and chit chat with your friend over tea, which is what the whole yum cha experience should be about.

I first came here after hearing people RAVE about a authentic, bona-fide Hong Kong chef. It was ALL TRUE.Walking in, you hear all the right sounds. Loud Cantonese from the kitchen. A grumpy auntie who ignores you until you wave in her face, then tells you to wait for a seat. A smiley auntie who clears your table, and cajoles a smile out of you as she complains about the grumpy auntie. And of course you see the rest of the crowd who's there to eat. And you know you can't go wrong. The food did not disappoint either. The steamed carrot cake was pleasantly surprising - bits of scallops and waxed sausage (lup cheong) mixed in an almost coarse pudding - and the XO sauce adds a little extra zing.The rest of the food passes by in a haze, and we harry the auntie for more, but you'll remember to order the Zhar Leong (cheong fun with you tiao), and have some ice summer milk tea - they cool the drink by placing the cup in a bowl of ice, so it gets cooled without being diluted. Old School much.And of course, you'll finish your meal with some Golden Egg Yolk Lava Buns. Everyone does, as long as they still have some in stock. You might call it Liu Sha Bao, but here at Victor's, everything's got a cooler name.A couple of months ago, we heard about a change in the family situation, and the food quality may have changed, but subsequent visits don't show noticeable differences. Give it a go, it don't cost much any way.

In a small and cramped shop space, Victor's Kitchen serves authentic Hong Kong dim sum that is cheap and good. It is a really narrow shop though, so be prepared to sit a little too close for comfort next to a stranger from the next table. To order, you tick your selected dishes on an order slip and hand in to a waitress. The waitresses, however, are extremely slow at attending to customers. It usually takes ages just to get their attention. Alas, they do serve a few recommendable dishes, the best being Golden Egg Yolk Lava Bun aka custard pau. The custard paus are unbeatable; I have not tasted any better. The piping hot custard filling oozes out the moment you break open the skin. The sweetness of the custard and the saltiness of the preserved egg yolk make a perfect marriage. Another good dish is the Siew Mai - a dim sum classic. Their version was tasty, had a strong porky taste and had a great texture to it.

Who said brunch had to be western? The Chinese have been getting up at noon and peeling wax paper off char siew buns for ages, and if you're sick of heavy and extravagant Western fare, but need a heart-warming Chinese entreé to start your day that won't hurt your wallet, you're at the right place.Start off by getting a basket of Victor's signature Golden Egg Yolk Lava Bun ($3.50 for 3), and be careful when you split it the middle to let steam out, because the glorious golden filling might just ooze out (and make a mess!). When it's cool enough to eat, savour the sweet-salty and gooey salted egg yolk-based custard. While we're still talking buns, a basket of Milky Custard Buns ($3.50 for 3) is sure to delight both pau & dessert fans with its decadently smooth custard interior and melt-in-your-mouth silky skin.And what's Yum Cha without har gow ($3.50 for 4)? Bite into one of these steamed prawn dumplings and be surprised by the crunch - wrapped in a crystalline, semi-see-through skin are three whole shrimps and delicious pork filling. Another dumpling that is a must-have is their Tasty Queen Size Siew Mai ($3.50 for 4). Larger than your average siew mai, these bundles of joy are sure to put a smile on your face with delight, though they might be too overpowering with umami and a little bit too salty.Order a cup of Hong Kong Summer Ice Tea ($2.00) to accompany the baskets of buns and dumplings, and be impressed by their genius - the tea is served in a cup that is placed in a bowl of ice, so you don't have to worry about your tea getting too mellow with dilution

Sunday afternoons are for family brunches, and dimsum was our food of choice today. Headed down to Victor's Kitchen for their liu sha bao since I was nursing a serious craving for them. Well, everyone else had the same brunch idea so even though we came down at 2+pm, it was packed and the queue was long. We queued for about 15 minutes before it was our turn. Note of caution: No one is going to serve you at the front of the restaurant, so head on straight to an empty table when you sight one. The place was completely packed, and at Victor's, that means Hong Kong-style claustrophobia. Be prepared to wriggle your way in and out of the restaurant (if you can call it that) because of the ultra dense seating arrangement. After a rather unpleasantly long wait for the food, cheong fun was served. It was one of the highlights of the meal. Another winner was the steamed carrot cake that was served pudding style. I enjoyed it, but I wish it came with more sauce. Some other dishes that came were disappointing. The siew mai tasted stale, and the ha gao was over steamed. The steam pork ribs and fried toufu skin with prawns were unmemorable. Fortunately, the liu sha bao was decent and satisfied my craving. Best eaten the moment it reaches your table, this bun is filled with a sugary and salty custard that flows out the moment you sink your teeth into it. The Hong Kong iced milk tea is good too.Not the best place for dim sum, but if you want a true Hong Kong-style dim sum dining experience, head here.

Ok 3.5 stars for this place may be a little misleading. I think it should be somewhere between 4 to 4.5 stars.  I would have expected the place to be mostly empty on a Monday night but it was surprisingly busy.Before going in, I was able to peruse the menu and they had a section of items going for up to 50% off.  Wow!  They had me at 50.  They had two maki rolls one at $7.80 and the other at $9.20 Singapore dollars.So why not?  I went in was seated at the sushi bar and I ordered the Roasted Salmon with Tenkasu Roll and the Sakura Shrimp with Sweet Shrimp Roll.  Let's be honest here.  I am not a roll fan cuz you can get some really weird combinations so I was taking a risk here.About 5 minutes later, my rolls were delivered to me and they looked delicious.  I tried the shrimp roll first and yummm was all I could think of.  I then worked on the salmon roll and bingo yummm yummm.  Once done and my bill came to $23 (coke and various taxes and charges).  Quite a steal and I will be back to try other dishes.As to the four stars I give five to the food. Service lacked a little but otherwise a great experience.

Being close to work and home, this place was one of my go-tos after a long hard day. This branch just reopened in January 2017 after a renovation. I usually order from the "Chef Recommendation" menu where you get better value for your money (they claim up to 50-60% off), and usually I don't spend more than S$20 on a filling meal here. This menu sells out FAST though, and usually the good ones are all gone by the time I arrive around 7:30pm on a weekend. Sometimes I think this is just some bait to get you in so you'll spend on their other dishes. Still, I like how the menu has plenty of variety and there are some interesting sashimi/sushi dishes that I don't commonly see elsewhere. Sometimes I'll pop by just to see what specials they have on the menu. I also really like the chawanmushi here (plain, without crab meat) ^^ smooth and straightforward with a few ingredients sprinkled about.

There is always a long queue so try to come early. I had udon with seafood tempura. The fried food was fresh and crispy. The udon was al dente. The lunch options allowed a 20% discount for chawanmushi with crab meat so I tried it and was satisfied with the taste. My friends had sushi and really enjoyed their food. Unfortunately, one friend ordered ramen which was unbearably salty and she had to change it. If you download the app to make an order above $20, each person gets a free scoop of green tea ice cream! Overall quality is good but staff is very short handed.

Itacho sushi is always be my fav sushi resto in singapore, i dont really go to mainstream of sushi tei... I love itacho more...Love the mango salad sushi, and for those 3 fav sushi that always sold out I feel that itacho sushi in orchard is the best but since i lived in west, this resto in star vista become my regularly visit itacho sushi in singapore

Either I suffer from rosy retrospection or this chain has seriously dropped in quality.When I visited the branch in Ion Orchard more than 2 years ago, I recalled fresh fish and well seasoned rice that, while not comparable to Japan, was close enough to stop me wanting to buy tickets to Tokyo.Alas, it was not to be. We ordered freely and were not impressed by any of the sushi or rolls, and ended up spending just under $50 per person. At this price point, we should have gone to Ikeikemaru.
Came here for dinner with some friends. The food was pretty good... until both my boyfriend and I came down with rashes a couple of hours later :(Will not be returning again!

I always feel like people have the perception that it is cheap, but in actual fact, it is not cheap at all!!! I was horrified when I ordered an avocado soft shell crab (2 pieces) for $5.80!! I could have 6 pieces for $6 at Sushi Tei! Beat that!! 2 pieces of Mango sushi at $4.80. Again? What is this ordering by per piece and making me keep re-ordering in order to be full? It always draws a queue whenever I am looking for a place to dine in, which puzzles me even more. Food wise, it is just decent. Not outstanding.

I wasn't impressed by this place and probably would have given it three stars based on my charitable American yelp rating scale, but I refuse to have my review of a place that left a bad taste in my mouth actually raise it's average score. I definitely expected more though after seeing the enormous queues when the place opened. The sushi was small even for Singapore and the maguro was unusually dark and hard. Do people like this place because it doesn't feel Japanese? I don't get it.

I think the reviews for this place is unrightfully harsh. When it comes to quality. I admit that the quality of the fish fluctuates pretty wildly, but usually it is pretty decent. I've always enjoyed the salmon belly aburi sushi, and at 1.70 a pop, it doesn't get better than that! Obviously, the itacho in hongkong (where itacho originates from) is wayyy better, but I think that the sushi here is not terrible. A very convenient place to eat at if you are craving that sushi and likes variety in sushi, because they sell a whole array of raw, seared, cooked sushi and have many small seasonal dishes to keep it interesting.

Good food, slow service on account of crowd. We had to wait 15 minutes in line despite arriving at noon. The sushi counter chef was friendly and gave good suggestions for the freshest seafood. Counter seating cramped and servers often handed hot items over shoulders from behind. I had the hokkaido-don which is a version of chirashisushi. The tuna was really fresh and the vinegared rice perfect.

All I've known of Itacho Sushi until I tried it yesterday was that it had an outlet at Ion with perpetually long queues (an immediate turn off for me because it means a) there's some price gimmic b) the food is good but table management is antiquated c) it's a die die must try place and I need to muster the energy, patience and hunger to go stand in line...none of which are enjoyable dining experiences to look forward to). On new year's day at 9pm, I thought maybe it would be a great idea to grab some sushi at Star Vista since it was nearby. There wasn't a queue and we got seated pretty quickly. A quick glance through the menu explained why this chain is probably popular - they have one or two items that are priced ridiculously cheap and there are "20-50%" offers on a product of the month. Other than that the sushi is actually pretty expensive. To put this in context, I'm the sort of person who likes eating good food that's of good value if I'm paying for it and unconcerned about the price if someone else is picking up the tab (usually for work). I therefore abhor chains like xyz-sushi/sushi-xyz that serve crap on conveyor belts and I used to frequent Sakuraya Fish Market pretty often until they started letting standards slide. Gimmicky promotions therefore don't really appeal to me and I'm looking for innovative or really fresh, well executed sushi and a filling meal for two at around $40 at a suburban location. Here's what I got...We ordered 6 pieces of the spicy lobster sushi, a tuna and chives "roll", an avocado and soft shell crab "roll", a "crab" meat salad, pumpkin tempura and a grilled mackerel. The "crab" meat salad came first and it was really a pile of un-chopped lettuce, a dollop of avocado mayo (with an emphasis on the latter) and surimi sticks. Guess I should have known eh. Next we got the sushi. The spicy lobster sushi was about $1.20 a piece and it wasn't substantial to say the least. Granted, the rice was suitably vinegared and mixed with black sesame seeds and roe, which scored innovation points, and the lobster was slathered in sauce as described... but the sushi was small. The tuna and chive roll was more balanced and didn't assault the tongue like our first sushi, but the roll consisted of 4 pieces? The last roll took the cake at 2 pieces. I thought the fish was decently fresh but not mind blowingly fresh-off-the-boat fresh like you would get with port-side sashimi joints in Japan.The pumpkin tempura was fine but again, portions were small. The grilled mackerel, a cheap and common grill dish at restaurants, was decently sized here but almost $4-5 more than what I'd pay at Sakuraya. Total bill was $60 and boy did we have to spend that amount at this supposedly cheap joint to feel full. Small point to note too is that they close at 10pm and have a strange last order policy at 9.20pm. Would I go to Itacho Sushi again? Probably not. Would I line up for "cheap" sushi that's limited to two pieces per customer? Err right I'm sure Oliver Twist dining went out of fashion before the stone age. Was the sushi life changing? Heck no but I'm guessing it's a step up if you're the kind who likes to eat at chain restaurants and thinks that eating food by the piece is somehow more economical.
Bad, slow service. Manage to forget some orders and had the audacity to accuse us of not ordering. What little sashimi that came tasted stale. Will never return!!!

They have good sushi and they have cheap sushi, but they don't have good, cheap sushi. My wife and I have deeply divided opinions about this place. She loves it, but I've been disappointed every time. I think it comes down to our different expectations for a sushi restaurant. I like the simple, basic things:  hamachi, toro, unagi; while she wants the "top shelf" experience:  salmon belly, aji, uni. Hamachi is my yardstick for a good sushi place and theirs is TERRIBLE. I've tried it on two separate occasions. But I agree that the salmon belly is quite good.

Great variety of fusion foodBeef rice - 5/5 quality of meat is great and sauce tastes goodSoy sweet potato fries- 4/5: sauce a little too sweet for meChicken rice risotto 4/5 - The combination is divine... but sadly, I personally can't take a lot of diary/creamy food, so I wouldn't order an entire dish for myself.Lemongrass chamomile 1/5 - very sweet.. reminds me of Apple tea, I was expecting something a little lighter and less sweet from the name

Hipster cafe, great for Instagram-ready fusion--style brunches, as well as cosy date nights. I went there on a Saturday night after 8pm and there was plenty of seats. You order at the main counter, serve yourself water and cutlery, and they bring your food to you. We had the mentaiko salmon pasta, the salmon pho and the salted egg mochi w ice cream. For the price, portions of the mains aren't particularly large, but maybe the restaurant's strategy is to leave room for dessert! The mentaiko salmon pasta was done perfectly. Al dente pasta, al dente salmon and creamy mentaiko. Mmm mmm mmm! The salmon pho, is a completely different dish. The broth and noodles are delicate, but the salmon was a tad overdone. Otherwise, it's a really nice dish. The salted egg mochi was ah-mazing! I dont know if any other restaurants do it, but it's definitley a heart stopper. They also give 3 mochis, so be prepared to fight if sharing between an even number of people!

Simple yet satisfying menu. The highlight for most will be the mochi balls with surprise runny filling inside, however, the savory items are worth a try too! The opening hours on a Saturday was surprisingly late at noon, but I'm glad my sister and I waited for its opening. There was no wait and we got promptly seated. The menu consists of 5 major components - risotto (rice), pasta, waffles, dessert and drinks. You pick your favorite and then head on over to order at the counter. We tried the mentaiko prawn pasta, that comes with a free drink. The mentaiko flavor was hit the right spot, the pasta was cooked al dente and the prawns were bouncy and chewy. The lemongrass chamomile tea I chose to go along was strong and intense with lemongrass, so might not be suitable for folks who are sensitive to its taste. The truffle fries was not anything special - freezer fries, thinly cut. The truffle smell is good but did not have much truffle flavor, as in many other restaurants. The highlight of the meal is the dessert! We got the salted egg yolk mochi balls and cookie butter ice cream. The delicious cornflakes gave amazing texture to the smooth ice cream. I would say the salted egg yolk could be saltier and the cookie butter ice cream was sweet enough without honey. I enjoyed the mentaiko pasta but it's quite small a portion, good for customers with small appetite. My favorite was the mochi salted egg yolk balls and I would be back to have more! My sister and I really enjoyed the industrial design and benches in the restaurant. Cozy and rustic. I would say the two person seat near the door was a little stuffy so try to sit closer to the inner restaurant.

A cafe located along Bali Lane, with 2 levels for dining in. The place is dim in lighting and popular with the younger generation. It is known for its thick toast and waffle.Classic Honey Toast ($12.90)butter & honey baked pain de mie, honey yogurt ice-cream, berriesThe thick toast is served thick and crispy. Just nice with the honey and ice-cream. The sour taste of the berries is balanced by the sweet honey and ice cream. Overall not bad except for the raspberry which tastes frozen.Blackcurrent Lemonade ($4.90)It looks quite cloudy when served. When fully mixed, I could not taste the lemonade in the drink. It tastes more like a soda drink. None of the grape flavour too.Overall not bad. The place is a bit dim in lighting, so difficult to take photos even when sitting by the window.

Cool ambiance, ok-only food. We stumbled upon Stateland while trying to find the famous Bugis Village. Stateland Cafe presents  a cool, inviting and hipster interior. The pictures of desserts on their menu looked pretty promising so we stepped in to try it out. Unfortunately, the pictures looked much better than the way the food tasted. We ordered a watermelon shaved ice dessert and an earl grey donuts with soft serve. The earl grey donuts had a very fragile and light taste to it, and the soft serve also had a light creamy taste that vaguely reminded me of Momofuku milk bar in NYC. The watermelon shaved ice dessert looked smaller in reality compared to its glorious pictures on the menu. But, there was more flavor in it, and tasted like a frozen watermelon smoothie. Stateland Cafe's got the cool vibe. All it has to do is give a little more punch in its food and it'll provide a much better experience.

The mentaiko (?) prawn aglio olio pasta was so nice!!! Perfect sized, not too heavy and not too small. It's also a lil' spicy which is a plus for me. At the moment Brother Bird is also housed in the restaurant,  which is great because it means I barely have to move for soft serve. The lemonade drink wasn't perfect though. Definitely needs to be more tart, sour and lemony!!!

We went to Stateland Cafe yesterday after reading Ladyironchef's post about the best waffles in Singapore. Stateland's ambience is pretty similar to most of the small "hipster" cafes in Singapore - dim lighting, uncovered ceilings, eclectic decorations that seemed to be randomly put together to give a rustic, simple vibe. The menu was more interesting. There were not many things on the menu, but the choices sounded delicious. I was intrigued by the unique waffle flavours and opted for the Red Velvet Waffle. My partner took the Bacon and Eggs Waffle.The Red Velvet Waffle looked impressive, with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and raspberries set atop drizzles of cream cheese frosting and dark chocolate sauce on a red waffle base. The first few bites were confusing. I couldn't recognise the taste at all. The waffle had a yeasty, metallic taste that had me doubting my choice. A few more bites into it helped to ease my concerns as the familiar bitter and savoury taste took over. It helped to combine all components in one bite to fully savour the waffle. It was good, but I would try other things on the menu next time.I prefer the Bacon and Eggs Waffle. It had a good, earthy taste that kept me wanting more. The scrambled eggs were fluffy and the onion cream sauce, infused with the smoky bacon aroma, added another dimension to the flavour. Two thumbs up.The prices were a little on the high side, though I wouldn't call them expensive. At $14.90 for a waffle dish, it's higher than most other waffle places, but the flavours are definitely unique.

Given what I went through to get Sunday brunch in Kampong Glam, Stateland deserves 5 stars.Initially, hubby and I went to Maison Ikkoku, but they were already fully booked by 10 AM. Trusty Yelp app pointed us to Working Title, where apparently the chef was running late which meant the sole person running the F&B portion was unable to cook breakfast.Almost ready to quit and just eat something at Bugis, I decided to give it one more try and check out Stateland.Available seating? Yes.Fully functional cafe with chefs eager to cook breakfast-y items at 10:15 AM on Sunday? Yes.Pitchers of water available for water guzzlers like my hubby so the waitstaff won't be bothered? Yes.Migs ordered the French Toast, which was covered in a berry compote of sorts. Looks too sweet in the picture, but trust me, it was perfect. I decided last minute to go the savoury route and had the waffle with the bacon and onion cream sauce. It sounds really weird and looks crazy but it actually turned out being wonderful. The waffle was firm enough to hold the sauce, but not burnt or overcooked. The bacon and cream sauce was balanced out perfectly with the sweet sauteed onions. Throw in some decent cappuccinos and brunch near Arab St was saved. Stateland, if you keep this service up, I'll love you long time.

Kampong Glam has always been a hot hit with people going there to shop, eat or just walk around. Cafes here are quite common as well in the area, such as La Marelle, CAD Cafe, and even the recently opened Elffin & Elffin. Stateland Cafe has become the newest addition to this area. Also operating a online macaroons business called Flag & Sac, this place serves all-day breakfasts, pastas and desserts.The menu here is rather simple, and reasonably priced.The coffees here are made using the Terra Firma blends from Papa Palheta. The Macchiato ($3.90) provides a single shot of espresso, which has a slightly acidic and bitter taste.The Latte ($4.70) tasted strong and firm with the right amount of milk added.The Belgium Waffles ($10.90) comes with a chocolate ice cream, fresh fruits and Stateland's waffle sauce. This is possibly one of the best waffles coming from a cafe. Crusty on the outside, soft and moist on the inside, this goes well especially with the chocolate ice cream.This place is a great place to come to for their coffee and food after some shopping within the area, so if you are around the Kampong Glam area, this should not be missed!

I've had a pretty tough, long week and by last night, was dying for some good alcohol (in moderation) and food. Given that I've tried most of the bars in the CBD (don't judge) and was sick of seeing the CBD, I thought the man and I should head down to Orchard and try Tanuki Raw. Orchard Rd has always been a conundrum for me bar-wise. There are so few good bars that you're often stuck with the same ones: No.5/Ice Cold for martini's/beer happy hour and the best har cheong gai, KPO if one wants to fraternize with traders or creative types working in the area, martini's at Hyatt,  maybe Cuscaden patio of you're really short on cash. So when I heard about Tanuki Raw, it sounded like a great addition to the Orchard bar scene - fresh, Japanese-inspired seafood and strong drinks at affordable prices. Tanuki is a little difficult to find if you're coming in from the side escalator, so I recommend you do it sober (oh come on now you know this is good advice). The bar itself is industrial chic with an outdoor area overlooking Orchard Rd and borders more on a restobar than a bar per se. The Tony Collins I ordered (which is broadly speaking like an old school one-up on the G&T) was very good. It was almost perfectly balanced so that I could taste a fine lemonade and the gin without one overpowering the other. That's quite a feat considering there's a gentleman's pour in there (that's +1pt in my book of awesome bartenders who know what some women really want). I'd say definitely give the cocktail list a shot (pun not intended) because they've really put some thought and care into it.Food-wise, I wanted to be blown away but wasn't. As drinkers and not restaurant patrons, you're looking for 1-2 dishes to go with your drinks and therefore the food has to excel out the door. We had the Ocean Rockefeller, Tori Karaage and the free Truffle Fries that came with a Yelp check-in. The Ocean Rockerfeller didn't quite work for me because it was neither punchy, sizzling or juicy.The dish was really salmon, scallops and jellyfish lightly seasoned and topped with grated cheese that looked like it came out a bag and torched just enough for the cheese to lump together but not melt. I mean guys, we're talking about a dish named after Rockerfeller, so one is hoping for intense flavors and at the least, good cheese. Even from an aburi sushi angle, I couldn't see the merit. As for the chicken karaage I have two words: 5 Izakaya. Bottom line, definitely drink. But maybe stick to the oysters that literally every table was offering or indulge in the simple raw dishes like sashimi. I do think the bar bites need some work because in today's bar scene, even the humble fried protein done well can lure many, many regulars for life.

Popped in for a late lunch, and was immediately in love with the space... sit outside folks, the weather's lovely! Okay, more that the balcony is lovely, since it's just above the ever-bustling Orchard Road, but just high enough to feel that you're away from the maddening crowd.An easy pick were the rice bowls - lots of variety here. Oyster mentako (yes, they're an oyster bar, you know), steak tartare, the Godfather(?!), and a Salmon bowl with sashimi, belly, aburi AND ikura(!!!): too many to choose from! I was in the mood for some Yakitori, and being greedy, we were recommended some Trio Carpaccio to share. Salmon, tuna and swordfish in different sauces? YUM. And this is coming from a new sashimi convert, so believe that this stuff is pretty solid.A check-in on Yelp revealed an offer for a free basket of truffle fries, and you know me, I can never turn down some fries, or something free... I need to come back for Happy Hour(s) [5-8pm daily], when they serve $1 oysters and cocktails at $11! Anyone with me?

Great happy hour deals on martinis, salmon sashimi and oysters. When we were there, the martinis were decent and the salmon fresh. However the swordfish sashimi we ordered was a little bit off as well as our second order of oysters. Could've just been an off day? I'd still go back, but would probably avoid the raw food to be safe! I think Alicia pan performs there on Mondays too.

love it for the ultra amazing value oysters happy hour! It was quite satisfying to see that we slurped up 60 oysters for $1 each in the check!Drinks are ok, standard cocktails. This is not the place to expect bespoke cocktails and note that you are also just paying $10 per drink during happy hours.Sad to note that the very appetizing cerviche trio in most of the yelp photos is no longer on the menu.Not a fan of this particular mall but the $1 oysters will be a good reminder to return.Note that in the evening, when the birds return home, you will need to outdo the hundreds of birds chirping if you choose to sit outdoors.

I've been visiting Tanuki a little too often; I am worrying for my cholesterol level since my two favorite items are the $1 oysters and the musubi sushi.The $1 oysters are so sweet and fresh that you barely need the vinegar or Tabasco sauce they provide. Best of all, it's consistent. I've had about two dozen oysters over multiple trips, and only chanced upon one stale tasting oyster. The waitstaff were quick to replace it with a fresh one when I pointed it out to them.The musubi sushi is so sinful but delicious. It's a little too salty (and I'm saying this even as a huge fan of luncheon meat), so it would be great if it had more rice, so the spam to rice ratio would balance the flavors out a little.Cocktails are cheap, delicious and especially strong. I once visited while nursing a hangover after a crazy night out and requested for less alcohol in my cocktail but it still tasted like a gentleman's pour, generous!The service is great, I was particularly impressed by our server who was especially attentive. He brought out an additional glass of water and menu within seconds of my friend arriving at the table, impressive! The manager of Tanuki also gave out free shots of a delicious candy flavored shot, called Alice in Wonderland.Outdoor sitting can get a little iffy because of the crazy amount of birds chirping in the trees next to the balcony and very strong fans positioned right next to tables.Am excited for my future visits, which will definitely be regular, I'm definitely gonna try the cheeseburger roll for my next visit. I hope the oyster happy hour (5 - 8pm) is gonna last beyond the soft launch months. Keeping my fingers crossed because it almost seems too good to be true! Pro-tip: Check in on Yelp or FourSquare to get free truffle fries!
It's a good place for drinks and bar food only. The Happy Hour $1 oyster is a superb deal. The oysters are fresh and big. Cocktails standard is pretty good too.

A friend who uses Tanuki as his Friday happy hour regular took me there one Friday recently. mylifeinsin.com/2013/11/…And a very happy Happy Hour it was! Of course it is with $10 martinis! I had Cosmos and Apple Martinis and friends went for standard vodka martinis and lychee martinis. We ordered some edamame, salmon sashimi and $2 oysters. Checking in on Foursquare earned me free salmon skin chips!I will be back :) Check out the full review with pictures on my blog! And then head there yourself, happy hour from 5 to 8 every night.

Wasn't expecting to love this place so much but I do! Great sushi rolls that aren't your conventional sushi-tei fare, coupled with $2 oysters and happy hour martinis: score! Try to grab a seat outside: you get a great view of orchard road and it's lovely when its breezy. Plus you get to see the live band

Tanuki Raw, founded by the people behind Standing Sushi Bar, has been gaining a loyal following thanks to its Happy Hour Treats (available from 5-8pm daily). Queues stretch once it hits 630pm and the working crowd is set free and many rush to enjoy the Martinis ($10), Salmon Sashimi ($3 for 5 slices, limited to 1 portion per drink) and Freshly-Shucked Oysters ($2 each, limited to half dozen per drink).The Salmon Sashimi was a gem, thickly-sliced and with a freshness that leaves us tempted to order more drinks just to get our hand at the sliced raw fish.Most patrons in the snaking queue during happy hour are waiting for this: Fine de Claire Oysters at $2 a pop. I don't usually eat oysters, but I gave these a try and were glad they did not have the fishy taste I detest about shellfish and was easy on the throat, especially with a dash of lemon juice.Drinks wise, I thought the Margarita was one of the worse I have had, so please don't order that. Other drinks like Sidecar and Mojito (all $11 during happy hour) were average, nothing to write home about.We also tried mains like the Salmon Mentaiko Don ($20) and Vegetable Don ($12), of which no photos were taken because the presentation was a disgrace. For $20, the salmon mentaiko don was also overpriced and I would just be sticking to the drinks and happy hour deals when I next return.For pictures and the full review visit voraciousappetite.wordpr…
3.5 stars. Popular Japanese fusion place. I had the chirashi-don. Food was Ok - you get a filling dish for ~30 with a  decent selection of fish. Truffle fries were excellent.

I have been reading Tanuki Raw somewhere and it kinds of remind me of Donburi with onsen egg. (Their marketing advertisement has been good to give me such good impression). We was looking at Minions Cafe in Orchard Central and it wasn't appealing to us and by chance we decided to dine in Tanuki Raw instead.Tanuki Raw is modernly furnished in an industrial interior tempered by eye-catching furniture.and has 80 seats spread across an outdoor balcony overlooking Orchard Road.It was fun sitting at the bar side observing how the tenders mix and prepare variety of drinks. As for our glasses of Water Melon Yuzu. Fresh watermelon juice were already prepared before hand and kept in the fridge. They just have to mix portion of it with yuzu and served them on the "rocks".Water Melon Yuzu - $10While Tanuki Raw is having a house promotion for happy hour daily from 5-8pm, we get to order Oysters at $2 each, limited to 6 pcs per glass of drink. The fresh raw oysters they served were brought in from Canada, France and Japan.Fresh Oysters - $2 EachBesides having that, we ordered a plate of 5 slices salmon that falls under the happy hour promotion too. It was great having Sashimi again with Wasabi and Soy Sauce!For bites, seeing Sweet Potato Fries excites me. These thick-cut sweet potato fries were deep fried with Tanuki Raw's spice mix, truffle oil and served with truffle aioli in an aluminium tin.Truffle Sweet Potato Fries - $10.90One of the recommended rolls on the Menu is none other than the Golden Kani Maki with deep fried house seasoned soft shell crab, fresh snow crab, cucumber and crispy mozzarella all in a roll. Divided into portion of 4, these delicious rolls were topped with toasted seaweed and drizzled with generous amount of golden salted duck egg hollandaise sauce.Golden Kani Maki - $18.90Well, we just did not have enough of salmon and here comes the seared salmon roll topped with Mentaiko sauce over some crispy mozzarella cheese, seasoned flakes and Tanuki's Oko Sauce! Yums!Superstar Roll - $12.90It was my first time there and would not be my last. Simply love the environment. Best of all, if you are having gathering with friends who are vegetarians, there are food for them too. Hope to be back soon.

I had a really good meal at Tanuki Raw. I came on the recommendation of a friend to get the truffle yakiniku. It didn't disappoint! The beef was well cooked and the egg was the perfect gooey texture. The truffle was just the right amount, not too overpowering but enough to taste it. I also loved the grapefruit tonic, since I'm addicted to anything grapefruit. The service was quite good in my opinion; I didn't have to wait long for anything, and I sat at the bar so I could easily refill my own glass of water with the bottle that was next to me. I'd definitely come back.

Apparently there is always a queue outside no matter what time of day. I had the foie gras yakiniku with onsen egg. Very fast to serve. I thought the rice was a tad soggy as I would have liked less gravy. The caramel matcha smoothie is very yummy.

Recently the casual Japanese restaurant has reopened at the shopping centre. It is now located at level 4, with a bigger dine in area. Similar to its previous location, it has both indoor and outdoor dine in area.As the restaurant was crowded, I decided to ask for outdoor dine in area, which was still has quite a number of tables as most felt that it was quite hot to dine outdoor. Compared to indoor, I felt outdoor was better as indoor was filled with cooking smell. Sitting in outdoor, one also can enjoy the great view of the busy Orchard Road.While looking through the menu, I was served iced water. A bit disappointed as the water was not refilled. Maybe sitting outdoor was not so good after all, as it was difficult to get the attention of the staffs.Although it was weekend, the restaurant offered lunch menu. Just add $2++ to the main dish to make it a lunch set. I decided to have a Premium Set by topping $5++. The set included miso soup, green salad, and coffee or "Back to work" beverage.Foie Gras Truffle Yakiniku ($19.90++)pan-seared foie gras, US black angus short rib, onsen egg, truffle soy, black garlic brown butter over Tanuki's signature mixed riceThe foie gras was quite buttery and melt in the mouth. The beef was quite tender and moist. The mixed rice was tasty on its own.Miso SoupThe soup was filled with chunky pieces of tofu and seaweed. The soup tasted light and flavourful.Green SaladThe salad was lightly tossed with ginger soyu dressing. Light and crunchy.Shio Smooth (a la carte $5++)fresh shiso, matcha green tea, lemon, blended with iceIt was my choice of "Back to work" beverage. It was light and refreshing in taste. Just the right to have during such a hot day.Overall the food was not bad. But the service needed to be improved as it was quite difficult to get the attraction of the staffs.

I think the food standard has dropped. The first time I was here was for an Yelp Elite Event and everything was of course amazingly good. Subsequently I had returned a few times and the food was still ok but my last visit last week was downright terrible.My favorite item was always the American Roll as I loved the beef with rice. However this was more chewy (due to the thick flour coating the roll) and carbs laden than before. More rice than meat. It was so bad I just removed the outer layer. No longer can I rave about this to my friends now. The Rockstar which my friend ordered was equally average to not so nice like before. Did the chef change? The only thing which had it going was its happy hour promotion of $2 oyster and $10 cocktail. Those were still decent though my friend said her drink was not as potent as before.

A Raw-Ing good time Another one of those places that have been opened a while but was skeptical of trying, primarily due to it looking like another upmarket restaurant that tries too hard to be different. While I still think that it's slightly on the pricy side, the food, I have to admit that it was a joy to have! Happy Hour oysters and Martini, shaken not stirred (sorry.. Just had to add that in)We were there before 8 pm (they do sell themselves as a bar so I suppose 8pm does makes sense for happy hour) and decided to give their oysters a try. At $2.00 an oyster with every alcoholic drink bought (at $10.00 for a martini, it worked out to $22.00 for 6 oysters, under $4.00 each), it wasn't too bad. As their name suggests, they do specialize in Raw dishes so the quality of the oysters were definitely there. Don't expect the super rich, high end $7-12 French oysters but still, decently sized and very fresh oysters. The Lychee Martini itself was pretty good too. Unlike most bars who taste like they're serving lychee syrup, you could taste the alcohol in the drink and it was nice that they gave 2 lychees instead of 1.(minor detail I know but for a lychee lover, it's a huge plus point) Ocean RockefellerThis would have made a great starter to any dinner. Served in 3 varieties, the raw salmon, scallops and spicy lobster was well thought through. Serves In a scallop shell, the torched Mozzarella tied the ingredients in nicely and added a touch of saltiness to the dish. The salmon was fresh, the scallops were nice and sweet and the lobster, while spicy to some, was a great way to end the trio. Sunshine Donburi Now this.... This is the kind of rice bowl we dreamt of as a kid (and definitely today too). What could be better than a bowl of rice, served with bacon, luncheon meat, smoked duck breast and an egg! I'm just happy that the luncheon meat and bacon were not fried to death. What could have made this dish better though was if they served it with a poached or Ajitsuke Tamago (the ramen eggs). The yolk would have helped make the dish a little richer and help tie in the ingredients better, making it a complete dish and not just rice with 3 ingredients. Can't wait to be back for their lunch specials, which IS slightly cheaper than their regular Ala Carte Menu. An overall great place to eat and meet up with friends, though definitely on the pricy side. Only draw back? Service wasn't as friendly as it could have been, given the fact that you're paying $15-20 a main.

Came here on a Saturday afternoon for a quick lunch, and without promotions, this place is really just... meh.I ordered a salmon bowl and a glass of house white. Can't go wrong with raw salmon on rice, and wine poured from a bottle. Fish was moderately fresh, rice was hot.They insisted we sit outside in the heat, and we did. Nonplussed with the non-existent service, would not come back.

Went there for late lunch, and don't be surprised to see a queue outside even after 2pm. The donburi was very fresh and tasty. They serve "savory donut" too. Ask for bar seat if you don't really need to be seated at proper table. It would expedite your waiting in line if there is full house.

Ah...now this is a long waited review. I've been here at least ten times now (based on my check ins via Yelp but I have been a frequent visitor even before Yelp launched in Singapore--so there!), and I've realized that I must have judged Tanuki too harshly in the beginning stages of our relationship.Service was slowed, waiters forgot my orders, and the food was pretty meh. Then, after the Japanese fusion bloom, I realized that Tanuki does fusion the best. Give the American Roll or Steak Tartar a try, or my personal favorite Taco Fish (though it should really be Fish Tacos...why are they trying to confuse people?)!Granted, the rolls here aren't up to par with the ones found in the States (Am I the only one who's heard of the Lion King roll?!) but for Singapore, they are excellent. I'm also a huge fan of their shrubs! Vinegar + Alchol = Bombdigitty! For $10 at Happy Hour, you NEED to order one! Blueberry shrub!

Actually this place is ok. Nothing horrible. The oysters are no good. I would say just avoid the happy hour food. The superstar roll and spicy salmon herumetto stood out for me. The "poutine" fries is not really a poutine. It's like a nacho supreme but with waffle fries.

Wow, I'm surprised by how generous they are with their alcohol. I was expecting a diluted drink since it was happy hour but what I got was the complete opposite. $2 happy hour oysters - very fresh, definitely the better oyster places in Singapore. However, $2 for oysters should be the market price, not the happy hour price no? I'd find paying $5 per oyster extremely steep. Would not come if it wasnt happy hour.Spam fries - Yummy, but a tad salty. I love how the spam strips are sliced thinly so you dont feel too guilty eating them :)Fried Salmon skin - Yum! Must order. Also love the chilli sauce that came with this.Great place for chilling!

Pricey, crowded and average food. Though the environment of the restaurant was quite pleasant, the food didn't match up to the standard. The rolls aren't that great though the beef bowl looks quite good. I guess if you're in the area and would like some Japanese food at a convenient place then Tanuki would be a good option.

I've been here twice. Once when my american professor was visiting Singapore and we held gathering for him and another at Yelp's Elite event. Overall, it's safe to say that the food is very much a fusion of American-Japanese cuisines. 1. American roll - A cheeseburger sushi, wrapped in rice, and deep-fried, tempura style. Enough said. I couldn't really tell all these ingredients apart when I want munching on them but it tasted pretty ok. Not as weird as my brain would have anticipated. Maybe it was a good thing that it was dim so I was not biased by my visual perception. 2. Spicy fish taco - Good. The taco was soft. The fish was fried (crispy on the outside & soft on the inside). They added some green chilis too. 3. Cheesesteak in a steamed bao bun - This reminded me of Philadelphia Cheesesteak that you can get on the side of any new-york street cart. Replacing the usual bun with steam bao was an interesting twist. I think I prefer baos to buns now.  4. Apple & Lychee martinis - They were generous with their alcohol. After 1.5 glasses, I could feel it hitting me. Although, I felt that the Apple ones were a little too sweet.  5. Truffle fries - Good. 6. $1 Oysters - I am not a fan of Oysters but if you are I am guessing this might sweeten the deal? AmbianceGreat for overlooking the bustling streets of Orchard road. Although beware of Singapore's unforgiving humidity when deciding between outdoor or indoor seating.

I came here with my mom to celebrate her birthday and had really high hopes for this place. Cute environment with patio seating.. I chose to sit on the patio. I came in right as happy hour started and was really pleased with the full HH menu. $2 an oyster and $10 select martinis.. Sounds good to me. I also read somewhere that they have a gentleman a pour, which I doubted because most places skimp out on the alcohol, especially during HH. However, I was really impressed that I had a proper tasting martini. Anyways, this place is really more of a tapas bar than a restaurant to me.. Lots of small bites and dishes, fresh oysters, sushi rolls.. I had no idea there was a very limited entrees.   The food is pretty good though. I ordered so much that I don't remember what I had, but I do remember everything being pretty yummy.  The service here was really mediocre overall, but one gentleman was really on his A game. Everyone else that was working seemed really unhappy or annoyed that I was asking for help or asking a lot of questions since it was my first time there. I would come here again, but probably only for HH.

Had the chirashi, and unfortunately, majority of the sashimi was not fresh. The tuna was crazy sour and the swordfish was yellowing. We usually come here for the beef, so I'm just going to stick with that. Disappointing on tanuki's side.

The medium-sized Hiroshima oyster might not be the biggest ones you've had in your life but fresh and perfect for any oyster addict. Our alcohol to go with the oysters was Singapore Sling, a mixture of gin, cherry and pineapple ($11 at Happy hour). There is also the choice of Martinis and other classic cocktails. the baskets of oysters from France displayed on the cocktail bar did not escape the sharp eyes of the oyster hunter. This explained the additional order of one oyster each from four different region with all at $3 except for one premium piece at $5Besides raw food like sashimi, we also tried the tapas and sushi. the sushi tasted much better than the tapas but it was understandably a raw bar and thus the targeted market might be narrower than those going for a full cooked fare..

My friends and I shared a Green tea Mille cake, Strawberry Shortcake, and Chocolate Arc-en-Ciel. The green tea flavor was lacking in the mille cake while the chocolate cake was rich in flavor. The strawberry shortcake had a nice balance in sweetness and texture. Probably had better cakes for the price but would recommend it if you haven't tried layered crepe-cakes before for the experience.

Two floors for this shopfront was pretty amazing. But one of my friends who is also an architect said that they could use some of the spaces to expand their seating areas.Came here at 9.20pm and there were queues for both take away and dine in. Looking at the display cases, there was not much choices left. Decided to get Apple Galette as it is specially baked at the Orchard Central branch for take away. Service was extremely slow. Probably because it is closing time and people are trying to take away or get their bills. Even though it is a big space, there is only one person in charged of the cashier, one person in charged of cutting the cakes. While standing and waiting for my order to be served, besides the lack of staffs they have, I noticed that most of the customers were impatient to get their orders. The waiting time was pretty long - 20-25 minutes even though they just had to put my order in a box without any plastic covers like the ones they put on the cakes. Was pretty disappointed at the service as I experienced a much better service at the Marina Square branch.Besides that, people was not in order especially at the take away section. They had to cut off the queue as it was about to close and they only had a few baked goods choices left when customers suddenly poured in. Since this is the first review of this branch, I will give a starting of 4 stars hoping that there is a change in this store in the upcoming future. I definitely love the modern touch for the interior design but would be better if there are more seatings in the store.

Not a big fan of crepe cake so went Feuille instead.  Taste is ok but nothing that will have me come back for more. We also had the signature crepe cake as well as the citron crepe cake, again it was just ok.  The ambience is good, service is good too.  But the coffee is terrible - luke warm and tasted worse than Starbucks.  Curiosity really killed the cat this time :)
Mille crepes are awesome but it's sad that their coffee are just normal brewed coffee without any specialty beans.

What's all the hype about?I've heard people talk about Lady M, but never had a chance to go in New York, so I was excited to see a few locations in Singapore. A friend was visiting Singapore, so we met up over dessert at Lady M. The two of us are San Francisco foodies, and I don't think either of us were impressed.Since it was our first time, we opted for slices of the signature Mille Crêpe cakes; one original and one chocolate. The reaction, "meh." The original was a bit too sweet and the chocolate one isn't firm enough to stand up--it fell apart after the first cut.And they don't have decaffeinated coffee or espresso.

Too pricey for the quality. It wasn't amazing or bad, just average. Had the green tea crepe and the flourless chocolate cake which were both pretty alright, nothing special. Though the ambience of the place is great for having long conversations.

This new Lady M outlet looks like a giant space ship that has landed on Orchard Road.  The high ceiling is indeed impressive, but beyond that I hardly seem to recognise the sleek and elegant patisserie that I first visited more than 10 years ago in upper east side.  Seating arrangements are funny and I am a bit blinded by all the spotlights and silver railings.  I guess Lady M has evolved into a different kind of creature in Singapore.  At least their cakes are still consistently good.  I also tried their salad this time - I had the salmon and pumpkin salad while my friend had the grilled chicken salad.  Unfortunately both are just ok, way too much dressing, next time I will just stick to cakes.  The green tea crepe cake was good as usual, that saved my evening.
Loved the green tea layer crepe cake! Wish I got the chocolate limited flavor but instead opted for banana which wasn't too great! Overall great!

The signature cake is nice and actually is better than other similar layered cakes. They do the layers even thinner with a subtle caramelized top. The banana cake was so so as I felt it was old. The crust and banana seemed aged. Possibly not a high turn around on that one. The espresso actually has potential. Tasted like it was extracted properly. BUT it came out cold. Cold not even luke warm. I guess do to the pre order process of the place. Oh that. We waited 30 minutes for a seat. The venue is charming but it designed not to hold many seats. End result? Line up for a seat. I still think for 8.50-9 for any cake is a pretty good deal based on the quality. Of course bearing you are willing to wait.
The service is so bad, order took forever to serve our cakes. And it took over 15mins to get  our bill

Nevermind its long queue and its lousy service, this is how a lady make us lust over her! nevermind about its breakfast and side dishes...its Green Tea Mille Crêpes is so exquisite!! Not any cake shop/cafes that sell cakes can duplicate that for sure! the texture of the mille crepes burnt a memory into my mind and tongue, i love how this lady torture me by burning me!Any budding chef should start doing intern here to perfect their skills!To cure my craving, i m going to buy a whole cake soon!

I've been wanting to try Lady M forever and after walking around the mall for a while, Lady M was an enticing option for a quick break. This particular cafe was set on a slope and seats are on multiple levels like in a stadium.We were seated by the window and ordered one slice of green tea millecrepe cake to share. I love that the cake is essentially a work of art. Given the dozens of layers, it starts to fall apart as you cut into it (or maybe that's just me because I'm clumsy). The cake had the right amount of sweetness without being overpowering. $11 later, we were done with our short break and headed out again.

The interior of this place is absolutely stunning, reminiscent of a fantastical glass palace straight out of a Disney movie. Floor-to-ceiling windows stretch across an entire wall, offering an uninhibited view of the pedestrians bustling below. The other side is lined with mirrors, which adds to the illusion of vastness. Tables are lackadaisically scattered across the two floors, creating a pleasantly bizarre look. My company and I got a slice of the Signature, Matcha and Chocolate (~$9 per slice). Each individual crepe is thin as a tissue sheet and meshes well with the adjacent layers of flavored cream. I especially loved the signature slice: without any extra flavoring, one can easily taste the freshness of the cream. However, past the first few bites, the richness of the cream becomes apparent and overwhelms one's senses. The simplicity of the cake becomes its downfall: there is nothing to mitigate the overly-rich taste of dairy and unfortunately, this ends the dessert on a sour note. Service is sadly incongruous with the extravagant and upmarket facade. Wait staff are clearly untrained students who seem more inclined to fiddle with their phones or chit-chat with colleagues. To conclude, despite the desserts failing to live up to the hype and price, this beautiful establishment is undeniably one of the best places to chill at along orchard road.

I've always wanted to go to a Lady M, but something always prevents me in the States.  So since we were just wandering around Orchard Road, pretty much doing nothing, sitting down at Lady M was perfect.  We ordered the Signature and Green tea mille crepes and some drinks.  The multi layer of crepes is definitely amazing.  While we weren't a big fan of the Signature since there seemed to be so much cream and overly sweet, we loved the Green tea one.  It wasn't too sweet, and the green tea flavor was delicious.The place was great for passing away the time by sitting at the windows people watching.  Great and friendly service.

It was newly opened in Shanghai and the queue line is always 200 meters long. Happy to enjoy Lady M this afternoon without waiting in Singapore. Signature Mille crepes is the best I've ever had. But coffee is a disaster. Maybe I shouldn't have ordered a coffee with such a girly name "Lady M iced coffee".

My favourite millecrepe place! The savory brunch items were decent too until they were sadly discontinued. Get the original and green tea millecrepes. The rest I've tried (including the special earl grey and chestnut flavours) aren't as strongly flavored or delicious. This location can be quite echo-y though. Not recommended for people who have issues with loud noise.Also, you need to share your millecrepe with a friend. Otherwise, it will be too gelat (i.e. you will be too glutted to enjoy it)!

Passed by Lady M at Orchard Central one day. The place looked contemporary, sleek and definitely looked like a place I would want to try. Took a quick look at the menu outside, they had pictures with yummy cakes. Told my sis we should do brunch one day and suggested Lady M.One Sunday morning, we arrived at what looked like the main entrance on the first floor. Lady M is a two floors restaurant. We arrived there at 10.40am, only to realize the restaurant opened at 11am. Never mind, we girls could check out the Zara nearby. Of cos, my niece and nephew were unhappy or should I say bored? After many many minutes passed, it was 11am and we went back to the restaurant's entrance. The "Closed" sign was still there and the door locked. We waited and waited. It was almost 11.10am. My sis got her kids to go to the second floor and see if that door was opened. From what I read before that day, the second floor entrance was for patrons to purchase and pick up their pastries. My nephew got back to the first floor and told us the door on the second floor was opened. We took the elevator at the mall, to the 2nd floor and headed to the restaurant. There were already a few other patrons heading into the restaurant. The two staffs seemed lost and did not know what to do. People started flowing into the restaurant. The restaurant seemed understaffed.We chose the table we wanted to sit and soon one server gave us a few menus.We ordered a few pot pies and paninis and two slices of cakes - the original Mille Crêpe and Banana Mille Feuille.The Black Pepper Chicken pie which I ordered was really really good. The pie was golden brown and really crispy. There were chunks of chicken and mushrooms inside the pie. The pie is definitely an A+ pie. The pie came with coleslaw (with raisins, a first for me but the combination was spot on) and some seaweed potato chips. Mille Crêpe - Very very nice. However, I could see why some yelpers complained the cake fell apart after some time. The cake really needs to be refrigerated and not sit out for too long. Best to be consumed in the restaurant.Banana Mille Feuille - Disappointing. The taste was good but there was way too much cream. There was more cream than the pastry. Like 90-10. I can make a better Mille Feuille.The Banana Mille Feuille was not what caused this two stars review. In fact, it was the pies and pastry that helped Lady M earned these two stars reviews from me. It was not even due to the alright service from the staffs or the fact that someone clearly forgot to open the door at the main entrance. What I could not get over was the amount of filth on the floor at the restaurant. See pictures. Doesn't anybody clean the floor before the restaurant opens every day? This is a restaurant for goodness sake. I felt the place lacks of basic restaurant hygiene. If no one cleans the floor, I wonder what it was like inside the kitchen :(Without the food and pastries, I am sure I will give this place only a one star (for the decor).

I have tried the cakes at all three Lady M outlets in Singapore and while this looks to be the biggest and airiest outlet, the mille crepe did not hold up as a takeaway. It went splat when I cut it with a fork, with the filling oozing out and the layered crepes flattening into a mess. So maybe it will be better to have it in store, or put it in the fridge if you buy it to go. I had mine about 30 minutes after purchase. I did not think it will require refrigeration as I was going to have it within an hour. The place was fairly big and encompassed two levels. Go directly to level 2 for take out as the cakes and cashier are on that level.
We had the Checkers and Lady M Signature Mille Crêpes. Nice.

The first time my friends and I wanted to eat here, the queue was too long. The 2nd time, I bought a few slices to take home. Not bad, the cakes were delicious. Finally, last weekend, I had a chance to get the full experience.It was Sunday at 8:30 pm. Got in through the ground floor, up through the staircase, saw a staff member (female) who told us to queue outside. On the way out, another staff (male) saw us and said "thank you for coming". He thought we had already finished eating.  Got to the queue and found no one there, waited patiently. In a short while the male staff came to usher us inside. On the way to our table, we bumped into another group coming up the staircase, looking for a table. While the male staff brought us to our table, the female staff took the other group to another table, without asking them to join the queue (there were a couple of people behind us). The table assigned to us was on the side of the staircase. It was difficult to get on the bench, and on the other side were high bar stools. Not easy for my elderly father, so we immediately requested a different table. I called the female staff 's attention, this was just after she had brought the other group to their table. I asked for another table and told her that the other group had cut the queue. She did not seem to realize that. We ordered a banana crepe and a chocolate ganache. Both took more than 15 minutes to arrive. They tasted ok, though I felt cheated because the banana crepe was mostly cream, with a few banana chunks. The chocolate ganache was rich and tasty, not too sweet.Overall, I think this place is just over hyped. The staff are friendly and helpful but the physical structure, with staircase and 2 entrances, do not help them at all. If I were the manager, I would strictly use the ground floor for exit only, to avoid confusion. The cakes are delicious, but not worth $9 for a slice.

Over rated. Over priced. Their Millie crepe was nice... But that was about it. It is about $9 per slice so I Guess I expected some wow factor. I was disappointed. I went on a weekday evening at about 845pm, near enough to closing time and there was still a queue. Waited not that Long, went in and noticed how big the place was. There were tables but i Guess they were understaffed. After they took our order (3 coffees, one water, two slices of cake) it took over 15mins to arrive. My Friend notice that that person slicing the cakes were so inexperienced that cakes that were being sliced were uneven and somewhat not that appetising. So the cake itself. Multi layered as it is supposed to be, nice texture and creamy and sweet cream filled between each layer. We had the chocolate and their signature. Preferred their signature one. The chocolate one was rather hard and each layer was sort of mushed together by the layering of the cream which is a bit too intense. Anyways, for our order, bill came up to about $40. Don't know what the hoo ha is all about, Glad that I tried it, won't go back anytime soon.

I'm in a dilemma to give this place a 2 or 3 stars. Food is not bad, but......Popped by for desserts after dinner with friends at around 9.30pm, and it's my first try at Lady M which I told my friend if green tea mille crepe is sold out I'll prolly not get anything. We just wanted a "quickie" and head home to rest since we are all working early the next day.We were joining the queue while we spied with our little eyes that there are many available seats. Me being me, walked straight to the service crew and asked if we could take their big table seating outside the cafe. So yes, we beat the queue and took our seat.The cafe was fully packed, so I went ahead to queue for take away in hope to ease the waiting time. I was standing there for a good 20 minutes before anyone spoke to me. A GOOD 20 MINUTES FOR TAKE AWAY. There was only 1 customer in front of me at the cashier. Entire service crew based on my observation include, 1 cashier, 1 lady inside the crepe area extremely busy cutting the crepe without stopping, 1 service crew whom I observed her job is to fold up the boxes and pack the crepe if there is any takeaway (by the way this crew has an issue if this is her only job scope), 1 service crew inside the kitchen, and 2 waiters, 1 to serve the dine-in and 1 to seat the customers.I was standing in a very awkward position in the line. There is an open service window for the servers to collect the mille crepe to serve dine-in, which intercepts with the cashier. So the waiter walked to and fro in front of me while waiting for this lady at the cashier ordering The good 20 mins allow me to observe how the entire team work and failed at their service. I think service could definitely been stepped up and better manage, to ease the queue into the cafe, to acknowledge customers' presence for take away, to fully utilize their existing staff strength, to better manage their cake distribution, ETC. Too many loopholes.I was really losing my patience since my friends and I were really tired and almost left for the day, the lady in front of me finally finished her orders! I jumped straight to my orders, when the cashier suddenly stopped me and carried out his SOP of telling me what are the items that ran out of orders. Actually I really can already see from my queue FOR THE PAST 20 MINS and have back up plans for orders that ran out, so I thought his explanation was really unnecessary and probably that explains why each order took so long. I snapped, but the cashier handled "this nasty customer" well. He lost a little patience too, but eventually tried his best to cool me down and returned wrong change.Eventually, I settled for a green tea mille crepe and a banana mille feulle for 4 to share. Both tasted really good, and ended my night on a sweet note. I like the creamy fillings of the green tea mille crepe that is generous yet not greasy, and the chunk of banana in the mille feulle (a little too much cream for this though). It's well balanced on the flavors!We finished, pack and go within 20 mins. It's not worth the wait for these mille crepes, and yes I will return only if there is no queue at all, be it take away or dine in.

Terrible. The tart au citron's crust was rancid, and the pot of English Breakfast was stained. And the kicker? The ice cappuccino ordered came hot and when asked, the server came with a glass of ice and said he was told to do so. Like, what? I don't get the hype and the queues. The cakes are quite normal, and you'd easily get places that aren't understaffed elsewhere with food served in under the 36mins we waited. Sanitary conditions leave room for much improvement, and the place had better step up its game before it gains some sort of food poisoning fame (hey it rhymes!).

Came here on a weekday evening to see what the fuss was about.PROS * didn't have to wait (I've seen some pretty horrific lines)* Spacious and pretty interior* good variety of cakes offered CONS* for the price ($16), I could have had a better cake and coffee* the place seems kind of pretentious. People sneaking glances at others and giving off a general cold vibe.* Mille crepe cake was good, but not amazeballsWouldn't come back unless my arm was twisted to. The chocolate Mille crepe cake is more or less the same as the one served at Awfully Chocolate.

To be honest, I'm not aware of Pompompurin till I saw its cafe launched in Singapore few months ago. Pompompurin comes from the Sanrio family which also feature Hello Kitty, My Melody & Little Twin Stars. Theme Cafe has always amazed me and as you know there isn't much Sanrio Theme Cafe here in Singapore and it sounds pretty fun to be involved in one.Looking at its menu, I feel like trying all as items was so attractive with cuteness overload by the Yellow Character. It's environment was featured in a theme of Garden City and everything looks peaceful and serene.Every table comes with a temporary "friend" to dine with - the Pompompurin plush. Do have some hugs to it and a photo session. Amazed by the cup of milk shake with printed Pompompurin Marshmallows topping off the gelatinous textured drink. The taste of refreshing fresh milk was really something I look upon to while the Mocktail of mango juice and fruits goes perfectly with cream and marshmallow in the fruity flavours.Puru Puru Pudding Shake - $12.99 & Fruity Garden Mango Juice - $11.99An adorable plate of slow-cooked mushroom stroganoff consisting deep flavours of scrambled eggs, onions and mushroom. Character Pompompurin was made up with yellow rice balls with meatball as its top and choclate fudge drawing out its eyes and nose, sitting on a bed of vegetables.Pompompuri's Mushroom Stroganoff - $17.99Like the Mushroom Straganoff dish, Pompompurin was made up by yellow rice balls but it was served in a cup instead. Pairing the rice with a little pot of stewed beef in delicious red wine sauce and sweet onions. Tasty and I like it.Red Wine Beef Stew - $17.99There are some desserts menu that exclusivelyy alloweed their customer to take-home a pompompurin sovenir mug. We have a lot of mugs at home and was not too tempted to have additional in the kitchen thus we had ordered the Mango Parfait without the mug. Served in a wobbly Purin with diced mangos  as well as little scoops of ice cream. Dig in your dessert spoon and check out the spongy cake at its base!Pompompurin's Mango Parfait - $19.99How do we resist cute stuff? It's so hard to do so. Having a Buddy meal that consist of 2 drinks, 2 mains and a dessert with $10 off the bill ends us up paying a bomb too as it cost about $90 in total after the discount. Drinks are considered expensive here and taste wise it is still ok.

Pompompurin Go for the theme if you have kids who are interested. Saw 2 women there without kids. I wonder why.Eat the custard pudding and nothing else. That's the only thing that was good.Pasta with mentaiko carbonara tasted weird. No taste of mentaiko, no taste of carbonara. Strange pinkish colour.

Just A-Ok. To be honest, I don't know what Pompompurin is until a friend suggested we check this cafe located on the 4th floor of Orchard Central. We went there on a Wednesday afternoon (2pm) and greeted with a rather short queue. Waited for 10 mins and managed to get a table in this very "happy wonderland" that I almost wanted to make a U-turn and leave. The cafe is garden themed, with it;s signature bright yellow (rather too much, really), Pompompurin and friends figurines standing while greeting their fans. The side booth seating is reserved for bigger crowd, also comes with a Pompompurin cushion for you to cuddle (if you REALLY love that dog) and take selfie with - which I think rather unhygienic so please bathe him with Dettol first before you cuddle or sink your face in it. haha. We were seated in the middle and I requested the cushion just so that my photos turned out nicer. The friendly staff attended to my request and within minutes, I have the cute mascot sitting next to us, though he remained quiet and didn't participate in our conversation.       Moving on to the food - it's on the pricey side. Drinks - don't even mention it. A latte with 2 pathetic marshmallow cost $12.90 without GST. My friend ordered a "Picnic Platter" which consisit of a half bagel, a poached egg with hollandaise sauce sitting on a muffin and a stone hard scone. All for $24.90. Overall, we paid $60 for one main and 2 coffee. It;s just the novelty that you;re here for, I don't think I'll ever return. Oh, have i forgotten to best part? Occasional scream by little kids as entertainment.
This cafe has now closed permanently. I visited on its last day of operations just to check it off my list.

The cafe was located just behind the lift at level 4. The menu was limited and the place was small. We queued about an hour for a table for 2 persons during dinner time. Do remember to take photos with the characters in the middle of the cafe.

This is a cute Sanrio theme cafe located at Orchard central level 4. Easiest way to locate it is to take the lift. I went on a Thursday evening (approx. 6pm) and there was a short queue. I was quickly ushered in, as those queueing were opting to wait for the booth seats. Upon ordering, the waitress warned us there would be a 30min waiting time,but actually we only waited about 10mins for the food to arrive. Anyway, while waiting, you can take photos with the cute centrepiece. We ordered the mango parfait, pancake stack, and coffee with marshmallows. The bill came up to about $70 with service charge and taxes. Quite pricey for 2 desserts and a coffee. Taste wise, everything was below average. The pancakes were cold and tough, like they were made in a microwave yesterday and left out in the open overnight to cool.  The mango parfait was alright I guess,and the coffee was very creamy, till you could barely still call it coffee.  Not anything you'd want to have again in your lifetime. +1 star for ambience+1 star for serviceScores zero for everything else

I heard about this cafe from a friend's fb visit.  As a still young at heart Sanrio fan, I've gotta try it and soak in the cuteness!  I came here with my children on a Monday around 11:30am,  there were no queue and waited a minute or two for a staff to greet and seat us. While the cafe was half full/empty, the staff asked if we wanted to share a table with a lady at the back.  I was puzzled by her request as I stared at all the empty tables around us.  Normally I wouldn't mind to share table, especially with children, if it means they could sit and eat quickly rather than wait for another 15-30 mins.  But with no queue and a half empty cafe?!  Anyways, we sat down, with no menus.  I situated the children and searched for a waitress.  I believe there were a total of three.  At random times, all of them are no where to be found, perhaps all of them are in the kitchen.  The service was prompt once you get a hold of the waitresses.  I ordered a cookie and cream caramel latte, a pancake tower, and a beef stroganoff.  The pancake tower came first.  While adorable looking, the pancakes were cold and tough.  Not the warm and fluffy pancakes that one look forward to devour.  The caramel latte, again, nice presentation, but the taste fall short.  It's basically a cold caramel flavored milk with whipped cream and one small piece of sugar cookie.  For $12, I'd expect a lot more. The beef stroganoff was tasty.  The sauce was rich but not overly salty.  The rice, again, looked cuter than its taste.  It was cold and dense.  I guess the kitchen staff needed to compact the rice into the pompompurin mold, hence the dense texture.  I could eat just the sauce with crunchy French bread.  Over all, it's a cute, yet pricey, cafe to take selfies and post of social medias.  Will I come again? Maybe just to soak in the cuteness.  Word of caution though, the cute pompompurin stuff animal got passed around so much, one is better off to just take picture without touching it for hygiene reasons.

It is my personal belief that DTF across Singapore comes with different service levels and quality of food levels. Although its a chain restaurant, I seem to find that some places (which shall not be named) are lacking compared to others. In my honest opinion the DTF at Wisma Atria is one of the best I've had in terms of both service and food. I don't think I need to wax lyrical about their dishes, because everyone else here will probably be better able to recommend you what to eat. But if you're going on a budget of around 40 bucks for 2 people here's the combo I'd recommend (and in fact its what I have every single time I go to DTF):1. Xiao Cai for starters2. Xiao Long Bao for sharing3. Fried Rice4. Beef Brisket SoupTah dah! Fills you up in no time.
Beyond delicious shanghai soup dumplings. Premium quality ingredients. Very fresh. Restaurant was so clean I could've eaten off the floor. Service was good as well.

Although a chain, Din Tai Fung bang them out with the best of them. Cute atmosphere with a great selection of team and an even better selection of buns. Get the Shao Lum Bao, soup dumplings with pork and crab. Chive and pork were also nice. If you require a little greens in you life, try the pea spouts sautéed in garlic.

The problem with Ding Tai Fung is not that it's terrible. Ask anyone that doesn't know better and they'll tell you it's good food. The meals are hot and arrive relatively quickly and they look well presented. But the problem with DTF in Singapore is they do not have a strong sense of the kind of flavors expected of steamed soup dumplings and even the Red Roast Beef Noodles are merely OK in flavor. It needs a lot more of that OOMPH and rarely delivers.

During my week long vacay here I must have eaten at a Din Tai Fung at least 4 times. I heart xiao long bao!!! The restaurant is clean, service is speedy and friendly and the food is great. There is a variety of things to eat other than soup dumplings- I love the noodles with spicy sauce. I devoured a entire bowl and forgot to share with my 2 other diners :) Oops.
