It's also pretty neat that you can watch them creating dumplings in the kitchen through big glass windows. I wish they had this chain in Dallas!

This was where it happened - my very first xiao long bao.As legends go, all xiao long bao (henceforth known as XLB) virgins pay the price their first time - scalding your tongue on the soup hidden within it's delicate skin. I was torn between letting it happen, or scheming up an escape... but then I thought: why spoil the moment? So I caved and let the XLB do to me what it was meant to; I bit into the plump dumpling, and was I was warned about the hot soup... but gladly got scalded any how. And the flavour... I haven't had any better, and after visiting even the other branches of this store, I don't think I will. Maybe the hands here are magic after all.Being caught up in the fantasy world that is XLB, it's hard to look around you and notice anything else, but of course, when you come up for air, everything is as it should be - the wait staff are mega speedy, and relatively polite (they say hi when they stop by to drop off each dish), they top up your tea often, and it just seems like a well-oiled machine. Before you think XLB is everything that they serve (but it should be), there is a sizeable menu of things that include a super tasty pork chop fried rice, and a mystery mix of veggies called "xiao cai". Don't think, just order.I now employ a break-skin-and-slurp-up-soup policy, but you never forget your first time eh?
All time favorite restaurant in SG. Moderately priced, and crazily delicious. Perfect for expats, locals, and tourists who grave a delicious little taste of the Far East.

Food was good but I thought it was better at their Kuala Lampur location.  The line was long and we waited about 45 minutes.  I thought I was getting hyppglycemic so we picked up a piece of duck at another place.  They wouldn't let us finish it without an argument once we were seated.  I hear the wait in Irvine (CA) can be 3 hours so I shouldn't complain about 45 minutes

My favourite place for xiaolongbao!!!! No other place can beat it even in Shanghai.All other dishes are also delicious. Good ambiance and very professional and well-trained service staff. Every dinning experience is memorable!

I don't have much to say about Din Tai Fung, except that it's delicious and that I recommend you give it a try. The very first time I came here was with a friend, and I ordered the beef noodles and of course the Xiao Long Bao - both of which were great. Since then, I've gone to different branches of the restaurant (including one of the ones in Taipei as well) and am happy to say that the quality is consistent throughout! (A friend in LA tells me that the Din Tai Fung there is the same as the one she tried in Taipei, though the American menu has a few different options.)

Real shame that I did not get a chance to take photos here. They are opening up one at my local mall soon. I found out about this place after driving home from Marina Bay. I must say if I did not drive by then I would be missing out. I must say this place is really awesome. Who knew three Chinese words can make a difference. This eatery "meats" the world standard of all restaurants in the world. All the items that make the restaurant famous are here. I really enjoyed the xiao long bao as well. Who knew I would find it at a better quality than any other dim sum place in the US and Singapore. This Din Tai Fung is bigger than any other ones in the US. Cannot wait until they open up the one in Valley Fair Mall. Only problem was that a dinner here is considered really expensive. It is a good splurge.

I love you, DTF. I've been eating here  (at various branches) a long, long time, and it only gets better. No-brainer order: get the xiao long bao, the beef brisket noodle soup and the dou miao (pea shoot greens with garlic). End of story.

I always try the various dishes there.  Everything is good, but I would wish if they can improve the noodles.  I recommend the rice dishes than noodles.美味しいのでよく行きます。どれも美味しいのであまり書くことはないのですが、ヌードルは止めておいた方が無難なのと、ここのレモングラスティーは美味いですねー。よくデザートをボンとサービスしてくれますが、なかなか美味しいです。

Ever since I came across Paradise Dynasty, I've just completely abandoned Din Tai Fung. It doesn't help either that there seems to ALWAYS be a line in this place. But to their credit, their service is fast & succinct enough to ensure that you don't wait too long for your table.Their food are decent, but I feel that the xiao long bao and noodles are outclassed by Paradise Dynasty.

I am obsessed with dumplings. Completely and utterly obsessed. To me, a great soup dumpling is the ultimate perfection. We ordered pork soup dumplings, shumai, stir fried spinach, pork noodles, and chili wontons. Overall the food and ambiance were nice, but the soup dumplings didn't totally do it for me. They were a bit small and the soup wasn't as flavorful as those I'd eaten elsewhere. The noodles were also a bit disappointing in the flavor department.

The 'xiao long bao' is very good-juicy and succulent. The skin is thin and perfect texture. It's also always fun to see them making the dumplings. Service is generally good and the selection is wide. Only downside is the long wait

I have been dining at this location for over a year, and though the food is consistently outstanding, the service is seriously lacking.Many times they have forgotten items which I have ordered and by the time I am able to flag the wait staff down (which can be nearly impossible), it has been 45 minutes and they bring it out with the dessert. Simply put, they need to do a better job making sure patrons are all taken care of and that their orders are fulfilled. Oh, and would it kill them to smile? Orchard Road is a convenient location and that's the only reason I return. ** Do yourself a favor and go to Raffles City location - they actually have it together.

I never thought I'd say this, but I'm all DTF'd out... I was so amazed by Din Tai Fung the first time I tasted those delicious dumpling morsels at the MBS DTF and since then I've gone back so many times, especially the one in Jakarta at Plaza Indonesia when I practically lived at the Grant Hyatt Jakarta on a project.It's amazing how consistent DTFs are across the world. We had to wait about 20 mins to be seated at this Paragon basement DTF, but again, consistently good food and quick no-nonsense service. They have it down to a science.

Favourite dumplings anywhere! Whenever I'm overseas I always crave these so much. If you haven't tried it you have to go. The xlb skin is the perfect thickness with just the right amount of soup and meat. While the normal one is still the best, the truffle xlb's are worth trying as well.As for the other stuff, I absolutely love the fried rice here (shrimp being my favourite) and I have no idea how they get it to taste so good. The la mian is alright but the ones at crystal jade/paradise are better imo.There's usually a queue at peak times but I find the paragon one moves the fastest out of the town DTFs (though now that the Wisma outlet expanded it's sometimes comparable)
Great value for money. No wonder it's alway crowded and we have to queue up. Hence one star was deducted!

I love Din Tai Fung. My favorite thing there is the Xiao Long Bao. You can see them making it fresh and it tastes so good. The beef noodles are great to because of the spice. The spice gives the dish a lot of flavor. Also the fried rice is so flavorful and delicious and you can't get better fried rice anywhere. I would HIGHLY recommend Din Tai Fung to anybody
Love love love DTF! This one even have the red bean chocolate dessert which is different than other countries. Must try!

I am in love.Instead of setting a portrait of my spouse on my bedside table when I travel to Singapore, I will be placing the business card from Din Tai Fung, which features a picture of a plump xiao long bao, on the table next to my bed.Soft, juicy pillows of steaming xiao long bao whispered delicious pork nothings to me last night during my first visit to the Orchard branch of Din Tai Fung, how could I have been so blind to this love affair in the making?What is so amazing about Din Tai Fung is that it is a large chain restaurant by the BreadTalk group, a type of business that I would never or rarely patronize, but the quality was simply decadent.  The service was average to nearly poor, however, the food was so spectacular, the rating could be nothing less than than a five star.

We came for an early dinner and managed to dodge the crowd. The restaurant was still quite full and bustling for good reason, the food was awesome. Not just the truffle dim sum, but everything that came out of the kitchen. Dinner for two with complimentary tea came to S$75. Window seats recommended if possible though you probably won't have a choice.The food court here is all around high quality. We avoid Orchard like the plague, but will certainly be back to Din Tai Fung if we are in the area.
Dim sum is the Tapas of China. The fact that it's the cheapest Michelin-star-restaurant you'll ever find, with great food!Highly recommended!
really great dumplings and fried rice. Ill come back again for sure (LA location though)

Consistently good food. Waitresses are all business - almost like non human robots. Very efficiently run chain restaurant. Diners mark selections on a clipboard either while waiting for a table or immediately when seated.  We go about once a month, all the locations are pretty consistent and we often tend to order the same things on each visit.  Sliced Cucumbers with Garlic, Xiao Long Bao,  Shrimp and Pork Dumplings, Shrimp and Pork Shumai, Pork Buns, Fried Rice with Fried Pork Chop, Wontons with Vinegar and Chili Oil are all extremely good.There is often a wait for a table so the trick is to arrive early before the peak rush. They open an hour earlier at 10am on weekends.  Din Tai Fung is a great place to bring out of town visitors for dim sum.  Even the most constipated westerner will find this food appealing.

Decided to give the restaurant a go after reading reviews on Yelp & other sites.  We had a 15 minute wait in the que, but received a list to record our order....had to get my own menu.We ordered hot & sour soup.  The soup was okay, not as flavorful as I was hoping.....edible after adding some vinager & spice.Our favorites were the chili crab buns and dumplings.  The service was attentive and efficient.  The only complaint was Jasmine tea was brought to the table without requesting it, so we thought it was complimentary.  Upon checking the bill, we were charged $1.00/person......not a huge deal, but at least ask the customer if it is wanted.  Other than that, a very pleasant, affordable meal.

I generally don't like Chinese food (I know, I know... then why do I live here?), so I came here partially as a way to see if I could convince myself it could be good, partially expecting to poke a hole in the hype with a low rating.The XLB were disarmingly excellent, and the pork and vegetable dumplings and chilicrab bun were also very good. It wasn't too expensive, except I wish the vegetables were cheaper. The service was unusually good, having had my tea cup refilled 4-5 times without having to ask. Even the air conditioning was at  a reasonable level. In other words, all of the issues that I usually complain about with regards to Singaporean restaurants (mediocre food, high prices, neglectful waiters, fake winter) were conspicuously absent. They won me over.

Food quality a miss for the second successive visit after years of admiring this place all round. Veggie Delight Fail.More Haha. Some genius decided to do away with "free flow refills" tea! So now it is ordered per pot, and you can sip tepid, over-brewed Bitter tea after the first few minutes. Or continually re-order a new pot. Another delight gone. Then mid-meal - need to close register so please stop eating, chatting, fumble, find card, wait while I go process, come back to stop you again and sign off the card slip. Finally, prices suddenly up almost 2x following an unnecessary facelift that feels like a downgrade.Way to go Bread-talk. Trouble brewing alongside the new tea pot idea. Stock at all time high, business toppy, will start to short some to make up for the 2x bill!

Great Chinese food at reasonable prices. My family comes here at least once a month when we're at Orchard Road. There's usually a 15 min wait to get a table during dinner time. Located at 4th floor of Wisma Atria, we find the xiao long bau unique and most of the dishes are done well. Kid-friendly and they provide high chairs and kids cutleries. Highly recommended!

Extra points just for being seated right away (we got there at around 11:30). In the US, two hour waits can be the norm, but there are just too many good food options here in Singapore.This Din Tai Fung was conveniently located in the Wisma Atria mall on there 4th floor (by the way, another incredible food court on this level as well), and was right across the street from our hotel. Wanting to see how it compares to the one in Bellevue, WA,  we had an early lunch here. We ordered:Seaweed salad and tofu with honey sauce appetizers: both were good. I had the seaweed salad before, but the tofu dish was new to me: nice way to start the meal.Fried shrimp pancake: this was new to me as well, and was my favorite dish. Love how crispy and not greasy it was.Shrimp fried rice: standard but good.Shrimp and Chinese gourd dumplings: just ok: not that big of a fan of the gourd.Chili crab bun: this was really good, but you order them one each (should have gotten another one).Overall, very similar to the Din Tai Fung's in the US. No wait to be seated, but we did have a long wait for our food, though.

After touring on the Singapore Hop On Hop Off "yellow" bus for the morning, we spotted a familiar restaurant from China and the US.  Din Tai Fung known for their delicate Siu Loong Baus.  Since we were hungry for a late lunch, we hopped off at the Orchard Road stop and headed upstairs to L4 of the Japanese shopping center.Had the Vinegar Based Salad, Shanghainese Chicken, Pork Siu Loong Baus, and Minced Pork & Mushroom Noodles.  Tea refilled constantly.  High quality food and service consistent with the chain.  Having non chain restaurant food tonight!

I had heard so much about Din Tai Fung that I was in a crazy pursuit after these bloody dumplings - never making it, until tonight.First off, staff is very nice, mostly. We arrived an hour before closing time. Before being able to order, we were told which dumplings   they had run out of. My husband does not eat meat so it wasn't nice to hear that all of the fish dumplings and most of the vegetarian options were gone. But then again we were late.So we ordered a concoction of food that was mostly noodles and veggies, and 6 pieces of crab meat & pork dumplings (for me). The order was placed shortly after 9 pm.Everyone around us seemed to be getting food (the place was relatively empty though) fast.Our first order arrived at around 9:35, everything else in about 5-minute-iterations, with a staff member asking us at 9:30 if we wanted to place a last order - which was a tad bizarre, with no other food having arrived yet. Also we had the dumpling-delivery-people stopping by our table often - only to carry on walking again after checking the contents - pretty funny, if you are NOT hungry that is. We finally had nearly all of our food (following a dumpling mix-up), when I was asked to pay and come to the till - where I had to wait for someone else to pay.Back to my- nearly cold - food, the last order arrived: the crab meat & pork dumplings, with samples of black hair. I stopped a waiter who immediately offered a replacement. That took some time, which made the whole experience very late - with the supervisor apologising profusely, for both the wait and the hair situation.All in all, food was just ok. Pretty bland.Two stars for the wait staff, one for food. I guess we just hit a bad day but I won't be back, especially since my husband found that there is a huge difference in quality between here and Taipei. Taipei it shall be then, next time :-)

The sun set as the darkness came quickly at around 6pm. Having exposed ourselves exploring Singapore under extreme heat, we couldn't help but finding ourselves dining in a cool AC top-notch restaurant like Ding Tai Fung. This Taiwanese establishment is located right in the heart of Orchard area. Famously known for its Xiao Long Bao, Ding Tai Fung also features a bunch of other dimsum goodness, which we were determined to try them all out.We started with a refreshing dish of Oriental salad. The salad was crunchy and delicious, with standout ingredients like bean sprouts, Korean glass noodles and vinegar, which we believe is a perfect match to create the appetite since vinegar dressing salad is our favorite. Afterwards, here came our Steamed Pork Dumplings (Xiao Long Bao), Steamed Shrimp & Pork Shaomai, Steamed Vegetable & Pork Buns, and Steamed Finely Mashed Red Bean Dumplings. Of course, the spotlight should be given Xiao Long Bao. Sipping the water inside each bao is wonderful. The inside meat is well-flavored.Recommendation: Xiao Long Bao, Oriental SaladRead our full review at: thecoupleeats.com/singap…

Xiao long baos are amazing as with their other outlets-only complain would be the smell (which somewhat resembles that of when you enter a gym??) Would strongly recommend the yam xiaolongbaos filled with ornee as well as their crab meat xiao long baos :)
The absolute best pork dumplings in town, cheap and yummy. They have a variety of dumplings but the pork ones are the best.

Love love love DTF. Go out of my way to visit in other locations when I travel like San Francisco and Seattle. Reasonable price, fast service and great tasting food. They are not known for their customer service, but the food makes up for it. I will never have pork dumplings better than at DTF.

When you're used to 2-3 hour waits in Los Angeles to eat here and pay much higher prices, it is like heaven eating here in Singapore where you can just walk in, sit down and eat.I can report that 4F here at the Wisma Atria Shopping Center felt to me as if I were in Foodie heaven.  So many choices and in the middle of this chaos of food teasing is Din Tai Fung.We sat down and were promptly served two orders of Xiao Long Bao and felt pacified as the soup explosion in my mouth placed me in a state foodie hypnosis.And that was just the regular order.  We then order the one with truffle flavoring and I felt like Buddha must felt when he found himself in reclining position as he attained Nirvana.Seriously, I really enjoyed the quality here and feel as if I have cheated the entire state of California whole will wait another 2 hours before they can sit down and have about 70% of the quality of XLB that are here.We also had the drunken chicken: simple and excellent.Then for a refreshment, I had the grass jelly drink.  Perfect.Then we had a mushroom and minced pork with noodle dish.  Simple and perfect.All in all, Singapore, when it comes to food is like placing money on bets you will never lose.That's what happened here tonight.  This foodie is one happy man.

How can everything here be so delicious? I think I had dim sum approximately four times during my one-week trip to Singapore and this was definitely the best of all of them. We didn't have to wait too long to get seated, and we were able to decide on what to order while we waited so our food was ready very quickly once we sat down. I honestly don't remember everything we had; I just ate and felt happy. There were a couple highlights though:- Xiaolongbao: delicious. I've often had xlb where the soup has leaked out by the time you eat it all. Not the case here. Full of soup, perfectly complemented by the ginger and vinegar.- Truffle xiaolongbao: If you like super strong truffle flavor, you could probably eat many of these. I could only eat one but it felt like the most decadent xlb I've ever had. - Chili crab bun: What's not to love? Chili crab combined with the fluffiest bun...heavenly. - Fried rice: I could have eaten the whole plate. Enough said. - Chocolate/red bean dumpling: I have never tried a dessert dumpling before, and I was a little skeptical of chocolate and red bean combined in a dumpling. But it was delicious. The flavors match really well and the chocolate is so nice and melty. Be sure to save room for this. Din Tai Fung really is the best and it lives up to the hype.

This Din Tai Fung is located on the 4th floor next to Japan Food Town. Was there on a Saturday for late lunch. The staff at the entrance gave me a number and a paper & pen so I could check what I liked to order while waiting. The wait was not bad at all. Good thing I did not have to stand in line. Think I ever mentioned in my other post, I do not like to stand in line, period! Staffs were all friendly and attentive. I like that the restaurant has those bag holders/stands, like those in Taste Paradise, which allow female customers to store their purses or bags. Of cos those at Taste Paradise were a lot better since they came with a flap attached to secure the top. The ones at Din Tai Feng were open bag holders which the staff would just put a cloth over it. Ok I know, I can be so nitpicking.FOOD 4/5The legendary xiao long bao (steamed dumplings) were yummy as expected. I also ordered one red bean bun and one meat bun just to try. They were tiny but were good.AMBIENCE 3/5It was noisy but I did not expect it to be calm and quiet. It was not a place I would suggest for a first date. More like a place for friends to catch up or family lunch.STAFFS 5/5Staffs were attentive, helpful and polite. Water was filled up constantly.

Andrew and I always wondered how Din Tai Fung (DTF) can consistently keep their rich flavour after opening many branches around the world. We visited a few Din Tai Fung restaurants when we were in Singapore and were blown away at their good quality control. At the same time we also thought that we were just lucky... ;-)Two things that we always ordered in Din Tai Fung were their shrimp & pork shao mai and of course the 18 folds original Xiao Long Bao. DTF's xiao long bao is really in the league of their own. Honestly we never found any broken dumpling skin although I never really counted the number of folds on their dumpling.The shao mai was also always very delicious with plenty of pork meats inside. I always add vinegar to shao mai and the xiao long bao as I love the additional sour flavour on the meat. Of course the price of their dishes are more than the other Chinese restaurants but the quality never disappoints us.

Din Tai Fung , the champion of dim sum,  this place is always packed and you often have to wait but once you get your seat it is time for business.  Oder and order and just wait for the steaming baskets of goodness appear at your table everything is so yummy.  You can not go wrong.  Have fun!
The food was tasty enough, but it didn't live up to the hype. I'd go again with someone who likes to eat here but wouldn't choose it myself.

Couldn't decide what to eat, and stumbled on DTF.  I've had such high expectations for their soup dumplings that when they came out, I was a little disappointed.  Not to say they weren't good or anything, because they were but just overly hyped.  The dumplings are small and succulent.  The drunken chicken was moist and full of alcohol. I don't think it's a 5 star restaurant but it's good.
Short wait for delicious food at a good price. We made our order on paper while we were waiting.

Omg! Another great meal, and we totally just lucked into this place. I was at Orchard Road with my mother, and we had entered one of the shopping malls to purchase some stuff from Lush and by the time the shopping was done, it was closing on 9pm, and we both were just super hungry. I had noticed a food court level located in the same mall as the Lust store, so just took the elevetor up there and then looked at Yelp reviews and this one come up tops.Honestly, it wasn't a great first experience as when we approached the restaurant front of staff and asked about vegetarian options for my mother, the lady said there was nothing vegetarian available. But I asked to see menu and there _clearly_ were veg options that mum said she was interested in trying. So we got in and soon afterwards folks were turned away as the restaurant was closing at 10pm. We hurriedly ordered pretty much at random from the menu to be honest (and the list of foods ordered is in my photos), but gosh, all the food we got was so good and scrumptious, each bite was a delight and I walked away super happy to have had the opportunity/ chance to eat here (sometimes the food gods are truly with you!) My one regret however was that in rush of ordering, didn't get to try the XLB so am going to make it my mission once back in US next year, to get myself to a DTF and try this (#foodie 2016 new year resolution!)

Back in California, there is usually a line hour deep for DTF, I was surprised that at around 8pm there was no line or wait at all here in Singapore.  Same delicious, yummy dumplings but sans line.The XLB is what you get here if you didn't know, you can get other stuff but the XLB is what you should put down in the box as soon as you sit down.  The food came out quickly, the cold sliced beef, the XLB, the pan fried shirmp pancake was delicious.  The beer was cold and served promptly. I wish I had a DTF near me that was like this, no lines, no waiting still yummy.
i reckon its the 'consistently' good and most mouth watering dim sums in the world! love the stir fry spinach , spicy sauce noodles!!!!
Very Good!Dumplings: Loved the Pork.   Pork / Crab were good.    The chicken we did not enjoy as much mainly because the green onion dominated the flavor.    The Veggies were Awesome.
Love all the savory options here: Spicy tofu, watercress, dates w/ rice, veggie dumplings. All tiny portions but very filling.

I know, I know, it's a chain restaurant. But it's SO addictive! I've been to different restaurants in different malls but they all manage to keep the flavor constant. It's no mean feat! The best thing on the menu is the seaweed glass noodle salad appetizer. It's light, it's tasty and packed with so much flavor! The xiao long bao is really yummy there too. The texture is not too thick or thin, and none of them are broken when they are served. Food snobs may scoff at the chain restaurant concept, but trust me, this one is worth checking out!

I love Din Tai Fung! Im always guaranteed a great meal when I come here. Service is always good and prompt. Be prepared to wait a bit during weekends and dinner time. The dumplings are definitely a must try here, as are their appetizers. I really love the honeyed tofu with peanuts. Its so good. Their shrimp fried rice and stir fried veggies are also really good. Its no wonder that this place is so popular all around the world. Ive been so many times and have ever been disappointed. Great place.

The restaurant is located at the far end of the building, with a unblock view of the merlion and Marina Bay Sands. The place was very stylish decorated with a cozy and old school feel. Currently the restaurant was having a promotion for Flavours of The Fullerton Heritage 2016. A 3 course set lunch for this promotion cost $35++ and available everyday.I was served iced water but it was not refilled regularly. The meal was started with amuse bouche and bread. The amuse bouche was a creamy truffle mousse, topped with crispy rice, which pop in the mouth. The bread was soft and warm, served with thin sliver slices of cheese.Appetizer : Burrata CheeseMango Olive Tapenade, Parma Ham, Rosemary FoamThe cheese was light and soft like tofu, where one can slice easily with just the fork. The olive mixture added a punch to the slightly bland dish.Main : Tagliatelle alla BologneseKagoshima Wagyu Beef Ragout, Parmigiano ReggianoThe handmade pasta was soft and tender. The dish was served pipping hot. Looked simple but it was delicious and very filling.Dessert : Coconut Panna CottaPassion Fruit Sauce, White Mango Compote, Mango TuilesThe dessert was light and tangy, without too creamy.Overall the food was great and filling too. However I was quite disappointed with its service. I had not finished my amuse bouche when I was served the Appetizer course. Turned out that there was a wedding dinner that night. The staffs were rushing the lunch crowd, so that they could start to prepare for the dinner. I wish that I had been informed when I placed my order. I felt kind of being rushed through the meal.

Romantic ambience with a great view of the marina area. Service was attentive and presentable. The appetizer bread was served with generous shaved cheese. Thick seabass fillet and wagyu beef that melts in you mouth, went down well with glass of champagne and reds. Long black was perfect to close the evening with choc lava. An exceptional evening.

Disappointing!  ...and overpriced for what it is. Let's start from the good part:  the view, the venue, the location. And the bread. After the bread, it went downhill.Maybe when Chef Forlino was there it was worth it. Now they lost it. Will go back to No Menu...

Disappointing dining experience. It was our first time and our last time at Forlino.The bar area was a sad dark corner opposite the restroom; we waited there for friends to join and had some cocktails. The Americano and Negroni were tasteless and watery.The service was absent and unpassionate. One did not get a sense of pride of the history of this restaurant which has had such a wonderful past.Appetisers: pretty good: cold cuts, burrata, and scallop tartar (not quite Italian though).Main courses: big disappointment: The Coniglioni with Duck ragu came over-baked and therefore the pasta shells were hard and tough to chew. The duck ragu was slightly too sweet.Risotto with shrimp: average.Spaghetti carbonara: too creamy and lacked the authentic flavor of a true carbonaraBranzino: small portion served in an uninspiring manner with tired vegetables around it.A great positive: The views are wonderful.Overall however, a tired, uninspiring and very overpriced dining experience with poor execution of Italian dishes ($150+ per person with one bottle of wine).

Came here for lunch. I really liked the view, and the setup is really nice and clean. Service was average, staff seemed a unfriendly when we made requests, but remained polite. I was vegetarian that day, and just wanted to check what dishes did not have meat. Staff did not seem sure.Anyway, I liked the bread, even though it was rather oily. Everything else all right - nothing bad - but boring. Ever had a meal where you cannot find much fault, but that's the only great thing? Pretty much sums this meal up. If I had to pick something though, I think I liked the panna cotta w/ passion fruit best. Slightly sour, but otherwise good. Overall, it felt like I was there more for the view and to have a chat, and the meal was an add-on/  secondary to that and was no cause for interruption.

Forlino is one of those restaurants that thrives on business clientele and ladies who lunch. It fits the mold of a perfunctory fine dining restaurant with it's white linen, sharply dressed waiters and a hostess at the front desk with a remarkable memory. Thing is while the food is good and the service is as it should be for people who lunch in 45 minutes, I feel like this restaurant lacks heart or passion and that's why it scores a 3/5. At a recent lunch, I had the crab salad to start with and a seafood casserole for my mains. I believe the menu changes monthly with the seasons so these items may not be available year round. The crab salad was light and refreshing with a mold of fresh, juicy crab and just enough dressing drizzled on the plate. My seafood casserole was deceptively filling, served in a cast iron pan. I had pieces of cod, lobster, mussels and other treasures from the sea, cooked perfectly in a tomato base. Before my orders came, we were given a plate of cheese shavings and bread, both of which were extremely addictive and threatened to ruin my meal. In all, I can't complain about the food, decor and view but the restaurant lacks a certain je ne sais quoi. I would return again for work lunches but wouldn't make the special trip out on a weekend.

Came here for a weekday lunch. Friends had told me this was only so-so, and I agree.Good things first. The focaccia bread was served up warm and soft, though the bakers leaned towards the liberal side with the olive oil. For mains I had the halibut filet, which the waiter recommended over the veal. It was crisply seared and succulent inside, and fresh.However, that was the only high note. The rest of the meal was technically alright but singularly uninspired.The starter, two small slices of raw salmon with pesto, was decent but not memorable. Our second course of pasta - garganelli with forest mushrooms - was better, but I didn't feel compelled to finish it. The pannacotta dessert that followed was monotonous and yawn-inducing.The sugar biscuits they served with tea/coffee after were a tad more interesting, but not compelling enough to save this.

Met my brother and his family for a little dinner and decided to try out this place.  The main items on the menu were the duck, various pork dishes and some dim sum... wait a minute... we were told they were changing that part of the menu.We ordered a mix platter of duck, crispy pork belly (siew bak), and char siu. For our carbohydrates we ordered porridge and noodles.  The mix platter arrived pretty quick and it seemed small for a big dish.  We also ordered some steamed veggies to round up the meal.Surprisingly the amount of food was enough to satisfy 4 people without going overboard.  My favorite meat was the pork belly.  The crispy skin was still crispy and not hard to chew.  The amount of fat was also quite reasonable.  The duck which was supposed to be the star attraction was good not great.Service was pretty good even though it was in a food mall portion of the Centrepoint mall.  Apologies for lack of pics as I was distracted by the conversation.

This place was conveniently located right across from the hotel I stayed at, so I took advantage of it as a pre-flight lunch spot. The large screen photos right outside the restaurant looked mighty delicious so that's what lured me in.There was only one other table besides my party of three on a weekend lunch hour. We were seated immediately and our server brought us water. We decided to get a half duck and a roast pork and roast pig over rice dish alongside charcoal roasted duck buns. I am a big fan of barley tea and as my last meal on this trip to Singapore, I didn't regret ordering it. Our friendly server made conversation with us and mentioned that the duck the restaurant serves is unique because it's sourced from England and boasts in its fatty and rich meat. I was expecting much more from this duck but it let me down. The skin was not crispy but very oily and meat rather stringy. The price for the half duck was not cheap either compared to what I'm used to getting. The roast pork and pig over rice was nothing particularly notable, but the flavors were not bad. The skin on the roast pig was also not as crispy as I'd prefer. What stood out the most were actually the Royal London Duck Black Pepper Buns that were packed with peppery duck meat bites. These charcoal buns had an interesting texture outside and a soft and saucy inside. Our server had asked us our thoughts on their food and we were honest about it as being "okay". This is an okay or decent restaurant for roasted meats but I cannot say they are exceptional. It was a casual and comfortable place to have a meal close by to our hotel.

Stumbled on this new eatery by accident when I popped by Centrepoint via the underpass from Somerset 313.Ordered the half duck ($25) to share with the bf as well as the duck xiaolongbao, watercress pork rib and a bowl of rice. The duck was tender and flavourful, just enough fat for a decadent mouthful but not so much that you feel jelak. The skin was crispy good! I like that the plum sauce they serve has a distinct ginger kick and the chilli, while probably produced in a central kitchen, is the proper fried dried/fresh chilli sambal type you get with duck rice. The duck xiaolongbao was meh. Couldn't taste the duck, it was more like a regular pork xiaolongbao. Soup was decent, brewed long enough to be sweet from ingredients. Oh they also have a fridge full of craft beers from Brewerkz. Service was super. The waitress noticed I'd put my bag behind me on the seat and came over to move the neighbouring table and chairs over so I could put my bag on another chair and sit more comfortably. She also popped by to promptly refill tea cups. #ftw The place is owned by Fei Siong group which runs the minced meat noodle chain Eat and lots of other eateries, so they've got the fast casual restaurant concept down pat.

Royally Disappointed. With a host of London Duck speciality restaurants opening its doors on our foodie island, it's no surprise to see another chain specializing in the "Wagyu of Ducks" jumping in. Opened by the Fei Siong group of companies, who for the longest time specialized in Fishball Noodles, Royal London Duck is located in the prestigious, upmarket, Mandarin Gallery. Looking at the menu and pricing, they are almost an exact replica of London Fat Duck, the first of London duck speciality restaurants in Singapore. Matching almost price to price and item to item, we decided to give it a try to see just how well they stand up to their rivals. London Duck Rice ($8.80)The duck here is a lot leaner than the London Fat Duck version. It was roasted well, and very tasty. We were initially disappointed with the lack of sauce but once tasting it, we knew why they gave significantly less as it would have overpowered the dish. The duck was tender, juicy but the skin wasn't quite as well roasted as that of London Fat Duck or Four Season. The dish was fragrant and tasty and the lesser fat may be more acceptable to the health conscious. That said, a lot of the fat went into the sauce, which gave a nice, rich, smooth coat on the rice, bringing the dish together very nicely. Unfortunately, that was the highlight of our meal. Royal London Duck Black Pepper Buns ($5.80)The buns were semi-decent. Not as sweet as other places selling it and not as light but the huge disappointment was the stuffing. While the sweet bun is usually used to compliment the slight spicy pepper filling, the ones here were over the top peppery. The duck was completely lost in the pepper and, despite being moist and juicy, you really couldn't taste anything else but black pepper. What's worse was that it left that bitter pepper after taste in my mouth after each bite and I felt myself cleansing my palette with Chinese tea after every bite, just so I could taste the other dishes. Royal London Duck Xiao Long Bao ($5.20) Offering something different here, it was a very forgettable Xiao Long Bao. The skin was slightly thick, making the tips a little hard to eat as it got a little doughy. The filling was, well, politely put, forgettable. Had I not ordered it, I would have thought it was just a regular Xiao long Bao. The pork to duck ratio was way off, making the dumplings taste like any normal pork Xiao long Bao. The flavors of the duck was completely lost and the soup in the dumplings were nothing but average. It severely lacked the richness you'd expect after trying the duck sauce. Instead, it was a very light, clear broth that, even in a regular Xiao long Bao, would have left you disappointed. No depth, no punch and well.... All quack with no substance.Despite the less than average food, nothing could have prepared us for the worst possible service we had ever received. Firstly, the senior waiter, expressionless, no smile, looked like he really didn't want to be there. Secondly, tea was served after ordering. Waitress was friendlier but the tea came barely luke warm. However, when she came to refill my tea, it was piping hot. Why serve patrons tea that has set for a while when there's a fresh pot?Than came the highlight. When our duck rice came, they brought 2 plates when I had ordered one. I politely told the waitress that I had only one and she apologized and said she'll check. However, from the corner of my eye, that same, I could feel that same "friendly" senior waiter who took our order, staring at me from across the restaurant. He finally came across, with suspicion in his eyes, completely full of doubt and asked "sir, you order one or two duck rice?".You should never confront your patrons in a defensive / interrogative manner and why would I send back one if I had ordered two?After the confrontation, he went back to his counter, started banging on things and started shouting across the restaurant to his staff that I had ordered 2 and he didn't get the order wrong.  I had half the mind to tell him I could hear him and he should say it to me directly and not pretend I'm not there. After that incident with us, another table had gotten an order wrong and as the waitress was taking the dish back, he started berating her in Mandarin, saying things like "I don't know what to do with you people anymore. This is not the first time, I have nothing to say, you all are beyond useless or beyond help" which is an absolutely disgusting behavior. You may be a senior staff but it is unprofessional to berate your colleagues 3 ft away from your patrons.If you feel the need to do it, take them to the side or to the back, not embarrass them just because you're on a power hungry trip or in a bad mood. That whole experience really spoilt our lunch for us and despite the duck being pretty good, everything else, along with the service left a sour taste in our mouths. Royal London Duck? More like Royal Pain in the Butt.

Discovered this place existed after reading a review on Yelp.  It's located in the newly renovated basement area of Centrepoint, and I assume is a cousin of London Fat Duck over in Scott's Square.I dipped my toe in gently by ordering a roast duck / roast pork on rice, my friend had a wonton noodle soup, and we shared the charcoal charsiew buns.Roast pork was good, but the signature roast duck (breast meat) was pretty disappointing.  Whilst the duck itself was good (lean, moist, but generous fatty skin), and nicely cooked, the flavour just wasn't there.  It was almost like it hadn't been marinated or seasoned.London Fat Duck manages to get the flavour better, whilst also achieving a crispness to the fatty skin.  Royal missed on both.The buns over at LFD were also better - pastry had a better 'bite' and crunch to them.Overall, service was attentive (though it was quiet when we went), and it was $32 for 2 of us, but I would stick to LFD in Scott's - especially now that the hype queues have died down.
Want to be at the top of the food chain? Then you gotta have some Shark Meat Lor Mee. Enough said.

Not sure what to expect with this. I knew it works be noodle to some extent.Someone else already mentioned, the shark tastes just like fish. So no reason distinction as it is battered.There actually wasn't a line when I went..just a guy in front of me. Ordering was painless...They give you a bowl of the broth(which I thought would be more fluid but it was kinda thick...Like gelatinous. I shuttle have preferred reg liquid consistency). Then you had your condiments in nearby bowls.If you are doing take away, they wrap each component in separate little bags(noodle, fish..etc)..so when you get home you just dump then into bowl. It was tasty actually but again I would prefer a more liquid broth as the thickness was a bit overwhelming for me.

To get things started, I don't like my food drenched in gravy. Dishes like Lor Mee, Hor Fun and Mee Fun incur my wrath - how can you enjoy the flavours when everything is soaked in thick gravy? Fortunately, Lor Mee 178 was worth the plunge and is probably the only Lor Mee I'll ever eat. (Please stay that way forever.)Here's the breakdown: you get a bowl of noodles in the thick brown gravy but that's not all, you also have fried shark meat, crispy fritter bites and more crunchy stuff topped onto your noodles. That might be what made it for me. The mix of crunchy with flavourful sauce that not too starchy and good noodles that blends with the sauce. I've read very opposing views on this dish, perhaps from people who prefer to more traditional braised variety but I like this adaptation. I will travel just for this one.

It's so damn hard finding good lor mee in Singapore - also, it seems like it no longer is one of those dishes you can easily find at any food court so that makes the search even tougher. So, in light if these circumstances, Lor Mee 178 acts as one of my trusty haunts I fall back on when I just have to get a bowl.The gravy is fantastic - it has good flavour of the stock but isn't overwhelmingly starchy. What I really like about this stall is the shark nuggets! Actually, it iss really just fried fish bits that sound a little more exotic. The crispiness adds a good texture to the dish. Each bowl also comes along with the usual braised egg, pork belly and ngoh hiang.Ask for extra everything - vinegar, garlic paste, chilli sauce. Best way to enjoy this dish is to go over the top.

My absolute favourite stall in Tiong Bahru market, which is saying a lot given that this food centre is teeming with loads of well-known stalls serving up excellent fare.The broth is flavourful and not too thick, and the accompanying fish is delicious. Make sure, however, to throw in shark nuggets for an additional 50 cents. These chewy and tasty morsels really propel the dish to giddying heights.I usually go a little crazy with the condiments, generously adding vinegar, garlic paste and chilli to the mix... but isn't that how lor mee is best enjoyed? Definitely a must-try, and easily a destination for those looking out for the best lor mee stalls in Singapore.

Lor Mee that kicks ass but might not get you kisses.Tiong Bahru market, another food paradise of Singaporean delights.What to eat? Obviously, you're not one who's keen on wasting tummy space... if not you wouldn't be reading a review.Well, Jonny boy is here to help. Do you like Lor mee? If so, Don't waste time. Order from this stall. Served with deep fried shark meat and super crunchy flour crumbs, this Lor mee is heavenly. Gravy that's thick and full of tasty vinegary goodness. The shark meat (I don't take shark's fin's soup because of the cruel ways they 'hunt' for these but I figure if they used the whole shark, there's no issue) is deep fried and it kinda reminds me of fish and chips, without the chips.You are given free reign of garnishes so I recommend piling on the freshly cut chilli and lots of garlic. Your breath will smell for at least two hours (non garlic eaters would never kiss you) but it's worth it. Corporate rats be sure to confirm that you have no client meetings after your meal! Unless you get them to go with you for the Lor Mee.

When a hawker stall has a long queue, join in. Even if it does not turned out to be super delicious, it won't be too bad either.  Fortunately, the Lor Mee($2.50) falls into the first category. Perhaps what draws regular crowd is the Shark Meat Fritters (add 50cents) and the braised gravy. Mix all the chilli sauce, grated ginger, vinegar, gravy, some crunchy stuff together with the noodles and you'll get a simple, comforting bowl of Lor Mee minus the braised egg and ngor hiong.

Obviously Shark meat isnt the most common ingredient you'd find being sold in a dish. In fact, almost never. But the shark meat lor mee is actually quite nice. The shark meat is coated in a light batter and fried into crispy nuggets. When you bite into it, the meat is tender and you can taste the freshness of the shark meat. It goes very well with the thick lor mee gravy and yellow noodles.

Given the popularity of sharks fin soup in Asia, I find it curious that we don't see more restaurants selling sharks meat. Sharks meat is what gives this veteran of Tiong Bahru market its uniqueness. It serves a mean bowl of lor mee for $2.50 - for an additional $0.50 they'll toss in a few pieces of fried sharks meat in your bowl. Like fish fritters, it tastes awesome when eaten crispy, especially when it is soaked in starchy lor mee sauce to give it that delightful balance of crunchy soupiness. While the fritters themselves were well fried, I honestly couldn't tell the difference between the sharks meat and normal fish, though. Having this exotic dish already also means the stall could scrimp on more traditional accompaniments to lor mee - I couldn't find many pieces of egg, or ngoh hiong in my bowl of noodles, which, if not for the sharks meat, was nothing spectacular. Still worth visiting though, if only to check it off your list of must-tries in Singapore.

Our friends recommended us this restaurant located in the Tanglin Mall, and it's delicious. One of the better QUALITY thai dining in Sing, which is hard to find. I dare to say that it was similar in taste and quality to some of the dishes at the actual Blue Elephant royal thai cuisine we tried in Bangkok, Thailand. But this is Singapore, and any of the quality dishes come with a hefty price tag, even if it's thai food. So expect to spend around $100 for a party of two, without any drinks. While we love other thai dishes, we just stuck with our typical favorite:Shrimp Pad thaiChicken Pad SiewPineapple Fried RiceMango Sticky Riceseems like a lot to share between the two, but the portions are tiny and we were scraping the plates for more. Mango sticky rice dessert was just okay- we still haven't found one that parallels the taste we fell in love with in Thailand.  overall, perfect place for a regular date night or couple dates!

The food is very good. There are some unusual dishes rarely found in Thai restaurants overseas, and execution is quite masterful. Service is courteous and competent. What makes this not a top-end restaurant as it aims to be and as reflected in its pricing is the very dated décor, more comfortable than smart.

Patara is located on upper level of Tanglin mall,  it is considered upscale Thai but that has to do a lot with the decor and ambience.  The food was good but not out of this world good. Thai green curry, soft shell crabs with mango, spring rolls and Tom yum soup were on the table for me.  Enjoyed it all.

Ate here recently with coworkers and the appetizers and food were very good. It is conveniently located in the Tanglin Mall. The service was fine. Enjoyed the food much better than the food at Jim Thompson which is a highly rated Thai restaurant in Singapore. It was better food and a better value.

The set meals are pricey but give you a chance to sample several little bits of multiple chef's recommended dishes. The Green curry with beef was spicy and went well with the fragrant jasmine rice. I also loved the creamy coconut chicken and mushroom soup. The Thai tea is a must have - so pretty you can't stop staring at the glass. For dessert give the coconut sticky rice a skip and have the mango cheesecake instead.

This is a review of a dinner date at Patara Fine Thai Cuisine.It is a beautiful room with numerous ornate appointments.  This is a true Thai fine dining setting.tinyurl.com/bb7lvqstinyurl.com/b3qaxmvThe service was extremely good.  Throughout the meal, they were very attentive and helpful.  The meal proceeded at a nice unrushed pace.The food ranged from good to very good.Goong Thod Saweay (A combination of deep fried prawn in crispy rice vermicelli, chicken and vegetable spring rolls and golden pouches) - Each of these were good. But the golden pouches are the ones that stood out.  Wonderful little pouches hiding away a small succulent prawn.tinyurl.com/bb5xe5pHoy Shell (Seared sea scallops on half shell with chili lime dressing) - These were very perfectly prepared scallops with a touch of spice and citrus.  It was also a beautifully presented dish.tinyurl.com/a8rhvbvTom Yum Goong/Talay (Authentic hot spicy and sour prawns soup with Thai herbs, mushrooms, and sliced of young coconut meat) - This was a good Tom Yum.  My date requested it be mild.  I did not object.  So, it wasn't as super spicy as some versions of this soup.  The ingredients all came together very well.  I particularly enjoyed the mushrooms.  The prawns could have been a touch more tender. But, this is often the case with Tom Yum.  They keep cooking in the soup.  I had hoped it would be served in the traditional way. However, instead, we were simply each brought a bowl.tinyurl.com/bgqfce9See Krong Kae Yang (Pan-seared lemongrass marinated rack of lamb served with papaya salad and crisp sweet rice rolls) - This was a lamb lovers lamb.  It had a strong potent flavour.  The meat was tender.  This was another wonderfully presented dish.  The rice rolls were quite a refreshing balance to the strong flavour of the lamb.tinyurl.com/b5c2pb5Gang Daeng Gai (Thai chicken red curry with coconut heart and baby eggplants) - This was a very good curry.  The chicken was tender.  There was lots of depth of flavour. Every once in awhile, I would run into a pepper.  The heat went so well with the sweetness of the curry.  It was my favourite dish of the evening.tinyurl.com/beym4nsKhao Phad Poo (Fried rice with crabmeat and spring onions) - My date selected their fried rice with crabmeat.  it was pretty good.  It melded well with the other dishes.Thai Coconut - She enjoyed it so much that she had two of them.  As for me, I had 7-Up.tinyurl.com/a2mxgg5Receipt (Dinner for 2) - $204.80tinyurl.com/agxsz9mWith Thai restaurants, there is often an expectation with price.  It is often viewed as a lower priced meal.  However, most Thai restaurants do not provide an experience that works well for a date or special evening.  They tend to be hurried meals with little service.  The food is often amazing but the meal is over in 30 minutes.  The food at Patara is good and, at times, very good.  But it is not better than many hole in the wall Thai restaurants.  The presentation is a step up.  In service and ambiance, Patara delivers beyond most of these and creates a dining experience.  I feel Patara delivers an experience worthy of the premium.Overall - This was a nice evening meal.  The ambiance and service live up to the expectations of fine dining.  The food was consistently well prepared and beautifully presented.

A-OK Thai foodPatara was probably one of the first Thai restaurants I visited in Singapore, and for that, I have pretty fond memories of it. The other outlet at City Hall has closed, so this is the only one left at this time.The setting is pretty elegant, in tasteful vibrant gold and dark wood, and the dishes come in gorgeous intricate plates. Expect all the staples that you would normally enjoy, including spicy tom yum soup (be sure to make your chilli tolerance known), and mango sticky rice. The best dishes are probably the wonderful olive fried rice, with bits of kaffir lime leaves in it, grilled jumbo prawns with lemongrass sauce, and roast duck curry - always a treat with hot fragrant rice. The service staff seem genuinely pleasant, a good indication of the quality of the Creative Eateries group (which this restaurant belongs to). Their sister restaurant is the more casual Bangkok Jam chain of diners.

This used to be my favorite place for Thai food in Singapore, but after having been disappointed with their service in more than one recent occasion, I can no longer recommend this place to anyone anymore.

Tucked away innocuously in the predominantly ex-pat Tanglin mall, Patara's charms may not be evident to those who think that the best food is found only in the high rent downtown district.  As is the case with most higher end Singaporean food establishments, the service is friendly and helpful.  The olive fried rice is superb and the spices and curries are complex in their heat and flavours.  We had the prawns as well as the eggplant dishes, all superb.  Do not miss the mango and warm sticky rice.  It's not cheap though, so be warned. Turns out Patara has branches all over the world, but the one in Singapore is well worth the visit.

They've got a good mango salad with soft shell crab, one of their signature dishes. However the other 2 other signature dishes we ordered were rather disappointing and certainly weren't worth the high prices. Water also comes at premium as they serve you glass bottled Evian water.

my favorite thai restaurant in singapore.pricey, but the food is excellent.the prawn cakes are amazing, so is the tom yum soup, and the mee krob, and the pad thai, and the jumbo prawn.for dessert, the sticky rice with durian and vanilla ice cream is a must have, if you love durian. :)don't bother with the red ruby. it's fancy and pretty, but it's not worth the price tag. (ps. i just looked at their menu online...they don't list the durian dessert anymore. oh no.)

Not 1 night in Bangkok, but in Singapore and we hit probably 6 gay bars. Tantric & May Wong is an eclectic bar which actually has 2 outdoor courtyards plus 3 distinct themed bars. One first floor bar was tantric and loungy. The other first floor bar had a "cool" vibe  complete with the air conditioner blasting and blowing to unintentionally feel like you're in a freezer. Anna May's upstairs is styled as a decadent Art Deco Golden Hollywood era lounge with gilded framed pictures of Anna May Wong, the first Asian American woman screen star. I liked the upstairs best with its unique decor and opulent feel, as if your rich gay uncle was the designer. It was really crowded and bumpy though, if you like that kind of thing.Most of the time we stood outside to drink and watch the parade of cute boys coming and going. This seems to be the only bar with gaysians and ex-pats/visiting gay white guys freely mixing. Since I was here with Dutch friends, we fit right in.
One of the main gay bars in Singapore with multiple floors and rooms. Drink ordering is extremely efficient (they come to you). Gets packed on the weekend nights!

Tantric is a bar that I go to when i want to get drunk for cheap. At $10 for a double shot, it's a bar that one never leaves sober. The crowd is spotty/awesome (depending on your taste) - you'll find a lot of white guys hanging out there, and a lot of Asian boys who like white boys, and the occasional straight person helplessly wandering around the bar, wondering what's going on. No matter what your taste, at $10 a drink, you'll find that things look pleasant after awhile. The bar itself is actually spread over 2 stories with an outdoor courtyard. The upstairs is decorated in a slight Shanghai theme, with posters of an old Chinese movie star called May Wong (yeah, no idea who she is either) covering most of the walls. There are really comfortable couches on the 2nd floor, though they tend to be really popular, so be prepared to fight it out with queens for a seat. The downstairs has way more space, and occasionally turns into a dance floor, depending on the time of the night, and the number of drinks that people have had. It tends to have a feeling of a meat market though at times, and people might get a bit touchy as you wind your way through the crowd to the toilets at the back of the bar. Whether that's good or bad, again, depends on your taste (:

You cannot not know Tantric if you have pink friends. This is an institution and always fun to hit the other gay bars around the area after that. Drinks are strong and cheap (by sg bar standard anyway). An awesome night of gay pub crawl starts here!

I've been coming here for years - and will be for years to come!Great drinks, noisy atmosphere, the place to be seen and see, and it could serve almost any social purposes - whether you're coming in a group, on a 1-on-1 date, a small group of friends, alone (with the intention of going home with someone or alone or to meet new people, etc)... there's so much you can do here!A recent improvement - the sitting area in the terrace is no longer for smokers (you have to be on the balcony now - but since the fans blow the smoke over the seats it doesn't make much of a difference, really) - but still not really comfortable for me unless I have a thirst to be there (and that comes along very seldom), so DYMK or Backstage will be a better bet if you want a comfortable bar - but Tantric is gay-city!

Two-storey bar for the boys, with outdoor seating and a very laid-back vibe. This establishment has been around for the longest time and is just opposite Taboo (gay club), so a weekend night usually entails drinks at Tantric before hopping over to Taboo or Play. The crowd can get pretty rowdy and it is often jam-packed on weekend nights. The upstairs has plush couches and the ground floor tends to be more crowded and crazy and there's standing only unless you are sitting outside.  The pros about this place: - STRONG drinks for cheap prices ($10 nett for a strong vodka tonic) - Good looking guys- I like the music : it's a lot of pop, top-40s and dance tunes- Easy to meet peopleCons: - Slightly grotty- Can get way too crowded, and crowd can be a little obnoxious sometimes

One of the oldest gay bars in the Gay Stretch, I've been coming here for.. a decade? It hasn't changed very much. It's still full of white boys and the azn boys who love them. But the $10 drinks really help, no matter your gender -- or orientation.The shophouse it's in is quite homey, if you can indeed call a gay bar homey. Most nights it's the same: a place you go to repeatedly if you're a regular. On special nights like on Pink Dot nights, it's packed silly to the brim.One of the standards. Can't recommend it excessively, can't say anything too bad about it either.

I usually go to tantric to get drunk, then head over to Play so that it doesn't seem so bad. Also because I like to think I'm an awesome faghag. The boys love me, I love the boys!But in all honesty Tantric is really pretty cool. There are not many places left in Singapore where you can get strong, potent drinks for $10 or maybe even less. As a girl, sometimes it is lovely to hang at a place where you can wear next to nothing and no one will even look at you. Isn't that very first world, progressive and empowering? Service is always fantastic- the staff are cherry and efficient. I especially like the ambience upstairs- theres always some random music playing into the background but nothing too load, the couches are super fantastic and non sticky (who cares they might be damn dirty, its comfortable) and its gets just the right amount of buzz for you to feel happz but still be able to carry on with a conversation.It would be great if there were separate male and female cubicles, because sometimes I really have to pee (especially when I drink) but then there might be some guy shitting inside :(. But usually its not a problem, and the people queuing up for the toilet are all super chill about things like that. If you're planning to pay by card, do note that unlike other places, here there is a min charge of $20 before you can do so.

Among the best pizzas in Singapore, deliciously fresh cheese and tomato base. Crust is crisp on the outside, but slightly chewy. Takeaway is pretty good value for money, as they give a slight discount and don't charge for service. Can't really speak for the service there as I usually get it takeaway. Nice looking interior, looks like a good spot for a date.

A few key points that I noted. The service of this restaurant is the downfall of the visit. The meats are either undercooked or overcooked. When we made a feedback, the Chinese staff didn't acknowledge. He just went to the next Indian junior staff, asked who took the order to pass the baton, and then just conveniently went about his way. The junior staff was just dumbfounded and didn't follow up. And then swept under the carpet. We were celebrating 2 birthdays. Asked for 1 candle to be placed each, on 2 desserts but instead still came 1 candle on 1 dessert. I had a baby, and there was no baby chair until I had to ask for one.  There were no plastic cutleries offered.

My husband and friends surprised me for my birthday.  Wonderful meal!  Portion size was PERFECT.....gnochi was delicious and were many of the other ravioli, squid ink pasta, etc...The Greenwoid neighborhood is quiet and pleasant.  I will definitely return.

Nice cosy location away from the city.. The food is very good with one of the best crabmeat liguine anywhere in Singapore. Good wine selection as well.They also have a brocolli and meat pasta cooked in white wine which is refreshingly light and very tasty. I must say that brocolli never tasted this good with pasta.Overall a nice place with good service and away from the chaos of a mall or the city.

Overall pleasant dining experience, great ambiance for a date night. Their dessert (the Mascarpone cheesecake) triumphs all! 1. Mascarpone cheesecake - Must try!2. Veal tripe (organs) - Pass unless you enjoy kway chap. Cooked in a rich, creamy tomato sauce. Overall good but I am not a fan of animal organs. 3. Saute clams - Very fresh :) 4. Pasta lobster ($68) - A very generous portion. I'd recommend sharing it. 5. Pasta crab meat - Good. Best main! 6. Spagetti cartoccio - Too much olive oil. Pasta was a bit overcooked. 7. Wine - Palazzo della torre ($98) 8. Frittura - translation: fried food (squid, prawns), served with baked potatoes and some cut vegetables. - I enjoyed the baked potatoes but the fried food was just ok. I usually enjoy my calamari but this time not so much.Mains were about $20+ except the lobster. Desserts were on the house (usually $9 each), in celebration of CNY :) We returned the kind gesture by giving the owner and his staff a hong bao each.

A casual and laid back place that serves up comforting renditions of classic pastas and pizzas, La Braceria is quickly becoming a favourite for many other like minded individuals who enjoy good food and a comfortable setting. Bookings are a must, with crowds swarming over the place and almost everyone makes a reservation. So if you don't, expect a long wait before you can try the delicious food on offer -- homemade cheese ravioli with porcini mushrooms, and diavola pizza with salami.

Tucked away on a back alley off the Greenwood stretch of restaurants and bars, La Braceria is a charming hideaway that serves fairly good Italian food at reasonable prices. They have an extensive variety of pastas and pizzas, although if your party is exclusively thinking of pizzas, it may be a better option to hop over to Pepperoni's because the ones here are decent, but not quite as good. The pastas, however, are quite pleasing, and I've enjoyed both the squid ink and crabmeat ones. My absolute favourite part of an evening out at La Braceria, however, has to be dessert - their mascarpone cheesecake is to die for, and it's truly a joy to eat. Definitely a must-try!

This place used to be located on Greenleaf Road about 30 meters from our house.  Close enough to crawl to but away from crowd noise and traffic.  Owners were quite friendly.  Food was decent.  Their biz was helped back then by having one of the worst ever Italian eateries in Singapore  - Cantina - located in the same courtyard.  Will have to checkout the new place on Greendale.  They seem to like streets with the word "Green".  Nice touch

Little too pricey but expected.  Was looking for better food options and variety as I have experienced in SoCal but one here in Singapore didn't live up to my expectation.  $82++ for a weekend night and not having decent food options except some alaskan king crab, eh.  I wouldn't come here or recommend my friends to give this place a try.

I chanced upon Todai on the internet, with its outlandish claim of being the mother of all seafood buffets, I thought it be nice to get my family together for an early Mother's day treat. I rushed to the seafood and waited patiently in line for my turn. After getting all the required seafood I wanted, I sat down and let the sashimi slide down my throat. Sad to say, the salmon or tuna wasn't any great, and I would say it for the rest of the seafood as well - that it tastes just like any other average buffet lines in Singapore, which kinda ruined my evening even before trying the rest of the stuff. However, it's safe to say that Todai does have some pretty good escargot. The western food selection is pretty unique, and the pastries has some of the most wonderful stuff. In any case, have a look at some pictures and make your decision thereafter.

Todai is a Korean-owned restaurant chain offering sushi and seafood. It prides itself as a seafood buffet. It is located at Marina Bay Sands (Shoppes side). Fret not, it's not as upclass as the celebrity restaurants in the vicinity. Actually, i would put it in the category as your regular 3-4* hotel buffets. There is quite a selection for the buffet: Salads & Cold Cuts, Sushi & Sashimi, Noodles, Italian Pizza & Pasta, Meat & Seafood, Brazilian Churassco, Korean treats, Desserts and More! Snow Crab claws and freshly shucked oysters are available too but it depends on which day of the week it is. :( Then again, i wasn't impressed with the snow crabs when i ate it the last time because they weren't sweet, that kinda mean that they aren't very fresh either. There is a small selection of breads and cheeses but they weren't spectacular. The Hot food section is quite extensive with a mix of Chinese and Western dishes, baked, grilled, roasted, stir fried etc. I loved the tempura prawns and i thought they were way better than the sashimi.Being korean owned, there were the representative korean dishes but they aren't comparable to those you get at the restaurants. They were mainly side dishes like kimchi and anchovies. Quite disappointing for a seafood buffet. I think The Line does it better for the same price.

Many people often ask,"What is the last meal you want to have before you die?" A more meaningful question would be "What is the dish you want to eat on your birthday?"In conjunction with their 4th anniversary in Singapore, Todai presents an array of birthday dishes from mainly China, Korea Russia. I was surprised that Longevity Bun and Yi Mien Noodles are served instead of mian xian (vermicelli) and red eggs because the former are usually eaten to celebrate the birthdays of elderly people. It might be good to bring the pioneer generation here to try the promotion.Out of the 7 birthday dishes, the Korean representative, Jap Chae, is the most deftly executed dish as the glassy sweet potato noodles were chewy and not clumpy. Stir fried in black fungus and egg crepe, the noodles released a very fragrant sesame aroma without being overly sweet. It marries well with the Miyeokguk, a seaweed soup that is rich with iodine and calcium. It is my first time trying African dishes like the Jollof Rice from Nigeria and Oto from Ghana. Perhaps due to the air-con, the dish became stodgy lumps of tomato rice that seemed unevenly mixed. A pity because the enticing mixture of coconut oil, fresh red pepper and spice blend suggested a high potential dish. Eggs symbolized purity and fruitfulness and this egg-mash of yam and oil might not struck one in awe instantly but is still quite a unique dish worth a try. Did you know that the "rainbow" cake originated from Russia? Deck in strong neon colours, the buttercream frosted sponge cake is fairly average and doesn't impress as much as the pillowy Green Tea Chiffon Cake, which is the better dessert out of the mediocre crop. Just like the rest of the desserts, the seafood and sushi did not taste as fresh or interesting even though efforts are put in to make them as creative as possible. A disappointment as Todai started out as sushi and seafood restaurant in California in 1985.After tasting most all the dishes, I realized that our favourites come from the Korean Section. The grilled pork and beef were cooked to the right degree with well-controlled seasoning. What piqued my interest was this Acorn Jelly, a gelatinous square that tasted like seaweed with the special korean chilli dressing. There is also a delicious variety of bancai (side dishes) to go along with the steamed rice. In case you are not sure where to start from, head to the Korean section if "quality" is the thing you pursue instead of "quantity".
Above average buffet. Sushi selection is good. Desserts are good as well. Overall better than any todai in the usa. In par with a decent las Vegas style buffet.

I was vaguely excited at the prospect of Todai. Seafood buffet. Oysters (on weekends), crabs, prawns, it was a long list of delicious sounding food.Firstly, they put out oysters in very limited amounts, probably to control costs.Secondly, they shuck the oysters, and leave them soaking in water while waiting to push out the next batch.I'm sorry, but WHO THE F... uh HELL SOAKS OYSTERS IN WATER before serving them! You lose all the 'liquor'. I mean seriously. Just. Urgh.There were a good variety of crabs, Alaskan, Hairy, and Red. The King Crabs were very good, though a little salty, but the sweetness of the meat offered good balance.There was this ginseng chicken soup that everyone was rushing for, but it was just... MEH. Mini-abalone and young ginseng in the soup must've been the main draws because the taste definitely wasn't that impressive.Cooked items were mediocre, on that day there was maybe... one or two cooked items that were good, the Korean pancakes were decent, the sushi and sashimi really weren't anything better than what you'd get at Ikoi or Irodori, and in fact, the sushi was probably worse. Urgh. The staff are also very bad at keeping plates filled. When we walked it there were 6-8 dishes sitting empty, and there was never actually a moment when I didn't see one dish plaintively empty.Considering the cost of the entire experience, I really really wouldn't go back. It's just incredibly mediocre, and poor value... for me.If you're a crab fan, and go there and basically GORGE yourself on crabs, I think you could make it work.

Todai also features signature dishes that are served year round, from snow crab legs to green mussels to cocktail shrimps. I love their crayfish but they only limit to 2 per person each time you queue. The snow crab legs is fresh and sweet. Plus there is a wide variety of selection of food in Todai which attract so many customers. I had to say, i'm upset and frustrated with the service there. The service is one of the lousiest i have been to. Waiters do not clear up my plates. I even have to ask them nicely to clear off my plates as there is not enough space to put anymore new dish. Even after several time of asking, they still did not show their professional attitude in dealing with the matter. For the amount of price spent, i dont think think Todai is worth my try of going back again. The service greatly affected my dining experience over there.

Located at the basement level of Marina Bay Sands Shoppes, many would mistake Todai for an upscale restaurant that is totally out of their reach price-wise. But on a weekday afternoon, buffet price for adults is only about $42++. But my favourite part is how they consider 'child - sized portions' to be anybody below 1.3 metres tall. This is a lot better in terms of fairness since I've seen some kids that at 11 can clear several plates of food!Todai is a Korean seafood buffet restaurant that serves both Korean style items as well as International Buffet items. They not only serve items like kimchi, but also Korean savoury pancakes, bulgolgi beef and chicken, and even bbq pork belly which is usually not seen at international buffets. There is a also section where you can order different types of pastas cooked in your specific sauces and style, and pizzas as well. They have a huge dessert area with at least 10 different cakes at all times - my favourite part of the whole meal.

This place is a hidden gem! Located behind a black door in the Marriott at Tang Plaza is this awesome little bar. The drinks were phenomenal! You are create with a coffee martini as a welcome drink. I had a raspberry sour type drink and then a delicious New York sour with smoke blown into it and a cute marshmallow garnish. I was hungry and got the sirloin as a snack. The entire staff was highly attentive as I also kept finishing my bowl of crackers and it was instantly refilled. I can't wait to come back!

The Other Room is a very cool newish bar in an unexpected place - off the lobby of a hotel and the Marriott Hotel at that.  But they are doing some amazing work here with both infused liquors as well as barrel aged Cocktails, so it's definitely worth seeking out.  Plus, if you ever needed a break from shopping on Orchard Road, this would be a great place although it is open only in the evenings.  Anyway, upon arrival, I received a welcome espresso martini which was served in an eye drop bottle!  Very cool although I opted not to use the tincture and went straight for the bottle .  I tried one of their bottle aged cocktails - Boulvardier - which was really good, as the barrel aging helps smooth out the Campari just a bit.  It was also served with a beer back, which made it doubly enjoyable.  I also tried one of my usual drinks - a Vieux Carre, which was also executed very well.  Overall, I loved the drinks, the concept and the excellent service here.  And it's also great to see a new cocktail bar that isn't on Hong Kong or Amoy Street.  There is a small food menu as well, which I didn't have a chance to try.  But there will be a next time, and definitely looking forward to it.
Definitely my new favorite bar in the area. Ambiance is just perfect for a nightcap and pre or post dinner date. Order the reverse gin & tonic!

The "Diner" set menu comes with five dishes:1. Rice2. Choice of one of three kinds of herbal duck (Angelica herb is fairly mild in flavor)3. Kai lan with salt fish and lime4. Sliced fish in broth5. Fish maw soup.The star was...the Kai Lan.  Stir fried with a miserly amount of salt fish, the lime juice elevated the dish into whoa!  Super interesting in flavor.  Yum!
Good food, fair prices. I really love the herbal sauce for the roast duck, though my mum thinks it's too salty! The roast duck is really really good too--even without the sauce. Everything is fresh!

The regular place we go for when we have celebrations. Service is good as usual. We had the duck, yam ring, mixed vegs, fatty pork & pork floss prawns. Skin of duck is very crispy, but sauce was not generous. We had to ask for extra sauce however was told that additional $1 is required. Wasnt reflected on our bill though. Give the fatty pork (东波肉) a miss. Mixed vegs for balancing our meaty meal and its a good mixture of nuts & vegs. Pork floss prawn is rather dry but prawns are fresh. Very family friendly place, baby chair & utensils provided. Air con is rather strong, good to bring an outerwear if your child is not used to lower temp. Bill comes up to $190. Portion is good for 5 full tummies.

While the decor is really tacky, the food they serve here is top notch. I've been coming back solely for the herbal roast duck. Laced with herbs with a really crispy skin, the meat is tender, fragrant and really sweat. Pity the sauce that comes with it is limited, and they charge you if you want extra. I usually get the duck, together with the spinach with three eggs to make a meal out of it, and I always leave satisfied. Prices are affordable and half a duck will be just right for two people.
