Good food, good service, and good ambiance.That pretty much sums up this Dian Xiao Er.I had lunch here with a colleague.We were quickly seated.  it wasn't long at all before beverages and food were heading towards our table.The staff was friendly.  They were also very prompt and available when needed.The room is pretty straightforward.  But, it is a step up from some of the purely functional spaces you find with some Chinese restaurants.Ten Wonder Duck - This was pretty good.  I did not think it was amazing though.  I thought  the flavor of the duck was a little masked.  The duck was just slightly on the tough side.tinyurl.com/8hvmnwgMongolian Spare Rib - I really enjoyed these sticky messy ribs.tinyurl.com/9yc8bqzSambal KangKing - If you've read any of my reviews, you might have picked up that I am not a huge fan of all things greens.  But, as greens go, these were very tasty.  These are greens that I would actually order.tinyurl.com/9dfxnz7So, as I started the review with; good food, good service, and good ambiance.  I know some people do but, with all the great food in Singapore, I do not consider this a destination restaurant.  But, if I was in the area and hungry, I would not hesitate to eat there again.

A Chinese restaurant that was named after the antique way of calling a waiter to your table was definitely interesting in my book. The dining experience here was quite satisfactory as well. The over décor of the restaurant very closely followed an old period drama style teahouse that we often see in dramas, with the waiters themselves dressed in character. The menu items were of course very traditional, but their specialty was the roasted duck and also their soups. I loved their high quality broths that were boiled for several hours at a go for sure - all of them were thick and not greasy at the same time regardless if it was a meat or vegetable based soup. The duck dish was amazing, and nothing like those roast duck rice that we often order at the local kopitiam. This was thick juicy slabs of duck, with a layer of soft fat covered with a crispy top skin roasted to perfection - best duck ever! Price point is a little higher than I would expect, but if you avoid dishes that are common or can be found for cheaper at a coffee shop, then you should be fine.

Dian Xiao Er is definitely famous for their roasted duck in 3 different herb sauces namely, Angelica Herb, Wild Ginseng or Ten Wonder Herb. The one i love most is their Ten Wonder Herb. Simply awesome. Even when writing the review now, i'm craving for this. Definitely must-try dish in Dian Xiao Er.Together with the roasted duck, i would order Seafood Fried Rice with XO Sauce. The fried rice is filled with seafood like prawn and sotong. Very generous of them. Fried Rice is pretty spicy because of the XO Sauce. But i simply love it.

Its been a while since I've been to Dian Xiao Er but if memory serves me right, or tastebuds for that matter, the herbal roasted duck is quite something. I probably have ordered more things from their menu but the one that sticks in my mind in definitely the roast duck.Each bite was really enjoyable and the meat was tender and flavourful. I should really head back there soon and get a refresher of more dishes!

Their herbal roast duck - the house specialty - is what you definitely must try when you are here.  They offer three types of herbs - Angelica, Wild Ginseng or Ten Wonder Herb - of which I prefer the Angelica and Ten Wonder.But if you are here for the first time, get their set menu which probably helps you sample the best stuff on their menu so that the next time you come back here to know what to order.My favourites aside from the roast duck are the Mongolian spare ribs and their soups which are always refreshing.

I would commit murder for one of these heavenly tarts. Having tasted a whole range of cheese tarts from Pablo to KFC (which was surprisingly decent), Bake trumps its rivals by a large margin. The buttery crust is firm and manages to hold together throughout the plate-to-mouth journey. Cheese filling is the right balance of sweet & savory, which produces the most divine flavor burst in one's mouth. Breaks my heart to drop $3.50 on just ONE tart, but sometimes this indulgence is necessary! Protip: if you're getting it to-go, microwave for 3 minutes to get the cheese filling gooey again!

Before I came to singapore, I heard there are many places selling cheese tarts. One of the cheese tart place was close to my hotel. Bake Cheese Tart from Hokkaido, have a crumbly exterior, fluffy inner texture, and cheesy warm soft filling!! I heard it has up to 3-hour long waiting lines. When I got there, I saw a long line outside of the bakery. But I only waited 15-20mins. If I could, I wanted to buy more but I had to be satisfied with one dozen. It is SD 3.50 per piece.It is just the most heavenly cheese tarts. One of the best cheese tart I've ever tasted. If it could last long, I would have bought several boxes to bring home. It's freshly baked, just so soft and melts in your mouth. I couldn't stop eating them. Sometimes I still dream about the delicious tarts!

Oh my dear Bake.. why oh why, can't you come to the US??? I've tried the impersonators and it's just NOT the same. Last time I visited I had to wait in a long line to try these tasty treats but luckily this time I was able to walk up and get my favorite treat. SO delicious - if you haven't tried 'em you seriously need to ASAP! :)

Full of hype? Check.Lives up to its hype? Check.I was lucky to be at ion at 11am on a Wednesday morning and there were only 3 people in line. I joined the line hoping to try this famous cheese tart.Every customer is only allowed to buy 12, and I ended up getting a dozen, because well, I'm already in line so why not?? The tarts are super delicious when they are fresh out of the oven. Sinfully rich but not too much that it makes you sick. They are pretty pricey at $3.50 per tart, but well, I'm only here once a year.

Line was long but moved fast. $3.50 per and $19.50 for six pieces. The cheese tarts are light and melt in your mouth. The cheese is a little gooey once bitten. It's a perfect accompaniment with tea or coffee. I wish I were able to bring this back home... I am already dreaming of eating more.

Its located near the candy store at the Ion mall. Love the original flavor, inside of tart was light as air almost foam like. The other alternative is the chocolate which i think is too sweet and taste like Milo

Super good!!! Heavenly tarts. But the strange thing is the line was nowhere to be seen. Then we found out that the line was someplace else! How thoughtful of the staff so as not to block the way. The tarts were So Yummy. 5 stars. Go get it now. A tat expensive thought. I guess they need to recoup as their packaging was top notch.

Your review helps others learn about great local businesses.Baked Cheese Tarts are the new in thing people! Especially with the famous Japanese BAKE Inc. (BAKE) leading the trend come 29 Apr 2016 with their first S.E.A flagship in Singapore! Located at ION Orchard, the Singapore store will be BAKE CHEESE TART's flagship store for Southeast Asia. YAY. For those not in the know yet, BAKE hails from Hokkaido, Japan, and that ensures the creamiest and smoothest cream cheese mousse in the snappiest shortcrust tart. The cheese mousse is created by blending three different types of cream cheese together - two from Hokkaido and one from France. The pastry goes through a two-step process which leaves it with a distinct crunchy yet fluffy texture. Absolutely gorgeous i tell you.  To ensure the highest quality, the cheese tarts are actually produced in Hokkaido and flown over to Singapore! Baking is done here so that we can piping hot, creamy and flowy cheese tarts. Such dedication to excellence i say. We can certainly expect the same flavor and quality from BAKE and it's even fresher than if you beg a friend to bring it back for you.For $3.50 a pop, you can dig into one of these rich creamy babies. I can't imagine why anyone would stop at 1 though! Get a box of 6 for $19.50 and share the love (WITH ME PLEASE)!

I was lucky to have my cousin queue for me once so I didn't have to. Tried one of the tarts right away and instantly fell in love with it! I'm usually not a fan of something related to cheese but this is stupendous. Literally the only kind of tart I'd eat again and again in my life. It's just soooo goooood.The tarts are really yummy but the price is a bit on a high side (@$3.5) but I guess that's fine considering the tarts are flown in from Hokkaido and the rental in Ion.Now that I have tried, I really love it and crave it every moment but I wouldn't queue more than 15 minutes. I'll repurchase IF I was in the area, and no sign of long queue.

Yummmm I went close to closing time and the line was super short. I only got one to try but wish I bought more! The cheese tart is sooo creamy, light, a bit tart, and super delicious. It is more on the expensive side S$3.50 but definitely worth it!

I happen to be in the Orchard area on a Monday morning and my first thought was "Cheese Tart for Breakfast!"  BAKE opens at 10am and I arrived less than 10 minutes before opening.  No one was at the queue, so I roamed to the store front to check things out.  The tarts are baking in the oven and one of the staff waved at me to ask me to queue.  When I got to the queue, there were three ladies waiting.  5 more minutes until opening and about 15 more people are in queue.  A staff came out to the queue right at 10am sharp to hand out confirmation cards to the first two people.  10:03am and it was my turn!  The staff looked at my baby and I and asked how many I was getting. When I said a dozen, she was like "oh, only 12, ok, here is your card" as if she was expecting me to buy more with a baby in tow. Thank you for acknowledging my baby as a person!  The cashier was very friendly and informed me that the tarts can be refrigerated up to 4 days, or kept frozen for up to one month! Don't microwave.  Reheat in toaster, oven or air fryer at 200C for 30 seconds to a minute.  Got it!  Out the door we go to try these babies.  By now my 20 month old is screaming "Chee taat Chee taat."  I carefully peeled the sticker off to open the box.  I really appreciate BAKE's thoughtfulness in designing their boxes.  Each tart has it own "compartment" so they don't bump into each other and become mush.  First bite into the freshly baked tart is the crunchy crust that snaps off, then comes the warm fluffy, light and whipped cream like cheese filing that's has a hint of tartness.  The contrast of the crunchy shell and of fluffy cheese filling is heavenly.  I slurped the cheese filling down like one would with whipped cream, and finished off the crunchy crust with the next few bites.  15 mins late, after I settled by baby down for a drink, the cheese tart shells are getting softer and losing its crunchiness.  Now it has become more of a soft cookie texture.  When I got home, put some in the fridge, and a couple in the freezer to try the different ways of eating these babies.  The refrigerated ones tasted just ok.  It's sort of like an over beaten cheesecake, nothing like ice cream.  While the filing is soft, it has a lot of air bubbles, so it's not creamy.  The frozen ones were more like frozen cheesecake, hard and crumbly.   Hubby and my children tried it and no one care for the frozen ones.  So my conclusion is that the BAKE cheese tarts are best eaten right after you buy them.  Enjoy the contrast of crunchy cookie shell and the fluffy whipped filling.  Are they worth 1-3 hr wait? Nope!  If I need a cheese tart fix, the bakery across has lava cheese tarts, while not as fluffy and whipped cream like, those were creamier, cheaper, and no queue.

Came here for dinner on a Sunday night and was surprised to see that it wasn't crowded!! Nevertheless, the food was exceptional and I would definitely want to come back to try breakfast, lunch, and afternoon tea.FOOD: (HIGHLY RECOMMEND)- SEAWEED & WASABI FRIES (Appetizer): The seasoning of the seaweed, pepper, and hints of wasabi make these fries (which are similarly shaped to Mcdonalds fries) seem so sophisticated and inventive. Definitely enjoyed thiss!! Portion wise it was very generous and easily made the three of us full.- HALIA CHILLI CRAB SPAGHETTI: One of their signature dishesss and it was absolutely delicious! At first I was worried that the sauce would be too heavy but it wasn't at all. And they certainly didn't skimp on the crab bits!!- HALIBUT EN PAPILLOTE: Another signature dish which I really enjoyed! My favorite was the buttery soup-like sauce the halibut, broccoli, and mushrooms were soaked in. It definitely helped add some flavor to the unseasoned halibut. The dish also is accompanied with aioli sauce for you to dip the halibut in!! As well as rice and cucumbers which seemed very japanesy like.*When you order two chili crab spaghetti, they give you two Singapore SlingsOverall, a really great experience. Not to mention, the service was really good and I really like the decor of the restaurant.

so disappointing. food, service and value were far below what should have been at such an iconic locationthere was no one dining there when we got there at 6:30pm. that should have been a warning. our waitress barely spoke english. if this was a hawker market food stall, sure, that's to be expected. but in the Raffles Hotel?!?! my colleague ordered a cosmopolitan drink which was one of their specialty drinks and she had no idea what we were talking about. we had to point to it on the menuclearly nothing was prepared to order. the apps came immediately and main courses a few minutes after. we both ordered the cheesy seafood dish (I don't remember the name). cheese and seafood is usually high-risk and this was no exception. no dessert, we both wanted to get out of there, but the price was way too high. with so many choices around Raffles Hotel, including Boat Quay which is just  few minute walk, I will never come here again

Very nicely done food. The chilli crab spaghetti is spicy and delicious. Even my picky mother approved. And it's a great lazy way to eat chilli crab. The fries with the truffle aoili and spicy mayo is good - we cleaned out the truffle aoili. I like the pulled duck salad concept with the cold soba but they could have had a lighter hand with the sesame oil seasoning. Their brunch menu had a lovely pancake which my friend's kid scarfed down. Service is fairly attentive and place is relatively kids' friendly

This cafe offers a good selection of food ranging from breakfast, lunch and dinner. The price is not as expensive as one would expect since its based at one of the most expensive hotels in Singapore. I had the pancakes which is definitely worth the deal. Portion was big and it was tasty. Will definitely return to try out the other dishes. Decent restaurant that offers good ambiance even for large groups both inside and outside of it.

The iconic Raffles Hotel has finally gotten itself a decent restaurant for brunch with The Halia coming under its roof. Afternoon tea at the Tiffin Room is one thing but ladies of leisure still need their morning coffee run and eggs of course! And what better place to do it than at the urban, casual-chic sister of the award winning restaurant. I much preferred the indoor space which has a bit more privacy as compared to the alfresco bar area. Plus the Singapore weather is not meant for dining outdoors, even with ceiling fans. Give me my ac please.Weekend brunch starts at 11am. The selection is extensive with both the Brunch Specials and the Main Menu available for the picking. I've been in quite a bread mood recently and the Assorted Bread & Pastries ($12) really appealed to the tummy. The croissant was delightful and i love that they serve clotted cream with the basket.The Pancake with bacon, maple butter, fresh strawberries & puree ($12) was one of my favorite dish. I always get overwhelmed after eating a piece of pancake but Halia's rendition had me going on and on. I like the slightly buttery batter which was fluffy and the thin flaky bacon was an interesting complement to the dish. If you're more the traditional English Breakfast sort, you'd do well with the Grilled breakfast with any style eggs ($23). What's interesting was the sweetened bacon which was thick and juicy. The scrambled eggs had this interesting layered texture and i like that it was runny but not too creamy. I'm getting hooked on buttery eggs.  I'm not so much of a fan of the White bean Iberico chorizo leek stew ($16) but if you like gumbo and the starchiness of such a stew for brunch, then this would be it. The stew was  rich and starchy with a tinge of sourness from the smoked chipotle sauce. The Celeriac "Lasagna" ($12) is an interesting signature with crunchy thin sheets of pasta. I thought i was munching on vegetables. This was accompanied with mushrooms, thyme, baby spinach, lemon and Madeira cream. Another signature is the Halia Chili Crab Spaghettini ($25). Piquant spicy finish that is typically Asian. The flavor of ginger was rather strong but it gave the dish a fresh note. I could also taste the sweetness of the crab meat. If only they would use a thicker pasta. The Sous Vide Baharat Chicken Leg ($28) was very tender and flavorful. It also had that smoky taste which was well complemented with the sweet butternut squash puree. I was intrigued by the crispy thin skin which had the texture of a baked potato skin. Served with a ginger, coriander and pepper salsa. I like how Halia caters to vegetarian eaters with their innovative dishes. The Mushroom, Lentil & Walnut Bake ($24) was absolutely delicious and even this meat eater was sold. It was nutty, cheesy, savory and sweet with the fennel seed cream and sun dried tomato. I would order this again.As you can tell, the Halia offers a wide variety for brunch and i found it quite perfect for group gatherings. Enjoy!

Ok so this isn't going to be the sunshiny review everyone seems to give Halia. I want to love the place - I mean, I really love the Botanic Gardens. I think what we have here in Singapore are some of the most beautiful - and I've been to many around the world. So, back to the review. Despite my genuine desire to enjoy Halia (over the years I've come back occasionally - each time telling myself not to bother after the dining experience), this last time was no different. Service was warm and helpful, and that was probably the only positive thing. My husband and I ordered a potato and leek soup, burger, and 62' egg on brioche (which sounded so sexy but was anything but). 15 mins after our mains arrived, the soup came -  it was brown, and tasted watered down and nothing like leek or potato. When we asked to return it, we were told it's homemade and definitely leek and potato. We said erm no.The mains, despite the wonderful descriptions on the menu, were underwhelming at best. Fries were anemic (you know, when they don't spend enough one in the deep fryer), beef patty dry (wagyu? Really?), and my egg dish was lackluster. It as as if the chef was rushing off somewhere. So I get that it's a lovely place in the loveliest of gardens. And like most food joints in attractions (or airports), you know people will come regardless. But for the prices Halia commands, I'd have loved if they had a wee bit more pride about the food.

Halia is AWESOME. Service is excellent and prices are fair for what it's worth ($50-60 pp with no alcohol, although we did order bottled water).Do order the cod fish.1 star off because the foie gras salad was bordering on saccharine.. had it been infused with different flavors I would probably have been more excited.

I like this place and have eaten here several times. The service is attentive, informal and really good. In terms of decor, it's a but dark (I guess that's in keeping with the Colonial feel of the Raffles complex) with heavy timber furniture, but it has windows all around to break up the mood a bit. The chef's soup is good, as is the bread basket. I particularly enjoy the Grilled Chicken Salad. Cocktails are good too. I'd come back again, no problem at all. Thanks.

really good food at this second branch of the halia-of-botanics at the wonderfully colonial raffles hotel. this place was impressive - and while it wasn't cheap, I dare say it was rather well worth it. friendly service, a quiet corner of the hotel, and retro furnishings (very appropriately so, and hence not too hipster) - and good food plus reasonable prices: I think this beats many of my recent gastroventures clear out the water. fine dining without poncy starched-up nonsense.the chef's soup of the day was a great start - a lightly truffled bowl of cauliflower puree. our middle courses carried the momentum of the great start: we were very pleasantly surprised by the beautifully arranged plates of cured kingfish and sous vide chicken leg. the flavors were intense but complementary; and the chicken might be one of the best executions of poultry I've had in a while. the skin was well-seasoned, the butternut squash a sweet counternote to the savoury dish - and really a feast for the eyes.their desserts were also really good. that makes it a winner from starter to fin - something that happens too infrequently. the sticky toffee was good - warm, with a slight drizzle of caramel sauce and topped with creamy vanilla-bean ice cream.the ginger nougat parfait was very interesting. almost like a room-temperatureish semifreddo, with a stick of puff pastry and grilled pineapple. it really is a lovely space - it might feel a little cramped if full house, but otherwise quiet and very cosy on a sunday. service was well-paced and unobtrusive, and so many things on the menu that I want to return to. one of the best meals I've had recently, from start to finish. wholly and unconditionally recommended.

This was one of the worst dinners I've ever had in Singapore. And it wasn't because of the conversation.Ordered our food and we waited two hours. I kept picturing that the kitchen must have one guy with one pan cooking and maybe he's one-armed because that's the only excuse for how slow the food was to come out.Also the $74 ribeye (the most expensive thing on the menu) looked horrible but tasted 'ok'. It was hilarious, everyone was asking me "what is that?". They were shocked when I told them it was the ribeye. Doesn't the management/chef/owner know that people eat with their eyes first? Guess Money can't buy them common sense. Anyways, save your money and go to Mortons if you want beef. If you want anything else try your local food court because the service will be prompter and the food will look like what you expect. BTW management, the dinner was on the 24th of October 2013. We paid more than $500 between the 4 of us. Want to comp my meal next time? Because even if you did I wouldn't waste 2 hours waiting for it. C-ya.

I never tried the food at Prive so I am in no position to comment but visually the food at Prive's fine dining restaurant looks a lot more appetizing as opposed to the food served up at Prive's cafe/bistro. The Prive Bar has a great setting with outdoor couches facing the yachting docks. For a moment it actually feels like you're not in Singapore. Back to reality, I had a  mixed berries mojito which was honestly terrible. The ice was not crushed nor blended properly leaving behind mini ice cubes. The mojito was quite sweet as well which made me wonder if fresh or canned berries were used. Lastly, it came in a really huge tall glass which just further emphasized quantity and not quality. I would definitely return but only for the location and comfortable seating!

I've been here for brunch, dinner and desserts and have never been disappointed once!Watch out for the crowd on weekends though this place is buzzing even though its not the most accessible.I enjoyed my eggs royale and coffee for brunch but what's unexpected was how good their mushroom soup was! Creamy, flavourful mushroom delight in every scoop.For dinner, I had the no frills burger, it was filling and scrumptious. Dessert didn't disappoint either with the refreshing lemon meringue pie. Even though it overlooks the marina with a nice view of the yachts and the waters, it's not exactly the most romantic place for a meal because it can get quite noisy. Unless you can luckily find yourself in a nice corner spot, at night the outdoor seating does get quite dark! Final verdict: Great food with one of the best views

Service is terrible where serving staff ignores your presence at entrance. So as per hawker centre style, you can help yourself to a table. Once, I had to help myself to the menu. We usually have dessert, small bites and beer. We enjoy the breeze, ambience and people watching.
Eh. Overpriced and inconvenient place to have brunch. Not recommending this place at all.

Kids friendly with a small outdoors playground. The quality and price of food meet the expectations of a rather upscale, not too fancy cafe-- clean, neat, nothing too special, common but still prepared with care. I visit once or twice a month for brunch for the nice morning view of the marina or for dinner for the serene atmosphere of the Singapore evening.

This month Nom's is organising its first Cafe Week which is happening over 2 weekends on 10-13 Dec and 17-20 Dec 2015. There is 14 cafes participating in this event, offering Brunch/ Lunch at $25/ person, Tea at $15/ person, and Dinner at $35/ person. The cafe is located at Keppel Bay, which is about 10 minutes walk from Harbourfront MRT station. The place looks like a different world from the nearby noisy and packed Vivocity. Here there is a spread of yachts anchoring around by the bay with expensive looking Condominiums in the background. Sounds like a place for the rich and famous. The cafe is located at Keppel Bay, which is about 10 minutes walk from Harbourfront MRT station. The place looks like a different world from the nearby noisy and packed Vivocity. Here there is a spread of yachts anchoring around by the bay with expensive looking Condominiums in the background. Sounds like a place for the rich and famous. Boston Clam Chowder ($14++)Served in squid ink bread with bacon, Idaho potatoes, celery, parsley and clam stockThe chowder is very rich and thick. Best have it with the crispy squid ink bread which balances the salty bacon's taste in the chowder.Charred Broccoli Salad ($17++)A healthy mix of Virginia ham, baby gem lettuce, avocado, spiced almonds, Spanish onions, blistered grapes and shaved parmesan, drizzled with honey-garlic dressingIt is quite a light and refreshing, although I would prefer the vegetables to be chopped into smaller pieces with more dressing added.Next for the main courses which also come with 2 choices.Linguine Aglio Olio ($18++ for spaghetti version)Linguine Aglio Olio tossed with Chilean scallops, sundried tomatoes, bird's eye chilli, wilted spinach and smoked baconThe pasta is quite tasty with the sweetness of the tomatoes balancing the spicy taste of the chilli and salty bacon.Duck Leg Cassoulet ($28++)Duck Leg Cassoulet served with carrots, pearl onions, mushrooms, Brussels sprouts, garlic confit and baconThe serving is quite huge. The duck meat is quite tender and flavourful, although I feel that the sauce is a bit on the salty side. The sourness taste of pearl onions quite stimulate one's appetite.Lastly for dessert, there is also 2 choices for us to choose from, although we are both quite full by this time.Sticky Date Pudding ($12++)Sticky Date Pudding served with housemade butterscotch and vanilla bean ice cream with sprinkled walnutsIt is my all-time favourite dessert which I will always order when I dine here. I am so happy when I notice it on the menu. The story behind this dessert is that the co-owner of Prive used to operate a restaurant called Brown Sugar which served great Sticky Date Pudding. Since then it is a well known fact that it is the must order dessert here. The sticky date pudding is served pipping hot. It tastes sweet, soft and moist, although I could not taste the bites of dates this time round. A great well done dessert.Chocolate PossetServed with summer berry coulis, pistachio biscottiIt is chocolate mousse, served in a jar. It tastes quite rich and creamy. However it is wasted on me who is a non chocolate lover. It tastes a bit jelat after a few mouthfuls.Overall the food is not bad. Comparing with the ala carte prices, having the $35 nett for the set dinner sounds like such a great deal. The place is packed during the weekend. Getting the staff to refill the water takes quite an effort, although they do check with us on the food from time to time.

Have always dined at Privé Cafe and this was my first time at Privé Grill.Service was top-notch and the wait staff were very attentive to our needs. My sole intention of dining here was to try out their steaks.Verdict:- US Creekstone Farms Angus Ribeye Cap (280g) at $88 - this was the most expensive steak on the menu. The waiter recommended this as I wanted something tender and juicy and boy was he right! My only teeny weeny gripe was that I asked for Medium Well and certain parts look Medium to me. Plus, there were 1-2 chunks of fat within the beef which may have contributed to it's 'tenderness' but I can do without the fat.- Appetizer of Crabmeat and Prawn Cake at $17 - our appetizer came as a set of 2 prawn cakes. Order this only if you are famished as the size of each prawn cake is rather large and you might be too full to feast on your main course. The prawn cakes were delightfully crispy and the meat stuffing sat well and didn't crumple as you cut into the prawn cake. Dish was served with rockets which acted as an excellent foil to the savory appetizer.- Roasted Barramundi Fillet at $32 - my partner ordered this and I had a bite of the fish which was amazingly fresh!- Lemon Meringue Tart - we asked if we could order this from the cafe and the staff politely agreed to our request while bringing us a menu to choose from. I remember having this tart a while back and felt that the tar/lemon portion was bigger then what was presented to me. Hmm, nonetheless still my favourite dessert at Privé Cafe.There was a nice end to the night where all the female diners were presented with a small brown paper bag with a wrapped brown package inside!

I don't really make my way to fancy restaurants unless it's for some kind of occasion. Trudged all the way to Keppel Bay for a friend's birthday dinner and I believe I'll like to make my way there for many future special events to come!First their service is excellent. The service staff are well-versed with their menu offerings and they are patient to help you make your choice if you are unsure. For the 4 of us, we ordered the 1kg Australian grass fed Angus Beef to share and it's a decision that we all totally DID NOT regret. Added on to the order with some servings of sides and another main dish - grilled seabass - absolutely love them.If you are celebrating your birthday there, just let the service staff know and they'll be happy to serve up a complimentary slice of cake accompanied with well wishes and a birthday song from the crew. We further satisfied our sweet tooth with a sticky date and pear pudding that's just simply...marvelous. The sweetness of the pear complemented the sticky date pudding well and it was overall, very pleasant!So who's up with a special occasion soon? Bring me to Prive Grill please! ;)
Burger good. Seabass dry. Soup and salad good. Ambiance very good. Ditto on the service. Price Very reasonable. Me likey.

Ok this is not your usual menu. We went to a special wine dinner with an off the menu selection. So the expectation was high in terms of food quality since we were pairing with some great wines from Australia. We began with the starter. The dish was nicely balanced. Though a hint too much lime and could have done with a little more salt. The Sauvignon blanc went perfectly with it. This was followed with the salmon belly, which was very good. It also paired well with the estate Chardonnay. The wine was exceptional and complex going well with the rich fish. For the next dish an air dried beef with truffle foam was presented. Another good dish, though I felt that the truffle overwhelmed the dish a little. Mains was an exceptionally good hanger steak. Perfectly seared and served plain with mustard. It was juicy and wonderfully tender and flavorful. Best dish of the night. Went well with the cab sav. Dessert was nice but not exceptional. The wine on the other hand was very good and was the star of the dish. Generally the food was very good, up to expectations. But the price with wine pairing of about $100 per person made it exceptional good value so I rate this a 5 star, though if I removed the wine and rated the food alone it would be a 4 star. Be aware that we ate at the aircon grill room with a special menu so I can't vouch for the standard menu. Nonetheless I'm impressed to want to come back again to try the normal menu.

Very honestly: 2.5 actual stars for the food, extra 0.5 stars for the ingredients and another star for the location. Prive cafe is situated right in front of a Marina, the perfect spot to feel like you are in Santorini, or Tuscany, or somewhere in the Mediterranean, with a view of the gorgeous (i like to imagine it as blue) sea, and private yachts. Need a vacation and have no cash, try Prive cafe!  It is also kids friendly with a nice little playground where kids can frolic while the adults caught up over eggs and coffee. All the good things aside, food wise, I was disappointed. I had their Prive burger, and fiance had the Ultimate breakkie. The first thing I noticed was all the fresh ingredients, the salad looked fresh, the beef patty looked thick and juicy, I was excited to start. However sad to say, the taste just wasn't there. The beef patty while thick was tasteless. The buns were soaked in butter causing them to lose their fluffiness. And the ultimate breakkie also nothing spectacular. While they didn't scrimp on the ingredients, the cooking would be better done to make full use of the good ingredients they have! Meh, I would still go back because of the location just to give them another chance.

This is a review of a dinner with a friend on a Friday evening at Privé Grill.First, as it is on Keppel Island, it is a little off the beaten path.The room is modern yet classic.  This is the type of room that defines what I expect from a fine dining experience.  My only issue with the ambiance is that, even on a Friday evening, the restaurant was almost completely empty.  This means the evening was missing the energy brought by other diners enjoying their meals.The staff is excellent.  They are friendly and professional.  But, more than that, they demonstrated an eye for detail and took extra steps along the  way to insure we enjoyed our meal.The food ranged from below average to excellent.  It is this level of inconsistency that left this just short of a five star dining experience.The meal was extremely well paced.  The staff had a knack of being there when needed.  The server was very helpful with our questions concerning the menu.  The food came in a perfect and never rushed order.After we had selected the bottle of wine, they brought an amuse bouche of sashimi.  When I communicated to the server that my dining companion can not eat raw seafood, the server quickly whisked hers away.  Soon after, a replacement of grilled watermelon was brought out.  tinyurl.com/dxc3e5utinyurl.com/cvexxd7A nice basket of breads was provided next.tinyurl.com/c2yyzbwWe usually order starters to share.  However, on this evening, we went our own ways.  We shared small bites but, for the most part,  we stuck to our own appetizers.I chose:JAMÓN IBÉRICO BELLOTA  (Saffron Pear Chutney, Tomato Bruschetta) This was very good.  The Iberian ham itself was excellent.  The sweet tomatoes provided a nice contrast to the ham's saltiness.   The bread was simply there as an organic spoon.tinyurl.com/bn8b3c9She chose:PRIVÉ GRILL'S CAESAR SALAD (Poached Egg, Bacon, Shaved Aged Parmesan, Garlic Croutons, Anchovies)First, my friend ordered this without the sliced anchovies.  From my taste and watching my dining companion easily complete it, this seemed like a very successful rendition of a classic.  The only negative was the large shavings of Parmesan were a little difficult to navigate.  They may have been a little form over function.  The salad would have been easier to eat with an even distribution of smaller shavings .tinyurl.com/cju9qolMy Main:NEW ZEALAND "HARMONY" ORGANIC (Sourced only from free-range farms, Harmony's cattle are all 100%grass-fed in open pastures. - RIB-EYE 340g) - Hmmm, with all of that fancy talk, I expected a melt in my mouth spectacular steak.   It simply was not to be.  It was cooked to a perfect medium rare.  However, through lack of seasoning or some other misstep, it was rather bland.  While not tough, it was also not as tender as I expect from a high quality rib-eye.tinyurl.com/c4bfl95TWICE BAKED POTATOES (Bacon, Sour Cream, Chives)This was barely edible.  It was more akin to overcooked baked potato than twice baked potato.  I love potatoes.  I really do.  For me to walk away from a potato, there has to be something seriously wrong with it.Her Main:JOSPER-ROASTED WHOLE SEA BASS (Confit of Garlic Bulbs, Lemon Caper Sauce) Every show has a star, and for this meal, the sea bass was certainly the diva.  It was tender.  It was buttery.  The garlic and the lemon were provided in a way that they were complimentary without dominating the flavor of the delicate fish.  This is how a fish should be served.  Unfortunately, it was hers and I only was given remnant bites here and there.One last little touch, when asked about dessert, we looked at the menu.  We both decided we simply could not eat anything else.  After we told our server, she soon returned with a small bag containing a slice of carrot cake for us to share later.  The receipt:tinyurl.com/d2tvq9vOverall, this was a very good dining experience.  The service was excellent.  All the ambiance required was the buzz brought by additional diners.  The food certainly had some very high points but there were also some low ones.  In the end, we both enjoyed our time at Privé Grill.(Special note: We  topped it off with a lovely and very peaceful walk along the water.  This is definitely a secondary perk from dining here.)

We had the quiche qnd duck leg confit salad from the brunch menu. Great location and tasty snacks/food. But service was very slow and bad. Salad portions are the size of side dishes. Granted we went on a public holiday, the place is either understaffed or staff needs to step up their pace. Overall, the food is overpriced and bad experience despite the wonderful location.

Ambiance is nice, overlooks the Kepple Marina/Kepple bay area. The coffee was good.   I had a steak sandwich which I would not get again but that being said the duck salad, seabass and spicy pizza my lunch - mates had were good. I would go back.

This place has come up in brunch location wish-lists the girlfriend sometimes talks about, so off we went one late morning (okay, more like early afternoon. okay 1.30pm).Even arriving at that time (when we thought most people would be done with lunch, let alone brunch), and it being a weekday, it was still a packed house. Interesting mix of office-y crowd, expat mothers, and... young couples? Seems like As we surveyed the seating situation, the hostesses came up to ask if we wanted to dine from the cafe or grill menus, and I wondered if it would make a difference to where we were seated, but we were showed to the first table inside the door all the same. Menus came out pretty quick, but perhaps someone could come take our order? The staff were incredibly busy bussing tables and moving things about, and considering we sat next to two dudes who looked like managers doing paperwork, maybe they weren't so keen to walk our way?We both ended up getting poached egg dishes, and when they arrived, they looked a little... conservative. I had the eggs benny, and while they were generous with the hollandaise sauce, everything was kinda room-temperature-ish, while I was thinking that the eggs might be warmer? I'd also asked for an additional side of hash brown(s), which appeared in a singular triangle that may have been more at home at a fast-food joint.The mushroom soup was pretty good though, chunky and flavourful, so it wasn't all bad.Perhaps I had my hopes up - after all, this is at a yacht club filled with luxury boats, and I'd heard such great things. Maybe next time I'll pick a quieter time, and hope the kitchen and staff aren't quite so busy?

We came to Prive Cafe for a spot of tea and found it a lovely place for a lazy weekend afternoon. Cakes go for 50% between 3pm-6pm on weekdays so if you happen to be at a loose end on a late week day afternoon, there's a good variety of cakes and such for a good chinwag with a girl friend or two.We liked the fruit tart with a generous topping of pears, mangos, raspberries and blueberries, as well as the carrot cake and the apricot almond cake. The chicken pie was also pretty good and the coffees decent.Service was pleasant and efficient.

One of my favourite places for brunch is the Prive Cafe overlooking a beautiful Marina filled with bobbing yachts in the breeze. This is one of those places that makes you feel like you're on a holiday and far far away from Monday blues. The only downside would be the really long walk it would take to the cafe/restaurant if you're not driving. Best items on the menu would be their all-day breakfast dishes! My staple items would be the Eggs Royale, with English muffins topped with smoked salmon and poached eggs, its everything I'd ask for in a big hearty breakfast. Try out a hot cup of their Hazelnut Latte, one of the best I've tasted! Its creamy and thick in all the right flavours, but not sickly sweet and balanced with just the right amount of coffee aroma. For dessert if you still have space in there somewhere (I'm a girl - we have a separate stomach for such things) the Sticky Date Pudding is awesome! It comes drowned in a sea of butterscotch sauce, a scoop of vanilla ice cream and lots of chunky half walnuts - yummy!Its a great place to take a stroll along the bridge or marina after your meal too!

Really enjoyed the restaurant week offerings at Privé! I'm not much of a shellfish person but Privé put the scallop in a very different gastronomical light for me. The ingredients used towards the scallop ceviche were fresh and complemented the scallops very well. The lamb saddle was nothing short of delicious and highly recommended. Their dessert could use a little work though. Had the mango tarte tartin with coconut ice cream which was more of a strudel a la mode really. Nonetheless both "tart" and ice cream were too sweet and rather artificial in taste. Overall, excellent food.

The thrill of dining here really comes from being next to a marina with yachts on a lazy morning than from the food. It paints an idyllic picture for brunch, complete with the famous eggs benedict. Also, the fact that Prive serves all-day breakfast doesn't hurt, especially for those recovering from a hangover or who just cannot bring themselves to wake before noon on week.The service staff is a little forgetful. But you'd probably do well to forgive and forget too, looking out over these calm waters.

Great location, great ambience, lackluster food. I've been here for dessert several times and brunch as well. The prices are astronomical for the quality of food they serve. If my friends didn't live right across the bridge @ The Caribbean, i would really skip it altogether

Great marina location on the water with a laid back vibe and beautiful view of the harbor.  Food and drink and service well attempted.  Nice location for group dinner or just a quiet location for a drink.

I came here for a work thing, which is good cos I wouldn't be able to afford dinner here on my own. We took up the private room, which was a big favor from Prive - perks of friendship eh? Lots of wine and orders off the Josper Grill - the grill is as good as it gets! Started off with the amuse bouche of crab meat cake, pan seared duck foie gras as appetizer and honey glazed beef short rib for the main. The short rib was.. wow. Just, wow. Sweet, smoky, tender, and it went down well with the caramelized onions on the side. Dessert was a lovely nut tart, such a beauty to look upon. Prive is a lovely setting for a romantic date, but only if you have really deep pockets.

Other than the pain of getting here (you need to drive or take a taxi), the views of the marina and the exaggerated pleasure of dining on a private island make coming to Prive totally worth it. The views of the bridge are somewhat similar to looking at the Rama VIII bridge in Bangkok. The alfresco seats are especially nice in the evening but only with a breeze and no rain prior.Most people dine at Prive Cafe, which serves breakfast favorites like eggs benedict and a dinner menu featuring lamb shank and a number of pastas. You must have the sticky date pudding and you can forgo the Kahlua and Cream milkshake.

Hainanese chicken rice is just chicken and rice but somehow it comes together in an amazing way. Yet Con does it right, in my opinion, especially since the key to a good chicken rice is actually the rice. The rice is the most flavorful thing and it's just delicious. Contrary to other reviewers, both times I've been to Yet Con I've found the chicken to be very moist and well complemented by the cucumbers. I also love love love the soup, since it's full of cilantro (aka coriander leaf). I love how homey and kampong-y the shop feels, having been around since the 1940s. Yet Con will always be my favorite chicken rice. I want to try the steamboat next time I come too!

Hainanese Chicken Rice is one of the most eaten food when one travels to Singapore. Since it is quite affordable, I decided to eat as much as possible with every chance I get.My first stop is Yet Con Hainanese Chicken Rice. Yet Con has been around since 1940s and have been serving the same style of Chicken Rice since then. According to purist, Yet Con is the traditional and original Hainanese Style. I was a little antsy when I saw the deco of Yet Con. I believe that it must have been in business for over 70 years and it is as old school as one can get. But at least, it is Air Conditioned, a luxury as compare to hawker centres. Trust me, you would appreciate that when it is 40 C + with humidity!So what so unique about Yet Con's Chicken? According to CNN's website, Instead of hanging the chickens up after cooking, they are put on enamel plates to prevent the juice from dripping, so that the flavors are retained. The chicken here is really lean with no trace of fat, the leanness of the chicken does make the meat a tad dry. However, I would say it is quite flavoured... flavour of the chicken?I do really enjoy the rice, which has great flavour and quite savoy!Sadly, I enjoyed the rice and the condiments more than the chicken itself..... Yet Con is worth visiting just for their old school vibe!

Air-conditioning and basic chicken rice fare is what you'll get here.  The chicken rice is subtly flavored, the chicken fresh with no OTT flavoring so you get down to basics - tender and flavorful chicken. Place is inexpensive and as you read in the other reviews,  a throwback in time.  Just don't expect service and don't talk to the chef!

Yet Con is one of those places where it feels and LOOKS as if it was a place your parents went on dates at. Hahaha! And I mean this in the best possible way. Much of Yet Con's look is very dated because it appears like it was never renovated since its opening and this establishment has been around for a while. Boasting yummy chicken rice (not the best in SG but darned tasty regardless), yummy beef crispy noodles (生面), fried rice with wok heat, and other comfort food, this is a place that the old faithfuls will go. And prices are still affordable.You gotta love the place. I give this a four stars for simply having that nostalgic favor. And for staying to their guns by serving simple yummy fare at unbeatable prices. Honestly, that's all we can ask for, right? My only hope that tourists will check it out. Manage your expectations. It is not The Raffles Hotel but once you step in there, you will be transported to Singapore circa the 60s. And please....don't disappear, Yet Con!!!

I've eaten a lot of chicken rice my day, but never alongside steamboat, which was a foreign idea to me. Apparently Purvis Street is the place to go for this, with Yet Con being one of two well known chicken rice/steamboat joints.  This place is so old school that I almost felt like I was in Malaysia (which I love)!  Chicken rice?  Check.  Good.  Steamboat with all the usuals?  Check.  Good too.  On top of this, we also tried the offal and hainanese style pork cutlet in gravy.  Admittedly, a massive lunch for three, but we somehow managed to put it all away.  All of the above recommended. Yet Con makes a good alternative to the usual chicken rice stalls a la Tian Tian.

It's the place to go if you are looking for traditional chinese chicken with more variety. Choices range from Chinese hot pot, wok dishes to chicken rice. To me it's so-so. The chicken is not very tender and quite plain in taste. The pork chop is quite yummy tho.

Stepping into Yet Con makes you feel like you've stepped back 20 years in Singapore's history with its retro furnishings - spot the orange payphone and the abacus at the cashiers! Thankfully, it's got modern air-conditioning so you can dine in comfort, though there are the occasional annoying flies that get stuck in there with you.People throng the place for its chicken rice, and the old uncle stands in his usual spot at the front entrance chopping up chicken and other meat. Several of my older friends love the chicken rice for its authentic and slightly muted flavour which somehow reminds them of their younger days - the steamed chicken is served without the usual sauce condiments you get in most chicken rice these days, and the rice is not so oily, but I personally wished it was a bit more flavourful.There are a bunch of other dishes which are popular as well - many other diners were ordering the fish maw, and the pork ribs were pretty yummy. The roast pork had a sweet burnt sauce which wasn't to my liking but the texture was not bad.Overall not a bad dining experience - go early if you're keen because it's a small place that gets crowded during lunch and on the weekends!

One of the most attractive things about Yet Con is that they offer quality chicken rice in the very heart of the city and provide you with an air-conditioned environment to have it in. Once you can make it past the queue you'll feel like you're stepping back in time. What I love about this place is that old tea house feel to the place, from the furniture to the decoration and even the abacus that the man at the counter still uses - none of those funny machine things!This place serves up the most genuine Hainanese dishes that you might find in Singapore, with tastes rather different from how you'd imagine them to be. You'll definitely be getting their chicken rice of course, but the rice itself isn't the regular chicken rice you've grown accustomed to, but is a less oily, more salty, with a less 'prima' taste to it. You might have to try it for yourself - I don't find that I can quite describe this properly...it really just so different from the norm. The chicken itself is more meaty than the average kampung chicken, and also a bit juicier. I initially found it a little uncomfortable because some bits appeared a little undercooked such that you could still see the red in it, but that's apparently how it's meant to be so I trust that they only get the best and cleanest chicken.We also got their roast pork, which I wasn't expecting to be any good in a 'chicken rice shop' but it turned out to be quite unique as well. Very very thinly sliced roast pork, drenched in a sweet sauce, with preserved vegetables hiding under it. There was a bit of that acidic taste, probably from the vegetables, but it was quite a wonderful change from the standard crispy and salty roast pork you usually get. Well, this was really quite crispy as well, but the taste was just different.We ended with a bowl of fish maw soup: very simple presentation, very simple soup, but very generous portions and very wholesome taste. Complete with squid, prawns, fish meat and lots of fish maw and vegetables, it packed a good taste in each mouth. Definitely worth getting.What surprised us most was that for the three of us with three dishes, the whole bill came up to nothing more than $24 (I even had a lime juice!), which I thought was stunningly cheap. Phwoar.

There are plenty of chicken rice places in the Seah St/Purvis Street area (Hainanese enclave, a long time ago), so why this one? I love Yet Con for the dark, thick, rich soy sauce, and for, when you are lucky enough to get it, their roast pork. It's much darker than the usual golden brown, but the crackling is light (can I say airy?), and the car adds a certain something. The sweet soy they drizzle on that is delicious too.When I am not eating alone, we like to order from their zi char menu to supplement the meats--there are some zi char favorites such as hot plate tofu, but the thing to go for is the stir fried fish maw. So good that I could drink the gravy! Steamboat is also available, though I haven't tried it and so cannot comment.I suspect Yet Con has not changed its looks (interior and exterior) or its staff since it opened. There is air conditioning, never fear, but the tiled floors, marble-topped tables (having long since lost their shine) reflect the age of the staff. I am especially fond of the white-haired uncle at the cashier. Do note that Yet Con is one of the more popular establishments in the area, so be prepared to come early, or to wait for a table. This is true both at lunch and dinner. Service is efficient bordering on brusque, but you're here to eat, no?

Amongst many of the chicken rice shops along purvis street, I prefer Yet Con.  This place has been there like forever. The deco can reflect its age. It seems like you are stepping back into the 80s. I remember growing up eating their chicken rice and roasted pork. Well, what is so special about Yet Con? Everyone talks about their chicken rice but for me three of my favorite dishes there are the roasted pork with salted vegetable, hainese pork chop  and steamboat. I love their steamboat soup broth is awesome.  It is not laden with MSG rather it has the flavors from the chicken broth. This place can get rather packed during lunch and dinner time. The service is fast and efficient. On the whole, the people working there seems to be food nazis.

You can actually taste the chicken! Flavorful and not greasy.This place is old school Hainanese chicken place since 1940. The chicken is delicate and flavorful. They have a jar of minced Ginger on the table that brings another flavor dimension with the chicken.Go for the Hainanese BBQ pork.  Crispy pork chunks with preserved mustard greens balance the chicken's delicate flavor.

While others might rave about the authentic Hainanese Chicken Rice at this old shophouse restaurant, I beg to differ. The chicken rice flavor here was way too plain and average for my liking. While the chicken rice does not suit my palate, I have found treasures out of other dishes here. The Hainanese Pork Chops are one of the treasures. This tomato-based sauce pork chops were tasty and flavorful. The pork fillet was well marinated and fried till crispy on the outside, and tender on the inside. Paired with the sweet and sour tomato sauce and onions, the dish was marvelous. This place is one you can feel nostalgic in, as you have a feel of what olden-day Singapore would look like. The setting is traditional and vintage, which seems to be what attracts the crowd.

We have been coming to Yet Con for the last 20 years, and not much has changed about this place, thankfully. The Hainanese proprietor is a constant, as are the staff, the marble tables and the general interior. Food : We like the chicken rice and the chicken itself is decent, but what we REALLY love are the Hainanese pork chops. Sliced to the perfect thickness and deepfried to a delicious crumbiness with a generous helping of sweet and sour gravy, it is a comfort food that transcends generations. The prawn fritters are also fluffy and delicious, but be sure to eat them while hot and crisp. The tofu with seafood and vegetables is pretty good too, with the distinct taste of wok hei in every bite. The steamboat is pretty good on rainy days too.Ambience : Old school. Love it.Service : Fast. Efficient. Good.

I've been wanting to try out Shiraz for a while. It came recommended by an Iranian friend when I mentioned that we were looking for a good Mediterranean restaurant. It's a little on the pricey side, so we waited till a special occasion -- a birthday. When I called to make a reservation, the restaurant offered to have the belly dancer bring out the cake, which I thought was really nice of them. The restaurant was empty when we arrived at 7pm, but it was full by 8pm. This was a Sunday by the way. I found the menu overwhelming, despite being semi-comfortable in most Middle Eastern restaurants.  I think it was the use of Turkish names that were non-familiar -- for instance there were two eggplants dishes that were not baba ganoush on the appetizers. I think it would have been helpful to have sorted the main dishes by type of meat, and also add a short English description in the title (not in the long detailed description), but the restaurant's been around so I'm sure they know what they are doing. Part of the menu is reserved for halal food.We chickened out, and ordered a platter for 4, the vegetarian option and a lamb stew. The appetizer list was shorter, and we went with both eggplant dishes, hummus and the lamb meatballs. The appetizers were awesome, especially the bread. We had three orders of bread, and they were complimentary...although we did order 4 appetizers. I'm not sure if they eventually charge for bread. After the appetizers, we were starting to feel kind of full. Oh, we were a party of 7.The main platter was huge -- definitely more than enough food for 4 people. I think we could have just gotten the platter for our party of 7. It came with a couple of roasted tomatoes and a few slices of carrots, so it was a good idea to add the vegetarian main to our dinner. The grilled vegetables were interesting -- there were the usual bell peppers, zucchini and potatoes, and then more. Roasted celery! Roasted lotus root! They were actually really good! The meat platter was done well, but I didn't find any of the food remarkable.The belly dancer came out after 8:30pm, and started dancing in the restaurant. The arrangement of the tables made it hard to properly see her dancing. After the first song, she danced outside the restaurant at the front door for 2 more songs, which we couldn't quite see. If you're here to see the belly dancer, you're better off waiting outside.The restaurant felt a little understaffed. It took a while for them to clear the plates, and a lot longer to bring out the dishes after the belly dancer gave us the cake. However, the wait staff was very friendly. We definitely had a great time.

If you are really in for a nice middle eastern food this is not the place to go.  Service was alright though a little on the rough side.  Had waitresses that speak English but just a little hard to understand.  Also one was real eager to teach us how to eat the food and stood there looking after she was done teaching :).  Anyway the real bummer was the food.  Grill fish was dry and came with some creamy topic which was definitely not middle eastern.  The only item on the grill platter that stood out a little better was the quail.  Dinner for 3 came to 215 and that is without liqueur.  So I figure most people head there for the smokes?

I tried the Shiraz twin platter ( gives you a good array of their signature charcoal grilled kebabs) and it was absolutely fab. The meats were succulent, juicy and very tasty. And they also gave us a complimentary portion of persian flat bread with hummus, which were really good too.But enough about the food! The most memorable part of the dinner was the belly dancer, who will perform around the restaurant and between the tables. I usually find it quite awkward to watch someone perform while I eat. The food will usually distract me from half the performance and yet you have to show some decent amount of appreciation to the performer. I felt a bit strange throughout the dance (juggling the eating and appreciative smiles and nods). But from my observation, that dance definitely kept the male guests happy if they aren't already happy with the food.

After seeing Shiraz on InsiderTV at my hotel, it looked very appetizing, and while bar hopping in Clarke Quay, I had an opportunity to give it a try.  Unfortunately, the TV version was better.  On a positive note, the quality of meat was good.  And perhaps in a kebob it would be ok.  But there are more variables with a the bread, veggies, and of course, the sauce being equally important, and unfortunately, Mezzah failed to deliver on all three.  First, the bread was all wrong, as it was paper thin - much thinner than any pita or taboon bread.  As for the veggies, there was an absence of any pickled vegetables, so you are stick with lettuce and a few tomatoes.  Boring.  Finally, you get a choice of sauces, but 1). they really skimp on the portion; and 2). they were all bland.  Plus, I like mine with lots of tahini, and that wasn't even an option.  So overall, despite being in a great location and looking good on the surface, Shiraz fails to deliver.

i love Shiraz... this one has late night hours so it always makes me mad when i cant get one during the lunch hours.  but last night when i went at midnight it was pretty amazing!not all of the locations have the Spicy chicken which is amazing!

I think it was someone I was following on IG where I discovered Lim Chee Guan.  I knew that this would be a shop my wife would love trying especially after hearing that their bak kwa was better than bee cheng hiang.  We headed here right after we ate an early lunch at Hawker Chan just to make sure they didn't run out of stuff.  The location is conveniently located right off of the subway stop (just make sure you head to New Bridge Rd and then turn right).  If we were able to bring back meat products home, we would've brought back a few pounds of everything.  We only ordered enough for us to snack on the plane ride home but did get a variety which were all tasty.  The jerky here is definitely one of the best I've had and yes it does taste better than bee cheng hiang (which is just a few shops down).  We didn't do a side by side comparison between the two but the flavors here seemed more well rounded and the texture seemed to be less tough and more palatable.Just wished they had a stand inside HKIA then transiting through HK would be even more enjoyable.  I just need figure out a way to get some of this awesome pork jerky back home without getting into trouble.  Will definitely be back the next time I'm in Sing.

I have no idea why I was here. All I know the 2nd request from my Sister during our Weekend in Singapore is to come to Lim Chee Guan to pick up some bakkwas.I guess I was really lucky and was here at Off Peak Hour as there were no one... at all queueing up. We have the full attention of the staff who was just so generous and let us sample most of the products they have for sale,I love the spicy bakkwas, I can eat that the whole day. The taste of pork can be quite intense as this is the real deal.My sister ended up picking up some items as souvenirs. Too bad I was not that lucky one!

yes, i am a bak kwa snob!yes, i only eat lim chee guan's bak kwa!!yes, you can put me to a blind taste test and i can tell you if it is the real deal!!!:)for the uninitiated, bak kwa is basically bbq meat jerky.and pork being the meat originally used in the manufacturing of this simple wonder.their signature here is the sliced pork bak kwa.and that is what i always get here.but for those of you who fancy some other types of meat, they do have beef and chicken too.so just what makes them so good?it is a sweetness without being cloyingly so.it is a smoky charred bite without tasting burnt ends.it is the distinctively chewy yet tender pork slices that is not minced.it is the exquisite dark red hue that exudes an unmatched richness and complexity.this used to be the one and only branch.then sprouted one directly opposite at people's park which many speculated was not authentic. but now both bear the same logo and shopfront look.and yet the queue lingers on at this original outlet.a queue that challenges sanity as each chinese new year approaches.this year, i heard an unbelievable mention of 7 hours wait in line.and the price was $52/kg.the bak kwa index, as i like to call it, is a gauge of inflation.normally, the price goes up at CNY, retreats a little but still trends up over previous year's price.so after the peaks during CNY, today's bak kwa index stands at $50/kg!the forties mark are now but a distant memory.lim chee guan has since gone upmarket with an outlet in ion orchard and it is there where queues are somewhat sane and in aircon comfort.but for the sadomasochist, who ironically believes nothing short of a 3 hours queue is worth his time, this is just the place to be before CNY each year.

Arguably the best and most popular traditional bak kwa (bbq pork) shop here in Singapore. During the days leading up to CNY, queues can easily snake all the way to the McDonald's at Lucky Chinatown, averaging 2-4 hours waiting time.Often quick to scoff at these queues whenever I see them, I found myself amongst them this year. For the record, I waited approximately 2 hrs and 30 mins before my turn. I still find it amazing how bak kwa is a such a prized commodity during CNY. Customers from Hong Kong and Malaysia can be easily found among the Singaporeans buying kilos and kilos as gifts for relatives. Yet It is not hard to understand why because the bak kwa definitely lives up to its reputation. Soft, tender and flavourful. Not greasy or tough and filled with fat like other commercial brands (i.e. Bee Cheng Hiang and Frangrance).  Once you tried it, you wont want any of the cheaper options.For those of you who have been hiding under a rock or just plain ignorant yet think highly of themselves, they have 3 shops in Singapore. The main and best is the one along New Bridge Road just beside Pagoda St near the MRT. Yes, thats the main one. Not the one across the road at People's Park Complex or the new fangled one at ION Orchard.

Although the 'other' yellow competitor seems to be more common place, my local friend recommended this one, so I accidentally stumbled across this in Chinatown, in between 2 Bee stores!Taste: flavourful, glazy, but what biggest diff compared to home is that it's a lot thicker, chewier...at first, thought this was better value but actually costs more, since you're paying for weight too.Packaging: much nicer here, own logo, a polished feel to it...pretty impressed w/ its history too.Customer service: impressive--these guys would put any hardworking union guys to shame.  can't imagine this tough work they do all day, under pressure w/ long lineups. also allowed to have samples.Flavours i got were: mini bbq pork, chill, bacon and pork ends.  didn't like the bacon as much.Verdict? between the BKH at home, i'd say it's 1A & 1B ;)

Lim Chee Guan's bakkwa has been a family favourite for as long as I can remember. Although I have had good bakkwas from other brand names such as bee cheng hiang and such, Lim Chee Guan's bakkwa has been the most consistent in terms of flavour and texture. It has almost become a family tradition to queue for the bakkwa at Lim Chee Guan during the festive period. While it indeed seems pretty ridiculous to be standing in line for 2-3hours, the standard of bakkwa you get from Lim Chee Guan cannot be found elsewhere.

Despite being expensive and oily, the many customers who frequent Lim Chee Guan every day are living testimonies to the bahkwa's tastiness. There are even those who buy up to 2 or more kg worth of bahkwa for the entire family, I'm guessing, maybe to make their time in the queue worth their while. I usually try to go during off-peak periods since I mostly buy for myself and don't need a lot, which makes queuing up seem incredibly tiresome.The bahkwa is not too sweet and fragrant, with a nice chewy texture. For a Chinese New Year celebration, I'd say that this is absolutely essential in any household to entertain guests.

La salsa is located at 11 Dempsey road, away from bus stops and mrts'. So bring a car or include taxis on your budget. Live band performance starts at 10pm and ends at midnight. Good thing Nick has a good voice and band, what he lacks in movement and audience interaction is compensated by his effortless singing. When my friends told me we are having a mexican friday night out. What comes to mind is songs like (Besame Mucho, or fast dance song with people wearing big hats, flowy flowery dress Etc) but the band play songs of sam smith, jessie j, adam levine etc. Two thumbs for their performance. The place is not big but just right to enjoy. They have wide selection of drinks and foods. I tried mai tai and quesadilla and nachos. And wow "The best nachos ever!" Can't help but have second servings. The staff are friendly and very attentive.

Authentic Mexican food isn't doused with seasonings and certainly not taco seasoning, so I found La Salsa much like the real deal. The restaurant has a nice ambience with a friendly and efficient staff to boot.My only complaint would be that our meals came out at different times. A minute or so would be fair.  However, there was an unpleasant stretch of time between our meals being delivered to the table. Not a typical Mexican pairing and being a lover of Moscato, I had Moscato (in which I was a bit shocked to see on the menu) and the chicken chimichanga.  Both were delightful.

Real Mexican - not Tex-Mex!  Great, fresh food and really good salsa (as their name would imply).  Queso Fundido and mole are superb.  Nice facility, great live music, pleasant, attentive staff - owners are on hand most of the time - great Mexican - Gracias!
Drunk review! Best Mexican food in Singapore! Stop searching. Kurobuta pork burritos great. Magaritas strong. Ribeye fajitas yummy. Pollo con molle chocolatey!!

This is a review of dinner with colleagues at La Salsa.tinyurl.com/a7uzgsuThe ambiance, while not extravagantly so, did have leanings towards Mexican decor.  It has an open and airy feel to it.  It is also quite colourful.tinyurl.com/ahwzu6qThe staff was friendly and professional.  Throughout the meal, the service was timely.There were no complimentary chips and salsa.  For a full service Mexican restaurant, this is a fail.  If you are going to charge $20 to $30 (and beyond) for relativity average Mexican entrees, there should be nice warm chips and salsa on every table.Tacos - My colleagues ordered beef tacos and chorizo tacos.  They then shared them so that they all had some of each.  They looked appetizing.  My colleagues seemed to enjoy them.  They were well presented but had too much lettuce.tinyurl.com/ard63rlSteak Fajitas - This was my main.  The meat was tender and they were very generous with the amount of steak provided.  It also had a nice mix of seasonings.  They were super stingy with the condiments though.  There was barely enough of each for one fajita taco, much less four.  Also, the quality of the condiments was very low.   No one in Mexico would make baby puke guacamole like that.  It was bland, bland, and bland.   The salsa wasn't much better than Tostito's, straight out of a jar.if they want to contact me, I will show them how to make real guacamole and salsa.This is what  salsa & guacamole should look like - tinyurl.com/ar6ektyThey also did not provide any beans and/or rice with the fajitas, epic fail!The steak saved this dish.  Because, in the end, meat on a tortilla is pretty good.   But the lack of condiments and sides definitely detracted from the overall fajita experience.These were the most expensive fajitas I've ever eaten and not even close to being the best.Fajita Steak - tinyurl.com/ajebtrtFajita Condiments (what there is of them) - tinyurl.com/awo878zReceipt ($116.52)For Mexican food, this was a pretty pricey meal for 4 people.  If they hadn't been stingy with some key ingredients, I would not have an issue with the cost.  The food just didn't quite live up to it though.tinyurl.com/a842829Overall - La Salsa has a nice room and the service was solid.  The food was inconsistent.  There were weaknesses in some core ingredients.  There were aspects missing.  In other cases, they were not very generous with portions.   This could have easily went either way.  With a few more weaknesses, it would have been a two star review.  With a little more thought into the food, it could have been a four star experience.  I am splitting the two and leaving it as a three star review.

Their food was delicious! Was really impressed. Only issue was how small their outdoor smoking area was, there wasn't any space left although inside was empty. But in general it was a really good experience. I was told that they have Mexican style hotdogs here by a friend, but I was slightly disappointed that they didn't. Must have been taken off the menu due to lack of popularity which seems crazy... Who wouldn't want a Mexican style hotdog!?

while not the best Mexican food i have had it was not bad in a pinch.  i loved the chips and salas and the queso was pretty good as well.the beef tacos were almost like the old El Paso type you make at home in the states, but the meat was a little off tasting.  it was almost like they didn't have much taco seasoning.  but still not badthe fajitas looked the part and they had all of the stuff you need to make one.  what caught me off guard was that the chicken had more of a curry flavor than a tex-mex flavor.all that being said, i will be back as part of a progressive dinner... this will be the apps part where i eat loads of chips, queso and salsa!

My expectation for Mexican food in Singapore are pretty low and yet, I still want the same kind of tacos I got in America.  The beef tacos at La Salsa, while slightly closer to Taco Bell than desired, hit the spot and make me happy.  The live music and excellent margaritas pull this into a satisfying eatery for me.  I do think it is a bit over priced since my tacos didn't come with beans and rice.  The service we received was great.

I really try to temper my expectations for mexican food in singapore since I have yet to meet a mexican here.  But to be honest in the past few years Ive seen a few new places open up and I cant really say that la salsa is all that great.  Its ok if you just want a burrito and a quick mexican fix but I wouldnt say its as good as some other spots here.  They do the basics but the menu really isnt all that extensive.  The ambiance is average but nothing exciting.    The staff is very friendly and attentive.  I enjoy the burrito here. The fajitas are good but way too expensive for what you get.  I know this is singapore but the lack of free chips and salsa is really annoying.  Its just not a real mexican restaurant without it.  Its a nice spot to just come grab a drink and chill in dempsey.  Its not bad its just not great.

Nice sandwich place, very casual and with a good offer of food and quite good quality for the price paid. It's not exactly cheap, but it's in a prime position so I found the food/price mix correct in the end. We had a burgher and a BLT sandwich, all very nice and well presented. If you are in for a quick bite it's a nice place to go.

Really like the way the cafe is set out - open, with high ceilings, huge glass windows surrounding the place allowing lots of natural light to come in - its a great place to stop for a coffee in such a convenient location just 2 mins walk from somerset MRT. Of course we all know that they coffee here is done really well - a little strong for me personally, but that's really a matter of preference.Of special mention however should be their Arancini - fried mushroom risotto balls that ooze flavour and cheese.  I have yet to try a better arancini elsewhere and it has me constantly going back for more!

Coffee here started out very good, but became only okay after a while. Food quality is quite inconsistent; the same pasta that I enjoyed can taste too peppery and bland on the next visit.Brunch is okay, nothing to shout about. Given that everything's average and you come here on a chance that you may get lucky with food/coffee that day, there's however something about this place that makes it great to hang about with friends (maybe not the nights with live music when you have to compete with the booming amps). If you sit outside, you can also watch all the beautiful people go by.I'd still give Oriole 4 stars, because I like it there when I'm with a group of friends, it's a nice feeling, and I really want to like this place and think it has the potential to be better.

Great coffee! i love the latte and the affogato. the vanilla ice cream they use in the affogato is deelish.  some days they have buy 1 get 1 free deals if you're using american express.this is also one of the places that have captain morgan spiced rum :)

The good: Attentive staff, tasty latte, good location for people watching. Will return to try their brunch because it looked good. The bad:  Food was average at best.  My Cuban tasted like it came from a P3 baking class.   The ugly: Has a little bit of everything, which makes its difficult to tell what the place really is. Cafe? Bar? Restaurant? Fusion?  I've been a few times and I still have no idea.

As others have said it used to be good, and not it's alright. Not great. Not even good most days. It's a pity because there was so much hype. Someone somewhere won a barista competition. It hasn't trickled down to the rank and file.The food is also average. So is the coffee. It's still a good meeting spot if you're in this area, though, but these days I would rather go to Brotzeit right across where I know I can get beer and okay stuff overall, than pay similar prices at Oriole, whose USP should be the coffee, but it isn't anymore.

Located conveniently in the heart of town, Oriole Cafe is a staple of the crowds of Orchard Road looking to perk themselves up with a caffine rush or to pick up some good nosh. I had a meal there during the festive season during which they dished out pretty unique bites like Ali Baa Baa ($16) is a unique offering where a tasty grilled Turkish lamb patty is paired with haloumi cheese, baba ghanoush, tomatoes and flat bread. For the ones with a well-travelled taste palette, the spices of the Middle East offers pleasurable flavours in one hearty burger. The Cod Fish Hash ($21) of smoked Norwegian cod fish, potato and poached egg.I was especially looking forward to some coffee since Oriole Cafe is known for its blends.
