Went to eat at this Vegetarian restaurant on a saturday and almost had no seats due to it being reserved to the max.  This was our first time there.Wife had the lunch set which by the way is 7days / week.I ordered Fritters and the lasagna.Soup of the day of Pumpkin was very good (9.5/10), though we both thought a perfect 10 score would be warranted if it was abit thicker.Fritters of eggplant and parsnip was very good as well.  Never knew parsnip could be so good ! Then came the lasagna... omg... it was very very good considering it is a vegetarian version.The chocolate cake and ice cream as some of the reviewers had mentioned was heavenly. oh, and not to mentioned our 2 kids (2.5 years and 8 months) was with us, and we really appreciated the restaurant / waiter accommodated when we found my daughter loved the soup and we asked for an additional small serving.  They were very kind to oblige.overall we want to go back again to try out other offerings... Very high potential that this will be my wife's new favorite restaurant !

We used to come here (and its sister restaurant and neighbour Michelangelo) a lot when it first opened in the mid-90's, then stopped when more exciting Italian dining options became available 10 years ago. For some reasons, Original Sin has always attracted a heavily-expat clientèle. It is interesting to note that the customer mix has changed from primarily European to primarily Indian, reflecting the changing expat community in Singapore. What has not changed? First, the décor, which now looks distinctly dated, down to the stains on the bench and chairs! Secondly, the food remains delicious, although one notices changes in the menu - maybe to accommodate new customer preferences? (They now serve veggie tandoori, and moved veggie burger out of the main menu). Prices are not high (especially the set lunch which is very good value). Service is knowledgeable and competent (unlike at the outlet next door). So, I guess we would go back here again!

Great location - two minutes walk from Holland Village MRT station.Came here on a Thursday night for date night, because I felt like a vegetarian dinner.I was pleasantly surprised, despite not knowing what to expect.We had the:1. Mezze PlatterA Middle Eastern platter with a selection of dips. Hummus chick pea dip, Aromatic pumpkin and carrot, Eggplant baba ganoush, Yogurt tzatziki, served with Falafel balls and ciabatta bread. (Summaries copied from the Original Sin menu)Oh my, this platter has amazing bread, freshly baked, and the hummus/eggplant were pretty darn awesome.2. Magic Mushroombaked Portobello mushroom with ricotta cheese, spinach, pesto, topped with a tomato basil sauce and mozzarellaI wanted an additional serving of this but my companion stopped me, because he wasn't sure about the size of our mains. Boohoo.3. Spanakopitabaked ricotta, spinach, feta and filo pastry served with grilled portobello and mixed vegetable ratatouilleQuite nice, but nothing special.4. Moussakabaked layers of char-grilled eggplant, potato, tomato and lentils, infused with middle eastern spices, topped with a white sauceI didn't like this because it was filled with lentils and tasted like a completely veggie lasagna. I would not order this again.I would come back, but maybe for the starters and different mains. We didn't have dessert here because they had a very small dessert selection and 2am was right opposite... But that's a separate review.

Friends recommended this place due to its location and food. Location is especially nice and quiet and not in a mall :-)The impression over the phone was a big let down thanks to an unfriendly lady taking the reservation. After we arrived at the place we were surprised by the nice interior but again the staff was not really welcoming without maybe one exception. Service is okay but nothing special .... And that's exactly what makes a restaurant different to others. Staff seemed not overly interested or charming. The mushrooms as starter were fantastic, calzone was average because of the dough. The other meals were good. Overall we enjoyed the evening thanks to the quiet atmosphere and having dinner outside a mall, but this place could be so much more with a few little improvements. We will anyway come again to try the rest of the menu. We would rate 3.5 if possible.

My meal at Original Sin was very enjoyable, but other than the fact that it was vegetarian and still awesome, it wasn't particularly memorable. If I could only eat vegetarian cuisine, or was dating someone that was vegetarian, or was vegetarian once a week, I'd probably rate this place 4 stars. But since vegetarian for me is a non-existence craving (I go when I want to really change things up, when I'm feeling very jaded, or very unhealthy), that makes Original Sin just A-ok. The Beetroot salad my companion and I shared was rather underwhelming. The salad snob that she is, she found the use of iceberg lettuce vaguely disappointing (the current online menu seems to indicate this has changed; it now says spinach instead of lettuce) and overall it just wasn't a particularly memorable salad, as salads go. Beetroot does not a star make unless it's been treated special or given a good supporting cast.The mains on the other hand, were delicious. The Spanakopita and Lasagna were both hearty, flavourful, absolutely addictive, and very filling. Just typing about it now is making me crave it. And considering I started writing this review over 6 months ago, maybe it's time to revisit Original Sin. Right after I satisfy my steak craving that is.

I rarely am a fan of vegetarian restaurants, but this one is an exception. This place takes vegetarian food to a different level - all dressed up and ready for prom!We had Mezze Platter for appetizer - the baba ganoush was excellent and so were other options on the platter.For the main course we had the following -Risotto - nice and creamy and cooked perfectly.Absolut - the pasta was yummy and the vegetables were cooked well and the flavor of the sauce tied it all together!Service was a tad bit too slow for my liking but the entire experience was very good.

Chipbee garden is for the more mature holland v crowd (except for the daily scoop), people who just want to chill out and enjoy a good meal in a nice ambiance and most of them enjoy wine and italian food. Original sin perfectly suits the strip. Nice ambiance, relaxing vibes, good wine, service staff is well trained and properly dressed etc. Everything seems right... except for the food. That is just plain and boring. Even a little bit more salt would do wonders. Trying to cut back on meat myself, I hope Original Sin doesn't turn people away from dining out vegetarian. If you want to go vegetarian a better option is to order a risotto at da paolo ristorante or get a mushroom truffle pizza at da paolo pizzabar down the street.

Had lunch with co worker here. I lived in HV area and  I haven't tried this place until recently. Highly recommended for vegetarians or anyone who eats healthy to indulge in! It is pricey for what it is but yes, it is sinfully delicious!

Yay fancay veggie restaurant in Singapore!Came here for brunch with friends. I already knew it was ganna be pricey - so i was pleasantly surprised with the lunch set menu, which I thought was a really good deal.the set  (for S$27 + tax/etc. = $30 sing) gets you:1) Soup/Salad/ or healthy juice2) choice of a main - I got the hummus wrap , my friend got the tofu burger (there are like 2 or 3 more other choices i forget)3) chocolate cake & coffee (REALLY good cake...comes topped w/ vanilla ice cream and was good coffee too)Another friend ordered the Mussaka - which was really hearty.  We also got the platter of cibatta bread, hummus, babaganoush, feta cheese, falaffel, olives, etc. Overall really enjoyed the food. The menu looks great - lots of  veggie italian choices, next time i'd like to try their veggie ratatouille =)
I don't always eat at vegetarian restaurants, but when I do, I eat at Original Sin.

It can be hard to find restaurants, especially in Asia, that understand vegetarianism, so naturally I was so excited to try Original Sin! The wait staff were fantastic - very friendly and happy to accommodate special requests. My girlfriends and I had a beautiful set lunch and the food was so delicious! Will definitely be returning.

Great little place in Holland Village. Even though it's vegetarian, it has a broad menu full of options. I had the capsicum with quinoa (and great tzasiki.) It came with olives and tomatoes and a side salad. it was all was delicious. My friend had the broccoli pesto and loved that as well. They had a nice wine list and the prices were pretty decent. They can also make items many items gluten free (but sadly not the pizzas.) It's a nice place to sit on the patio and enjoy a meal. It started to get real busy around noon so you may want to arrive early for prime seating.

Great vegetarian restaurant with vegan options as well in the Holland Village area.  A bit pricey compared to other places, but definitely worth it. Went there with some colleagues. I had the Strozza Preti; great combi of pasta and veggies.

Original Sin specialises in vegetarian cuisine that has Mediterranean-inspired flavours. The restaurant feels very sophisticated and posh, and can come across as a little high cuisine rather than casual dining. I was definitely impressed with the décor and the ambience, and had high expectations of the food.The party I came with was certainly not let down by either the service or the quality of the food. The portobello mushrooms (or Magic Mushrooms) were juicy and flavourful, and we could not get enough of them. The Mezze Platter was also a instant crowd favourite, with the hummus dip and eggplant being particularly mouth-watering. Having had the perfect appetiser, our entrees only continued the momentum. I doubt I had ever gushed over vegetarian food before coming to this restaurant.Do note that prices are rather steep at this restaurant: be prepared to pay above $40 per person if you intend to have an appetiser and mains for each. I'd recommend you try this once - if only to challenge your conception of vegetarian food and how tastefully it can be done.

I made a huge mistake by taking a seat before looking at the menu and finally realized it is a Vegetarian restaurant! Don't get me wrong, I am open to tofu burgers and all things vegetarian but I was in the mood for some meat that night. The surrounding restaurants were packed so I decided to stick it out and stay. Nothing in particular on the menu caught my eye so I just played it safe and went with a risotto. I think it was a mushroom based one. Risotto to me is like Italian porridge and if done right, it could pack quite a load of flavor. The one I had at Original Sin was a tad bit bland  or maybe it was my taste-buds that were being stubborn. Either way it just tasted like comfort food without the meat. Not much to rave about but great environment to enjoy an alfresco dinner!

It's nice to have a vegetarian restaurant in this area and Original Sin does OK. There's a nice environment and the food isn't bad, but it's not inventive or extraordinary either. The menu is mostly pizzas, pastas and salads. There's a risotto and a soup and a few good but overpriced appetizers. The food is hit or miss. I have had tasty items but the potato leek and cauliflower soup could have easily been from a can. Try it once and see for yourself but don't get over excited or you may be disappointed.

If you love vegetarian food, this is probably one of the best places in Singapore.  We had the Meza platter as starter and then the Bosco Misto and Risotto.  All was wonderful and there is also a great winelist.  You will need a reservation on the weekend.  I am giving it only 4 starts because the menu hasn't changed much over the past few years, but hey - never change a winning team... - !

First glance.  This is off the hook.  Service is exceptional and of course it would be.  Tonight was crab and lobster night. I've never seen so many types.  We got our moneys worth in the first two giant crab claws...and didn't stop there. Breads were really good.  Fun selection of tastes.  Lamb and roast were perfectly done.  Mashed potatoes holy geez. Best mashed potatoes ever.  Desserts the Genoa and linzer torte were brilliant. The flavors made me want to cry for food joy. We are walking out with food babies.  AMEX cars holders gets you 15% off.  That's a deal.

This buffet seems impressive at first glance, but you're probably better off going elsewhere. The price seems a bit expensive, but you get a free flow of fruit juices so it isn't that bad after all.The variety of food on offer is pretty good, though it pales before the Line (certainly I didn't see many of the premium items other reviewers mentioned, though it might be because I was there for weekday lunch). And they had the horror that is chicken ham and none of the proper stuff.The food quality on the other hand is slightly uneven - some dishes were good, some were mediocre, but most were alright. Overall the food quality was below what you would find at a premium buffet in Singapore.For example, the Indian curries were bland (though the tandoori chicken was really flavourful, yet the tandoor fish and lamb were forgettable), and the naan was not very fresh. The other food sections followed this pattern. The many duck dishes in particular were all slightly overcooked - possibly because they had been stewing in the buffet section for too long.The desserts on the other hand were the most disappointing part of the buffet: the waffles were dry and overcooked ,and some of the cakes were dry too. Meanwhile the ice cream had a few ice crystals in it, and the flavour was only alright (not quite premium level). None of the desserts had the wow factor.On the up side, the service was good - they took away plates quickly, and quickly folded my napkin though I wasn't away from my seat for very long (and the restaurant was quite crowded).

This is the international buffet place inside the Mandarin Oriental Singapore. On this visit, decided not to go for the buffet, but the Hainanese chicken rice instead. The flavour and the sauces of the Hainanese chicken were quite authentic and good. However, the texture of the chicken was somewhat on the tough side, not tender enough. The decoration and service are similar to what one might expect from a modern, international 5-star hotel. Quite good, but within expectation.

Say hello once again to one of the best buffets in Singapore! Melt Cafe at Mandarin Oriental, Singapore is back, prettier and better with their all-day dining buffet offering.Melt Cafe got it right by tantalizing us with the extensive dessert and patisserie counter right at their doorstep. But if you are savory sort, you're not that far away from the fresh seafood counter where you'd be greeted with neat stacks of shellfish and crustaceans, sashimi, sushi, and cold cuts. While people were distracted by the seafood (which is quite the standard fare at buffets), i went exploring and found the a la minute Japanese Wagyu beef Shabu Shabu live station. O.M.G. Way too many servings of the tender beef over flavored Japanese rice.At the Chinese food live station, there's the super rich Boston Lobster laksa (though we didn't quite taste the lobster), and not so Drunken Herbal Prawns.A small roast and carving corner presents decent meats which were quite juicy despite it being on the buffet counter. Cook-to-order pastas can also be customised with a choice of toppings and sauces.Melt is known for their Indian cuisine and it remains a top favourite. Their freshly made naans are the best! Ask them for the cheese ones, they are really amazing with the different types of spicy curries and Tandoori meats.There're also the European and Asian spreads which offer a variety of soups, vegetables, rice and meats. The garlic bread is perfect with the white wine mussels! Head outdoors for some alfresco dining amidst lush greenery while enjoying a special barbecue showcasing grilled lamb and beef steaks as well as seafood and roasted vegetables during dinner. Save some space for the desserts! I was crazy about their freshly made crepes with filled pastry cream (ask for more), topped with the rich and creamy ice cream (loved the chocolate and vanilla). Of course cakes and chocolate fondue cannot be missed. Skip the macarons though, you wouldn't get them in your mouth anyway because they crumble so badly (just as well). The cheese selection, though small, was decent. The price is fairly reasonable imo.Lunch: $62/pax (Mon - Sat)Dinner: $78/pax (Sun - Wed), $88/pax with bbq (Thu - Sat)Sun Brunch: $98/$158/pax (latter with free flow Veuve Cliquot champagnes, wines, cocktails, beers, juices and soft drinks). Overall, quality over quantity does it for me. Melt Cafe is definitely a decent and affordable buffet option in the city.

We are very impressed by the spread of food presented in the breakfast buffet. Being hotel guests at the MO, we are certain we needn't look elsewhere for breakfast options. Local favorites like nasi lemak, roti prata, fish ball noodles, assorted congee and exotic fruits nestled among galore of pastries, breads, meats and desserts...one is surely spoiled for choices. Everything tastes authentic and scrumptious. The restaurant is run by managers who do not hesitate to greet and assist and their staff who gives prompt attention and superb service. If not for our dinners already scheduled for the duration of our stay, we will not hesitate to try their dinner buffet as well. We're sure it will be equally delectable.

Great selection and beautifully spread out. The lighting is great for photos. The food is very good here. They did cultural dishes well spanning from Pancakes and Waffles to Congee. It's a bit pricey but worth it if you pack in the calories during breakfast. Nice touch having wheatgrass and aloe shots available.

The Melt is the only breakfast venue opened at the Mandarin Oriental. I thought that $400/night would get you complimentary breakfast, but nope. The Melt is a buffet style restaurant and at $53 SGD a person, it's a very pricey breakfast. There's a wide selection of food to fit all kinds of eating habits. But I wasn't thoroughly impressed with anything in particular; I'd recommend getting breakfast via room service instead.

Arrrrr! T'was here at t'first tide of ye year, a fancy meal with me matey. Me and me hearties exchanged 108 dubloons for ye new 'ear's brunch, forsaking ye unlimited drinks (sparkling wine or champagne, pah! Only rum will do for this lassie!). Grub only, but me and me laddie had ye good 3 turns of ye olde hourglass 'ere.Ye chest o' seafood was filled with loot from ye se'en seas, oysters, mussels, scallops, crabs and lobsters. Now, me 'ave no taste for the clawed creatures, for they bring danger to me pirate's tongue, but me matey gave an Arrrrrrrr of approval. Oysters and mussels were fresh as ye sweet ones from ye Caspian sea.Meats were a'plenty, those landlubbers got it good in their bones. Ye beef cheek and ye steak were as soft as a fine lassie's bosom. A giant slab of veal reminded me of me fair maiden, and was wonderful on me tongue. But ye best of the loot t'was ye desserts. Blimey! Cakes after cakes, all shiny like ye oyster. Chocolate sculptures which me pilfered, crepes which me pillaged. Me and me matey had a good time plunderin' ye dessert section.T'was a good port-o-call, me thinks, and a fine meal for this corsair. Yo ho ho and a bottle of rum! Arrrr!

This review is based on breakfast 4 days in a row while staying at the hotel.  Yowza - the buffet is probably second best to what I've had at the Shangra-La in Shanghai.  Food from all over the world, all of it good.  Want museli?  They have two kinds.  Yogurt?  4 or 5, all homemade.  Indian, Chinese, Japanese, American?  Yup.  All sorts of breads, muffins, juices, fruits.... Only thing I didn't see was oatmeal (so I had congee... they had 2 or 3 kinds, with all sorts of toppings).  I ate way too much every day.I would imagine if I was paying for it (it was included in my room, and I wasn't paying for that myself!) I'd find something elsewhere, since I'd have to guess that on its own it's outrageously priced... but if you're looking for a hotel with a phenomenal breakfast buffet, this place hits the spot.

Freshly arrived from London (and jet-lagged), this was the first place M & I went to unwind and catch up. It is very schmancy and very posh, might I say.We had the Champagne Brunch ($138++), and dove straight into the cheeses and seafood and pâté (a very huge luxurious spread, I must say) before peeking around at the Indian, Italian, Dim Sum, Wagyu beef and Foie Gras stations (oh la la!) and getting our fill of Moët & Chandon... burp!The $138++ price tag does come off as a little extravagant, but oodles of culinary (and bubbly) enjoyment abounds and awaits you! Never regretted the experience we enjoyed here.

I struggled about what rating to give this one, and finally went for 3 stars, which I interpret strictly as "A-OK."  Let me tell you why.  The positives:There is a pretty good selection of dishes: sushi, salads, cheeses, made-to-order pasta and noodles (both Western and Asian styles), carving station for roast beef and chicken, hot dishes (in Western, Chinese, and Indian style).  Most are pretty good.  The sushi was good by buffet standards, especially the salmon.  The Indian dishes were also nice, as were the lamb shank (western) and roast beef.There is also a juice bar over by the desserts and fresh fruit.  I like to mix mine to get a P.O.G. (pineapple, orange, guava) in homage to the Hawaiian favorite... although P should be passionfruit instead of pineapple, it's still good.  Unfortunately you have to ask every time which juice is which because the carafes aren't labeled and they change position.The decor is nice, giving adequate light without being glaring.  The service was mostly friendly and efficient.  Whenever we got up for another round, a server would come and fold our napkins for us.  This is a nice touch.  Our used plates were cleared off generally promptly, and the busser was polite in asking if we were finished with a plate.  The wait staff overall were pleasant and in good temper, too.The negatives:We went for lunch on a Friday, with a reservation at noon.  We arrived at 11:59 (yeah, I checked the clock on my phone) and were asked to wait because the buffet doesn't start until noon.  Um... OK.  We weren't the only people there, but there certainly was plenty of room for the few people who were waiting.The desserts were not as impressive as we expected, despite the apparent selection.  The waffle was awfully spongy without any crisp to it (even when it just came from the iron). The cakes were stiff and dry (even ones that should be cream cakes).  The panna cotta was salty.  The one highlight was the apple crumble with vanilla ice cream... which isn't exactly haute cuisine.The chocolate fountain is actually chocolate sauce, not molten chocolate: that is, after it cools it stays liquid.  I'm not saying it was Hershey's chocolate syrup, but it was rather reminiscent.  I think if it were better chocolate, it should harden as it cools, but not quite like the chocolate candy shell they use at Dairy Queen.  By contrast with Melt, the chocolate fountain at the Rose Veranda at the Shangri-La hotel is really chocolate-y rather than syrup-y.Lastly, the price is fairly high for lunch at $68++, which comes out to about $80 per person (although you get 15% off if you pay with the right credit card).  This is pretty steep, even with the broad selection.  On top of that, the only beverages you get are a glass of water and the juice bar.  Seriously, no coffee or tea to go with dessert?  You are charging that much for a cup of coffee?  No.Summary:We enjoyed the meal and ate a good amount, and we appreciated the decor and service.  The desserts and charged caffeine were letdowns.  We would consider returning.  Still, I'm not ready to call off the search for the ideal buffet lunch.

Brunch can be a pricey affair here in Singapore, especially if you decide to go for decadence and have a champagne brunch ($138++) instead. And while Melt - The World Café is pricey, it makes up for it in quality and variety. There's your usual seafood counter brimming with the freshest lobsters, crab legs & claws, scallops and freshly shucked oysters. Then you have an outdoor BBQ station that serves up wonderful mini wagyu beef burgers, tenderloins, lamb racks and grilled skewers! If that isn't enough to whet your appetite, you just have to pay the other stations a visit. One of the highlights, apart from the free flow Veuve Clicquot, is the Belgian waffles and crepe station that makes the best desserts to have after pigging out on the amazing fare on offer.

This ranks at the top of my list of buffets around Singapore. I've been here around two to three times in the past year and they've never failed to please me. Always leave this place stuffed and happy.Attack the seafood first would be my recommendation on how to start. They have a great variety, from salmon and tuna sashimi to crab and lobster to smoked snow fish. ALL are great and I particularly like the snow fish better than the sashimi. Oh and did I mention there are also oysters on the menu?Next, move on to the Indian food. I hear that they are famous amongst the Indian community because the quality and variety of their Indian food is really top-notch. Personally I love the Tandoori meats.Near the Indian food spread is a cooking station that serves up some really lovely pasta with lots of condiments thrown in. Customise it the way you want, I normally go for a mix of carbonara and tomato base.The Chinese food section is pretty decent, I would highlight the crayfish from this part, can't really remember anything else that I had from this side of the buffet line.And finally, saving what I feel is the best for last (and how things should be) is the dessert line. They have THE BEST Bellgian waffles I've ever tasted in Singapore. Made right on the spot when you place your order, there are just so many things you can plonk onto your waffle that you should make an attempt to try them all. The clotted cream is really well done, it feels home made rather than something bought from a supermarket. Ditto for their ice creams as well.Other desserts worth focusing on are the panna cotta and some of the cakes.Will definitely be back here.

probably the best buffet I've had in singapore - in short: high quality food - not the best in themselves, especially if considered separately  - but very good for the fantastically large range on offer. even better than the line at the shangri-la, which has seen standards dwindling in the past years. heavy sticker on this one too, but we waddled away overstuffed and happy - so perhaps an occasional treat?they have a lovely garden outside near the barbecue area - very lovely. there's a lovely spread of bread and salads on offer; the cold seafood section was rather fresh. I rather like the barbecued section - though it was a little occupied (pitiful singular waiter grilling up everything), everything from the roast pork to the seafood made us happy.they had a european section with stews and loads of vegetables - something very often missing in buffets. a decent indian section too - but I think straits kitchen wins out here.and a nominal section of east asian offerings - chinese cooked food and a japanese section. the sushi was rather paltry though - I'd say to keep the space for something else.there was a rather fantastic dessert spread here though. the long of the short is that the desserts span cakes, mousses, little mignardises and modernesque dessert-in-spoons, fruit and a cheese board. and a waffle maker.layered mousse cakes, apricot tea cakes, american-type carrot cake, a berried trifle and local kueh kuehs - my sister went a little nuts over their tiny spoonfuls of dessert  - I think there must have been more than ten on offer.I was quite impressed with the cheese counter. it was small but satisfying, especially since none of us had much space left for cheese anyway. a pretty good range of fruit too that was frequently replenished.the restaurant isn't super modern, but rather homey old-school, good for large family dinners; it was noisy and vibrant, and everybody was kept happy with the spread of food. it is probably one of the more expensive buffets, and so wasted on me - but if you have a decent appetite, this will do right.p.s. I've got probably a million photos on the blog if you want to check it out before you visit.

I have heard many good reviews about Melt at Mandarin Oriental Hotel from my friends. So I decided to organize a team bonding dinner with my colleagues to Melt. The moment I walked into Melt, I was fascinated by the wide varieties of food. There are a wide spread of seafood. I think the snow crab leg alone is totally worth the money for. The freshness and sweetness of the snow crab is totally fabulous. Not forgetting about their oyster dip with lemon and Tabasco. Thumb ups! We went on a Friday. So there is an outdoor BBQ station that will grill up mini wagyu beef burgers. The wagyu beef burger is very juicy. You would definitely be craving for more after the first serving. I would have to say for the price I'm paying for, Melt is really worth a try if you want to go for a great buffet feast.

Stew Küche also known as Stew Kitchen when translated from German is located in one of the hipster coffee shop in Singapore. If you feel that enjoying your European meals from air-conditioned Restaurants or Malls is too mainstream, try visiting here for a different experience, also skipping the additional service charges.The Swiss Farmer Platter is good for sharing for about 2 - 4 pax and consists of the Bavarian / Germans Staples like whole crispy pork knuckled, 2 selected German sausages, Achar, mashed potatoes, harsh browns and darkbeer sauce for pairing. From the look at it, the Asian Cuisine had somehow influenced the "supposed-to-be" German platter as the sauerkraut that I'm looking forward to has been exchanged for our Asian Achar. Portion are large and definitely economical as compared to the usual ones.Schweizer Bauern Platte (Swiss Farmer Platter) - $40.66The scene-stealer was perhaps none other than that salivating big pork knuckle that were cut into pieces. Meat was moist and fare better than the chain German Bistro that I had visited. Meat was marvelously tender and best to go with the given sauce.The Bavarian Pork Sausage was perfectly served in its plump texture and lend a good savoury bite with its juice bursting as we sank our teeth into them.Though those shredded potatoes that make up the Rosti may not be as fine as what we had from Marche, it was more fragrant and not very oily. Together with the platter, we topped up this at $5.50 only.Rosti - $5.50Having good memories from Hofbräuhaus München in Germany, I had the Hofbräu original. This is brewed by the brewery in Germany and the acquired taste was refreshingly light to go with some good german food! While for my guy friend, he prefers something stronger in flavour and went for the darker beer.Original Weiss Beer - $11 (1 Pint)Paulaner Dunkel - $11 (1 Pint)Stew Küche may not replace the restaurant environment and have limited seating but you can still call in for reservation. Overall, with menu being extensive, I find that its a good alternative if you are looking for more German Food options in Singapore.

Pork Knuckle was crispy and meaty too. Good price for the taste. We got the platter with the sausages and the platter was good. With cheesy sausages and mash and hash browns. Excellent platter to share with the group of friends.

Quite a chill place.. The weather wasn't too hot as we sat outside. It might look like a typical coffee shop from the outside but all the food here are good even two wings and Eskimo are here! Pork knuckles and bubble tea! Can't go wrong with that! :) and so we ordered the squid ink pasta and 1.3kg pork knuckle total costing $40 but it was more than enough to share between 3 people :P we even had extras to take home! I think there might have been a kitchen cock up because we waited over an hour for our pork knuckles and we watched patrons that came later than us get their pork knuckles before us... It was quite aggravating and by the time the pork knuckles came.. I had already digested my stomach walls!!! Oh well! At least the squid ink pasta came out within 10 minutes of ordering!!! I would recommend making a reservation!

I came here 2 times before and the main attraction here for me was that they served Hofbräuhaus Bier. Unfortunately when I got here at around 6+ on a Saturday evening, they ran out of it.Well, somehow they were probably having a lot of pork knuckle orders (I understand why) and our mixed grill order came first. The meats were ok, I guess for the price, it is fair. Next came the salad which was lettuce based with cucumbers, cherry tomatoes and onions. And then the wait began, we finished those 2 dishes in about 20 minutes. We kind of have to check on our order 3 times and about 1 hour 15 mins later, our pork knuckle order with sausages came. While the pork knuckle was hot, just cooked, the  sausages, hashbrown and potato mash was cold. Which means they prepared everything way before the pork knuckle and served it cold. The pork knuckle was cooked a little too long, the meat was very dry and the skin was hard rather than crispy. I must say that it was a very disappointing wait when this is the final result of it.Well, I'll probably give them one try again (Hofbräuhaus bier being the main reason) and hopefully the pork knuckle experience will be better and they didn't run out of the bier.
Pretty successful version of hipster kopitiam.  Has many other modern stalls. A seafood stall, dessert & ice cream, French, Two Wings, noodle stall (with local version of Ramen burger)

they probably played second fiddle to de burg in terms of patronage at the coffeeshop that they are both located.but they definitely hold their own when it comes to food.the mushroom soup was tasty and filled with plenty finely chopped bits.consistency however was more watery than creamy.grilled cod was a big slab.$24.90 is not unreasonably ex, as such.freshly grilled but way too many bones.sauce was refreshingly lemony but not really necessary.the accompanying mash potatoes had sweet onions in it's mix.a complimentary tiramisu made it more value for money.moist and liqueur filled.and easily the best part of the whole meal.the wait here is way shorter than de burg.and they are also not self service.additionally, they provide a nice dining alternative to burger centric de burg.will probably be back to try their stew since they are after all a stew kitchen.

Interesting proposition: a Swiss-German stall in a kopitiam in Bukit Merah. It's accompanied by its neighbour, the awesome burger stall De Burg.The sausages are above average. Better than many a fancy Swiss/German bar or restaurant downtown including some more famous ones, but still a long way to go before it is as great as it can be in... well, Germany? I haven't had the pork knuckle or oxtail stew yet, which is what they are famous for. Every time I am here I eat a huge burger and then I can't move for the rest of the evening, what more eat a pork knuckle. But they also sell Archipelago beer. And any place that sells beer and pork and is in a kopitiam gets a huge thumbs up from me!

This place is so adorable. We arrived pretty late at night and I was surprised to see diners dressed up in what appeared to be Harry Potter cosplay - but no, the cafe has outfits that you can wear to get in the spirit of things! The decor is so cute and very appropriately Hogwarts-like. Had I come in the daytime, I think the natural lighting would have made for some amazing pictures. We got the butterscotch ale, and though I've never been to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, my friend who has said it tasted JUST like the butterbeer you can find there. It was delicious. The food was surprisingly good for a theme cafe. We got the confit chicken with pesto spaghetti and the pesto mayo pork ribs. Both were really well cooked, not too much pesto on either but enough to give you a could flavor. The pork ribs were super tender and the sides that came with it were delicious, very American-style like mashed potatoes and sweet corn. I loved it and that's coming from an American mashed potato addict. The witch's brew, although I didn't try it, seems like it's something you can't miss here. I was excited to see another diner get it, and the flaming drink looks exactly like a potion from Harry Potter. If I have one regret it's not trying that!

Located along 1094 Serangoon Road, lies a newly opened Harry Potter themed cafe. The moment you stepped in, you will be welcomed with brown decorated interior (brown chairs, brown wooden tables, brown wall tiles and etc...) that adds up to the theme. We asked for the signature drink and was told that it was on the menu, "Mr Lich's Brewing Brew" ($15). When served, it is a cup of neon blue colored drink that looks like magic portion, which is actually made up of lime juice and Curacao liqueur. A spoon full of Barcardi 151 Rum, was then torched by the server before pouring it into the mixture. You will be given cinnamon powder to sprinkle for the sparkling effects. Abracadabraaaa boom!We ordered the 2 cakes that taste as good as they looks! The Lychee Cake has a very nice fruity lychee flavor, very fluffy and not too sweet. The Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake is interesting good, with a complex flavorful the first spoonful.Tips: ~ Feel free to pick a few props from the side table when posing with your food and Goblet of Fire drink.  ~ They accept reservations, call them in advance as they get pretty booked for dinner and on weekends.[009/100]

Being an incredibly huge Harry Potter fan, having a themed Harry Potter cafe really excited me. Unfortunately, I must admit that it was pretty underwhelming. For a themed cafe, I expected more; to see the theme being reflected in the food, the drinks, the decor, etc. Ambience wise, the only thing close to Harry Potter were the brick plastered walls... they had props, but there wasn't enough to go around (& also, they only had gryffindor robes :/). To give them credit, they did try to create "potions" which lit up, but again, that was only one drink (their signature)  Taste wise, everything was pretty standard; drinks needed more alcohol,

If not for the theme, my expectations would have been much lower. Food-wise the menu is the usual brunch and cafe fare with a twist. You can also play dress up with the ropes for Gryffindor, Slytherin, Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff. Interesting drinks as potions. It would have been better if the staff were more upbeat or dressed to fit the theme instead of just black tee shirts. Wouldn't mind coming back to try the dinner menu.

With the promise of delicious steaks and free-flow fries ahead, I could barely hide my excitement when taking a seat amongst Les Bouchons' auburn honey dining room. Although the setting is white linen tablecloths and classically French, there were no glares from fellow patrons or staff as three old friends gathered and joked nearly as much as they ate. The Os A Moelle/Bone Marrow with Toast is the must order Entree ($18) - definitely some of the best bone marrow I've ever had! Make sure you order an extra serve of thin, crisp toast too - the warm and springy rolls from the bread basket just don't do this dish justice! As far as Steaks go, I thoroughly enjoyed the Grilled Rib Eye with Vigneron Butter ($38.80) and Grilled Sirloin with Herbs ($38.80) - it was very classic and kept simple to highlight the steaks, which were both cooked to a perfect medium rare. The house made fries are so crisp and moreish, but ironically enough - we were so full that we gave the endless supply a miss. The only disappointment was the Créme Caramel Maison ($12) which was all booze and no caramel crackle - which, in my opinion, is the best part of a créme caramel! Be prepared to spend a little over $60/pp for three courses but I'd definitely pop by again for just the steaks alone.I highly recommend enjoying the sights and sounds of the scenic walk back into Clarke Quay after a hearty meal at Les Bouchons - there's no better way to work off those juicy calories, then to enjoy good company in the cool evening breeze!

The outdoor seating by the river is a great experience in itself. In addition the food is pretty good! But best of all is the wine selection. The pesec leognan wine was a perfect combination with the salmon. The salad and the fries were very good as well. The waiter knew the wine and the food pairing and made a great suggestion! I am definitely coming back again!

When it comes to Entrecote-style steak places I tend to do in with very low expectations... so with that in mind, I wasn't exactly 'disappointed' with Les Bouchons Rive Gauche.Let's talk about the good first. The steaks are generally excellent value. The amount of meat you're getting for the price you pay? Plus free flow fries? And deliciously crisp and fluffy fries at that? It's a great place for the hungry meat eater.The desserts are HUGE. We had... something. It was a sundae of chocolate and vanilla and it was delicious chocolate sauce (the real stuff, not chocolate-flavoured nonsense), ice cream, and basically it fed four already very full people quite comfortably.Why just two stars after that though?Our steaks were all underdone. We ordered one rare, two medium rare, and one medium, and I think I can safely say that they were all roughly one step under-cooked. My rare was closer to blue, but that's splitting hairs really and overall I was happy with it. The medium rares and mediums though, those were noticeably undercooked. When a medium steak still has slightly translucent glossy bits of meat, that's definitely underdone. The beurre cafe de Paris was absent, and while some other (not very tasty) butter was provided instead, they was definitely a little stingy with it.Beyond the steak, the terrine was possibly one of the worst, worst worst terrines I've had in my life. Yes, including the ones you buy from a supermarket, or the ones you find in an international buffet. This one was barely edible, and I'd highly recommend you give it a miss.So after all that, would I still recommend Les Bouchons? Sure.Great value steak, great fries, and wonderful desserts. Recipe for a good evening here: skip the starters, order your steak slightly overcooked because it'll turn up undercooked (net result = just right) and then use the remaining space to have one of their gigantic desserts to yourself.I might go back... except none of the people that i went with want to.

This was the first French restaurant i went to and was a good exposure for my taste buds, quite tantalising food. I normally like to eat steak and it was one of the better medium priced steaks I had eaten in Singapore. They serve free flow of fries along with the meals and the bread there is excellent as well, a good way to stop you from eating more fries.Ambience was quite good because it was facing the river and you could eat and chit chat and chill out facing the water. One of the things that turned me off was the service and it was really bad. The restaurant opens on the dot and even if you were early the manager and waitresses would just stare at you until it is time for opening.The service rendered was terrible and the staffs were very arrogant and had no idea what customer service is. I would go back to the place probably after awhile but definitely not too often.

Came down for a company dinner based on recommendation from a colleague. If you are need a good amount of meat, maybe with some sides, maybe with some wine, but meat, more importantly - this is the place for you.There was a number of us so we got various cuts along with a grilled meat platter. We ended passing our different cuts of meats around - not quite the best of dining habits but 'twas good to be able to try the different cuts for starters. I liked the slight charred taste to their steaks, which adds a nice kick to the bite. My lamb was unfortunately just that bit too rare for my liking but otherwise, the beef is good. You may get tempted by fanciful sounding other names on the menu (like I did) but just get your favourite cut and you can't go wrong. Test it out with the different sauces - mustard, honeygrain mustard, etc.Now that we got the meat part aside, you get to start your meal with unlimited buns. You also get unlimited salads and frites to go with your steaks. They were good, but the steaks stole the show. We didn't go for refills in the end. Expect to fork out around $60/pax. Quite alright if you're looking to indulge. I've read a couple of compaints about the service. Though the staff was quite alright, just wish they didn't make it like it was a bad thing not to wine with the steak. I mean, all I wanted was just meat.

I should have followed my first instinct when there was no answer at Les Bouchons when I called at 5pm to reserve a table inside....We arrived on a balmy, but clear skied Tuesday night around 7pm and found the outside tables very nice. When asked if we had a reservation I said we had tried but there was no answer......before I could finish speaking...the Chinese Singaporean Maitre'd said that was ok, there were plenty of tables outside. We said wonderful we would take a table outside and I mentioned I would like to see the inside just for my curiosity.  I was body blocked at the doorway and told we had to "go outside, go outside, go outside.....no tables inside"....The wait staff looked sheepish and so we began our dining experience at Les Bouchons Rive Gauche....The menu is as other reviewers have described. Beef steaks of various cuts and sizes. A marinated lamb dish is also available. We passed on desserts based on previous reviews. All reasonably priced. The wine list of 10 whites and 10 reds is adequate but as expected, weighted to European names. We ordered 2 Ribeyes, a caprese salad, accompanied by a 3rd Cru Pomerol Bordeaux listed as a 2010 vintage. The waitress brought the wine, showed me the label from about 6 feet away. I asked if she could bring it closer and immediately saw it was a 2002. 12 years in the bottle would have only detracted from this wine and I asked if she had the the 2010 as listed. More puzzled looks, more explanations, another offer to pour this vintage "at the same price" .. More discussion on why I didn't want the 2002 and after determining they did not have a 2010, I asked if she could please bring the wine list back. We eventually had a wonderfully similar 2012 St Emillion. The steaks and frites were fine. This establishment could be between a 3 and 4 stars based on its food, improvements in its wine list, its location and the fit out. But from my experiences with many Singaporean restaurants with heavy tourist traffic, the evening is ruined by poorly trained front staff and a constant push to turn over the tables quickly while playing Russian roulette with what wine is poured.

The steaks here are good and value for money. The sirloin and ribeye that I tried were done to the right doneness and came with a heap of yummy fries.Pleasant ambience and service. Definitely worth a try if you are craving some steak!

Came here with high expectations because of the good reviews but was quite disappointed. I had the rib eye steak which was quite good but the fries are burnt. My partner had the Normandy steak but there was nothing special about it other than the portion was huge. I would actually recommend just getting the rib eye. We had creme brûlée  for dessert and was not impressed at all. The sugar on top was too thin and not burnt enough to have that crackling sound and taste and the custard was too soft. Comparing it with another french restaurant with the same theme, I prefer the other place more

Les Bouchon has become a tradition for my visits to Singapore. The food is great, probably the best place to get steak and fries in Singapore. Thanks to Sam who manages the place, the service has always been awesome!

Come here for the steak, and only the steak. Our ribeye medium rare was grilled to perfection. Some medium rares end up difficult to chew but Les Bouchons' was nothing but tender. Sadly, everything else is subpar. Avoid the escargot, which clearly wasn't fresh, and the cold hard bread.

"Nailed it," I said no less than four times during my meal tonight at La Strada. Every thing about this place begs me to come back for more. Hands down my favorite Italian fare in SG. Go here, and thank me later. This restaurant is worth every dime. Sweet, fresh, fragrant and balanced bruschetta.  Tender and responsive gnocchi. Healthy, juicy and succulent pork chop. Best of all, the bolognese is the best I have had since eating the mindblowingly amazing bolognese of Osteria dell'Orsa in Bologna, Italy, itself. I will come back here again and again. The non-pretentious osteria-style decor and home cooked quality food will invite me back with open arms every time.

Was recommended by a friend to dine here, and there were really no regrets!Quaint little place in the heart of town with one of the best risottos I've had in a while. Came here for dinner, but their set lunch menu does look very affordable, and value for money. Had the squid ink risotto with scallops (typically only on the lunch menu but they acceded to my special request), and they were extremely generous with the squid ink sauce, the scallops were well cooked (not too dry). The fiancé had the lobster risotto which he polished off really quickly! The seaweed made the rice extremely tasty. It is a little pricy but it really was worth it! The service was excellent as well; the waitresses were really attentive.

Casual-feel Italian restaurant that everyone can enjoy. Same owners as next doors Aoki and Le Amis, this place is somewhere you can get a great tasting appetizer, flavorful main course dish, order a reasonable priced bottle of wine and relax. Highly recommend their Vongole as a starter and their lobster spaghetti as a main course. Not sure if they still have their spinner crab pasta but if they do, get that.Get a nice Amarone with those courses and you are set for the night.Service is great, very friendly staff.Not the best or freshest Italian in the area but definitely recommend for a good night out.

This is a hidden spot behind Orchard Road so if you don't know to go in search of it, you won't find it. I was able to snag a reserved table even though I didn't have a reservation because I went at 6:30pm and they didn't need the table until 8:30pm. If you go after 7pm, make a reservation because they were turning people away at the door. I settled on the braised oxtail ($36). This was very delicious and someone put a lot of love into this dish with the teeny tiny carrots cut up and the amount of thyme. However, for me, it ended up being more of an appetizer portion (I was hungry - Piggy Power was in effect) and it needed some mashed potatoes or more bread to sop up the gravy. I ended up ordering the beef and pork ragout gnocchi ($28) and that was phenomenal. Just pillows of gnocchi covered in the delicious ragout. I want more! I had a glass of Barbera ($15) to wash it down. I can't wait to go back!

Nice and cozy place with great pastas, especially loved the seaweed risotto and tagliatelle pasta ! The fish croquettes to start were really good tooYou can also order off the menu if you have your usual basic pasta favorites  Liked the concept and the food, although the small place did not ventilate too well, left you coming out smelling like a kitchen.

They offer an appetiser + main course + dessert 3 course lunch for $35. You add extra for special orders. Went with my family so we all ordered a variety of dishes to share. Overall, the food wasn't that impressive and I'm on the fence about whether I'd return. If I do, it'd mostly be for the ambience and service.AMBIENCE - 5 starsCute and cosy. My kind of place.SERVICE - 4 starsGreat! They were accommodating in allowing us to top up to change the dessert to the dessert of the day (cannoli). They ran out of pistachio gelato which accompanied the cannoli, didn't inform us and simply swopped it with vanilla ice cream. I don't quite like ice cream so the waiter kindly gave us a complimentary scoop of yoghurt gelato, which was delicious.APPETISERBurrata (+$4) - with applewood smoked salmon - 4 starsMy favourite starter. Comes with a huge ball of burrata so definitely share this. I really liked the salmon, which didn't taste fishy at all.Capesante (+$3) - seared scallops - 2 starsSkip this. The scallops are rubbery.Indivia - endive salad - 3 starsSimple, good saladMAINPollo - chicken stewMy sister liked this so much I didn't get to try any!Tacchino - breaded turkey breast stuffed with fontina cheese - 2.5 starsDidn't quite enjoy this. I suppose it's what you might expect of the dish, and it was too rich and heavy for me. The brussels sprouts were over-salted.Risotto (+$3) - squid ink risotto with scallops - 2.5 starsAgain, I thought the scallops were rubbery. The risotto was alright, but I'm not a fan of risotto.DESSERTYoghurt gelato - 4 starsMy favourite dessert. Refreshing tangy taste.Limoncello tiramisu (+$3) - 3.5 starsA nice twist on a traditional dessert. But too much cream for me.Pera (+$4) - 3 stars - poached pear, red wine, vanilla ice creamNothing special.Cannoli with pistachio gelato - 2.5 starsThey ran out of pistachio gelato. The cannoli itself was soft and nothing special - I don't usually enjoy it and this dish didn't change my mind.COFFEE/TEAThey serve Clipper tea, and can do cappuccinos/lattes with skim milk, which was a nice bonus. No soy milk.

Nice little gem located at Scott's Road just right next to shaw center. Love the food there - we ordered a set lunch which consist of an appetizer, main and dessert.The appetizers we ordered were: beef carpaccio with truffle dressing and burrata. First of all, the truffle dressing for the carpaccio was good topped with a very distinct taste of the truffle dressing. The burrata has got to be my favorite. It has an excellent buffalo mozzarella - thick and creamy, followed by the amazing taste of the salmon on the side. It was a great combo between the two, accompanied by breadsticks. For the main I ordered risotto in squid ink with scallops. The risotto was up to par. But I preferred more of what my boyfriend ordered which was spaghetti carbonara: with truffle butter, egg confit and bacon crumble. It was delish. The dish was overall very creamy and buttery, with a strong kick of the truffle taste. It was a pretty small serving for this one, I guess becoz it was rich and creamy. Oh, and it was topped with an egg and it was just excellent! Must come back!
Delicious food, great service. Little on the pricey side.The risotto was delicious and I highly recommend it.
Small restaurant . Nice food. Average service. Hard to find --look for it behind the 1 Scott large complex--alike to an alley.

Excellent value for money, enhanced by amazing tasting food and good service. We had the set lunch here recently. Appetizers were scallops done just right and a cesare salad with yummy dressing. For mains we had the ravioli with sage butter and carbonara. Both pastas were delicious. Dessert was a true treat - lemon tiramisu and cassatta. Will definitely go here again.
Love t wine list ... And altho kitchen has close We stayed to finish our wine & t water ar really frendly about it and polite & did not shoo us out ... Lovely lunch

Oink Don $29.00++ *Highly Recommended*We highly recommend the Oink Don, if you're very hungry, craving for quality pork and love carbs! Starting from the top, take your pick on Deep Fried Pork Cutlet w/bone, Grilled Pork Chop, Roasted Pork Belly and Pull Pork Carnita. There's so much meat here, I think an entire piglet died for this main course! In all seriousness, the meat were very flavourful, juicy, not one molecule of the variety of meats here was dry. Add on the black pepper cream sauce and every item has a tinge of smooth and delicate peppery flavor.Check out the thick layer of pulled pork carnita covering the fluffy egg and Sambal Fried Rice w/ Black Pepper Cream and Bacon! The pulled pork is the most tender, most juicy pulled pork ever, definitely took alot of time to slow cook this to perfection! Yea Baby!Sea Don $35.00++  *Highly Recommended*This Sea Don comes with a spectacular sight of a Whole Lobster, King Salmon, Squid set above another "treasure", the Seafood Fried Rice w/ Garlic Butter Sauce, Prawns, Scallops, Octopus, Egg. I'll be very honest with you, the seafood fried rice is the best fried rice I have ever tasted. The rice itself has a distinct "wok-hei", and the rice absorbed all the sweetness from the variety of seafood cooked altogether. The crunchy prawns embedded in the rice also provide a nice bite in between the soft and pillowy rice.Enough about the rice? I could go on for days about the yummy seafood rice, but! The highlight of this dish, the Whole Lobster, showcases the high quality grade ingredients used at the Benjamins. The lobster has a sweet juice crunch and it's easily removed from the shell, a good sign of the meat being fresh. The salmon fillet is huge, it's actually longer than the bowl itself!Molten Lava Cheese Burger $25.00++Probably the next new hyper on social media is this Molten Lava Cheese Burger, served with a Choice of Fried Chicken Cutlet, Soft Shell Crabs, Beef. The soft shell crab here is also huge, I'm starting to realize that everything served here at The Benjamins is on the generous side! The cheese comes oozing on and it's great as a dipping sauce for the potato tater tots.Pizza Burger $28.00++ *Highly Recommended*Brand new on the menu is the Pizza Burger. The Benjamins takes pride in making their ingredients in-house, such as this Beef Patty, Pepperoni, served with a fusion of Black Olives, Grilled Artichoke, Spinach, Monterey Jack, Mild Cheddar. The minced beef patty has a good mix of meat, breadcrumbs, fats and seasoning making it extremely delicious and addictive. This meat patty looks to be approx 250grams.Overall : The Benjamin's continue to amaze our tastebuds and eyes with their innovative creations. Definitely try out the Sea Don, Oink Don and their smoothies, I'm quite confident you cannot find anything quite like these items in any other eatery in Singapore.

I popped by here on a Sunday afternoon for a bombastic milkshake. While I found our milkshake really quite pretty (and pricey!), taste-wise it was nothing special. Basically a plain vanilla milkshake with various biscuits and candy floss put on top. I would have loved it if the shake itself actually tasted good. Meh.
I used to like this place but my last visit was underwhelming as the waffles were undercooked, my order was mistaken, and my food overall wasn't tasty.  I hope they I hope they improve.

Came here on July 3rd, the same day as their re-opening day after renovation. I had waffle with bacon and scrambled egg (S$18), which is not bad overall- taste wise. The texture of the scramble egg is pretty good- it was fluffy, but I just wished they give some herb or whatever into it to enhance the flavor cos it turned out pretty plain to me. For the Bacon & Waffle, we all know how easy to prepare them.. but even the waffle was just mediocre. Honestly for that price range for such a simple dish, I expected much more. The same thing with the seafood pasta (S$23). It was just ok only. I've had better. The texture of the pasta is a bit wrong - like it was over cooked. Pasta is the easiest dish to make with high margin. I'm sure that I don't ask to much if at least I want my pasta to be al dente. I could name some cafe that offers brunch places at a lower price and higher standard of food. On the plus side, this place offers free wifi, comfortable seatings with elegant & relaxing ambiance.

I like the food here.  It takes a while to be served, but I think their Italian food quality is quite good.  Try the pasta.一見単なるカフェにしか見えませんが、きちんとメニューには料理があります。イタリアンが多いですが、トマトパスタも悪くないですし、日本人的にはアリかと。料理が出てくるまで時間がかかるのが玉に瑕。ちょっぴり高めかなと思う部分はありますが、まともなのでまたいつか行きます。2015/11p.s. 同じビルに出来たjamiesもそろそろ試したいところ。空いてきたかな？

Had lunch there with wife and kids...we had a Cesar salad, spaghetti bolognese, chicken tenders and fish and chips.The Cesar salad was nice, a nicely poached egg on a bed of salad with crispy bacon.  My wife loved the dressing.The bolognese was nice...minced meat and bacon along with a wedge of Parmesan cheese...it was clearly made fresh...The chicken tenders were nicely fried and the fish was not touched as the chicken tenders were enough for a 3 and 1 year old to share.The biggest turn off to the place was the tables are cramped and the service was a bit spotty.  For example, the adult food came well in advance of the kids food.

This place is awful. The Aussie cheese fries seemed like it was dug out of a garbage can from yesterday. So stale and barely any heat. The wings looked nothing like the menu and seemed like it was deep fried in old oil. I felt a bit sick to eat it. Ribeye was ok , my lady thought it was very disappointing and actually they brought out a medium rather than a medium rare. Staff seems a bit green. The table smells like it was wiped down with a rag that was soaking in old milk overnight.Actually we came here because of the 30 percent off special they had running but seriously not worth it with the discount.

Conviently located in Orchard Gateway is outback steakhouse. We arrived at 9pm on a weekday and the dining room was pretty much empty. The staff were still very cheerful and friendly.Based on their menu, it seems to have pretty much the same stuff you would find at any Outback in other countries.Outback Steakhouse is a steakhouse concept with more than 1,000 locations spanning 22 countries. Established in Tampa, Florida in 1988, each restaurant is a friendly, casual and relaxing place embodying the spirit of the Australian Outback with bold flavorful food.Outback takes great pride in serving the freshest, highest-quality food. I remember having some good memories with their grilled seafood, steak and blooming onions!The dining area is mainly made up of booths.1. Typhoon Bloom $14.90++For an appetizer, you cannot go wrong with the Typhoon Bloom for all onion ring lovers. It is no blooming onion, and to be honest. It looks like alot less effort went into this compared to a blooming onion. It is a hand-cut, fresh onion, dusted with Outback's own secret seasonings, stacked high and cooked until golden. The sauce provided in the center is their spicy signature bloom sauce. It's kind of tangy and I liked the creaminess of the sauce. I felt like the onion was fried abit too much and hence it was slightly on the dry side but other than that. It met my expectation of massive fried onion!2. Sirlion and Baby Back Ribs $39.90++This is a 6oz. siganture USDA sirloin paire with half a rack of smoked baby back ribs served with aussie thick cut fries. It is an okay portion for just one pax. But the juiciness of the steak justifies the pricing.medium steakThs ribs were also tender and though it didn't quite fall of the bones. It was tender enough for me to consider whether or not it was completely fresh, or fresh-frozen. Either ways, for $40++ you are getting a decent dinner.3. Toowomba Chicken $24.90++Sauteed shrimp and buttom mushrooms, tossed in a tomato cream sauce and served over grilled chicken. The shrimp and the mushrooms were delicious. I wish I could've asked a top up of a side of shrimp for this! The vegetables were steamed and had the right texture. I felt that the chicken was on the dry side and I didn't quite enjoy it. The tomato cream sauce, helped make the dry chicken slightly more bearable.

Tried Outback Steakhouse even though I'm a tony Tomas frequent patron. I gave a 4star because Outback Steakhouse at orchard central was worth the 5 star rating. They offered really good service, complementary bread just like tony Roma's. But their food and great is great too! As compared to tony Roma's baby ribs, Outback Steakhouse wasn't as nice but their other dishes are just as good! The fillet steak is really juicy and tasted really good amazing. Worth the price as its huge in portion.

I had good memories of this chain from the 90s, but was unsure if my memory was reliable (or if my palette had been as sophisticated almost 2 decades ago).However, everything here was great, except the fresh fruit chiller.The complimentary bread and butter was quite unusual - it's the first time I've gotten black bread at a casual American restaurant (yes, Outback isn't really Australian!) The black bread was quite light and not bitter though, so I suspect it was just food colouring. The butter was quite light-tasting - almost closer to clotted cream than butter, but not everyone might like this.The Baked Potato Soup was quite flavourful, though it was a little thin and I would have preferred a bit more potato inside. The cheese and bacon on top was also quite measly.The Chicken Fried Chicken was good, despite the strange and repetitive name. It very well brined so despite being chicken breast it was very moist and tender. It could have been a bit crispier though. The white sauce on top was alright. It was served with mashed potatoes which were tasty and coarsely mashed with skin, giving them character.The Mushroom Swiss Burger (not sure about the name, but there was mushroom) had a well-grilled, hearty flavour rare in a Singaporean burger. Online reviews have people complaining Outback's burger doneness is always off, but my companion asked for medium and got medium (though the waiter forgot to ask at first, coming back just a minute later to enquire). The fries were flavourful, unlike most fries in Singapore, and crispy too.Oh yeah, the fresh fruit chiller. The only thing I could taste in my supposedly mango smoothie was sugar (and it wasn't even that sweet).I came for lunch on a weekday, so the prices were really good. If you come at other times you'll be paying a bit more.

I guess for the price, one can't really complain. The bread and butter were terrible. The steak was done the way I liked it, but it's hard to elevate a mediocre piece of meat. Salt does the trick I suppose. There is nothing special about this place, and there is nothing really bad.

The 4 stars if for the food.  We have been visiting this outpost since they opened.  Each time back we notice that it has become less and less of an experience.  A lot has to do with the front of the house floor staffing.  Our last visit was on January 10th.  It amazes me that restaurants in Singapore complain about the cost of everything and then let their front of the house greeters walk customers out the door.  Customers willing to spend dollars with only the slightest of accommodation request.  This was going to be a birthday and business meeting dinner.  We did not want to be jammed into a corner already stuffed with guests when the rest of the dining room sat empty.  Staffing should not become the customers issue to deal with. Sunday January 10th visit. Reason for visiting one of our favourites was for My birthday. We approached the guest services desk at 7:15 pm that Sunday night. The dining room was empty and we asked for a table for 2. We were shown to an area just inside the door. All the dinner guests at that time had been herded and coralled into this small area of booths. We asked for another option and were shown another booth in the same exact area. We have had this happen here twice before with deficient service. Obviously there is a staffing crisis here. No offer was made to seat us at the bar. We chose the best option by walking our dollars out the front door. This story has a happy ending as we found another dining outpost with sufficient staffing and. Had a wonderful birthday dinner. Guess we can cross Outback Orchard Gateway off our list. No equals next.

We'd initially thought of Outback as an Aussie barbie version of Pasta Mania, so it was quite a big surprise that the food here was decent, almost commendable. This isn't Wooloomooloo, but at these price points, it's the cheaper, better Morganfield's.We had:1) Baby Back Ribs & Alice Springs Chicken Combo ($34.90): half a rack of juicy, fork-tender ribs burnished with a tangy bbq sauce that was finger-licking good, and petite chicken breast layered with sauteed mushrooms, crisped bacon and smothered in melted monterey jack and cheddar was flame-grilled to a moist perfection. This was sided by hearty handmashed potatoes, skins and all.  2) Seafood Mix Grill ($29.90): a massive platter of smoky grilled mahi fillet (watch out for bones), seared shrimp and scallops, set atop a piquant mango salsa, and paired with buttered steamed vegetables, and a somewhat middling corn on the cob. Of note was the fat succulent scallops, which were done perfectly

This is my absolute most favorite place to have hot pot in Singapore! I especially appreciate the array of sauces that one can choose from (at a price). The meats are quality, the taste of soup refined, and the dining experience is extremely pleasant. Love this place!

It beats eating Macs for a midnight supper, however, it burns a hole on my partner's pocket!! :P We ordered the package $88++ for a starter and for meat lovers like us, we topped it up with 2 more portions of pork belly aka bacon! The meat is really good, if you compare to those buffet style hot pot at Liang Seah Street and if you are willing to splurge!! I think this place should place $$$$ sign on it. I especially like the handmade cuttlefish noodle here and it comes in a wrapped plastic bag for you to squeeze it out like a long woolly worm! ;)The pork bone soup that we have selected has a thick aroma and it comes with a chunky pork bone as well. I think the soap tastes so much better than those at Liang Seah Street but again the hefty price tag that comes with it may deter you from visiting more frequently than the rainy days pouring in Sg. Next time it rains, maybe you will think of the hot pot here and it opens til 3 am :)

I hardly have steamboat in restaurants as it is usually a home affair. The only steamboat place which I went quite often is COCA and it was only because of the chili dip. So I am quite at a loss here as it is a la carte style, and the cost will all add up, making it a very pricey meal. You do get what you pay for as the ingredients were fresh and the soup was premium. The place itself was comfortable and nice, with proper serving chopsticks (for each diner) as well as a common pair of serving chopsticks and soup ladle. That was a very thoughtful touch. What we had:- USA pork (thinly sliced)- USA marbled beef- meatballs- tang o- Tianjin cabbage- assorted mushrooms- geoduck- squid- drunken chicken soup base (10 types of soup base available)I loved the condiments and sauces (12 types to choose from). The server mixed it for us and it was very tasty. The soup was delicious with am initial  strong wine taste which kinda tapered off after the meat and veggies were cooked in it. The soup became thicker and richer at the end of the meal. Service was good, with the server coming over to top up the soup, check the temperature and remove any empty baskets/plates.The tianjin cabbage was to die for - the sweetest I have ever eaten. The fleshy white base was very soft and sweet. If you dislike vegetables, this could change your mind. The meatballs looked handmade but I did not think much of them. They were alright to me. The other highlight was the meat. The thinly sliced pork (like the Japanese shabu shabu pork) had not porky taste/smell and was very good. Likewise for the marbled beef. That was very tender and could just melt in your mouth too. The mushrooms and veggies were quite usual. Fresh, which was good. The squid and geoduck were probably good but as I was not a big fan of both, I did not have much. Oh and a quarter chicken was actually included in the drunken chicken soup base. So we had 3 types of meat in the end. You could do 2 types of soup but at an additional cost, so we did not bother with it.Oh and it opens till 3am, so it is an option for late night supper.I am not sure if I will come back often. I like the food and the quality but the pricing is a bit prohibitive. The average is probably $50 - $80 per person, depending on what you have. The cheapest set is $88++ for 2.

I LOVE this steamboat restaurant in Singapore. The prices are steep but quality is guaranteed :)All the steamboat items are good. My favourites include:- assorted squid/ pork/ prawn balls- frozen tofu (interesting texture)- fish-paste noodles- sliced beefIf you feel generous, be sure to order the geo-duck. SO FRESH and goes really well (sashimi-style or dip it in the hotpot for a few seconds) with soysauce and wasabi.Great place for family gatherings or special occasions !

This is a review of a Chinese New Year's Eve dinner date at Imperial Treasure Steamboat Restaurant.tinyurl.com/al53pz9This was a set menu. There were no other options.The ambiance is pretty no frills.  It is traditional.  It is conservative, basic and functional.The staff is professional and, in the beginning, helpful.  I would not say they are overly friendly though.  Also, after bringing all of the food, they really didn't check often to see if we needed anything or assistance.I never really know how to go about reviewing steamboat.   I am going to keep this pretty basic.We started with Yu Sheng.  I admit it.  We were relatively reserved in our tossing.   But we did get it properly mixed. The ingredients (including the salmon) were all very fresh.  Unlike the Yu Sheng I had at work, I actually ate some of this.  There was a nice mix of different flavours and textures.  Even though I did not eat that much, I thought it was quite refreshing.  The salmon was very good.tinyurl.com/b2y6qgttinyurl.com/av8hmfkAs for the steamboat itself, we had the standard soups with one side mild and one side spicy.   Even though it makes me cry, cough, and turns my face red, I prefer the spicy soup.  It also provides my dinner date with an opportunity to make fun of me.I am listing the key items below.  I will mark my favourites with a (*).*DumplingsFish BallsGreensBean SproutsDried Fish SkinAbalone*Cuttlefish*Crab*BeefTofuI think that covers most of it.  The ingredients were all fresh and of high quality.  i did think they were a little light on the beef.  This was very good hot pot.Soup:tinyurl.com/cmgyk5fThe basics:tinyurl.com/d6lqrytAbalone & Cuttlefish:tinyurl.com/bwhfcqaCrab:tinyurl.com/c7ap7q4Beef:tinyurl.com/crmayulReceipt (Dinner for Two - $419.01):tinyurl.com/brhzlo5Overall - This was a high quality steamboat experience with a little CNY festivity thrown in.  The service is reasonable.  The space is functional.  At over $400 for two people, I felt it was expensive.  That is quite a bit for a hot pot dinner.  It is certainly, and by far, the most expensive hot pot I've ever enjoyed.   It was CNY Eve though.

The food from the Imperial Treasure chain usually won't go too wrong.  This place serves one of the most delicious and expensive steamboat I ever had in Singapore.A few friends were invited to dine at this restaurant with a friend who self proclaimed as the steamboat connoisseur.   We left the ordering of the dishes to the host and was very pleased with his ingredient selections.  Well, the selections of the meats and seafood they offer were premium quality.  The beef were nicely marbled and the fish fillets were tasty and firm.  All was great, loved the food but don't quite agree with the hefty price tag that comes with it.  The steamboat here is not buffet-styled. It is al carte orders so the prices can add up. BTW, they do charge for the sauce and condiments. So hehe.. better not be just using soya sauce as the dipping sauce. lol.  In all honesty, I love steamboat but for the amount we paid for the dinner, I would have rather patronized their sister restaurant Imperial Treasure Super Peking duck.  If you are looking for late night dining, this restaurant is open till 3am daily.

Probably the most posh steamboat I have ever had in my life, with a bill to show for it.This is not your $10-all-you-can-eat steamboat place. To be safe, just add another zero to that number per person. Depends on what you order, of course, but I think $50/person is the least you could get away with.It's all worth it. The soup bases are very good. The quality of all the ingredients is very high. You do get what you pay for.The massive number of sauces and condiments is a plus too, they're all tasty.  I adore the fermented bean sauce whenever I can get my hands on some. Mix and match and make up your own sauce to go with the food. A note: check with the waitstaff on the price of the sauces. I don't remember what it costs, but I do remember quite a number of other people complaining about this at various times.You'll be stuffed.I don't think I can eat such a high class steamboat all the time, but it's nice to have such a fancy, well-deserved option.

Very good quality food and excellent service. However the set meals don't seem to be proportioned large enough for me and my wife lol.. ended up spending well over $200 for 2 pax.. the  was largely to blame at $78 a pop haha..

Awesome dinner with humongous proportions.I ordered a set meal - the sukiyaki that came with 5 pieces of sliced marbley beef, 2 watermelon slices, a salmon sashimi dish, rice and udon with eggs on the side.I once mentioned when you're at ichiban, its always good to share.  Now that I'm smarter, I convinced my friend to share with me. But of course greed took over and we ordered a kaisen salad and NEARLY over ordered with chawanmushi.Struggled we did but we conquered our dishes.The food was lovely though I felt the soup base was a tad too sweet but the beef was then winner of the day!Woo hoo!
Food is great and value for money! I especially enjoyed the salmon salad dish- refreshing and appetising

This is news to me, but apparently different Ichiban Boshi outlets have a signature dish that they specialise in, BESIDES sushi. The outlet in Parkway Parade focuses on Kyoto Katsu.Knowing the quality of Ichiban Boshi, I wasn't expecting mindblowing katsu, but for some reason I was really curious about how it would turn out, especially since they have a larger, separate menu that hypes it up, AND they mention the Kyoto Katsu on their signboard outside.I ordered the Kurobuta Hire Katsu, and it was on the pricier side at $17.90. The meat was, dare I say it... a little mushy. It tasted fine, though. The panko flakes were a bit too coarse and I would have preferred finer flakes, but that is just me being nitpicky.Overall, not a bad choice for katsu, and one thing I really liked was that they were very generous with the rice. I'd still go to Katsuya on East Coast Road for my fix, but this one's a-ok if you've got a craving.

This particular location of ichiban boshi is located at parkway mall. It is also PACKED with customers for dinner, so if you're feeling Japanesey for dinner, I would plan on going to a different location (i.e. centerpoint--way less crowded). I like that the menu is so extensive because I always have a hard time deciding what to order.
