In most cases, I will walk into a Japanese restaurant wanting sashimi or sushi with salad or chawanmushi and an entree. At Ichiban Boshi, I can have that. The "add on" option to the ala carte items allows you to order a particular entree and then choose what kind of things you want to "add on" for a very reasonable price. If nothing on the ala carte menu tickles your fancy, they also offer "sets" that come with a whole range of small dishes. My favorite is the Sukiyaki set. I love the sukiyaki broth and if you're in need of more broth, it is super easy to get an extra bowlful from the waiter. It also comes with salmon sashimi, miso soup, rice, egg, cold tofu and fruit. The sets come out on huge trays to acomodate all the small dishes of this and that, so don't try to squeeze onto a table with a large party. Sushi is also ala carte, so you can order sushi items as appetizers. As it can get hectic at this location of Ichiban Boshi, service isn't always the best and the chaos aded to the fact there there are so many gosh darn plastic plates makes for loud accidents at times when the servers drop things.....awk. But in all, I've had good experiences here and would recommend it, especially if you come during non-peak hours.

One of those functional spots to have ok Japanese fare when the craving arises. Dishes are executed well in a consistent manner, though it doesn't always translate into superb. Good, but not great, though that's satisfying enough. I always come across Japanese at this establishment, so I suppose it's where they head to when they feel a little homesick. My favorite picks are the pumpkin croquette with spicy dipping sauce and tenzaru chasoba. So good! The croquette is panko-ed and deep fried to a golden coin, and breaking it open reveals a soft, sweet, sunny orange interior. It's my must have on every single visit. And the soba? With the weather sweltering nine times out of ten (and SUPER sweltering on the tenth), I usually hanker for a cold, light meal to eliminate the heat, stickiness and general grossness. Here's where the chasoba hits the spot. Icy noodles dipped into a light soy broth garnished with seaweed, spring onions and wasabi... mmm... A side of tempura-ed stuff accompanies the cold noodles - medley of prawns and assorted vegetables of the day that could include lotus root, sweet potato, lady's finger or even mushroom, depending on the chef's whimsy. Service is prompt, no complaints here. Together with the satisfying fare, it explains the queues that are always present, much to my chagrin.
Nice place, daylight! Not the usual dark shopping mall basement ambience. Good selection of sushi on the belt, quick and attentive service.
I ate here a few weeks ago to have my craving for jap food satisfied. I was so full and happy when I walk out.

The best unagi I have ever eaten! I didn't know about this place until my friend recommended to me. You won't miss this place with its long queue outside the entrance. Everyone is orderly with a small number queuing right outside the door and an empty passage way for pedestrians to walk through then the longer queue starts so don't be deceived if you only see a few people at the door. My friend and I waited an hour which would have been longer if we were a bigger group. The place is pretty small which explains the long queue. We got a seat near the counter where they prepared the food. We were lucky to face the side of grilling the unagi instead of the side of slicing the unagi which was quite a bloody and unpleasant sight. You can also choose not to look up and just dig into your food. The unagi had really crispy skin and tender meat. To justify the waiting time to myself, I ordered the medium portion which was definitely filling and satisfying. We each paid about $30 which is value for money given the quality and portion of the food. Service was also polite and pretty attentive.

Oooooh-nagiAnd so, the 2017 Michelin Singapore Guide is out, with a bunch of new entries and new recommendations. One of them? Man Man Japanese Unagi Restaurant. I've heard the reviews, I've seen the  queues and I have to admit, my first reaction was, "crazy, I won't queue for that".How wrong I was. If not for my colleague suggesting Man man for a group dinner, I might have never gone to try it, despite my love for Unagi. #1 Tip. If you're going to be arriving anytime after 5.30pm, be prepared to wait. We got there at 5.20pm (our office is pretty nearby) and still ended up being the 6-7th group in the queue. The restaurant is small and cozy and really reminds you of Japan. What makes this restaurant different from other restaurants serving Unagi? The Unagi is freshly killed, skewered and grilled  in the restaurant. Medium Donburi ($25.80+)We decided to go with the basic, although the sight of everyone having the Hitsumabushi made us regret that decision a bit (oh well, gives me a reason to come back). After one bite, all I could say was......... life changing. What ever idea I had of what a good unagi should be and taste like went completely out the window. The sauce was flavourful without overpowering the natural sweetness of the eel and the eel.... oh my. It was tender, juicy, it melts in your mouth and tasted so.... pure (I can't even find the right words to describe it). Bottom line, I can see why it received its Bib Gourmand. Only draw back would be the queue but despite that, it still easily gets 5 stars from me.

Man oh man what a unagi place!Ever since I watched Friends I have been wanting to eat Japanese Unagi but all past attempts were just soso (even in Japan) and in my opinion could never compete with Western eel dishes.However, as I am a sucker for Japanese food I had to give Unagi one more try. Thank God, I did because the Hitsumabushi set (eel three ways) is one of the most delicious meals I had in a long time. I had the large set: it was way too much food but I still finished all since it was so good.Aaaaaand, although the restaurant is super busy the service is awesome. All wait staff is mega friendly and attentive (yes for regular tea top-ups).So, delicious food and awesome service: 5 stars!! Worth the hype!

The restaurant was the latest by Chef Teppei. Interestingly the entrance to the place was at the back. Reached the place about 20 minutes before it opened and there was a queue of about 15 persons in front of me. The 6 counter seats were the first to fill up.  The place was quite smoky. One could even smell the smoky grilling smell before entering the place. The place was decorated in a light wooden look. By the way I did see a customer who bought a couple of fresh eels back too. Tables were placed quite near to each other. There was barely place for bags but lucky I selected a table by the shelf, therefore got place in the shelf for bag.On the table, there was condiments such as sweet sauce, unagi sauce, spicy, Japanese pepper and chilli powder to help yourself to. Refillable Iced tea was served.Kimoyaki (Liver) ($9.80+)Looked quite charred, It was chewy with smoky although it was a tab bitter at certain parts.Yahatamaki ($14.80+)Unagi roll stuffed with pickled radish in it. Crunchy and tangy.Large Kouhaku Histsumabushi ($39.90+)Unagi Served with Mentaiko Sauce, Soup, Pickles, Broth, Spices.The dish was a January special.To eat Histsumabushi, divide the serving into 4 parts.1) Have one serving in the small bowl which is also known as torizara, to enjoy the dish in its original tasteyakumi2) Second serving, add the yakumi (condiments such as fresh wasabi, chopped spring onions and green onions). I spend quite a lot of time busy grating the wasabi. The fresh wasabi really peaked up the dish.3) Third serving, add the lightly-flavored dashi (made from simmering fish or meat) broth. The dish reminded one of teochew porridge.4) Eat the Last Serving the way You Like best. As for me, I like it with the broth and freshly grated wasabi in it.The layer of Mentaiko Sauce was a tab too little to make a different to the dish.Although there was long queue, most customers finished their meals quite fast.

Man Man Unagi stands out in Singapore as a restaurant that is passionate about serving quality, authentic chargrilled unagi at accessible prices. The entrance is humbly tucked in a back alley that you might not notice if you weren't looking for it. As you walk in, you're greeted by nothing less than two pools of live unagi. I like a restaurant that knows what they stand for and isn't shy about it. Around 8:30pm on a Thursday, there wasn't too much of a line and we were seated almost immediately. Most of the tables are cozy, which is typical of a Japanese restaurant, so smaller groups are more ideal. Most come here to try unagi three ways, and that's exactly what I got, the Butamabushi for S$18.80+. The unagi was so fresh and perfectly basted. Basically the three ways are unagi with rice, unagi mixed with the side ingredients (seaweed, scallion, and wasabi), and lastly unagi with the ingredients and with a soup/dashi broth. You actually divide the serving into four parts, and the last part is eaten in your favorite way. My favorite was with seaweed and a hint of wasabi. The refillable ice green tea was also very welcome, and I'm glad they didn't pinch on small things like drinks. We also got a small side dish of unagi bone crackers for S$6, which probably wasn't necessary, but it was different and fun. Bravo for going all out on unagi by sourcing and preparing it like nobody else in Singapore.

Love this place a lot!They import their live unagi from Japan and they guarantee that this is the cheapest place to enjoy Japanese unagi in SG. My partner had the kabayaki unagi set $26.8 and I had the shiraiyaki set with the same price. The unagi tasted really really fresh! My partner and I agreed that Man Man Unagi tasted better than the one in Japan with one michelin star. We also had mini unagi with vinegar as appetizer, really nice but a bit too salty and tamago which was really fluffy & delicious. I was also lucky because I didn't have to queue as I came during odd hour, otherwise be prepared to wait at least an hour. Location a little hidden, but the area outside the restaurant is very conducive for queuing, me thinks!

What a sinful Saturday...  This is my second attempt to dine in this restaurant. First time I quit because the queue was ridiculously long... and I determined that I would succeed this time. The dinner starts at 6pm. We arrived at 5pm, and we were the second in the queue. Less than 10mins, another 10 more group arrived... and  by 5.30pm I couldn't see the tail of queue at all. Not exaggerating... it's really loooooooong queue! It is a small restaurant, and if you miss the first round, it will take another 1hr to come to your turn. They don't limit the time, means you can eat as slow as you want. The unagi is so delicious. It is so fresh as they slaughter the eels on the spot. It is so yummy that the price is no longer important. The staffs are very friendly and know very well the food they serve. I ordered Hitsumabushi, and I love it! I am not a porridge person but i am really falling in love with this one. My favorite is adding the unagi rice to the soup, and sprinkle the spring onion and seaweed. And I like to grate some fresh wasabi on top. The price range is $30 per person. Reasonable for this quality.

Really nicely chargrilled unagi - shipped in weekly from Japan and grilled by a team of Japanese Pretty authentic experience However don't think the broth meal is worth getting , not too much a difference for the three different ways you can have the unagi and rice ; then again we were not porridge people $20 odd for a meal - hearty and nice though long crowds expected due to the small restaurant tucked in keong siak - worth the wait though!

Having lived in Nagoya, I really miss hitsumabushi, or grilled eel eaten several ways, e.g. with rice, with wasabi, with soup, etc. My benchmark for hitsumabushi is Atsuta-Horaiken in Nagoya, so it's quite high.  So I was excited to hear from my Japanese salon that a place specializing in hitsumabushi opened up nearby.  I finally had a chance to check out Man Man, and I can say that the experience exceeded expectations!  Sure it helps that the eels are shipped live from the Nagoya region.  But the execution of the dish also was excellent, with just the right amount of sauce and char.  Service was also excellent (and no service fee either!).  The place fills up quickly on weekdays for lunch, but seems to also empty fairly quickly, so if you would like to avoid a queue, come a bit later around 1.  Definitely a great addition to the Japanese food scene in Singapore!

A very small restaurant that specialises in eel rice. The food gets five stars. The eel is chargrilled to perfection, and served on a bed of short-grained white rice, with a side of fresh wasabi. The price is reasonable for the quality. This place does not take reservations so wait times can be long. The line that forms outside the restaurant on the park connector makes it awkward for others using the park connector. The ventilation of the restaurant is also wanting, you will leave smelling like grilled fish!

We found this restaurant on the Lonely Planet guidebook.  Interesting restaurant with red plastic tables, chairs, bowls, chopsticks and soup spoons.We ordered the the Fish Head Soup.  We had the Grouper.  The fish was excellent and the broth was fantastic.The Bitter Melon with Salted was a great food find. Tasty, crispy and delicious.We also have the Hokkien mee (noodles).  Not sure how Hokkien meeting should taste like - I'll reserve judgement when I have more experience ( Ie. eat more)The server suggested that we try their Porkchop and Spring Rolls.  We declined since we were trying to limit our intake of deep fried food.  I'm guessing that the 2 items we declined to order could be delicious given how delicious the Salt Egg Bitter Mellon tasted.I highly recommend Nan Hwa Chong for a novel (for non SE Asians or non Chinese) visiting Singapore.Service was fast, friendly and efficient.

Our list of Fish Steamboat places are limited till we explored another place here in North Bridge Road. Nan Hwa Chong Fish Head Steamboat Corner adopt the use of charcoal instead of the ususal gas can operated steamboat pot. It is said that the use of charcoal to fire up the broth gave a smoky flavour and an even heat distribution to the broth itself.Location is rather prominent as it is located at the traffic junction. However, one thing that one might be worrying if driving would be the parking spaces.Not long after we settled down, we notice the constant stream of patrons walking into the shop. Everyone who walks in were promptly attended by the server. Most who came in had already made reservation via phone call before hand and they were directed to the air conditioned corner of Nan Hwa Chong.Seeing this station as the toughest job of all standing in front of the flames ensuring that the charcoal are evenly burn and stuffing them into the every steamboat that comes out from the kitchen.Supposed to be their recommended egg dish, however we got it served with the middle part burnt. Nevertheless the texture still remains fluffy and taste ordinary with a handful of oysters.The plate of stirred fried broccoli is my kind of home cook dishes. The light taste of broccoli greens is cooked with carrots, ginger and button mushrooms with minced garlic.We had chosen the grouper fishboat. The grouper fish comes from the sea-bass family.It is low in fat and cholesterol with firm texture and mild flavour. A healthy choice that does not compromise in taste. Three other types of fish offered will be Pomfret, Song Fish Head and Snapper Fish.Grouper Fish Medium Pot - $35Ingredients include fish, vegetables, seaweed, fried taro, flat fish, white cabbage and grouper fish. Soup is rich and sweet.While the cloudy soup may be made up by the yam, unlike other places they were done by adding milk to it. If you are wondering about the familiar taste in the stock, its the generous portions of flat fish added to the soup that gave a different taste to it.Not only that the fried yam added had also elevated the soup taste.Simply love dabbing the fish meat into this sweet sour and spicy chilli.If you love traditional fish steamboat with charcoal, Nan Hwa Chong Fish-Head is a very good choice. Not only that, they do have a variety of Cze Char Dishes in the menu for selection too.
Good business here... call in advance for call confirmed table in AC dining hall. 1st time here.... overall they do serve a reasonable food here. Fish soup is good, but I hope more taro in the pot.

Good stuff, quite hard to find charcoal steamboats these days. Generous portion of fish, tasty with quite a lot of flesh. Soup base was really good as well, and I really liked the ingredients, especially the yam.We also tried the homemade beancurd, with chilli sauce, amazing. Really the only negative is that the drinks aren't made in-house. Service was prompt and prices decent, about $30 per pax. Will be back if I'm in the area.

This is one of the best "old school" charcoal style steamboats that you HAVE to try if you enjoy fish based charcoal steamboat.They sell many other oh-so-yummy sze-char dishes too even if you don't feel like steamboat.They get VERY crowded around dinner time especially on weekends from 6pm - 10pm. They did however take over the unit beside them and have a small air-conditioned area.Parking seems to be quite the problem here though like others have mentioned so do take note about that or just park further away and be prepared to walk a bit. Oh and they do close quite late! Most of the staff seem to speak Chinese with very little english so communication may be a slight problem if you don't speak the language. Maybe to avoid grumpy staff scolding you when they're busy, come for supper when it's less crowded? Haha.. it does get pretty hectic during dinner time! However, if you're a foodie, its definitely one of the "must try" steamboat places to visit to take your taste palette down memory lane. :)Things I normally order and enjoy - Grouper Fish Steamboat and Salted Egg Pork Ribs!4.0 Stars

Pros:  the ingredients were fresh and the soup base was tasty.  Cons:  service was slow and sourly, and orders were forgotten; some of the side dishes had small portion sizes and although the fish head was large, the best parts (ie, cheeks, fin area) were missing.  For the price, it felt a bit like paying for lamb and getting mutton instead.

It's been here since 1927 and this is the 3rd generation running the place. Traditional teochew steamboat - choice of fish, fried yam pieces, ti-bo (fried fish), cabbage, etc. Yumm...an awesome bowl of fishy goodness served in a charcoal steamboat.They also have good tze-char dishes - fried pork were great, the braised intestines yummy, sambal crayfish and a variety of others.There is AC upstairs if you find it too hot. The thing that kills me here is the parking. I wish wish wish that they provide valet parking.3.5 stars for the food, 0.5 stars for tradition! The boss himself still brings up the steamboat to the table.

Dropped by for a weekend dinner last week and it didn't disappoint. When your steamboat uses charcoal, you hardly go wrong. There's something about a charcoal steamboat that you can get with an electric one or even a gas steamboat. It's probably all that traditional smoky goodness that adds a load of flavor and depth to the soup. Their other dishes are pretty happening as well. Definitely worth a go. If you're heading there, best not to drive though. Parking isn't the best around the area.

A lot of business meetings happen here during lunch time. We got here at 11:30 to beat the crowd. This place fills up by 12:00p. Great for people watching and having conversation as there is adequate space between the tables and the surrounding area isn't too loud. We ordered the brussel sprouts and the Bufalo Margherita pizza to share between two people and it was enough food for us. The brussel sprouts were surprisingly good! A little sweet, sour, and salty all at once. A little twist on the typical bacon-brussel sprout combo you usually get at high end steak restaurants. The brussel sprouts here don't taste as bitter or have as much of brussel sprout taste as what you would get in California. The plate was a bit oily, but expected. I really liked the pizza crust. I'm a huge fan of bread and get pretty picky with crust. The crust was nice and crispy on the outside, yet soft on the inside. A little thin in the center, but I still really enjoyed the pizza. The tomato sauce wasn't sweet, which I liked. The cheese was nicely melted. I mostly enjoyed eating the crust and I usually avoid crust on pizza. Total bill was almost $45, which isn't too bad for the quality and location. Would definitely come back to try out some of the other pizzas!

Decent pizza, but no 'wow' factor for me. Having lived in Asia for a few years, I know that pizza is not one of its strengths which is what might give this place a above average rating.I ordered the spicy pepperoni. I couldn't taste any spice (asked for extra chili flakes) just extra saltiness. The pizza arrived looking promising, but the crust was pretty chewy and after a few slices both of us noted how much work is was to chew it down.We also started with a chicken casaer salad. Lettuce, a few croutons, shaved cheese and dressing. The chicken was something pulled out of the refrigerator and dropped on top. Disappointing. Best part about the salad were the croutons.We were lucky it was an usually cool evening for Singapore since there was no indoor seating. The outdoor seats provide for great people watching, but on any normal evening it would be too warm to sit there, especially while eating pizza.

Dragged the whole family to have pizza, in honour of my hubby's BDay. The StarterCaesar Salad - really good sauce over fresh Vege and nicely grilled chickenThe PizzasPistachio Pesto - interesting pesto taste, not bad tasting but not likely to order again tho  Spotted Pig - nice flavour and kids loved itSeafood - seafood is fresh and taste okPepperoni - I was slightly disappointed as the taste is not bad but I expected more from gourmet pizzas mahThe PastaMeatball - this was for my pasta fan in the form of my girl. I tried the sauce and it's tasty. My girl obviously loves it too as there was none for me. The ServiceWonderful service. It could be because we were there quite early and one of the staff even folded a tissue rose for my girl! Winner!!The Ambience - on the night we went, it was very balmy and the kids had a kick sitting on the high chairs!!Not exactly a place I'll return as the price for the food is not really worth it. It's more of a chic place to hang out with decent pizzas.

I'm not saying that this is the best pizza in the world. Pizza is just one of the many international food options that Singapore doesn't exactly excel at (unfortunately). But it is quite likely the best pizza on this little island. The ingredients taste reasonably fresh, the crust is just right in terms of crispiness and chewiness, and the toppings are fairly interesting but effective combinations. I like the al fresco seating (some may hate this as it's the only option but I'm totally down with the heat over here) and the buckets of Peroni certainly come in handy as does the Kirin on tap.Also, I've been here several times (it's downstairs from my office) and can only describe the service as hit & miss. But the largely Filipino staff serve more hits than misses in my experience, they are normally very nice and, if anything, a tad over-eager. Not sure where all the service-related complaints from my fellow diners are coming from but, by Singapore standards, this really isn't so bad.Best pizzas are the spotted pig, the pistachio and the spicy pepperoni, in my humble opinion. And if you have a health-conscious fellow diner, the cauliflower romesco is surprisingly decent. And this comes form someone who loathes cauliflower.

Being a New Yorker, pizza is a major food group for me and this place did not disappoint. We had the margherita and spotted pig, both were delicious. The crust was that perfect chewiness and toppings were also, pretty good.  I'm still daydreaming about that NY slice but I'm really happy to have this option in Singapore and I will definitely be back. PS..outdoor seating only and happy hour everyday.

Really, really good pizza - the best I have had in Singapore and this New York pizza snob was impressed. We ordered take away (they had a 3 for $50 special) and got the Spotted Pig, the Spicy Pepperoni and a Four Cheese. Also got an order of the Oven-roasted Brussels Sprouts. What a meal! The dough was like home and the sauce, cheese and  toppings were really tasty. Absolutely worth a visit. I would even eat the crust if I found it in the cushions of the couch the next morning :).  Anxious to try it in the restaurant. Highly recommended.

There's been a lot of things said about the service here, and I have to agree that it is pretty astounding that they're still in business. However, the delicious pizzas they keep churning out makes it okay (for me at least), to turn a blind eye to the sub-par and not-too warm service. After all, I'm here for the food. And if you don't like to dine here, there's always the takeaway option (within the CBD area unfortunately). Dining here can be a sweaty affair as there are no indoor seats, so come at night if you want to avoid the heat. I find it okay as there are lotsa places you can smoke in secret. As the Pizzas are made to order only, waiting times can be a little long when they're packed, so expect some downtime after ordering. The variety on offer is really great and you can taste the freshness of the ingredients. The crust is just right and not too skinny or flaky. Price wise, it's really affordable for the quality of the pizza you get. So yes, I'd come back for more or just order takeaway.

I'm so glad that this place is somewhat hidden from popular restaurant spots, because it's definitely a favorite of mine.FoodComing from New York I've been searching for my pizza fix in Singapore and I've found it! Extra Virgin pizzas are just what I look for: thin crust, tasty sauce, and quality toppings. I love it!  I'm also addicted to their caesar salad, fresh orange juice, and piccolo latte (a must-try).ServiceI've only been here a few times and the wait staff remembered me and my order!  The food also is extremely fast.  I've been in and out here in 40 minutes flat.  Considering most pizza places take at least 30 to get a pie out, I was impressed.DecorIt's all outdoor, which I can see may be a bit of a problem for some people.  I say just go at night and avoid the drinking/smoking afterwork crowd.

Ya know, this place could be a 5-star if it tried... the pizza is pretty good, not NY good, but pretty damn good for Singapore with a thin (but not too thin) wood fired base, a variety of toppings and not ridiculous pricing... however the service stinks! Went on Friday lunchtime, joined the queues (rookie error going at 12.30 on a Friday) and was seated after about 15 minutes (so not too bad). However getting menus was something we had to ask for, and after placing our order, it took over 15 minutes for 2 glasses of house white wine to arrive - and this after asking 4 different staff members (including the manager) if we could be served! I don't understand how hard it is to pour 2 glasses of wine? Especially by this stage the place was not jam packed full either... Staff looked stressed and unprepared (once again, not sure why, it wasn't overly busy at this stage) and once our glasses were empty, there was no offer to get us another? I really don't understand this, such a simple easy upsell opportunity and one that many mid-tier restaurants seem to miss... I noted that 4 other diners also had some sort of follow up or complaint they had to do with staff members so I don't believe I'm a solo case. The pizza itself was good (we had the meat one) and we also had a caprese salad which was decent, with both the mozarella and the tomatoes packing some flavour. Frustratingly, I would eat there again as the finished product is good, but however I know now to order my drink before I'm even seated!

For a full review, please visit: urbanjourney.com/food-an…When judging a pizza you have to start with the basics: Pizza Margherita ($16).  This pizza passed our test with flying colors, so, since then we have also tried our luck with several other versions that we would highly recommend, including the Mushroom Bianco ($22), Spicy Pepperoni ($24), and Meatball ($24).  If you're in the mood for something other than pizza, the veal and ricotta meatballs are also great.Picture this: the cheese is hot enough where it's not running off the slice but has the perfect texture, so when you bite it, it follows and does not create a mess.  The tomato sauce is not only that perfect blend of salty and sweet, but there's enough to make for proportionate tasting between the 3 key ingredients.  Plus, the dough cooks beautifully and at the right temperature in their woodstone ovens, making the perfect base and backbone of the pie. In our mind, a city can't be "cosmopolitan" or "cool" if it can't get a pizza right.  But with the addition of Extra Virgin, that's one more stamp of approval for Singapore.

Was searching for cafe with airconditioning in Katong and this was one of those that came up. Great ambience, good coffee, delicious waffles, fabulous airconditioning. Came across their shop name in some coffee/food guide online and realized this was a branch of the original shop in Duxton. It's located in a relatively new Hotel cum tiny Mall. Katong area is known for its tough/painful parking experience. Was really surprised to find many parking lots in the mall/hotel outdoor parking. Major plus point. Another mall slightly further up, 112 Katong, parking is a complete pain. Ordered a Latte, Mocha, Almond Roasted Latte, Orange Juice and two waffles for about $50. Pretty pricey but definitely not a deterrence to many. The shop was running full for the two hours that we were there. The coffee were fragrant and absolutely delicious, the strength of coffee and balance of milk is awesome. The waffles were really good too.Would definitely recommend this place for all the factors (coffee, food, aircon, parking). One star short for the high price tag.

Just about average - coffee acceptable but nothing to write home about, food options similarly a bit bland. Prices actually quite decent, friendly service is a redeeming factor. I kind of prefer the cafe upstairs tbh.

This is my favourite cafe! No qualms about this. It is so underrated. They sell food with a heart. It is moderately priced but the portions are good. Non pretentious and honestly tasty food. I love the handmade granola bowl and warm oats with fresh fruits. I was also once addicted to their bacon aglio olio. The caramel cappucino and roasted almond latte literally soothe your soul. The Katong branch is rather quiet during weekday evenings and exceptionally crowded on weekends. But this place is an AWESOME gem.

The eastern branch of their original outlet at Duxton, this outlet does not disappoint. Generous portions, great breads and I do love a good homemade hollandaise sauce. They are also very accommodating in customizing my orders, which is great.Love their coffees too, which is rich, robust and full-bodied. None of that tannic aftertaste. On lucky days, you may also get homemade yummy baked goods from the owner's mum secret recipe. The only thing gripe I have about this place is that it is located within a mall, which takes away a lot of its personality, unlike its sister outlet at Duxton. You'll be surprised how busy it gets with the expat crowd who lives in the east every morning, even on weekdays.

Quite a few people were sad when they left their Everitt Road location, so I'm glad that these guys have resurfaced in the neighbourhood! Well kinda... it's not EXACTLY the same, but Katong's just down the road, right? This new spot in a spiffy new mall, and it's not the most obvious, but it seems like that how cafes like it now... if you're coming in by East Coast Road/"The Roxy Square Side*", then you'll want to walk the the other end of NTUC Finest. If you're coming in from Marine Parade/"The Parkway Parade Side*", then you're looking to go one level down from the street. It's a decent 40-ish seater spot, so you're all right to come by unannounced... for a while, before it's discovered by the hoards.They've got a more generous menu akin to the mothership in Duxton, so that's a welcome upgrade from RG. I got some Crispy Corn Croquettes with my capp this morning, and that made for a fun snack. The croquettes come with a deadly Japanese sesame salad dressing as a dipping sauce - I'm a mad sucker for that stuff, so I gobbled it all up.Lots of expats here too (it's Katong lah) so it makes for a cool people-watching spot as you pretend to tap away at your keyboard!

Meh... I'm underwhelmed by the $8 root beer float. I ran out of root beer before my ice cream melted. Having 'fun' trying to eat the remaining ice cream with a straw as apparently a spoon was too far fetched. Ditto the missing napkins. Maybe this is meant ironically and also sustainable spiel?

The cafe smelled amazing. All you could smell walking into the cafe was truffle oil. Me - truffle fan - was overjoyed. The menu was pretty enticing too. Lots of great brunch choices. The sour-faced cashier took our order not too willingly. Coffee we got were flat whites. Can't go wrong with them. They were made pretty well except that it was served in a cup slightly bigger than an expresso cup. Size wise, disappointing for the $5 price tag. The food arrived pretty soon after. I had the croque madame, a sunny side up on top of two dry and thick pieces of bread with ham bacon and a measly amount of cheese. This is not how you do a croque Madame. No way. The cheese was pathetic, they were so stingy with it that it didn't even ooze out. Usually a croque Madame would have some béchamel sauce and cheese melted on it. Nope. This was dry, tasteless and not worth $16. The sarnies I make (and I don't cook much) are way better. Really not cool to disappoint someone who wanted great brunch. My friend had the poached eggs with smoked salmon and hollandaise sauce. The sauce was not too bad but the eggs were overcooked. No runny egg yolks oozing out when you cut them. Well, isn't the runnier texture the point of poached eggs? We got the chicken wings too. These were just battered wings that were deep fried without any seasoning. It was a what the... moment when we bit into the chicken. Unforgivable. My take: if you want to be a coffee joint, then stick to it. Don't offer food you don't know or can't make well. The coffee here, yes. The food, never again. The cashier could do with a smile on her face too.

Poached eggs on thick toast, salmon. Love the hollandaise sauce.Big plate - poached eggs, brioche, sausage, bacon, salad and mushrooms. I wouldn't call the toasted white bread a brioche. A bit disappointed.Roasted almond latte - nice flavour. Poor latte art compared to chock full of beans.Americano with extra shotStill prefer chock full of beans.

I love this place in the mornings.I had an assignment that lasted a week that involved a stay in Katong V hotel, and where do I hang out for my coffee fixes?Group therapy.A little too cosy when its packed,  but hey, as long as I get my cuppa, I'm happy and I give hugs.Had a number of chances to try their dishes and kept coming back for more. My highlight of the day was my pulled pork sandwich. I asked for takeout and even with that, I had people coming up to me exclaiming "oh my god! It looks so yummy!"  to proclaiming "I have to try this!!"And the best part was I haven't even taken it out of the plastic box. Cheese baked on top of the pulled pork with mustard, and pretzel buns. The roof of my mouth was sore because of the bun but... Oh my glob.... The pork.Another day I came back and had the pancakes. Oh my glob. It was lovely. And the honey comb bits?  Ingenious.

Nice cosy cafe to chill out. Relatively quiet as the mall is away from the main buzz. Love the wooden and rustic / industrial look. Coffee was good and a good selection of cakes and eats. Prices are reasonable as well.

We visited the other Group Therapy a while back and really liked it - we had high expectations for this morning's visit to the one in the east and were not disappointed. The food was excellent, the service fast and the place is very family friendly (we travel with two little ones). We both had the poached eggs and everything about them was very good - the salmon and hollandaise were both really tasty. I really appreciated the service as well - they were very happy to split an orange juice for our kids, brought an extra plate for them to split a waffle without us asking and said hello to them every time they walked by to deliver food. There were several families out for breakfast with wee ones and it is obvious they don't mind catering to a family clientele.  We will definitely go back!  Looked like a fun place to grab dinner or a glass of wine in the evening too.

Just came back for a third time. The Roasted Almond Latte is even better the Caramel Cappuccino, who da thunk? Everything I said in my previous review remains. Some of the dishes: poached eggs and the Pancakes, can be a little filling (difficult to go finish). Overall, a top-notch cafe.

2.5 StarThe only reason we are here at No Signboard Seafood is because of the location.. This place just feels like a tourist trap...I really don't like wait staff trying to push me to order something crazily expensive with shark fin or what not.. I know what I want and the only reason I am here is for the Chili Crab..Chili Crab here definitely not cheap, but I find the sauce deliciously good.... sweet and with just a hint of spiciness and so thick and sinfully tasty. I can eat the sauce alone with buns or rice..Stir Fried Vegetable with garlic is standard... at least I don't feel too guilty just eating the crab..I doubt I would come back to No Signboard for a repeat visit. * The huge patio in the front is amazing nice with a great view of the harbour!

I'm surprised that this place is so expensive and so popular because honestly i've definitely had a lot better seafood. it's true that we didnt order their white pepper crab but their chili crab, but come on, you shoudnt really mess up chili crab in a seafood restaurant. the sauce was way too sweet and not spicy enough. The portions here are also really tiny. We had the chinese water cress malay style (fantastic), sweet fried squid (okay), noodles (good) and broiled shrimp with this soy sauce that was pretty boring. I've had better.

I went here with a group of friends for dinner. None of us had been here before and had read mixed reviews regarding the food and service, but figured it was worth a shot. The place was fairly busy and despite the somewhat expensive menu, seemed family friend (read: lots of kids). The menu seemed 'standard Asian', there was nothing about the place that seemed special.I ordered the white pepper crab and a side of veggies to share with my boyfriend. The side of veggies (well, veggie, because we were asked to choose one vegetable that we would like) was pretty standard, but came out a good 20 minutes before our crab. The crab itself was good, nothing to rave about though. I felt a little silly in such a seemily fancy restaurant wearing a bib.The service was really quite average. I understand it can be difficult to manage groups of 10 in a busy restaurant, but I felt they didn't even try. It took a long time before anyone came to even get a drinks order from us, and was even more difficult to get anyone's attention for refills throughout the night.We didn't walk away full, but the food wasn't really anything to complain about. I wouldn't return there next time I was in Singapore though.

tough 3.5 stars to give; on one hand, it's a 4 star for food quality, that signature, white pepper is out of the world, for a crab lover to me.  I get it if one isn't into that, so an easy 3 star for those differing tastes but if you're as pumped as i am, it's a 4.but for service, how hard is it to ask for drinks/water to be refilled---3 times before a server finally does it?! sigh...the chilli is also a close 2nd, more sauce w/ those cute little square bread things to dip; i'm sure there's a name for it.And the coffee spareribs? wow, that's original too.spiffy restaurant by vivocity, what do you expect lol.easy repeat for me.

Brought many company dinners to this location and while the service is decent, beer is cold and there is enough food variety to keep locals and visitors happy it is a bit too traditional Chinese, lazy-Susan based and not very creative.  Get your Chinese-Singaporean fix in a large expansive room that is over-lit, loud, and soulless.  Enjoy.

Much better than Jumbo's. No Sign has amazing chili crab and it's worth the hefty price. If you end up buying chili crab for 10 bucks, you are being duped and eating sub-par chili crab. I was shown here by a local family who regularly dine here, so I assure the "tourist trap" claims are false. You get what you pay for.

The No Signboard Seafood of yesteryears whipped up one of my favourite chilli crabs of all time.It really baffles me when the standard drops so much. Customers who are new to No signboard may find it passable but I think those who knew the old No Signboard would feel abit sad about it now.The feel was so-so, not to much to rave about. But it was the prices that more or less made my mind up that I wont be going back anytime soon. Its a bit too pricey for the standard that they serve.I really do hope they somehow find their way back.
i came here and got chili crab w/ my bro a few yrs ago.  i found that the one at long beach was better, particularly the sauce.

This joint is one of the many competitors of seafood resaturants popping out. We usually go there for the crabs itself. The White Pepper Crab is the specialty of this restaurant, and it always keeps my family coming back for more. It is not overly spicy (as compared to the typical local favourites, namely black pepper and chilli crabs) and has a very exciting twist to it that makes the succulent tasting crabs even more flavourful. The Chilli crab is not bad either, the mantou is a must have when eating this dish to soak up all the thick chilli sauce well mixed with eggs. All Sri Lankan crabs cost $40 per kg.
I've been a regular here for the past 2 years. Generally decent service if a bit rushed because they're so busy but good food and atmosphere... However today the food and service was not their usual.

Indian restaurant known for fish head curry and other Indian curries.Tried both the fish head curry and chicken tikka masala here. They are both excellent - tasty, and a bit creamy in terms of style. Accompanying naan is warmed and has a homey tasteOverall, a safe bet for good Indian food.

I wanted to love this place. And it started so well - the Tandoori Chicken was succulent and tender. The Masala Prawns followed in a similar fashion. The Fish Head Curry? It lacked a kick. You could taste a heavy tomato base, and it didnt have the spice or excitement you'd normally hope for.The service was efficient due to ipads for ordering - but you also got the sense, from rude waiters, that this was a substitute, rather than compliment, to human interaction.And for $34 each? You expect better.

Wow, this place is very good. I tried multiple plates like: tikka masala, curry beef, lamb, and other. I also tried three types of naan: traditional, butter, and with some spices. Another spotlight of the place was the mango lassi, it was very delicious and fresh. I would definitely come back to this place for more!

Good restaurant in Little India. I had the Bindi Masala which was fairly tasty but wasn't my favorite variation of this staple dish. The Ramala Roti was probably one of the best rotis I've had though -- very light. Papadam were brought out soon after seating, but with no dipping sauces.

OMG YUM!!!! Not only was the food good, but the service was great as well. I got the Mutha's Chicken Chuuka and it had a wonderful spicy taste to it. I will definitely be back for more of that!! Definitely get the mixed appetizer as well. I left so full that I needed to be rolled out of there. Lol. Their cheese naan is great also.

Muthu Curry was the place that the Folks insisted on visiting when I said I wanted to have some delicious curry fish head. It's been more than a decade since I last visited Muthu and I had long forgotten the taste. Indeed, the signature South Indian style Curry Fish head ($22/$27/$32) that has secured numerous accolades differed from the Chinese fish head curry in many ways. The colour was intense red instead of yellowish. According to the Folks, this kind of curry uses less coconut milk, so it was less creamy but the gravy is still rich because of the heavy spices rather than curry powder. There were no sight of brinjals, cabbage or tomatoes but ladyfingers and the piquant pineapple slices. Those who are adverse to spicy food will be able to handle this pot easily as the curry is NOT spicy at all. No sweat.We all love the gravy and could ladle it non-stop onto the fragrant Dum Bryani ($4/head) or white rice ($3/head), though the fish was not too fresh that day. If the menu looks Greek to those who seldom have Indian food, there is also display counter where one can pick whatever food that looks tantalizing. The Mysore mutton ($11) was too tough but the Tandoori Chicken (below), chicken marinated in yoghurt, was smoky and flavorful. As a big fan of Indian Vegetarian food, I love all sorts of creamy paneers and Daals. But I decided to ditch the gravy laden veggies and try something new. The Vegetable Sheesh Kebab $9 was a mistake because it turned out to be dry rolls of mixed vegetable potato pattie, though the accompanying green sauce was zingy enough to perk the tastebuds. But the Gobi Manchurian ($9) turned out to be one of my favourite dish that night. Didn't know that it was actually an Indian Chinese fusion dish. Perhaps the Chinese aspect comes from the cooking method--coating the cauliflowers in batter and deep fry just like Sweet and Sour Fish. They are later sauteed in soy and chilli sauce. Not spicy but super sour.Another first try is the Peshwari Naan ($5), a sweet naan in coated with almonds. The Folks commented it was strange to have sweet naan with savoury curry but I thought it was a nice balance to offset all the savoury food. So I rejoiced when I could have the entire naan all myself ( the rest took charge of the remaining rice;)As usual, free flow pappadum, free flow of side vegetables (yellow cabbage was ok but the sautéed long beans were too salty). Together with the fragrant non-greasy Bryani rice, it was a great satisfying dinner. Even Ah Ma nods in agreement.

I usually do not go to Muthu for the fish head curry because I and my wife cannot finish it and we don't want to be limited to trying one dish only :)I go here for the smaller dishes like the chicken tikka masala, chicken 65, tandoori chicken.What makes this different is that all their dishes come with a bit of spice that reminds me of how these dishes are cooked in India instead of the mellowed or 'Singaporeanized' recipes.Very reasonable pricing for food vs others in the vicinity along race course road.

This outlet of Muthu's is probably the one that still tries to maintain the high standards it was once renowned for. The one at Dempsey is just a poor excuse to overcharge people for simple dishes. The fish head curry over here is still as good as it was when I had it as a little kid, while the rest of the dishes have not really been consistent.

This is an easy to locate indian restaurant. It is along Race course rd. There are a lot of other restaurants as well. I love their mutton and chicken briyani sets which come up to around $10 or more. They have a lot of varied food. Spicy and delicious. I often go there every 5 months once. To celebrate and to dine alone sometimes.

We visited Muthus on a Sunday night and visiting Little India on a Sunday is an experience in itself...! However, let's talk about the Muthu's experience shall we?! I have previously visited Samy's in Dempsey on a visit to Singapore last year and it has set a fairly high benchmark. Unfortunately Muthus, which also serves curries on a banana leaf, while decent, is definitely not on par with the likes of Samys.Had a mango lassi to drink which was delicious and I slurped it all up far too quickly. The complimentary bowl of poppadoms at the table was a nice touch but the stale soft ones at the bottom weren't! We tried their famous fish head curry, the almond chicken, a beef vindaloo, saag paneer and the garlic naans. The fish head curry was tasty but prepare to be poking around for some decent chunks of fish. The beef vindaloo was also quite delicious. I found the almond chicken quite boring, with bones in the chicken (I had naively assumed boneless) and the saag paneer very bland and tasteless.  I had expected rich tastes of spinach and cottage cheese, instead the lukewarm dish lacked any flavour whatsoever. In fact most of their dishes were only warm rather than the steaming hot curries of my imaginations.  Service was probably in the third quartile, i.e. below average. Quite hard to get their attention when we needed more rice/naan. By which stage our curries were definitely approaching the cold stage. Restaurant is clean and modern, and they do much of their cooking at the kitchen situated in the middle of the restaurant. I wouldn't call it a bad experience, but I wouldn't probably go back either given the host of other options in the city.

They used to be good in the past, but standards have fallen and prices have kept on rising. With so many other better and affordable Indian food available in the market right now, I'd say that only those die-hards and those that are unfamiliar with Indian cuisine in general would still continue to eat here. I cannot justify paying so much for food that is really mediocre and up till now, I've not managed to leave the place after dining, happy.

Muthu's curry was a random choice for a group of us feeling hungry after a bout of shopping in Little India. We were looking for an air-conditioned place serving decent Indian food along Race Course Rd.I had the naan with butter chicken and the chicken-65. Chicken-65 is something that you can find everywhere in India, it's fried chicken coated with spices. No complaints at all, my naan came piping hot and I devoured it with the scrumptious butter chicken in seconds. Their specialty is of course their curry, my friend had their curry chicken and I had a taste - its definitely far spicier than many indian curries that I've tried. Final verdict: Recommended for those who love their Indian food really hot and spicy!

standards have fallen since I came a while back - but it's still good enough eating to still make a visit.nam nam is part of the lauded les amis group, which is known for consistently decent food (as with aoki and their flagship restaurant), and that shows in the cooking: the humble pho retains its easy-going nature here, with not-obviously-MSGed broths cradling silky noodles and tender beef.I particularly like their bouncy meatballs, which have a good mix of proper meat and gristle - just enough of the latter for a little interest and texture.their not-noodle menu sections extend to banh mi (which seem popular at lunch, but which I've never tried), and delicious appetisers/ sides like a fishcake-topped salad of crunchy pickled vegetables (very delicious and moreish), expertly crispy fried chicken wings topped with a sweet-sticky glaze of onions caramelized in fish sauce, and spring rolls abound with crunchy skins and sufficient filling.the portions are adequate, but by no means large - so feel plenty free to load up on these (as well as bowls of extra meatballs, please).portions are noticeably smaller, and the food seems saltier/ more reliant on MSG than before (though it's more due to a suspicious sweetness of the food rather than that telltale thirst). it's still not at a point where it's too offensive to eat, and this place still certainly retains good value (especially in town) - just that you'll probably want more than just a bowl of noodles when you're here.

Consider this as the fast food chain of pho. Expect crowds during lunch as they have lunch sets for quick orders and plenty of seating at the Suntec outlet. I like the banh mi for takeout as it's a different taste to Subway. Love the tangy vegetables they add and the toasted crispy French style baguette. If you want authentic Vietnamese food, it's best to visit Joo Chiat where there a home style cooking restaurants helmed by Vietnamese cooks.

This is the first vietnamese place I've seen in Singapore... one that actually made me curious. I ordered the Wagyu pho with a side of bean sprouts (which you have to pay extra for... odd for me especially since in California it comes free). I think I made the mistake of getting the Wagyu.. it made the broth super greasy. The girl in front of me ordered just the steak and her broth looked semi oil but mine was outta control. The "chili sauce" which is supposed to be something like Sriracha was not very hot... it was kinda sweet actually. I'm used to the BIG bowls of Pho in California (maybe that's why americans are so big) but this place was meh... I honestly don't think 17 singapore dollars is worth it. In cali we get big yummy bowls of Pho for less than 8 bucks.... and you get all the fixings for free... so I don't think I'll be doing Pho in Singapore again.

Definitely a giant drop in standard since the last time I ate at Nam Nam. Not sure if it is this particular outlet in suntec that is not up to par, or just generally the entire chain.Pho was disappointing and just simply not good. Tastes were off and not worth the price point. Won't be back.

I'm not a pho connoiseur, but i've had pho in the states made by vietnamese immigrants and pho on the side of the street in saigon, and i'd say nam nam is alright! It's definitely not as bad as some of the reviews (in the other location) made it out to be though if i see a snaking queue out of the place i wouldn't bother.I almost always go for the beef steak slice pho. Sometimes i get the beef balls, but always pho. I'm ashamed to admit even though i've been here 5-6 times i haven't tried anything else on the menu... I guess nam nam is so synonymous to pho to me that everytime i think to go there, i was always craving pho and don't want anything else.Their guong cuo is pretty good too. I have it if i go for a lunch here bc it's included as part of the lunch set. I'm a huuuuge fan of vietnamese spring roll bc i love the texture of rice paper so i'm not really hard to please in this department. As long as they dont mess up the rice paper, all is good in my book. The peanut sauce they give to dip your guong cuo in ain't half bad either.Their price is good - you won't spend more than $15 unless you got a bunch of sides, but if noodles is your only thing then you won't even spend $10.

Nam Nam Noodle Bar is my go-to place for a quick fix if I have a craving for Vietnamese Beef Pho.My usual haunt would be the outlet at Raffles City which always has long queues come rain or shine. However, since other outlets have opened up, namely Wheelock Place and Suntec City, I have been patronizing the outlet at Suntec City quite a fair bit (i.e. less crowds!).This time, my group of two friends and I decided to try their Lunch Set @ $9.90 (excl. GST) consisting either1. Beef Steak slices Pho + Salad + either coffee or tea OR2. Chicken Pho + Salad + either coffee or teaVerdict:- Beef Steak slices Pho - The soup had all the usual goodness of beef flavourings but it lacked the punch and oomph that I was used to. The beef slices was a tad too stiff for me; not that it was over-cooked but I've tasted better on other occasions at this outlet.- Salad - Refreshing and had a tangy sour taste reminiscent of the Peranankan 'ah char'. The small side dish consisted fish cake, pickled cabbage, carrots and a sprinkle of nuts and chili flakes.- Iced coffee with milk - I found it bland and bitter for my taste. Totally unlike the famed Vietnamese coffee that I had in Ho Chi Minh City.Tip: The place gets pretty crowded from 12.15pm onwards with the office lunch crowd. Do stop by at 12pm sharp to get pretty good seats and enjoy 15 minutes of quiet lunch before the crowd sets in. Otherwise, it might be hard to get a conversation going among your lunch group.

Great fix to that Pho craving, taste similar to Vietnameae joints along Brookhurst in LA, beef taste much better than the authentic Pho I had in Ho Chih Min and Hanoi. Soup taste good especially if it's really without MSGAs they claim. So far, one of the best Pho I have tried in Singapore.
Not bad. Yes it is messy.The place is a little off the norm. But, hey I am from California. That is the way I like it!

Recently the place started to have lunch service. To promote its lunch during its first week till 22 May 2016, it was offering burgers at $7 each during lunch times (including the weekends). It was great deal considering that the burgers cost between $18 to $24 each. The place was packed with mostly families during the Sunday lunch time. It looked kind of colorful and bright, instead of the usual dark and loud place it usually was at night. Remember to help yourself to the condiments such as mustard and Tomato Ketchup, as well as, the kitchen towel on the table.Red Chili Burger ($24)Beef patty, beef chili, cheese, jalapenos, French's mustardIt looks kind of dry when served. I wish it was served with dripping chili. Kind of disappointing.Buffalo Chicken Burger ($20)Fried chicken fillet slathered in house-made hot pepper sauce, lettuce, red onions, blue cheese sauceIt looked super spicy, overflowing with red sauce. It was sinfully juicy and greasy. We had Hard Shakes to go with the burgers.Chendol Shake ($18)Abuelo Anejo Rum, Coconut Cream, maple, vanilla ice creamPandan flavoured and milky with alcoholic aftertaste, although I wish there was some green chendol jelly in it too.Salted Caramel & Bourbon ($18)Bourbon, sea salt, caramel, vanilla creamThick creamy milkshake with alcoholic aftertaste, but a bit difficult to drink with the thin straw.Overall the food and drinks were filling, even although the burgers looked kind of smaller this time.

No doubt about it: looks-wise, this place is hot shit. I think it sets itself apart from a lot of other places in the area because it's dark and edgy (but not dingy.) There's really cool art on the walls, and the lit up letters spelling "Singapore" across the bar and kitchen are pretty effing cool.Food-wise, I thought it was okay. I had the dead hippie burger, which was made up of 2 mustard flavoured patties. Honestly, the mustard wasn't very strong. I also tried the cheese fries, which were not covered in cheddar like I expected. I didn't read the menu so I'm unsure what cheese they used, but it was a white cheese that didn't melt very well so there would be chunks of cheese here and there and lots of uncovered fries.They do have a strong drinks menu, though. Cocktails take up almost an entire page, and my boss, who knows her beer, recognised a lot that was on the beer list.Music was very loud, so be prepared to raise your voice over songs like Peaches' "F*ck The Pain Away". If you know this song, I'd say it pretty much sums up the attitude of this place.The food isn't mind blowing, but it's definitely a cool place to be seen. If you don't mind shelling out a few dolla dolla billz to be in a cool spot, then go for it. Just know that they only take reservations for 10 people or more!

For something that's lauded as a popular burger joint from London, i have to say i've never heard of it and i've been to London twice. Granted one does not exactly look for a burger when one visits the city, does one?Anyways...Get the dead hippie burger. The sauce is to die for (heh heh). It says 2x the patty, but even though you do get two patties i think the overall volume of beef is still the same as other burgers. Maybe the double patty is to serve as more surface area for the sauce? Whatever it is... It works for me. So, some may disagree with me and some may even consider this comparison to the God of american burgers to be blasphemous, but this burger reeeerally reminds me of a cleaner version of In-n-out animal style (I KNOW RIGHT?). At least, this is the closest i've gotten to that taste since I moved away from socal.We also got the chili cheese fries to share. Which can easily feed three people. The chili was a bit dry but definitely packs a punch in flavor. It was pretty spicy even for my standard (i love spicy) but not unbearable.Huge bonus for them: protein style (replace bun with lettuce) is available right off the menu. I miss being able to order this without having to specifically ask for it and getting odd looks from the server...Another draw of the place is its decor and ambience. Definitely fitting to be the new resident of Duxton Hill.

My initial introduction to MEATliquor was through deliveroo, and after trying a couple of burgers since I've been here, I'd have to say this one def. stands out.  I've tried a couple of different ones, but the plain jane cheeseburger is my favorite.  Don't mess with the old classic, I'd say.  Their onion rings are also bomb, but their fried pickles leave a little to be desired.  I like my pickles in slices fried, not one big spear, but it's a matter of preference.  The next time I ran into Meatliquor was on the way to spin, so I thought I would completely blow my kick ass workout and pop in for a burger.  The place is pretty cool, good crowd, and nice cocktail list.  Decent prices, and solid burgers.  I'll continue to be a fan :)

The place was fairly crowded on a Friday night, usual Duxton crowd. They took about 20-30 minutes to deliver our orders, thankfully my pals and I were in a fairly good mood. The spot we were at had blaring music, which made conversations difficult. The burgers and fries look and sounded better than it actually tasted. The patty was undercooked and they actually didn't ask for done-ness.Yeah, overall not recommended.

Finally, a bad*ss blues, rock, and punk tavern in Singapore with proper buffalo wings, incredible burgers, and IPA micro-brews on the menu!!!I've found a new home. Reminds me of home (lower Manhattan). Go here. Eat, drink, be extraordinarily happy.

My British friend giggles like a teenage girl every time I say the name of this place... Fitting then, that this is a British import to the Singapore dining scene...I like to imagine that the owner experienced an epic trip one night somewhere down in bayou country and created the ambiance of the restaurant based on his foggy, neon laced recollections...Rock, blues and honky tonk tunes blare while stylish wait staff prowl the floor with cut offs and fashions straight out of the closet of Dukes of Hazard era Jessica Simpson...On both visits, service has been snappy and attentive... Prices are high for burgers, but in the stylish environs, perhaps fitting...Burgers are well built and tasty and the onion rings are sized more appropriately for the Indomitous Rex than the humble Homo Sapien... Not that I'm complaining, they are thrillingly large and wonderfully crispy!Drink list is thoughtful and fun, but definitely priced in line with an upscale cocktail bar... Bring your plastic!No one was dancing, but the music screams for an impromptu dance party!  Maybe next time!PARTING THOUGHT: if you think of Meat Liquor as a fun night out, throw caution to the wind and splurge, but if you are bringing your McDonald's budget here, you'll be sad...

If after eating a burger there's no mess, it wasn't a good burger - is something I happen to believe in. This places embraces it, and then some. The kind you gotta clean you're arms to your elbows once you're done eating. The burgers are undoubtedly quite good,  extremely juicy and delicious. I had the Bacon Cheeseburger and enjoyed it. My friend went with the server recommended Dead Hippie and she liked her's as well. We grabbed ourselves some Shambal Fries that weren't to my liking, but my friend enjoyed them.Strong cocktail list as well. Quite extensive, you'll find something for your self. Quirky decor and unusual music choices make for an interesting atmosphere. Does feel a little pricey, but if that doesn't bother you, go for it. It's the cool place to be.

Just as good as their chain in London!!! Good selection of drinks and even though the menu is small,  the servings are just enough. Good place for groups of 2 or more. Wouldn't recommend coming alone since the burgers are quite filling and if you want a sife it makes more sense to share dome chips with someone else instead!!

Burgers delivered a good taste and a responsive bun. So I give it a 4 star burger. Fried pickles tasted delightful too. I miss deep southern american comfort foods. The music was too loud for any conversation and we had to wait a while, so I knocked it down to a 3 star rating. Our meal was free as well because we won a game at the restaurant. So I cannot complain about price this time.

For a burger joint to setup here from London, they either have to be really ballin', or have an ace up their sleeve.It must be the former.Just getting a table was an experience in child labour. My freind arrived before I did and asked to be put on the waiting list, but said I had to show up as well, to be placed on the list. Ok, she was now pissed off. Then we were asked to wait for about 20minutes for a table. We got one 15 minutes after. Yippeeeeee!!!The food was basic. Shrimp covered in batter, with 'cajun' spices, (I need to bring my bottle of spice the next time I go there), buffalo wings, and double patty burger, paleo style. Sauce? What sauce?I think the beef patty was the same quality to Potato Head. Which is why I stopped going there ages ago.Including a beer, the total bill was $84!Eeeeks!The place reeked of a cheesy, american diner, with owners who have a lot of creativity, and no art gallery to put it in.Even more eeeeeeks!The music was blaring loud. Rock, I think that noise was, and the tables were tightly spaced together. On the plus side, the servers were super attentive and detailed in order taking. Yes, that matters. I still consume no dairy, so, I asked for no cheese, and no bread. They gave me a huge piece of lettuce, and delivered my order correctly.Please. Don't waste your time and money.

This is one of our favorite places in Singapore. The crowd is a bit raucous, the music is loud, the art is fantastic and if you are a music or film buff you may find some quotable quotes on the tables or walls. The food is hot, greasy and spicy if you want it. The craft beers are quite good, although the draft selection was a bit lacking. Best part is if you come after 2230 you stand a chance to get a discount on your food. High recommend for late night eats!

I love coming to Duxton Hill. It's always bustling with people, there are so many restaurants to try, and it's the perfect precursor to a night out. So when I chanced upon Meatliquor, I was quite excited. The vibe is grungy and cool, and the food is pretty decent. My husband had the green chili burger and he devoured it within minutes. I had the hotdog and it was a bit much with the onions, chili, and jalapeños, but I'm sure others would love it!

First of all, how does a bartender not know how to make Virgin Piña Colada? I ended up ordering a regular one and it had a very confusing taste.  We ordered five different cocktails on the menu and it was all D-. Definitely wouldn't go back for the drinks. We got Sambal Wings, which was dense with ingredients and not flavor, if that makes any sense. The Chili Cheese Fries was filled with instant mix flavor instead of the hearty homemade touch. The Chicken Burger, Cheeseburger, and Green Chili Burger were all quite mediocre. I give it a C.  The joint is fun and really loud and roaming with people and the staff was really friendly but the food wasn't up to par. If you really want to try it, I suggest you order Onion Rings and some beer to be safe.

Super cool looking place. I had walked by it the night before and knew I'd have to try it out. Cool atmosphere, great music, and good food, but way too overpriced. $50+ for a burger, fries and one bottle of beer is just ridiculous. I know Singapore is an expensive place, but this just seemed a little overboard. The burger was really good but the fries were forgettable. Cool place to hang, but just too expensive for what it ultimately is, a burger place. Maybe I'm just spoiled in Canada.

Michelin Star?Is Tsuta good? Yes, but I don't see how this deserves a star. I stumbled upon Tsuta while I was looking for a place to eat. I figured, there's no line outside the "line starts here" sign, which indicates this place must get fairly crowded. I decided to check them out.The dish is really simple as it only comes with one egg, a piece of pork, noodles, and broth. The egg is perfect. That's the only way to describe it and it's the restaurant's saving grace. I just don't think the price scales with what you get. Ichiran in Shibuya and Shinsengumi in LA's Little Tokyo tastes so much better compared to this pricey ramen. Would I go back? That's a solid maybe.

So So SobaFinally! After over a year of it's opening, over a year of waiting, looking on enviously at the crowd queueing up, after a year of anticipation, I finally had the opportunity to try Tsuta and it......disappointed.Don't get me wrong, I still think it was a fairly good bowl of noodles but for all the hype and build-up it came with, it didn't quite hit the "one sip of the broth and the heavens opened up" mark. Because we were there at 3pm on a Wednesday afternoon, the restaurant was empty. The service staff was friendly and explained to us their signature dish and the steps to order. Ajitama Shoyu Soba ($16.80 + $2.00 for 2 Yuzu Wantons)The soup was very fragrant. You could smell that rich umami from the Shoyu and the hint of truffle oil was prominent as the hot soup brought out the fragrance of the truffle. The soup was light and had that prominent taste of the Shoyu that just about lingered as an after taste. Strangely, I may have actually preferred the soup without the truffle and felt it could have used an additional punch. The noodles were interesting though. Because of the mix of wheats and flours, as well as how thin it was, it felt almost like skinny ramen / Mee kiah (the thin yellow noodles normally eaten with Minced pork noodles). I did feel that because the noodles were thin and straight and with the soup being fairly light, it didn't quite pick up the soup as you ate. The wantons were alright? A little pedestrian and it really made me feel like I was having a bowl of wanton Mee soup but the star of the bowl had to be egg. It has to THE best ajisuke tamago I've had..... EVER! The egg was cooked to perfection, with the yolk being soft and sticky and the flavours were amazing! It was sweet, salty and had all these subtle tastes blended into a beautiful, harmonious ballet of flavours Overall, this bowl of noodles left me very confused. When I first left the shop I didn't think it was fantastic. When I started writing this post I felt it was slightly above average but as I wrote, I felt certain elements deserved more praise while certain didn't live up to expectations, so for now, I'll give it a 3*. I have this funny feeling I would head back, just to give it a second go but this time, I'll try the Shio and I just might end up giving Tsuta 4*s.

The outlet was the first overseas outlet by Tsuta 蔦 which originated from Tokyo, Japan, which was also known as the world's first and only Michelin-starred ramen eatery. The outlet was quite small and could only sit 18 at the counter. Order was taken through the self service machine. There was no queue as we reached the place past 9pm. The place was just half filled. We were showed to the end of the counter with water served to us.Ajitama Shoyu Soba ($16.80)Char Sui (1 slice), flavoured egg, bamboo shoot, leek & truffle pureed in truffle oil Selected the original version.The soup base smelt quite nice of the truffle, with a hint of it in the taste. The soup was surprisingly light in taste and not salty, just nice. The noodles was cooked just nice. The char sui was tender and tear easily. The egg had the beautiful yolk flowing out easily, while not salty in taste.Ajitama Shio Soba ($16.80)Char Sui (1 slice), flavoured egg, bamboo shoot, leek & green olives pureed in truffle oil Selected the original version.The soup was made of a chicken-seafood blend, with additional of Okinawa sea salt and Mongolian rock salt. The soup base was lighter than the shoyu version, with a very distinct minty taste.Overall it was quite refreshing light and simple version of noodles soup without the fancy add on. There was none of the too salty soup base which I heard about.

I've heard many things about Tsuta. When you have a Michelin star ramen come to town, it's not something people keep quiet about, ever. I've heard it all, 1 hour queues, too salty, underwhelming, the worst ramen I've ever had. Despite this, I felt like I needed to try it to decide for myself. When I got there, there was pretty much no queue and I got a table within 5 minutes of arriving. You place your order on one of those vending machine (much like in Japan). In case you're not sure about what you want there's a staff member there to help you. Although on the menu it states soba, I can assure you it's the ramen with all know and love. Food didn't take long, and with the kitchen in plain view, I was very excited. You could see them even scorch the chashu for the rice, which made me think I should shave ordered that instead. The decor is a very sleek old style ramen bar.I ordered the shoyu soba, which a less salty broth after being warned about it by everyone. I will say it's passable. I paid about $22-23 for the ramen with egg and chashu, and I'm not sure if it's worth it. The broth is still salty, despite it being a less salt variant. I'm not new comer to ramen, having eaten my way through Japan last year, almost exclusively in ramen. I feel the Japanese like a salter broth but this was nothing special. The noodles were well cooked, and the egg was eh. The chashu is really good though, with well-marbled pieces of meat, with the torched marks not unlike the one for the rice dish. Overall, Tsuta was underwhelming for having a Michelin star. Will I come back? Probably not at that price point. Is it worth a try to weigh in on the world famous ramen? why not.
Not only it is not worth the Michelin, it really has nothing that worth the q! Much is said about this, I m speechless after patronising this shop

Well, first of all, it's not really ramen in the traditional sense. If you go in with the idea that it's your typical pork-bone broth ramen, you'll be sorely disappointed. If you keep an open mind though, you might be pretty impressed. The noodles are really soba and made of buckwheat, the soup is clear and extremely flavourful without being too thick (I had the shio noodles), the vegetables were really fresh, and the char siew had just the right amount of tenderness. Service was friendly and efficient. I came at 11.30am on a weekday, and there wasn't any queue. You order and pay at a kiosk before sitting at the counter, so it can be pretty fast. Overall, I didn't expect much, but I think it lives up to the reputation.

Seen many reviews on Tsuta and in fact was not too good ranging from too expensive, too salty and too long a wait etc.  My take is its good enough for me to come back for more.  Originally wanted to try while in Japan but just could not make it especially since you have to pickup a ticket for your allocated time and return when it is your turn.  Was quite happy with this ramen place to be in Singapore so really i would give a thumbs up for choosing Singapore.  We got both the salt and soya but the less salty version.  Fortunately the excitement have died down so the Q was not too bad.  I say service was pretty good.  The char siu is pretty unique.  Thinly sliced pretty elegant.  The stock both the soya and salted were pretty refreshing unlike most ramen stock as when u are done eating u need to drink 1 liter of water to rehydrate.Ordered the rice bowl too think the one with butter was better.  All in all a good experience.  Ok now the egg was a little over done as u don't get the oozing of the yolk but i won't fault them as we probably took too much time taking pictures and appreciating a michelin star ramen :).

Now that the novelty effect has worn out, no more Q (or a short one at meal times). The shioyu broth is indeed distinctive, and the ramen is not bad, but once you load it up with all the extras, it's SGD 30 per bowl - not worth it. When I first visited the place almost a year ago, it had at least 10 staff members for the 18 seats in the restaurant; maybe that was for training purposes (as they opened a second branch), because now there are only 5 or 6 staff members, which is more reasonable. Tsuta mee does not cause any tsunami!

Ramen tastes can be very subjective as there are quite a few variables.  Some prefer thick noodles while other thin; some like a pork-based broth, others like chicken, etc.  So any place that claims to be the best will have its share of fans as well as detractors, but after visiting Tsuta, I can say that this is definitely different.  How is it different?  Start with the broth, which is a combo of chicken and asari clams.  This is then seasoned with their own soy sauce and even some truffle oil.  Is it Michelin star worthy?  Honestly, I'm not sure, but the result is unique and tasty.  The pork is also quite different, as they shave a generous portion into each bowl with a deli slicer.  So give Tsuta a try and see for yourself - you may love it or hate it, but it's good to try something a bit different.

Was in the area a little early for lunch and managed to grab a seat without lining up. Went for the shoyu ramen. Definitely really flavorful. The truffle also made it one of the more interesting shoyu ramen I've had. Price is also pretty comparable to similar ramen shops in the area. I think if you can snag a spot without too long of a wait then it's definitely worth it.

The ramen was good but for the wait time, I would rather go somewhere else. They have less than 20 seats and they're all at the bar... which makes it extremely difficult if you are dining with a large party. I got there when it opened and there was already a 20+ people line on a weekday. The line was extremely slow due to the seating set up. When it's finally your turn, you order from a digital menu, pay, and then wait some more inside to get seated at the bar. After you get seated, the cooks wait until they have a few orders before they really start preparing your ramen noodle dish. I got the regular shoyu ramen with an egg (only comes with one slice of pork). The place is called tsuta Japanese soba noodle but the noodles tasted like regular ramen to me.
